comment: Professor Zheng is a clear structured professor with nice personality. What he taught in class are really practical and the group project gave me a lot hand on experience. He is patient and willing to spend extra time solving students' problems. I would give him 10 out of 5!

This professor has a clear and effective teaching style, making complex concepts easy to understand and applying practical exercises to help students truly master the material. The professor's patience and professionalism make the learning experience enjoyable and rewarding. Definitely a great teacher you don't want to miss!

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects']
comment: Kristen Lennarz is an very carrying professor. She tries to make herself accessible during times that work for the student and understands that students are humans too. She is very enthusiastic about teaching and goes out of her way to help her students. If you have any troubles or concerns, she is a very approachable professor.

Kristin's professional experience and high level of intelligence make her an awesome prof. She impressed me by adjusting to different learning styles. The textbook she chose was solid and she gave us spreadsheet of awesome digital tools. Plus she connected me with professionals during my job search after class ended. 10/10 would take class with KL.

So unorganized! Most of the class had a hard time understanding the requirements of her assignments and even the lectures. She always includes a lot of redundant information in her lectures and makes them so confusing.

Pretty easy A. Workload is a couple of 1-2 page papers. Will make you break out into groups. Otherwise- Funny guy, with entertaining lectures. Never once asked for our names tho (Pretty small class size)

This class was an absolute joke. I learned literally nothing and barely went to lectures after I realized how irrelevant they are. Just show up to the class right before the midterm and final and he will give you all the answers.

You will get an easy A, however you will learn nothing, and if you do learn something it won't be what you expected. The course description is clickbait. If you ever want some humor, just pop in and sit through a lecture, but don't sign up for the class unless you desperately need the grade.

Can be entertaining at times, but no essential material covered. Nothing is needed besides doing the homework, which isn't even explained at times. His TAs are essentially running the entire operation and do not explain anything. Your time is more valuable spent elsewhere. Get used to seeing the same two outfits on him.
Literally learned nothing unfortunately. Really nice guy, but he just rambles and I got nothing out of lecture. You only need to go to the classes before exams in order to do well.

His class was a joke. Our class was a mess, no one paid attention because he was such a bad teacher. None of us learned anything, and we didn't need to because he gave us the answers to the midterm and final, word for word the class before. He was a terrible lecturer. Super unclear. Worst professor I've had here by far. What a joke.
His TA does everything. He uses cursing words a lot but he is fun. And his midterm and final are very easy. He will have test review in the class before exam which is exact same thing on the test.
Takes issue with sitting cross legged.

Professor DeAngelis runs an interesting course with a reasonable workload. The exams are mostly multiple-choice and readings (outside of those for discussions) are not needed to do well. Though not always the most engaging, he incorporates fun examples of the phenomena he is explaining and does a good job of breaking down more complex concepts.

comment: Learned a lot from this course.
Very smart, good lectures. Take home exams can sometimes be very  hard but doable
Great, loved him!

he is very smart, but the exams are really hard. I do great on the take home exams (trust me, be prepared to spend about 50 hours on them) but one thing I hate is sometimes he is very unclear what he wants on an answer. Many times, the entire class missed a question, not because they don't know the answer, but because he was very unclear.

He's a great guy. Incredibly intelligent and definitely knows his material. He delivers an interesting way to look at neuroscience. His exams are half take home and in class. The in-class is pretty much straight up memorization of the lectures. The take-home, however, are much more difficult and require thought and knowledge of the material.
Don't take her class
She would if she was ordered to

Very tough grader. Marked down for things that were not listed in instructions. Uses a small grading scale for assignments, so a single mistake can cost you 33 percent. Uses a contract system where missing class reduces your grade by 2 percentage points. Heavy workload of dubious value. A lot of in class discussion, not much actual instruction.

This class was boring. The topic of the class was careers in America, so I didn't expect it to be FUN. Towsley was kind in front of a class, but it felt fake. Sometimes I didn't really know exactly what she wanted, but we got a bit of freedom when choosing a topic to explore. She's not a harsh grader IMO. Writing hw prompts were annoying but doable

1. Excessive homework, and much of the homework both inside and outside of class is repetitive, resulting in low learning efficiency.
2. Unclear grading rules and teaching expectations.
3. The professor offers individual office hours, but they are not very helpful, she will not read your papers or give you specific advice.

This professor was so terrible she almost left me in tears on several occasions. This class is tough but that is really only due to this professors grading. As someone who took several high level writing courses I thought this class would be an easy A; I mistaken. There is no need for this class to be so difficult and useless at the same time.

Although kind, she is an incredibly tough grader for a freshman writing class. Gives way more work than any other writing class and grades everything. Has a stupid contract system that makes no sense. Do not take this because it is not as easy an like freshman writing should be.
Do not take this professor I can't stress this enough. You will have a horrible semester if you're in this class.
Would not recommend, do not take her classes
Do not take this class!
I did not like her.

Do not take this professor under any circumstances. She does not teach you anything substantial about writing whatsoever and makes you do many assignments. I honestly do not know how she is a professor at the University of Rochester.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Not my first choice. Dr. Towsley is probably the worst professor I have ever had. She does not sincerely respect any of the students, and assigns hours of tedious busywork. We had to do a pointless "portfolio" (among other things), that no other writing class had to do. By far the hardest writing class that the school offers. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.
Fine. Uses contract grading which is really harsh, if you're late a by a few minutes more than twice your grade drops. Overall far less papers than I would expect from a writing class.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']
comment: Wasn't expecting much from WRT 105 and Dr. Towsley's Careers in America section pretty much met my expectations. There were a few big papers, but most of the writing assignments didn't seem that helpful. Class discussions can be agonizing but your grade will plummet if you skip one class. Wish that we could have discussed a better variety of works

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Unforgiving with attendance and usually assigned tedious and boring homework after every class. While her demeanor was usually friendly, I felt like she didn't really like anyone in the class and could have shown more respect. If you do all of the work she assigns and don't miss it isn't hard to get an A.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Grade knocked down because of one missed class. Extremely and unnecessarily tough grader for a resume and cover letter class. Unresponsive to feedback. All of class is dragging on unhelpful discussions. Unhelpful and unclear with expectations.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Compare to what I heard from other 105 classes, she definitely gives more writing assignment than others do. And she always has class discussion. She is more like a high school teacher instead of a college one. If you miss one single class, A goes to A-. ATTENDANCE IS EVERYTHING.

You literally don't have to put any effort into class and you won't want to because its not super interesting. The entire thing is based on just showing up and all assignments are completion grades. The only thing that matters is the final portfolio which you do in the last two weeks of class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Probably the best WRT105 session at the University of Rochester. You actually learn a lot
Really an awful professor. I left the class after three weeks, as there's lots of busy work, most of which was at a 9th grade level, and she seems to have this really fake smile on all the time.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor Towsley was an overall good professor. The class was easy, but there was a lot of work that you had to put in to get an A. She cared a lot about attendance and participation so if you didn't show up then it would be hard to get an A. None of the grades were put in until the end of the semester so it was hard to know how you were doing.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: It is very easy to do well in her class, but it is very tedious. If you are late or don't show up for a class your grade will be substantially affected. Also, nothing is due until the last day of class so you'll have no idea what your grade is for the whole semester. Despite this, she is a very nice person and knows what she is doing.

This professor has no idea what two credits mean. She gives so much reading and writing outside of class. She also expects you to practice for 30 minutes every day of the week. She frequently goes on long tangents about the following topics: Her trauma, sex, and female periods. It's so weird. Unless you're into that, DO NOT TAKE HER.
Loved his teaching style. Many assignments to get us engaged with the material but they were not too tedious. Tests were hard but overall loved the class. He talks about his kids a lot!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Very manageable if you keep on top of all the hw and keep on top of the textbook. just read it before class, pay attention, and submit the work on time. tests can seem tricky but if u paid attention u should be ok! he is also a pretty knowledgeable guy and will be willing to answer any question u have in class

Lectures based 100% on the textbook, so not worth it to read and go to class. In class participation exercises were very chill. Frequently went on tangents with students who asked ridiculous questions, which was nice for them but annoying for me

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Dr. Seplaki was a very good lecturer and although there were a lot of assignments, they were easy and online, making it easy to do well in the class. If you paid attention in lecture and reviewed a little before exams, they were pretty straightforward and manageable. There were a couple guest lecturers, whose material was included on exams.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Test heavy']
comment: Seplaki is not the worst professor I've had; he's test-heavy but has homework, quizzes, and other assignments (readings). Lectures are pretty much the textbook, just simplified (I just read the textbook and came to lecture for the questions). Homework is time-consuming, but answers are in the textbook (the textbook is easy to understand).

Everything revolved around 3 tests. Loved the structure, but didn't like when the tests were harder than any of the work we did before. Everything can be done online, and all from the textbook, word for word. He has a lot of passion for his field, I just don't think a blanket intro class is where he thrives.

Dr seplaki is amazing and so passionate about public health. Lectures are CRUCIAL to attend if you want to succeed since the class is graded by two tests and a few low weighted homework assignments. He is very caring and always will stop to explain something more if you ask. He is hard to reach outside of class but always stays late for questions.

He's available for help, but for a limited time. Class is only based on a few items graded, overall it's test heavy. His exams are very difficult and worth a lot compared to the couple of assignments given, which are worth very little of your grade. Lectures are mostly guest speakers and sometimes asynchronous, but they're pretty straightforward.

Two exams make up 70% of your grade, so it's really hard to get a good grade if you don't do well on the exams. Lectures are pretty boring and not really anything new if you've taken PH classes before. Tests aren't super difficult, but hard to study for because questions are a little random and tricky. HW is long but easy and graded easily.

Once in a while, we had an interesting lecture. But overall, the lectures were boring, and the test questions were unfair. He asks very specific questions about a quote that a guest lecturer had on their slides. He also gives very time-consuming assignments that require us to write several paragraphs, and we usually only get five points for them.

HWs are stupid easy, tests are specific and difficult. He provides no materials to study, is barely at lecture at all because of guest lecturers. Course policies are insane, 89.99% gets rounded down. Late HW by 1 min is 0. Only way to get an extentino is providing DOCUMENTED proof of an illness or family emergency. Overall, very unpleasant class.

grading system = absurd. Students can only get 100 points TOTAL in the class: 2 exams 40 points each and 4 homework assignments 5 points each. The homeworks take a lot more work/time for just 5 points toward grade, which really annoying. I'd say that the exams consisted of very specific topics/facts from modules, so kind of asked a lot. Leplaki

He literally is the least flexible professor I have ever had at the UofR. He gives no feedback on his grading and does not allow any extra credit or help. He didn't even show up for like 4 weeks because there were guest lecturers. Unfortunately, this class is required for public health majors but take it with caution.

He is very clear about grading policies from the start, and encourages lots of questions regarding class guidelines. I took 102 online and I think the open note and open book policies during tests were great, I recommend watching the lectures too b/c 70-80% of exams are based on lecture material (including guest lectures!). Overall, pretty easy.

I wasn't a fan of her teaching style (not sure if it's the blackboard or the way she explains things), but she's very nice. She provided an online link to the textbook, but reading isn't mandatory. The point system allows you to pick and choose what assignments you want to do. Practice exams are very similar to real exams.

She is truly an amazing person. Although people think freshmen orgo is hard, it's very easy to get an A becuase of the point system. the class is interesting and the workshops are great. She's very empathetic and helpful.

Very good lectures and was willing to help outside of class. Problem Sets and Midterm practice tests were very helpful. Tests were hard, but the class is graded on a points system, so getting a good grade isn't that difficult. She really emphasizes fundamentals instead of mechanism memorization, and she is an overall caring person and great teacher

Great person but not great at teaching. Class is a points system, making it easier to get a good overall grade in the class. Every assignment is optional and basically graded on participation. Lectures are confusing and I only learned the material by reading the textbook and watching videos on my own. Be prepared to do a lot of self learning.

While many don't love her lecture style, I was a fan. Orgo can be hard, but thanks to her giving more points available than possible (ie 625 points out of 500 total) it will not tank my grade. In addition when I came to her about being unsure where I'm missing understanding she offered to review my exams personally and give me feedback.

Dr Jacobs was always very helpful and always able to be reached. There were 3 main coding homeworks which were not too bad if you give time to work through them and 2 multiple choice exams which weren't the worst. Overall I would definitely take this class again, as well as any other classes he teaches.

Dr. Jacobs is very nice and passionate about the material. Perception and cognitive modeling are his field so he is very knowledgeable in the field. No tests, 6 coding homeworks, and short final paper. Perfect class if you don't want to stress about exams and don't mind coding.

This course is Prof. Jacobs specialty. If you are interested in computational methods and Bayesianism, take this from him. All the readings are recent publications in the field so it's a great way to get exposed to the research going on. There are no exams, just some tricky homework coding assignments and a final essay.

Professor Jacobs is really interested in the subject and you can tell he's just a big nerd about the material. There is a lot of readings to do, but the lectures cover a lot of the readings. There are no exams, but the homeworks can be quite difficult. I think his lectures are fairly interesting, but sometimes they are heavy on the math.
Helpful and competent, but unfortunately a very dry lecturer and confusing test-writer.

So amazingly boring. If you need to take this class do not take it with him as a professor. The only grades are all multiple choice tests-all of which are super confusing. He is also confusing during class. The only reason to truly go to class is for the review questions.

Boring boring boring. Probably can do without attending the lectures. The things that he says are often confusing. The review sessions were helpful though and he often told you things to focus on while studying at them.

He's a wonderful professor! Very clear in what he expects of you. His exam questions all come directly from lectures, there is no textbook. He is so helpful during office hours, and the class before a midterm is always a review session. Great professor! Midterms are fairly easy if you study, the material is interesting/ fun to study.

Really clear and used great examples to relate the material to every day things. Also, extremely nice and kind to students. Tests are difficult, but he normalizes grades, so all you have to do is score higher than average (average is usually ~70%), and you'll get a good grade! Also, no textbook and no hw. No outside work... just learn the material.

His commentary on lectures really don't help, you could probably skip class and get the same grade. For instance, I hardly studied for the first test, got a grade I was not satisfied. I must have spent about 15 hours or so studying for the second test and got about 5 percent higher. I'm not a bad student, I've made the Dean's List.

HORRIBLE! Just reads from Powerpoints which are full of jargon and don't clarify anything. He might add an example here or there, but it's usually vague and doesn't help. His exam questions are obscure, and hard to study for. Wasn't even around to take questions for reading period and finals! Take this with someone else.
He seems to love what he's teaching, but he reads right off his slides.  You can skip class, read his slides, and you'll get the same education.  His exams are impossible though!!!
The teacher no longer uses a real textbook - instead, articles from various books accompany the powerpoints. He isn't a great professor, but he isn't horrible, either.

Teaches strictly from powerpoints that are dull and incomplete. Requires two expensive books, neither of which are helpful since he uses terms aren't listed. Tests are 11 questions that cover a months worth of material, and grading is heavily subjective. The TA knew more than him...
Not a good teacher.  Do not take 111 with him.  His grading is subjective, and lectures are boring.

This class was awful!!! The worst I've taken here.  His exam grading is purely subjective.  Lecture was horribly boring.  The book he chose was USELESS.  And his powerpoint slides aren't helpful either.  Don't take BCS 111 with him.  Take it with Achtman or anyone else.  He is terrible.
the material itself has the potential to make a great class, but he's reduced it to a monotone run-through of powerpoint slides
No Comments
He's really great and very helpful, esp. if you go and talk to him during office hours.  I love him!
what a horrid professor.  pointless slides, tests are hard because he picks obscure things to question.  i don't even think he does research, he is just unhelpful and dumb sometimes.
ugh...so inconsiderate
good professor, interesting

Lots of Reading, but it is engaging. Can also get away will not reading for one class and just discussing topics she brings up. Lectures are concise and well informed when she does lecture-- although generally more discussion and reading based. Classes small enough, she'll tailor discussion to you. Open-ended essays-- she wants to see your ideas.

tags: ['Respected', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: She loves reading and she enjoys discussions. Show up to class with notes and ready for discussion. Skip class and you won't do well. She's well regarded.

She is amazing and willing to assist. She cares about her student and always available during office hours. She is very patient, but you will need to read and contribute to class discussions. She is passionate about what she teaches and I took five classes with her. She knows me well and I know her very well!!
Love her. She can be a little absent-minded, but she's the best professor ever and the coolest person I know. If you try hard, and don't screw around, you'll do well.
Course materials horribly hard. RUN if you are taking for credits

by far the hardest ECON class out there...too bad its required for the major..but Dahl i feel does a decent job teaching the tedious and boring material...paper is very interesting and its agreed that you'll learn more from the paper than from the book or class...plan to spend a lot of time learning the material, 1st weeks of sem. is eco 230 review
Great guy, but makes lots of mistakes! Sometimes there will be glaring errors on the board and he'll correct the less important ones. "Oops, forgot the i-subscript."

Class was hard, because Dahl assumes that you've read and re-read and re-read the material before he ever showed it to you. If you're lucky your TA will be helpful, otherwise your screwed. This class is required so take it as soon as you can before senior year.

Econometrics was really easy for me since I have a math background and enjoy economics, but Dahl is a good teacher.  Class was straight forward, I always got help when I went to talk about the research paper and had him as my advisor for a short time.

For people interested in a future in Economics or Finance, it's a must. Too much memorization, should be more analytical. Homework grades based on 1-2 random ?'s. Exams are tough & overweighted. Paper is the most informative part of the class, Dahl doesn't let students pick own topic though.
No Comments
His classes were very engaging and he made sure that students understand each and every thing.

Prof. Bernal was really great - he offered many materials to get students up to speed even if they did not have necessary prerequisites and was often available outside of class (even after the semester ended!). Given his experience in industry, the class also highlighted the DL techniques currently in use and offered many guest lectures.

Prof Bernal is really nice and full of sarcasm! He makes the material very accessible and helped me with deep learning even after the class ended and he had no obligation to do so. That says a lot about a professor! Also, there are tons of extra credit opportunities for undergraduates if they are inclined to compete graduate assignments.

Prof Bernal was really great. He prepared for lectures well and poured a lot of effort into preparing slides and code for lecture. He also provided a fair bit of code for the homework to get students started and was always reachable through email with a response time of 30 mins on average. I would highly recommend you take his course!

Do not take this class. He is not even a professor. Worst course ever! Grading is very subjective. he is busy with rationalizing the grading. You can learn deep learning in youtube. homework called "project" never helpful. If many friends in your class, you'll get a fabulous grade by sharing answers with each other. He never cares.

Prof Pye is very kind and understanding. The class is well organized and information is shared clearly. He's a generous grader and it's easy to get a good grade if you put some work in. Make sure to participate in class, though. I honestly have no complaints about him he's all around a nice person and good professor.

Prof. Pye is genuinely such a nice guy. The biggest thing is he gives exams every 2-3 weeks which can be a pain. There's a lot of work for Spanish 101 but I learned a LOT. No final and its a fairly easy class if you stay on top of the work.

The lectures for BUS118 are pretty chill. Professor is also a very nice person and classes tend to be interactive. He grades the homework and exams VERY generously. As long as you don't write misinformation then you will be solid. Minimal work required compared to other classes: 1 easy midterm, 5 very short writings, and 1 term paper.
I literally learned nothing from this class, and the attendance is mandatory. Just don't take this class.
Never take his class
Funny, intelligent, and interesting. Lectures were always involving and very tangible.
He makes the subject very interesting. One of the best professors I've ever had.

He teches right off the book. The only good part of the class is the presentation...u actually learn....he doesn't teach you to help you on the homework but the hw is grade ez...the final is a killer if u fail it u do really bad...it was ez clss until after the class....he laughs alot and has no incentive to help
He got his PhD from MIT but it doesn't mean he is brilliant:)..He follows everything on the book, nothing comes from his own mind...
keeps your attention during lecture, even though it's basic stuff from the textbook. You can tell he's brilliant.

Took this class on a whim and loved it. Your grade is composed of participation, 2 essays and 1 final project. She is teaching her research so it really laid-back. You watch 1 film a week. Discussions in class are more about the historical climates and director's influences, not the technical cinematic choices. Take if looking for an easy class.

Rita Safariants is one of the newer faculty members in the MLC department and one of the best professors I have taken. Insightful, respectful, and wants you to learn while exploring your interests even if they don't perfectly align with the course. Mostly seminar based in my experience, a manageable level of work, and easily reachable if need be.
While a little unorganized, he genuinely cares about how his students do in class and will put in the extra effort to help you succeed.

Scott treats his students like adults. He has high expectations from them, he treats them with compassion and respect, and he is always available for extra support. He is primarily concerned with empirical research, so don't expect a huge amount of theory. Show up, do the work, be honest, and ask for help if needed.

I loved this man's lectures. He was slightly unorganized at times, and had a habit of going on tangents unrelated to the class, but his lectures were still easy to understand, and that's how my brain works. He was very willing to help students outside of class times and very approachable.

He can be unorganized at times but the slides are posted and they're easy to comprehend.  Lectures are straightforward, though they can be boring, but overall it is a fun class due to the material.  This class is an easy A; he goes over the exact questions that will be on the final (take-home), so it's stress-free and you can just learn for fun.

Professor Abramson is fine. His lectures can be rather boring but they're fairly straightforward. The problem sets were confusing but the final wasn't bad. As long as you look at the slides (which he usually posts before lectures) and do the readings you'll do just fine.

A good professor. Disorganized at times, but very passionate for his subject matter, and a very fair grader. He is very kind, and if you go to his office hours, you will do well. He goes fast at times, but if you try hard, you will succeed. Problem sets were fairly challenging. Midterms were easy, but the final was hard.
Unorganized.
He is awful and unorganized. Hands down the worst professor I've had so far here.
Scott is very caring but he gives very boring lectures, and he's powerpoint is so unorganized, it is very hard to understand what he wants to say.
Unorganized, not good at explaining.
I really enjoy his lectures and I think I can learn a lot from him. Amazing professor!
Boring but clear lecturer, teaches based on a YouTube channel (I'm not kidding)

He is scatter-brained and does not care about the class. It is sad because the lecture material is interesting and I think that I would love the class with a different professor. Lectures have no correlation to homework, which is all math for a humanities class. He is inexperienced. He would not give us any hint on what to study for the exam.

Dr. Basu is a VERY intelligent person. Of course you will read alot on your own. Read the chapter before coming to class. The tests are easy if you study. If you wait till the day or so before, you'll fail test. Lab is tough. Put the time in & you'll be fine. If you put the time in and gradually learn the material, you'll make an "A" easily.

The Dr. thinks you should study 30+ hours a week.  recommend lecture but he puts it all on BB. must ask him for help personally. no help in class by question. uses multiple books in class. TA's do EVERYTHING! they take the test and make the key, so hope it matches theirs. prepare for long nights in lab and hours studying. HE LOVES CHARTS! MUST MEMO

Dr. Basu is a very interesting lecturer, passionate about his subuject. However he is a little disorganized in his lecture style. He is intelligent and helpful but at the same time is very demanding and has high expectations. You must work VERY, VERY hard to get a C in this class and double that if you want an A. Overall enjoyed the class.

At first I didn't like Mineralogy (EES 204). It was a tough class and the material seemed to go way over my head. And the labs were difficult to understand. But it got really fun in the second half where Dr. Basu went over phase diagrams ( love diagrams). You WILL have to study ALOT for this class. Put in the time and effort and you will pass.

Absolutely terrible! relies so heavily on technical jargon, its easy to get confused. Not clear about expectations for exams. Will take points off if your answer is not framed exactly the way he wants it, even though the questions are broad/vague. Class average was at a 60% immediately before the final. Worst professor I've ever had!

Extremely knowledgeable instructor. Intimidating at first, but really a nice and caring person if you get to know him. The material is memorization heavy, so be prepared to study. But it is very interesting. And always ask questions in class.
Hard to understand and teaches like you have the knowledge of a grad student. Expects large time commitment for studying outside of class.
Interesting material but tests hard. Study!

Choose Professor Carney over any other professor if you have the choice. You get to learn in a stress-free environment with arguably one of the best math professors in the U of R. His jokes are the good kind of cringe, and if you take his classes you won't be cringing at your grades as a plus.
his enthusiasm and clear teaching method make the class better :D I really enjoy his math jokes
He made math entertaining. Super funny guy in like an awkward way. Highly recommend

His enthusiasm makes the class better, This is a hard class but he is extremely accessible outside of class. He will give you hints for the problems and not just straightly tell you the answers, which is great! It's a pity he had a haircut though.

This was Carney's first semester teaching and overall did a good job. Very helpful and wanted you to know the material. Course went from fairly easy to extremely difficult as semester went on. makes a bad joke halfway through lectures. Tests a lot easier than webworks and lecture material which meant there was no test curve.
-danc 202- Very caring professor, expectations are clear and homework is graded mainly on completion. Show a little bit of thoughtfulness/care while you are in her class and you will do well.

I looooooove Mariah! She's really nice and she always encourages us to share our ideas. Though there were various tasks, they weren't hard, and Mariah gives us chance to earn credits back. We watched a lot of wonderful dance videos on class and Mariah also tells us some fun stories about the person we talked about. She made this class awesome!

Ok so I can't say what class it is because it will just give away who I am but i sincerely wish I read all of these comments before. She is the reason why I've been so miserable this semester. Very unorganized, she gave no syllabus, every week was something new and not revelant to topic, and essays every week with no propt. Also shes miserable af.

she is a disaster. if you like being belittled, disrespected and confused as to what you should be doing every week then this is the class for you. if you are a fan of mumbling, tangents and eye rolling then again, this is the class for you. are you extremely self-loathing? like feeling bad about yourself? look no further than a class with fordham.

She is very knowledgeable but a bit nuts. I felt like the entire semester I was trying to guess what she wanted. She often mumbles and is hard to follow. I think he's a really nice guy, and generally a good professor, but he does occasionally make mistake in his example problems that can be confusing. Taking the class with him was just fine, and he easily accommodates for any issues.

Professor Burns do sometime makes the lecture sounds difficult. However he is super reachable after lectures, and he's very willing to explain any confusion you may meet. Spend more time into this class and it shall be a easy pass. (i admit it's not that easy to get an A rank)

I took solids (226) and materials (280) with him and I think he's great... His lectures are hard to follow but his tests are similar to the homework and workshop problems and if you can do the practice exam type problems, you'll do fine. Burns is really understanding and just a great guy. Enjoy!
Very friendly and enjoyable to talk to. Very helpful one on one, a bit confusing with the organization of lecture notes. Good jokes.

Never expect to take coherent notes. Disheveled, and unorganized. Nevertheless a pretty understanding guy. (In our class he pushed back the homeworks almost everytime we asked). Goes off on tangents a lot.
Shouldn't be the chair.  Very unorganized.  Tests were a surprise not related to course material.  Reviews don't help.
I love him.

Seems jovial, but really is stubborn, not too interested in the students, and is often unclear. About 20 minutes before the end of almost every lecture, he would go off on some calculations/problem and leave almost all the students scratching their heads.
Very unorganized.
He is very boring and inconsistent.

I took his surveys class at SBU. He is a really chill professor. Whenever I needed extensions, he was always understanding and whenever I needed extra help, he was there. The class itself is not the worst, but if you're not good with statistics or using software like excel or SPSS, don't take the class since most assignments require its usage.

Lectures are boring but contain a lot of useful material. Great insight on quantitative analysis. There's a sign-in sheet, but you can work on other projects if you feel like sleeping in class. You can use class readings and outside research for the assignments. Handwritten feedback isn't always useful, but he's very accessible outside of class.

Michael is a good instructor. Lectures are kinda boring, though. Most of the grade is based on a 15 page paper about a single piece of legislation. Meet with him beforehand, and during the writing process hell help you out. Always accessible. Quick replies. I barely read any of the assigned readings though. Still did fine. No exams, just writing.

No written feedback on assignments. Hard to hear. He spends the lectures going through slides (too fast) and discussing statistical trends/theoretical scenarios rather than basic congressional mechanisms. He doesn't go over the readings and neither they nor the lectures are needed for the assignments. Stony Brook University.

The only class I've ever taken in 4 years that I can honestly say by the end of the semester I had no idea what was going on. I would never recommend
He is really easy.  Really nice guy.  He will help you all the way through the class. Not a ton of work. Slides posted online.  Kinda boring at times, but it's a good A.

The book is helpful for the first half of the class! The second half you have to read his lecture notes and go to class. The professor himself is not really interesting or exciting at all. He's quiet so sit near the front of the class. Recitation is KEY for homework help. Sign up for Martin's section if you can.

comment: My Dutch GOAT! Love him!

Wolfs is great. Lectures are straightforward and the test material is fair. There are no curves but grade cutoffs are far more lenient than other classes (read: 80 is an A). There are pop quizzes basically every lecture so attendance is almost mandatory. Labs are really boring but there's only 5. Overall it was a great and imo easy class.

His lectures are not helpful at all. He gives you 30 different slides with a bunch of formulas but doesn't teach you how to actually apply them. I had to teach myself all the material by reading the textbook. He doesn't listen or care about any feedback. I wish I had done self paced phy121. He's a nice man but he doesn't know how to teach.

My main concern with this class is that the workshops, lectures, and homework don't really feel like they transfer over to my exam grade and mostly just how well you study the practice exams and not so much if you understand the content. The lectures are very interesting though as there are regularly live demonstrations of the topics.
Chill guy but a midterm the week before the final is lowkirkenuinely kinda insane
The content itself was not that hard, but the way he lectured was not enough to prepare you for the test. I never knew what to expect on the test, and the instructions were unclear.
Hard to communicate with. One time, my alarm went off, and he called it academic dishonesty. I was required to visit his office for an investigation, which I found unreasonable.

Very very good Professor, helped me a lot.

You should definitely not take PHYS141 if you don't have previous physics experience. Wolfs does an excellent job making lectures entertaining and has limited office hours but will put a lot of effort into answering student questions during them and after lectures. Amazing. He doesn't waste time in trivialities and obvious physics (good!). Provides derivations for theorems that were just accepted in previous physics courses. Very funny; free pack of sparkling water per person every course. Lab reports are fair (8-10 pages), exam questions parallel recitation/homework problems. Always willing to help.

comment:
"Class average was 50" 

If this reviewer had went to recitations, they would've been fine. The test was very easy, don't let them scare you. 

The tests are probably the easiest part of class. Homeworks and labs are brutal. Lecture is optional but there's a quiz every class. Everything's graded on accuracy, but he's willing to help you succeed.
50.8 average score on the midterm... Good luck taking his class

Wolfs is a decent professor. He does his best to help out the class and is typically understanding. The content and textbook are a bit different from a standard mechanics class. The worst part is that there are 3 midterms, but you can have your lowest midterm dropped.

The professor is a good man. But the course is extremely difficult. His PowerPoint don't help usually and you need to figure
something out by yourself. The lab sucks most. You need to write a 10 pages long lab report each time. The homework is very tough and usually covers things not
discussed. Exams were relatively okay but not curving.

His Labs are the worst. There are much better introductory physics textbooks out there like Young&Freedman, Serway & Jewett, Giancoli , Resnick & Halliday, so many more. Matter and interaction is literally the worst textbook out there. His slides are not at all helpful. Entered Loving Physics , Left Hating it.

Somewhat intimidating, but a good teacher if you put in the effort. 237 is, in principle, a difficult course, but it is easy to do well. His expectations are very clear for exams. Homework was pretty difficult, but a good learning experience. The textbook (Eisberg & Resnick) is horrendous though. It's so wordy and, in my opinion, needlessly dense.
Helpful, but can be intimidating. High expectations, but will help you meet them. Labs are very important to your grade.
Very challenging class, but he really helped make it possible to succeed.  HW was near impossible, but he will help. He is nice and a great lecturer.
Fun class, fun guy. Perfect science course for non-science majors.

He's a decent guy, and very good for non-science majors completing a cluster.  He's a good lecturer, but not the most approachable guy during downtime--if you want help, go to the TAs. The class was challenging, but the grading system makes it easier.  Go to class and recitation--do not skip or fall behind or your grade will suffer.

Had him for astronomy, awesome teacher. Great sense of humor and really cares about his students. Takes time to think about and answer the questions posed to him. An extremely organized and thoughtful man, always planning ahead. Very patient as well. Dope accent.

Professor Wolfs is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He truly cares about every one of his students and everything in his class is geared towards their success. The subject material is hard at times but he presents it in a clear, organized way and is always willing to help.

Brilliant professor and truly the best kind; He expects a lot from his students and does everything he can in his power to get you there. Go to his office hours and USE THE TEXTBOOK! He pulls problems from the textbook for exams and if you can do them on your own you can knock them out of the park test day. One of the best teachers I've ever had.

Prof. Wolfs definitely knows his stuff, and makes himself very available for extra help. However, be warned: the online description of the class says you only need Calc 1 as a prerequisite, and it can be taken at the same time, but you should really have two semesters of Calc behind you going in. If this is not the case take 121 instead.
He rode around in a fire extinguisher powered wheelchair, if that doesn't want to make you a physicist, you should gain knowledge.
He's tough, but he knows this and adjusts his grades accordingly.

Wolfs is an excellent professor. Some comments on this website are too harsh. It is true that powerpoint is his mode of teaching but all of his lectures are online. He really makes this a fun class. Weekly homework, biweekly labs, 3 midterms and a final (though the lowest grade is disregarded) 80 is an A. Also, he has a song and dislikes PCs.
Fantastic Professor, one of the best I have had yet at U of R (I'm in my 3rd semester now)
Entered loving physics, left hating it.
Great guy, homework and tests can be long or difficult but overall a great class and professor. Very organized and concerned for his students.

This class is extremely difficult, but he does a pretty good job of teaching it. He uses Powerpoint for EVERYTHING and puts the lectures on the internet. The lab reports are very long. The only time he really isn't that great is when he tries to introduce multivariable calculus otherwise he's a good professor.

Uses Powerpoint religiously, and can be difficult to understand due to his accent.  However, he is a fair grader and teaches well.  Makes physics students right up their labs rather than doing cookie-cutter "do the lab, write data down, answer a question" format.
Very tough class but extremely nice professor.  Very will to help and seems to genuinely care about his students.  Does fun demonstrations in lecture.  Good sense of humor and sweet accent.
He knows his****

AMAZING PROFESSOR! He is incredibly helpful! He goes way out of his way to help students.  He is very tough because the class must cover a lot of material, but even a poor grade is worth taking a class from him.  He's excellent! He's also funny and enthusiastic.  He knows what he's talking about.

He has a tendency to repeat things when he speaks, but his attitude towards teaching is great. The tests are nice and challenging, but it's relatively easy to get an A, even if you mess up a problem. An 80's an A.

Very tough teacher but he is a great guy. If you go in to ask for help he definitely will help you. Very encouraging and never acts like your questions are too stupid to answer. Just be ready to work your butt off!!!

He is serious in trying to teach basic physics and will have great classroom demonstrations. He is a fun professor but his heavy accent may discourage some to go to lectures. His exams are hard but test your understanding of the material. Webwork is hard and not the proper way to do physics homework.
Only one person ever returned Frank's greeting.  Even though he used cigarettes for experiments during lecture.
Like everybody else said -- fair, but tough.  Prepare to work.  Very thorough and helpful if you have a problem.
Tough professor, but fair. Wants student to learn material; willing to aid student. Good for higher level physics than introductory -- very high expectations. Be prepared to do work.
Tough teacher, gives more applied homework but tests deal more heavily with theory.  I didn't mind, I liked the material and thought he was a reasonable teacher.

The lecture material didnt seem to match up at all with the exams. also  Lecture slides with ideas already dervied arent so good.gave webwork, which is horrible for learning physics.  Id never take another class with him.

he IS a very very tough prof, but I can tell that he really does want us to learn.  he has a hard time getting down to the level of the students, but he explains things clearly and he is very willing to help.  plus, his accent is VERY nice...

As mentioned by others, Reichman is a very curious guy and will inquire about your background if mentioned--especially if it relates to his research or the topic of discussion (especially if the former). comment: Whatever you get out of Reichman's class is proportional to the amount of work you put into his class. Lectures cover engaging material, there are weekly group discussions if that's more of your thing + there's room for extra credit even if the exams and paper are very fairly graded. Also super insightful to talk to in office hours. He's great.

Class was pretty easy, not draining or that demanding. Only assignments were ethnographic assignments which were fun to do and not that hard to write about. Class is mostly discussion, of the assignments or whatever other topic based on light readings. Also had Q&A's with other Anthro professors who talked about their careers/research, was cool.

He always pushes you to think in depth. It is quite challenging, but his class is absolutely worthwhile taking.
He is a very nice guy, and really cares about what he is doing.
The material is really interesting, but the lectures are very monotonous Definitely has favorites (observationally, based on who laughs at his 'jokes'). Would not take again.

Great guy, interesting subject matter that he clearly cares about. Reading is a significant component of his classes, but isn't unmanageable. Response papers were graded more than fairly, as were tests. Class got boring sometimes, but other times it was fascinating. He gives you all the information you need to succeed, and expectations are fair.
The material is great but his lectures are draaaaaggggging. He must be passionate about what he teaches, but he has a hard time showing it?
Reichman is relatable and interesting. The material for the class was applicable and the books were worth reading. He is a pretty hard grader though. Very hard to get an A.

The course is just how a circuit course should be taught, but he is a charismatic lecturer. I don't understand the comment about working in his lab because my experience in his lab quite positive—not to negate the other person's feeling, just want to provide reference from the other side.

The class was standard, but my experience in Dr. Lalor's lab was intimidating. There was a noticeable bullying dynamic, and if you didn't fit in, you were excluded. I like him so much, just simply did not do well in his class.

Lalor is a great professor. Very caring and understanding towards his students. Material is pretty tough especially if you're not into circuits. Make sure you don't fall behind as this class moves fast and it builds off of previous lectures. One of the best professors at UofR imo.
Professor is really nice and understanding. Make sure you don't fall behind bc the material piles up real quick.

lovely man. subject is tough if you don't like circuits and if you're a bad test taker. he is really willing to help students out and genuinely cares about students success -- great professor overall.
He explains material well and his class is really interesting. Hes my favorite professor here at U of R! Big recommend.

Very good class. BME 210 is great for biomedical engineers. The course is rock solid, prepare to learn a lot of things. Lalor is great at teaching and a very chill dude. Exams are tough, especially the final. If you study, you will do well. The course picks up a lot during the last month, so prepare.
Pretty chill professor and always available for help. DON'T SKIP CLASS. Before exams, do as many book questions as you can then do more.

comment: Prof Lalor is great. A good communicator and very responsive to questions and requests for help. Cares a lot about the students.
He literally doesn't know how to teach properly, just copying down the textbook. Just read the textbook and you will be fine.
This man is God.
