Prof Lalor 's lectures arent the best, the amount of math in this course is hard to demonstrate in real time so he just took slides from the book, BUT thats because the book is amazing. Read the book and pay moderate attention and you'll do good. He's great to talk to outside of class and clearly wants to help students any. Great listener.
Lalor is the man. Class isn't that difficult, but the homework is long as well as the final.
John Nichol(s Wilder) is god's gift to 123. Couldn't have taught it better myself.

One of my favorite professors ever. The lectures aren't anything extraordinary, but the structure of the class motivates me to learn the material thoroughly. Wouldn't recommend this professor if you are not able to self-learn. I enjoy how the class employs a 'teach a man to fish' approach and have an immense amount of respect for the professor.

Professor Nichol's PHYS 246 was definitely one of the top three physics classes I have ever taken in college. PHYS 246 was challenging. Though maths is simple linear algebra, a lot of the learning processes depend on in-depth understanding. Nichol did very well in providing explanations that were not offered in the textbook.

Prof. Nichol explains things so well for quantum theory (PHYS 246). He knows how to explain and is very good at identifying if students have questions and even predicting what questions we have and answering them. The material is very challenging, but he is very good at making quantum theory as painless as possible.

He's not a good professor; he really doesn't know how to teach. The one redeeming thing about him is that if you talk to him outside of class, you'll see that he's super nice and wants you to know the material. He just can't teach it.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Professor Nichol does not care for teaching this class well nor does he care about his students doing well and understanding the material. Apparently, the lectures were meant to reiterate what was stated in the textbook. The textbook used for this course just proves the exact same derivations of equations that the professor did. TAKE SELF-PACED!
The lectures were mundane and the class itself lacks enough information to be interesting - it's literally too easy. Taking it felt like a chore.

Professor Yang gives fun, interesting lectures if you enjoy the subject material. Your grade is determined by quizzes, discussions, and homework, and the quizzes/tests are not difficult if you review the lecture slides. Lectures are also recorded. Yang gives a good amount extra credit near the end of the semester too. I enjoyed the class.

He is very nice, but he is also incredibly boring. The lectures are hard to pay attention to, given his monotone voice and the pacing of the material. The class is in a large space and he has a microphone, however it doesn't really work. He also has a lot of memes on his slides. Genuinely such a sweet guy tho.

Dr. Martin Yang might seem a little monotone at first, but his dry humor is actually so good. On Black Friday, he posted a “Black Friday Deals” and gave a bunch of extra credit. Absolute angel. If you actually study, the exams are not tricky at all. One word of advice; this class is lecture heavy. Make sure you understand everything on the slides.

Extremely knowledgable professor who is great at breaking down complicated theories into more digestible concepts. He records his lectures which is extremely helpful. One of my favorite professors here-- encouraged me to pursue a minor in BCSC

While he is a very nice professor, he is probably the most difficult professor to understand. He teaches in a large lecture hall, and has his microphone volume very low. He also has a very thick accent with not great pronunciation, so when he discusses more in-depth topics with complicated(ish) vocab, it gets really muddled.

Dr Yang is a well-versed and dynamic researcher, as well as a caring and proficient teacher. He is excited about the material and is approachable. Class expectations are clear and fair. I knew I could go to him during office hours with any questions. He has been my favorite during my university experience.

Seems like it will be a demanding class but it's very manageable. The big assignment is broken down into components over the semester. Small assignments throughout. 3 quizzes you will do well on if you just listen in class. The lab assignments are very easy if you just follow what he does in class. Dr. Yang is very available for extra help.
dreaded this class, by far the most MUNDANE prof at uofr. never take this prof again

Prof Yang is so very sweet and reaches out if he sees you are struggling. However, his lectures are a snooze fest- he speaks very quietly and he puts a lot of memes on the slides but then doesn't explain the actual concepts very well. From a learning perspective, it's frustrating. This is a class that you pretty much need to teach yourself.
great prof ever!

Very caring professor. He was clearly willing to assist me when I asked him for help and responded email quickly. Also, there were multiple opportunities (Optional Quiz/Discussion + Extra Credit) to help us make up for our mistake. I enjoyed this course and was glad to be in his class in my 1st year. Looking forward to having him again in BCS152.

Martin explains things clearly and there's lots of opportunities to do well. Quizzes, homework, midterm + final, and discussions. Well balanced and easy to do well, the only reason I got a B was because the topic of the class was boring to me and I wasn't motivated, but I wouldn't say this class was hard.

Dr. Yang is a really nice and caring professor. I appreciate how he grades us by more than just quizzes/exams; homework is 25% and there's a redo quiz. However, his lectures aren't great. It is hard to understand him from a language prospective and he explains the content terribly. The basics are even unclear. It's too bad, as he's a great guy.

great guy but an average professor at best. lectures have slideshows with 50-60 slides and he does not explain very well. quizzes aren't too bad but you need to teach yourself everything, going to lecture does not help that much
One of the sweetest profs ever, brought candy to class a few times, tried to keep lecture entertaining      -not always succeeding though-, still one of my favorites
Dr. Yang is so cute. I want to put him in my pocket. Chill class.

Super clear about what you need to do well in the class! Lectures are informative and to the point + recorded. Genuinely a good guy who wants you to do well. Decent amount of assignments (HW + discussion posts) but boost your grade. Wish he taught more classes!
A bit quiet but lectures are interesting and informative overall!

If you're looking for an easy class, take one with Professor Yang. If you're looking to actually be challenged and learn, find a different professor. He's a nice guy, but his lectures are super boring - he basically regurgitates the textbook - and the exams are silly. They are all multiple choice but super specific and full of grammar mistakes.

Yang is very easy. Tests and quizzes are multiple choice, lowest quiz score gets dropped. Lectures are a little boring but they are all recorded. I will say that the only downside of the recordings is that it's hard to see things he directly references on slides. Not many people attend lecture, so if you go consistently he will recognize you.

Although his lectures can be boring, he is a very caring professor that has a passion for what he teaches. I loved taking courses with him because his structure was always straight-forward. Also, he records lectures, which makes it easier if you need to miss a class.

Really sweet professor. Lectures may be boring but quizzes and exams are very doable (you still need put in the effort and study). Not the best office hours because it's 1 on 1 and there is usually a really long line with people just hogging and taking 20 minutes of his time. Multiple choice tests, content on the slides. lectures are recorded.

Great guy, super nice. Low maintenance class. Gives quizzes that are supposed to help boost your grade. A lot content to remember for the 2 exams but not difficult. Gives easy hw to help boost grade as well. Personally didn't find the course content as interesting, but people who like linguistics like this course. Love Dr. Yang.

He clearly wants everyone to succeed in this course. He gave optional quiz, optional discussion and extra credit to help us get higher grade. Lecture is a little bit boring but very clear. If you miss classes, you can still know what the contents are by watching recordings which is useful for both learning new things and reviewing.
Very hard to understand (spoken and written language), predictable with all class criteria (BCS 111 compared to 152), easy points for HWs and Discussions

Super nice guy. Also took his 111 class. He can be a bit dry and boring, but if you just pay attention to the lectures and have a reasonable understanding of what is going on, his classes should be an easy A. Tests are easy and his "participation" points just involve writing your thoughts on a certain topic.

Martin was an great professor. This was my second class with him and I enjoyed both of them. His exams and quizzes require you to know specific examples from his lectures so make sure to go to class. Some questions can get challenging so make sure to look over your notes. Very accommodating and offered extra credit to boost your grade.

Oh Martin...

I have had this man for 3 classes now, and can't even begin to describe him. He's such a sweet man and genuinely cares about his students. However, so boring. So so boring. BUT, once you figure out his classes it is easy enough to do well in them. Martin truly is the BCS department here, so just get used to him. 

Live love martin

Dr.Yang is super nice, and very helpful. I've been in 2 of his courses (111 and 152) and is now in BCSC153. I'm very glad that so many of my courses are teached by him. He is creative and leads us to think and discuss on class. Provides clear recordings and crateria of exams. Likes him a lot!

Dr. Yang is one of the nicest professors at UofR. He is a very caring man and he'll often wave to you on campus or in the dining halls. The class material is easy and as long as you attend lectures and read the textbook, the class should be an easy A. He also gives optional quizzes and extra credit.

Martin is a really great professor, and super nice and funny during lectures. All the quizzes and midterms are multiple choice, and the final wasn't cumulative. He really knows the subject and breaks it down so that everyone can easily understand. The homework was also very easy. I highly recommend his classes!

I absolutely love Dr Yang. His grading system is one of the better ones I have seen. He offered a bonus quiz to have our lowest quiz grade replaced which he did in my class last year as well. He also added some extra credit if you submitted discussions early. Sometimes I take the silver line with him (he parks down there & I live in southside) :)
If you're struggling with a topic, Dr. Yang will make time to help you outside of class. His quizzes are fairly easy because everything is mentioned in the lectures.

The class is so much smoother compared to 110. The content is digestible and you can almost always see how they relate to each other. The homeworks (which are just experiments to do on your friends) are always fun and an easy way to get an A.

Nice and approachable. Reply email quickly even at midnight! Very generous with HW extensions! Give information about career paths or research opportunities in certain lectures. His wording on the slides may be confusing, but if you go ask him he will clarify or paraphrase! Exams are MCQ or T/F questions, revise the notes and you'll be fine.
Very nice professor.

Never went to class and studied strictly from the textbook and slides. It probably would have been more helpful if I studied before class to solidify material, but I have a learning disability so I struggled with paying attention during his lecture (it was very boring for me so I struggled to follow along) but the material itself was interesting.
This was my second class with Martin. He's a very nice man but his tests are nothing like his lectures are difficult to understand.

Martin is one of those professors that, at the beginning of the course, seems kind of boring, but he has this sort of dry humor that makes the class really enjoyable. All of the homework assignments and discussion assignments were easy points, but midterm and final were a bit difficult. Depending on how well the class does, he will scale the exam.
The midterm and final are pretty easy, the quizzes are a lot harder! The class is pretty easy but definitely boring. Dr. Yang is really accommodating and understanding!

Dr. Yang is EXTREMELY understanding of extenuating circumstances. He became one of my favorite professors and really pushed me to continue BCS. He is a bit difficult to understand, but you can always go to him and he will sit down and clarify with you. The material is heavy and difficult, but he is very approachable. Highly recommend him!

I loved this professor and you can tell he cares for his students. He checks up on those who fall behind or have failed a quiz. He holds office hours and the TA's in this class are super nice. Study and look over lectures to do well on his exams and quizzes. Understanding the concepts is important. Sit in the front because he can be hard to hear.
This class isn't too difficult as long as you review the slides before the quizzes. I took 3 BCS classes with Yang for my cluster and found him to be fair and consistent with grading.

Prof Yang's lectures are generally pretty engaging! He cares about how successful students are and is flexible in terms of quiz or exam make-ups. The homework's were very clear and pretty easy. Quizzes and tests are all multiple choice (at least for BCS152) - tests are important for your grade, but as long as you pay attention in class you're fine

Professor Yang is one of the kindest and most caring professors here. He really cares that you learn the material and there's a strong initiative seen from him. He's passionate about his subject and makes the lectures a little humorous and interactive. Absolutely recommend him.
Enjoyable lectures. It should be an easy-A- class as long as you don't miss homework like me (6.5% each!)

This is my 5th class with Dr. Yang, super awesome instructor! I had office hours with him to discuss about applying for grad school and about my participation in class. He was always helpful, super flexible during COVID, and gave us make up opportunities/extra credit. BCS 261 is a seminar based class, so readings and discussions are a must.

Martin Yang is an amazing professor who gives awesome lectures. The scores are determined basically by quizzes and exams. There will be study guides provided before each exam that would be extremely helpful.
Nice professor, he is funny and try to make the class engage. Had him for BCS111 and 153, will sign up for his experiment class

Dr Yang is a very nice professor and cares about his students. I took BCS 153 with him in person and BCS 152 with him online. He wants his students to do well and always makes time for their questions and sometimes offers easy extra credit. Overall good guy

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Almost all of the grading is done through quizzes and exams. You won't be given the chance to practice the format of these quizzes or exams, you will simply have to learn their obscure question-formatting on the job. The lectures are unclear and take a lot of time to discuss very little. He is easily distracted by students asking random questions.
Dr. Kegl makes her lecture content accessible and easy to understand, I enjoyed her assignments. She is a caring professor and excellent lecturer.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Really nice professor. Very understanding about missing class, clearly cares about what shes teaching.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: I've taken four classes with Prof Kegl & I really enjoyed them! She's a very understanding professor who is very available for feedback and advice and takes notice of student interest. She's not instantly engaging while lecturing but she's worth listening to. You basically get out what you put in. Make an effort and the classes will be enjoyable.

Rosemary is one of the worst professors you will find at this school. Her class talks are so boring. She grades like a middle school teacher as she's more concerned with grammar and citations over information. You can walk all over her by emailing her you're sick to get out of her class. She should never lead a class on Rochester. Disgrace to PhD's

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: This was my first English class at U of R and I really liked it. Some of the material was difficult but Professor Kegl did a great job of explaining what we should be looking for. The discussions were really interesting, and they added a lot to my understanding. Overall her lectures and feedback were really helpful and I feel like learned a lot.

Professor Kegl is an awesome instructor and I would definitely take a class with her again! She showed the most respect for her students out of any professor I have had in college. There were definitely some technology barriers during this course but Kegl did her very best to adapt when there was an issue and went above and beyond.

She is very intelligent and well-spoken. Amazing at lecture and creating good discussion. A lot of reading and homework (mostly writing). I found this amount of work to be uncalled for given that this only a 100 level course. However, because of this work, I am a much better reader and writer. I left this course knowledgeable on the subject matter.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: This was my first English course at the University and she made it very worthwhile. I liked her accommodation to students and her willingness to help us as much as possible. There will be a lot of reading but it is never too overwhelming.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: She is wonderful at taking students' ideas and times seriously & meeting students where they're at. The workload is reasonable and she makes it clear that she is for you as a student. For example, she added flexibility with our due dates multiple times and was willing to work with individuals on adjustments when they had extenuating circumstances.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: I am a huge Shakespeare fan, so this class was a disappointment to me. I liked reading the stuff but class was so boring. Overall, it is so easy to get a good grade in this class. There are no tests just a lot of essays, but she grades them really easily. I skipped at least half of the plays that we were supposed to read and still did really well.

This was my second course with Kegl and she's become one of my favorite professors. She makes even the driest material entertaining with her easy-going personality. Participation is important and she gives awesome feedback on essays. Lectures are always interesting.

Prof Kegl managed to make an interesting subject, Shakespeare, incredibly tedious. She seemed to grade arbitrarily, chose to teach plays she didn't find interesting, and struggled with technology every day. Her class was also lecture style, which I found to be a poor choice for an English class. Attendance and turning in papers on time is a must.

Professor Kegl is a very fair, honest, grader. She gives very good feedback and appreciates every type of student---whether you're there to simply listen to lecture or if you want to comment on every  point--as long as you pay attention. If you hold an interest in Shakespeare, her way of analysis is very clear and helpful.

Was consistently late to class and often was late on giving us an assignment. I could tell she was passionate about Shakespeare, but her lectures were thoroughly unengaging - if not for mandatory attendance, I probably would have never come to class.
Really knowledgeable, really nice. Sometimes got off topic, but usually not too bad. Just repeat back what she says in class in your papers and you'll do great!
Definately fell asleep during many of her classes. She knows her stuff and is passionate about it. Might wanna look into someone else to teach Shakespeare though.

"Meh" is the best expression to describe Kegl. She's clearly passionate about her work, but the material was just a hair away from being painfully basic (even for an intro class). Grading is a tad confusing. She's not terrible, just mediocre. Well intentioned, but flighty. It seemed to me that the LENGTH of papers (less so content) was important.

I had Prof. Kegl for many classes, and her courses always held my interest. She was especially helpful to me during a thesis paper. I always found her comments on papers especially helpful, and she was always willing to meet with students.
Knows her material, but lacks the ability to hold a classes interest; without the mandatory attendance, few would show up regularly, but there is rarely any incentive to participate in class.
Very mean at times and unhelpful at office hours. Grading seems arbitrary and often punishes for not conforming to her feminist views.
No Comments

I liked Professor Kegl a lot. She helped me with an independent project, and I really liked talking to her. Except then at the end of one term I was really stressed and decided to take her up on the option of not doing the final paper, and since then she hasn't spoken to me. Weird.
A very unhelpful and mean woman. Unable to meet students needs. Grades tough and often arbitrarily. Recommend avoiding.

He's a very detailed professor. He teaches every step of Python, which has definitely helped me build a strong foundational understanding of the language.He also focuses on using real-life examples, which makes the lectures not boring at all. I attend all of his lectures because he's such a great professor. Highly recommend taking his class.
Terrible decision to use paper exam for a coding class. As with any professor that do exams for coding, does not understand that coding is a language and how to teach coding effectively.

He taught introductory programming extremely well. His lectures were very clear and organized, and had lots of examples. He made class super fun and easy. I still program a lot today and he set a very strong foundation.
He is a nice person but the class is difficult and the grading is not clear
Very approachable and a nice professor. Explain things in an elegant and concise manner. Would take again.

The course is difficult, the readings are not easy to understand. But prof weslake is a very nice person, very friendly and approachable. The workload also is okay.Come to his office hours if you have any questions, communicate more and you should be fine
Very strict grading, unclear grading criteria.
Took his Global perspective on society at NYU Shanghai. Prof. Weslake is nice and approachable. The ideas in his lecture are thought-provoking, but are not that easy to understand.

I have taken a LOT of philosophy classes and Brad is probably the best professor I've had in any of them. He's young enough to really relate to college students, and he's smart enough that he always understands and can always explain complex ideas. He does assign a lot of reading, but hey, that's how he got so smart.
awesome proff!! reason why I am a Philosophy major!
No Comments

Very clear about the material, very helpful, nice, and approachable. Goes through the material at a pretty slow pace, but not too slow. Does a good job handling the obnoxious kids who raise their hands without thinking. Very approachable and friendly. Possibly the nicest guy I know.
Philosophy is definitely one of the worst classes I've ever taken.  Brad, on the other hand, is INCREDIBLY SEXY.  That Austrilian accent, oh yes! Lecture me baby, lecture me!
Lecture may be long and a little dull, but if you really like the material, it could still be a good experience.

Stunningly boring, but she's clearly knowledgeable on the subject matter, which is a shame considering her teaching style is about at interesting as watching paint dry. Probably good idea to go to class--I did--but you can just as easily learn the philosophy from the internet with ease.

Dry and boring professor; does no justice to the interesting topics under discussion. Has a lot of expectations but gives no clue to what she expects. Places no value on comprehension of topics and has no care for original thought; she things she tells you what she wants and you know, but you must magically know what she wants to make the grade.

Impossible not to sleep through class. Modrak does the impossible and somehow makes Aristotle and Plato more boring than they already are. Philosophy majors, beware- take this class either as a junior or a senior, seeing as Modrak is a very rigorous grader.

She's enthusiastic but her teaching style (direct from overheads) can be dull at times.  I found that the individual tests are graded somewhat harshly but she was forgiving in the overall course grade.

She is the most boring professor ever. You'll hate going to class, but you have to or you won't be prepared for the tests. She knows her stuff, but it was painful being in her class due to how she lectures.
Ancient Philosophy is really boring but she is really nice and does her best to get discussions going. very nice, helpful and understanding.
Clear, understandable, and overall just a good professor.

i love how he does a bonus program at the end of the course so you can give your grade an extra boost. i dont love how the exams were tough, this is universally one of the most difficult undergraduate finance courses so keep that in mind.
Take this course
I don't think he explained stuff very well and most of time I just google and ask GPT. Tests are easy

Derek Mohr is an exceptional Finance professor—engaging, clear, and deeply committed to student success. His classes blend real-world insights with challenging coursework, ensuring students grasp complex concepts. Approachable and knowledgeable, he's easily one of the best professors you'll ever have. Highly recommend!

Incredibly boring professor who rambles during lectures and it's honestly a waste of time to go. 5 assignments total, one due every few weeks or so (takes the best 4/5 for hw grade). His exams are just like practice exams, and he even takes questions from them.

I think a lot of these reviews are over-dramatic. If you find finance boring, then it will be boring. Yes, he is somewhat monotone and not necessarily exciting. But, he does seem to be very knowledgable and relates the content well with real-life scenarios. If you find finance interesting, which I do, I think he is a great professor.

While it is incredibly difficult to listen to this professor for more than a few minutes at a time, the material is important, and he makes it somewhat relevant. While the assignments are more difficult than they should be, the TAs are accessible. Furthermore, the final is optional, which is always a benefit.
His lectures are so boring, Mohr does not care about the material he is teaching! I wish I took this course with a different professor. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HIM!

Lectures are boring, and questions on tests/homework are often hard to read. He does less teaching and more of expecting you to know the material. Most lectures are not worth going to. The only important parts are when he gives you excel formulas.

there is no clear grading rubric for homeworks, he does give you 2 extra credit opportunities, he doesnt teach from the slides, he basically doesnt use them at all, he talks as he goes. hes pretty boring and attendance isnt mandatory so you can watch the recordings on 2x speed. if you can, dont take him, if you have to, youll be fine

Professor Mohr clearly wants students to do well in his class, by giving plenty of extra credit and fairly straightforward assignments, but it is hard to stay engaged in his lectures. He is very monotonous and often goes in tangents that don't really help with the content at all. Not a hard course if you know basic finance, though.

Literally the worst professor at the business department. if the class is offered with anyone else - take it with them. He is simply not a good lecturer, gets lost in his words, makes finance an even drier subject than it needs to be. He schedules exams right after fall break and thanksgiving, so you can't spend time with your family. Beware!!!!!!!

Not a good professor, doesn't really teach much, but not terrible. Gives lots of practice tests so you just have to master those and you'll do well on exams. In class assignments are not bad either, you should go to TA office hours to ask how to do questions. Offers 2 extra credit assignments at end of class.

His lectures are do droney and he hardly gets through any important material per class. gets distracted easily. will spend all class on yahoo finance rather than teaching us the material. he skips around slides and is not organized.

A nice guy, but his lectures were incredibly boring. Not a hard class to pass. All of the exams are made up of questions from previous exams, and he gives them out. You would honestly be better off learning the material online than going to class.

Super boring during class. Don't even bother going to his class because you won't learn anything. Use Investopedia and other online resources to learn the materials, and stick to a good group for the homework. He almost always skips office hours, has messy lectures, has unclear wording for the exams, and is very unfit to prep you for the exams.
Ridiculous professor

I don't know whether Derek Mohr really cares about his students. I makes tons of mistakes on both slides and handouts. Most of his class time would go off topic. There is no way to learn something during his office hour since he always skips it.

His way of teaching is pointless. It's hard to keep notes because he always jumps in between slideshows. He claims there are problems with them so he would not teach in sequence but a comment in 2019 stated the same exact thing: he knows and never fixes these issues. It creates so many hardships when u prepare for exams. DO NOT TAKE HIS FIN205 RUN!
His assignments and tests are clearly worded and he makes clear what is demanded. So no unpleasant surprises on the exam.
great professor
He is a really nice person who provides sufficient materials for students to prepare for the exams. Extra credits also provided.
Great Professor, very fair grading and lectures are clear and interesting.

There are other professors at UR teaching fin213. If you really want to lay a solid foundation with the corporate finance material, don't choose his class. Derek doesn't respond to email, and yes, he neither appear in his office hour in most cases. Tests are fair, 65% related to homework and past exam, 15% lecture content, 20% from nowhere

I don't know why his rating is such high. I took the course this year, and he is one of the most irresponsible professors I ever had. He never replied to the email and he never appeared during his office hour. The tests are extremely hard and the contents are totally unrelated to his lectures.
Tests are usually very fair and not really difficult

Great professor! Really cares about his students. Sure the lectures can be boring at times but hes very knowledgeable about finance and often talks about finance in the current news. His grading is very lenient and offers extra credit. Will take him again!
You will learn everything by searching investopedia. His lectures are boring and won't help you do well on the homework or exams. The textbook is confusing and doesn't help too.
Best prof ever, loved lecture
Best professor ever. Could listen to him all day. Very organised, respectful and educated. Every student loves him. Amazing slides and best lectures ever.

Took FIN 204/205 for easy A. Group HWs similar to prev years w/ changed #'s (ask prev. students for answer keys), easy 100%. Exams have formula sheet and q's are variations of PPT,HW, and prev test questions. Memorize Prev test q's, how/ when to use formulas to solve ppt/hw/examples/prev test questions easily. Curves exams. generous Extra Credit.

This professor frequently will read off slides ( he uses the ones provided by the book) and every class he says there's issues with the slides but after years of teaching it seems like he doesn't care enough up to update them. I found him unclear and very difficult to reach. It seems like he just doesn't care.
Professor Mohr is hands down the best professor that I've had at the University of Rochester since coming here. He's respected by his students and deserves to be recognized for his work.
Easy class, clear expectations

Perhaps one of the best professors you will ever come across. Focuses on learning and scoring a great grade (which you can easily manage if you follow instructions). Super easy-going and friendly, he welcomes seeking help/discussing ideas beyond the classroom. I also highly recommend taking the course as it is extremely interesting and unique.

I was in 181 (not listed). Probably the best math professor I've had, he's caring, gave very helpful examples, helped us through homework problems and gave enthusiastic explanations of mathematical principles. He also made himself very available outside of class. I'm sad to see him have to leave, I hope he comes back to RIT to teach in the future.
Shashank is the best professor I've had. He was always available to meet outside of class and help with practice problems. The lectures were very clear and he demonstrated a lot of practice problems.

I got an A in this class but only bc he MAAD curved our grades at the end of the course. he seems to care for his students but mans just did NOT convey the subject material well. I don't think I learned enough in this course as I should've but it's his first semester at RIT so I can forgive some of the stuff? just don't take him for multivar/vect

Professor Chorge was really helpful in me understanding and learning calculus for the first time. His lectures are not bad if you pay attention and follow his work. He is a little unorganized when he works out a problem but he explains everything clear. He was one of my favorite instructors I had this semester and I recommend him to anyone.

In this class I ended up having to teach myself most of the material. I got little to no feedback from him on exams or quizzes.

There were multiple times where I would only have a calculation error on a quiz/exam and he would not give any credit(even though he said he would).

Chorge is very nice, but  I would not recommend this taking this class.

Can be a little hard to understand, but is fun if you get to know him. Homework every class but it takes 5 minuets to do and is graded on completion. If you show up and pay attention in class its a easy A or B
He wasn't the best but was by no means the worst. Just wanted his students to do their best and made himself super available in order to help!
I don't understand why this professor rated so low, but he is the best professor I have ever met in the university. He answers every question thoroughly, and I can understand his lecture.

Professor Gresens is one of the nicest professors I've ever met. If you show interest in the material he will bend over backwards to help you and support you. He is also just a great person who you can trust with personal information and life advice. Amazing professor.

Do not take this class unless you need it. I made the mistake of taking it for "fun," but it wasn't worth it. It's very essay-heavy, with lots of busy work, and the professor is strict about paper outlines. I wish students new to this class had better supplementation on correctly citing sources instead of just being expected to know it.

Best professor I've ever had. Funny, engaging, extremely knowledgeable, genuinely passionate. The only time I've ever seen a professor's eyes literally light up when I asked a good question. Accessible and cares about students. Lots of reading but you don't really have to do it, fair grader but you do have to try to do well.
Honestly, I am inept and do not understand Greek, but Professor Gresens has been understanding from the beginning and has pushed me to do better but is extremely gentle
Just a good professor and a good guy. He expects a lot but is available for help. My favorite prof so far.

He's probably the best professor I've ever had. He's so understanding and genuinely wants the students to succeed. He's incredibly helpful and that's made it so I've done better in this class than any other language classes I've taken

He's my favorite professor I've ever had. He's made it so that I want to learn the language for the language itself rather than wanting to learn it just so I could read things. He's also incredibly kind and understanding. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I know I wouldn't be able to pass the class if I didn't actually go to class

I usually HATE language classes but his Classical Greek class was awesome! I did better in that class than I've ever done in a language class because he made things actually make sense. He's also really understanding and just generally great overall
Prof G is the best! Lectures are super fun and casual, and he really cares about both students and the material. Lots of interesting and relevant tangents.

This class comes with a lot of work --hw assignments due every class, vocab every week, with 2 mini quizzes but all are necessary to keep up with learning Latin and are definitely manageable! Gresens is a very nice, caring and understanding professor and I am definitely taking more courses with him :)
Professor G is really nice, and he won't call on you in class if you don't raise your hand first (so don't worry about getting anxiety over not knowing answers).

Took two classes with him. Gave a lot of reading, but I did extremely well just by listening in class. Flexible: Gives multiple options about when to write essays. Lectures are extremely interesting, and he likes to connect the ancient world to the present. Really nice guy who actively tries to learn everyone's name and is extremely approachable.

The majority of classes focused on translating passages from the book, and the rest were devoted to learning grammar. He described everything clearly and in an interesting way, though, so the class was not boring. There was homework between classes to be turned in, but it helped reinforce the material you had already learned.
Incredibly passionate about what he teaches, engages the class in inspirational and interesting discussions and, above all, best dad jokes.

Really enjoyed taking a class on Catullus from Prof G! He expects a lot from his students but doesn't overload on the work. Very smart, friendly, and open to new ideas and perspectives. Would definitely take again!

An all around great guy and prof! Class is fast-paced and there is a lot to memorize. Very willing to hold individual office hours to help one-on-one. Attendance is graded, there is online and written HW. Weekly quizzes (not hard).  Oral midterm and final (grades leniently on both). Short writing assignment. Must watch online videos and self teach
Best professor I have ever had.Funny. Smart. Makes material interesting and exciting. Always available to help his students.

Prof G is awesome. He knows his stuff. The material is fast paced and can be difficult at times. However, he is a really helpful guy and will make an effort to be available for you either after class or outside of class. His teaching style is energetic and enthusiastic. I enjoyed his class so much!

Very enthusiastic about the material, very approachable and open to questions in and outside of class; when he cannot be reached in person, very accessible by email.  Knowledgeable about the language and broader subject matter, and expresses his thoughts, knowledge, and experience fantastically.

No need to attend class b/c tests are from the book. He is extremely inflexible when it comes to grading however and has extremely high expectations for tests given the amount of allowed time. REFUSED to curve the class despite the class average being a C+. You'll learn but take at your own risk. could just buy the book instead to be honest.
Professor's pace is super fact. He expects you to know everything in advance. Lectures very hard to follow.

Very knowledgable professor. He can explain things relatively well. I like how he is able to take complex ideas and find trivial examples of them. However, sometimes he can get side tracked and begins to make things very complicated, skipping steps, etc. 
One thing I liked is that he went over each student's test 1-on-1 in person.

Made me feel dumb for getting a problem wrong on a test. Told me to "use common sense" and laughed at my answers while reviewing test together. This class is hard enough, but his teaching is very difficult to follow -- ended up not going to his lectures and using Chaves's notes instead. Would not recommend him for this class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Inspirational']
comment: He is very patient and cares about students. He would have students going to his office and give feed back one by one after midterms. He has lots of thoughts that leads to deeper understanding, but sometime his lectures are not organized very well. Need to preview the text and review your notes.

Hands down one of the worst professors in the department. He goes out of his way to make you feel stupid (and then can't figure out how to do the proofs himself). His exams had little to no resemblance to the review sheets and his handwriting is absolutely god awful. His classes were so disorganized. I'll never take a class with him again.

Absolutely one of the worst math teaching styles I've ever experienced, and for first year U of R students who are starting CS, it's important to feel confident in this course. This professor is not it. Brushes lightly over MAJOR topics without highlighting its importance, does not review notes before lectures, and spends lots of time on tangents.

Mth210 is a pretty difficult class but Prof Thakur always explains things concisely. His tests are mainly based on lectures and are not that challenging if you go over his notes. He's also accessible outside of class and responds quickly to questions. Great professor!

The concepts he goes over in class are really something you can't learn anywhere else, making it hard to study if you didn't quite understand things in class. His lectures can be pretty dry if linguistics is not super interesting to you. He gives opportunities for extra credit, but his tests are extremely difficult.
Incredibly helpful, especially to students getting involved with research. He's intense, but definitely accessible.
Hard, Hard, hard!

People who care about getting a pretty good grade with low effort love this class. People who come wanting to really learn about language research... prepare for disappointment. The professor is nice, but spends a lot of time talking about himself and, when on topic, he often makes no sense. As an eager learner... I resented the time I lost here.
Interesting class, but professor is a bit full of himself and refers to his own work excessively... and he's not very clear a lot of the time, but is so sure of himself, he will likely never notice.

Great Professor. His idea about the discussion forum is great since it answers a lot of questions quickly! Gives a superset of exam questions which makes studying super easy!Also he is adorable and super hot with German accent ;)
Excellent teacher! Florian is the MAN!  He gave out a superset of test questions before each test.  It made studying a breeze!  Class was still challenging though.

He moves a little slow at times (spends way too much time explaining things), but he is so kind and willing to help.  He really cares about his students.  And the class is interesting (lots of interesting guest lecturers) and not hard.
really nice guy, good lecturer, he also gives you the test questions before the test so that definitely helps.  you don't always have to go to class either which is kinda nice.

Florian is very helpful and routinely sends out e-mails to remind us about the homework or explain something from class. Tests questions are always provided in advance so you are aware of what will be on the exam. Also, he's really hot (especially with his German accent) :)

Professor Braun was the best professor I ever had. He explained philosophy in a way that was very clear and allowed me to evaluate old questions in new ways. He is very inspirational. I am 38 now but took the class almost 20 years ago.

Prof. Braun is a great guy.  Knows his material very well.  Funny, nice, and smart.  Has a quirky way of getting some of his examples across, but it keeps interest going.  I will be taking him again next semester.
Adequate.  Don't expect any inspiration or anything, though.
Has a very absurd and sick sense of humor.  Knows his material very well and encourages thoughtful discussion.  Excellent lecturer.  Most enjoyable professor I've had from this school.
Knows logic in and out. Practically wrote the book. Good explanations, makes sure you know what you're doing. Kind, considerate, learns your name. Great professor.
take notes exactly as written on the board, don't miss class, don't read the text, don't bother with the T.A. Prof. Braun is a smart man, learned my name, and the class was interesting.
Rote memorization, mathematical proofs applied incorrectly and irrelevantly to philosophical concepts, but mainly incorrectly. There is no clear use of logic to derive philosophical conclusions.
ehh,its just rote memorization on exams, dont read the text, but take notes (exactly as written) for the tests
No Comments
All you have to do in the exams is write what he gave you in the notes verbatim.
Seems like a brilliant man, learned my name, but doesn't make himself accessable to students. the T.A. is a shmuck.

Prof Brown is one of the best teachers I've had a U of R to date. She gives great lectures and explains difficult material in a way that is easy to understand and comprehend. She's always willing to take the time during class to answer questions and is accessible after class and during office hours. I highly recommend taking this class with her!
Erin is an amazing professor, and was especially able to teach the more abstract concepts that come with multivar. I felt very prepared for the tests just from going over her notes.

Professor Homerin is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He has a very deep understanding and love for what he teaches and definitely hooks the entire class. I took his class as a senior and wish I had done it sooner so that I could take more classes with him. Truly an amazing professor.
Homerin is a wonderful professor.  He is extremely enthusiastic about his subject are and has inspired me to pursue it further.
this guys truly knows his islam... the best class for him is islamic mystic poetry, he is truly a poet at heart, and i def enjoyed mysticism thanks to him

I am currently taking Speaking Stones with Dr. Homerin. He is a great professor, he has his ways of making what i thought would be boring material very interesting. Fantastic professor. Really cares about his students, challenges people to think in ways different from their own. Can be a hard grader but definitely worth the time and effort - you'll never regret taking one of Homerin's classes.
Great Guy!  Very well-spoked and extremely passionate.  Lectures were full of interesting facts and were entertaining.
TAKE SPEAKING STONES! Homerin is a fantastic teacher. so passionate
Amazing professor. A complete genius when it comes to history of Islam, and a wonderful Qur'anic reader.

Speaking Stones was an AMAZING class! Very little work other than readings, and if you follow his editing marks on papers you are virtually guranteed an A. Very personable and enthusiastic. I may change to a religion cluster just to take more of his classes. Great guy.
Awesome professor - extremely passionate about the subject, always open to new questions. Hard grader but it's totally worth it.

Homerin is awesome...especially in the Speaking Stones class. He is so helpful and makes the class so interesting. He does grade pretty hard though, but the projects aren't bad at all. Definitely a great guy!
No Comments
EXCELLENT!  Excited about his material and an extremely clear lecturer.  Extremely helpful to students and interested in their success and well-being.
insightful and thoroughly engaging

Easily the best lecturer in the math department. He clearly cares a lot about the material, which translates to the course and makes it very engaging. He also goes off-book for a few weeks to talk about manifolds and topological groups, which is very interesting.

His lectures are easy to follow compared to others. Content was enjoyable but i hate that we had no idea what our grade was whole semester. Maybe its the math dept. tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Prof. Pakianathan's lectures can be a bit dry but that's only because they are heavy on theory. I didn't like his lectures a lot but the abundance of homework problems helps a lot with preparation for exams. His exams are heavily inspired by questions asked on HW assignments so do them sincerely and you will be fine. Classes are well structured.
His lectures were incredibly funny and he made linear algebra enjoyable.

Jon gives incredibly enjoyable lectures on a difficult subject. When the math gets tricky he'll openly call the problems "obnoxious" and "a pain". If you have an opportunity to get the Pakianathan experience, you should absolutely jump on the opportunity, and enjoy the wildly entertaining and educational ride.
Solid lectures, very knowledgeable. Make linear algebra easy to learn.

This course wasn't easy but Professor Pakianathan made sure to go over examples for each topic in great detail. Though he followed the book, he sometimes diverted from it to show easier ways to do problems.

He's the best of the 165 profs, in my opinion. His lectures were very clear and engaging, and he did a lot of helpful examples for every topic (about the same difficulty as homework and exam problems).

His tests are a unique format. On our 165 final this fall there where: 2 multiple choice sections, and 3 long answers with answer boxes that broke the problem apart. Thus little to no partial credit on these questions. I also thought there was going to be more of a curve considering the average final grades where Part A- 77%, Part B -67%.

One of my favorite math professor. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about math. Lectures sometimes can be confusing very his office hour is very helpful. Exams are relatively hard compared to the past and he sometimes tend to over explain questions. However, outside of class he is very accessible to answer any questions.
By far my favorite professor. Very amazing person both in and outside of the classrooms. Gives very clear examples and is more than willing to help outside of class periods.

His lectures are so helpful!! He does lots of examples and wont have super complicated problems that are a higher level than the tests. Hes super reachable outside of class and always willing to help students
Out of the 165 profs, he is probably the best. If you have to take 165, take it with him.

Professor Pakianathan is a very nice guy and definitely knows what he is doing. Midterms are on the rougher side, know your rules, properties and how to apply them and you will survive.
Very great professor. He cares about students, highly accessible outside of class.

Excellent overall. I followed his lecture for 1st and 2nd midterm, and I think he is great. Paki is really nice and also a really good professor. His lectures can sometimes be fast paced or boring, but I think that's more of a consequence of the material than him.

Professor Pakianathan is one of the best professors I had for math. Although, his lecture is fast paced, but his lecture notes are amazing and have enough examples to clarify the concept. His exams are not too hard and you would do great if you go through the homeworks and lecture notes.

Even though this course is not mandatory, I didn't miss a single course. Each of them was too valuable to miss. The professor is passionate to teach, and appreciate every student. I would definitely take his courses again!

The best professor! He's enthusiastic. Lectures are so good.

Best prof ever

Passionate, clear, and wants his students to succeed. He goes over the material very thoroughly and prepares you well for exams. He's such a sweet and funny man and makes calculus 2 totally doable!
He's a good teacher but he's constantly saying sorry and if you pick up on things quickly he goes too slow but if you're not clear he's just right.  He rambles but is a real sweetheart
Great professor, he explained everything very clearly in class so that I didn't even need the textbook.  He's also very helpful during office hours and seems to genuinely want to see people succeed.
He is really really good. I really enjoyed having him as my teacher. He was one of the few that kept me very awake in class.

I had Jon a few years ago for Discrete math. The concepts were easy, but a bad teacher could have seriously obfuscated them. Jon's very organized in his teaching style and speech. Pay attention and you'll be rewarded.

really passionate about certain topics but it was clear that there were things he was not interested in, which made a few chapters difficult to sit through. little leniency on exams, which were all online. he adores questions. i didn't love him but he's an interesting guy and a pretty good professor.
great prof
Truly amazing professor. Cares for his students and giving all the perspective which astronomy is

hilarious and entertaining. i love astronomy to begin with, but he just makes it even cooler. he's passionate about what he teaches. i'd take another class with him if i could.

Great professor! He is funny and makes lectures zoom by. He can be a bit slow on putting up review questions for exams but he's working on it. He also plays really great music before class and at the mid-lecture break. Take a class with him!
One of the best professors in the world! He is just simply amazing. I wouldn't be surprised if he was jesus, himself.
A good speaker, inspiring and humorous!!! Easy class!
Love his class, makes his 75 min lecture fly by most days -  intelligent, clear, enthusiastic, great taste in music - overall really cool guy

Prof Valdez is really nice, you can tell she's passionate and wants students to succeed (and understand/learn the language). He has accent but it wasn't that huge problem since its math class. He is very helpful during his office hour.
worst professor ever !

Enjoyable and clear lectures for the most part. His slides for the last unit got disorganized and didn't match what he was saying. Very approachable and understanding. Dr. Holz is awesome. Physiology is definitely a challenging course with a lot of material, but he breaks it down pretty well and assignments/workshops are well targeted. Lectures can be a little convoluted, so rewriting/organizing notes might be helpful.

One of the best professors at U of R. So caring and makes lecture content enjoyable. Accessible to students and very responsive when issues or questions arise. 10/10 recommend taking physiology with him, it was an awesome class

Great professor. Exams can be hard, but if you study you'll do fine. He is receptive to questions and feedback and genuinely wants students to succeed. Attendance is only required at workshops as lectures are recorded.

Hilarious professor and a great human being. Makes you want to participate and times jokes that fit in and make class more enjoyable. Bump offered for every exam based on avg.

comment: Dr. Holz is a straight-up collegiate-level professor. His class requires significant time and dedication to excel in. Unfortunately, the course leaves little margin for error and one or two mediocre performances on exams will tank your average; however, I realized that this course opens your eyes to the high degree of competency required in life...

Dr. Holz is one of the best professors I've had here at UR. He encourages class participation, is receptive to feedback, and the lecture style keeps you on your toes. Exams are quite tough, however there's a so called 'bump' that accounts for the difficulty. He'll definitely make you work for your grade but by no means is it impossible.

Dr. Holz is very enthusiastic and tries to engage students and make class interesting. However, there's an overwhelming amount of material covered on each exam and he doesn't refrain from testing on trivial details. Most exams are curved heavily as a result, but if you try to memorize EVERYTHING on the slides you'll do fine.

The class is a typical upper-level biology class. A lot of content- if you memorize lectures you will do well on exams. As for Dr. Holz, he is unapproachable, lazy, and lacks sympathy for students. For one writing assignment, my peer and I received the same exact feedback, down to the typo. Unprofessional and rude-- the worst I've had at UR.

Has a ton of material to cover in each lecture, but tells you exactly what you need to know on exams, and also throws in well-timed jokes. He also listened to the class when we wanted to switch to live lectures. But damn is there a lot of content on his exams. Made me work for it.
Kind of lazy but definitely a fun guy You have to work in this class

My favorite bio prof at UR. Why can't all professors just be like him. He speaks clearly, uses powerpoint, and his tests are fair. The class isn't easy by any means, but your effort is usually rewarded.

I took BIO 204 with Dr. Holz during the Fall 2019 semester and LOVED it! Definitely my favorite professor ever! He talks fast in lectures (and tells jokes that are actually funny), but they're recorded so you can go back and fill in gaps in your notes. Super nice and genuinely wants students to succeed and enjoy the material.

Dr. Holtz can help you believe that you can succeed in the natural sciences. Dr. Holtz does his best to be entertaining and informative, even while juggling insane amounts of responsibility. IDK why but he sometimes bugs me; I guess it´s a me thing. If you get him as a professor, then cherish the experience.

If you have the opportunity and find interest in Tai Chi please take this class. Bob is a sweet older man who just wants to teach the basic forms and principles of Tai Chi. Love Bob. He is such a sweet man and cares so much about the subject and his students. You will feel guilty if you don't go to class, and why wouldn't you, its so fun!
A lot of reading. A lot of paper to write. A lot of work for 4 credits. A lot of reading. You even have 2 presentations
Very caring professor, very passionate about what he teaches. All papers are graded very kindly, hard to not get an A.

a 4+ credit class took that for fun but it messed up my GPA

this is a 4+ credit course definitely

He was extremely nice and interesting, very understanding and genuine and seemed like he really cared about tai chi and teaching it to students of different abilities. great prof., wonderful class.very clear and precise about what he wants.class is very laidback and relaxed, great atmosphere for learning taichi.very helpful, gives detailed feedback on all assignments.in general, a very welcomed change from all the rigorous stressful classes. i looked forward to each class; planning on taking his other classes :)

thanks for my gpa boost

I LOVE THIS MAN. SO FUNNY. and also genuinely wants everyone to do well in the class.

THIS MAN IS AMAZING

This class was very interesting and was a nice break from hard classes I was taking. Professor Rogge is a super cool person who makes the class interactive which keeps everyone engaged.

He makes class super fun and entertaining; I actually look forward to going to class and even though there is a lot of content he wants his students to do well and succeed. He is absolutely hilarious. Love his personal anecdotes - they show he cares and that he's passionate about the material. Everything is straight from the book but he gets the information across in a funny, understandable way.

Best class ever. Best teacher. You will learn so much but it will be so easy.

Super funny and laid back.  He is enthusiastic and makes the class interesting while still teaching you the material. His tests are a breeze because of the review sessions and if you need help he is very accessible.

He's great! He's really funny and refreshingly real with his students. His explanations and really clear and he really puts in a lot of effort to make himself available to help his students. I loved this class. It's what got me to be a ling major. Prof Sol is a well of knowledge and I wish I got the chance to take more classes with her. We didn't have too much hw and got a lot done in class

WRTG273. This class is so boring and I hated it so much. learned nothing from her class. Avoid at all costs. none of her comments are constructive. this class made me a worse person.

literally avoid this woman at all costs

Just like what the other comment said about her, her instruction's always confusing.

comment: Prof Sol will go down as one of my least favorite teachers I've ever had. She is unorganized and unclear with instructions and feedback on essays. Not a difficult class, easy way to get some credit but she does grade harshly. Wouldn't take it again, will not take her classes either

grade relies too heavily on participation. she seems to grade people's 30% of the final grade by memory. for tests and homeworks, she takes off points for subjective reasons. spent 10x more of my time on this course than all of my other courses of that semester (I got A's for all of which) combined and still cannot get a good grade

Professor Lenoe is one of the best professors at the UR.

I was really excited for this class at the beginning of the semester, but GAHHHHHH it's SOOOOO BORING!!!!!  A lot of what he teaches is so obvious that it makes you feel like you're wasting your time being there.  He also likes to ramble.

meh. not impressed

Pretnar displays mastery of the subject matter, along with arrogance, pedantic lectures, and inaccurate slides. loved her lectures. shes so sweet. exams were fair.

super sweet and remembers names. thoroughly explains complex problems which i love. the exams were fair and a little challenging. overall loved the class and her.

Overall good prof. Works through examples and gives out worksheets in class (+remembers names and faces). Easy course until the end of the semester when the content got harder and she had to leave so there was a prof change.

Professor Slane is a very kind professor. If you took ME104, the first half of this class is just a repeat of force diagrams. Lectures aren't recorded so make sure to show up. It's a very up close and personal class, and she remembers names and faces.

ME 260 is a two-credit course but having the workload of a five-credit course. Do not expect this two-credit course as easy as a normal two-credit course. She had three hard, complicated, time-consuming projects in one semester which is unbelievable and frustrating.

Her project is so annoying. I know every knowledge that being used in the project but it is very awful when you look at a thousand of instruction and must follow the guideline to get score. Very heavy course load.

Her grading criteria is shit. You will be deducted point due to drawn figure has flaw in a coding course. Her requirements on format is driving me mad as well. It is super crazy!!!

Prof Slane has a perfect way of teaching the course. She uploads the slides, examples she went through in class and worked solutions to worksheets and homework sets. She's also always enthusiastic about teaching and is a very fair grader. Go to lectures as she explains everything clearly.

Prof. Slane gives great lectures with enthusiasm. Quizzes and tests are always covered in class.
