He is also one of the most approachable professors I've ever known. I am grateful beyond words for all the help he has offered.

He is a sweet guy but rather unapproachable and awkward. He is a stickler for grammar which can be really annoying if you have to write papers for him. If it was not required I would never take another class with him again. Also he is very vague in his lectures and what is actually useful for the exams

If you are an IR or PSC major, you should really take a class with him. He is very informative and explains examples very well. If you dont like the topic he teaches, sure you will probably hate the class. He is by far the best professor I have had at UR. Best class was Junior Honors. He makes sure you will get a good grade too if you put in effort
Much more work in this class than you word expect for an elective political science course, prepare to do a lot of writing (even if you're not taking it as a writing course). Otherwise interesting.
SO BAD!  he is full of himself and boring to listen to.  I would never take a class with him if its not required

My course was taught by both Niemi and Linda Powell.  This was the funniest ****ing class I've ever had.  Dick is hilarious (in that old style grandfather way).  His relationship with Linda was also highly comedic.  The  class was somewhat boring, but very useful (for poly sci majors).  The TAs were really good and able to teach the class.
the best poli sci prof at the place.  I LEARNED SO MUCH, more than i expected to.
probably the best professor i've ever had.  a lot of fun, makes class interesting.  always available for questions.
great guy, very knowledgeable but nice, not stuffy or arrogant, great with discussions, even when working with boring material,

I was literally so lost on the material days before finals -- TAs and friends couldn't help. Joined an hour-long office hour with Professor Gregory the day before the exam? understood everything. Got an A. She's a miracle worker. So so kind and committed to her art and the lives of her students. Definitely recommend!!
Really good professor. If you are fine to attend the lecture, definitely a great choice to take her class.

Highly caring professor who is a joy to be around. Highly knowledgeable of music theory. As long as you put in a little effort and enjoy what you are doing, it is not hard to get an A (I did and had no prior music theory knowledge). Additionally, office hours are available if needed. Outstanding Professor!

I enjoyed Prof Gregory and her Musc 101 class. If you went to class and stayed on top of the homework (1 short assignment per class), it is hard not to do well in her class. She's super sweet, passionate, and always willing to help outside of class.
She is so good. Friendly professor. Easy grading, and easy exams. But mandatory attendance and need to buy textbook.
She's good. I feel like even if you only wrote name on your exam you would still pass it.
AMAZING PROFESSOR. Accessible outside of class and will remember your name in a room of a hundred students.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Good very nice professor. Felt like a lot of HW at the start but then it gets normal. Attendance is mandatory and few pop quizzes are given in first half of semester. Exams are almost exactly like practice exams making it easy to do well.
Prof. Gregory's class is definitely not an easy A, but she explains the material so well and explains what she expects on writing assignments and exams, giving great feedback from them.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Prof. Gregory was a very caring and enthusiastic professor who wants to share her passion for music with her students. Super accessible outside class and gives plenty of practice to work with. As long as you keep up with homework and readings, achieving an A is very doable.
I joined the class a week late and she made it very easy to catch up. She great at explaining the concepts and homeworks. It's a pretty easy class if you go to class and do the homework sheets.
A very good class. The content is not hard, and the professor is very nice!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: This is an OUT OF MIND extremely hard course. I know it's the minor requirement but this class is definitely not for people who have only taken theory 1&2. You have to memorize all the pieces and composers studied in class (20-30) & style, about 40 terms definition which you can't find in ppt or book. 5 part essay at the end. IMPOSSIBLE CLASS WTF

Professor Gregory made online class somewhat tolerable. I can't say her lectures kept me on the edge of my seat, but they are clear and easy to understand. The homework can be somewhat tedious but it's easy credit if you watch the lectures back. I joined the class two weeks late and she was very kind about the whole process. Also has 2 music PhDs.

This professor is good at what she does. Her lectures are well executed and she is very helpful during office hours. The TAs are nice and grade very fast. The only thing is that the homework is very repetitive and long. Only take this class if you're interested in music. It IS NOT an easy A.

What not to say about Oberly. One of my favorite math teachers of all time and I also believe he is one of the smartest teachers I have ever had. He is an amazing lecturer, and although attendance isn't mandatory, I encourage everyone to go to an Oberly lecture.
Best 162 prof by far.
Best math teacher I've ever had. His course covered difficult material, but workshop and homework helped a lot. Fair grader, if you put in the work you are guaranteed a good grade.

Explains concepts clearly, but speeds through them because there's a lot of content to cover. Very caring, and accessible for help if you reach out. Definitely go to workshop (graded on participation)/study groups because those TAs have a lot of good info to share. Look over/practice with past tests before exams, similar material will be covered.

His lectures were good, but he could have went through more practice problems for each topic. Small mistakes were worth a lot of points on the midterms and final, so make sure you check your work multiple times. Highly recommend doing the practice exams before the exams.

Poberly is actually the goat. His lectures really clearly outline the content you need to know, and he's such a chill whimsical guy. Definitely the best 162 professor by far out of the bunch, so take it with him if at all possible.

I love Poberly so much I wanna be like him when I grow up. Don't miss the lectures because the content is much harder to learn on your own. Exams were pretty easy compared to the practice exams/questions that we did. I love the brain breaks as well.

In Math 162, I thoroughly enjoyed all of my lectures throughout the semester, regardless of the material being covered. I felt that professor Oberly was very clear in the concepts he explained, and I believe that the class became much easier as a result. I thought this class was fun, and I am disappointed that I will not have Oberly next semester.
I took math201 with him. he explained stuff very well and always ready to answer questions we have

This class flat out stinks. You will fail tests and it will be okay. This professor's lecture were too much and confused everyone. Read the textbooks, watch videos, and know how to do what is on the homework. It will be your hardest class you take and is more work than any of the other math classes. Most majors just need a D or better to pass.

I spent two semesters at UR, taking Peter's Calculus II (162) and Linear Algebra with Diff Eqs (165) courses. Both were challenging for freshmen—162 required heavy practice, while 165 introduced new math concepts. Peter was a great professor: patient, caring, and approachable. I asked him for a transfer recommendation, and I will miss him.

A charismatic professor who gives amazing lectures and provides useful notes. He definitely has the personality to teach. Choose him!
He is very considerate and caring. I registered for the course late, and he offered to walk me through the topics I had missed. 
I will definitely take his other math classes.

Oberly was a great professor and very caring! The class itself was very difficult, especially the second half. Oberly was very helpful during office hours though. I also recommend going to study group and tutoring through the learning center if you need help with webwork problems.
Awful course, but a great professor. If you have to take Math 162, take Oberly.
Tough course but he is always available to answer questions and enthusiastic

Challenging class consider if you have ap calc ab and jump straight into college level calc 2, a lot of students I know have bc or equivalent IB background. I recommend watching corresponding lessons from professor V on youtube before coming to class.

Big difficulty spike in the second part of class with series. I recommend going to office hours, the 162 study groups, and finding a (free) tutor through the learning center. Oberly is a caring and available professor even if his lectures sometimes drag on, and if you do the webwork consistently then you should be on track for a good grade.

I thought he did a great job with teaching this class and his lectures were genuinely helpful. I must say that a common struggle that many had was the wording of this semesters exams which really confused me because of how unclear some sections were. Otherwise, he is an approachable professor and I highly recommend asking questions!

Oberly is a kind professor who takes time to answer your questions and teaches in a good manner. Sometimes he skips a few steps or goes a bit too quickly but overall, he is pretty good. Out of all the math 162 teachers, I recommend him because when talking to my peers, he seems to be the best. But math 162 as a class is hard and tests are unfair.

Peter is super accesible outside of class, passionate about teaching, and welcoming! This class is definitely pretty hard, especially since the final makes up such a large part of the grade, yet lectures and recitations are helpful. Lectures can feel a little dense and overwhelming, but overall a great class!

Super knowledgable and cares for his students a lot! His lectures are quite content heavy but that's expected for any math course. Not necessary to read the textbook but it makes the lectures easier to understand if you skim beforehand.

He is a very engaging lecturer, and the course overall is very interesting. It's clear he cares a lot about making sure everyone understands the material, although that sometimes means he goes pretty slow. Would strongly recommend knowing linear algebra before this course as I feel you get a lot more out of it if you do.
Great class
He is such an amazing professor, he was so caring that he gave us 50 extra points on the final because our TA did not give us enough time to complete the exam.

tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Tough content but he is a great professor. He adjusts his teaching to fit the understanding of the class. For Spring 2025, there was three problem sets, one midterm and one final. He says the course gets easier over time. The unfortunate truth is no one tells him when they don't understand so he moves on quickly. Need to know linear and partial dif
Very accessible outside of class. Understands this is a difficult subject and tries his best to help students.

Fantastic professor, really cares for his students. Gives great feedback and is super accessible outside of class. Some of his homework's were phrased incorrectly, however he graded very leniently for that. Has a great ability to break hard material down into bite sized pieces.
Hard class but really interesting. Attend lecture and don't be lazy.
Very smart guy

The midterm and final take about 70% of the course points and be prepared for them! The grading is relatively loose since this is a hard course, just write your ideas about the questions in exams and if your are on the right track, he will give you the points. His passionate in lectures and definitely worth to go to the lectures.
Great guy. During lecture he makes sure everyone's clear on the topic before moving forward. You can tell he cares. Not sure what all the hate's about.

It is a very difficult class due to the nature of the material. Even if you do not score well he is very understanding and will help improve your grade. Going to office hours and recitation is essential to learning the material and way he solves problems similar to exam. It is hard to fail the class and he does have a generous curve. Love the guy.
Worst Class

He lectures as if we have all already seen the content before, and all have a high understanding. Although the class is really hard, he is very available outside of class and good at teaching one-on-one.
The classes always went overtime, never finished the class on time.
The easiest course I have taken in UofR. Really Easy A!
GREAT
Worst class ever!!!!!!!!
His exam is bad. It requires too much work to show your knowledge. I dont understnad him.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Great instructor, difficult class but overall very helpful.

Great person! Humble, passionate, friendly, etc.... As a professor though, well lets just say his lecture treated my Insomnia better than anything else in the world. He's probably a great researcher/project teammate, just not a great instructor.

The class by its nature is very difficult but he does not make it easy by the way he teaches it. He goes over concepts extremely fast and I think his teaching style is more suited to grad level than undergrads. Extremely hard to get a good grade in his course. Otherwise, he is a respectful guy and was always approachable after class.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: By far the worst professor I have had at Rochester. If you care about your grade, then don't take him. You have been warned...
Not sure what all the whinings are about. Good professor, explains concepts well PERIOD
WORST FINANCE INSTRUCTOR EVER

Drills over easy stuff and then goes through difficult stuff very quickly assuming that you know it. Makes you feel dumb if you ask questions outside of class and tells you you should have asked in class, even though it's a large lecture. Homeworks are nothing like the powerpoints he presents. Assumes you know excel fluently

She never remind you about anything and will give you a very low grade in the end. When you email her and want to discuss about your grade or ask her anything else. She never answer you back. The worst ever.

Nice guy, kinda wild. The class was pretty easy; he got rid of homework for the class, so your grade is 80% tests, which isn't great. He learns your name and is very fun, says some very out of pocket things during lectures. The lectures aren't mandatory, but they're worth going to mostly because Stu is hilarious. He loves Beyoncé.

This class was way more difficult than it needed to be because of the amount of homework; it was mostly all just busy work that was tedious and hard to understand in relation to the topic. Lectures were optional, but you had to attend them because the homework wouldn't make sense. All exams except the final were pretty easy. The final was hard.

i wish i could have him as my professor forever! he learns everyone's names almost instantly which made this class feel less daunting. all the work is online, and attendance is optional except for testing days (yes, even recitations are optional). grading scale is kinda funky but very forgiving (A- is 87.5% - 96.25%) he has a ton of passion!!!

There's a lot of work in this course. Not difficult work, but the topics pile up and it will take time. Still, Stu is genuinely worth getting to know, his office hours and recitations will give you most of the answers, and it is a great intro to formal models. Despite 120 students, he will try to learn your name. That tells you all you need to know
amazing professor. talk to him in office hours, he is super duper cool, chill and smart!

Stew is one of the nicest professors I've met yet. He actively works to memorize the names of his students and is always open to talk with students. The homework is a very large part of the grade, but the instructions are often listed on the assignments. However, the TAs can grade weirdly at times, but Stew is always open to talking about grades.

I absolutely LOVE Stu, he is one of the sweetest and most caring human beings. His class was pretty good, ppt is very homework heavy with at least 6 hours of homework a week. But his grading criteria is very clear and tests are very fair. Overall, he understands that we do not want assignments or tests unrelated to the lectures.

Homework takes time but the instructions posted for the lessons and before each COU basically walks you through everything you need to do them. The exams might add some new twists but Stu will walk you through everything beforehand. Very fair and considerate when addressing questions and regrading concerns. Super accessible via office hours/email.

The content was more difficult than I expected, but this professor's lectures certainly made up for that. Homework(50% of grade) and rubrics are easy to find, but little partial credit. He is not joking when he says the homework takes 5 hours a week, and as the semester goes on more math becomes involved. Very good office hours and clear test prep.

First of all, I love Stu as a person. He's a king. But this class made absolutely no sense. He tests on material not covered in lectures. Work is very tedious; not necessarily difficult, it's just really confusing. I don't recommend taking the class. Don't think I absorbed any useful knowledge.

I disagree with most others. I found this class to be a thunderously worthless waste of time and energy. The content is easy and simple but he turns this into tons of frivolous busy work that's graded harshly for no reason. I learned next to nothing and I would never take a class taught by Stuart again.
Amazing and brilliant professor. Highly recommend talking to him in office hours as he has lots of interesting information and knowledge to share.

Prof Jordan is a good prof and takes the time to help students outside of class. Make sure you do the COU's because they are worth half of the grade. The course is MUCH harder than in previous years and time consuming with the work, so be aware. The course being more difficult was annoying considering how much easier years previous had it.

To be honest, I don't think you need much mathematical ability in this course. If you have received systematic high school Math education before, you definitely will handle those questions. But in each exam the total points is so low that if you make a little mistake in a single question you will lose a large percentage. Jordan's lecture is great.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: a lot of work to do , make sure to do the COUs cause theyre worth hallf your grade. but the class is much more difficult then last year. The professor is nice though.

If you are taking this course in the fall of 2022 or after, be aware that Stu has changed the curriculum and it is MUCH HARDER than it used to be. There is much more math and algebra involved, and I find it very hard to understand and keep up with. I love Stu as a professor, but this course is not what I was expecting and I am disappointed by it.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Stu is one of the most supportive faculty members at UR. He cares a lot about students (like learning the names of everyone who has ever raised their hand in a huge lecture hall) and wants you to get something valuable from his class. Grading criteria is very clear. The content is pretty basic/easy, but assignments are still a big time commitment.

Stu is amazing! He gave out stickers to people pretty much just for showing up to class. He also bikes to work, and that's amazing. If you show up to office hours, he really puts in the time to make sure you understand the material. He wants everyone to do well in the class and is just an amazing professor. 10/10 recommend.

Stu is such a great guy and I painlessly learned a lot in this class. Seriously, go to office hours to get to know Stu!! He genuinely cares about his students. Attendance is not mandatory, and though the homework can be time consuming, but you'll always be able to figure it out.

really great guy. super accessible, easy to digest lectures with ample help and assistance. if you're thinking about or are already majoring in political science or international relations i highly recommend taking any class with professor stu, just an overall good-hearted empathetic guy with tons of expertise and connections to help you succeed.

LOVED THIS CLASS AND STU. Definitely get the W credit because it's really easy and you do fun activities in the Rochester community. Stu is super caring and is more than accommodating with his students. 10/10

Stu is an absolutely amazing guy. He has a tendency to be very redundant with the material, but he does make it extremely clear. Although you don't have to go to lecture, the work really comes in outside of class, so be prepared for that. I thoroughly enjoyed this class despite its simplicity.
Lovvveeed this class, local gov is the best. Really easy to get the W credit and has fun OTB activities around the Rochester community. Stu is also a great guy and professor.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Local govt has been my favorite class at Rochester so far. Class has very clear syllabus. Did very well in this class, and learned so much more than I had anticipated about Rochester+ how local communities function. Class gave us the ability to explore Rochester and meet with guest speakers working in the Rochester community.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: The class required a significant time commitment and came with numerous challenges. Certain aspects of it had a steep learning curve, but there is so much to learn from him. Dealt with real world projects and situations, not a lecture-style environment, but collaborative working space. Experienced more of a real life scenario than academic.
Stu is a real gem! He can light up the room and make everyone laugh but can also teach you so much. I wish I could have taken more classes with him.

Really nice guy. (too nice in my opinion). His version of 202 is much easier than Gamm's. But grading is up to the TAs so grading might be extremely different between TAs. Fair amount of readings and assignments. A solid class!
Professor Jordan is great. He's very intelligent, clear with his requirements, and the nicest guy you'll ever meet. Any class he teaches is worth taking

Stu is the best. I took PSC 280W with him and it was the best W class I could have ever hoped for. Instead of having to write a 25p research paper like most W classes. We wrote 5 5p papers. It was awesome. I highly recommend all of Stu's classes.
He is a great professor. Extremely nice. Very clear. And he teaches you stuff you will actually use.

This is the second course I took with Prof. Jordan. As always, he is incredibly helpful and makes sure everyone has a good learning experience. What I especially like about his classes is that while he has fairly high standards of grading and does not curve, he is always available for extra help and gives regrade opportunities.

Professor Jordan is just a great guy.  Its a pleasure to be in his classes and he is always willing to lend a helping hand upon request.  If you're a poli sci, I suggest taking as many classes with him as possible.

Although the professor tries very hard to revise his instructions for assignments, it is ultimately up to the TAs to grade assignments--who were not able to provide help for the assignments until after they were due. Unless you already have knowledge of game theory, economics, etc I would not recommend taking this class .

Best professor I've ever had so far! Whoever has a problem with his teaching style in PSC 202 is one who expects the professor to feed him all the class material. This class is for people who actually want to learn. Also, if you have good intuition of logic, game theory, economics, etc., the class will be extremely easy for you!

He completely restructured the course from what it had previously been this year, and did so rather poorly in my opinion. It seemed like he knew as little about his assignments as we did and his explanations of them were rather esoteric as well. I would not recommend taking this course until he has had time to fix most of his assignments.
Amazing professor!  So helpful and friendly. Lecture could drag on so bring a computer.
Best prof I have had at the UofR

He is the greatest guy in the world. You can tell that he actually cares about his students and wants to help them do the best they can. He is clear in what he wants out of students, uses good readings, and engages everyone in class discussion as even when he lectures! Also, he's adorable.
Ridiculously good with names.
awesome professor, funny guy, makes some small mistakes but manages to correct himself, & engages all of the students in discussion
Excellent professor. I actually looked forward to going to class. He makes the discussions very thought provoking.

Sometimes he was very unclear and made some very important mistakes/mix-ups, but I think a lot of this had to do with him being very green (he's only been teaching for a couple of years).  He really isn't bad for someone who's so new.  The material was a little hard, but he made it easy and tried to explain it as best he could.

Homework 20% / Exam 80%. Good professor teaching a tough course. Little to no opportunity for partial credit, which motivated a strong curve but stings when the average for an exam might be between 50-60%.

He's a great professor, is very caring, and is always very helpful in office hours. The course is very math-heavy, and the homework assignments are designed to stretch beyond the course material. This makes it interesting/engaging but also kind of hard to follow at times, especially when the expectations are a bit unclear.
Stefankovic is passionate about the class and its material. Solve extra problems outside of class and do HWs on your own. Exams are hard but not very challenging.

He's a great professor and a kind person, but the course is extremely math-heavy. Unless you have a math degree, it's impossible to follow. He often writes long math expressions on a blank page from his mind almost no visual guidance. I constantly felt lost, had to teach myself most of the material, and spent an enormous amount of time to keep up.

My favorite prof in the CS dept. Great lectures, really cares about the material, and is great to explore ideas more in depth with in office hours. Also took CSC279 with him this semester and loved it. He didn't follow a textbook for either class, so he explored lots of interesting ideas/topics. Highly recommend taking a course with him if you can.

Great professor, and easily accessible outside of class for questions. The material is tough, but also really interesting and applicable outside of class. The homework is difficult, but the TAs are helpful so go to office hours.

Horror stories you may have heard about this class are from years ago, it's much easier now. It's still hard, but Stefankovic is an interesting professor. It's easy to get full points or close to it on the homework, just listen to the TAs at workshops. Prepare for a really hard final exam.

Actually this is the evaluation of CSC 484 - Advanced Algorithms in Fall 2022. He use no textbooks nor slides but writes a lot on the blackboard. 5 homework assignments (some with coding), no exams. Generally you should spend much time after class to learn how to code about the notions learned in the class. But the final grading is not tough now.

He is really a good professor. He explains the materials well and give you solid knowledge in very important topic (Algorithms). He is 1000 times better than Zhupa. He is a tough grader and exams are usually hard but he is exams are getting more reasonable over years. If you want to LEARN take Stefankovic not Zhupa.

I'd recommend taking 282 with Stefankovic because I think you end up learning more from his lectures than from Zhupa (at least based on what people say). And apparently, he also became a little more reasonable with his exams this semester (Fall 2021).

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']
comment: The material is really hard. Stefankovic does his best to explain in a way that makes sense. Your grade is decided by 3 exams. Final is 40% and cummulative so pay attention all year. Best advice: do a lot of practice exams well in advance of the tests. Exams are more difficult than in-class material. This class takes a lot of effort.

Rumor says CSC282 exams might have median scores of 0, but this is not the case. Homework and exams are difficult but still workable if you pay attention in the classes and practice a lot after class.

One of the best professors in the department. Extremely clear lectures, useful office hours, and he's just a really nice person. Just know that this is strictly a math course. If you go into it with only MTH 150 as a background, you're going to be at a disadvantage. It's best if you take as many math courses as you can before CSC 282.

Stefankovic is incredibly intelligent, and delivers phenomenal lectures. Is very open and respondent to questions during lecture. Knows the material extremely well. One of the most difficult graders you will ever have. One small mistake on a written response will get you a 0. If he graded easier he would be the best professor I have ever taken.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Awful professor. You will have to teach yourself. If you're stuck, too bad. Maybe try tutoring.

He's lectures are the ones that I learn the most in all my courses. Extremely smart and willing to answer all your questions. The materials are one of the hardest, but also one of the most interesting, so do follow what he's talking about in lectures.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: I honestly found his CSC282 class to be unfair. 50% of your grade was determined by six questions, no partial credit. He is not afraid to give you a bad grade, no matter how hard you try. This class is not the best for mental health... Overall, I feel like this class measures raw intelligence, rather than how hard you try. Is this bad? Up to you.
the worst professor and does not respect students who fall behind at all

absolute worst course I have ever had. His grading policy was that he takes the minimum of all your scores and uses that as your final grade, which in the end, ends up punishing the student unless you're the top of the class and don't get any grade under a B. Tests so unreasonably difficult that the class average was usually in the 20% range

tags: ['Respected', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Hes really freaking smart. Lectures are good, but you have to be 100% dialed in, otherwise you will get left behind.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Very chill and down to earth person, ready to answer any question and help with any problem. Seems a bit intimidating at first but is a one of the nicest professors in the department. Material is quite tough, but follow lectures, ask questions, read the books, practice questions regularly, go to office hours and recitations and you should get an A!
90% of grade depended on exams.

Daniel is a great professor with clear teaching style. The material is kind of difficult but he makes it easy to follow. There is some math (quite a bit of math thinking) required for this class. If you don't have enough math background you might have a hard time.
The exam questions were not making sense with lots of unnecessary information. He just made things unnecessarily complicated.

The lecture is not making sense and no lecture note at all. If you don go to class, you will fail. His exams are not clearly worded and has some ridiculous real-life problems. And he will never show respect to students. I don't think students will choose to take his class if its not mandatory.
Super cool dude, super cool class
Easily the worst lecturer I've ever had. Be prepared to teach yourself.
Legend
An interesting course but the grading criteria is tough for a good grade.

Don't get me wrong, this was a very interesting class. Lectures were boring, but I really enjoyed reading the textbook and teaching myself the material. However, the testing and grading criteria for the class could be better. I understood the material really well, probably better than most of my classmates, and I still got a B-.

This guy REALLY knows his stuff, but that stuff is very difficult and abstract. He really does care about his students, if you know what's going on in his class. But it's hard to see that. If you can't keep up, don't count on a lot of help from him.

Excellent professor that facilitates a great learning environment with thoroughly explained concepts and insightful info on research. Lectures are dense with info, and the exams are tough but open notes and she gives you a superset of exam questions that she'll choose from. Answer those questions ahead of time and take good notes and you'll do well

Prof. Kurumada made me wish that I was a BCS major. While the exams were difficult, if you prepared good notes (exams are open-note), you could absolutely do well on them. Fascinating material, and the course design facilitated a greater understanding of and appreciation for it, which made the experience much more enjoyable. 11/10
Had her as my PI for a research class. She's incredibly helpful.
Giving low scores. Compared to other professors in the writing department, Kara really disappoints students a lot. I will never recommend this professor at all.

She's an absolutely wonderful professor. She teaches with great interest and skill. I want to study medieval literature because of this class now! She makes class interesting and fun. You will grow a lot in English writing after a class with McShane.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'TEST HEAVY', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Her English is not pretty good. The examples she used in lectures are too simple compared to tests. Reading the textbook is much better than attending letcures. Tests can be hard but there will be curve.

Professor Blackman stands out in the way that he wrote homework/test questions. In principle, they were never difficult, but they tested the fundamentals of a subject at a very deep level. Homework, and exams especially, were fantastic learning experiences. He's also a very kind person and amazing to chat with. Stand-up guy and brilliant physicist.

Prof. Cook is such a huge role model of mine and 350 characters isn't nearly enough to explain how incredible she is! She is so kind and truly cares about her students. She sat with me for hours answering all my questions without making it feel like an imposition. 201 is hard, but she makes it manageable. I will miss her next semester :')

Good with lectures but exams are unnecessarily hard and not reflective of Webworks. Partially reflective of Gradescopes, but not really. Exams are graded on a curve because of this and everyone scores pretty much the same so there's not really a way to get an A.
Reallllllly nice professor
Very harsh

She is just so nice 😭 I had a panic attack during the exam and I had to leave. She was just so caring and so helpful throughout the whole process. I love her😭 Thanks to her, otherwise I wouldn't have passed the course.

Great lectures, and cares a lot about making sure everyone understands the concepts. I never liked probability in the past but found this class interesting, especially once we got into more complicated math.

Mary Cook is one of the best math professors I ever had! She was accommodating and accessible outside of class. The final was a surprise for all of us since the questions were harder than previous years. Due to the midterm averages being higher than the final averages, our grades were curved. If I studied harder, I could have gotten at least an A-

Dr. Cook is an amazing professor. She is patient and explains things clearly. She's accessible outside of class and always willing to provide support if you ask. Her lecture notes are extremely well-organized, just like her lectures. Def attend her classes. Her office hours are incredibly helpful too. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you need it.

Dr. Cook has extremely concise lectures, but even more concise complimentary notes. She is EXTREMELY accessible outside of class, and will give great advice for non-class related matters such as course selection. I didn't go to class much because the notes were so good, but I definitely recommend going to recitation or study hours. Great professor!

She is a very nice professor who lectures well but the math department at this school is just awful. The exams are difficult and the webwork is harder than 141. She records lectures which is nice and she is accessible outside of class. She also posts filled-in notes and blank notes. Definitely try to get 100% on the webwork and workshop.

I was never able to get above a B+ in a calc class, finally was able to after taking 164 with her. She is so clear and concise when teaching. Everything was thoroughly explained. Exams were difficult though, review her in class examples when studying for an exam.
Mary Cook is a good professor, explains topics well and is very approachable. If she is teaching multi you are in good shape.

Cook is a great professor, the class is quite difficult tho. All of her examples come directly out of the book. The Webwork is quite challenging. Recommend using prof Leonard on YouTube for help to make the class more manageable.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Coming into college,I thought I wanted to be a math minor. To say the least, I never plan to take another math class again. The homework for this class is ten times more difficult than what we are taught. You basically have to teach yourself everything. I attended math study halls for roughly five hours every week to just get help, and I still bad.
Cook is great, but this course is toooooo difficult

She is so nice. I wouldn't have passed without her. If you need to set up an appointment or her notes, she will get back to you. The material and webwork is still difficult, so I recommend using Paul's Online Notes or CETL alongside the class. One of the best math professors I've had.
He was the best professor anyone could have asked for.
Dr. Dietsche is an amazing professor. I miss his class so much!!!

Dietsche is my most memorable UR prof - you will never forget this guy! His stories are great & I loved his life lessons - he showed a Kevin Trudeau "Natural Cures They Don't Want You To Know About" infomercial & then revealed all the misleading BS! He wants to produce thinkers & successful medical students. Great prof!

He is the best ever! He tells many stories about the time he served in the navy, and those are so much fun to listen in class. Tests are very straight forward, but doesn't mean they are easy. Nobody could teach physiology better than him!
Best teacher ever. This is a class about taking notes and memorizing. you would be surprised how many people havent developed these skills by the time they enter college

Not a bad teacher, tough class especially over the summer.  Tends to not be the most organized guy but could be worse.  His stories were great.  Tests are short but are hard.  Teacher recommended summer class is not (to much info to fast).

Very unorganized.  Though he is a very charismatic man, he fails at being a good lecturer.  He doesn't even bother to let us have access to the slides he puts up and his tests are quite difficult compared to what he teaches.

Excellent lecturer.  Very fast paced.  Straight from the book and lectures.  Glad to see he's still teaching.  I had him in 91/92 and I kept my binder from that class because I was so amazed (and still am) at how much I learned.
Awesomeness incarnate. Tough class, but he keeps the material interesting with his personality and stories. Very friendly and personable.

This man is one of the most caring professors I've had.  Makes a point to meet every student during lab (and remember names) and give them on the spot advice for life.  Lectures are fast paced, but the tests are very basic and easy to pull an A.

The class was rough with the amount of material that you were expected to memorize.  All tests were multiple choice and non-cumulative but really specific.  He was a very good teacher though and extremely funny.  The little annecdotal stories he told during lectures definitely helped with remembering material for the exams.
No Comments

****ing awesome- bitter divorcee, proud ****, ex-farmer, vietnam navy veteran, outright crazy and one hella charming man.  Teaches each lecture with a moral for life, and gives you a lot of other valuable life lessons along the way, mostly through didactic horse breeding stories. Take the class
this man, while hillarious, has no sense of organization. I'm also pretty sure he does no preparation for this class... i mean honestly is an overhead with some key terms to much to ask for?
He's quite literally very very crazy, but entertaining. And the class is relatively easy too
Fantastic lectures, I didn't skip a single one.  The guy is hysterical.  Painful amounts of memorization, but all tests are non-cumulative.

I really enjoyed this class and professor.  There is alot of memorizing in this class, although it's an easy course concept-wise.  A few students do comment that he doesn't have much organization within his lectures, but I didn't find this the case.
I love this man.  I am a man myself.  Boy that is wierd.  Anyway, an amazing teacher who can make even physiology a fun and interesting class.
Very direct - brute memorization class ... great naval stories

can be very sarcastic if you match his energy. Will give back points on exams if you deserve it. you'd have no idea what your grade is and even after getting the semester grade, takes a while to understand how he created the scale. I think he cares for his students but takes just a little bit of pride in making exams with 65 average.

Solid lectures, entertaining, clearly passionate about the material. Does a decent job explaining things. Accessible outside class and cares about his students. The homework is a bit tedious. The exams are hard, but study and you'll probably be fine. Fairly lenient grader, you can often convince him to give you a few extra points if you go to OH.

His lectures were great, he had many "hands-on" examples throughout the semester and even if you can't go to class his online notes are great (class is better though). This was my first real physics course, and although it's not my strong suit at all, it went much better because of him. Legitimately a great prof and I'd take him if you can.

Professor Manly was inspirational to me this semester. 123 was the first physics class I took at UR, and he certainly continued to inspire the love of physics that I got from a good teacher in high school. The tests are difficult, but doing the problem sets and practicing from old exams makes them absolutely doable.

Manly is a good prof. Lectures are energetic and entertaining but he would often miss a week of classes at a time do to research commitments. Exams were tough and given in a 50 minute time period so you had to race against the clock. All in all the guy is a good prof but the logistics of the class could be much better.

Manly was the professor for my E&M class that was self-paced. At first, he seems really helpful and genuinely interested in the students. Soon, it became clear that was not the case. He and his TA would send emails weeklysaying that he would "laugh in our faces" if we didn't get all the work done and needed help. The emails really put students down

Genuinely invested in teaching and really wants you to understand physics, but not always great at explain things - lecture is often unhelpful. Tests are really tough but fair, and he let's you bring in a formula sheet. Going to workshop and doing the problem sets are essential to passing. The book is super helpful - definitely a must have.

I have a love hate relationship with him. Love him until an exam then hate a few days after exam then I forgive him. You will literally not pass if you don't study and actual learn. You can't just pattern match the problems with how he writes his exams. Very conceptual and creative with writing problems. But I still love him

Manly is funny, interesting, and wholly devoted to his students. There were moments in lecture where he'd lose track of a problem he was doing, but he'd always inform us of the right solution once he'd worked it out properly. His tests are fair, but they're definitely difficult. One of the most dedicated teachers I've had here in a long time.
Great class, don't be concerned about his curve. He respects the effort the class requires and grades accordingly. He's also pretty funny.

He is a funny guy and know the material very, very well. But, if you were not studying regularly, it's very hard, i mean VERY hard, to keep up with. His exams are conceptual and tricky. Understand the concept is a key to do well in his class.

He's pretty interesting in class.  Sometimes he slips into just showing lots of slides in a row, making me painfully aware of the clock above his left shoulder.  His curve doesn't really make sense to me (normalizes all tests to an 70% mean, even if it means students losing points) but my grade in the class turned out alright, so I can't complain.

Took 113 as a freshman. Not a phsyics person but pulled off a B. Manly is a good prof. Exams are hard but not impossible. He curves (even if that means curving DOWN). Graded homework is a booster.  Don't skip lecture.  Workshop was alright.  Labs are easy.

Very enthusiastic and clear. Lectures are usually interesting. 142 was a very challenging course. My average test score was in the 40's but I got a B in the course. Homeworks aren't worth very many points but DO THEM. They will help you more than anything else.

EXCELLENT communication--he e-mailed us constantly with corrections, helpful hints, & other info, and he always added bits of humor to keep things entertaining.  He used a light saber as a pointer, and his method of using a tablet PC projected onto a big screen for lectures was perfect.  Demos were exciting and lectures were interesting. Great guy!

Seems nice, but can turn on you.  Is a bit full of himself. Lecture was at times entertaining. Exams are difficult.  (but people still got 100s, I have no idea how).  Workshop was somewhat helpful.  At least he renormalizes the grades.
What a terrible teacher! And he thinks he's funny too.
best prof in the physics department
Great Guy.  Definitely knew how to party back in his time!
Learned a lot.  Great professor.

Excellent professor.  Very clear/Instructs well.  Uses effective in-class demonstrations.  Instituted small groups which really help learning the material.  Tests are generally fair, and well representative of material that was supposed to be learned.
Manly's awesome!  Good natured, and a great professor.  Makes a painful course slightly easier.
Eager for the students to do well without being overly easy.
He liked White Russians.  Very helpful even though the class was mad hard.
No Comments

funny, remembers what it's like to be a college student
enthusiastic, extremely funny

Amazing lecture. I hate math and statistics. He made it interesting and somehow I learned the content.

the GOAT. He's hands down the best professor in the stats dept. He is super understanding and he cares about his students. He does all he could to make sure we get supported. He is very organized. He goes above and beyond and bakes cookies for his students. He is such a kind soul.

Although I did not take any courses in person with this professor, his lecture slides are the most structured and logically comprehensible I have ever seen in any other course here at UR, and I have been taking tons of Bio and Econ courses with both Scientific and Statistic contents. Highest admiration and respect to him! Thank you!
Best Prof in Stat Department
Good class. It requires good math skills. I wish it could include broad topics in regression. eg, non-linear regression, ridge, lasso, etc.

I have taken multiple classes with Professor Ciminelli, and he is the best professor I have had at u of r. He is extremely knowledgeable and caring. You can tell he truly cares about his students and what they learn from his classes. Exams and homework can be lengthy and tough, but it is truly worth it.
best prof ever
taken STAT216, best professor ever met
Best stat prof ever

To say that he is a good professor is an understatement. Unlike most of the others I have had, Professor Ciminelli explains concepts extremely well and is always willing to help students who are struggling. Would strongly encourage any CS or stats majors to take a course with him.

Ciminelli is genuinely one of the best professors I've had here. While the content for the class can be quite challenging, his lectures are extremely clear and break everything down. He recognizes when we're not understanding a topic and adjusts accordingly. He genuinely wants you to succeed.
Best professor ever. Amazing lectures. Reasonable and helpful homework. Clear class notes. Students can really learn solid knowledge from his class.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: This is a relatively hard course, but prof. Ciminelli is really helpful!
Best professor ever and STAT 218 is relative easy.
The reviews are true, Dr. Cimminelli is a great professor and will help you outside of class when you need it. Workload is kind of heavy, so get started on assignments in advance.

Fantastic lectures, very passionate and caring. Will respond to emails quickly and is very generous and respectful. 262 was very easy, but stats is not a difficult subject. Prof Ciminelli was a pleasure all semester.

Joe is the best professor in terms of teaching not only in U of R, but also in my grad school. I took his STT218 in Fall 2018 and STT223 in Spring 2019. I feel so lucky to have him during my senior year. He is the one that makes classes organized, easier and interesting. More importantly, you could get a lot of extra help outside of the class.
Rarely do you see a professor that's both a nice and easy-going person while at the same time also a great instructor. One or the other is usually what you hope for.
Good

He is probably one of the best professor at U of R. Not only does his class is super organized and the lectures are very informative and useful. He is very helpful after class and supporting his students. Fantastic teacher!

I've taken STT212 with Prof Ciminelli before and I'm taking his CSC262 through zoom. For each model he listed, he would sliced the content into smaller pieces of videos with clear titles. He cares for students and keeps sending reminding emails with specific responses to questions. He is PERFECT. Such a regret that we cannot meet him in person.
He is one of the nicest professor I had for my undergraduate.

He really is one of the best professors at the University. Caring, gentle, takes time to get to know you. Interesting and really great introduction to statistics. You can't really go wrong with him. Was struggling a bit in the class and he set me up with a great tutor. Great guy.
Professor Ciminelli is a gem at U of R, one hw assignment per week and gives out practice tests that are very similar to the actual ones.

Ciminelli is by far the best professor I've ever had at UR. He truly cares about how his students are doing , and does his best to make sure no one is left behind . The way he approaches the material is easily comprehendible. There is one homework assignment each week , but I feel the assignment directly reflects the types of questions on tests .
He goes above and beyond as a professor. He is very sweet and is always willing to help students out.

Professor Ciminelli is hands down the BEST Professor Ive ever met. Though our class became online, he is very responsive and caring to his students. His tests are reasonable and gives opportunity to correct for credit. His lectures are also super coherent and organized. Simply a great person and lecturer! Thanks for everything Professor Ciminelli!

Super good and helpful prof. Really detailed, clear, and organized slides. Lectures are boring but not required. He often uploads supplemental videos of him solving problems if he thinks he didn't explain something well in lecture. He also made cookies for us on the last class!
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is an amazing professor and cares about his students.
He is just amazing. The only bad thing is at the end you realize how BAD your other professors are.

Really nice professor in Statistics Department! For students planning Data Science major: if you haven't decided which course to take among 212/213/262, then 262 can be the best choice for you, which is also the best connection to DSC265!

Easily best professor I've ever had. The material isn't particularly difficult, but if you ever have any troubles with it, Joe is there to help you at almost any hour of the day. And he makes cookies for all his classes. <3 Joe

If the class experience given by professors is normally distributed, then we can reject the null hypothesis the Professor Ciminelli is like other professors, with p<0.0001. Ive never seen a professor devote so much to teaching well. Proof: made cookies for 150 students at finals. thats not a requirement; it says a lot. He wont leave anyone behind.

Professor Ciminelli is the best teacher i've had at the university so far and is my favorite teacher ever. He genuinely cares about his students understanding the material and enjoying his class. His lectures are interesting and he makes sure the students understand the material before they leave each day.

Amazing, amazing, amazing professor! He's one of the most caring and thoughtful people I have encountered at the UofR. He's fully devoted to the class and will try his best to get you to understand this stuff! He was of great help! 100% deserved his Professor of the Year award!

Dr. Ciminelli is literally my absolute favorite teacher. He really wants his students to succeed and works really hard to make sure that his students understand his material. He's extremely accessible and makes stats interesting to learn (he is very knowledgeable). He got the professor of the year award for a reason. TAKE STATS WITH HIM!
I love ciminelli so much that I created an account so that I can hype this man up. TAKE HIS CLASS
I would die for this man

One of the best professor Ive had in college. He cares about students and is approachable outside class. The homework needs some time work but its doable. Class was very helpful in learning RStudio. Definitely recommend to take his class.

Definitely one of the best professors I had in u of r. Always care about his students and respond emails super fast. He even baked cookies himself for 6 hours for us during final week. Strongly recommend to take his class.

comment: He's really approachable and easy to talk to. The homework is challenging, but it makes you to learn the material. This class is awesome if you enjoy statistics and learning more about different tests and models used by statisticians.

Best professor Ive had so far! Hes so organized with his class material and he actually made me interested in statistics (a class I took just for the premed req)! Plus hes very accessible outside of class, which is very nice. Go Joe!!
He really cares about his students and so far one of the most amazing professors.

Joe is by far the best professor I've had at UR, I've taken STT212 and STT218 with him and thoroughly enjoyed both (never in a million years thought I would enjoy stats). His passion for stats and teaching is blatantly obvious and he always makes time to help his students and make sure they understand everything. Restored my faith in professors.

Professor Ciminelli is one of my favorite professors. He is very friendly and approachable and will respond to emails very very quickly! He makes statistics easy to understand and he explains concepts extremely well. Highly recommend Ciminelli for any Intro Stats courses!!

OK SO- Dr. Ciminelli actually is easily the most accessible and well-read professor I have come across at U of R. STT212 is needed for lots of kids and he makes the class so FREAKIN' interesting and easy. He is super big on examples, makes great study guides, responds to emails ASAP. I haven't met a teacher like him and I'm scared I never will.

Dr. Ciminelli is by far the best professor I've ever had. His class was wonderful and I learned so much! He was always available for help understanding material, and he even baked us cookies for the last class of the semester! Also, can we talk about how insanely cute Dr. Ciminelli is?! Easily the hottest professor here!
Inspiring teacher!

He is an excellent teacher. Materials are clear and organized. And he goes through everything in great details! I asked for several office hours l, and he made great efforts to cooperate. Good teacher!

The content covered in his lecture has no connection. His teaching method always tried to mess me up and made me even more confused! The worst professor I have ever met. And the exam is quite different from what he taught in his meaningless lecture.

Not sure he has any idea about what he's teaching. He gave difficult coding assignments to students with 0 Python background and was being tough on grading. If you don't have a strong stats background, don't even consider taking his class.
He is a fantastic teacher. Very funny. Did some reviewers confuse him for somebody else? He never gave extra credit
His lectures are disorganized and the slides dont help in the slightest. However, he offers up to 2% extra credits. If you only want a good grade and dont expect to learn much, take his class.

The lectures were not very clear and Professor Yang sometimes rambled on about a study or an example that wasn't making sense to the students. The content overall wasn't difficult so as long as you did well on the homeworks and studied for the quizzes and exams, you can get a good grade. The textbook can be helpful, but not mandatory.

He's a nice enough guy but his lectures make no sense whatsoever. He would bring up a topic, say a few sentences about what it is, give 10 minutes worth of examples and say the important conclusion once and move on. The thing is though, is that the slides that he posts don't have the important parts so you have to read the book if you miss.
Ok guy

Prof. Chaves is a bore to listen to lecture and does not do a great job of explaining material. Like all math courses here they are ungodly difficult for no reason. He did care and was open to questions and would help but was not very good at getting the material to click with students and went very slow in lecture.
has got to easily be one of the worst professors here at u of r.

MATH 200: Easily worst professor and class Ive ever taken. He does not care about his students. Contents in lecture and hw do not match, sometimes hw has content not in textbook. This class is to prepare us for math proofs but he DOES NOT PREPARE ANYTHING and expect us to write like we know everything. Not even a hard class but harsh af grading.

I have never had a professor who makes more mistakes than him. EVERY SINGLE assignment has a mistake on it and there are 10 emails of me CORRECTING HIM. IM THE STUDENT I SHOULDNT BE CORRECTING THE PROF. THERE WERE MISTAKES ON THE FINAL, MULTIPLE IN FACT. He is so disorganized and such a harsh grader and isn't lenient at all. Avoid if possible.

Professor chaves has one of the best methods of going throught examples. His notes are also a piece of art, more than enough to study everything with examples and be able to answer questions in homework and lectures. He made discrete math an easy A for me!
This guy is great. He's a talented mathematician and can cast light on some really difficult topics. The class is difficult, but he does a great job of showing the more beautiful side of mathematics.
really good!! hard to pay attention in class, because its pretty boring/monotone, so its easy to doze off
Laura is a gentle and interesting professor. Her classes are very relaxed, but attendance is very important. Only when you attend classes on time can you gain a lot.
Pretty solid professor. Not much to say because this class isn't very demanding. If you go to class and put in 40% effort you should be fine.

She's a great person—as long as you complete and submit assignments on time, you're guaranteed an A. She'll also help you with any questions about papers. I'd absolutely take her class again if I had the chance.
nice instructor, just select her course without worry

Laura is a very nice professor who gives clear and useful feedbacks to students. She is good at teaching too. I'm not a fan of writing, but I enjoyed writing in her class. She is a fair grader that if you have done your work well, she would give you the grade that you deserve.

I absolutely loved professor Whitebell for my required writing class this semester. She was super flexible with my schedule and was understanding about extensions. I'm not a huge fan of writing in general, but I'd take this class again with her any semester. Would definitely recommend!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I am the one who got an A from WRTG 105A on 1/20/21. Everything is similar. She is always respectful, kind, and structural in teaching. I would love to take a future writing course with her if I have a chance.

Although the readings she assigned weren't all that in-depth, I thought the provided material was still interesting enough to have a pretty fun class. Lectures weren't too heavy, so long as you participate in discussions and submit the papers on time, the class is not too difficult.

For her 105A, what really matters are the two formal assignments (two roughly 5-pages papers), which add to 60% of the grade. As long as you do all the homework, you will get the rest 40%. She is very caring and serious about academics. She is open to paper extensions as long as you are hard-working and respectful. Sincere thanks to her.

Awesome teacher. She is naturally funny and will always give super helpful feedback. Her style of teaching is very collaborative (making sure you get feedback from different sources), and she's always available if you need to talk to her about something.
Takes herself very seriously and has no sense of humor, which is probably why she didn't get that 273 is a joke. It's an easy class though so it doesn't really matter that she's not great.
She's a really caring professor and is very open and wants to make sure that her students succeed. While she is a tough grader in my opinion, she gives good feedback. Really great class.

She chose super boring readings and topics for the course. Was forcing us to do a lot of group work, during which she was doing her own stuff and didn't even pay attention to us. Surprisingly, the requirements were more harsh in this  class than in WRT 105 (according to my friends' feedback). Laura is nice as a person though and gives extensions.
Best professor I had in this university yet; love her.
Super nice, really into her class. Had some great discussions. I would recommend if you are picking a WRT105E class.

If you just read the syllabus for this course, you will quickly understand who your dealing with, "You may consider the reading load for the course to be totally unreasonable! My response? Too bad!" "  I know your generation “doesn't read.”Again, too bad." He does not care about his class or students; he only cares about pushing his political views
he genuinely cares about his students and his lectures are full of wisdom

I've never had a professor phone it in this hard. Johnson is crazy disorganized, unfocused, uninteresting, and clearly not trying. I can't believe he has so many positive ratings. Nice guy though. Very easy class. But, you won't learn anything.

Amazing professor with really insightful lectures. Likes to go on tangents but he's funny. The readings are fairly dense but definitely manageable and engaging. Very lenient grader and super flexible with extensions too; he definitely cares about his students. Also really helpful if you go to his office hours if needed.

Took during covid. Lectures are him talking about the reading the whole time (great if you don't get the readings or if it was really dense) I skipped like the whole class the entire semester (it was rough okay) and I still passed with just skimming the reading. He was amazing though. So kind and understanding please talk with him if you need help.
Professor Johnson's class was really good which I learned a lot from. There is not much reading, approximately 50 pages per week. Recommend this class!

James Johnson was a fantastic professor, he was interesting to listen to and he was understanding of difficulties caused by life. His class was super reading heaving and was mainly discussion based which made it fun and easy to stay entertained/involved. The paper at the end was challenging, but also fun because of how much freedom you have with it

We love Professor Johnson for his humor. He can always keep students awake--even when I'm taking his class in the middle of the night! He loves reading, and he makes sure his students love reading as well. So get ready to read a lot, otherwise you won't understand what he's talking about. A good grade will ensue if you do all the readings.

Very relaxed class. All discussion based with a lot of reading but not a lot of assignments. Very understanding of students and flexible around certain things. He just wants his students to learn and grow and doesn't care about grades, which is scary but it works out in the end. Course is really unique and changes your perspective, highly recommend

Terrific guy! Down to earth, is there for the students, humble, and makes the dull subject matter (e.g. 17th century political philosophy) understandable and, somehow, interesting.  My favorite professor this semester and would definitely take another class with him again.  You really only need to hustle for the three big papers he assigns.
He is a good professor who really cares about the students.

Johnson is a character. He likes to be agreed with so don't argue, he has favorites, he expects a lot of "smart" comments but if you try, pay attention and care about the subject you will be fine.  I really actually like him, he's  kinda disorganized but i'm being negative, he is actually really good, so overall i think you should take his class.

Prof Johnson is extremely good at getting you to understand political philosophy, and teaches the "lectures" in a seminar style that allows people to really get to the heart of an issue. He can be redundant but that helps drill crucial points in. I will try to take another of his classes ASP.

Prof. Johnson is amazing! Really smart and eager to help students out. I've never found him to be arrogant, for being as brilliant as he is, he is really down to earth. His classes can be easy, but he always assigns great readings and offers great insight on them.

Very funny and relaxed, Johnson will keep you somewhat interested in going to class, although his seminar does have a lot of reading and discussion so definitely be prepared for that. He is VERY lenient about time pressures, so gives extensions liberally as long as you're not an atrocious student.
He is very smart, interesting and cute.

Johnson is one of those professors who you'll want to wake up at 9:00 in the morning and listen to. His overwhelmingly benevolent and hilarious nature is what makes his class so honestly enjoyable; don't get a Poli Sci degree at Rochester without taking one of his courses.

Sort of annoying. Take notes on everything he says and then regurgitate it to him in your paper. Although you can input some of your own opinion, it is important to show through your essays that you know what he said.

Gives great lectures.. If you take good notes it is easy to do well on the writing assignments even if you have not done all the readings completely.  He is very helpful and understanding if you go to his office with questions/concerns.  Lectures can get long but he is pretty funny and is a good teacher.

Very interesting and well informed professor. I don't see how that other person could have said that he would mark you down for different views. Really enjoyed his class, he's pretty funny and very nice.

Chris is hilarious, such a g. Great class, just study for the exams and you'll do well.

Take him, easy/funny - you dont have to show up to class to get A, he records all lectures -4 multiple choice tests worth 50 points each -2 mini courses offered by TAs (attendance and a small asaignments to do- you choose the course) worth 25 points each -2 discussion/debate session worth 2 points each (for showing up) - can get extra credit
Very easy class, but still interesting. Niemiec is a great guy and makes the lectures enjoyable.
Such a nice guy. Lectures gave you everything you needed for every exam. AKA don't bother buying the textbook (sorry Professor haha)

Awesome teacher but the class isn't easy. Study for his tests, attend class and you'll be fine. He's also extremely friendly and personable.

One of the best psych classes I've taken.  This professor is one of a kind (in a good way, could not believe he has a phd when first saw him). no tests!!! Assignments were easy as long as some effort was put in. Professor was knowledgeable about the field and ecouraged discussion and questions. VERY approachable

Good professor.  Expects students to work hard but rewards those that do.

This was by far the worst class I have ever taken on this campus.  The prof. is boring, and grading is very unfair.  He is too specific on tests because he teaches in a very vague sense.
LOTTTSSSS of reading, feels a bit redundant and long at times but worth it in the end. Really good teacher, you can tell he cares a lot, good lecturer.

comment: I thought the class itself was really interesting, and his lectures were informative. Professor Devaney gives a lot of dense material to read which can get a bit repetitive, especially in discussions. tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: He makes the class enjoyable and is a great lecturer. It's not that hard to do well but the readings can feel pointless and unnecessarily long. The papers and tests aren't that bad as long as you go to lecture. He answers questions and you can tell he loves what he's talking about. Do the readings because a lot of the lecture is discussion based.

Devaney is a really good professor in that he is tough, but he also cares about you. He does make you do some unnecessary reading, but he has a great way of explaining things and making you tie things together. He can get dry in lectures, but it's still a good class if you need an elective.

comment: Provided A LOT of readings for every single class (Had to buy 5 books), which were then discussed in class. The lecture was just an hour of information being thrown at you. Professor was really knowledgeable and helpful. Doesn't give away A's but fairly generous if you do the work.
Lectures are solid background, what made the class are the very interesting readings and discussions, which were well-facilitated.

Professor Zach is the best professor I have had as a first-semester freshman. He is an amazing guy who is extremely passionate about teaching. Nice guy. Harsh grader. Gives good feedback. Too many long, complex readings. Boring subject matter if you're not interested in ethics. I only took it because it was the only one that fit in my schedule.

comment: Zach is the best professor I've taken so far. He's extremely welcoming and will always do his best to ensure you do your best. He always has a smile on his face and loves hearing what his students have to say. A guy who truly loves his job as a teacher.

Zach as an amazing teacher, esp for freshmen! He genuinely cares for his students and makes the topic worth writing for. I came in with mild interest and left almost sad that the class was over. His passion for the material and his students trickles down to his class and def shows in their writing. Take his class if you can, you wont regret it!!!

Had Zach for both WRTG105 and 266. Legitimately a great guy who's passionate about the work he's doing and cares a lot about students. Some of his advice from 105 still sticks with me; he'll help make you a better writer as well as encourage you to really grapple with the course material. Can't say enough good things.
great professor one of my favorites

Zach is one of my favorite instructors I've ever had, period. He teaches with a passion that just radiates off of him but really lets student opinions shine, as well as making seemingly boring topics pretty interesting. I could go on but I totally recommend his class and am excited to have him as an instructor again.

Zach is a completely fair grader. He puts so much time and effort into helping each student improve their writing. If you do the work, you will get a good grade. Zach was a great professor for WRTG 105! He is so nice and genuinely cares about each student. You can tell that he is passionate about the subject matter. Barber is an excellent instructor--he's friendly, gave individualized feedback, graded fairly, and fostered a collaborative atmosphere. We learned to write essays/citations/etc, but I most loved the riveting discussions (eg, esp. the one about what happens to us when we die). This course represents the ideal of a first-year writing course. Bravo!

Instructor Zach puts a lot of efforts into structuring his lessons with his students' best interests and intellectual development in mind. You will find Zach to be very approachable and open to feedback, so don't be hesitate to reach out to him whenever you have any concerns regarding academics or criticisms of the lessons.

Zach is a phenomenal writing instructor who truly cares about his students and how he can better their writing skills. My writing improved so much from this class, and the discussions we had were always intriguing. Highly reccomend taking him even if you're not a fan of philosophy.

Professor Barber was amazing and the only Writing professor I had an amazing time with. Take his class if you love discussions!

He's actually really helpful and responsive. He's nice and understanding. He's a good choice for a writing professor but the way he designs his class is very demotivating. The sheer amount of essays and other assignments is very overwhelming5. I felt like it was my most tiring class this semester.

TOUGH GRADER but he is really passionate and kind. He tries to be understanding, responds to emails fast, also enjoyed conferencing with him. He gives really great feedback. If you are not a great writer though, you won't do too well.

Brenda is wonderful- I had her as my prof for 105 my first semester as a freshman, and she was super understanding when I had trouble getting things completed on time and with all the stuff that comes with starting college.

I absolutely love her

This is a lecture I don't really want to take again

16% of grade is hw and 84% is tests.  Exams are extremely hard and so many people fear having to retake the class. They really are the worst. Best Econ teacher I've ever met!

comment: Very sweet woman with an obvious love for the source material. Knows her stuff and encourages her students to think differently when analyzing the readings. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Osucha is very sweet and knowledgeable about American Literature. Class is heavy on reading and participation, but that's the usual for an English class.
