I took 171-173, she is hard to understand at times, but definitely one of the  most intelligent people I've had as professors.  I was a TA for her one semester, and witnessed her commitment to every single one of her students firsthand.  Do not miss the opportunity to take a class with her.

I didn't realize it at the time, but this lady's a pretty good professor, especially when you compare her to some of the other people in the math department (cough, Segal, cough). She has the most annoying voice in the history of the world but if you can get through that she's not bad. She's damn annoying but a pretty good professor.
She is out of control for workload, and she has a tendency to lose turned in work...and exams, blaming it on the students.
Most intelligent person I've ever met.  Assigns lots of work.  Always willing to help her students.

depending on the subject she may be very clear or not so clear...but regardless she is ALWAYS willing to help her students.  to her, teaching comes before research.  i have never seen such dedication from a teacher to her students.  i'd even be willing to say that she places her students before her sanity.  great sense of humor too.

At first you might be a little thrown off by her and think she is not a good professor...but once you get used to her, she is always willing to help at any time.  She is probably the only professor who answers webwork by herself at 2:00am the night before it's due.  She's a great person outside of the class and will help anyone.

She tends to move quickly in class (yet slowly because she assumes the students aren't as smart as we really are).  I guarantee she will assign more homework than any other class you have ever taken, and she will give tests that could easily run 3+ hours (my last exam was about 18 pages).
brilliant
She's completely nuts.  Her lectures can be confusing, but she's pretty helpful when you ask her questions afterwards.  Tests are manageable, but the curve always helps.

Very enthusiastic, however, doesn't know how to teach.  Is an easy grader if you do your homework, but she gives insane amounts of work.  Her tests are insane, though curved generously.  The end result is a decent grade with nothing learned.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Such an icon.
Bad professor ever!!!

Some reviews are harsh (she recently became a new mom), though the descriptions aren't wrong. Homework from mid-October was graded just days before final grades. Classes were not well thought out or prepared. Expectations were unclear and felt inconsistent, with high demands despite limited support. She taught as if we were grad students.

She gives terrible lectures. Although materials for this course are not hard, she explains it in a difficult and difficult to understand way. Her homework are related to the textbook materials but different from her lecture material sometimes, since her lecture usually teaches wrong things other than textbook.

Worst professor ever. She smiles at you with fakeness and she loves to see you suffer. One hw problem had us do 200+ by hand calculations. If you want to be dehumanized take this class with this awful monster. Also randomly slanders students saying they use chatgpt when they dont. That is actually harassment the school should fire her.

This was the most stressful and discouraging class i've taken. The grading criteria was always confusing, and the workload was extremely heavy. The course structure made the experience very frustrating.

One of the most boring and mundane classes I have taken and the way material is presented feels very mundane and dry. Please be careful with what you get into when taking this class. Be prepared for a lot of unnecessary work and forced attendance.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Dr. G is very knowledgeable. She teaches almost solely based on formulas, which is excellent for some but not others. Exams are only 50% of the grade, so getting high marks is achievable.  All exams also have formula sheets. Labs and homework require effort but are graded generously. She also gives a lot of partial credit, so show all your work.

Nice teacher. You get a lot of partial credit back and the practice homework is always super helpful to do before homework because they're pretty similar. Homework takes a while but you use it to study for exams, so it makes the exams much easier.

Dr. G really cares about your education and seeing you do well. Her class is designed for you to do well if you do the homework and go to lab (each is worth 25%). There are even multiple opportunities to earn extra credit or bonus points. I scored a 70 on my first exam and still managed to get an A.

Dr. G is the MOST organized prof I've seen in U of R. Her lectures were very clear and thorough and it was clear that she was willing to help her students. Although she was a bit nitpicky at some point (especially in exams) and there were lots of HWs, there were lots of extra credits and chances to learn from your mistakes without much penalty.

I felt she didn't do a good job helping students understand why a solution was the answer to the problem, and her slides and information were very uninformative. I am not the best mathematics person, and I really did struggle to grasp concepts. Thank goodness homework and lab are 50% of grades; I wouldn't have survived otherwise...

Dr. G is one of the best professors I have had at this school. She explains R in a way that is clear and easy to follow along with. Lectures are mandatory and for good reason, they are key for following along in the class. Hard homework, but the assignments teach you a lot about R. I really highly recommend taking 275 with her.

Only halfway through and already the worst professor I have had in my 3 years here. Most boring lectures I have ever sat through, with a horrible style of teaching to top it off. She treats this introduction to statistics class like it is the most important class we will ever take, but I am so serious when I say it is common sense. VERY dramatic.

Amazing professor, probably my favorite. If you are a math based person she is easy to follow. Lectures had a lot of order and structure; she explains all concepts throughly. Class was hard, there is homework and R lab (coding language), content heavy, but she makes it enjoyable. Loved her!

Large lectures, the class was held in Hubbell. Weekly lab was very easy and rarely took more than 30 minutes. Content can be a little tricky at first, but all the later units are VERY similar, with slightly different procedures, and so the class for sure gets easier as it goes on - do no give up hope. She did lots of examples, and explained well.

this was the one class this semester I was not excited to go to and really struggled to remain focused. I felt like she overcomplicated incredibly simple concepts and had a very slow paced class when you would normally expect math/stats to be fast paced. Content itself and exams are easy and u could honestly self study this whole class

Dr. G is very helpful and patient, especially during office hours. There may be a lot of homework and the class may seem slow at times, but doing the homework is extremely beneficial as it gives you an understanding of concepts you may not understand just from lecture. I highly recommend taking this class as it is easy but it just takes effort.

Dr. G is very helpful and patient especially when you come in with questions to her office hours. Though the class may be a bit slow and there are many homework assignments, I believe these homework assignments truly did help my understanding so I would recommend spending your time on them as they also contribute to your grade.

Though the class may be a bit slow sometimes, Dr. G is an incredibly kind and helpful professor who is very patient when you come into office hours with questions. She gives a lot of homework but the homework truly helps with your overall understanding of the class.

The class was so boring (as someone who really likes Stat & Applied Math). There are so many opportunities to use statistics to actually research something you're passionate about & gain a deeper understanding for whatever that material is. The labs don't do that at all. She's a good lecturer, with good slides, but needs to change the curriculum.

Homework assignments are overly simplistic and require detailed work on basic problems, which feels like unnecessary busywork. The lack of challenge makes it hard to stay engaged or develop new skills. It makes everything worse when attendance is also required. If you want a class that pushes you, I'd suggest reconsidering this one.

Dr. G has a lot of patience when working with students. I was always the only one in her office hours and she would always be more than happy to clarify confusion. This course is R studio heavy so be prepared to memorize codes for exams.

Dr.G is an amazing professor. Her lectures were super easy to understand, although a bit slow. The homeworks were really helpful in understanding the material and if you do the practice questions first, you'll do well on the homework. She's also super organized and the extra credit from the practice homework problems help your grade a lot.

219 is one of the easier stats classes I have taken- would recommend. Some of the material can get complicated, but Dr. G acknowledges that and doesn't expect you to perfectly grasp all the theory. She teaches it in an accessible way. Heavy on the group work, most hw is done with your group but isn't bad. only 1 midterm exam and final project

Tough and hard professor. She won't let student do anything easy. The most mean professor I have ever seen in UOR. Though lectures are not bad, lots of rubrics and standards make it hard for students.

her lectures are incredibly clear and everything's super easy to understand. honestly i didn't go to a single class and i just watched the recorded lectures and got an A. the projects can be tough at times but you get to work with people so it's not as bad. homework was easy and based entirely on the lectures. dr g was also really nice.. love her

276 isn't an easy class if you have no coding background (if you do it will be easier). Tests are HARD, def study, and homeworks are really time consuming so start early. However, Dr G still makes it possible to get a good grade if you put in effort, so show up to class and ask for help if you need it. Overall, difficult but learned a lot.
She is so nice!! She uses a lot of her own time to help students and sets extra office hours! She gives lecture recordings so you could study at your own pace! She explains concepts very clearly.

Dr. Grzesik values the learning the process in her classes. You get out what you put into her course. She offers plenty of office hours and is very responsive to her email chains. Those who don't spend the extra effort to learn the material that they struggle with are just lazy... 5/5 Stars
Dr.G is so kind and amiable! if you have any question and email her, she would definitely reply very fast!!love her!!!

Professor Grzesik is really nice and you could actually learn a lot from her. However, she grades homework and exams extremely strictly. It is really nice of her to give out extra credit but unfortunately not really help to boost your total grade. Be prepared or you might freak out every single Sunday night.

While Prof. Grzesik is nice, she focuses too much on the conceptual calculus part of statistics, which is not in the homework or the exams. She covers so many equations that by the point she says something that's actually relevant, I'm not paying attention. I got much more useful information from lab, but I don't recommend taking a class with her.
Very strict in grading and do not accept any mistake caused by third party factors.hard to understand during the class

She was really nice and I really liked her as a person, but I just don't think I learned too much in her class. I'd recommend one of the other professors. She often brought up concepts in lecture that we didn't need to know, which just confused me and distracted me from what I did need to know. The only topics I did well on was what I learned in HS

Wow this class was tough. Really interesting class to take and you learn a lot from her. She grades ridiculously strict on homeworks, but gives good feedback. Start them early in the week. A lot of all nighters pulled on Sundays... Midterm and Final are closed book coding exams. Very hard, but she was understanding when it came to grading.

Good teacher. If you're interested in statistical analysis take her, she knows what she's talking about. However if you're just in it for the credit, take a different prof, it's easier. She gives you everything you need to succeed on her tests, but you have to work. Graded the group project tough. Is a stickler about being on time and office hours
I would rather try the course offered by some other instructor instead. She is an elementary school grammar teacher.
Very clear explanations of very useful information to know. 100% worth taking if you have an interest in statistical analysis

I lost interest for stat after her 276. She is nice, but her grading is cruel. She always takes off points for tidy mistakes. Heavy workload, however, exams are way harder than hw (basically close book coding exam). If you care about your grade, consider it before taking it.

Dr. G is generally nice and straightforward with her grading. Sometimes the course can be frustrating in that it is super focused on formulas rather than critical thinking and understanding. I recommend doing at least some of the practice problems (especially before the homework and exams). Workshop was also quite helpful, but it depends on your TA

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I took Statistical Coding in R with Dr. G (I couldn't select this option in the rating for some reason), and she is extremely knowledgeable and helpful. It's not an easy class, but it's the kind of class that will actually help you get a job after college. I highly recommend. Also, she's a wonderful person.

Professor Grzesik is an okay professor overall. She's straightforward with the grading and what is expected of you, but boring. Homework every week gets harder as the class goes on, but even if it's time consuming it's not too bad. Prepares you well for tests, but some are harder than others. There is one basically semester-long group project.
The professor is great if you don't have any disabilities, medical issues, sickness, or anything relating to being late or needing to change when complete the course.

Dr. G is an amazing professor and will go the distance to help you maximize your learning. I was intimidated at first because of all of the negative reviews, but they seem to all be from when this course was taught online or lazy students. Sometimes the HW is a bit long but exams are very fair if you did the HW and the practice questions.
If you do the homework and discussion, then it's easy to get an A for this class.

Very time consuming. Students are expected to watch pre-recorded lectures, attend workshop, write discussion posts, and complete homework WEEKLY. Aside from the heavy workload, Dr. G is very accessible. She answers emails very quickly and clarifies problems during her non-mandatory Zoom meetings.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: I think that something Professor G forgets is that this is an introductory course, which means that a large number of the people taking it have to as a major requirement. So they aren't going to have a lot of background knowledge that she assumes we all do. It's tough, especially if you aren't very talented when it comes to math.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: It is a LOT of work. Especially for an introductory course. I spend about 10 hours a week on this course, which is twice what I spend on any other. You have to watch lectures, watch videos for notes, attend workshops and then do homework (which can take hours) and then do your discussion. Which is outside of revision needed for the multiple exams.

Dr. G is a really good teacher and she puts effort into her lectures. The recent poor reviews are probably lazy first years who wanted an easy A. The biggest con is that it's too much work. She is a bit nitpicky with tests. Homework is a bit annoying, but this is a math class after all. Yellowdig participation was a complete waste of time though.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: You're just going to spend every week listening to hours of videos that she filmed years ago. 50% of the test material was never taught in class so you better have done outside-of-class research on top of the weekly videos, lectures, workshop, homework and discussion requirements. And you're going to lose dozens of marks for nit-picky remarks.

A really difficult class. It's called Applied Statistics but there isn't a single opportunity to practice application within class-time. If you want to take notes on the (re-used) videos, attend class, practice tests, attend the workshop AND do the assignments you'll need AT LEAST 7 or 8 hours a week. And the tests are covered in un-taught material

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I've only had her online, but I've had no problem with her recorded lectures and the discussions so far. Many of her exam problems have been straight out of her notes or similar to practice and video problems. She's given more work than I expected, but she's approachable and responds to emails quickly if you have questions. Def possible to do well

Assigns more work that the allotted credits, used lecture time as a discussion so all lectures had to be watched on your own time. Does not care about the students and acts as if her class is the only one you have. Tough grader, but gives partial credit for the work she deems fit (which is not much). Not taking her again if I can help it.
She don't really care about student. She just want to finish her own work of teaching.
Lot of work and you should prepare yourself to work a lot outside the class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Dr. G was fine. She will tell you how to do well in her course throughout the semester. Follow her advice. She can be nitpicky and wants you to solve problems in certain ways she mentioned in class but she makes this clear. Besides that, discussions and workshops were 30% of our grade and are a giveaway, and she gives EC opportunities.

could really do without her passive aggressive emails to the class. her lectures themselves are fine, but she's a pretty strict grader, so just be mindful of that. i really hate her attitude and her personality is the most discouraging factor for me.. may just be because we're online, acts like her class is top priority
She gives a lot of work and the class is not completely helpful.

Her lecture is very organized and clear, and so are her lecture notes. She takes off points on even tiny mistakes for both homework and project (often not necessary). Attendance in discussion required. Tests are relatively easy, and it doesn't cover all stuff in lecture and homework.
A solid choice if you are looking to take a stats class. Speaks clearly, very organized, helpful during office hours. A very fair professor.

Stricter in terms of grading than other professors in the statistics department. As a math major having taken classes with Dr. Mueller, McDermott, Nick, Joe, and Heckler, I can say that Dr. G is very nitpicky and takes off points for tiny details, although most people understood the bigger picture. A lot of people lost motivation because of this.
Always open to help (especially during office hours), lectures are slide-based (accessible outside class), weekly homework and recitations, no textbook, and take notes!

Prof. Grzesik really cares about her class and students. She is a good teacher and tries to help people out as much as possible. I would always get an email back within 12 hours or less. I found her explanation of concepts quite clear and she has a good balance between theory and demonstrating problems. Would definitely recommend

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Dr G.'s lectures are clear and easy to follow, w/ tons of example problems. Her assignments reflect exactly what she expects you to know - no surprises. Everything is very straightforward. Office hours are helpful & she makes herself accessible to students to really make sure everyone is understanding the content. So glad I took this class!
Dr. G is the best, she's super organized, so much so that I still use my stats notebook as a reference. Exams are fair and office hours are super helpful. I definitely learned a lot!

Incredibly organized and straight-forward lectures. Material is super accessible outside of class and the homework is very manageable. She cares about the students' success and is has very helpful office hours.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: Professor Grzesik is a great lecturer. Lectures are always organized and she does a good job of making sure the material is clear. Easy to get to outside of lecture and helps in every way. Exams can be really long for a short time frame and if you miss lecture youll be lost in homeworks and coding can be difficult.

I've had Dr. Peck for 200 and 203. Very nice and helpful guy, but very disorganized. On the plus side, he's really lax with deadlines, but he also tends to revise the syllabus often, which can be confusing. He's very passionate about German literature and culture, and you'll get a lot out of his classes if you put in the work.

Dr. Peck is a great teacher, though at first I believed his teaching methods were a little weird, I eventually got used to it and I find myself understanding german texts after about 2 months of classes, his exams are fair, work-load is light and he is very friendly and cares about teaching German.
He is a very good Ger101 teacher. His tests are very fair and the grading is decent. He is a nice guy and cares alot about German.

Very difficult high level German course. Grading was harsh and only vaguely explained. This was listed as a 200 level class but seemed more like a gradate course. Two ten page papers in german in addition to 100 pages a week and two exams. Do not take course unless COMPLETELY fluent in german or you will flounder.
Salty banana.

i freaking love this guy. He's great, his lectures are good, he knows what he's talking about. Super friendly and nice and also unintentionally goofy at times. Lots of memorization, but I had a lot of fun in 110! Know the brain diagram super well! For studying, I found blurting/active recall and feynman technique useful.

Great lecturer, the course is difficult because of the sheer amount of things you need to memorize but you can tell he wants students to succeed. If I took this course with any other professor I would've definitely failed.

Professor Davis is the absolute GOATTT!! you can tell that he is very passionate about what he teaches and wants students in his class to succeed. He is very understanding and caring. Although the course may be heavy material, he makes it easy to understand.

Great lectures and a great professor. The course is notoriously challenging in the BME department, but my friends and I concluded that we cannot deny that it is indeed fun. He gave a proper amount of mathematical deductions to nearly everything. Homework and exams are hard though.

Very difficult but interesting material. Dr. Davis is super engaging to listen to, and makes coming to lecture that much more worth it. He curves exams because the class average is usually around a 50 but he is the nicest guy and this class is hard to fail.

Love him as a professor, but the way he structures his grading system is just flawed and brutal. The only grades being 4 exam grades and an optional final. Although they're curved, the amount of content for each unit and how intricate the memorization is, makes the exams feel impossible. Especially with how the exams, themselves, are structured.
As long as you study throughout the unit and not the last minute you will be fine.

I would 100% take his class again if he gives doable exams and makes it less exam heavy. His lecture is the BEST among all classes, but his exams are really difficult. Curve helps, but you will have to study A LOT for good grade. Go to class, do what he tells you to do (tablesss!!), memorize brain diagram, and please, go to his office hours.

Dr. Davis was kind and understanding but is very content heavy. The grade is based on 4 exams and an optional final and that's it. The exams are curved but they're still really hard. I will say the course said some inaccuracies (i.e. he said you could sleep for 1.5 hours every night and probably be fine, he said coke has no negative impacts).
Oh Prof. Davis. What a legend. 11/10 would recommend despite the lack of sleep I got the week leading up to one of his exams.

Loved this class and Dr Davis is hands down my favorite professor here. The best advice to do well in this class is just REALLY familiarize yourself with the paper structure because it's always going to be the same.

The material is interesting but in order to get an A, be prepared to spend every day looking at notes. You'll have to study your butt off if you don't memorize things quickly. Expect to study ~14 hours a week (at least) to memorize everything well. This class made me emotionally numb and I burnt out quickly. Don't take it if you don't need it

the nicest professor ever. his exams are really difficult though. you need to understand his questions and try to predict them. lecture heavy. highly recommend going and/or watching the old recordings he provides

Having him for a year in 110/201, I say he is very passionate about the material, caring and accessible, and an all-around respected professor. My suggestion for studying would be drawing on a whiteboard, writing down notes of recitation concepts, understanding his testing style, active studying, and getting OH with either TAs/Davis. All the best.

Dr. Davis has so much passion for what he teaches, and his lecture style really did help me grasp super hard concepts. Extremely effective professor. I looked forward to his lecture every M/W/F. Probably the most difficult exams I've taken in my life (you do have to get used to his question style) but otherwise a great time.
His fits and tests could use some work but he's chilling fr. Very content-dense lectures.
K dawg is the man. Best professor at UR hands down no questions asked.
really difficult tests given by one of my favorite professors on campus. don't take it if you don't have to, unless you want to. in that case, enjoy it!
Kevin is the best teacher I've ever taken in U of R. He's fun and really excited about his teaching. However, be ready to fail his class since he's the worst grader.

tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Its hard to enjoy a class with such hard exams and content but Kevin Davis really did a great job. I really enjoyed his class and the content but you really cannot get through this with a good grade unless you study. He is also extremely understanding and accommodating! I highly recommend his classes but do beware that it might hit your gpa.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: He did a great job, his lectures were clear and posted in case you need to rewatch them, and he was very clear about what you would be tested on. Generally a great teacher. However, the class is incredibly difficult because of the sheer amount of material within it. It sets up a great basis for the rest of the major but it is so damn hard.

Loved the material of the class and the professor. Didn't love the tests. Probably spent 15-20 hours a week studying, and even with the curve averaged out an 88. Study a LOT for the exams and review the material the day you get it. There is tons of content loaded into his lectures, but it's generally easy to understand if you go to lecture and rec.

Dr. Davis is a great professor. His lectures are well-organized, entertaining, and super informative. That being said, this was the hardest class I have taken at U of R. If you haven't taken BCS 110 before hand, prepare to learn a lot of material and feel way behind. That being said, he is super accessible out of class and cares about students.
Professor Davis is truly one of the most caring professors on campus. He actually wants you to succeed. There was also a lot of generous curves given on the exams.

Dr. Davis gives high-quality lectures and the slides are of the most organized among all courses in the university. He is caring and accessible after class and gives extra office hours before exams. His exams are truly tricky, but if you organize your notes and try to think a step forward and predict what will be on the exam, you will be fine.
He is one of the best professors I met at UR. He is caring and he explains concepts clearly. The course is interesting but really time-consuming. There is too much content to remember and understand.
Lectures are fun & enjoyable, however there are only 4 tests & an optional final so beware... Pls go to lectures he talk about what he'll test on in lectures only, and you need to study a lot. A LOT.
Super hard to get an A. As someone who cram a lot, I feel my brain is about to  explode every time before the exam. The course is informative and interesting, except that it may destroy your gpa!

I love Professor Davis, he was so amazingly helpful in office hours and he has a really big curve. I took BCS 110 as a transfer student who was not familiar at all with how harsh the U of R education system was going to be, and he made it a really welcoming experience for me personally .I think his lectures are fair and you need to study though!

Very engaging and interesting professor who has great lectures, just a very difficult and lecture/test-heavy class with lots and lots of studying outside of lectures. Despite all, he grades pretty fairly and passing is very feasible. It's just getting an A that is extremely difficult.

BCSC 110 is my second course with Dr. Davis, and I have grown to like him and his classes a lot more because I am prepared for the workload (which is a lot). Go to class and record the lectures yourself (the older recordings are less relevant). Pay attention and write down every word, reorganize the content later, and ask him questions to survive.

Dr. Davis has the most organized, detailed, and understandable lecture slides of all my professors. You could ask him anything you want during his office hours. You can't give him a low rating just because you didn't put in enough effort. The content is challenging, but not impossible, given the generous curves that he gives on every exam.

Prof Davis is such an amazing prof and person. You can tell he is super engaged in his material. BSC 110 is just an extremely hard course, but he makes it his best to make it engaging. He is very animated.The curve in the class is insane, the tests are like no other. The entire class is pure memorization. Be prepared to study and study for the exam

Amazing professor who actually knows a lot about his area of study and is genuinely focused on teaching. However content are hard and exams are harder. Curves helps but each lecture and exam results just leaves me so strained and hopeless. If you are a very sciency person who wants to learn lots about bioscience go ahead

Super great lecturer but tests were no joke. The curve works in your favor so most people don't do worse than a B- but you definitely have to put a lot of effort in to do well and understand the concepts.
Nice as a person and lecturer but he made this class so much harder than it has to be and will not recommend if 110 is not mandatory in your major

Dr. Davis is a hilarious and engaging lecturer, however I found his lectures very confusing. His tests are notoriously nuanced, specific, and difficult. He will re-do lectures for you in office hours which is great. If you want to do well in this class, expect to study A LOT. I also hope you like memorizing tables and diagrams...

Dr. Davis is a hilarious and engaging speaker. I felt more alert in his class than in any others I took this semester, and he definitely put his heart and soul into lecturing. That said, the recitations are mediocre at best and the tests are unnecessarily arcane. Dr. Davis and BCS 110 demand a lot for you, don't underestimate the low course number.

His lectures are quite engaging, but there is so much content to learn that the exams are really difficult. The wording of his exams can really trip you up so asking clarification questions on the exam is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. I recommend going to office hours too. You need to think like Davis thinks, and not just know the content...
Great lectures. Tests are super nuanced and difficult, great curves though. Tests are on his lectures, you don't need to get a textbook. You need to study hard if you want to do well.

Professor Davis is a really funny and great lecturer but really does not care about his students' success. His exams are hard and he usually writes them the night before so you do not know what he could be adding to them. To do well in this class you really need a good TA.

He's a really engaging and thoughtful professor. He puts everything in a way you will understand and he's accessible outside lecture if you need help. As long as you study really really hard, you'll be okay. If you put the effort into the class, you'll get a good grade since his curves are really good.

He is an interesting lecturer and this class got me interested in cognitive science, but he makes his test unnecessarily hard. He curves every exam average to an 83 so if you study hard you'll be fine, but there is absolutely a way to teach the same material without such difficult exams, and that is the only thing your grade is based on.

DR.Davis is my favourate prof of university. He is so nice and helpful, give clear and good lectures. And he is Always delighted to help us on Office hours. I also took BCS110 and would like to take more of his lectures. His tests are hard.

If you're someone who crams, you will fail. I can personally tell you that you should be scared if you always cram lol. I do mean this is the best way possible. I did take the class online and so he made it more difficult so others wouldn't cheat, but even then, please go to lectures. The exams were multiple choice (online) and he made it so hard.
Loved the class! By far my favorite class and I took it online. Professor Davis is a great lecturer and explains complex topics in way that is interesting and makes the class fun! :)
Dr.Davis is super nice and experienced. Give good lectures and explains everything very clearly. But his course isn't easy, get ready!

My absolute favorite professor this semester. Funny, clearly cares and wants you to succeed, and his lectures are well organized and clear. Extremely difficult topics so you’ll need to study a lot but exams are generously curved. Go to his office hours too; he’s super nice and always willing to help!

In order to do well, you will have to memorize every single detail of what he says and puts in the lectures. No getting around it because most test questions include multiple concepts stacked on each other. But, his info is organized nicely on the slides and if you study A LOT, you can do well .

Homeworks are Tedious. I literally busted my computer disk, so that I can save his funny requirement of saving a million screenshots to collect some stupid data from a lab. The worst professor I think I will ever have. Currently doing a project but the guidelines are so arbitrary and nothing is clearly explained. Got so pissed that I want to kill myself and will leave this review behind as my last words.

didn't learn a single thing in lectures, don't even know why i went every single time just to play 2048 on my computer. easily one of the worst professors i have had, he has a monotone voice and you cant pay attention with him for more than 5 min because of how boring it is. the labs and projects are difficult, exams you get a cheat sheet for!

Great professor!!!!!

Going to lectures was pretty much useless, I was able to gain a better understanding through internet resources. Be ready to teach yourself a lot of the material. Pretty generous grading scale though, and most exams are curved.
He is too underrated so I had to give five stars. Great explanation and passion.

Zhupa, what to say. He comes off as a tough guy at first, but towards the end of the semester he lightens up and even starts making jokes in his own horizontally-striped-sweater-way. Very nice and caring professor and will do his best to make sure everyone understands the materials. He also started teaching CSC282 which is a LOT more doable than Daniel's class. class is very tedious and man this guys is a tough grader. i didn't learn much from his class. He is unorganized as hell.

Tries, but fails, not good lectures, hard to read project descriptions

Professor Zhupa is a very caring and respected person. He understands the difficulties of international students, and he doesn't make things hard on students just to show he has the power to do so, unlike many other professors in the department.

The professor is the book, or maybe the book is professor. Lecture contents are ctrl C and ctrl V from the textbook. In the last exam, there even existed prompt like "remember code line 57 from lecture 11" without any referencing codes. Genius

DO NOT take his course, esp 172. It is not worth it. It will destroy every hope that you have for a CS career unless you are already very good. Imagine you spend 5 hours for every lab for 7 labs and got your grade ruined by one midterm, because the midterm worth exactly the same as 7 labs total. he is so hard to reach by email he basically won't respond.

Horrible... can't teach at all. Lectures suck. Doesn't help. Just, don't.

Professor Zhupa cares about his students and really puts in the effort to make class clearer. I see so many negative ratings here but that seems quite an exaggeration. He is a very bad professor. He doesn't know the material well himself, and when you asked him a question, he would never answer directly. You feel like you are taking this course alone, without a teacher.

The worst teacher possible ever. Confusing and chaotic teaching which made materials harder to understand than it was supposed to be. No partial credits in grading: incomplete answers will get you zero marks no matter what you accomplished. Appeared to not care about students at all.

YouTube taught me. Terrible lectures. So sad because 172 is important for future courses.

Just avoid his course. CSC172 is not a hard course if your professor is not him.
It's unfortunate he is the only professor teaching data structures and algorithms, which is arguably the most important class in the CS major. there are other professors who could do a better job.

Definitely the WORST lecturer in department of Computer Science, even in the whole university. He always gives wrong codes and unclear lectures. Pretty tough grader compared to other WRTG 105 teachers. Definitely much more confusing, however Nasheed will 100% make you a better reader and writer.

easy to get angry.

comment: No real guidelines on how the assignments are graded are shown. This unclarity is detrimental to the structuring of many assignments. Her class is super duper abstract; there's hella reading. comment: The professor does not have strict grading criteria making it hard for students that are following the guidelines to excel as she doesn't follow them to the dot. Brilliant professor, but you should be aware of a few things:

2. The material for this course is EXTREMELY difficult even for both grads and undergraduates so attend class.
3. Attendance is mandatory. 1 class session = 1 quiz grade.

He's an interesting guy and very knowledgeable about the topic. If you're into theoretical CS stuff, CSC 280 is the place for you. You'll be learning and solving many interesting problems from complexity theory. The small class size definitely helps with the in-class discussions and group activities. One of the best class formats I've seen in a course.
Genuine, caring, attentive, passionate, enthusiastic, loves to share stories (often over-shares random (but subjectively fun) stories), accessible, interesting course content and materials.

He is a nice person, and what he says in class makes sense, but I had to rewatch recordings to understand. Most people would complain about mandatory attendance when you can easily get 36% just based on attendance! Lane makes us do tons of practice that makes it impossible not to do well on the exams! Great professor that is awesome about feedback and has amazing lectures

FAST Talker. Unclear half the time, also cause the material is fast, but he expects us to understand it as easily as he does. Fair grader though, grades people individually rather than a class. If he sees you doing work and at least tryin, you won't fail.

Worst professor EVER~!!!  Rambles and talks too damn fast  :(

Just be thorough with the Study Guides posted before exams and all will be good!
He's a chill, nice professor and it's easy to do well. However, some of the concepts covered in this class can be kind of confusing and requires reviewing outside of class to understand them better.
Jack Mottley is a pillar, the leading light, and one-man bastion of the ECE department.

ECE101 is an easy course, and Mottley especially designs it so that it isn't jarring or difficult if you have no prior knowledge of calculus or physics. Lectures are optional and although I recommend attending, they can be off-track pretty often. Homeworks are sometimes graded incorrectly based on the TAs, but labs and workshops are also not bad.
What a nice guy. He sets every student up for success and is always there to answer questions.

Mottley is so kind, so caring, really wants his students to succeed. All lectures are recorded, but go to class anyway so you can ask questions. Recitations and labs are mandatory, but the labs are actually really fun. Mottley also cancels labs on exam weeks to have an extended Q&A. Great professor.
Very nice man, very easy class. Even though a good portion of the final grade is the exams, they are straight forward and everyone should be well prepared for it. The practice exams really help!
He went through lots of examples in class, and he posted all the notes online which was very helpful. The exam questions were very similar to the homework and examples in class.
He went through lots of examples in class, and the exam questions were very similar to the homework and examples in class.

Professor Mottley is a cool dude. I took this class from 3:15-4:05, and I fell asleep nearly every class. He has a very relaxing way of speaking that almost instantly puts me to sleep. Not a bad thing but it made it very hard to learn, but luckily all of the lectures are recorded ane when I can stay awake, the lectures are very informative and the information is valuable.

If you pay attention in lectures and put in effort in lab this class is an easy A. The homework and tests(do the study guides) all go along with lectures and nothing comes as a surprise or is too challenging. He is very quick to respond to emails and help students with any problems. The labs are simple & fun and for most of them you get out early.
Chill teacher, but he speaks quietly and isn't to engaging. Class is relatively boring but easy, as long as you generally know what's going on you should get the A.

A real stand up guy. Very accommodating towards all needs. Class can get a little bit on the boring side, but as long as you focus and do homework, you should be all set to go for tests/final. He breaks down a lot of the content which makes things very easy to grasp. You will be more than prepared with Jack!

This professor is not motivated in teaching, his class very boring. Exams and homework too easy. Before the exam, he gives all previous years' handouts. Questions are almost the same. I feel that I almost spend no time learning this course and learned very little. Compared with my friends from other top universities, I feel I learned a fake course.
It's just a harder ECE111. Mottley is still a very good professor and the lectures are still a bit dull. The labs for this course are pretty useless.
Class drags on sometimes, but he does his best to keep intro topics interesting.

Professor Mottley is a great teacher who really cares about his students. His lectures aren't super entertaining but he explains all the topics very well. The labs, workshops, homework, and exams all fit together nicely, so it is easy to learn all of the material even though there is a lot of it. Overall great professor.
Jack is genuinely a very good teacher and a very nice person. His lectures can get a bit dull, but you will always understand the material after them.

I like professor Mottley a lot. He's super friendly and easy to talk to, always willing to help. His lectures can get a little messy but he'll go above and beyond to make sure you understand. I recommend attending to recitations where you can ask any questions and you can get more one on one.
Attend class and its easy to do well.

Mottley taught my 111 class in a "flipped-classroom" style at times, but most of the year was just him lecturing. If you put in a decent effort you're likely to do very well! Mottley says he likes to challenge students with hw assignments, so he made the tests very straight forward.

Professor Mottley (as monotonous as he is) is very helpful and clear. He knows and loves what he's doing with circuits so he's always willing to help. The homeworks, labs, workshops and tests all match up to complete one another but they are very difficult so study hard and you'll be fine.

Mottley taught ECE 111 very well. It's a fundamentals class, and Mottley gave students a strong foundation to build more ECE knowledge on. Students were well prepared for exams, which had material on them consistent with the homeworks, labs, and lectures -- something which is rare and underappreciated by students often. Well done, Jack.

Lectures are boring and don't provide enough examples for you to even start the homework problems.  Workshops are somewhat beneficial at best and the labs are pointless.  I barely learned anything in this class.  Mottley is a nice enough guy, but he lacks teaching skills.  After taking this class I still have little idea about how a circuit works.

ECE 101 is a simple class that's just following directions from a provided book or packet and building robots while programming with VHDL.  It's a really fun class that'll get you into ECE.  Sometimes Mottley teaches the class basics, and it's always very clear. He grades very kindly and helps you readily.  He's also fairly likeable to chat with.

This was my least attended class in my history.  He is a terrible teacher, no organization, no enthusiasm, terrible TA's, confusing labs.  This class should be extremely easy, but it becomes difficult because of the lack of support of material (hw doesn't support lecture, labs are confusing, lectures are pointless)

Very nice guy, but bad professor.  Lectures are boring and don't help with the homework at all.  However, if you email him that you are having trouble with a specific homework problem, he will usually do it for you in class.  You should go to workshop; that's where I learned most of the material.

The tests are nearly exactly the same as previous years. Labs suck but they are easy. You will leave the class thinking that you learned very little but will find that you learned more than you thought.

Really nice guy, but not a good teacher.  Lectures don't help with homework, and labs are hard to follow.  Get a good workshop leader and you'll do fine.  Tests are really easy- very similar to previous years.  The book is useless.

Homeworks didnt really help.  Tests were easy because they are the same as previous years.  Spends to much time in lectures deriving.  Don't expect him to respond to emails or to even know what grade to expect.
HW are sometimes pointless, and lectures are fairly boring, expect to take 40 mins writing notes to have him tell you you only need to remember one small equation at the end. Nice guy to talk to.

pointless homework that didn't match tests, awful labs, poorly chosen TAs, boring guy.  stresses professionalism when he doesn't even follow half of what the syllabus says, and in general holds a really boring, difficult course.
very consistant. within 5 minutes, i was asleep.
Lecture notes not relevant with homework, lectures trivial compared to homework, boring, labs are stupid
I have never heard anyone speak in more of a monotone in my life!
Nice guy, kind of aimless class though.  no real goals.
He seems like he should be a highschool teacher.  The class was fun, in an easy way, but not all the benefincial to my life.
CANT TEACH!!!!

One of my favorite professors ever, inspired a love of dynamics which changed the course of my career in research. Insanely smart and passionate lecturer, classes were always super fun. The class was also tiny, so it felt like a topics course with lots of room for discussion about the material.

prof quillen was always super reachable and incredibly kind. when i was struggling my freshman year she let me submit all of my missing lab reports a week before grades were due- and graded them herself. the sweetest lady ever. be aware though the lab reports are awful plz j take 121 instead

Alice Quillen is like a sweet little old grandmother who bakes you cookies every time you see her. This class heavily relies on homework and they are a bit difficult but Quillen is very reachable. She is such a wonderful and kind human being, and she loves seeing students in her office. I really enjoyed this class with her, she is such a fun spirit and is really helpful during her office hours!

Professor Quillen is the nicest human being I've ever seen. She is intelligent and knows how to teach students. She is very accessible outside class and likes to talk to students. Very inspirational and encourage me to pursue physics and astronomy.
She has really good notes and lectures are fun to attend because of how passionate she is about what she's teaching. Homeworks can be challenging but she is accessible outside of class.

Quillen is the best. She no longer does tests, but you'll still learn a lot in her class. The way she weaves in modern physics in her lectures is incredibly helpful without being overwhelming to first years. Even without tests, 141 is a ton of work, but it's worth it in the long run.

Adds a lot of junior year level content which made her lectures confusing (I'd taken IB physics), so don't worry about understanding everything. TAs were great at teaching, go to recitations! Collaborate on the problem sets (took me many hours) and do the labs well (multiple days worth of work). She is caring and will help you a lot in office hrs

Pros: Very good lecture notes, very easy to reach, and cared about students and tried to make the class fair. Cons: all-over-the-place lecturer; I took honors physics 1, which required having taken high school physics - had it not been similar material to high school, I wouldnt have learned. Lecture notes taught me better than lecture.

I am not a physics major. But after I took this class, it seems like I'm a physics major. I spent an entire day to do the assignment each week, and take another 2-3 days to do lab report. She is very kind. Lab reports can be a bit intense.

Alice has perks and cons. Although she had great knowledge in physics and she is extremely strong mathematically, she usually overestimated our ability to understand what she says. Sometimes I lost track of her. TA was more helpful than her. Her lectures are not enough to understand. However, she is caring and understanding and NOT tough grader.

She should not teach freshmen.  Although high school calculus is recommended for AST 111, the calculus in her presentations involves multivariable calculus.  Additionally, her lectures are hard to follow, due in part to her poor ability to teach AST 111.

She hates teaching freshmen and it shows. She teaches things that juniors who took the class never learned in AST 111 and either learned them in higher level Astro classes or not at all. Her lectures are ridiculously confusing and include multi-variable calculus, even though only a high school understanding of calculus is recommended. Fall 2016
She is great.

Real chill and smart. She knows her stuff well. It helps to be genuinely interested in physics and astronomy otherwise you'll find yourself getting a little bored because she's extremely passionate about that stuff.

Such a nice person and really enthusiastic and smart. It's sometimes hard to follow what she's saying if she gets carried away by her excitement and wanders from topic to topic, but she's always willing to back up and explain things if you don't understand.
Awesomest teacher ever.  Plain and simple.

comment: Amazing professor. The course is very challenging, but if you attend lectures and work hard, you will learn a lot. Professor Chen is very approachable outside of the class and always being so supportive and enthusiastic.
Hard to understand

10/10 professor, he is so funny, lectures are AMAZING. The class this semester was only graded on 12 HW assignments which were not hard at all. His office hours are so AMAZING. Professor Chen is great! He is very enthusiastic about the material and brings a lot of context into his lectures, for example which theorems were handy in his own research... His office hours are very helpful and pretty much helped me survive the course. This class is very demanding but also incredibly rewarding, you will learn a lot!
This course is very challenging but Professor Chen is very enthusiastic when giving the lectures and can make everything easier to understand.
fantastic professor; very willing to help with long and extremely convenient office hours
No need to buy the textbook.  Everything he says in lecture is crystal clear and his love of teaching shows.  Open book/notes/whatever tests!  One of the best professors I have had in college.
Fantastic Professor.

Best math professor I've ever had.  He's a well-oiled explaining machine.  281 was the first time I've seen a lecture hall still full by the end of the semester - Clark actually teaches the material.  Great guy and funny too.
Amazing teacher.  Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it should have been.  Extremely helpful, extreme nice, extremely clear.
Sick nasty teacher, love the guy

He is the best teacher I have ever hard.  Both classes have difficult material but he teaches them very well.  He is organized, clear and helpful.  Very concerned with students' progress.  If you can take a class with him, you should.
Clark is God.  Best professor ever, period.
Best professor I have ever had.
Ouch, this course killed me.  Good professor and a nice guy, but way too difficult
One of the best professors I've ever had. Kind, considerate, clear, patient, fair, extremely knowledgeable, and down-to-earth. Teaches Statics, Fluid Dynamics, and ME201/MTH281.
Dr Platt was an amazing professor and a better teacher. Utilize his office hours. Hes handed over the reigns to Dr. Clark, but still remains very active.

Overall, Bio 112 was a decent class, and much better than the alternative, Bio 110 with Olek. A lot of the material taught (especially at the end) was researched by Platt himself and I found that aspect quite interesting. The key to success is to go to lecture and work on the test questions (he gives them to us in advance) in small groups.

When selecting a biology class I was apprehensive to choose Bio 112, but I'm glad I did. Professor Platt is likeable, a great lecturer, and brilliant. A lot of the material you will discuss in the class he had a role in discovering. As tests go the material is difficult but manageable because this is primarily a biochemistry class. Take this class!

Platt is a brilliant man. He teaches a rough subject and is much better than the alternative, Olek. He gives you the questions beforehand and that forces you to learn the subject matter. It will take effort but its rewarding.

Go to lecture (sit toward the front so you can hear him, he's soft spoken), go to workshop, and take advantage of the exam questions that are given to you before the test and you will be fine. Reading the text before like he recommends helps during lecture.

Platt deserves better scores than he has on here.  Honestly, my friends in 110 with Olek struggled much more than me in 112.  He's a really smart guy so sometimes I'd get a bit lost but he wants his students to do well (he even gives the test Qs in advance).  The class forces you to think so it can be difficult but it's interesting.

If you go to class and go to workshop, you'll probably be okay.  Also, work in groups on exam questions because they're really really hard. Get Lehninger on PDF because it's used way more than the one we bought.He's helpful if you ask him questions, but can get confusing with diagrams.Some stuff is over a freshman's head but he makes it interesting

If you can get past the fact that the required textbook is not actually used, you will learn a ton. Like the other reviewers said, he basically teaches biochemistry.  Great teacher with genuine interest in his students (and the subject matter) and you feel like you are actually a scientist when you leave the course.

Professor Platt's lectures are possibly the most fun out of all the classes I have. Furthermore his exams are not difficult and he provides many thought provoking quotes before each of his classes. I'm very happy that the University of Rochester decided to have such a capable Professor conduct the course
One of the best professors in the school

The lecture is boring useless. I personally felt I didn't learn a lot from this class. Many people I knew who wanted to do bio major decided not to after taking class...To survive this class: go to workshop, review session and buy biochem book!

Biochem 250 was one of the most useful classes that I had before entering medical school.  If you can do this class, you can basically sleep in when you do biochem in med school because you've already learned it.  Platt is a fabulous teacher, and I owe much of my success to him.

Platt has a biochem degree,  and teaches this course straight out of the biochem textbook. If you have a photographic memory you will do well on the tests, otherwise you're screwed. Lectures will put you to sleep, as will his rambling stories of his dad in the 50s. Workshops are the only way to learn anything. Very useless class with little bio.
He does a terrible job of teaching this class. Biochem majors soon realize how useless this class was and how stupid minute details cost big points on exams. Lectures were atrocious.
buy Lehninger.  that's the only book he teaches from and it's not required to buy.  the required book is never used

worst biology professor I've ever had, Lectures are useless as he glosses over many things. The tests are often straight out of a upper level biochem text book and only require pure memorization to pass, No understanding at all is needed. Only the truly brain dead can enjoy the lectures or fail the tests.
He scares everyone into thinking they will fail, then gives everyone A's. You'll either hate him or love him, but don't take his learn-it-yourself take-home-test approach for granted.

Like Slughorn from Harry Potter. If you're "smart" you're made, if you're not then you don't exist.Class is well taught but there is no question that his tests are hard, the material dense, and the prof clearly plays favorites.It's great if you're one of his favorites but otherwise...be prepared for a bit of disdain.
Tests were just regurgitating information taken from anywhere but the text book. Boring. Dont even bother going.

A really helpful and knowledgable man.  The class had a ridiculous amount of stuff to learn.  He claims to try and teach you to sip from the firehose of information but then tests you on the entire firehose.  Workshops are useless and designed with only pre-med students in mind, not science students.  Interesting class, I recommend it.
Does a pretty good job of covering lotssss of material in great detail in one semester.  The key to doing well is to memorize everything and to start studying for his exams well in advance.

Awesome prof who actually cares about his first year students. He practically memorizes everyones name in a class of over 100. Test questions are given out before test, but not all appear on test. Material, thus, while challenging, is not hard to master. Definitely recommend and will miss not having him teaching biochem 250 anymore.

Although this class was challenging, the way Dr. Platt taught forced you to research on your own. The way his exams were structred forced you to fully understand all material. As long as you go to workshop and study for tests I fully recommend this class. Oh and don't bother buying the Purves bio textbook, buy Lehninger's Principles of Biochemistry

While 112 is honors bio, it is still a survey course, so I expected there to be some review of AP Bio material. This class is truly a waste of time for freshmen.

don't take Bio 112 with him unless you plan on taking chemistry too. He uses a textbook different than the one we were required to buy. He teaches biochemistry in biology 112. Tests are completely different than what we are assigned to read and what is taught in class. It's very confusing.
very helpful. study and memorization is a must.

Nice for the most part, but sometimes when you go into his office hours and tell him that you don't understand something or that you are having trouble with something; he blames you. workshops do not match up with class material at all. tests are INSANE and the material is sometimes all over the place. You might cover metabolism one hour and plant anatomy the next.

awesome teacher
Dr. Platt is truely awesome!  His knowledge deserves everyone's admiration.  I'm glad to be in his class; he does not limit his teaching to textbooks but expands outside knowledge also!  Great!

Prof S is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. He wants every single one of his students writing to improve, and his feedback reflects this. Terrible attitude.

Professor S has passion for his subject and it shows. He gives great feedback and is very accessible outside of class, even on short notice. Excellent professor, easily one of the best at this school. I took screenwriting with him and I enjoyed it very much. Would highly recommend taking a course with him.

I have him for screenwriting and I love the class. I have learned so much from discussion and he really knows his stuff. He gives fantastic and helpful feedback, while encouraging you to write your story and be creative. The semester project is writing a full length screenplay and at first I was intimidated but now I'm 25 pages in! Def take him!!!!

He's my absolute favorite professor. He's been extremely helpful in class and out of class. I've decided to become a creative writing professor after taking this course. We read amazing authors that have become my favorites. I loved this class so much. We had a great energy because he was such a easy-going guy. I wish I could take it again.

Cool, energetic professor. Class was very in-depth. Lecture heavy, somewhat overwhelming at times. Dante and the Comedy make more and more sense as both the day's class and the course continue, but her explanations and analysis often are a tad roundabout or unclear. Extremely knowledgable teacher! Classes are 95% her lecturing on the book. Very straightforward, and the content is interesting. You have to pay attention though, and attend the recitation.

She's a great teacher. I took her year-long Dante course in 2001-2002 and loved it. My favorite course in college. This class was so much like high school we even had a library session. She dumbs the discourse with her teaching style. Also, BAD TAs.
Brilliant woman, amazing class, learned a ton. DONT MISS THIS GREAT COURSE
I fell asleep in her class every day. She just jumps into lectures and starts babbling. Although she is certainly knowledgable, she killed Dante for me.
Best professor Ive ever had. Absolutely brilliant, approachable, nice, and clear. Fascinating lecturer.
awesome teacher. must take one of her classes. it must be the italian charm.

Muthu teaches very well and encourages questions from students in the class. The Crypto course is theory-heavy and the assignmnt problems are really good to get a good grasp of the topics. the good part was the lecture. the bad part was pretty much everything else. there was no syllabus, 40% of grade was up to chance due to these wacky weird quizzes, and he never responded to student questions. he also gave a take home midterm which was a terrible idea and this caused unfairness bc EVERYONE used internet, but only some got caught.

4 reasons I regret taking Muthu's course: 1) has a tough time seeing things from the student's point of view 2) doesn't see himself as accountable to students 3) doesn't make himself accessible to students 4) makes claims but doesn't follow through. says midterm will take 2 hours, it takes 12. says grades back by mon, changes to wed, then fri, etc.

He cares about his students, welcomes feedback, and genuinely wants you to learn the material.

I was skeptical at first because I heard mixed things about his 281 class, but CSC 280 turned out to be a fascinating, well taught, and delightful class. The professor seemed to genuinely care about his students and tried hard to make sure everyone understood the material.
Daily quizzes are annoying, but if you paid attention in the previous lecture then you'll do fine. Has good TAs and lectures are good.
Teaches some cool subjects. Not terrible by any means.
Hard homework, tough TA and grade.

Very sad that she's retiring this year, but this was a great class to have taken. Lectures were short, homework was the same as exam questions, and she was there to help if you were stuck on questions. Amazing professor.

Her lectures are generally very fast paced, and she almost always doesn't take the full 75 minutes. She uses lots of examples to illustrate concepts which is really helpful. She's always willing to help out with homework questions. Exams are really straight forward. The final project at the end of the course isn't too much to worry about either.

The content of the course is very interesting and applicable to real life and she was able to explain things so well that I'm pretty sure a 6th grader could pass this course. One of the best courses I've ever taken and one of the most helpful professors I've ever had.

An amazing professor overall. Caring, inspirational, hilarious, knowledgeable, passionate, and accessible. She very clearly understands students' struggles and thus has made efforts to support students in all ways. Her online readings, recordings, homework, and workshops are all that you need to succeed in this class. I recommend her to everyone!

She is very nice and is the least harsh grader I have ever had. On exams, you have the choice to just write RCode that you would use to solve the problem which helps A LOT. I have put wrong numbers in and only got a half a point off.  She also only lectures for 30 minutes, sometimes more or less.

Professor McDermott is one of the best professors I've had at UR so far. She genuinely cares about her students, and is fair and reasonable with what she expects you to know. She's also good at using analogies to break down tricky concepts to make them more digestible. As long as you attend workshop and study the examples/homework, you'll do well.
Very nice and accessible out of class. Gives very clear instructions. She want students to be successful in her class.

Professor McDermott develops a series of online statistic videos, combines them with textual introduction of each teaching unit, thus making the content very easy to understand. She really manages the class well despite teaching asynchronously. All the grades she gives are reasonable. Put some effort into the class and a good grade will ensue.

Professor McDermott was amazing! Given STT212 isn't a very difficult class at UR, her lectures were very easy to understand she went over lots of examples in class. Provides practice exams that are very similar to actual exams and very accessible outside of class.
Most amazing professor ive ever come across

She's the best professor I've had since I started college! She is so respected and caring of her students, not only academically but also to a personal level. She started this semester doing popup quizzes but she lets you drop the 3 worst grades. Her lectures are really entertaining and she explains really really well and makes the class quite easy

I absolutely love prof McDermott. Shes always striving to improve her class and make it a better experience for the students. Shes also incredibly funny, and taking the time to go to office hours and meet her one-on-one is an experience every student of hers should have. One note dont try to bs her, shell be a hard ass if she thinks ur lying!

She posts everything online, but her lectures are far from helpful. She basically reads off the slides. She is nice and answers questions, but you're better off teaching yourself.

Caring professor, but lectures can get pretty dull. Practically everything is available online, including the powerpoints from lectures, so there is basically no need to go to class. Content is not too challenging, and half of the questions on the exams are copied and pasted from the practice exams.

Easiest class ever, she has powerpoint slides for every class. You can just look at the powerpoint slides without coming to her class. Her class was huge and just went over all the lecture slides. To be honest, I went to all her classes but always slept in the front row.

Professor McDermott has very clear and organized lectures that help tremendously with the online homework and tests. She is very kind and funny and genuinely cares about her students and what she teaches. She is the best professor I have had so far and would definitely take a class with her again.

I would say she had trouble explaining the concepts and her lecture just reading through the slides. This is my first statistic class; I can get good grades for the exams but after listening to her class I am still lost. She wears headphones during the office hours and she is not really helpful!
This class is very easy
One of my favorite professors at the U of R. Super approachable and there to help.
Class is incredibly easy.

She's a sweetheart.  Her lectures are clear with real-world examples and she's so approachable- she's a real person who understands and is really considerate.  As someone who had zero experience in statistics before this course, I got an A.  She made me love stats!

McDermott is just a great professor all around! She is understanding, approachable, and explains concepts clearly in class, not that concepts are all that hard to grasp. Tests were easy and we got a cheat sheet every time. Textbook is somewhat useful if you missed a class or if you just want to go over what was discussed in class. Take this class!

Great intro to OLS. Super helpful as always. Final was a tiny bit tricky but overall great class with fairly easy homework. Lectures never lasted an hour and we got to work on the project the last month of class instead of having lecture.
I took two classes with her and she is a great professor. She is very nice, helpful and clear. But remember never try cheating in her exams. She is very serious about academic honesty.

Ridiculously easy class. 3 MC exams that you get a cheat sheet and graphing calc for. HW can be annoying but it's easy.  She really wants everyone to enjoy the class and do well. She's also one of the nicest profs at UR. Highly recommend her and this class
Easy class. Great experience. East to follow. Got a cheat sheet for every exam. Best class ever!
She is a great professor. Definitely take a class with her!

Extremely easy. you can learn if you want to. Mcdermott is really nice and informal. Textbook readings probably won't be necessary, but do them if you want the material reinforced or if you miss a few classes.
Very easy class but if you pay attention you do learn a lot. Very helpful and a good opportunity to receive an A while learning. I wish more classes were taught like hers.

Such a sweet professor! She always made herself available for help and taught right from the book for the most part. The class seemed like it would be extremely easy but the first couple exams and some homework were hard. However, the final and final project were a great opportunity to boost your grade (so work hard at first). Take this class!
I took this as a pre-requisite for econ and highly recommend it. Learned a decent amount and wasn't overly challenging. Professor McDermott is also extremely helpful.
Professor makes herself readily available. Cover a lot of statistics concepts. Recommend taking this class.
Middle school was more challenging.

This class is a joke. Textbook is useless and expensive; homework questions are poorly worded and often misgraded; and lectures are just reading off powerpoint slides. Take this class if you need time to slack off and party; DON'T take this class if you need it as a prerequisite and/or to prepare for your career.
Easiest/Best Class offered at UR. Great for a GPA boost, or just a better understanding of statistics.
very friendly and nice, wants you to do well in the class. power points are online and tests give you a cheat sheet. definitely do it.

Dr. Roessner is incredibly knowledgable about his field and imparts as much of that knowledge onto you as he can. The class is very project heavy, and requires a lot of time commitment outside of class, so do not take it if you are overloading! Lectures focus on theory and you learn recording skills in lab. TA's are usually pretty good as well.

GREAT guy! Very approachable and reasonable if you have any troubles regarding assignments. He's a great resource if you have any questions about the music business/audio engineering field (and he's excited to answer them!). Do your studying and be curious about the lectures--this is how you'll get a good grade and get the most out of this class!
great teacher but tough grader
yes she is kinda harsh on grading but that totally makes sense and you can learn a lot from her regardless of what final grades she gave you

Anne is a very nice lady, however, she's  a harsh grader. For a 2 credit intro to ballet course she takes her grading way too seriously.
