I thought Professor O'Donnell did a great job teaching the Writing 105 course. She offered great feedback on each submitted assignment and helped guide the students through each required paper. She helped keep students engaged and encouraged group discussion on various social movements.

Rachel is so funny I literally want to get a drink w her outside of class.  A great teacher and genuinely cares about her students. Her writing 105 class is easy and engaging, I'd love to take more classes with her!!

Prof O'Donnell was a great professor who really cared about her students and understood that we were all stressed. She gave good feedback on brought drafts and final drafts and her office hours were amazing if you wanted more feedback. 10/10 would take again.

I had Prof. O'Donnell for WRTG105 contemporary social movements and would definitely recommend her. She is approachable, understanding, and flexible. Gives good feedback and isn't a super tough grader. The course in general is a basic 105, so it's nothing too crazy and isn't that difficult.
Prof. O'Donnell is a great WRTG 105 professor! She cares about her students and is very understanding and if you participate and don't skip class you will easily walk out with an A

Professor O'Donnell is a very caring and compassionate person and her class is very enjoyable. The work is very fair and entertaining and her flexibility helps keep the stress at a minimum. The classes are set up to maximize the material and engage with classmates. A great class.

Professor O'Donnell is amazing. Participation is a big part of your grade, and she really appreciates students speaking in class. There is quite a bit of reading and you have to do them to be ready for the discussions. For papers, go to the Writing Fellows to get feedback. This was probably my favorite class my first semester.

She is extremely nice and understanding which makes the class so much less stressful. I had her for her WRTG105 class on social movements and I loved it. She also gives back great feedback and facilitates group discussions and feedback well also. It really makes the class go by fast.

Super kind and understanding professor. She makes lessons accessible and shows that she cares a lot about the students. Even in a social distanced classroom, we had lots of small group discussions, so come ready to talk. Directions/grading criteria can feel a bit too vague sometimes, but she's always available to talk if you need clarity.

Great professor, teaches writing in a very accessible & managable way. Gives amazing feedback, is extremely understanding and works with students to help reach their full potential. Take her class if you are interested in gsws or social science. She's very supportive and easy to talk to. Readings are interesting, very managable.

She's a great professor, very caring and kind and easy to talk to. She works hard to get everyone engaged in the work and gives great feedback on papers. I love how she structured that class and made a writing class interesting to the best of her abilities. We have similar academic interests, so I'm planning to take another one of her classes.

Reachable, kind, patient. She gave helpful supports and suggestions during office hour. I took contemporary social movement with her. If you work hard in this class you will get an A and feel more confident about writing.

She's one of the best professors I've had during my time at Rochester! There are some students who believe that they can get away by doing the bare minimum, but as long as you put in your effort, the class will not seem as intensive. As like any other class, if you want an A, be proactive, and you'll see your results.

I was recommended Professor ODonnell by multiple other students prior to taking one of her classes. She encourages creative thought and discussion, while also enhancing students learning on each topic presented. Shes extremely supportive and easy to talk to. Shes enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and one of my favorite professors Ive had.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers']
comment: She seems like a nice person but I feel like she takes this class way too seriously. It's basic required writing 105, not advanced 400 level English major specific writing. Also, she is not a very warm person, she acts like she is very funny and friendly but her comments on our papers and work make her seem harsh and cold.

I met at least five other students who took her classes and everyone shared the same feeling about professor O'Donnell: thought-provoking, funny, caring, clear. I took her Modern Social Movements class, the assignments were challenging, but her guidance was excellent. The readings and discussions: absolutely engaging. Very supportive professor.

Professor Welte's passion for science and teaching really made this an enjoyable class. I really appreciated that he took the time to get to know his students, and offer help. The assignments were challenging, but very applicable to a career in biology research. I thought this was the best course I've taken at UR.

It's obvious that he is excited about his art and wants you to share his passion as well. I guess the best way to make a person swim is to throw him in the water. This is exactly what Prof. Welte does. He would make you read loads of papers and come up with project proposals and give presentations and actively participae in class discussions.

What an EXCELLENT professor!  He answers any questions you have and encourages discussions toward which he contributes very clear and concise information.  He has a passion for the material, and his German accent is awesome.  Oh, and I think he's gay which would explain his apparent fabulous-ness :D

Genuinely, very smart, you can tell she knows what she's talking about. But so unpleasant and hateful to students that it made me dread every single class with her. Her entire demeanor is punitive and though I'll have to take other classes with her to graduate, I will be loathing her the entire time.

I was trying to give her the benefit of the doubt w how condescending her demeanor can be sometimes, but the way she graded and left feedback on assignments.. It just felt like she assumes too much out of intro level students, and doesn't make things accessible enough for us to understand. Then acts like its our fault.

Dr. Miller can seem harsh sometimes, but she does care. Lectures are dense, but you can record her to listen to later. Make sure you stay on track because it is very hard to catch up if you fall behind. As long as you study with enough time before exams, this is definitely a manageable class. Just be ready for it to take up a lot of time.

I honestly really liked Dr Miller but did not like this class. Unfortunately, this class made me switch my major (not because it was too hard, it's manageable). this class is unavoidable for any student pursing neuro so be prepared! The content itself was rather interesting but I thought we would have done more with this class.
Most condescending teacher i've met; reason why I'm not a neuro major.
my number one op. went to all lectures and OH in this class and she never learned my name. content was interesting, but she was very demeaning.

NSCI201 lab is graded by too few things. If you did terrible in one assignment or quiz, no matter how hard you try in other assignments, you will still be screwed. It is not a "graded on completion/effort" course, but it should have been, because many questions in assignments, even in quiz, are open ended.

She explains well and is available for extra help. However, she is a tough *very tough* grader and the class grades always stay the same. Her way of asking questions in exams is very "her" so write what she would answer and not how the book might answer it

I respect her and she is very knowledgable. I struggled with the content and had to rewatch every lecture to understand (self recorded), but if you have more bio/research background it may be easier. My ability to read research papers has improved, and if you demonstrate interest, she is really nice and understanding (including with grade bonuses)

201Lab was tough, since there were few assignments we were graded by. Listen to her instructions and copy them EXACTLY (take crazy notes or record her) and you will do well enough. She really likes when students demonstrate interest - go to her OH or chat with her and she might grade more nicely...I liked her overall and found her very knowledgable

She is such an intellectual and knowledgeable person inspiring her students to think critically. 301 is made up of discussions and presentations covering interesting topics that bridge science and society, like neuro ethics, scientific integrity, neuroeconomics etc. Do the readings, show up, and talk and talk. then you will get a A in this class.

Dr. Miller is such an amazing professor. I was told by peers to avoid her, so that's what I tried to do, but it's near impossible as a neuro major. I took two classes with her and I don't know what my peers were talking about. She was incredibly caring and kind to me, and explained everything so well, and was more than happy to answer my questions.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Professor Miller is one of the least understanding professors I have had at the university. She quizzes you on small details, grades really hard, and is not clear about the expectations for her assignments. She is the reason I switched my major, and I have heard similar experiences from others.

I took her neurochemistry course in summer online. The content was dense but hard. A lot of paper discussions and write-ups & presentations. You have to attend the lectures and discussions as well as prepare for lecture quizzes and exams, but none of them was too difficult. Definitely learned a lot of things in depth and she is very helpful.

Dr. Miller is very knowledgable on the topics that she teaches and is clearly passionate in the field of neuro. Her class is tough and she definitely makes you work for it, but it's a class worth taking. She is also very helpful and caring during office hours, which I recommend going to.
A tough instructor, but a very intelligent and caring woman. Always prepared and likes to make you think. Class participation is very important.
Her class was overall very easy to succeed in however the book assigned was completely useless the only way to get a good grade was to go to class and memorize her slides.

She is my favorite professor at this school. Yes, her tests are hard, and she makes you actually learn and apply the material, but she is very willing to help you if you go to her office hours. Once I went to go over a test and she ended up giving me 5 points back.
She is very difficult to follow. Avoid taking a class with her if possible. Literally just throws jargon at you and is extremely rude.
Extremely helpful. Best professor at the school.
Had her as a lab professor. She was very nice and I thought she was approachable.
She seemed very nice to me and approachable. I only had her as a lab professor though.

Steven York is not a professor, rather, he is a TA for this class. The professor Mark Povich is a very good professor, but this TA ruined our interest towards this course. He deducted 10 points in midterm for using sth. instead of something???

Was more like an anthro class. She is definitely well-read and experienced but if you disagreed with her she could be rude. SO many rules in the classroom and felt like being back in middle school/being babied. Would grade super harsh then blame the class for our low average even though there were only 16 people in my class.

Was VERY political, and if you didn't agree then you were wrong. She only focused on female archaeologists and she always bashed the male archaeologists. Was more like a history class tbh. There is 2 exams (no final) and there are 2 long papers and presentations. Attendance is graded and she has a lot of classroom rules. Felt like I was 10 again...

Felt like sitting in a middle school class. I thought the class would be based on Archaeology, but it was more like Anthropology and she was very political. Not the best grader and she only considered "one correct answer" in many cases. Also could be rude and had very harsh in classroom rules, I felt babied often.

I had her for ATHS381, She is very passionate about the study, and it's obvious she cares a lot about the subject matter at hand. She did end up canceling a lot of classes, and since the class was only once week, I feel like I missed a lot, but outside of that, when we did have class it was very insightful and I feel like I learned a lot.

Did not teach archaeology as a science based course, but rather as a history class, based on the struggles and social issues faced by archaeologists across history. Not what I was looking for, felt like taking a high school class all over again: long syllabus, harsh class rules, etc.

"Inkas & Their Ancestors" class crosslisted as Anthro and History, but it obviously is an Archaeology class. Her lectures are VERY information heavy and definitely focus on Peru's prehistory (briefly discuss the Inkas for 2 weeks). Time consuming projects (make a khipu, study a site via Google Earth) but she's nice and passionate about her field

Bautista is a sweetheart, very knowledgeable, and incredibly caring. Class was almost entirely discussion-based with a few scattered lectures so participation is important. There's a lot of reading but it's difficult (though not impossible) to participate without the readings so at least skim them. Bautista expects a lot but she's a fair grader.
The class was difficult but it was helpful that Professor Bautista was very passionate about the topic.
Dr. Goldschmidt grades essays leniently and will give review sheets right before the exams covering everything you need to know. Funny guy, great class. Exactly what I'm looking for in a phil course

Funny Professor but can also explain harder concepts (e.g. Metaethics) very competently. His class is super chill: there are three midterms all of which are very manageable, plus an essay which he provides clear guidelines along with an example essay for. PHL102 is a great class to start a PHL cluster, especially if you have never done PHL before.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Only four assignments, three tests and one essay. The tests are pretty straightforward and you can learn everything straight from the book or internet, you really don't need the class. The facilitation of discussion is quite boring, frankly. The professor usually complains about his salary and that gets old after awhile. Wouldn't take again.
Funny professor. Cares for students that show up to lecture. Tests are straightforward. Makes lots of jokes that make more complex topics easier to understand and remember. Overall good professor.

I've taken 2 classes with Lacina and they're not bad. However, for this class, your whole grade is based on 3 essays so make sure you are good at writing and studying the content throughout the semester. My only complaint is that her grading criteria varied for each of my essays so it was hard to understand what she was looking for.

Professor Lacina is kind but not the most engaging professor. This class is incredibly reading-heavy, so make sure you can dedicate enough time to read a book a week (or at least skim it thoroughly). Her feedback sometimes varies, I wish she was a little more specific at times, but overall not a bad course!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Professor Lacina is a skilled political scientist and kind person, but sometimes not the most engaging as a professor. My biggest issue was that the amount of reading assigned was completely unrealistic, and this is coming from someone who has taken quite reading-heavy courses in the past. Feedback is useful and grading is not harsh.

Would not recommend Prof Lacina. She came across as very awkward,unclear, and not very confident with the material. The assigned readings for the class were interesting, but Prof Lacina was boring as an instructor and killed all interest I had in the class.

The course itself was an easy A, but the instructor was frequently confused and not very knowledgeable. Professor Lacina was also just socially awkward and not good at interacting with students, which made class meetings uncomfortable.

I love her.  She seemed kinda dry in the beginning, but by the end of the class she was my favorite.  She is not a pushover, she is organized and expects something from you, she is really smart and you will learn a lot.  She is an excellent lecturer and very inspiring, she treats you like an adult, in a good way. She's just really great.

Prof is helpful, approachable, passionate about the subject, but poor lecturer.  Frequently pauses in mid-sentence as if confused. An overall interesting class and not too difficult, but lectures are not inspiring and usually lackluster.  Take the course if you are interested in the subject. Lacina probably won't inspire.

Professor Lacina is awesome. This class was very interesting, and she managed the discussion in a way that kept it quite engaging. I would call her neither difficult nor easy, but students should expect to at least skim the reading. Her knowledge is vast, but she's still very friendly and funny. Acts more like a grad student than a professor.

one of the best econ instructors I ever had. No slides in class, so you truly have to attend class to follow the material. He encourages discussion during lectures. Assignments are challenging, and there are no completely “standard” answers. You can only perform well if you read the  materials and fully understand the concepts he explains in class.
You need to understand economics in his logic because his logics are logical and correct. Tests are awesome! Love this course
You have to understand economics through his own logic or else you won't pass. Grades are solely based on the two midterms and the final exam. Tests are hard.

Respected and well-known professor who is truly knowledgeable about economics. Might be a little controversial on his published books. Materials he teach is very clear and concise. Follows a nice logic and time line. Very well-structured lecture and information.

Landsburg is really smart, and the course content is quite fun. The course is 100% homeworks, so take it if for the low stress environment. The homeworks are a little challenging, but nothing absurd, and the grading is fairly generous. You have to do well in 207 in order to get into the course (you apply for it), but don't let that scare you away

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Very hard course, but he is good at explaining concepts. Lectures are enlightening, but homework is hard. This course is only open to those who have got an A/A+ in Landsburg's 207 course. So, you will meet the top students there. Students are amazing!

Fantastic genius! A true legend in Economics. If you study hard, put effort, and are good at math. You will definitely get an A. He is good at separating the hard-working and non-hard-working students. Grades will tell.

Prof responded to "no partial credit" myth with some stats. Unfortunately, the data is likely to be biased. Even getting 1% credit falls into the "partial credit" category. It would be more convincing if the actual distribution of the grades is shown. His course might still be good, but I hope people correctly understand what to expect.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: He is a nice person and very approachable outside of class. However, his grading criteria is vague, and he has his unique way of solving problems and understanding economics. Highly recommend to do all the homework, but tests are much harder than that. His lecture is inspiring, but you do not need to attend if you just want to have a good grade.

Professor Landsburg is definitely one of my favorite professors. His lectures are always fun, and he makes a boring economic concept very interesting. You will learn a whole new approach to microeconomics. Make sure to do your homework because those questions are very similar to exam questions.
Final was nearly impossible! Econ is not just about understanding econ! You have to understand his logic, the way how he want you to do it. If you don't, good luck!

Not very accommodating when it came to COVID and quarantine. Also, 90% of lecture were very boring (even for someone who loves econ). Tests were very difficult but the curve was fair. Don't look into his background bc he has said some controversial things that you prob don't want to know about.

His logic makes such little sense, and exam grading is actual crap, you either understand Econ HIS way or he fails you. But my biggest problem with him is that he doesnt post solutions for any previous exams he shares, nor does he tell his TAs about anything, so if they solve a question wrong and teach that, youll never know.

Final grades are available. Again, this is one of my favorite class at UR. It has been my pleasure to take both 108 and 207 with professor Landsburg. I am not sure if he is still teaching ECO108 and ECO207, but if he does, you should definitely take economics classes with him.
I am still waiting for my final grade for this class. But still, this is one of my favorite class and favorite professor. I like economics because of him.

He's not as bad as people said, but you really need to hit the point to get a good grade. For his class, either you are an A student or a C student, and there are NO in between. Sometimes even F... There are no partial credit even if you demonstrate you understand some of the materials.

This professor only gives a grade based on 2 midterms and a final. In these papers, he doesn't give any partial credit so it's very easy to mess up in one small area and get a 0 on that question. The concepts he teaches are not that hard but his explanation sometimes confuses me. I've understood more from TAs than him.

Homework does not count towards grades. If you get a question wrong on exam, means that you did not pay attention in class or did not completely understand the questions you got wrong on your homework. I can tell that midterms are fair, and the grading is not that harsh as what you said. So it is surely your problem for not doing well on the exam.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']
comment: Lecture is good, but homework and exams are really tough... Insanely harsh grader on exam. Either you get the full credit for a question on exam or no credit at all.
He is a really good economics professor! His explanation and the logic of his lecture is extremely clear! I like economics because of him, and I need his rating to go up!
good teaching skills

Professor Landsburg shares a lot of inspirational stories in this course. He introduces several useful and also interesting topics which might change the way you think about economics and business. Definitely should take this course if you are interested in economics.

Professor Landsburg is one of the best and smartest professors here at U of R. His lecture is well-organized and inspirational. His logic is clear and easy to follow. Spend times on reviewing lecture notes and HW problems, then you will get a good grade.
He knows what he is doing.

He is a great lecturer and you do not need to use the textbook after watching the lecture he really covers everything there. The only concern for this course is that exams counts for 85% for your grade and they are pretty difficult. Still, the curve is good 85.1% is an A in this semester so I think overall thee course is great!

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']
comment: A different vibe comparing to Rizzo

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I like this class because we only get a few webwork problems each week, and as long as you pay attention to the lectures, these problems are easy to finish. Exams, two midterms and a final, are fair. You do need to spend time review the course materials and do practice problems if you want to do well on these exams.

Amazing class, amazing professor. I learned so much and his lectures really stick in your memory. Class is homework based entirely; the work is very difficult but rewarding and doable. Anyone who wants a true in-depth understanding of micro-economics should take this class

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']
comment: Ridiculously tough exams. I attended every lecture, understood every concept and did every homework and still got a B+ because I messed up one long question in one exam. The margin of error is razor thin. The class is very interesting, great intro to econ. Highly quantitative teaching style.

His logic is extremely unique yet clear. This class is mainly graph-based and is easy for some people yet hard for others. Study hard makes an A easy. This course definitely gives a great introduction to microeconomics and some macro at the end of the semester. Worth the time to take this class with one of the most respected economists out there.

As long as you understand his unique logic (may take some time), you will see that his logic is extremely clear and simple. It is very important to follow all of his lectures and logics, and this makes an A relatively easy. People who tend to fail are usually people who do not go to lectures or people who don't seek help when they don't understand.

Professor Landsburg is excellent at presenting topics clearly, and answers all questions with as much explanation as is necessary. Tests are challenging but very fair, everything you need to learn is extensively covered in class.
People who got a bad grade come here to complain. Yes, I am, and trust me, u will be no exception. Ridiculous exam and grading. Ready to fail.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Only two midterms and one final in his class count toward your final grade. It is and he always makes the test hard as hell. Not recommended to take his class.

He is one of the smartest professors around. He will make you question simple things around you in a good way. His classes are more organized and structured which allows you to do well if you go to all the classes and review your notes. I was told his classes were math heavy but I would say they are more logic heavy than mathematical

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']
comment: Take landsburg if you hate yourself. Just kidding, take landsburg if you love math and are majoring in econ and suffering. Take Rizzo if you prefer a more abstract and accessible approach to economics. This class taught me some hard lessons. I burned out because I hated it. He and his style are not my preference. Be self-aware and save yourself

The class and professor will truly change your outlook on how the world works. If you want to know what Econ is all about, take this class. The material is easy to understand if you pay attention in lecture and make an effort to learn. There is not much homework but it is vital to continue to think about what was discussed in class.

ECO208W is the most challenging but also the most rewarding course in the economics department. It is the class where you see the Armchair Economist at his finest, and you really learn how to think like one of the best economists out there. The topics in the class are relatable and make you see the world around you differently.

Professor Landsburg's ECO207 gives strong foundation to more advanced topics in the field of economics through easy-to-follow lectures. Although many found his exams tricky, the key to succeeding is being able to apply key facts that are repeated clearly in every lecture and when reviewing HW in class.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Professor Landsburg's class is the better choice for ECO108 at U of R. He provides both a quantitative and theoretical foundation in economics, so you will be prepared for all other courses in the economics department. His lectures are very clear and easy to follow. If you learn and apply the basic rules he presents, you will succeed in the exams.

The content covered is pretty much the same as ECO108, but the homework and exams are much much harder. He only covers very basic examples in class, and you have to really practice to get much harder questions right on exams. The final is mad tough, and you're probably gonna get at least one impossible question on it.
Easy course material, doable exam, great lecture.

Going to class was actually fun. The lectures are very clear, with lots of interesting real-world examples. Also, he always hangs around after class to take questions, which is really helpful. Tests are pretty easy if you study, impossible if you don't.

After I blew an exam problem, he sent me a long email, with diagrams, explaining exactly where I'd gone wrong. He also told me the rest of my exam was great and I shouldn't be discouraged by this one mistake. I really appreciated this. Lectures are clear and sometimes fascinating. Best course at UR so far.

I dropped this class because almost everything in this class is a nightmare Not very respectful to students in his office hours and gave out exams testing stuff that makes no sense. For the sake of my time and gpa, I dropped his course.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']
comment: For Gives 0 partial credit on exams. Must read book, copy correct HW answers shown in class(Completing all these correctly can bump grade by .5 to 1.0 letter grade) & all he writes on board, do prac exams and go to review sessions. Get either A or F, but all based on you. Prac exams q's/HWK directly correlate to the topics you need to Ace class.

Professor Landsburg is an expert in economics and teaches the material well. He efficiently and effectively translates difficult concepts to allow students to perform well on very straight-forward exams. The class really is not too difficult if you apply yourself and try to understand the concepts. I really enjoyed taking ECO108 from Landsburg.

He is a really good professor, and I highly recommend taking a class with him! I think I learned the most in his introductory courses and I really enjoyed his graph-based explanationsthey definitely helped to clarify and elucidate concepts. Most students Ive talked to enjoyed his class, but you do have to put in effort to get a good grade.
If you have the opportunity to take this class, do so.
Now that I am about to graduate, I can say that Eco 207 was the best course I took at the University of Rochester, and Professor Landsburg is the best teacher I've had anywhere, ever.
He was an extremely tough grader and really unfair. Barely gave partial credit and wasn't very approachable after class. He also seemed to really enjoy roasting students.
Difficult class but worth it if youre willing to put in the effort. Make sure to do lots of practice problems before exams. The exams are difficult but doable.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Just go take Rizzos. I love everything about this professor but not the final test. You either get it or none. I almost failed the course because of my test performance even though I understand all his concepts. Now Im retaking micro with rizzo and I feel so much relief.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: His class tests your critical thinking rather than the concepts that you learn. You can do all the problems on the etxtbook but it will be useless if you dont reflect on what you did.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Just avoid and take Rizzo's 207. It's that simple.

Ok Landsburg is not a bad lecturer. But his exams are HARD.. I know 3 people who failed ECO207 last semester and we went to every lecture and did all the homeworks. My point is no matter how well you know Microeconomics, you may fail the exams (100% of your course grade) and the class. Beware if you have to take this awful course.. otherwise avoid!
AVOID. Period.
Spent time, got nearly 100% on midterms and received a B-. Hmmm.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Trust me, you are more likely to get an A in the honored course than Landsburg's 207.

I feel sorry for all students who have taken or are planning to take Landsburg's ECO207. You basically wastes a whole semester of valuable time and get yur life ruined. His grading criteria is more like a lottery and god please stop all this nonsense. Good luck to you all, you are all talented students and will succeed in yur future career.

Professor Landsburg may be a well known economist, but his class is unbearable. I did okay in 108 with him and took 207 and devoted lots of time and still didnt pass. Exams are impossible as he tests you on your critical thinking skills, and not the course material. Dont recommend if you need Landsburg unless you have to take the class with him.

Good lecturer and economist, but the exams (3 extremely difficult exams determine your grade) are crazy hard and this course will ruin your GPA. I'd avoid this course unless you have to take it or are very passionate about economics.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: For students taking as cluster course, I strongly suggest you to think twice before adding this course. This course is nothing different from ECO108, i.e. learning repeated knowledge but A LOT harder exams. If you do not plan to invest excess amount of time in Economics, expect to have 50% grade or less in your exams and be prepared to retake.

ECO207 with Landsburg will not be easy. He is a fantastic lecturer with decades of experience to share. You will learn so much about economics in class. Now his exams (100% of your grade) arent easy since they dont necessarily test if you just know the material or not. You need to do a fair amount of critical thinking to do well. Practice lots!
Simply the best professor I have met at UR so far. His lecture is great because he explains things clearly, and he is super nice when you turn to him for help after class.

Great lecturer! Very inspirational, gives lots of real world examples to tie to microeconomic concepts. However, his tests can be improved where there's not too much ambiguity on how pts are awarded. His class is basically graded on 3 exams.. too much pressure on the student
His lecture is so great! I literally expect to take his class every Monday and Wednesday! Lots of inspiring cases introduced in class.
His class is really inspirational! Best lectures of this semester.

Amazing lectures but exams are way harder than the homework and very confusing. I advise that you do not take this class unless you absolutely have to and if you have to, work very hard to get good grades in your other classes so that this class doesn't do too much harm to your GPA because your grade in this class is very unpredictable.
Amazing lectures. So interesting, easily the best class I've taken at this school.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: If you are interested in real Economics, only taking his lecture is not enough. What economic textbooks and theories tell you are often contradictory to what really happened in the world. But overall, Landsburg has done a good job in classes

Exams basically determines your grade, specially the final. But if u understand each question in the weekly homework which will not count in your final grade, you will be able to solve them on the exams and get an A.

The lectures are fantastically clear and usually interesting. There is a lot of homework, but Prof Landsburg goes over every problem in class and explains exactly how to solve it. The exams cover exactly the same ideas and methods as the homework, so if you pay attention in class, it's easy to do well.
The man is a fantastic economist, but unless you have Einsteins ability to overcome academic question papers! do not take his class!

One of the smartest guy have ever met, grading based on exams only, but will bounce if you do nice homework. The course isn't hard if you participate the lectures, and the lecture videos are also available.

He has a clear thought of what he is teaching. Some people might think his exams are challenged compare to what he taught. However, he did teach evey basic principle need to use in the exams. And his homework is also helpful. I have to admit that if you work hard and follow the pace you should not find it is hard on the exam.

Really inspiring prof. His lectures are clear, entertaining, and really the only study material you need to go with the course. Just do it. Take all of his classes.

He is the best Eco professor I have ever met. His class is not fun but well organized and the only thing you should pay attention to is to listen to his lecture carefully. Attend the class, get an A
Good Professor

Great professor!! ECO 207 has been my favorite class so far.  His tests are hard but fair.  You must put a good amount of work into this class but well worth it.  Highly recommend taking this class.

Very light work load, Difficult exams, Difficult Quizzes. Went to the TA's every week, because he is unapproachable. Has to time to be writing controversial blogs but not to meet with his students. Very light work load, Difficult exams. Went to the TA's every week, because he is unapproachable. His lectures do not prepare you for the exam, he is interesting, but his exams are VERY difficult.

great lecturer, explains concept clearly and logically but REALLY HARD EXAMS. understanding only what he teaches in the class is not enough to help you get a good grade...

comment: He is very nice and loves game theory. He is a little unnecessarily math heavy for such an abstract course, but he is always available to help. Lectures are mandatory but confusing so prepare to teach yourself everything at home. Go for extra help, he can seem a little condescending but he means well. As a whole just really hard but you can do it.

You have to work hard to do well in this class. You have to go to office hours. He is one of the most caring, and respectful professors I have ever had. The way he was able to help me throughout the semester really helped me turn things around. It is hard but he will help you succeed if you are sincere and go for help. Extra credit is also there.

I adore this woman.  She's brilliant, funny, and absolutely amazing.  A-maz-ing.

Repeats herself to the point that the information is hammered into your head. The class is elementary, and Professor Iyer does a great job and explaining the basics of Accounting.

One of my favorite professors, super personable and helpful. Tests and homework's can be hard, but he gives extra credit. Class work is easy to follow and super helpful in learning more about excel. Would definitely take another one of his classes.

One of the hardest classes I have taken at the school. However, Dan is an exceptional professor, and CIS 211 is an extremely useful class. I definitely would recommend Dan to anyone who can take him and his classes.

Ok if you just want an easy course for an easy A, Prof doesn't know a lot but I guess sufficient for a business course in this University. Horrendous TA and grading that made the course a lot more frustrating that it needs to be.

Dan Keating is the best professor I've had as of yet. Professor Keating is the best Professor I have ever met in the U of R. He is very vice and approachable and explains the material very clearly. I would like to take his class again.

He is curtious and genial. His classes are always interesting, he tends to go off topic. He is a ridiculously easy grader. Definately go to his office hours, he is a nice person to talk to, and if you show interest in his class you will do very well.

He's definitely a nice guy.  If you take one of his classes, definitely go to his office hours so he can know you by name and face.  Once he knows who you are and let him know that your interested in his class, you'll automatically do well.

useless

comment: Mind-numbingly boring lecturer that spends much more time than needed on very basic concepts. Assigns weekly homeworks, mandatory workshops, and discussion posts. Pop quizzes scattered throughout the sem, which I'm convinced is the only reason anybody actually attends the lectures. Nice person, gets the curriculum across, but just so boring.

The professor is nice but boring. The only thing that kept me interested was the content. For an intro class, I would say it takes a lot of effort to learn this new information. Lots of my peers said they struggled. There is also a mandatory recitation that is extremely helpful. Take advantage of that. The exams are simple if you study.

As an introduction class, there was little introduction material. Topics were discussed without proper understanding from students. Exams and quizzes are correlated with homework not lectures.
Very nice teacher, very helpful.

Best math teacher I have ever had. Hands down. He is so clear and helpful! A great teacher and was one of the reasons I was able to do well in the class. he is also funny and jokes around a bit, which makes the class enjoyable.
One of the best professors for calculus 142. A friend with another professor went to Haessig's lectures because he taught better. Hes also witty if you're quick enough to catch his humor.

Alex is the best professor I have ever had. He makes 165, a highly abstract and hard to comprehend topic, graspable and breaks it down easily. He could teach this to a child. Alex Rice. What a bae. One of the clearest lecturers I've ever had and the most helpful and thoughtful office hours I've gone to. Wouldn't have wished for any other professors my Freshman year. He barely do  examples of question types in class. He is not at all helpful in office hour. Rude to talk to.

Clearest professor in the world. The examples he gives are extremely relevant to the problems you'll have to do and he explains them amazingly well. Makes great use of class time. I wish he could teach me every subject for the rest of my life.

Alex is the CLEAREST math professor you could ever have. He literally writes EVERYTHING on the board & explains it all. Not only is he great at teaching, but he's just a very cool person in general. He is kind, respectful, and helpful, but his greatest downfall is the massive intelligence gap between he and his students. I think he often genuinely believes a difficult topic is "simple" or "high school level," and doesn't mean it as an insult.

I have to admit, this guy is arrogant. He will literally make everyone around him feel stupid. If you dont care about math too much, dont take a class from him. Dont get me wrong, he is funny, and he gives good grades. And to be honest he is a genius. But your motivation will basically go downhill.
The curve is sooo nice. Also Alex is a great guy. Great lecturer, really funny.
The BEST math teacher I met ever! He always challenge you during the lecture. Watch out and pay attention!

Attendance isn't mandatory, but he remembers who shows up and who doesn't. He's very helpful and accommodating, and I could tell he really wanted us all to succeed. If you're willing to learn, he'll do everything he can to make sure that you do. He also regularly brings his dog to wander around during lectures, which was kinda fun.

Going to lecture did not help at all. He just made things more confusing. If you have to take a class from him, stay home and read the book. You'll be better off! And don't even try going to office hours - he'll brush you off.
If you have to suffer through a math class, this is the best guy to help you through it!

This is a hard course, but not because of the professor.  He genuinely wants his students to learn the material and will help you as much as you want, but only if you ask him for it.  He's very funny in class, although that often leads to getting off-topic.

His class is very easy to follow because he makes sure you understand the concept with multiple examples that make you think outside of the box (ironically, he uses a box and other items instead of standard variables). Always sets office hours and review sessions that work for the entire class, and he runs the review.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Iosevich doesn't get to teach many undergraduate classes, so if you have the good fortune of taking his class you are very lucky! He is dedicated to his class and will go out of his way to help you even after you complete his class. He is a funny guy and a great lecturer. He makes sure you understand the math beyond equations.
Fantastic!!!!

Very funny. He cares about his students, and often asks how they're doing before class. His lessons are usually crystal clear, which is impressive for such a difficult subject. He's always honest, and is a fair grader.

I graduated from U of R 4 years ago, if I had to basically say there was one professor who was not professional, it was Professor Chao.

I would basically say that she's in a cult. And you will get bad grades on your work if it does not justify Falun Gong. If you research using official narratives such as NYTimes you will be penalized. No fair 4 me

I mean, I really like her. Since this is my last semester, if I had the chance, I would take her class again. Very nice lady who is professional and caring for what she teaches. But please do the readings if you want to write good essays. Once you read, it won't be hard to get a good grade. Please take her class.

She is incredibly repetitive, makes tons of errors and still grades very harshly. Please do not take her class! The only regret is I didn't check her up on rate my professors before I signed up for her class.

Extremely tough grader, very repetitive and sometimes contradicts herself. She couldn't spell properly and make tons of grammatical mistakes in her materials but expects us to hand in papers with perfect writing. The only good thing I can say about this class is the interesting readings. Overall 10/10 do not recommend.
Not much good to say. She made the lessons hard to understand, was repetitive, and not very helpful even when the students reached out.

The other reviews here shocked me - I've had nothing but good experiences with Professor Chao. Her English is fine, her grading isn't that rough (I got a B+ on my midterm and actually thought she was quite generous with that), show up and do the readings. She's a little repetitive but I always left class understanding the important points.

Insanely hard grader. If you miss a keyword that she's looking for, but accurately describe the concept, she will count it completely wrong. She focuses on tiny details- be prepared to really memorize every little thing in the readings. I'm taking this class pass fail because I just don't know how to meet her standards and she is not helpful at all
Was condescending and not particularly helpful, can't recommend this class to anyone.

This professor is absolutely terrible. She does not speak English well enough to teach this class. She says contradictory things in her lecture, and when you write down what she said on exams, she counts them wrong. When you go ask her about why you got it wrong, she doesn't explain herself and is extremely condescending. Don not take her classes.

This guy is a GOAT. He is extremely helpful to those students who strive to stay on top of the class. As long as you read your articles, attend lectures, and ask questions, I guarantee your time will be spent wisely. For those interested in journalism, I highly recommend this course! 

Be warned that there are pop quizzes and long articles.

Professor Liu is an excellent teacher. He would give ample examples on techniques he wanted us to learn and have us try it out in class, and he is great with constructive criticism. He kept the class engaged and interactive by having us read really interesting journal articles and by having us work with each other on in-class work.
she keeps asking posibly can not think for herself
Great professor!

Dr. Jeannine Dingus is a great professor! She is HIGHLY intelligent and extremely helpful.  Most of my classmates were too immature to appreciate her because she is a no-nonsense type of person, but she is truly great.  She is the very best professor at the Warner School!
No Comments

Easy class, easy prof., but def. not open to others' opinions, and not a high quality prof. I just finished the UR's M.S. in Teach. prog. and I regret attending the U of R because of Profs. like Dingus, with little classroom teaching exp. She focuses on the negative and fails to prepare us for anything but teaching in urban schools.
No Comments

Assistant professor Dingus obviously thinks that she is a great assistant professor.  It is apparent in the way she teaches and speaks about herself.  However, it is also very telling.  Watch out my fellow students, assistant professor Dingus definately has some issues in the race department.  Buyer beware: her class is not free, but should be.

If you want a professor who is upfront and tells you how it is, Dr. Dingus is the one for you. She is an excellent professor who is fun and engaging. She is a critical professor, but who said that was a bad thing? She gets you to think outside of the box. If you want easy...go to MCC!
She isn't HARD, she is CRITICAL . . . welcome to grad school people. If you want easy, go somewhere else.
No Comments
Too hard, too much to read!
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH DINGUS!!!  WORST TEACHER EVER, WHAT A WASTE OF MY TIME AND MY MONEY.  SHE SUCKS.  I HOPE SHE GETS FIRED!
No Comments
He teaches you to think like a mathematician and it way more important than any calculus topic

We were behind in the first two months. But then he made less errors and got ahead of the other classes. His class is the calmest & simplest. Pick him if you're good at Calc BC concepts, pick a diff prof. if you want to learn the most. Responds very fast to emails + sometimes does hard HW probs in class. Confused in lecture? Ask questions then lol

Doug was an alright professor when he taught integration. However, his class lectures on polar coordinates, parametric equations, and series were often confusing because he would skip some important information on those topics. He did go over many examples for those three topics, but never really explained his process clearly. Get a tutor for 162.

Nice guy and very smart, just one of those people who just cannot teach and should not teach math. His lectures are very confusing and rather than teaching how to work through problems he just does them with little to no coherent explanation. His lectures are similar. Do not take him if you are poor in math.

Awful. Bad lectures. Doesn't know what's going on. Learned everything on my own. Gave our class 20 mins less time on 1st midterm. Whole calc department awful. No one willing to give points back on exams. Graders are so tough. Go to rec and do all webwork to boost grade and you might survive. Never taking a math course at U of R again.

Doug's lectures range from pretty boring to very interesting. He uses a lot of real life examples which many math professors at this university don't seem to do. However, he is very constantly making computational errors which slows down the lectures a lot. Also, I'm often leaving lectures not really feeling confident I learned very much.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Doug is nice and starts lecture by showing famous mathematicians' contributions. He's not great at explaining concepts. He teaches by running through example problems which is only sometimes helpful. He's often out of touch with what's on homework, which tends to be harder than tests. Use previous tests to study as questions are recirculated.

Doug isn't the greatest teacher and has a hard time explaining concepts, he just does a bunch of examples and hopes the students understand. However, he is a caring person who is very funny. For the tests, just use the practice tests, as the tests are very similar year to year. Don't procrastinate WebWork!!!

Doug tells math history stories before every lecture, the highlight of my day. Do the practice tests online; they basically mimic the actual tests and don't cheat your webwork since it's the only homework you get assigned. He's very approachable during office hours and loves to chat with students.

Not a big fan of his teaching. He tries to make class engaging by talking about a random math fact every class, but it got pretty boring. In fact I skipped his lectures altogether and simply just followed the textbook content to self-study. I would recommend choosing the other 162 profs such as Charles Wolf or Bogdan Krstic.

His way of teaching is working through example problems to show you the different techniques. This makes it hard to organise the content as you don't always know what technique he's covering. So, I had to use the textbook to know what exactly was being covered and make additional notes after lectures. He's not the best lecturer but you'll be fine.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Arguably the worst math lecturer I've ever had! He starts every lecture rambling about a non-math tangentially related topic, and then fails to cover relevant parts of the course. Teaches poorly, and though the exams are what I expected, the lack of proper teaching and his nonsense exam curve made the class overly frustrating. Take it with Wolf.

Starts every lecture with an unrelated story and always connects himself at the end. Has a pretty big ego. Lectures make no sense and he jumps right into applications without explaining concepts. His favorite thing to do is start a very complex problem in class and make mistakes solving it, only to say "you can figure that out". DO NOT TAKE RAVENEL

In the first part of the course (integration). His lectures helped but afterwards you need to look at other resources to understand everything. He is a bit slow in my opinion and does not explain everything included in exams. His exams are extremely difficult, but they have great curves. You can get 80ish on every exam and still get an A.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Calc II sucks, he's useful until sequences and series. After that, just watch Khan academy and patrick jmt. Starts every lecture with a story relating to that day's topic, which I liked but others didn't. Other students were pretty noisy, and lectures aren't recorded. Notes are posted but good luck deciphering them. Hit or miss mostly, but fine.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Worst ever professor. Not interested in teaching. Makes easy tests. I don't understand the purpose of his class.

Doug is fantastic. Class time is structured with an eye towards applications, hitting on just how the major concepts are useful in (mathematical) practice at a high level. More technical/detailed aspects are left for homework. He's also a sweet guy, and peppers lectures with awesome stories and fun tidbits of information.

I highly recommend his class. The stories he tells are amazing and very funny, but they all have to do with math, in one way or another. He does lectures on his Surface Laptop so his handwriting isnt the best, but if you go to class and see the notes he post later, you can understand it. He loves participation, dont leave him hanging. GREAT PROF

Loves to start class with his stories but will jump right into calculus. If you ask for clarification in class, he will elaborate. Posts notes online , but his handwriting is atrocious. Tests are hard, but there is a generous curve at the end. Go to recitations and do the quizzes. Everyone can get at least a B+ if you're dedicated.

Prof. Ravenel gives very interesting lectures, but he won't go very deep into proof. He have lots of stories to share before classes. He is also very approachable and nice during his office hour. But tests are somehow challenging, so you need to work harder!!

I LOVE HIM!! Best math professor I've ever had. He explains everything really well and all his notes are online. Always available for office hours. He has a bunch of great stories he shares at the beginning of every class. Coolest guy I've ever met. AND! He has a cute dog he takes to class every day :)

He's very nice and understanding. Lecture math classes just overall suck and his tests and homework can be very difficult but he's an overall nice guy. The homework requires some outside help and is accompanied by frustration but he's easy to talk to during office hours and is very approachable.
GOOD
Dougie Ravs is a straight baller. HE has massive curves which counteracts the difficult tests. His stories are legendary.

Really difficult class. Ravenel was the best out of the 3 MTH162 professors this semester though. ADHD though - is always bolted back and forth across the room when explaining something. Usually starts lectures off with a short story - sometimes they are math related, and sometimes they are so random you can't help but laugh.

Okay at explaining things, but tests are very difficult. Also, dont listen to him when he says he is a lenient grader, he isn't! Also makes a lot of mistake while working on examples in class and rarely fixes them. Not the best professor you could have, but I guess not the worst either.
He tells fun stories before every lecture. LOVE!

He's pretty good, he always opens class with a historical/funny anecdote about math. His teaching style is fairly clear and if you're unsure of something he's usually ok with going back and explaining it again. He puts his full lectures online (he has a touch screen computer that he writes his lecture notes on). He makes his exams super hard though

A pretty quirky professor. He always starts lectures with some other interest (astronomy, math history, etc) and paces a lot. All lecture notes were posted online. Tests were pretty hard and had low averages, but they were always curved. If you work hard, do the Webwork, read the textbook, and do the optional textbook problems, you can get an A.

Brilliant guy who has a lot of interests, including astronomy, math history, and so on, that he sometimes talks about in class.  Lectures go at a good pace (speaking of which, he paces around a lot).  TONS of homework but exams are easy.  He is a little disorganized at times.
He was alright. His lectures are better than most other math professors. But he's not easy. His test medians are usually a failing grade, so you actually have to study to do well.
Prof. Ravenel gives interesting and clear lectures. Seemed intimidating at first, but proved super helpful and friendly.
Good teacher, easy to understand in lecture.  Only need text for extra problems, none of those are ever turned in though.  I liked him a lot

Impossible to get ahold of outside of class. I struggled with the class and often reached out but never got a response. The class was entirely exam based, just a heads up. He wasn't there to proctor his exams, and the final in particular had so many spelling and grammar mistakes that it was impossible to figure out what the questions were asking

The entire course was based on tests, which were incredibly similar to the practice questions he released. He goes over basic topics which is on the tests, but then he goes into harder/more advanced concepts which are fun to learn. He has a tough accent but it's manageable. I would recommend taking with the other professor, usually Kalandrakis

Prof. Audi is particularly hard to rate; he assigns two professional-level philosophy paper readings per week; this quickly becomes difficult to keep up with. However, the corresponding assignments for the reading are very easy and easily done if you read the article/use the Stanford Encyclopedia. He is very caring, passionate and fun to be around.

His lectures frequently devolved into complete nonsense and the TA was no help. Granted, the ideas in the readings are usually convoluted and require a lot of time to deeply understand. He was super chill when I had a health issue and had to miss some time though. Overall not much work but suprisingly draining.

Class not mandatory to do well, pretty lenient grader and a very nice guy. Lectures can sometimes be tough to sit through if you aren't interested in the topics but overall he is a very interesting lecturer.

Pro: Very easy-going, flexible deadlines. Really knows his stuff. Likes to make jokes in class. Gives few graded assignments, which can be both a pro and a con.
Con: Lectures all over the place, talks about whatever pops into his head, which takes some getting used to. And for some reason, his class is always super early in the morning.

Love the guy, but his lecture style isn't for everyone. He jumps from one topic to the next as comes to mind, which is really interesting if you already have the philosophy background to follow along. Grades based on short essays, so how well you can explain theories is as important as your understanding.

Professor Audi is a fantastic person and was always willing to provide feedback to students. However, he was an unfocused lecturer, which made learning impossible. In addition, the TA's were ridiculously harsh, which made it difficult for anyone to do well. If you need structure to succeed, do yourself a favor and do not take this class.

Audi is a great guy and always willing to discuss content or assignments. The material can be a bit scattered, but as long as you look at the slides and ask questions when you have them, it's not too hard to keep up with. I recommend sending in papers in advance for feedback. "Required" readings aren't that necessary.
Audi can be a bit disorganized but he really is well informed on the material and genuinely cares about his students.

Professor Audi is definitely knowledgable on philosophical issues and does a good job explaining a variety of perspectives. One of his strengths (which is unique among philosophers) is that Audi does very well exploring positions he disagrees with as well as those that are more familiar.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Seriously, this Professor is the worst Professor I have ever encountered in my college life. He has the worst lecture because he don't prepare anything before class. His worst part is his grading. All the grades come from exams and essays, they are graded very subjective by TA instead of him, if you ask about your work he will just let u talk toTA

Professor Audi is actually a chill guy. I took a class with him during my first year in College. It was an incredible journey for me that began with a difficult start of the semester due to how philosohical and critical the class is. His office hours are helpful, and he even allowed students to redo their papers if they did not perform well.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Professor Audi is a true philosophy fanatic. His knowledge on the topics he's teaching is extensive and it shows. He also is extremely empathetic to his students and it allows him to better connect with the class as a whole. I would recommend to anyone to take his class. Lectures are hysterical as long as you do the reading.

He's kiiiiiind of a mess - lectures are all over the place. But that's totally OK, given how much material the course needs to cover, there's time for it. I enjoyed going to class and participating, but a lot of students never went to lecture and still had no trouble getting As on the exams. There's a lot of extra credit anyway.

Audi cares a lot about his students. Classes can occasionally get a bit dry, but he has become one of my favorite professors I have ever had. Very intriguing concepts and he is absolutely hilarious. I had no interest in philosophy before this course, and I am now considering majoring in philosophy thanks to him. REALLY cares for all of his students

Had him for two classes: 101 & 110. He is actually a pretty good professor, but a lot of his lectures are disorganized. I'm personally pretty terrible at attending lectures, so I end up reading more by myself--and I got an A in both classes. Not hard to get an A if you take the time to learn the material. Also, he's hilarious and very approachable.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: His lectures are so boring, he's even a worse lecturer than the TA. But the tests were super easy, just read the study guide before exams and don't go to class or read, you can get an A.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He is a bit of a scattered professor type. His thoughts seem disorganized and they are poorly conveyed to students. His lectures don't make sense a lot of the time. Graded by 2 papers, a midterm, and a final.

Professor Audi is a super friendly and easy-going guy with a genuine interest in the material he teaches. If you enjoy philosophy then you will really enjoy his class, because no subject is off-limits.   The one down-side is he is so interested in the subject that he can get sidetracked easily, so sometimes lectures get a bit scattered.

An average class with a friendly instructor. The content is fairly straightforward, but it felt a bit standard for the price of tuition. It's fine if you need the requirement, but otherwise quite forgettable.

A little overdue but here goes. She is approachable and helpful with papers, but the course was dry and uninspiring, with minimal exam prep, and I didn't learn anything new. Overall, it felt like a waste of time—I wouldn't take it again.

As long as you do the readings and come to class, you'll do fine. It's not my favorite class in the whole world, but it's not the worst either. She's a super cool and fun lady and even though the subject isn't something that I am personally interested in, the class was still okay in my book.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: One of the only professors I took at UR that was willing to meet with me outside of class, and answer emails. She cares about helping students succeed, and prepares interesting reading and class sessions.

Although Professor Mannheimer can be a tough grader, if you go to her for help, she is more than willing to give you feedback and help you improve your performance in the class. As long as you are willing to put forth effort and genuine interest , taking a class with her would be very beneficial. She was very helpful with papers.
She's okay, sometimes class tended to be boring, not much preparation for the midterm or final.  She's really cute though.
I took her class on Jane Austen. Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic. The class was not demanding, just two essays and two midterms. Also, cute as hell.
Mannheimer has to be one of the most enthusiastic and bubbly professors I've ever met. She's great.

His lectures are quite fun, and he's genuinely an entertaining professor, and can teach well. My main complaint is that the lectures are often very repetitive of some topics, and then speed through other topics much too quickly. The exams themselves are also generally not that easy, but due to the grading scheme of the class it's completely fine.
Dr H is my guy! Engaging lectures, plenty of extra credit/point opportunities (that algebra quiz was light-work), and GREAT sense of humor (6-7). Would recommend.
Dr. H is an amazing person, very approachable, and very accommodating. Even if you don't like his teaching, you should appreciate his personality!

One of the worst professors I have ever had. He does not respond to emails, cancels office hours, is very UNACCESIBLE outside of lecture, never updates the course materials, and just sucks at teaching.
Dr. H is a nice guy but he writes on the chalkboard the whole time and never posts slides or recordings. His tests are badly written and hard to study for. He made me crash out.
if you're pre med either switch career goals or transfer, NOT GOOD
Expect to learn little in lecture compared to the practice problems and workshops provided. Then proceed to have the practice problems and workshops provided not be related to the exam.
shiny bald head makes me cry
he sucks and lies about what's gonna be on the exam. Good luck

Engaging lectures/office hours. Difficult to study independently. We got no workshop keys, reactions list, or past exams, and homework was reduced by half. Content was also shuffled so it didn't line up with the course lab. Like a math class without problem sets: all concepts, no practice. The material is a lot of fun! I hope 204 is more rewarding.

He is a caring and funny professor, however his teaching is just not it. He oversimplifies so much to try to make orgo easy to understanding (which is good to an extent), but he will make exams so hard. Workshops do help, however I wish he would spend more time in lecture on test-level content.

*Chem 203* Dr. H explains concepts well, but for me they were sometimes a bit too surface level. Workshops go more in-depth and are very helpful. The content order could be better, leading to early concepts being harder than necessary. The “Orgo as a 2nd Language” textbook helps a lot. Make sure to attend workshops consistently.

~CHEM 203~ Great guy, I enjoyed going to lecture (at least compared to other professors as a STEM major - I'm looking at you Fall 2025 BIO198 professor). However, tests are quite hard and lecture content is pretty surface level so there is a lot of self-learning in this class. Workshop helps, OH format kind of stinks. Hard class but its worth it.

He is super caring, engaging, and a great professor overall. However, the class format can be frustrating. There is no curve and exams feel different from homework. He explains concepts well but sometimes jumps topics and doesn't teach linearly.

You will learn the most from the workshops than anything else. It is a difficult class, and his presentation of certain ideas usually need a YouTube video to fully understand. A good guy overall, but this class is hell, the exam averages are low so be prepared.

Awesome lecturer and brings a very personable approach to instructing. The exams are difficult but fair. The grades are moved to ensure fair grading, and you always know what you need to do to get an A. Has MANY office hours, which are helpful but usually full

I wouldn't recommend taking Hafensteiner for upper-level chemistry courses. His lectures often lack clear explanations and feel disorganized, which makes it difficult to grasp complex concepts. Key material is sometimes glossed over or presented unclearly, leaving students to teach themselves outside of class in order to keep up.

Overall, the class was fine, I got the grade I got bc I didn't show up to my workshops or really do the hw. The first exam was quite easy, but after that, the exams became a lot harder. He tends not to be that organized in his lectures and kinda jumps back and forth. Go to class, workshops, and do the hw and you'll be fine.

The most kind professor I have had the pleasure of learning from. He does not make Orgo II easy, but he wants you to succeed and makes himself available outside classes. If you go to office hours and stay on top of workshop, everything will start to make sense.

I didn't find his class to be amazing, but I learned a solid amount and he's clearly a good and thoughtful professor. He puts in effort, seems to actually care about his students, and honestly my issues stem mostly from the class itself not his teaching style.
Awful......

Lectures are very organized and he highlights the main concepts well. Lecture is definitely the most important aspect of the course. Workshop questions are difficult and only some are helpful. Tests are very challenging and contain much harder examples of the concepts learned in class. Overall, harder than CHEM 203 but lectures are more helpful.

I was shocked to see some of these bad ratings. Dr. H is a caring professor who genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He made a lecture recording request form to encourage attendance, which was a little annoying. Yes this class was challenging but that is because it is Orgo 2, its a challenging course anywhere you go.

Dr. H is a friendly, chill dude. His lectures are good, though they can feel fast paced at times and are necessary to rewatch. His exams are mostly fair but always have a few problems that catch you off guard with their difficulty. Make sure you don't fall behind with the content, make connections between concepts, and do the HW for easy points.

GOAT for 131, good at answering questions in lecture, blackboard+chalk notes so you can take written notes, gives 5 chances for aktiv questions, hard exams with extra credit question that requires spamming past exams to get high score, optional attendance but no ppt only recording, though textbook becomes unnecessary if you focus during lecture.

Dr H's lectures were very unorganized and hard to follow. He drags on and only teaches in examples. However, his office hours (if you can fit it in your schedule he usually only has 1-2 hours per week in the middle of the day) and workshops are helpful. The grading was pretty lenient, but the second half of the class was much harder.
He had really good lectures and was always available if you needed help outside of class. I've always struggled with chem but this class was very good and prepared me for the exams.
Recommended for everyone who want to take chem131, his office hour is also very helpful.

Although this is the intro to chemistry, it was still an entertaining class. All lectures were recorded, and you didn't have to pay for the textbook since it was online, but you did need to pay for the software for homework. Grading was a points system that I really enjoyed and it was a surprisingly good course to learn the basics of chemistry.
As someone who took ap chem I still struggled a little with this course. Do the practice tests because what he teaches in lecture is only the basis.
slow lectures. however great for someone who has never seen chem before. tests were fair. easy A if you do the work.

Dr. H's lectures can sometimes be confusing and tedious, but there are resources outside of lecture that help a lot. His office hours were great and really helped my understanding. Test difficulty is somewhere between the Aktiv homework (easy) and workshop problems (hard) so I would recommend keeping up on those if you're struggling.

Dr. H's lectures are super hard to follow and for me, useless. If you're really struggling in the class I would attend office hours and pay attention during workshops. He does want you to succeed and will help when prompted, but going to lectures alone probably won't help you—they're all over the place. I had to teach myself a lot of basic content.
he is a nice professor. the content is easy just focus on workshops. class is a bit disorganized and confusing. wayyyy better than other chem professors
The best professor I ever had.

He is a great guy. Super nice and charming. However, lectures are confusing and hard to follow. He basically does math problems on the board for an hour and 20 minutes and half-heartedly explains why he does what he does. He gives lots of points and really wants you to pass, but the style of teaching just wont work for everyone

As someone who came from only taking one chemistry honors course during the pandemic, I would say Hafensteiner didn't help me the most as I transitioned into college-level chemistry, as he wasn't clear on concepts and was scattered. I guess the point system was a redeeming factor in his class. Does talk about his kids a lot.

Dr. H is funny and engaging but his lectures are a bit scattered, so going to workshops really mattered. Either way TAs grade very nicely (lots of partial credit) and Dr. H and TAs are available through office hours often. Did not regularly attend lectures and still didn't even need to take the final to get an A (but you have to take the final)

Professor H is a friendly guy, but his teaching style can be hit or miss. While lectures may lack organization, workshops and past exams are key for succeeding. Leveraging resources like Unstuck ai alongside the textbook can make this course manageable.

Dr. H is a good professor for 131, but for 204, he's not very good. Orgo is complicated and having a prof with good organization is essential. His lectures are poorly organized and jump around. Compared to Prof. Dinnocenzo, his class is confusing and requires a LOT more memorization. Learn how to do mechanisms solo because he doesn't explain them.

Yea Dr. H doesn't seem like a great prof during the course however, compared to Matson and Knowles (CHEM132) he is amazing. The class is very easy to get an A in with the amount of extra credit and simple concepts. Dr. H goes on annoying tangents about his daughters and does not use slides so you have to take your own notes. Ok prof.

Dr. H is super friendly and willing to answer questions, which often makes lectures feel like office hours. If you have a background in AP chem, you're set. He explains concepts decently well but they could be better. However, Dr. H is very willing to help you out during office hours.

Honestly if you took AP Chem within the past 2 years you will be fine. Class is on the point system, which if you play your cards right, you might only need a 20% on the final to end with an A. If you're confused in lecture, I would recommend reading the textbook, doing past exams and definitely going to workshop.

Dr. H seems to be a genuinely kind and passionate person who wants his students to succeed. However, his teaching style is not for everyone. What he covers in lectures is very different from the types of problems that you are given on tests. I'd say the most helpful things were workshops and past exams. Study and connect concepts outside of class.

This class is the reason I changed majors. It was hard for a gen chem, especially because I have no chemistry background. It had workshops that were helpful to an extent, labs that I enjoyed, and homework (Aktiv) that you had to pay to use. Lectures didn't apply too much to tests, workshops were better for studying. Funny guy tho!

Dr. H, at heart, is a good person. Lectures are funny and he is accessible outside of class. However, I struggled in his class. His lectures can be hard to follow, so put in the time outside of class to understand the material. I walked out with an A which was mainly a result of doing really well on the final and teaching myself material.

Dont get me wrong. Dr. H is a wonderful person. However, I do feel that his lectures could use a bit more organization since a lot of the time, I found it hard to follow. I recommend to study at least every time you open the textbook. Other than that, this class is very doable and can even be cheesed if you're satisfied with a B.
