Very fun professor, likes to tell stories about cases he's handled.

Awesome Class...Awesome Prof...hes an adjuct lawyer who teaches only in the spring, but his class is hands down one of the best here at the university...even if your not into poli sci/law, take it to learn your rights...he loves to talk about crack dealer

Fiandach is funny, sweet, and entertaining.  His charm and charisma keeps every class really interesting.  Taking his class will teach you a lot about being a lawyer, especially how to think as a lawyer.
Doug is very accessible outside of class for help.  He cared about the success of his students as well.  The class material was very dull IMO.

I had Kelley for 246 (Junior Lab) and 255 (Senior Design), and I can honestly say he is one of the best professors currently in the department as of Spring 2018. While I feel he unfairly misinterpreted my junior lab report, he is extremely knowledgeable and caring and was able to help every senior design group regardless of their topic.

Visit him outside class for help- his office hours have 5-6 students at a time before an exam. He'll really try to help. The class is quite difficult, the curves are dramatic, he's soft-spoken so it's hard to hear in the middle and back rows. He has a really laid-back attitude though so I didn't feel intimidated at all.

Had Hopper for MATH 141, not 165. Hopper was excellent. His lectures were straightforward and it was easy to understand the content. It definitely helps if you took calc in high school though. I just wish they had a curve in 141, but other than that, no complaints really.

BEST professor ever. I took 141 and wished he taught 142. Lectures/notes are VERY clear; he is amazing at teaching. He helped me understand concepts I struggled w in HS for the longest time. Exams are easy, as long as you do at least 2 practice exams, since they're exactly like the real exams. If you have Qs, he will help you until you understand.
one of the best professors in this university. great handouts. lectures are so clear that I don't even have to review after class. sure would take his class again.

Prof. Hopper is amazing. MATH 235 is an extremely hard subject. His homework is very very hard and time consuming, probably gonna take you over 15 hours per week. This can be stress out but you really learn the stuff. His exams are hard, but way easier than HW. He is a nice grader so don't worry about your raw score. The most caring prof I've met

The most difficult course I have ever had at this Uni. It is difficult because the course materials get so wide and don't go too deeply, and TONS of homework go deeply. The exam is freaking hard; He doesn't make even a single problem similar to the past exams or the homework. 

DON'T TAKE IT. (EVEN NOW I AM STRUGGLING WITH THE HOMEWORK.)
One of the best Math professors at U of R. Lectures are super clear and organized. Go to his office hours.

Eric is easily one of the best professor I've had in this university so far, and I'm sure he will stay in my tops. He makes really good handouts and give them out before classes. Lecture is super clear and understandable. If you go to his office hours, he will clarify things for you and explain them patiently. Try your best to register his section!

Professor Flores gives great and unique lectures on American cultural history. He assigned compelling essays and texts that enriched the classroom experience. He expects consistent participation from the class and will try to draw out responses from you. Overall, an enjoyable, easy enough class that offered interesting content.

This man is an amazing professor. The history of Mexico class I took with him was just amazing. He is super knowledgeable about US-Mexico relationships, and very enthusiastic to share. I loved that he was able to talk and actually answer all of our questions about it. He bases his grades on papers you can submit as many times as youd like.
She's interested in what she is teaching. Tested on concepts and not on knowing every minute detail of a pathway. Was approachable and willing to help.

Lectures were straightforward. Tested on material she covered in class and material she had hinted would be important to know. Was genuinely helpful in class. Attempted to keep things simple and seemed to care whether students understood the lectures or not.

Dr. Balakrishnan is an amazing teacher. She delivers her material with clarity and constantly reiterates what she expects the students to know from her lectures. Though, lots of independent reading associated with this class.
makes an effort to actually teach!

CAD is easy, but it is still college and effort is needed. Go to lectures and do not be shy with the TAs. Make sure to always check over work because they get you for little things and most assignments are worth a few points and it will add up quickly. Get workshops and homeworks checked by TAs. Test can be challenging so do some studying for them.

Prof. Ronald is a wonderful professor, able to teach CAD in a very good way regardless if you have previous experience in CAD. If you make sure to do all the homework and workshop assignments, a good grade is almost guaranteed.

Really chill guy. He's one of the more human professors you'll have (probably because he's technically not a professor). He cancelled a workshop once because everyone had a thermo exam. It's harder to be independent in this class compared to others if you don't have CAD experience, so prepare to be comfortable asking questions to TAs or friends

Taking a course as part of a cluster and with no context or experience for engineering otherwise. Professor Ronald's lectures are clear and easy to understand, and he takes the time for all the students to understand the content and catch up.
Professor Ronald is a nice dude and makes the class enjoyable and gets the basics of CAD down.
Professor Ronald is so caring and nice, he makes the heavy courseload bearable and is so down to earth.
Really a nice professor! A really kind person and easy to reach out. He explained the points in the lecture pretty well with some good examples. I will definitely take his course again!

He's really nice and understanding. The material he teaches is clearly related to the exam. He also gives practice exams which are basically all you need to know before a midterm. One of the best professors ever!

comment: Really nice guy, super helpful and personable. Don't skip lectures, because they're only once a week, but if you need to miss one he will help you figure it out. I had this class during corona and he was awesome and understanding.

comment: Great class!

He is good at explaining class material and he walks you through the processes of how to use CAD. He has a group of TAs that are in every class to help students whenever they have a question about the material. However, he is not really accessible through email. He did not respond on a timely manner to any emails I have sent him.
not very responsive to email

Prof. Ronald is an amazing teacher. He really tried to help his students understand the material and how it will relate in our work as engineers in the future. He was always available by email and in person to answer questions. One of my favorite professors so far at UofR.

Ronald is a great teacher and a super genuine guy. He makes the material pretty easy and enjoyable to learn.  He also ordered us a pizza during the middle of the final, if that gives any indication of what kind of person and professor he is.  Honestly probably my favorite professor yet, Ronald is awesome. Definitely take his classes!
He is one of the best professors i have had so far. He is helpful, approachable and his classes are always interesting.
One of the best professors I have had thus far. Does a great job explaining the material. Very accessible, approachable, and entertaining, as well as a fantastic teacher.

Ronald knows his stuff.  He is an actual engineer with a real world job so he makes his lectures much more applicable to the outside world.  He has a thorough understanding of the concepts and will make sure you do too.

smart guy who knows his stuff but he doesnt forget that he is teaching, not just reciting, wants you t do well and will work with you to help you, not just say it.

claims to be a really easy professor but that isn't actually the case, though the class is still very manageable. truly cares about students' success, and along those lines sometimes bends his grading rules to help your final grade. he's really cool (and smart!) as well. fall statics is a small class so he likes to keep a casual atmosphere as well.

Ronald is the man ... he's a great teacher, and he can make the most complicated concepts understandable. He's funny, considerate, and interested in his students' success. He's part-time but if you have a chance to take one of his classes, you should.

He never gives clear instructions on anything. Instructions might be changed without notice, or contradict each other. Also, this 2-credit lab has a low-weight final exam scheduled on the very last day of finals week.
"What do you think?"

Maybe he is a good researcher, but not a good professor. He is a little bit disorganized. Every time you ask him a question, he wants to tell you everything he knows, but without key points. Bad professor

comment: This semester he taught hybrid and made it clear that none of us would fail. He really just wanted us to learn one thing. He was super kind, understanding, and was willing to give extensions to us. His classes are difficult, but he is willing to help you succeed.

Jim is a great guy. When taking his class it really is a you get what you put in type of thing. He will spend all day with you if you don't understand something but you have to ask him questions. His notes are sometimes not helpful. But he believes that learning is a process and curves.

I had Jimmy Z for a class a while ago, and I found that any affection he had for his students gets masked behind a layer of talking down. He is a nice guy, but the kind who is so much smarter than us that he is hard to relate to.
Jim's a great guy but a poor lecturer.  He gets off topic too easily and has trouble getting back to task.  His work on the blackboard could use practice as well.

Zavislan is a great guy & not boring, BUT his notes r not too helpful, he doesn't show many (helpful) examples, no previous hwks, his responses r vague & he ends up rambling about something completely different. his lectures r either way to over my head or not good. i'm struggling a lot in this class! while doing fine in the rest of my classes
he's a cool prof.
He knows everything about geometrical optics, and makes you work hard to learn it for yourself. When you succeed, you feel completely rewarded.

For some students the material comes easily and for many it doesn't. Either way, Zavislan is willing to spend a LOT of time making sure you understand.  It's just up to you to schedule an appointment.
Explains things in a coherent manner
Hahaha, yeah, Jim IS good at life
He doesnt write on the board so you have to pay attention in his lectures.  Its a very tough class if your used to learning off of notes.
Jim is good at life
No Comments

Absolutely amazing professor. Kind, funny, and enthusiastic. I love that she always comes to class ready to learn and adjusts to the class's abilities instantly. I enjoyed my time and always found extra help and practice to be available.

Moves fast through the alphabet so can be hard for those who did't go to Hebrew school as a kid, but Michela will work with you if you seek help. Other than that, super easy. Show up, pay attention and you'll do great. HW takes 10-15 min max. She is also great and has fun joking around with the class.

Michela is a caring, charismatic professor. Her lectures are very smooth as she makes sure everyone in the class understands what is being taught in an efficient way. Very accessible outside of the class and always eager to help you. Hebrew is not an easy language to learn but her pedagogy makes it very easy for students to get a grasp of it.

Michela is an incredible woman and professor. She really cares about the students and Hebrew, and is very good at explaining concepts and teaching in general. The class can be a bit slow if you know any Hebrew, but picks up around the second half of the semester.  If you have interest in Hebrew, definitely take this class, it's great.

Such a doll.. Probably funnier than most of my friends, extremely nice, very clear with assignments/exams, very down-to-earth, etc.. I can't think of anything bad to say. Lectures can be a bit boring if you're familiar with Hebrew, as we mostly just work right through the book, page by page.

She has an Italian accent but she's still very understandable. She's extremely nice (once you realize that "pay attention" means she's about to say something important, not that she's accusing you of slacking off), clear, and knows her stuff. She adjusts her teaching to students; she's made handouts based on things we asked about the class before.
Great professor. Loves engaging with his students. You learn a lot about your writing. If you ever have the chance, take his course!
Prof is a little weird but chill
Really cares about the students. Very kind and funny guy.

Prof. Hansen is definitely one of the best professors I've had at UR. I was nervous about sharing my work going into the class but he makes sure that the environment is kind and constructive. He's also a really fascinating person and is just inspiring to be around. Highly recommend taking English 121 with him.
I love David and I think he is an incredible professor especially at the introductory level. Would HIGHLY recommend taking his course. My only note is perhaps teach in warmer rooms.

David is everything you want in a creative writing professor. Chill guy. Very helpful feedback on work, always has interesting things to say. Fosters a welcoming class environment. Workload is minimal, workshops excellent. Assigned readings aren't too memorable compared to the workshop stories though. Regardless, I strongly recommend him to anyone.

By far one of the best professors I've ever taken. He's very insightful and gives excellent feedback on your writing. The readings only last a few weeks before you begin writing your own fiction. Workshops might seem scary, but he makes sure everyone is respectful and engaging, so it's more fun than anything. If you get the chance, take his class!

Provides the perfect atmosphere for an introductory creative writing course. The workshop aspect of this class might be intimidating, but he ensures that your stories are discussed in a productive and respectful manner. Highly recommend.

David's great! He facilitates student discussion really well and makes sure everyone's voices are heard. There's a couple short stories to read a week, but the workload is VERY manageable and he gives plenty of time for writing assignments. When work is being workshopped in class, the discussion is always very respectful. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Without a doubt one of the best professors I've ever had. If you ever have the opportunity to be in one of his sections I would absolutely take it.
Best course taken by far at the university.

Took it last semester; even in an online setting, he made sure everyone got the chance to contribute and created a very open and non-judgmental environment. Made me cry in workshop lol but he really thought he was complimenting my story.

He's a great professor! In online class, he made sure that everyone felt heard and that people were able to speak about the readings we did. Also, the readings were only for about the first two weeks in this class, before you started writing 5-page minimum (double spaced) stories (fiction). After we critiqued each other's stories and it was fun!

He's a great teacher--writes a ton of helpful feedback, funny, approachable, brings SNACKS to class. If anything he's too nice. He seemed to genuinely care about everyone in the class and was always encouraging and kind I highly recommend taking a class with him if you can, it's a blast and you'll learn a lot.

Loved having professor hansen for eng121, he always made our entire class laugh and still have great discussions on the stories we were reading, whether they were published or during the workshop. Highly recommend!!

It is very clear that Covach loves what he teaches, and that makes every lecture better. However the three exams are the only grades for the course, but he is willing to work with you to improve your grade.

Prof. Covach was a true rock n roller. Very knowledgeable of rock music and its history. Classes are very interesting if you like the Beatles. The quizzes do get a bit annoying (about 1 quiz every 2 weeks) and are mostly trivial stuff like identifying songs and memorizing facts; writing section was graded very generously. Still worth taking, tho!

Professor Covach is a wonderful professor, and his lectures are very interesting. However, his tests are ALL memorization and you will be spending HOURS brute-force memorizing useless information that you won't remember a week after. His test questions are often worded very vaguely and looking for overly-specific answers. Great lecturer awful tests

Taken 125/130/131, all fairly easy. Exams are fill in the blanks, a listening portion (name the song/release date/album/band depending on the class) that's around 5 songs (out of ~30 supposed to know but fine if you don't as long as rest of exam good), and short essay questions. Pay attention, focus on slide content, big ideas, and connections.

His exams are easy, yes he talks a lot in class but because he's passionate about what he teaches so he gives a lot of background and details that are unnecessary for tests. Interesting to hear/learn about but if you don't care you could honestly zone out, the key: pay attention when he talks about things directly on or related to the slides.

Lectures are usually interesting, with stories, anecdotes, etc. Sometimes they get a tad boring but usually not. The tests are almost entirely memorization based, but everything you need to know is in the lecture slides. Professor Covach is a cool guy, very responsive to email and student concerns, and offers extra credit opportunities that help.

Professor Covach is a very enthusiastic and engaging lecturer and I thoroughly enjoyed his Beatles class. The quizzes are definitely memorization heavy, but are definitely fair and not to difficult if you pay attention in class and study.

Super kind and genuinely cares about all of his students. Takes time to make sure each student understands and very accommodating for extra help. He teaches using interesting examples to make the theory more engaging. Homework is graded just on participation, and as long as you go to class and study for the midterms, you will do great.
dont take this class

Instead of focusing on the main points gone over by the lectures, the quizzes went over trivial facts that do not impact music or the class in general (Beatles year of birth, month an album was released). The lectures barely focus on these facts and consist of tangents about specific songs. Less teaching and more showing off how much he knows.

Covach is a great storyteller who cares about his students. His tests and listening quizes require a fair bit of studying, but he gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Papers are graded by the TA and are an easy A if you use the ppts. Tests are difficult and require trivia-level knowledge of minute details
great!! loved his lectures, learned a lot. very easy to understand.

Easiest class EVER, and fun! (Rock music in the 1970s)... definite GPA booster while listening to awesome music. Tests are trivial but questions come directly from lectures which are posted online, attendance is not necessary but you'll miss out on some great lectures.

I thought the class was a good general course to take, but it just talked about the major happenings and didn't really increase my knowledge...the tests are essentially trivia questions and aren't really reflective of the main topics of the lectures.
No Comments

Had Covach for Theory III and Beatles - absolutely AMAZING prof. Loved every class and learned a ton, fantastic lecturer, genius, grades a little tough but completely fair. A definite highlight of my college career!
Very helpful class. Great Professor.
This prof is organized. He gives out copies of his notes, which is very helpful. They should make him teach more graduate courses!
knows what he is talking about, is very organized, requires a lot of work but you learn a lot too. best professor in ECE.

Basically recites what is in the textbook (which itself isn't the most clear) but in a less clear way. Macro is hard and she somehow makes it harder. Homework and exam questions are a huge leap above what is taught.

If you value your time or sanity do not take this class. Yena Park is easily the departments poorest professor. She is not good at explaining concepts and rushes through things in class. The exams are very difficult and she does not do a good job of preparing students to do well on exams. I'm not even sure why she got hired. Bad teacher all around.
Get ready to teach yourself everything you need to know.
- Lectures are very boring.  - Doesn't encourage class participation. Almost never pauses for questions.  - Almost never looks at the students to see if anyone's raised their hand.
Poor Lecturer. Very heavy accent makes it hard to understand. Little to no Explanation of topics. Misunderstands questions all the time. Avoid her as a professor at all costs.
Very poor lecturing. Gives almost no explanation to anything, explanation that she does give is poorly worded.

I can't believe the U of R takes themselves seriously with Yena Park on staff. She can barely speak English, is horrible at explaining concepts, doesn't adequately answer questions, and is hard to access after class (1 hour office hours per week). It sucks you can't always avoid her with 209, but, if you can, please do.

Dr. Kennedy is very organized, but can be picky about small things (you won't get any credit for the problem set if you don't assign pages in gradescope). Reading the textbook isn't required and there is a lot of extra credit.
Almost no way to receive high points on assignments. Always picky about some minor irrelevant stuff to have points off. Boring lectures that are not helpful at all for the homework.
Picky about wording. If you got one word wrong, even though you were right, you won't get full points
Very clear and organized lectures, and readily available outside of class. Exams are difficult, but points system makes it possible to get a good grade. Problem sets and exams are well written.

Very nice and organized. A good teacher but exams are really tough. Almost everything is graded on correctness. Points system makes it possible to do well in the class even if you don't do well on exams. Her notes are clear so there's no need to read the textbook. Professor Clark is honestly the best BIO teacher I've ever had. He is the Sheldon Cooper of the BIO Dept.,  and his office hours are very helpful (GO TO THEM!!!).

Clark was one of my favorite teachers this year, he clearly cares about the subject he teaches and tries to make it interesting for students. The lectures can get kind of dry, a lot of reading off of power points, but they're still interesting. He's very clear, and won't try to trick you on tests.

Dr. Clark is an amazing professor! He isn't the easiest professor to approach, but his crisp clear lectures make up for it. His presentation slides are the best I have seen.  He is very clear about what to expect on the exams. Take biochem with him over the summer and it'll be worth your while!

Dr. Clark is one of the best professors at Rochester. Tests are tough, but you will learn a lot in his class. His passion for biology is apparent in all that he does and his excitement is contagious. Great class.
Dr. Clark is a great lecturer. He is hilarious, friendly, and always in a good mood to help. I wish he offered more classes.
Clark's passion for biology is infectious. Overall amazing professor
Clark is a great lecturer. Great lectures, sorta difficult tests.

Clark's class was good. If you pay attention to him in class you will do well in the class. His lecture slides are great if you miss a class but him speaking in class is definitely way better, he really knows the subject and communicates the important parts well. Textbook was a waste of money because he is such a good lecturer.
Only class I never miss because it is both interesting and helpful. Clark is a great lecturer and keeps me interested in the subject.
He is amazing! very funny and very clear!

He reminds everyone of Sheldon Cooper. Seriously he is really helpful. He explains concepts very well. He has discussions with the class. He really makes you think about the reasons why things happen. Great professor.

Best lecture slides I've seen thus far. He is really enthusiastic about the material and explains things so well. Take his class in the summer if u can. My class had 11 students this summer, going to class was fun and the material was soo interesting. I'd be surprised if anyone got less than a B

Clark's class was unbelievably interesting. He tries so hard to apply what he teaches into life and medicine. I loved going to class, and he is adorable. His exams are pretty tough though. Memorize anything and everything he tells you in lecture - and believe me that's a LOT. The curve is nice, I expected a B but got an A-!

There is a TON of material that must be MEMORIZED to succeed in this class. Covers majority of it in lecture slides, but some random terms and definitions are only in the book. Good lecturer, can be unclear or assume concepts are simpler than they are at time.  Midterms are doable if you study, but tough.  The 300 pt cummulative final is BRUTAL.

Dr. Clark is a great professor. His lectures are interesting yet concise. The material that he teaches can be difficult to understand but after reading through his powerpoint again is manageable. His tests are definetly hard. And one of his downsides is that you never really know what grade you have in his class until the end of the semeseter.

Clark is a quirky and charming professor who is often nicknamed "Sheldon" (from The Big Bang Theory) across dinner tables. His lectures are evenly spaced and difficult concepts well-explained, but his lectures also tend to be long, dry, and occasionally coma-inducing. Exams are very difficult - lecture and workshop attendance is a must.

I have mixed feelings about Clark. On one hand he is a great lecturer and makes the topics interesting. On the other hand, even though he claims his tests are not all memorization, they are. Definitely a challenging course.

Clark pops into the lab occassionally, which is pretty great considering most lab instructors could care less about checking on their students.  The lab manuals are pretty well written and the techniques you learn/use are actually relevant to modern research. Two big write-ups are long and tedious. Practical and other assignments are easy.

Clark is very full of himself and only accepts the answers he has in his head. The tests are extremely hard and it seemed like all the points on multiple part questions went to the most minor detail. He does not know how to curve, and has a preset class average prior to even administering the exams. If you're thinking of taking BIO 112, just don't.

Definitely one of my favorite professors this term. Incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He is also very helpful in office hours. His tests are challenging, but they really encourage you to think critically apply the concepts taught in class experimentally. For me, it was helpful to review his lecture notes right after class.

Genetics lab was incredibly educational. His labs teach you useful, real techniques and the class is designed so that you aren't mindlessly following a procedure, but so that you understand what you're doing. Lab manuals are occasionally poorly written, but the TA knows what's up no it's not a big deal. Curves the class to a B.

Clark is quirky and funny, and lectures are clear and for the most part, interesting. But his exams were extremely difficult, long, and to some extent unfair. The exams are difficult, and you really do have to work hard to get a good grade. Do not take this class lightly and make it one of your top priorities.

Dr. Clark is a solid professor and I would definitely recommend him. Although his lectures are a little long, they are fairly easy to understand. Tests are tough but fair, keep up with lecture notes and readings and you should be fine
He's a rather mediocre professor. He tries to be helpful with office hours but is unclear and confusing. His tests aren't bad. I just didn't like his style of teaching.

Dr.Clark is a very smart and nice professor. Biochem is not easy! Definitely attend his class cuz he mentions all the important points which will all in the exams. I didn't do really well in this class but it's my own problem not Dr.Clark's. I really enjoy this class and learn a ton! Office hour really helps and he is very approachable! Best ever!

Professor is a little awkward, but he's actually really funny and nice.  Lectures are dense but all the slides are online.   Biggest advice is keep up with material, it's impossible to learn it all right before the test. I've never gotten below an A- in any class ever, but I got a B- because I didn't keep up with lectures.  My fault, not Clarks.

He's a pretty good professor. Lectures are long and dense, but this basically means there's never something on the test that wasn't mentioned. Take good notes, don't just study slides. Tests are hard, but he knows it's a tough class and the curve is nice at the end. Overall, a great class. You learn a TON. He's a nice guy too.

He is a pretty good professor. His lectures are clear, if a little dense, and cover everything on the tests. Tests can be tricky, though. He is also very helpful in office hours. Don't worry too much about the bad reviews from earlier - he was still a new prof. He has clearly gotten the hang of how to organize good lectures and teach well.

He is very clear about what will be on the exam, but make sure you take note of questions asked orally in class or questions on lecture slides. Lectures are long but are good study tools. Office hours are also very beneficial because questions asked during office hours might come up on exams.

He is a good professor. Not amazing, but good. The class is tough with a ton of material to learn, but it's all in his lectures and he's helpful at office hours. I came in thinking I could breeze it because I did well it a tough AP Bio class and got a 5 w/out much work. WRONG. So for you smarties, put in some effort. But really, study and you're ok

It's a tough class and you really have to know your stuff for the tests, but everything is in his lectures. He lectures from power points and sometimes doesn't finish them, but posts all of his lectures online and will finish the material at the next class. Take detailed notes. He curves at the end so you'll probably do better than you think.

Clark is crazy smart, but he is not a great lecturer. He's awkward, but very approachable.  Lectures are way too long, and the slides tend to have so much on them that they're overwhelming. Pretty rough for an intro class, a lot of hardcore biochem.  Exams are NOT easy, you will have to study A TON to do well.

Lectures are awful. Each topic is rushed through in 4 or 5 slides, and Clark never finishes his absurdly long powerpoints. Exams cover only powerpoint materials, but the slides are poor to the point of indecipherability. Your only chance of getting a respectable grade is to review in workshops and in office hours.

He has a lot to improve but I'm sure he'll do better with a few years of lecturing under his belt. Memorize EVERYTHING because he will put anything and everything on a test. He looks like Sheldon from the Big Bang Theory

Clark is a new professor so he's still learning how to present material efficiently and clearly. He isn't bad but he needs a bit of experience with his lectures. His PowerPoints tend to be a little too long, so he usually has to rush through the last 15 slides or so. Biochem is really tough; he's apparently helpful at office hours though.

He can be a bit awkward, but he's a nice guy. His tests are very hard, but the answers are always in the lectures - missing a lecture WILL hurt as making sense out of the slides isn't that easy. He's certainly approachable, but it may take a little bit to get the answer you need. Office hours are helpful, but crowded.

The key to succeeding in this class is memorizing powerpoint slides. Also, piecing them together into an understanding of the bigger picture. Clark is awkward and not very helpful. He is new though, and he has to live up to the name of the great Terry Platt. Exams are hard, and the fact that he doesn't give enough time makes them harder. Work hard.
He is mostly good.   Tests are hard, but only covered lecture material. Office hours help simplify things.

Exams come from slides- Memorize them. MUST go to office hours to do well on exams. Very helpful during office hours - ask questions! Lectures are often long and tedious but he is smart. He's so awkward that it's funny. You have to put in lots of time to make sure you understand concepts - Loves it when you "appreciate" the "big picture".

He's a new professor. It's apparent that he does need more time to improve, but everyone does. His review sessions are extremely helpful. You will not complain about him if you don't keep facebooking and texting in the class. Good person and good professor.
It's obvious that he's never taught before.  There is no cohesion in the material and he over-complicates things.  Office hours do help somewhat, but he's often too busy helping other students.

(For Contemporary African Poilitics) Professor Harding isn't a super easy A, but he has clear, organized lectures that build on concepts each week. The readings and lectures go together really well, but even if you read you really should go to class. He is very knowledgeable about the ideas and clearly interested in them which shines through.

Professor Smith is very kind and passionate about the material. The way she lectures is not the most engaging but the material is not very challenging and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. She is always happy to help and answer questions.
straight forward lectures, very available, class content is simple enough, but she makes it easier. very understanding. good calm and "easy" engineering course

This class was pretty easy. A basic understanding of math is needed. Dr Smith herself is obviously passionate about the material but isn't the best lecturer. She is also not the most consistent with posting assignments on time, something that became prevalent in AME 141 (the next class in the 140's series). Labs are pretty good, and TA's are great.
TOO EASY LMAO

This class was really easy for me, Sarah Smith is very very nice and made the lectures really clear with her pre-class notes. Explained everything from the basic math and physics principles for people who haven't had much experience with it, and overall very helpful in both the lectures and labs (when she comes).

literally the most caring professor ever. he makes an effort to get to know you and will help you out with anything you need. he works around your schedule in order and helps you out whenever you need it.
Really nice Prof, he read drafts of my papers before each submit and if he did not get around to it he would extend the deadline which was really nice of him.

Jimbo is my absolute favourite. I adored every single class with him he is so fun and kind and his classes are super lightweight and not very work-heavy. He gives great feedback on assignments that if you just follow, you'll get an A and the assignments are very lenient. You get given a style of article and you choose what you write about.

I <3 Memmott SO MUCH. Lil Jimbo is my life. He is so kind and caring, he's happy to give you extra time on assignments and all the help you need. His classes are super light-hearted and not content-heavy AT ALL. He's amazing, I really adore him and his class so much.
one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. Makes journalism digestible for everyone, even pure engineering students.
Took 3 of his classes. Such a great man. Might be an Easy Class but you can learn a lot from this man.
So little work. Smart man. Kind teacher.
I <3 Memmott
Best Professor and overall genuinely great person. Take his classes if you want an easy-going class that is also fun. They are few and far between at the U of R.
Any class with Memmott is a treat.  132 is, by far, the best the class I've taken in 3 years at UR.  If you have the opportunity, take a Memmott class.  You won't be disappointed.
Who loves Memmott? WE LOVE MEMMOTT!!!
Jim Memmott is arguably the greatest man in update new york. this is not a joke, best ever. Memmott should be a major within the Eng. dpt.
Memmott's the MAN!!
Awsome guy, awsome class. Really down to earth.
Jim is awesome!  Funny, honest and wonderful.  Highly recommended!
An awesome guy! Fun class, easy assignments and grading. Laidback and helpful. I'd recommend him to anyone for any class!

I love Memmott.  I could never say it enough.  Not only does he look like Larry David, but he has a wonderful personality.  He befriends people so easily and takes an interest in getting to know you, even if all you do is read the CT in his class!
great guy, always a joy in class and very helpful
easy easy easy!  a little flakey perhaps, he lets you turn in your assignments basically anytime before he records the final grades, but no complaints here. he knows everyone.

One of the best lecturers I've taken a course with; he's extremely knowledgeable, engaging, and willing to help you work through any issues you have or anything related to the course that you're interested in outside of lecture. Highly recommend this class; it's so much fun.

Heyworth is incredibly intelligent and is more than happy to share his knowledge at all times. In class, he's always focusing on how students think and look into nuance. He has high standards but is committed to helping his students reach those standards, ultimately for the better. He cares a lot about his students and has a high degree of respect!

It's obvious that Heyworth knows his stuff, but sometimes during our lectures, he would focus on small points and we would end up losing class time because of it. He's very passionate, but it would've been nice to have a more structured class and paper set up. He grades fine but he really nitpicks sometimes on things that aren't that important.

Professor Heyworth is very smart, but it tends to show in his lectures that he makes a good amount of the stuff on the spot, although it sounds good. This makes his classes sometimes feel like it's all over the place. He also occasionally concerns himself with little lines that sometimes cause a drag to the class. Not bad, but he is a tough grader.

Really enjoyed Ravi's classes. It's a LOT of work, but very rewarding and with so many resources provided for out-of-classroom self study. Need a solid MS Excel foundation & willingness to play with code & tools. Genuinely get the impression he wants you to succeed. Homework and tests are well documented and fairly graded.
Great class.

5 homeworks, no exams, 1 Group Project
But that does not mean the course is easy.
If you do bad on some of the homework you may not have a good grade.
The lectures are carefully arranged and the slides are easy to follow, but the pace in class is very quick so you have to focus.
But after all this course is fruitful.

Took Writing 105: Argumentative Detectives. Interesting class, lots of papers but it's a writing course so it should be expected. I had a hard time staying on top of work this year but she was really understanding and really helped me out. If you're swamped you can get an extension. Great professor. Grades fairly and sincerely cares about students.

This was one of my fav classes at this school. Prof Grimm is so well prepared and really knows her stuff. She assigns A LOT to read but is okay with you not understanding it all as long as your bring your questions to class.

Professor Grimm was somewhat tough. Lectures did not always follow the reading that was assigned prior to class. Also, took a while to get back to me on emails and assignments. Not a lot of help on assignments before due dates even though there was not a clear rubric for some assignments.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: The class is like 3 courses in 1. It's lang doc./ling readings, tech stuff, and cult. anth stuff. Her feedback half time is critical w/o any substance and other times it simply makes no sense. Take when you have time to read a lot and only take it if you want to do linguistic-oriented fieldwork.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: I took Ling104 randomly my first semester and this is the class that convinced me to become a Linguistics major! Nadine is a great professor and very understanding of her students' personal problems. This course was also very interesting and a pretty easy A as long as you do the readings (usually around 30 pages every class) and try on the essays.

Prof Grimm is kind and sweet, but she is very vague with her assignments. She takes a long time to give grades back and is a slightly tough grader. Very nice and understanding person, but not the best with feedback.
Takes forever to give back assignments and is very vague on assignment instructions. And when asked for clarification is kind of flaky. I would not recommend this professor under any circumstance.

Dima is a great professor, although he is a tough grader. He fingerspells too fast during exams, even for ASL 101. I wouldn't  have pushed myself this hard in this introductory class without him, yet I think this is still a bit too harsh given this intro-level course. Overall a very enjoyable experience despite the grade.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: He's great! I love him.  He's really helped me understand more about Deaf Culture, and there's so much learned from him despite the lack of speaking, which I was a little hesitant about at first but now realize was a silly worry.  He's very caring and will help you with something over and over again until you get it right.

Very friendly, approachable, helpful and humorous, I've taken two of his classes and he's always a pleasure. Does have a tendency to pair strong and experienced signers with less skilled ones, which can be awkward for both. Don't listen to the MCC students-he's a good teacher, he just doesn't tolerate rude behavior  like speaking or texting.

If you're looking for a good way to fasttrack your ASL education, then Dima is the way to go! He is a hard grader, but that is because he really wants you to learn.  However, if you put in some effort outside of class an A shouldn't be too difficult to obtain.  Just realize that you MUST put in that effort. Otherwise, he is super funny and nice!

Dima is an excellent teacher.  be forewarned, however, he expects you to take the subject matter seriously.  That should be obvious, but in my experience, it apparently isn't.  Dima is a great teacher for people who genuinely want to learn ASL.  Those looking for an easy credit should look elsewhere. For serious students, there is none

DO NOT take his class if you're looking for the easy way out.  Also, show up on day one knowing ASL alphabet and numbers, at the very least, otherwise you WILL be confused.  I like a challenging class, but the challenge should not be based on inability to understand what the professor wants you to do.  Other than that, great teacher all around.

I love Dima! He is definitely my favorite teacher in the whole school. Because of him, I was inspired to change my major to ASL. Like said previously, he does seem cold but once you get to know him he is so much fun. And even though he is the toughest grader, it totally pays off!

I took 101, 102, 105 with Dima. He is the best professor I've had at this school. At first he may seem a bit cold, but he is the friendliest person ever. He is known to be harder the hardest grader, but it is so worth it. In 101 I was able to communicate comfortably with people in 105. I wish he taught more classes so I could always have him!
He was funny but the same thing happened to me as the previous commenter, I got a B in 102 even though I worked hard and seemed to get good grades throughout the semester. I still like him though.

I enjoyed having Dima as a teacher until I received a B in his 105 class last semester.  I put much more effort into his class than what was expected.  His grading policy is unfairly vague and subjective, and it has made me dislike him.
Love Him!
He's hilarious.
Love Dima! He helped inspire such an interest in ASL and he is so helpful!

I cannot express how upset I am that he's no longer teaching 105.  I was seriously going to plan my whole schedule around his class.  I took his evening class in Fall '05, with only 10 other kids (small classes are the best esp for ASL).  Best class ever.
Amazing teacher.
dima is awesome!!

he was an awesome, fun, and helpful teacher. i took 101 and 102 with him and he was always incredibly helpful and had great activities to practice your vocab and the projects and tests weren't hard at all. a great guy.
No Comments

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Dr. K. is a great professor that teaches content meaningfully and spares no effort in making the class accessible regardless of whether you've taken MUSC101 or 110. Homework was over half of the grade, and was distributed on a weekly basis (usually no re-dos). More than enough time is given to complete the exams, and they match the practice.

I absolutely loved her MUSC 111 class. She isn't harsh at all on grading but still gives great feedback on homework assignments. Her lectures are more hands-on so you'll interact with the material a lot more in class. Plus, she's incredibly sweet and cares deeply about her students. She even brought us cookies for our final which was super nice.

Professor Zeng isn't the best but he really tries to make sure everybody understands each topic. He covers a handful of examples for very topic and for the most part tries his best to be very clear and direct. Probably the most interesting math class of the 160 series and he definitely was a solid professor.

I won't say he is an amazing professor. But he is just about average. His lectures are clear. He is also very nice and would try his best to answer your questions. He got accent, which might be sometimes not that easy to understand. But he is very helpful if you go to his office hour. very patient.

Taught a section in virology. Very good lecturer, but make sure to take notes on his slides since he doesn't have anything but the main point down written down, which is why I say attendance is mandatory for more details on his slides. Definitely has a sense of humor. Super nice professor and answered any and all questions I had :)

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: One of the worst professors I've had. Makes his TA do all of the work and grades notes subjectively. Slides are not helpful and lectures are lackluster. Tough grader with little empathy for students. Used to consider going to grad school for Art History but reconsidered because of classes/professors like this.

Quiz and test material is only from the lectures. The slides barely have any words, so you have to go to the lectures and take good notes to figure out what's going on. People record the lectures on their phones so that if you miss anything you can go back. A lot of hw reading, but it's a history class so it's what you sign up for.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This class requires 40-100 pages of reading after every class. Almost the entire grade of this class is based on notes taken from these readings, with no guidelines, arbitrary grading and no feedback. Lectures consist of him rambling off trivia facts on the lecture's topic, with no class discussion (which was promised in the syllabus).

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: He makes his TA do most of the grading. The requirements for notes are not immediately clear and you are graded mostly on your notes. He directly refused to record lectures as required by the school. He does not care about the students. Do not expect any flexibility or kindness.
He's a decent professor and explains math concepts quite well. Also open to answering questions in class and helping students understand. The only con is his handwriting can a little hard to read.

This man explained chain rule in the most diabolical way possible. I honestly ended up just teaching myself most of it. The lectures weren't very engaging. The tests can be pretty hard especially if you're underprepared. This is not like calc I in high school.
Math 161 should not be this hard. Does not explain well, lectures boring. But, need photography advice… GO to Pham!
Great professor, very accessible outside class. Attended all his lectures, had fun all the way through. Handwriting could be sometimes hard to read, otherwise good at explaining concepts.

He writes *really* quickly on the board, which can be incredibly hard to follow (especially when he's doing proofs that are completely irrelevant to you). One on one he's really helpful and a nice guy to talk to.

Fili is a really nice guy and extremely helpful when you go to his office hours. 164 is a tough course and with his help it isn't as bad. He does a lot of proof based work towards the end of the year but going to office hours will definitely help you get some good examples and explanations.

Fili is a smart guy and a great professor. He moves along at a reasonable pace and is probably the most helpful professor outside of class I've ever had: responds quickly to emails and is always helpful during office hours. 164 is tough, but he makes it manageable. And to top it all off, he's super friendly. Really top-notch.

He's super nice and helpful, but I often got the feeling he was too smart for our class. His lectures are very proof/theory based and unlike the tests. I found it helpful to search lessons on YouTube. This was his first year teaching discrete math, though, so I'd cut him some slack. The class isn't too hard.

He is a nice guy. However, I cannot follow him at all! He is very smart and maybe too smart to me. I don't know. The good thing is that he IS the textbook. If I don't understand him, I will check my textbook.
Fantastic Professor! He really cares about his students and is passionate about the material. Take his classes!

Lectures move very fast and are sometimes less than clear, so stay on top of your note-taking. Fortunately he's patient and helpful in lecture and especially in office hours. HW is a lot harder than tests. Overall a great professor who's passionate about his subject. Decided to add a math major after taking his class.
Really nice guy, but tends to rush and skip steps which leaves you puzzled trying to figure out what your notes mean after class
Great professor. He gives a lot of work (at least at the beginning of the course, it dies down after a while), but he is both very accessible and willing to help.

Stella is such a nice lady but her class is very homework heavy and unless you do extra work you will automatically receive a B grade. The class isn't very difficult and she is very understanding but expect a lot of tedious work.

Professor Stella is wonderful! Both inside and outside the classroom, she is a student advocate who takes mental and physical health very seriously. She's very accessible outside of the classroom because she would stay until 10pm to provide support. Just a person who has a great spirit! I definitely recommend her classes.

Ms.Stella is an AMAZING professor. She is very caring and understanding which is a trait you hardly find in most professors. She has experience in different writing styles and techniques and has helped me to find a citing style that would benefit me for my major. She's just the sweetest professor ever. I recommend her class a ton.

Professor Wang genuinely cares about your growth as a writer or a student. She is always available for meetings outside of class. The course has a heavy workload but everything is graded based on completion. If you do everything you need to do it's an easy A. You will get as much as you put into the class.
Easy to get good grades but don't expect to become a great writer after taking this class.

Please do yourself a favor and never take a class with this women. She never gives feedback, she wont teach you about writing and she will constantly remind you to breathe. I have no clue what i am doing in her class. She just randomly comes up and tell me that she doesnt like my paper and thatI should resubmit it 3 weeks after submission.

Stella is about the nicest, most caring person you can imagine. She has a "labor based grading contract", which means your grade depends on how much work you do (basically just participation, if you do the work, you get an A). Expect homework almost daily. She doesn't really give feedback, so don't expect to improve too much as a writer.

Stella is such a caring and understanding person and shows that love to each of her students. Her grading is pretty much just participation and just getting your work in on time. Her only downside is almost daily homework (though it's not too intense most of the time, just tedious) and she doesn't really give feedback on your writing.

The grading criteria is clear. You submit the tasks you get A. As long as you do everything, the grade is under control. However, you will not get any benefit of the class, she gives no useful feedback no writing materials. You never expect to be a better writer after taking the course. In short, wanna easy A without learning, take this class!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor Wang is super supportive under this special circumstance. She replies emails very fast, she always come prepared to class, and she is genuinely concerned about students' health condition. Put effort into this class and a good grade will definitely ensue. She is just so so kind! Wish I could take her other classes

She is a very caring and accommodating professor, unfortunately I never felt like she actually made us better writers. She often gives criticisms in order to make you conform to her perspective instead of finding ways to help you argue your point more effectively. Overall having her as a teacher was not a great experience.

Stella is very caring and gives very thorough feedback. Nothing is graded until the very end of the year, so it is a low stress class. Not a lot of homework and she is very flexible with due dates (if you have a test on the same day, just reach out to her and she will change the due date). Always accessible outside of class! Very sweet teacher.
You think you can go to her class and get an easy A? Go find another professor to get an A

She is a wonderful person. Very engaged with her work. Truly and positively motivating. If you have an ambition you can create a wonderful project thanks to her amazing supervising, feedback and inspirations. She's truly openminded and let students explore their ideas.
She is one of the nicest professors at UR. Always so passionate in class discussions and is very accomodating to students. I would definitely recommend her for WRT 105!

I don't mean to take this class in the beginning, but I really love it and learn a lot from Stella! She is very nice and gives helpful feedback during office hour. She talks a lot in class and expects class discussion. And she will try her best to help everyone to enjoy writing. I love her WRT 105E!!!

Stella was an amazing teacher. I went into this class ready to hate it but she made me enjoy it. We didn't have to write as many papers as the other WRT 105 classes (only wrote 2). She gives amazing feedback, too!
One of the nicest professors I've had. She will do anything to help you, and puts 100% into the class, helping students, and making the class engaging. Very fair in grading as well.
she is nice but i find it is not helpful to take this writing class at all

Nicest professor I've ever met. I love this woman and have great respect for her. Well informed, helpful and very nice. She has a tendency to talk a lot, but she tries her best to make the class interesting.
I took Cosmology with her, and she was absolutely hilarious.  She graded tough, but fair, and her assignments were never too onerous.  One of the best writing classes I've ever taken!
by far the worst teacher I've had. expects you to already have the writing skills of a grad student and grades very harshly.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He looks out for his students, explains things well, and assigns actually engaging material. Really recommend his class!!

Professor Chitrakar gave great feedback for each paper and it was clear he cared for his students. He was very easy to reach outside of class and would respond quickly. There were few homework assignments during the semester. Overall it was a manageable course and I without a doubt became a stronger writer.

comment: a lot of work but great professor
i love Professor Rogers. Best professor I've had a Rochester. His intelligence and ability to teach in an understandable way is outstanding. I would recommend taking anything with him!
Simply the Best
Very interesting guy and great at explaining. The constant presence of examples makes the class feel tangible and reduces the abstractness.
Hes the best at everything he does.
I loved having a rogers as a teachers, he's a big goof ball who is insanely good at math and teaching

This is the Best professor you can ever have for a Japanese for film class. She is knowledgeable and passionate, and she's still trying to learn from her students. Don't be daunted by the seemingly overwhelming syllabus of her class, workload is actually not that much.
Amazing. Passionate. Kind. Thoughtful. Interesting.

She's a rockstar. Organized, knowledgeable, and humble. I had no background in Japanese culture but she introduced it so fascinatingly. One of my favorite college professors. Her grading criteria and assignments are simple and well organized. Gives ample time to complete tasks - you'll have to watch 1 film/week + 90 mins of other work.
Had prof bernardi a couple of years ago and her classes were the only ones i truly enjoyed.  Very caring teacher.  And yes she deserves a chili pepper.

Boring class. There are no discussions. He almost seems offended if you ask a question or show up to office hours. You also have to show upto every class and note down everything he says to get a good grade because there is no other material to study (like slides). If you are willing to do that, it is pretty easy to get a good grade.

Earl isnt particularly great. His lectures are turbo BORING and can be hard to understand at times. The class exams are fairly easy if you remember most of what he talks about in class, but the class itself is boring since you only hear him talk for most of the time. He also doesnt value original responses very much, wanting answers from class.
No words... horrible hand writing.. no slides.. mandatory attendance and he is all over the place. Do not do it to yourself.

Conee is not the best professor, his lectures are very boring and he tends to ramble. Also, the grade is only determined by 3 midterms, so no final, but also no homework. However, the tests are all based on content from lectures, so just go to lectures regularly. In my opinion, the content was easy, so having Conee wasn't the worst.
Earl Conee will inspire you profoundly. I cannot stop thinking about him. Taking Ethics with him changed my life.

I think I misunderstood what the meaning of life was before this class because it is the most boring class I have ever taken. It's an easy course as long as you regurgitate what he says on paper, exam questions are not difficult either if you go over the things he talked about in class. Be prepared to fall asleep in every class.

Lectures are often dry and overly textbooky, so it is hard to pay attention and understand the material at times. There are no note handouts/lecture recordings so you MUST attend class. Your grade is only based on three exams, and he tends to grade harshly. Focus on the arguments for/against the theories, as that is what he will test on.

He is a boring lecturer. I am in this class right now and I have never cared less about the meaning of life. I am a philosophy nerd too it's not like this guy is just too abstract or dense he is just completely unengaging and his readings are generally also this way.

Professor Conee is sweet and knowledgeable. His Phil 101 class was entirely test-based, with exams only on content introduced in class. Exams aren't super difficult but do require studying. His reasoning can be hard to follow, but he uses accessible language and makes an effort to answer questions. He's a decent lecturer and his class is manageable

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Material is dry enough, but he does not make it any more interesting. Only 3 exams determine your final grade, but they are pretty lenient (ex: choose 4 out of 7 questions to answer). Tip for notetaking/studying: focus on the objections to the theories - he rambles a lot, but this is all he will test on. Don't write down everything he says.
Rambles during lectures, hard to distinguish what will actually be tested on. Only grades based off of three exams and does not offer any other way to boost your grade.

Classes are just rambling and rambling essentially incoherently. Tests are graded specifically on *his* views and only the stuff that happened in class, so the readings and original conclusions barely help you. Class isn't unbelievably difficult but is totally pointless and frustrating.

Stick figure diagrams and sentence fragments on the board. If that isn't your learning style there is little recourse. I've always struggled to absorb a lecture and take worthwhile notes at the same time so I almost went crosseyed. For the final 15 people pooled their notes and pieced together his lectures like a lost ark. Please give note hndouts!

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He made too explicit, at least for non-native speakers, explanations on philosophical points, and it takes you years of time to make sense after class. And the tests are graded on strict but ambiguous criteria; you would be surprised about your grade on a you-seem-to-know-well topic. That is a class that you will regret for rest of your college.

Hes terrible. He will grade you based on his opinions. He will not be fair. He has a lot of issues like OCD and paranoia. I will never take another class from him again. This was terrible. He cant give lectures. He cant explain himself and he shouldnt be teaching any mandatory courses.

Really nice professor who cares about the students. Lectures are kinda boring, but that's more the material than the professor and he does his best with them. Tests are easy and he's more than fair on them. Reading is optional, can easily end with an A with no reading and minimal studying as long as you at least kind of pay attention in class.

I have taken both PHL 102 and PHL 227 by Conee. Trust me take PHL 102  if he ever offers it its a great class and shows a great analytic approach to philosophy and is a lecture hall. PHL 227 is a whole different story. Small class and he takes a analytic approach to simple details. He does not appreciate your own thoughts on the subject.

Connee is the worst professor I have ever had. He is so confusing, he rambles, he is SO boring, and is absolutely useless. Lectures are miserable and if you miss one sentence you will never hear it again, even though you will probably be tested on it. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! You'll regret it.

I transferred to UR studying philosophy for 2 years. One class with him, and I knew philosophy was quickly becoming a quite worthless, boring field. Too analytic, not enough common sense. He makes easily expressible ideas difficult to comprehend. Suffice to say, I changed my mind about studying philosophy at UR, but not about studying philosophy.
Good professor, interesting lectures with the all bizarre examples he gives to illustrate a point. An easy A if you go to class and thoroughly understand the material.
Whether or not you will enjoy his classes depends on your initial interest in the subject. Can be hard to follow at times but he's helpful and his tests are easy.

great professor!! I loved his ethics 102 class and hope to have him again before I graduate. really makes an effort to be engaging and funny. the subject matter can get a little dry, but he does his absolute best with it. tests are very fair and there is no homework. highly recommend this professor.

Found the text to be interesting at times.  The lectures were pretty boring though.  Sometimes he lectures on stuff out of the book though, which makes it necessary to go to class.  Would not recommend taking this class "for fun."
His teaching style is horrible as is his class. Don't take a class with him if you can help it. He is not at all helpful and acts as if he is insulted if you show up at his office hours.

I enjoyed the coursework very much, but Conee is a boring lecturer with dogmatic interpretations.  I did poorly on the midterms because the answers I tried to express my own interpretations of the text, and Conee clearly didn't appreciate it.
If you go to class...and actually pay attention in class and do your reading you will be fine...onlii thing is it is BORING...atleast PHL 102 ethics was...
hes as awesome as he is bald!
His class (Ethics) is incredibly boring--both the books and the lectures.  I learned a lot more in my high school philosophy & ethics classes.  Do not take this class with Conee.
Easy class if you take notes and go to the lectures, but i was only awake for approximately one lecture in its entirety.

Professor Connee is great!  He is extremely enthusiastic and doesn't really assign work out of class.  The tests come straight from lecture, so if you go, you will do well.  His lectures are also very humerous with all the examples he gives.  Definately recommend.
Mr Clean - who knew he taught a class at UR... not a bad class - just go to it, and def. go the class before the test because he will give you the test right there.
No Comments
Yes, he's hilarious and gives easy A's, but it's impossible to stay awake through his lectures.

SO awesome!  He's like Mr. Clean and a turtle combined. Though some may think the lectures are boring, its really just the material.  If you don't like philosophy, you wont like him.  I think he's halarious and 101 is an easy class!

very easy to get an A as long as  you go to class.  his tests are word for word from his lectures, and as long as you spend a few hours studying before the test you're golden.  and plus, he's completely hairless and hilarious...what more could you want&#6
Not very intersting or easy to follow in class.
Just take notes in class, dont worry about the book. class notes are the same as the book and he basically gives you the test the class before.
Ok, basically, he is a bad teacher who teaching a slacker class (ethics) who tries to get people to take him seriously by giving bad grades.

Okay, so yeah, his lectures are long and the material isn't the most engaging... but the man is hilarious!  His exams are really straightforward and easy-as long as you attend class- there's no reason someone that has attended class should get below a B.

A really funny guy.  I learned a lot about various philosophy theories in his class.
Bring a pillow...

If you are inexperienced in BCS, you might struggle. You will also have a lot of easy assignments, but they take time. If you are struggling, the TA and professor are helpful.

He is really a good and expert professor. He explains concepts and reading materials well. The tests are not that hard if you pay attention to the lectures and go over the slides. The homework is also interesting as a Twitter-like comment is required for each journal article. I really like him.

Professor Dodell-Feder does a great job of teaching the material. His lectures are interesting and interactive, which makes the class enjoyable. He cares about his students and has a good sense of humor. Overall a great professor and a great guy.
A very solid choice as a German teacher. Adjusts the course to the class's needs, cares about her students, and all around makes a very good teacher.

Frau Becker is a phenomenal teacher. Beyond just her teaching skills, she is one of the most caring professors I have come across at this school thus far. I have nothing but kind words to say about her.

Frau Becker assigns a one page Aufsatz with each set of Test/Vocab Quiz, so make sure you drill the vocab with flashcards & pics. The more vocab you know, the less time you spend looking words up. For flashcards, I cross-reference Linguee, LEO Dictionary, Beolingus, & Collins 8th Unabridged Dictionary. Also, use Language Tool for grammar.
She's very sweet, helpful and understanding, with a good sense of humour!
Frau Becker is one of the best Teachers I've ever had, and certainly the best German teacher!!!

Professor Ren's lectures are so effective, they could put Melatonin out of business. With only a handful of students willing to brave his chalkboard monologues, the rest have found the ultimate sleep-inducing experience in his classes.

He's super nice and lenient on grading -unlike other engineering professors who care about nitty-gritty like writing down units and sig figs. As long as the final answers are correct, full credit. His exams are short (3 mids 1 optional final, 2q on each), but they are super easy. You will get a good grade unless you just have no idea whats going on
He just write everything from the textbook, even draw an exactly same image. His lecture is worthless.

He is the worst professor I have had at the University of Rochester by FAR! He has no idea what he is doing, and is completely worthless without his notes. He makes frequent mistakes during lectures. On top of that, his grading scheme is broken. He will only ask 8 questions, each one being worth 10% of your grade. He gives almost no partial credit.

His lectures were easy to listen to even when when we were digging deep into the mathematics. I also thought his final project of a PIC code was a great idea. You end up remembering what you learned a lot better when it's part of a big project. Not to mention it gives a great introduction to PIC codes which is important for research.

I really enjoyed this class.  He does teach right from the book, but I liked this style of teaching as I knew where he is getting his information and where he was going with it. Also, if I missed something in class, I could easily look it up. He was very helpful at rec. and extremely fair grader.He really captivated my interest in thermo.

Taught right out of the book.  His lectures and examples were almost completely from the book, so they did not add much more than what the textbook already outlined.  Professor Ren probably gets more criticism than he deserves, but he can definately improve his taching style.

He sucks. He doesnt like to help you. He will give u the hardest quiz and tests ever. He will save 60% of yout grade til the last week of the semester and murder you with an impossible project and exam
Bushleague teacher... Don't know anyone who enjoys his class.

tested new concepts from a chapter never taught in class on the final exam. why?!?! you have to study a new chapter while taking the final exam, you either get it or fail the final and get a grade below B

He talks very quietly with an accent, boring lecturers, not helpful outside of classes.
Very good lecturer, makes complex statistical derivations very simple and elegant

His lectures are bad. His english is poor, he speaks quietly, and is not very clear in general. He refuses to use blackboard or provide any study materials. His lectures consist of incoherent babbling. He is soft spoken and English is clearly his second language. You will rely on the textbook as your primary teaching utility. This would be fine except some of the material is quite difficult. I strongly advice getting in the habit of visiting the TA weekly because you will learn nothing during lecture.
sit in the front for his class or you can barely hear anything cuz of his accent. Skips steps and goes fast.  It's probably cuz he's taught it for so long he don't remember how hard it actually is
