Good prof but needs to get some TAs who speak English.
Professor Rao is fairly clear during office hours and in his writings.  He assigns a lot of material but the toughest homework questions generally are not on the exam.

His lectures consist of his mumbling voice and he never tells you what's going to be on his midterms.  He's not effective in his teaching and not one student is actually learning anything from his lectures.  You are screwed.
His accent is too heavy and he doesn't explain proofs and theories.

He is very clear with what he expects and gives you lots of practice material that is very representative of the exam. It is a time-demanding course since there is a ton of content, but I highly recommend.

the semester just started and i alr dont like the guy. office hours arent helpful bc he'll just agree with everything you said. he doesnt explain anything at all- almost like he expects you to learn it yourself. a few TAs are awesome and very accessible, however most of them arent (not having OH when it clearly says on the syllabus that they do)

Very unclear about what will be on the exams  (could spend 2hrs in recitation talking about a topic, just for him to admit the day before the exam that it won't be on it- but some obscure material from last exam will be!) Exam grading is done by undergrad TAs who are very stingy about giving out points. Very biased, & never in the student's favor.

Nice guy but subpar instructor. Lectures are unhelpful since he's hard to follow as he goes on tangents and unfortunately he doesn't give practice exams either. Redeeming quality is that he gives you learning objective questions on his slides, and I basically learned everything by putting them into GPT to memorize. Teach yourself and you'll be OK.

Listen to the other ratings, what they say is true... His grading criteria for exams were so specific, yet his questions weren't so clear, and students were left guessing what he wanted. Some of the stuff on the exam wasn't really talked about in class, and I had to self-teach myself a lot. Wouldn't recommend.

He made an already difficult class, more difficult. He often got lost trying to explain the material on his lectures. It seemed to me that he didn't really know what was going on. He often looked up the material he was teaching online. Not great.
A class like physiology should not be taught by Cunningham. Great guy but he's terrible at teaching.

Interesting guy that is passionate about the material. I appreciate that he is not overly serious in lecture. Makes time for questions both during and after lecture. His lectures are slow but still engaging to listen to. Low rating because he can be VERY rude speaking 1 on 1 (snarky as John Fisher students put it). Reminds me of Dr. Matson.

He is an amazing professor and teaches a class where you genuinely learn something valuable. His teaching style is clear and engaging, making complex material easy to understand. He is also very kind and truly cares about his students' success.

Both LAW 205+250: He is an exceptional professor who makes the lectures engaging and adds fun anecdotes about his law career. Grade is made up of mandatory attendance, two exams (last exam is not cumulative), and a case presentation. Easy grader on both exams and presentation is completion. Pay attention because he does cold call during lectures.
Great professor. Take his class

Professor Shanahan is one of the best professors I've had at the University of Rochester. He truly cares about his students, makes content engaging, and keeps assignments minimal. Tests align with class discussions, and his teaching made a 9 AM class enjoyable. I learned a lot and had a fantastic experience. Great teacher, great person!

Prof. Shanahan is a great professor. His lectures consist of a PowerPoint and 2-4 student case presentations. Class is mandatory & there are no recordings. Computers are not allowed so be prepared to always show up with a notebook or an iPad. He is EXTREMELY lenient in his grading but exams are no longer open notes. Material is dense but not hard.

he doesn't give out bad grades, if you get 60% or less on the midterm, its a b-. he tells alot of storys and tends to get off topic. lectures are not recorded and his tests are based off of the lectures. he says he uses the textbook but i never read it and i did good. he sometimes cold calls and there is a oral presentation

Prof. Shanahan is one of the best professors at UR. His lectures are generally in the mornings and can get boring, but they're interesting overall. In LAW 250 they become a lot more intriguing since he has guest speakers. But for both classes, there's an easy presentation and tests are online open notes/open source.

Wonderful professor! He made a morning law class my favorite in the semester! Materials and classes are very interesting and the professor is well connected with industry leaders. There is essentially no homework beside one simple presentation. He doesn't allow the use of electronic devices in class, though. Exams are open notes, and aren't hard.

Great professor and great guy. His lectures are straight to the point, and the use of student cases helps to explain the concepts. The tests are open notes, and as long as you are paying attention in class, they are not difficult at all.

Professor Shanahan was one of the best professors at the U of R. He gives the best lectures. He shows you pictures of him and many celebrities and also tells you funny stories. He made business law so interesting. Tests are open-book and you can do it in your dorm or in the classroom. Definitely take his class! Highest recommendation!
One of the most engaging professor's at the UofR. Great guy, tests are on major material covered. Go to class and you should do fine.
Great lecturer who manages to make classes interesting, even when the content gets dull. Almost no coursework, and the exams are easy if you've made a decent cheat sheet.

he is an amazing professor. even for a student have no law experience in law i still made through this class. also, he is warm-hearted, he would help you a lot with anything you concern . and, past exams he posted is very helpful.

No electronic devices in class, but he's so good at lecturing you won't even want to use one since he's easily one of the funniest professors at the university. One easy assignment for a huge chunk of grade. Make a good cheat sheet and you'll breeze through the tests. Highly recommend the course and professor. Was one of my favorite classes at UofR

One of the most caring professors I have ever had. The lecture with good content. I did not have enough background in music, but it is the course that you put some work into and you will get an A. HWs are durable, and the exam is a fair game.

Frank is maybe the best lecturer I've had at U of R, very clear, entertaining and up-to-date. Funny guy. The curriculum isn't super set in stone as he can linger a bit long on certain topics, though that does make it easy to internalize info. The exams and hw are very reasonable and he grades fairly.

Dr. Frank is by far one of the best professors I've had. I wouldn't rate him any lower than a 5/5, despite MUSC116 being an exceptionally grueling class that I would not wish upon anybody. If you need to or want to take this course, I recommend waiting as long as you possibly can in hopes that it gets offered at a different time in the future.
very good professor

I took Prof. Frank for MUSC 112 and find him to be incredibly passionate about music and a very considerate professor. His homework is short and concise and his lectures are very informative for what you need to do on the homework.
Attendance is mandatory; he gave me a hard time when I missed a class due to illness. Good teacher but spends a lot more time than necessary on certain topics when we could just move on.

Professor Frank is incredibly easy to get help from outside of class hours, is a flexible grader with very obvious care for his students and he never tries to stress us out. He is also really understanding about granting extensions when needed. Overall, great class, would definitely take it again.

Dr. Frank is the most caring professor I've had at UR. He even takes the time to learn every students name on the first day. His class is pretty lecture heavy, but his homework and exams are very fair. If students are struggling, he slows down to make sure everyone understands the material.
AWESOME professor. Highly recommend.

Dr. Frank is a caring, knowledgeable professor! I love his lectueres and he makes music theory so easy to understand. He's the most caring professor I've ever had and genuinely willing to help his students succeed.
Dr. Frank is very nice!!! He makes music theory interesting and it is easy for me to focus on the course materials. He cares about his students and he is always happy to help.

Dr. Frank is the man. He gave me a new appreciation for music theory, and if you have any previous experience with playing/reading music in high school then his introductory theory classes will be a piece of cake. I have nothing but good things to say about this quirky music professor.

From day one, Professor Frank made a conscious effort of learning each and everyone's names. Every class, he calls on every single person to answer questions and provides hints and help when needed. He's hilarious as a person and teaches with clarity. 9AM classes wouldn't be bearable without him!
He's the man. His dad humor is what got me to campus at 9:40 MWF.
Great teacher! Really cares about the students and tries to help them learn the material. Class is interesting yet also acts as a good GPA booster. Would recommend taking a class from him.

Prof. Frank is great! He makes a point to learn everyone's names, and calls on you during class. Pay attention and participate, do all your homework, and you'll be golden. I get the feeling he doesn't like handing out bad grades, especially to people who participate in class. I don't think attendance is mandatory, but he does call roll.

Absolutely awesome teacher. I would encourage all prospective music majors (and anyone interested in music) to take every class possible with Dr. Frank. He makes it his goal to know each student personally and is an overall great guy. Amazing pianist as well..

Dr. Frank is an amazing professor. He doesn't require you to buy the textbook, he makes classes so much fun, and the homework is usually fairly easy. He's also extremely lenient; if you forget to do your homework, then he'll still let you get it in to him before he leaves that day. All in all, Dr. Frank is awesome and highly recommended.

Dr. Frank is incredible. He is a talented musician who cares deeply about his students. He knows how to keep students' attention, knows everyone's name, and is respectful and knowledgeable. Great guy!
Great

Easy course. Lecture and seminar not very organized and he seems to be too nice on grading papers. Very caring for students. A good professor over all.

Professor Kaeuper is this university's greatest treasure, and one of the greatest living scholars of medieval history. Not taking a class with him would be to do yourself a disservice. You will be challenged, and rewarded. You will love him, the class, and the material.

He is the nicest, sweetest professor I've ever met. A bit absentminded, but that only adds to his charm. Lectures can drag, but his enthusiasm is contagious. Great professor. His knowledge of Medieval France and emphasis on the usage and interpretation of primary sources makes every class illuminating.
best professor in the world. super passionate and knowledgable- he knows everything.  he's such a kind soul and just really very witty in the style of Monty Python.

The very best professor I ever had in any subject.  His passion and devotion to his discipline affected keeners and rocks the same way, and he left no one behind.  I write books today because of him; I still go back and ask him to explain thorny questions of history.
Best professor I ever had, hands down. Reason I am a historian today.

Professor Kaeuper is completely invested in his students' success both in and out of the classroom and is willing to do whatever it takes to make sure you are well. The greatest professor I've ever had. Mentor, teacher, friend; he inspires everyone around him and all of his students.
Memorable.  Makes the subject come to life

Best prof I had in undergrad. I have taken away more useful info from this man than any other. We still chat about stuff and he continues to provide me with his sage comments on history. he's great
As funny as he is brilliant.

so cool.  office is full of dusty medieval gizmos. By far the best professor I have had at Rochester.

Had three classes with him in the early to mid 1990's. The best professor I had in terms of knowledge, story-telling, sense of humor and a tough, yet fair grader. 3 hour seminars flew by, even stayed late at times. I added a history major because of his class.  He tells great stories and gives students really interesting research experience.
Absolutely funny in class
Threw chalk and ppl sleeping in class, monty python references, actually made me look forward to a 940 class, great prof
One of the best classes I ever took.  Great lectures that were funny and interesting. If have any interest in medievalism take this class!
Had him as a teacher in the late '80s and still remember his with freat fondness.  In fact, he's the reason I changed my major to history.  'Nuff said.

appearances can be deceiving.  when u meet him u wouldn't expect him to be as funny as he is.  his classes are great.  definitely has notable quotes to remember.  he knows his stuff.  one of the best professors U of R has to offer
the best professor, riveting lectures
He is the best history professor I've encountered in my college experience.  He tells great historical anecdotes in class to illustrate his points, and he loves talking with students.
Gives very interesting lectures.
Had him for medievial history 15 years ago, still remember his class well.  Possibly the best teacher I have ever seen.
The best ever, ever.

I learned so much in this class, and Prof Meguid is a good lecturer minus one thing. comment: Teaches the material well. Detailed note taking is key. Lots of reading, BUT DO IT, it's vital. I disliked that the midterm and final only captured a small portion of the scale of the class. Midterm feedback/grading was vague. At the same time, I learned a LOT. Prof is interested in what you have to say. Tough but rewarding class, glad I took it.

Professor Meguid is very knowledgeable about what she is teaching, gives good lectures, and is available outside of class. There is a lot of reading and the class grade is made up mostly of 2 tests. Requires a decent amount of time outside of class to get a good grade in the class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Class requires a lot of readings and the midterm and final are a very high percentage of your grade. Can be a bit nerve racking not knowing what your grade is until the end, but grading is very fair. Professor covers a lot in lecture and is very approachable if you have any questions.

I really enjoyed intro to comparative politics with Professor Meguid. There are a lot of reading but I found all of them super interesting. Her lectures are mostly easy to follow and added helpful background along with another layer of nuance to the readings. I studied a lot for the test but looking back going to office hours would have been smart.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Prof is knowledgeable but goes through material quick. Requires heavy weekly readings (several books) that is required to be read to get an A. Grades are only from two exams and participation from recitations, so be ready to study well and speak. Okay class, but stressful at times due to exams being worth so much.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I really loved Professor Meguid! She's unbelievably smart and really cares about her students. She is very accessible outside of class and super responsive to emails. You can't BS the readings though so don't make my mistake. I was not happy with the grade I received in this class, but that's entirely on me not putting in the necessary effort.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Lectures for this class are necessary as there is no textbook. Meguid does a great job making the lectures interesting but you have to attend. There are also a lot of readings that are necessary to read for recitation and the midterm and final. Overall a great professor.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Had Meguid for PSC/IR 101. All in all an excellent professor. Meguid clearly establishes her expectations and gives you clear directions for what she expects from her students. As long as you pay attention in class and do the expected readings you should do fine in her class. Also very open to helping students after class and during office hours.
Connected to students and does a good job lecturing very knowledgeable

She is an amazing professor. The class is difficult but manageable. If you attend lectures and take notes you will be fine. I didn't do any of the readings and I still did really well. Her lectures are very engaging, and I didn't even like the material. She is one of my favorite professors and I intend on taking more classes with her.

Professor Meguid is terrific, professional, and clear.  Her lectures are absolutely necessary; no attendance required but, without being present in class, you will miss vital information.  She gives a lot of info very fast, so be prepared to type very quickly.  A lot of reading for an intro class.  Grades based entirely on two exams and recitation!

She is a BRILLIANT professor. She is super knowledgeable and fills each class with lots of good information. Very respectful of students' opinions, too.  Her grading is tough, so be prepared to study a lot for the midterm and final but if you like polysci or IR, the studying is interesting and the class is worth the work!
He has a very hard grading system and the tests are so hard.A lot of reading
Very organized lectures and clear expectations. I admire her a lot. She's soooooo freaking smart it's mind blowing! AND she's professionally nice.

It's easy to get a B but very difficult to get an A. Meguid is very clear and organized in her lectures. If you want an A, you have to do all the readings, but to get a B you only need to skim the readings.

Excellent lectures, crystal clear on expectations. The material was interesting. Excessive reading for an intro class - it was unexpected. Her lectures are kind of dry but the class goes quickly. Tough grader. Generally an above-average difficulty class.

She is clear, but 300 page readings in a 101 course on "theories" gets old quickly. Material is rather boring, but if you're really into poli sci you might like it. Just don't make my mistake of thinking 101 is an intro course, because it's really not.

Her class was very structured and clear but not interesting.  She was not very lively and just spit out  lot of information.  She did make a joke... once.  If a question was asked in class she seemed annoyed.  She was clear about what she wanted on exams.  Make sure you go to class and take good notes.  Doing the readings is not so necessary.
She is mad hard, but she is very clear and it is clear what you'll have to know. There is a lot of reading, but she does a good job explaining it all
She is very clear and organized. Her lectures are interesting and very easy to follow. Everything she says is important and relevant. Not too funny or lively, but a great professor.

Meguid is very structured. She provides outlines for all her lectures and tells you exactly what she expects from her students. The only thing that bothered me about her was that she talks too fast during lectures. It is easy to get a B in this course but not a A. There are a ton of readings. Some topics of the class are really interesting.

PRofessor Meguid is very knowledgeable and her lectures are very structured. It might not be the most interesting material to everyone, but, she makes it crystal clear what she wants. Also, she is very helpful in class and out of class!
She does not know how to connect ideas, and just spits out information.  When you ask her a question, bank on her having no idea what the answer is.  TAs are more qualified and better instructors.

In her 267 class, you do have to read and attend lectures if you want an A. You can't BS her exams, and she knows when you don't know the material. Lectures are a tad bit dry, and there's a good amount of reading, but the content is not difficult to grasp and she is very open to helping students.
horrible
Dont take Bonnie She is not a good teacher, Patrick the TA would have been better
Stellar!

Professor Meguid is fantastic: she has excellent command of her field of studies, and is approachable and very helpful. I got the impression she was vested in my success as her student. Highly recommended.

The thing is, her lecture is great if you actually attend. Like she once said, her lecture cant be supplement for the reading and the reading cant be supplement to the class either. So go to lecture and recitation (20% of grade)!! Expect A TONS OF reading, she will ask you to finish a 400 page of book in a week.
A decently designed course, organized, but not always interesting. Robert Putnam readings can be tough to take, too much emphasis on social connectiveness. Otherwise, nice and engaging.
extremely boring lectures and unbelievably boring reading. tests are okay, way too hard to stay awake both during readings and lectures
A's are very hard to get, however she is not a harsh grader. Very friendly and makes the extra effort to help students.
Excellent teacher. A's are not easy to come by in her class, but she is still a wonderful lecturer.
easy teacher! if you want an "A" sign up for a course with her!
Very helpful, very smart. Good lecturer. Assigns too much reading.

She's the reason why I decided to do a poli sci major!!!  I loved her class, though the reading was a challenge in both quantity and difficulty.  Solid lecturer given that the class covered a lot of ground and many theories and cases.  I plan on taking her 267 course.
Great professor. Clear and straightforward. Get ready to do ALOT of readings. Extremely smart and very approachable. I am taking a third class with her! Fair grader.
Smart and serious.  Assigns LOTS of readings, of which most are pretty useless.  Asks easy test questions but grades a bit harshly.  Good lecturer with occasional bouts of boring.
nice professor, but her reading materials can be very boring and somewhat useless (made us read a book and didnt even put it in a exam)
Class was ok, readings were terribly boring. Meguidster is very smart, explains things clearly.
A little full of herself
Very good at making complex theories understandable.  Interested in individual students and very enthusiastic about teaching.  Will challenge you.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: FANTASTIC PROFESSOR! He got to know everyone personally and chose really interesting material to discuss. Reading the plays out loud was an absolute joy! Tests were easy to prepare for, and plenty of time was given for our research paper. Wish I was a classics major just to take a class with him again :(

Dr. Dwyer was an amazing professor, and I would recommend him to anyone looking to take a classics course! His lectures were very engaging, and I really felt like he got to know us all. Although the class was a bit reading heavy, all of the tests, assignments, and papers were very accessible, and the grading criteria was clear.

Dr. Dwyer is a fantastic professor! He is very personable, easy to approach with questions, and gives good feedback on assignments. He uses slides but expands vocally, so note-taking and attendance are imperative. He is entertaining and engaging, so you won't get bored. I wish I could take every class with him! He also wears great sweaters.

Dr. Dwyer is the best! Overall, his lectures are really interesting and CLST 172 examines a lot of very interesting films and readings. He does a great job making the class manageable in terms of weekly work. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with him.

I would say his class is not well-paced overall, since the first several weeks we seat tight and do nothing, while all the materials are thrown at you at roughly the last two weeks. Group project takes great percentage of your final grade, while there is a chance you might get a rough grade without constructive feedback as well
Our first midterm was disastrous and little review was done. Average grade 48 and he said we should work harder...
He was a horrible teacher and had impossible exams and projects

I really enjoyed the material in this course but Koomen is a terrible teacher. The class was not well organized, we were given assignments on things to be lectured on the following week, and quizzes on things not covered in the course. Not too difficult (got an A-), but all in all the class was low quality. Would avoid if possible.

He enjoyed teaching the class but through not fault of his own the class was very disorganized. The robots themselves were complete messes but he tried hard to fix that. Wanted us to learn but tests were completely random with no structured review
You know you suck when 1/2 the class withdraws after the first project because they got under a 50 on it. LEARN HOW TO TEACH

This guy is more serious than Pawlicki, which can be good or can be bad.  He's an adjunct so he is not very "connected" to the campus, and doesn't really know how things work around here.  So he's a bit aloof.
Nice guy but puts trivial multiple choice questions on his exams. Teaches almost completely out of the textbook, including labs.
I liked him a lot.  He's an adjunct professor, so it can sometimes be difficult to contant him, but he's very clear. Many CS kids dislike him, but I'm a fan.

I don't know what the other people were complaining about... Professor Koomen is a _great_ professor.  He is demanding, but is willing to help you grasp the topics in any way possible.  If you aren't willing to work, possessed of any aptitude for CS or interested in learning, he's not the prof. for you.

His method of testing is God-awful.  He's very uninspired when it comes to helping with tests.  He doesn't provide practice tests, doesn't tell you what format it's in, and likes to surprise you with ridiculously specific questions.  When we asked him what to study for the test, he said "pages 1-400."  No topic overview, nothing.

Loooove his crazy voice.  Class is a cake walk for 7 weeks, then BOOM and Javascript tabling takes over your life.  I attended 4 classes.  What a strange guy, well organized, very specific.  Awkward most of the time

Koomen is a funny German dude.  The class is not that bad if you do all the work and study some.  If you fall behind or are a lazy you're f---.   It was funny watching him try to hit on the hot female Psychology teacher that taught the class before us.
Death on earth. If you don't already know java, do not plan to do well. If you know java, still don't plan to well. Its a split between easiness and reaaallly hardness.
No Comments
Class was fine.  His teaching inspired me to attend <1 time per month.
this class should be taken only by computers or nerds. the teacher is the devil, with his only saving grace being his entertaining voice cracks like a 13 year old boy.

Worst professor ever. He doesn't see students raise their hands. There are two weeks until finals and he has yet to return the one midterm and one homework assigned, so we don't have any grades yet. He is difficult to follow, doesn't finish sentences, posts assignments last minute, and overall, doesn't care about teaching.
What a great guy!!! So helpful and nice, I love his mustache!

So, I'm sitting in his class right now and he hasn't looked at the class once.  It is like this everyday.  The material is so interesting but the monotonously boring and uncaring man puts me to sleep twice a week, when I want to learn.   Not a fan.
WORST EVER

Requires memorization of topics not taught in class. If you cannot rotate molecules in your head, DO NOT take this class - you are not allowed to use a model kit like in orgo. It is definitely tough, but Dr. Neidig is fun and is a great lecturer so it makes the course more bearable.

Neidig knows what he's talking about - the dude is smart, no doubt about it. But doesn't know how to teach. Tests were too long, felt extremely unprepared despite lots of studying. He was very condescending and rude. Never felt comfortable talking to him one-on-one. Liked the content, hated the course & prof.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Love Professor Neidig - very fair grading and he definitely knows what he's talking about Don't be intimidated by the beginning of this course

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Dr. Neidig explains concepts well, and his TA's are incredible at clarifying them. The exams are fair and representative of the homework. I took this class when it was hybrid, and found both the in-person and virtual lectures easy to follow. He maintains some professional distance, but he's approachable. Go to office hours and ask to see his dogs!

Clearly a very smart guy, also is nice. Has office hours, don't be scared to approach him. Do all his problem sets and workshops and you'll be set for his exams- his averages didn't dip below 75%, so they're pretty fair and representative of the hw/workshops assigned.
This is a very interesting class if you enjoyed organic chemistry. Challenging but definitely doable. Tests are representative of lecture notes.
Yes, he is young, kind of funny, easy to understand, he uses multiple colors of chalk, BUT I wouldn't go as far as far as calling him THE BEST teacher that I've ever had.  Maybe that's just me.
Smart Approachable Easy tests Easier homework sets

I guess he's one of the better professors in the lower math courses (but that isn't saying much).  Most of what he explains is done really well, but he did just graze over some things that were more important than he made them seem.  The two midterms were exceptionally easy.  The final was a bit harder but fair.
Great professor, but teaches right out of the book.  He's easy going and makes himself available to students.  A kind man.

HOT!! He has an adorable accent! Also a great professor! Takes the time to explain everything in detail everytime and doesn't assume that you should know things. Is very helpful in office hours and wants students to succeed. Tests are fair and mirror class notes.

To his credit, he is a good teacher and explains things very clearly and points out intricacies that other professors overlook or assume you understand. Additionally, tests are very fair and mirror the practice tests. As a teacher he is excellent, HOWEVER, he is a jerk and an ass at times.
Excellent teacher.  Makes everything perfectly clear.  Has tons of office hours and will help you however he can.
Awesome teacher, very nice and willing to work with the students.

Heap is a math god.  My roommate and I call it "going to the Heap concert", and we get front row tickets, everytime.  I hated math, but thanks to Heap, I can now tolerate it.  To all the ladies out there, be prepared to fall in love.

"Heap is a god!" Heap one of the most clear speaking and devoted teachers I have met at this school. Be prepared to work your butt off on homework sets, but if you have any problems he will take you through step by step (and he makes himself readily available for help). It's really unfortunate that he has to leave so soon!
boring class...great teacher
No Comments
No Comments
Great professor who is eager to help students.
very cool guy.  office hours are more than helpful.  great to joke around with.  what a math-lete!
Awesome prof. willing to help. really nice
best math professor ive ever had, he gives clear and useful notes, and hes always willing ot help you figure out the webwor
Great professor who will help you whenever needed.....be happy if you get him.
He's the nicest guy and really enthusiastic and helpful.  His lectures are a little boring, but he knows his stuff.  Go to office hours!

He opens his office hours for students 3 days/wk, 2 hrs/day. Plus he comes to most of the workshops which is nice cuz the ta's aren't superb. He comes from Texas and use to be a minister. It's his first year teaching, so maybe his enthusiasm will decrease, but he wants people in the class to succeed
Professor Jarrell is perhaps the best finance professor in Simon school, I still apply what he taught me 6 years ago in my job on a daily basis.

If I could go back and take courses from anyone, it would be for Prof. Jarrell. He is definitely one of the best things that has happened to Simon. He is an absolute authority in the domain of Corporate Finance and Business Valuations. I will cherish every moment that I spent in his classroom. Your education at Simon is incomplete without him.

The best Professor I've had so far. He is one of the most brilliant individuals I have come across and he knows his stuff inside out. His communication is crystal clear and notes are amazing. He is in one word a masterclass.
Great Design but Rude Professor
Best course ever
Outstanding teacher
Awesome Teacher Not organized, hard to get in contact with
He is really good. Makes difficult things very easyyy
No Comments
Cool teacher
He is my dad, so I have to say he is good

Professor DiPiero is the best professor I have ever had at this University. He is extremely smart, approachable, funny, and encouraging. Though the class is really difficult, he makes you feel really smart when you finally understand a tough concept, and helps you get there when you don't. TAKE CLASSES WITH HIM. I'm sad this one's over.
I became a French major just so that he would be my advisor.  By far the best part of my college experience.
Smartest man I ever met, amazing teacher, and really understanding. Tough grader.

I hope you are not overloading if you are signed up for this class.  It's not so much the amount of work as the diffculty of the readings in this class. Be prepared to think outside the box and if you are not an avid participator in class, be prepared for a B+ or less. Talk, talk and I mean TALK in class.  You have to have the mindset to talk!

Major Seminar with DiPiero is the Organic Chemistry of the Humanities Department.  Your writing skills will be whipped into shape by the end and your preconceived notion of anything in this world will be flushed down the toilet as new ideas emerge in his class. Readings are difficult to comprehend and often leave you wanting to cry.
Very knowledgeable and entertaining. Work is not easy, but classtime is extremely enjoyable.  I was definitely very sad to see this class end!
Absolutely brilliant--the best.
greatest prof ever.  we all loved him.  he's absolutely brilliant.  i wish i wasn't finished with french so I could take more classes with him
He is absolutely the best teacher at the U of R.  I have taken courses of his just because he's teaching it.  Entertaining, funny... excellent!
Bridy was a great teacher for MTH 161. Go to his office hours because he helps a lot and clarifies the important concepts you need to know for the exam.

His lecture is very clear and organized. His notes on the board are very tidy and clear. Exam difficulty is fair. His office hours also help a lot and would like to answer questions. A great professor!!!

This guy is a pretty average math teacher. He knows his stuff, and answers questions accurately and helpfully. If Bridy's math class fits your schedule the best, take the class. He's by far not the worst math professor.

He's genuinely a nice person who just loves math. He tries very hard to make sure the material is accessible to all students and does a good job fully answering any question he is asked. Overall just there to help. Occasionally will spend too much of a lecture on the basic info and throw all the harder stuff in at the end but he's always clear.

He was amazing. Always answered questions, and really loved the subject matter. Would change lectures to help those who weren't understanding what was being taught, and was very aware of different learning styles. Honestly, one the best teachers I have ever had.

Professor Bridy really knows his stuff. He always explains topics clearly and if you follow through the course and do the work you definitely should come out doing great. If you get stuck or confused, he does an awesome job of explaining in office hours.

Really great guy. Loves math and is really good at explaining concepts and answering questions. For MTH 150, don't focus too hard on the proofs he gives since they aren't in the exams. All examples he gives are useful and matter the most.

Really sweet guy. He is very clear, organized and definitely knows his stuff.  He does tend to breeze through some of the more complicated topics, forgetting that we're not all PhDs, so he's a little difficult to keep up with at times. However, he is very encouraging, takes all questions and requests seriously and respectfully, and loves math!

I found Rubin's course to be delightful. I took her for a History seminar which was mostly discussion based. She led good discussions and seemed genuinely interested in the lives of each of her students.

She is an easy prof. Attendance is mandatory since all her tests and everything is based on her notes. She gives 3 tests and a 5min project to do. She has a passion for art and thats what made me stay awake. Dont buy the book because its useless, just be in class and youll have all the notes you need for the tests.

Appears to look down on people who she deems below her social class. That's made clear if  she has her suspicions about you. Does not seem at all interested in the students, in general, actually. Rather insincere. It's not that she asks you do do anything difficult. In fact, she treats most students as though they lack intelligence. AVOID!

Terrible at leading discussions and organizing classes. Bland and self-absorbed. Thinks very highly of herself. Learned nothing from the course and her reading selections were all irrelevant. Stay away if you can. Gives no constructive feedback. Every student in the class felt let down. Crimminal that the U of R can take money for her courses.

She is a great professor. And contrary to a prior post, she does not hate men, she just probably despised that student because he seems close-minded. I was a male student in her class, and she was always helpful. If you didn't understand something in class or wanted to debate further, you could always  go to her office hours and talk on end.

nice lady, means well...but she's very unclear in her lectures. she is often scattered and the notes you take don't make much sense later. Part of this is because she is not very engaging. I love American History, but this was soooo boring. I also felt that her essay grading wasn't too fair.

Prof. Rubin got me excited about American cultural history -- I never expected that to happen! But she made history come to life. She asks good questions and really gets the class to think seriously about American cultural life. She is one of the most helpful, kind, and compassionate professors I have encountered at Rochester.
Hates men and makes it very clear. Rude and   Unless you are very liberal stay away
No Comments
Rubin is sweet, intelligent, and I enjoyed her lectures.
No Comments

Course is too hard bic professor gives no practice and no HW. no class recording and no textbook. Exam is hard, u even don't know how and what can go review before test.  Average gpa for this course is low. hard to get A. professor is nice but i hate this course

I really enjoyed Professor Cardot's class. He has funny, engaging lectures and is enthusiastic about people talking in class. Exams/homework can be challenging, but he and TAs are available for help. You can also work on homework with classmates.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Caring']
comment: Metcalf really cares about her students! Classes are mainly just her talking, but it's still enjoyable. There is quite a bit of reading, but she seemed to be pretty nice about grading papers as long as you somewhat showed that you read the material. My one point of critique is she does not give a lot of feedback on papers (but you can talk to her)

Prof Metcalf is very nice and sweet! I agree with the fact that lectures are not that necessary but they are indeed hilarious. If you do your best on your papers you will get a good grade on the class.

Professor Metcalf is really cool but if you don't do the readings she will know. The only grades were papers synthesizing the readings so read them!!! Attendance and participation are graded too but if you're doing the readings it's really easy to contribute.

Lectures are kind of pointless as she just talks about the readings. However, the books she assigns are compelling and she is an easy grader. Its an interesting class, but her lectures aren't so great. Seems like the same lecture over and over again.

First off, she does make smart comments occasionally, however, as a rule, she perpetuates offensive stereotypes and generally condescends third world countries and their state of being. Her analyses concerning the world can be refuted by any fifth grader, and ultimately, I see her as a model employee for Fox News. Amateurism at is finest.

I got an A. Class material interesting, but lectures can get dull as she just likes to talk and talk. 2 take home essay exams and 1 research paper - Very vague grading and guidelines but she is always willing to meet with you to help you as best she can. She expects all papers to be clear, although she doesn't care as much about a "correct answer"
Medical anthropology was one of my favorite classes. She's an engaging professor and helpful. The class is not hard if you do the readings.

Such anamazing prof, she is so interested in what she teaches and loves to discuss, as long as you pay attn in class you will get an A, on the test and paper as long as you put in a lot of effort you will get an A. she is amazing, favorite prof of all four years..VERY FAIR

never took an anthro class before and I loved this class, the books are really interesting, she keeps the discussions going and is just an overall awesome professor, gives you general questions to study before the exams that are really helpful
I HEART METCALF!!! She is so great.  She really enjoys talking about the material and loves going off topic even more.  It's a really easy yet interesting class.
A really great professor. She knows what she's talking about.  The readings/materials are just as great.  I think probably my favorite professor of all my 4 years
The class is alot of fun. Her laugh is worth going to class!
Easy class
A little weird, love the haircut but overall she's very fun and knows what she's talking about. She seems to enjoy teaching..I never skipped a class..so that says a lot about her.
Good class and prof
This professor is the reason I chose to major in anthropology! Lots of reading, but great review and excellent preparation for upper-division classes.
No Comments
Great Professor
really nice professor, lots of reading but reviewed in class
Personally I think he is very good at teaching and he has a weird sense of humor and is funny and the class is pretty long but it will still be amusing.

Amazing professor, modifies the course constantly based on the students' feedback and makes it engaging. I've learned loads and became interested in philo. The lectures are discussion based and provide useful insight into the readings. 2 essays are challenging but you get the chance to rewrite them so getting a good grade is easy if you put work.

Prof. Sherman is great. Lectures can get a little bit dull over time but his killer sense of humor and bright personality save the day. Makes it very easy to do well if you put in a bit of effort. Very little hw and problem sets and reviews are almost exactly what you can expect to see on the tests. Very passionate about the material. Recommended!
Formal logic sounds like a dry subject, but Sherman is genuinely hilarious.

You don't really learn much in lectures. The workshops saved my grade. He posts practice tests that are extremely similar to what will be on the test. The textbook is online but as long as you do the practice problems at the end of each chapter then you're set.

His lectures can be sort of confusing, especially when he goes off on tangents. When he needs to be clear, he can be. Super nice, very approachable, incredibly helpful in office hours. Sentence logic is pretty easy, predicate logic is harder. Midterm and Final, both super easy if you study a bit. Graded Problem Sets are kind of tough and annoying.

This was my second class with him.  I dropped another class just to take this class because I like Sherman so much. One of the most approachable, hilarious, & genuinely kind professors I have ever had.  His lectures can get confusing, but if you go to his office hours, he will explain everything to you.  I highly recommend taking a class with him!

This was my second class with Sherman.  I love him!!!  Highly recommend.  Easy classes--but you will get a lot out of them.  Also, super helpful in office hours and VERY FLEXIBLE.  I wish I could take more classes with him!

He's the best, he knows his stuff, really tries and cares about his students, he is funny, a great lecturer and he's really fair.  I highly, highly, highly recommend him.  Really, there should not be a doubt, if you like the subject matter go for it.  Also he is very helpful, a really cool and super approachable guy, math oriented though.
He is the coolest teacher at rochester. You can get an A if you try.  This guy freaking rocks though.  Really a fun class and a great prof.

Holy heck, this lab class is one of the hardest, most engaging classes the UofR offers.  Make sure you have lotssss of time for revisions and reading.  You really need to plan your time well or you won't get above a B. She's a great teacher though, and take this opportunity to LEARN HOW TO WRITE!
The class is very hard but fun and she is really nice, very helpful, and easy to talk to.
No Comments
Course work is very rought, but expected.  She is super nice and easy to talk to.
No Comments

It is impressive how the TA manages to treat the rubric as optional while still grading as if unstated requirements were obvious to everyone. Losing 20% on correct code for missing features that were never required gives the strong impression that students are being graded less on correctness and more on how well they can guess the TA's mind.

He is approachable, encouraging, and caring. He listens to students' feedback and is willing to adjust activities right away. He also answers questions thoughtfully after class. I always felt respected and heard. He is also clear about grading criteria and expectations, and overall he is very kind and supportive.

BEST PROF EVER. He is willing to listen to his students. Love the soft deadlines for assignments. He gives timely and constructive feedback. The class is very beginner-friendly, coming from me, an international student. His papers are intriguing but def not without challenges! Outside of class, he is very accessible, attentive and understanding.
Amazing professor! take his class!

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I like him!!!

Highly recommend everyone at UR to take Orisa's writing course! He is not strict with deadlines and cares about his students. As long as you do all the informal and formal assignments, you will be okay with this course.

One of the best professors I've had at Rochester. Takes the time to listen to his students, gives great feedback and suggestions, and is accessible even at night on a weekend. Also a very lenient grader!!!

I personally found the class more boring than what I went in expecting. However, I don't regret taking it. I'm probably in the minority, but I did not enjoy the readings and didn't feel super interested in the material. However, I did enjoy the environment of the class. Santiago is very caring, understanding, and just an overall amazing human!
One of the best professors I've had here. Truly a gem in the Rochester community!

Amazing instructor and person - he cares for his students and frequently takes time to hear out (and apply) our opinions/suggestions in class. Course content is very engaging if you are interested in his writing course topic. The course schedule is structured so that all writing assignments are doable on time without unnecessary stress.

Professor Morrice is a very caring, thoughtful, and human professor. The readings he selects are very insightful and the discussions that follow are very well mediated and enjoyable to participate in. He also gives lots of freedom in his writing prompts which means that you can almost always find something fun you would enjoy writing about.

He is AMAZING! You will have the best reading discussion ever in his class! He also gives you fair grades, and they are usually pretty good as long as you follow his suggestions. Don't be afraid to catch him up after class and ask him anything you don't understand! He'll explain every comment he gave to your paper and help you to write better :)

What a legendary professor! He became a professor in the writing department of Rochester last year, but he has already become one of the highly recommended professors! His lectures are inspirational! Take him!
Professor Morrice holds AMAZING discussions in classes. I really enjoyed attending his writing classes and he gives you both fair grades and constructive feedbacks.

You can really tell Prof. Renninger cares about teaching. He explains the material so well, and he always gauges student comprehension in class. Go to class and workshop, and the homework and exams, while not being a walk in the park, should have no surprises. If you are considering graduate school in physics or optics, this class is so valuable.

Prof. Renninger is clearly an expert in the material and his homework and exams are very fair.  The course material is easy to follow, and closely follows the textbook, which is a good resource if you need additional explanation.  If you listen to his advice and go over material on your own you'll save yourself a lot of time and frustration.
Prof. Renninger teaches a hard class, but he is very well-organized and makes the content seem easy. Homework is well-written and useful, exams are extremely fair and easy. Great class overall.
He was a great professor, but really hard class. Super grateful he let me pass.
Midterm is easy, but the final, wow.

Professor Renninger is amazing. He is clear with his lecture content and you can tell he wants you to succeed. He is always open to answering questions you have about the course content. He will involve students in his lectures by asking questions. I highly recommend you take his class if you are pursuing physics.

His teaching style is easy to follow and you will learn a lot of helpful concepts that you will use outside of this class in other classes! Homework assignments can be difficult but office hours and workshops set up help a lot!

Know that I took this class in spring 2022. A lot of people who took this class last year rated it very low, but you can clearly tell he took feedback and seriously improved. His lectures are some of the best I have seen, and he clearly cares about students and is always willing to take quesitons. He has seriously improved.

Prof. Renninger is great. He is so passionate about his job, and you can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to do well. His lectures are clear and go hand in hand with the hw assignments. He is always willing to help and he actually listens to his students when we give him feedback about the course.

This was hands down the hardest math I've taken. Not because the material itself was extremely difficult, but because his handwriting is near impossible to decipher, and the things he teaches are only a light skimming of what he asks for on the 12-hour homework assignments. The TAs are going to be how you get through this class.

He was not helpful in learning what is likely some of the hardest math people will attempt to learn. He can be unforgiving and when asked to do explicit things by students he would often not do them. All the learning is done through the TA's and workshop so attend those and be prepared to take a graduate level course.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This man was such a lazy professor and all your learning is through the TAs. His handwriting is impossible to read and he never responds to emails. It is apparent he does not care for students and does not care about actually teaching us anything.

Taught the Undergraduate class as a Graduate class and was one of the most confusing math classes I have ever taken. The professor seldom cares about the students and doesn't really respond to emails. It's possible that it may be better taught in person, but this semester was especially difficult.

Professor Lee is excellent for MTH 162. Going into the course I was very scared, but he presents the material in an extremely clear, straightforward, and organized way. He frequently pauses and asks the class if they have questions. He has clear answers to these as well. Super nice, very helpful if you speak to him one on one. A great Prof!

Best calc teacher I have had so far. During class, he gives examples of the concepts and uses student participation to answer them. Constantly asks if anyone has questions. Tests are very straightforward but the calc deparment expects you to memorize everything & work hard. Don't fall behind!
Lectures are boring and he just throws everything to you. There is no connection between chapters, or at least he failed to find them.
I barely understood what went on during lecture, I basically taught everything to myself
hard, but very understanding teacher and personable too.

he's a really nice guy but the lectures are not very engaging and content is gone through very quickly. exams in my opinion were also pretty difficult, having a good calc background would be beneficial. if you have to take 209, take it with a diff professor.

The instructor relies heavily on slides, but the slides did not include concepts in very detail, many concepts were not organized, and he was only reading them. He needs more practice in teaching. He focuses heavily on math when discussing intertemporal models and utility maximization problems, although he was unable to explain the math clearly.
Not very experienced with teaching. Lectures were complicated and unorganized. In-class time was just him reading off the notes.
He does't know what he is talking about.
Classes aren't worth going to.

Prof. Seiferas is very helpful, inviting students to his office anytime. Main problem is many students are forced to take class without having the prerequisite, for them the class obscenely hard and the lectures cryptic. I wish he would stick more closely to a textbook- papers he gives for us to read require reading many other papers to comprehend.

The guy is ferociously talented. I have got to give him that and due to that nature, he is far beyond comprehend-able. It is impossible to follow him in class. Just terrifying difficult in the beginning but it gets better. Still teaching could be a lot better. he is dedicated though but too brilliant to understand student are not as fluent as him!!

Really cares about his students and welcomes feedback.  Not a very good lecturer though, especially when he uses Powerpoint slides.  Tests were surprisingly hard.  Expect to do a LOT of extra studying outside of class.

Great prof, and exams are very true to the course material (clear format; she tells you some things she will ask beforehand). The final project (which you can do either individually or in a group) is very interesting and fun, and you can pick any topic you want. Also very relevant to actuarial roles if that interests you.

Prof Polak is incredibly nice and flexible. She is receptive to feedback from students and TAs and ensures that grading is completed quickly and accurately. Her lectures are easy to follow and reflect the content on homework and exams.

I really enjoyed her lectures and the fact that she takes time to answer questions. Recitation are very helpful if you have a good TA. I wish she wouldn't use textbook officialy because university adds it to course costs. The book is free on line.
She is engaging in class, and makes an effort to try and interact with students.

Assignments every week which aren't lengthy, but they're so horribly worded that you it's hard to understand what she wants you to do. There's no curve in the class. Also her teaching made me upset because she doesn't really know what she's doing, as she's new to Java. This made it harder to learn because she was also learning

CSC 161 was fairly easy for beginners in programming. Polak did a pretty good job of lecturing and demonstrating coding while she was teaching. The hws and midterms were not hard, though the final is a bit tough. Overall, she was pretty nice and approachable. I like her.

Polak does care about students, but she cares more about Cryptography than this class. Outside of the boring lectures, she uses AI to generate labs/projects (said so herself). The only project she made herself was given over Spring break, was difficult for no reason, had unclear instructions, and wasn't relevant at all to the the class material.
She gives curves and practice exams and plays video about dancing.

Would never take her again, It was a mistake. She is understanding but her teaching is so egregious and she is unapproachable. Her office hours are so short and she does not respond to emails. It seems as though she is new to teaching.

Polak struggled at the beginning because the official language of the class was JAVA, but she is used to coding in Python. As the semester progressed, she became better at it. To me, the class was easy because I learned everything but graphs in high school. The lectures were okay and I liked her project because I am a cryptography enthusiast.

Polak was lit. She explains hard topics in a way that's easy to understand and makes sure the class is following along with the info. Also very thorough with lectures and explains stuff step by step. Hw was kinda hard tho but the exams were light.
Interesting lectures

Never before have I seen a professor who cares so little about his course. He claims that attendance is mandatory and that you will lose points if you do not attend, and yet he himself seems to not bother showing up half the time. You only find out that he wont be there when the TA tells you since he doesn't bother sending an email.

Is a super careless professor. He rarely shows up for class and makes his TAs teach whatever he doesn't feel like doing that day. Attendance is mandatory, but it's a joke because he doesn't care if you don't show up. Assignments are easy once the TA tells you what they are.

This was a pretty ridiculous class. No one showed up on time and people just stopped trying, and the prof just didn't seem to want to do anything about it. He'd tell us each day, 'it'd be nice if you showed up on time' but there weren't any repercussions if people didn't. I would have actually liked to get a lot of out this class, but alas.

If you do your work and ask the TAs for help, you will come out with an A without using too much brain power. However, Brady is incredibly negligent in showing up to teach the class or the students. The entire class is disorganized, and your grade is determined by one assignment that he won't teach you how to do.  It is a miracle he has a job here.

Don't take a class with this professor. Last semester I took his intro to debate class, and he would skip every other class leaving his overworked TAs to teach the class. He just wants to stack the debate team with people. 
His absences though did make the class easy because he gave up teaching after a few slideshow monologues.

He doesn't really teach much about debate, he just reads off long slideshows about the structure of debates. The class isn't as much about critical thinking and argument as how to win at a debate tournament. He's pretty much impossible to get ahold of outside of class and can be extremely unorganized sometimes

he does not teach at all, he reads off of long slideshows. he is also extremely unorganized, he tends to forget what he put on the syllabus. not once did he ever explain how to do projects/group assignments. he doesn't even introduce debate, all just trying to get you to join the debate team.

Two reasons I didn't like this class: 1. This isn't "how to construct a dynamic, thought provoking arguments". This class is "how to win at the sport that is college debate", unless you love high school policy debate, you will hate this class as I do. 2. For a debate class. Fletcher is incredibly disorganized and extremely frustrating to work for.

Four total debates (midterm, two finals and one SPAR/spontaneous debate) and one group presentation. Great and accessible professor! Even though this was an intro class, more experienced peers made debates more challenging and fun

He saw that I was really struggling with a major depressive episode and worked with me outside of the classroom to get the help I needed. It's a demanding class and the first difficult CHE course in the curriculum. I loved it so much I'm taking it again (definitely not because I need to fix my gpa) next year!

His lectures are great; he writes out the notes with you and adds extra details, but read the textbook to supplement the material. Sometimes, the sample problems in the textbook are similar, or at least they give you a better idea of how to approach HWs and tests. Recitations — he does a good job of going through problems. Slack him with questions!

Foster was really funny in lectures, most of the time he just writes things on his ipad the entire lecture, but lab is really fun and if you get to know him and talk to him hes going to be very chill and really down to earth. Once we made him seat every single student to where we sit usually and he did it easily so that was impressive.

His lectures are great and he is easy to understand. He makes things pretty entertaining but the exams tend to be really hard. However, he gives a ton of partial credit and the curve is pretty heavy. He's very clear about what is gonna be on exams but sometimes throws in questions that no one can do, but it all works out in the curve.

The exams take a large amount of your final grade, and they are usually pretty difficult. Average will be like 50% 60%, but he will decide final grade wisely. His lecture is perfect. The problem comes from the course material that is not difficult to be taught in general, understandable language

Very full of himself. He claims he's accommodating at the beginning of the year but is not. If you are struggling in his class talk to the TAs they will be more helpful than him. Go to office hours as frequently as you can.
Foster makes Separations a class you want to go to. Legendary stories and immaculate lecture notes every time. Homework and Exams are a breath of fresh air compared to CHE 243
This legend sips on luxurious beers.  Very positive guy, nothing but respect for him.

Foster is so chill in CHE250.  He beat us up in 243 but he's an angel in 250.  Lectures are laid back with fun stories told by him, hw is not long, exams are short, and he is a much nicer grader.  You'll still learn a lot as he still keeps things professional once he gets his "acting gear" together.

Foster is very full of himself, and hard to reach out to. Very "my way or the highway" mentality, which, when you reach out to him when you're struggling, is very unhelpful. Also your grade is almost all based on your exams, with no way to earn points if you have a bad day. Homeworks are also often long, confusing, and very difficult. Prepare.
The workload is a lot but this is one of the more interesting courses that I took from the CHE department
Great at explaining concepts. I hate his exams and the way he grades them. Way too long, difficult, and a tough grader.
Great teacher, but the grade is test-heavy (75% is test-based). Labs were fun, but make sure you do everything that is "suggested." Take his advice about getting ahead on the work (esp labs).

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: He is kinda like the big brother that likes messing and tormenting his little siblings only to say "gotcha!" at the end. Very big ego but overall not that bad.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Test Heavy is the best way to describe this class, although its not outlined in the grading criteria you're grade will be decided entirely by your tests. The final isn't as bad as it seems, but do not have a bad day on a midterm as it will cost you your final grade. Very clear and direct professor, definitely full of himself but you'll get over it.

Professor Foster a high opinion of himself, and a lot of his decisions and actions are guided by his own ego. He tries too hard to appear intelligent, often brags about how he likes to solve equations in his free time, and purposely obfuscates questions and material. He also acts like a brofessor, maybe so students will like him more.  I dunno.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Great professor. Clearly intelligent and well-read, but also expects a certain level of effort on your part. Homework isn't a large portion of the grade, but is critical to understanding the problems on exams.

This class is k, but the final was quite challenging. It also requires a lot of time doing HW. A lot of people think Prof. Foster is a good guy but I can definitely feel that he is kinda biased against students whose English are not their first language.

I came into this class thinking I was going to hate it.  Instead, it turned into my favorite class thanks to Foster.  His lectures are incredibly detailed and engaging, and seriously help you learn.  He spends time after every class just answering students' questions.  Incredibly helpful and friendly.  Best prof I've had in my two years here.

Foster is an amazing lecturer! Very clear and organized, but if you don't go to class you don't get his notes. Gives lots of homework that if you do yourself and actually understand the tests aren't bad. Always willing to answer questions or go more in depth. Gives real world applications to make it more interesting. Best professor I've ever had.

Learned a lot in Fluids. He's very passionate about the subject and does a good job explaining tough material. Tests are tough but if you do the homework, go to office hours, and study you'll be fine.

Great teacher and knows his stuff for sure. This is a really difficult class but necessarily difficult given the subject manner (Transport is really hard everywhere according to friends I have taking it at other universities). Foster is approachable and his lectures are fast paced and give you what you need to understand the material.

This professor might have good verbal communication skills, but that is it. He tries to make himself seem like an expert, who is really into it. His answers, to questions are brief and lack any depth. He assigns the same homeworks and solutions are typed over from other sources. He simply copies the book over onto the board. Too superficial.
Fantastic, brilliant, helpful, and the lessons stuck with me.
He is a very interesting man. I love the way he teaches the course, but honestly he's a monster. I call him Captain Kodak. He puts on a quality act.
Possibly the best professor I have had at the University of Rochester. He will make you work, but he is definitely helpful and extremely enthusiastic about the material.

Also had him for CHE/BME 259. Great teacher.  He works in this field, so he really loves what he does. Helpful, clear, and organized. I actually LEARNED from his class. One of the Best professors I've had.
Enthusiastic about the material and always available for extra help.  Really loves teaching and wants students to succeed.

He really cares about what he is teaching and goes the extra mile for it. The class is hard, but he's fair and wants everyone tp succeed. Be prepared to work your ass off but your actually going to be learning a lot
Foster is the man. Fluids isn't an easy course but he endlessly facilitates help. He even goes to the recitations! This man knows and loves what he's teaching. One of my favorite professors at UR.
Be prepared to work. Look over your notes after class and ask questions about stuff you don't get.

Professor really cares about students, and does his best to keep you up to date and make you feel good about yourself... Sometimes he doesn't answer questions clearly and bypasses them... but overall a good professor
Great professor; really likes teaching.  Hard class but as long as you go to lecture and keep up with the homework you will do fine.  He really wants his students to do well.

One of the best engineering professors in this university. Lectures are fast paced but informative. Exams and homework are difficult but supportive of the course material. Very approachable and a great guy.
good
Great Prof, yep VERY HOT....I love his class.

Excellent Prof.Expert on material, cares about students, I learned allot.I wish he taught every course I took.  No doubt the best prof in the university. Yea, he's hot, but the great thing is that he doesn't know he's hot, or at least I don't think he does. Very approachable, cares about students.
um.. yeah, good prof, I like his class but... come on girls...he could be our dad...do we get distracted by our dads?, I think not...lets rate the class not the looks.
Well known at the UofR for two things:  1. an excellent prof who really knows what he's doin and a great teacher who cares about students, 2. total hottie, distractingly good looking.
Excellent Prof, really knows the subject, and distractingly good looking. Brilliant and HOT.
Excellent Prof, knows his stuff
Excellent Professor- communicates well

I don't think he teaches well, not only because he's not an AI expert, but also due to unclear slides and assignments. There are no hints for homework in the slides, and his exams have too many questions to finish. The midterm average was 79/100. His slides are fixed by Berkeley's CS188, but it's better to watch the videos than take Kang's course.
Professor Moon is funny and seems like a great guy. However, beware that he takes a long time to respond to emails and grade papers. Overall, good class.
No clear grading guidelines and harsh essay grader

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Amazing prof! Very reading intensive, but if you pace yourself and are strategic it's fine. He does take a long time to grade, but his feedback is thorough. Attendance not mandatory, but go to lectures because they really help and he gives important updates about assignments. Also go to his office hours-he's really hilarious and great to talk to!

He grades extremely late (papers weren't graded for around 2 months, while in the meantime he would give more papers), he was very vague with assignments, and would have papers listed on the syllabus for a date that was nowhere near the date he gave them and gave no warning about assigning papers or finals, and his lectures are very involved.

Professor moon is overall okay but there is definitely room for improvement. Homework can be a lot of reading but you can definitely get away with not reading everything; it's more tedious than difficult. Grading can be a bit subjective but not horrible. He takes ages to grade your papers and assignments.
this is the worst class I have taken in my four years as a mechanical engineering student

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Prof. Borrelli's lectures are really in depth and a bit technical, but this is not always the information that we are expected to know. It takes a bit to figure out what you are expected to take away from each class. But it's a super interesting class that crosses over a lot of disciplines!

Not very suitable for non-environmental majors. I didn't feel like learning anything from this class, and the test was graded very harshly. Although Professor Borrelli is really nice, the materials are heavy to study. I received all As in other courses but received a B+ in this 100-level class. You have to get 95 to earn an A so it's tough.

Professor Borelli is knowledgeable but very unapproachable. She does have lots of extra credit opportunities but the class material is too heavy for an intro class or anybody looking to take an elective. The TA in charge has an attitude and the exams are fair but it is a lot of material to memorize. Would not waste the time in this.

Didn't really care for her class. Borrelli was very dry and just reads off her slides for lectures, making it very difficult to pay attention. She has extra credit which is nice, but there is no curve. Tests are kinda hard, but if you study you'll be fine. She grades strict on homework and tests. Class is hit and miss.

Professor Borelli is a real sweetheart. Even though this was her first time teaching over zoom she made sure to be well-prepared for classes and made a lot of effort to make sure we all knew what was happening. She also provided a lot of optional extra credit to studnts and even allowed assignments to be attempted again after initial submission.
Not too interesting in class. Speaks real slow, but is a fair grader and organizes awesome specially curated trips into the archives of George Eastman House.
Good professor. Explains things well, likes discussion.
Boring lecture with awkward questions (followed by awkward silences); unclear syllabus/assignments.

Lectures can be kind of boring and important material kind of hard to pick out. Field trips to George Eastman House can be interesting, though. She is flattered when students take interest and asks questions during her lectures. Sometimes she pulls material out of no where for the test though. You really do get a good base knowledge. Lenient grader
excellent teacher
interesting subject, knowledgeable teacher--looking at slides in the dark makes you want to sleep every time though.

She's nice but the class is rather boring. The material could be interesting but she talks from the second you walk in until class is over. She expects you to already know a lot even though it was an INTRO class.

Only saw the guy once the entire semester. The worksheets seem to have been in use for like 20 years and are kind of cluttered and disorganized. The course website is a total mess. Seems to just be completion graded.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I never had any contact with him, all of my learning was done independently or with TAs. It's clear that he's tired of teaching this course given that he has no part in it whatsoever, and he gives out Incompletes like candy to those who procrastinate. It is a hard course but if you start early and pace yourself its not too bad. I, however, did not.
I never even exchanged an email with this guy, never saw him in person. The TAs were great though! Just make sure you start the workload before the last few weeks of class.

If you're here because you are considering self paced physics, DO NOT DO IT. 
First of all, he has no clue how to use Blackboard. Assignments are nearly impossible to find, somethings are listed in multiple places, or nowhere at all, and he never updates his assignments ever. Not to mention the TAs will yell at you in front of the entire class.

This class is not worth it if you can't pace yourself. There are weekly homeworks and quizzes(13), 4 midterms, and a final. It is a lot of work. Ask the TAs for help and attend workshops. I learned most of the material through Crash Course, Prof Dave Explains, & Khan Academy. The homeworks & answer keys are from 3 years ago and haven't been updated

tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Honestly, Dr. Rich's lectures are not engaging at all, he just reads off of outdated slides I don't think he even made himself. Tests (only 2) are pretty easy if you just memorize info from the slides. Pop quizzes are graded on completion, so show up to lecture. Didn't really learn anything long-term, but if you just do your work it isn't a hard A.

PHLT 103 was a snoozefest. Rich mainly reads off his slides or speaker notes. I felt as though I learned nothing of importance in epidemiology. Adding on, I wish the grading criteria were more lenient. If you lose 1 point on your homework, your overall grade goes down by 1%. My TA graded my homeworkers harshly, so be aware of the grading system!!!

tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Boring lectures (made me hate epidemiology even tho it's my major). Lots of pop quizzes. HWs took really long and TAs grade so harshly. Tests are just the slides so just memorize those (if you can memorize 60 slides for every lecture lol). He barely shows up to class; the entirety of December was just guest lecturers/recorded lectures.

Dr. Rich was near impossible to reach outside of classroom hours. He would take days, if not weeks, to respond to my emails, and even then was very difficult to schedule with. To be honest, he made me disinterested in epidemiology.

Dr. Rich's lectures can be somewhat boring, but some of the guest lecturers are pretty interesting. Although there was a textbook, all the test material is from information from the slides so you don't really need the textbook. Know the definitions of different terms for the exams.

Dr. Rich is a good person, but his lectures were somewhat boring. I think this might just be because epidemiology as a whole isn't the most exciting. Try and memorize the slides he presents in lecture, since the exams mimic these slides. I purchased a textbook for this class but never used it and did fine, so I would recommend going without one.

If you do not have interest in epidemiology, you will find this class very boring. Dr. Rich just reads exactly what are on the lecture slides and adds nothing else. The guest lectures are interesting. One midterm and final which are multiple choice and are easy if you memorize the important concepts. Homework isn't hard, but tedious.

Professor Rich speaks in a monotone voice and his lectures are very boring. The course is difficult because we are given no study material except for the slides and pop quizzes. 60% of your grade is from two exams so you must do well.
