If you are good at memorizing and teaching yourself concepts, you'll be fine. Otherwise, this course will be hard.

Professor Rich does not care about his students and reads off the slides which is not helpful. He does not try to make the class easier and the exams are difficult. Every class consists of around 60 slides that need to be memorized for the exams. He holds his office hours off campus which is not useful for students.

I thought I was gonna like Public Health but I was wrong. This man is boring as hell, I don't pay 80k for a slide reader. His guest lecturers he hires while he is on vacation in Europe are somewhat better than him. There are only a midterm and final which determine your grade. If you are actually interested sure take this, otherwise don't bother.

tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: This class may be easy if you have an interest for epidemiology, however I would not recommend taking this class if it is your first time doing public health.Professor Rich constantly reads off his power point slides during classtime, and his voice is rather monotonous, which may make it hard to pay attention. He only gives one midterm, so do well!

good lecturer, not too boring that youd fall asleep in and stays on track. Always willing to help students and answer questions/emails. Class is pretty basic, not very hard content, but there is a lot to memorize. Textbook is nice but not necessary, 99% of the exam is covered in lecture slides. Stay on top of hw and pop quizzes, will be a breeze
Honestly the reason I am going to study Epidemiology. A really kind, down-to-Earth professor. Just go to lecture and take notes and you will be good to go!
Very nice and accessible professor who really knows his stuff. You do need to study for his class (he gives pop quizzes) and homework grades are somewhat dependent on your TA.

The class itself was fun for me personally as it actually involved getting out and doing activities. What ruined the class for me was the very harsh grading of the final which to me seemed like was on track to do well based off of his comments but ended up getting a bad grade which tanked my GPA.

You have to spend 1.5 hours outdoors every week on top of homework. Also, he grades based on what he thinks and if he does not agree with you, you will get points off. He will set up meetings with you which almost automatically gets you a better grade. The class was not difficult itself, I just did not enjoy it at all.

Gave surface level feedback, often it seemed that he skimmed the paper at best, sometimes giving feedback that was resolved in the next paragraph. Often seemed to not take students opinions in class discussion seriously until someone said his opinion. Grades arbitrarily. Grading and email replies take a long time.

didn't feel that the class was hard but i never felt like he took my perspective seriously in class discussions and he rarely gave insightful feedback. readings have to be finished before lectures and some of them are strange. interest in the outdoors is almost a requirement

He will probably be harsh on your initial drafts, but just follow his notes and revise accordingly, and you will receive a satisfactory grade for the final draft.
If you are not very passionate about outdoor activities, he might not be the best choice for WRTG 105.

Grades randomly. Many times he would leave feedback that clearly showed he did not read the entire paper and that he was unwilling to see things from a different perspective. Also, for an outdoor-based writing class, he brought up issues like class and race a lot. Cool guy, bad professor.

If you are an incoming freshman AVOID THIS PROFESSOR at all costs. He is the most unfair and illogical grader ever. He grades without a rubric, and deducts vast amounts of points for small errors in papers. I came into this class as an experienced writer writing for my high school newspaper for 3 years, with over 50 published articles.
best professor I have ever had.
He will tear your GPA apart for ambiguous reasons. No mercy!
I really liked him but he grades his papers hard. Class was discussions based and mandatory attendance. Daily assignments are light but the 3 papers hits hard.

Justin was an extremely helpful professor and always gave useful feedback. The lessons were interesting a discussion-based. The assignments were difficult, but he is helpful with them and is allows for an extension if it means it will improve your work!
Hes nice enough, but somehow he made an interesting course boring. Extremely tough grader, I got a D+ even though I took AP English in high school. Use the writing center, not him.

Professor Coyne is patient to answer students' questions, and he gives specific and helpful suggestions to students' essays. He is always prepared for course so don't forget to read the reading materials before classes!

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Group projects', 'So many papers']
comment: He managed to make a class on inequality boring. The professor doesnt know how to teach, doesnt know how to facilitate a discussion, and grades harshly based on a super niche criteria of his work. I managed to get an A-, but there was a lot of work, and only a few things actually mattered for my grade.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: He is an extremely friendly professor who wants you to become a better writer. He gives very specific and good feedback but you have to be willing to talk to him either outside of class or during. He helps you analyze all the texts we read (and there are a lot of them!) and really wants his students to understand the topics.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: - Three papers over the semester - Readings for every week - Mandatory attendance - Tough grader
Seem like as long as you do spend your time and effort on the papers, you will get a decent grade. The workload is not heavy and the prof is really nice and willing to help anytime

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: He is a pretty nice guy, quite accessible outside of class. You do need to go to class. He gives good feedback sometimes. He seems to lack the motivation to fully read/understand what you write, almost like he skims. It seems that he reads but not fully like he should, for a wrt teacher. He picks uninteresting topics.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Pretty hard grader but gives good feedback so you're able to learn from your mistakes and improve over time. Attendance super important, but if there are extenuating circumstances he's pretty understanding. He's pretty much always open to talking about concerns or ideas outside of class, so just reach out if you want to talk about your work.
Yes, he is a tough grader. But he is super approachable and friendly in and out of class.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Very strict grader and will take off a significant amount participation points form your final grade even if you arrive a few minutes late to class or don't participate. Is ready to read and provide feedback for several drafts of your assignment given that they are sent at least a day prior to the deadline

The professor is nice, but beware his class is not well organized. The first half of 448 will be your easiest class. But in the second half you will be thrown into tons of difficult coding assignments. The notes are half pictures so studying for paper exams is impossible.

There is no exam, no homework, only (six) projects that will make you put your hands on and get to learn parallel programming using some initial samples from lectures' codes. The TAs and the professor do answer your questions but it is your code so don't expect them to find your errors, they will tell you maybe what to look for.

He is great at teaching programming and you will learn a lot from him. BUT the quizzes were quite tricky. The exams and projects were fair game except the TA's made mistakes in grading them VERY OFTEN.
A really good introduction to quantum formalism, and very organized lectures and notes!

I really like how he structured the class. Cheat sheets, drop lowest exam score, AND each exam was curved. I do think he genuinely taught the content well in a way that non-physics majors could understand. Physics II is a lot of your own understanding and practice regardless of the professor, but I think he still did a great job.

Prof. Blok's Quantum Theory course was easily the most interesting rendition of quantum mechanics I've ever taken. Because he's a quantum computing researcher, he had lots of interesting examples to connect to in class, and he was very clear about what were still "open questions" in the field. I struggled with the math in the course, but LOVED it!

During the first day of PHYS 114 lecture, Professor Blok said he was here to guide us through the material, not teach us. This was highly discouraging to hear. I also did not like how homework was only 10% of your grade and some of the exam questions were worded weirdly.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: One of the best professors in Black/African-American literature. Very kind and understanding. Great lectures. Clear grading as well - class structure is a few reading responses, and 2-3 essays, participation, and lesson plan questions.

Prof. Tucker is so clearly a master of the subjects which he lectures on. If you're willing to participate in class (which you totally should), you will grow so much more. He's kind, responsive to emails and questions, and all-around is a professor I've learned a lot from. I look forward to continuing to take his classes.

Always respectful, super happy to help, wonderful prof. My class was almost entirely discussion based and he always found a way to keep it going and get people engaged even on a Monday morning. Very light workload, technically all readings are required but you can do well only reading the ones that you have to respond to (trust me). Great guy.
Excellent Professor who gives great lectures and detailed feedback on your assignments. Also gives extremely clear grading criteria which I found to be extremely helpful. Would definitely recommend!

EXCELLENT PROFESSOR. I absolutely loved his teaching style, and you can tell he genuinely loves what he does. He speaks softly, but you hang on to every word. He facilitates a classroom where you walk away having a better understanding of the course and why you study what you love.
Professor Tucker has an amazing ability to keep everyone in his classes involved and interested. He has a genuine ability to make students feel as though they and their opinion truly matter.
One of my favorite professors.  Genuinely interested in his students and cultivating their intellectual pursuits.

GREAT professor.  Taught a very intresting class and attempted to get to know everyone in a large class.  Assigns a fair amount of work and you will do well in the class if you keep up.  Plus, he gave NO tests!!

Jeff Tucker is a kind, patient, helpful, reliable teacher with a genuine concern for education and a strong desire to foster intellectual interests in his students.  I couldn't possibly say enough nice things about him.
Anyone you can make Poe boring is a terrible professor.  Staying awake during his class was the only challenge I faced.
He's awesome, really helpful and a professional sweetheart --make sense?e

Prof Korn is an excellent professor. He would always make sure that his students are learning the Italian language and that they practice their writing and conversational skills. As a matter of grading, he can be a tough grader sometimes but he would always give good feedback. Because of COVID we did not have quizzes, instead, we had papers.

Although he was not bad last semester in IT101 he has made a 180 in his teaching and his grading. He is a strict professor and does not listen well to student feedback, as he finds ways to justify his harshness. You need to go to class, but even if you participate don't expect 100%. Exams- he will take points off even if your answer is right.

Andrew is passionate about Italian language and culture and has vast experience inside and outside the classroom.  I was afraid to start learning a new language and he gave me the confidence to not only try but persist, which is critical in language acquisition.  When Andrew tells me, bravissima!, it is worth all the work.

He is charismatic and dedicated to being a good teacher. Told a funny story about eating raw chicken in Japan. Did a final showing of the class' final project of sound design though it's not necessary. Since there are few jobs in sound design, I don't recommend taking more classes. Definitely read the book on sound design to prepare for quiz.

Prof. Lavaque is so passionate about what he teaches, he makes the class so fun. He is quite hands-off in his approach and mostly leaves you to figure things out by yourself, but he or the TAs will always help if you get stuck. The projects take a lot of time, but they're not brain-rackingly difficult.

Esteemed professor with loads of industry experience. Projects are structured with real-world-clients in mind. Genuinely cares for his students' success and is understanding when life get tough. Don't slack off or you can easily get behind. 

*another rating said he expects you to know certain software, but it's literally listed in the pre-reqs

He is known for being irresponsible, not only been ignoring the students questions via Zoom, but also been a procrastinator in terms of giving grades and assignments. The class is frankly boring and irrelevant to the topic. He would talk about softwares which we should be already familiar with. Therefore, I don't suggest to take this course.

If you're planning to take this class, think again. Previously, I expected the class to be super fun and interesting. Yet, it turns out to be unpleasant and unsatisfying. He's known for his unpunctuality of getting the class started, his irresponsibility, ungenerous, and his irrelevant teaching. Thus, I won't recommend students to take this class.
Easy and fun class, just do the work and for the most part you will be fine.

Professor Lavaque is a great guy.  He's heavily decorated and really knows what he's talking about when it comes to sound production.  He's always quick to give good feedback, and won't hesitate to help if anything isn't clear.  His classes aren't easy per se, but it's the kind of hard work you have fun with.

Very fun and worthwile class! Class is mostly project-based, and it really gets you familiar with the tools that professionals in the field use (of which he is one - an Emmy-winner). His demos can be rushed somewhat unclear at times, but he takes a "learn by doing" approach to teaching the class.

Professor Caie is undoubtedly brilliant. He completed his Doctorate in 2011, and already has 2 papers published in the Philosophical Review. Many of the best tenured philosophers have only achieved just 1 publication in the Review throughout their careers. However, he has struggles as a lecturer in presenting ideas clearly and stimulating a class.

Michael Caie is a professor that means well, but ultimately fails at teaching. He is a nice enough person, but isn't the sort of person you want teaching you. This becomes particularly important when his specialties are logic and philosophy of language--two areas that are easy to become confused in. Ultimately, I would have to say to pass on Caie.

In case he hasn't retired by next summer, don't take this course. His grading criteria is based on regurgitation of definitions, not demonstrated comprehension and ability. He's rude and condescending to students. Don't make the mistake of ruining your summer by taking this course- you won't enjoy it, and  you won't get the scores you want.

Taking this class in the summer might be the worst decision you ever make.  Unless you have previously taken the course or AP Chem in high school I would not recommend taking it.He does not teach during the year and there's a reason why.  Don't be a fool in thinking it will be easier over the summer.  It's not and you won't get the grade you want.

15 weeks of gen chem in a 6 week session is difficult.  Dr. Hickey paces the course as well as can be expected, but without any time to let the material sink in, it can be tough to keep up.  The fact that Dr. Hickey demands a level of mastery in excess of other faculty at the U or R translates into brutal exams on a very compressed schedule.

Tests really don't reflect what he teaches. He asks you to fully interpret things that he gives you a rudimentary description of. He does know his subject material quite well, though. But most importantly, he might be the slowest teacher ever.
He is a very good teacher but his tests are extremely hard he wants you to be a master at the topic and talk about it as though you have been studying it for years for a general chemistry course.

You won't learn economics directly in this professor's class; he shares trivial details from his own life and leaves it to you to reflect on what.if anything—you've actually learned. he assigns bizarre CK. If you're the type of student who expects knowledge to be delivered straight to you in the classroom, dont take his course it will be a disaster

Super entertaining lectures that you can learn a lot from if your open minded. But homework is very time consuming and mostly busy work. Tests are also very rough, they are hard to study for and unnecessarily off topic.
I passed, but did I learn anything? Not really. Did I enjoy it, not really.

Long and diffcult Exams/HWS. Lectures are interesting, but can be confusing and rushed. If you want a straightfoward class, not for you. Very manageable if you do all HW/EC, exam grades can be forgiving if you do those. Outside of class, hes a awesome guy and very knowledgable, just nuts. He teaches how to think economically. !!Read the syllabus!!

I think he's an exceptional intro economics professor, and I always enjoy discussing intellectual questions with him. IMO, try to speak to him one on one, and brush off his lecture persona. There's a lot you can learn from him. However, be aware that he lacks professional boundaries—I had to learn to not take *anything* he said to heart.
confusing lectures, really long weekly homeworks, bad attitude. just don't do it bro

He often goes off on tangents and jumps around / skips more than half of his slides. He comes up with unnecessary references and takes hours to explain logical things that could have been easily explained through a few beginner-level terms. No textbook. You'll also be forced to dedicate hours every week to assignments (TA said 8 hours on average).

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']
comment: Ends up being more confusing/frustrating than helpful. Homework's extremely wordy, long, and dense. Expect tons of unnecessary stress for an intro-level course. His teaching's also very unstructured and disorganized. Exams and grading criteria don't make any sense and are often arbitrary.

rizzo is so silly and i love him dearly! he's very accessible, go to office hours, you have to care about the class to do well in it! the homework assignments for 108 were a bit on the denser side, but they're rewarding!

Professor Rizzo is a character but I think he is a professor you need to take at some point at the U of R. His homework do get long but they are not graded hard and every project is a guaranteed A as long as you do it. His lectures are all over the place and it seems like he is on acid but he's just super enthusiastic.

this course is about thinking about the way the world works. There's no use of textbooks, and lecture is not required, but homework is quite tedious. The exam questions can be confusing sometimes and not related to things you learned in class. Extremely engaged professor and his lectures are fun to attend. Has a very unique teaching style.

8+ hrs of hw weekly! Lectures are fun but are more ranty than econ/mathy. You'll learn about understanding human motivation...feels like glorified psych with some budget analysis. Tests are brutal and feedback is non-existent. You either get it or you don't. He cares about you though. Want a sample? -> can we conserve species by eating them?

His lectures are super interesting and definitely changed the way I viewed some things. However, if you're looking for an easy grade, don't take this class. The homework takes a lot of time, and the exams are hard. The lectures are fast-paced and it's important you actively listen in class.

Great Professor, engaging during lecture, very accessible outside of class.  Show up early to his class because he frequently will give insider knowledge to his exams, homework and extra credit during this time.  He remembers faces very well.  Assigns lots of Homework.
I understand the frustration with him, his assignments take forever and can frankly be quite mindless. However, he's a treat to talk to and genuinely cares about his students. Great guy, hard class

Participation isn't necessary but you should go to lectures and recitations if you want a good grade. Office hours aren't very helpful academically but definitely helps with learning to integrate EWOT. Homework took 10+ hours a week for me. HW/Test grading is TA-dependent and not very consistent. However, a course revamp is coming next year.

A lot of people don't like Rizzo and he isn't for everyone but if he's for you it will be your favorite class. I think it's worth giving it a shot. Even if he isn't for you if you do the work and actually pay attention to what he's saying you can still do really well.

More of a writing class than an econ class, if you wanna rip your brains out throughout the semester, then sure, take him. If not, I'd recommend someone else. Also has the most corrupt TA's of all time. Countless TA's would give answers to the exams during review sessions. He rants about his personal life.

Don't take him, he might be the worse professor i've ever had. Overcomplicates things by telling us stories from his personal life, talks about his kids, ex wife, and his gf MJ, overly long rants about random bs. I could've taught my myself the whole course.

***Read all of the reviews on RMP***

I personally loved Rizzo's class. However, a few notes on ECON-108:

-The syllabus is 31+ pages. Read it.
-There are two homework assignments each week, but we got skips.
-Lectures are not mandatory. Show up.
-Supply and Demand curves don't show up until the last week
-Go to office hours
-AI use was encouraged

Run

One exam question:

How much do you think you should write for this question?

Definitely not economics.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: He struggles with teaching. If you are expecting to learn economics, do not take this god-forsaken course. You will be learning rizzonomics instead of basic textbook econ. You will be confused when he goes on various tangents, assigns random readings that are barely relevant to the course, and asks the most pecuilar questions on exams. Good luck

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Horrible. Should quit to be honest. I didn't learn a single thing when I took this class. Save your time.
If you have the opportunity to take a different professor for this course... TAKE THE OTHER PROF. IF you're not on his wave length, you will fail.
my fav class my freshman yr fall, gen one of the most interesting courses I have ever taken and the mindset you learn in this class is applicable to so many different aspects of life.

I wouldn't recommend taking any course with Rizzo. His lectures frequently go off-topic and lack a clear structure, making it hard to grasp the core material. More importantly, the content covered in class often doesn't match what appears on the exams, which is frustrating if you're trying to genuinely learn and succeed in higher level classes.
Professor Rizzo is one of the greatest teachers there is and fundamentally changed by life in a positive way. I truly cannot thank Professor Rizzo enough.

Exams were very lengthy and the rubric for them was pretty wanky. A lot of times the response he was expecting was so exact it was hard to get full credit. He sometimes curves the grade at the end but just a little. Go to all the lectures; it'll help you understand his mind a bit better. 207 is a lot easier than 108, but you still have to study.

Best lecturer I've ever taken a class with. Super engaging and entertaining to listen to. Genuinely cares about the material and helping you understand. That said, he is horrible at writing exams, and grading criteria often feel arbitrary (e.g., no one gets full credit because no one guessed what he was thinking). Gives a lot of extra credit.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I think Rizzo's great. If you don't vibe with his style in the first couple of weeks, drop the class and take it with a different professor. Don't get to the point in the semester where you hate the class and can't switch out. That said, he teaches a very good class and tries hard to make the Econ topics engaging and interesting to learn for y'all.

His classes are hard, have a fairly heavy workload, but you learn a lot!
Don't take if you an easy A, But you will do well if you work hard in his class and engage with the material. 
Do take if you want to learn Economics.

Writing this before I get final grades, but I am doing fine rn. Not suitable for everyone, but ime, i have gotten so much out of taking Rizzo's class. 

3% EC, super caring (helped me with internships), and respectful/engaging (even though I disagree w/ him a lot). 

Make sure to pay close attention (and record if you can) to his lectures though.

Rizzo's teaching style is definitely not for everyone. It's non-traditional, emphasizing some philosophical/psychological ways of thinking and viewing economics. You should attend every lecture as his stories are what's in his exams. TAs are amazing and will help you through the class, def go see them and regularly attend office hours. I loved it.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Too much homework if you're taking this class outside of your major. Lectures are interesting but not well structured.

Weekly homework that is writing heavy. The class teaches a mindset, which you will take with you, and truly embracing this mindset makes the completion of the exams and homework significantly easier. The recitations, while optional, are very enjoyable. Very open during office hours where very enjoyable conversations can be had.

Rizzo is a cool guy. Fun lectures and is truly interested in making you love learning. Be curious and attend lectures or else this class will be a living nightmare. Some of the homeworks are kinda redundant but overall a great class to take.

Everyone says that Rizzo is a nutcase, and they're probably right, but his class was fun and although there was a lot of complaining, the workload wasn't that bad. TAs grade all your assignments and you can use ChatGPT on everything, even tests, but don't let that fool you into thinking its an easy A. Overall pretty good class would take again.

Took this class out of pure curiosity. It's definitely a hard class, and the way to a good understanding of the material is murky at best (hence the low rating, this class should be made more accessible), but it's fun if you appreciate learning that's more than rote memorization.

Worst unorganized lectures I have ever attended. A 5 year old with a lisp could teach economics better. The tests seem to consist of his diary entries and are graded harshly. First two were open note probably because he knows none of his teachings make any sense. Very subjective questions, none of the tests are multiple choice. So much homework.

Only take this class if ALL of the following is true:

1. You're a good test taker. Tests are nightmarish: ten short essays with convoluted prompts. NO NOTES OR CHATGPT.

2. A philosophical approach works for you, and you can teach yourself math. 

3. An interesting class is more important to you than your final grade.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Would definitely take a class with him again if I had the opportunity to do so. His style of teaching a little different, but if you get used to it, there's no class more fun and interesting than Econ 108 with Rizzo
Good man good lecture

never ever take this professor, his lecture makes no sense, and never teach you what is economic, instead he just be yapping about why his wife left him and other nonsense. The test is useless,  three hour long, and ten short essays, what people do is just copy from chatgpt

He's big on yapping and you'll never know what he's trying to teach you. It's obvious he knows a lot about economics but he's bad at teaching the concepts without talking about his ex wife or kids (specifically his daughter). No one scores well on the tests and they are not curved. I have to take him again but would prefer not to.

Honestly one of the most fun classes you can take at this school. There are no exams, simply two projects during the semester, with at least one being a group project, and some weekly homework. It's a chill class where you can just come to listen about sports economics or you can choose to engage in the discussion. Would recommend it to anyone.

I received a higher grade in 207 but I enjoyed 108 more. Rizzo's 207 is not math-based and sometimes the exam rubrics can be controversial. He is less organized than other instructors. Besides the class, he is a great friend and we had serval in-depth conversations.

The approach of his ECON 108 is a little bit different and more towards humanity, which can create good insights. It is a lecture-oriented class so understanding his stories in class is important. It is easy for me to see the connections between his homework and lectures but I understand that others might not feel this way.
Rizzo's class can be challenging, but it's worth the effort. The lectures are engaging, and you'll learn a lot about economic principles. Unstuckstudy AI and the free textbook are great study aids.
There is a lot of homework, and the lessons are not related to the homework.

I had no idea what he was talking about in his class, it felt like he was giving assignments that didn't have a single thing to do with the content of the class, that you had to write a lot every week in order to complete the assignments, and that you weren't going to get a good grade, even if you had the finances to do so
I love Prof. Rizzo! I chose to major in  Economics because of him. I'm a huge fan.

I enjoyed Rizzo a lot for 108. He goes downhill for 207. It does not feel like a real micro class at all. A lot of the things he chooses to cover in the course are based on what he likes to teach, NOT what is important for us to know. He stays away from the math which makes future classes difficult. Definitely not meant to teach a complex econ.

Rizzo is an extremely misunderstood professor by students. I know a lot of the other reviews say to not listen to the reviews like mine, but I think that his class was great. Somewhat difficult but great. You learn a lot in his class. Overall, it teaches you how to be a better student. The microeconomic topics are explained well and in a fun format

Rizzo is def one of the professors that you either love or hate. I personally enjoyed his lectures a lot, as they are more casual and conversational. He is also VERY knowledgable. However, his homework are extremely stressful, so be prepared to spend 5 hours each week for this weekly research writings. He also yaps too much on HW/exam questions.

Professor Rizzo is a amazing lecturer. He can make something as boring as CPI interesting. He truly cares for his students and only has the best intentions. He is a professor you will not regret taking. Just make sure to ask for help. This is what your TAs and office hours are for! It is an extremely rewarding class if you try. Thank you Rizzo!

Rizzo gets so much hate for his storytelling lecture style and his grading scale, but he is one of the best professor's at the University of Rochester. He is caring, knowledgeable, and always willing to help his students. Please get to know him! I took 108 and 207 with Rizzo and I have learned so much. Don't listen to others, take the class!

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: tough grader!
Very stressful.

Probably the most fun class I have taken so far. It is hard, but you really learn a lot and lectures are super entertaining. It is a lot of work but 100% worth taking the class over the other 108 option.

Love the guy. He's definitely better and more interesting when it comes to elective courses (sports econ, environmental) so take those with him for sure. I always learn something new and worthwhile during class.

Ignore all positive reviews, they are written by sycophants. Lots of homework(4-6 hours a week) and tests with unclear questions that are also a large percentage of your grade. I'm taking 207 with him and have noticed a large drop in quality recently(talks about taking his own life constantly!). Can't recommend him to anyone majoring in economics.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Guys. Do not look at the rate, it is not accurate. I just calculated the weighted average. The result is 789/216 which is approximately 3.65. NOT 5.0. Again, !!!!! HIS SCORE IS 3.65 NOT 5.0!!!! Do NOT take this class with him!!!

Theory of econ rather than an intro econ course. More about the principle of econ, applying it to different scenarios and learning how to think like an economist. 2 hws a week and can be difficult if you don't understand how Rizzo works. If you like straightforward classes with textbook-based information and tests then this is not the class for you

He is a great professor, very engaging and never a dull moment. But, tests were confusing and graded weirdly imo. Homework heavy, around 5-7 hours of homework every week. But I really learned a lot from his class and would like to take another course with him. He is genuinely one of the only professors that I learned life long lessons from.

Could not tell the difference between his rambles vs actual course material, he lectures in a very strange way and is all over the place. Exam questions are hard to nail, reviewing the answers afterward was very frustrating bc you would never have guessed that's what he wanted out of it.

Lectures are entertaining, he mostly tells stories. But the stories are confusing and it is hard to extract the intended meaning from them. Lots of homework, usually unrelated to lecture material. His tests are totally bizarre. Grading feels unfair. Rizzo is a great guy, but I can't recommend his class.

It is not like AP econ. You will see supply & demand curves 2.5 weeks before the final. This class is a grade wrecker. He grades in a very specific manner and makes it extremely hard to get anything above an A-, yet complains that many students are dropping his classes due to the harsh grading scale. Take 108 with another professor.

This is a very bizarre class. He is concerned with teaching how to "think economically" but what you get is very vague and bizarre examples and anecdotes that try to make a point, but they are difficult to understand and don't work well. In the end, I didn't end up knowing much about priniciples of economics or "economical thinking".

Rizzo is a great lecturer and a really nice guy, but if you want to get an A I wouldn't take him. The ideas of the class are vague sometimes and TA grading can be extremely frustrating. There is also a lot of homework. Basically if you are fine with not getting an A and doing a lot of homework, econ 108 with Rizzo is very enjoyable.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: biggest yapper i have ever met. obviously misses his ex wife based on the number of times he brought her up. just a dude who loves yappin and yappin. All the info you need is in the slides during his lectures but he forgets to go through them because he gets carried away talking about his ex wife.

He does not teach economics, he teaches what I like to call "Rizzonomics" which is basically his views of the world. He's clearly hardcore libertarian. Exam questions make no sense, he just wants you to write down his views for the answers. 2 writing papers a week for HW! He talks a lot about his divorce. He's Unhinged. I'm taking 207 with Ashby

You either love him or hate him. Rizzo's such a unique character, his lectures are something you will never get to experience anywhere else. Be sure to attend his lectures, everything on the test will be from lecture or somewhat related to them (there are recordings but they're from fall 2022). No slides, just take good detailed notes. great prof.

Amazing professor and wonderful lectures! I learned so much from his class and would seriously recommend. Go to study groups and office hours. Attendance is not mandatory, but you will not do well if you do not go to lectures. Try and start weekly assignments early in the week as they are long and tedious. Tests are open note and internet.

Truly one of the best professors I have had. The lectures are engaging and completely changed how I see the world. Class is lots of work (I would often be writing 15-20 pages weekly), but if you put in the effort, I promise that you will leave a better student and person. Strongly believe that everyone should take at least one class with Rizzo.

Very tough class, but so rewarding if done right aka put in the work! The way he asks questions is VERY similar to a certain liberal arts interdisciplinary competition which is particularly popular among intl HS students (not going to specify, but iykyk). Its helpful to have prior econ knowledge. In exams, think like him. Go to study groups!!

Lectures hardly cover economics and are mainly him venting his opinions. Same thing with his exams. The only good thing about this course is that the homework is actually doable assignments and can save your grade from his terrible exams.

Rizzo's class has way too much homework for no reason. Also, he grades extremely precisely. If you get an 89.999999%, it doesn't get rounded up. It would be a B+. His exams aren't economic based it's basically just what he thinks. The tests are also graded on "vibes" -an actual quote from a TA.

Professor Rizzo is by far the most approachable professor on campus and has the most passion for economics I have ever seen by someone else. His exams are difficult, but possible to do well on as long as you go to lecture and make use of office hours/TAs. Overall, I'd be excited to take another course by him and hope more people do.

Everyone loves or hates him. I personally hate him. He does not teach, people will literally show up to class because its entertaining. I think he talks about him divorce more than he does economics. The tests also make no sense don't take this class.
Take Ashby's class if you care about your GPA, not GPB, GPC, or even GPD.
Take Ashby's Class if you care about your GPA
I wish I could understand half of what he spews.
GPA Destroyer

As a freshman, I found his class to be very intimidating and dropped out of it immediately. Professor Rizzo is very passionate about economics and is a funny and eccentric lecturer, but the downside is that his class is very disorganized, which is terrifying when there are so many readings and assignments. His ECON 108 could destroy your GPA.

Go to class if you want to do well in Rizzo's class. You either love him or you hate him, but he grades very fair and most of the tests are open book and you are allowed to use the internet. Personally, I love rizzo and the style of the lectures but it's not for everyone.
Will give extra credit and drops lowest exam grade as well as adds 8 points to overall exam grades. Must go to lectures to understand material. Open note tests

Most entertaining yet informative professor I've ever had. Course consisted of weekly assignments that took 1-3 hours each (best to work as a group) and 4 exams that made 60% of your grade. You HAVE to show up to lectures otherwise the class won't be easy at all. He dropped an exam plus 8% grade boost so it's pretty easy to get an A.

His lectures got me interested in Econ. He puts all the concepts behind a story so it may be hard to decipher at first but once I did, I felt like I had a stronger understanding than if he just delivered dry lectures. Super funny, and watch out for the money he gives away on the first lecture...

comment: He is going way too fast with his lecture, and the amount of homework is demanding.

207 with Rizzo is a must. You could replace 2 exams by doing a group project with an entrepreneur where you talk abt econ in their business. Rizzo is the best professor ever. If you come to U of rochester and do not attend Rizzo's lectures, then your tuition is wasted.

Great man. I did not know an ounce of econ, I learned so much from him, although I couldn't tell you anything I learned. Prof Rizzo is easily the most unique professor I have ever had. He is definitely a tough grader but I enjoyed every minute of the three classes I took with him. He is very funny and makes class so enjoyable. He taught me how to view the world in a different way - a very unique thinker. His concepts can be confusing but overall very good professor.

Rizzo is awesome! I took AP Econ in high school, and I must say that Rizzo makes economics so much more applicable to real life than a heavy analysis of graphs. His energetic, hilarious personality turns otherwise "meh" material into engaging content and homework that encourage you to pose questions about real life you never thought about before.
Really funny, can be hard to understand, abstract teaching style. Lectures not technically required but if you don't go nothing will make sense

Rizzo is chaotic good. The lectures are not very organized but they are super engaging and really make you think about the world in a different way. one of the most talented, friendly, and interesting professors at this school.

Lecture based

Is super engaging in class, but expectations are confusing. Professor Rizzo is the most motivational and inspirational professor that I've ever had. He is the sole reason why I switched my major to economics. Rizzo is a very polarizing teacher.  He is also very busy, but if you reach out to him he will make sure he answers your questions. a lecture-based class. no math involved. extremely difficult tests.

Definitely go to his classes, you will get more than knowledge itself! Well worth

ECO108 Fall'14 Rizzo is a really awesome and interesting professor. However, he doesnt baby you. He doesnt provide much notes and the tests are tough. Yay Rizzo! Cool dude. Interesting classes but I'm not sure how technically he is compared to what other professors might teach.

Yes, Rizzo is an extremely difficult teacher, but ultimately he loves those students that put in the effort and those students are rewarded.  If I could go back, I would have built a strong relationship with this professor in the beginning of the year because he is a brilliant and interesting dude.  He is my favorite professor by far.

Prof. Bobkova is adorable. She's an enthusiastic lecturer, and leaves lots of time for student questions: she will stop lecture and stare the class down until someone asks a question, so bring some to class. The material can be challenging, but she's pretty good at explaining it. If you do the problems in the textbook and study, you'll be fine.

This class is HARD. The final is 20 pages long. Her lecture was literally her running back and forth along the chalk board writing down her notes from a piece of paper she brought with her.  She gets confused and disorganized during her own explanations. If you gotta take 161 instead of 141, find a different professor.
It is extremely hard to pass this course if you did not take Calc AB in high school. She is very confusing and moves VERY fast.
Not very helpful only talks to the board and absolutely flies when writing. Never gives enough time to read what is on the board. Very tough to get a good grade in her class.

Irina Bobkova is not a very clear professor, and this is not just because of her thick accent. She teaches Calculus in a very roundabout way that is hard to follow. I would not recommend her as a professor.

Super energetic, really bubbly, opens up room for questions often, for 142 slows down on tougher subjects and provides lots of examples, but as homework (Webwork) and exams are managed by the Department, her examples don't often translate to work. 161 was hardest class ever. Webworkexams made no sense. Wolfram Alpha is a godsend. Take 140 track.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: The professor is not a tough grader, in this course, she offers blogs that most of the time she will give you perfect on it. GET READY TO READ!!!! A lot of reading materials but focus mostly on the book chapters if you don't have enough time to read everything. She is nice and her lectures were SUPER educational. Amazing class!!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'So many papers']
comment: Prof Yarborough is nice and teaches interesting material. Be prepared to write 10 page papers, but with pretty chill grading

Professor Novy-Marx is wonderful. She really cares about her students and tries to involve everyone in group discussions. Make sure to come to class ready to participate. Tests are what you would expect, she does not try to trick you. Strongly recommend taking a class with her!!

You need to know what the reading talks about since a lot of the class is group discussion. She basically tells you what is on the midterm and final so it's not hard to study for. Most of your grade is from your final group projects and she's very lenient with grading. She really cares about her students and wants them to all succeed! Love her <3
Skip is the bomb. Nobody can understand how spellbinding, hilarious, and soul-deep his classes are without being in them. TAKE HIS CLASS.

You think you know all about theater until you meet this man. This is perhaps one of the best classes I've ever taken, and I'm really sad that this is the only course he teaches. He makes it fun and enjoyable, but you really learn a lot. But get what you want out of this class, don't just sit there and expect to be lectured all day.
Amazing professor with very clear notes. She prepares you well with her lectures and past exams. A good amount of memorizing but nothing super difficult.

Hands down the best prof I've had at this University-- cares about students, remains engaging through the semester, and hosts helpful office hours. 3rd and 4th exams are tough and graded harshly, but success is ACTUALLY possible... this time (sorry). Don't expect it to be a breeze just because she's nice-- biochem is challenging but rewarding.

Funny and caring person and overall a pretty good lecturer. Last two weeks of lectures are A LOT of content and could benefit from more in-class review. Wish she put less emphasis on memorizing names and minute details, but a lot of that is just the nature of biochem I guess. The content is hard but there's lots of other ways to bring your grade up
She has an attitude and every time students asked her for help she would blame them for her own shortcomings as a professor. Another superiority complex. An insult to the institute.

very kind and wonderful professor I could tell she really cared about her students and their success and she is a great and engaging lecturer her class is almost entirely exam based for grades so very little homework the exams are not to bad if you study and prepare ahead of time, but are often graded harshly with very detail answers expected

Loved her class. She truly cares and listens to students. If you struggle, tell her and she will help you find solutions. Lectures are dense because it is biology, but she explains clearly and wants you to succeed. Stay on top of notes, and you will do great.

Very chill person and wants everyone to succeed. Biochem is just a really hard class, and metabolism is 100% memorization based, so you can't fault her for that. Plenty of ways to pick up a grade in addition to exams, and she is very open during office hours. Curves to the average.

Stein is a kind soul, a good person who wants you to succeed. However, exams were graded incredibly harshly; they take off so many points for not mentioning super specific details even if your answer conveys a solid understanding of the content. If you did not specifically mention certain key words/phrases, you will get little credit.

Dr. Stein was OK as a lecturer and seems chill personality-wise, but I wouldn't recommend this class. You could know the important details and gist of the concepts but constantly get docked off on exams for not having some trivial factoids you wouldn't even think of no matter how hard you studied - she doesn't always include them in lecture slides!

Would recommend taking her class if you can, probably the best prof in the bio department. Grading can be harsh but most of the time if you submit a *reasonable* regrade she'll give points back. Plenty of points to get an A (4 exams, 3 PSets, 1 Project, points for recitation). Curves the class to wherever the average is. Very engaging lectures.

You could know everything about metabolism and more and still not do well in this class. Gotten unnecessary points off everywhere for not hitting key words that couldn't have been more obviously implied from what i wrote. Explained it perfectly but didn't explicitly state “x” is obviously a protein? -2 points
Harsh grader. Unless you can remember every minute detail, do not expect partial credit.
Did god's work to curve the class.
very difficult but FAIR exams

Dr. Stein is a good prof and really cares about her students. She is fair on exams even though content is difficult. I would start memorizing metabolism ASAP. Grading is fair and there is credit for recitations, projects, and exams. Sometimes she was unclear about exam content, but overall she is a good professor.

This was a great class, and Dr. Stein explains things great, but do NOT do what I did and get behind for the final exam on metabolism!!! I do not love that she saved so much content for the last exam, as this exam brought me down to a B+.

Amazing lecturer, so funny, makes class fun. This class has a lot of tedious content but she makes it learnable. 2 exams + 1 exam (not cumulative) during finals week - last exam has a lot of info to memorize. Recitations are helpful + boost your grade. Mostly depends on your midterm grades tho. Possible to curve exams/class, 1 EC opportunity.

Prof Stein is one of the best profs I had in the U of R. Despite biochem being new to her, she was so good in explaining concepts despite having Dr. Fu's slides. Her office hours one on one were pretty good. She's funny and gives good explanations. If you keep up with the material and problem sets, you will be fine. Labs are long tho.

I really enjoyed learning the material Stein teaches and I think she's a very knowledgeable person. I just don't think the exams are well written, and it's hard to earn partial credit points. It sucks that she doesn't give any practice exams, and the third exam was information overload nearly impossible to memorize it all.

In office hours she is funny, cool, fun to listen to, and just a nice down to earth person. Even though I absolutely love her as a person, as a professor she just isn't good. Across Genetics and Biochem the lectures usually felt disorgnaized in the way information was presented. She is a tough grader and not very understanding despite her niceness.
I loved Dr. Stein! Super accessible outside class and was a great lecturer. She made genetics fun!

Dr. Stein is a very reasonable professor. The content itself is difficult, but she is very approachable in office hours. The practice exam and practice questions she gives are very good at testing your understanding of the material. The same goes for the homework and recitation content. The course is curved, so it is a difficult but doable class.

Very difficult class but Professor Stein is a great professor. She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject which makes her class interesting. She is also very kind and willing to help students understand difficult material. If you have the option to take one of her classes, highly recommend doing so.

198 is very dense and she moves too quickly during lecture. It's difficult, but doable. Memorize the slides, go to workshop, know that it is not a point system and partial credit is skimpy. Overall, Stein is a great, caring professor and an even better role model, especially for all the women entering stem. Professors like her are hard to come by.

She goes into depth on all topics and expects a lot of details on exams and doesn't give partial credit easily. Her lectures are easy to follow and she offers good explanations although she does move quickly. She is very approachable during office hours but is hard to reach via email.

Professor Stein is one of my favorite professors so far. Her lectures are easy to follow and she has good slides. You definitely have to put in the work for an A (use the lecture outline questions on the first slide), but she makes it doable.

Dr. Stein is very caring about her students. Her lectures are dense, but she makes herself accessible and breaks down content more if you ask. There is a lot of hard material, but if you go to lecture and understand key concepts you can pull through. The big group paper at the end of the semester is also really helpful for your grade.

The key to doing well in her class is to memorize the slides. If you can remember everything you'll get an A. Class isn't a point system so if you don't realize that early it's hard to reach an A after messing up an exam.

There is a lot of material to know, so it's important to connect the concepts. Dr. Stein is super accessible outside of class for questions. She explains concepts clearly and makes genetics very interesting!

Professor stein thoroughly explains topics and homework is helpful to understand. She gives learning objectives and practice problems that are helpful. This class is a lot of information but she is lenient and willing to help. I would recommend her even though this is a tough class. If you work hard outside of class and come to lectures it is easy

Stein is awesome. She's exceptionally knowledgeable about the material and judges nobody for any questions, and is willing to help not just with course material but study habits and other topics as well. Explanations can be confusing but again, she's willing to clarify anything. Very transparent with grading and expectations.

Professor Stein seems like a good person but she should stick to 50 minute lectures. She sped through way too much material every lecture and expects you to know minor details in her ppt slides. Study the slides hard, go to recitation and get outside help if needed. Exams are difficult but manageable with the curve.
Great teacher, passionate about the class and the content she teaches. Exams are very fair if you study and do the practice exams. Definitely go to recitation if you want to do well!

Dr. Stein is horrible at explaining difficult topics. She speeds through challenging units in lecture and expects you to know intricate details for exams. If you are not specific enough during exams expect to lose nearly all points on questions. Dr. Stein should also never teach an 75 minute lecture because the lectures are often dry and boring.
Dr. Stein is great. She's an engaging lecturer and very respectful towards students. Tests are easy, and she's funny. Regularly talks about the genetics of her cats.

I had Dr. Stein for this past summer term, and she was amazing! Lectures were pretty info-dense, but she explained concepts extremely well. She wants her students to succeed and enjoys students actively engaging with the material. Grades were mostly based on exams and a paper. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Stein!!

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: I really liked Dr. Stein. Her lectures were info-dense but they clearly outline what she wants you to know on exams. Assigned hw that wasn't thaaaat helpful, so focus on her lectures when studying. Her exams were tough but she made them open-note and gave us 2x time than normal. She does make you work for an A, but it's definitely doable.
Always helpful at office hours

The material for this class can be hard sometimes, but Stein is a great lecturer who really cares about teaching. Plus there are many other resources to help understand the material outside of class such as workshops, TAs, office hours, discussion boards, and the textbook. If you put in the time, this class is rewarding and not that difficult.

Dr. Stein's lectures (virtual now) are very info-heavy, but the exams are open note/-book. She has office hours twice a week with thought-provoking conversation (and occasional visits from her cat, Monkey!), and she patiently reexplains hard concepts. She cares about us and once moved a test because it coincided with orgo. Kind & easy to talk to!

Love Dr. Stein! If you study the lectures you'll be fine - textbook could be helpful to understand concepts she explains but typically her material is already overlapping with the book and you don't need to actually get it (even if you are a book person). Material may be tough, but Stein is incredible!

I 100% do not recommend anyone to take this course. She gave us 7 difficult 3-hour midterms every other week. HW was so long and tedious. Promised short videos but posted 5-8 20-30 min videos in each chapter for each 7 modules. Too much content and not enough time to review. Don't make this mistake of taking this class now during a pandemic!!!!!!!!

Dr. Stein changed the format of her class for COVID and I much prefer this new way. Instead of 3 closed note, memorization heavy midterms, it is 7 open book conceptual module tests. She is an amazing lecturer who cares about the material and her students, and is flexible when she needs to be while still delivering the required amount of content.

Dr. Stein is a decent lecturer; I learned a lot from her class. However, as much as she makes it seem like she's doing us a favor amidst the pandemic, she's not. She gave us 7 exams, each being 3 hours long. The class was split into online modules, where the lecture videos add up to more than in-person lectures. The exams were also graded harshly.

AVOID! This class was the worst class I've ever taken in my academic life. We took 7 3-hour exams every other week + she teaches way too much content in 3 1/2 months! Awful exams! I am exhausted and the hw is longer than the exams! If you leave out a slight word that she was looking for in the exam, you get points off! BEWARE. It is not worth it!!

Where do I even begin. Taking BIOL198 this semester was the worst decision I've made of my entire college career. This semester, amongst a global pandemic, Dr. Stein felt the need to give 7 full-length midterms every other week. Although I believe she is a great lecturer and I understood her content well, the structure of the class was not it.

Rather than in person 3 exam schedule, she gives 7 exams harder and longer than the typical exam. No practice exam, even if you follow what she teaches, you still get points taken off. She looks for extremely specific things in exam that no one would never expect. You dont get answer key for the workshop. She doesnt show up to her Office Hours.
Really fun class. A LOT of memorization, but the teacher is great and the tests are fair with a curve.

One of my favorite professors at UR thus far. She made genetics easy to understand and very enjoyable. Not to mention she has a wonderful personality and her passion for genetics shines through. Wish I had attended more of her office hours.

Dr. Stein gives really fun lectures for BIO 198: Genetics. Clear-minded, intellectual, humorous and explains everything clearly. Homework and exams are neither too dense nor too hard. Accessible outside classroom and very patient at answering questions.

I took genetics with Dr. Stein over the summer term. It was online due to COVID, but nevertheless I learned a ton and would take it with her again. She's fantastic at what she does, is super passionate, and gives great feedback on tests. There were 6 tests and lots of homeworks. The textbook didn't help much, just pay close attention to the lecture
Very helpful professor.
Heidi is so nice and a very sweet person. She is extremely helpful..made my CAS class seem so simple...and passed with a good grade :)
No Comments

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: In terms of grading, there is no clear rubric, so you have little idea how your work differs from an “A.” Evaluation feels subjective. In discussions, he often interprets comments in exaggerated ways and uses extreme examples, making meaningful conversation difficult.

Just don't take the meaning of life with him. He will literally try to tell you the sky isn't blue if you say it is. His feedback is ok, but if you don't have the same view as him, just be quiet and sit through the lecture. Easy class, ROUGH prof.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I mean he wasnt a bad professor but he definitely played devil's advocate for a lot of the conversations discussed in class. It felt as if he wanted to argue but not in an easygoing manner. Idk i just felt that it was weird how he disapproves all the students' povs. There is a lot of reading and writing required so be weary of the deadlines.

I took his "What is Human Nature?" writing class, and Professor Stauffer is insightful. He gives you great feedback after every submitted paper and is easily accessible outside of class. There are readings and summaries, but it's not a bad class as long as you show up and do what you're supposed to. Not the hardest class, but effort is needed.

Dr. Stauffer gives very good and detailed feedback on all the papers you submit, which helps a lot. Attendance is part of the grade, but as long as you attend, it is relatively easy. There were readings and summaries due before almost every class, which could be long sometimes, but otherwise, the class was relatively easy and helpful.
He was a great prof. He gave helpful feedback, and the lectures gave a good perspective on what is expected of job application materials. Highly recommend taking this class with him.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Very kind and respectful. Attendance is important, so if you show up, you're all set. Always willing to meet or discuss during the week if you need help on anything. Overall, I'd highly recommend his class if you want to have fun in-class discussions and want a great professor.

He's really nice, I liked him a lot. The only thing is the 8-10 page paper at the end of the semester is 40% of your grade. He's a pretty light grader though. He also cares a lot about attendance, so make sure to go to every class. He doesn't ask much, there are just short readings for each class.

Stauffer is an incredible instructor! Always accessible outside of class, they offer valuable guidance and are highly knowledgeable in their field and writing. Their passion for the subject makes learning engaging and enjoyable. I would take their class again!"
Perfectly good teacher for the WRTG105 class. Teaches you what you need to know, and doesn't make it painful. Has students email assignments instead of using blackboard, which I found annoying.
While not the hardest teacher, he definitely makes sure you learn in his class. Definitely take his class for the WRTG105 credit if you get a chance.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Took his "The Meaning of Life" course and the readings & discussions were very insightful and makes you think. Super nice guy and always is able to add on to your comments in a discussion. Very clear grading, as long as you follow the criteria you'll get a good grade. Great prof for 105!

he was very nice, and quiet. but, i feel like the class is hard to do well in if you are not the best writer. I feel like it is hard to get the grade you want. I think he has clear expectations on what to do for your papers. I tried REALLY hard on my final paper and went to so many resources for help and still didn't get the grade i wanted.

This class was definitely not an ez A. However I do believe that this class is a great seminar style class with weekly discussion and interesting readings instead of a dry writing class like other classes. I think Dr Stauffer did a great job by making the topics interesting and always available to help his students with their writings.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I always enjoyed Stauffers' class. Interesting (and long) readings that led to great discussions, always asked us interesting questions and created a good atmosphere in the classroom. Amazing at giving feedback on essays, and a very fair grader. Answered emails very quickly and I felt that he cared about all his students. Great teacher for 105!

Even though I typically don't like writing, I really enjoyed Dr. Stauffer's class. The one I took was about life in the digital age so the content actually was pretty interesting and the essays weren't bad at all. Show up, participate, and put a decent amount of effort into the essays and you'll do well.

Definitely take him!! I took his life in a digital age this semester, which is always very intriguing. He really like to bring up critical thinking question and statistics to drive the class discussion further. For his essay, make sure your organization and logics flow well then you should be fine.

He is THE BEST writing teacher. I took his human nature class. We basically had to show up to class, participate in the discussions and do the papers by the deadline. Easy to satisy requirements for A and the teacher is very kind, accesible and gives very good feedback. Take him!

I LOVE his class. The grading is extremely clear and as long as you follow the instructions, you will get good grades. We had lots of terrific discussions in class. I put effort and I also like the content of this class. The final paper (8-10 pages) is the college policy, but he helps me a lot through developing ideas on this final papers. THE BEST
I love his class. We had lots of interesting discussions in class, and the professor gives plenty of good feedbacks on your writing. I hope that he can be my upper level writing professor!!!!
Very friendly and accessible out of class. Interesting topic. Participation is highly recommended. Will recommend his course to peers.
The best professor ever!
Great professor, I had him for WRT 105 Posthumanism. I saw that he's teaching one of my other writing course, so I'm definitely taking it with him again!
A really good professor talking about American's society and politics.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Great professor!

Making of Trump's America is pretty much your typical WRT 105 class. It is not just a Trump roast-fest, more of an examination of the state of modern america. It won't blow your mind, but Stauffer is fair, and the assigned readings are quite easy. He does not put grades online quickly, (or at all so far), but I can't imagine getting less than an A-

BLST156/ENGL116: Intro to African American Lit is an inspiring course that enables students to explore myriad literary works dealing with a wide range of topics from the 20th century to the present- from DuBois's book to Octavia Butler's short story. Professor Omelsky is also caring, kind, and supportive! Regardless of your major, you'll enjoy it!!

Took Black Speculative Fiction in Fall 2024- learnt a lot from it. The course examines a wide variety of literature, short stories, and films...etc produced by Black authors worldwide. The material is very interesting. Professor Omelsky is one of the best instructors I've had. Highly recommended!!

Amazing professor. Would 100% recommend this class to anyone looking to explore great authors from all over the world. Truly changed the way I view literature, his class was the highlight of my freshman year!!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: He's such an amazing professor who actually genuinely cares about his students and what they're going through. He assigns really good reading material - I also took his Black Speculative Fiction course, and to this day, it's one of my favorite courses. His class discussions are so insightful and engaging; he really tries to pull his students in

Professor Omelsky does a great job facilitating class discussion and helping students become passionate about the material. The workload for my class was fairly light, and he was always very willing to help students outside of class.

Good guy and easy to get a good grade, but not a good professor. Way too reliant on TA's and recitations (sucks if you have a bad TA), teaches overtime, hasn't changed the course in 20 years, projects are incredibly redundant, condescending when you ask a question, unorganized, poor use of lecture time (whole class used to hand draw excel sheet).
Prof. Perucchio is absolutely amazing to me his class was a really fun intro to engineering. The projects were interesting and his lectures were not at all ambiguous.
Great guy but often goes over time for lectures and content is very repetitive

Professor Perucchio is passionate about his 'Engineering of Bridges' class but was harsh when grading the group presentations for my final project. His TAs were very helpful though for the homeworks!!!
Perruchio is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable; however, he often doesn't express exactly what he wanted in projects and his “time management” is poor.
Teaches things very clearly and makes it easy to understand. He will 100% go 5-10 minutes over time though after lectures.
Do not schedule something right after class, he will always go over the time allotted for lecture.
He is very passionate about what he teaches and the energy is contagious. Great professor. "Very fundamental!"

Perucchio was one of the most passionate professors I had as a first-year. He was relatively understanding and wanted his students to succeed. GO TO RECITATION. I learned most of the class through recitation and found that lectures were easier to follow after going to recitation. Be prepared to do important group projects. Utilize office hours.

Very good professor that makes the material fun and interesting to learn. Material is hard to understand at first because it is new and unique but can be learned quickly will little practice. Recitation are very helpful if payed attention to and the homework are only long because the material has to be taught first. The projects are kinda hard.

He teaches forces, vectors, and equilibrium stuff from the ground up. If you've taken physics before, the class should be pretty easy. Homework is relatively light for most of the semester, but the last two weeks are a GRIND. We had a homework, a project, a presentation, and an exam all within five days.

A bit overrated. His homework dates are very generous. Lectures can be insightful but often boring, there was once a lecture when he spent time drawing out an entire excel table. Practice exams are old and didn't feel representative of what the actual exams were. Recitations and TAs are the MVPs of this course. And he's a good and patient person.

He seems nice, but the grading scale is not forgiving at all and he is very harsh and blunt if you dont know something. Most of the time he won't criticize you for not knowing things directly, but he will ask you many question that you cannot answer to make yourself look stupid. He gives no extra credit either and is very harsh when you appeal him

Amazing professor. You can tell that Perucchio has a passion for mechanical engineering. The lectures were boring, but applying the concepts from his class was fun in workshops, homework, and group projects. Beware that Perucchio gets scary during the third project.
Interesting guy. Lecture can be a bit boring but overall good.

Great intro to ME. Lectures can feel slow, but only because he explains everything in great detail and will take as long as it takes to answer a question fully. He's a great personality and really cares about each student. Workload is totally manageable and there are plenty of resources to get help if you need. Don't buy the textbook (ME104).

Professor Perucchio is a great lecturer and fully applies the lectures. As Chair of the ME Department, Perucchio's class is a great base for entering the ME track. His class is a decent and fair amount of work but the projects and group work is fun and knowledgeable. A must take for ME.

Professor Perucchio is a very caring teacher and is willing to answer questions if you have them. He is very passionate about engineering as a whole and architecture as well (including bridges). His lectures are a bit dry, but going to office hours with the TA is very enlightening. As long as you know the process, the class won't be too difficult.

I don't have the space to say everything I want to, but, for context, I received a 4 on the AP Physics C: Mechanics exam. Now, listen carefully: for the love of god, don't take this class if you have had *any* physics experience; you will be punished for it. The grading method for this class is beyond asinine and I can't understate my hatred for it

Very passionate about his work and what he is teaching in class. Kind yet straightforward when talking one-on-one. While he is fairly good at explaining concepts, his greatest strength is attracting and finding the most competent, knowledgeable, and helpful TAs who show you how solve problems on homework and exams. Taking ME104 helps with ME120.
Great introduction to mechanical engineering

Dude's great. Be prepared to get blindsided by the amount of work the first project is, but from there it's an easy A as long as you do your work and go to lectures. The lectures are sometimes confusing because of their fast pace but overall Perucchio is engaging and helpful and I would recommend taking his class if possible.

"Are you with me on this guys?" - Professor Perucchio can give in depth lectures in engineering, and paying attention is a must, because if you are not "with him," you lose track of variables and ideas. Not so good at explaining when asked a question. You may have more questions afterward. All in all, he is a solid choice, TAs are helpful, etc.
DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. Amazing professor, very very passionate. Make sure you find a group of four students asap because you dont want to be stuck working with someone who doesnt care.

Professor Perucchio was extremely helpful as he would explain any question you had with as much effort. He does sometimes get lost in what he does as he is very passionate about it but he definitely teaches all the material that is needed.

Great professor. Lectures can sometimes get boring because he drones on and on, but I still found the material very interesting. His TA's are fantastic and are great resources for help. He's more than willing to explain concepts and help if you go to his office hours. One of the most passionate professors. Very tough on the final project

Do some preview before you go to class. Answer his questions and go to lectures. Although his homework and projects will cover almost everything you need for the exam, his lecture will give you some very very interesting and helpful info. Enjoy.

Be warned: although this man looks like an adorable old Italian man with a strange obsession with strange hats, this cat's got claws. The homework was really hard, but he picks good TA's for the class, so you can usually just do it during office hours with their help. Also, he gets scary during the final project.
Awesome professor, great class. Really sparked my interest in Mech E.

He's a really great guy, with a deep passion for the subject. Really comes through for each student (more so than any other I had this term); as an example, he attended a play in which one of his students was acting. Office hours are very helpful. Don't be afraid to go to them. Highly suggest anything he teaches.

He's really passionate about whate he teaches and really wants every1 to do well. he tries to make ppl pass with higher grades when possible.  unfortunately for him, he's teaching a boring subject. the lectures tend to put atleast 5 students to sleep.

Perucchio and his stereotypical Italian accent are great.  He was always excited about the class and did his best to make it interesting.  Unfortunately, many times his lectures would put half the class to sleep.  Other than the occasional boring lecture, Perucchio did a good job teaching the basics of ME.

Perucchio is a complex professor. For several lectures, he is interesting and the the point. For several others, he repeats the same information over and over and over. This accent is a HUGE plus, and his trademark slogans ('Is everyone witth me on this?') almost put you to sleep. Good TA selection and the course is a blast...you'll remember him!

Prof. Perucchio is very passionate about the topics in class.  He knows what he's talking about and makes sure to ask if everyone is clear on new concepts.  There are 4 group projects throughout the semester that can be a little hectic to complete, but none of the homework or tests are unfair.  You get to play with "KiNex!"
Great teacher! Spends extra time to make sure everyone understands and presents the material in a clear, concise manner. 104Q was my favorite course at college so far, mostly because he taught it.
No Comments
such a cool guy. so interested in what he does and making you understand it. all around great teacher.

Cares immensely about student wellbeing and understanding of material. Fair and thoughtful. Interesting guy, too (and his Italian accent will keep you at least mildly interested no matter the lecture topic). I've TAed for him, so I speak from experience.
condescending

Very nice person, cares for students, and gives LOTS of extra credit. I had over a 101% in the class before the final project. Final project is difficult, focus on something simple, but do it according to the process. He did seem very overwhelmed though and it hurt the class, since he was disorganized, probably cause he didn't have much time.
He defines awesomeness.

I loved the way Prof. Hoque was able to relate the materials to real-world scenarios. The guests lectures were very helpful to make the connection.
