Cranking up the prerequisite so that students with solid programming and research focus could only take this class will help. Otherwise, you are bound to see a bi-modal distribution in the feedback.
Prof. Hoque is a great teacher and genuinely cares for the students. Anyone who gives you him a bad review clearly did not enjoy being put on the spot in the class or was just hoping for an easy A.

HCI class has historically been a very easy class. A lot of students including myself took this class with that pretense and it backfired. On the bright side, I appreciated the way Prof. Hoque always responded to the anonymous feedback. He likes to  randomly check on people in the class; so you gotta always pay attention.

He is probably the worst professor I've ever had from the CS department. He is extremely condescending and has ridiculous expectations. He basically never taught anything in lecture-just talked about his research or brought in guests. The projects also took over my life, and I wasn't even rewarded for it.

Hoque was a new professor and he taught this course for the first time here. He pushed the TAs and the students to work really hard. He graded based on his personal preference on your projects, no matter how hard you worked. Plus, you need to warm up yourself with the skills to be used in the projects. Watch out!

The course was interesting at the first glance, but I quickly got bored after two weeks. Prof. Hoque taught superficial stuff in class, and simply by asking students a question and asking another to repeat what the previous one's answer was insufficient to draw the audience attention back from facebook, youtube, and games to the class.

This class ended up being lot more work than what I had anticipated. But the final project was a lot of fun, and Prof. Hoque is an entertaining lecturer. I personally loved the guest lecturers as our final project was inspired by one of them. If you know how to code/build, you would love this class.

The class topic wasn't HCI, most lectures were irrelevant "guest lectures," and you were basically graded on how good a project you could make with skills you were already expected to have, not taught. He told us on the first day no web programming skill was required, then told us 2 months in to drop the class if we didn't have extensive experience
I took his HCI class which is the first he's taught. Prof. Hoque is a great professor and will be great to have in the university. He really cares about his students
Prof. Hoque is new at the UofR, and very obsessed about his new class. I think he put a lot of effort in teaching HCI, CSC212.
The class was very unorganized and the processor is extremely condescending. I do not recommend taking courses with this Prof Hoque.
Great teacher, really personable and fun!
Amazing teacher. really really easy tests, you can ues a calculator, he lets you get extra points after the test too.
Great Teacher, hard workshop problems. He has a good TA as well
Really good teacher. Very clear, students in his class get very high scores.

Wei is hard to understand... I almost walked out the first day due to his accent.  However, he is the best math professor ever!  He will answer questions over and over again until it all makes sense, and he responds to emails very quickly (roughly 10 minutes, at most hours).  I learned more with him than with the "better" ones.
smart guy, helpful, easy grading

Almost impossible to understand in class. Very unorganized as well. Probably the worst math teacher I've ever had. It'd be a lot better use of time to read the text book to go to class. Also the quest workshop has nothing to do with class and is pointless and the TAs are less than useful.

He's a really nice guy, but it's a little confusing when he teaches. If you ask him for help, he's very nice and will show you how to do the problem. Great one on one. I'd recommend having taken calculus before, though.
I like his lectures. As he warned it, MATH 285 is a tough course and putting 9 hours after class each week is not an exaggeration.
He's the best professor in the math department, take his class
Best professor in the math courses I've taken
Geba is very respected and you could do a lot worse, but to be honest I didn't think he was a great lecturer. He's  a nice guy though.

Prof Geba really made me love math again. Clear and thorough lectures, he did one example from the practice problems and there was one worked out in the book for every topic. He was late to almost every class by 10 minutes, but still got through the content. As long as you stay on top of practice problems, especially with vector spaces, its fine.

He is a super harsh grader, no curve, and is very rude when you go to him because he graded someone differently that you  when you had the same thing. Overall rude when one-on-one and his notes are terrible.
His lecture is clear and understandable. You can learn a lot from his lecture.
For those who love mathematics, especially proof-based mathematics, you cannot miss Geba's classes!

Great Professor. Friendly and approachable in office hours. Early content is pretty easy, but get ready to read the book for the second midterm. Tests are tough, but reasonable. Do your work, and you won't have to worry about your grade.

MTH190 is only 1 credit, but Geba's very available in office hours. Problems are very difficult, but he helps a lot. The first time I went to office hours he made sure I knew that his door was always open for any questions/concerns I had about my future math studies. My favorite professor this semester, can't wait to take more of his classes.a
Best teacher I ever had. Got me really interested in the material. Especially helpful in office hours- take advantage of these.
Great professor. Prob the smartest guy I've ever seen. Take his class(tho I dropped because I had to take another class...)!
Great professor. Very funny!

Prof. Geba is awesome! He is so smart that he doesn't need to read or copy any of his notes. And he really teaches you what math really means. He talked a lot about motivations. He is also the funniest person on the planet. Love him!
Geba is awesome. Tests were straightforward for this class IF you knew your stuff. Would have done better if I had taken the time to really understand the concepts.
great professor, really cared about the students and made sure you understood the material
i never actually went to him for help outside of class (even tho i really needed it), because he scared me. and i almost never skipped class, and always had no clue what was going on
Professor Geba is the smartest man I have ever met. I love him.
No Comments
Definately not the most interesting class in the world, but if you actually pay attention, he's not so bad. The final exam, however, is the hardest thing in the world.
No Comments
Hands down the best professor I've ever had. She's taught me everything I know about reading ethnography and how to write well. Incredibly knowledgeable and interesting

I think I learned more about how to write well in this class than I did in my WRTG 105. All the readings are super interesting, and class is usually just discussion about the readings, which everyone participates in and is really helpful when it comes time to write the papers. Overall, I loved this class and had a great time.

Professor Doughty is overall a great professor. I actually feel that I learned a lot over the course of the class, although it was very reading intensive. She talks fast, but her lectures are interesting. She prepares you well for tests and grades pretty easily. Also, she was very flexible and understanding in terms of attendance and due dates.
Amazing professor in every way. Grading criteria is clear, she cares about her students, and provides great reading material and discussion. One of my favorite classes I've taken.

The best professor in the whole university. She taught me how to write and think for myself. She takes the time to scrupulously comment on your papers so you can improve your writing and arguments. The topics covered are tough, but the class discussions mixed with her beloved rants humanizes our detached univ. Highly rec for every major!
Just pure awesomeness. She even helped me with an outside project.
Very amazing professor. Definitely recommend anyone who can to take her courses!
Professor Doughty had amazing lectures. I admire that she tries to fit so much material in a 101 class, which shows that she cares about students actually getting something from the class.
The most passionate professor I've ever had. Knows her subject well. Has changed my college career. Highly recommend!

She is tough, but fair. She expects you to engage with the material, but is understanding of the fact you are a college student. She is really helpful, despite the fact she might ramble a bit. But, her ramblings are always helpful! Even if they sometimes cause you to think more deeply about the issue. She is really great. Be prepared to work hard.

She is very passionate about what she is teaching but does tend to speak very fast. Readings are mixed with some very interesting ones and some you just have to get through. Exams were pretty difficult but if you take good notes and know the structure of the readings then you will should do fine.

Speaks really fast, but you get used to it. She was nice and helpful when you go to office hours or as a question after class. Doesn't lecture often, sit in a circle and had group discussions of the reading. interesting topics, hard exam essay questions, easy weekly journals. MANDATORY attendance-she will notice if you arent there and email you.
She is very nice but she talks really fast and there is often no information provided to you except the readings.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Did not enjoy his lecture style did not feel like it was meant to be accessible language for undergrads and often pretentious. No grades were submitted in Gradescope throughout the semester.

Burges is the best professor I've had at U of R. He is warm and funny in class and most class periods were devoted purely to discussions, which were almost always effective and insightful. He was accessible and helpful outside of class. Midterm and final assignments were hefty, but he gives ample feedback for both. Would give 6 stars if I could.

Professor Burges was born to be a professor. He seems to truly care about what his students have to say. Discussion in his class can be lively and invigorating. On top of that, he is incredibly kind and accommodating. As long as you clearly communicate with him, he will ensure that the class will never be too much for you. He is great at his job.

Professor Burges is a great teacher who really cares about his students. The class is tough, be prepared to put in effort into writing papers but if you're interested in the material, you'll find it really engaging. Be warned - attendance is mandatory and they are strict on it. If you're someone who skips class, this is not for you.

Joel really likes his essays. I ended up with 5 for the rest of the semester which was really rough. He taught a class on television which was a flop because of his constant replanning of the course syllabus. He's a smart guy who can lecture well, but this class was not run well (which he is aware of).

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'So many papers']
comment: Ridiculous amount of workload for a non-W course. Your grade largely depends on the group project, and he picks your groupmates for you. Allow two absences, takes attendance every class.
Took his class as a first-semester freshman. A three pages paper each week. But you can surely learn things and inspired by his class! One of the best teachers I had at UR

His lectures are very fun but solid. Every lecture was prepared and delivered well. Definitely an inspirational course to learn about all kinds of media and how to analyze them. Very heavy load of homework though. Lots of papers and readings to do. The good thing is that the topics and times are relatively flexible. Take attendance every time.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: I love Professor Burges! Took me some time to adjust to his class because there was a lot of papers to write and a semester-long group project but he was very flexible and cared about his students. He took individual concerns seriously and was determined to let everyone learn. He's very intelligent and his lectures are amazing. I'll miss his laugh

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: The man clearly knows what he is talking about. For an intro class, the workload is very extensive, although sometimes he is understanding. The no technology policy is very helpful because some of the material can be dry, but one can still pay attention. Midterm focuses on specific details so be aware.
It's as if the light of God is reflecting off his bald head. Great teacher, good guy, would definitely recommend. He's so pretty! And smart. The end.
He's absolutely brilliant, and Intro to Media Studies was one of the best classes I've taken so far.

Took me a while to get used to his type of teaching (no technology). He uses his extensive vocab and flaunts his aluma maters quite often however i learned a ton in his class, even though it was the hardest class i've taken at UR thus far.
Took me a while to warm up to him, but he's a brilliant professor. He knows his stuff. Classes can sometimes be boring, but that was more the subject matter than the professor.
Amazing.

Interesting material presented in a fresh and intriguing way. Burges is an incredibly passionate and intelligent professor but teaches at an elevated level. If you're not willing to do the reading and participate, this is not your class. I learned a great deal and felt positively challenged. Highly recommend.

His lectures are so boring that nobody cares or listens. He takes attendance at random times. He asked why there were so many of us in the first lesson, and he added a midterm because of that. The exam was challenging. The slides were very poor, and the assignments were AI-generated and unclear. It's not an easy A anymore. Don't take this course.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Prof. Xu is really knowledgeable and engaged in research. Lectures were inspirational but involved little coding, so be prepared to learn PyTorch on your own. Easy A. No exam. 2 projects and 1 final group project, open-topics. Level of difficulty really depends on the topic one choose. Clear grading rubrics and instruction.
A terrible professor with poor character, a bad attitude in class, and no respect for students.

Actually CSC 298:

Abysmal communication. Slides intentionally hide info (you cannot learn / review after class). Lectures are poorly structured and delivered: always derailed by simple student questions that he spends 10min answering at *extreme* length. Project instructions self-contradictory and intentionally incomplete.

He is the professor who spent the least effort in teaching. He's lecture PowerPoint was borrowed from another school. You could feel that he had never prepared his lecture before class. He had 1 hour/per week oh and he didn't reply to the email. His TAs put the minimum effort too, when you asked someone he would let you find the other TA and so on.
Prof. Xu is great!
CV is hard but Prof. Xu can explain everything in a clearer and easier way.

The whole operation is tightly run. The class is such a struggle, but it leaves you with the feeling that you can only blame Xu last. So that's good learnin'. The assignments are where it really all connects. Wouldn't recommend this class for credit if you are just casually interested in the material.
Professor Xu is a very nice guy. His slides and teaching are very clear and you can tell he loves what he does.
I like the paper discussion.

This professor is not very responsible. She usually posts review question & solutions or homework solutions like only 2 days ahead of the midterm day. I am not very sure what other students feel, but for me it's very overwhelmed. Imagine when you looked at some weird review questions and there were only 2 days left.
If you did the homeworks, the midterm will not be any trouble. Im not trying to trick you *Class average is a 50% on the midterm...
Her tests are almost not related to what she taught. Read the textbooks! Dont trust her slides.

Her lecture slides are very vague and given the material is quite dry and difficult to comprehend, it's hard to follow her lecture. Once you're lost in lecture, you ain't finding your way back. Go to TA office hours for help! And read the textbook. It's much more detailed than her slides. Study hard. Not an easy class!
Write out the definition of Competition Equilibrium. That worth 10 points on the midterm

Lu's first time teaching ECO 209. Nice, a little quiet, and approachable in office hours. It's important to go to class lectures,  the recitation when offered by the TA, and to read the textbook. That's the only way to really understand the material, since it is very dry. The homework can be challenging, so go to office hours for help if needed.
Her class goes really quick. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS!
The exams were a little bit challenging, but I found them to be reasonable, and it covered essential materials.

Worst Econ class I've taken. No textbook. Doesn't explain things during lecture. Isn't clear about what we need to know or don't need to know for tests. Puts way too much material in each class and assumes from her barebones lectures outlines she puts up online prior that we have a complete understanding.

Professor Brown's Optics 101 course was an exercise in arrogance. He consistently dismissed student questions, openly acted superior, and seemed far more interested in showcasing his ego than teaching optics. Lectures were condescending and unhelpful, making the entire experience miserable. Avoid at all costs.

Overall Thomas Brown's class was an amazing overview of optics, from basic thin lens to holography  The test were very fair and resemble the practice tests very closely. Definitely not impossible to do poorly on but if you know your stuff you'll be fine. Lectures made me a bit sleepy at times, but the professor is still very passionate about optics
lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but prof is very caring and kind
He is such a sweetheart and clearly passionate about what he is teaching. If you pay attention and go to workshops you'll be fine. Take the time to talk to him one on one! He is a great guy

Professor Brown is one of those teachers who cares about his students and ensures everyone's success. While he does care about his students, his lectures are extremely boring. He took lasers, LASERS!, and made them not interesting to me. I learned a lot more from the workshops and practice tests than from the lectures, but that's just personal.

Everybody loves Prof. Brown. It is clear that he is very passionate about what he's teaching. There is graded homework and the tests are relatively easy if you simply listen in class. That being said, because optics is not widely studied and we don't use a textbook, his lectures are the only place you find what you're learning.

TGB is the real deal; he knows his stuff inside and out, but he explains it in ways that anyone can understand. He mixes up the lectures, homework, and tests with jokes and fun stories, and really cares about each individual student. Amazing person and professor!!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: He is such an amazing professor, but this is a difficult class. If you do not go to the lectures or watch his videos you will be lost in the class. Also the homework is difficult so don't procrastinate, and go to his office hour for extra help.

Freshmen taking this class with no understanding of Optics, Brown made it interesting. This class is straight forward: he is a hard grader on hw but give you guide for test just rearranged test or with different math. He is willing to answer any questions, bad thing about him he just speaks and shouts in the same tone. Optics major due to him.
My insomnia is cured by him. I don't know what he is talking about. And the grade is ridiculously lowwwwwww.
Tom is the bomb!

class is completely of matlab...tends to be quite boring and frustrating when matlab gives you problems and there is no textbook except a short lab manual used for lab and class....hard to keep up with all of the work. good guy tho

very nice guy, very personable. his class is all matlab which is very dry but he does a pretty good job with it. little tip; if nothing else put lots of time into the take home midterm and final, its the easiest way to get a good grade...heinsight

I took OPT 442 in 1996.  Tom can be boring, but he's clear.  I've never met a professor who had as much concern for his students.  He once taught the recitation because he felt he had done a poor job explaining a concept in class.  The "seminar style" of the last few lectures covered loads of material very useful for job interviews.
Impossible to reach!
class is all matlab. totally disorganized. always goes overtime, and even starts early. speaks in slow motion. friendly, though.
Very fair and clear
No Comments
Learned a lot.  Good professor.
An intersting, challenging teacher.  Somewhat boring at times, but certainly learned a lot.
Lectures were pretty interesting and Dr. Davis definitely has a passion for math. He was always willing to answer questions and was very accessible with office hours twice a week.
His lectures are enjoyable. He teaches at slow pace, willing to answer and explain questions. He has quite a sense of humour and is friendly and approachable.

He's a great lecturer, but can move through the material pretty quickly at times. He's always willing to help. Since most of the grade is based on tests and they can be challenging, it's best to start studying at least a week ahead.

I don't consider myself to be a math-oriented person, but Prof. Davis' class was super great and helped me understand a lot. He obviously cares about your retention and learning of the material and is very helpful in supporting your understanding. He is also an engaging lecturer which helps.
Great at explaining concepts, and has great lectures with many example problems. If you take 141, definitely consider taking it with him.
Maybe a good practitioner, but does not know how to teach. She blames students for not asking questions during the lecture. Maybe she needs to learn teaching in graduate class 101.
Bad instructor, doesn't care about student's needs.

For being in grad school and teaching, she is doing very well. She was always more than willing to help at her office hours, and she would answer questions at midnight sometimes. Very knowledgeable for being so young. I wish the course had less math.. that was one thing I think the course could do without. Great person!
seems smart in topic, yet has difficulty conveying information to other people

Absolutely terrible professor. She is extremely boring and hard to follow along with. She also is very unclear and doesnt explain things even when asked for clarification. She will just ask students to explain it, not herself. She doesnt know what she is talking about and will try explaining something for awhile before realizing that she is wrong.

I loved this class. Only class I looked forward to going to. Depressing topic, but really informs you about Refugee and Immigrant situations in America. Class discussion based, sit in a circle, several films shown. She does a great job of engaging and encouraging students to talk in class.
Bickel doesn't seem to care about his students success at all, and is very unwilling to answer questions about material, and is also very unwelcoming and unacommodating.

1. The lectures and the course materials are very disorganized.
2. The exams are graded strictly and carry a high weighting.
3. There is a lot of paper reading, and if you don't like ecology or macro biology, it's very painful.

Thought lectures were interesting and engaging, but topics often felt kinda disorganized. Prof Bickel had only one office hour per week--thankfully it fit into my schedule but I wish he was more accessible. Not a lot of opportunities to boost your grade if you do poorly on the tests, which require more critical thinking than you might expect.

Difficult class with interesting lecture material. My advice is to not just memorize the information he tells you but to completely understand the concepts. Slides are image-heavy so take good notes during lectures. Info on recitation papers are tested. Use the resources provided to you, office hours and review sessions are helpful.

He apparently hadn't taught BIO113 in over a decade, and it shows
Students are responsible for learning everything on the slides. His words, not mine
Exam avgs have been ~75s but there's no curve and he gives like 2 points of extra credit
Has so much material and gives so many examples he can't finish lectures on time

Lectures are enjoyable and the content relatively easy, however the test grading is brutal. No extra credit, no practice exams, unhelpful study guide, and harsh on regrade requests. I am no joke scoring higher on my exams for organic chemistry than for this class.

Really really caring and understanding. However, I felt like I understood the material well and still didn't do great on tests. No extra credit allowed in the class, and it is hard to do well if you slip up on any exam.
This is a lecture heavy class, but they are all recorded and he is available for help outside of class
He's a nice guy I guess but the worst biology professor I've ever had. Boring class too
He is great! Very clear, very helpful. His accent is a little hard to understand at first but in time it gets cute. Overall he's a very kind, well-qualified teacher of calculus.

One of the best professors I have had at the U of R. He is very organized and clear. He also always explains the reasoning behind calculus concepts. I knew several people who were registered for this class with other professors but would attend his lectures instead because he was so good.
He is soooooo cute! Very intelligent!

Lai was very soft spoken but if you sit close to the front, you should be fine. He was very clear with presenting material and covered revalent examples. All test questions were more than fair and he often went over complex webwork problems. Overall a great teacher
Great professor for differential geometry, knows his stuff.

A nice and funny person, a brilliant researcher, but a very bad lecturer. He just goes through slides and bases classes purely on mathematical equations. The lectures are not engaging and difficult to follow. Exams were very easy - he's a lean grader.
brilliant researcher but not suitable for teaching

Physics113 with him was nothing to write home about. I'm sure he's better at higher-level physics, but struggles to explain physics at a more basic level. Lectures are dry and feature a lot of derivations that are sometimes helpful, often not. You should still attend since he sometimes will get test material from what he says in lecture or workshop
For Intro Physics II, it was miserable.  Like the last post said, lectures were so pointless less than a 1/4 of the class would attend lectures.  Without the book, students would be doomed.

Rajeev is woeful. Students stopped attending lecture because he goes on tangents unrelated to class material. He has a sense of humor, but beyond that no redeeming qualities that merit him teaching a class of UR's caliber
See previous listing -- I concur.

Rajeev is an advanced theorist, but his courses are well-paced and enlightening.  He explains the material in a way approachable to newcomers and still interesting and illuminating to those who "already know it."  Homework assignments are light.  Tests are reasonable.  I recommend him very strongly.
The professor seems nice, but the lecture was pretty average and lacked depth.
I love her

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Searle is a gem of the University of Rochester anthropology department. As a class discussion heavy class, doing the readings helps you get the most out of this class. She is thoughtful, engaging, funny, and really cares about how material is presented and student engage with it. I found class periods to be really engaging!

I have come away from each of her courses with the feeling that not a second of my time was wasted and that the experience was truly valuable. She is always available outside of class, super helpful, and really fun to talk to! Her classes do require serious participation (and a good amount of reading), but doing so is incredibly rewarding :)

Llerena Searle is a phenomenal professor. She is one of the most intelligent and well spoken individuals I have ever encountered. She genuinely cares for her students. She is a tough grader but in a fair way, if you put effort into the class you will be fine. She is the reason I want to major in Anthropology.
It's really easy for you to get A even you scored 80 percent or less in your exam, not just because of the extra credit but also the fair workloads and student hours, and workshops, etc.

The course moved very quickly because it was an accelerated summer class, she made the material feel much more manageable. You could tell she cared about her students actually understanding the material and doing well, rather than just making the class unnecessarily difficult. She created such a positive and encouraging environment.

Taking Orgo 1 in the summer is a lot, but if prof Tichy is teaching it, TAKE IT!! It is so worth it; she genuinely cares about her students doing well and is super understanding of the summer intensive schedule. Numerous extra credit opportunities and take home assignments that help boost your grade. It is worth it to take Orgo 1 summer with her
She's great, clears up any doubts, understanding and fun! She's very passionate and always looking for constructive feedback. Great experience

I had her for the lab lecture and lab of CHEM 131, you work in random groups, she does not really answer questions when you email her, and makes labs more confusing than they actually are. Also, be prepared to code :(

Dr.Tichy genuinely want her students to do well, and is great at teaching/explaining concepts. Summer orgo is intense, but if you show up consistently, it's doable. Class size is small, which is nice, She gave multiple extra credit opportunities . Her own set of lecture notes template and workbook problems are helpful for exams. RECOMMEND!

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: FMS 131 was the worst college course I've taken. Big lecture-style class but attendance was mandatory and for some reason they tried to make it discussion-based? The "lecture" part was mainly powerpoints with quotes from that day's reading (aka lazy&pointless). Oh. And the convoluted prompts for "response papers" (graded by TA's--very inconsistent)

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: I took Intro to Media Studies with Professor Haidu last semester and I liked the class, even though it was for Humanities Cluster. There is a ton of readings (some are pretty difficult) for class but she explains it pretty well. The class is graded on midterms, weekly journals, and participation. She grades pretty hard in general, but is nice.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: This class was terrible for me. The professor is alright. She's a lot nicer and more helpful at her office hours. The topic of this class is just dry and uninteresting to me, just required for my major. Tons of reading about useless things. Go to class, do the homeworks, ask questions, go to office hours, study and you will get an A+

She made this class super interesting (sparking my interest as an AH minor) and helped a lot outside of the classroom. Studying for the tests were lots of work and the readings were dense and difficult, but very well explained in class and super interesting (the responses helped me grow as a writer too). Definitely recommend.

I had Haidu for Hist of Photo, and she made the class very interesting. The exams were a little tricky as you had to remember lots of photo ID's and there is alot of emphasis on participation in class but she knows her stuff and her lectures are very interesting :) I recommend taking her classes
Engaging lecturer.  A very fair, but tough grader.  The readings are difficult.  Helpful outside of class.
She's amazing!
Man, I wish I were in her league

The course was interesting on its own, which helps things along.. She's not the most interesting lecturer (class was 1.25 hrs and i would start checking my watch around a 1/2 hr to 45 min through), so when the stuff we discussed got less exciting the second half of the semester, I had a lot more trouble paying attention.
No Comments
Some problems with course, readings too hard/boring/much.  Overall not a harsh grader and fair.

Class entirely lecture, with occasional student participation. Prof obviously extremely knowledgeable, but lectures unfocused, tangential, hardly spent any time on the actual readings. 90% of grade was three 7 page essays, not an easy grader but not an especially tough one either. Feedback was brief. Fairly low workload, mostly short readings.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Classes are basically discussions about the reading, so make sure you read to know what is going on. You're graded off three 7 page papers which he grades relatively easily, but you should definitely pay attention during discussion because you can always use that in your papers. Boring at times, but if you are interested in lit then you're good.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Test heavy', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: I like this professor but i wish he would give us less homework and lower his voice. I always end up getting a headache.

I loved Professor Michael. He was kind and knowledgeable and respected every student's input. Participation is not required and he won't necessarily call on you randomly, but you get so much more out of his classes if you're part of the discussion. Every class consisted basically of discussions about the books, so you'd be lost if you didn't read.

Great Professor! Deeply cares about his students and will go out of his way to gte to know you/help you. Very articulate and enthusiastic. Tough grader but willing to work with you on papers and often gives opportunities for rewrites. One of the best professors at UR!

Nice guy/decent professor. Is very good at leading discussions, but values certain students comments over others. He basically calls on the same four people all class and it can get pretty boring. Easy to approach and very clear on objectives. Pretty tough grader. Overall, pretty good teacher.
Very Nice Guy, but classes are very boring when he lectures. When they are discussions they are better. Fair grader!
Really smart guy, which can help and hurt. He is clear on what he wants, doesn't waste your time with busy work and treats you like adults.
only real problem was he jumped around a lot in class, switching subjects than going back, etc.
Very enthusiastic about the course, lots of reading, but the book choices were decent.  Papers weren't graded too strictly, if you write well you won't have a problem.

I took this course for my public health major. It is an interesting class that shows your a different side of health and gender studies. The class, though, it extremely heavy on history and not on public health. The course readings are all about women and health, but they date back to the 1800s and before.
Super chill professor, very passionate about what he's teaching.
He's great.

(WRTG 273) Wayy too much work for a 2-credit class. Assignments are almost all written and mostly talking about yourself. (easy?-ish) Stay on top of everything or you will fall behind. She is nice and will work with you if you reach out. She obviously knows a lot about English, so if you have questions about that, her feedback is valuable.

Ashley is undoubtedly one of the kindest professors I've had at the UofR. Provided excellent writing feedback and truly cared about our growth as writers and students. She provides ample opportunities to improve your grade through draft revisions and peer feedback. If you are looking for a good WRTG105 professor, look no further!

Please take this professor's class. Don't hesitate. Even though the class wasn't interesting enough, her grades were very nice (almost everybody gets A in my class). The workload isn't that much comparing to other professors. The only thing is it's a small class and you cannot skip one without any reasons.

In my writing class, the workload revolves heavily around reading assignments, making it quite demanding. The teacher's approach involves regular low grades after each task, which initially seemed daunting. However, the silver lining lies in the promise of a curved final exam grade, offering hope for those struggling along the way.

The professor is responsible to her students; grades are fair. If you submit everything and participate in class, you will be fine. The professor's feedback is very useful. It's not tough to get an A.
He is the best professor I have ever had at the University of Rochester. He inspired me to major in philosophy.
Extremely approachable and I willing to help every student out to his best ability. It's been a great semester!!
He is the teacher you want for EVERY class. What a great guy and a great teacher! Extremely helpful and very approachable.

Jeff Glick is the man! I had him for ethics and introductory logic. His enthusiasm for teaching and willingness to help are outstanding. If you attend class (which I'd bet you'll actually want to attend his classes), you will not need to do much additional work to get an A. The textbooks are both cheap and are used a decent amount.

He's very engaging with the material and current day. Best philosophy professor i've encountered so far. In a semi large class, he still gives detailed feedback on every paper.  He's very dedicated to teaching students.

Glick is a really nice person and is always willing to help a student with things that aren't understood in class. There are a few intersting topics in this course. If you are really intersted in philosophy, he is a great professor to learn from.
Unbelievable. Amazing. Hands down best professor that I have had.
Great professor.  Makes class fun and interesting, good at explaining hard stuff.  If you work hard in this class you can do really good but if you don't its pretty hard.

Jeff Glick is the man. In my opinion he is the best professor in the philosophy department at UR so far. He knows his stuff and knows how to convey it to students in ways that he does not come off as "arrogant" or stuck up like many others. He is very kind and will go out of his way to help you understand the material. Take a class with him.

god bless this guy, he is so charismatic, he is even theatrical, but i wish he gave himself more respect, and acted like a professor, i mean i wish he were more cocky, cos he could be, i mean, this guy is great, bless his soul, he should also dress more like a professor, give more of a professor aura... i love him though
He is a great professor. He is very fun and makes it as interesting as he can. I would highly recommend taking a class of his.
Very helpful and easy to understand. Take his classes!

Jeff is a smart engaging guy, he knows a lot about the subject and is always willing to go back and do something over and over until everyone gets it.  The class moves slowly because of this, so if logic comes naturally to you you may find the class boring.
She makes the tests very easy to study for. Not an incredibly interesting lecturer but easy class.
Strict grader and not the best lecturer. Extra credit will get you the A in this class.
it is ridiculously easy to get above a B or even get an A in this class you could not take a single exam and get a B but I do not feel like I actually learned anything in this class
Difficult topics but easy to understand with Youtube. So much extra credit that it's almost impossible not to get an A. Can't really teach so don't rely on lecture to learn anything.

The prof either goes too fast at some points or way too slow. It feels like you are not learning much but end up with an A at the end because of the point system. Her lectures were not very organized.
get them to like you without being annoying or a suck up if, one likes you they both do and you're chilling

Much better lecturer compared to Knowles. Matson seemed enthusiastic and actually interested in what she was teaching. Easy to earn an A in the course due to test corrections and extra credit opportunities.

Bad professor. Bad lectures. Extremely easy class if you took AP Chemistry. Very low cut off for an A (you can fail every single exam and get an A if you do all the easy extra credit). If she didn't have required attendance I don't think anyone would go to her lectures, you're better off reading the textbook or learning from YouTube.

The lectures themselves were fine and understandable. You will feel like you know what you are doing and then you will get to the exam and everything will hit the fan. Notorious for making exams too long and difficult.

I can cut her some slack because it is her first year doing 131, but holy shit. The lecture slides were practically the same for every lecture and somehow things on the test were nowhere to be found, only verbalized in class, which makes it literally impossible to do test corrections because they ask you to cite the slides you got it from.

I and many of my classmates found the lectures to be easy to follow but on the tests themselves there were things that just didn't match up or were hard to study for. Honestly overall it was just a really awful class for me and as I understand it, for many other people as well.
You will never have any idea what is going on, then as soon as you understand the lectures, you get to the test and it is completely different content.

1. Topics can be complex and lectures good, but can be hurried. Study, ask qs, engage with the material and you'll be fine (grading system is generous!).
2. Empathize with her! You'll adopt a different perspective that'll get you farther in class & life.
3. The two of them are part of gen chem. Have an open mind, and try to work around problems.
Is incapable of teaching concepts without either overcomplicating concepts or completely rambling. Overall terrible.
I learned nothing in this class and bombed all the tests, but extra credit allowed me to get an A so I can't really complain!

1. Teaching ability has improved relative to Prof. Knowles.
2. Office hours are helpful.
3. Provides a large number of extra credits; learning is not important.

I enjoyed her lectures--she's clearly enthusiastic about what she teaches, and is better at highlighting important info than Prof. Knowles. Office hours are helpful if you're struggling with anything. 

Same with Prof. Knowles, tests are difficult but extra credit is plentiful. An A is possible even if you bomb every test.

I find it absurd that the exam averages were so low in the class and yet almost everyone can do well through completing constant extra credit opportunities. That's not the point of a class! I learned practically nothing since the profs never seem to notice when people are lost. I wish they put in more effort, since this could be a neat class.

This class was honestly a very funny class hence the tag. Matson was very egotistical and was a bad teacher. Everyone got 40-50% averages on exams but got A's as long as people did extra credit. I did not learn much from this class I just freestyle on the exam questions lololol.

yes matson is tough, but i liked her better than knowles. i never really found her passive agressive, but i agree that the exams were long but you get a cheat sheet. however, i thought she lectures really well, knowles i usually wanted to fall asleep. if you don't test well, just do the extra credit and you'll get an A. very nice in office hours.
lecture rlly bad the slides dont do much save urself now xoxo j major in humanities i love you
Nicer than Knowles but still lectures are very confusing and many things have to be self taught.

Even though she is a college professor, she behaves like a high school, condescending ap teacher. I felt she rushed through slides and was quite passive-aggressive and rude at times, especially when a student tried to leave after attendance and said "don't forget to slam the door behind you" after a test. Knowles>Matson

I prefer Knowles over Matson. I felt Matson was sometimes a bit rushed and her slides didn't contain enough information. The class has so many extra credit opportunities that it doesn't really matter though. It's relatively easy to get an A.

Her lectures are easier to follow than Knowles'. But I don't like how she talks down to us like we are 5yo. She says things that rub me the wrong way sometimes. But not a hard course, lots of extra credit to get an A. Points system. EC is graded harshly but attending class gives you points. Lecture is recorded. Final is optional.

She was good for explaining some concepts of chemistry in class. Although her exams are pretty tough, there were lots of extra credit opportunities to make up for. She is decent in office hours, and I think y'all can get a good grade if y'all attend in every class and do not lost for extra credit opportunities.

Matson is an okay professor. She teaches the easier concepts in 132. Despite this, the questions she puts on tests are SUPER LONG and detail heavy, so memorizing her fixations are key to acing exams. However, this doesn't erase the fact that Matson, despite her bubbly and high school teacher vibe, is a very passive aggressive professor. Not great.

Worst class you will take freshman year. She is really passive aggressive, creates difficult tests, and chooses super inconvenient times to do attendance. She speaks at a level that shows she doesn't fully understand what she is teaching, and is kind of rude when people ask questions.

Matson made me appreciate Dr. H more. She even admitted to several of her students that her lecture slides suck. Additionally, Matson is quite an unaccommodating professor and tends to act fake in lectures. Even her exam grades in her were so bad that she almost curved the exam for the first time. Matson needs to give out more practice tests.

I thought her lectures were atleast better than Knowles. However, she is the worst. She masks her rudeness with this fake elementary school teacher vibe, and acts like the class is at fault for the low exam scores. You won't learn shit in this class. Just do all the extra credit for an A.

Matson's teaching is convoluted. Basic concepts often become confusing, leaving complex concepts impossible to understand with just her lectures. I didn't interact with her at all, but she seemed slightly condescending to us during lecture. Overall, don't expect to learn much (from her). You'll be fine if you do most or all of the extra credit.
The best teacher ever. I think I learned everything I need for chemistry in my life through this class. Definitely recommend 10/10.

Professor Matson is like if you took your favorite elementary school teacher and crossed it with a chill and helpful college professor. Those who complain she "treats us like children" are L students! Like brozo(s), you want a professor who doesn't let you get a free A for her extra credit "art projects" so you can not take the final exam? (satire)

Tests were graded very harshly, averages lower than 50% and lectures were rushed and confusing. Your grade depends on how many extra credit assignments you complete, so I learned nothing. As many others have mentioned, I felt like an elementary school student with her. I honestly don't know where I would be if not for AP Chem.

She's funny but she's a terrible teacher. She can't explain things without overcomplicating things. Grading makes no sense and her expectations are never clearly outlined. The entire class basically depends on extra credit. You can pass the class. Don't expect to learn.

As mentioned by many others, Matson treats us like elementary students. Even worse, she is not a good lecturer. She rushes through her lectures. She includes practice problems in her slides but doesn't actually do them during her lectures. She has the answer already typed out, and brushes over the process. Chem 132 was an awful experience.

Rushes through lectures and is not good at explaining challenging concepts. Treats students like children and has very obvious favorites. Overall, class is challenging and you will have to learn material on your own.

She rushes through her lectures. She is very open about her opinions on her students, and is a tough professor. The tests for this class are unnecessarily difficult but this class is point based which is nice. Matson was my least favorite professor for this class because she was not consistent with her teaching.

Prof. Matson is better than Prof. Knowles but by a little bit. She can be quite passive aggressive at times and treats us like we are in kindergarten... Her exams are so hard that test averages were never above 50%. Going to class vs. sleeping in and teaching it to myself later made no difference. Horrendous experience with chem yet again.

Class contents are very different from chem 131, and much more difficult. Extra credit can't even help even though it seems like there are a lot extra credit assignments. Had to take it as my major requirement and now I changed my major.
I think Prof Matson was the better 132 prof, but she was still very hard. Goes through lecture slides very fast, but is very helpful if you ask a question or go to office hours.

Matson started out the semester looking promising since she's super enthusiastic and has passion for what she teaches. However, her grading criteria are super harsh (gives out zeros often and doesn't give partial credit on exams under since the class was a point bucket system). She was also not accommodating and brushed away student complaints.
I freaking love her and her humor during the lecture, though CHEM 132 is problematic.

Professor Matson was an interesting professor. She started off the year strong in teaching, but as the semester went on, it seemed as she got more and more frustrated with the class. She also graded extremely tough on inforgraphics, PAC's, and exams. However, I will say, she was a very nice individual.

She did sort of belittle us sometimes and I do think its a problem that the exam averages are so low. The point based system should not be an excuse to have shitty lectures and terrible exam questions. I 100% recommend doing the infographics and PACS - they were graded super unreliably until the end of the semester, but the points still help.

Initially, I was thinking she would be a great professor, compared to Prof. R, whom she co-taught with, because I just could not understand R's lectures, but about halfway through the semester, I found it difficult to retain information from her lectures because she went incredibly fast. Rewatching her lectures helped, but it took extra time.

She comes off as friendly at first, but don't be fooled... she is rude, does not respect students, a harsh grader on silly assignments. would not recommend. I WOULD recommend doing as many of the infographics and profile a chemists as possible bc the tests are practically impossible.

She is overall a poor professor. She goes too fast in lectures and the tests are not at all fair, nor do they accurately test your knowledge of chemistry. You'll probably get an A if you put in the effort but it requires a lot (a term project and 3 module infographics on top of tests for me). Unless CHEM132 is required for major, don't take it.

I liked Matson at first. I don't now. The grading on PAC and IG is ridiculous. The tests are insanely hard (49% and 38% averages). She is condescending, has a fake personality, and acts like poor test grades don't reflect poorly on her. I didn't go to class all semester but still got an A, focus on projects not tests.

At first, I liked Matson, she kept the class interesting in comparison to Rothberg. With this being said, she is my least favorite professor now. She treats the class like high schoolers who are far beneath her. If you scroll down on her reviews, you will see someone quoting her, and I bear witness to that exact statement she made during lecture.

Matson seems like she's gonna be a good lecturer at first, but her lectures are too fast and hard to follow. She comes off as very fake and doesn't have a good reputation (she apparently is mean to TA's). Also, everyone knows that PAC and infographics are also graded way too harshly, you have to do way too much work to get a decent grade.

Professor Matson is one of the best professors in the Chem department. With all the opportunities she gives for extra credit, her grading style is fair and if you pay attention you will do well. Also, her lectures are pretty clear and not too complicated, most students that struggle in this course do so because they don't put in the effort.

I like this grading system, I think it is actually very reasonable, but the difficulty of the exam is too hard, and the lecture assumes that you have already learned everything, and it is not very helpful. The grading of info and PAC are too subjective and the lab report's score comes out too slow.

Matson can be quoted as follows:
"so what we're doing moving forward is if students have demonstrated no effort in their infographics we will not be grading their assignments... there's no reason we should be having a less then 50% average on the exam." She is openly resentful of the students, and makes everything more difficult for no reason.
Nothing made sense honestly. I have never cried more from a class. The frustration was horrible and when I asked questions I feel like I never got a straight answer.

Probably the hardest grader I've ever had. She seems like a nice person but she'll take off points for literally everything. You can probably make it through without going to every lecture if you have taken chem in hs. I did like that she had different assignments we could choose to do for credit. And she made our quizzes optional. She was alright.

Professor Matson is a very good professor. She thoroughly teaches the topics and relates them to real-life scenarios effectively. Her grading strategy is very nice; it allows you to demonstrate how you know the material and score well in the class. Chem 132 is a hard class and she teaches it well.

Professor Mandala is an interesting man who's clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The guidelines may have been a bit vague with no specific grading criteria and limited communication from the professor, but I thought the course was worth it.

I love the approach of how Prof. mandala teaches. Even though he speaks so slowly, but he presents the lecture in a way everyone could understand. My favorite thing about him is he challenges us to go for office hours and also allows students to resubmit a paper if they did not do well. I will definitely recommend him because he is so good!

great professor. gave useful feedback on essays and allowed students to rewrite and resubmit their papers if their grade fell below the average. entirely paper based so there is quite a bit to read and write but very manageable. would definitely recommend!

Take it, take it, take it! The best History Professor I have seen out there. Always encourages his students to attend office hours, and even asked students to redo their papers if they fall below the class average. An incredible professor he is.

Professor Mandala is a gem. Hes extremely experienced and knows how to present the lectures. The most incredible thing about this class is being thought from the perspective of an African. Even though he is a tough Professor and has an accent, hes understanding and he dedicates a lot of time to his student in ensuring that they do well in class.

comment: I learn so many things in this class. If you are interested in History and want to learn more about Africa from a perspective of an experienced person, you should give this guy a shot. This class requires so many writings(short papers), but it is worth it because all you need to do is to get the work done. Take it!

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: An experience Professor who has been teaching his entire life. Well-knowledgeable and up to date about the topics. I got to learn so many things about global and African history from this professor. Though he is old and he teaches slowly, he is the very few of the best you can find out there. I will admonish you to take his history classes.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Syllabus is extremely vague, gives almost no instructions about homework, gets mad at you when you contact him to ask questions about the extremely vague assignments, refuses to give feedback on assignments, extremely rude and condescending to students, seems to grade things arbitrarily, INFLEXIBLE!!
One of the best History professors I have had. He's not a tough grader and makes the lecture accessible for all. Just show up, participate and do your research paper.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: His classes are really insightful about the history & geopolitics surrounding to Africa. The readings can be very painful to read, but they also teach you a lot about subjects like the Angolan Civil War. What's critical is that you learn to separate the actual history from the class' pro-Communist indoctrination and to think for yourself.
Amazing Professor, I loved every bits of his class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor creates an atmosphere for good classroom conversations and loves when students have questions and dialogue among themselves. It is only boring if no one does the reading, so don't take this class if you are not willing to read at least 30 pages a week. Not an easy A, you need to read, participate, and submit quality papers.

I don't by any means dread his class, but it is incredibly boring. I was very interested to learn about Africa, however my own research and the assigned novels have taught me far more than he has. Not a bad guy by any means, just rambles without giving much actual information. The novels are good, but the articles assigned are also very boring.

This class strongly influenced how I think about both history and the current world order. There are many assumptions that have become mainstream in the social sciences and policy world about the Global South and what is best for it, which this class challenged. (Of course he has his own biases too.) Work hard, ask questions and you'll learn a lot.

Mandala's classes are as good as you make them.  If you expect your professor to outline the path towards an A, you should avoid his classes.  But his classes are very informative, and if you try to talk to him 1-on-1 about the course material he's very accommodating.  Classes require lots of writing, but he's lenient on deadlines.

I loved all my classes with Mandala. He is a truly inspirational man. It is a great thing to be taught about Africa and the third world from someone who is actually from there. He makes you work hard, but is available during office hours. Truly kind man.  He wrote me a letter of recommendation for grad school. Learn from someone different.

Don't be afraid of his accent; he is actually a pretty witty guy. However, he is the type of teacher that wants particular things, but will not hint to you what those things are which can be pretty humiliating during class discussion or result in a poor grade on assignments. Besides the novels, class material is pretty boring.

Professor is very hard to understand, the class consists of people going over the readings the whole time - basically a book club you're paying a ton of money for.  Never had any real lectures.  He fell asleep in class a few times, showed a bunch of movies.  Was generally a nice guy, though.

Made a class with incredible potential into one of the worst classes ive taken at school.  All he had us do was summarize readings which we read out loud in class while he just sat there for 2 hours (he fell asleep in class one time), and he simply lectures the last 30 mins of class. also it is hard to understand what he says due to his accent.
Avoid his courses at all cost!!!

All comments here are extremely harsh.  Mandala is an interesting man, while sometimes his lectures can be extremely boring at other times you will be completely enthralled.  He does not express his views as openly as some have previously said and seems to be a very intellectual nice man.  Would recomend this class to any history major
This teacher is one of the most closed minded individuals who, at times, has the ability to make students feel as though their insight is absolutely useless.

Overall, I appreciated my experience in Mandala's Class.  However, I work better in a seminar environment rather than a straight lecture.  Although finding his class difficult, I learned a lot.  Elias may not be hot, but he has a style all his own.

An intelligent man but a poor lecturer.  He assigns good readings and provides pretty decent instruction on a basic level, but his classes are a chore and so is he, sometimes.  Not recommended, but not awful by any stretch.

I think he does a good job in lecture, very interesting material.  Not the most clear professor out there, but he does have sense of humor which clearly can be interpretted as being patronizing.  When I went to office hours for assistance with a research paper, he was very helpful.
Mandala does not give effective feedback about how you are doing in his class and his course objectives are not clear.  In the end, though, you still learn, and he grades easliy.
Worst professor ever. Do not take his classes. Doesn't even know what he is talking about
Ruined the class for me basically. Very patronizing and wants you to be able to read his mind. Take a class with this guy, and you'll greatly wish you hadn't.
he cares about you, if you think is too hard or complicated just reach out!!
The class was very fast-paced and was heavily reliant on test grades and problem-set scores.

comment: Always read the statistics portion of the textbook, because there are quizzes (important!) and he only tests the numbers. No need to stay for class after the quizzes (always at the beginning) because lectures are the same as textbook and they are not very useful (participation is count as extra credit but earning it does not help much).

Professor Druckman is an amazing professor and genuinely wants his students to do well. Lectures were really interesting and well put together. Exams are straightforward to what we cover in class and readings.
I love Druckman, he really wants his students to succeed.

Great Professor who really cares about his students! While participation is not necessary, it will definitely help you out to do so. He usually tells you about pop quizzes before they are given, and the assignments are not bad at all.

Druckman was a great teacher. responds to emails within minutes and is super understanding and down to earth. Focuses on learning rather than purposefully making things hard for students. loved his class.

I took the W with him and it was well worth my time. By the end of the course I had a whole experiment design completed, and his feedback was really helpful and encouraging. He's incredibly flexible, genuinely cares about students, and gives equal respect to student comments, regardless of political leanings. I only wish I had him sooner.
Very good professor highly recommend

Prof. Druckman is an incredible teacher with wonderful insights into polarization, polling, and misinformation. He also cares about his students, always responding to emails with great feedback. Finally, he loves teaching research methodology--an underemphasized topic at UR. Don't miss a chance to learn from one of the best political scientists!

One of the best professors I've ever taken, and I'm not even a Russian or Comparative Literature major. This man cares deeply about what he teaches, his students' well-being, and keeping them engaged in class. I have learned so much from him, and he has become one of my favorite professors at this university.

You wouldn't believe how funny the faculty think it is either, but I can't speak for them all. They have group chats exactly like you do.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: This is, of course, not for everyone - but if you are sensitive to course loads, do not take this class. The professor does not care about you. If you think he is going to waste your time, he will. Past students of his have almost committed or overdosed, and he has proudly spoken about it. Read The Dark Triad by Grayson Wick.

Professor Givens made all of his lectures really engaging and encouraged input from his students. He had a clear enthusiasm for the material that made me eager to attend class. Assigned a good amount of reading but the workload is very manageable. Overall a great professor. His Tarkovsky class has been one of my favorite at the U of R.
Really fun class and great professor!

I love Professor Givens, so knowledgeable about the subject and matters at hand. He cares about his students and really strives to make class as thought provoking as possible. Lots of reading for this class, and he does grade harsh, but it has driven me to become a better writer overall, he WANTS you to understand the content.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Taken numerous courses with John, and he's an amazing professor. One of the smartest and kindest individuals I've met. He makes you work for it in his lit classes, but you will be a better writer and reader because of it. At times it can be lecture heavy, and I wish it was more of a seminar style, but office hours are where you can really learn.
Really energetic and engaging. My interest in Russian is now higher. Offers a lot of extra credit so if you go to classes, you will be fine.

He is awesome- very entertaining and funny in class, sure to make you want to learn Russian. He's nice and very supportive if you have a problem. Tests are mild- if you study, you'll probably do well. They're fair at any rate. He's very knowledgeable and engaging. Great professor.
Best professor I have had at U of R!

AMAZING. Funny, great teacher, goes the extra mile, really enjoys the material and makes you enjoy it too. A lot of work but you will learn a TON and learn it well. Take his classes, they will be the highlight of your college career.

I love him. His Russian courses are good, but try one of his others and you'll be forever enchanted! He is an extremely hard grader with essays, but he really cares what you learn from the novels and discussions. He wants you to be involved with the text and for it to change you in someway. He's just awesome.

Prof Givens is the reason I'm still involved with Russian. I took 101/102 with him, and though he takes a little getting used to, he's an extremely good professor who knows his material. The tests could be better, as could the fact that Laura TAs the class, but the class overall is awesome. He will go out of his way to help anyone really interested

I still love this man! Entertaining lectures that double back a little so you get reenforced as you go along. Very hard paper grader, however, he reads everything with a very attentive eye! Extremely hard grader, but amazing and helpful and I just love him!

I love this man. I've taken two of his courses, plan on taking two more, and I just finished up a summer doing research with him as my faculty mentor. He's extremely helpful and very entertaining in class. He's also very accessible and eager to help out anyone who shows an interest in Russian.
Really great guy, MUCH better than his wife. Funny, helpful and informative. I felt like I learned a lot, even though I didn't do so well. The only trouble with his courses is Laura as the TA.
I love this man. He is what convinced me to major in Russian. Great guy, very kind and helpful.

Took 101 and 102 with him, fair grader, easy tests.  As long as you can learn some vocab, you'll do fine.  He's a funny guy, and makes the early morning lectures worth it most of the time.  A bit crazy with his sayings and poems.
Lectures vary, but are generally entertaining. Very accepting and funny. Very fair grader. Exams were a tad lengthy.
wonderful!
No Comments
Very entertaining and funny, take as many of his classes as you can, tests can be a little tough at times, very approachable and understanding
I'm absolutely smitten with him.  He's incredible.
AWESOME

comment: There's only three exams in this course, but plenty of opportunity to get credit to make up for where you might not do as well. For example, if you come to class frequently (or at least have a friend in class to tell you when they have their "discussion" cards) that's an easy 10 points to weight on a decent amount of your grade.

The professor was the biggest problem in this course. Lectures often felt disorganized and unclear, and it frequently came across like he was not prepared or not fully on top of the material. The exams harsh are harsh and the lack of clear direction made studying feel like guessing everything is fair game and nothing is posted.

comment: I enjoyed how this course was driven by data and how its focus was looking directly at how race impacts political trends and Professor Komisarchik is incredibly well researched. The grading criteria is super vague. You don't know what you write is correct or wrong. The textbook is amazingly hard to read and difficult to understand.

Amazing professor, has relevant work experience and brings that to his class. Super helpful and knowledgeable in his field, great class overall! :)

very good professor. Very intelligent man and knows what he is talking about. Very clear and straight to the point when it comes to things. very sweet and caring :-)

Professor Moon is very Nice and Helpful. Always there for students.

Professor Moon is one of the most talented and humble professor I have seen in ECE department. Very understanding
