Most caring professor I have ever had. Always willing to extend office hours and respond to emails in detail. Very receptive to even the dumbest questions during class, so don't be afraid to ask. Do the suggested exercises before the exam and you will get an A.
Amazing professor, knows her field really well, will answer any questions in or out of class. Put in the effort and you'll get an A.

Prof Salur was great. She was very clear at communicating the most important topics throughout the semester and was very upfront about what we would be tested on. Lectures could be a bit dry but that comes along with the course material. All in all would highly recommend.

Sema is super smart and a very nice woman. Her class was difficult and she tried really hard to help her students understand the material. There was a lot of webwork homework, but that is the case with any MTH164 professor. She moves quickly, so if you have trouble grasping a concept in a few minutes you may need to get extra help.
Wonderful lectures and easy to comprehend
She's crazy smart and sometimes it's hard to understand because she goes so fast. If you ask a question though, she is great at explaining things in a different way. Don't be afraid to speak up!

She knows her stuff and is pretty enthusiastic about but goes through her lectures very quickly (hopefully you're a fast note-taker). Do as much practice as possible and get as much help as you can because you're gonna need it! Not an easy course.

Salur's brain goes faster than her chalk a lot so her lectures can end up mildly confusing and frustrating if you like things to be neat and in order. She loves people coming to office hours and will help you after class too, you just need to be proactive.

Sema was the best teacher!!! She was clear and concise, explained all the concepts fully but never wasted time dilly-dallying with extraneous information or explaining things that were implied. She made the material seem super easy, and practically told us exactly what would be on the exams. Also she gave us candy on her birthday. :)

I had Sema for MTH 162.  She's very kind, clear, and intelligent. In my opinion she was the best professor of my semester. She gave extra review sessions on friday/saturday for those who needed them.  Only down side is that she goes through problems at a semi-quick pace.

She's an awesome teacher. Sometimes she goes fast, but she's willing to stop and clarify if students have questions. Also, she'll usually summarize the previous lecture for the first bit of class and make it even clearer. Oh, and she's really nice.
asd

Very enthusiastic teacher. Cares very much. thick accent, but you adapt after a week or two and hardly even notice. Always a good laugh or two for each lecture. Makes VERY easy tests. Highly recommend and I hope to TA for her in the spring

She's so helpful. Refuses to move on until every student is comprehending the material presented. She wants to see people do well, so she doesn't make the exams too hard, and also will give out "bonus points" if she felt that the test was "too hard." My favorite professor so far.

best calc professor i've ever had. she truly cares about her students and will do anything she can to give you a good grade. find a way to make her class fit your schedule, this is honestly a time where you should take the professor, not the class

Professor Salur is amazing. She's funny, teaches stuff that actually appears on the test, and cares about the success of her students. I'm pretty lousy at math and I'm actually doing pretty well in the class! Really cool lady.
Awesome person! Very easy class. Reiterates material over and over and over...Great for those with little prior exposure to calculus-based math
Witty, cheerful, helpful.  Salur really cares about her class.

She cracked jokes to wake us up, and went out of her way so that we could get better grades on our tests (she allowed a re-test for the first midterm, which only our class was offered). She answered homework questions in class and focused on what she thought was most important for the final.  Very good teacher. Funny and enthusiastic!
really great professor--nice, helpful, a good grader
Great teacher.  Always goes over the material well, and has a good sense of humor.

Extremely helpful, tried hard to give new information. Some students were rude because she was young and inexperienced, which caused her to fumble during the lectures, but she was fair and always answered questions quickly.

Confusing,not well spoken. Unable to get through a sentence without saying "um" and "like" 10 times.  Didn't learn anything. Doesn't seem to know what she is talking about. What she has written and what she tries to articulate often don't make any sense. Makes embarassing grammatical errors. Fair grader though.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: This class is a wild ride - you'll learn a lot, but the workload may make you nauseous. The Real Reader grades are like a blindfolded monkey, and Laura's feedback is as helpful as a screen door on a submarine. So hang on tight, because your grades will be a mystery until the end!

I really enjoyed Laura's class. She was well prepared and the lectures were organized. Something I really liked was her clear grading criteria for the WRT 273 class, which helped in indicating my course grade during the semester.
Exceptionnel teacher

This is a terrific course and Prof Harper really knows his stuff.  He adds lots of interesting interesting information about the history of math, well beyond what's in the text.  He comes off as intimidating at first but soon you realize he has a gruff style at times but is really very helpful and funny.  Take away:  math is incredible!

He mumbles a lot in class and his handwriting is near impossible to read. Luckily, the whole class is out of the book. The lectures themselves are near useless, though he is willing to explain things outside of class.
Overall the class isn't bad.  Harper looks, a kinda acts, like the old guy from back to the future.

Probability. The textbooks he uses are really terrible.  If you are taking a course with him, research the textbooks and pick anything but the one he lists.  He purposefully put a question on the exam stating that he expects no one to get it, but is curious.  And then there was no scale...Unclear explanations, and difficult homeworks.

Class gets kind of boring but he has a good sense of humor and occasionally has interesting comments.  Easy grader - assignments and tests are stress-free.  He's very approachable.  Expect to spend time reading the textbook, though.
If you have any questions he is really willing to explain. Sometimes the explanations are really long, but they are thorough!

Horrible professor, definately the worst I've had here. Unclear in class, mumbles a lot, and half the time you can't read what he's writting on the board.  He also has a tendency to randomly hit the board. Really confusing!! and horrible book too

I've had this dude for 2 classes. He is a  bit unclear at times and meanders but he is always willing to handle questions during class. The thing is that you have to speak up, or else he'll just continue on. doesn't do a lot to make the topic exciting, unless you're interested in it don't prepare to be entertained. Does have a good sense of humor

I never know what he is talking about in class, extremely unclear and confusing.  Never explains anything.  Only good quality is that he always lets you out of class early and homework is most of your grade.  Also, he confuses himself quite often with stupid mistakes when attempting to do "examples."

There are so many negative reviews about prof. enck but i thought he was a great professor. he really knew what he was talking about. he was also more than willing to help his students to work around deadlines if they missed class. the feedback he gave on work was always constructive and he graded based on effort/improvement.

Being in this class made me dislike drawing. Enck is harsh, unreasonable, and doesn't understand that students have things to do outside of his class. He openly disrespects students in class, grades extremely harshly, doesn't give any extensions, and doesn't even teach. This class made me constantly anxious and felt like a waste of time and effort.
This professor is the worst professor I have ever met in UR!!!!!!!!! Disrespect for the efforts, harsh in grading. This man ruins my day!!

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Prof Enck grades everything very harshly and expects a lot out of students for an intro drawing class. Your art projects will not be graded on effort, but quality, which is why he rarely gives out As. He's extremely petty and takes note of who's late to lecture and takes off points from your grade bc of this. This man honestly made me hate drawing.

Good person, bad teacher. He doesn't understand that "Art is Subjective". He grades and critiques everything based on his opinion. As an abstract sculptor himself, he teaches drawing surprisingly and wants you to follow every rule and rubric. Class is boring. It's more like a math class instead of an art class.

He might be a good architect, but definitely NOT a good teacher!!! He actually does not "teach" us knowledge, but just let us study by ourselves. He always grade the homework based on his own opinion, ignoring the progress we made through all the semester!!!!
The hardest class in my college, but not because of the course..... even though he is a good guy.

Sooooo many homework, three exams, seems fair, but he will give extra homework, he will even record extra videos for you to study in the spare time, and it is really frequent......even during the break.....  He is a good guy though. No words to say much about, he is a caring professor, and a good resarcher, he teaches usful things, but painful.

Javier is def a good person, but not a good professor. The class is disorganized and you should expect so many unexpected changes. This was the first semester he introduced exams (2 in total) into this course. This is a bad idea since it was a rush for him to make exams, too. Lastly, grades weren't on file before the deadline from registrar.

Bautista is far from a good lecturer and going to class is rarely worth it. The exams and assignments, however, were super fair! The semester-long group project is kind of a hit and miss tho, and really depends on who your group members are. Really easy overall, but I think I learnt most of the material from the textbook to be honest.

Even though he isn't the best lecturer, Professor Bautista is the nicest, most caring professor I have had. He truly cares about his students. If you have solid AP Stat and Math 201 knowledge, this class is an easy A, with a ton of available extra credit from HW.
Easy A, but you don't learn things. The only useful thing is SAS coding. You can learn from YouTube yourself within a week. Tons of extra credits.
Even though his lecture is hard + Difficult + Not Easy to Read, but he is a very nice professor who is willing to help you when you needed.

-2 Midterms and a Final(65% total), A project(25%), and homework(10%). 
-Each exam easier than the last. You get a cheat sheet. 
Got a 60, then a 75, then a 90 and got a B in the class. 
-I'm BAD at math and got a B. Got a D+ in MATH 201 if that helps. If you got a B- or above in the 160 series, you can very easily get an A
-javier is a good human
The most boring lecturer I have ever seen, the software we learn in class can be super useful, unfortunately he is just terrible at teaching, therefore this class is a waste of time and effort.
Why is everyone give out 5/5 when he is a bad lecturer, we didn't learn anything in his class, please ignore the fake comments from whoever it is, I just want to help you all to aviod the pain.

He is not that great of a lecturer but is extremely helpful and kind. He is always willing to meet with students outside of class to discuss projects or help with homework. He is truly a kind and caring guy

Kindest professor I've had, very caring and gets to know all of his students. Class is 40% project, 35% Homework, and 25% in class assignments. Project grading is really easy as long as you follow the guidelines. You will do poorly on the homeworks if you are sloppy. In class assignments are free 100s. Easy A if you give effort.
Really nice. Lectures you don't learn much, but if you study on your own you can do very well. 25% of the grade is a group project!!! So good!!!
Fake professor and don't know what he is talking about, any rating over 1, do not trust it.
Terrible professor, acting like a university professor, but doesn't even understand the material he is teaching, learnt nothing, super boring, waste of time.
Generous and kind professor. Lectures are not good enough, but tests are easy. The professor is very willing to help students.

Professor Bautista seems nice and willing to help. However, really don't enjoy his lecture. The material is not clearly taught. I didn't learn anything about how to use R studio. Cheat sheet is allowed. Hope I will still get an A though.

Professor Bautista did not give any curve for the test which means if you screwed up one midterm you might as well just drop/withdraw. His lecture sucks, just read by yourselves. Don't even bother if it's not a mandatory course for you.
what can i say
Terrible, run!!!

Not very good with lecture or teaching overall, read the textbook yourself and work with youtube instead of focus on the lectures, which are mandatory. If you had AP stats and math 201 you will know most of it so you don't need the lectures anyway. He will make it more confusing for you and you may un-learn what you knew.

comment: OK. Bautista is a super nice friend but definitely not a choice for learning math stats. u almost learn nothing from his lecture, even from his slides or materials. The course is not hard itself but he tends to make it very bad.
He is extreme unorganized and very forgetful. From his lecture you can easy tell that he is NOT prepared AT ALL! Try to avoid this professor if possible.
HWs are heavy but exams aren't hard.
Starting this semester, there are semester-long group projects for this course.
He is really nice and he skiped the hard parts. I just don't understand how can he get so many awful feedbacks here.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Um no
He probably is a good researcher, but not a good professor.

oh Javier, what can I say. Most caring professor I've ever had. Yet very unclear in his lectures. Left most of us more confused than when we came in. The mark of a good prof is when they have clear lectures, expectations, and exams. He had none of those. That being said he is the most accessible professor I've ever had. Wanna be friends with him.

Had him for HIST: 128 and 126. His lectures were by far the best I've experienced. They were very engaging, which was a key motivator for attendance. I wish he had recorded his lectures because I would definitely rewatch them on my own time. Very supportive and encouraging during and outside of classes. Exams are easy if you have studied.

comment: If you are looking to this class for an easy A, then I would recommend this class to you. Fleischman was concise, encapsulating, and funny. Unfortunately, I could trust neither historical nor current statements that Fleischman made, since sometimes he prioritized politics over objectivity. I hold no ill will, but he was rhetorically irresponsible.
Fantastic Professor, the lectures were interesting, the group project was fun, and the final is open note.

very easy to pass, amazing & info heavy lectures with vocab words, images, and videos. does have pop quizzes but he literally hints at when its going to happen. also sometimes plays music that his kids are interested in. aside from quizzes, tests are open note
Made each lecture extremely interesting and made me excited to go in each morning. After taking the class I feel like I know a lot about the subject and I wish that there were more teachers like him.

One of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures were electric and gripping. Our class had 60+ students, but he was still personable and accessible outside of class. Would strongly recommend to any student.

Not my favorite. He made the midterm the tuesday coming back from spring break and has unclear grading criteria for the midterm. Everyone told me that this was an easy A class but so far it is not looking like it. I personally didn't like his lecture style and he jumps around a lot making it hard to follow along. I would not recommend.

The class is self-graded, which alleviates a lot of the pressure of a college course. With that said, the readings and lectures are pretty interesting and worth completing! The final project is manageable and on whatever topic interests you. He wasn't always the easiest to contact outside of class but overall fine. Readings could be a bit long.

One of the best professors at the school. The class itself is self graded but he still makes it interesting enough that you want to come to every lecture. Readings can be pretty long but it really is a treat to listen to him talk about these topics. Very little work besides a final project and readings. Overall an amazing prof

Easy class while not being too boring either.
He is a fun professor that keeps lectures going.
If you don't mind a bit of reading a week, you'll probably enjoy his classes as a lot of the grading just has to do with discussions about what you read.

Attendance is not graded, but there's no way to catch up if you miss a lecture. papers are short and fun to write, but the final is very lecture heavy. Homework assignments are insightful and a good read. All in all, Fleischmann slays!

Professor Fleischman was a good professor overall, lectures were generally interesting and informative. The only real complaints that I have are that lectures weren't recorded, and that we could sometimes lose class time due to Powerpoints that weren't fully completed (lots of jumping around slides, or missing slides). Gave good feedback on papers.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: I had Professor Fleischman for postwar Europe. He is a good lecturer, but a bit disorganized and unclear about grading criteria. He doesn't really use slides with his lectures, so make sure to take in-class notes, as they will be valuable. He's definitely pretty laid back and tests and all graded assignments are pretty writing-heavy.

He's amazing! The class material is really interesting and he's so enthusiastic about what he's teaching. Lots of reading, but the readings are interesting and definitely worth your time. He is very accessible and clearly cares about his students and their success. Highly recommended!!!!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Simply the best, outstanding, and knowledgable about the subject to the peak. I really enjoy this class and also learning from a very young person. Trust me, it is worth taking this class, even if not this one, another class being taught by Professor Fleisch should do you fine.

Professor Fleischman is a great lecturer. He is very knowledgeable about the subject matter and you can tell that he is passionate about it. He is approachable, kind, and made the heavy subjects we talked about feel relevant and important. I really recommend taking a class with him - even if you don't necessarily like history!

Had Prof. Fleischmann during the "all online" semester-- but he was a fantastic guy through and through. The lectures were early morning but super interesting if not outright entertaining, there's no way I could've fallen asleep. Any time anyone had even the most esoteric questions, he'd almost always have an answer, too!

I had Fleischman my first semester at UR and he has by far been my favorite professor. Lectures are engaging and class discussion is encouraged, although not required. He always managed to give the class a laugh and rarely went off track, and even his tangents were fairly interesting. Highly recommended to anyone wanting to take a history course.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Favorite class I have taken out of all 3 years, best lecturer I have had in 3 years.
Probably my favorite class this semester. A great professor and very interesting subject matter.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: Fleischman is incredibly passionate about his course and is quite hilarious as he seems to constantly be having a crisis with technology. Lectures are very fun but be aware, he will sometimes randomly call on people from the roster for answers to questions when its a little too quiet. Overall, 11/10 professor.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: The class material itself was a lot of fun to cover. The professor is charismatic and clear about what he wants from you. His lectures are well structured and they're to the point, but he also slips in a lot of real life advice and jokes in there to lighten things up. The class isn't hard and the papers were manageable. Overall, a great experience.
Whenever you have a problem with someone in your course, he wants you to solve it on your own. What a wonderful person. Funny guy.
Funny for serveral years of low quality and high difficulty grades, his reputation suddently reversed in 2026

Great class, Vamivakas clearly cared that we understood the material and were doing well in the class. The textbook he wrote has everything you need. Test questions were all similar to problem banks giving lots of practice. Favorite class of the semester.
His lectures and textbook for the class are great. Tests were extremely fair as they are taken from problem banks shared with us for practice. Funny guy

Great professor when he lectures instead of using class time to solve problems you could do on your own. Unfortunately, most of class time is spent solving problems on the board. The way this class is structured currently makes it very easy with problem banks provided. All exam questions come from the problem bank with a minor number tweak.

I think he gets a bad rep from past years, but has changed his way of doing things. He was a great lecturer. Very engaging and made sure students understood the concepts. Given a problem bank every module and test questions were taken from that so very easy to do well if you study.
Avoid this man like the plague if you can. I'm so sorry for optics majors that have to suffer through his class.
Just avoid this class at all cost

comment: Generally okay

The TAs do all the work, but somehow never know what's going on either. He was so lazy this semester and everyone took the heat for that.

He cares very much whether you're understanding the material but sometimes his Exam questions have confusing wording. Work with TA's, read the book and make sure you understand the homeworks. The more time you spend studying and doing problems, the better you will do on the Exams. This is a difficult topic, but he's not a bad professor.

If, you are a optics major student, I feel sorry to inform you that you have to face Nick's education. And that experience would make you better because you cannot meet something tougher than this. If you are not Optics major and you have the option to take OPT 261, no matter what, just pick the alternative option.

Content of class is really helpful, but the overall quality of this class gives students a hard time to follow the pace of instruction.
If you don't have take it then don't take it
homework have nothing to do with class

Dr. K is a caring and personable professor who will find a way to connect with each of his students. The lectures were engaging and he incorporated group work frequently into classes, which kept things interesting. The workload is very manageable and he offers meaningful feedback for every assignment. I highly recommend taking any of his courses.

Professor Peterman is exceptionally knowledgeable about the topics taught and can answer anything you ask about it. Her class is structured in a unique way that does not require exams or papers, but a semester-long project that you submit in phases. I highly recommend her class.

As someone who has no interest in philosophy, she made PHIL 101 pretty palatable. Her lectures were relatively interesting and the readings were mostly engaging. She is very understanding and flexible, but basically all of the grading is done by the TAs. There is really not a lot of work for this class, 4 easy assignments and 2 essays.

We need to read a lot and the material is hard. Participation grade is an important portion of this class, or the most important. However, I would prefer if we are asked to write essays about different philosophers instead of only one. Feel like that would benefit my understanding.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Prof. Peterman is amazing! At first, I wasn't excited to take this class, but she makes modern philosophy way more interesting than I thought was possible. The assignments are pretty easy and she tries to make them more fun/creative than most philosophy profs. She's very accessible outside of class and eager to chat with students. No final exam.
Professor Peterman knows her stuff. She talks a lot in class but it is all interesting, and she leaves time for questions and discussion. The project is cool.
Not responsive to students' questions. Not very respectful to students either. The project seems to be fun but she is not very helpful since you can't reach her after class.
Really great!

A lot of the lectures are very heavy on reiterating what was read, but when this lapses into long discussions that's where the learning really happens. The 2 papers were a great chance to apply what we'd been learning. Before exams she gives a list of 20ish questions and 5ish of them will be on the exam.

History of Modern Philosophy is not the most interesting philosophy course, but Peterman presents the material in a clear way, and assigns a doable amount of readings. Requirements and grading are also fair.
A very nice, down to earth professor, which is rare in the field of philosophy. Her classes are very fair as well.
It's a class all about metaphysics.  Really vague and boring material. She's nice though.
Easy 105 course

Prof. Schaefer was approachable, clearly cared about and was invested in student success, and provided clear feedback that helped me understand exactly what I needed to work on. Her assignments are tedious at times, but make sure NOT to miss a class, as you WILL be behind.

Dr. Schaefer is undoubtedly a knowledgable professor. However, she is a professor who has favorites and does not employ empathy or consideration for what extenuating circumstances a student may be experiencing. Additionally, her grading scheme is SET. On the cusp of a letter grade? You won't bumped up, regardless of strong participation in class.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: This course helps me a lot. You can get an A if you could send many versions of revision before the deadline. The only thing is that you need to put much more effort in the class than the writing held by some other professors.
Very clear grading criteria. Good experience. She's very nice and always provides feedback to students.

She is a good professor and gives enough respect to students. And she will make student revise and revise and revise until your paper is good enough or reach the deadlines. I personally don't have much opinion on this, and I think this is a way to educate students. And I do learned a lot from her. But she is really a hard professor with good heart.
As long as you put in effort, you will get a good grade but it can be tedious. She is not specific enough when it comes to assignments. But, visit her during office hours and you'll do just fine.
Amazing professor. 272 helps prepare you for post graduation so it's great to take. Very helpful feedback. Favorite professor of mine.

Class: Disease and Society. Class is SUPER easy as long as you send her many versions of your essays. Send her your essay, she will put comments, edit, and do it over and over again until the essay is due - You will get an A like this! Go see her in your office if you need more help. VERY LITTLE readings and very little work. Just revise a lot!

Eberly was a great and funny professor. He knew his stuff and would always make a point to praise your question as "very reasonable".

Rest in peace professor Eberly. You will be missed greatly.
hes cool

Prof Eberly is truly a great lecturer. Though, you shouldnt take his class if you are not a genius in math and physics. PHYS 143 is very rigorous and need very advanced linear algebra, calculus to master this. I'd say it probably harder than PHYS 237 later. but definitely a great course if u dont care about pressure

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Time consuming weekly Homework with few helpful resources for questions. Tests are extremely difficult, and practically impossible to study for due to lack of practice problems and brain teaser type of questions asked. Lectures are just derivations with no conceptual information. Would not recommend PHY 143. Extremely difficult with little payoff.

I am sort of NAVY guy and want to be the Professor myself. Cannot imagine being dressed like Eberly at the lecture in a suit church-like perfect style and teach not wearing uniform or para-uniform at the same time. Enormously difficult job for me. Perfect lecturer under extremely heavy conditions. Perfect lectures. Dream home exams, my favorite.
One of the best professors in the Physics department. Definitely take his class. I wasn't interested in Quantum at all previously, but now I am even considering it as my specialization.

Best class of college so far! Loved him and his teaching. Difficult, but worth the feeling you get when you figure his problems out. Very particular sense of humor (dry, witty, and sarcastic), so beware of taking things he says too seriously! :)

One of the best classes I ever took. It cemented my love for science and math. If you go into the class with an open mind and expect it to be the most rigorous class in your schedule then you'll be fine. If you disrespect it, you will get burned. The more you put in, the more you get out.

Makes Quantum actually easy and very graspable. Only gripe is that he spends a lot of time going over math, and the math is beyond what the prereqs require. But if you know basic diff. eq. you're golden- if you don't, I'd suggest looking over a book before taking the class.
I would say that, with pretty good confidence, most of my fellow students agree that Eberly is just not what he's meant out to be.

May be smart, but bad at teaching. Very hard to follow, and most of material is math, and very little concepts. Tests are unreasonable. Class requires a lot more work than any other class, with lab, wrkshop, lecture, weekly graded hw. Would not recommend.

He's brilliant. As a professor, he's great if you're interested in the theoretical aspect of physics. He emphasizes creativity in proofs. Several of his proofs left me open mouthed and profoundly excited about the subject. I'm a physics major because of professor Eberly.

His tests were awesome...they really aligned with class material, you got to pick and choose questions, and doing extra questions gave you bonus points.  Great lecturer.  Homework could be tedious at times, but a lot of the time hw questions appeared on exams.
Prof. Eberly is an incredible person and a brilliant physicist. It's worth getting to know him.

His lectures are very difficult to understand, focusing entirely on derivation.  Besides the few times when he talks down to students when we miss something on a test or don't answer a question in class, he generally ignores our presence.  You probably have to take his class - just use the book and TAs and hope for the best.

He's incredibly smart but expects too much of his students. Lectures focus entirely on the math rather than concepts and it's hard to follow what he says in class. He's the classic case of a teacher who thinks he's teaching well but no one understands him and so workshops are where the TA says "So here's what you should have learned..." Annoying.

He's a really smart guy with a quirky sense of humor. His lectures are excellent, and very clear. It's true that he has high expectations. He expects his students to be competent. Willing to answer questions. And he's the President of the Optics Society of America. Wow.
Does well explaining hard material. HW is indeed loooong, but interesting and not terribly difficult. Tests are easy, but easy to lose points as well. He makes lectures pretty interesting.

He is very discouraging because he treats you like an idiot. Very demeaning and possibly ****. Its better to go to the TA's and not him because he will just make you feel bad for not knowing EVERYTHING about physics

many people say he's difficult but that's easily compensated for by lax grading and an abundance of extra credit--120%!  he's a good guy as long as he thinks you're busting your butt--i went to off hours once without being read and got my butt handed to me for it.  material till first test difficult but the rest is piece of cake.  hw VERY LONG.

He is an excellent lecturer, but he gets quite upset when people don't know their basic trig identities, formula for solving geometric series, etc.  However, his temper does get in the way of his teaching on occasion.
A bit "aloof" in person, but an excellent professor for a challenging class.  Also has a good sense of humor and keeps lectures pretty interesting.

Teaches a course that is very challenging in the best way. Rigorous, difficult material is presented fast, but he isn't aloof to students' needs or difficulties. Responds well to interest shown outside of class (e.g. students going to his office hours).
Good, intelligent and clear professor but with a nasty temper

Took Comics & Culture with Prof. Mohn and loved it. He can be harsh w/ feedback and light on praise but will genuinely make you a better writer. If you're ever struggling with a paper, see him in office hours and he'll help you work through it. Fun guy, will nerd out about comics/anime/video games. Would 100% take more classes with him.

Karl seems like a nice guy but he cares more about the writing than the student. If something comes up it'll be hard to get him to be understanding. He's kind of strict, but he does try to make lectures interesting.

Very caring and understanding prof. You can tell he wants you to succeed and gives really good feedback. I went into WRTG 273 thinking my LinkedIn and resume were already fire but he helped make them so much better.

comment:
Nice professor willing to answer and help with your questions.

A lot of work

He cares about the students. He understands that students have things that are more important than life design notebook entries. If there's conflicts between actual interview/opportunity and class time he is open to communicating how to work that issue around. He is fine with you turning a LDN late by a couple days, as long as it's not over a week.

Amazing professor. His office hours are also very helpful as he gives a lot of specific instructions to edit the essays. One downside is that he is a REALLY TOUGH GRADER. With that being said, the educational process is the most important, and he is one of the only professors at the university who knows how to teach.
He gives the grade not very well although I did a huge effort on the paper.

This class is not an easy A class, but getting an A is worth the effort. As long as you participate in class discussions about the reading and put decent effort into your papers you will do just fine. Karl gave me great advice when it came to my papers, and I definitely improved thanks to it. I'm glad I chose to take this class, it was fun!

Karl is strict with his class structure and grading criteria, but he is also flexible and understanding of his students. He gives amazing feedback and I feel like my writing really improved because of him. My interest in writing increased after taking this class. You have to work for your A, but it feels deserved and not given to you.

Professor Mohn was fantastic. My writing really improved throughout the semester and he always brought a great attitude to class. His office hours were incredibly useful he is very good at giving one on one advice on how to improve your writing. You do need to put some effort in for his class, but I would recommend taking it.

The best writing professor I ever had. Talk to him if you do not have a clear idea about your paper. He gives amazing advice on your paper. If you work hard and willing to talk and discuss with him during his office hours, you will at least get an A-. If you just hurry in the last hour and imagine getting an A, this class is not for you.

Not much homework which was nice but also this means 75% of your grade comes from the three papers that you will write. However, he gives good feedback and you have peer review days which are very helpful. It was easy to pay attention in his class as everything was interesting. I would definitely take again.

I took this course online. Karl is really an interesting person, and his class is overall joyful. I myself did a lot research for the final paper, but I do like the result. His comments on the drafts are useful, you can learn a lot if you want to.

During my freshman year, I took this class, and I have to say Professor Mohn's lecture is one of the best lectures I ever had. He is a harsh grader, but he is usually easy to reach out to and gives you a lot of useful feedback.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Professor Mohn is definitely one of the hardest graders out there. I would suggest not taking his class for a grade because frankly you wouldn't get an A unless you are really good. However, he is really nice person to talk to and get your writings cross checked from. A really nice person to be around
A good indtructor over all. Not so much reading. Not that tough on greading papers. Try hard and you'll at least get a B.

If you want easy A's, don't take Karl. If you sincerely want to learn, please do. He is a tough grader, but he lets you know exactly where you are at and makes you work hard to better your writing skills. I find reading materials and some of his feedback immensely useful for future use.

I would recommend every comics/anime fan to take Professor Mohns class. Professor Mohn is always willing to assist with papers and is ready to meet outside office hours. His feedback really helps in revising drafts and with his cooperation getting an A is not hard if you are will8ng to put in effort. Going to his office hours helps a lot.
