comment:
Difficult Class. Rigid guidelines. TAs aren't given rubrics so grading can be confusing and different for each person. Many co-curent deadlines, rarely gives extensions, late hw not accepted. Only two midterms (therefore weighted heavily). Requires writing an entire publishable paper. Lots of coding. Flipped classroom. 
Professor is a nice person.
Online lectures are great.
She doesn't teach at all. Just give recorded lecture and you need to watch them before class. The lectures are useless

A lot of materials to be covered in one semester so the explanations are not as detailed as I would prefer. It appears to me that she's trying her best to make things clear and she gives amazingly organized notes. Very "Asian style "of teaching. Quite a lot of work indeed but I don't think it's too hard to get good grades in this.

Terrible professor. Having taken a statistics class already, I already knew much of the information in advance. She overcomplicates the concepts that are much easier than they seem to be. She unnecessarily makes the homework so long. This class is required and she clearly hates teaching it.

At first I did not like her but throughout the semester I learned she does care. She is not great at making things understandable and is quite unorganized during lectures but solids is a hard class and it is hard to teach. Read the textbook, pay attention in class, and be prepared test scores might not be great. The labs are terrible too.

Lectures are borderline useless with way too many mistakes and very poor explanations. Labs were poorly explained and had unclear grading. We would frequently have homework due the same day as she taught the concepts. Exams were brutal and not representative of the homework in both difficulty and content. Only helpful part of class was the textbook

Prof. Abdolrahim has good intentions, but the execution needs work. Grading was fair, but lectures had frequent errors, notes were hard to read, and homework was often due near the day material was taught. That said, I appreciated that student feedback was usually considered and applied. The textbook was really helpful too.

The textbook was the only helpful part of this class. Lectures had frequent misinformation, notes unreadable; TAs weren't equipped to help, especially with labs. Tests included barely covered material, and homework was due before topics were fully taught. Student requested example problems were poorly explained and full of errors.

She put so much effort into listening to feedback, thats why she earns a good rating. If you didnt like class at the end maybe you didnt give good feedback, I personally saw my feedback get implemented. She makes mistakes, yes, but forgetting a sign during math isnt the same as making conceptual errors. The work is gruesome. Hardest ME class so far

She does not explain things well and often will not revisit important ideas or equations. Her notes are mistake riddled, messy, and do not give a step by step walk-through(Including homework and test solutions, most of which are screenshots of the textbook) The tests dont cover the same stuff that we were taught and the review for them is unhelpful

Easy because nicely graded but the lectures are awful, just read the textbook. Never answered any of my emails, despite saying she's accessible outside of class and willing to meet the needs of students. Also test questions are poorly written and often have many mistakes or missing info. Was excited for solids but not anymore because of professor.
Nice to answer questions and provide help. The grading is very nice.

She gives incredibly hard homework and her lectures are not very well organized. The textbook is the saving grace of this course because without it you're done. TA's are helpful for the most part, but OH can be crowded as they are really the only time you can learn the content. Tough times in ME 226. Take it with the other Prof. if possible.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: One of the worst teachers I've experienced in my entire life; her lectures cover tons of material yet seem all over the place. She consistently gets things wrong on the board, is hard to understand, and has 0 relationship with the class. If you read the textbook it is WAY more helpful which is embarrassing considering how expensive this school is.

Does not answer emails or provide assistance, very unaccommodating. Will make many many mistakes on the board when doing lectures but is not lenient with others' mistakes. Does not give any real test prep.
her lectures were useless -- if you read the textbook and go to recitation you'll be fine. there is a huge curve on exams too
She is great in explaining materials. She really cares about her students. Highly recommend her.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Very dry lectures with LOTS of mistakes, homework and most textbook problems don't prepare you for the tests, and long homeworks.
Though she makes mistakes on the board, it does not take away from learning the concept. She really cares about the students. You can argue for extra points after receiving your test.

Her lectures are okay but she's really bad at math. Every time she does math in lecture there are lots of mistakes. She talks really quietly but is really nice, accessible, and good at explaining topics clearly outside of class.

Actually mind boggling that people like this professor. Mediocre lectures, unreasonable. Once used r as a constant without saying it was a constant for a test question IN OUR UNIT ON POLAR COORDINATES. Bald and deserved to be bald.

Love Professor Wolf! He explains things in a detailed manner which is easy to understand. He starts with the very basics to make sure the higher level concepts have a good foundation to them. His notes are very easy to follow and his office hours are extremely helpful as well. If he taught higher level math class, I would take those as well.

I hated Calculus, but I would go to office hours often, and Wolf does a great job of working through the problem and making sure that you fully understand the concepts. He also made sure to do extended office hours the days before the midterms and final if you needed any help. Definitely utilize CETL and recitations if you need help.

He explained things simply and efficiently. He's a solid choice for an intro math class and a friendly guy. Webwork (homework) is unlike the lecture examples and exams. When studying for exams, review notes/lectures and then work on old exams.

prof wolf seemed like nice little man until we got into the material. he rlly did try his best to teach us, was v accessible outside of class for help, but is one of those insanely smart guys that simply cannot impart knowledge. class was mostly just doing an example prob and then expecting us to pick up on concepts and letting us loose on the hw.

Nice guy! He is patient and gives us time to write and makes sure we dont have any questions. Theres just the weekly webwork homework, but I reccommend going to study group for help, much harder than examples in lectures. Dont do what I did and bs the homework. Spend time everyday on them. I failed most midterms because I wasnt serious about study

Herman is a great prof. He is very approachable and kind and explains stuff well. The class had some moderately difficult parts but overall it was pretty reasonable. I had him for 161 as well and had a similar experience. Would def recommend

Incredibly caring professor, and the best lecturer I have had in the math department so far. Expect endearingly bad jokes. The exams are intentionally difficult, typically at the level of the hardest problem set questions. But he writes them knowing he will curve the letter grades. My section had a 58 avg on the midterm, which he curved to a B.

Very caring and approachable understands he's teaching math.  He keeps the class engaging by going off topic but with only to break up monotony.  Very helpful if you ask for help. For calc 161 he is the course organizer so he writes your tests if your in calc 161.

Notes are super organized and he lectures very clearly. Definitely go to lectures if you want to do well in the course. Witty humor and although it may seem like he's harsh at first, he is an awesome professor who understands what it takes to do well in the course.
Great professor, notes are super

Amazing professor, can't recommend him enough. Explains calculus in a clear, simple way, and if you pay attention in class you won't fall behind. Lectures are engaging and funny, but not to the point of being distracting or off-topic. The class moves fast, and it's easy to lose momentum, but if you stay focused and do the work you'll be fine.

Great lecturer and provides well-motivated and clear but simple explanations of all the major topics. He's very enthusiastic which is great, the lectures are high-energy. Sometimes a little intimidating to contribute in class but great guy. Effectively references the textbook as a good supplement but not required to read.

Dr. Herman is a phenomenal lecturer; he's very engaging and passionate about the subject, and he goes about teaching in a very clear and concise manner. The course content wasn't the easiest (as somebody who isn't the best at math), but he breaks it down in a way that makes it a lot more manageable. Highly recommend!!

This dude is hilarious. He'll talk to himself making jokes, tell random stories from his life, advertise Pepsi, and on top of that he's a remarkable professor. Answers questions, explains things clearly & legibly. The class is tricky, but I wouldn't want anyone else teaching it to me. If you ever get the chance, take this guys class.
BEST MATH PROFESSOR!!

He is a really great guy and always more than happy to help with anything. The class isn't easy by any means, and the exams in particular were hard. Homeworks are not too bad if you ask for help when needed. He just wants you to put in the effort which is great to see. Also he makes funny jokes.

Diverting and amicable, as Mark always has been, Math 208's quizzical materials were broken down into palatable piecewise information that was fairly tested on. Had the assignments been easy, the class would not be a banger. Challenging as they are designed to be, they siphon out students' thoughts.
he is nice

I'm typically not the rate my professor guy that will write comment or rate the professor, but I signed up the account for him! His class is truly interesting and engaging. I really understand a lot of concepts that I didn't get before with his help, he's just amazing!

He was hilarious and knew how to teach so well. It was a morning class and the attendance wasn't mandatory, but I didn't miss a single lecture even though I did most of the material in high school. If you take cal 161, take it with Prof. Herman.
He is funny and nice! Explains concepts very clearly!

Prof Herman does an extremely well job in teaching math. One of the most brilliant math professors. He does however teach extremely fast and sometimes can be very direct and rude at times. He definitely cares for math and genuinely tries to teach students, but i found his teaching style to be sometimes difficult to grasp. Be ready to take notes.
He's very fast but he also teaches well. If you pay attention and do webworks you should be fine.

Hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. Professor Herman is incredibly helpful and genuinely wants his students to succeed. I have developed a greater interest for mathematics because of his excellent teaching. Great class!

Prof Herman is a great lecturer and gives many examples for each topic. He also explains why concepts in calculus exist instead of just giving you the formulas, which really helps with understanding. That being said, the pace is fast and it's almost impossible to cram for the tests, so it's important to stay on top of your homework and studying!

The best math teacher I've ever had, never got the chance to lean from him or talk personally, but his lectures were awesome. He connected so many dots for me that had been floating around from previous calc classes. There have been multiple times I've thought "Why didn't my teachers in HS just day that?". I wish I could take him for 162 :(
Great professor
word hard, then you will get an A

Professor H is a great math teacher and really funny. Showing up to lecture is very important. My advice is to really focus on the homework because that is what prepares you for the test and the practice quizzes.

Great professor, walks you from the eaiest ever examples to the hardest ones. detailed lectures and alway on point when it comes to what really matter for exams. I would recommend attending the lecture he gives pretty great examples in them.
Amazing 161 professor. He gives a lot of examples to help understant.

When talking about the Dijkstra algorithm, I am confused. Taking so many years of algorithm competitions, I am surprised he is teaching algorithms this way. I can feel if I am new to these things I might get confused. He gives me a feeling he wants examples to explain algorithms, but those examples may not be suitable and confuse you more.

I think this class is fine. I went to his office hour and he helped me a lot. Sometimes I just cannot follow this class or missed a class, and I can go over his notes. He basically includes everything in his notes.

This guy is the bomb. I have no idea what these other dudes are talking about. Maybe they are not attending class. He clearly pours his heart into teaching this class. Take it if you get the chance. He's smart and hilarious and super helpful if you go to office hours.

I have no idea why we are going to class. His lecture is sooo confusing, and I just couldn't follow. Notes are extremely confusing with lots of useless phrase though I have to review it to know how to do homework. Takes lot of time. Why am I taking this class??? If you want and easy class, take it, and get ready to study everything by yourself.
Notes are not clear. Lectures are not understandable. Homework is hard. We are struggling.

Amazing professor, would definitely take him again. Cares about his students and is very understanding. Funny and gives clear explanations, lectures are recorded with notes. Difficult tests, but they are the same regardless of the professor. HW load is reasonable. I'll never love calculus, but Professor Herman made me hate it a little less.

comment: Very nice teacher and class. The pace is fast, and the exam is hard, so you should always review the notes and webwork assignments.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: The course-load is not very heavy. There is homework due at the end of the week, which is very manageable, and the tests are hard, but not if you understand the material. Overall, as long as you can grasp the lessons, it is a great class and Herman is a great Professor who always answers your questions and emails and cares about his students.
Class moves pretty quickly but he's very helpful outside of class. One of the best math professors at UR.
Lectures were not recorded. He's very open to questions and good at explaining but will not stop moving forward (pretty quickly might I add). Overall one of the better math professors I've ever had.
He's such a fun, quirky guy! His lectures are extremely fast-paced and hard to follow but the perk of that is you get many helpful examples.
Such an odd and funny guy which makes class interesting. He gives good examples during class that will mimic those on Webwork so it's important to attend class.
He has a true passion for math. His interest in the subject during the lecture draws me into it a lot. Always answers your questions with enthusiasm.
THE WORST!!!!!!!! I DON'T EVEN UNDERSTAND WHY THE HECK IS HE TEACHING 150!!! I AM AN A STUDENT AND I HAD TO STUDY EVERYTHING ON MY OWN!!! WHY THE HECK ARE WE PAYING $5000 FOR THIS COURSE ALONE???
He just does not know how to teach probability or math in general. Lectures are boring. Reading textbook is better
Great professor, a little fast but honestly he is amazing. Take him.

comment: soooo boring and assumes you'll know things that you don't when lecturing

Great intro to discrete math. Very funny guy and explained things well. Always took the time to answer student questions clearly. You will need the textbook but you can find the pdf, and the questions from the book always translated very clearly to what he lectured in class.
Prof. Herman is very skilled in his expertise. His lecture are fun and organized. He is also very respectful to all the students. Overall, he is a great professor. Fully recommend to anyone.

I really love Prof. Herman. He is one of the few professors who listen carefully to the students. You can ask him question almost anytime and he would explain clearly and patiently. I would fully recommend him to any students. Go for it!

Herman is a great guy and answers questions well. That said, he just writes notes way too quickly on the board. I spent all class trying to keep up and get the notes down without being able to process anything.

Don't miss out! He has perf amount of humor in lectures. Office hours are worth going as he explains things well. He doesn't talk into the board! He responds quickly and is impressively patient despite how busy/knowledgeable he is. You can feel his effort to help students learn. He has  great comedic timing- I 'd definitely have him as prof again.

You'll be fine as long as you pay attention and take notes. He tends to move a little fast, but his office hours are helpful and he replies to emails pretty fast. Woe unto you if he's the one setting the exam, though. Otherwise, he's a pretty decent professor. Don't take too long to seek help for problematic areas, it's hard to play catch up

Herman is a really great guy and a wonderful professor. He gets really excited about the material, which keeps class entertaining. He explains everything clearly and gives examples of every concept. Highly recommended

Unnecessarily long and repetitive hw assignments, though they're pretty doable. Good intro to math logic without killing you on it. Lectures are better than the book for notes and understanding the material. Practice exams super helpful. Not a walk in the park, but if you put time into the course you'll ace it. C or below if you don't.

Herman is one of the better teachers in the math department. He is extremely knowledgeable and explains things clearly, but he moves very quickly through lectures. Always go to the lectures, you basically have to in order to do decently in the class.

Herman is a decent professor. I probably wouldn't have him as my first choice for a class, but he's a good back-up plan. He does write and talk fast, but you get used to it after a few lectures. The class itself is hard, especially when it gets to infinite series. Herman does help to explain the harder concepts, but it's not enough on its own.

MTH 162 is an awful class, and Herman didn't make it any better. Moves ridiculous fast in lecture, and his handwriting is terrible.  Can be condescending and rude if you ask a question he considers simple. Webwork is really hard, and doesn't help you prep for exams.  The book problems are a lot better. Midterms were tough. Final was BRUTAL

Out of all the MTH162 professors, Herman is the best. That, however, is not saying much. He speeds through lectures and uses exact examples from the textbook. I found it much more useful to just read the textbook and watch lectures online. The tests in 162 are pretty fair, aside from the final, which was ridiculous.

Herman is a great professor! He does tend to go fast, but this is because he is giving you more in depth coverage/examples than the other professors. Also, he is open for questions.  He goes deep into theory, but once you understand that you can understand anything that could possibly be on the exam. For the harder subjects do look a the book.
Excellent professor. I really enjoy be in his class though he speaks super fast and provide students lots of notes. He is willing to help students after class in his office hours or by appointments.

Excellent professor.  He is super helpful outside of class and makes himself very available to his students.  His lectures were almost comically speedy at first (but still clear), but he slowed down by October.  Must have been the weather... Also a good guy to know (Director of Undergraduate Studies)

He's young and has a sense of humor. He can be eccentric but he always seems happy to help out students who are making an effort. He writes & talks at supersonic speeds which makes note-taking a challenge but his lectures were good enough that I barely had to crack open the book all semester. I would definitely take him again if I had a chance.

Lectures are always very engaging and he throws in a nice bit of humor. He speaks really, really quickly in class, but you get used to it after a while. Really patient/helpful in office hours. Very helpful professor who is always willing to spend extra time with his students. His lectures move at the speed of sound and will burn through a dozen pages of notes in one day. His curves are helpful and generous but not obscenely large. He is gorgeous and I want to run my fingers through his receding hairline.
Very good teacher. Although he goes over stuff bit fast in class, he is very helpful afterclass. He explains the problems to you until you get bored. His test can be long and a bit hard

his love of math is inspiring and sparked a deeper interest in mathematics. Very thoughtful professor, we need more professors like this.
I have been hate math in high school, but this lecture is inspiring and I think I have found some of my confidence in math now.

Pretty good at teaching, obviously really passionate about math. His notes were a little bit messy and he's kind of awkward, but if you asked him for help, he helps you. He wants the student to succeed. Just take practice exams to do well on the tests.
Enthusiastic and approachable. His passion for math is inspiring.
his love of math is infectious. genuinely wants students to succeed. explains anything you ask

makes you work for your grade thats for sure. He does explain the material fairly well so go to class, review your notes later that day(<that is important), study for a good amount of time and you should be ok.

Very poor instruction, guidance or interest in student's education. Do not waste time with this instructor. Do not be misled by her authorship of textbook.

It is doubtful the text written for the class is used anyplace else, it reads like a high school science book, and is very lite on science.  Tests are poorly written, and do not relate to the material covered in class.  Overall a bad instructor in a bad program.

Amy Karch's class is extremely poor quality.  Concepts are overly simplified in the textbook she has written.  As A graduate of a Top 10 university, Graduate classes taught by Karch are worthless.  Tests are not based on facts from an easy textbook, but on abstract NCLEX style questions, that do not correspond to the material covered in Lecture.

Brilliant teacher. Very knowledgeable. Breaks down complex information and makes it entertaining and easy to learn. Uses case scenarios as writing assignments, which forces students to use critical thinking skills to connect ideas.

Extremely difficult class. Tests are impossible to prepare for and there's no partial credit. A perfect score on all the projects and test scores at the median will get you a C. Take this with another professor if possible.

He told us straight up he doesn't like teaching and it shows, his lectures were hard to follow at times and he is intimidating. I recommend watching the old recordings from 2021 they helped a lot. Doesn't respond to emails and has extremely limited office hours. TAs were great tho, start projects early! Hopefully he gets happy again.
The course was hard but a lot of fun!

Great lectures and slides, tests are extremely difficult and make up a lot of the grade. Projects are also very challenging. I was a bit intimated by him at first, but he is quite nice in office hours. Project grading took a while but that is more so a TA thing.

He does not know how to teach at all.

AND THE TWO GRADUATE TA SUCK. I doubt they understand any of the material and grade your exams just by mood.
Horribly irresponsible! He tries to pretend that he cares about the students but actually doesn't at all and don't expect him to reply to your emails :( This whole class does not even make any sense.
He encourages you to reach out to him if you have any questions. However, he did not reply any of my email throughout the semester.

The class materials are so beneficial and he is good at teaching I enjoyed the class a lot. But grading is horrible. Exams are super hard. Assignments are so so hard and you need to study on your own to do them the class materials do not help a lot with assignments. And yet he does not curve the class. I hate his grading criteria but good teacher.
Got above average grades on both my midterm and final and an A average on my projects but got a c+ in the class because he didnt curve the class at all.

Professor Zhu is easily my favorite professor in the CS department. His lecture style is very detailed and manageable, the projects (homework) are difficult but well-designed as they are from the textbook. Does a good job of making computer architecture very accessible. Start projects early, go to class and you'll do great. A really nice guy, too.
Great prof. Class is hard but it's a hard topic. Lectures are dense but good. If you can pay attention through lectures and start the projects early, you'll be alright. Really nice guy too.
Prof Zhu is great! His lectures are clear even though he covers a lot of material, and he's very nice if you reach out. Definitely a hard class though. Start the projects early.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: The course is very difficult. You will have to work hard to keep up. However, Zhu's lectures are extremely comprehensive. He makes extremely complex concepts easier to follow. The projects are hard as hell, but if you utilize the TAs and start early, you will be fine. (Take CSC172 and MTH150 first!!)

Computer architecture is a difficult subject but the professor is really good at explaining the concepts both structurally and in details. Very organized lectures and if attending class consistently you dont even need to read the textbook

Trust me, the material covered in this course is very interesting but the problem is with the instructor. He doesn't care at all whether or not the students understand concepts and just rushes through the lecture. He is extremely bad at explaining and answering questions and makes extremely hard exams without providing enough practice material.

He is a horrible lecturer and is terrible at explaining concepts. You learn more by reading the book than attending the classes. In fact, attending the lectures would confuse you more. Also, he is extremely condescending and does not help a lot during office hours. Try to take this class with a different professor in the Fall.

Yuhao's lectures often lack some in depth explanation... students often have to ask questions to get the 'why?' behind most of the course material. But, nonetheless, Yuhao is a down to earth, pretty memey guy who I would certainly choose again.
great professor

Prof Kuzgun is kind and caring and she respects her students. She's willing to slow down when it's necessary and she cares about whether we understand the material. This was the opposite of the MATH161 experience. Key to doing well is YouTube videos that follow the txtbook and getting WebWork done as quickly as possible so you can actually study.
take this class with someone else.
Professor Kuzgun is such a nice professor. She always explains things in details and always provide numerous examples. I would recommend anyone taking her class:)
She is an amazing professor, very caring. Fun fact about her: she wears a T-shirt with text "Monday" on it every Monday.

Professor Raqueno is an awesome professor. The GIS lectures he gave are down-to-earth and fun. He is also very accessible outside of the classroom and truly cares about his students. GIS is overall not an easy class, but you shall succeed as long as you treat your labs and final project seriously.

A great teacher, but not an easy grader. If you genuinely show interest, it will go a long way. She is a meticulous and detail orientated teacher. She is always willing to help her students. Pay attention and follow directions closely and you will do fine in her class.
i love dr. mitchell! taking nsci 203 with him. grading criteria could be better but he is the funniest prof and very fun love him makes this 3.5 hour lab bearable and interesting

Don't ever reveal anything about yourself that makes you seem even the slightest bit incompetent, even if it was something you did as a young child or that occurred in a dream. Don't ever trust him with any responsibility. I'd avoid him altogether if possible.

Though he witnessed how much of a struggle it is to do my work, he claimed I was too smart to have ADHD. He bluejacked my phone, took a Freudian interpretation of everything I scrolled through, and followed me around. At CVS, he put on an elaborate show, meant to say I don't need to take my medication, I just need to chill and smoke weed with him.
He is really cool and made me more interested in BCS! You have to be prepared to study hard because the exams are challenging but you learn a lot.
He is a very smart professor and he cares about his students. You can't be lazy in his class, you have to put in the work, but you learn a lot if you study hard. Highly recommend.
I would stay far away from him. He has many tricks up his sleeve and he's smart enough to know how not to get caught. Don't trust him, trust your instincts.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: I heard this course is good and it wasnt. It was GREAT! Professor Jorne has been teaching a long time but stays so up to date he is amazing. He knows whats happening with fuel cells, electric cars etc. In my four years here he is in the top three of my favorite professors. He is very encouraging and very patient. Hard tests but grades fairly.

Dr Jorne is a great professor. You will learn so much and he is on top of his field. Any question you have in Microelectronics Processing he can either answer or work together to find the answer. You can tell he likes to teach and really likes lively students who care about learning. If he sees you making an effort he will help you achieve.

Prof Jorne teaches well. I took his course on Separation and learned so much. He does a great job of explaining things in a way you can really understand. He is always available to students and will give good career advice in addition to course advice. Also, if you like basketball, hes your guy! Seriously though, he is smart and funny and kind.
Great professor, very smart. Has changed my outlook.

Scattered, unclear, boring, unprepared.  He has a decent understanding of most material but can't convey it to students.  Horrible planning of exams and scheduling.  His exams were also not at all a good representation of what was taught or covered in HW.  He gave very poor descriptions of what would be covered on exams.
Can't explain course basics. Uses a poor textbook.  Doesn't seem to want to be around students.

has in-depth knowledge but lacks proper skills to communicate with students.  very unsteady in terms of mental mood stability and is prone to lash out on students.  not very engaging and helpful with graduate students. no innovative ideas for research.

This class was very easy, barely studied and got an A. Her notes are nice and clear and the practice is helpful for exam review. Only complaint is that the homework assignments were very annoying to do.
Uses MyOpenMath, a HW service that will sometimes delete your work for some problem sets.
Very bad professor theres no extra credit and she does not know how to teach. Everytime I asked her a question she wouldn't answer the question DONT TAKE THIS CLASS
Fair syllabus, plenty of practice, and a kind professor. BUT, she really needs to get rid of MyOpenMath. It has to be the worst design and UI for any assignment-website I have ever used.
Best person ever.

Well, a mixed bag. Very poorly organized lectures. Basically friendly in a phoney way. Not evil, just not helpful. Disappointing, mediocre in general, as a historian and teacher. Will make some good observations about you papers, but that's it.
HES CHILL

Professor Borus is a so funny. He is so quirky but it works for him. He definitely keeps the class interesting and he tell you straight forward what he wants you to know for the exam. He's a good professor
Definitely a unique guy.  Pretty funny too.  he speaks a a little too quickly for good notes and is a little weird when you come to talk to him alone.  Overall though a good guy.
I had to keep myself from bursting out lauging in the first lecture; he has a very "unique" speaking style. He's a nice guy and grades easily, though a bit obsessed with certain eras.
He's a really sweet professor.  Fun lectures.
Great at teaching 301 class.  A lot of work but interesting readings and topic discussions.  Willing to sit down to discuss papers and grades.  Interested in teaching and his students.

i don't consider him one of my favorite teachers or the best by any means, but he's definitely more enjoyable if you get past the first few lectures. a bit pedantic in his manner of speaking but will make a few jokes.
Very helpful, insightful, keeps the material fresh and interesting.
No Comments

I took 273 with her and start to regret that I didn't do 105 with her as well.
One of the best professors at the university! Liz is very caring and the homework is manageable

One of the best professors I've had at the University of Rochester! Her workload is manageable, her feedback is helpful and constructive, and her chill, approachable demeanor makes learning enjoyable. She even brought treats to celebrate our Midpoint Portfolio! If you get the chance to take her class, I highly recommend it!

Excellent professor all around. The class cirriculum is super fun, she cares about her students and makes the class engaging. On top of all that, she's an easy grader and gives good feedback. Probably the best professor I've ever had.
Solid 10/10 writing professor. Best Professor I met at this stupid school ever. She really nice and patient to listen all things you talking about:)
My favorite professor!!

Professor Tinelli is amazing, she is more than approachable and is always willing to help. She gives good feedback on papers and you also spend a good amount of time doing peer reviewing and reflecting on all of your papers. Despite this, she manages to keep the class fun and easy, as there are readings, but they aren't typically required.

Professor Tinelli is my favorite teacher and truly a gem. I really enjoyed her class; she put a lot of effort into revision feedback, and her assignments were very clear. I highly recommend any class she teaches.

Liz was one of the most fantastic professors I've ever had. If you have a chance, make sure to sign up for any of her classes. She's funny, understanding, and a very fair grader. One of, if not my favorite teacher ever.

An amazing professor. She is always wiling to help and gives fantastic feedback. Doing the assignments were genuinely beneficial to my writing. She also gives good grades as long as you out in some effort.

For a required course for Hajim students, she made it very fun and enjoyable. Her feedback on assignments was always incredibly helpful, which was beneficial since our assignments were things like cover letters and resumes, so her feedback can be applied to future professional materials. I loved Liz! Highly recommend taking 273 with her!!

Liz was amazing! The workload was so manageable, and she made an otherwise boring topic seem interesting. She was so understanding and kind, and an easy and clear grader. Despite this class being an easy A, I actually learned a lot about academic writing. Liz felt more like a friend than a professor, and was super understanding about absences.
AMAZING PROF EVER MET if u have chance definitely take hers and enjoy your semester
Love her! She gives great feedback and is very helpful. Show up, participate, do your work, and you'll get an A. She makes writing less intimidating and teaches you very useful skills.
Really an excellent professor! She is very inspired to teach and will give you really useful comment on your paper. I would definitely take her class again in the future!

Goes above and beyond. Phenomenal professor. She is aware that WRT 273 is a mandatory course, but does her best for the students to get the best out of it. She actually cares about the course and the students. Highly recommend.

The only instructor who I would love for life. She helps you to always have hope. The A- during my first semester of this two-part course was a pity but it was largely my own fault. And during the second semester, she decides to award everyone who is responsible and respectful an A, which is exactly my ultimate standard for education. God Bless You
She is very kind to students, loves to inspire students in class. She is very friendly in grading paper.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Although her class is very great, to get an A in her class is impossible. Her comments and her final grading criteria are very different. You cannot get any improvement for your writing in her class.
She's very nice
She is the best of best professor I have ever met in my entire studying life. Would recommend to every student to take her writing class.
Knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and approachable. Always willing to discuss abstract concepts with me so that I could develop and clarify my ideas in writing.
One of the best professors I've ever met! Really inspired me a lot!
This this the best professor since I enter college!

Great Feedback!! She reads your papers really carefully and give useful comments. Don't worry if you miss two or three classes, she doesn't care! But don't miss a lot. Class is relaxing, and feels quick. She is great, overall.
Guy is basically a genius, but gives his best every class.  Always willing to encourage other views

Very bright, though a bit abstract at times. Sufficient rigor but fair in assessment of student work. Not ideological. Encourages students to express different ideas. Flexible regarding deadlines and understands that adult students often must prioritize professional and/or family issues over their studies.

Excellent professor; a lot of reading but it all ties in together and is very helpful.  Makes class interesting and does not sit up in front and lecture all the time.  If you do the reading and work hard you'll have no problems.  Very engaging and knowledgable and willing to help students.

Dr. Holz was my favorite professor out of 4 years of undergrad. He is not only intelligent but also incredibly kind, caring, and witty. Highly recommend taking for all pre-med students especially. He makes a lot of time outside of class to help students and is good with email. Makes effort to know students' names too. Amazing professor and person!!
Great, engaging professor. Highly recommend Physiology if you are willing to put in the work!

He is a caring person, but his lectures are not well-organized. Tests are hard but curved. This course is content-heavy; the amount of content you need to memorize is crazy a lot, which is presented in a not-so-clear way. You need to do extra work to reorganize them. I don't really like this class, reminding me of BIOL 111, by Minckey, but harder.

If you don't test well this class is not for you!! TOUGH grader. curve is based on errors in grading. Lectures move very fast and often doesn't go into as much detail as he expects you to know for the exams. Past exams given for practice are very different than the actual exams. Nice guy but exams are unrealistic for the average student to do well.

Genuinely a caring person, I failed 2 exams and he reached out to check up on me. When we met he apologized to ME because he usually tries to check in if everything is alright after the first exam (if bad). The class is fair, weekly open note BB quiz, exams based on lecture content, probably fine as long as you study (I didn't, S/F, changed minor)

This is my second course with Dr. Holz. He is absolutely great as a professor, but is sometimes a little bit disorganized. Anatomy definitely isn't an easy course, and requires a lot of memorization. I really recommend going to lecture, because tests are only on lecture content. Over all, Dr. Holz is entertaining and cares a lot!

Dr. Holz was very entertaining in his lectures, and he showed he really cared for students. BIO204's difficulty lies in the large amount of content he is trying to cover in a short time, but he is available for questions and office hours. Tests are tough but curved - would recommend rewatching lectures over reading the textbook!!

Good lecturer. No textbook, and most of the information is on the slides, but I'd definitely recommend going to the lectures because he gives context to the information and studies on the slides that you wouldn't be able to get from just looking at the slides. If you go to class and study the slides well, the tests are very fair.

Really enthusiastic about the material and the exams were fair. The 4 non-cumulative tests are the only things you're graded on, but as long as you go to class and study his lectures in detail, you'll do well.

Great class, great professor. Explains things very clearly, and tests are extremely fair (not easy, but your grade will be proportional to your effort). Probably my favorite class so far, and I'm excited to have him for BCS 246. Highly recommend him.

Lectures are incredibly interesting and he knows a lot about the blues, including firsthand accounts of musicians that he's met or is friends with. He plays lots of music in class, keeps lectures light and interesting, and makes sure it is easy to pass the course. One short paper and weekly music listening is the only homework.

Laid back class that discusses the story we read. The class is based on a couple of essays and he is a very fair grader and gives helpful feedback. He is more like a friend than a teacher. The class is more discussion based so dont worry about having any prior experience on how to analyze (arabic) literature. I really enjoyed this class.
Excellent teacher

I took almost every course Dr. Beaumont taught. He is an excellent teacher and such a pleasant person to be around. He makes going to class a joy. I learned so much and I feel I'm a better student having had the opportunity to interact with him. His enthusiasm for learning is infectious.
Loved his Arabian Nights class. Readings are very enjoyable and he is a fun guy. Very helpful too. I would definitely take another of his classes.

Fantastic lecturer and a cool guy. Lectures are very well organized and easy to understand. Useful office hours too. I think this is his last semester here, but highly recommend him if he sticks around.
Professor Snyder is the best math professor I've had at the uofr. He explains things in a really straightforward and clear way and is super accessible outside of class.

Take this class. Never thought I would love (writing) poetry, but Professor Wessels changed that for me. Definitely challenging at times, but in a good way. Loved the workshop atmosphere and how he managed to make us all feel comfortable sharing and receiving feedback—I could really tell that he cares about his students. Brilliant professor!

I had Prof. Wessels last semester for ENGL122 and I have to say it was one of the best classes I've ever taken. I'm a Bio major and I haven't ever really liked English classes, but Prof Wessels always made me feel welcome and supported me while presenting my work. He changed my perspective on poetry and I am so thankful that I took his class.

I won't take this professor again. I didn't feel like he created an environment where we could learn. The feedback wasn't good enough for me to improve and I don't think he took it seriously. I'm not sure how he got his position.

Taking a class with Christian Wessels was a lifechanging experience. I would take any class this man teaches. I had for poetry two semesters in a row and he is absolutely brilliant. Those classes alone were worth my entire tuition. My fellow classmates often referred to him as the best professor they've ever had or could imagine having.
this was the second class I took with Christian, and he continues to be my favorite prof at U of R. he cares about his students so much and gives very encouraging feedback. highly recommend!

True gem of a teacher. His knowledge about poetry is remarkable. I've rarely had a professor who puts so much effort, thought, and sincere reflection into feedback. If you are truly interested in growing as a writer-poet & don't just want your ego stroked, you should take the class. The progress I have made, thanks to Prof W, is invaluable to me.

Apparently this is controversial, but Prof Wessels is truly an awful teacher. He doesn't seem to have much background knowledge on what he's teaching and the lack of effort he puts in is maddening. He barely gives any writing feedback and has a laid-back aura that makes it seem like he just doesn't care.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Prof. Wessels is a hilarious and insightful guy! As a new poet, he gives you excellent feedback and truly cares about his students. His class is workshop style, and he ensures that everyone feels safe and comfortable when their poems are being workshopped. He also has hilarious stories and comments! Recommend his class, 10/10!

One of the greatest and most dedicated professors I have had at U of R. I thoroughly enjoyed how thoughtful and insightful he has been in not only improving my abilities as a "poet" but reviving my interest for creative writing as a whole. If I can, I will be taking a class with him again in a future semester. Cannot wait!

I loved this class so much and will recommend to all of my friends. Not only did I learn a ton about poetry, I also felt comfortable sharing my own work because of the class atmosphere and the professor. Professor Wessels cares a lot about his students, was always available and gave tremendously helpful feedback. He even made us food!

Christian is an amazing professor. He is insanely knowledgeable and his passion for poetry is truly infectious. I will be taking more classes with him next semester and recommending him to any friends. His class is not "easy", but it is so fulfilling, I find myself excited to finish work for it. 10/10!!

Professor Wessels is hands down my favorite professor ever. He is so knowledgeable about poetry it will blow your mind and cares so much about his students. I got AMAZING feedback on my own poetry and grew so much as a poet, thanks to this class and Prof Wessels. If you care for poetry, take this class (and follow the prompts)! He's also funny.

Manipulates the content in a distasteful way & seems more interested in the cadence of his own voice than the literary themes he claims to analyze. Talks down to students in a very uncomfortable way. Don't waste your time with his misguided passion.
Really good teacher. Gives great feedback on papers and very quick at responding to emails. Class was so chill and pretty easy so it's not hard to get an A. Genuinely very fun class!

Wessels is a great professor. He's really chill and easy to talk to. I enjoy going to class. Second semester was more fun than the first semester because everyone knows each other more and we do more class discussions and have fewer readings.He's nice with grading and enjoys teaching. I'm not much of a writer, but I enjoyed his class.

I love the way he lectures. Super funny but also very well informed and great at giving feedback. Would take a class just because he's teaching it. I really enjoyed his class even though I don't necessarily like writing.
Do you work and attend class and you will get an A. Attending class was also fun cause Christian is pretty funny.
Not a bad experience

comment: I really don't understand why our school need us to take this recitation. The recitation completely has nothing to do with its lecture. Also, the class is trying to teach students topics such as "How to be successful" and " How to prepare for lecture". I think those questions are all depend on personal situation. They are totally nonsense.

Professor Reis's PSYC 263 class is the reason I'm a psychology major. His lectures are really interesting-- both in content and the way he frames them. He uses real-life scenarios in order to convey his information and regularly engages with students. All in all, 10/10!!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Professor Reis is my favorite professor/lecturer at this school thus far. His tests are hard and you definitely have to go to class, read textbook, etc but its worth it if your'e interested in the topic. He also offers additional optional assignments which is very fair -- if you work hard you'll get a good grade! Definitely recommend to everyone!

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: My experience with this professor was not the best. The lectures were very interesting but the tests were VERY hard and unfair. He wouldn't accept feedback and the TAs told me he made it intentionally hard to prove that psych wasn't easy. He doesn't curve and isn't phased by failing class averages on tests (which happened frequently).

Dr. Reis is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are interesting and engaging, and he incorporates relevant articles into the course. His tests are very hard, and if you don't read the textbook, you will be unlikely to do well. The extra credit he offers is a lifesaver, well worth the effort, and not too hard either.

If you pay attention in class, do all the readings, and study a lot for the tests, you'll do fine. Oh! And do any extra credit you can. Overall though, interesting class, cool professor, would recommend to anyone.

The tests are not tailored for the lectures in a meaningful fashion. Reis is a good lecturer in the sense that he can get your attention and make you think or laugh sometimes, but he fails to present the significance of the material related to the topic  epically.

Generally, very clear, but he's got a very weird dymanic with students and is not terribly approachable. Also, on certain topics, his personal feelings win out over empirical evidence, and that is lame.

Prof. Reis is one of the best lecturers I've had at the UofR. PSY 263 was an amazingly interesting course and I would recommend it to anyone. Doing the readings, attending class and STUDYING are extremely vital in order to do well in the course!! However, because the course is so interesting, actually doing the work is not so much of a chore.
He is such a funny guy, always makes us laugh in class. can see he emphasizes on writing, essays are required even you take 263 without w. the materials covered are interesting. haaaaaaard tests.

Interesting, engaging, funny and brilliant. The tests can be tricky but they're exactly like the practice tests he puts up (even the same questions sometimes). If you pay attention in class and do the reading, it's not too bad. Probably my favorite class I've taken so far.
not that great. his tests don't really relate to the teaching and they can be unfair. all common sense. i didn't learn much. he is a nice guy thouh but i think the class wasn't worth it
hard exams hard exams hard exams... get ready to study
Reis is a GREAT lecturer and 263 was my favorite psych class at UR because of him!
I loved the course, hated the exams.  The reading is a chore.  Best lecturer I've had yet.

Harry is the best professor at the univ. His tests are pretty difficult and you do need to attend every class and read everything if you want to do well, but he teaches in such a down-to-earth way, trying to relate each topic to his students. He's incredibly nice and wants the students to do well and learn.  Very passionate and respected. Love him!
He seems like a funny and interesting guy.  He's also well published and his studies are often cited in the text.  I like him!
This guy is really really bad.  He just needs to smile and be open.  It would be painful for Harry Reis to smile.

Easily one of, if not the best studio art teacher at UofR. While his style of teaching is anything but ordinary, and he can come off cold and uninterested. If you take the time to converse and actually talk to him, he is a wealth of knowledge, well thought out critiques, advice, and jokes. Literal textbook zany art professor.

His drawing classes do not teach you how to draw. Want to learn and improve your technique? Nope, not at this school. But they're pretty valuable in that they teach you how to think creatively and critically about art-making. He gives you a prompt and you have a lot of liberty as to how you work with it. Note: he's demanding. doesnt seem so at 1st
I absolutely loved this class.  This professor.  Easy.  I suggest you take this class.  He is funny, and has a great sense of humor.  HOT
Best professor ever. Seriously. The kind that changes your life.

I would get into trouble if I wrote what I really thought of this man. But art is his life, he takes it very seriously. That's respectable. But I don't respect much else. Short temper, hard to work with.
Very friendly. Low stress course.  Definatley improved my drawing skills. Great as a first studio art class.
great professor, easy to talk to, relaxed, funny and helpful.
amazing, amazing man. my hero.
He encourages creativity and is fairly personable. He doesn't teach you much HOW to draw however and he's scatter-brained and disorganized.

I know people who did not like this professor, however, I thought his lectures were good and his tests were fine. There isn't a final because the class is project-based, which is nice. I would recommend using office hours for the homework assignments. Overall, a good intro level class that was not very difficult.
Porosoff is such a chill guy. He makes it really easy for students to do well in his class, very gracious with grading on exams.
One of the best professors I've ever had, very caring with a lot of ways for you to boost your grade, and the course illustrates basic chemical engineering principles very well.
I had the honor to TA for Professor Porosoff, he is such a kind person and genuinely cares about his students. He is a very generous grader and wants students to engage with the material.

Professor Porosoff gives really good lectures that are clear and easy to follow. He makes it clear what will be on each exam/quiz and gives comprehensive study guides/practice problems. He is very helpful and genuinely wants every student to succeed. He's probably the best professor the school could have chosen to teach an engineering intro class.

Professor Porosoff does a great job at easing the freshmen that take CHE 150 into chemical engineering and university life in general. He reassures students whenever they happen to not do good on an assignment and has rather engaging lectures with bits of humor sprinkled in. The textbook is not required. Everything is covered in lecture.
Great teacher, really passionate about his subject and finds a way to make his lectures personal and not stuffy. Willing to meet outside of class and wants everyone to succeed.
Professor Porossof is such a great professor you can clearly tell he's passionate about his work and he genuinely cares about his students.

Professor Porosoff was very good at teaching and had very clear expectations. His lectures were easy to follow along and he made sure the whole class understood. Not the most accessible out of class, but if you email him, he will make time.

Good lecturer for PSYC101. Delivery can be quite monotone, but lecture material is interesting. Incorporates many studies and is pretty funny. Grading guidelines somewhat unclear, 4 midterms, 2 TA led 3-week mini courses, 1 TA led 2-week debate session. Each midterm 50 mcq and easy to score well through memorization of lecture material. No HW!
honestly I don't understand the hate, bros genuinely funny and I love the lectures. Just show up, do the work and you will do great.

Neimic teaches a lot of major lectures at the University of Rochester and because of this records a lot of his material for student to use as asynchronously. He seems to care and you will come away from this class knowing the material but he definitely is a character - is a little polarizing. Overall I think he cares.
LITERALLY SO RUDE.

This course is discussion-based, so be sure to do the required viewing/reading. Very reasonable exams, so long as you come to class and the review session you'll do well. She's also understanding of long/difficult texts, and will go over them in class.

The structure of the class is a bit odd but definitely helps you achieve the goal of practicing writing. We talked about generally interesting topics but the readings were long and often hard to follow, leading to class be much more of her explaining it to us than an active conversation. Otherwise, understanding and definitely knows German well.
