comment: She is genuinely the most uninformative and last-minute professor on the planet. She attempts to teach, but the slides she posts, if she posts, are empty, and we all end up learning a grand total of nothing. With this knowledge of nothing she has bestowed upon us, she gives out quizzes that expect us to read her mind or think like MATLAB. (1)

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Graded by few things']
comment: bad professor, doesnt know how to teach and barely was able to give e us the stuffs

for BME 201P: impossible to pass any quiz or exam unless you can read her mind to tell what she's grading on. does not take feedback. doesn't release assignment grades until months later so you have no clue how you're doing in the class. doesn't respond to emails or show up to class.

Dr. Ganeshan was okay when it came to explaining concepts when they were first introduced, but if you forgot something a week later, she would look at and talk to you like you were stupid. She treated the material as if it was common knowledge for everyone after we had just learned it for the first time.

Horrible teacher with an insane amount of course load. Following the instructions on the lab report gets you a 70. Lab reports are long and irrelevant. She prepares you to join her life mission to stay in a lab and replicate smarter people's discoveries and basing your entire career on it. Be prepared to hate BME to the guts after this class.

Hands down one of my least favorite professors. Labs are a ridiculous amount of work for no reason but have little to no purpose. Barely teaches you anything, and often expects for you to know exactly what you are doing. Instructions for labs are often unclear, so you do not know whether or not you are doing the correct thing.

Veena was my instructor in the Signals class. She was very approachable when I needed her help with the writing part which is the difficult part of the course. She was good about giving clear feedback on reports. My first graded report was hard to accept but after the second one I saw how much I improved as a writer.

Veena Ganeshan is a professor for the super hard Circuits class. It is always hard to understand the lab since it is so much ahead of the class. Veena helped me on so many occasions when I was having trouble and guided me through each step. We had a full class but she still gave me the time I needed for each question.
She doesn't help students and if you ask her a question she will berate you instead of actually helping. She also doesn't respect social distancing and gets within 6 feet of you.
Unclear grading. Get marked down for things she never asked for to begin with and were never in the assignment. Posts things late and then expects you to get them done in the same amount of time.

Veena is the lab administrator for a few BME courses and is just plainly a bad teacher. She offers very, very unclear instructions and if the equipment is faulty during lab, instead of helping you fix it, blames you for not knowing what to do (even if she also does not know how to fix it). Just the worst teacher I've ever had, avoid if possible.

Classes discussion-based, very effective, every student led 1-2, encouraging strong understanding of material. Makes sure everyone understands stuff b4 moving on, participation always felt encouraged, welcoming environment. Thorough feedback. Personally met with each student 2x during semester. Lots of freedom to pursue interests in final project.

MATH-171 was my introduction to higher math. I found the course incredibly difficult, but am very glad that I took it with this professor. He packed an insane amount of information into each lecture, which was at times overwhelming, but in the long run rewarding. The textbook, Calculus by Michael Spivak, will be your saving grace.
He writes faster than I can think omg. The only reason this class is somewhat doable is because of the workshops and the good TAs. still not easy tho
He ruined my life :)))))))))))))
There are many abstract examples in his class, but if you can understand them, you will find the exam pretty easy

just a heads up, while sevak is def one of the better math profs out there, 150 is seriously no joke. he is an amazing teacher but i found the material so ridiculously difficult that by a certain point even with the office hours (which were v helpful ALWAYS TAKE ADVANTAGE OF) i still had to google for so so much clarification by the end of semester

Excellent professor! If you need to take Math 150, definitely take it with Sevak. He explains things very thoroughly and clearly during class and is very accessible. The class itself can be challenging at times, but I barely needed to touch the textbook at all - his lectures were usually enough to understand the material.

Take MATH 150 with no one but professor Sevak! He creates a laid-back classroom atmosphere and does a great job at explaining concepts and distinctions. He also tries to answer every question raised in the classroom and makes sure students understand his responses.

Sevak is my favorite professor during the freshman year. I barely did anything for the course rather than his lectures and they were more than enough. Although the topic are difficult sevak made them easy so that I got an A without studying much. If you are going to take Math150 then take it with no one but Sevak! He gives it only in fall though

He is my best professor so far! Clear and helpful lecture and notes. I recommend skim the important or complicate sections of the textbook. Go to every office hours of him even without questions! In addition, if you know how to solve every problem from the past exams, you will surely get an A.
The best professor for math 150! Very accessible and willing to help during office hours.
The best professor ever! If you want to take math 150, take his class! He is willing to help outside class. You can ask anything related to the course during office hours.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Great professor! Very accessible! Best Professor for MTH150.

He is a good professor and does really care about his students. The lecture material is quite complicated, but he does his best to explain it. He's helpful during office hours and the webwork is very helpful. Make sure to do the webwork and practice exams. He kind of has a thick accent, but he's willing to repeat what he said.

If you have to take MTH150, make sure it is with Sevak. He is by far the best of the four teachers who teach it. The subject is extremely difficult, there's no getting around that, but he does it the best. You walk in, and the lecture starts immediately, and goes until the minute class is over. He never wastes a second of your time.
mth202 is hard class but he is very good teacher

Very good professor. Make sure you do your webwork and practice tests before each exam to do really well. Not the easiest class, but going to Sevak's office hours and doing your work definitely makes this class very doable.

Easy to follow along and always willing to answer questions. 162 is a very tough course but Sevak is one of the better professors to prepare you for exams. Use the textbook to supplement before or after lecture

Sevak is generally a good professor, not the best out there but better than most of those teaching MTH 162. The class itself is pretty hard but I think he's one of the most helpful professors. Use his office hours, he's really useful in them
Very helpful and approachable. Gives lots of examples, and is always willing to go over a concept again in class. However, you will have to go through the textbook to supplement your learning.

Explains concepts really well through examples. Attending his lectures and practicing problems from the textbook helps. He is extremely helpful during office hours and is ready to explain a concept from scratch.
Flies through lectures but if you ask him to explain will take the time and provide extra examples. Expects you to try it on your own and read the book first.
He is great.

Ken is a nice guy, and pretty laid-back, which makes the atmosphere of the classes cool. Unfortunately, his idea of teaching debate is more like shamelessly plugging for the Debate Team. 90% of what I learned in this class would only ever be applicable if I decided to do Academic Debate on a team, which was not helpful for my legal minor.

He is very funny and lively, so "lecture" is entertaining. He's also very nice and approachable. The workload really isn't much at all- just a couple research projects take a while. He's also pretty clear, and tests/quizzes are pretty fair.

Ken is an interesting guy. The class is not easy because you need to do the work. The drag of the class has to be the tests about the book and vocabulary. Ken does show favoritism to those who are on the debate team but it is just the same type of favor that other professors show to students they already know.The best parts are the inclass debates.

Ken is a very good professor. He is extremely approachable and possibly the nicest professor I have had here. Many have said that the workload is large, but I didn't find it difficult at all.His assistant Brad is also unbelievably nice and very helpful. I look forward to any other class I have with Ken.
Tough class. Lots of work but I learned more than I have in many others. People complain about his style, but pay attention and it all comes together ...

Ken is super funny and he has tons of hilarious stories. Lectures are not the easiest to follow.Notes on the board are hard to understand but he will always answer questions during or after class. He is really helpful. He also lets you edit the biggest assignment for a better grade. Focuses more on competitive debate but still a great class!

First up, this class is a LOT of work. I would have liked more focus on debate techniques and less on politics. That being said, Ken is a good guy, easy going and interesting. If you have an interest in competitive debate, this is a great class. If you don't and just want to learn general techniques with real life applications, it's less useful.

Although an extremely funny guy, Ken's lecture notes and style is very messy and difficult to understand. I thought it was going to be more debate, but its a lot more lecture and him trying to convince you to join the debate team, favors students that are on the debate team. Unless you are on the debate team... don't take this class!

This class is a ****load of work!!! BE WARNED! If you can do it all, you will do well. Do not get behind, and attend every class. Ken is amazing, and definitely makes the course worth it. He's really funny and keeps the course from dragging. Always there to talk to. Definitely a worthwhile course if you're up to the challenge.

Ken is a funny guy and a good teacher.  He teaches in a very down-to-earth style that makes the material much less intimidating.  Assignments take some work, but they aren't too difficult.  He'll ask very pointed questions and force you to defend your answer, which makes everything feel like a  debate.  It's fun though - keeps you on your toes.

Very nice, friendly, funny.  Not a great teacher.  It's kind of unclear how knowledgeable he is about his field, but he does have pretty impressive credentials.  The class was boring to me, but he did his best to keep it interesting.

He's the man. A very interesting and funny guy who teaches a good class. He knows his stuff as well. Class starts out a little boring but gets good once it gets going. He might play favorites with kids who are on the debate team, but that's not to say he's not cool with everyone else. Ken Johnson=Jack Black+Conan O'Brien+Philip Seymour Hoffman.

Blankenship started off rough and gave us a lot of homework/tests that we didn't really have the capacity to finish, but that's just because he came to a River Campus elective class with an Eastman degree. Now his assignments are really lenient and he's a very knowledgeable and passionate guy. If you want to know theory well, I highly recommend.

Michael was a very nice guy, but was very unorganized making it difficult to know what we were learning about. We never followed the syllabus and he moved at such a fast pace, we often had to redo tests and quizzes because he eventually realized the class did not understand the concepts yet.

Dr. Dove was my favorite professor this semester by far. She was everything you would ask for in a teacher and more. She was accessible, clear, and a very fair grader. She makes you work for your grade, but in doing so you become a better writer and student. I am extremely excited and nervous for HON272 next semester. I would highly recommend.

Dr. Dove is awesome! I highly recommend her. She is kind, respectful of your comments and ideas and facilitates class discussion well. She also chooses interesting and applicable readings and is more than willing to help with papers in office hours, unlike some other HON272 professors.  I would take her class again in a heartbeat.

Dr Dove was an AMAZING human event professor. Kind and helpful, she was excellent at facilitating group discussion and creating a class that was surprisingly very interesting. She always appreciates the comments that everyone makes and makes achieving a high grade a possibility. Coming from someone who HATED Hon 171, I loved this class. TAKE HER!!

Had her for hon 171 and she had a lot of energy and enthusiasm for the subjects. Her grading is fair, a little rough sometimes, but the weighting of grades work out that you get the grade you deserve. She is not mean at all, super nice. Three papers, and a one paragraph response due every friday. Not bad. Highly encouraged.

Dr. D. has a very interesting approach to her subject and you can tell that she is passionate about it.  It's easy to ask her questions and she is more than willing to help in any way that she can.  She provided the class with entertaining projects and helped us to improve in areas we were struggling in.

she's a pretty cool and down to earth professor. helpful when you need her and is always smiles. she tries pretty hard to make the class interesting and the films for the class are pretty good as well as the paper topics. she grades pretty fair- you get the grade you deserve
No Comments
She was pretty chill, but her grading is a little rough...overall a lot better than other CAS techers
Most passive aggressive (sometimes not so passive) lady I've ever met
Explicitly told me that the University of Rochester may not be for me.
not understanding of students experiencing mental health
Glad that lab is over
Though she is a good person, her lab lectures and her criteria of both prelabs and postlabs are driving me crazy both this semester and last semester.

Had her for lab lecture. Lab is fine, only 1 lab report and others are just post-lab worksheets graded super easily. Lab lecture attendance is basically mandatory, easy hw assignments. Feel like lecture is a waste of time tho bc you don't learn anything lab related, you just learn life skills - feel like my time can better be used for smtg else.

It is one thing to genuinely care for a student's ability to succeed, it is another thing to fill countless *Chemistry* lab lectures with assignments solely about study skills. Students need to learn about lab techniques, not how some student managed to go from F to A with the prof's study techniques.

A lot of people said that she is mean and picky, but if you follow every thing said on the syllabus, it is easy to get a good grade. If you are still worried, you can go to her office hour. She is actually quite approachable and funny sometimes and very willing and patient to answer the questions you have.

(*Note the 137) Yeah she is strict and her lab manuals have several spelling errors, but it never affected her teaching or my learning. Her office hours were always reliable and so were the TAs'. If you're afraid of losing points or whatever they're happy to check if you're right or not. The labs were a good supplement/review for the main material.

Semi-regular homework assignments, dull lectures, only one credit. This add on was begging to be treated like a class in its own right. Just go to lab and do the assignments and you will do fine. They removed the need to do lab reports so it'll be a breeze.

The labs were a good learning experience and also and taught me how to keep an organized scientific notebook. She's a kind professor and cares that her students understand the experiments. I liked her lectures.

We get very lengthy instructions in our lab manuals but we're given little to no help beyond that, directions can be very confusing and contain many typos, making some questions impossible, and grading is wildly inconsistent across different TAs. Points can be taken off for things never explicitly asked for in instructions. Awful class.

She's strict about things but honestly the lab manual carried my entire grade. While there are grammatical errors, the lab manual takes you through every single step and actually teaches you how to do problems unlike some professors. A good TA is still pretty important, but she makes them all have office hours so you can just go see another one.
She's helpful during lab lecture but oftentimes not very accommodating. Her TAs do the grading which was relatively fair. Her homeworks were easy.

The lectures were mainly just teaching basic Microsoft skills and filling in a worksheet for attendance. The labs were fine but did take a long time to complete. Your lab grade is a quarter of your overall CHEM 131 grade. There is a few extra credit points towards the end to boost your grade. FREQUENT EMAILS
Your grade mainly depends on your TAs. Pray for good ones.

I heavily disliked CHEM 131 lab and lab lecture. The labs were shoddily designed and confusing, and Dr. Stanford was not receptive to genuine inquiry from my classmates. On the other hand, the lab lectures were dreadfully easy and gave me a minimal knowledge of Excel I could just as easily get off YouTube. Only take this if you absolutely must.

This is her second or third year doing CHEM 131 lab and she decided to rewrite the entire lab manual. The experiments are standard, but the manual is riddled with errors. Seriously, did anyone proof read it? Additionally, the post lab questions are way beyond the scope of our 131 lecture. More communication is needed between 131 and 131L.
Terrible teacher.
She took off all 3 points for one small missing calculation which is just ridiculous because it is not an accurate representation of the work completed.

This professor is the most awful one that I have ever met in U of R. The whole CHEM 131 teaching team is chaotic. There are no clear guideline of how to complete the post-lab work, and it's even due before the first lab lecture. She can be hardly accessed by email, and her words on webpage indicated "Don't contact me for most of the time". Worst!!!
Prof Stanford inherited the old guys labs and didn't have enough time to change them for her first year but she did what she could to make them easier to understand/complete
Dr Stanford is a very good instructor.  She is very well prepared and presents things in a organized manner. She does make you work for a good grade,

I had Dr. Stanford for first semester and initially was not a fan because the lab lectures had a lot of information packed into such a short amount of time. However, this semester, the material in lab lecture lined up with the course, so it was easier to follow, and I actually learned more in lab lecture versus regular lecture. Love her dogs too :)

95% of the lab lectures were useless, the only good parts were the last 4-5 slides with sample calculations for the lab. I asked her to check my work for one question during lab lecture and she told me I was wrong, but when she showed the answer it was the same as mine..? Luckily the TAs were often just as confused as students so they helped w/labs

comment: Lab lectures were confusing and not helpful for completing the post lab report or making sense of experiments. She would speed through slides and then tell us to work on the worksheets and yell at us when we were confused. Not very helpful and very critical in a destructive way. No way to get around having her if you take chem though.

The lab for CHEM137 is stupendously long and incredibly awful when it comes to grading, can you believe that merely the TA signature takes up half of the points for a lab?! You work your ass off to get all calculations correct, yet you lose half of the points because of the absence stupid TA signature! Even you took all the data!

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I don't know, the lab lectures were incredibly confusing and I didn't even understand the material until the actual lab to be honest. Her emails also seem very passive aggressive when you ask her a question. Like, one word responses when you type an entire formal paragraph length email. I did just fine in labs with TAs being the ones teaching us.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Dr. Stanford is new at the university, taking over for the old department leader (I think). The labs given were from the last head and don't relate to the class and are often very confusing. Dr. Stanford is remaking the labs to be more reasonable and relatable to the class. I appreciate her effort in bettering the curriculum.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I have so much respect for Dr. Stanford. She knows the labs we have to do are brutal and don't make sense, and she's spent a lot of time adjusting them and teaching us calculations step by step to make it easier on us. Makes the math and concepts understandable, & has a pretty good sense of humor. Very grateful for the fact that she made lab easier
A professor clearly does not know how to teach undergraduate students. Made homework during the exam week and was vague about homework expectations and labs.
He's an awesome lecturer and cares his student a lot. Even though the freshman organic chemistry is much harder than the sophomore one, it worth it.
This professor has a wonderful teaching style and know very well what he is teaching.

Freshman organic chemistry is very hard. However, Professor Weix provides you with everything you need to make it through. If you put in the effort, attend all the lectures and workshops, you can make it through. After every test he gives the class a pep talk (avg. is usually around 60%; big curve as a result). Gifted lecturer

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: Good lectures make the class interesting and if you keep up with the reading you shouldn't have any issues

Dr. Weix is a great lecturer who genuinely cares about his students. He's accessible and understands the student's perspective, so it's nice to talk to him during office hours if lectures don't already make sense. Tests are totally fair for the material (for Chm 171) and lab is exactly as challenging as it should be (Chm 210).

Beware, this guy plays favorites. He might not try to, but in this class he definitely reached out to the freshmen way more than the sophomores. The grading scheme is confusing, so it can be hard to do well if you haven't ever written reports for him before. In spite of it all, if you get on his good side the class will go well for you.

He is a great lecturer and cares so much about the course and the students. We definitely had a great understanding of what to do in lab before we got in there and why. The lab was a ton of work both in lab and for lab reports, but it makes everyone a way better chemist. Only gripe is that the grading system is not straight forward, so it stressful
Same grader as the previous rating. I made a mistake th class is CHM 171 not CHM 173 my bad.

The class is a lot of work to keep up with the material and the exams are definitely challenging but his curve is nice and he's very well-liked by the students. He's funny and ties the stuff from lecture into real-life chemistry lab work. His lectures are definitely the most important, especially later in the course. I'm very glad I took the class.
It's clear cut- he really cares. The textbook sucked though- get orgo as a second language.

Pretty nice guy who is rather knowledgeable in the area of organic chemistry.  He is very willing to help you out if you have questions.  The lab reports are rather grueling, however, and the class really should be at least 4 credits instead of 2.  But that isn't his fault.

Course was based on comedy. He helped make the homework interesting through videos and movies. Discussion based classes that often became boring, and he would get irritated when we weren't engaged. Very harsh grader on papers, and his comments weren't always helpful.

The class structure was genuinely ridiculous. Grading was inconsistent, we had weekly chapter quizzes on Tuesdays that we never got any feedback on or got back at all. Problem sets were graded harshly and got little help or guidance from course staff. Professor was quite awkward and unengaging, he tends to ramble on without making much sense often.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: this class was extremeley stressful. gsis were not helpful and assignments are very confusing. if you don't have a lot of prior coding experience you will be lost. prof is responsive but problem sets were graded harshly

This class was structured very theoretically, with all the readings, yet the PSETS were entirely technical. His instructions for assignments were often very vague & unintuitive for students, which made them more difficult than they should've been. Professor Piantadosi was nice and caring, but I think the course could've been run a bit better.

Caring professor, super nice and approachable (open to all questions), and very knowledgable in his field of study!
The homeworks can be a little tough/time-consuming, but they're really interesting and you get a lot out of them. It's easy to get full points too, as long as you make sure to thoroughly answer the questions!
Would recommend
Steve is a hilarious person and great lecturer! His class is pretty hard, but engaging lectures more than make up for it
Caring and kind professor! Clear lectures as well. The assignment-based format of the class (no midterms/finals) made it easy for me to emphasize learning over grades.

It appears that all of the people who found Prof Piantadosis class difficult go to U of Rochester, which isnt exactly known for its rigor to be blunt. Steve is a truly great prof. His lectures are informative and his attitude is caring and fair. While the class was disorganized, it was easy to look past that all else considered
Boring
Lectures were easy-ish to understand, but I was really unsure about in what way the materials are going to be tested. No sample questions or whatsoever to help.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: I did not find this class to be anything but disappointing. He should really stick to research. He seems to find making the class difficult fun. His lectures were sometime difficult to follow. The exams were hard and he was not the most helpful, nor was he willing to explain things in a clearer way. Do not take this class.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Tough grader. hard class. Weekly assignment with tough grading and you dont even get feedback on your assignment. Concentrate a lot on research which is confusing during lecture. lecture was helpless but had to go because attendance is mandatory. Hard exams ! And final is worth 30% of your grade!
He is not a lecturing professor and needs to just stick to research
Really enjoy this class! The assignments are really inspirational! Love him!

Professor Piantadosi is highly knowledgable, and it comes across in his lectures. The material is tough, but totally fascinating. Tests are tricky multiple choice, but there are also weekly writing assignments to boost your grade. Attendance is not taken, but there's a large amount of content so, functionally, you won't pass if you skip lectures.

Amazing professor. Have heard many good things about him from others. Shame that most students wouldn't be able to fully appreciate his style of teaching. Makes you think and opens your eyes to not only classics, but the whole world and what it is made of.
This man was instrumental in my departure from the cave.
Simply amazing. I have learned more from discussing translations than all my other classes combined.
took 202 & 142. BEST TEACHER EVER. adorable...Zeus in human form.  he really just wants you to try to understand. discussion class. not much work.

Geier Is AWESOME! Really nice guy. I took his intro greek class as a potential for my cluster and his classes has definitely been some of my favorites. His classes are what you think college classes should be like...before you actually start college

The living reincarnation of Socrates minus the annoying factor. If you really want to learn the philosophy of the Ancients, you go to this man and avoid the philosophy dept. He might seem unclear, but the more you read Plato, the more you see Geier's quality in teaching. He is a living treasure and a fortune to those who connect with the readings.
The man is none other than Zeus himself

Very interesting professor- loves the material and makes you appreciate it because of that. He isn't your conventional teacher when it comes to grading- he wants you to learn. He also wants you to succeed, so he grades in your favor. Discussion based- speak up in class.
He seems like a space cadet, but he's a good thinker.  Do your homeworks during class.  You don't need to take notes to do well.  His grading is sketch, but there are no complaints about it from me.

Oh man, such a beautiful human being. If you're at all a student (in the ideal sense) and you're interested in the material, you should have no trouble at all. He's very discussion oritented, very intelligent, and occaisionally it goes above you, but if you act at all interested he will help you as much as he can.

He's all about class participation; his grading policy is one huge gray area, but in your favor.  He loves nothing more than when you show interest by asking to meet with him right before essays are due.  He's a very optimistic grader, looking for all your good points, more than criticizing the bad parts of your essays.  He's awesome.
greatest prof ever.
really interesting, just take notes and write your essays from them for ideas of the greeks, i really liked him
No Comments
Very nice guy. Great thinker. Interesting course for those that like philosophy or Greek Ideas.
Great philosphy/religion professor
Very entertaining lectures, and she made psych engaging for everyone

comment: LOVVVVED her class. It's super easy and interesting as long as you actually show up!
She graded papers a bit harsher than the requirements she had posted, but otherwise Jess did a decent job at teaching about writing.

She was a good professor. It wasn't boring and I feel like she went easier on us than the other writing professors did. She offered help whenever you needed. As long as you put in a good effort, you can get a good grade. But she does grade papers extremely hard.

There's not many assignments throughout the course. The deadlines and grading are pretty relaxed, and it's very discussion based. You won't be learning much about the software used to develop apps or sites, but you'll learn a lot about the user research process.

If you're someone who's already familiar with photography, videography, and/or Adobe on a basic level, this course is a breeze in the park. If you're a beginner, it definitely is a bit more work, but Kirby is a super kind grader. You get the time to pursue your own projects rather than do meaningless assignments which I really appreciate.

While Kirby is one of the passionate people you'll ever meet about photography, that same passion does NOT translate to his teaching. His classes are easy, especially if you are somewhat creative, but unless you go out of your way to get to know him outside of the classroom, he will put minimal effort into seeing you excel.
Chill guy but basically doesn't answer any email even when he sees it. Gives extension when asked. Just make sure you do the assignments and follow the requirement can receive good grade.

I have mixed feelings on Kirby. He is obviously really talented and passionate about photography but I don't think he really enjoys teaching this class. Lectures are generally quite useless and consist of looking through the works of well-known and critically acclaimed artists.

The material discussed in lecture is totally irrelevant to assignment. He shows us artwork by virtuosos, but never mention how should we do with the software for assignments. He even just left us a pdf file to let us learn how to operate!! So, I learned these knowledge from YouTube. What is the purpose for the existence of professor?
Very knowledgeable and genuine teacher. Takes interest and value in what the students create. Make sure you put in effort.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Hilarious']
comment: Took intro to photography with him. He's very knowledgable and willing to dive deeper into whatever you have questions about. He is flexible and understanding but also doesn't take bs so just show that you care. I missed two critiques because the class is in the am, but I made up for it, bless him. Great guy.
Kirby is really understanding if you express that you're having difficulty with an assignment as long as you show that you're putting in effort.

She would go over like 1 or 2 practice problems in class, then give way harderquestions on the exam, she expects you to just know it from the 1 time it was shown + the homeworks, and she would have pop quizzes which she would pause class for an extended period of time and hover.

She is nice but she cannot teach. She spends the whole class talking about how difficult chapter 7 is, but the only reason that it is difficult is because she barely teaches it. She will go through one practice problem and then give you something 100x harder on the exam. It doesn't matter how hard you try, it is exceptionally difficult to do well.

Dr. J is what everyone hopes for in a college professor. She was very clear that as long as you came to lecture, you would succeed in the course, and that is exactly what happened. The final exam was the most prepared I felt for any test in my life because she made study materials easily available and made herself available constantly.

The material can be challenging at first but if you come to class and do practice exercises on the slides, you will be fine. There are many examples in the slides for you to practice. You aren't allowed to use laptop but you can use iPad or notebooks. She's willing to help and and encourage you to come to office hour if you have any questions.

I thought the beginning of the class was by far the most difficult which was discouraging but I did end up enjoying it. The class is fairly difficult, at least on the exams, but the lectures, homework, and labs are all well organized and helpful.

Honestly I think Prof.Jay is great. She is helpful and energetic. She encourage you to go OH everytime. But since it's a huge lecture. It can't make sure everyone get treated. So your own Participation and effort is important. She is also kind that 20% Lab is nearly given you if you do the Lab. PPT is useful and Tests take high percentage.

Labs feel convoluted and homeworks are hard to get a hang of, but you almost always get a 100% for labs and if you discuss homeworks with others you can usually put together something good enough to get a decent grade. Concepts can be kinda chaotic though, but if you take the time they're not the worst thing ever to make sense of.

HW not too hard but takes a long time to finish so get started early. Sometimes lenient with extensions, mostly not. Wants students to understand/enjoy the content, but can move too quickly through lectures. Attendance not mandatory, but since the unmarked lecture slides are posted on Blackboard instead of the annotated ones, u should go to class.

I don't really understand why wouldn't she post the lecture notes, she should be aware of students are having a hard time following. No computer or phone is allowed, means we handwrite everything. She goes through slides so fast, a full page of solution and she only showed for a minute. But gives extra credit, and  is a nice person.

Lectures are unorganized and confusing. She does not post the answers to solutions on slides, which is a problem because even if you attend class she speeds through them before you can finish writing. Labs and HW are just busywork and not very helpful. After chapter 5 everything went downhill. If you can take anyone else, please do.

She's very organized on the surface but her lectures are really difficult to follow. Like don't get me wrong - she definitely cares. If YOU have to take this class then I'd recommend you spend time organizing the concepts and use cases on your own. In retrospect this class could've been a cheat sheet.

She was nice and engaging lecturer. Gotta go to class tho cause she don't post notes. Her slides were kinda disorganized but understandable. Ngl so much tedious work tho if ur taking other harder classes too (weekly mandatory labs, long hw)

its not too hard to understand her, the hard part is trying to decipher what she is trying to say because she tends to say something wrong, correct it, then correct it again, then go back to the second thing she said. no recorded lectures, no work notes posted but says attendance is not mandatory. do not take her if you don't know stats before
Not a difficult class. Professor is patient to teach everything.

A very caring person and a fine lecturer. She is understanding and will give extensions if you need one. Her tests are not too hard if you review lecture notes and do the past exams. Homeworks can be a bit difficult, but the TAs are helpful. She is great at answering questions and getting to know each student in the class. Attendance is important.
She just yaps and yaps. Whole lot of nothing being said. Atleast its easy content, and she does give bonus points.

She is nice and always answer your questions in Officehour(she didnot work during the non oh time so go to ask questions directly). You can even check all the HWanswer with her, and she will help u if u have questions. The most problems are this lecture is not hard but seems rly difficult, you just need to remember how to do question is enough!

Lecture heavy and she won't put answers (for practice problems) on the slides in order to "encourage attendance". Pestered us for attendance so we could get an "attendance point" that didn't end up happening. Very accessible outside of class and willing to answer questions. Lots of homework (around 6) and a final project. The labs are easy.
Pretty accessible outside of class, lectures are okay not that fun to sit through

- If you attend class, you can get her full slides. It's not a big deal
- Between her own and TA office hours, there are hours every single day 
- She does answer questions via email
- Her lectures are interesting and stay on topic
- I had to study a TON for tests

I've never taken a stat class before, and I've learned a lot! I recommend her class.
Her lecture is so good

The biggest thing is that she doesn't post the examples from the lecture slides which makes it difficult to review materials outside of class. Homeworks are graded pretty strictly and she often rambles/gets off topic during lectures.

Very tough grader, and makes her self inaccessible. Refuses to answer questions through email and will only answer questions during her limited office hours. Does not teach the class, just flips through a slide show and expects us to immediately comprehend the information as she quickly skips. Not allowing students to access class notes after class
Her notes are so good. Take the course if you have experience of math 201 and math 203, then it would be great experience

Very condescending to students, talks down to most of the students as if we are in elementary school. Consistently complains about how nobody talks to her, but makes herself very unapproachable by essentially fighting back if you have any questions. Her lectures just become her rambling then asking us to participate. Tests are their own content.
Says a whole lot of nothing with how much she says, must have been a lawyer in her past life but she is friendly...
Explained concepts well and criteria were very well outlined. Pretty easy to get an A.

she puts a lot of effort into teaching, but self-study is still more effective. Attendance is mandatory, and tough grading for homework. It's suitable for individuals who enjoy doing extra work to take on.
She is the best stat prof that I ever met!! Some hard work but it will be worth it

She was very sweet and tries her best to help her students. However, lectures often go off topic, and notes are sometimes unclear. Exams are way too easy which makes it hard to justify studying hard for this class.

Anyone who doesn't give Ming-Lun a 5, please ignore them. Best professor in the ECE Department!

An extremely thoughtful instructor that cares about the understanding of their students. Makes class comfortable and conducive to learning by putting effort into details which is evident in concise, thought-out explanations and examples. Accessible and easy to talk with both in and out of class.

Very knowledgable and smart. He puts real efforts into customizing the course materials instead of blindly following textbook. His lectures are very helpful and insightful. Professor Pai is REALLY knowledgeable and smart.I like how he gives very important resources to explore and for us to "learn how to learn". really amazing guy. if you took AP stats in high school this class will be easier to understand. does a very good job providing resources and material to assist with lectures. my only downside is that the lectures can be incredibly boring. i slept in every class and still ended up with an A. amazing professor regardless, just be prepared for such.
Great professor! Very knowledgable and caring! One of the best professors from the political science department.

Curt is extremely smart and very knowledgeable about R and political science in general. He's really fun to talk to and a genuine human unlike some professors at Rochester. a very good liberal economist. The homework may be tough and time-consuming, but it really helps to understand macro well.

Very AWESOME professor! She is clear and her handwriting is like that of an angel. It helps to read the textbook about the section you are going to learn about before you have it in class. Exams are difficult, but studying is the best way to prepare!
don't take the math 200. its homework could cost you more than 5 hours and endless frustration when you are trying to write PROOFS.

Dr. Olek is an interesting professor.  The main key to succeeding in his class is to think conceptually and in a "creative" fashion.  I really like how he taught us to think critically.  You will have to put in effort in this class.  I went to class, actively participate in workshop, and went up to him to ask questions and managed to pull off an A.

Very disorganized. Made us buy textbooks but never used it (said textbooks were "dinosaurs"). He is helpful if you try with an open mind. Gives away some questions on his test in lecture, so make sure you don't miss those. His slides can be very vague but he bases his tests on his them. The workshops are more helpful.

I wouldn't go to class because he goes over the slides so quickly, you don't learn much. He's also very condescending and hard to respect. I wish I would have just solely taught myself from the slides and would have done much much better in the class.

People like to complain about him, but if you keep an open mind he's not terrible. He has a unique style but if you make the effort to learn it, you'll be fine. Not as bad as everyone says. Went to lecture, went to workshop, got an A. Fair grader. Go visit during his office hours on finals week and he is 10X more helpful

SKIP STRAIGHT TO 112!!! DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WORST TEACHER EVER.

Really glad I took Intro to Topology with him. He wrote and explained his notes as he went through the lectures AND recorded every single one. It allowed me more time to stew over the more difficult proofs/theorems. You really should not try rushing topology proofs, it will only rot your brain.
A fantastic professor with adequate humor. I feel shameful did not get an A.
My saver for calculus II

He recorded all his lectures and posted his notes which was very easy as I would print his notes after class and watch the lecture at my pace. Whenever I had questions and emailed him, he would always respond quickly and  he really want students to do well in his class. For 162 - he is the best professor.

Bogdan's lectures are very fast paced and cover a lot of material daily. Miss a class? You're behind a week. Miss a part of class for the bathroom? You could have covered 2 sections of material. Class is dense, attend recitations for WebWork help and you will survive. Curved at the end.

I had this professor for MATH 162, one of the hardest classes in the basic calc sequence here. He had a mazing lectures with lots of examples and was easy to reach via email or in office hours. He even did a great series of review lectures at the end of the year

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: the worst... the most critical as if we are submitting to the highest rated medical journal out there. Often inflexible, unrealistic expectations for reading and comprehension. Rigid with high expectations. Unsure how a student is expected to pass if they have not yet completed the writing lab course, because skills we learn there are relevant.

I do not mind a tough grader, but this instructor is so hypercritical that she is looking for missed periods, missed spaces in your APA papers. If you make mistakes she threatens to reject future papers. Absolutely no sense of compassion and care. A robot. Does not teach, just throws redundant reading. Instructions unclear, students must clarify.

I found his monotone voice quite good actually, grading is done by TA so don't worry, he might just have higher expectations and he doesn't like grading. Will give long detailed answers to your questions. Will work with you if you need accommodation. Best person I've met through UR.
If you go to class, go to office hours, and do the readings and you'll be fine.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: His lectures are really interesting but your grade is heavily dependent on the TA you are assigned based on last name, since he doesn't grade your assignments. Super valuable class to take but somewhat unlucky on the grading front.

Extremely boring lectures. Mandatory attendance (done with paper instead of Blackboard codes for some godforsaken reason). If you're confident you can stay awake, you should be fine grade-wise. Though I agree that he is a pretentious and obnoxious grader at times.

Very passionate professor- he explains everything thoroughly. The TAs, as of now, are pretty strict, so you should take the time to talk with them outside of class to get feedback. I will say that the TA I was assigned is extremely unkind over emails and pretty harsh, so prepare for that if you can.

I enjoyed this class up until the final week... The content is interesting and he opens up the lecture for discussion a good amount. That being said, he took out his stress from the TA strike on the papers that he graded during finals. Gave no solid feedback and marked down for disagreeing with his opinion. Meanwhile, the TA gave everyone else As.

VERY boring class.speaks monotone. Reads off slides.preferred 103 instead. 255,gave his opinion way too often.TAs graded the papers way too harsh.During the strike…Fitz graded the papers and brutally terrorized them-and according to HIS OPINION.I don't see any rubric for this grading.I answered questions w/my opinions. VERYbiased-his opinions or 0!
Phenomenal professor.
Mandatory attendance marked by in-person homework submission. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Nice professor outside of class. Tests are taken remotely and papers are easy.

One of the most boring professors at the school. Every lecture is read mostly off slides and spoken in a monotone voice. Unlike every other professor I have had, you have to buy an expensive textbook to do the 2 assignments(cant find free pdf anywhere). It is also very easy to see his personal biases shine through his teaching.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'So many papers']
comment: Does not give room for proper discussion and just his opinion and refutals to a philosophical theory. Always runs out of time so even in the small discussions he does, he won't let you speak and will interrupt you for the sake of time. Good guy to talk to after class.
Very nice and approachable professor. The material in phil103 is extremely interesting.

Fitzpatrick is one of my favorite professors and his class has sparked my interest in ethics. I really like how he fosters thinking and curiosity rather than memorization. He promotes that by requiring homework and by making tests open note. Tests and papers are graded a bit harshly but the criticism is very fair. Great class to introduce ethics.

mandatory attendence for a 9 a.m. course? no videos?
banned the use of chatgpt for everything, too old school
with midterms plus two papers
workload is too much if you take this one for cluster

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: He cares a lot about his students and definitely knows a lot. Very prepared. Lectures can be a hit or miss. Either very interesting or incredibly boring. Def go to class and take notes. TAs grade papers way too harsh. Textbook is so expensive so I didn't get it and I was lost half the time. Prepare for group discussions everyday.
Short homeworks and reading due before every class so you have to go to lectures. Is a tough grader but all exams are open book and open note. Overall a good and interesting class

Great professor, horrible TAs. Fought for my paper grade that my TA put in the dumps and Fitzpatrick was very supportive of my argument. 225 was more interesting to me since it had less philosophical theory to it. The examples used in class are very interesting. Would highly recommend going to his office hours to review your paper outlines.

Amazing professor and I learned a lot! You could tell he knew what he was talking about and how to convey it. He liked to hear what students had to say and you could tell he genuinely cares. Class was graded based on HW each class(v easy), open note midterm & final, and 2 papers. Make sure to go to OH for papers and use the study guides(v helpful).

I think he's a great professor especially if this is your first time taking a philosophy course! Class is solely graded on 5 things, 1 Midterm, 1 Final, 2 Essays, and homework (assigned for every class). It's pretty manageable, make sure to utilize all the help and make use of your time. TA's do majority of the grading, they can be a bit hash...

Prof. Fitzpatrick is a knowledgeable and respectable professor. Good lecturer and well prepared for every class. There's homework assignments to submit at the begnining of each class, as attendance. Papers can be tough, depending on TA- office hours should help. The exams are fair and pretty lenient. Overall, great class with interesting topics!

I learned a lot of interesting philosophy ideas from this class. He was a really nice professor, lenient on late papers but only if you have a good reason, not too hard of a grader in my opinion and felt like he really cared about his students. The only thing I would've liked better is if we had had more open discussions in class.

PHIL225 is an interesting class (as far as philosophy goes) and his lectures were quite engaging, but boring at times. Class is graded by two papers and one final. The open note final is really not bad. Papers are graded by TAs so it's completely up to them how your grade turns out. Would recommend putting a lot of effort into papers.

Professor Fitzpatrick is a really great guy, he's super knowledgable about the subject and really helpful if you go to office hours. The tests are open note and really easy, and you don't need to study if you take good notes because his slides are very comprehensive. The papers were very manageable and easy to write because of the clear criteria.

Probably one of my favorite professors of all time. Professor Fitzpatrick is truly knowledgeable and passionate about his subject and will teach you a lot of things that are both useful in and outside of class. Showing up to classes is required and the workload is very manageable!

Really recommend taking this class. Grade was based on 2 papers, attendance, homework, and a final which was entirely online. Attendance is mandatory but the homework is very easy and the class is manageable. A very approachable professor and if you put the time in it's an easy A.
I loved Prof. William FitzPatrick. His lectures are very straightforward and super interesting!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Good intro philosophy course! Fitzpatrick broke down all the material really well and is very accommodating. The lectures could get boring, but was over all good. Turning in homework at the beginning of every class was used for attendance, and he doesn't record lectures. So attendance is definitely mandatory which is a little annoying.

William is the best professor I've met so far because he is super polite, gives wonderful lecture, and a wonderful logician. I often email him for minor questions and he always responded with few paragraphs to make sure that he is clear. He is also very handsome and dress in good taste!

One of my favorite Prof's I've had at UR. Super engaging if you sit near the front of class - more difficult if you don't because the class is so large. If you participate and build a good relationship he'll be more willing to bump your grade if you're in-between letter grades. Seems intimidating but is kind if you show you're willing to work.

Super engaging lecturer; ask good questions and sit near the front and he'll be sure to remember you. As an aside, the TA's grade all the papers and their feedback can be confusing, so be sure to contact him with any questions about topics your papers are on during office hours.
Great Professor. Lectures very interesting and he breaks down the concepts well for students. Available for communication with students and willing to assist.

He is the greatest philosophy professor I ever met! Give specific study guides for each exam and give out essay prompt a long time before it is due. As long as you give out good logic in your paper you will pass. He covered a lot of topics in his class but give out good examples to make them very easy to understand. A very good introductory course.
Nice guy but a tough grader. Not a breeze class.

Professor Fitzpatrick recognizes that he has a monotone voice. That's why he chooses early mornings to lecture. When you're having trouble sleeping, attend one of his sluggish speaches. It'll do wonders.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Fitzpatrick was a really good lecturer - engaging and interesting. Outside of class, I relied a little more on the TA for help, because he seemed kind intimidating. #silverfox

Fitzpatrick is interesting but not mind blowing, assigns a very easy homework assignment every class, and a little annoying about technology- no phone use or laptops in class. He will make you feel a little like you are back in high school, but is a fair enough guy. When you get past the history of philosophy, Socrates, etc, the class gets better.
Miserable class. Boring lecturer. Avoid this class.
PHL 103 is an awesome introduction to Philosophy and FitzPatrick is a great professor. Definitely take advantage of office hours and talking to him after class, you'll get a lot out of it.

My favorite professor at UR. I took 103 for fun and decided on a philosophy minor because of Fitzpatrick, and took 225 just because he was the prof. He's a fantastic lecturer and down to earth--just all around an awesome guy.

The most boring class I've ever taken in my life. He's a nice enough guy and intelligent, but he just repeated exactly what we were supposed to read the night before. The exams were kind of difficult, but I was also a freshman first semester, so I probably could have studied a bit more. Definitely not a breeze class. I fell asleep a few times.

Very clear professor. If you go to class and pay attention you will do fine in the class as he is very clear in what is important in the readings. The TAs grade the papers and tend to be a bit harsh, but he is also flexible with changing your grade if you feel it was unfair. Great professor!

Best professor I've had at U of R so far. Incredibly bright guy, makes the material and clear as possible and presents it in a logical manner. He does tend to talk for long stretches of time, but makes it very clear what the main points are and brings up a lot interesting ideas. Overall a pretty easy and super smart dude, such a great professor

Overall a wonderful professor.  In class, he tended to ramble a bit, but if you paid attention and took notes, you learned a ton.  FitzPatrick is also a really cool guy--go to his office hours and get to know him!  He loves to talk to students and share his passion for philosophy.
Stay away.  Awful class. Rambles on and made me fall asleep every single class. The TA's were way too harsh and I did not learn a single thing from the course.
He is a bit boring, but a good teacher

Figlio is great! Public is easily one of the best classes at UoR. It's rare to find a class that is both extremely easy and fascinating at the same time. I appreciated how he balanced conceptual teaching with class discussion. Also, go to his office hours- had many great and thought provoking convos.

Professor Figlio was the best econ teacher I ever had! He made the material fun and understandable. After struggling in previous econ classes, I could not have been more fortunate to have him as my prof. He genuinely cares about his students, both in and out of the classroom, and is great to talk to. I'd happily take his class again!

Knowls and Matson are def hard teachers to get by, their lectures are fast paced and confusing and tests are almost impossible. Clearly they know the way they teach is flawed because the amount of Extra Credit this course has makes it literally impossible to not gen an A. While you might suffer a bit just focus on the EC and you'll be alright

The class is on a point based system, so go to lectures to get attendance points. Highly recommend doing test corrections and the extra credit assignment. The tests are very direct, so as long as you know the material you should be fine. The final exam is optional, so if you have enough points you don't have to take it.
just show up to lectures and workshops, pay attention, do the homework and you'll be fine.

Even though it is easy to get an A in this class, you would feel that you would not be learning much. This professor is monotone and reads off her lectures. It is hard to follow from this professor. I would advise that if you have this professor for chem 131 you need to review again thoroughly afterwards to prepare for chem 132.

Easy to earn an A without learning much. Knowles would be passive aggressive at times telling everyone to shush. Spoke so quietly, no one could not hear her lecturing most days even with the microphone on. Matson, on the other hand, actually seemed interested on what she was teaching.
Bad professor. Bad lectures. Extremely easy class if you took AP Chemistry. Very low cut off for an A (you can fail every single exam and get an A if you do all the easy extra credit).

Literally does not explain anything, simply reads the slides, which are barely helpful anyway. Also gets so peeved about people lowkey just existing, like yeah one person is talking, why are you interrupting the whole class bc of it.

Genuinely just reads the information off of the slides and doesn't explain anything. The information on the slides isn't even really helpful.  Exams are generally difficult with no curve. She did let us do exam corrections this semester though.
Same as matson, knowles can be passive aggressive at times and not helpful, and I am just glad I am done with my cluster with this class, despite not learning a single drop of knowledge of chemistry.
Tests are hard but fair, expect tests to be math heavy but the study guides prepare you well.

This class back in freshmen year was completely underwhelming in my academic journey, and I don't think I learned a thing from my time thus spent in her class. Both knowles and matson don't care about actually teaching you, more so just speed running slides and then testing you. If extra credit wasn't a thing, I wouldn't have passed...

Knowles is thr goofiest, most profoundly silly professor that I've had the displeasure of being taught by. She is so slide heavy on complex topics that it doesn't surprise me that UoR is dropping ranks.
Can't lecture

1. The professor has limited teaching abilities, so it is necessary to attend office hours.
2. The course offers a lot of extra credit, so you can get an A without studying (although I think this is unreasonable).
3. A terrible learning experience, too many extra credit assignments fostered a negative attitude toward academics among students.

Not a huge fan of her lecturing style; it can be difficult to follow. Has a decent amount of office hours, which are very helpful. She's friendly and will walk you through problems step-by-step.

Same with Prof. Matson, tests are difficult but extra credit is plentiful. An A is possible even if you bomb every test.

Prof Knowles may genuinely be the worst teacher I have had in my life. She has no idea to teach complex topics, recognize that the class is lost, or even do example problems clearly! Plus she's sometimes rude in class or in office hours, not extremely so, but enough to be a little off-putting.

This class was honestly a very funny class hence the tag. Knowles read off the lecture slides nd that was it, not good at explaining content at all. There was this one time where she didnt know how to answer a question about chemistry on a certain topic and another student in lecture answered for her which was lowkey funny.

The only saving grace for this class is the amount of extra credit. Matson and Knowles assume students know everything and make the exam questions impossible to answer. You will learn NOTHING cause the extra credit will be the only thing keeping you afloat
not very good its not very good run run run its bad run the thermo is bad run

Very rude, and when asked questions in class responded more often than not in an unkind manner. I lost 50% of my points for incorrectly addressing a scientist ONCE in my paper on accident and lost more points after that on the rest of my work because she took it personally. Brings politics into the chemistry classroom which is unnecessary.

Doesn't take class seriously and sometimes in lecture she brings new concepts as if we already know them. I needed to do a lot of studying outside of class just because her lectures were a waste of time
I think Knowles' lectures are a bit more helpful than Matson's. Both professors are very accessible outside of class. There are a bunch of opportunities for extra credit.

Everyone says her lectures are bad but they're fine. She's really nice if you talk to her. Class is on points system + has lots of extra credit even if you don't do super well on exams, but EC is graded super harshly. Get points for going to class but lectures are recorded. Only took 2/3 exams and still didn't need to take the final to get an A.

Lots of the reviews are a bit harsh. I'll give a real review. Knowles is an okay professor. Not the best, but not as and as some of the other reviews. Knowles is probably at her best at thermo and worst at quantum mechanics. Other than teaching, Knowles is very nice and is patient with teaching (since Knowles teaches the harder concepts).

Dr. Knowles was at least a bit more consistent than Dr. Matson. Her lectures however were boring and super dense, and often it seemed like she was skipping over or assuming students understand the material. I appreciated that she didn't talk down to students like Dr. Matson did, but I feel like the quality of teaching was no better.

Honestly, not the best professor I have had. Her lectures are confusing and exam grades are really low. Her and matson teaching does not work at all. It feels like they are on two different planets. The topics are hard and go to class. Recitations will help you so much so GO TO THEM.

Knowles is the second chemistry professor that made me appreciate Dr. H more. She is not the most accommodating person and tends to speedrun her lectures. Exam grades were low because she and Matson cannot teach well and fails to give out sufficient exam practice exams to her students.

Knowles is very caring of her students. She sometimes included problems students had trouble doing. She is not very good at teaching though. Her lectures are fast paced and some of her test questions felt like they weren't representative of the content learned. Overall, I think she needs time to become a better professor.

This professor looks like she tries, but simply can not teach. You can definitely tell she has very little experience teaching the course. Lectures feel like eternity and the slides are not fun to look at.

i think she genuinely does care about her students, but she just is not good at teaching. i do get that this was her first year teaching. she kept assuming we knew foundational information to understanding concepts when we didn't. whenever someone would ask where she got this information from, she would say that we should just know how to do it.

Unlike the other 132 prof, she's actually a nice person and cares about you. However, this doesn't erase the fact that she is a terrible teacher. She speeds through slides, makes test questions so hard and long that no one finishes the exam, and doesn't know how to use a mic. She doesn't know how to do her own problems, but expects us to. Pray.

Super sweet and accommodating professor. I understand it was her first year teaching, which shows. She goes through complex lectures quickly and really likes calculus for some reason. I believe she could be a great teacher once she gets more familiarity to students. Tests were tough, but with the amount of extra credit, 132 should be an easy A.

Personally, I think Professor Knowles was the better of the two professors. She paces her lectures much better and spends a lot of time on practice problems. She was kind and accommodating. My only issues with her are the cluttered slides and lack of energy. It's clear she is not used to lecturing to such a large class. Overall, she's decent.

This year was her first year to teach, and it could be seen. She was very nervous and unconfident. She essentially just read off of her slides, which she posted on blackboard. I liked her a lot better than the other professor, because she was nice and very approachable. I loved her modules as they were more interesting to me. She talks very fast.

I left Dr. H's class thinking I'd have a better experience in CHEM 132. Let me tell you, that was a funny assumption... I was so wrong. The average for every exam was consistently below 50%, and that really shows how horrendous the class was. The only reason I survived this class was because of the extra credit. I don't recommend this class at all.

Someone needs to tell miss girl that flying through slideshows at 4523648768mph and assuming that your students just automatically understand everything isn't teaching. Though considering the overall poor quality of U of R's chem department, I guess the bar is pretty low.

If you are searching for this professor, I'm sure you came across Professor Robert Minckley before. One of his ratings was "I drove without a seatbelt and hoped I got into a crash on the way to campus." 
Compared to Professor Knowles, I Love professor Minckley. Knowles' lectures are so fast, It's almost like she assumes us to understand immediately
Mostly just horrifically boring.  Bring things to do in his class and drink caffeine!!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Rose was an awesome professor. She really genuinely cared about her students both as people and as writers. Homework and essays were very clear and class time was very helpful in understanding college writing. She gives personalized feedback that is very specific and really gets you thinking. Would 100% take her class again.
This class was incredibly easy as long as you did the work.  Prof. Manni is so sweet and funny in class and she genuinely wants her students to do well.

Professor Manni is really sweet and definitely cares about her students.  She is a very easy grader but makes you want to do well.  She does expect you to already know a lot and sometimes doesn't understand what you're confused about since she's a native speaker but will always try to help. She made herself very available and was overall wonderful.

She does blow off some grammar structures that she thinks you already know but if you ask her questions in lecture she will definitely answer them and go over something again or in a different way. She certainly cares about her students learning and tends to be flexible with deadlines.
very clear in class. provided good material for taking the exams.
He's pretty good.  Doesn't have patience with people wasting his time.

DMST 272 is the best course I've taken in the DMS Department by far. Everyone in the course has improved so much, and it's a testament to Nancy's teaching! It is definitely more work than DMST 171, so be prepared to spend some more hours each week working on your projects, especially if you've forgotten or are not familiar with Adobe software.

Nancy is amazing! If you're interested in learning graphic design from scratch, do not hesitate to take this course. She's super funny and very knowledgeable about the topic. If you need help, she and her TA are always open to giving you resources and feedback. Her class is not very lecture heavy, and you're given class time to work on projects.

Her passion for the topic shines through her lectures. You want to participate in class because she is so caring and energetic that it feels bad to sit and let class happen around you. A super relaxed and fun course, taught by someone with a genuine interest in making sure students get what they want out of it.
He's nice.
I was in his class two years ago, he's great at explaining new concepts, but you have to really focus on the lecture.
He's very helpful and offer extra office hour.
He showed lots of examples in the class, which is helpful for me to understand the concepts.
He literally cannot teach . Hell do the math hisself on the board and give his own un understandable explanation .
He's nice, knows lots of stuff and very helpful.
The instructor is good but this course is so difficult to me. His office hour helped me a lot.
This guy is smart and the lecture is amazing. One thing you need to be aware of is that the exam (especially the midterm) can be so hard but the grade is curved in the end.

For a creative writing class, I found Prof. Higley's in-class feedback to be consistently highly critical and disrespectful to students, noticeably impacting class morale. She seemed to struggle taking any feedback or feelings into consideration. She didn't add a content warning for assignments, even after being asked. Not professional or unbiased.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: She's tough and takes no disrespect from anyone, but she knows the material she teaches very well and gives interesting lectures. She cares how you are engaging with the material and wants to hear your thoughts. I found her to be kind and caring, but she also liked me. I saw her be... blunt with others. Regardless, she's a great teacher.

I can't stress enough, do NOT take a class with her! She's a bully! She talks down to her students, makes them think they're a bad writer, etc just bc she doesn't personally like their story. If you want to be publicly degraded and humiliated, take a class with her! If you value your self esteem, avoid her (she's not intelligent, just opinionated).

This professor is disrespectful. Don't take her classes. If it's a requirement, find another way to satisfy the requirement. She speaks down to students as if she's superior. Her mood will change in an instant. Assignments are vague and arbitrary. She grades harshly and punishes you if you share any ideas in your paper that she doesn't agree with.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! She is the worst professor I've ever had! She bullies her students, is rude, moody, cranky, and an overall terrible person! No matter how hard you work on your story, if she personally doesn't like it or agree with the ideas in it, she'll give you a terrible grade! She traumatized me and made me cry a lot. AVOID HER!

Dr. Higley's strict but I think she's fair. Her class is solid, but be careful. Put extra effort into your paper. Double-check your citations. You do NOT want to be on the receiving end of her sass. Also, you should probably email her if you're going to miss class.

Awful Professor. Will yell at you if you disagree with her in class. Gets really moody and cranky and is sometimes very insulting towards students if they don't agree with her. Overall bad experience. Wouldn't recommend.

The worst professor I have ever come across in life. She says she "sympathises with students with anxiety,.blah blah" but makes condescending and personal comments about your mental state when you go to her with your problem. I had the worst experience with her and would never want to see her again in my life let alone take a class with her.

Professor Higley is engaging and is clearly passionate about the materials taught in the class. The only thing I disliked was the way that she acted towards students, as she can sometimes be very moody and impatient with them. All in all, a very good course. I would take a class with her again just for her outstanding abilities in teaching.

She reminds me of a nice version of Meryl Streep's character in The Devil Wears Prada. She's smart, funny, and passionate about the subjects she teaches. I think some people get intimidated by her (she's sometimes a lil'bit moody, who isn't?) but if you think she's being "mean" or "rude"... you might be taking things a little too personally!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Kind of flyaway and disorganized, but engaging and passionate about the material. Wants you to think, not regurgitate or give her what you think she wants. Values communication, very understanding, gives you slack when you need it as long as you've demonstrated that you care about the class.

Amazing professor. Doesn't speak down to students, expects actual scholarship (GASP), and is genuinely concerned about each of her students as individuals. It's ridiculous to me that so many complain that she has actual expectations of them. I suspect their parents are paying, and always will be. Show up. Behave like an adult. Be a scholar.
Higley is the abject fecundity in the best way

Higley is funny and amusing, but she is also very insulting. In both of my papers she would write rude demeaning comments. I disagreed with her once in class and since that point she has consistently called my points "wrong" no matter what I argue. Her essay prompts are extremely vague. Get a different teacher.

Really enjoyed the classes I've taken with her. She is funny, passionate, eccentric, and awesome! If you tire of boring, stick-in-the-mud professors, definitely take a class with her. She can be intense, but only if you didn't do your homework, participate, or were late. If you're responsible and take college seriously, you are good.

i would suggest not taking a creative writing course with her.  very awkward to hear her call out people for 'mistakes' when the class is about CREATIVE WRITING.  comments were very disrespectful sometimes- its called CONSTRUCTIVE criticism jeez
She is a wonderful professor. Passionate, fun, knowledgeable, and her classes are creative, as she is open to suggestions of all kind.

lots of material but altogether eye-opening class.  higley's a brilliant woman with an unique personality.  get involved in class discussions.  don't come to class late.  she can be moody at times so best to learn sooner than later how to navigate that - it could be hard to recover from a bad encounter or even a moment of memorable disagreement

She is a very enthusiastic and knowledgable professor, and clearly a nice person.  However, she is very fervent about gender issues.  You don't come to it until the end of the semester, but she definitely holds a some sort of grudges.

Very good professor. Bring a "Get tough or die" approach to her courses - i.e. don't come late or unprepared, don't b.s. her, get involved in the discussions, and defend your ideas. In my class, the people who disliked her were the ones trying to just coast through the class. Then, of course, they'd accuse her of favortism. Whatever, dudes.
She's a good professor, very cooky. However, I truly believe she hates males.

Sarah Higley is one of the best professors you will ever meet. Yes, she plays favorites, but if you work hard, you won't get shafted.   She is so funny, it is not unheard of to leave class with aching sides. I miss her lots.

Although Higley is an extremely intelligent professor, it seems like she allows her personal life to interfere with her emotions often. For instance, one day she broke down crying for some reason, and wouldn't explain why. This was in addition to her regular eccentrism, which is somewhat tolerable. You also cannot show up late or even have a cold in class (I'm not joking), because it "disturbs the class". Workload: medium - heavy.

Okay prof, she's knowledgeable and you will learn something from her course.  She is engaging enough as a lecturer but plays favorites.  She is given to dramatics, and is rather childish about discussing sex, with a lot of giggling.  I didn't dislike her class but I did dislike the favoritism.
be careful of her bite, but don't let it intimidate you.
good teacher, but could improve by having clearer objectives, is set in her ways
No Comments
