But he'll make a big stink if you walk in two minutes late because it's a "reflection of your character". Kinda insufferable and the work is hard.

Slow grader, slow responses to emails (will not respond to emails sometimes), and does not upload lecture materials. Programming project writeups are confusing and the tools you have to use for them are difficult to work with. Can be condescending and full of himself at times. Would've gotten more out of an online course if I'm being honest.
This class was incredibly well-taught, I almost forgot I took this class!

Professor Criswell's CSC252 is an exemplary showcase on teaching with passion. His lectures are filled with fun moments and performance arts, alone with energy that can only be found in hospitals. The lecture is very informative and usually require a whole page of post-it note for every lecture to fit in all the information taught.

This course by professor criswell was an amazing example of why all CS researchers aren't fitted to teach. In this inspirational course, I have accumulated knowledge that can be distilled onto a single 8x11 standard printing paper. His lectures have never failed me, if sleeping in his class was my goal.

Took CSC 252; this is one of the best professors I've met. He has clear grading criteria and words he uses are exquisitely labyrinth; the quizzes are well phrased and weighted reasonably where one question on the quiz is only worth single digits of your total grade. He gives timely feedback; homework is graded usually within 5 to 7 business weeks.

I was in Prof. Criswell's class for both CSC278 and CSC256(not currently available in the course selection field). Prof. Criswell is one of the best I have had the pleasure of learning from. His lectures are great. He explains all the concepts in a way that is fun and very easy to understand. Plus, he is always willing to provide guidance.

Prof. Criswell is condescending and disrespectful. He doesn't have the students best interest in mind and frequently brags about how he gets to do things (like be forgetful, not respond to your emails, not show up for office hours) because he is a "professor". You need ask the TAs for coding question (he doesn't know much about Linux internals).
Grades late, not receptive to feedback. Doesn't post lecture slides. Course is uninteresting.
Ms. Kiggins is "cool", "calm" and "collected" and she certainly brings a breadth of practical experience and expertise.
the first prof that impressed me profoundly

He is my favorite math prof at u of r. He laid the foundation of my mathematical mindset that benefited my later math-related studies. As a first semester freshman class in the university, it was a hard transition from high school math to proof heavy analysis but he helped me make it interesting and worthwhile. I cannot thank him more
Professor Haessig gives very well-organized lectures and is willing to answer students' questions.

He is very smart, gentle, polite, nice, organized and patient:) He teaches u how to think and his class is full of logics. I think all the students in our class love him!!! Because of him, I decide to change my major into math. Never need to be afraid to ask why and expression my confusion, feel very comfortable to learn math with this professor><.
Very nice professor. I'm considering going to math graduate school after taking his course.
My best decision at this school was to take this class. The lectures are clear and well paced, the content is extremely interesting, and the grading is very fair.
Really good professor. The class was fun and you actually get to learn. The book is really useful too.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: The professor often starts class with a good story related to the matter. He jumps into teaching soon enough, and may be fast on some topics, depending on the student. Don't skip class, because you can find yourself lost in the next lecture. And don't expect to read the online notes; the notes on the projector are close to illegible.

He is really helpful. He explains things patiently and clearly in his office hours. He doesn't give an easy curve though. A lot of students got pretty bad grades in this class. Overall, he is definitely one of the better professors in math department.
Great professor. He really did a great job at teaching the material. He made sure that students understood what he was talking about and he prepared us well for the midterm. Great guy too.

Definitely the professor to take!  He is a math genius who is super approachable and nice and who genuinely cares.  Even the following semester he remembered me and asked how I was doing.  If you don't understand something he is always there to help, and his problem examples are perfect for studying for the exams.  Take him!

Prof. Haessig was a very good professor. At times he seemed a bit unorganized, but it's clear that he knows what he's talking about. He also does a very good job of explaining why things are a certain way and relates to students well. The class isn't super-easy, but it's very manageable. All in all, Haessig is a good choice for a Calc professor.

You quickly realize how smart he truly is. He genuinely cares and wants you to understand the WHY behind math. I actually enjoyed coming to this class although math isn't my favorite subject because he's such a great lecturer.

He is really nice and always is there to help the students. If you have any questions be sure to ask him or just go meet him during office hours. And if you have the slightest interest in majoring in maths or joining research, he is probably the most helpful person around.

Haessig is a nice guy, sort of awkward, but in a good, funny way. Lectures aren't super exciting, but he does a good job of preparing notes that are helpful.  If you go to his office hours he's great.  Exams aren't bad at all if you go to class and do the homework. He really wants his students to do well, and is very willing to help

I love this man. Everything he does makes me laugh, and I was always disappointed when lecture was over. Very clear instruction, the notes I was taking were so useful I felt like I was back in high school. :)

Prof Haessig is a wonderful math prof- and I wish we had more like him at this school. He covers every topic at a good pace, makes sure we understand it, and is very approachable. He always has fun jokes and is always smiling. He genuinely cares about his students and is, over all, a great guy. I am very glad he was hired for a professorship at UR.
This class alone was very difficult, but he in no way made it easier. the only reason i would go to class is because he is hot.

The class was mind-boggling hard.  It was all proof-based, so it sucks for all math minors and majors.  The prof likes to talk to himself during class and then makes crazy exclamations that make no sense, especially if you could not hear what he was mumbling about.
Great professor. Explains concepts very clearly and is extremely helpful. MTH 162Q is a hard class, but grading was very fair. Highly recommended.

One of the top 3 professors I have had in college.  I've had him for 282 and 233, and his lecture notes are flawless.  He really cares about his students and loves what he does.  He even took time out of his busy schedule to have an independent study seminar...please stay at UR Doug!
Good Lectures, feed back, character. Tests are hard, but appropriate curves.

Great teacher. So many teachers at UR are either smart but can't teach or are nice teachers but don't know their stuff. But Haessig is the perfect balance of the two. He's really smart, but still great at explaining difficult subjects. He's very fair when it comes to grading, and he makes class enjoyable with his enthusiasm and sense of humor.

Best teacher I've had at UR (MTH 141+142) He is approachable, friendly, and can make sense out of anything. EXTREMELY helpful; this guy would stay past dark in his office helping me with problems. The class material can be a little tough, just stay on top of WebWork and you will be fine. The tests are almost verbatim from WebWork so do it.
Haessig really wants everyone in the class to learn. He is extremely helpful especially with homework questions. He also will let you turn in homework late and redo your homework if you ask him.

Had Doug for 141 and 142. If you took calc in high school, dont bother going to lecture.  Just do the webwork.  Doug will help you if you have questions, or just go to recitation.  Exams are easy if you've kept up with webwork.  Doug seemed like a good prof, but I didnt go to class much.  From what I hear, the other 141 professors are terrible.
He's a pretty nice guy who honestly wants to teach you the material.

He looks like the dude from scooby doo. (lol) Well he was prolly the best math professor i had at uci. He is clear and concise unlike all the asain math teachers at uci. His tests are straight forward and you should ace his class if you go to lecture.

Professor Jessica Robinson, does not give good feedback. Her feedback's are mostly a comment " I agree" in response to the peer feedback a student gives on the paper. Moreover, if you go to her office hours for feedback, She says no to give any feedback and says if I give you feedback, I will have to do that for all students. She is not helpful.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Not approachable and biased grader
Interesting class, very reasonable professor who's invested in your learning.

Professor is clearly invested in his students. Approachable for sure and gives amazing feedback. In class, he always seems to brighten the mood with his teaching style and takes the questions of his students seriously. I definitely improved on my writing skills after taking the course. Awesome professor.

He really cares about phil and students - he went out of his way to meet with me in the evenings bc of my busy schedule to make sure I understood concepts. He also helped me with another phil class b/c I was struggling. Lectures are long but philosophy isn't exciting stuff - puts in more effort than any other PhD I know - worthwhile class!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Clearly cares about students. Lectures can get dry and long.

Classes are absolutely useless and extremely boring. Readings are boring and terribly useless, too. Gives good feedback and is a pretty (I'd say overly) cooperative guy with deadlines. Just skip classes when you can (cause participation is part of the grade) and don't waste your time on readings, they don't matter at all for anything.

Professor Rowley is a really good guy The class is boring and very dry, again it's not hard or impossible but Ethics at the Edges of Life is a very dry class, but he's a great guy and it's good he's teaching it. I can say I definitely became a more purposeful writer after taking him. He gives great feedback on your papers so you can correct them
Great professor. He tends to ramble on a bit though. He gives great feedback on papers and is clear about what he wants. Interesting topics as well.
Great professor. Hard class, but interesting

I love Julie! She's such a nice professor and this course is also pretty interesting. And we got chance to sing with those amazing chamber singers which is so cool!!! I will definitely take it again next semester and probably for every semesters in the future. Grade is based on attendance and two concerts only, so come and have fun!

She is such a nice woman, and she is very understanding. She never asks too much of students, and she's very chill all the time. If you like singing and want to relax, join. It is a nice thing to do once a week, and it's not very taxing, mentally.

Professor Otis is great. He was my favorite professor freshman year. Very kind and respectful, and lets you know what he wants. Very approachable, and great at writing. The work load Is very doable and light. If you're going to take a writing class, take his! GOAT

Good guy. If you want an easy intro to ethics, this class was fine, but it was honestly too easy. I don't feel like I walked away with much. If you're really interested in philosophy, other classes are likely a better use of your time. However discussions among the students on their ideas were always interesting, and I liked his use of class polls.

Professor Otis is very nice and has good and interesting lectures. He also gives feedback on the quizzes and final paper before you turn in your work to help you get an A. Highly recommend his class to any students looking to gain a basic understanding of philosophy and ethics.

Man Machine and Morality is a great writing class, not too much work and Otis gives genuinely good feedback and can provide more if you ask. The structure of the class is writing focused so you don't learn too much the second half of the semester outside your own research but it serves as a basic philosophy intro. Otis makes things clear and easy!

he is a little bit lazy and sometimes slacks off
but i promise there's no easier way than taking his class to get A and 4 credit, just submit every assignment then you got it

Professor Otis is a nice guy who will give you great feedback when you need it. If you follow the directions and put in reasonable effort you're almost guaranteed an A. If you're struggling to choose a Writing 105 class and you want an A, Otis is the best pick. He'll almost always give you an extension if you ask.

Clear grader on writing, and very good at providing feedback outside of class, and a fun professor to talk to. He makes it easy to succeed if you put in the work (which isn't much compared to the other writing profs.)
BEST Writing Professor!!

Man, Machine, and Morality is probably one of the easier WRTG 105 courses. Very little reading outside of class, and the only big assignments are the short essay and final research essay that all the other 105 courses have. He also gives good feedback on drafts, so it's very easy to get an A in his class.

Man, Machine, Mortality was the easiest class ever. As long as you come to most classes and try the slightest bit you will get an A. If you are looking to genuinely learn then this not the class for you, however, if like many you are just trying to fulfill WRTG105, this is the best class.

100000% recommend taking his writhing class. It is not hard and it really helps you develop as a better writer. He is understanding and really cares about the topic. He drops 2 of your lowest informal assessment grades and grades a lot of things based off effort. I learned a lot about the ethics of AI in this class and would love to take another.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: super chill professor, is willing to give extensions if you just ask and tell the truth, topics revolve around ai and morality, you're graded on some in class informal assignments (3-6 pts), a short essay (100 pts), and the 8 to 10 page research paper (you will not pass if you dont turn it in). miss 1 informal assignment, it wont hurt your grade

Super nice guy, and very willing to give extensions. The essay criteria was super clear and the assignments were easy enough to do. My only gripe with him was just that he didn't give a lot of assignments so if you got a few points off a formal assignment it kind of did a bit of damage.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Professor Otis is great. He has clear guidelines on his papers and understands that most people going through his class aren't English Majors. He is very accommodating and gives great feedback on papers. He also lectures well and gives good advice on how to approach argumentative essays.

Man, Machine, and Morality turned out to be way more interesting than I thought. James is very engaging and knowledgeable on the topics discussed in class. He is also very empathetic with students and understands our busy schedules. He is incredibly kind and truly wants you to succeed. Take his advice carefully and you will be more than fine.
Such a great professor. Easy A if you attend every class and complete the project on time.
Would like to take this professor's class again

he is a great professor. i am a stem person but i found his class very interesting. flexible teaching style, go with the flow guy. no final, just 3 short essays. does miss class sometimes but usually gives enough notice. you're able to submit your own topics to talk about. no hw, some in-class assignments.

Somewhat reading heavy at the start of the semester, but once we got into the writing portion not so much. Less writing assignments compared to what other WRTG 105 classes had, and he is a pretty fair grader, and can be lenient with deadlines if you ask.

Easy to follow lectures and lenient grader. Majority of assignments are graded by completion, including part of the grade for the final research paper. Half the classes at the end of the year are just doing your work in class, which should be optional to attend, but he randomly check for attendance. Easy A if you do the work.
He is very sympathetic with students. We had good discussion in the class. Grading is not hard at all!

I took "Man, Machine, and Morality" and it was a super fun class. His lectures are short and sweet and encourage class participation, and he gives plenty of time to work in class so there's not too much work to do outside. If you want to write about something a little different from the prompt he's, laid back about it as long as you do it well.

Really good professor. Makes it clear exactly what he wants in the papers and is very easily accessible outside of class. He understands that writing isn't everyone's strong suit so he gives plenty of time in class to complete assignments. Often makes attending class optional.
Good
Good professor, cares a lot about the material, and makes it challenging but fair. If you really commit to this class, you'll learn a lot. You get out of it what you put in.

Professor Oakes is a bad professor. He simply derives equations in class, and then quickly and poorly goes over examples. He does not explain concepts well, nor does he really teach understanding. Like said by others, his tests are not similar to the hw. The only reason I got an A is because I took AP Physics. Do NOT take his class, take self-paced
Do not take this professor' class!!! You will learn nothing because you could not understand anything.

All he does in class is derive equations. His exams are nothing like the homework or workshops, which he claims to base them off of. Overall, not a good professor, but is very knowledgeable as a researcher.  He curves this intro class to a C. Those who do well seem to have taken the course before. Good luck to you if you have this professor.

He is a great teacher! He has a presentation for each lecture. The way his test work is that he makes it really hard so that the average is around a 55% however he curves the median to a 75 so usually curves are +20 points. He is understanding when it comes to mistakes on a test. Great professor. Dont trust the last review.
Tough for people who aren't familiar with his teaching style.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Rebecca is an amazing writing teacher. I feel so much more confident in graduate school after taking her class!

This instructor is nitpicky. She looks for spaces, periods missing or inadvertently present in the APA format, claims that citations are missing when they are there, gives written directions that change when grading. Weekly APA quizzes, assigned reading from an APA MANUAL. A five page paper with at least 3 revisions, all for a ONE CREDIT COURSE.

Prof Tzeferacos clearly cares about his students and about teaching - he always answers questions in class and will meet with you to go over stuff you don't understand. However.. his lectures are a mess if you're in the class to learn. He goes over super complicated examples but doesn't really teach you the basic concepts. It's unfortunate.

Maybe he saw the reviews and changed things cz i don't get why people are complaining. Content is hard but it's easy to get an A, I barely studied. Lectures might go off into unnecessary integrals sometimes but I don't think he was bad at explaining things. Kind person, clearly cares for his students, wants feedback, curved the final!!

Easily the worst class I have taken at the U of R. E&M isn't easy to begin with and he absolutely does not make it easier. Thank whatever you believe in that lab and workshop count as a notable part of your grade. He seems like a genuienely nice person that does care lots for his students though. It's unfortunate that the lectures are not helpful.

To the rising sophomore at U of R who needs to take 122, do not fear. Do not fall for the horror stories. I don't think Petros is the best lecturer I've ever had but he curves so generously and genuinely cares about us students. Read the textbook, try on the homework, and you will be completely fine.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: He is trying to make this course better and it shows. He provides in class review sessions before a midterm, and the class averages on exams have been around a B+ or A-, the semester I took the course. If you just try in the class, you will pass. The office hours are helpful, and if you did poorly on an exam you can still bounce back.

Physic 2 is really hard, but he does not make it easier. Really nice guy that cares about the students, but he lectures are a waste of time and he never explains the concepts of what we are learning. He cares more about making crazy integrals on problems. But you can get awful test scores and still get a passing grade.

This course is hard, but he doesn't make it any easier. Lectures are rushed and he opts to go through complicated problems instead of teaching the concepts needed to understand them. Reading the textbook and seeing a tutor is far more beneficial. The TAs are wildly inconsistent with their grading, so HW grades largely boil down to who your TA is.

Worst class I've taken at UofR. Had to watch Youtube videos and read the textbook to learn this course. Lectures make the course seem more complicated then it should be. He is obsessed with academic dishonesty. He posts fake answers on Chegg and will edit old HW answer keys and make them wrong in order to catch people for academic dishonesty.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Nice guy but awful incomprehensible lectures done quickly on slides
Grade class

The professor is excellent; his personal qualities are understanding and helpful. This professor does not have much to do with pedagogy and researcher than a professor. Lectures are complex and incomprehensible.Students stopped attending lectures after the second exam, and there was no class activity, hence the lack of motivation to attend lectures

He clearly cares deeply about the students and is a nice guy, but lectures are difficult to follow, confusing, and not super well organized. After the first month or so we were at about 40% lecture attendance and it gradually declined from there. Get a good study group, get ready to read the textbook and watch videos.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Lectures are pointless, you will not learn anything from them, he rambles through PowerPoint slides, going over complex integrals and theory as opposed to the actual inner workings of E and M and focusing on genuine understanding. Read the textbook.

Professor's lectures are a bit convoluted and winding, but he is super kind and willing to help. Homeworks are killer, but the tests not so much. Class structure, with the workshops and all, is very helpful.

Professor Tzeferacos is a very nice man and is very accessible to students. This class is the hardest I have taken at the U of R. The material is very difficult and the workshops are long and treacherous. With that being said there are ample opportunities to get an A in this class with several point opportunities.
He is a fantastic professor. The course is really hard; however, there are a lot of ways to get the final grade higher.

His lectures sometimes were a little unclear, but he clearly wants you to succeed and there are many ways to boost your grade (HW, labs, extra credit) in the class outside of exams. Workshops are helpful, so make sure to attend them.

He is the worst Professor I have ever had at this school. He teaches the material poorly and tests on concepts that are not made apparent in the practice exam. The midterms make zero sense, and he truly sets you up to fail.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Dont even bother going to his lectures, it is totally useless. Practice exams totally irrelevant with wrong answer key. Doesn't post all information for exams (hw/workshop solutions etc)

He clearly knows the material well and is passionate about it. His lectures can be a bit confusing as there is a lot of information on them, but they help a lot for the homework as some questions are exactly the same. The TA's can be a hit or a miss, luckily I had a good TA which really helped with my understanding. If not, read the textbook!!!

Avoid if you can, if not it'll be okay. He grades nicely (85 is an A), but learning anything from his lectures is impossible. Also, the TAs are very rough. E&M is a hard class. Completely learned this course from the textbook which is good, so recommend renting/buying that.
Do not write. Most of the explanations are done through slides (maybe because of the online classes, it's 2020). Not very engaging but is flexible on gradings.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: A lot of homework, I hate engineering process procedure, that's a waste of time for easy questions that you don't even need to think about the steps and you can solve that with 1 simple formula used. The professor is good btw.
Kind of weird grading scale, but great professor. Homework quizzes are easy if you did the homework.

Dr. Brown is super helpful and cares for his students! Unfortunately, the class is very difficult. There is a ton of homework, and some weeks I had up to 10 hours. The homework is a very good reflection of the tests, though! The lectures are sometimes helpful, other times not. Lastly, I S/F grading and got S.

Writing 10 pages of homework that requires reading 20 pages to do, 2 hard midterms, no past exams, final as a group presentation project, grade ranking instead of grade curve, all means this is an extremely hard 101 course. But Dr Brown is not a bad professor by any means, and an A is possible if you put more time after lecture than your peers.

All around great professor. Really good at what he does, and his passion for biomedical engineering really rubs off on his students. He is the only professor that teachers BME101 so first-year BME students do not have a choice but to have him, but he is such an awesome teacher that I would not have it any other way.
He is a nice person, though the assignments are a lot and he really cares about the sig fig. Also, the criteria are vague so you won't get detailed feedback on your final grade.

Great Professor, take the time to do the homework and attend office hours. Go the extra mile to make sure all instructions are followed (i.e. pay attention to sig figs/boxing answers/etc.) ASK QUESTIONS IN CLASS!! Dr. Brown responds to emails so don't be afraid to reach out.

Dr. Brown is a great professor and a great person. I really enjoyed this class. If you want to succeed in this class, GO TO OFFICE HOURS! There is homework every week graded on accuracy. Its a tough class and you need to put in the work
love him but also hate him. You will never know your grade until the last moment

A lot of people struggle with BME101 and here's why: nobody expects that it will be hard so people go in thinking they can barely study and be fine. The average for the first exam was 35/78. The exam time is just 50 minutes, so don't expect to finish, it's okay. The average of the class is weighted to a B-, so just hope you are above the average.

Clearly passionate about the subject, but not great at explaining topics. Makes the course frustrating if you haven't taken physics courses before. He instructed the TAs to grade more harshly midway through the semester because he wanted a "wider spread of grades". Overall felt like a weeder course for BME students. Interesting material though.

Dr. Brown was very understanding and always willing to help his students. The class is tough but if you put in the work and use the TAs office hours, you will be ok. Put a lot of effort into the homeworks because they are worth a lot. Brown is a funny guy and his class is enjoyable too.

Not an easy A, probably because this is not an easy major. Professor Brown is so funny and gets the material across, but ultimately it is up to you to do well. The readings are helpful to do before class and a lot of material comes from them. I had fun though and would definitely take him again.

Focuses in class on the math parts of the class, but you need to read BOTH textbooks for the homeworks and labs. Homeworks are pretty hard and the TAs are useless, but the prof is great. Charismatic and you can tell he genuinely cares about what he's teaching. If you can, get on his good side and get a letter of recommendation from him.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: The tests in this class are brutal. Nothing like the practice ones that are posted. They are also in class so you have very little time to finish. He's a nice guy and an interesting lecturer, but this is a very hard class. There's a reason lots of BME students switch majors.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Dr. Brown's BME 101 is a very physics heavy course. Homework is heavy but managable with good planning. Put effort into the HW because it prepares you very well for the exams. THE EXAMS ARE TIME INTENSIVE, RUSH THROUGH THE QUESTIONS AS FAST AS POSSIBLE. You are not expected to finish every question, get as many points as fast as you possibly can.

Dr. Brown, who most BME students will take for BME 101, is an absolute gem of the university. I strongly recommend that you take his Biomedical Microscopy course, BME 270. He takes the class seriously, because it is his passion, and that passion bleeds through every lecture and activity he prepares for the class. Take this course.

Dr Brown is the most energetic teddy bear. He makes any topic fun and interesting because he is clearly so passionate. He is a bit all over the place so it is hard to know what to expect from homeworks and tests, but you will understand the concepts.

The intro to neuro class is a good introduction to neuroscience at UR. His class is fair, but hard, and the tests are easy if you study hard enough and listen to lectures. Bring a recorder, his slides are only pictures.
He is very nice, but his class is very hard
He leaves no holes in his explanations, he is my favorite neuroscience professor at the University of Rochester
good lecturer, knows the subject really well

He's an exceptional lecturer: while he's not funny nor animated, he is very clear, organized, and genuinely interesting. Be sure to bring a recorder, as the slides only have pictures. The class is challenging, but the practice exams help a lot. If you're interested in neuro, you'll probably enjoy his lectures. NSC249 is much better than NSC201 IMO

Nordeen (the man...he also has a wife who teaches) is a very organized lecturer and clear on the material. He is, however, kind of boring. Slides are useless unless you have the lectures recorded (the ppt's are only pictures, no words).
slides fairly useless for studying but pretty good lectures

I thought he did an alright job.  He is always there to meet with you in office hours if you need it.  The tests are not hard if you do the back ones.  He is kind of boring and not excited about the material.  But overall not bad

Instead of worrying about fluffing up his vocabulary in lectures, he should turn his attention how he treats students.  The intro neiro class is used by him to pick out the brightest students to work in his lab.  He told me getting my masters in Neuroscience would be a waste of my time.  The favortism is sickening.
No Comments

Prof. Nordeen didn't care the least bit about the fact that I couldn't write a paper because my mother was sick with cancer and eventually died later that year.  There is another student I know who had a similar situation and he didn't care there either.

Horrible lecturer, simply just read his slides. Somewhat responsive to his emails, but doesn't work efficiently. Unclear about what he wants in homework/projects/exams. Your codes could execute all the things he asked in question but still would deduct points because you didn't do it the way "he expected".
Professor Schwarz is a good professor with passion; I would definitely work with him again if I have a chance to become a TA.

This course is honestly the most speechless course I took as a BME student. He assumes everyone has a good foundation in coding and starts giving extremely hard midterms. We don't even know what exactly are his expectations for a good presentation. Also, the final is like a pain in the ass. He just likes to see his student suffer from tons of tasks

tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Ok, the course itself, fine, the labs especially were helpful. Lectures on the other hand, not very helpful. I went to most of them until the end and honestly I did better on my own versus going to lecture. The project at the end was a nice topic but good luck trying to get a group to work well together. At least he responds to emails?

Let me preface this by saying that this course is NOT beginner friendly. Do NOT go to lecture. He says the same things on the slides (better off on your own). Comments are very important in your code so don't skimp on it. His attitude in class is very monotone and not engaging. He will give you pretty much no help on the project at the end. GL!

The professor only reads off what is on his slides word for word and does not explain much after that. The textbook is optional and you need to do practice outside of class for the midterms. He does demonstrations, but most of the hand-on coding will come from the labs and the TAs.
Very easy class, don't actually have to do the readings for class, BUT you do have do do them to write the two papers required. If you actually attend, she's a good professor and you'll learn a lot.

Bigelow seems like a nice guy, but he is near-unintelligibly quiet in lecture, doesn't respond to email, and generally explains topics very poorly. Even if you learn from the textbook, there are certain things you will be tested on that he does not give outside resources for. He will also not give you an preparation for what will be on exams!

Aside from not posting a syllabus (he announces everything each lecture). He is a very straightforward professor and incredible lecturer. He not only introduces basic quantum, but prepares students with more advanced topics such as Entanglement and Dirac notation. Contacting him takes time, so don't be afraid to talk him about meetings after class.

He has short lectures and while they do have examples they can be a little too much theory. He can be hard to reach outside of class and tended to post homework late and not actually do the weekly quizzes
Easy to get an A in his class and he is a good researcher, yet he is really bad at teaching.

Did not attend more than 5 lectures for the entire semester. Prof Bigelow is a very nice guy and cares a lot but his lectures are not useful at all. He presents the slides and then reads and explains them. There is no working through long problems in class. Workshops are a complete waste of 3 hours. Class material is not bad if u r in engineering.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: His grading is very inconsistent, as he says he will have quizzes every week but at the end of the semester we've only had 2
Learned a little, but mostly was frustrated by group assignments and professors style. He definitely likes the sound of his own voice and has a large ego. This class is required.

I think of all the stem professors I've taken in this school, Professor Bigelow ranks in the top 5. His physics 113 was not graded on a curve but he didn't need to. His expectations were clear on what to do to ace the class in terms of number of points needed to earn for certain grades and was available outside class for help!
Possibly the nicest human ever. I had to take Physics and I am terrible at it. He was super helpful, caring, and patient. If you have a class with him, you are lucky!
Incredibly knowledgeable, helpful, and all-around friendly nice guy.  Take a class with him if you possibly can.
No Comments
A difficult course (but then quantum always is), but an EXCELLENT teacher and a great all-around guy.  Very busy, though, so be sure to *schedule* office-hours & other appointments.

She is, although a confusing lecturer at times, good at clarifying what she means, and very accessible. Her exams are also very fair, and if a question is missed by a majority of the class, she will often remove it from grade calculations.

Make sure to attend lectures and learn from the lecture slides. Tests were pretty okay. She's a very sweet professor and tries to give extra credit opportunities to boost your grade. She often goes overtime during her lectures though. Try to find a good studying/note-taking method for this class.

Took her Bio 112 this year and her lecture style is not for the weak. If you are coming in wondering if you should use your AP credit and take this class and you are on the fence about your decision, I recommend you don't take this class. She is a very sweet person, but her lectures get super off topic and she hardly finishes her slides on time.

Her lectures are all over the place and she seldom finishes her slides in time. She's a really sweet person though, and her tests are very fair. There's a lot of material per exam and no cheat sheet but overall it was manageable. She's very open about grading and gives opportunities to boost your grade.

Took her 112 and attended all lectures. Usually easy to understand but can occasionally get off track. A good but not great lecturer. Her lectures on mechanisms (DNA replication, translation, etc.) are the most comprehensible. Guest lecturers are usually a tad better but can be worse. Overall a good professor, and an incredibly sweet person.

Really sweet professor that will help you if you put in the work to understand class material. Slides don't have much text, so you really need to understand the concepts. Make sure to sit in the front and record lectures if possible. Overall, just make sure you are making a faithful effort.

Very memorization heavy exams but nothing difficult. Lectures are not recorded so you should go even if it's not factored in grade. Strongly recc. flash cards & study guides before each exam especially to keep up w/ all the terminology

Lock in and you'll be fine. She DOES NOT RECORD LECTURES! The information in lecture is overwhelming and excessive relative to what is tested on, but it's interesting and she's clear about what will be asked about (you'll catch on eventually). Exams are not that bad, and she's very much willing to work with you to set you up for success!

If you go to lecture and put in the work outside of class, you will be fine. The entirety of the grade you receive will be focused on how well you do on the 3 exams. Overall, it is a tough course, but not impossible. Mary is willing to help you out if you need clarification. USE OFFICE HOURS.

The most unorganized professor I've ever had. The first test was impossible, and nobody finished because she made it twice as long as it should've been. Her lectures consist of her stating random facts that nobody understands. There are no words on her slides, just hundreds of slides with pictures. Class isn't recorded so attendance is a must.

The rating seems low because he teaches a lot of intro courses and people don't like coding. As a CS student who has taken several courses with him, he is a very knowledgeable, intelligent, and helpful prof.

Honestly, people don't appreciate the effort that Ted put into organizing this course. The materials are actually very clear, the textbook is easy to follow, and the labs have straightforward instructions. The structure is THERE, you just have to keep up.

Most boring lectures of all time, expect to have to force yourself to go to them. Instructions on labs can be confusing. Expect to learn most of the material independently. If there's another professor you could choose instead of Pawlicki, I recommend choosing them instead.

Pretty chill guy! Gave extra credit on the last day of class just for showing up. His exams are on the tougher side fyi. 5 homeworks/projects, 2 midterms, 1 final. Homeworks weren't that hard, exams are tricky. The material is difficult to begin with so all in all i had a good experience.
His lecture is confusing and unorganized, hw interaction not clear, would not take with him again

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Exams were difficult!!! 5 homeworks in the class aka cs projects. Professor Pawlicki is not the best at lecturing but at this point in my cs journey it doesnt make a huge difference in my learning. He uses his exam questions out of the textbook so there will be some reading. Overall i had a good experience.

His lecture is a disaster and a total waste of time. PPT makes no sense. If you wanna really learn something, you can just google CS 188 Berkley and watch their recorded lecture. Not recommend going to his lecture.
I fw him heavy
The exams in this class are very bad. They ask you a bunch of random obscure questions about the textbook like its trivia night.

I would say the course was difficult but not that bad. Lectures are not top-notch but taught with passion. Be prepared for really heavy readings before exams and even if you do so, don't expect to receive a decent exam grade. Fortunately the curve was pretty good.

It is beyond me that UofR still lets this man teach this class. Horrible lecturer, never lectured on anything that was helpful for our projects. The projects would have extremely confusing instructions and often would be straight up wrong. The only good thing about this class was how easy it was graded.

Poorly run class. Few attend lectures which are hardly useful to either test or understanding. Slides taken for granted from UCB CS188, HW from former lecturers w/t changing their names. Tested subjectively on part of irrelevant AND untaught materials on books. Vague instruction on exam preps. TAs are the good. Get ready for self-study.

Prof. Pawlicki is a disorganized lecturer, often switching topics without clearly explaining any one thing. He assigns tests such that you are required to do them on weekends. He is curt at best and snappy at worst if you go to talk to him outside of class. Though lab assignments are helpful, the instructions are often poorly written and confusing.

I believe Prof. Ted Pawlicki is an excellent professor. The negative comments he is receiving likely stem from his willingness to express his views openly. He is highly experienced and has a strong command of his subject matter.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: DSA is supposed to be hard but to be honest, I actually learned stuff because of him. Not because he taught well, but because I had to teach myself. If you just need the credit, take this class, go to workshop and watch Abdul Bari and you are good to go lol.
Fake Professor
True Professor!!! Lectures are told to be bad but they are actually helpful! The test weren't hard at all!! Projects are also easy!!! True Professor!!!!!
Decent professor, lectures could be dry but class was easy overall. Lots of extra credit to boost grades. Unstuck Study AI was a big help for exam prep.

While a mediocre CS Professor at any other university, he is one of the few alright CS professors here at UofR. His classes are brain numbingly easy, but there is usually A LOT of busy work within these classes, and almost no real application of skills into projects besides a couple classes here and there.
Very weird guy, seems disorganized and often has unclear instructions for assignments and weird/pointless assignments.

I haven't even finished this class and he is by far my least favorite professor at the university. His profiles shows a trump 2020 shirt that he's wearing which tells you a lot. His teaching style in unclear, his projects are vaguely worded and i have the heebie-jeebies every time i walk into that lecture. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH A DIFFERENT PROF.
Takes 3+ weeks to grade coding assignments for a class of 20 students or less (summer asynchronous). Pretty pathetic considering there are professors who have to manage classes 10x that size
Excellent
Excellent. True professor.

By the end of the semester, lecture attendance was about 20% and he was giving extra credit to people who showed up. Lectures are pointless since the online quizzes every other week are about things that aren't covered at all. If you ever need help with the projects, just go to the lab and ask the TA's, they are very helpful.
No body come to the lecture
Always available outside of the class and is willing to help. His lecture is not that good, but there are extra credits and lenient gradings.
Trash

His lectures are not as engaging as top professors, but they aren't mandatory so you can choose to learn from other places. If you aren't busy, go for the extra credits in lectures. 
Really easy grades, online exams, all multiple choices. For those who are willing to learn yourself, this is the perfect course to earn an A+.

He was actually an okay professor. Was not good at lecturing but it didn't matter because he gave us all the resources to do well (Zybooks textbook) and he did care about our success. Class was not too hard and gave lots of extra credit.

I really don't get the hate for Pawlicki. His lectures were decent and covered the material promised (along with some additional topics towards the end of the semester). Projects were interesting. He was always accessible during office hours and willing to answer any lab-, project-, or quiz-related questions. Also, a lot of extra credit.
Lectures suck but attendance isn't mandatory. Assignment directions are confusing but it's almost impossible to fail the class. However, the online textbook is $90.
Lectures were dull but the projects were pretty cool. Everything reused from past years. Easy A if you are willing to do the work and time manage well.
Bad lectures. Also Bald

Pawlicki took whatever interest I had in game dev, and tried his hardest to throw it out of the window. Lectures are boring and useless, with the occasional sexist remark as well. I had to learn EVERYTHING from YouTube which was a thousand times more engaging. The only plus is that quizzes and assignments are super easy, so his class is an easy A.

Somehow easy homework,  many many opportunities for you to get extra credit and fixed A lines, so it s pretty easy to get an A for CSC172 he teaches. In fact, many of my friends even get 100+ in his class so A+ is quite common (tho he only uses A in workday).
However, he's awful in teaching, so get ready to learn everything by yourself via youtube.

Lenient with deadline extensions. Online quiz, no midterm & finals. Quizzes are reused from last year, sometimes with questions not covered in class. No one goes to lectures. It's a dull but easy A class as long as you do the work.
He will reply to your email but will never solve your problem. Seems to be responsive but not caring at all
love this guy
Pawlicki and Zhupa's lectures are as difficult to read as their names.
TRASH. HE IS JUST TRASH.

Completely useless. If you want to do well in this class, utilize the TAs and put in the effort for the projects and labs. No one goes to lectures once they realize that he just repeats the textbook, but explains it in a worse and more unclear way.

His tests are the worst. He recycles questions EVERY single test, but it's not material found in lectures or online really. ZyBook will be your best friend. Should have worked with a partner to get a better grade. The extra credit assignment is what saved me-- bumped it up a full letter grade, so def do it.
I learned everything from YouTube & Zybook. Don't go to the lectures. There is a big extra credit assignment, which is nice.

Contacting this professor is easy, getting help is not. Zoom chat was an unmoderated distraction, his long lectures made no sense & he had a sour, dull demeanor. His CV is nowhere to be found. Main textbook is a work of art, wish the author taught it. Online made it 10 times harder. Horrible way to begin CS. Use YouTube. Avoid at all costs.

Did not enjoy the lectures, were all over the place, and learned everything through others or online. If you do the work though, you'll get an A. He did post lecture recordings online, even when classes were in person, so that was nice.

Horrendous lecturer. Crappy tests. Labs and projects have very poor directions and he is not very accessible outside of class either. TAs will be your best friend in any of his classes. But overall not a harsh experience as the grade scaling makes it very easy to get an A.
His lectures and readings are not related to quiz.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Prof. T is kind and helpful and accessible outside the class. He is also willing to extend deadlines for students. However, his lecture is a little bit dull for me. Be ready for a lot of reading on Zybook if you want to take CSC172, it is really important. I learn almost everything from Zybook.
toooooooo much tedious work ughh, 131 is def an evil class ...................

Responsive, and always available. People speak to the difficulty of assignments, but not about his amazing office hours. Always dedicated to working with you until you fully understand the assignments. Lots of example code that helps directly with the projects and is available for personal use.

There're ten sympathetic inevitable tragedies i.e Pompeii, Hamlet. And then there is TP's CSC 172. He is the Mount Everest of computer science that wields all the power for all explorers to CS and only if you had help or luck, you may not pull it off. And just like Shakespeare, he makes sure the pain is prolonged and sinking in your puny sad soul.
Bad experience of my CS journey.

Boring lectures, Pawlicki always starts a new chapter each time even if he did not finish the previous one before, and just reads the slides. His weekly online quizzes are worthless as few questions really focus on the key concepts and you can always find the answer with Ctrl+F on the textbook. Try to avoid him! If cannot, then just teach yourself.

I really loved the course material but the lecture was not useful at all. O totally depended on YouTube and the textbook. The professor is a bad explainer he fails to explain any complicated topic. He is a a slow coder so the lecture is always wasted while he is trying to show us example code.
High quality lecture slides. Lab assignments are easy but projects are pretty hard. I do not recommend this class to person who has not any CS background knowledge.

Honestly, you could learn nearly nothing from his lectures. All of the quizzes, labs, and projects are directly taken from previous years without change, even if there are tons of mistakes in these materials, including misleading instructions and wrong questions. Quizzes, lectures, labs and ZyBook are all grades but totally irrelevant to each other

Same as many poor guys here, I say that his lectures are worthless and disappointing. My suggestion is to complete self-learning before the semester begins. 172 with TP is an inevitable misery to many ones. When you feel down, cope with it, and don't let it ruin your expectations for future CS courses. CS should be hard, but this is undeserved.
I'm not mad, just disappointed.

CS172 equips its students with some of the most important knowledge of their cs career. This should be a fun and enriching class, though Pawlicki turned it into a nightmare. The two textbooks, assignments, exams, and lectures are completely unattached from each other. Just self-study... DONT WASTE YOUR PRECIOUS TIME GOING TO LECTURES.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Do not take this professor. Unfortunately it's impossible to major in CS without him as he is the ONLY professor for CS172. Even one of his TAs left him. He doesn't explain anything. The only way to survive his course is to teach yourself from the textbook. His political views are quite scary too, but that's for a different site.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: This professor is trying too hard to make it harder for students to understand the material. Instructions in his assigments are not understandable and tremendously incomprehensible
Absolute dogwater! Disgrace to the CS community, anywhere.

I honestly feel bad for the CS kids at UR. They're all talented, bright, eager to learn, and have extremely creative minds. It's sad that they're not being supplemented with a quality professor for a class as important as data structures & alg.

One of the least specific and detailed professors in computer science I have had. I respect professor Pawlicki's charismatic personality and hilarious charm, but he is not a good educator who seems to care about holistic learning, but just sits and watches students. If you want to take data structures, I highly urge you to take it in the fall.

He really make algorithm very unclear. It is hard for you to study from his lectures. Please go to other materials, learn from greeks for greeks and other platforms. The lecture slides can then guide you the list of thing you need to know. But do not try to just rely on slides, you can not understand without very clear explanation.
Students may not like his political views. But I personally found him entertaining. Fun guy.
Mental breakdown simulator. Except it's real.

CSC172 is an extremely useful class full of fascinating algorithms and clever data structures. But Ted Pawlicki nearly ruined it for me. Two labs a week forced me to rush through material instead of fully learning it. In lectures, he explains the material in a way that only makes sense if you already know it. He is also rude to students.
You will regret taking his class.

I can't help to feel like I am paying to self-study here. I mean, I used to like doing homework and practice questions. Not anymore. The homework, along with EVERY OTHER CONTENT, is so not clear. I don't even know what he means in some homework questions. Cost me a lot actually.

He turned what used to be a 2 Midterm class into a 5 Midterm + 1 Final class. I would not say he himself has bad intentions, but also adding an additional set of homework each week (so from 1 set per week to 2), I don't necessary have the time to think well of him. My conclusion? This has become a class made for students to STRUGGLE!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: yeah, we all know about the notorious FB post he made, and I was wary of being in his class too. But I've found he's probably one of the kindest teachers I've had. I'm in CSC131 so it may be a different experience than 171/2, but he seems to genuinely care about his students and explains the material well, too.

teach well, not possible, not for this life. good lectures not capable, just hua water to keep life. 171 boring, 172 online is like home! Students are all self-study genius and can do 100 labs a week, wow!! very like 172 online.
Homework and Projects will suck up every single second. A lot of questions are not related to the lecture or the book. You will need to find resources online often. Why?

Very accessible outside of class, and really gives you all the tools you need to succeed, even if he doesn't always have the best lecture slides. So few students regularly attend his class (since attendance isn't mandatory) that I find it hard for so many students to give him a bad rap without taking advantage of what he offers.

Starting this semester (2019 fall), this course requires textbook online. It takes 60$ to use, and it counts for 10% of the grades. Also, the professor barely cover any useful material in a logical way. This means CSC 171 is a self-teaching course which cost you a lot of money besides tuition, and the professor is useless.

Prof. Pawlicki's lectures were usually a loose run-through of how to use parts of Blender without any real structure. Most of the time I think he was just playing around with the program and sending us off. It was enough for the lax nature of this course, but with a more intense class like CSC 171 I'd stay far away.

Worst teacher ever! You would never want to have any classes with this guy! Tough final, useless lecture, and endless homework. He doesnt know the material, and he is not able to answer questions. By the way, you never know rubrics for guest lecture report.

Probably the worst professor at University of Rochester. I could learn more java programming through an online python course. Talks more about his wife than java. If this is your first time coding, don't let this class deter you from further programming.
Lectures are relatively useless. Easy class to do well in. Just do the assignment and self-study and you'll be fine

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: He is the worst professor at this university and sadly he is the only one who teaches CSC 171 for both semesters. I can honestly say that its is not a "Introduction" class its more like review for people who already know java. During lecture all he talks about is his wife then briefly cover the material. The two assignments each week are difficult.
Stopped going to class midway through the semester. Got an A. Self study, learn from the TAs and online, and you'll be fine.

This course is really quick for an intro course, especially for anyone without any prior knowledge in Java programming beforehand. TAs & Google are your saviors. Read recommended books; they are more useful than Ted will ever be. Ted is at least fairly lenient with extra credits for projects, so work hard on those. It is rough, but not impossible.
His lecture is extremely useless. You can come to his class and laugh and do other things, but you will not be able to see the whole code and you won't learn much. Go to TAs, they are better.

Don't take his class. If you want to major CS, and come to UR for fall semester, just explore the first semester and hopefully some other professor will take CS171 next semester. He cannot teach and just assumes you have all the knowledge you need for Java EVEN THOUGH ITS AN INTRO CLASS. He is bad for your self esteem and your future in CS. AVOID

He cannot teach. Period. Don't waste your time in his lectures, go to CSUG, go to CETL, get a upperclassman willing to help and use the internet to learn. Read the books, and you should be able to learn by yourself

If you have no prior exp with Java, don't take this class. This man will not teach you anything and if you're very very lucky you will get a good lab and workshop TA who will guide you. He doesn't go over basics even though it's an introductory course and you're not supposed to have prior programming experience.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: The worst class I ever had. This was supposed to be a introductory class. He teaches as if he's reviewing everything we already learned. Horrible class AVOID if you can

I am not sure how Pawlicki has managed to keep a job for so long. It's currently week six and he has not even made a syllabus yet. And No Ted, sharing your course "calendar" spreadsheet with wrong dates is not a syllabus. It's evident that he does not read the textbook-provided slides before presenting, which would be okay IF he knew the material.
Well he is a fun inspiring mentor.

Don't get swayed by his political views. He is passionate about CS and manages to convey what he wants. He can be a bit boring at times but the labs and workshops are super helpful if this is your first time coding. Oh, and attempt extra credit.
I couldn't understand what he was saying. His lectures were not in logic. If you want to take this course, be ready to learn by yourself.

Please learn Java before you register for the course. Your TAs and workshop leaders are your saviors for this course. If you have no prior coding experience, you can avoid the lectures, but I would definitely attend the labs and workshops for practice.

Too bad CSC171 is required for CS majors and only Pawlicki teaches intro. If you have no java experience, the course will be a nightmare! Lectures are absolutely useless (I stopped going to them) and the labs are very confusing and stressful. Then the midterms are very difficult... Avoid this professor or learn java on your own. Beware

Horrible teacher- lectures are complete nonsense and the homework is frequent and difficult. This is supposed to be an intro class and it doesn't describe anything in detail. I had no prior coding experience and the class is geared towards students who have lots. Do not take this class with Pawlicki if possible

Truly awful professor. The worst professor I have ever had. Waste's students time during lecture rambling about random things which are not going to help us learn computer science or do well on tests.
Terrible guy terrible professor
Literally makes no sense. He goes on mental tangents all the time and expects people to be able to understand him. Reminds me of the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland.
Highly engaging lecturer. Tied together disparate concepts. Very passionate about computer science.

worst professor ever. Non-responding to emails, weird exam content, ambiguous instruction on lab, which took me 30 minutes more on each lab on average.  But this is a mandatory class, what can you do about it???

Terrible professor, probably the worst CS professor.  His lectures and code are terrible. He is unhelpful during his office hours and told me to study for the wrong thing when I had asked. I am so glad I am done with this class. I was able to get an A+ by: going to lecture (helped with meeting fellow students), workshop, labs, CSUG and CETL tutors.

Engaging lecturer, but otherwise the single worst professor I had in undergrad - unresponsive to emails, often hard to find during his scheduled office hours, typos and ambiguous assignment instructions, harsh grading, callously mean to students (in person or via email), and had little apparent concern for the synchronization of lab to lecture.
One of the worst professors I have had in my life. He did not teach a single thing. It was a self-taught course. Learn everything you can from the workshops.
Basically a self taught course. However he is very generous with extra credit and the curves. As long as you're willing to work for it, you will end up doing well in the class.

Very poor Professor, very bad lecturer. Powerpoints, tests and workshops would have so many typos it was hard to read Pay attention in workshop if you want a good grade because labs and lecture are useless
horrible lecturer, mistakes in all his powerpoints
The lectures do not help, and this pretty much sums up my experience with Ted.

Pawlicki is the worst professor I've ever had the misfortune to "learn" from. His examples and explanations were always ridiculously unclear, he tends to spend half the time lecturing on academic honesty, and he doesn't respect his students at all unless they worship him. If you take this class, be prepared to self-teach all of it like I had to do.

Pawliki expects you to understand the concepts basically instantly and then be able to apply those concepts. His examples tend to be convoluted. If you are not an intuitive programmer, you will struggle a little bit. Do NOT ever leave the middle of his class (unless it is directly after a quiz). He gives "random" pop quizzes after people leave a lo

He's enthusiastic about the subject but his lectures aren't the most helpful (you'll do much better in labs). He may be reluctant to help if you email him but go to him directly and he'll be more than willing to help!
Not nice to students. Bad attitude. Classes are not helpful.
Took this course over the summer, there was a lot of work but it was a lot of fun.
As nice a guy he is, he's very unhelpful. The assignments were unclear in what they wanted and were riddled with typos.

His course guidelines are clear and well organized. AKA you know what you need to do. His exams were difficult ( I averaged a D) but aren't worth much (10%) each. I still managed to get a solid A (yes I mean A, not an A-) because of the sheer amount of extra credit. I feel like he puts a lot of effort and has ideas, but his execution is horrible.
Honestly the worst experience I had in my history of education.

As quirky and endearing Pawlicki can be, he is not a good professor. He teaches concepts well at times, but there's an overall lack of direction given to students. Many times, his lab TA's haven't even read the labs and cannot help at all in lab. I don't even go to lab anymore and I just go to tutoring 247. The class isn't that bad though.

Very poor professor, can't explain anything at all, poorly designed quizes.  Also, can somebody explain to me how a 63% class average for midterm projections is considered acceptable? I'm personally getting a B+ in his class and im working on it 4 hours a day, but im appalled to see how many kids are doing that poorly. A mark of a poor professor.
Rude, disrespectful, and unhelpful. Dismisses student's concerns and provides no support. Also actively alienates girls in his classes all the time.
Terrible class. No support on assignments. Unclear lectures. Never responds to emails on important topics.

If you have no previous coding experience with Java you are going to have a bad time. Pawlicki is a quirky teacher and classes are lecture halls instead of computer labs. Most of your learning will come from yourself and the other will be from your workshops and labs. If you have the coding experience you'll be fine, if not good luck you'll need it

Odd but kinda funny prof. Lectures/his speech were choppy, though he teaches concepts ok enough. I learned a ton from the labs, but they took FOREVER because you have to learn examples on own. No homework otherwise. Fairly easy if you put in enough effort on your own. Many who skip class + don't do practice problems bomb the quizzes and complain.

Ted Pawlikci gets a lot of hate because he expects his students to put in the work required not just to get a good grade, but to actually UNDERSTAND the material on a fundamental level.  If you are interested in CS and willing to put forth effort to not just complete assignments but to do them as best you can, you will have a great time with Ted.

In-class quizzes and mandatory workshops are BS, but he's great apart from that. Fun lecturer and not nearly as repetitive as his colleagues. Plus he probably gives more extra credit than any other professor in the university!

I learned a lot in this class. The main strength of this course is it's structure. The weekly workshops and labs are helpful. The projects were all doable and not terribly hard. He's fairly entertaining in class. A programming course has to have good structure, a good lecturer isn't really helpful when you're home doing assignments.

He is awful. He fails to realize how what he says, makes no sense and constantly goes off on computer science related tangents. Outside of class he is extremely difficult to reach and is quite helpless when you do reach him. I learn a lot from lab and the TAs, but nothing in lecture.  He is awful, avoid if possible.

He is the epitome of an absentminded professor. People don't get that his "pedagogical philosophy" is not only teaching CS but also teaching self-sufficiency. I came with 0 CS experience, worked & struggled through his classes & learned so much from doing it myself. Every single thing is graded by TAs so don't blame him for their decisions.
Not helpful or on topic most of the time.

Is not clear at all. Does not teach you what the labs are on. I had no CSC experience before this class and i basically had to teach it to myself. Don't believe him when he says it will be a even playing field for everyone. He also takes off a ton of points for even the slightest of error.

Although he's a weird guy, he's funny and teaches the material well. He explains things better during office hours and explains complicated concepts in advanced theory in a really nice way if you ask him about that. He makes mistakes on purpose so that attentive students can correct him. The class is also pretty interactive.

Avoid like the plague. This guy is supposed to be the undergraduate director, but doesn't know what a "pedagogical philosophy" is, has a petty attitude towards dotting is and crossing ts, and rarely takes responsibility for highly ambiguous lab directions or mismatches between lecture, lab, exam, and syllabus. Difficult to reach outside of lecture.

If you have previous programming experience then you'll do just fine without much effort (and should probably take 172). I would probably have been incredibly confused (as a lot of my friends were) if I were just starting out with CS in his class.

He really knows his stuff, but his lectures aren't always as useful as they could be. Make sure to 1. Ask questions 2. read the book (ESPECIALLY the first week, when he gives you the one and only pop quiz) 3. switch recitations until you get great TAs 4. Start assignments ahead of time so you can ask about them 5. Work in groups

A kind of scatterbrained, but nice guy. The course is easy if you read through and do the labs; most of the meat of the teaching seems to be there instead of in-class, where you can behold his dubious typing skills. Note that practically nobody will succeed any tests he gives in class.

Straight up horrible teacher.  Will assign projects immediately teaching a fundamental concept.  Without prior programming experience you probably wont receive an A in this course.  Personally have an A-/A and I have 2 Java Courses in a New England Prep School.... It is amazing that the University of Rochester has this guy as a tenure professor.

He may not be the best professor, but he's a good laugh. He can rush a little bit sometimes and can get mixed up. I'm not sure how he grades our assignments and tends to knock off a lot of marks for minor mistakes. But you can't help but love his enthusiasm.
I really enjoyed 172, it inspired me to major in CS.
It's a fun past-time to poke fun at him, but in reality he's a great professor. Just pay attention in class. I know it can be hard sometimes, but his examples and slides are very clear.

If you don't have programming experience, you'll have a hard time THROUGHOUT the course. Pawlicki's a nice guy if you get to know him, but he's not a good teacher: he doesn't make a lot of sense very often(even in writing), he teaches fundamentals too late in the course (if he covers them at all), and very often fails to respond to emails.
class not even worth attending. jumps from topic to topic.

Jumps around, does not teach fundamentals before he introduces the intricate complexities and obscure uses.  Teaches an idea and expects you to apply it immediately when he teaches the reasoning behind it two or three weeks later in the course.  Students with prior experience have a leg up in the course and it's never a level playing field, ever.
He says that people with no prior programming experience will be caught up with those with experience by the end of the semester....Nonsense..

Good class, entertaining and helpful lectures, though Pawlicki is a bit scatter-brained. However, the lab TAs are probably the most incompetent people I've ever meet. They are always late and reluctant to offer any help.
Very good teacher; entertaining...very helpful outside of class. Always willing to answer a question, related or unrelated to the topic at hand.

Not very focused in lecture, assignments are unclear, and test/quiz material never seems to be taught in class. Honestly if I hadn't taken AP CS in high school, I probably would've failed this class. If you're new to CS, good luck...
He is cool. Explains stuff well too.

His lectures are great. His grading is horrible, instructions on projects are bad, and he's not very helpful out of class. E.g, He will chop off 20 points off a project for a print line error, and not be very helpful if you've made some mistake on an assignment or midterm. He randomly changes how much assignments are worth in the final grade too.
I learn nothing really.
None.
Inspirational !

He's an amazing teacher.  I was really very worried about starting out in CSC171 when I hadn't programmed for a couple of years (and even then not at a very intense level), but he's made it one of my best/favorite classes.  He's an extremely interesting and helpful teacher (even if he can't spell and disses English majors a lot).

Despite what other ppl say, I think he's pretty clear and really very helpful whenever you need him to be. His teaching teaching style isn't too boring, but I can see how it would be significantly more difficult if you didn't already know some programming. However, I found that he taught the things I didn't know already pretty well.
Easy if you know CSC well.  If you don't, well you better learn to use the internet A LOT.

There are two things about Ted that people need to know, he is a great guy, hilarious during lecture, who teaches a mandatory, but acceptably easy class for CSC majors, his flaw is that he is very absentminded.  He is usually acceptably clear during lecture but his tests are much harder then his lectures/labs.  GREAT guy in person, alright prof.

He seemed like a nice guy, but he was a terrible professor. Really unhelpful, unavailble when he said he would be, would move up the dates on assignments without much notice, wouldn't respond to emails, etc etc. Also, if you dont know much about csc going in, be prepared to figure everything out from the book, the TAs, and from your friends.
Yeah, he's a decent guy, I'll give him that. But I don't think he's very clear about things.
He sucks

I took an independent study with the guy. FANTASTIC! I didn't like writing the papers (and they were half-assed) and I think he didn't like reading them. Plus, I never submitted the final paper because I saw an "A" on my grade report before the thing was due.
Thought he knew what he was talking about... will just haveta wait and see... i think hes pretty cool though
Class was uneccessary, the should of just had labs.
I don't understand why he gets such a bad rap. I think beacuse he teaches 1st year courses, and freshmen complain alot.
Nice guy, but not a great professor.
Polarizing figure, isn't he?  All I know is he's defensively responsible and uses his size well, unlike that cherry-picker John Kerry.
No Comments
Good Person, bad teacher.  Hope that you get an english speaking TA, cuz the class is no help.
Totally unhelpful.  Teach yourself, and if you don't already know it, sucks to be you.
Decent teacher, though nothing special.  Nice guy though.
Most absent-minded professor ever.

Sink or swim type evaluation to ensure that the number of CS majors remains small. Not as much of an ass when you get to know him - he's actually both nice and somewhat helpful in a non-class setting.
Bad Teacher, doesn't care about students

comment: Best English Professor I've ever seen. Very easy to approach. The workloads are very manageable. The paper in the class didn't weigh too much on your final grade. So don't worry if you are not a good writer.
The best professor. Very fair and class was excellent.

comment: She's a great person overall. Her lectures are good and not boring. The class is designed to be discussion based so you'll end up talking to your classmates a lot more than the professor herself.

Workshops are the most important part of this class. The lecture material barely corresponds with the book and some test questions seem out of no where. I feel like I learned nothing in class and had to figure out most of the material with the TAs.

Many years ago,(25) I had the misfortune of taking Prof. Eisenberg's honors introductory general chemistry class.  He made his exams hard by the inexcusable method of making them far too long for the time allowed, NOT because they were intelligent or clever. I still became a physician, but I AGREE with today's students: AVOID Prof. Eisenberg.

I took his honors chem class...for the record, anyone taking honors classes in college...it's not like high school anymore...honors classes are extremely difficult. Consider taking them if you are majoring in that subject.  Class was ridiculously hard. Of course it has to be, they have to weed out the pre-meds somehow. Stay away from Eisenberg
ok, to sum it up. Salutatorian here, got a 5 on the AP chem test and dropped this course with a D.  I'm not retarded, this class was hella hard.

THE WORST TEACHER EVER! He is not approachable. In fact if you ask him questions, he hates you and gives a BS answer. Teaches random things that undergraduates have no clue about. Thinks he is always right. He probably never even looked at the book he uses because his lectures are incoherent. He uses other people's PPT. NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!

Took his honors chem class and was definitely bumped away from pursuing his course by the level of difficulty.  The class is curved and material is covered rapidly and overheads are essential. If you are pre-med, put some time into this class.
horrible horrible person. doesn't deserve to teach or be called a professor. Don't have enough respect for him to call him that. needs to learn how to be a person before becoming a professor.

Out of touch with students, does not give clear information about what will be covered on exams, assigns homework that often does not coincide with course material, preaches about the journal he edits and how important it is, congratulates himself on predicting the winner of Nobel prize award...but hey--it must be the next best thing to winning it.
