comment: HIST 189 NOT 157 I took a women's history class and it was really interesting at parts. I thought her emphasis on intersectionality was good and her personal anecdotes were good. Sometimes it got a little boring and the lecture was way too big but in all I enjoyed it. She was nice.

Professor Theobald always makes class interesting and engaging. Lots of reading for homework but about different topics so it isn't repetitive. She is very approachable and is my favorite professor on the entire campus. Take all of her classes, you won't regret it.
Half-decent lecturer, but graded harshly on open-ended assignments with unclear rubrics. Class was filled with busy-work.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I took History of Native America with Professor Theobald and highly recommend taking this course. There were about 10 pages of reading per week as a minimum but the readings were always on different topics so it didn't feel redundant. The lectures were engaging and class participation was highly encouraged. Great class, even better professor

Aaron is fantastic. My time in his class has only deepened my interest in the topics we discussed. He's always ready to accommodate and treats his students as equals, not condescending in the least bit. Sometimes it really feels like we're his colleagues not just his students, in the best way haha. Thanks for a great semester!

By far the best professor at UR.  He is so caring, understanding, and happy, and truly wishes to see students succeed.  Having a difficult week and need an extension on an assignment?  He'll tell you to take as much time as you need.  Not understanding something?  He'll explain it in such an exciting way.  Dude is awesome, 10/10.

Professor Hughes has not only been my favorite professor at UR, but has also had the biggest impact on my education and career path. I've never had a professor who genuinely loves his students and wants to learn from them. if you have any interest in religion I highly recommend any of his classes. He is full of so much wisdom and knowledge !

The class was very difficult because it's a 6-credit class, but Aaron is an easy grader and a really considerate professor. He can be quite cynical and sharp, but he is also very passionate about his students and what he's teaching. I learned a lot from him, although I wouldn't recommend him if you're sensitive about religion.

The guy who gives me the only A in my last semester at Rochester. I feel that he gives me the hope to live on. What an awesome guy! I wish that every instructor could be like him! There were only two papers and his aim was always to let the students enjoy writing them! God bless you!

comment: Best Professor ever. His material is dense and classes are more of open discussions. Very lenient on grades and also go to class or you will fail. Very well regarded and also down to earth professor.
interesting and very fair

Class discussion tended toward the boring side. The secondary source readings were awfully boring, too, and extensive (though primary sources were good). There were only 3 assignments, and they were not hard. I would be willing to take another class with him, but preferably a lecture-based class, rather than another seminar-style class.
He is a really great professor. Attending class is optional, but I feel like I learn a lot when I go to class. He posts the notes on Blackboard as well. Just an all around interesting professor.
shes super sweet but its easy to fall behind in work
she's very nice but doesn't really explain things in a logical order. not much work, but it's a bit of a challenge.
kind of boring but you learn a lot
Very nice teacher, very understanding of extinuating circumstances. Highly recommended if at all interested in learning Arabic.
outstanding professor.  any talk of consolidating the two-person arabic department and leaving her out is borderline idiocy.
one of the nicest professors ever...very lenient and understanding.
Very Nice. Recommended if interested in arabic. Coursework is minimal and not too difficult. Recommended.
The professor is rude. Has absurd rules in class and is full of himself.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Really knowledgeable and updated with the latest developments. Course is intensive and the Verilog Projects are difficult, but really helps to understand the low level details of designing a modern processor. Really learnt a lot and easy to get A if one can do all the projects (including bonus parts) :)
Great thanks
Extremely knowledgeable. He is a good lecturer and works through many examples on the board. If you attend class and pay attention, you will learn a lot.    Tests are tough, but he curves.

I honestly have no idea what the grading scheme is. This has been the hardest class I have ever taken.  The curve was at least 30 points (i.e if you had a C you get a A). He's a guy that knows his stuff and he seems like a good person but hes not a great professor.  My grade was a F and was curved to a C-. Mind you I worked HARD for an F.
Avoid at all costs or enjoy your suffering. 10 mins quiz is worth 25% grade. Good luck.
the grading criteria is amazing.

He insists on using a programming language that isn't used by any other CS professor or grad student, leaving me resource-less and frustrated on every assignment. His TAs have to post the grading scheme and office hours because he doesn't remember to do it himself. Assignments are completely unrelated to lectures or the textbook. Avoid at all costs
The worst professor ever! an alive example of delusion.

She was well spoken and overall the class and her teaching style was favorable. I would recommend this class if your willing to show up, the reading is not really needed to get an A on the exams just on the papers.
Was my graduate advisor for 2 years during my master's. Excellent Prof

Alex is rad. He expects a lot, but makes it fun and is invested in your learning. Funny lectures go by fast and it's clear he's passionate about what he does and puts history into current events. Attendance counts, but there's extra credit. Kinda a slow grader but not harsh. Would totally take his class again.

Totally a tough grader. Will never take his course again. Try to take other 1xx courses. He asks for attendance and participation for 20% in total. Three lab works and three papers. Extremely harsh on grading papers, so if you are not an excellent writer, do not try his course!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Class mostly prof-led discussion of readings, not very structured. Would've preferred more student/group discussion, sometimes didn't find prof too engaging. Liked options for main project. Final was comprehensive and satisfying. Workload was just readings, tho sometimes a lot. Great guy, alright prof. Course itself was flawed imo, too cursory.

Awesome prof! Majorly discussion based class, but he makes a comfortable environment to share your views on the material, so discussion feels natural. I enrolled later into the semester and he made sure I knew exactly what to catch up on and the major themes. Overall cool guy who really seems to be passionate about what he teaches.

lectures were very interesting!! he is a very insightful man and made milton way more interesting than i ever thought it could be. it was fascinating just to hear him speak about milton and blake- his passion really shines through. super caring and accessible and supportive- helped me through a tough point in my life
great prof

Took what could have been a polarizing topic and taught it in a way that was both fair & respectful all while looking at aspects of Christianity through a lens of literature. A truly excellent Professor!
Great Professor who uses his broad knowledge of Literature, Philosophy and Culture to create a wonderful learning and discussion based environment.

An engaging professor who seems to truly care for his students. Encourages dialogue & discussion between classmates and actively helps students formulate their own interpretations of the readings. Would highly recommend!
The worst professor I came across.  Stay away!
Impatient. Horrible handwriting. Confusing. Gave the wrong formulas in class and did not realize that the ones in the book were wrong at times as well. Avoid her class if at all possible.

Horrible Teacher. Terrible Handwriting. Impatient. Gave the wrong formulas in class. Didn't realize the textbook also had errors. Made mistakes on her own practice exam keys, and did not sent out corrections though they were pointed out by a student.

Provides wrong formulas in class.  Her practice test solutions have many errors, and not just at the superficial typo/miscalculation level. She makes fundamental mistakes on her own tests.  The textbook is also horrendous and of no use.
she explains everything very clear. ^_^
She's clear and helpful. Doesnt compromise on homework deadlines.

Good lecturer but very slow grader. Expect to receive grades at least a month after assignments are due! She is very disorganized when it comes to grading and it seems like she assigns too many assignments because she cannot handle the grading herself. Expect final grades to be posted after the FINAL grades are due.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Courtney Jones. One of the few caring professors in the public health department. Her personal stories and amazing lectures made it feel like she actually cared about us; she is the reason why I wanted to go into public health. I wish she taught more undergrad classes because the other PH professors are just not it.

Courtney Jones is extremely accommodating. I love her lectures because she always adds personal anecdotes that help students understand the content taught. I wish she taught more classes at our university. She is wonderful.

Dr. Jones is the best professor I've had. Her lectures are fascinating, and she is an inspiring individual. She gives fair exams and is very accessible outside of class. She is also very understanding of extenuating circumstances. She is caring and knowledgeable; I cannot recommend her enough.

Very nice guy, but the class is dull beyond belief. All of the assignments are take-home essays, so going to lecture is only useful to get lecture notes (but most of the information can be found in your books). You don't really have to do most of the reading either. You'll forget you're taking this class sometimes.
Not much interaction but very nice. Easy grader.
Class is very boring but, there are no in class tests all papers.  There is a lot of reading but, you don't actually have to do most of it.  He is an easy grader.

An extremely unfair grader for a 100-level class. Admitted to me that he has become "cranky" with his old age and that his knee problems impacted his grading. I typically do well on papers, and I put a lot of effort into his class, what a waste of time. Take something else.
lots of reading but a great prof to take a class with. very knowledgable and his classes are like story time with lots of disscusion.
This professor is terribly paranoid about student plagerism--but he is NOT upfront about it.  For the innocent student, it is unnerving and very insulting.
No Comments
Great prof! Extremely knowledgeable and interesting
Easy class.  He's interesting, and doesn't grade hard.  Take classes with him if you're interested in Asian History.  You'll do well.

Such a horrible professor. If you take him, you'll have to learn everything on your own and will still get a low C on the class. He is a very hard grader. He expects you to know the whole book and beyond. But at the same time, he doesn't know the material very well himself. He always comes unprepared to the class and makes tons of mistakes.

When she lectures, she doesn't give room to answer/ask questions. She will barely explain things and she has zero tone of voice. She doesn't seem to teach material, just writing down a script given to her to read and then we as the class write down the script that she writes. She doesn't teach. If I had her paper I could teach her class better.

Prof. Kose is my favorite professor (at least for now). He really cares for the students and wants everyone to do their best. He talks about the importance of learning the topic rather than getting a high grade. High grade comes with the love of the topic, he says!. I like his lectures and labs so much!

Prof. Kose rocks. Many extra credits in terms of bonus pop quizes and the final was out out 110 points, instead of 100. Final was harder than midterm, but was manageable if you attended lectures and follow his tips regarding what kind of questions can appear in the final. Overall, he is a generous grader and he really cares.

Kose communicates the material well, mostly because he's following the textbook exactly, with lectures based on presentations of textbook screenshots, as such the lectures are a bit uninspired. The homework isn't bad if you don't do 3 weeks in one day, and is very useful. The final is hard and weird in the material covered but TAs grade it nicely.

He is a good guy. I love his accent. He is well prepared and always offer help to explain again if anyone raises any questions. Stops regularly to ask everyone if there are any questions. Overall, one of the best professors in Rochester. In addition to being a good teacher, he seems to be a great researcher. often gives examples from his research.

Kose is a good professor, better than any other ECE professor. He understands how difficult this class can be and makes sure each student learns during the lecture. He is very patient with some not-so-smart questions during his lecture. Highly recommend!!

Every ECE student needs to take his course. Luckily, he is a great guy and very approachable. While the content of the lectures are difficult, the homeworks are long, and exams, especially the final is quite long and difficult, Dr. Kose really makes sure each student has a good grasp of the material. Highly recommend!

Kose is a good professor. Highly recommend skimming the textbook chapter before each lecture, otherwise lectures might be a bit confusing. But he always answers questions, and tries to make sure most students understand before moving on. Recitations are optional but really really helpful. Don't procrastinate the homework!
Great instructor. He really cares!
No one understand what this guy is talking about

The class was difficult on its own but if he explained things by writing on the board instead of giving lecture from slides, it would have been more useful. If you try listening to his lectures carefully, I think it's possible to understand the material and succeed in this class. For my year, he gave extra credit to student who took the pop quizzes
He's terrible at lecturing. Also he makes the final super hard. Average was a 50% on the final and no curve.
Dude is terrible at teaching
Does not explain well. If you ask him questions he will clarify, however, his lectures are a drag. The best way to learn is by doing homework problems and asking TAs for help.

He teaches based on the textbook slides, and he isn't good at explaining concepts. The midterm is very easy but the final is very hard. Learn by doing homework. He said he will give extra credit if you attend every class, but I didn't know how he could memorize all the people since we never sign up.
Teaches through pictures of the textbook, moves fast, and isn't interesting. The topic itself is unintuitive but his uninspiring lectures and bad English make it difficult. Learn by doing homework.
Selcuk Kose is a brilliant professor that cares about his students success. He is always there to help. I found his office hours useful. If you want to get an A, don't miss the lectures.

Prof. Kose is one of my favorite professors. He is very helpful both in and out of the classroom. The course was challenging, however, Prof. Kose was always there to help. I would definitely recommend taking his course(s).

The professor himself is a great guy but he needs to redesign the course a little bit. He teaches off of a boring Powerpoint slide and in his lectures, it is very hard to stay awake. The first half of the course is do-able but the second half is where stuff gets crazy.

Dr. Kose's taught well but he was sometimes a bit rough around the edges. He really only cares that you get near the right answer, not how much work you put in. He's super willing to meet outside of class and really wants his students to attend every lecture. For my class at least, he gave extra points to people who came every lecture.

Literally the easiest class I've ever taken. It's just basic statistics. If you have a pulse, you'll get an A in the class. The tests are copy and pasted from the review, with some numbers different, and some exactly the same. If you want to do well, just memorize the review. Overall, ridiculously easy class
Extremely kind professor, who is very passionate on the topic of abolition. Although I might not agree with every single one of his views, I thoroughly enjoyed his course.
Prof Dubler is an incredible lecturer and can tell really cares about the topic. He is very understanding and doesn't assign much work, mostly weekly discussion and like a few papers.

Don't really have any critiques about Dubler, more about the course. It is not the inspiring, life-changing, mind-altering course they tell you it is. Some of the readings were interesting, but others as well as many discussions were just buzzword after buzzword-- lots of loud people who think they're far smarter than is the case. Easy A though.

Recommend going to first two weeks of class then dropping it. Ideas are new and interesting only until the second week. After that it is almost merely repetition of the same ideas. Not very in depth nor very practical/empirical. Required discussion sessions are waste of time. Community engagement opportunities are great though.

One of the most inspiring people I've met in my time at this school. Very passionate and well-connected around the subject matter. His course was very unique and fostered lots of engagement in and out of the classroom.
Incredible class so inspiring

He is awesome. Very passionate, caring, and doesn't try to kill you with work. The class is graded on a couple papers that he grades very easily. Lots of reading, but you don't have to do it. I would recommend doing some of the reading- only the ones on topics that particularly interest you. Everyone should take this class- you will learn a lot!

Overall I enjoyed the class and thought the topic was interesting. However I thought much of the material was too hypothetical and overly optimistic. I wish the course looked at more tangible solutions to incarceration, and that the course wasn't so biased towards compete prison abolition. The guest speakers were the highlight of the course.

Josh is by far my favorite professor. He encourages students to actively engage with the community, goes out of his way to bring in a variety of perspectives, and is always willing to spend time talking to students about their own views and lives. I've learned so much about the structures in society and so much about myself in the process.

This was a super interesting class and I learned a lot from the lectures and speakers we had. I wish the class wasn't cut short by covid, but still solid online. Make sure to do the readings and pay attention to the authors and quotes he points out and you should be fine.
Meliora Seminar Class - Open to help - Gives good feedback and opportunities to boost grade - Class based on weekly book readings and papers
Super easy class just show up and study hard for midterm and final. Need to do the readings and Dubler is a great guy. Very passionate about his work and everything he is involved in.

He's very understanding and it's clear he loves his job. He's always available for feedback or for working through the heavy topics brought up in lecture, and he truly wants his students to think for themselves and learn how to analyze what they're reading. He's also a great facilitator of discussion! Dubler is the best.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Great guy! Always willing to meet outside of class for help. Has answered numerous questions even unrelated to class through email and even, per request, created a meme board for the class for a bit of a laugh. Lots of reading. Acknowledges his faults. Intelligent, lots of big words, so sometimes confusing. Likes hearing opinions/debating - A+

Worst class Ive ever taken. Hes the most subjective and biased grader Ive ever experienced. He also thinks hes WAY smarter than he is and it comes across as condescending. The class didnt teach me much that I didnt already know, either. Got all As in other classes, this was the easiest by far and got a B because hes biased.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Exams are slight variations from textbook/webwork/workshop/lecture examples. Workshop get 100% for showing up. Quizzes are group and are from examples you will have seen if you look at the upcoming week's workshop sheet beforehand, do webwork a week early and read notes/book sections for current topics (get 100%). Curves heavily 45%/55% ->80%/90%

So as a non-math major this class was hard af, but he's really nice and helpful and will do everything he can to help people out, including going over confusing hw problems in class before they're due. He can go a bit fast at times, but he's happy to explain things in more detail if asked. Genuinely good person who cares about his students

Explains concepts very clearly and logically - makes lectures engaging and easy to follow. Exams were kinda difficult, but they were prepared by another professor from the Math dept. Yamazaki is very caring and wants his students to do well.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: This professor is knowledgeable in his field, but he really is not a good teacher. Honestly, you will learn more if you do not go to class and just teach yourself out of the book. He just makes the subject material confusing with his poor explanations. Again, he's a nice guy, but a bad teacher.

Nice guy, and means well. English isn't his first language, but he talks faster than I can understand it (it is mine). Really difficult class, and I never felt like I understood a concept before the homework was due. "If you aren't getting it right, try again, and if you still aren't getting it right, try harder".

Very strict grader-- in math there's only correct answer and incorrect answer, so instead of arguing for partial credit you might just as well practice and get it right the next time. That's the important thing I learned from this class. He makes concepts really clear and easy to comprehend. A is not impossible to get as long as you work hard.
Explains in a way that makes you understand the questions easily, gives funny and creative examples to support mathematical concepts.
Get ready to read. Hard exams, tough grader

Favorite professor EVER. Cannot say enough about her. I found myself interested and moved by her every class. Also HILARIOUS and has an amazing sense of humor. I would take any class of hers just so I could listen to her lecture!
She's a busy lady, but she's interested in what she teaches and she teaches it well. If you memorize the material, the tests are easy... and there isn't that much material.

Dr. Ghera was a good lecturer. Her enthusiasm and humor made classes a lot easier to sit through.  The class was pretty easy, but her presentation of the material was well done. She's always good about giving tangible examples to whatever concept or theory she's teaching.

I loved her class.  She was engaging, entertaining, and educated.  Yes she has a lot on her platter with working at two colleges; but whenever I needed help on something she always managed to find the time.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Tried to be funny and appeal to teenagers but it was completely unfounded. Class was a complete waste of my time--a child could have done a better job teaching. I just feel sorry for her children because they will grow up with the knowledge that she shared personal details about them in her classes.
She was super entertaining and her anecdotes were extremely helpful. Definitely worth going to class

Perfect example of an adjunct with "better things to do". Never felt like UR was on her priority list. Let's the students who like to hear themselves speak do just that and never curtails their tangents which resulted in a whole lot of wasted time. She did share some funny stories and had a good sense of humor, but overall- horrible experience.

Don't listen to the other reviews, I took his Self-Help writing 105 class and it was awesome. There's a good amount of work per week, but it is engaging, and he is a really great guy and very engaging

Lots of readings and essays due every two days of class. Class is about "self help" but leaned more into ancient philosophy/religious readings. Leaned into redpill rhetoric sometimes during discussion? (Read his articles on the Good Men Project). Don't write too well on your first drafts or he grades your final drafts way more harshly.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: confusing feedback, no grades/feedback for informal assignments (there were 10 and they were worth 20% of our grade?), course had interesting topics but kind of felt like they had a misogynistic lean at times

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: Dr. Hinds is a very straight-forward teacher. She sets clear expectations each week of what must be completed. She can be a little blunt and seem uncaring, but her ability to give fair and clear feedback is noticeable. The class is an easy A if work is put into it. Do NOT expect to sit around waiting for it.

There is a lot of material to cover but this class really gives you an idea of all the interesting fields of study for BCS.  I really like Hinds as a teacher and I like that the tests are about applying material rather than just memorizing facts.  I would definitely recommend this class.

What a waste of time this class is. Don't skip lectures, but ignore the book. Recitations are a waste of time, and the tests are just a matter of being able to speak Hinds' language. You will be able to narrow each question down to 2 answers, but for a small sample of the test the 2 answers you're left with will be indistinguishable.

I wish Poujet still taught this. The tests aren't hard, they're just chalk full of terribly chosen and badly formulated questions. Hinds says this class is not about memorization, and she's right, it's about figuring out what the hell her questions are even asking. Lectures are unclear and I'm not convinced Hinds is knowledgeable on the topic.

The topics covered are interesting, but Hinds teaches directly off of the powerpoints.  Can you skip class because of this?  Perhaps, but it is always helpful to hear the material from her and take notes then in order to lower your study time.  Overall an easy class, but you should be able to apply the topics learned to different situations.

Nice woman but HORRIBLE teacher. Obviously knows her stuff but doesn't know a thing about how to teach. She teaches through Powerpoints - you can skip every class and get a decent grade. Many required readings but no textbook. Texts are somewhat easy but require lots of studying. Not the worst class ever but SO INCREDIBLY BORING.

The lectures are kind of boring and it feels like you don't actually get through much material because she spends half the class asking rhetorical questions. But her tests are really awesome. She is somewhat understanding. But she works here part time so it's really hard to meet with her if you need to talk to her.

The class covers many topics which is why is moves so fast. Overall, you can learn everything from her slides and do decent on the tests. Read the textbooks, because it will help you understand the concepts well enough to apply them on the tests.

Hinds is really intelligent but the lectures are drags. She tries to put an effort into teaching but it's as if she mostly does it for the purpose of being able to do research. The tests are difficult if you can't apply the material, which is really important if you want to pass. She posts slides online, so you can skip as long as you study hard.

admittedly her first course after receiving her doctorate -- hinds makes an entry level "organ grinder" class as engaging as possible.  A broad spectrum of topics over one semester -- would have liked more on clinical cases and abnormal psych, guess i'll have to take an upper division course for that.  very helpful during office hours as well.

She is the type of teacher that reads off of her powerpoint slides with very little commentary. You can tell that she knows a lot, but she seems to lack passion during her lectures which makes attending her class a dry experience. Her exams are fairly easy; you just have to put in decent study time and utilize the textbook for clarity of material.

Hinds is knowledgeable and seems very passionate. Lectures are dry because she talks "at" you rather than "to" you, but the quality improves over time, as the materials increasingly allow more interactivty in learning. Exams cover only lecture materials, but extra reading is recommended for clarification, as huge topics are rushed through in class.

Lectures are dry and not engaging. Attending class is not necessary as all the material explained with more clarity in the textbook. Her lectures move too fast and she touches on each topic too briefly, but she is somewhat helpful during office hours. Overall, her class is easy if you are willing to put in a lot of independent study time.
Grading criteria are clear from the very beginning. This class requires some prior understanding of chemistry or a lot of reading. He is incredibly nice and funny both during and after lectures

TOUGH CHM 173 CLASS. Lectures are very broad and general, doesn't really go over examples in class, so make sure you take full advantage of workshops offered. Sign up for a tutor asap with CETL because for this class, they get booked fast. Cares about students.
It's a tough class, but he is on the students' side and grades generously. He doesn't stress the math as much, but focuses on the concepts. He is very fun and always willing to help.

People who say he doesn't curve/add points didn't listen. Everyone bombed the first exam because it wasn't identical to old exams (oh no, it's not like this is college) and he gave a chance to get all those points back on the final. He's a fantastic lecturer, he's inspiring, and he's super nice to his students. He's the best professor I've had.
Maybe he's better teaching upper level classes?

He will not curve. In my class the average of the first exam we took was 28% and he would not add points or anything. He's pretty tough that way, but I also feel like a learned a lot more with him than I did with other Chemistry teachers. If you take him, be ready to put in A LOT of time and effort.

Awesome teacher. He teaches you everything you need to know plus makes it interesting. Very fair exams, very approachable. Read the book ahead of each class and you'll understand everything he says. Anyone who says he expects you to know chemistry before just didn't try. It's not hard if you listen to him and read. One of my favorite professors.

Bad teacher. if your schedule allows you to take it with a different professor then do. The class isnt too hard but he complicates everything, doesnt teach whats on tests and expects everyone to already know the material.  His test used to be like practice tests but the last two years, this year especially his exams are getting harder and less fair

Attendance is not mandatory, but he gets really angry if you don't come. I did not particularly enjoy his lectures and was often bored and distracted. Overall, he is better than the other professors for the course, but that isn't necessarily saying much. The material is also not his strong suit so he isn't that enthusiastic about it all the time.

Of all the other professors for this class, he is the best choice - TAKE HIM. You should go to class or else he will get mad, although it is not mandatory. WORKSHOP will teach you everything! Class is very unorganized so you need to review the notes he will upload online. Do the practice exams, although the actual test might be totally different!
Literally one of the worst professors I've had. He was really unfair. Tests were reasonable, until they became impossible because he had a personal vendetta against the students.

Farrar is constantly using environmental or other examples to create a true understanding of the application of the material. He is funny, makes lecture enjoyable, and definitely cares about his students and their level of comprehension. Tests are not difficult as long as you attend workshop and study with practice exams.

Farrar is probably one of the best professors that you will have if you decide to take his course. He made the material very understandable and really helped me to develop a passion for chemistry. He is entertaining in class and I look forward to going all the time. Tests aren't hard if you study and go to class. He's the man.

He's not a bad lecturer, and it is possible to learn the material from lecture, but it's probably the most time consuming and confusing way to do so. Very little of what he says in lecture is on a test (1 to 2 formulas per lecture if you're lucky). Just read his lecture notes, do the homework, go to workshop and you're good. Lecture is unnecessary.

Farrar is the man!  His lectures can be confusing, but if you read the chapters and do the homework, you'll be fine on the test.  Farrar is probably one of the smartest professors here and amazingly funny at times!  Great class overall.

DIfficult course to understand. Exams are difficult and lectures move too fast to prepare you for exams but workshops help. Chem Engineering majors seem to struggle with the content as its geared more toward (what seems to be meaningless) derivations.

Although I found this course challenging, Prof. Farrar made it manageable.  He always made time to help students outside of class and always welcomed students to office hours or set up more convenient times to meet.  Lectures were interesting and exams were fair.  I feel that I learned a lot of physical chemistry in this course and enjoyed it.

CHM131 is a difficult course, but with sufficient work put into it, it can be done. Farrar is an extremely smart guy, and seems to help the students with what they need. Probably one of the most hip professors on campus. Lectures get very hard to follow at times, but notes are always online to review.
Farrar uses the chalkboard to teach, which I found quite helpful.  He is willing to meet with students and answer questions.  Workshops are very helpful.
farrar is one of those teachers who is simply too brilliant for an intro level class.  it takes him a whole class period to explain not too difficult a concept
Haaaarrrdd Class.  Prepare to be challenged.  The TAs are helpful.  Farrar is confusing in lectures but recitations help you understand the material.

Awesome teacher, very helpful and caring.  I struggled through the first test, but then went to his office hours regularly, and pulled off a good grade.  Definitely go see him after exams, he will do what he can to find you an extra few points!!!

Very nice and extremely helpful. Take the advice and go over all your tests with him afterwards! Who knows, there might be an error or two in your favor! TOUGH exams! He does hold review sessions and stays until you exhaust the questions tho!
A-mazing.  He is an awesome prof and really helpful. take the time to go over your tests with him...its worth is.  hes also a snazzy dresser.
Good teacher at first then lost his love for the students and killed wveryone in the final. Very disappointed at him.
This man and Professor Krugh are practically the same.  They are both the top 2 nicest people in the entire country.  But man, do they give tough exams.  Farrar is tough if you never took AP Chem.
good professor
I find his teaching very good. I pay attention and actually stay awake.
No Comments

At first I thought he was great because he wrote his notes on the board and that forces me to take notes/learn better.  However, he spends a majority of his time derriving equations and going into irrelevant facts that further confuse people.  Going to class was a waste, he never taught us how to do problems.  Use the textbook, Zumdahl is the man.
Interesting class, nice guy. Knows a lot and is not afraid to share it.
Boring as hell. The man makes the same jokes repeatedly and is totally dry. God did not grant him the gift of speaking at all.

I can't believe people are giving Farrar good grades.  He is the worst professor I had so far in my college career.  The dude DOES NOT teach anything.  We'll come to recitation and we'll see stuff we've never seen before that we were supposed to have learned in class.  He's horrible.
the class is long and boring...so sometimes i doze off....but it always leads to a sticky situation....the man is soo hot that i cant help but want him...wet dreams are dangerous in class fyi

lectures are boing and he tends to do a lot of unnecessary algebra with equations.  however, he does tend to crack some jokes and loves "liquid water"...  sit in the back of class and make your own jokes to make note-taking bearable.  he's a cool enough guy, though, i guess...
Jimbo is the man.  He is a great professor and an awesome guy.  Sometimes lecture can be a bit dry, but when he cracks a joke its worth it.
He is always willing to help. His classes are kind of dry, but he is a very kind teacher. And a very kind grader.

All around, he is not that bad of a professor. Disorganized at times, but a few minutes at his office hours can clear up any questions. He gives lots of practice problems (and answers) before every test, that are very similar to the actual test questions. The notes are very thorough and the papers are really easy.
Very disorganized, no idea what he's teaching in the class. The exams are not consistent with course materials. Terrible experience. My sincere advice - avoid him at all cost.

This guy has no idea what he's teaching. He actually does not know the class material and makes mistakes every 5 minutes. He is most definitely not qualified to teach and should not be allowed to teach this class. Do not take his classes. Naturally his notes are completely useless as well.
Highly quantitative mixed with a very dry professor. Tough class with some exam questions unrelated to the course material.

Yes, he reads off slides and his lectures aren't too helpful. But he is very accessible outside of class, is quite good at helping individually, and is very enthusiastic. Depending on the class, homework may be difficult, but exams and quizzes are always written easily and he grades quite leniently. Far from your worst choice for a professor.

Probably the worst lectures I have been to for any class. Uses slides which are copy and paste from the textbook and somehow explains the concepts worse than the textbook does. If he picks up chalk the rating could definitely be higher.
bad at lecturing. for a heavy calc class, he just reads powerpoint slides. its identical to highlighting and selecting text to speech. has never picked up chalk.

ASTR111 is one of my favorite class! The professor is really interesting and fun to talk with. He gives helpful advice, is patient, and always willing to guide you through the assignments or chat more about astronomy! The homework is hard, so you need to put time to it. He do speaks a bit soft during lectures, but overall, it's a great class!
He was very helpful when it came to assignments and talked about the lore behind subjects not just the content itself. Also is ALWAYS fitted up. Overall 10/10 for the suits

Dan Watson is a beautiful human being. His lectures can be a little boring, but his passion for the topic of astronomy and his amazing suits make lecture worth it. The grading of exams is extremely fair as Dan looks for any excuse to give partial credit. All around an amazing person, I cannot recommend taking him enough.

Dan Watson is an amazing professor. ASTR 111 is challenging, but he grades kindly. If you put the work in you'll learn a LOT. Watson is really kind, helpful in office hours, and always willing to chat about astronomy. He wrote me rec letters and connected me with alumni in the field I want to go into. Top tier professor, I hope I have him again.

Very enjoyable professor, he makes lots of funny quips and he's very interesting. He does spend a lot of time explaining math that isn't exactly relevant and you do have to go back into the slides to understand a lot of things, but the website and slides are laid out very well

I believe the homeworks were a bit difficult, and they do take a lot of time and work, but I really enjoy Watson as a person and overall as a teacher. He is very helpful and wonderful to talk to during office hours (oftentimes he even gives cookies!). Sometimes I did get sleepy during his lectures, but I really did learn a lot!
Love his class. Great guy, very accessible, and surprisingly funny during lectures. Also, the suits are impeccable.

If Dan Watson has 10,000 fans I'm one of them. If Dan Watson has 100 fans I'm one of them. If Dan Watson has one fan it's me. If Dan Watson has no fans I'm no longer alive. If the world is against Dan Watson I am against the world. 
This man's style is IMPECCABLE, also he is super forgiving with extensions and very available outside class.
Love
Very passionate about teaching astronomy and has easy-to-follow lectures. Would recommend taking the class

If you don't have a science background I would not take this class unless you're willing to work. He goes into extreme specifics that you don't need to know for tests, and the tests are on webwork which sucks. Go to lecture and recitation, and DO THE PRACTICE TESTS, half the questions are on the real tests. He's very passionate and a great lecturer

I cannot believe that my 70,000 dollar a year tuition is going towards this man attempt to teach me physics. Every time I went to lecture I left even more confused than I started. He never responded to emails, tests were insanely hard (over half the class failed his second midterm). His class was harder than the honors version of the same class.

Dan is really bad at conveying any idea to students. He also makes you feel dumb for asking questions and gets some weird joy out of assigning homework questions that even the TAs can't solve. He's also just an all around jerk.

-Assigns homework due the day before a midterm (only two midterms in the class) -Tries teaching Calc-based Physics through powerpoint -Never has homework due on the same day every week (could be Monday, Wednesday, or Friday. You never know) -Tries writing his own homework problems that even the TAs can't solve

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Since day one he threw equations that were not explained at us. He knows the course but does not teach it well at all. Does not take into consideration the fact that this is most people's first time dealing with this subject. If possible take this class with someone else or at another place.

He is smart but he does not have the slightest clue on how to teach. He is completely out of touch and teaches a class that clearly requires someone to do out problems by hand, with lecture slides. He is horrible at teaching PHY122. He know the material but does not understand that the people he is teaching may be seeing this for the first time.

I'm not a science person. At all. I heard this class required little math -- not so much. There is Web Work involved. T.A.'s aren't that helpful. Lectures can be confusing/boring, but his eccentricities make them bearable.

Dan Watson is funny, smart, and adorably nerdy. He loves what he is doing and does his best to help students. I learned more in Astro 142 from him than in any of my subsequent classes in higher level astronomy. Only thing to beware of are magically appearing variables in his powerpoint slides.

He may well be the least helpful person on the face of the earth. More than half the class had issues taking a test on webwork and he told us that we probably did something wrong. Oh, he also says "Uh" or "Um" between every word and moves his arms like a penguin.

He knows that most people in the class are only there because of requirements, and he makes it VERY easy to get an A.  The lectures are generally boring / sometimes incomprehensible, yet he is very helpful if you have questions outside of lecture.

I could NOT stay awake during his lectures.  He seems like a nice guy, but when I tried to introduce myself it was awkward; I never talked to him again.  His lecture notes don't make sense unless you hear the lecture.  The homework isn't hard, but the tests are tricky.  He knows what he's talking about, but he's not very fun to listen to.

Lectures are pretty boring, but he teaches well nonetheless. The test is based entirely on lecture, so the book is really just for your own use. The powerpoints usually don't make sense unless you hear him explain them, so you need to go to class most of the time.

Actually, he's a nice guy outside of class and sometimes makes more sense if you go to him for help.  But the class is very dull.  He just reads from powerpoints and puts you to sleep.  Lots of equations, naturally.  But his powerpoints are not very good at explaining things.  And the book is rarely any help, though it can be amusing.

Prof. Ahmed is honestly the GOAT! Not only is she extremely well-versed and passionate about what she is teaching, but she takes the time to listen to student feedback and actually incorporate it into her teaching style. Exams are open-note and full access, but you really still need to engage with the course to do well on them.
Professor Ahmed is one of the best professors at this school. She loves anthropology and really cares about her students, giving engaging assignments but never overloads you.
Absolutely lovely and the most understanding professor ever, she's also really passionate about what she teaches and makes classes really engaging.

Dr. Ahmed is very understanding and wants you to succeed in the course. She's very helpful and caring. She makes things easy to grasp and she is passionate about her studies, classes, and research. She is fantastic.
She is such a great professor!!!!!!!!!!
U of R needs more professors like Dr Ahmed.

GREAT professor!! She's incredibly passionate about medical anthropology so all of her lectures are well planned out and thought provoking. I've learned SO much in this class. She really cares about her students! This class is definitely worth taking especially if your pre-med or biomedical engineering!

Professor Ahmed is hands down the best professor I have come across in my college career. She is caring, wants all students to succeed, and is passionate about her field. If you happen to take an anthropology class, make it one of hers. She may even convince you to change your major!

She is a great professor! She is so passionate about the field she studies. She is also very patient and caring to students. Her classes are not lecture-heavy. There will be group discussions every class. The class will just have two open book tests and one final essay, but she is not a tough grader. Definitely will take her course again.
The lectures are basically watching youtube videos or documentaries. The 1 project was fun, but lectures are extremely boring and it's mainly focused on classical music.

yea grading is harsh. and the course should be called: experience Dr. Harman's music. You either get A or B(with just a single mistake you make on the exam) make you go to concert and unclear what he wants you to know.
If you are in his orchestra, you are more likely to get a good grade in this course.

Dr. Harman is a really amazing conductor.  He tells jokes, gets everyone involved and expects you to give your best everyday.  Because of his high expectations, he may seem arrogant, but he really just realizes everyone's true potential and strives to bring that out every day.

I don't agree with the previous posts. I took Harman's Symphony and the Conductor class and I loved it. Harman is just very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about music so he may seem arrogant, but he's really only passionate about what he does.   For MUR 121 he teaches with more of a discussion-based style rather than a lecture which was great!
he's not the usual conductor, but he knows his stuff and he's enthusiastic
i agree with the people who have called him arrogant. his grade scheme is such that 1 point off on any assignment is 1% off your semester grade. the assignments are also unclear and pointless.
agreed with previous post (4/28)
One of the most arrogant jerks I've ever met.  Fails to realize he's not at Eastman.

Harman is arrogant and not helpful. He makes you go to the concerts he conducts so he can brag about it the next week in class. The only bright spot was the TA, David Plylar, who was very helpful and nice.

Professor Heidi is seriously one of the nicest and most caring professors I've ever had. The textbook is tough, but she gives lots of extra credit and her practice exams are super similar to the real ones. She replies to emails fast and is always happy to help with anything. She's exactly a humorous and patient professor.

She's exactly a humorous and patient professor.
This class made me want to drop out of my program. It was very hard. I ended up skipping class becuase she moved too fast and did not answer questions well.

she tends to go off on tangents about her boat and kids. shes very nice but is not scared to show her anger in front of everyone. she reads off of her slides and only sometimes does she add anything to them while lecturing, lectures are recorded. shes the only one that teaches 224/5 so youre stuck with her. talks pretty slow
I loved this professor! Great Classes very caring and explains things really really well

She is the only professor that teaching intermediate acc 1 and 2 so you should get used to her, she goes off topic a lot, tells stories about her boat and kids, and laughs at her own jokes. she is very accessible outside of class, 3 homework assignments and you have to work in a group. first midterm is hard, second and final are okay.

I enjoyed being in Heidi's class just about as much as she enjoyed teaching it. Which is to say, Not at all. I second other comments about the fact that she plays favorites. You can clearly tell that she does not want to be teaching, and takes out her stress on students.

comment: i went to her office hours to see my test and she was very mean to me

Heidi is the BEST accounting professor I have ever had. She is incredibly smart and so nice. She is willing to help you out with WHATEVER you need. She has even helped me prepare for interviews before! I am better prepared for my job because Heidi has taught me so much. You do have to work hard for a good grade, but it's so worth it!

Great professor teaching a rather dry topic. Her exams are fair and the homework can be daunting, but she encourages you to solicit feedback from her and your assigned teammates. Do the work, get a good grade; it's as simple as that. Respectful of the fact that working adults are taking graduate classes. Highly recommended!

She is a great professor and provides all the material you need in lecture and online but it's very heavy.  She does not curve any tests or homework or offer any extra credit so your grade is your raw score.  Because of that there is no way to recover if you do poorly on a test or homework and many people have been known to take ACC201 twice.
Too much materials covered

She likes to play favorites, if you're on her good side you're good; if not, she will be rude to you. She screamed at me once during a midterm when I asked for clarification. Her lectures are okay, but filled with material. She assumes you can understand something in 1 second. Please take Prema Iyer instead, she's absolutely amazing!
Wonderful professor. She wants to teach anyone who wants to learn.
Great professor, is willing to help you if you put in the effort. Very funny and great person.
She makes the lectures fun.
She is tough but will give you all the help you need. As long as you do all of the work, the class isn't bad
She can't stop making unfunny stories. Her exams are really though, and she crams the class to the brim with material.

LOTS of reading, but class was never boring. Professor Rozenski is an engaging and interesting professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about classical + scriptural literature, as well as music, medieval Europe, baking, Internet culture, and more. Quizzes and responses are easy to do well on, and everything's graded very leniently.

Very passionate and has great suits, and overall a super nice guy. I can't say I found old english particularly riveting, but he made me want to come to class and participate, plus there were plenty of extra credit opportunities despite the quizzes being difficult!

this guy made my whole year so much better. i always looked forward to going to this class and honestly it gave me the will to start trying again in school. smart, interesting, kind, hilarious. makes everything interesting. the course material was fascinating and he made everything so exciting and engaging!! my favorite class i have  taken here.

Prof. Rozenski is by far my favorite professor I've had thus far. Super smart guy who knows his stuff, but makes every class really fun and engaging. Lots of reading, but totally worth it to get to talk about it in class. Manages to make tests fun. He's also great with communication outside of class via email if extenuating circumstances come up.

From a STEM major with clustering in classic literature, Rozenski is awesome. He's extraordinarily knowledgeable and receptive to literally any opinion on any topic related to the readings at hand and willing to discuss it seriously. I learned a lot about literary criticism and left the course feeling like I gained something I didn't have before.

Although he's a funny and overall nice person, Prof. Rozenski is not a good professor. I didn't learn anything in his class, and when it came time to write the midterm and final papers, I really struggled. Be prepared to read A TON! We read 100+ pages for each class and 1800 lines of Middle English. Essays are HARD. Class has no structure at all.
Good lectures, easy to pass. Make sure to participate and show up in class, because he grades a lot based off of that.
Adorable. What a great guy.

Wonderful professor and human being--we had to read the frickin BIBLE and he made it entertaining. You can do traditional response papers or creative responses which is always fun. You do have to read a lot, but he does a good job prepping you for the quizzes with study guides. Oh, and he's adorable.

Rozenski is amazing. He's the funniest professor I've ever had, and he genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is also creative and flexible with the lectures and assignments and does his best to make sure that everything is clear and fair. 12/10

comment: Lovely person, but poor professor. By the end of the semester, nobody wanted to raise their hands for discussions because she would always interrupt them to make her own point. It was less a discussion class than a lecture class listed as discussion heavy. She grades at a level much higher than undergraduate, so if you take this class, be prepared.

While she knows what she's talking about and is passionate about the material, it's difficult to participate in discussion as she doesn't leave space for discussion on average when she is lecturing. Tough grader for papers and leaves lots of constructive criticism. However, I've found she's pretty kind and with it.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I hate her...tough grader for real and she gives vague instructions on her criteria of paper...She said she's liberal but if your idea violates w her central beliefs...be ready for a B and less...She also interrupts when students talk, like a lot of times...

This professor is BORING. All she does is read off of a sheet of paper for the whole class. You will read 100-200 pgs for hw per class. She grades REALLY tough and writes very critical responses to students' papers. The essay exam is ridiculously hard and you have two other long papers. She requires participation but interrupts when students talk.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Professor London is absolutely amazing. She genuinely cares about her students succeeding and learning. I had one 6 page paper where she left well over a hundred comments. She' super knowledgeable and smart, but she's also very approachable for her students. You will read a fair amount, but I didn't find it unmanageable as long as I planned ahead.
Learned a lot about literary elements. This professor is dedicated and passionate about her material.
Great lecturer and promoter of discussion. She is a tough but fair grader with plenty of constructive criticism. Would recommend!
Prof London is a passionate, intelligent woman who leaves room for discussion while also managing to teach new material at the same time. she is by far the best english teacher I'ver ever had.

Professor London was great! Her class was very discussion based, and she is a tough grader when it comes to written papers. However, she wants you to succeed and grades fairly and takes improvement into consideration. She is very helpful outside of class during office hours. Would highly recommend!

I loved this class. The books were great, and Professor London really contributed to my understanding of them. The writing assignments really made you think, but it challenged me and my writing has greatly improved since I've really learned what makes the difference between an A- and an A paper.

I have had Dr. London for two classes and I really enjoyed both. The entire class is discussion based, so pretty much everyone is forced to get involved. The books she assigned were excellent; she had a lot of good insight to share during class. Also, when you ask for help, she is more than willing to give you a hand, and is very encouraging.

Excellent teacher, she was very helpful with helping papers, more interested in making sure students learned than paper grades (allowed revisions and went over papers with students). She will ask for input in her classes, but doesn't call on anyone. Good class.
Very interested in what she teaches and very intelligent. Understanding and easy to talk to. Great prof. overall.

Very easy class to sit in and not pay attention if you want to...but if you want to participate, its really difficult because she likes to talk. Very opinionated. If you are writing something she disagrees with (shes liberal), she will say your argument is weak (even if paper, truthfully, is good). Annoying mannerisms - including stutter.
She fabulous, encouraging, insightful. She provides feedback and helpful comments and she kept me incredibly interested.

I think Prof. London gives incredibly comprehensive and high-quality feedback on students' papers, something I often find lacking from other professors.  She's kind, sympathetic and very insightful.  I've learned a great deal from her classes and talking with her during office hours etc.
had her for contemporary women writers. it drove me crazy listening to her speak. she said nothing of importance. i watched the clock that entire class...books were decent though.

Woah, I think it's pretty extreme to transfer because of ONE teacher in ONE class. I found Professor London clear, interested in the material and organized in leading discussions. She let you revise papers and books assigned were varied and enjoyable.

I had London last fall and I never knew this website existed until now,  and I am so glad because I feel it is necessary to tell people just how awful this professor was! I have transferred schools because of the poor experience I had with this professor!
One of the best professors that I have had, very knowledgable in his field. I would defiantly recommend you take his class!!
very fake person. exams are terrible.
he's so slay. 10/10 would recommend.

Overall, this was a good course and Professor White was an excellent professor. Not a harsh grader, and very accessibly outside of class time. In-class questions were answered well also. I would recommend
sucks

To all ChemEs taking this class: push thru it, you'll never need it again or have to deal with such a rude professor

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor White is great! His lectures are so useful, and he is also really funny!
The contents of this course is useful. I wish this course was taught by a different professor.

Professor White always wants to teach as much content as possible in his courses. The syllabus updates constantly each year to match some state of the arts tools used in the computational field. But, if you don't have any programming background, you'll struggle in this course cause they are not taught during class.

Professor White is truly outstanding. He sets you up for success in his class. As the student, you have a full control over 60% of your course grade -- homework, project etc (he might/might not change this in the future). Exams are worth only 40% total. He even texted me while I was out of town to make sure that my question was answered.

Does not know how to interact well with students. If you ask a basic question to him, he appears frustrated and impatient. The school should just hire an actual compsci professor for this requirement, as this professor is disliked by the vast majority of ChE students for obvious reasons.

All the lecture notes are posted online and very organized, so it's easy to access them for the homework. There is a lot of homework, but it usually reinforces concepts well so that you can be prepared for the midterm and final. He could improve on how he explains concepts because he often repeats himself instead of explaining things in a new way.

Extremely rude professor and condescending. Not even the suck ups in the class like this professor or thinks he is actually funny. Does not respond to slack messages and needs to reevaluate some of the TAs for this course. Some of the TAs need a serious course in the basics of respect.
Worst class I have ever taken. A lot of material is stuffed into one semester and the class is not taught well and it in general is confusing. Final was absurd. Barely a curve at the end- good luck.

White puts all his lecture notes online so attendance isn't necessary. He basically just reads through the notes for class. He passes on a lot of questions he gets to TAs and has them teach and give most of the examples in recitation. Upside is the final is open everything so you can look through all the notes.

It was his first class as a new professor at UofR, and so some parts were rocky. He got much better at lecturing and connecting with the students throughout the semester. His homework sets are tough but the exams are easy if you've done all your assignments. He is totally reachable and cares about you learning how to program in Python.

This was the first class he ever taught. He improved greatly throughout the semester. Keys to succeed in this class: Go over the lecture notes until you understand them, do all the homeworks, go to office hours when confused. Class uses Python programming so experience with this helps.

Super nice, he let me rewrite my final paper and even told me specifically what book to check out and use a source for my paper. Goes off on tangents about his experiences with certain cathedrals; can be boring if you're not reallllly interested in the subject. Lets class out early in the fall when it's hot (average of 20 minutes earlier).

Walsh reminds me of everyone's favorite grandfather. He occasionally rants and rambles about something vaguely related, but is extremely knowledgeable, and passionate about his classes. There are only 3 papers of average length and he's not the strictest grader, cares more for ideas presented than the manner of presentation. Amazing class.

An interesting course. Walsh makes it very easy to succeed. He is flexible with extensions and edits drafts. Entire grade is three 4-6 page papers. Get a seat at the front, take good notes and don't miss a class and you'll do fine. He seems like a very jolly old man. I plan to take more classes with him!

Prof Walsh is a very nice man, but I found his lectures rather boring, and since there were no exams (only three 5-page papers), attending class was unnecessary. The notes I took in class were not helpful to me. Despite my spotty class attendance, however, I got an A in the course - so either I'm an excellent writer or he's an easy grader!

Walsh is very nice, passionate and knowledgeable about his field, and really wants to help students succeed. He's very soft-spoken so try to grab a front seat. Sometimes his lectures are dry and boring, follow his train of though. Tangents a lot :) This class was graded on 3 short paper (4-6 pgs) - a GPA booster if writing is your strength.
Have taken multiple classes with Walsh all of them easy. You have to write 3 5page papers. Lectures are a little dry but tangents are good. He loves what he does and its evident

Reall nice guy, sometimes a little bit boring, but very passionate about the subject.  You can tell he really loves to teach it.  Just 3 papers which you have to put in good work on to get a good grade.  I learned a lot in the class and it wasn't too difficult.
He's an ok teacher, a little boring at times and a little weird but what can you expect from an AH teacher?

I personally never found a dull moment in this class.  Something amusing always seemed to happen.  My only complaint is that while Walsh was soft spoken and polite in class, I sometimes found him difficult to approach, though he was very accessible to students.

An enjoyable class if you sit up front and can hear him, maybe it was just the room, but you really had to strain to hear him talk, shows way too many art slides (ok i know he does art history) but this is just a history course. I went to every class took great notes, yet i still felt i didnt know much for the papers. Still expecting an A though.

Very knowledgable and the course is interesting. He welcomes questions and concerns from students and makes a point to make himself available. The work is some what demanding but quite rewarding. Walsh is an excellent professor and would suggest taking any of his other courses.
Professor Walsh is extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and entertaining.  I highly recommend any of his classes.
The most boring class of my life!

This class was painfully boring! It had such potential and he ruined it. It's entirely lecture, and he really knows his stuff but shows no enthusiasm. He's a nice guy, but I would rather be one of those artifacts buried in the dirt wasting away than to sit through another one of his classes.
Professor Walsh is extremely entertaining and definitely knows his materials.  His classes are always enjoyable.
Dummit is a great person, who provides detailed notes for the class and excellent lectures.
Such an inspirational, funny, and intelligent professor! He is very helpful, and you can tell that he wants his students to do well.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Hilarious']
comment: He is such a funny guy! I love that he gives an opportunity to make up for a bad midterm grade by doing well on the final. He is very helpful during his office hours. Just overall a great professor and the lectures were very enjoyable (he always gave out candy too! )
COME TO CLASS AND PASS

Professor Dummit is an amazing lecturer! He explains difficult concepts very clearly and often in a humorous way. He is also very willing to help us outside of class. I will definitely continue taking his class. Who does not like a professor who brings his students candies and brownies every class after all.

He is such a fun teacher! He gives out candy in most of his classes and is a hilarious dude. He is also such a good teacher and a genius! I wish he would stay next semester because he made calculus so fun! Don't hesitate to take a class with him.
A very fun and easygoing professor. He is always willing to help on both email and office hours.

I loved my multi-dimensional calculus course with Professor Dummit.  He is an excellent teacher with a knack for explaining and demonstrating mathematical concepts.  His lecture notes for the course were also outstanding; they can almost replace the textbook.
A laid back but very clear and concise professor, understands his students, and has a nice dry sense of humor!

Professor Dummit is the BEST!!! I took his Number Theory class. And although I signed up late to the class, he was very successful in preparing me through the process of learning the material. Also, HIS NOTES ARE AMAZING! My suggestion is dont buy any textbook or something, just refer to his notes if you need help. In conclusion, he is the BEST!

Clear and concise. Said on the first day of class that you wouldn't need the textbook as long as you paid attention in lecture and he was 100% right. Very intelligent, clearly knows his stuff. Prepares you well for tests, is respectful of student questions. Dry sense of humor is a bonus.

The best of the best for number theory lectures. Very honest and in touch with the learning process of upper level math students. Will publish lecture notes which are as good if not better than any textbook.

Fantastic professor. He's clear, helpful, and posts concise course notes online. Available for help if you need it. Responds to emails very quickly. Very intelligent. Textbook not necessary because of the TeX course notes he types.

She can be a bit more organized in explaining the assignments because she doesn't have clear rubrics or guidelines. However, her class is informative and very fun. She brought in food for us as well. Very sweet and caring professor.
Great professor, lots of readings but the material isn't bad. If you attend the class and do most of the readings, you will be fine.

Professor Ball's class expanded my interest in history through her extensive knowledge on a continent that isn't informationally accessible (due to its comprehensive history and culture). She made the class not only enjoyable but digestible. Recommend both the course and the professor!

She's one of the best professors I've taken so far. Although the class involved a lot of reading (from her "moderate selection" of books), a lot of the information comes from a high school U.S. History class. She could be a little more transparent on what she wants in an assignment, but she's approachable and wants the best for everyone.
Molly was awesome! Great teacher, rally cares.

comment: Really nice class. Indeed, NOT a trustworthy person. He will say one thing to your face, then act like he never said it. He will even say that what you said isn't true, and he is very careful about what he puts in writing. You can learn a lot from him if you are willing to ignore the constant condescending remarks.
One of my favorite professors ever! Gives extremely clear explanations and challenges students. Enjoyable if you are enthusiastic about the subject.
I wouldn't characterize him as a trustworthy person.

One of the best professors I've taken at UofR. The lectures are compelling, office hours are helpful, and the professor is an expert in the field. But the class is hard. He moves through content quickly and it's easy to get lost.
5 homeworks, 1 exam, 5–10 pop quizzes total. Lectures not recorded. Posted slide decks are sparse, so go to lecture.

Ralf can seem intimidating, but is actually a really nice guy. I chose to have him as my advisor. This was by far the most practical class I took as an undergrad. It seemed that many things I had learned in the past came into an alignment, and that I was in the right place. I would highly recommend it for anyone interested in doing research.
She's one of the best professors in the language department!!! She's super caring and tries to make the class engaging!

I like her, but she kind of has a boring way of teaching. 80% of her classes are just "Talk to the person next to you about the current topic" or "Give your answers to the reading guides." Fair warning the readings can be super dense and quite violent. Also SPAN 200 feels more like a literature class than a composition class

Professor Alfaro is such a kind and understanding person. Attendance is graded, but if you email her and have good reason to miss class, she will not penalize you. There are good opportunities for extra credit, and the tests are straight forward and easy as long as you actually engage in class. There is very minimal homework, and it is all easy.

Professor Alfaro is the nicest professor I have had at the U of R by far. Although I am only in my second year, I don't know if I will have a professor that I will enjoy more than her during the rest of my tenure. Although her lectures can be a tad slow or boring sometimes, she always finds ways to keep us engaged and she wants you to succeed.
Best professor in the languages department!

The best professor ever in the university. I took this class as my second foreign language so this course is pretty intense and covers a lot of material. However, she's just so nice to provide extra help I need and office hours to go over my questions. You need to spend a lot of time ready for oral and other exams. But you will learn a lot!

It was a little bit more work than I expected for a two credit class, but Amy was super chill and caring. I think she is done teaching now but I really enjoyed class with her. She was very down to Earth. She did sort of grade the final project harder than I was expecting. Also her class I a little disorganized.

Don't pick her if you can't handle her energy. I don't know how to describe it but she kinda has like sassy girlboss humor. She's the director of the Speaking Fellows, so she gives pretty good advice when it comes to dialogue and self-image. Yeah, the class is a lot of work, but you can't really blame the professor for that. Blame the department.

Seems nice, but is a unreasonable amount of work for a 2 credit class. Harsher grading than necessary. Was sick halfway through the semester and had some late assignments and it hurt my GPA for no reason. If you are busy and don't have the time to do the excessive amount of work, def take it with someone else as there are many prof who teach it

There's a good amount of work in this class, but its like any other college class, difficult and long! Amy is easily one of the best professors i have ever had, she is funny, kind, and someone who can be there for you!! Amy ily

Amy is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so kind and very thoughtful to all her students. The work in class is sometimes hard and can feel overwhelming, but she is really supportive and has many great pointers and tips for doing your best!

I did not prepare for a bunch of work that was needed to be done for a 2-credit course. Amy's lectures are full of fun, and she is a good professor herself. However, she is not a good grader, and the criteria is kinda misleading.
Love her she's the best. Took her for the Taylor Swift writing class. Super engaging and funny. Super understanding, just communicate with her. Really fair grader, not hard to do well in her class.

Amy is a great professor at UofR! If you have the opportunity to take a class with her do it! She is so funny and really cares about her students. There are lots of readings for the class, but they are fun and work well with discussions. OYS!

Amy is a great professor! Class was pretty easy and she gives thorough feedback. You could get away without doing the readings. Some of the assignments were corny, ngl. Peer review and discussion are huge so be prepared for that! Amy is super lenient on deadlines and she cares about her students a lot.
I LOVE AMY. She's so kind, so helpful, and so funny.

If you have the opportunity to take a class taught by Amy, jump at it! She is so engaging, funny, and well-spoken, and the class materials might be lengthy, but the discussions make up for it. Amy really cares about her students, and making her courses as perfect as they can be. Feedback is a major theme in this course; peer review is huge!

Amy's Wrt 273 class was great. She always balanced relevant advice instruction with funny stories about her kids. Some of the assignments felt a bit cheesy, but choosing a real reader was a great part of the course, and she was always around to help with resumes and cover letters.

Amy is the best professor! She gave lots of good feedback and taught you lots of good writing strategies. The reading may indeed be overwhelming, but it is all worth after since it is so helpful. It is not an easy A, but it is definitely the class you can learn lots of things that can apply to your future writing. Take her class!
