comment: Dr. Chin is a very good prof. She is empathetic and caring of her students. She is also very passionate about her field. The textbook largely covers the same points she does in lecture. However, attending lecture is crucial, as some points come from the in-class quizzes and the class itself is not curved and graded by few things.

Dr. Chin is perhaps the best professor I have had yet at U of R. She is very empathetic and the coursework is definitely interesting. One thing for sure is that the class is graded by a few things and it is pretty hard to secure an A. She definitely sparked my interest in public health and the guest lectures are also very interesting.

Prof. Chin is a respectable, kind, and knowledgeable professor. She really cares about student's mental health and values our needs. The guest speakers she brings in are actually really interesting and relevant to coursework.The short in class writing assignments and blog posts are rather simple-just make sure your points are clear.Learned a lot!

Dr. Chin is one of the few professors at the UofR that genuinely cares about their students well-being outside of class. She takes time every lecture to check in with how we're doing, and always makes herself available for help. Dr. Chin is the reason I decided to become a Public Health major, and has inspired me in so many other ways.

Dr. Chin is an incredible professor, and the material in this class is fascinating! The emphasis is placed on applying material to help be a more informed, conscientious, serve-minded, global citizen. The class itself is not very stressful which makes it a much better environment to truly learn and apply the material. I would recommend to anyone!

Dr. Chin was great. She takes the time to know each of her students and cares about them. There are only two tests for the semester, and a really awesome group project. Her class was very interesting and engaging. She loves to challenge her students to think in real world scenarios. If I could, I would take this class again!
One of my favorite professors at UR! Very nice person and a great lecturer. Got me interested in public health!

Nancy is an excellent professor-one of the best at UR.  Her passion for public health really shows-and inspires.  I can honestly say that I am a public health major because of her.  Take her class if you have the chance!

Very interesting class and a great introduction to the world of public health. Class was almost always discussion based. Do the readings - helps you understand material. One very easy exam and one very hard exam. Go to class - if you do, you won't have to study much outside of class. Lectures are helpful. Chin is VERY SMART! Great guest speakers!
She is great. Very easy to understand and really makes public health fun.

PH 101 is by far the best class that I have taken at the U of R.  Prof Chin is not only a professor but also a mentor for students in public health.  She is approachable and extremely helpful.  She is also probably my favorite professor also.  She makes public health exciting, fun, and unforgetable.  I would take seriously any class she taught.

Prof. Chin is the greatest professor I've ever had. She is thought-provoking and wise, and she pushes students to think 'outside the box.' Inspiring and wonderful, she has changed the way I look at health, behavior, and society in almost every way. Not to mention, she's a total badass. I would take twenty courses with Prof. Chin if I could.

Difficult course, incredibly kind and caring professor.

Prof Nyibule is a pretty cool guy. Dr. Nyibule was amazing. He was very understanding and if you have issues with ANYTHING he helps you out. I struggled in Physics but he was also very understanding with grading and lays it out very clearly what will be on each exam. Amazing curve and is always available to help

Good, can speak kind of quietly though

Dr. Nyibule was one of the best professors I ever had. He is so incredibly caring for his students, having office hours every day of the week. He is such a caring person through and through.
Sheth is awesome! Super understanding. He assigns a lot of work but it helps with repetition. Material is hard but he is very approachable.

Def one of the best at UR! Sheth's truly a kind-hearted individual who wants you to succeed. He gives tons of extra credit, makes content understandable for those with no physics experience, and gives the fairest exams ever. He's very available for office hrs and actively encourages students who are struggling to talk to him. Highly recommend!

SHETH IS THE GOAT. It's obvious that he cares about his students and enjoys teaching, but sometimes it can feel a bit fast and the test questions can be pretty different from lecture ones. I had Professor Nyibule for PHYS 121. Lectures covered all the main points comprehensively in a manner easy to understand. The Professor is kind and accessible during office hours. Tests for the class were easy if you do the practice problems in lecture and the homework problems.
I took his class for a requirement even though it is not my strongest subject. He was very kind and helpful outside of class. The class was organized.

I am not good at physics but Dr. Nyibule was able to help me after class to pull off that A-. There are plenty of resources available to do well, but I will admit it is a pretty time intensive course, at least for me. Gives iClicker quizzes during class which count for your grade so make sure to show up.
I took PHY 113 over the summer with Dr. Nyibule and had a great experience! He cares about students and wants to help them succeed. Very kind and a good lecturer.

I did not like the fact that he made us pay for a subscription for iClicker quizzes, but besides that I have no complaints. Definitely talk to hm after class about questions you have, it will be helpful. Go through all the textbook problems and do the previous exams and you should do ok. I had to work hard for my grade, but it's doable.

She really tries to drive her point across in this well designed introductory course. She makes a good effort to remember everyone's names. The required readings are really interesting. She's very knowledgeable and helpful if you're willing to ask for assistance

The only thing worse than this professor's rote, pedantic teaching style was the oblivious, green-lantern t-shirt wearing TA, Greg Fowler.

she's smart so you can't **** your way through this 101 class...so in a sense I feel like this class is pretty rough for a 101 class - not an easy A. awful class

Tries to show off, you don't learn anything in class, tests are very hard, no clear grading criteria, horrible teacher. Such a waste of time.

He is not a good teacher. He likes to show off and doesnt teach anything substantial for the exams. He shows up late to office hours all the time. He is mean too. His exams are impossible and he does not prepare you for them. He throws new things at you he didnt teach.

BEST PROF HERE! His lectures are unconventional, although they are the most interesting. It feels like you are learning by going through a journey. Everyone needs to take one of his classes.

Absolutely amazing lectures. Made me very interested in eastern philosophy. Can't wait to take other classes taught by him.

You'd be crazy not to take his classes! He knows what education is really about, and if you find it incomprehensible it is only your own understanding which must be opened and revitalized.

Brooks is one of the most inspirational teachers I ever had.  He is an amazing asset to the University.

Prof. Huang is the best professor I've ever met in my life! He's amazing! Thanks to his early class on Monday, I was motivated to get up every Monday. He has a good sense of humor, his teaching content is very clear and easy to understand, and he is very patient to answer any questions raised by students. He made me fall in love with programming!

AHH-MAZING. Passionate, intelligent lecturer, makes class super interesting. Very flexible, wants to help students succeed. An expert in the field and has worked with many of public health leaders. No other course/professor at U of R has been more eye opening and increased my interest in a subject as much as TB.

I took both 116& his 373 with professor Brown.Although his lectures are clear, the courses he teaches are repetitive in nature. As well, he is not open minded. Ph 116 wasn't bad since the TAs did half the grading but HIS 373, the average grades were B-/C+ on essay assignments. Would not recommend, I changed my major from HLP to Econ because of him.
He is very passionate about the problems of the U.S. health system. I enjoy his lecturing style, even though it can be hard to follow for taking notes. Exams are fair.

I would not suggest this class to anybody who is open minded and doesn't want to hear only a lecture of opinions and one side of a every issue covered.  The class was not very difficult and the homework was not necessary to get a good grade, but I wish I hadn't taken this class.

Ted Brown is a great lecturer, advisor and professor.  While he does tend to express his opinion moreso than exploring both sides to an argument he also includes valuable facts and information.  I took more away from his class than the majority of the core PH requirements.  I would definitely suggest taking 116

The only way to succeed in this class is to have great notes, and since Brown only lectures, you're going to be seriously lacking if you don't go to class. He's a great lecturer, but the classroom (B&L 106) is warm and I actually fell asleep a few times. I did the readings, and even after missing sections a day, I managed an A. I reccommend HIS 287

Grading is very arbitrary and has three different graders so there is no form of standardization. Point system is ridiculous since one ends up receiving scores like 4.3 and 3.65 for short answers. How such numbers are reached is beyond me. Very spirited in lecture but lectures are one-sided and should not be taught that way.

The worst class I have ever taken. I had heard he was an excellent lecturer and, to be fair, his lectures were fairly engaging. However, I have never sat through a more one-sided class. The class is 90 percent HIS opinion so if you came to college to learn, I do not recommend Ted Brown.

Professor Brown is very expressive! I like his lecture style, he's never boring and has a bit of humor. The topics he covers are things really worth thinking about and are actually applicable to life.

Ted Brown is wonderful. HLS 116 is fantastic...such important topics to know about. He isn't shy about expressing his political beliefs, etc. but who would want him to be!!?? It makes class that much more interesting. The man is a genius. Office hours can be intimidating to go to...but go anyway! He is very helpful with papers, etc.

As mentioned previously, likes to ramble and tends to be verbose in conveying an argument or point. But he's knowledgeable and a fair grader; not difficult to get an A if you do you work. Recommended.
Smart guy but talks way too much.  He talks for the entire class time and does not really try to elicit questions/discussions.  Very slow grader.  Exams are fair.

Could have been an interesting class, but not well constructed and lectures were rather boring. Intelligent and somewhat interesting prof, but given to rambling unnecessarily for long periods of time - no structure or obvious point to his long lectures. Also tends to ask a lot of questions with a very specific answer in mind, hard to respond to.

Arguably the best professor at Rochester on many levels--Brilliant man, very effective teaching style, and available to students for absolutely anything. A true leader in his field, Professor Brown is inspiring. TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM, even if you aren't in the public health or history fields.

This man inspired me to change to an HLS minor -- he simply made me love the idea of public health and made me want to learn everything I can about it. Tests aren't too bad as long as you go to class. Take all his classes -- you'll thank yourself later!
AMAZING. Take all of his classes. Every last one.

The absolute best and most inspiring professor at the university. He knows his subjects well and is incredibly passionate about sharing his knowledge. His course truly did change the way I look at health care in America and has motivated me to choose a different career. Very highly recommended!
No Comments

Wonderful professor, makes the material truly interesting.  Not the easiest of classes but if you need help he's generally around (sometimes he can be very busy due to travel) to talk to and get help from.  Best professor I've had so far and I'm a senior.
Simply an amazing prof. - most dynamic prof. I have had.
great professor, i love his courses. He's very interesting and makes class fun.

He marked points off for minor details that should not have constituted several letter grades' worth of a drop. He is unclear in explaining assignments. He was unsupportive to students and had a negative attitude when answering questions. He gives very monotonous lectures and conveys little information over a long period of time.

I took the Swift variant of the course. Arthur's slides are well-prepared and he knows what he's talking about due to his background. The homework/projects tend to be fair, although the estimates on how long they will take are not accurate—intend to spend twice as long as prescribed. Arthur will call out AI usage and there is a group project.

No exam or quiz, grade based on hw and project. He's a nice professor in general although he can be rude sometimes but he actually reply email and give extension if you indeed need one. iOS easier than android class. homework post every week's Thursday and due next Monday but not hard and you can change his in-class coding work to do hw
Avoid at all costs, very rude, and doesn't follow syllabus. He also doesn't provide students with an accurate rubric.
Lecture very unclear, talking about the same thing over again and again. Very Rude in lecture. Would never take his class again.

Professor is an okay guy, but can be rude in his emails and calls people out sometimes. Class can be overwhelming at times with lots of code to learn quickly, but if you really understand the app he builds right before the project, you'll be able to do the projects well. His attendance tracking is not graded, but I suggest going to learn better.

says attendance is mandatory but its not. nice guy, if you show you care for him then he will show he cares for you. sometimes online sometimes in person. just an fyi, dont p!ss him off and send him redundant emails, hes not gonna respond to you with what you think he will. dont ask for extensions unless someting actually happens, too.
Nice Professor
Easy Class

Lectures are insanely boring but the class is easy enough if you follow the assignment directions and what he does in class. Lectures switch from being in class or online and in the syllabus it says attendance is necessary but there's no grade for it so it doesn't really matter.

hes a weird guy. very difficult to understand as english is his second language and he mumbles and whispers. he can come off as rough and abrasive, sometimes it was difficult to understand his grading criteria. YOU MUST HAVE A MACBOOK FOR THIS CLASS or you will not be able to code! this is for fall iOS dev. :)

He comes across as a hard professor but he has a style which if you follow you can be confident that you can do mobile app development. The class has a lot of homework but it is helpful. No extra credit but getting an A is not too hard if you work constantly. He isn't very flexible otherwise but the card itself is not too hard.
Took android dev. You can basically copy his code and finish every project and HW. Every HW can be done the day it's due. Projects take 1-2 days.

His lecture is about wasting your 75 minutes listening to intro content that doesn't worth 5 minutes and never mentions anything useful. He even shows how to use a plugin that is not in the marketplace and he does not release the install pack; all he does is to show something you can't use and say "but I already installed it". Hilarious.

comment: I highly recommend being in class for this course especially if you didn't do the readings. He does a really good job of breaking down philosophical concepts and relating them to real world experiences. The midterms are pretty straightforward, don't write how think a philosopher would write, write in your own writing style and be sure to cite.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Professor Feldman is definitely well versed in his field. His classes are very lecture heavy he just talks about the reading he assigned for the entire class. He goes over material in depth and assigns a lot of reading throughout the year but youre only graded on 6 assignments and 1 final. Imo his biggest flaw is  his grading scale is very unclear.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things']
comment: definitely make sure to do citations for like everything because if you don't i fear the highest grade you could get is like a B+, but his grading scale is honestly unclear 'cause I had to like test the waters for like everything. but he's really passionate about what he's teaching and could probably go on for hours if it wasn't for the time limit

Professor Sum is an incredibly sweet, caring professor who is clearly passionate about Anthropology and China. Her class was well structured: readings were relevant, assignments were productive and fairly easy. She balances lecture and discussion really well and she clearly works hard to keep our workload manageable.

He's the man! His nickname is Carcara, which in Portuguese means "hawk." This should give you a good idea of his personality. His course is certainly not for the faint-hearted, though any level of fitness will do fine with enough motivation. Grade is an easy A, just show up and participate.

I could not walk the day after my first class. Watch out when you are rounding corners with this one. Very unorthodox, real style of teaching--do not take if you are weak of heart. Always full, many drop out within the first week. He is not the standard university professor so be prepared to think outside the box. Please wear deodorant.

He very harshly graded assignments, and his feedback isn't helpful especially when you used this feedback only for him to tell you to remove it in future comments. Lectures were never helpful when it came to completing formal assignments and it was hard to know what he was looking for. He is a nice person, but his grading is all over the place.

There is lots of busywork that is often not related to the idea of writing or argument. Although he is a nice person, his grading felt very random- there was no rubric and minimal instructions, as there is no rubric. His feedback also felt random, with some of his new feedback contradicting his old feedback.

This class assigns significantly more homework than other comparable writing courses. Grading often feels arbitrarily assigned, inconsistent and sometimes contradicts earlier feedback. While he's a nice person, his class was frustrating enough that I canceled all plans to take another writing class at this university because of it.

Harry is a very kind person, but I feel his class isn't structured very well. We had many assignments that seemed unrelated to the actual subject (writing/argument). He could be unclear with his expectations on assignments which made his grading confusing at times, but he did give lots of feedback and gave us the ability to amend our projects.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: I would say that Harry is a good person, but I would absolutely not take this course with him again. Not only did grading seem somewhat arbitrary, but the amount of assignments he gave outweighed other writing courses by far. It was his first semester teaching a course, so he could improve, but without change, I would avoid this course.

Tessa was a fabulous professor! She took the time to get to know each student, curated an open discussion environment, graded papers fairly with great feedback, assigned interesting readings, and was extremely flexible! If you are looking for a great WRTG 105 class, Tessa is the one!

Lisa Cerami is an inspiring Professor, especially for someone who wants to go into academia. When she speaks you can hear her passion for the subject, she especially loves hearing her student's opinions and perspectives on the material they read.

One of the best professors I had at University of Rochester. She is very knowledgable and organized, and she is willing to help if any students had difficulty with the content. Although she talks fast, she does many practices to make sure you understand the materials. I rarely been to her lectures because it is recorded but I truly love her class.
Great professor. Made ACC 201 enjoyable. Class was cumulative, so attending lectures is important. Exams were not difficult.
Just so good. I take note and listen carefully every lecture and do all questions, just do your work and it would be very good outcome
She is kind and helpful.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: - Pretty straightforward - Open to help during office hours - Lecture heavy (attendance is not mandatory, but you won't pass if you do not attend class) - Exams reflect class material - No graded homework

She is the best professor you can ever meet in U of R. She is so willing to teach whatever she knows to her students and always ready to help students either inside the class or outside classes. Though she teaches fast, you can always learn a lot if you pay attention. I thought I did not like accounting until I met her. She is so amazing! Love her!
Either you like her or not. Her lectures are too fast and she covers topics VERY quickly. She's willing to help outside of class and is a nice person.
Hands down the best professor I've come across! Makes learning Accounting interesting :)

Prof Iyer is hands down the BEST professor I've ever met! She makes the tedious concepts of accounting really easy to comprehend and she is always glad to offer help to students. ACC201 is a basic class to be honest but I would be more than glad to take more of her classes in the future if she offers. Just amazing!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Very helpful and wants her students to succeed. Gives lots of additional practice and even conducts additional lectures to answer questions and help students.

The class is graded on just 3 exams, so it was stressful to get a good grade, especially if you fall behind. I look at the reviews below and they all say tests are easy As. I disagree. Or maybe the tests got harder this year. I did not find accounting concepts easy and the tests seemed rather difficult. She teaches really well and is respected.

I really enjoyed Professor Iyer's class. Although, I had no prior knowledge of accounting, her comprehensive lectures and chapter problems she gave made it easier to understand concepts. Exams aren't tough if you pay attention in class.
Amazing professor! very clear lectures. exams are not hard and there is little homework.

She genuinely cares about the students and directly helps them understand how to get their scores reflect what they know, and not be overwhelmed by exams. She has in-depth knowledge of accounting and does her level best to deliver it to students effectively. Great teacher.

Amazing professor, who makes you interested in accounting. Goes through concepts very fast, but if you pay attention and ask her questions (she is very helpful and approachable outside of class and via e-mail), you will be fine. I did not do any of the HW from the textbook, but went through all of the problems sets before the exams, which helped.

So I didn't do so great in her class because I the material is very easy so I thought I knew it and I wouldn't prepare. She actually genuinely cares about her students though and will reinforce ideas and make sure all of the students are up to date and up to speed. sometimes she holds review sessions which are extremely helpful.
Professor Iyer is a great teacher and explains everything really well. Very helpful and accessible too. Would recommend her class to everyone.
Easy class. Great teacher. Save more. Live better. Walmart.
Super nice professor. She explains everything clearly. I went to her office hours a lot, she will slowly explains everything again to me.  Easy test, if you study a lot and do all the exercises.

A natural at teaching! She gives thorough answers to the questions asked both in and out of class, super patient, and provides plenty of learning material and examples. Like the person before me said- Prof. Iyer's business professional outfits are absolutely perfect!
She explains thoroughly, gives good application, and her outfits are always 100% on point. What a classy lady.
Easy exams, goes slow in class with multiple explanations and examples to make sure people understand the material. Hands outs problem sets, notes, and old exams
Textbook is better than professor, she uploads all her class materials. Easy exams.
Basically a no open book exam version of intermediate macro with more stats. Generous curve, but the exam is hard.

Wow, what a curve...Ronni Pavan is the best man to walk on this planet. Don't be scared of how difficult this course is, because your sweat and tears will be rewarded in due time. Just do the homework and practice exams, and show up to lecture because he will hint at what will be in the exam.
Great professor, caring, although the tests are hard, but grading are goooood though.

Yes, this is a very challenging class, but I genuinely learned a lot about metrics and can understand the methodology/math in Econ papers. If you want to do Econ research/grad school, take it with him. If you just want the A/credit, take it with the other professor. Difficult homeworks, but graded really nicely. Exams are also curved generously.

only speaking for 231W, if you are not solid in stats, don't take his 231, it's very painful to catch up with stats and proofs.If you skip lectures, it's hard to succeed in his class. Homework are hard but grade leniently. The exams are kind of hard, but curved very generously, and don't worry too much if you perform poorly on the midterm.
Don't take this course if your knowledge background for statistics is weak, or you will struggle a lot!

Super boring class. He reads off the slides, and rarely ever talks about real world examples. Luckily he uploads the (very detailed) slides. The homework is pretty hard but is graded leniently. The exams are also generously curved.
Generous curve, the exams really aren't bad if you study the hw assignments and recitation problems.
board work is not organized and has sloppy handwriting. great personality, grading is pretty easy in terms of the curve.
sloppy board work, thick accent, and little commitment to the class. he's not completely unapproachable outside of class. after taking this class, I have lost all interest in being an econ major.
No Comments

Good professor, teaches straight out of the book but does a good job explaining concepts.  Don't be afraid to interrupt him if he is going too fast.  The curve in this class is very generous so don't worry too much about your grade as long as you are keeping up with the material.

Professor Barber was great! I enjoyed the class and even though it was the first time taking an ethics class it wasn't all too bad. There was a learning curve and it definitely isn't an easy A, but do the readings do your homework start the essays early, and it's manageable. Above all class made you think and was interesting at all times!

Krauss is a boss, but his lectures are hard to follow - go too fast. His tests are VERY difficult. He is the hardest out of the CHM131 profs. However, you learn the material more in his class & wkshps are fun & hmwk is optional. He is helpful after class & in OH, very personable. I struggled b/c the material didn't interest me.

I'm not someone who enjoys chem - I took it to fulfill pre-med requirements. This class was an upward struggle for me, but Krauss was really helpful and as someone said, he makes sure you know it's your responsibility to do well. Study hard and the tests really are not that difficult, rather they're more conceptual focusing on your understanding.

I got an A so I'm not being harsh because I did poorly. This class is VERY difficult w/o AP Chem prior so don't take this class if you haven't taken AP. I only did well because I put tons of hours into the class - the lectures were good but the exams were impossible. Krauss is just a genius professor - can't do much about that. He is funny though.

AWESOME PROFESSOR! His class can be tough, but I really enjoyed it. I took AP Chem and this class was a breeze for me. Homework is assigned for your own good, but is not collected and is completely optional. I highly recommend this teacher! He cares about his students' success, but makes it clear that it is your responsibility to do well.

AWESOME CHEM PROF! I am a bio major and CHEM had become the highlight of my day. He is fun and an all around a nice guy. BONUS: He actually writes notes on the board and uses presentations occasionally. He does many examples and will answer any question you have DURING lecture. He WANTS you to go to office hours. Class is tough, but manageable.
He is funny, easy to understand and teaches all the material you need to know for the tests in a helpful and fun way. He made me go from hating chemistry to loving it!
Krauss is a great lecturer, funny and entertaining. The exams are overrated in terms of difficulty just make sure you go to the extremely helpful workshops. They will save you.

As someone who took AP chem in high-school and did well in the class, I found this class surprisingly hard to get an A in. Material in lecture and workshop is straightforward but tests are difficult. Krauss is a cool guy I just hated how hard the tests were.
Tests can be fairly challenging. Not a good choice for someone who has never taken chemistry before. I personally really did enjoy the class.

Avoid this professor. He is a nice guy and very funny, but he is not a good lecturer. His tests are difficult, much more difficult then the alternative professor Krugh. If you have the option take Krugh, you will thank me when your friends are complaining about the tests.

First, I did not take AP chem and still came out with an A- with ALOT of work. Good proff, entertaining lectures with LOTS of examples. He changes the tests every year but expect one easy test and 2 difficult tests. You can drop one. Final was reasonable. 85% is an A-. Overall, good proff, difficult class (without chem background), recommended

The class was not that challenging. If you have taken AP Chemistry class, then you would not have any problem passing the class. He gives us tons of examples to make sure we understand and gives variety of sample questions so that students understand what will be on the test.

He is so clear on his lecture, and he gives tons and tons of examples, so it really helps to go to class! He is very funny and keeps you entertained throughout the class. highly recommend take his class for chem 131

A very solid professor. He's very good at explaining stuff, and always provides plenty of examples for the material. On top of that, he's just a nice guy, and he's always ready to help you outside of class or on the online chat sessions. Extra props for his Fridays, which include a song and a few lame jokes.

Great professor!  Very funny and intelligent guy!  His exams are challenging but he really makes you "step-up" your game.  I learned so much from his course.  I took it a year ago and still remember so much from it.  Definitely recommend him! A+++++
Krauss is great! My favorite professor so far, very entertaining. Class is harder than I expected though.

Krauss was a decent lecuturer, especially considering he had a class of over 200.  The workshop format he uses, rather than recitations, works really well and makes the class much easier to understand.  The class was pretty fun for a chemistry class.

Krauss was my favorite! His lectures, while presenting quite a bit of hard material, were sometimes a blast! He really does help at his office hours, and he wants to see everyone do well! His tests are only hard if you don't study, and workshops kick arse over regular recitations. Great TA selection, great course, great professor!
Makes class interesting and somewhat entertaining.  Very helpful at office hours.
Krauss your the man. Good class, personality, helpful!
His teaching style is good and easy to understand, the concepts of his course are hard and he presents them well with lots of examples.
His tests are so cruel
Hate Krauss. He asks us to do hw online and doesn't give a damn about electronic problems we encounter.
his jokes are kind of corny, but in a cute old man kind of way; understanding concepts is much easier to learn with krauss than with olek
Very humorous!  A relaxing class!  His teaching style is easy to understand!
No Comments

His powers of explanation are incredible.  He presents the material in an extremely organized fashion and demonstrates problem solving technique so thoroughly that I found I did not need to study.  Besides that, he is an unbelievably engaging lecturer.
Fun class even though it is chemistry:)
I never wanted to miss lecture. i had so much fun in a class whose subject i hated.
Takes really boring material and makes you want to come to class to see what he'll do next.  Can make a 200 person class room seem intimate.
No Comments
fun, funny, and totally cute.
This prof really knows his stuff and is an awesome lecturer
Excellent, funny and thorough professor. The kind you wish could follow you throughout your chemistry learning experience!
She is an awesome professor!

I had Professor Li for Contemporary American Memoir.  She is a phenomenal teacher.  She lets the class take the lead discussion-wise.  She is tough but fair and very smart as well as passionate.  I highly recommend her.

by far the best professor I've ever had, and she is just a wonderful person on top of that. She is a tough grader but is entirely reasonable and acommodating. Talking about rewrites is great, because she is really supportive of growth; but do it in a timely fashion. Do the readings, even though there is a lot....it's very worth it.

Her lectures are great. For someone that didn't know a lot about American Authors, she opened my eyes up to a lot of good literature. The discussions are thought engaging. However, her grading needs work. She gives little positive feedback and interjects her opinions into her grading which often leads to low grades if she disagrees (happens often).

One of the University's best Professors yet! She actually cares about you learning as opposed to being obsessed with tests like some teachers are. The concepts you discuss make you rethink your own values and really allow you to get to know the literature and yourself more. It can be a tough class, but she's more than willing to help!

I had Professor Li for both American Lit and Toni Morrison. In the A.Lit class, she had a good selection of books and ran class similar to many other intro courses. My class with her on Toni Morrison was more group discussions than her lecturing. Overall, I think she is a wonderful teacher that is both knowledgeable and approachable.

She's really awesome... I wish she was ACTUALLY more of my teacher.  The class was split up into 2 sections and I got stuck with the lousy TA every Friday plus he grades all my assignments and papers.  That doesn't seem very fair at all.  Hes not that awful but I feel a little ripped off, know what I mean?  I want a good freaking teacher, not a TA

If attendance wasn't mandatory I wouldn't have gone too often--but I'm glad I did because she actually tests you on her lecture notes. Weekly quizzes made it feel like high school. Outside of class, however, she is extremely nice and accommodating. I thought the book selection was decent, too, but very lengthy.

She's a fairly tough grader but the challenge is worth it. Definitely go visit at office hours, she is very friendly one-on-one. Her lectures on Hemingway were super interesting. And she digs on Lauren like woah.
intelligent, pretty interesting, not my fav prof, but definitely a worthwhile and enjoyable class

Li definitely is knowledgeable in English, but has no clue how to handle a big class (aka 35 students). Assigned seating, power point presentations that go over just the surface of every book, reading quizzes almost daily? I was not personally a fan of her style of teaching, but she always was willing to talk about a book and hear your ideas.

She seems a little cold and subdued at first, but go and talk to her during office hours.  she warms up a lot and will like you after that.  also, she's really helpful one on one.  I thought the class was great.  Shes very knowledgable and really wants you to succeed.  She helped me learn how to write good research papers.
Really good teacher but lots of reading

She was really was not a good professor.  Her midterm was atrocious (one word questions to be answered? C'mon) and she was so strict on papers that she required a Works Cited for a 4 page paper on one book that everyone is reading in class.  She bumped you down a grade if you didn't have it!  Also, the discussions were not great, mostly opinions
A wonderful teacher, very knowledgable and inspiring. take this class if you're at all interested in american lit.
I had her for Am Lit and I really liked the class, good material, Prof Li is enthusistic and open to discussion - not an amazing teacher, but definately very good
AVOID TAKING HIS CLASS. YOU WILL FAIL OR DESTROY YOUR GPA. Take it over the summer elsewhere please!!!!!!

Though reputedly easier when teaching thermo, avoid taking fluids with Thomas at all costs. He is infamous for failing students and trashing the GPAs of survivors. Friendly guy, but extremely difficult prof. Problem is compounded by his tendency to assume that poor performance is result of student laziness. Take fluids elsewhere over the summer.

Tough teacher. Only understand his way of thinking.. which is different from the book at times which get confusing when you ask him about it. Erases constantly so take fast notes. A lot of people end up having to retake it or barely passing. The final is impossible.

very easy exams until you miss a minus sign, when he mercilessly tries to fail you. asks same questions on all exams, except for final, where we got major curveballs. i asked him to help me prepare for the first exam but he was unwilling to do so outside of his obligated office hours. unreasonable atendance policy. overall great experience though.

Excellent teacher.  Really knows his stuff, barely looks at his notes.  Very passionate about thermo, and helpful in office hours and workshops.  He demands excellence, and is tough with partial credit.  He wants you to do well though, so talk to him.  Factors in improvement a lot when it comes to grades.
Wonderful lady and incredibly helpful one-on-one... but she is a terrible lecturer. Read the book, study with friends, and go to her for extra help; don't rely on just sitting there and listening.

She is a very nice lady but is incredibly quiet and boring.  It was difficult to stay awake (especially because I absolutely hated the material), but she cares so much about her students.  She's extremely flexible and always willing to adjust to extenuating circumstances.  She will always give the students the benefit of the doubt by far.

She's a sweet lady, and she means well, but she's the most horrifically boring prof I've ever had. The material tends to be simple enough, if you can focus long enough to figure out what she's talking about, but her quiet, timid teaching style is completely offputting.

She's quiet, but an amazing professor.  Extremely helpful, understanding, can talk about her subject for hours. Only caveat: since she's so quiet, it can be easy to get distracted and feel bored in class.

I really enjoyed the class.  She is quiet, but not humorless.  She gives good examples and smiles when students come up with good ones.  It made me feel like she enjoyed the material, which helped me enjoy it.  I liked the HS style question and answer classroom set-up.  She knew everyone's name and history.  Wasn't too tough to stay awake in class.

She is the nicest lady, but her quiet disposition doesn't make for the most interesting.  As fascinated as I was by the material, even I found it difficult to stay awake some days.  But she is extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and easy.  I'd take another one of her classes, but I can't say I wouldn't fall asleep again.
Though well meaning, Gunlogson is a terrible professor.  Avoid her.
AWFUL!!

If you can manage to stay conscious for an entire one of Gunlogson's lectures you either an insomniac or incredibly high on ceffeine.  Nothing against her personally, but she seems very disorganized and is hardly ever prepared for class.
Christine is a great teacher, but a bit boring at times.  Just bring something to do that isn't too distracting and you'll be fine.
Very nice, and very knowledgeable, but WOW -- what a snooze.  Especially with the 85 degree classroom and a 4:50 PM class.
very helpful
Not a bad professor, but BOOOOOOORRRRRRRRRIIIIIIINNNNNNNNNGGGGGGGGGGG. Nevertheless, if you so much as show up and sleep through class you will do very well.
soooo nice, but soooo boring. i slept in this class everyday and still made it out with an A! she is also very understanding. i would take another class with her if i had the chance.

A relatively easy class. Although she is quie boring but if you have the attention span to last you could definetely take a lot from her class.

The Nicest lady, but the combination of my triptophane sandwich and her lecture is an instant cure for insomnia
Very difficult. Bordering on impossible. He teaches undergrad class like it's a masters class. He is ridiculously intelligent; too smart to be teaching 200 classes.

This is a very difficult class but he is a great professor. You must attend class, if you don't expect to fail. He is extremely intelligent man, and can answer just about any question off of the top of his head.
He is a great teacher and always Knows his material.  He might skip steps because he assumes you know it.  Go to class and you will learn a lot.
Lots of hard homework but there is a lot of extra credit. Lectures are boring but required. Read the textbook and go through the slides and the test is easy.

His lectures are not the most entertaining, but he cares for the class and his grading is fair. The material is learnable on your own through reading the textbook chapters that he assigns, and he assigns them clearly.

Professor Hosseini requires attendance, but your mileage out of the lecture may vary greatly and it's highly recommended you take time to read the textbook to learn the content. The grading for midterms was not incredibly generous, and the average for them hovered around a 65-75%. Finals were graded with leniency. An A is a 91, and there's a curve.

Lot of homework that is graded tough but there are lots of extra credit to help make up for it. Tests are very fair and straight from slides or examples. Lectures are boring and hard to get through but you don't really need to pay attention.

I thought that his lectures were pretty good. A little difficult to follow sometimes, but still enjoyable. His exams were not bad if you reviewed the slides and went to recitation. His office hours were empty the times I went, so I got my questions answered pretty quickly. Sometimes he was harsh on the proof grading, but it is an advanced class.

The homework is graded harshly but there are tons of extra credit to more than make up for it if you actually try. The tests are straight off the slides or the examples so if u just study they're not hard. The lectures are incredibly boring however and I had to mostly self study after since I couldn't pay attention. Overall not bad.
Hard test with no curve, lecture feels like reading the PowerPoint

Kaave was a very fair professor, the lectures were actually pretty organized and informative. Extra credit was offered on homework and the final, and the exams were not more difficult then the homeworks.

The professors lectures were actually quite organized, with the lectures being posted to the Slack. Attendance was required but you could miss 4 classes with no penalty. As long as you attended class the tests were very fair, and with extra credit on homework it is very possible to score well.

The lectures is disorganized and difficult to follow. Very bad lecturer, homework grades are tough. Avoid.

Professor Olek was very knowledgeable about the subject and also about other related subjects. H e frequently pointed out relationships between subjects that are at first not obvious but are in fact very illuminating. He cares deeply about the material. He is humorous but in a pretty understated way.

Olek tended to jump between topics in his attempt to teach. Thank god he posted his LECTURES in FULL on Blackboard! He has some crazy theories about nutrition which probably explains his body shape. We NEVER used the textbook because he didn't like it. Don't be too discouraged if you don't do well, many change majors after this, but it gets easier.

One of the most ridiculous professors I've ever had. He answers questions like a politician. Tony Olek is the man. He is different, but you appreciate him more as the semester goes on. Very generous curve at end of course as well. So if your getting B's, dont be bummed bc you'll probably get an A.

Olek was my favorite professor thus far. He had a unique and genuine style of teaching. He was perfect. He answered questions in a very clear manner. His mustache was jaw-dropping. Overall it will be very difficult to find another professor like Olek. He was perfect.

Dr. Olek is an interesting professor.  The main key to succeeding in his class is to think conceptually and in a "creative" fashion.  I really like how he taught us to think critically.  You will have to put in effort in this class.  I went to class, actively participate in workshop, and went up to him to ask questions and managed to pull off an A.

Olek is a professor that not many freshman are expecting. He doesn't just make you regurgitate information, but instead he wants his students to learn how to think critically. His powerpoints are great, and he puts them online. There's a very generous curve at the end of the class. Definitely my favorite class so far.
Very knowledgable and puts A LOT of work into his slides. But you do have to work hard to get a good grade. He curves at end which is nice.

This class takes work, and Olek is not what most people are used to, but if you have an open mind, he'll teach you to think for yourself and you'll learn a lot. He also assures students that the curve will have an average of B/B+ which is very generous, so he clearly wants his students to do well in the end.
don't take his class! give ppt in class, but make no sense answering questions. When the midterms come,  I have no idea what his question asking for..he absolutely fails his English class at college

Everyone complains about Olek at the beginning of the semester and he can be somewhat confusing but once you get used to his style it's much easier. Class is really easy... he presents the lecture material in a very confusing and non intuitive way. I stopped going to lecture and still get A's on exams. Would not take another class with him. Ever.

UGH! Hard to explain. He only uses presentations. EXAMS ARE NOT MEMORIZATION! Only a small section is. Exams are mostly about applying an experimental outlook to a concept. IS NOT A NORMAL BIO CLASS. Class is called "Principles of Biology", and is mostly a microbiology course. I will NOT take another course from him if I can avoid it.

Olek has an interesting style of teaching.  He moves through slides quite rapidly and doesn't always explain when he starts to use an abbreviation or words interchangeably. The class is a lot easier if you took AP Chem or Bio, or at least honors classes in high school. He does care about students, he just doesn't always understand their questions.

Olek teaches material visually and then expects you to be able to apply it experimentally, in words and numbers, on the tests. If you study, go to class, and go to work shops, you will sit on top of the curve an get in the A range. If you spend all of your time whining about how the course is unfair and too hard, you won't. Go to class! Seriously.

He is actually a really smart guy.

I read all these comments before taking the class and I was scared. But he's not bad at all if you take time to study/organize the lecture ppts on your own time. Don't bother going to class. Be prepared for workshops. MEMORIZE his slides. and get to every question on the test cause something is better than nothing. I did fine in the end. :)

Attempts to introduce vocabulary that differs from the traditionally accepted lexicon - sometimes helpful but other times completely unnecessary; learning the words he wants you to use often detracts from the material he expects you to understand.  Is unclear in lecture, materials are different from what he tests on more often than not.  useless.

Boy, a lotta hate for Dr. Olek here.  I understand the feeling.  But he's a good guy with a good way of thinking about how he teaches, even if the execution is completely sloppy. There is a difference between teaching experimentally and being a confusing fool. This class is supposed to be easier than 112, and I regret taking this over 112 because I thought it would be easier. The exams are hard to study for because the past exams are all confusing, just like him.

This professor is just fail. I took AP Bio and regret not taking 112. I thought I'd be up for easy stuff if I'd take intro bio, but really just take 112. I used to love bio and now well because of him I abhor it.

This guy is awful. If you can take Bio 112, make sure you do so. This guy is sooo bad. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He is awful. If you do take this class do not buy and save your self some money. Oh did i mention he sucks. PS he looks like Coronel Sanders.

If you're up to the challenge of trying to figure out this at first seemingly adorable, witty professor, be my guest. His ppts will only make sense if you sit at your pc for an hour and half by yourself to go over it. Classes are pretty much pointless. Barely any curve at the end of the class. Better off taking 112, heard the class is much easier.

His teachings are completely disorganized. If we ask a question, he answers with another question which leaves the students completely clueless. His tests are bizzare and questions are hard to understand. He does not let us use the conventional words "Jargon." The class requires some knowledge of psychology to understand olek's mind rather than bio

nice guy and everything but DAMN he sucks as a teacher. the material that he teaches in class has nothing to do with the exam. some needs to just let him know that his time as a professor is over. he needs to go back to the lab where he belongs. again like i said hes nice and a smart dude but i am not paying to get a C
His classes are useless, his tests are confusing. The curve at the end does NOT make this class worth it.
Very unclear - worthless lectures. Just study ppts at home, or do not take this class.

Dr. Olek seems like a nice man but I think he is a really sub-par professor. i don't know why students are saying all these gibberish about dr. olek. i would rate myself as a student of average intelligence who stays up until 5 to study and believe that this is as easy as it get! He tells you whats going to be on the exam. In fact, you don't even have to go to class because he puts the power points online.

I actually enjoyed this class. His powerpoints may look foreign for someone who does not attend class regularly but quite honestly, it is very easy to get at least a B in the course by just going to class/recitation/ and reading the lectures. He's just so..Olekey (and should be made an adjective in merriam-webster). Largely did not like presentation of the material, or teaching methods. His tests were arbitrary. thats jargon

Dr. Olek is an amazing professor. Probably one of the best at this school. If you read his extra clear power points you are more than likely to get a B or an A in class. People who complain are ones who are too lazy to take their time to memorize. You don't even have to know what you're doing to get an A, JUST MEMORIZE.

The people who say that Olek is a bad teacher are the ones who sleep during class or refuse to review the powerpoint slides. Yes, all colleges are going to have different methods of giving students the most up to date material (which is why the txtbk is not used), but Olek does it in the most efficient way and I'd learn from him again if i could.

i have no idea what's going on in class whatsoever.

bad

The guy seemed absolutely terrible until you get to Bio 111 with Sajdak.  Go to class, do the old exams, and you'll be fine.

His class has decent lectures, he is an excelent power point maker.  To get an A in the class do the following: Study THE OLD EXAMS FROM THE PAST 2-3 YEARS. GET your TA to give you the answers from previous years and study them.  you will do fine if you do this.  otherwise you will do poorly.

im happy to have come out alive and still pre-med

Really easy class, very interesting information presented reptitive at times.  ALL lecture notes are posted online for student convenience.  Great class.

Worst teacher on campus. Boring lectures, poor lecture slides and unhelpful workshops are traits of his class. If you actually go to lecture, this class is just about the easiest class possible.  Exams straight from lecture.  And Olek is histerical always so condecending when people ask stupid questions, makes it amusing.

knowledgeable and a good guy, hard exams...need to know what he wants to hear or you won't get credit

I really liked his class. He oversimplifies a bit (which can complicate things later on) but overall, I found the class enjoyable. It helps if you have a good TA though just to fix the occasional slip ups he has
His notes are disorganized and he contradicts himself daily. This man should have never been allowed to teach.
HATED HIM; HATED THE COURSE. KILLED MY GPA

the material is really elementary. professor olek on the other hand is just very intimidating. he's not the type of person who would give encouraging words, rather he's the type who would and can really discourage you.

Not the worlds greatest course but a good basic course.  You need to constantly study to stay current with stuff but this course is DEFINITELY doable.  If you want to get into med school this course is a must.
lectures stupid

Really wonderful professor! Always available during office hours, too!

Really great person overall. Stimulating but chill, nice course. Interested in what you have to say which is a fantastic quality in a lecturer, especially for philosophy. I also loved that the mathematical background sometimes showed as it is great for all the logic.

Good Professor easy and interesting class. 100% recommend.

Genuinely one of the kindest, most inspiring and intellectually stimulating Professors. Knows what she's teaching very well and does everything she can to help her students succeed in the class. The best Professor I've had at the UofR.

The best professor I've had so far. Lectures are very clear and straightforward, workload is manageable, and Zeynep is always available to discuss and clarify. Participation and attendance aren't mandatory but the more you participate in class, the more you'll get out of it.
I have to say professor Soysal is really caring about students. Whatever problem u met, just email her and she will respond as soon as possible and be patient enough to help u solve the problem.

Make sure to do the extra credit assignments ;) She is a lot better than you think

She splits class each week into two sections: first call of the week is "lecture" and the second is "small" group interaction with the 3 TA's about the readings for that week. She's really cute and entertaining. Her film class is actually pretty fun and I'm glad I took it. Her tests are really not that bad, but attendance does matter and the movies can be kind of boring sometimes.
She is great, absolutely inspirational and awesome.  I took two more classes with her :)

doesn't go over any vocabularies or technical terms in class but expects you to know them on the exams. makes exams harder than they need to be for an intro class. doesn't care about students' grades.

comment: He's kind of all over the place. Some of the worst grading system I've seen. Though, he teaches well and the class is structured in a way that if you do the right things you can get an A in this class. To those who will take this class: getting an A is NOT easy so you'd better put in the work. The grading leaves NO room for error.
Very passionate about the class and always happy to help you if you show you're trying.

Prof McGrath was fantastic. I personally dont care about mechanics but his lectures are really fantastic. He does a great job introducing concepts and explaining how to go about solving the problems youre expected to do in a very logical and concise way. Homework is unnecessarily difficult at times due to grading but the class teaches you a lot.

Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful professor. Dr. McGrath really knows how to teach mechanics and he is very, very direct with what is expected with every test. Didn't go to this class for majority of the semester and it is one of my biggest regrets. Class isn't curved and it's also not that easy of a class, lots of work and high expectations.
Class isnt curved even when less than 20% of the class is in the A/A- range.

He has his personal labs and he is much more concerned with his labs than he is with the class. It took 3 weeks to schedule a meeting with him in regards to an exam and 2 days after that meeting was the next exam. Also he reuses his notes since 2003, when the class was started and he is starting to misinterpret those notes.
Learned a lot of great tricks for ways to think about and approach problems from him. Class is definitely not his first priority, but he is a brilliant man and I very much so enjoyed his class.

This professor is really clear and a great lecturer. He tries to be helpful, but doesn't necessarily give it to you so that it's too obvious. class is not his main priority

homework each week takes about 8 hours and then is only worth 10% of your grade while hour exams are worth 20%... the graders are huge ****es too take off for random****

comment: Professor Howard, while challenging, is a great professor. Middleton is awesome!! By far my favorite class of the semester! He's a great lecturer and really nice and understanding with students.
