I learned very little from Cline.  He goes through material very quickly and isn't very clear about it.  Do the homework and learn by practice - it's the only way.  His tests are fair (though incredibly hard).
Should be teaching graduate classes not undergraduate pre-med physics. Most people fell asleep or didn't come. Preparation consisted of studying yourself because he never applied concepts in lecture.

Although lecture was a bit dry, he is very vested in his students.  He weekly sent out tabulated excel sheets with our grades and the class averages for comparison.  Tests were fair. Slightly tricky, but if you studied the workshops, and hw, you could master most questions.  Good professor.  Would have him again!

He wants to give everyone A's but he makes the class so hard that no one actually does.  He's really a nice guy, and supposedly prepares students for upper-level physics classes, but I wouldn't say so.  Supposedly harder physics classes have defnintely been easier.

Very helpful, likable, easy to get along with.  Lectures sometimes a bit complicated, but nothing a bit of studying can't work out.   [In response to earlier comment:] Doesn't expect students to be "brilliant" -- just to be willing to think and

Nice guy.  Really does want all of his students to pass, but won't set his standards any lower than postgraduate level.  Very poor at explaining ideas in a lecture, fair at explaining them one-on-one, he just expects too much background for an intro class
Do not take his class, you will fail most definately. Has the highest expectations from students, Educated at Oxford himself. Genius mind, but can't teach mediocre U of R pre med students.

Very friendly interesting and helpful.  Unfortunately he's brilliant and expects everyone else to be as well.  Not a good teacher for an intro level physics class.  Even as a physics master, YOU WILL BE LOST!(but an excellent choice for advanced courses)

He is a horrible professor.  He isn't clear in his teaching and he pushes too much material too quickly.  Plus his grading system isn't great and he is incompetent when you ask him questions about the homework (he will lead you on a wild goose chase).
Cool guy teaching a great class.
I could have done a lot better. The class was not too difficult when you include how massive of a curve there was. He's a good lecturer.

The class is really hard with heavy class notes. Tests are 85% of the grades, and the class note is not assembled with the lecture slides he posts. Attendance is not required but if you miss one class is hard to catch up. His office hour is not helpful, but he has responsible TAs. If you think you are smart enough then you can take this class.
Dude's a genius, probably the best professor in the ECON department.
very prestigious and knowledgeable professor
You will realize how amazing and well-organized his lectures are when you go to a grad school. Excellent professor!

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: If you miss one lecture you will be lost for the rest of the semester.

Asen has method of lecturing that is very easy to follow, which is useful for a class that can get very dense at times. He will spend more time on certain topics of he sees that the class hasnt grasped the concepts. He makes his notes available, and they are clear and organized. Overall amazing professor.

Prof Kochov is a cool guy. His classes are interesting. This was a new class, and wow did he impress. His lecture notes are amazing, well organized and clear. No textbook, because there is no textbook for this subject of economics. He made his own course out of nothing and deserves serious credit. Innovative! Take him, accommodating and reasonable!
Very clear lecturer with a sense of humor
He's great!

Very passionate about the topic and an engaging lecturer. He posts his own notes online which are very helpful for doing homework problems and reviewing for exams. It's a very interesting topic, but I definitely had to work for my grade. However, it's been the most rewarding ECO class I've ever taken. Would definitely recommend.

The class is mind-blowing, but can be very hard, especially if you don't know multivariable calculus. (Not too hard to pick up if you know univariable calculus.) I thought this was just going to be applied psych; it's not, it's like advanced micro. A grad student suspects Asen will get picked up by Harvard; I can see why.
I like him, really interesting. Tests/homeworks fair enough.

He loves what he is teaching, but since he is new it is sometimes hard to follow but the hw's and tests are very fair and the material interesting, although not easy. This is not a blow off class. Would recommend!
Little bit wacky sense of humor, long labs, and overall lecture vocabulary based exams. Penny is great

Dr. Higgins is awesome! Her love of Geology is infectious, and she is lively and funny lecturer, although at times she would drag on with jokes when she should have been lecturing. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you'll do fine on the tests. Overall she's a really nice and accommodating woman. I highly recommend her!
Penny is awesome. Her classes are never too hard, but always pretty fun. She's friendly and helpful, and also good at making animal noises. Like, really good.
Great, funny professor! Very organized and clear. Easy to contact with even after class. Exam is not hard and totally follow her lectures. I like her!
Good.

Penny gives enough information to understand the topic in class, yet still gives you room to think about a scenario that could arise. Her exams are very straight forward and offer extra credit. Used twitter for the first time and answered almost every tweet within an hour of it being sent out. Take this class if you can!! Worth it!!

The course itself was mediocre. Lectures were boring and uninspired. Homework assignments were uninteresting but at least they were aligned with the lecture material. Readings were interesting -- most likely the only good attribute from the course. Can I get my tuition refunded?
Professor Tresan is always willing to help during office hours and after lectures. The lectures were a bit boring but he explained materials thoroughly.

There are 22+6+331 journal entries for three assigned books in this course, but you seem to receive full credits easily as long as you read and write carefully, and only materials in the first book (with 22 journal entries) are discussed in class and tested on exams (there are study guides and online revision sessions helping you to review).

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: This is the worst organized college class I've ever taken. Unclear lectures and expectations, there are journal entries from different books that are due in class but other entries from other books due by email with no due dates just all due by a certain date and you can't submit more than one every 48 hours-yes it's as confusing as it sounds.
Terrible, boring lectures. The class is way too hard for what the class should be.
Hilarious is the descriptor that would best work for describing the man's talent at interrupting himself and other students from talking. He repeats and drones on with filler words "um" and "like".

He assigns a lot of reading, yet he never goes over the material in class. He would much rather discuss topics that aren't in the reading. Jon doesn't make himself available and left Rochester before he assigned an exam. This class has so much potential to be better than it presently is and the University should revisit the topic of keeping him.

Jon generally doesn't understand how to teach. He seems like a nice enough professor, however, he goes off on unwanted tangents and never explicitly addresses what he expects from you. It seem as though he doesn't even value his own thoughts on subjects, as his tests are open note and will mark your answers wrong for repeating concepts he taught.

He gives notes for almost every class and specific study guides before every exam. He always makes himself available after classes. Even if you are not in this class, he is happy to talk to you about some topics interesting. His feedback is clear and useful. And the grade is fair.

"Umm uhhh." -  Professor Tresan. He's a great guy and cares deeply for philosophy but his class is extremely unorganized. I really appreciate him as a professor and you can tell he's very good at viewing things from a different view. The tests are difficult but its possible to earn an A if you work for it. I'd take him once if you have the chance.
I wouldn't take a class with him again. Likes to hear himself talk, his study guides and reviews are just endless thoughts he writes down but never gets to the point.
Great guy- very helpful outside of class but lectures are extremely unorganized and hard to follow. Hard to keep up with the material if you do not attend class regularly.

He's undeniably a little eccentric (as many philosophy professors are) but he definitely grows on you when you get to know him better - I particularly recommend meeting with him one-on-one - he has a lot if interesting perspectives and insights.

He may not deliver his thoughts clear to every student and he could be hard to follow some times, but the lecture material he put in the study guide is logical, clear, and easy to understand. He is super helpful. Definitely talk to him about your thoughts or ideas. He will provide you a lot of related materials to enrich your view.
Do NOT do this to yourself. "Right, um, okay, yeah" and study guides the night before that are as unclear as he is. Terrible experience. Just. No.

Loves to hear himself talk - half of every lecture is nothing more than him walking back and forth, muttering "Right, hmmmmm..." over and over again. Makes you take a midterm the day after spring break ends and often times fails to reason properly. Pretentious, and obviously thinks he's brilliant, even though his doctorate is in a humanities.

He is all over the place, super unorganized, really laid back, is interesting though, kinda makes we want to keep attending just to see what he will do. I kinda like him, as a person but not so much as a professor.  Seems really smart though and is super nice.

Professor Terlazzo is my favorite professor I have ever had. She is extremely well informed in all of her subjects she teaches, she is easily reached, connected and kind. Grading can be tough depending on TAs but go to office hours to discuss paper outlines and you will do more than fine.  Highly recommend any and all courses with Rosa.

She is inspiring, clearheaded & has a straight-to-the-point attitude. If you review the syllabus, & plan accordingly, you will pass the class. Weekly readings are very quick to become tiresome, as she assigns two professional-level philosophy readings per week, and corresponding required responses; however, thoroughness is not required for these.

PHIL223 was a challenging philosophy course but hugely rewarding. Marking is tough but entirely fair. Lots of readings as well. You'll learn a lot from doing all of it, however, and she is immensely knowledgeable, thoughtful and articulate. One of the best profs I've had in uni and one of the best classes I've taken.

shes very nice, HOLY READINGS, new reading for every class and most were 10+ pages. classes are spent going over and conversing about the paper that was due before it. must annotate readings online and is graded. end of the year group presentations, you pick which topic you want but are randomly put into groups, would take again
Rosa is an incredible teacher! Very down to earth and approachable. The class itself was reading heavy, but easy to understand if you made an effort to attend class.

disclaimer: for PSCI 293, not PHIL 226
Rosa is the kindest, most well-educated and empathetic human being; engaging and insightful professor who truly cares about her students. 11/10
LOTS of reading and in-depth class discussion about them, def go to class bc it helps a lot with the 3 take home essays (only 2 pages and thats the hardest part)

I had Professor Terlazzo for Phil 226 and she did a brilliant job. She never failed to make students feel welcome to share even if they were way off base with their response. She's a great professor, so much so that I took another one of her classes because she was teaching it (and for credit too, but she's a benefit of that course)

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Really great lectures and insightful connections of how the content she teaches connects to the real world. The readings are difficult and can take a bit of effort to understand. But the grading is fair and as long as you understand what's being discussed in class, you should do fine on the exams. Take the class!

Rosa is amazing! I wish every class was structured like Philosophy of Law. She is genuinely caring about the students, provides so many opportunities to engage with the course content both in and outside of lectures, and she is very knowledgeable about her subject. Unlike most philosophy profs, Rosa always connects theory to reality.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Some of the texts are challenging, but the program she uses makes it easier to understand since you can access other students' comments on the reading. She's very accessible and easy to talk to, so I never felt bad asking for help. If you're curious, definitely sit in on a lecture or two.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Rosa was amazing at explaining all the concepts in the readings, and really broke everything down to make it super clear. She padded the grades a lot with easy completion grades for the reading and gave extra credit, and the papers weren't graded too harshly. Highly recommend!!

Professor Terlazzo is a good soul. She is so kind, non-judgmental, and asks thoughtful questions. Loves to make the students do the philosophy instead of lecturing at us. Make sure you show up, participate, and do the readings. Amazing course and professor - one of the best at UofR.

Such a horrible/difficult class to take. Nothing against Prof Terlazzo tho, she seems like a perfectly nice lady. But the class requires huge amounts of hours of reading and the TA who grades the exam is sooooo harsh. Make me wanna hang myself. Honestly, this is way too much work. Dont choose this class for ur own sake, unless you LOVE philosophy.

Rosa was very understanding and easy on students, especially during the pandemic. Did not demand a whole lot. Used a program that allowed us to discuss philosophical readings with other students, which helped me because some readings were hard for me to understand. Willing to add extensions, and is usually available for help.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: If you draw a Venn diagram of someone who is smart and someone who is nice, there's really no much overlap. But Professor Terlazzo is definitely in the overlap. She was very supportive under this online circumstance--genuinely cared about students' mental well-being. She always came super prepared for class and respected students' opinions.

She exaggerates her lack of knowledge in the field. Whenever someone asked simple questions in class regarding the material, she froze, gave a confusing answer, then emailed me later giving me an answer from Wikipedia. Her tests are terribly worded and she refuses to admit she is wrong. The TA at the time was awful! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!

She clearly is new and her skills as a teacher shows it. Her lectures are disorganized, her explanations are poor at best, she can't admit when she's wrong, she doesn't give exams back neither does she explain why answers are wrong. Going to her office hours is useless, and the TA at the time didnt even understand the material well enough to teach.

I enjoy interacting with Dr. Kline out of class, but in class, it's very clear that she's a brand new professor. Powerpoints, exams, and assignments are badly made, and she holds an attitude towards her teaching and course that feels unnecessary and unprofessional. In talking with her outside, I must reiterate that she is a wonderful person!

Really nice person, but kind of a mess as a professor. She is often late for class and always seems a bit unprepared and flustered. Definitely has trouble commanding attention of a big lecture class, so I feel like she would do better in a smaller class setting. Lots of errors on tests, and sometimes really confusing examples in class.

The content of 281 is minimal, and paying $2k+ for it would be a total scam if not for HA's amazing lectures. He really tries to teach the intuition! But 281 is a rough class... The projects are obscurely graded and impossible to complete well without seeing the TAs. Fourier methods are all it covers. But again, HA does a great and caring job!

Professor Aluie is one of the best professors that I have had in my entire college career. The way that he teaches truly builds an intuition for math. Rather than simply telling you how to solve problems, Professor Aluie teaches you how to think through the problems. But make sure to ATTEND LECTURE, otherwise, you will get nothing out of the class.

I would like to throw shade at other reviewers who suggest that the course is incoherent: it isn't. Lecture attendance (or recordings) and note-taking are essential in this course (as in other conceptually higher-level courses), and homework follows directly from it if you're paying attention to the elegant explanations. He clearly knows his stuff.

His courses are not organized at all, and he won't even be there for lectures sometimes. Although he doesn't have any finals, his course is not easy to get an A because 95 is an A. What's more, his homework has nothing to do with his class, toooooo hard. He also has three term projects which is also not organized, and not enough instructions.

You can tell he is incredibly smart, but not in a way where he doesn't know how to explain things in simple terms. One of the best lecturers I have ever had. There aren't any exams which is nice but weekly homeworks and 3 group projects. Give lots of time for the projects because they are sometimes not that clear what to do so you may need to ask

Prof Aluie is great with his lectures, hard class! As long as you understand his lectures, you should be able to do the homework, no exams. Projects are rough but I did not have any CS background. It would be very helpful to know some coding. If you need extensions, better to ask him in person! He recognizes where you sit if you go to class often.
I really enjoyed the lectures and found them very stimulating. I've never had a professor who could answer complicated questions so quickly and in such an intuitive way.

Prof. Aluie is very knowledgable and very willing to help students. The subject material itself is difficult with long tedious homeworks and grueling group projects, but Prof. Aluie knows this and gives students plenty of time to tackle these. Do not procrastinate, and reach out for help, and he will be amazing.

He's a pretty good lecturer and explains concepts well. Homework and exams are challenging for sure but the lecture material is directly relevant, plus- Aluie is the nicest person and incredibly helpful in office hours!
Homeworks and tests are difficult, but the class and concepts are taught well.

Professor Aluie is exciting and full of energy. He always has useful ideas and made connections between math and physics. He is also very friendly. Sometimes I could guess he did not prepare well but I always enjoyed his lectures. I think this was the first time he teached this course.
An awesome Professor, passionate and very friendly. He has a strong understanding of the course and tried hard to make us understand what he was teaching. He is good at explaining difficult concepts.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: I worked hard for this class but I liked it the most. Lectures are great even though they are at 9am :( Perfect teacher for this class. Tries to guess the answer before solving the math which is very helpful. Jumps a lot between big picture and small details. Good balance between theory and examples.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Difficult but manageable class. The textbook is very helpful but the exams reference many in-class examples and demonstrations he does, so it's important to go to class. He's very helpful one and one (more so than in lecture) and definitely rewards effort and initative.

Great guy! values intuition, shows demos and exams are fair. MCQ's makes you think and are tricky but are identical to practice exams except for subtle differences. It's good that he uses the textbook for notes because you don't have to spend much time reading it. If you are a Physics major, probably one of the easiest PHY classes out there.
+1 Truther here. Average class at best, lectures straight from the book, certainly not as great as the reviews say. The book was really good thankfully.
By far the best professor I ever had in all of my courses. He is so cool and gives very interesting examples from the real world.
Good lecturer, very intelligent guy, for my personal learning more examples and less derivation would have been helpful. Would have been nice if tests were curved slightly.
Good Professor,  very helpful but expects quite a bit from his students.
great guy!!!!!
Professor Aluie is by far one of the best professors I have met in college. He is one of the smartest people I have met he is a good person and he is HOT!!!
One of the best professors I had. He values intuition and is tough but fair.
He is an awesome professor. He really cares about the students and his lectures are fun a lot of the time.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: His tests are very different than most professors. It really tests you if you can apply the material to real life and articles.

Best professor of the MBA, I learned a lot he is an amazing human being who cares about you learning the reality of the Canadian market, he even helped to improve my resume, I would 1000%. HRMT has bad reputation but he made it so easy that I would totally repeat again.

Too bad he's currently full time at RIT, it's really our loss. F I guess this page has no use anymore. Bobby if you're reading this, come home!! Your lectures were the golden days. 1/2 the class was restarting the Apache server and all nighters but I think that was my fault. You always called out front row dorks for their pointless questions.
Amazing teacher. Great lectures. Chill dude.
He was an amazing professor. Loved his lecture, tons of examples. He did make the class harder than it had been in previous years but we were prepared for it.

Great lecturer, clear grading criteria and awesome powerpoints. The projects he gave us were a little bit challenging but I had so much fun working on them. You can really learn a lot from him. Strongly recommend!!!
Had him for the one semester he taught this class and it was awesome. Really nice guy that gives good lectures.

The Prof is very engaging in lectures and enthusiastic about the content. I've taken multiple courses with her, and every class was fun and had a comfortable environment. The courses can be a bit content (reading&film) heavy at times, but Prof Rosenow is very understanding and open to extensions as long as she has a forewarning.

James cares about her students. Sometimes expects students to do lots of reading and watch several movies in a week for her comics class particularly. She's very loose with projects/presentations/papers which are easy to do well in. Participation is a large part of the final grade. She's very knowledgable and passionate about the field.

One of the few college courses where the professor genuinely treats you like an equal and not only respects, but actively encourages joining into a discussion and sharing your perspective on things. You can clearly tell that she knows so much about what she's talking about and her enthusiasm is fantastic!
James Rosenow is god-tier. I love her. Best lecturer at UR.

Professor was nice and accessible for the most part, clearly knew what she was talking about but the class was incredibly disorganized. I have little to no complaints about the professor herself, but the way she organized the class was one of the worst things I've seen at my time at UofR.

I've greatly enjoyed both classes I took with Professor Rosenow. While young, she's clearly very experienced and knowledgeable about film. She wants all of her students to share in her passion and conveys so through her lectures. My only gripes would be ambiguity around assignments though she's far from a tough grader so it doesn't matter much.

Ok i found it really annoying how there were pop quizzes so you absolutely had to show up to every class. Wasn't fond of his teaching style, his final exam had 19 multiple choice questions so your grade can easily fall down to a B with just a few questions wrong on the exam. Couple of hw assignments nothing too bad.
Great professor. Even if you do not enjoy finance or if it is your first time studying, he makes it seem easy.
Great class, great guy. Would recommend.
He could teach a class on 100 ways to tie your shoe and I'd take it.
Great guy, easy class, show up and you'll be good

Prof. Jordan is clearly extremely intelligent, and as is often the case, this makes understanding him at time difficult. I think Jordan would help society more if he was completely be dedicated to research. The lectures varied in their difficulty; some I loved, some I hated (from frustration and being lost).

Jordan rarely explained topics in a way that was clear to those who had never taken Physics. The class was not meant as a class for physics majors, but rather was full of mostly students in other disciplines who were required to take it. He was unclear, and would focus on discussing the theoretical aspects of the problems, instead of how to do them

Not a good professor at all. His lectures are really confusing and the math he uses is well beyond the scope of the course. You 100% need to read the book to learn anything. The HW assignments are long and tedious. 1st midterm was easy, 2nd was challenging but fair, the final exam was RIDICULOUSLY HARD and very unfair. Pray for a good workshop TA.
His instruction will leave you confused. His tests will leave you angry. Avoid at all costs.

Be prepared for long grueling homework assignments. Oh and the TA's will grade at most 2 problems of the 20 asked to turn in. So if you mess up only 2 questions on the 20 question assignment and they only grade those 2 questions you get a 0, for literally hours of work.

Jordan isn't that bad. He only uses variables in lecture so that can be hard to get used to, but it really does help in the end if you put in the effort to follow it. Physics is just a tough subject, there's not going to be an easy way to teach it. You really have to change your way of thinking to be successful. Try to really learn the CONCEPTS.

He seems like a nice guy but I think 90% of the class would appreciate it if he "came down to our level" a few times per lecture instead of zooming through so much material and examples on the board. Get a tutor.

Not the greatest at making lecture interesting though he does have his moments. Does a lot of derivations in class that are not necessary for passing the class. I definitely suggest knowing the homework very well, tests are heavily based on them
A smart guy, but feels the need to derive and integrate everything. Take this course if you like the greek alphabet, as you will be seeing a lot of it.

Prof Jordan is a terrible teacher. He may be good at physics but he can't convey his understanding to students at all. Going to class was useless as well as the book. His tests were mostly unfair and difficult.
I took AP Mechanics in high school, so the class hasn't pushed me too hard. I've done pretty well. Other students with little previous physics experience tend to struggle, though.

Professor Jordan thinks that everyone is a calculus super star and that we all scored 5's on our AP exams. His lectures are extremely boring and his tests are ridiculous. He likes to say they're possible maybe because he's the professor. If at all possible stay away.

Jordan is one of the worst professors here. I understand physics is a challenging subject, but this guy can't teach it to save his life. If more then a 3rd of the class continually fails, then it's HIS fault! We study hard! He might possibly be worse then the intro to French professor here, Madame Lutkus. Both need to be fired. NOW!
awful class. very difficult, no review in or outside of class. goes quickly and assumes everyone is a calc genius. class did not help me or my gpa. lab is awful as well & is included in your grade.

I survived, this guy is tough and his lectures are almost useless, spends the a lot of time deriving formulas but no time on how to use them.  Real world examples are nice though.  Though when I started studying for MCAT's wow he did a better job than I thought.  Still tough though.
blamed us when the whole class didn't do well on a test
Jordan was not very clear and quite boring.  I consider him to be the worst professor I had during my freshman year.  Would not recommend taking a class with him.

This professor needs to improve his teaching skills and make the class more interesting in a way where the students understand the work and also have fun. More than half the class has failed both of his exams, and he's not to blame???

AVOID AT ALL COST!! lectures are useless! homework is differernt from lectures and the exams are 100% different than the lectures and homework!!...dont even ask about workshops.......He is without a doubt the worst professor I have ever had. Do your GPA a favor and dont take Jordan!! ...take it over the summer if u had to

His first midterm wasnt extremely hard but the second one was off the charts crappy. 45% is not a good average. He said something along the lines of "I can't believe you did so poorly when I gave you all spring break to do your homework and study." in regards to our lack of knowledge on a certain type of problem. Avoid him if possible  for you gpa.

Jordan is the most arrogant person I have ever met. He knows physics well but is horrible at teaching it and doesn't listen to students at all when they make suggestions or complain. The average grade on our last test was 47.5 and he told us that we clearly weren't studying enough. Never take a class with him if you can avoid it.

The material is simple but very engaging. Prof. Pazda uses great examples to explain his material and although class isn't mandatory it's fun to attend anyways.  He's a great guy.  As long as you read as well as review the slides from class, you should be okay test-wise.
This class is pretty easy as long as you go to class and then study by going through the powerpoint lectures. The material is straight-forward and I never needed to use the book.
Really awesome professor!:)  Super sweet
Interesting lectures and very good at explaining material. Tests were fairly simple with a lot of multiple choice.
Great Class.  Professor is very clear with his lectures and exams.  Can be dull at times, but his examples and stories are great.
He's an amazing professor. Class isn't necessary but very interesting, he uses great examples to explain material. The exams are simple but you do need to read the textbook for a few questions.
He is really willing to help you with your questions and grades !!! And there are many ways to get extra credits!

I took this class my freshman year and it was my favorite class of the year, mainly because of him. The material taught is pretty easy and the tests are usually multiple choice questions and short answers but you need to know all the stuff to score well in  his class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I have no clue why he's rated so low. The class was structured well, he taught coherently and assignments were graded fairly. He's a very nice person.

Randall Curren's philosophy classes were unbearable. His lectures were consistently biased, prioritizing his own viewpoints over balanced discussion. Rather than teaching critical thinking, he preferred hearing himself speak, shutting down any real debate. Avoid his courses if you actually want to learn philosophy.

I don't understand the grading system and he absolutely has no business assigning such low of grades for this class. He is stuck to his ways and is willing to debate anything BUT his grading system...

Way too much work for an ECE core course. Two presentations a week, random group calls—so you always have to prep. Spent more time on this than on my ECE core classes. Tough grading, trash course, trash prof. He doesn't care about your opinions at all. WORST COURSE FOREVER

manditory in the sense that you had to go there to be prepared for this useless debates. not in the sense that the lecture was. graded exams so harshly that U barely got points. main thing is that you learn NOTHING. like we all know this stuff is wrong. graded my reports all wrong. took all points off. He is a SHA BI

The trashest course ever manditory for ECE. Gave me a C, had three big tests, and useless non-stop debates on those useless Engineering Ethics stories. Why would you have us debate on something that had no opposite sides. Like we all agree with the stories on one side. There were no arguments to be made. Talked non stop. Harsh grading on everything

PHIL120 shouldn't be mandatory for ECE majors. The case studies are general engineering, not ECE-specific. If required, it should be for all engineering students. The 4-credit load is too much—I'd rather focus on senior design. The workload is heavy with exams, presentations, and strict grading. Feels like a waste of time.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Dr. Curren is a very kind professor who is quite passionate about what he teaches. While his lectures can be boring at times, I found his tangents as incredibly interesting and surprisingly funny. He truly cares about his students actually LEARNING and is willing to put this over the letter grade you receive.

I found his lectures extremely hard to follow, he tended to ramble and didn't make it clear what was actual material and what was fluff. We had a guest lecturer for one week and it was the only time I felt clear on the material, and his review sessions were pretty much useless. It made it very difficult to study for the final exam

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Curren is a very nice person. However, classes are mind-numbingly boring, so much that I needed to chug an energy drink before class to stay awake. He has no slide shows so if you don't go to class/aren't paying attention, ur screwed. I took this as an elective and it was my biggest mistake of that semester. Can't not recommend this class enough.

CONS: Extremely boring lectures, no visual learning, no clear grading rubric, wouldn't recommend taking unless you have to.

comment: Assigned good readings and brought up interesting points in lecture, but there was a lot of overlap between the two. Lectures were often regurgitating material from the book. When he brought up new material in lecture, it was interesting, but that was not a guarantee and lecture was often somewhat boring. Assignments were fair and not too hard.

Curren included quality readings, excluding his own writings, throughout the course, but it was a shame we never really got the chance to talk about them. Professor Curren frequently goes on topics that are tangential to the readings we have due in class and assumes that we haven't read them. He's very narcissistic and this slows his class down.

Professor Curren frequently interrupts students. This causes students to retreat inward and discontinue discussion. Curren personifies the Professor that doesn't care about the opinions of his students; instead, he blatantly disregards the views we have that differ from his own.

This course is about the ethics of technology and the amount of information that Curren lacks on technology is quite staggering. It's amazing that the University of Rochester hasn't replaced him with someone more knowledgeable about the subjects discussed within the course. Overall, I would strongly recommend staying away from this course and him.

I feel sorry for him. I guess he over invested his resources into the wrong field and is now trying to compensate for his many shortcomings. To cite a few examples, he, often, highlights his own personal life, his travels, and his leftist views on many subjects. There're some good articles included, however, these are ignored. It's quite shameful.

Professor Curren is excellent. He does tend to go off on 'tangents' but often they're actually quite relevant to what is being discussed - I view it as broadening the scope of what we're talking about and find it improves my understanding. His class is engaging and useful. I plan on taking more classes with Professor Curren.
BORING!!!, just him standing in the front droning on and on about how great his own views are. Biased and useless information. Do not take any class with this idiot.

I don't know why Curren is getting poor reviews. He is a great professor and extremely inspiring! This has been my favorite class at UR and I recommend it to everyone, especially if you have an interest in the environment. He rambles a bit but tells GREAT and RELEVANT stories.He is a wise teacher and a good soul.
No studies, no readings, no facts, just him rambling on and on about his own opinions. Very narrow worldview.
Terrible.

Horrible. The stuff we covered was interesting but class was a JOKE. He rambles on and on about nothing and I am so glad it's over. Go to the TA's office hours if you need help, but if you read the book you'll be fine.

Curren is a good guy, he just tends to ramble here and there.  His lectures can sometimes get a little boring, but the good thing is that the tests are fairly easy as long as you study.  Utilize the TA's office hours to brush up on notes you miss and you will be fine.  READ THE BOOK!!!  the tests are straight memorization.  Good luck!
this proff is all over the place, knows his stuff a little bit buy horrible overall, talks abut religion in one context then talks about flowers the next. he is all over the place
BORING BEYOND WORDS. intolerable. sooo glad its over

A truly great thinker, and excellent teacher.  If you are willing to really put your mind and effort into this course you won't be disappointed.  Would recommend taking any course he teaches.
Great prof.  Challenging course, but it will really make you think.

Poor teaching but having high expectations
The most authoritarian professor I've ever seen at the University of Rochester. The class material and tests are easy. High school level and not worth the tuition.

Exams are exactly off his slides. Just memorize his slides and you will get an A. His slides are funny and he is a great guy! Also, I love how he lets you choose one question that you don't want to answer from each section of the exam.

Elliott is a solid professor. The lectures range from very boring to interesting. He'd always add humor, though. You can do SONA and surveys for extra credit. The tests can be tough due to the written answer and fill-in-the-blank aspects. Papers are graded very generously, but only a small portion of the grade. Overall, the class was fine.

Love Andrew Elliot! Probably my favorite course at U of R, his lectures are engaging and fun, and I could sit through the whole lecture without getting bored. He tells lots of stories and is friendly, and the information is clear. Exams can be difficult, but if you pay attention, you will be fine. Test questions from the textbook are minimal.

This course is definitely worth taking, with three interesting essay topics for homework and three non-cumulative exams. The exams were straightforward, based on lectures and readings. The Professor used comic pictures to explain concepts, making it fun and relatable. I'm so glad I took it, it's literally the most interesting class I've ever taken!
Prof. Elliot is very kind and cares a lot about his students. His class is interesting and engaging and it is clear that he is passionate about the topic. He's also really funny.
Class was very interesting but tests were really hard to study for and know all of the material.

The class was pretty easy and if you study, you will do great. There's extra credit + questionnaires (kinda extra credit??). He has 3 non-cumulative exams + 3 really leniently graded essays (just follow rubric and you'll get 10/10). I highly recommend this class as a fun and interesting topic! He also does little fun personality tests.

Great guy. Took an intro class so content was v basic + lecture could be boring. Enjoyed his stories that gave us a break from material. Have to purchase the reading, don't need to read it but the bolded vocab words WILL be on the exams. Need to list what he has on his slides on exam. Easy class, j. memorize evtg. 3 essays are not graded harshly.

Great Professor. Exams are generally not too hard and mostly multiple choice. There is a good amount of extra credit opportunities. Attendance isn't mandatory and lecture slides are available on Blackboard. My only criticism is that Prof. Elliot goes on long tangents that often make lectures drag on.

I found Professor Elliott to be a compelling lecturer with clear knowledge and prestige within his field. The class itself was straightforward with the final grade determined by three small papers and three exams. The content was interesting and presented succinctly.

Exams are multiple choice, fill in the blanks and short essay. He uses a lot of cartoons in class which is really funny and he is very easy to follow. In my opinion, the best psychology prof. here with applicable things in real life.

He's a very good professor and is fair in his grading scheme (top 30% get an A). His tests aren't too hard and you can skip one question per section but they require a lot of memorization. There is not much info in each lecture so you won't be frantically writing the whole time. The three papers are very easy and take at most 2-3 hours each.
Prof. Elliot is very nice and is a good lecturer. Not hard to get a good grade if you go to the lectures and put some efforts.
Interesting class, lectures aren't boring; not that hard if you go to lectures. The assignments/essays are not graded harshly (as long as you put some effort into it you'll get a good grade)

Professor Elliot is a fantastic lecturervery engaging and clear about what material you will be tested on. Apart from his effective teaching style, the material covered in PSY 161 is fascinating and highly applicable to your daily life. Great class to take for psych requirements or just for fun :))
Professor Elliot has been one of my favorite professors so far. His lectures are well-organized and engaging and he is good at explaining the information. The class is very interesting and engaging

This class was one of the most engaging online classes I have taken. The material is very interesting and applicable. It is relatively easy to do well in the class by going to lecture and just focusing on the vocab from the textbook. The professor is very engaging and provides personal anecdotes in each class.

Not a hard class. The topic is very interesting however you can't not study for the tests. People go in thinking they'll get As and leave with Bs.

Never rated any professor, but this professor deserves it. The best professor I have had here so far, very interesting, laid back and funny. Highly recommend taking his class.

Go to class, even if you know he could finish the lecture in thirty minutes but wastes an hour and a half on it, read the chapters a few days before the test, memorize the vocab and you'll get an A. Rambles on at points, talks about himself a lot (which is fine sometimes), doesn't seem to present or stress empirical and scientific data/studies in depth enough

easy going! interesting!!

Not a hard class but you still learn a lot. Elliot makes class interesting by taking breaks to show cartoons and tell funny stories about himself so we can get to know him. He has a great sense of humor and is a great teacher.
Great class, watch out for tests, they can be a little tricky.

The best sensei ever! Very fun, very enthusiastic! The class is extremely easy! Easy A! Don't be afraid, take it!
Shino-sensei is an amazing teacher. She is really helpful one on one as well as in a class of 40.

I really enjoyed this class!

His essay comments were unhelpful and unkind, and he graded them very harshly. He tends to ramble a lot in his lectures and uses a lot of unnecessary big words. Worth the time but with a different prof.

It seems like what I am seeing from other ratings, he seemed like a good professor at U of R. I am at Geneseo and this class is one of my hardest. It's not so much the in class lectures that is hard to understand, but the papers I have no idea what he is looking for. There is no rubric and his comments on the essays are really hard to understand.

Prof. Carrick is one of my favorite professors. I decided to take his class after I read an interview with him where he mentions that he sings songs to his cats. If it's not enough for you, he is also a former football player in Manchester United. Such a versatile personality! I see him sometimes on campus playing with his ball! He still got this!
Dont think this man knows what hes looking for. Has no rubrics, asks you to include certain things in your papers but then grades against you for using those same things. A very poor teaching style

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I recommend it! It's a very straightforward class and if you do your assignments and pay attention it's an easy A. I took the summer course so the workload might be different, but I found it manageable though there was a lot of reading- but if you skim for main ideas he'll go into more detail during lecture.

Easy class in terms of workload.  Very little actual work, more just reading of the material.  Elliot does a great job explaining material so it is important to go to class.  Tests are difficult if you do not take decent notes in class.  All the readings are online so no reason to buy a textbook.

Dr. Elliott is great at teaching things clearly. He emphasizes what's important and is great at answering any questions that come up in class. The assigned readings aren't necessary to do well in the class, but they augment understanding and most of them are very interesting. His tests are also very fair because he gives good study guides.

He's the man! Made me want to take more philosophy classes. You have to go to lecture and take good notes if you want to do well - he breaks down all the readings so they make more sense, and spoon feeds you arguments. Midterm, final, and one paper (not a lot of work). Also really helpful in office hours and very interested in what his students.

Dr. McAleavey is one of the most caring professors in the Biomedical Engineering department. You can tell that he is extremely passionate about ultrasound and his lectures are interesting and informative. He is always happy to help a student who needs assistance. Overall, Dr. McAleavey is fair, knowledgeable, excited, kind, and resourceful.

Is the class the most interesting thing ever? No. But he's a great professor, a little quirky, very friendly and approachable, and he's very accommodating. He grades fairly, and, for once in my college career , he ACTUALLY tests the same things he's covered and asked about in homework, and the tests are straight forward. Overall great dude

He is a very friendly teacher ready to be there fore you at any time. He is also very funny and full of stories. He doesn't want you to dumbly remember things, he rather makes you work through each concept of physics by yourself and REALLY understand it.

Prof. Kovanis is a great professor, if tough. Very willing to help, very thurough, very intelligent. He is a bit tough and will push you, but that is why you came to college. I hope. If you do all the work, you will do very well. I handed the final (one of the hardest I've had) to him and said with a giant grin "Is that all you have?" =)

He is very insightful. He is not a normal teacher and rarely if ever uses the book. He is concerned more with what you will take away from the class rather than memorizing useless information. if you pay attention and write notes, it won't be hard. He hooks it up with extra credit if needed.

I thought he was great. He was kind of funny. His tests and homeworks were pretty hard, but if you have done all he has asked, you'll do well. I've tried to get him for calc 3, 4 but it just doesn't seem to line up with everything else I have to take.
very funny, and helpful if you are serious about the course. does not like when you sleep in class
"You are masters of calculus" is his claim ... you will not be a master of calculus after completing his class period. Very hard to understand and follow during lectures. No calculators allowed.
quite possibly the worst calc teacher at RIT
horrible...stay away

Professor Turkkan did a great job supporting us as students and was a pleasure to work with, and always provided insightful feedback on our work.

I really benefited from the feedback Prof. Turkkan provided on my work. It allowed me to understand my strengths and use them to improve my writing. She allowed me to feel more confident in my work and my writing abilities.
Sevinc Turkkan is a great and passionate teacher. Also, she makes the best baklava I have ever had.

Professor Turkkan is one of the most jolly professors I have had this semester. She is just full of life and her lectures are interesting. If you want to learn how to be a better writer, take her class. She gives really good and quick feedback and wants you to learn. Plus, she made baklava for us!
Good teacher! Take her class if you want to learn something.
She is great! Really helpful! She gives great feedback to essays and is willing to allow extra time if you have difficulties with some activities.
The instructor is helpful in and outside the class, and gives great feedback. The grading is clear and objective. I had fun time writing my stuff, especially the last two papers.
Well worth the time and effort. She opens up your eyes beyond the ordinary.

Dr. Turkkan is positive, determined, enthusiastic, and brilliant. I learned so much under her teaching and enjoyed getting to know her in and out of the class. I am actually sorry her class is over and she is not teaching anything new next year. I would take anything with her. I will miss her next semester.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: I love Dr. Turkkan! She is always available to help outside class. She loves her students and she is an excellent instructor. She is not "easy" though. No easy As here. You have to sweat but it's so much worth it. You walk away having learned something. I have become a better writer thanks to her. Take her, you won't regret it!

comment: This professor: Made going to her book signing an extra credit assignment Assigns more homework than all of my STEM courses combined Has no coherent grading system Called the entire class lazy on multiple occasions Thinks that writing formulas are bad but requires us to use them anyway Is not a native english speaker (bad spelling/grammar)
He Brings a lot of professional experience to the table. Extremely knowledgeable. Asks for professional delivery as well as quality contents.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Brings a lot of professional experience to the table. Extremely knowledgeable. Asks for professional delivery as well as quality content.

She is very clear and smart but she will take your art and draw on it, too. That bothers me because it's not her art, she should respect their art. Yes, I encourage feedback on what should be changed but not changing it for them.

Paula is an excellent professor. She always make sure EVERY students understand their assignments. She even gave some students few chances to improved their grades. Some students complaining about their low grades so they blame Paula. It is wrong because they didn't do THEIR effort to show up the classes or give homework on time.
She was not helpful to me at all and she does not clarity anything. Her ideatools website is very confusing and her relying on it all the time actually caused my failure.

She's very open-minded, likes to chat with students about almost anything before and after classes. Relies a LOT on IdeaTools, but everything on there is needed for anyone who might need extra help. Fantastic artist, enjoyed having her for the last three years!

Knows the material but can have trouble conveying it sometimes. Got confused/made mistake once in a while (not a huge deal). Can make funny jokes. However, grading is harsh, especially on homework. If you dont submit your work exactly the way she wants, lots of points will be taken off. Can be slightly condescending. Overall, okay professor.

Good professor. Make sure you pay attention in class and read the book, as the concepts are not hard to understand if you study them. Homework was graded with a rubric, but there were never typed reasons for points taken off, just the question number (answers were posted though). Exams were online and mostly multiple-choice.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Tough grader']
comment: Flat out mean to students, especially when they ask question. Constant homework and extremely strict grading criteria for all assignments. If you don't do it her way, it is wrong. Got confused at her examples in class and would often backtrack. I would strongly advise taking anyone else, especially for CS Theory.

Idk how Susan has over a 1.5 rating. She is blatantly mean to students, gets confused with examples in her own lecture, and has exams with things she hasn't covered in class. I wish someone told me this - DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER. She makes you feel belittled and stupid.

Dr. Haller has adjusted well to online classes. Lectures are detailed with examples (with the occasional hiccup), hw is relevant, and tests/quizzes were fair. Textbook is required but no online codes, hw is all handouts & pdfs in mycourses. Recitation is mandatory, 1/week. Final was murder, be prepared. Would recommend, Haller makes you work for it
I will echo what others have said: her way of grading is frustrating and she can sometimes get confused when doing lectures. I do not plan on taking another class with her.

She's not bad, she's not good. She's meh. You'll learn a bit from her lectures, albeit her lectures are quite scattered-brained and she confuses herself while lecturing. She's forgetful, a harsh grader, quite hostile towards men (don't you dare ask her for a favor as a male, you'll regret it). Would I recommend her? Nah.
Very well rounded course and professor. Course was structured very well. Adapted well during covid-19 situation.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: One of the worst professors I've had so far. Extremely scrutinizing grading policy, and very unfriendly when you go to see her in her office hours. Boring. Does not set her grading criteria clearly, will take points off for changes outside of the rubrics bound. Half of our final consisted of 2 sections we had never gone over in class. Do not her.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Dr. Haller isn't bad at all. A lot of people seems to think that Dr. Haller is bad b/c of the coding assignments. They help boost your grade / are not to hard! tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']

Her lectures can get a bit boring sometimes since she reads from the slides. Just don't be disrespectful in class or a moron.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Caring']
comment: Professor Haller is a great teacher. I have struggled severely in this class, but she's always been a good teacher and it's not her fault really. Go to her office hours, she will give you great motivation and is such a sweet person. Make sure you aren't just a name to her, she cares about those who care about the class. Solid option for CS

Just a phenomenal professor. His lectures are engaging and enjoyable, and he makes a subect that honestly is somewhat boring into a really fun class. He's really lighthearted and jokes around a lot with everybody. This class has a lot of work, but he's super helpful.
I really enjoyed Professor Humphrey's class!

He was a good professor who was very knowledgeable about the subject matter. Half of the class was lecture and the other half was independent work during which he and TAs would be available to answer questions. There is a fairly large amount of homework but it's doable if you don't procrastinate.
likes to laugh at his own jokes

Extremely flaky on schedule. Consistent mistakes on HW, derivations, proj defn and seldom beyond the 50 minute class time. Took a month to get exam graded. Only 2/5 HW have been graded, and the next exam is next Monday, w/ no knowledge of how we've performed (by grade). Orig syllabus was 10 HW, 10 quiz, 3 proj, 2 exam. Only 5Q, 5HW, 1 exam so far.

After disliking his MECE117 course, my opinion of Prof. Humphrey improved considerably while taking Vehicle Dynamics.  The course is very theory-heavy, but was very cleary presented.  My biggest gripe with him is that he is extremely flaky with the schedule of the course, but these changes do not ruin the course. Takes forever to grade exams
Lectures are boring but he's a good teacher, interacts well with students, and is willing to help outside of class.

Prof Humphrey is a pretty good professor, even though 117 is a bit of a drag in the first place. He does well in lectures to introduce what is being covered, and makes sure it is thorough enough so someone with zero coding experience can catch on. He is also prepared to explain questions in detail if needed

MECE117 is a drag regardless of who you take it with. I found Humphrey the most helpful and willing to explain in intricate detail the problems you're having while coding. Beware though, the lecture days drag on forever. I think this will happen regardless of the professor. Go to OH, get the work done ASAP, and enjoy the rest of the week.

He was the most supportive teacher I had this semester. I kinda hate Matlab but he made it bearable. He'd occasionally post homework/lectures last minute but was understanding if you needed more time. T.A.s were helpful, homework is difficult but not graded harshly. The midterms suck, but they're the same no matter which 117 teacher you have
I would say that "mid" perfectly describes this guy. He will go over some crazy stuff in lecture that you never see again. Also, tests are mildly annoying as you have to write down lines of code.

Professor does not respond to emails, always post homework too late (he kept saying he forgot or did not get the chance to post it), and takes too long to grade exams. Gives me a terrible grade for final project with no feedbacks or reasons. The only thing that is not bad from this class is that the professor is friendly.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Great teacher, super nice person. His lectures were dense, but the studio work always supported what he taught and he was there to answer questions along with the TA's. There wasn't too much homework and tests were manageable. Incredibly helpful during office hours and is always kind and understanding. Any hate for this man is misplaced.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I honestly don't understand the hate he gets. It isn't too hard, and everything is manageable. The lectures are clear with lots of examples, you have hands on practice with every topic (that's graded for effort), and he is very accessible outside of class. I would highly recommend going to his office hours, because he is a huge help!

We're living in a pandemic; things happen (e.g. technical difficulties, life). Please be kind. Lecture videos are available online, class time used to explain problems and work on hw. Programming felt impossible until I went to office hrs regularly. Professor Humphrey knows how to GUIDE your understanding. Get to know him; down-to-earth friendly.

So a homework I submitted a month and a half ago still has not been graded. Along with 5 or so other homeworks that have been submitted and not graded. Last few times I tried to go to office hours to seek help he just wasn't in the zoom meeting.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I was hoping to love this class, but the professor makes it nearly impossible. The class is heavily lecture based and then pull us into the lab, with him and Mr. Fly expecting us to solve it based off of what examples were provided on the slides. It would be much better if they guided us through one problem and had us complete one by ourselves.

Humphrey does not try to trick you at all with his tests, the questions are straightforwards and he provides the formulas! He does a good job at using stories and his industry knowledge to explain concepts and his enthusiasm is evident. Lectures are engaging. He does, however, often take a while to get grades back to students.

There are too many sections of this lab in a week and so Prof. only takes about 2-3 of them, but he holds office hours that are open to all students. The other labs are taken by TAs that have been trained by him. It's an easy class to do well in, attendance, quizzes, surveys and test reports are graded. He gives bonus credit quizzes too.
Class is pointless, doesn't respond to emails, and grading is harsh and not logical.

He uses iclicker for attendance (it's partially that you are there and that you answer the question correctly), he encourages everyone to talk during the iclicker questions. Lectures are pretty boring. First test was easy the other two were so-so. No homework is graded. Weekly quizzes

Optional HW helps you practice for exams. 2 exams and final are 70% and quizzes + participation are 30%. He is very knowledgeable but often times PP links to videos don't work or makes an error in his in-class calculations. Very nice guy but takes forever to return anything. Makes TA and visiting professor do a lot of his work. Overall average

Honestly, Humphrey is by far, the worst teacher I have ever had!!!. Every single week he showed up at least 10 minutes late to class . He always had an excuse blaming traffic. He promised lab reports to be graded by the end of each week, but it is week 15 and I still have not gotten the week 1 test report back!  He also NEVER replies to emails.

He only showed up to 3 labs the entire semester.  He let his TA (who was extremely good) do all of the teaching and all of the grading. I don't actually know how hard of a grader or how clear he is because because he didn't grade or teach anything. When he was there he was really good, but he was only there 3 times and only for the experiments.
He will NOT return graded assignments to you until the very last minute. Lectures are minimally helpful. Tests are easy and he is an easy grader.

Let his foreign TA(who no one could understand) teach every lecture. Would walk into class 15 minutes late and spend the rest of the time on his cellphone. He didn't even show up to some labs. If you did finally get him to get off his a$$ and do something he was usually quite helpful. Never got grades back. Worst lab professor I have ever had.

Knows his stuff. Class is very interesting. Well structured; however, he takes forever to grade or return items. Tests and quizzes are clear and he prepares you well for them. Class often lets out early. Recommended.
Cool guy, if you go to class you will do fine. It takes him forever to hand back work so you won't have a clue what your grade is going to be till week 11.

Cool, chill guy. If you go to class and pay attention, you'll do fine. During office hours, he will explain everything from the very beginning, so make sure to take advantage of that! I enjoyed the class, though he takes a while to hand work back sometimes.
Just pay attention in class, and maybe watch the videos and you'll do fine. Takes awhile to hand back work.

A good guy who knows the material. I knew nothing about programming until I took his class. Very clear in explanations. Class is very easy if you show up and pay attention. Does take a while to give back assignments.

He is an okay professor, he just teaches a course that I can't stand. He has daily one question quizzes, he does not hand work back until right before the exams. Has a grader grade all of the work. Great guy, not so great professor. I'd give him a 6 out of 10 for teaching.

He has a hard time getting work back on time so you don't know how you are really doing in the class until it might be too late, but he has a lot of students work to grade. If you just go to his office hours the class is enjoyable and easy I like him a lot as a teacher!!!!

Awful, avoid at all costs. He has potential to be a good teacher, but he is so lazy and so hard to meet up with to ask questions. He never grades anything until week 10 and takes points off for stupid things.
I haven't gotten any of my work back until week 10, so I had no idea that I was doing something wrong on the problems the entire quarter.

Awful teacher. He ate pizza once at the beginning of his lecture while teaching. Never gets any work back graded until the very end of the quarter when finals are done so you can't argue the grade. This guy is the laziest teacher I have ever seen. Lost 15 points on a lab for "format" and nothing else. All the content and everything was correct.

Terrible at handing back work.. Gives a policy for how homework is graded, but doesn't grade the homework himself; The TA grades the work without following what the prof said. Quizzes are easy if you read the book. Posts when his office hours are, but often arrives there late. I hope he's better for Problem Solving with Computers

He shows up regardless of the weather. But if you think you're going to get /anything/ back, good luck. It's the 8th week, I haven't received any work back, and I stopped getting grades all together after the 5th week (participation points). Multiple people have emailed him, he just doesn't grade ANYTHING. Fun fact, he sounds EXACTLY like Kermit.
Not good at returning graded work, some discrepancy between classwork and book definitions. Quizzes are easy, extra credit for answering  questions during class.

Had for Materials Processing. Seemed to teach pretty clear. He is unorganized, doesn't get things graded and returned. Example, during finals week he had 1/5 quizzes graded and posted that had been taken throughout the quarter. He blows it off when brought up and says that he is going to be grading in his office right after class, but doesn't do it

I had professor Humphrey for Materials Science Lab for the 20094 quarter.  The lab was very easy going. Professor Humphrey was very clear and easy to approach if you needed help/more info.  I would recommend him.

Ridiculous amounts of homework. Prof is an adjunct + fulltime engineer. Expects students to have similar level of knowledge and experience as him. Very unforgiving if you miss even one deadline. Lots to learn from him but this class should be two semesters long based on the amount of work. Half the class dropped because of how much work :/

Professor DeRooy is an incredibly sweet professor, and she puts extra effort into making the lectures as thorough as possible. The material itself is very easy to learn and this class is a great way to fulfill an ethical perspective requirement.

MORGAN NICOSIA IS THEIR NAME. "If you do the readings, take notes on the lectures, watch and take notes on the films, and do all of the assignments, you'll be fine!" That is a large amount of work for an intro class. Flaky, lots of personal issues affecting class time. Material was uninteresting, very read-and-regurgitate. Do not take this prof.

She would cancel class last minute for emergencies, which I understand. What I don't understand is why I would see her sitting around on campus after she canceled class. She also takes forever to grade stuff, so you never know where you're at. I had an A at one point, then suddenly it dropped to an F when it was near the withdrawal deadline.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Nicosia is a very knowledgeble and passionate professor, and has a decent course calender. BUT they expect to put a huge amount of work for an intro class, and they are very rarely available outside of class. To save you time the other prof ain't good either. textbook is the bible and, don't blank out during lectures and discussions good luck.

Do not take this class. A nice person, but not a good teacher. She cancelled class about 7 times, which made me feel it was not worth the money. If you do take this class, expect 40+ page readings, long movies, and tests and quizzes with no answer leniency. We were basically "own our own" for studying, given no study guide, blaming her ADHD.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Mostly discussion-based and graded on monthly assignments, some essays, and general participation. The only "test" is a final presentation with a group. This class is not a traditional "I tell you this and you remember it" type.  Often, tangents start based on the reading and turn into more. If that's not something you want, don't take it.

The only good part about Nicosia's class was the reading material and screenings assigned, which anyone could find on their own. They gave WAY too much homework for the class, went on and on about their personal life instead of teaching, and frequently canceled class out of nowhere many times without proper notice. I would never their class again.

By far the worst instructor I have had in my entire life. Emotional, unprofessional, sent several inappropriate emails throughout the semester accusing cheating. Late and unclear grading, assigns grades sporadically on a unspecified rubric. Very judgmental of students and often gets annoyed in class. Started crying for sympathy during one class.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Professor was interesting, but I would not recommend their class for a perspective. You were assigned a film journal every week where you had to write 500 to 750 words. Early on you will think you're doing well in the class because they don't give you notes and then suddenly their grading will get harsh. Overall this class wasn't worth it!

I didn't know the amount of reading I would have to do, but nonetheless, this professor cared about the circumstances people were in. Overall I wouldn't take it again, wasn't my type of subject. If you are into it I would say go ahead and take all these reviews with a grain of salt!

I went into this intro class thinking it wouldn't've be that bad. Little did i know i was swamped with readings. The content that was on tests wasn't clear in the readings because you couldnt find what you needed. its about 30 pages a week, with a weekly quiz, and essays... The most boring lectures that turn into opinionated conversations.

I took VISL.120 expecting it to be an easy fun class. Unfortunately this was not the case with Dr.Nicosia. Lectures are very long and boring and often filled with them ranting about their personal life. Papers are graded months after the due dates and are graded unfairly given the vague grading rubric. Do not recommend.

This professor is extremely passionate about what he is teaching. Over the course of the semester the course was cancelled and although it could have been disruptive to learning, they stayed in continuous contact with the students. They had unexpected family emergencies that required cancellation of classes or moving to an online session.

This class was disorganized, the professor cancelled class multiple times, assigned way too much work for a 200 level course, and they were extremely defensive of their teaching style. They did not grade fairly or in a timely manner. I wish I had taken something easier, but I had no idea the class was going to be this hard.

Very knowledgeable and passionate. However, usually cancels class and assigns excessive extra homework instead. Very defensive and difficult to approach. Seems to expect everyone to have an extensive formal writing background, grades very harshly, and offers little to no feedback on assignments, including large semester-long ones. Don't reccomend.

This class was supposed to be a fun senior class about movies but turned into a confusing nightmare. Dr. Nicosia was absent half the time, then would assign random HW and get angry when students asked for clarification. Assigned work we never discussed in class then midterm and final included information never covered. I don't recommend.

Dr. Nicosia cancels class all the time as well as assigns work that is very confusing to understand. They give work that they cannot even grade in a timely manner and then give out grades just to give out grades. Goes on tangents during boring lectures or watch a movie that we can watch at home and we don't talk about the movies we do watch.

Nicosia is a good lecturer and is clearly passionate about what they teach. They can sometimes go on tangents but they're usually entertaining. Class was cancelled a fair bit which is a bit disappointing but they did their best to make it up. Homework was graded pretty easily, but they are not very keen on giving extensions on big assignments.

Dr. Nicosia seems like a really cool person but I think that they have much more passion for film and theater than they do for teaching. Class was cancelled probably more than half of the time and they seemed disorganized and unprepared. We were assigned way too much work last minute, and I didn't really enjoy what could have been a very fun class

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I took VISL-120. I dropped the class due to missing the online midterm deadline because of a personal issue, which Dr. Nicosia was not understanding of at all. I only went to one class and as far as I know it's literally just watching movies. I'm more upset that Dr. Nicosia apparently let everyone retake the midterm after I withdrew...

He was a really fun teacher and managed to engage a lot of students that weren't previously interested in theatre. There is a group project that is pretty simple, as long as you do it you should be fine. All the exams were online and open note which meant if you had the textbook you could easily get an A

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Great class, great professor. An appropriate amount of work for a 300 level class.

Professor Nicosia is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and treats them more like his peers than students he lectures to. There is quite a bit of reading in the class but you can get by without doing the readings. You have 3 exams during the semester, mine were all open notes online, and one large group project for your final.

Dr. Nicosia is an amazing professor, and his classes are thoroughly interesting. I've taken 3 classes with him so far and hopefully will continue to in the future. There is a lot of reading, there is a fair amount of writing, so be prepared for that.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: performing identity: wordy articles to read, a movie or two to watch every week, & a short easy paper due each week based of the reading & viewing. can easily get an A by just trying & showing up, dont even need to be active in discussion. 1 group project & final 10 pg paper. overall the prof is great, easy to talk to , knowlegable & open minded

Grades his women & gender studies class as if it were an English course. Makes a big deal about not invalidating other writer's pieces for small mistakes, but will demote you two entire letter grades because your indentation is off. Avoid him if you can.
Awesome class about science fiction film and television. The theory can be difficult at times but he always takes time in class to explain and answer questions.
Feels like a lot of work initially but it's an easy class. Professor is always available if needed to meet outside of class.

I really really enjoyed Intro to Theatre with Nicosia. For sure there was quite a bit of reading and writing, but the prompts are very straight forward and it is really not hard to put out the two page paper if you actually did the reading.

Going in I didn't know what to expect.  There was a lot more work than expected.  There was at least one two-page paper due almost every week.  However, the prompts were not that difficult.  Nicosia took students feedback to heart and changed somethings along the way, even the time of our final exam.  He truly cares about his students + the course.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: This coarse had more work than my Computer Science class. While that should say it all I will expand on that. Assignments: A chapter read through before each class, a two page essay on a play every week (at minimum), an essay on a live action play you must attend, and a group final project including two essays and a power point.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: I took this class thinking that hey its an intro to theatre class how hard could it be.  DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!
