I highly advice you to re-think your choice.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: He is a nice guy but - A 2 page paper about a different play is due every week. Some weeks, 2 papers are due. - REQUIRES A SPECIFIC EDITION OF TWO TEXTBOOKS - Requires students to read long 40 pages chapters of the textbook for class. A chapter due almost every other class day. - Regurgitation exams Avoid him unless you really like theatre

While the lectures are boring and drawn-out, he is good at explaining difficult concepts. I never felt completely lost even when learning new topics because he explained it thoroughly and clearly. As long as you go the the lectures, take notes, and pay attention, you'll do fine.

While I certainly learned in this class, it was not enjoyable nor did it help on exams. He insists on using R to show problems, despite not being able to use it at all on tests, and the final being commoncore means that while every other prof teaches minitab outputs, you will be floundering when it comes to the final. Only grades are hw/quiz/exams.

Professor Gratton wasn't a bad professor by any means, he was a very fun and chill dude with very clear lectures. While his notes are somewhat hard to read, if you go to his office hours for 1 on 1 tutoring, he is incredible at explaining even the most complex of things in a way that makes it feel so easy.

Had for Graphical Math. Lecture consisted of notes for 3/4's of the class and an attendance question that very minimal with 5% of your total grade. Worst was tests, no matter how much I studied I never seemed to get over a 50% grade and no TA's present in the class, get ready for lots of note taking and 3 midterms and every topic final for 35%

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: If you're taking this teacher, please understand that this isn't the math teacher you can skip class until exam day. You will inevitably fail. What you gotta do is take notes, learn to understand his learning style, and go to his office hours and LA sessions (hes AMAZING at 1-1 tutoring). Do this, and you'll pass (with the VERY lenient curve).

His lectures are completely written by him during the class and are accessible outside of class. He teaches a lot of in-depth info in each class. He is nice and is willing to answer questions for each topic. The class is difficult, so there's a curve in the grading. But if you show up and take notes, you should be fine.
This guy reads off the lecture slides. He has no backbone, no spine. He knows his stuff but he is an atrocious teacher, and it would be advantageous to not take his course and take someone elses.
On the one hand, lectures were dense and boring, and even when you pay attention you will probably have to teach most of it to yourself. On the other hand, the grading curves were spectacular.

You would have to teach yourself if you never took calculus before. I took calc in high school and barely managed to get an A in the class. During lecture if you ask him a question he just answers with where to find it in the textbook. However, one on one he explains the topics well. There is a quiz every week in the class plus classwork.

I found that the lectures were difficult to follow. There were too many definitions and proofs in the notes, and not nearly enough practice problems.  I learned the most when doing the homework. Besides that, I found that his end-of-semester review sessions were helpful and he was open to questions after class.

prof is an okay guy sometimes will drop a bad hw, or quiz grade. However, he is super boring and hard to understand during lectures. I will say if you have to take him utilize your time doing your own practice problems and self studying and go to his office hours that's where he really shines. don't slack exams are 70% of your grade.

For lectures he takes straight from the textbook and then proceeds to make it more confusing than it needs to be, you'd be better off reading from the book yourself. On top of that, most of your grade is based off of four exams that sometimes contain material that never gets taught.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Test heavy']
comment: Exams count for 85% of the grade, and test material is never made clear until the last lecture. Gratton shoots himself in the foot with how he lectures and communicates with the class, but is kind and can curve. If you take his Linear Algebra class, teach yourself using the book and only come to lectures before a test, saves time.

This guy does not teach, he overexplains simple stuff and doesn't go into detail about actual content. Bro will sit there for ten minutes doing simple arithmetic but gloss over the main content. He's so obsessed with "getting ahead" that we didn't do any practice problems in class. He made me want to fall asleep every lecture.

Dude loves math but cannot teach it for the life of him. Lectures were so boring. He just recites what the textbook says and does not go into depth with anything important. His notes are crowded and not easy to understand. Be prepared to learn everything outside of class if you don't have calc experience.

Organized, posts board work every day, clearly communicates homework deadlines and test days. Goes over problems on the board in a simple manner, not a lot of in-depth explanation. Very large class size (for my class at least), so asking questions is hard.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Graded by few things']
comment: this dude is genuinely the worst professor and he lives to make student's lives miserable. do everything to avoid this guy.

He overcomplicates and underexplains. His grading is meticulous, which is a standard he doesn't always meet in his own lectures. Not flexible either.

The lecture's engagement can be measured by the sheer number of my peers playing video games or doomscrolling. Not flexible either.

He's nice, but I wouldn't recommend him if you intend to learn.
Only reads from book. Does not explain material well. Goes through the material too fast, and grades exams hard. I would not recommend taking this class with him.

Extremely test-heavy makes the first exam incredibly difficult, so a bunch of people drop the class. No curve is given, even if the class average is a 50% on the exam. Doesn't teach; all he does is read straight from the book, and he reads through material very quickly. You learn something that is on a quiz either the week before or 2 weeks before.
I don't even take this guy's class, but what I've heard has been bad enough so I figured I'd contribute
If you have any use for a gpa, do not take this professor. Though he is a genuinely nice person, the structure of the class is more of an obstacle than the actual content.
Reads straight out of the textbook with very few modifications to the exact words in the book making it very hard to follow and not clarifying anything at all.

He is very smart. But oh my goodness does he really know how to suck the life out of you during lectures. It is probably honestly better if you look up help for content online since Chad literraly just says what is the in the textbook, which is very confusing and not helpful.
He's a nice guy, but not the best teacher. His lectures are often pretty boring and his handwriting sometimes makes it hard to read. Your grade is comprised of 3 exams and 1 final.

Chad Gratton is a nice enough guy, but such a lazy teacher. Half of the homework answers are on mycourses, but he doesn't grade any of it. The lectures are mind-numbingly boring. The only 4 grades you'll get are for 3 exams and a final. He let my class have 1 paper for notes on the exams, which is why the difficulty is only 2 for me.

Chad loves the material but hard to understand.Grade is based off tests as all the hw is optional.If he sees the class is struggling he will add a huge curve to your tests.He will let you bring in a page of notes both sides for the test.He will also give you a study guide before each test.Copy down those questions because on the test it's the same.
tests are large part of the grade, he's a super great guy who loves the subject but not much can prepare you for tests being 85% of the grade.

Professor Gratton is a great guy and he loves the subject, but his lectures are some of the most dry, abstract lectures I have ever heard. He doesn't give any graded assignments, our grade is 85% exams. He flies through concepts back and forth, there is no time left to recover. Only work is optional HW which vaguely matches what we learn in class.

Chad Gratton is a stand-up guy, super friendly, and genuinely loves his subject. However, as a student it becomes nearly impossible to learn through his lectures. He uses incredibly complex words to explain sometimes simple topics, which in the end just makes it harder to parse what he actually means. He gives online HW that isn't on the tests.
Awful professor, would have had less trouble on discrete math but this guy proved otherwise. Dont take him unless you like your life hard.

I just couldn't understand the material, and he doesn't explain very well. If you can independently learn, then youll be fine. Otherwise you should not take this class. The final was all multiple choice. If you can, take the class from a community college.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: If you have no other choice but to take Gratton, don't be that worried. While his lectures are boring, they do cover the material that is on the tests (which are 90% of your grade), honestly you can scan over the notes for an hour and pass the tests. Not very interactive but had a very fair grading system to account for the difficulty of the course
Boring professor but class is not hard to get a decent grade in.
One of the best professors at RIT. Gave a lot of extra credit.

The best professor RIT has. Had him for Calc II. Exams are super easy as he gives the same problems from homeworks and worksheets. Very lenient with grading as well and gives tons of extra credit. Highly recommending him.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I hate math but Chad is the man. Is he a bit of a boring lecturer? Yes. But he posts everything online, including answers for worksheets we are still actively working on. He so clearly wants his students to succeed and even though his hw is a pain he will help you through every problem at office hours. Hard and boring class, but nice and great prof

tags: ['Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: He is a great person and very personable if you get to know him. His lectures are pretty boring but he does not take attendance. Given that, I would try to attend class because it moves quickly. He assigns webwork almost every week, worksheets at the end of class and 5 tests total - not including the final. He has long office hours after classes.

Chad's cool. He gives off really strong math teacher vibes. He's very formal about everything. Lectures are pretty boring, but always recorded and very thorough. Grade is based entirely on 4 open note tests and the final. He is always available and willing to give extra help and answer questions. Don't expect to get your tests back for 3 weeks.

Honestly, He is extremely nice and smart. However, He is not the best at making his lectures engaging. More than half the class failed his exams, so he gave generous grade replacements. Would not take him again for the sake of my mental health.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']
comment: Chad is a really smart guy, and you can tell he cares about discrete. With that being said, the lectures are boring and unintuitive, graded on a few homework assignments and mostly tests. I stopped paying attention in his lectures because it was a waste of my time. Good professor if you like learning from the book and asking questions in class.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Lectures are taken directly from the book. This makes some wording weird and a lot of problems don't follow the material closely enough to be useful on their own. tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Dr. Gratton is a great person, very kind, and accessible outside of class, however he is not the best at teaching. Lectures are long, constant, monotonous clumps of confusing terms and symbols that aren't always explained. Even with open note quizzes that you could work on over a 3 day period, many students struggled to get more than an 80% on them
Very considerate. Love this guy!

Really rushing through the material for some reason. Each lecture is rather fast paced due to him constantly skipping steps when solving things. Good about homework extensions. Very, very slow grader. Online exams are horrible due to not being able to backtrack. Feels like he ignores a lot of criticism, especially if brought up during class.

Chad's calculus 2 class is the hardest class I've taken in my life. His lectures are vague and fast paced, nearly useless. If you're so misfortunate to have Chad, get ready to binge YouTube videos trying to catch up on course material. Chad will also cover material that other professors don't touch, and will then complain that the class is behind.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: (MATH 185) Goes through a lot of material at a fast pace, but doesn't do a good job at explaining things. If you doze off for even a little bit, you will be lost. Not recording lessons doesn't help since the notes he writes are unhelpful chicken scratches that need explanations to understand. Does offer a lot of help outside of class though.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Hardest class I've taken in my entire life. What sucks is that it didn't have to be. Chad is obviously very intelligent, but that often makes me wonder why he chose to become a teacher and not go invent time travel or the COVID vaccine. While he's very understanding and caring, I never kept up with him and every problem seemed like a new topic.

Take chad if you want an easy credit. I didn't learn anything but all the exams are take home (at least during COVID times). Goes too fast in lecture to understand. Very kind professor and is willing to stop and explain anything if you ask. I enjoyed him.

Very passionate about the math itself, but instead of teaching he rather presents the concepts for you to learn on your own. Lectures are mainly notes taken very quickly, if you lose focus at all you'll be trailing behind re-writing notes. But, he's always looking for opportunities to help you, his office hours are very helpful.

This man really cares about his discrete, and doesn't quite understand why everyone else doesn't too. Despite his passion for the topic, Gratton is INCREDIBLY BORING. This dude could make you fall asleep talking about your favorite movie. He lectures super fast and monotone and note taking is near impossible. He does give practice exams, though!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Calculus is already a difficult class. Unfortunately, Chad does not make that any better. He quickly goes through topics with little explanation, often just doing problems on the board without explaining why he did the steps he did. The tests are also very difficult, with decently strict time limits.

Whether or not you should take Gratton depends on your motivation for taking a Calculus class. He basically gives away answers if you ask him so, if you are in the math class because you have to be there, Gratton is your guy. If you are a math major or math enthusiast, you may find him annoying for that reason, but hes still a great prof overall.

Dr. Gratton is a bit awkward at first, but he truly cares about the success of his students. The day before every test, he comes in late for a last minute study session, where as always he will make sure you understand the answer. He gives out detailed study guides for the tests, so even when the material was hard, I was never cheated or surprised.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Dr. Gratton is your typical math professor. Gives 15-20 homework assignments on top of MATLAB assignments which makes his class outside of lecture very time consuming, as a math class usually is. Prepares you for exams well, gives out exam guides which really helps your studying methods.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Dr. Gratton made sure that every topic throughout the course was explained to completion. His pace was quick and could seem unclear at first, but if you enjoy calculus, he is the professor to take for this course. The test topics were made clear before the exam, and he would not test on certain topics if he did not yet prove them. GREAT guy overall

Gratton's lectures focus on the theory and he is a very dry lecturer. He makes the class hard, but not unbearable. Proofs are likely candidates for exams, which makes them difficult and really forces you to understand the material. However, his exam study guides practically give every question away and you know what to prepare for.

He is a nice person and is pretty excited about maths. But he rushes through the class because of which he does a lot of silly mistakes on the class board. Sometimes these mistakes can confuse the students. Basically, he is a nice human being but not a great professor.

To put it bluntly, I was an absolutely horrific student to have in class and Prof. Gratton was always super patient with me even though I was a total nightmare. If you are a good student, you will love this class with him. It's hard but rewarding and he really makes you care about the subject matter.

Chad cares about how his students. He is always available outside of class. However, discrete math does not have as many resources online as the other maths. So in order to understand your homework, which is on the test, you have to understand his vague lectures. He breezes over difficult to understand subjects and has awful notes.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Caring']
comment: It saddens me that I have to give him a poor review because he is caring and very excited about math, but he does not do a good job of teaching it. He rushes and skims over overarching topics that would make the lectures much clearer I assume because he doesn't realize that they are not common knowledge. At least he is an easy grader though.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Chad the man! Great guy who definitely knows his stuff. Lectures can be a little hard to follow but if you take your notes, you'll be okay. Very much theory-based which makes tests very difficult. However, weekly quizzes are fairly okay (he goes over them before you take it). Offered a lot of attendance quizzes, so if you're there, you get a 100%.
Umm he is very nice person. Amazing personality, just not the right person for teaching 181.

Chaddy freaking Gratty is the best professor around. I had him for Discrete Math. He knows his stuff exceptionally well, and is very passionate about it. His lectures can be difficult to follow sometimes, but he is always willing to answer any questions and meet outside of class. He has unlimited patience, and is one of the most sincere guys ever.
Amazing. Chad the man is great. Take him and you will not regret it.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Professor Gratton knows his stuff; no one can deny that. However, if you struggle learning from fast-paced lectures and complex wording, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He is willing to answer any questions you have, but his lectures are way too fast along with complicated Homework is optional but grades are almost entirely test-based. I'd never take again
Lectures were boring. He gave little to no partial credit on tests and quizzes. The one good thing he did was swap your lowest test grade for the final if it was higher.

Professor Gratton, or just Chad, is the man as the others have already stated on here and in my class. He is inconsistent though, with 3 quizzes being skipped in favor of review, as well as changing the homework assignments during week 3 from mandatory to optional. He also offers lots of office hours, sometimes 4 hours at a time.

Mr. Chad Gratton is the man. This guy knows what he is talking about. A genius at heart, sometimes he even takes it upon himself to bake cookies for the smart students in class. . His Discrete math section is literally so discrete, that if you're failing, no one will ever find out. Realistically, he is really a good teacher, would highly recommend.

He presents material clearly and moves through at an excellent pace. Homeworks are not necessary and just for practice. He'll always take time out of class (or office hours) to answer questions. Very fair. He'll give credit where he can. Overall one of the best professors I've had.
Chad was an awesome discrete teacher! He is always available for help during office hours and graded very fair. Take him if you can!

Chad is a great professor. I've had him for Discrete I and II and have learned so much and have no been overwhelmed with homework. His balance of homework and quizzes is perfect and teaching style is great. Highly recommended.
Chad is the man. Take discrete with him, he knows EVERYTHING, and is very helpful when you have questions. The grading curve is also very generous. I highly recommend taking a class with him.
Take Chad for Discrete I and II. His teaching style is amazing and grading scale is very fair. He will get you through Discrete. Highly recommended

Chad definitely knows EXACTLY what he is doing, however none of the students do.  He is a grad student in math and I don't think anyone has taught him how to teach yet.  His material is VERY complex and he doesn't have a good way of explaining it.  He rarely uses numbers in examples and usually prefers obscure mathematical symbols and bad wording.

I would NEVER recommend taking a class with Mr. Gratton. I had a starting class size of over 35, about 15-20 students are still in the class. I felt as if I was in HS again b/c everyone just laughed and joked about the material because he was trying to teach material that would take DAYS to learn in MINUTES! His past discrete class average was a 50

Very nice, fair, and enthusiastic teacher!  His material is quite difficult which is unfortunately unnecessary for most students that are taking the class who will honestly probably never use the skills and just forget them as soon as the class is over.  It's a lot of work to do well, but he has a good curve and you can do well if you work at it.

Chad is a great teacher, Midway i was going to drop the class, he was able to teach what i should have learned in the previous Discrete Math class and this class, in time for the final. He made review sessions when everyone had time to attend and was available to talk before class (When he wasn't getting his monthly haircut)

Chad is great, he is a UofR grad student working on his PHD in math. He knows his stuff. He really helped out a lot. There is a very very generous curve and he is always willing to help. We had review sessions on the weekend. He is great and I learned a lot about a tough subject.
Great Teacher! Tests have right about of difficulty, shes always willing to help in a bind. Extremely knowledgeable, well spoken, and approachable.

This was my third class I have taken with Mishra and I can still only say positive things about her. She is an excellent lecturer and is extremely helpful during lab periods. Course work is moderately difficult but she will help you out a lot of if you are struggling. She definitely knows what she is talking about, unlike some other professors.

She is a great professor, and I learned quite a bit, but be warned. If you don't provide course feedback she won't round your grade, which feels unfair. The other issue is with the labs. They are so poorly written that it's funny. Sometimes the instructions would just say "do it" and you would just have to figure it out.

Mishra is highly intelligent and a great professor. She can really break down tough concepts and make them easy to understand. She gives you lots of advice on how to do well on the graded assignments and makes every effort to help you. Highly recommended!

Easy to understand, willing to take the time to meet with you if you have questions or need help. Answers emails quickly, ensures that you know what is going on in class. I would take her again for any other class.

This is my second time having Mishra as a professor and I have to say she is one of the best in the department. Very clear during the lecture, answers emails almost immediately, and makes all material available online. She knows her stuff and is a really nice person. Definitely recommend.
She knows her stuff, answered all the questions i had. Made slides available. Just a really great class
I enjoyed having Professor Mishra for Routing and Switching.  She's a brilliant professor, and ensures that each student will succeed.  Hope that I'll have her again.
Very helpful professor, probably the best I have had in the networking department. Answers emails immediately, and she knows her stuff. I highly recommend her.
Bill was a super cool guy and i took him for 2 semesters.  Relatively easy grader and helpful in critiques if you ask.  Ask for feedback if you want it or he wont say much.

Bill is a nice guy, but my class struggled a lot with time limitations. His quizes are a little hard, but he does offer a retest. He is a perfectionist and most points are lost during ideations. He literally wants to see every step of the process.

Great teacher. Taught me everything I needed to know about how to see a form in 3D space. He's really nice and really funny. A stickler for rules and deadlines, but not too harsh. He gives a pretty heavy workload. Overall, best professor I currently have.

I had Wolff for 3d design (I, II and III). He was a nice teacher and likes students who show interest and work hard. He grades fair: gives you the grade you deserve. Friendly and willing to help and give you advice/ suggestions for improving your work.
Nice guy, low key. So far I have enjoyed this class.
Nice guy, low key but knows his stuff. I enjoyed the projects.
Low key, nice guy. Knows his stuff.

Quiet guy. Doesn't keep class under control. Show interest, be polite to him, and he'll like you. Very willing to help his students that show interests, and knows his material WELL. Getting used to teaching intro to 3D, so gonna be rough. Overall, enjoyable guy.
horrible experience to have him as a teacher after having an exceptional teacher for the first 2 quarters.

Dr. Cockburn was a terrible teacher. He was disorganized and a poor lecturer. He wrote random stuffs and uttered random things in class. I understood nothing from his lectures. Students like me were getting nothing out of the disorganized, unstructured and poor teaching style and materials.
The worst professor I've had so far. Unorganized, lectures and course materials are full of mistakes. Incredible how they have such a garbage professor teaching such an important class.
If you can take the course with someone else DO IT!

comment: Well...I'll keep it simple. Even with chegg study HW can take hours, exams are supposed to be "easier than hw" and "similar to class examples" but only about 50% of the exam will hold true to that. Has office hours but doesn't take time to thoroughly explain grading criteria or questions you might have. Use the Text, it will help big time.

He's a great professor, very funny and clear about what he expects. I would recommend him for controls, because I learned a lot from him. I believe he is also teaching modern controls. Knows the industry well and has connections to FAANG companies. Gives recommendations

Professor Cockburn is a special man. Don't have any questions because if you ask them, he will simply repeat one word and repeatedly point to the same thing four times. I learned a decent bit in his class, but I feel that was sort of parallel to his teachings and not because of him. I needed to rely heavily on the book, and I do not recommend him.
Hilarious jokes. You will be an expert in controls and MATLAB after this class. Hookups with big companies. Man is a legend. Always go to office hours. A P P L E $$$$$$ wassuppp ayeeee

Be prepared to work hard and it will pay off. This my long term investment. It is true what the other students said, besides the lies some groups will tell. If you want a good electrical engineering career then I would consider taking his class. please learn how to use fortran his class.

Everything is accessible online. No need to come to class. Great professor and has helped me answer questions through email. I only showed up for midterms and final and received an A for doing all the homework and tests. Would recommend if you are a self learner and interested in controls.

spanish is basically a prereq for this class. please only take if you understand spanish. I am studying for modern control basically and im looking at my notes and some of the words are in spanish. cinco de mayo for extra credit. remember to put it on your exam. hint. class easy for me because i took spanish in high school. modern control easy

Took Prof. Cockburn for Modern Control Theory. Terrible at effectively teaching. He will provide basic theory during lectures with barely any examples and expect the student to do incredibly complex problems on homework/quizzes. Good luck finding him for office hours because he intentionally makes himself unavailable. Avoid for elective courses.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Really nice guy (great in office hours) but not a very good lecturer.  Will need to ask for help to do well on the HWs, which are penalized 50% if late, if he doesn't give solutions that day.  Need to write down his examples, online slides say "continued on board".  Tests are generally tough, but each can be replaced by the grade of the next.

Lectures are pretty much useless. He's disorganized and often rambles about unrelated topics. Late penalties are 50% per day for homework. His requirements for projects are unclear and he strictly grades them

Class is not too bad. The homeworks and algorithms are tough, but manageable if you put lots of time in it. The professor, however, is very unclear and nearly never says anything helpful in class. I have heard that he is helpful sometimes in office hours. Assignments are unclear also. Good luck.
He is improved significantly! He will also treat you like you want to do something with your life so be prepared to work... as how you should be working.
HE is a good professor if you are willing to work. Doesn't hold your hand and treats you like an actual college student.

Really upped his game since Applied Programming. Definitely was listening to student feedback. He explains concepts more clearly and makes sure everyone knows what's going on. Office hours are amazingly useful as well. Good stuff DJuan

Made significant improvements from previous years' feedback. Was willing to listen and adjust schedule and assignments based on student request. Although he gets a lot of complaints, he genuinely wants to do better, so talk to him about your concerns and he will make adjustments.

Cockburn is a poor programmer and speaks in too much math language for CE students. The homework is not hard if you just follow something online- in fact it doesn't require listening during lecutes, but exams are very specific (and bad) questions that could be googled and don't reflect your knowledge at all. Third year CE's should already know c.

Will not prepare you for his ridiculous exams. Class under Cockburn is about memorizing equations and derivations. 0 practical knowledge gained for a practical class. Homeworks are doable but take an disproportional amount of time. Tests are very difficult, little to no review is given. Make sure to get the textbook because his notes are useless.

Awful awful professor. The subject was difficult to begin with, and he occasionally gave outright incorrect information on his (largely useless) slides. Expects you to memorize many equations, specific statistics, and definitions for exams that aren't actually necessary to any future classes. No cheat sheets.
Terrible. Hates knowledge.

He is the worst professor I have ever had in my entire life. His lectures have no structure, you have to teach yourself out of the book, and the exam questions are never based on the homework. You will have to guess what to teach yourself from the book and hope that it is what he puts on his exams. He outright refuses to help during office hours.
A very frustrating experience.

comment: Fully synchronous online class—participation is mandatory, so you can't multitask and catch up later with recordings. large portion of the grade comes from writing assignments rather than coding to enhance your actual skill. Heavy workload so plan to be busy, you don't have time to cook (waste money)!

- No programming assignments given relating to distributed systems, so you will not learn anything useful for the workforce.
- Grades on a research report and a group project, both of which he grades based on personal opinion, which he never fully reads, and poor feedback.
- Lectures are on topics from 30 years ago, irrelevant today.

I should've listened to the other rating on here. I took CSCI 620 as well with him and it was a very similar experience but not as bad. Very tough grader and his remarks are always confusing. His guidelines are very strict and it seems like he doesn't actually read the reports or run the code. The projects and lectures are very disjointed. Not fair

No exam (if you think it's good, trust me it's not). Instead, needed to do one project, and a research report. 

The group project required a project report and a poster presentation. The research report is an individual task divided into 4 phases. Be ready to read a lot of papers. Lectures are not that good.

Can I describe this professor in one word? Rude
are you going to learn something from him? close to 0
don't take him
Very rude and condescending. I would never suggest anyone take a course under him.
Would be better if he gave better feedback instead of sounding condescending towards the students and making them think they're stupid.

Intentionally makes his quizzes very tricky, in terms of wording so you have to think of wording of the answer from HIS perspective and waste your time in the process, instead of learning something of value. Will also make you track progress of every group member in a project assignment so be ready for that inconvenience.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Professor is really good. Always accessible outside class and office hours. If you have any doubts in the assignments or HW given, you can ask him and he would always help you with it.

He says industry wants teamwork-savvy people so he requires you to track in a graph the contribution of every member of your group mates every day over the course of the project. His lectures don't help with the work he assignes. He gave us satellite spectrometer data and refused to elaborate on how to use it and told us to ask our groups.
A little bit rude at times. His lectures are rather dry and lack substance. You could probably get away with skipping lectures if you just read the slides yourself.

Constantly talks himself up about previous work experience, barely covers anything in lectures, and doesn't seem concerned with practicality. Entire semester is one group project, and he is a very harsh grader. Stay away from this professor if you don't want to hate every second of the course.

One word - Chatty. Hell just read the slides and tell stories about his background. The best (or worst) part is, the stories do not even add up and you can totally catch him lying. Office hours are waste of time. TIP: Just write a long paragraph for anything, hell be happy.
very attentive for a professor of an online course

He doesn't teach the material in any detail, so it's only useful if you come in without a background in security whatsoever. The class basically amounts to an entirely self guided group project where you have to make a secure system or some malware without any guidance. He cares more about the paper about the project rather than the technical stuff

You'll write 3 research papers that are vaguely related to Secure Coding. This guy will avoid going into any technical detail, so you will learn nothing practical from this class. He'll mention a lot of topics and spend a ridiculous amount of time bragging about the people he knows and laughing at you for not knowing things that are irrelevant now.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: Extremely pathetic professor! Just puts up slides and papers and enjoys at home. No help whatsoever. Emphasis on style of writing rather than the content in a report. Save yourself the trouble and do not take any course under him since CS department won't do anything to help you overcome this pathetic course or professor!

He's the worst professor I have ever had. I learned nothing of substance, he nitpicks on quite literally every single possible thing you can nitpick on, and his grading scheme is there to the detriment of students. I read these reviews while picking classes last semester but didn't think it was going to be _this_ bad.

Not a great professor for so many reasons. He teaches pretty clearly and seems like a nice guy, until it comes to academics... His grading is tough, and almost no one feels prepared for his tests. Worst thing by far: he calculates your grade 3 different ways, and TAKES THE LOWEST. Why? Does he want people to fail?
Professor taught us well. Hr was very fluent and nice.

Gentle Advice. Just Don't take any online course under him. He just uploads the slides and expect from you to learn by yourself. Never clear your doubts. You will not learn anything  from his course. Worst Professor.
Not a good professor for the course.

This guy is useless and arrogant. He converted a regular class into a blended one and kept assigning research papers for students to read, while he himself sits at home. He is never in his office. Most hilarious is that if you ask him something he doesn't know, he will tell you a long story about the work he did at Morgan Stanley 20 yrs ago.

Took for PLC, do not recommend. Lectures are meaningless, tests are brutally specific. Projects are simple but very poorly explained both because instructions are unclear and because he doesn't teach the material required. Prepare to spend a lot of time in his office or exchanging emails, which he can take a day to respond back to.
Do not take him if you want to learn something. I got nothing out of his lectures. Was a waste of my money and time

Goes off on long tangents/unrelated anecdotes. Clearly knows the material, but seems to sometimes have a hard time actually explaining the concepts. Tests are brutal. Absolutely brutal. Projects/labs are a good grade buffer, though. Overall would recommend him if you want to learn, but not if you want an A.

Seriously, don't take him if you really want to learn something in database. His grading is mostly related to how many times you meet him in his office outside the class. Doesn't discuss any coding at all, doesn't even look at your codes for the project. Teaches from PPT slides only. You'll learn more from books and Google than anything from him.

Unhelpful analogies, tangents, skimming over slides, no coding exercises before tests or project, heavy on the theory, low on the syntax but tests are all SQL/XML/relational algebra syntax, surprise graded activities, mandatory graded surveys, tested on project material, you are expected to write project in 3 weeks. Grade is Tests: 50% Project: 40%
Got to learn a lot, he guides you through the course and we get to do major part.
Very helpful and understanding, medium skill set but ready to experiment with new trends in CS.
Folks, If you value your money never take him. I was surprised at his lack of knowledge and in defense he said "This is a grad course, you dont expect me to know everything", duh?

Professor Raj is an all around good professor.  He is clear and you will understand the material.  His tests are not easy but they are not overly difficult if you pay attention.  I would recommend him for DBC.

He's pretty easy, and if you already know what you're doing, I highly recommend him.  He's got the clearest accent of any of the Indian professors except maybe Teredesai.  If you're shaky on material though, avoid.  You won't learn enough from him.
Simply horrible. If you DON'T WANT TO LEARN A WORD, TAKE HIM.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. She has the mentality that as engineering students we have to "figure everything out" ourselves. She uses this mentality as an excuse for her own laziness when it comes to teaching and clarity about the awful hw/exam problems that she comes up with.

Dr. Carle is a very passionate person and it really shows in her MCET110 lectures. She explains the material and concepts very thoroughly and clearly. The class is a difficult course though, and you need to work for your grade.
Ask for help, and you will receive. Tutors will help a lot with any Matlab problems you have

Really depends by person, if you're on her good side she's awesome. If you get on her bad side she might be a bit tougher on you. Could explain material better as there's no prerequisites for the class (Expects students to understand calculus right off the bat) but overall very helpful.

Took her for Foundations of Metals. One of the tougher professors of the MCET department. The lectures hit hard and fast, so you need to pay attention and take good notes. Definitely not an easy A, but an A nonetheless. Having a good group really helps for projects and workshops.
If you don't respect her she will know and you'll have a hard time. If you need help she is great during office hours.

Professor Carle is not one to give fair grades. Simply get on her bad side and she will lower your grades with strict interpretation of wording on her assignments. Carle herself missed more of her own lectures then I care to count with vague excuses that leaves you wondering why did you pay for this class. Strongly recommend you stay clear of her.
You are better off teaching yourself because if you try to learn from her in class you will fail. Don't make the same mistake I did AVOID HER!!!!!!

This is one of the most frustrating classes I have taken. In the beginning of the term, it was made clear that minimal help will be given to us, in order to prepare us for the real world. However, I do not believe that giving students assignments with no prior knowledge of the software and no lesson on the softwarrequired for the assignment is fair

She is so confusing, very hard to understand, assignments thrown around and not even mentioned due date. She needs to get her act together. She makes me want to change majors so I do not have to deal wit her again.

took her for intro to materials tech. her lectures were not very clear, but I asked her questions during office hours, and somehow she made the material clear. IDK why she doesn't lecture the way she answered my questions during office hours. Her assignments are challenging, Grades papers strictly, tests are somewhat hard. Not an easy A.

You will not learn anything in this class with her being your prof. The homework, and the tests will not reflect anything you learn in class. If you can avoid taking her  class, I strongly recommend it.

You will learn nothing from her, and that is not an under statement. Currently have A's in every class (including hers), but that's because I google all questions on HW. You find yourself asking other students how to do the HW, and they respond "I have no clue, we never learned this." If you use google you can pass, but won't learn a thing.

BAD. You will learn nothing from her, and that is not an under statement. Currently have A's in every class (including hers), but that's because I google all questions on HW. You find yourself asking other students how to do the HW, and they respond "I have no clue, we never learned this." If you use google you can pass, but won't learn a thing.

Works "with Leonard", meaning Leonard does all the work and is the only one who knows anything about what she's presenting in class. Assigns HW that takes way longer than is acceptable; HW average is around 60, and the test grades reflect it as well. Spends least amount of time going over the material most heavily questioned on exams. AVOID.

She is the worst professor in the entire RIT! She is simply pathetic at teaching and she clearly doesn't realize her methods of teaching is so horrendous that it drives every student crazy. I can't believe they haven't fired her yet because clearly everyone fails in the class. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND AVOID HER AT ALL COST!!

She is a very smart person, but terrible at teaching. She gives way too much work that doesn't make any sense. She doesn't ever explain anything about the materials and her test are VERY DIFFICULT, so don't even bother studying. The class average is usually a 60, but she does do a curve in the end. I recommend not HAVING HER AS A PROFESSOR!!!!
knows the material but doesn't know exactly how to say it to the 1st year students who have no idea

she knows what she is teaching but presents it in a way that is above what the average first year student would know.  her tests are hard, before the midterm i asked her what i should study and she didnt help much at all.  the onley way to learn the material is to teach yourself or go to office hours.

She is an absolutely terrible teacher.  She was so dry in her lesson and her jokes.  The work is hard and there is not much guidance.  She is also anti-social.  She didn't even say what her name was on the first day of class until I asked her.
Horrible teacher.  She goes really fast when teaching the computer part so you cant follow and does not slow down or answer questions.  She also gives insane amount of work at the end of the quarter
This teacher if very nice and understanding although she is a hard grader you will learn the material.  I recomend her to castro.
Great teacher, knows the material really well. makes you actually work for your grade unlike castro. highly recommend this teacher.

Had her for Solid Modeling.  Took it online over the summer.  It was outside of my major, but I wanted to learn another CAD program.  While it was mainly self taught, it wasn't bad, and she answered questions well through email.

This was her first Quarter teaching Dynamics and i must say that she did an exelent job. I have had her for other classes and i disliked her but this class she was very personable and did a great job teaching dynamics. I WOULD RECOMEND HER OVER LUI!!!

Terrible teacher for both solid modeling AND Intro to materials tech. Teaches poorly, and grades extremely harshly. Tests are nightmares, and you won't get a damn thing out of the class except a lot of stress. Castro is worse, but grades much easier
Horrible, horrible teacher, go for castro, he may not be a great teacher but even he is better than carle, so annoying and harsh, she loves shutting down students

Worse Class and Teacher I have ever had. Doesn't know how to teach. She just uses other peoples powerpoint and prezis along with videos to teach. Learned little to nothing the entire semester. She requires you to buy theatre tickets for shows off campus and quizzes you on the show. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!!

Had her for Introduction to Theatre and enjoyed the class but took little away from it. She's an enjoyable person to casually converse with- but she can really talk... Most classes become rambling lectures... There's a lot of little assignments as well- easy, yet time consuming. Overall, she's an easy professor that takes up a lot of your time.

She's a really nice lady and fun to talk to but I can't even. She gives you a 10-15 page paper (she expects 20) for the final and pretty much all of the "mini-homeworks" are projects. If you take her, prepare to work and put up with extremely vague prompts.

For off, Prof. Peace has a ton of experience with theatre, so if you have questions chances are you will get an answer.  As for grading, she doesn't has an exact rubric for projects.  This does allow room for creativity, just remember to include what she says to include.  It really isn't a bad class, just do the work and take notes.

If you don't live, breath, and sleep theatRE, you're SOL with this class. I had to take it as a perspectives class and by week 3 I wanted to rip my hair out. She gives oodles of assignments, rarely updates her grade book, and expects you to magically understand the assignment with a minute amount of explanation. URGH!

Where to begin? How about the fact that this woman is out of her mind. The other Intro to Theatre class had almost no work to do throughout the semester while she made us do an intensive assignment every week. We had to write a 5 page  minimum play review on a dress rehearsal. I had to withdraw to save my grade. Avoid at all costs.
She is an awful teacher. She will prattle on for an entire hour and you won't have learned a single thing. She is crazy, and her homework amount is ridiculous for a non-core class.
Worst professor ever. No need to explain.
DO NOT take this class with her. Worst teacher ever. Tons of homework; has no idea how to teach. She is easy to talk though.

Do not take intro to theatre with her. Professor is a time waster just to fill class time, assigns more homework than my core classes, does not get grades back in a timely manner. My most stressful class and has made caused me many mental breakdowns because of harsh grades.
Tons of homework

Do NOT take Intro to Theatre with her if you are expecting a blow off. She is one of those professors that thinks their class is the center of our education. Even though it is a college level course, the amount of work assigned is a little over the top. She grades very late, but doesn't hesitate to assign more work. Do not buy any books.
Gives a lot of homework. Doesn't know how to teach. Finds ways to waste time class throughout. Grades the paper extremely late. Got most of my papers 1-2 months after I submitted them.

I love Amy so much! I had her my freshman year for Drawing 1, and decided to take Intro to Painting with her, and she's just as amazing! I've never painted before, and Amy really makes me feel comfortable and able to paint to the best of my ability! She is also always willing to help me out whenever I need it!

I loved Amy's way of teaching; it was very fun, and she's super nice. Her help and descriptions on how to do or fix something can sometimes be a little stressful, as she does it in a very hyperactive way. But she will definitely help you if you're struggling, as she fixed one of my eyes for me in my portrait. She also isn't harsh with grades.

Very funny, but if you're not a super great painter, she doesn't talk to you for more than a few minutes. Doesn't post guidelines for projects, gives confusing advice for what to fix. Generally frustrating class, also creatively restrictive. Doesn't like anything that isn't slightly stylized realism.

Amy is by far one of my favorite professors. I took her 8 am class (which she starts at 8:30) and I loved it. She is a great professor for any class, as she is such a funny and creative person. She could (verbally) tear your art to pieces, but she is so good at critique that you finish with a smile on your face and a good idea of what to fix.

I absolutely adore Amy, she is such a positive energy and wonderful instructor, I've taken her 8 am classes (which she starts at 8:30) twice and have enjoyed every minute of it. Her critique style is so well done, no matter how problematic your piece is you come out of it not only knowing what needs to change but also feeling confident.

Prof. McLaren is an honest grader, and she'll point out flaws in a piece with a very no-nonsense attitude. She looks for students who go above and beyond: staying late, asking questions, coming to the studio outside of class. Her teaching style is a lot to get used to, but all of her insights are worth it. Not a lot of projects, but a lot of work!
She has lot of energy at 8am somehow. She's very flexible, the class needed extra time on one of our assignments and she gave an extra two weeks. I also learned more in this class.

Amy was wonderful!  I had her for an 8AM class, and her energy made it worth waking up early for it.  She genuinely cares about her students, and is very understanding that some of the people who take the drawing foundation course may be photo majors that have less drawing skill.

Amy is amazing! I had no drawing experience before drawing 1, and she has been so helpful and good to me! I had Amy at 8am and she let us come in at 8:30. She also had an extra night drawing class just for anyone to finish up their final! As long as you do all of your drawings, Amy's class is an easy A!

As a first-year I was nervous about what to expect from drawing but Amy was amazing! She is extremely warm and welcoming and always wants to help her students improve. There aren't crazy amounts of homework if you use your time well in class, and you can always contact her outside of class even if you need help on anything.

Amy is amazing and I'm not exaggerating when I say she kept me going throughout my first semester. Class was always fun and my drawing skills improved significantly in her class. She started at 8:30 instead of 8, and we regularly got coffee breaks. I built my whole semester 2 schedule around getting her again.

Amy is hilarious and a great prof. Made class start at 8:30 instead of 8am. She is full of energy and makes class enjoyable. Kinda tough grader but gives you multiple grades throughout the project to improve. Super encouraging and gives helpful feedback. Don't buy everything on the supply list at once, I did and ended up not using 90% of it

I knew it was going to be a good year as soon as I walked into this class at 8am on a Monday. Amy has a lot of energy. She allows coffee breaks. She gives more than one grade per project. She doesnt give much homework, although she does give you her phone number in case you want to text her for feedback on anything. Be ready for constant feedback!

As a freshman who didn't have a lot of drawing experience, I was scared. The first day of class with Amy, I knew it was gonna be just fine. She is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had and is really passionate about what she does. She brings the class together and everybody's drawing significantly demonstrated improvement.

She is a hilarious professor and loves to get the class participating in a fun way during class. She is easy to talk to and is very helpful and providing suggestion to better your work. She even encourages you to text her at any time and she is willing to give feedback on your work when outside of the classroom.

By far, Amy is one of the greatest professors and teachers I've ever had.  Her advice, teaching, and honesty is unparalleled, and only surpassed by her personality.  She will push you out of your comfort zone and is not afraid to tell the truth plus, shes pretty funny.  I only wish she taught my illustration classes :(

Amy is the best drawing professor at RIT. She is energetic and passionate about drawing and helps each student fulfill their potential. She grades you on your ability  and not in comparison to others. If you show up and turn in work you will not fail her class. She gives out her number so you can her outside of class.  If you can, take her class!

Amy is probably one of my favorite drawing professors! As long as you manage your time in class theres a ton of freedom to leave the class to grab a coffee or anything. Would love to take a class with her again since she's so fun and funny! She's there to help you and show you how to draw better. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER.
She's my most favorite teacher in my whole life. If I have a chance, I would take any classes with her no matter what! I had a class with her at 8 in the morning, she has a plenty of energy!

Amy was nice, although I didn't really care for most of her projects.  I did well in her class even though I'm into computer arts and not drawing.  If you had a question on your work outside of class you could takture and send it to you and she would help.  Overall a pretty easy class.

An amazing teacher, probably the best I have ever had. Classes are casual and she always listens to student feedback. Be prepared to learn about "happy accidents" and bricks that "make you want to cry". The big project of each quarter is usually finished by week 9 to help ease the burden of finals week. Would absolutely take her class again.
great teacher. super enthusiastic and knows what she is talking about. she expects a lot from you though. take her class if you want to GET BETTER at drawing, not just to get an easy A.

I thank her for my improvement in drawing... and art in general. Great teacher. She is a TRUE artist! She pushes her students to get better.. and they sure do! Fun and friendly lady!! Even though I was frustrated throughout her class (lack of drawing skills), she made me want to come to class and do better.

Great teacher! Really knows what she's doing but sometimes it's hard to understand the point she's trying to get across. Helped me get into drawing and improve amazingly. If you want an easy class don't take her: She's hard as hell, but she'll make you an amazing drawer.
Amy was my favorite teacher this year. She pushes you to your limits. Not clear on things- speaks in sounds rather than words. Take her, she's fun :)

Amy is a wonderful professor, willing to help you whenever you need it, and she genuinely cares about your growth as a student and individual, unlike most of the foundations teachers here. She's really hard to understand sometimes, but is very challenging and pushes you out of your shell to be better. She's adorable and full of energy. Take her.
She is sometimes hard to understand, and she can ask a lot of you, but if you push through and do the work, she definitely rewards you.

Great teacher, I absolutely hated drawing, design etc. before this course, but she really tried hard to make it fun and relevant. She gives a lot of freedom with assignments, so that was great for a foundation class, because I could still work in whatever medium I wanted. She was absolutely nuts, but I would take her again if I could.

She took over for Cliff Wun when he went on sabbatical, and I have to tell you- she was tougher than him in a lot of respects. Getting an A from Amy is nearly impossible, but you will learn a LOT. She is wacky, crazy, and a ton of fun. You'll love her.

Amazing teacher! I wouldnt replace her with anyone! She's tough but I've learned an incredible amount.  She likes to customize projects to what students want to do, and tries to keep people motivated.  She always has things to challenge people on, but gives enough compliments to boost confidence as well. Take her if you want to learn something.

Incredible teacher, I have learned a ton from her this in my drawing foundation classes. My class with her has improved much more than most other foundation classes.  She works you long and hard, but she'll take into account what students want to do and will try to make things fun.  Take classes with her if you want to learn something.
Soft spoken and very straightforward. He will assign homework and then proceed to do the problems in class. Everything is open notes, so as long as you take good note you should not have a problem.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: It was his first time teaching the class, but he did pretty good! He kept handing out extra credit so that everyone could get to at least a B and therefore no one would need to take the final. He's also beyond chill about the course structure, so if you don't like something, just tell him.

Class was really easy if you took electronics in high school. His voice is raspy and kinda hard to understand sometimes. His motions are really awkward and its really funny. But he is a nice and understanding guy if you forgot to do the homework or left it back at the dorms. Don't slack off when he teaches binary it is essential throughout the clas

The class I took with him was pretty much show up to class and work on that weeks project. Every now and then he would give a 20-40 minute lecture, which was always thorough and explained the concepts. There however was little guidance with setting up the technology unless you specifically asked for help. I really enjoyed the class.

Great debates was a really great class overall. Relatively easy assignments that are mostly graded for completion with one major assignment for the whole semester. Lectures were relatively interesting and she's clearly very passionate about a lot of the subject matter.

Dr. Edwards really made this class worth it. She teaches this class with a real passion, and as a result her lectures are quite engrossing. There's almost no homework, only three one-page papers and a three-page final. She's quite approachable if you enjoy talking about baseball, and she's obviously really informed about the sport and its history.

Edwards is very knowledgeable about baseball and history, so her lectures are good if you're interested in the course material. She also frequently opens the floor to discussion. The only grades in the class were participation and "letters" in which we summarized what we learned throughout the course, which were very open-ended.

I have taken classes by Professor Edwards before and I would take even more if I could. She is hilarious and extremely passionate about what she teaches, and it shows in her lectures and after-class conversations. Highly recommend her for any class she's teaching.

You can tell she really cares about what she lectures about. Attendance was a sign in sheet and your grade consists of participation (which was just attendance and submitting 3 or 4 discussion posts in the entire semester) as well as 3 essays that she grades leniently. Take her for a gen ed.

I absolutely adored every lecture by Professor Edwards, as she was passionate, engaged, and hilarious. Class discussions were important to this class, but there was no participation grade. She even cancelled a paper because she could tell we were all burnt out. I highly recommend her to anyone passionate about history and ready to laugh.

I absolutely adore this woman and recommend her History of Baseball class to anyone who wants to fill a perspective or have a chill time with an interesting class. I do not care about baseball at all but this woman's lectures had me emotionally invested. She is super engaging, banters with the class, does YOPS interviews, and has easy assignments.

History of baseball was super easy and I was typically engaged even though I'm not a baseball fan. You don't really have to do the readings and I think there were like 6 short papers you had to write for 100% of your grade. Easy A if you pay attention

I loved Dr. Edwards' History of Baseball class. She's very funny and makes the class super entertaining. While she doesn't take attendance, it can sometimes be a struggle to figure out what's going on if you've missed a class or two, but she's very good at keeping MyCourses updated and all around a great personality.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: She really likes sports and the class was on the history of baseball, so she was knowledgeable about the material. It was very easy, mostly asynchronous and easy to forget about, but it didn't really matter. Literally BS your way through every essay and you'll be fine.
History of Baseball was super easy. Outside readings, a couple 3 page papers, and a final report. Lectures were very interesting, you can tell she loves teaching this course.

Dr. Edwards is an absolutely phenomenal professor. Although the class is mostly lecture, it very much is an open forum for discussion. There is not much homework and the homework that is assigned is fairly short readings that are talked about in class the next day. She also tells hilarious but relevant stories in class, which are simply fantastic.

You have to show up to classes, she passes around a sign in sheet. This class has no tests or quizzes, there are only 3 short essays throughout the semester. Other than that there were a few short readings for homework but you could get by without reading them if you ever took a history class before.
Dumb class, all we did was look at her family tree and write papers about it. She tried to make it interesting, but eh.

History of baseball, great class. I had no interest in baseball. Passed the class with ease. Never spoke, the entire class is basically lecture but it doesn't put you to sleep.  She is very passionate about this class and loves to teach about baseball.

She is very opinionated, and if you don't agree with her, you're wrong.  She gave me an opinion C- on a paper because she didn't agree with me on my opinion.  Also, there are next to no guidelines for any of the papers.  On the plus side you can show up late for class because she is always around 10 minutes late herself.

She doesn't believe in giving exams because not all people are test takers.  She wanted very much for people to be involved in class.  You don't have to buy a book which is nice, but you do have to do all of the reading online (which really hurts my eyes). But get ready to read for every class

All she do is talk too much during the class and no tests, quizzes and exams except only 2 papers and projects. It wouldn't be helpful for you to get A for this course since i thought it is easy to pass but NOT. She is very harsh on the grading system and flexible on attendance, and optional assignment. It is hurting on your grade to fail this.

She talks way too much, goes off on tangents.  She grades really harshly because she thinks that all students should have the same writing abilities that she does.  She did give out two extra credit assignments though.  Wouldn't take her again.
Was so excited to take this class. She just talked the whole time and went on tangents. Wasn't helpful at all and winded up hating the class. Don't suggest a class with her.

She is very passionate about baseball, so it makes the class more fun. The textbook is useless, so I'm glad it's cheap. The only problem I had is that she talks the entire time, and if you miss a point or a name, you're screwed on the notes. Hopefully she gets a study guide. We always got out early, which was awesome!
Awesome Teacher, have her for Hist of Baseball, really energetic and really into the material, class requires little work, but goes over a ton of information, great teacher for a great class.

She knows what she's talking about but goes off on tangents and can get quite boring with the lectures - she just speaks with no visualizations - as much as I am a die-hard baseball fan. Women teaching baseball - don't know how I feel about that.

I loved her as a teacher, I took two of her classes, American History in Disabilities and Deaf history in the US. She was very interesting when she spoke and knowledgeable and always available for help.
She graded us based on our writing ability, not on our understanding of the material. This is History, not writing.

She's pretty biased in her essays. She only offered two essays, all were worth 30%, the remaining 10% was participation. First two essays, my opinion conflicted with hers and I got a C. The last essay, I changed my opinion to conform with hers and I got a B. It kind of says something.

Had her for American History:History of Baseball.  She knows her stuff well, obvious red sox fan(though i didn't mind as i hate the yankees anyways).  Grades pretty easy, oppertunites for extra credit, class doesn't usually last the full time, decent professor
I'm taking her again next year!
classes are discussion-oriented, very involved with interesting readings and field trips. interesting and intellectually challenging but it's not difficult to stay on top of material.
Very knowledgable in history. Her classes tend to be long, and most times boring, but she has a wealth of information to share. Grading is pretty easy.
She is awesome.  I loved going to class.
Hated this class.  She is totally type A.

Professor Clark is a great guy. Funny personality (very dry sense of humor), not a lot of work, lenient grading and will talk about things that matter, not just the curriculum. I'd take him again if I didn't have a scheduling conflict. He's a great option for comm.

For a communication teacher he was very bad at communicating to the class which made the work confusing and infuriating at times. He was also rather rude to the class and students making condescending jokes and put down. He also had little respect for boundaries and would look through my notebook or ask too personal of questions.

Fantastic lectures, extremely nice and helpful.  Would recommend.
