The website with the homework is buggy which makes the homework more frustrating.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Most would think David would make things simple for those trying to get their artistic perspective done, but this couldn't be any further from the truth. Every class is a dry lecture and no virtual notes are allowed. The volume of online homework is absurd and the website you pay for is not user-friendly. Reading the textbook is required for tests!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Knows his stuff. Moves very fast. Will introduce a new concept with 2 minutes left in class and assign homework on it. because of this it can be challenging if youre coming from no musical background. All that said, he's a great guy, is always available for extra help, and cares about the students in the class

Took him for applied Piano. I learned A LOT in his class. He is very inspirational and really knows his stuff. For a one-credit course, the homework (which is either learn a piece or do review exercises on the book) took a lot of time outside of class. There is a term-long project that is learning a big piece. It takes time, but it's very rewarding

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'SO MANY PAPERS', 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: This class is so time consuming! The tests are frequent but open note. You have to spend at least 6 hours preparing for the test. Why you might ask? Because we have to memorize music and get every detail out of the book. If you want an easy elective, do not take this class.

Before taking Intro to Music, I knew some things about different types of music.  During this class, that knowledge was greatly expanded to a point where I truly appreciate the music I've always wanted to learn about through lectures and attending concerts.  I can honestly say that I'm not done learning about the music taught or w concerts!!!

Mr. McCarthy is a really friendly dude, he likes talking about music. Just try not to fall asleep in class when he plays music. No textbook. It's important to take notes if you want an A in the class. You have to write a long paper at the end of the semester, just find something worth writing about and you can breeze through it. Would take again.

To pass this course all you had to do was go to classes and take notes. Teacher is very engaging, friendly, outgoing, and funny. It was nice having his class first thing in the morning. Would take again.

just pick somebody else if u need to take this class. u have to go to concerts n make report. u have to write term paper, u have to listen to a lot of music and recognize the music for listening test. also, he asked u to write down contour of melody he played on the piano for the test.

All you have to do is show up to his class and take notes. He tells you exactly what's going to be on the test, and all of the tests are open note. He gives a lot of bonus questions on tests, so it's pretty hard to NOT get a perfect score.

Fun class. Enjoyed taking this course as I listened to good music and learned a lot. There are 6 tests based on lecture material. You are allowed to use the lecture notes during the tests, so make sure to take good notes and listen to the required music pieces on youtube channel.
Just show up to class, and take notes and you will be fine. 6 open note tests with plenty of bonus. Must attend 2 out of class classical music concerts, but no text book. Enjoyed the class
Easy A if you do the work. 3 concert reports and 1 term paper. Tests have a lot of bonus points! Very clear on what you need to know for the test and you can use your notes
Makes learning music fun and makes learning it extremely easy. Puts tons of bonus points on the tests because he wants you to pass. You do have to go to 3 out of class concerts so keep that in mind.

This class is an extremely simple class. Show up, take notes and you will receive an A. He gives tests that have 40 extra bonus points possible. If you are willing to do one hour of homework twice a week, this is the class for you.

Very great teacher, easy A in the course if you show up. The main hw is listining to about 5 pieces a week and you're tested partially on those (just be able to identify them). All tests are open notes. Anyways,  he's really cool and also has up to +30 in bonus points for tests, but you can't get over 100...

With suttin like classical music,he does his best 2 make the class less boring.seems 2 kno his subject wel.makes u listen 2 a hell lota music in each class-some may like it!Grading:3 concert reports must,6 xams,or best of 5 plus final.students with prior music bckgrnd seem 2 scorn him 4 sum reason.moderatly unhlepful,bt no other severe drawbacks
incredibly unhelpful, attended every class and haven't learned a thing. terrible teacher.
No Comments

He shoves his opinions down your throat, and just randomly says thing that makes you do a double take and has you thinking about the stupid comment for the rest of the class.  He also contradicts himself severely.  He is also a bad grader.
Where are you and have you gotten your Pretty Hair Degree?
he has my exact name, so its kinda funny seeing people say that this guy beat chuck norris and won haha
an interesting man. always keeps class fun and has some crazy antics at times. Class is extremely easy to get a good grade in. Tells alot of "back-in-the-day" stories. i thought he was awesome

Bill Scarborough...really funny guy, makes people laugh a lot during class. Not sure what we learned, but the whole class got an A so it's all good. He'll entertain you with stories about the Delphi days.
yellow dry erase markers

He is an amazing teacher.  His class was the most fun, most interesting, and by far the most enjoyable class I have ever taken.  If you ever need any help with anything not only the class he is teaching he is more than willin to help you.  ABSOLUTLY take him if you have the choice.  He makes jokes all the time so his classes are very layed back.

Bill Scarbrough is the only man who ever challenged Chuck Norris and won. I still have no idea what we did in his class, but it didn't matter because he grades really easy. Don't mess with him or you'll get a 4 jawed chuck to the face. Many references to funnels and his wife make for interesting classes. Bill Scarbrough, God among men. Alllriight.
My favorite class of the week. If you can take a class with him do it you will be much better off than with any other professor. This class was the best.

*thumbs up* Great teacher. I enjoyed his teaching style thoroughly. You learn a lot and the class is quick paced, but he is very approachable if you need help. Clearly enjoys his job and is extremely knowledgeable due to a long time spent in the industry. Very funny guy. Glad to have had him!
one time at delphi...freakin aweseom, approach him with any question about any class and he'll hop up grab a board and a marker and make you a genious
Awesome guy, knows his****, and is funny...
Has a completely arbitrary system of grading. I would recommend all to stay away. He tries to inspire but fails so desperately that it is unbearable to be around him.

Derek is a nice man.Thats about the best thing I can say about him. He wants to teach but has no idea how too.His class discussions can be fun but are often elementaryEx: he will demand answers to questions like "What does it mean that people learn differently?". This class is not fun, you dont learn much and its clear he doesnt put effort into mat

Would not recommend to anyone, not specific on what tests will be on, (each inclusive of about 100+pgs from textbook) and all essay style. Text used is highly debated for credibility and usefulness. Sparked good debates in class but when it came down to grading, was outrageous with difficulty even with following the reading diligently. Try to avoid
guy is a joke. dont bother taking him in any course

Professor Meneely is a fantastic instructor who keeps things interesting by focusing on the why behind the material, rather than just the how. His lectures are always engaging and filled with humor and never had a boring lecture. He also posts all his lectures on Panopto so if you miss a lecture don't worry.
Professor Meneely always finds creative ways to penalize students.

One of the most passionate professors in the department. I wasn't too excited to take security, but it turned out to be one of my favorite classes in the major. The class is no freebie - there is work and you are expected to churn out lots of high quality work.

Had him for performance engineering. For once in a Software Engineering class, I didn't have to push myself to not browse Reddit during lecture. I got lost in listening in his passion for the subject. Best professor in Software Engineering by far.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Class topics are not difficult, but grading criteria is often unclear and thus extremely subjective, especially on exams. Instructor is arrogant and ironically lacks knowledge of modern security topics.

His grading is extreme. Three times during the semester I lost major points due to the requirements for a project changing after the due date. Feedback is vague, and not helpful. I even got a 0 on an eight assignment that I spent more than 10 hours on, and no feedback explaining why I got a 0.
Andy was a super helpful and understanding prof. Pay attention (at least most of the time), and he'll work with you if you don't understand or if you mess up.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Took performance engineering. He's great at pushing you to go further and learn more on your own. Very rewarding class if you put in the time and effort. You will not learn from just showing up to lecture. The labs are the true value of the class, take them seriously.
His lectures are dry. It's difficult to follow him. A difficult grader and a difficult person in general. I wish I had taken this course with another professor.

His passion is unable to be matched (you can tell he loves security). He enjoys this course and it shows. Some aspects needed a little more planning than was given, but overall, I learned a lot in his class. It was not an easy a, but I expected that going in.

Professor Meneely did a great job with 331. He took material that would normally be considered dry or uninteresting and actually made it intriguing and his passion for the subject shows that. The projects were kind of fun. Some people don't like them only because they don't want to do the work. One side note, he very rarely replies to emails.

I wouldnt take him. This professor completely destroys you with due dates. First project due before spring break 1week to do it along with a compsci project due 1day after everyone elses was due after. Thats not all at one point in time there was a project activity and exam due on the same day if hes your only option get started earlyon everything.

Meneely is superbly brilliant.  Any software topic you've got a question on, he has a realistic answer for.  He knows what's important to teach and his lectures are more organized than any other professor I've had.  He definitely cares about the success of his students too, if you try hard and seek out help, you'll do just fine.
He is a great professor, and would highly recommend him to anyone. The assignments are tough and many, but is very helpful if you go see him outside of class. Sincerely wants his students to succeed.

A great guy. Enthusiastic about security and his lectures are engaging and useful. I enjoyed coming to this class.  I did not enjoy the homework. Expectations are unclear. Be prepared to be graded like this is English class, not SE. He's always right for the things he takes off points for, but they were not laid out in the assignment.

Awesome class. The lectures are great and if you do not attend you will not pass. Available outside of class to help. There is A LOT of work in the course and he makes you work for it but is very understanding at the same time. Would definitely recommend.
Awful. Very unhelpful. Avoid at all costs. Lectures were very unorganized, obviously didn't really care about the class. Very arrogant. I got an A in the class and still loathed the experience.

Really helpful guy. Sometimes his explanations were a bit lacking (he stutters a bit when he talks, which was sometimes confusing). Always willing to help if you need it. Also is very helpful in intervening in groups with lazy members. He is very fair and easy to talk to. Clearly defines what his expectations are for each assignment.

Foster is a sweet woman, but sometimes I believe her issues with computers/online courses gets in the way.  Sometimes quizzes aren't open, sometimes grades aren't posted, etc.  She does take mercy on her students by downgrading assignments, which has been very helpful.  Discussion boards are always fun to participate in.
terrific
Shelly has been my favorite Professor at RIT thus far, and made English class much more fun than I thought it would be. Great Professor, it's a shame she won't be back at RIT next year.
She was nice and helpful. Very fun to talk to. Her work was fair. I don't have a single complaint. Taught with confidence and knows her stuff.
Awesome professor. Very laid back and a lot of freedom on the final paper. Great in class discussions. Great in class format overall. Grades are lenient, but also fair.
Very laid back class, lots of room for individual interpretation of the course content.

Amazing teacher. Second time having her. I took her class and it was very interesting. The best part was I had it 8am and I did not drift to sleep once! Myth, very interesting stuff. Assignments are fair, grades fairly, papers to write, lots of reading but overall fun class! I highly recommend her!

Very easy going professor. She makes the class interesting with thought provoking discussion. Participation will make this class more enjoyable. Fair grader as long as you follow the criteria. Highly recommend her.
Amazing professor. Really helpful and a pretty easy class. All assignments have really loose topics and are relatively short. Highly recommend her.
Make writing seminar fun. What else can you say. Grades most assignments on completion. You can show up late with no penalty.

Shelly is actually a good professor. Writing is probably one of the more boring classes out there in my opinion but the papers she has us due are very accessible by students. We can actually write about things that affect us personally. She is a great teacher overall.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Doesn't grade his own work, instead has students grade it for him.  He is lazy and plays his gameboy during class.  Has an attitude if you ask him any questions.  Written portions are worth 30% of your exam and they are all or nothing, usually nothing.

If you can't get to class on time, this guy's not for you. He'll make you stand in front of the class, explain, and apologize. Didn't happen to me, but happened to a lot of other people. Lectures have a nice theme every week but once the anecdotal story is over it gets dry. Exams are tough. Nice guy in general, but can be rude. Don't recommend.
Bad teaching skills.

Puts all notes and lectures online. His tests can sometimes be extremely difficult due to the fact that its required to memorize an entire program from a lab and write it by hand.  Sometimes can be misleading during labs and is very hesitant to help you. Google is your friend here. Required essay (whole semester to do it) and grades rather harsh.

You have to read the assignment sheets to understand what the written assignments are all about.  The final group assigment allowed us to be creative, but it was hard with 3 other people on the team.  Liked the two tests being only 30% of the total grade.

He likes creative critical thinking, and this makes some of the assignments difficult.  Assignments have a sheet on what it is all about, yet there seems to be a wide range on what is acceptable.  Liked the open book tests, but they were not easy.
The grading and assignment requirements are so unclear, it is nearly impossible to know what to do for his papers.  His feedback is completely useless, and every assignment is an absolute crapshoot.

On the plus side he likes to mix it up with guests and videos. Unfortunately, he changes his mind on what he's looking for constantly - even changing requirements after the submission date. He says it's to "separate the As from the Bs from the Cs." What he says and what he means are often two totally different things.
Liked the mix of special speakers, videos, and discussions.  Some assignments were hard, because of lack of clear outline and wanted creative answers.

Took course online. Textbook was necessary. Participation was mandatory for online group discussions. Needed to post more than 5 times a week. The topics for the 3 papers are very vague, while the long length required is not. Tests were held online and were open book. Additional paper and reading on "The Goal."

His assignments are the most vague, incohesive things I have ever laid eyes on. I generally cruised through my entire college career getting As and Bs, and this guy just gave me a 50% on my last paper. No clue what he's looking for and his feedback doesn't help.

Professor Traub is a nice and knowledgeable guy. While I think he enjoys the subject his class was to lecture heavy, and lectures were just powerpoints from the book publisher. He did bring in two great speakers however which aided the learning experience.
He's amazing teacher. He's sweet and very good with deaf people. He will make sure that deaf people understand it clearly. He also believes in giving deaf people an hour extra for exam. He's awesome.
Professor Traub is a great professor he is interested in his students learning and is helpful.

If you come to class it's an easy grade. Open book/notes midterm and final. Essays can be a bit complicated and hard to understand what he's looking for, but hes willing to clarify if you go for help. Overall not a bad teacher.

WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! I could teach the class to myself. It was pointless to go AT ALL! Tests are open note open book and pretty much a joke. Take this professor if you want an easy A and to be annoyed for 10 weeks
He has traveled many places and was in UAE during class. Pushed creativity and that made it hard on some assignments because we were not sure what was needed. Learned a lot. Great class.
Kept students engaged and really liked the guest speakers.  One speaker was a president of a company.  Presentations were tough, since we had to work in teams.  Tests were open book, but hard.
Alright teacher, not real clear on expectations, and brings in graduate level professors to grade the undergrad presentations. Brings in local business leaders.
Great Professor.  Brings a lot of industry knowledge into the classroom!

Professor Wood is lovely and the class is very low pressure. Do the work and attend classes because they're fun, and you'll be fine. He doesn't give feedback right away so you can enjoy the writing process, but when he does it's very detailed and helpful.
So chill but meaningful lessons, and the work is not time consuming at all.

Really nice and funny guy. Not too much reading, and he shared some really good short stories with us. Grade is based off a few writing assignments and a cumulative portfolio, neither of which were very demanding.

Funny and down-to-earth. Really passionate about writing and his lectures are made extremely valuable by his perspective as a writer himself. Absolutely recommend him. The class itself is an extremely easy A, but you can get a lot more than that out of this class if you put a lot into it. (Has 4 writing assignments, 3 of which are below 500 words.)
Chill professor but be ready to receive homework on the first day!

Anselm is very easy to talk to, and he treats his students like they're real people. For his Metals Lab, some of the labs were organized very inefficiently which made one or two groups consistently have to wait and stay later, but otherwise the direction he gave was generally enjoyable and straightforward.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: His class model for Semiconductors or Automotive Electronics revolves heavily on him teaching a subject for one week, then having everyone in the class present a PPT made from a research paper. You then get feedback from him and the class. It helps you learn a lot, and is really fun. Prof Anselm a very chill guy. Just don't be late.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He use a flipped classroom format when I had him, and he nailed it. he assigns 3-5 min videos for you to watch and then quizzes you on them. watch the video and get an A on quizzes. He assigns a lot of homework only because you do really need to practice a lot to get better at statics. also hes a lenient grader on tests lots of partial credit.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: anselms the man. very personable, dedicated, and funny. he will work with you and listen to every question. he is very open to suggestions about the course. theres a ton of homework but its not too bad once you get used to it. my only complaint is the lab portion of the course. its ran really inconsistently across all the sections. not his fault
Could be better
Easy A. Easy going. Good resources.

She's a great professor! She makes the course work very enjoyable and very easy to talk to. She's very passionate and knowledgeable in the field. Very understanding and her work is not hard. Like anything else, you will do well if you put in the effort! GREAT PROFESSOR!

Not a good prof. Pretends to be nice in front of u but will hold grudges. She can't even remember the contents of her slides. Cuts marks for grammar errors in assignments (in a Pack Course! How funny!!!). Assignment grading instructions were not clear. Evident that she was dealing with personal issues and taking it out on students.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Great professor, the class is lecture heavy and the tests are based off the lecture material but are also pretty easy if you take good notes and do the readings. About half the class is based on labs and the rest is reading quizzes and 4 exams. If you go to class and participate just a little, you'll do great.

Probably don't HAVE to go to class but is helpful to get little pieces of info for exam questions. You have to put little effort into assignments and there's maybe 7 for the semester. Do study for exams if you want to guarantee an A. Reuses exam questions so if you find an upperclassmen to give you them you should set. Also Lexi is pretty awesome.

Lexi's classes are always fun. She cracks jokes and listens to student input. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does give tests and a lot of group projects. Overall an easy class as long as you show up and study. I had Lexi for both Packaging Sustainability and Packaging Distribution.

tags: ['ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Good Professor, soft spoken but very nice and likes the sustainability side of the course

While not the most accessible out of class, KP was a fun and amazing prof. He will give you back the same amount you give him. If you pay attention and contribute, he will be your best friend and give you an A+. Such a nice guy!

KP is a great guy to talk to, he's funny and has lots of industry experience, but this class falls flat. It's much more about the game industry rather than actually making a game. The final project can either be make a prototype of a game, or write a giant design doc for the game. Would recommend the doc as there isn't much time for the prototype.

Fun guy, has industry experience working in games. However the class did not really focus on creating games and more talked about the theory/logistics of how one would create games. In other GDD II classes you actually create a game during the semester. Did not learn much in the class aside from broad strokes gleaned from lecture.
Very easy and chill, fun to work with. Works with you to make sure you get your stuff done and that it's quality work you're happy with

My class with Joe was a delight. Great instructor, understanding, interesting, and challenging but manageable projects. I learned a lot about design and materials and he made a great impression. The class was a 6-hour studio at 8 am so the time slot was awful but he made it so worth it. Super funny and you can tell he loves his job and students.

Dr. Parsa is very knowledgeable and a great physicist, but not a very good teacher. I interviewed her for a different class and she flat out told me that she dislikes teaching, and only does it because it allows her to get research funding. She is a tough grader and can be a little condescending. PHYS150 was easy. Her other classes might be harder.

I like Dr. Parsa as a person and lecturer, but as a grader she was extremely harsh. She's the nicest woman when talking to her, but her grading policy did not reflect this. Ask her for help and feedback when you need it, she's more than willing to give it you and her in-person explanation of the feedback she gave is much clearer.
Dr. Parsa is very confrontational and not afraid to get snippy with students, even for asking questions.
Professor Parsa was overall a good Professor. She understands the material very well and is a very intelligent person. You will learn when taking her class.

Was next to impossible to get help from outside of class and would constantly skip steps when going over example problems and her explanations were often not clear, causing many to rely of the TA for help with problems. She uses a "flipped classroom" and honestly the pre-lecture videos were far more helpful than she was in learning the material.

Not accessible outside class. One of her first emails said in bold at the bottom "do not email me I will not respond." She tries to do 'flipped classroom' where we watch another professor's lectures as homework, and do the 'home'work in class. The problem is there is so much work we still have to do the homework outside of class.
He never codes in classes and never does demonstrations in class. He just uses slide which is wasting your time you need to do everything by myself without support.
Great Professor
Great professor. Classes were a little dry but overall, he taught awesome stuff. It's such a sad thing that he's gone and that no one else will know what a wonderful teacher he was.
Great chemistry professor. Incredible guy, really cares about his students. Truly upsetting that he's passed on now. May he rest in peace.
He was a great teacher for gen chem and his memory live on in all his students.

He doesn't respond my email and I dont know why. his tests and homeworks are hard but you will actually learn stuffs. My schedule doesn't match his recitation section so Id rather depends on myself. I dont like him tho, but he's a nice one.
Extremely helpful professor and an excellent guy. Tests and homework are very difficult though
Lectures are boring and monotone but is a very good teacher and is always willing to help. Online homework is hard but helpful.
A great teacher, take him if you can. The class can be challenging at times, but he is super helpful. Go to his office hours!

His power points are completely useless. I got SO lost, especially because on mycourses, they are in a different order than he presents. Some aren't even there! Easier to just keep up with the reading by yourself in the book. Recitation n tests are HARD, REALLY hard, but he does let u use a cheat sheet. but it's week 3 so we;ll see haha

Monotone voice and boring lectures but overall nice guy. Drops the lowest test grade which is nice because his tests are damn near impossible. The online HWs are difficult too-- super finicky about your answers and usually cover things we haven't even learned yet.

Dr. Langner is very willing to help.  I think this class was very difficult and I struggled through the entire thing.  The school should have a pre-req for someone who has never taken chemistry.  I am hoping the next 2 sections get better!!  From what I have been told, if you have to take this class Dr. Langner is the one to get.

He is an excellent teacher who never gives up on any students so long as a student is willing to work hard. His lectures are difficult to comprehend if you do not have the background but overall he is a great teacher and wonderful person. The amount of material you learn outside the class if you can find him is enough to pass the class very easily.

Great teacher... if you go to class. Make sure to read the book and study the quizzes during the week (online) for the tests (most questions are similar to these) Go to class too, because about 1/3 of the questions come directly from lecture. Good teacher if you go to class.
Excellent lectures! Organized and a great sense of humor! He is dedicated and willing to help me achieve a clear understandign of the subject matter.

very difficult class, especially if chem is not your cup of tea. def. go to recitation and do HW. lectures... print out notes-- other then that, it's not really necessary to go. tests are very hard, especially for the short amount of time. you basically teach yourself out of the book...
his class is very hard and he uses these olnine homeworks that take about 4 to 6 hours or more to complete. its crazy

His lectures are so boring, and he doesn't really count attendance since it's in an auditorium. Just go to recitation, do the homework, and go to class for tests. It's so pointless to attend. Only go to class if you want clicker bonus points.

He is a really friendly guy outside of class, and his office hours help somewhat. (if you actually get a chance to talk with him.)  be prepared to teach yourself everything right out of the book, his lectures are dry and fast and almost pointless to attend.

Good teacher. Kinda boring and monotone, and his class is 8 in the morning. Never went to class and still got a B. You would have to be an idiot to get less than a B. Has a total of 5 test grades and only counts 4. Definitly recomended.
Boring as hell, need to work on his presentation, but a nice guy.
Nice as he is, he's also pretty boring and the subject's pretty difficult.  I also find that he's not very good at explaining things in class. =/

Nice guy. I slept through a test and he let me take it after he said no retakes. if you're not a morning person there is a lot of catching up and outside work involved. he's def. a monotone. test's were fair.
a good teacher overall, could work on his voice, very monotone, and explain things a little bit clearly.
Dito on the last entry. Monotone @ 8am...not good. But a great teacher sometime in the afternoon. Record lectures and listen to them later if your not a morning person.
Decent teacher but monotone and it is impossible to stay awake at 8 AM.
this teacher is very good. he's really care about the students progress and really able to help you. i love this teacher
The best professor in RIT
awesome teacher, I love how he teaches and paces the course for us all to better understand!
very good, but a lot of work

Media Narrative was the only class available for a writing intensive that worked with my schedule. As someone who has a major that has nothing to do with media narrative, I thought I was going to absolutely dread the class. Professor Gordon made this class so enjoyable with fun lectures, reasonable work, clear grading. Awesome class and professor!

What a wonderful professor and woman, and an interesting class to boot! Coursework is mostly 2 essays and a final 7-8 pg paper, and classes are largely discussions built off of the slideshows/media we view. She's incredibly kind, patient, and knowledgeable about history. Take this class with her, especially if you need a writing intensive course!
great class, thank you
His class is incredibly useful and he genuinely cares that his students learn. Always willing to help if you come to him too.
His classes are among the most useful at RIT, and teach more than what any student expects to get out of the class.  As a photo student, you can't afford to miss a chance to take him.
Very nice guy.  Knows the course material very well.  Is slow with grading and can move a little fast over some subjects.  Answers questions in class readily and is very approchable.

Professor knows what he is talking about. Easy going, and is helpful as long as you ask questions. Only down side to his course is that he is slow with grading. Other than the grading, I have no problem taking other classes with him.

great guy, teaching is ok. he is very lenient with grades, but never got ANY until last couple weeks so you never know how you are. lectures had NOTHING to do with labs nor did labs to tests or tests to lecture, just really sloppy jumbled class/lab/test material although most of it is departmental wide stuff so not sure how much was his fault

This man is full of himself. He loves to overly explain useless parts of the lecture slides (which he rarely follows) to demonstrate his knowledge of the subject. Exam questions were always a shocker; he never prepared us for them because he was too busy drawing on the whiteboard. Asks obnoxiously specific questions in class. Just useless and awful

I think he did a very good job at allowing Cyber Self Defense class to drive itself with the discussions brought about in class.  No textbook, fair grader and very approachable.  Show up to class, do the little work required, and get an easy A.

Good guy, but not a good professor. Teaches off of a pre-made powerpoint, asks tons of hypothetical and rhetorical questions, and then doesn't explain himself. Overall, did a bad job at explaining the course material.

Giving a lot of lectures but homework not much. Participation doesn't really matter but can make up for it by some submission the professor can offer. Very sweet and motivating professor if you love politics, criminal justice, society.

Wonderful Professor, she was very well knowledge in her field. Reading the textbook was required as classes supplemented the readings meaning you had to do the homework AND attend class. PowerPoints were helpful to study from with class notes. Helpful in class as well as outside of class. Overall the class was a great learning experience.

She is a very nice person, but a poor teacher. She contradicts herself. Her power points and reviews aren't descriptive. All her tests come off the books website, which sometimes contains material we never covered. She claims the test is all definitions; it's not. Also, the final is cumulative and she refuses to give back prior tests to study from.

Took the Auditing course with Dr Dey. She was great and the course was amazing. I learned so much about auditing and how auditors look at companies. I highly recommend this course with Dr Dey. She is great and the course has been very helpful.

Dr. Dey is a high quality instructor.  She is an expert in the field of auditing and is concerned that her students learn the material. Furthermore, she makes the class enjoyable by bringing in guest speakers to discuss accounting careers.
The professor really cares. She is passionate about what she does and really learn from her class. She also brings in professionals and you learn a lot about auditing.

Took prior accounting classes with another prof because he was recommended, but Dey was so much better! I got lower grades with the other prof and found that he was difficult to follow. Dey is very straight forward, and her interactive notes were lifesavers on her open book quizzes and tests!

take her, she's knowledgeable. don't expect lots of clip art and cute animations in the slides, she is an accountant she just does black and white straight INFO no fancy graphics. also she doesn't grade HW so you better do damn well on the weekly quizzes...

Prof Dey is pretty laid back and she knows her topic extremely well. She gives extra credit on the test, and she does half online and half in class for quizzes and test. The quizzes are open book open note. Easy to get a good grade if you attend class and fill out the powerpoint notes packet she provides. I would suggest you take her for managerial

no HW only quizzes, online quizzes and exams none of which can be retaken. online quizzes are tricky as heck. you can take in class quizzes home and return next class but they will be graded out of 40 instead of 50. quizzes are open book. i wish there was more HW so my whole grade didn't depend on tests, i suck at ACC so i am nervous as it is...
Fair professor. Read the book and pay attention and you will get good grades.
The subject by nature is hard. Online hw takes time, but credit for good effort is given.Tests are a LOT of application and based on hw and examples in class. Gives out note packets, easy to follow.

Her class was very difficult, but she definitely knows what she's talking about. I was really struggling but I went to her office hours every week, and that really helped.  the second test was much easier than the first which was terrible.  I didn't like the online homework system we used because there were flaws, but the practice really helped.
She's nice, but kind of confusing.  The first test was hard, but the 2nd test and final weren't bad.  HW was online and annoying, but she was lenient with it if you made an effort.
She made the material more complicated than it needed to be, how ever she was nice an fair.

She is a good professor.  Clean notes and explanations.  If you do the HW, you will do fine on the tests.  Some of the test questions come right off the HW assignments.  She is always willing to help if you don't understand.  Recommend!
Fluid Mechanics:  He sets an easy pace and is easy to understand.  Tests focus on core principals rather than anything abstract.  Easy to get along with.  Would highly recommend.
Mechanics of Materials:  Dr. Gee is very good at teaching the material.  He is easy to get hold of outside of class and is eager to offer help.

Nice guy, but not the greatest professor. Likes to repeat himself a lot and his notes can be pretty disorganized.  He would always rush at the end which would make everything even more confusing. You really need to read the book if you want to learn the material and do well on the tests.  I wouldn't take him again.

Great guy, writes really fast, OK at getting the material accross, He really wants you to do the HW. Tests were hard - he really wants to make you think - test questions weren't necessarilly like HW..he really stretched it. It was personally a very challenging class for me, got a C
Great professor. Kept me awake by going through the material quickly and precisely. I am taking him again for Fluids. His tests were fairly easy but I took him when it wasn't common core tests.

Anton was a great professor. The class grade was 70% homeworks which were similar to the class problem sets. The midterm was take home and the final was a project. He cares a lot about his students and is accessible through email and office hours. The in class content is heavy and his lectures are at times slightly confusing to follow along to.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Anton was a wonderful professor. He was always ready to help in office hours if need be. Most of your grade comes from homework, which was nice. Homeworks were interesting! I would for sure take a class with Anton again.

Anton is a great professor. Most of the grade is homeworks, he encourages the use of external help, and will help you generously if you go to his office hours. I would take him again. From what I hear he had a rough start to teaching as he was relatively new but he has now gotten the reins and is great.

Overall very  professor! wants to help you and is very accessable in office hours. Homeworks are a good part of your grade but if you understand the material you are good. Midterm was online which was nice but also if it was in person you would have been fine. Final grade is mostly from homeworks and there is one final project ( 2 options u do 1 ).

Overall, nice professor, wants to help you understand the topics.  Homeworks were straight forward and usually interesting.  As long as you regularly attend class and listen to the lectures you will learn a lot.  Mid term was take home which was nice.  Final grade is mostly from homeworks.

It's clear he knows what he's talking and passionate about the course material, but he is an awful teacher. Very difficult to understand due to his accent, does not lay out the subject matter in a logical way, and doesn't answer questions succinctly. I would recommend you avoid his Machine Learning class at all costs.

Prof. Selitsky's class was not what I expected at all. His teaching method was underwhelming and disappointing. If you're repeating the class, then I guess his class is for you, but otherwise, I would not recommend it for a first-timer. Again, I wholeheartedly believe he wants the best for his students but he is not fit for his position.

It's really hard to understand his lectures, it seems like it's his first time teaching this class, however, he never prepares the contents before he teaches us, whenever he pulls out a slide, it's like his first time ever seeing the slide. While he is teaching, he kept looking at his TA for guidance. He's a good guy, but just not a good professor.

Selitskiy demonstrates genuine concern for students, yet spends lectures not going over what's on quizzes or even upcoming labs/assignments. He can be hard to communicate with when you have problems, but I ended up figuring out assignments myself using notes and google. Watch out for written exams, they end up having stuff you wouldn't consider.

Was difficult to understand his lectures, and the materials didn't seem like they were created by him. You learn a lot more from the TA recitations than you do during his lectures so just listen to those and go to SI sessions and you should be fine

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Test heavy']
comment: Does not seem to know the material as I would normally dismiss his forgettfulness, he was using chatgpt and having multiple tabs of it open while teaching to remind him. I do not think he made the material/ slides himself and I would also go as far as to say that he does little to hand check and review assignments. Very hard to contact.

This guy does not have the best teaching style in terms of getting material across. I think he just kind of rolls with each lesson as it comes. But honestly, he made me want to come to class because he has such a good vibe. In the end, make sure to pay attention to recitation and review slides before class and you should do okay.

It feels like Prof Selitskiy is out of his element teaching. He often is forgetful during lectures which slows everything down. Many concepts are explained at surface level and then you are expected to know how to implement them in more complex scenarios. Pick a different professor if you're able.

This professor completely fails in conveying the material required to do well in this course. When he gives his lectures, it feels as though he is looking at the PowerPoint slides for the first time, and he tends to speed through them because he doesn't feel like teaching.

If you have some programming knowledge, you should be fine. If not, GL.

This is professor doesn't not take the time to explain anything. He speeds through the lectures and expects you to know things you have never learned before. Sometimes he will end lectures eraly and you feel like you barely learned anything. This is for CSCI-141.

An incredibly talented mathematician and computer scientist. He gives fascinating lectures that, sometimes, can be a little hard to follow. He's a good communicator but his Math PhD (versus CS) shows through. Overall though, once you get used to his style he really is one of the best professors I have had at this school.
Lackluster education, difficult to understand, expects you to know topics without any teaching. Completely learn Python yourself before taking the class.

Very nice and accomodating. Very passionate about what he does. The HW is most of the points, so don't skip it. Midterm I found pretty difficult, but it's worth less than a HW. No final, only a project which is a glorified HW. Biggest issue were lectures being hard to follow, and can be a little chaotic with the class participation exercises.

Professor Selitskiy is a fun guy and seems like a genuine person. However, you don't really learn anything in class from him. Lectures are dense and hard to understand, he's a math PhD and teaches like one. expect a bottom up approach. Its hard to synthesize concepts. Study groups are a must in this class (HW is 77%). But office hours are helpful.
always good feedback, ty

Forest was an excellent professor, really knew his stuff and brought a lot of real world knowledge and experience to the classroom. Critiques were fun and insightful. The working photographers are always the best teachers, Forest is a good example of this. Sadly Forest was adjunct and only taught for two quarters, I hope he comes back.
Literally the nicest person in the world. Gives off Hannah Gadsby vibes with her comedy during class. Super knowledgeable and caring, would 10000% recommend
Lorraine makes this class very easy but still keeps it interesting. She's very enthusiastic during lectures and tasting.
Great and entertaining lectures. Informative if you listen, but it is definitely possible to pass the class if you don't pay attention. Light on assignments, but not a fast grader.

Lorraine is a wonderful lecturer and a great person.  She loves what she teaches, and it makes you love it too.  She is VERY well qualified, and it shows.  Don't buy the textbook ahead of time, it will likely be included in the lab fee.

Attending class felt like going to a comedy show. I could listen to Lorraine for hours. She made everything interesting and easy to learn. If there was one thing I didn't like about the class, it would be that we had to pay over $50 for the online textbook that Lorraine wrote to be able to take the mandatory quizzes.

Really, really nice and understanding person, just not a good professor. Is not accessible outside of class, does not post grades until the end of the semester, and is unclear about assignments. I definitely recommend her but warn you about this.
Everyone loves Lorraine. shes a riot. The class is fun, not too much work and very informative. I highly suggest both this class and professor.

Great class & great professor. She's very animated and this class won't bore you. She suggests a textbook written by herself. I bought it and I know of a few others who hadn't... and I became very annoyed by people asking to borrow it. Theres only two exams, midterm and final, and a final project that you will absolutely get an A on. STUDY

Incredible teacher- she knows what she's talking about and LOVES it, and it shows. She inspired a passion in me through being funny, caring, and most of all, understanding. Impressed with the way she structured the class, and how she gave students no opportunity other than to pass. LOVE her.
nice class. Around 6 types of wineclass
Very good prof. Keeps you interested all class (plus you drink wine). Learned a lot. Looked forward to every class. Highly recommend.

Hems is an amazing teacher and makes the class fun and interesting. WOW II is a little more advanced then WOW 1 and focuses more on the specifics but still introduces you to new things. Attendance is optional but you're own loss if you don't and drink the wine. midterm and final are only 45% which allows you to still do well overall

Lorraine is my favorite teacher that I have had. She is very knowledgeable and keeps you interested in the material. Very energetic and positive. Does not take attendance, but coming to class will help on the tests.
One of the best Hospitality professors in the department. Extremely fun, and will keep you laughing. Class is extremely easy as well!
took lorraine for wow 1, wow 2, and beverage fermentation and distillation
Great professor, extremely knowledgeable on the subject matter, you will learn A LOT about wine. Makes the class very enjoyable and something to look forward to every week. Highly recommended!

Focuses a lot on lecture material and gives A LOT of reading, then proceeds to give super heavy exams throughout the semester that include things from outside the material but relating to the topic, so also expect to have to read online to score well on his tests. He's a little flexible if he's in a good mood, but usually expect hardship with him.
cant really understand what he is saying, thick accent and slow teaching style, lectures are legit the most boring i've ever seen, save urself and dont take his class

Overall really nice old man with funny grandpa vibes, but lectures are incredibly boring and it's hard to understand his accent. Very kind and understanding for the most part. While exams could be difficult, he was very lenient on the grading (especially for more open ended questions).
He was not in many lectures, but it was fun to learn the math perspective behind the cryptosystems for some of the topics.

I would never take this professor. Exams are worth a lot, and it is EXTREMELY unclear what will be on them. Expect things that were briefly covered in class to be worth a large part of the exam. He is very smart and knows the subject, but he doesn't teach well. He will teach everything about something but give no examples or practice problems.

Exams are worth a TON of your grade and are not straightforward. Expect random minor things covered for 2 minutes in lecture to be worth between 20-30% of each exam grade. If you don't study, you won't pass. Homework is hard but completely manageable if you stay on top of it. You do learn a LOT from lectures and dude is usually super chill!

Very knowledgeable but not so good at explaining concepts. Long, slightly disorganized lectures. He is very accessible and helpful outside class and polite, explains solutions very nicely on white boards. Easy-going exams with cheat sheets allowed.

I had the unfortunate experience of having Professor Radziszowski as an instructor. He was not only very rude to students when we needed a little more help, he was often innapropriate with how he handled conversations. He would make creepy remarks that no professor should make. This is all on top of him being a rediculously hard grader.

As respectful as I could possibly be, Professor Radziszowski was just awful. With all due respect, after all these years at RIT, he is by far the worst professor I have had. He is clearly very intelligent on the subject of Cryptography, but his abiility to teach is terrible. The fact he continues to teach at such a prestigous school is beyond me.

Had him for cryptography. On the one hand, he clearly loves this subject and is enthusiastic to teach it. On the other hand, several times during class when explaining new concepts he would skip over crucial steps, leaving you to try to put the pieces together in your head. He assumes you know what he knows to often.
Poor organization for unstructured 761 class. Lectures are dense and topics are not explained well.

No programming projects, rather the exams are used to gauge your understanding of the material. Highly recommended that you take MATH-371 (Number Theory) before taking this course because it is so theoretical. The professor is indeed a genius, but not necessarily the best at teaching.
Stazek might be the smartest person I've ever met. He can be hard to follow sometimes, but if you go to office hours he will make sure you understand.

The bonus is that you see a working mathematician/computer scientist in action. He succeeds in demystifying some concepts. What I'd change with the class: Assign specific pages to be read before class, then spend valuable class time by solving problems. Unfortunately, I still haven't developed the intuition behind algorithm design.

He taught me Algorithms. He made his classes so boring by only focusing on the theoretical parts and not indulging in any programming or algorithm development part. All his exam and homework questions are like that. Too much theory, very little fun.

Extremely intelligent, always willing to help if anything is unclear. Assignments and exams can be very difficult, but they are appropriate for the course. Definitely my favorite professor in the CS department.
It was honor for me to take his classes. He really loves wht he is doing. Lectures are very interesting and inspiring. Great professor!
Had him for Cryptography. He was impossible to understand and not good at answering Questions.

Lectures were always a pleasure to attend: he has a very warm and friendly demeanor, is skilled in presenting complex concepts in an accessible manner, and has a profound understanding of the material he was teaching (CS Theory.)  Constantly made an effort to remain aware of the level of comprehension of the class and adjust accordingly. Great prof

Awesome with a side of awesomesauce. Staggering amount of crypto and math knowledge. He has an accent, but isn't difficult to understand. Grades hard, but curves a lot. For example, I got a 40% on the midterm and a B in the class. Don't be discouraged by the grades - he knows the material can be difficult. Do the work and you'll be fine.
Awesome professor. He's really excited about what he teaches and is more than willing to help if you don't understand something. Class is pretty tough, but you really learn the material well.
Tough tough professor, but couldn't be a nicer guy.  Wants you to learn and is willing to go the extra mile to see that you do.

Seemed like a realy hard, strict guy, but he's really great.  Has an effective teaching style, and is always fair.  He even has a sense of humor.  If you can make a class like foundations of cs theory interesting, you got to be good.

Chaim Sanders is the most condescending professor that I have ever had. He's pretentious, gives difficult assignments, and doesn't help students or teach the content of homework in the slightest. Any review that gave him above 2 stars is either flat out lying, or Chaim himself giving himself a review. The school literally fired him. AVOID HIM.

Expect to spend on this class as much as you spend on all of your other classes combined. I questioned whether or not he knew he was not the only class of the semester due to the amount of load he threw on us. Secondary to your main assignment, you'll be spending the majority of your time learning how to use tools that are not taught in this class

His class is taught entirely through videos and labs, the tests have nothing to do with the videos, half the time the labs don't either, and he's extremely hard to get a hold of on top of all of that. Even when you manage that miracle, he tends to not be especially helpful. On top of that his custom site for the class is broken as all get out..

If I could rate this prof a 0 I would. They are terrible at responding, you might hear back in an hour or you might hear back in a week. The lecture videos are old and outdated. The assignments require knowledge of tools that are not taught in the class (or any of the prerequisite classes). Most people have to retake the class at least once.

Chaim is by far the least organized professor I've ever had. He is almost never accessible via Slack, the website that is necessary for homework is often down (it's his own site) and his lecture videos are rarely helpful for doing the homeworks. He even forgot to give my class the password for our final! Definitely avoid Chaim at all costs.

Learn the LAMP stack before taking this class and you wont have any issues. Learn Docker (and docker compose) as well, and the class will be a breeze. If you know nothing about web technologies, this class will be incredibly hard.

Chaim was nice to me and always went above and beyond to answer my questions. That said, the class is so poorly organized that he forgets his own deadlines, is often unavailable via Slack, and makes you teach yourself the material. Homeworks and project can be hard if you don't have the background - start early!
Doesn't teach class material.

The material is decent but the way he plans out the workload is terrible. You have to figure out a lot on your own. A LOT. He puts us under so much stress that it's hard to learn or enjoy the content.
He made me feel so inferior to him, I decided to change my major.

The homework and project are a little bit messy but if you spend enough time with it, you'll figure it out. This is an online class so you will need to really motivate yourself to work on stuffs, or else you will get dumped with it along the semester. Although Chaim is a little bit harsh, I can say that I've learned a lot after this class.

This man is the saving grace for the Computing Security department. Passionate and devoted to making quality security education available for students. I strongly advise as many classes with him that you can.

Lectures are interesting and consist of lots of tangents. Very meticulous grader but you know exactly where to improve. If you are offended by profanity take someone else. Frequently available outside class for help and advice. Workload for the course wasn't too bad, but other classes with him can be heavy. Moving CSEC dept in better direction.

He is definitely a difficult professor - but you will actually learn something. I have been going to RIT for 4 years and can honestly say that I have learned more in his classes than I have in all my others combined. I would definitely recommend taking him.

He may be smart, and witty, he's pretty funny, makes loads of pop culture references and really loves what he does, but he speaks so fast that anyone whose first language is not English, of if they require interpreting (ASL) you're screwed. Rude, swears all the time, and does not respect interpreting services and doesn't care about adapting.

The guy is pretty harsh. He sets the new standard for the CSEC department, where the older students are screwed if they take a class with him. Prepare yourself for x3 the workload of a standard professor

Would not take again. First time ever teaching and is outright rude to his students. If you don't know something he does you're insulted in front of the class. Assigns labs not relevant to the class and isn't there to help at all with them. Takes forever to grade anything. Wanted to get way more out of this class than I did.

Class --> MEDS 440H 
Super sweet lady! Loved her. Classes were all lectures but no tests/quizzes. Just one big presentation that is an easy A if you understand the material well.

Took her Diagnostic Imaging class. It's a 2 credit joke. Class is mandatory (& extremely boring so bring other work), but it's only once a week and she usually cancels it. Tests are online through mycourses and are directly off of her powerpoints. It is impossible to fail her class.

The RIT scheduling system has him listed as SRIRAMACHANDRA MUR, but his real name is Raj Murthy. See his other RMP reviews here: http://is.gd/sDm6AS - He's an amazingly good prof, knows marketing, tell stories, gives great examples, and is willing to help in any way he can. No mid/final, 4 quizzes, 5-6 hmwks, 1 large ongoing project. highly recomm.

The lectures are very well done, and he does a great job at explaining each topic. There are 2 online tests, a midterm and final, along with a few online assignments and quizzes. There is an attendance sheet that gets passed around every class, but you can miss 3 times without an excuse. Also, he ends almost every class at least ten minutes early.
A good professor imo. He knows his stuffs

Super nice professor. He knows his stuffs and are always available for office hour. Tests are open book and online. You will be tested on whats on the slides as well as some of the important things he says in class. Make sure to take note and you will be good. Highly recommend!

Professor Wang was alright. It was a very easy class with little workload and for the most part simple concepts, but he didn't explain things well. His lecture part of the class was for the first 10 minutes of class and the rest was doing examples. Much of the class time was waiting for people to do the work on their own.

Wang's ECON 101 is extremely easy. All quizzes and exams are fully online and open note. You're given a week for each homework assignment. Each assignment only takes about an hour, and there's only 4 assignments. As long as you take basic notes, you'll be good. If you need your global or social perspective, take ECON 101 with Wang.

Smart person, but lectures were dry. He doesn't use PowerPoint and only talks during lecture, so it was hard for me to follow. Not helpful outside of class. If you miss class, it's on you to get the notes from someone else. Exams are online. We never used the textbook so you don't really need to buy it. Only 2 homework assignments. Overall not bad.

Extremely knowledgable and smart, good at explaining the material. Lectures are interesting based on the subject itself, but no fluff otherwise. All online quizzes and exams, and homework consists of a couple assignment sheets throughout the semester. Helpful outside of class and answers student questions thoroughly.

Actually best teacher in RIT. Online Exams + Final. Basically 0 homework. Attendance doesn't matter as you have like 3-8 days where you won't attend class anyways. No class on exam days. Lectures are top tier with actually good explanations and not just slides no jitsu. If you hate this teacher or fail please get help as you cannot be saved.

He's just alright. Lectures are dry, and some explanations better than others. Textbook is wholly optional (don't need to buy it), as everything you'll be tested on is mentioned in class - especially obscure examples.
Yiwei is a chill guy, and meh professor, and lets you out early sometimes. It's a 101 course so he gets the job done.

He was a pretty good professor who cared for the students and wanted them to succeed in his class and others. There were not too many assignments, 3 online homework assignments, 3 online quizzes that were done outside the classroom, then a final + midterm.

Overall not bad. The class is basically all lecture, and his lectures can be a bit dry. He gives a good amount of examples, but I didn't always find them to be helpful. He is willing to help outside of class, though, and I would recommend taking advantage of office hours as well as the practice problems he posts online. All quizzes were online.

He has a lower score than I would have thought. He is a very straightforward professor, gives lots of examples, and tries to get the class to interact with the material. Homework/quizzes are very fair and for the midterm and final he allows a cheat sheet. If you are having trouble, go see him, he will be happy to help. An overall solid teacher.

Prof. Wang is ok. His lectures are incredibly boring and he doesn't seem enthusiastic about teaching. The class has 3 HWs and 3 Quizzes plus midterm and final. His examples were hard to follow for me. He does let you out of class early a lot though.
He teaches with a lot of graphs like a regular econ teacher would so it was helpful for me. He always let us out 5 to 10 minutes early. His midterms were also online.

Yiwei is a very inoffensive professor in the sense that he does exactly what he says he will do. If you are really there to learn and are interested in the material you will have no trouble; and if you do he will answer any of your questions and stay after class to answer as well. Easy grader and quick to reply to email.

His lectures don't make any sense and aren't engaging at all. Also relies a lot on textbooks. He also doesn't give a study guide like most professors so basicly for finals and mid terms you are screwed. But his home works are fair.

The lectures were either extremely easy or extremely difficult. Difficult topics were not explained well at all. The homework and tests were overly difficult. You could find him outside of class, but the help he offers suffers from the same problems as his lectures.

You're expected to attend class. If you miss it, you're to email her to let her know beforehands. Basically every class she outlines the steps and go over a sizeable amount of mock problems to show you the step by steps of those formulas she provides. Class attendance matter if you rely on that type of teaching style

Pros- If you do bad on a quiz or test, you can take it home with you to fix for a higher grade.  Cons- She expects people to participate but it doesn't help that she picked on the same people over and over again.  She lets students use MyMathLab or the textbook to do homework.

Great prof.  Canceled class 13 of the time, let us go early most of the rest of the time, but she taught us what we needed to know for the final.  Tests and quizzes are very fair if you study for them-- drops lowest quiz and hw.  Makes you participate.  Easiest A  I've ever received.  Does not require the online code.

Clear and straight forward. Gives you the chance to do quiz corrections and test corrections. Lowest quiz grade gets dropped. Homework every night, but only a few problems, it doesn't take long. Pretty easy class.

Joe is the GOAT, all of his classes are a must-take if you're interested in the Graphics Industry. All of the assignments are super open-ended (you can use the languages/framework of your choice) and there's a semester-long project instead of a final.

Low workload. Good at explaining during OH. Decent at explaining graphics concepts, but usually rushes the lecture and lets you out 20-45 minutes early lol. Don't have to fully understand what you're doing (I recommend you do), just need to implement the code from lecture slides. Friends and I thought subject material was boring but easy.

Awesome professor. He makes the classes fun and to the point, discussing the implementation of graphics concepts rather than the theory. Assignments can be resubmitted to regain any lost points. Sometimes lectures finish before time. Weekly activities are fun too. I actually looked forward to doing assignments in this class
Very helpful if you get stuck. Wants you to actually learn the material. Grade doesnt matter.

If you would like to develop an interest/ pursue a graphics career in the future, this course helps you get a gentle introduction to the field. The Professor is amazing, cares for the well-being of students, and focuses on how much the students learn over how many grades the students get.

Joe is probably my favorite professor at RIT. He will make you work for your grade, but if you do work for it, you're guaranteed an A. His lectures are incredible and he keeps things interesting and easy to understand. He's very available outside of class for help. Great sense of humor, great lecturer, great professor.
Best professor, makes you learn the concepts.
Very thorough with explaining the concepts and giving out assignments. Doesn't let you worry about the marks, just makes sure you understand the concept in detail.
The professor really liked the topic, and the class was easy (a little too easy in my opinion).  Class consisted of a mini project each week, as well as discussions and two exams.
Excellent professor. My favorite so far!

Evolutionary Algorithms.  Class was easy, lectures were pretty interesting for a CS class. No tests, only meaningful projects.  You're guaranteed to learn a lot, if you do the work.  Geigel is a good lecturer, and tries to spice things up with videos, guest speakers, etc.
Nice guy, popular for setting up the great and painful CG2 course(if u know what i mean). Knows his stuff, helpful might be a little unclear during class but helps outside class so its even..

great guy.  i've had him for multiple classes and have enjoyed him every time.  he's consistent and fair.  he's always been approachable for me, and if you're having trouble he will work with you.  he has all his notes online and they're very helpful.

Extremely nice professor.  Good structure and layout of the class.  Will guide you toward an answer but not outright explain each step. While it may be challenging, it helps with learning the material.

Useless professor.  The only things I learned in the class were from the textbook and other CS4 professor's slides (so if you have him...make sure you get the book).  I ended up going to other non-CS professors for help, because nobody in the department had a clue how to help his students.
Useless with CS4.  I had to go outside the department for help because he spent an hour staring at my code, then took a cell phone call and left.  He's nice but clueless.
Best CS prof I've had yet.

He's a nice guy and has a very structured class setting (i.e. he lays out what you need to know in PowerPoint presentation notes).  He is sometimes unclear and unavailable for questions, but when he is available, he is very approachable.

All he does in class is just reading powerpoint slides. He expects you to read textbook, but he never goes with it in class.  You will have quiz every week, 60% of the course. Quiz is not only based on powerpoint, but also on textbook ; you have to study by yourself. Quiz problems are sometimes stupid. I will never ever take his class again.

Amy is incredibly amazing and it's a joy to have her as my professor for capstone classes. Clear, communicative and you know what exactly she expects of you. That expectation can be quite high, but it is not unachievable.
Very passionate and loves what she does. Clear project criteria. Make sure you pay attention and put in the work. Group project heavy. Listen to her feedback.

One of the worst professors in the math department here at RIT. Makes his boring lectures mandatory, which are filled with mistakes that inadequately prepare you for the homework and exams. Provides little to no valuable feedback on tests and curve grades to cover up poor averages. Get ready to rely on the book for homework and test preparation.
