Professor Cliver has really figured out being a professor. He constantly encourages questions; I was skeptical at first but it became clear that he is right, you learn while you talk, not while he does. Great person who truly cares about student success, I wish more professors were like him.

Very nice guy and great professor. Quizzes and exams are just like the homeworks. Lectures are clear and informative. Only problem was he got behind on teaching VHDL so the lab section was teaching me VHDL a week before he covered it in class.
Cliver is great. Kinda dry lectures, and easy homework. He is well respected and knows his stuff very well. Great professor and great person overall

Professor Cliver is an incredible lecturer and a very kind individual. He has worked in the industry for decades and is always open to learning. He is very open with what he knows and provides helpful feedback. Professor Cliver loves questions.
good guy

Professor Cliver is a truly incredible lecturer. His lectures can never be boring and he has made an environment where we have inside jokes in the class. His lectures are still very informative and he provides the information in a way that all of us can understand it. Even with the amount of classes he teaches, he is still accessible outside.

The Goat, best DSD teacher makes lectures really fun, really enjoys teaching his classes. Labs might be a little tough but the lectures for the labs are really amazing if you pay attention. Quizzes are not that hard and Exams allow a Cheat Sheet.

One of the best instructors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable and can go far beyond the material in class, drawing on examples from his time in industry to explain the application of what you are learning. He effectively managed a class of over 100 students and took the time to answer every single question, no matter how small.

Cliver is definitely the best professor I've had at RIT. I entered DSD1 with lots of prior knowledge and experience, but I can say that I couldn't have taught the material any better. He's the most flexible and chill, yet effective professor you'll find in a major-based course at RIT. All of the students love him and he LOVES questions.

Cliver's lectures are incredible. He's very animated and while he doesn't often use slides for his lectures, he draws out the concepts and breaks them down very simply. His teaching style may be challenging for those who need slides to learn. He's very friendly and loves questions. By far my favorite human in the EE/CE department.

I legitimately love this man. He has such a contagious passion for what he does, he is hilarious in lectures, and he LOVES questions. Cliver will explain the same concept in 7 different ways without a qualm to make sure that everyone understands the material. He's got some amazing stories and you will never find a better DSD teacher. Truly a 12/10

Cliver knows his stuff and wants to help you do the same. He loves when people ask questions (and he'll make sure to let you know that every chance he gets). He makes his lectures engaging and fun, but still makes sure that you learn something
Cliver is amazing. Amazing support outside of and in class. He's so clearly excited to teach and highly encourages questions. Such a great experience taking his class.

Took DSD1 with professor Cliver in the spring of 2020.Wonderful lectures, clear explanations, and he cares about the material. When I had him for this class, he had recently just left his engineering job to lecture full time and he brings a wealth of knowledge from industry into the classroom.

I took Circuits 1 with Professor Cliver in fall 2019. Cliver gives amazing lectures. He has real industry experience makes it clear that he cares that you learn. He will actively seek out questions by pausing his lecture and going to the back of the room and waiting until someone asks a question. He is passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Cliver was honestly the best professor a 1st year could ask for. He was laid back and loved to connect with his students. He loved questions, so if you ever are confused, never hesitate to ask. Cared for each of his students and worked diligently to make sure each one understood the content in class.
Cliver is the GOAT, this man is so funny. He cares about his students and makes sure you know the material. 10/10 would take again, wish more professors were like him!

He assigns homework assignments with content that he hasn't taught in class. He is also teaching content that differs from what you are supposed to be learning for lab so you will be struggling in two classes at once.

Cliver is the GOAT in the ECET department. If I could, I would take all my classes with him. Just be aware that all the knowledge you learn builds off each other so if you ever get stuck or confused ask questions. Cliver loves ?'s. He will do his best to make sure that everyone is on the same page so that you succeed in labs and on exams.

Cliver is an amazing professor. He is always answering questions and wants you to ask a million questions. This was one of the first EE courses I took and truly enjoyed it. I was nervous about labs because I had never used EE equipment, and he went with me to a lab after class and explained to me how to use the equipment.
One of the best professors here at RIT. He is a divine entity worth every second of your time. If you don't stay for the incredible lectures you'll stay for the unmatched charisma.
Honestly, one of the best professors I have come across so far. Knows his stuff, and will not rest till he makes sure you know it too. Super kind and caring. Fair grader.
Best Professor at RIT

Professor Cliver genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is very good at breaking complex content into easily understandable material and often uses humor to keep lectures interesting. I highly recommend professor Cliver.
best professor here on RIT. He enjoys teaching and makes it fun
Probably my favorite professor here at RIT, can't wait to attend his class in person next year.

If you have the ability to take a class with this professor do so! He is one of the nicest, most chill, and most amazing professors RIT has to offer. His philosophy is for students to worry about actually learning the subject instead of learning how to pass quizzes and tests in the subject. Ask questions especially when it comes to his career.

Probably one of my favorite teachers of all time. He's hilarious, super smart, and answers every question a class has, whether it be super simple or super complicated. His motto is "You have a limit of asking 1,000,000 questions, so after that limit is passed, I'm not going to answer anymore". He teaches super well and connects with the students.

I specifically made my schedule so I can have this professor for a year straight. I took four classes with him and regret nothing. He is super organized and student-oriented. If you are lost in class ask questions since he loves them and he will explain the same question from different perspectives if the message isn't being understood completely.
I felt like we rushed through the lessons too much.

One of the best professors here on RIT. He enjoys teaching and makes it fun. If you have any questions he'll do his best to help you and make it easy to understand by giving examples. HE LOVES QUESTIONS!

Professor Cliver LOVES teaching, and LOVES to see the reaction on a students face when he explains something in a way that is easy for them to understand. This man TRULY cares about the wellbeing of all of his students, and is extremely accessible outside of class. Also, his wife bakes cookies, and on Wednesday, you can go snag one from his office!

Professor Cliver is easily the one of the best professors at RIT. I took him for DSD2, and he did a fantastic job organizing the lectures. The lectures were actually fairly easy, as long as you paid attention and did the homework then the quizzes are very easy. Lab is very difficult, but Cliver was very helpful during office hours.

Love's questions, like loves them. Great person. For DSD I, here's how class goes: -Starts with an example of what you'll be learning and goes from there, can be confusing, so ask questions, he loves them -More and more questions, and you start to understand. -Everything clicks in the "Aha!" moment and class becomes both fun and educational

I might have to take points off because you are only allowed to ask 1E6 questions per semester, and if you go over your limit he will have to allocate you more and its inconvenient. Seriosly, probably the best professor at RIT, and his humor helps you understand the material.

Genuinely a nice person, and cares deeply about his students. He will have cookie days to encourage students to his office hours, understanding towards if a student is having a hard time, and just a overall amazing person. You can just talk to him about any and all problems whether it is related to class or not

The lecture from Cliver was actually incredibly easy, but it was probably due to the nature of the course - DSD2 lab was extremely hard. Cliver is an amazing professor who cares for his students. Super reasonable and wants you to do well. Definitely go to his office hours and you will get great feedback and help.
Loves answering questions. Explanations are precise and clear.

Classes are enjoyable - Cliver puts a ton of effort into making sure students are getting material. Office hours are very helpful & he allows note sheets on most tests. HOWEVER!!! He has a tendency to jump from topic & imply stuff. If you find that you do not do well in loosely structured courses, don't take his course.

Very caring person and understands the students, like he's in our shoes. Very empathetic .Office hours are enjoyable. Be sure to take notes/understand topics that he covers for multiple days: most likely on the test. One thing I disliked is the switching from topics to lab discussions, ruining the organization.
Easily one of the best professors on campus. Makes sure everyone in the class understands the material and is always willing to help. Super friendly, super funny, and all around a great guy.

He is a really fun professor, don't get me wrong electronics I, is a very difficult course. But he somehow makes it a little easier. He absolutely loves questions. He is very willing to help even if you are completely lost. Easy to talk to and find. Fair warning he does give lots of Homework.
Great and understanding guy. Super nice in lab and is very helpful no matter how lost you are. If you can't make it to lab it's very easy to reschedule for another lab time.
Professor Cliver is a great man and great professor. He is hilarious and worth going to at 8AM. You will not be disappointed.

Professor Cliver is the best professor I've had. I've taken 2 different classes with him now and both have been amazing. He doesn't just understand the course, but his students. He will re-explain things multiple ways if he senses people don't understand him, an will adjust the material day-to-day based on student feedback and understanding.

tags: ['LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Knowledgeable professor who is always fine explaining concepts/questions multiple times(and ways) in class. Also accessible outside class; hosts office study sessions with cookies. Cliver is very good at understanding what might throw students off and then ameliorating. HW is from the textbook. TAs are not all as great but grading's standardized.
Take his classes, you won't regret it. This man is amazing.
Professor Cliver is perfect. Even though I only took one freshman level class with him, I continue to learn from him even 3 years later.

I've taken as many courses with him as I could. Cliver is the single best professor I've ever had. He really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. He is always there if you need help. In class he always makes sure to answer all questions so everyone understands the material.

Professor Cliver is hands down the greatest professor at RIT! He truly cares for his students and makes you comfortable to ask as many questions as much as possible. Overall, if you see Cliver for any class, take him!

The best professor I've ever taken at RIT. His lectures are incredibly useful and enjoyable. He had regular office hours and was very helpful during them. He makes sure everyone in his class is very comfortable and encourages questions to the point where he will stop lecture until someone asks something. Worth the 8am 100%. TAKE HIS CLASS

Took Digital System Design 1 with him. Probably the greatest professor I've ever had/ will ever have. Enthusiastic  every day, high energy lectures, pleads class to ask questions, bribes students with cookies to attend office hours, "Cliver House": on Friday nights provides free dinner at his house in addition to tutoring.
Sparked my interest in computer engineering. An amazing man and an amazing class. You will not regret taking Cliver.

Professor Cliver may very well be the best professor at RIT. In his lectures he breaks down complicated concepts into simple easy to understand concepts. After each concept Cliver will literally stop and beg the class to ask questions. He is incredible in office hours, and he bribes students to come with cookies. He loves teaching and is the man.

While he may show up several minutes late to lab often, and frequently disappears for 20 minutes to go get coffee, or goes back to his office and gets distracted by some project only to be reminded that he was in the middle of lab. I love having Cliver as a lab instructor, he is funny, upbeat, clear in his explanations and is willing to help you.

Really tries to help his students, and makes lectures extremely bearable. He constantly stresses the importance of questions and how they take no time at all to answer. Can go a bit fast sometimes but always slows down when requested.

He loves when you asks questions. So never be afraid to ask. He will encourage questions and will try to make sure everyone understands the material. The material is hard, but he makes learning it as easy as possible. Take his class! he is funny and very helpful

Everyone should have a class with Cliver, there's no other experience quite like it. The course material was hard (Signals, Systems and Transforms), but he's really good at explaining it. Go to his office hours, even just an hour a week can make a huge difference, and sometimes there's cookies!

Awesome professor. Really cares about your success in his class. He feels that your grade is a reflection of him as a teacher and does everything he can to make sure you succeed. Absolutely loves answering any and all student questions. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Great professor! Takes things at a good pace in class and is willing to answer any question in or out of class. Fair tests, makes sure you're well prepared for them. Really cares about his students on a personal level. Used the textbook a lot for examples and homework.

TAKE HIM!!! He attended RIT and understands what it is like to be a student at this school. He lets students come to his house on Fridays for dinnerextra helpfunwhatever. Only some of the questions on his exams are a bit unclear as to why they are worded the way they are. He assigns HW with required and recommended problems. DO ALL OF THEM!

I had Prof. Cliver two semesters in a row and he definitely did not disappoint. He is an amazing teacher who really knows how to make you understand the concepts. If you're struggling and you go to his office hours, he troubleshoots to see how he can explain the concept differently in terms that you understand. Extremely helpful and very kind.

He's clear, hilarious, and extremely helpful. The only negative thing I could think of is the fact that the exams had to be crammed into 50 minute periods and were therefore really short, and he didn't give partial credit. So a mistake cost a lot. But other than that, he's fantastic.
Seriously, Take him for every class. I guarantee it is worth the 8am. Trust me!
Take him every chance you get!

Professor Cliver is so enthusiastic and cares so much about his students. He is an amazing professor because he truly tries to get into the mind of his students and sees what teaching methods work well for the class as a whole. He loves it when his students ask questions in class and see him during his office hours. Extremely helpful and nice guy.

Cliver is the best, he really puts his focus on the students and their needs. And his wife bakes. I didn't have any problem taking this class, he practices what he teaches so it's easier to learn from him, he's great.
Best professor that I have had at RIT. Going to class is always fun and Cliver is always willing to answer any and all questions that people have.
Great teacher. Really invested in his students, has gatherings outside of class to help. Class is usually a lecture supplemented with lots of questions and him calling on people to put up answers.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. He's a great teacher and has a great personality. He makes students feel totally comfortable asking questions. He moves fast in lecture, but stops often to answer questions. The lab section of this class can be difficult, but the lecture is easy.

Cliver is an amazing teacher with a great attitude toward teaching. He loves to teach, and he makes students want to learn. He is very helpful and makes it very clear on day one that if you do not ask questions you are wasting your OWN money. My only criticism would be that often the homework assignments were not on material covered in class.

Professor Cliver is a good professor and is great at relating to the students but sometimes tends to get off track. It's sometimes frustrating to sit there when you don't fully understand a concept and he's making jokes at the front of the classroom; still, a stellar teacher and if you pay attention it can be an entertaining, moderately easy class.
Extremely good professor, funny and always enthusiastic about class.

Professor Cliver is the best professor in the world. He knows what he is doing. I guarantee that you will smile and enjoy each class with him. Also you will finish the class with the best knowledge you can get in the class. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking his classes.
Great professor who really cares about the students both in and out of class.
My favorite teacher at RIT. Hands down. I'm not a nerd by any means and this guy made me smile every class, a great teacher to get to know out of class as well. A great teacher, a better man.

Makes the material enjoyable and makes sure everyone understands it in the classroom. However, in the lab, you're pretty much on your own. If you take good notes and pay attention in class, along with keeping up with the homework assigned, you should fare decently enough in his class.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. Despite having class fairly early in the morning, I enjoyed this class a lot. Cliver encourages questions if you don't understand things and has a very clear teaching style. You will learn a lot.

A phenomenal teacher.  Every lecture sort of revolves around questions as they are the best way to learn.  Knows exactly what he's talking about and can explain everything in numerous ways to accommodate different mind sets.  Very little homework with one quiz every week.  Should be an easy A with average effort.
Great teacher, really makes sure everyone understands what he is teaching.  He even does this thing every Friday where you can go to his house for tutoring and free food.

Great professor. Knows everyone's names on the first day and LOVES questions. Very helpful professor. Quizzes tend to be a little tougher than the weekly homework assignments but not too bad depending on your grader. Hosts Cliver house nights every Friday night. Never got the chance to go but heard they're pretty fun.
A very excellent professor.  Always encourages questions that are answered clearly, has a great sense of humor, and above all, COOKIES!!!

Very animated instructor. Asks for questions like crazy. However, you must ask questions to understand everything. That's how he designs his lectures. The book is extremely hard to understand but his lectures clearly lay out the content. He is very funny and excited about the material. One of the best instructors that I have had at RIT.

Top-of-the-line, incredible professor. His lectures consist of explaining everything in beautifully perfected detail and clarity. Practically squeezes questions out of students, and encourages students to ask questions about virtually everything he says. Attend his Friday night parties. The food is INCREDIBLE. Exams are easy if you do the homework.

Cliver was my favorite freshman professor. His quizzes were the only very hard part (but if you do your homework you've seen it all before). Tests were very fair. Homework was as long as you wanted. He however was very fun and loved questions. He had friday night parties at his house as tutoring sessions for students!
Go to class, do you homework, and do your part. And you will be more then fine.  Best Professor at RIT.  He cares for his students, and wants to answer any questions you have.
The best professor I had in RIT! Explanations are clear, but u have to do HW and attend  classes.

Great professor! Knows what he's teaching and knows how to teach. Keeps students awake. Loves questions and makes you love to ask questions! Quizes go straight from hw,  Tests are not easy, but not too bad. Do your hw, ask questions in class and you will succeed!

One of the best teachers I have ever had! He works at Kodak doing the same thing that he teaches, so he truly understands it. HIGHLY encourages questions and is very good at responding to them. If you do your work, his class should be easy. If you do not understand what you are doing, ask and he will help you until you do understand.

My favorite teacher so far! He loves what he teaches and loves teaching it. He begs for students to ask questions because he knows he's not perfect, which is great because it makes you pay attention more. He uses the text only for hw but always for hw. I highly recommend him!

Very nice guy, great teacher. Loves questions, ask away! Goes over things you need for lab which is great! i hear other professors dont, and it makes lab a LOT harder for their students. Weekly quizzes are usually only one question taken directly from the (weekly) homework. Easy stuff, just pay attention and attend class. he's awesome!

Loves to teach. Encourages questions all the time and tells people to shut up if they ask someone to stop asking questions. Very approachable. Can talk to him about anything. Learn how to use the $15 calculator from the bookstore, pay attention, and ask questions when you don't understand and it would be easy to ACE the class. Tests can be hard.
You will not find a better professor at RIT. He is the BEST. Very clear, he makes sure you know the material. Nicest guy you will ever meet.

lots of fun. Had him for circuits 2. He knows his stuff and makes the material very easy to understand. Maybe oversimplifies material sometimes. Optional homeworks kept me from retaining material very well because I didnt do them.
Professor Cliver was one of my best teachers I had at RIT.  He made the material easy to understand, and made sure every student understood the material before advancing to other topics.

Definitely the best teacher i ever had while at RIT. Ive since left Army and then to another college and his teaching abilities still stand out in my mind. He cares about learning the material and it shows

He is ok, not as great as everyone makes him out to be. The class is extremely easy, if not TOO easy to learn anything. Quiz questions come straight from HW, which is not collected. Test questions come straight from quizes, so just do the hw. The only thing that helps is the hw, not his lectures, which are pointless, only examples, no explanations.

Awesome professor. Takes time out to know the students, encourages questions, clarifies doubts very well and is available and helpful during ofice hours. Free Cookies too. He may not be the easiest, but if you want to learn, take his class!
One of the best Professors at RIT. Explains very nicely. Good teaching methods. Labs are fun. Encourages lots and lotssss of questions.

I HIGHLY recommend Cliver! One of the best professors I've had. He gets to know all his students by name, always wants students to ask questions, will keep you involved in the class and ask questions to make sure you know the material, sometimes a hard grader but keeps you interested in the material
Cliver's tha best teacher in the Engineering Dept., and at all of RIT as far as I'm concerned.
No Comments
No Comments

One of the best teachers at RIT.  He relates well with the students. His classes are well understandable due to his ease of teaching skills and he is always helpfull after hours. Also his wife bakes, so stop in his office and get a snack!

I did learn alot but had a tough time at the end when my project failed and expected a little bit of consideration from the professor because I know I didn't deserve a bad grade at the end of the course. Otherwise, professor is very good and approachable.
Amazing professor. Happy to have taken his class.
The professor is very good and intelligent and will help you when you are requiring it. The teaching is cool and helps you.
Nice professor. Actually learned from him
Just an amazing professor ! Simply brilliant. Teaching methods are really good !
Very good teacher, helps clears the concepts and carries a smile in and out of the class
Very helpful teacher. Helped a lot. Good teaching methods
Good teacher, clears the concepts
Awesome teacher

The subject was well covered and he expressed passion for it.  He was also good at adding a personal touch with his real-life examples of networking phenomena.  Occasionally, he would attempt to demonstrate an algorithm that he hadn't rehearsed well enough.  Understandable with the schedule change and curriculum redesign, though.
Amazing professor. Tend to always walk away from his class smiling

Humorous professor to be with.  Straightforward, to the point.  His exams come right out of his lectures so read the lectures and practice on your own then you will definitely be fine.  He requires a lot of work, so don't slack off the class!  I will recommend to take his classes again!

Like most everybody else said, professor Kwon shows exceptional interest in the class and in how well his students are doing.  Work load was rather heavy (data comm II) but you learn the material extremely well! For sure my favorite professor at RIT

Kwon is a great guy and a great teacher. Explains everything thoroughly and actually cares that people are learning. He is a good grader too and always helpful if you need it. Just make an effort and getting an A or B is not a hard task! One of my favorites

Very nice person, very eager to help, I don't see any problem from his accents, maybe he has improved his accent problem during the years? He is a very very nice person again, and very engaged in class and outside of the class as well, I had him for data comm network 2 and I thought all the projects and homework were very interesting.

I had him for 3 classes in a row, Computer science 1 2 and 3. They were studio classes and I found the workload quite managable. He can sometimes be a little difficult to understand due to the language barrier. A lecture hall would be hell with him. Extremely willing to help though.

He's a very nice guy, although he doesn't make the concepts very clear. Not too tough of a grader either. He will gladly help you if you need it. If you don't have much programming experience I suggest not taking his class.

I could not understand anything that he said  and even though its a class on writing java code he never once ran one piece code as an example, if you know java take him because he does not give any homework but if you want to actually learn java avoid him

I don't know why people complain about accents.  I imagine if you went to a foreign country and spoke a different language, you would have an accent too.  Kwon is very helpful and knowledgeable in his field.

Very nice guy, a little problem with the accent, but you'll get it very soon.  Probably not the best teacher for CS 1, he tries though and he is new.  Pretty sure they send all the new guys the crappy jobs like CS 1.  Willing to help though.  Probably better in his field of networking.
This guy is so unclear about what he wants us to do.

JKwon is a really cool guy, makes jokes in class, very friendly. Some difficulty with understanding what he is talking about from time to time, and sometimes he has trouble correctly understanding and answering student questions. Definitely worth taking though.

Awesome prof, would gladly take her again given the chance. Dr Comer makes lectures worth coming to, super lenient grader, extra credit, great at explaining things, and offers more things than the textbook as well as a different take on the content in it. Only negative is that you need a 120 dollar online textbook for the class.

She's an amazing professor; she makes things very easy since it's an intro class. She has a sense of humor, which definitely helps me keep awake in classes. All of the work is online and very easy to do as long as you finish it on time. She's not strict on attendance, but there are some days when she makes us participate, and it's for a grade.

Very good lecturer, genuinely passionate about behaviorism, well written projects and assignments. Strict but quite reasonable late work policy. Your final grade is heavily impacted by the semester-long project so don't wait to do it last-minute. If you're struggling, talk to her, she will help you figure out how to catch up!

Professor Comer was amazing, and if you could take her class, take it. She drops your lowest grade for almost everything and gives a lot of extra credit. Her lectures are super engaging, but you could miss 2 with no consequences. She did require an online textbook, but technically you don't have to pay for it if you really lock in first week.

Everything is online. There are quizzes every week, but they're super easy. Offers extra credit every week for your tests, and there are only three papers that are graded by the TAs. Go to class because she randomly does participation activities. There are weekly assignments too, but you can do the whole course ahead of time if you want to.
For Comer, all homework and turn-ins are online, making the class easy. However, if you miss class, your grade tanks.

Dr. Comer's teaching is very enticing and makes her presentations very engaging. You often have paper-based activities within class that you do for attendance, so attending class is very important. A lot of items are graded by her TAs, so be aware of that when asking most questions. I would recommend this class for your science/math perspective.

Took intro to psych with her. Really easy class with a plethora of material available to use for the quizzes. She's also hilarious which helps keep you awake. Attendance is partially mandatory as you need to be there for the activities which constitute 20% of the grade (she won't tell you when they are but they're really easy).

Her lectures are fun, and the material is easy to learn. She does open internet quizzes each week and the final is open internet. She does about 20 participation activities throughout the semester which you need to be in class for, but otherwise you don't really need to be in class because she posts the lectures online. Easy class, fun professor.
A thoroughly engaging teacher with clear and concise expectations for grading. Also has a great sense of humor.
Amazing professor, super engaging and I enjoyed the course a lot. Would love to have this prof again

Absolutely amazing! Would totally recommend her for any of your psych classes. Her grading is very common-sense and she gives great feedback. She puts a lot of weight on discussions, but if you participate you're good. She knows her stuff and is very insightful!
Comer is GREAT! Go to lecture, participate when she asks, and enjoy it. By far one of the best psych classes I have taken. Final exam was online and she gave a study guide
All online grading things except for class participation, only reason to go to class. Lots of "busy" work. Very nice and funny professor. Have to buy online hw application. Easy A if you do the work.

Very easy lecture to sit through despite being a 9am, not very difficult, especially if you took AP psych before this. If you didn't i could see you struggling more than I did, but the work is very manageable. Overall really good class and really good lecturer

She's great. Her lectures are pretty good and she pops a few jokes here and there. Homework is online and needs to be purchased. The textbook comes with the purchase and is heavy on assignments. Lots of extra credit opportunities but take this class if you are a workaholic and are desperate for a slight gpa boost. I like it so far.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Amazing lecturer, absolutely no complaints there. In terms of pure teaching skills, she may have been the best professor I had this semester. One small complaint that I have is that she didn't really come off as approachable for help. She was a bit hostile when I came to her after making a mistake early on, but other than that she was great.

Easy to fair amount of work. Just a weekly textbook reading (skippable) and online activities. Generous extra credit opportunities, and multiple assignments dropped. Lectures are pretty engaging too, and I actually learned from them. 12-16 random participation activities throughout the semester, but you only need 10 for full participation credit.

She makes Psychology fun to learn, her lectures are entertaining and engaging, her quizzes & tests are open note, what more can you ask for? Side notes: attendance is recorded randomly via "Participation Activities" throughout the semester, HW/quiz are due at the end of each week, the slides she lectures on are posted in the myCourses. 9.2/10

Absolutely loved this course and Dr. Comer.  She is a very easy grader, and she splits up the big paper into multiple sections, so it is not that much work. There were weekly readings and assignments that were extremely easy, and the exams were all take-home. Overall, this course is very easy and interesting, and Dr. Comer is very nice.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I mostly enjoyed the celebrity project, but boy, it was A LOT of work. Nonetheless, the class was good. She was a tougher grader than in PSYC 101. Take advantage of her office hours, it REALLY helps out significantly! DON'T skip class; you only get UP TO three freebies.

Dr. Comer does a wonderful job in turning the dense content of the course into an easily digestible lecture. The way she teaches clicks for me and I feel encouraged to immersion in psyc because of her. All tests including the final are open-book and online. The textbook is imperative as it has most of the HW, and she periodically grades attendance.

Dr. Comer is amazing. Her lectures are fun and the homework load is not heavy. She is well educated and will answer questions in class. It is a goof course to take, just to be familiar with the content. There is 3 writing pieces throughout the semester and one gets dropped. All quizzes are online as well as the final.
Such a great teacher. Genuinely learned so much and always looked forward to her class.

Easy A for $80. You have to pay for the online textbook bc thats where you do the hw. Final was online and can be taken anywhere. Certain days would be taken down for attendance. Attend 10 out of the 15 days, it would be 100 for attendance.

Professor Comer is a fantastic professor! She has awesome lectures and provides lots of opportunities for extra credit and drops the lowest scores for papers/quizzes. I've really enjoyed my time taking intro to psych with her, and I can't wait to take upper-level psych with her again!

Dr.Comer is a lovely teacher. She has an online quiz once a week and homework assignments that are multiple-choice. She gave many extra credit opportunities and it's hard to fail the class if you complete the work. She drops a bunch of grades. No exams and the final is online. She does a random participation activity but no attendance besides that.

Turned boring perspective into an interesting few hours each week. She was able to make lectures not sound boring and fairly interesting and easy to follow along, and provided the slides/resources online to access anytime. She uses an online textbook for all HW, which can be frustraing but okay. Tough grader for essays, but drops some low grades.

This rating reflects more of her TA's than her as a professor, as I see her more as a lecturer. I'm genuinely not certain she ever graded any of my work herself, contact her TA's for any help you need or grading complaints. An hour of homework a week with quiz questions straight from the textbook or lecture slides, it's an easy A if you do the work

She's terrifying, but she's also funny and knowledgeable. You can tell she's really passionate about her research. She's not really accessible outside of class, and she's very intimidating when you try to talk to her. I'm not sure if attendance is mandatory, but she does in class participation activities that count towards your attendance grade.

Really fun lectures, participation is earned by attendance and it random per lecture, not every lecture has a attendance but her lectures are really fun to learn. HW is easy just a few questions online and response pieces are graded easily

Good experience with her for intro to psych. There are basic assignments to do every week but they are graded for completion only. She also does random participation activities which are required, so its good to miss as few classes as possible. Quizzes and exams are all open notes. Overall an easy class if you put in even minimal effort

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Her lectures were really interesting. However, she does not cover everything that comes in the quizzes. You have to read the textbook to know everything. The weekly assignments were really easy. The response pieces are generously graded if you follow the rubric. A great course and you also learn actually helpful things.

Prof. Comer is an amazing lecturer. She had a joyful demeanor and was very helpful when it comes to answering questions. The textbook is online, and she doesn't teach everything that's on the quizzes; she is very up front about this. The assignments were very short and the material itself is incredibly helpful for everyday life. This isa good class

By far, one of my favorite classes at RIT. The workload is reasonable, the lectures are interesting, and the class itself is easy. Professor Comer is a very nice person and she is accessible outside of class, along with TAs. Only complaint I have is that she doesn't always cover all the material during class time.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: For an asynchronous class, this was surprisingly well done. Everything was laid out plainly, and it was always clear what needed to be done each week. She used myCourses better than any other teacher I've seen. The class is a bit of a slog because of the amount of reading and note-taking, but it works if you spread the work over the week.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: While Professor Comer is a very nice person the way she lays out the workload is awful. Each week was broken into two sections and had about 4-6 hours of work attached to it depending on if you truly read the assigned readings. Also breaks just mean the same work load over less days so 3 day weekends means you're working on homework like normal.

I took the class asynchronously. The lectures were good, they were engaging and a good length. What frustrates me is that at the beginning of the semester she sent an email asking people to stop sending her "unnecessary emails." This was an asynchronous class with lectures recorded over COVID, all she had to do was grade and answer emails.

I took this class asynchronously, but Dr. Comer's lectures were so interesting that it felt as if I was with her in person. She definitely makes you work for a good grade, but is flexible, gives great feedback, and is very easy to meet with outside of class. I really enjoyed working with Dr. Comer and I hope I can have her again in the future.
difficult grader, you will WORK for that grade
Lots of mundane quizzes and homework.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: I absolutely loved this class. The online format is the best, hands-down. Dr. Comer is quick to respond, super helpful, and her lectures are easy to follow. Tests were open notes & textbook. Just make sure to go through all the material and keep up on deadlines!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']
comment: Gives an insane amount of homework, quizzes, and assignments. Very overwhelming.
Very interesting lectures and Professor Comer's personality makes them even better. The test questions came right from the notes which were all posted online. A lot of resources for studying as well.

REACH OUT! Honestly, in a setting without much one on one it could be easy to fail this class. Especially if you come into it with a gen-ed mindset. But if you send rough drafts to the TA's ask for more feedback (doesn't give a lot), and work hard it will turn into an interesting and mind stimulating class.
Dr. Comer is an ok teacher and the class content is easy. She produces a very toxic learning environment which makes one feel like they cannot approach her for any help or conversation in general.

This was one of the few lectures I've taken that have genuinely interested me. Comer makes psych 101 fascinating and easy to understand. It's not an easy A, but if you put in a reasonable amount of work and follow (the very clear) criteria provided for papers, you should be fine.

Dr. Comer was my favorite professor of the semester--her lectures are interesting, she's funny, not too many graded things in her class (4 exams, 3 response pieces, optional final). Would definitely recommend to anyone.
make sure you study for exams and GO TO REVIEW SESSION. the ta's help you a lot before the exams.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Dr. Comer is awesome. She is far from the stereotypical college professor -- she curses like a sailor and loves to make the subject material relatable and straight-forward. The lectures are simple but interesting. All that really goes into the grade is three reports and some exams. Her final is optional and replaces the lowest exam (Yay! Easy A!)

Dr. Comer is by far one of my favorite professors at RIT. Although the exams cover a lot of material, if you do the study guides and put time into studying you can easily manage a high B at the very least. Her lectures are interesting, and although they're some work, the papers assigned helped my grade and were worth it. Take Dr. Comer if you can!!

Psychology 101 was a tough class for me to take. I am not really interested in psychology and the class was very lecture heavy. However, Dr. Comer tries to make the lectures as interesting as she can while she has to go through all of the content. Gives extra credit, very clear with grading criteria. GO TO THE TEST REVIEWS!!!
A great intro course with interesting lectures. Workload is manageable, and tests are fair, and study guides are very useful.
Teaches so it's almost always interesting.

Great class if you're interested in psychology. Great professor, she is interesting and has you participate occasionally. Tests include a lot of material, so you need to always be reviewing the information if you want to pass.

I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you are looking for an easy class to fill in a perspective, but if you are interested in Psychology it's definitely worth it. She posts study guides that outline everything that will be exam, including practice handouts with the exact short answer questions. You have to study, but it's worth it.

This class was my favorite for the entire year, I already have enrolled in another class with her. Her teaching assistant grades for her and the one that I had was amazing. I would recommend writing your notes ahead of time with the powerpoint she posts and then listening in class. Also going to the exam prep with the teachers assistant is helpful

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: She is so entertaining to listen to. Jessamy makes you actually want to go to class. Her tests are a little hard, but she makes study guides and practice handouts. Overall super awesome professor.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Dr. Comer is an interesting professor. She is quirky yet very passionate about her field of study, especially Developmental Psychology. She sets a clear grading criteria and gives out study guides before the tests. The tests aren't impossible and she gives bonus points on some tests. Study a week before and you'll be fine!

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Attend ALL classes or be sure to get a D. She doesn't correct anything except the final exam. Her teaching assistants (masters students) correct all the homework and response pieces and they are pretty horrible graders.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Hilarious']
comment: Dr. Comer is a great professor. Her lectures are very interesting and well organized. Her tests can be very difficult, but if you do the practice handouts and go to the review sessions you will do well. I highly recommend taking a psych class with her as long as you're willing to put work in.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: This was one of the more challenging ones that I took during the semester, but she manages to make the lectures both entertaining and educational. I had to study for the tests quite a bit, but they're not unreasonably difficult and won't destroy your grade if you can average "B"s on them. Despite the I had to put into this, I have no regrets.

Dr. Comer is an amazing lecturer. She makes sure to relate the course topics to real life. As long as you do well on the three written response pieces, 4 exams, and attend class, you will not have to take the final. Dr. Comer does rely on her TAs to grade everything. They can be inconsistent, so attend the review sessions to find out what they want

Excellent professor, engaging lectures, and the tests are fairly easy if you show up to class, pay attention, and skim over your notes a few times. Would take again. Attendance isn't "mandatory", per se, but there are some small bits of graded classwork that you'll miss by skipping.
Very fun and easy if you pay attention in lecture. 10/10 would take her class again
She's one of the best teachers I ever got at RIT. Hilarious lectures and very passionate about what she teaches. She helps out a lot and makes class fly by. I would keep taking all her classes.
Dr. Comer knows her stuff, and her lectures are interesting and easy to understand. I ended up double majoring in psych after taking her class!

She is a great professor. I am a Computer Science major and I seriously considered changing  to Psychology because of how great she was. Take her class if you actually want to learn some interesting things, don't take it if you just want to get it out of the way. I have to admit that it is fairly easy to pass the class though.

Comer is an excellent professor. She puts all of her lecture powerpoints on mycourses before class, making note taking easy! Her tests are fair; make sure you study. She also gives numerous extra credit opportunities and makes the class interesting. This class made my double major in psych.

Dr. Comer is a great professor - HIGHLY recommended. Her lectures are interesting and she only gives 4 tests all semester. There's absolutely no way to fail these if you study, she basically gives you the answers in her practice handouts. Only 3 papers all semester, also, which are simple. A++ on this professor  course.

She is a fantastic lecturer. She explains material well and makes it interesting. Study guides are posted for each test which covers all material on the test; these are long but if you do it, you will do good. Would like to have again.

Loved her. She is definitely pretty strict, but when you have classes with over 150 students, that's not a bad thing. It was a class I definitely enjoyed going to. Exams were tough, but she gives you a clear outline of all topics that will be on them so you can focus your studying. Overall not too bad at all if you go to classes.

Very tough grader. If you don't come to her classes and take notes from her power points, you are screwed, because the book doesn't help you much.  She expects you to memorize everything on this planet Earth that is related to psychology. Wouldn't recommend it for people who are not into psychology.

AWESOME professor. Extremely hard grader and tough tests but I learned a ton! I want to sit in on her lectures even if I'm not in the class! She is really a great professor and I highly suggest taking her if you are willing to put in work.

If you plan on taking her. Read the textbook. Her lectures can be helpful. However. Her study guides for the test are massive. Need to know too much for too little on the test. Doesn't use textbook at all. Read off of slides. Test challages are worthless.

This class is NOT easy, but certainly worth it. Dr. Comer is an excellent lecturer and really knows her stuff. Her exams are pretty tough, but she gives you tips throughout the semester on ways to memorize. As long as you come to class and take notes it should be easy to keep up. I Really really liked Dr Comer

After taking this class, I decided to get a minor in psychology. Dr. Comer made the class really interesting by supplementing the lectures with video clips or interesting photos. 3 easy essays, 4 tests, and a participation grade (which is given by the amount of in-class exercises you hand in). As long as you study and pay attention, you will pass.

Class was interesting, and Prof Comer was a good teacher, however, the tests were extremely difficult as they each contained so much material, and the study guides don't really narrow anything down, so you have sometimes hundreds of topics to go over before each test, which I found very difficult.

I like Prof Comer a lot, and I found her classes interesting, however, the tests are extremely difficult as they are so far apart and you have to know so much material for them. I am not good at memorizing, and while I would study for hours before each test, I still struggled, and I got a lower GPA than I would've liked.

She's an awesome teacher, one of the best I've ever had. As of this year, her tests are IDENTICAL to her study guides. Not an easy course, but anyone can get an A if you just look over study guides before the 3 tests. I highly recommend her. She's awesome, great sense of humor and willing to help you in any way. She wants her students to succeed.
The class was very interesting and she is a fun teacher,  but her tests are really hard and a lot of what is on the long study guide isn't actually on the test.

Great teacher! Definitely sit in the front of the class so it's easier to pay attention. Tests are definitely harder, and so taking good notes is essential. If you do not print her powerpoints before class then you are screwed. Take excellent notes and study and you're golden! She's awesome!

Great teacher! Take good notes, print out her lecture slides and actually study the information! Yes, you actually have to put in some work... shocking! If you want to be lazy and get an easy A don't take this class. You do need to put in some work to learn the info but it is well worth it. Compared to other psych classes this class is a breeze!

Class is a serious GPA killer. Reads off PowerPoint slides the entire class. Doesn't assign homework so how you learn the material is up to you. Don't take her class if you can't memorize concepts or hate reading out of a book.

This teacher is okay for anyone who can learn easily by reading a book. However, everyone else can expect a C or less if you do not learn from reading easily. She will not help you develop different strategies for reading and rather will just tell you to go see the tutors.

the course is not too hard. had to study a little bit but as long as you pay attention in class all you need are her power points. The book can be used for things she didnt cover in class but only a minimum number of questions are asked from the book that wherent covered in class. plus she usually gives curves on exams. 2 exams and 2 easy papers

If you miss a class, you're screwed. If you can't memorize 10 pages of vocabulary for each of the 3 term tests, you're screwed. Seriously, this class is damn impossible. She explicitly told the class "I expect the class average to be a C through the course". GPA killer.

You will be graded for two term projects, three exams, and attendance.  Be thorough with her lectures and the detailed book.  She grades you for participation in the class.  Very picky grader.  She talks for 110 minutes per lecture.  She focuses more towards the research rather than understanding the subject.  Not a very helpful course.

She expects you to be thorough with her lectures and the book.  Book is elaborate.  There are 2 term projects and 3 Exams.  Exam include 50 X choice questions and 5 SA. All her lectures are based on power point slides which are available online but you have to be in class to have all of the info. Only 3 exams based on at least 5-6 chapters:50 multip.choice & 5 short answers where you have to be very specific!! its super hard to remember 6 chapters and be specific on any possible question she may ask.Must read book

Bill is VERY unclear about what he looks for in the projects. .  . Bill is a great guy who really cares about his students that ask for help. I thought he was a great teacher and you can tell he has a passion for what he does. Class requires a significant amount of time though but it is worth it. I had 30-45hrs in each dimensional project but I received all A's so just try and you'll be fine.

Bill is a very honest and no-nonsense professor. If he knows you're a slacker, he'll give you a hard time. (I'm sure everyone here who posted bad feedback fits in this category.) If you simply listen to him, and do what you're supposed to do, you will learn a lot. Extra points if you ask him for help outside of class; he loves that!

This shouldn't be a full class.  Bill frequently runs out of things to say, and then makes uncomfortable chitchat for hours rather than letting the class go early.  The content in both is so limited you wonder how 10 weeks of class are filled.  Bill comes off as a desperate salesman with frequency, so afraid of not being taken seriously.

I still remember the first day of INTRO. to digital illustration.  He said and I quote, "This is not a class to learn new programs in."  A prof. saying this now might not get the same reaction now but when I took his class, students didn't come out of HS equipped with basic vector program knowledge.

Bill is absolutely horrible at composing sentences,his bumbling repitition clearly shows his lack of knowledge in the illustration world.If you try asking him a specific question all you will hear is "well uh...ya know, uh, fur, uh play with it."  Isn't creative, doesnt respond to individuality, has no aesthetic sensibility. Just go to his website.

Bill is a great guy, maybe his teaching style has changed since these posts. I had him for dimensional 1 and 2. Never really taught any digital techniques, he showed us a few projects he was working on. But that was it. We never did anything in the class! just crit, and going over sketches. He never would give and Constructive advice. just that ur idea had 'potential' or 'thats interesting'
Bill was an awesome instructor, his crits were helpful and strict. Kept his class proffessional and the way it should be. His teaching method was something that helped me progress to where I am now.
he plays favorism -  you have to kiss his butt to get an A, otherwise the best you'll get is a B.

Finewood is very critical..pays attention to every single detail involved on projects, from the sketch phase to the final piece. (which could be good or bad in your opinion) He tends to expect a strict, professional level and is not very friendly or flexible in terms of critique and grades.
Boring.  Reads from a book.

An outstanding teacher whose efforts and enthusiasm towards making students understand the science behind the facts are unparalleled. Don't take her class if you just want to memorise stuff and use MCQ. Take it if you want to learn and be able to explain what you learnt. Finally, a class where I could apply scientific logic and intelligence.

Teacher is horrible. She really needs to stick to research since her place is clearly not with undergraduate students. straightforward and fair. Teaches you everything you need to know. You will learn something in his class
Coolest professor ever. Tests are straightforward and fair. Teaches you everything you need to know. You will learn something in his class

Even though the course was presented in a somewhat easy format, I was still able to know the material as if I were taking it as a rigorous course with a challenging professor. If you managed to get below a 'B', then you are laziest mofo ever. He said he has a contract with RIT for one more semester so you better take him while you can.

Class consists of lecture on Monday, group discussions Wednesday, and open note quizzes Friday. Make sure you have a laptop otherwise quizzes are impossible to do well on. The readings each week were terrible. He basically tells you exactly what's on the final so that was super easy. One essay. Overall okay class

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: Professor Na will make you work for your grade. Each week consists of 2 or more papers to read, each roughly 20+ pages, and an ensuing commentary. Prepare for many extra assignments as well. If you actually read each week the quizzes are easy, and the final is comprised of the questions from the quizzes. BE READY TO WRITE A LOT!

Professor Na is truly a caring professor. He understands daily life occurrences and is lenient with such things. A lot of academic writing will occur in this class. There is a lot of reading each week and online discussion is mandatory too. Take this course at your own discretion.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: His lecture style is a real gem, something will last in students 's minds for a long time, amazingly passionate, original, making complicated topics MUCH easier to understand. However, if you hate/dislike reading, this class may not be for you, as you'll have to read about 20-50 pages a week. Homework involves a lot of academic writing.

Assigns significantly more work than any other professor for the same course. There are weekly readings that are long and time consuming. There are also weekly quizzes on the readings which are open book, but are full of obscure questions that would be completely impossible without the readings. Save yourself and avoid!

Dr. Na is a wonderful person. I definitely have a greater appreciation for Environmental Studies after taking his class, and he's clearly passionate about the subject. A bit biased sometimes (like on organic agriculture) but it doesn't get in the way of learning. Quizzes are open-laptop. If you have one, this is an Easy A. I didn't, got an A-.
He is an amazing professor, his lectures will last with me in a defining manor of my education. He truly cares, and the material taught will help you beyond the defined topic of the class.

Very thick accent, and very tough grader, tests are all open book, but it would be impossible otherwise, all of the questions on the tests are "complete the quote" or "what was so-and-so's opinion on this issue?" very based on knowing obscure facts rather than actually understanding the subject matter
worth taking. She is quite fun and walks around to help students. Class is organized into groups and she offers help when ever
This professor is worth taking. She is quite fun and walks around to help students. Class is organized into groups and she offers help when ever possible.
Very nice and understanding professor.

Had this professor years ago during my days at RIT. Really hard to get A. Makes you do work but you learn a lot. Pushes you to work your best. Her examples are great. Brought pizza for the class.
Professor requires the use of HonorLock for certain tests. Grading on discussion posts felt fair, but grades on assignments felt all over the place with no real sense of direction.

Bros the goat, I think it's my 4th time having him as a professor, with one more time next spring, he's just the goat nuff said.

Very nice and caring person. You can tell he knows what he's talking about and wants his students to succeed. Projects are a lot of work, but if you get started early it's not bad. Professor French made databases extremely easy. Oftentimes he had very boring classes but it's worth paying attention. He is also very friendly and reasonable if you just talk to him.

Great guy, learned a lot from him in class! He is super responsible!! Have him as my capstone committee and he even helped me to find another committee professor as my second committee professor is leaving school!! If you need a capstone committee don't hesitate  go ask him!! LOVE HIM!!!

Amazing professor. Teaches a lot of stuff and gives a lot of homework which help you learn and improvise. If you ask for help he is always there and makes sure you got everything you asked for. Easy on the grades.
This teacher was pretty awesome went over material then you can leave or do the in class.  Very helpful and friendly when you ask, will work with you and try to help you get a better grade.

Great professor, interesting lectures, reasonably intelligent in helping solve coding problems, always willing to help students, responsive to emails, willing to work with you, cares about students. Would definitely try to take him for another class.

great guy, great teacher. Tough subject, but makes it manageable, most professors couldn't. will help all you need, stop, slowdown, etc. lenient on times due (due midnight,most of mine avg. 3am-noon the following day)never lost points. will run around room person to person to help keep up during lab. ask for help and you will receive gladly, A++++

Had him for my 2nd java class as well as PHP - if you show up and do your work he will help you.  Basically, if you're not a complete jerk you will be very successful in one of his classes.  Also, he can be fairly lenient with a project being a day or two late if you do show up all the time and participate etc.
Great Guy. Really helped me out when I needed it. More of a people person than a number person in grading style. If you can get his class take it.
Great teacher...some of the stuff was a little hard to grasp but he works with you and make sure that u can understand it. i Recommend this professor if you are taking programming for info tech 1!

Great professor, I had him for Programming 1 and I came into the class with no understanding of java.  He makes everything very clear and answers any questions you might have about the topic!  I wish i could take Programming 2 with him.  If you go to class and do the In class assignments plus the homework you will learn a lot from this prof.

He talks too fast on lectures and covers too much detail in them and forgets to explain the fundamentals for those who don't know or are rusty with certain programming languages. However, he is helpful if you ask questions and has a good attitude.

Bryan is a great guy overall. He's willing to go over something multiple times if you don't understand it. He's a fair grader with a very easy-going personality. I would definitely take one of his classes again!
Great teacher for java and database

He's an awesome professor. I would recommend you to take Professor Whittington or Professor French as your primary choice for any programming class. He is a nice guy, teaches class kinda quick but through, grades easy, gives you more than enough time to finish ICE's in class.  Lets you use a cheat sheet for the pratical.  Highly Reccommend to anyone.

Extremely helpful and clear. He is more than willing to help you understand anything you need. Recommended

French is a great guy, very helpful outside of class, guiding you in the right direction after the class is over, etc.  Found I learned the most from doing the homework and learning myself, or seeing him outside of class.

Certainly didn't have any trouble getting an A in this class, i felt the teacher was clear and detailed, and he was very helpful if you requested extra assistance, and was always available through First Class and email for extra help.  He did speak in a bit of a monotone, but it was tolerable.

This is the most difficult professor I've ever experienced. I am genuinely serious when I say I'd rather have my spine ripped out than take another class with her. I only took this class because it was online asynchronous, which was a good decision. She wasn't terrible, but was not good in any way. It often felt like she didn't care about the class at all. Not organized, plays favorites with students, guided my group in the wrong direction for a project and we had to restart at the end of the semester. Almost tried to get her fired at the end of her class because she was rude and a terrible teacher/person overall.

Prof. Napieralski really cares about her students and is always willing to help. Content-wise the class was a bit boring but she lectures very well which keeps them engaging. Professor Napieralski genuinely cares for her students and wants them to do well. Her lectures can be a bit boring at times, but overall the activities balance it out. She uses PowerPoint in lectures and expects you to read the textbook before class. Overall, as long as you put in effort, you'll be fine.

Very good professor at RIT from fall 1999.

I took his writing seminar class in 2015. He noticed I was struggling with English and told me to have appointments with him. Every appointment with Panara, was so clear. He explained carefully and repeat until I understood. Professor Panara always add examples to explain to my class as we were improving our English.

He's picky, tough, and gives you a lot of assignments. He has high expectations from his students but overall, his teaching is effective. It makes me motivated to stay in class and work on my writing skills. It's very difficult to get an A grade but it's not impossible!

Professor Panara is a cool guy with a very animated personality. He assigns essays almost every week and the required length averages between 4-5 pages (double spaced). He offers essay revision at least 1-2 times per essay so you're almost sure to get at least a "B" on the final draft. As long as you don't BS assignments, you should get an A or B.

I had him for Written Communication II. He was one of the best English professors. His lecture and strategy for writing in class was so unbelievable! I learned everything from him and help me prepare in Writing Seminar.  If you want your grade in good standing, follow what he says and do well on not-so-hard quizzes. I recommended you to take him!

Professor Panara is one of the best professors I have ever had. However, he overloades his students. He has high expectation and gives lots of homeworks. If you are good in English and want to have a good writing skills, Take his class!! I promise you will be thankful for  taking his class when you move to writing Seminar.

He is a good teacher. If you look for a good professor for Written Communication II, then go take this professor. Just trust me. I am currently in his Written Communication II class this quarter. He is not really helpful to emphasize the students on essays because he expects them to be independently working by themselves. It is almost impossible to get an A. Do not take this class if you are not good writing.

He's one of challenge professors but he's not feeling bad about his students well. He's using high expectations about essays and quizzes. We all love him because he knows how to make us laugh during the class. If you have him then you must read a lot.
Easy? NO. Flexible? NO. Tough? Extremely.  He is a great teacher, but don't even look for an easy A, you have to work for it!
Prof. Panara is arguably the best writing teachers, hands down. He is easy to approach and enjoys talking with you outside of class time. I had to write a paper worth 2000 words.

Likes to mingle and chat with students during class, but be careful to pay attention or he'll make you a target out of the entire class and embarrass you which he doesn't do very often, but consider yourself warned.

If you're looking for a flexible one, this is not for you.  Very strict, very picky about tardiness and absences.  If he tells you he'll be flexible, trust me, he's not.  If you're in the Panara plays, he won't give a good grade just because you're in the plays.  He'll be very tough.  A nice man.  Tough grader, I got a C, and I'm a RIT student.

He is AWESOME teacher in NTID history. He always love picky to students about the homework or late for class during the class because he is very strictly man. But, he is still very soft heart to our students!

he is AWESOME teacher and he is very picky but it don't bother me.  Lots of homeworks but mostly are not like ALL essays just few essays and few other homeworks.  he's keeping it balance to make sure students to get the concept and understanding.  I recommand students to take him.

He's great teacher! However, he does give a lot of work and expect a lot from us.  He explain things very well.  Students just need to take him seriously and he'll glad and give you more respect if you do your work well enough
Excellent and motivated teacher! Lots of homeworks, though.
not helpful or understanding

ITDL-150. Very kind and knowledgeable. The classes were very interactive and enjoyable.

Professor Burns' feedback was rude and unhelpful. She also missed/cancelled a significant amount of classes. Prof.Burns was an amazing lecturer who was incredibly funny and engaging. Her lectures are interesting, her activities are so fun. Genuinely, one more interesting class you'll take. The only flaw was how little you were being graded on.

I really wanted to like Sarah. She was funny during class, but it was literally just during class. There was ONE miscommunication between students and her and she just kind of lost her chill. This class is all about the readings she gives you and reading online articles. Because of the virtual delivery, we missed out on in person debates and she gave an extra credit opportunity since most of the class failed the midterm. She's a really nice and caring professor but expect to spend most of your time reading.

comment: Get ready to spend any and all of your free time reading just to learn absolutely nothing.

Professor Burns is AWESOME. She's super engaging, down to earth and way more laid back than I was expecting for a PolySci Professor. The class wasn't hard, but you really got out of it what you put in. If you participated in the class discussions it was a way more fun experience. 10/10 professor. I wish she taught more classes.

Professor Burns is the best. She's hilarious, knowledgeable, and gives great lectures. I've learned so much about history and politics in this class, and enjoyed all of it. She's a fair but hard grader, especially for papers, but she will help you get your paper to where it needs to be.

I read these reviews before taking her class this semester and was a little worried. However, she is by far my favorite professor I have yet to have. Her class is engaging, she's funny, and you can tell she truly knows what she's talking about. She cares about students getting the best grade they can and learning as much as possible.

Great professor. Her lectures are super engaging and interesting and really makes the material accessible. She needs to be more professional. She acts like she is 18 and a stand up comedian. She goes on  about the election or funny jokes and forgets to teach. While this is entertaining, its not helpful. She is funny and hot, and she is doing her best to keep the 3 straight hours lecture interesting. Do the require reading and papers on time, give them the time and effort they need, and you will easily pass with at least a B plus.

Professor Burns is awesome. She is so funny in class and is very enthusiastic. She loves Politics and shares her love with the class. The best way to teach history is to tell it like its a story and she does exactly that, which makes the class much more interesting. She is a fair grader and she gives great feedback. Loved the class. Fave professor.

Really loves political science. Class is entertaining and informative. May refer to the founding fathers as "dudes". Tests are easy, readings are optional but recommended.

She is very engaging and will kept you interested and it makes her class go by quickly, if you pay attention in class you will do well. She is funny and witty and hot so definitely take a class with her.
She is a very energetic professor but also overconfidence. Do NOT take her class except you want to waste time on useless discussions and watching someone tell her own story all the time.

Awesome professor, brings a lot of energy into the classroom. She gets really hyped about her material and makes her topic really interesting. Her board writing could use some work, though and be a bit more organized.
She's a new professor and you could tell. Thought this class was going to be interesting but it was really hard to follow and enjoy. She swears a lot too, don't understand why!

One of the toughest teachers at NTID.  Makes you work too much for nothing.  She never considers your priorities.
Tough teacher, but you will learn a lot.  Do the homework and you'll just do fine.
BKK is a decent ASL professor. She was consistently late to class or cancelled class which is very frustrating. I'm not saying avoid her for ASL but she's not my first choice.
For this class, he really focused on making sure we understood the CAPSIM simulation and was determined to have successful students.

comment: I took the honors level course with him and had a great time! As long as you are willing to dedicate the time, you should be able to get an A. Oh my was it challenging not the content of the class but what was expected was not always clear. My advice, take really really good notes (he doesnt use powerpoint or even write things on the board) and ask questions. Do not wait until the last week to write the final because you will forget everything you thought you knew but didnt actually learn
The professor made me want to drink.
Great guy and thought provoking professor.  Seems to really care about students learning and professional development.  Attendance is integral to success in this class.
One of the best!  I've been graduated for 4 years now and he's still an extremely helpful resource.  Very genuine and top notch!!!!
