Awesome prof best course in college of buisness ever (well ethics in tech env was great too). Would highly recommend, made class very entertaining!! Allowed entire class to comment even encouraged it.

Sophia is passionate about astronomy and is not afraid to show it! Nearly all her lectures were themed based on pop-culture or video game interests and still did well to convey the course content. She brings high energy fun to what would otherwise be a boring lecture-heavy class while remaining on task by explaining equations, theories, and more.
nice

This by far, has been my favorite graduate class I've taken. Kayla is down to earth, open and honest and prepare to be part of class discussions, which she makes really interesting and valuable to the content. You DO have to attend class, but don't worry it's worth it!

Amazing professor.  You do the reading on your own. Some class discussion on the reading but otherwise the discussion is open and very interesting. Her experiences are really great to hear about. She's genuine, clear, helpful, and encouraging rather than demanding. Definitely take her classes!

tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Do not expect this professor to help you in any way. Has high expectations for an art credit course at a tech school and will not give extensions. Will not reply to your emails. Will randomly CC your advisor with a suggestion to withdraw for missing a single deadline. Highkey looks like a gnome and has an annoying voice. Bad lecturer.

Professor Gabak does not have clear guidelines for what should be included in your papers. His feedback is all over the place and is not helpful if you are looking to improve your writing either for your next paper or revisions on the current paper. Not the most friendly when writing emails directly to students about problems he feels are relevant.

tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Super chill honestly, I really liked him and I'm taking another class this next fall. Attendance is not mandatory, he posts his lectures, is very easy to reach, and gives great feedback on papers. Also gives chances for regrading if you did badly on a paper so I recommend him :) Great guy!

I loved having Professor Gabak. He has three assignments: a museum report, a midterm, and a final. Participation, even synchronous, was where you got to feel how passionate he was as a professor. He's very caring, and he's also accommodating. He sends email updates about deadlines, and he's extremely motivated to make you into a art historian!

Hes a pretty good teacher, and youll get everything you need to know to complete the essays. However, he does fall into some eurocentrism discussing for example north american art history, describing full cities as "tribes"- while we spend an entire class going over michelangelo's biography, not one North American artist is referred to by name.

I took professor gabak's online art history 135. I would have preferred to have this class in person, but Gabak made it work online. The class only had 3 grades, all essays. This worked well for me, Gabak was not a hard grader on his essays.
Only 3 papers for the class, was good at teaching. Only needed the book for the papers, used the library copy

He is a great teacher and tries to make the subject more interesting by cracking jokes every now and then. The only assignments given are papers but they aren't that hard to write if you pay attention and use correct vocabulary. He is sweet and encouraging and he is always willing to help.
cool teacher, i really like my teachers at RIT. thanks a gain.

Very knowledgeable and has an amazing personality. I thought the class would be difficult but he has realistic expectations for exams (take-home essays). Uploads all his slides online so you have no excuse to do badly in his class. (tip: don't take the 3-hour class. His lectures are interesting but very heavy and you might not be able to handle it)
Very funny. Very willing to help you and clarify things if asked. Very passionate and loves to see students who want to participate

He is definitely a nice guy, and knows his stuff when it comes to art history, but his grading criteria is ridiculous. He tells us to write papers in MLA and doesn't know MLA format himself, which infuriates me.

If every professor was like Peter Gabak, the world would be a much better place. Peter is what a professor is supposed to be, an expert in his field, engaging with students, and demanding when it comes to expectations. I'm a recent graduate of RIT and I've never rated a professor before, but I felt compelled to come back just to rate Peter. 10/10

Peter is awesome!  You have to be on your game and ready to actually work, but he could make any topic entertaining.  If you write the class off and don't show up, you won't do well, but as his classes are more entertaining than anything on TV or the interwebs, you'll be glad to go!

Peter is by far the most engaging professor I've had, and he's not even a professor for my major. He makes an effort to get to know you as a student and his lectures are engaging. You will have to write a fair amount, but he grades very fairly and allows for early paper submissions so you can rework it. I would recommend Peter to anyone.

I'm a software engineering student and was really not looking forward to taking art and architecture 1. After taking the class with Gabak, I know find myself wishing I could retake the class again. Fun, engaging and overall a pleasure to listen to. I was fascinated by this class. The grading was fair and justified.

Peter is the most passionate and engaging speaker, his lectures are interesting and you want to listen to him talk. He can make the most mundane thing seem like the most interesting thing in the world. I regret not taking all of my art history classes with him.

Fundraising and grant writing class -> Peter's lectures were concise, effective and extremely beneficial.  I cant imagine staying awake in the class with out really good professor.  If you care about learning about art history or grant writing take Gabak, even if you hate the topic you will enjoy it after his class

Peter is INCREDIBLE! He is so easy to talk to and just a generally funny and friendly guy. He's also brilliant- he knows a ton about art + architectural history and he makes everyone excited about learning it. Take as many classes with him as you can!!
teacher is awesome and energetic. easy to talk to. I never used the book. the title was fundraising and grant writting but 90% of the course was marketing (making brochures ect.)

Peter is awesome. Cares about you inside AND outside of the classroom. He grades a little harshly (got a 94 in his class and still got a B), and he didn't mention that in the syllabus. BUT Peter is amazing and I highly recommend him to anyone and everyone.
Such a great teacher.  Really cares about students learning and can make even boring classes and topics extremely interesting.  Take as many classes as you can from this incredible professor.

I accidentally butt dialed my mom while in Gabak's Western Art lecture one night. I looked at my phone at the end and realized she had been there listening to his lecture for the past 40 minutes. My mom knows nothing about art history and she said she couldn't stop listening, it was that good. Gabak's lectures are amazing.

Peter is amazing! By far the most passionate, interesting, and helpful teacher I've ever had. He knows so much about art history and you can tell that he absolutely loves teaching it. He does not give multiple choice tests, but rather gives take home essay tests. This is a great way to learn the material. I highly recommend him as a professor!!

Everyone should take Peter,not only does he offer extensive knowledge in art history he is the goto source for all of your grant writing and fundraising needs.  Great to have a professor as inspiring as peter

Prof. Gabak's Survey of Western Art class is great! He knows art history inside and out and loves it. He speaks quickly so make sure to listen intently. Whether you do well is entirely up to you. Some people slack off in his class but those who don't will do well. He is a fair grader and gives you multiple chances to raise your grades.
so bad. i didn't learn anything
Dr. Marengo is a very kind person. The class was very informal, with no exams. He often would go over time. Overall a great person and an okay professor.

As a person I love him however as a professor not so much.
He only checks the exams. 
Hw can be almost a blank to get 100%. The exams are difficult and don't relate to the material covered in class 
The textbook doesn't help.
He is very quiet and needs to bring his own Bluetooth microphone. Which doesnt help. Essentially you learn nothing

Dr. Marengo is a tricky professor to rate. On one hand his classes are easy to pass and don't take much effort to get a good grade. On the other hand when he is teaching topics you should be knowledgeable in he is fairly useless. His lectures have no substance to them and rarely relate to homeworks or exams at all. He just talks about whatever.
Very quiet and goes off on random tirades about math history that are not important to the course

He's very nice and understanding. Even though he may be soft-spoken he enjoys teaching mathematics and is very knowledgeable. All exams are done online (also final). However, it's difficult to raise your grade. HW is not collected so your grade is just your tests and quizzes. Do the HW because many of his test questions are from the textbook.

Gets sidetracked a lot in lecture and can spend multiple days on a single topic, putting the class behind schedule. Only grades two midterms and final. As long as you put in the effort and he sees you're trying, you'll pass.

Prof Marengo is one of the sweetest professors I've had at this university. He upgraded his personal home internet after complaints of poor stream quality. He goes out of his way to make the class as low stress as possible - If you show up and do the assignments you will pass with at least a C. The only way to fail his class is to turn nothing in.

I'm sure he's great in person but online was just not good. His lectures looked as if he was recording with a potato. His answer keys he sent out were blurry as well, couldn't read them and when students complained, he didn't even send out a better one. Hopefully he can go back to teaching in person soon..

Prof. Marengo has failed to transition to online learning. The audio/video often cut out, the doc scanner he uses makes his handwriting illegible, & there is NO POSTED CONTENT in mycourses. 95% of the grade is quizzes/exams. You'll be self-teaching the entire time, there's no point to showing up to class. Every other prof I had adjusted fine.

I enjoyed taking Prob & Stats with Dr. Marengo this fall. The class challenged me for a level 200, but he understood that and graded exams/quizzes leniently. He also replaced the lowest exam with the final, which boosted me from a B to an A! The only way to really fail is by doing nothing. Pay attention in class, do the optional HW and youre good.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Great professor for Mathematical Statistics I. I'm looking to take II with him as well (since he's the only prof to teach it). Go to class, read the textbook, attempt the homework. He'll give you full credit (even if the answers are incorrect or incomplete) if you put effort into it. I'd recommend him to anyone.

Don't do it. He will pass you some how but if you want a decent grade in his class don't take this. Go anywhere else. I found calculus 1 and 2 to be easier than this class and more fair. This class was harder than University Physics 1.

Class was very tough but lectures were very interesting. His tests were very tough but grade seemed to be on effort shown not on grade on tests. Don't receive homework back after turning it in. Great professor, just expect class to be difficult.

Fantastic class. He really cares that you learn the material; always doing stuff to bump peoples grades up so that they weren't so focused on them. Goes slowly and in depth to make sure you actually understand things, rather than just regurgitating formulas. Also, he may be going completely insane (but in a good way)!

His lectures are very clear and he generally has good charisma, which makes lectures not boring. The only complaint I could possibly bring up is that sometimes he's a bit quiet, which is a bit of an issue if you're in the back of the room. Otherwise, the class was great. Homework is optional too, but helpful.

"I have spoken for 42 minutes and have told you nothing relating to today's lesson" is an actual quote from a Tuesday lecture. He decided to then quiz us that Thursday. He instructs us to memorize things only for them to not appear on quizzes. Personally I do not know how I should prep for my next exam. Textbook is a must, you gotta teach yourself

Dr. Marengo is an incredibly nice professor. He's very understanding towards his students and gave 2 weeks for each take home exam. Homework was worth the most points, and he offered a HW help session each weekend where he would go over the HW solutions before the HW was due.  He really loves math and statistics, which made the class very enjoyable

Very good professor, goes over the material well, does a lot of examples on the board and goes over the solutions in detail. Homework is not collected and he's a very fair grader. He gives quite a bit of partial credit. He gave my class 2 tests instead of 3 like most calc professors.
GREAT PROFESSOR! He is extremely helpful and makes sure you understand everything before moving on. I would recommend him to everyone. His tests go hand in hand with what he teaches in class.

he is funny and smart.He is extremely helpful and makes you cannot live without math.He doesn't want students to use calculator i like this cause I don't like to use calculator.easy grader.clever teaching and flexible with anything

Great professor! He knows the material in great depth and is willing to explain it to you. He does get really close if you don't speak loud enough so really project your questions. Funny enthusiastic and clear professor. He is slow so bring the text and stay ahead if you tend to get bored the tests are hard.

Nicest and most helpful teacher I had at RIT so far. He is more then willing to help you if you don't understand. He's definitely not the easiest teacher but it's not hard to pass his class at all. DEFINITELY recommend him. He's my favorite teacher. He LOVES classic rock  and loves to talk about music if you want to get on his good side!

Teaches laboriously slowly. Assigns brutal homework problems. Elaborate test questions involving several weeks of content. This guy was born to be an Honors professor. You will learn, oh, you WILL learn. I think everyone got Cs or lower on every homework and every test, but I had a B, and others got As. Honors classes are so weird.

Teaches at a very slow pace. He's very approachable and helpful but the material is presented slowly and carefully. Some classes we barely made it through 2 examples in an hour. This can be a blessing or a curse. It's all about your style.

Dr. Marengo is an excellent teacher. He goes slowly, but you learn the background of everything. He is great at breaking problems down and explaining each step, how to do it, and why you can. You will learn the subject inside and out. He has a hearing problem, especially with women's voices, so don't be offended if he doesn't understand you!

I had Engineering Mathematics with Professor Marengo for the 20094 quarter. I found him to be a very good professor. I loved to explain the topics beyond what the book cover.  He often repeated himself, to make sure you got the point.  He was very interested in getting the students to succeed.  No attendance, homework not graded (bad for me).

Sometimes the material was dry but he did his best to keep it interesting.  Didn't take attendance, didn't collect homework.  Tests and quizzes were fair and enough time was given.  Is very helpful during office hours if you need them.

Extremely boring and frustrating.  If you learn at a slow pace he's great but if you know what you're doing you'll just pull your hair out, he repeats things way too much.  Only went to one hour of each lecture and did fine the other lecture is just a repeat of the first, his tests and stuff aren't too bad.

Sometimes he has trouble understanding students questions, but I thought that he explained things pretty well overall.  A really nice guy.  He gives you partial credit on quiz and exam questions based on your work, so that is really cool.  His notes that he writes on the board are very neat, organized , and clear.
Insane. Very. I learned way too much about Calc in that class.
Best for the person who's an independent learner. Doesn't hold your hand but presents well. Can be quiet, try sitting closer to the board. Easy grader.

Pros: VERY easy grader, nice guy  Cons: extremely boring, tests are on the difficult side, doesn't seem very organized.  I personally didn't get anything from his lectures - I might as well not have ever gone to class!  Take him if you are good at learning the material on your own.
He is one of the best math teachers. Will make you feel like a mathematician.  very smart, and always knows the answer.
Stresses common themes, never changes the way he presents material or the way he approaches the problems so students learn. Sometimes it gets a little dry and tiring, but its worth it.
My Grade: C. Dr. Marengo was very helpful. Though he wasn't always easy, he thoroughly explained everything. His grading was pretty liberal (lots of partial credit).
very fair, will help you if you ask
Talks to the board all the time, class falls asleep, boring, easy to get lost
Hes a chiller

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Would take again']
comment: Makes a 3 hour night class fly by. Extremely knowledgable and structures the class so everything builds on itself, but he makes it accessible and interesting. Already signed up for another course with him. Sense of humor and is great at explaining/assisting if you are struggling. Need to go to class if you want to understand anything.
My favorite professor by far! If you have the opportunity to take him, DO IT!

Great use of real-world examples for problem solving.  Several times I said to myself - "So THAT'S how you do that!"  Useful stuff, not just theory.  John is very engaging to everyone with a sense of humor.  I will take any class that he is teaching.
nice experience

My interest going into the class was extremely low. John was able to inspire me to want to learn more, and more about finance. His teaching style is all about involving the students, he will not move on until the students are comfortable with the material. Granted, the class was not a cake walk, but it is very possible to receive an A!

Professor Striebich is awesome.  He is really helpful and outlines the problems clearly before tests.  Tests are open notes, but they are not cake walks.  If you do the hw problems and practice then they aren't bad.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you expect to do good you must attend.
Very interesting lecturer.  Combines theory and current events with a sense of humor.  Class time flew by and was never boring. Will definitely take other classes from him.

I never liked my economics courses at my undergrad college.  He brings in articles and current events to make economics interesting.  I've learned a lot and see how economics can be used in business. Will definitely take other courses with him.

Great course with team and individuals projects and papers.  He's a real interesting speaker using current events.  I learned alot in this class.  Would recommend him to everyone for any econ or finance classes he teaches.
Such a good class.  He really makes you understand the material.  Alot of HW that is pretty hard, but all the test are open book and it helps you.

Katie is extremely kind and obviously wanted her class to have a good experience; it was her first time teaching in the department.  However, she took human-computer interaction, already not the most interesting topic, and made it worse.  There wasn't too much work, but what there was was tedious.  Lectures were horrible.  Avoid if possible.
such a great man funny with lots of fun for the whole class
Funny guy if you get to know him. Very straightforward when explaining tasks, pretty chill overall.
This professor is the freaking best. Also, he will make the best jokes about any student.
Blended course. Half class Half online. He's nice. Sometimes boring. But easy.
Yells at students, frequently loses train of thought, unhelpful in lab. Tests and quizzes have incomprehensible and misspelled questions. Avoid.

Do not take his class. During the labs he seems to not know what he is doing. Gets mad when students do not ask any questions.  But doesn?t answer the questions that are asked. Take wireless with any one else, NOT HIM!
Useless lab professor for wireless.
No Comments
Good Guy but a little hard to understand. Monotone voice put me to sleep sometimes but he was always there to help out.

Doesn't speak English very well, is very unclear in his lectures, and gets very upset when you get one of his in-class questions wrong. Very boring. Not helpful. When asked a question, he usually just repeats the last thing he said. Also gets very upset if no one has any questions.

I had Ms. Pickard for both orgo 1 and orgo 2 lab. Overall shes not a bad teacher, but I feel like there are definitely better choices. She is extremely slow to turn around grades, to the point where she actually submitted our final grades to the school late. In class shes friendly, generally helpful, and a relatively easy grader.
Excellent Teacher

This guy is awesome. He does curve the final grade a bit so that's great and on top of that he really helps you review for the exam. Just come to class and actually pay attention and go over his slides and you will do fine.
Great lectures, great feedback and support for students genuinely interested in the course.
I disagree with the previous review.  Dr. Lalonde is incredibly helpful and I found his tests to be more than fair.

Dr. LaLonde does not really focus on teaching.  He just challenges his students with hard exams.  Grading is straight-forward but knowledge is not really conveyed through.  Online lecture slides are boring with a monotonous voice.
nice
I enjoyed his class to the point of taking him again next semester! Be prepared to shoot alot, and don't let his early time slots freak you out! It's worth it!
Kirby is the best photo teacher I've had in the three years I've been here.

Not in photo illustration, just SPAS. This guy is great. Totally knowledgeable, sarcastic, and really helpful. He's someone I want to interact with and someone I'm not intimidated by. He's not afraid to tell it like it is and people really need to hear that. Please take his class, if you're committed to photo, you won't regret it.

Gary is an awesome teacher! I had him for ethics in bio and medicine. He starts the classes by playing music. We have fantastic discussion and he is very funny. There are no exams in this class, and there is very little work outside of class. Would recommend.

Exams took me 15 minutes max the entire semester. Easy material and easy-going personality. Attend class because the slides alone will not give you the info needed for the tests. Has fun guest lectures and gives more than enough freebies. The only shame is how much the material is repeated from other courses, but this depends on your schedule.

Professor Skuse is a really good professor and I enjoyed his class. You definitely don't want to miss his lectures because they have a lot of good information that you won't get from just reading the power point slides. His Exams can be tough but he gives you a lot of great study materials. I would definitely take another class with him.

Waste of time. It felt like Skuse gave up halfway through the semester and the last few quizzes and exams were complete jokes. On one hand the easy A is cool, but it's disappointing that I'm spending money and time to learn absolutely nothing. Skuse was nice but he would be kinda snarky to students and it didn't seem like he wanted to be there.

Dr. Skuse rocks I can't even lie. His lecture notes are vague but his actual lectures are very informative and helpful, so even though attendance isn't mandatory, it's a good idea to show up to every class. His exams are always online and entirely multiple choice/true and false, whatever. Easy class. SO EASY.
Show up to class, take good notes.

Good is as far as I can go for him. He is alright, knows his subject quite well, can make a joke here and there, and can be understanding about students. At the same time, he can be quite rude/condescending. I can definitely tell he cares about being a good teacher, sometimes he just misses the mark.

Amazing teacher. Third class in a row with him and I wish I could take a fourth. This class was my favorite that I've taken so far. Interesting topics with no busy work. It was a big paper on a topic of your choice and a presentation of a topic of your choice. Super interesting and I was always excited to go to class.
Dr. Skuse is an amazing professor and just an amazing person in general. He is  really fun and cares about your success, always always always take again!!1

Ethics in Bioinformatics. Dr. Skuse is an amazing professor and person, and you should take every class he offers. Course itself was taken for Writing Intensive req. Dr. Skuse is excellent at lecture, but he tries not to lecture at you too much. Topics are interesting. He always knows somebody that... story which is interesting and relevant.

Skuse is a great teacher!  Really chill, funny and wants you to understand whats going on in lab.  Always willing to help till you understand the material.  Labs are generally pretty easy, and you can leave class as soon as you finish.  Best yet, no tests, quizzes or homework.  Would recommend in a second!
Awesome teacher. No for for Intro. to Bioinformatics. Funny and always plays rock solos are beginning of class. 3 tests, amazingly easy.
Excellent teacher! Really talks a lot.

One of the greatest professors of all time, offering the best lectures on campus. He truly cares about class and loves it when people ask questions. He provides real-world examples to help relate the class to everyday life. He is also almost always available to help with an assignment or just give some advice. Highly recommend this professor.
Pretty solid professor, no complaints. There is a decent amount of homework, but he posts everything early, so you have a lot of time. He is one of the best professors I have ever had.

For a 200 level course, Professor Kesgin makes this class seem harder than it is. The lecture speed is okay, but the workload is insane. Be ready to do two chapters' worth of material some weeks. I wish I had taken this class with a different professor, could've been more interesting.

Kesgin is very nice and the class is very easy! My only complaint is that he is so unorganized. He often has due date posted at the last minute and the lectures or so boring. He take the lectures very slow and I feel like they could be sped up. Unexpected due dates and unorganized assignments are my biggest concerns.
While his lectures can sometimes be boring, you do end up learning the material. Not a lot of homework, 3 tests, 1 paper and a group project.
Basically just teaches right from textbook. Very strict will call on you even if looking down for one second. Seems always in bad mood. Not helpful.

She was awful.  She was worse than awful. She thought she was the only one with any knowledge of nutrition and refused to acknowledge anything anybody said.  I actually watched her notice someone's hand in the air and purposely turn away so she wouldn't have to answer it. She shouldn't still be teaching.

Made and interesting subject very boring. She will show a video, then expect you to stay in class while she reads from powerpoints exactly what the simple little 20 minute video just said. very uninteresting
Professor Jesse was a very nice Professor. He gave perfect feedback, and was not a tough grader at all. Really enjoyed the class with him, and would definitely take it again!

Took MKTG-430.He had high but reasonable expectations. Projects were designed to increase our knowledge of working with potential clients and how to navigate that by having us work with businesses local to Rochester. You do need to have presentation and communication skills. Easy A if you just do the work, which is reasonable given the class level.

I have terrible anxiety with group projects/presentations. This professor failed to acknowledge my anxiety and failed me from the course because of my inability to complete the group project for the class. He was very difficult to work with and did not care about my situation at all.

Professor Redlo is great! His lectures are fun and interesting and he gives many examples and practice activities. Projects consist of working with a random partner or group but are straightforward if you pay attention in class. Quizzes are based on the textbook and tests are based off lecture, he usually gives test review that is very helpful.

Dr. Redlo really knows his stuff. He is a phenomenal lecturer and keeps the class lighthearted with his sense of humor. The work is not difficult, one paper or other assignment roughly every 2 weeks. Always willing to help if you are struggling and is forgiving with his grading as long as you participate. He is extremely organized in myCourses.

Dr. Redlo is an amazing instructor. He is open-minded and often encourages students to share their perspectives and ideas with the class. In my experience, Dr. Redlo grades based on paper content and a few short quizzes every now and then. I thoroughly enjoy his class and hearing him speak, especially when he ties his own stories into his lessons.

Professor Redlo is a really funny guy I took him for one of my learning communities Freshman year it was so engaging and I loved the class not very many lectures it was more discussion based and you have 5 question quizzes pretty often
Redlo is an amazing professor, a little tough on grading but gives amazing feedback and really cares about your success,

Redlo took a boring subject and made the class fun. He gives a lot of homework, but it's a bunch of small things, like chapter reading quizzes or two page assignments. It's a decent amount of work, but never too much, and he's a great guy who will tell hilarious stories that make the content relevant.
Lots of simple work so assignments and quizzes are low stakes. Enjoyable and upbeat, if not sarcastic, personality. He genuinely wants to see you succeed.

Professor Redlo is a humorous professor with good lectures. Homework is given 1 week in advance, and all quizzes are take-home. Feedback for the writing assignments is comprehensive. Since he is an adjunct, he doesnt host any fixed office hours but is willing to meet up outside of class.

Is very passionate about his subject. Easy and fun to talk to in and outside of class. . He lets his opinions out about the world a bit, but it is related to the topic.  Overall, he cares about each student, and knows exactly what we have been through, because he is a recent RIT grad.

Dr. Professor Dude Guy is a new instructor at RIT, but he's bringing his A-Game to the job. He's funny, charismatic, heavily encourages an active classroom, and is all around a great professor. Do what's asked of you (which isn't much) and you won't have any issues.
Very nice and wants the best out of the students, even though it was a YearOne class
Very professional, yet funny.  Down to earth, great for a conversation.

This man made a boring class fun. He is easy going and ready for a laugh. Just do what little work he asks of you and participate and everything will be great. He is extremely relatable and someone who is ok with you just stopping by and making seemingly pointless small talk. All in all, a phenomenal professor.

comment: nice stuff

She is GREEEAT!!!! She is the most awesome teacher I have had through out RIT! She is very friendly, nice and she is really funny! She is very helpful towards her students she thinks about others than herself. Great teacher! I would recommend her!
Love her!  The best art teacher in the art department!
Awesome teacher! TAKE HER!!!

She's a great person to host Freshman Seminar! She's interesting, and had her husband, Quinsland or as per many, Dr. Q, to be part of her in-class activities to teach about the reproductive system.... Though don't get me wrong, when she teaches, it's like high school all over.

Sad that he is retiring, probably the best professor i have had so far in my CE flow chart. I realized during every lecture he never said a single filler word like "um, uhh" he knows his material very well and can teach for hours about a single small thing. Amazing professor!

I am absolutely devastated that he is retiring after this semester. He takes ZERO flack and writes epically sassy emails. Dr. Moon has inhuman grading speed; where there will be thorough feedback within an hour of submission. Dr. Moon has now set unreasonable expectations for other professors to not be able to meet. I aspire to be like Dr. Moon.

A lot of the class is equations derived and discovered by Moon himself. He knows the material better than anyone. Lectures are informative, but not overwhelming and he often lets students out early. For labs, you get infinite resubmission attempts if a reasonable effort is made on the first try. There is no reason not to get 100% in that section.

Awesome professor. You can tell he is genuinely passionate about what he talks about and is also never late and never takes up too much time. He also posts all his notes in the exact tone of voice he would speak them in which is very helpful. Also cracked at grading and emails, usually having responses within an hour and great feedback.

Dr. Moon is one of the most phenomenal professors I have ever had. He is extremely patient and incredibly clear when answering questions. I was very intimidated in taking this course as this was the first Electrical Engineering class I ever took, but pay attention, ask questions, and do the homework and there is no doubt you can succeed.

Dr. Moon is built different when it comes to grading lab reports and tests as fast as possible. His lectures are great and he gives students every possible chance to get a 100% in the lab section because there are unlimited resubmissions to make up lost points as long as you submit on time the first time. Tests were open notes.

Very solid professor. Good policy of having exams open notes, it shifts your focus from trying to memorize everything to understanding the concepts more. Best Professor.

Be prepared to be spend adleast 6 hrs outside class a week doing homework. Very Smart man, known's the material inside and out.  As most people have already said, Very helpful and willing to help. EE Department DR.MOON #GOAT

The best professor and most dedicated in the EE department at RIT hands down. The only thing he cares about is that his students learn the material, He is easy to understand in lectures and extremely helpful. The tests are kinda hard but if you do the hw you will do fine on.

Excellent professor. While his course is very hard his lectures are extremely clear and explanations in office hours always clear up lose ends. homeworks are very challenging, but he is very good about helping through email and in office hours. tests are open book, open notes. class takes a lot of effort, but overall not too bad.
The main difference between Moon and god is that God took a rest on the 7th day.  Seriously, the best professor I have ever encountered anywhere

A god among men! You can not do much better then Dr. Moon in the EE department. He knows the material like the back of his hand and justifies it in his teaching. Hands down the best professor at RIT
Amzingly Best Prof in EE Dept

Explains the material clearly, gives a lot of notes during each class period, is always available to help with homework, collects homework every friday and is graded by Monday, gives tests every other tuesday and is graded back by the next class period, tests are open book, open notes, the material is difficult but fair, wants students to learn

Agree with all above, he is the best and one of the smartest prof in EE dept. He graduated from Berkerly, CA.. His test takes long time to finish even tho there are only 3 questions. Very good professor. One of the smartest men you'll ever encounter. I was luck to take him in my final year.
Easily the best EE professor.  Knows his stuff and if you put a moderate amount of effort in the class u can get an A while still learning a great deal

Dr. Moon is an excellent teacher.  Covers everything you need to know, is very organized, always willing to help, open book/note tests, and is a fair/lenient grader.  You can easily get a good grade, but you'll actually learn a lot, too.
By far one of the best prfessors i have ever encountered.

HE IS AWESOME, that's all I have to say.

he's the best!! totally recommend

He is a very kind man and has a strong passion for his career. I admire how dedicated he is to helping people in need.

Great professor, Really kind and helps with the course. Great time.

He is the best professor, I have never met anyone with such great knowledge up to date, and fair in everything!

Thanks professor!
great professor, easy grade

great class, tells you exactly what he wants and understand that students have other things to do outside of school. He gives amazing lecture, ;like he guy

Absolute goat of a human being, his lectures are by far the easiest to follow and actually understand the subject instead of just memorizing formulas. Will include trick question tho, which I guess is what the other people are going on about interms of "making it harder than it needs to be".

Absolutely awesome professor. He lets you bring in note cards for exams, and is available outside of class. Ottman absolutely cares about students and wants you to succeed.
Don't be shy he is very helpful and open to questions. He explains through examples so if thats not your style beware.

comment: Significantly better than many Calc 2 professors. Tries to keep lectures interesting with jokes, but it's often difficult to do when the entire class is lectures. The course is hard as hell though, but I think that's more of the fault of the math department's harsh grading than him (leaving out parenthesis can dock points) Absolutely spend time outside of class reviewing, the lectures were kind of confusing to me, but he's a good guy.
His teaching is awful and not explain clear. He is too rush to finish classs

His class was way too confusing for me- his lectures often involved him saying he did not agree with the textbook and didn't want to teach us it. Exams were difficult and often a very very strict grader. I have had math professors who have been picky about grading but not as bad as him.

If you understand calculus fairly well, Eric is great. That being said, his quizzes and exams are harder than most but I never went into an exam not knowing what to expect. I felt he graded fairly and was clear on his expectations. If you struggle with calculus, you may want to find an easier professor, but otherwise Eric is an amazing teacher.

I had Eric for calc 1 and 2. He is a great lecturer, keeps class pretty engaged. He doesn't curve his tests, but they are very fair. Super chill dude, and easy to access outside of class. Even if you fail a test, you can still do good in the class. Wish more professors were like him!!

I'm torn with this professor, his lectures were good and he knew the subject matter well and was certainly passionate. However, the difficulty of his exams and quizzes are extreme I think. If you are not a savant that can grasp and abstract mathematic concepts easily then you won't do well in his classes. His exams are very conceptual and difficult

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: I can't solve a word problem in the class, because we aren't taught what anything means. Literally the only reason for showing up to class is because he doesn't post what we cover online, so I have to show up to have an idea of what we are learning. If you just want to be able to do the math, he's fine, but not if you want to understand it.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Caring']
comment: Eric is an amazing teacher. Not only does he wish the very best for his students, he makes sure he does everything in his power to provide that chance. His grading is always in your best interest, and if you get something wrong, he still looks at your work as a whole. His quizzes and homework are weekly based, and everything on them is reasonable.
Best math professor at RIT

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Best teacher I've had at this school. Lectures are very organized and his explanations are very good and goes past how to do math but actually wants you to understand why it works. Very good at answering questions.
Explains stuff really well and has clear grading requirements. Tries to give you many credits for questions.
Fantastic guy.

Throughout the semester he is always there to ask questions and get clarifications. Even early in the morning he is very funny and makes the lectures enjoyable. If you start to struggle he has many office hours and if those hours don't work for you he will gladly set up another time. Professor Ottman is a great professor and I would recommend him.

He is a bad teacher. He expects notation he never mentions or is not found in the text book and cripples test grades when you dont use it. Being online, he takes points off if you dont show every line of math. He took 5 points off of a 9 point question because I didnt put a line of basic algebra in my answer that is written with a mouse. Avoid!

Eric's good at what he does. He explains things well and makes it clear when you can expect to see something on a quiz or test. Quizzes and tests are fair; you never see anything on them that you wouldn't have expected to. Homework is due weekly and the weekly quizzes based on the homework. He can be a bit awkward but it's worth it in the end.

Eric is a great guy. He tells you why you should care about what hes teaching. Linear is a tough class because it deals with a lot of conceptual topics in math. Weekly quizzes that are very fair. He's a little nerdy, but the best math professor I've had at RIT yet. very much recommend him for any class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Eric is a great Professor. Very kind, a little nerdy, and always available. If you cant make office hours, he will schedule appointments and always answers emails. The topic is tough and Professor Ottman is very DEFINITION heavy. You have to understand many concepts to answer a singular question. If you ask for help, and study, youre good!

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Overall Eric is a good professor. He is a good lecturer that tries his best to keep the lectures from being too boring. It feels like he is more personal than other lecturers in his lecture. His quizzes are a good representation of what will be on his exams. He is a fair grader that will try to give you as much credit for your answers as possible.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Lectures are good, though they can feel a little "ripped from the book." He's sure to make connections to past material you've already learned, and to things you'll be learning next. As a person, he's a cool guy, and it's really nice to have a younger teacher. He can make you feel dumb when answering a question, but it's totally unintentional.

For about a month, Dr. Zacharakis filled in for my Phys-111 class. This was BY FAR the best month of that entire semester. I talked with a few other students, and they all shared the same sentiment; that with her, they learned far more in far less time than with their original professor. Zacharakis also hosts a handful of reviews prior to tests.
Course requires effort but she gives you what you need to succeed. Overall great professor.

She's incredibly compassionate and manages to keep an academic focus in the class, while still behaving and treating us as human. Understanding of student's struggles and willing to meet them where they are. She has very clear and very reasonable expectations for the course, which she articulates well and in appropriate frequency.

Prof. Z is a great professor. Her lectures are clear and time is managed well. She conducts the labs in a way that is both fun and educational. She gives very clear feedback on exams and quizzes and offers ample time outside of class to get help 1 on 1. 9/10 would recommend!

This professor is simply amazing. She gives wonderful lectures and is committed to her students success. She works incredibly hard to ensure everyone does well. There is a fair bit of homework but it is there to ensure you have a good grasp of the course material. If you do the work and put in effort during labs you will do great in this class.

Simply amazing professor. She is committed to the success of all of her students and will work incredibly hard to ensure that everyone does well. She has a fair bit of homework but it makes sure you have a good grasp of the material. If you do the homework and put in effort in the labs, you will do quite well.

Very condescending and immature.  If you don't understand a subject she says she wants to help, but then is demeaning when you ask questions.  I end up teaching myself most things outside of class or asking the TAs who are also not the most knowledgeable but at least try to help.

This is the only course I have had to drop, and I graduated Summa Cum Laude. Within the first week, she was rude, condescending and provided zero helpful feedback or assistance with understanding the material. I would have to guess people that found her "nice/caring" were males. I noticed special treatment to certain individuals...

The immediate diving into the subject of physics was unhelpful as concepts are gone over rather than explained, so you just have to understand what you can to a certain extent, so instead I had to learn physics from watching YouTube videos so I could actually do the work.
Lectures were completely off-topic and unhelpful

To be straight up, Prof Z is probably gonna be my top 3 professors of all time. It is extremely rare to have a professor come in on weekends to help you prepare you for an upcoming exam. Yes, the other comments are right on how harsh the exams are weighted, but that does not reflect on Prof Z, that's the horribly job of the department. Just show up

She actually wants you to learn and improve and will always spend extra time outside of class, even on the weekends, to help. As long as you are willing to put a little time and effort into class you'll be fine.

She was very nice and open to providing extra help, but the tests were weighted so insanely high that a 70 on the first test basically ruined my grade. She also assigns these absurdly long packets in class. Attendance is required except for the lectures. You also can't pass with a test avg less than 70, even if you get 100s on everything else.

This professor was racist (frequently mixed up the few Asian students in the class and was rude to them as well as touching black students' hair), incredibly condescending and disrespectful, didn't provide good feedback on assignments, had boring and unhelpful lectures, and refused to help when we were struggling. Very uncomfortable experience.

Andronique was such a GOAT this semester. I was a little worried about her and physics before this semester started but OMG is she awesome. She is really caring about her students and all she wants is for you to do well in the class. Saturday sessions before exams were an incredible asset in getting a good grade and her doing that shows she cares.

I have never before had a professor that would come in for a Saturday review session and she will absolutely do it every time we have an exam. She takes a minute to grade but she is one of the best professors I've had at RIT in the last 4 years.

I took this as an online summer course. Our weekly assignments and labs were group work, which sucks if your teammates aren't good and can bring down grades. Exams basically followed the homework problems and were at the same level of difficulty. She would post slides and make us watch videos with *few* in-class examples unless prompted for them.
She is very dedicated to helping her students do well. As long as you apply yourself and work it is a good class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Dr. Z is awesome! Forgot major concepts and equations for the course but she made me understand everything, albeit slowly. The lectures are fast-paced but it's not her fault (that's how dept structured it). She tries to teach to the best of her ability and would redo equations. Lots of homework but it is for your practice and understanding!

Horrid. Her lectures are worthless and she talks down to you, then in the same breath gives you difficult problems that are so much more difficult than anything remotely on the lectures and that you are completely unprepared for

She frustrated me so much! She told you about homework on Tuesday or Thursday but wouldn't assign it until Friday night and it was due Sunday night, which meant you had to do homework over the weekend. Her lectures were very monotonous. During labs, she did not go around as much to help groups with problems, the TA was more available than she was.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: So, for starters I am not the best at physics or math in general. I took this class and found it to be the most difficult one I have ever taken. Dr. Zacharakis, however, was a very approachable professor and was willing to assist, but there was a great deal of self learning that needed to occur for the course that I couldn't keep up with.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is very clear and concise and I feel like she really does care about you learning the material.  She was also very approachable and always available to help.

Lectures are clear and concise, and she explains the concepts really well. At first, I thought all we were doing was learning remedial math, but a look at the textbook I realized that we actually just went over two chapters worth of materials. She's that good. She's also very approachable and helpful. Exams are easy if you know what you're doing.

She is one of the nicest professors I've had. Unfortunately with teaching a class of nearly 100 it is hard for her to help you out. If you do ask her 1-on-1 questions she can be very helpful. Class wasn't structured the best, but I feel that the department is more to blame then her.
She is a terrible professor. Won't give any examples and thinks you should be able to teach physics to yourself. The only thing she thinks we need to learn from her is remedial math.

I hated physics in high school. This professor made me think that I should have chosen physics as my major! She uses great examples and animations, is always cheerful and encouraging. You get help whenever you ask right away and her grading scheme has substitutions to help you get the best grade you can. Choose her sections for this course!

I did very poorly on the first test and quiz, but she let the class retake the first test and quiz as homework assignments if you did good on the second quiz. I thought I was going to fail halfway through the quarter, but ended up with an A because she dropped the lowest test and quiz also

Had her for quantum chemistry and she is by far the best! Will work with students after class and is always cheerful and happy which makes learning better. She gives extra credit and there is alot of homework but the homework will only benefit you. Definitely recommend her to anyone!

She gives ample opportunity for extra credit and even threw one of the exams out. She was very receptive when the class was doing poorly and was a great help when I didn't understand topics. I highly recommend this professor.

Seems extremely knowledgeable about polymer technology and chemistry in general, but lectures can be confusing if you're not good at chemistry. Most quiz questions are straight off the homework, so if you do the homework you will do fine. She also gave multiple very easy extra credit questions that add points to your OVERALL average. Easy A.
will never take her for physics again

MacDonald was a great teacher- sometimes she drove me crazy and it wasn't easy, but I worked really hard, and when I didn't understand some concepts she worked 1 or 1 with me to make sure I understood it. If you need to take NTID math class, get this teacher! (better than Miriam)

Judy is a nice teacher to be with. Very patient and motivating. She is not strict or hard but will be very flexible with every student who pass through her hands. I have no regret recommending her to any student.

This class is unbelievably easy, as for my case though.  A very straight-forward class -- simply complete homework, study little by little daily, and should easily be able to pass quizzes and exams.  She's willing to help students for those who are in need of help.  However, the classes can periodically become boring.

One of the best professors I've had. He's really good at explaining math conceptually, not just going through the process. He answers questions very well and always double checks to make sure the student understands before moving on. He's also very generous with exam grading, and very easy to talk to in his office hours or after class.

If you get this teacher, prepare to learn everything on your own, his lectures are very hard to follow and the tests are terrible, the only advice I can give is expect the unexpected because no matter how hard you study there is going to be everything you didn't study on the test.

Dr. Hoffman is very enthusiastic about math, which I love. He never shies away from students' questions and cares deeply about them. His lectures were initially incredible, but got worse throughout the semester. Exams are significantly more difficult than the homework (WebAssign required) and he expects you to apply the material in every which way.

The professor himself is a very charming and approachable guy, however during lectures he would go off on tangents and get sidetracked very easily. I stopped attending lectures after the first exam and used my time to get help from outside sources. His exams are very easy once you get a proper understanding of the material - not from him though.

Pros: Exams aren't too difficult.

Cons: We would have homework (graded on accuracy) on a topic, then get a recitation quiz on it, and only THEN, after the homework and quiz would we learn it in class. He gets sidetracked in class a lot and could do more examples.

First math professor I've ever had who's lectures are not completely useless. There are weekly in-person recitation quizzes with zero make-ups which can be a little annoying, but they aren't too hard. Tests are about as hard as the homework, meaning if you understand the homework you'll do fine. Also kinda cute.

Professor Hoffman is the calc professor you want. He breaks down complex topics into easy to understand pieces. He always posts lecture notes so you can get caught up if you miss class. Quizzes and exams are graded fairly and lots of partial credit is given for understanding the topic. Absolutely would take another class with him.

Hoffman does a great job at making sure you don't just know how to do something, but also why we do it a certain way, ensuring that you have a conceptual understanding of all the math you're doing. You'll have to spend time learning a lot of formal definitions, but will come out of it understanding everything fully.

Great professor-- extremely knowledgeable, very clear communicator and does a great job explaining anything you ask him. Very straightforward/thorough, when appropriate, will stop to make sure everything makes sense and is clear mathematically before moving on. Positive environment to ask questions, good class pacing, & group work is super helpful.
Tolerant of jokes as long as they don't disrupt class. Very comfortable atmosphere. Nice looking face.

Dr. Hoffman is a great guy and great professor. He tends to over complicate things and will throw a lot at you at once, but he is very fair and gives help to those who need it. He prepares you for tests by providing a review guide on my courses and the homework's provide videos and extra problems. Read the textbook and do the work and you're fine.

Very formal lectures, sometimes he can make things in calculus seem overcomplicated, but that's partly because he teaches the formal definitions for concepts in math. It might take a little bit more effort to understand if you're new to calculus.
Like a second father figure, always has great conversations with students that does and doesn't relate to the material
Knows what he is talking about. This course is really hard, exams are open note but still difficult. Took this course during covid so it might not be online anymore.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Hoffman's a certifiable genius, he knows everything about the class and can answer any question you have. His lectures are great, and as long as you write down what's going on you'll be fine. The class itself is really confusing, especially at the beginning, but it's mostly examples you use to solve similar problems.

Hoffman is amazing. He has recently been made head of the Master's Program at RIT. He is very easy to talk to, and very friendly. He will do his best to answer every question, and he provides the right amount of challenge in his classroom. I have to work for my grades, but he does grade fairly.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: His teaching isn't very intuitive but if you pay close attention you'll do well. He is helpful in answering questions.
Take him! Don't think about it twice. If you want a professor that cares about your grade and is really approachable this is him!

He takes the time to make sure you understand the material. His lectures can be a bit hard to understand theoretically, but he gives good examples so it's not a huge deal. Pay abstention, take notes, do the homework, and you'll do fine on the quizzes and tests. If you do need extra help he's there for you.

He is way too theoretical.  In the one or two examples of problems shown per class, he would often not explain his steps or say to 'guess' that a certain equation applied to the problem.  I felt that I was often teaching myself all of the material while doing the homework.  Exams are straight forward, but expect doing a lot of work outside class
He did a great job of making the course easy to follow. He had many methods for relating the hard-to-grasp subjects to well known applications. He kept the class engaged and was a blast to talk to.

Great guy that makes lectures interesting. There's a lot of material to get through and he will make you laugh and make the material easy to understand. Very helpful and understanding, he cares that you master the material, not if your homework is a few days late. Take him if you can!

Makes you generally interested in the subject. Always taught concepts remarkably well, such that I could usually understand the first time around, or would clarify well if asked a question. Definitely take him.
Fantastic professor. Truly, the best.

He's very helpful if you go talk to him one-on-one. A lot of his lectures get really boring and are hard to pay attention to. The homework isn't bad and quizzes aren't hard if you review for them. Tests can be a little challenging. A lot of other Calc teachers at RIT will curve grades but so far Hoffman hasn't so its far from an easy A

Dr. Hoffman is an extremely good calc teacher. He makes concepts clear and uses excellent examples in class. Weekly quizzes are easy. HW is moderate. Tests are challenging but fair since problems are about the same level of difficultly as class examples. Would def recommend.

Matt Hoffman is the best.  If you have the option to take his class, take it.  He is a brilliant man who is down to earth, nice, funny, and very helpful.  He's very understanding and will help you out in almost any situation.  Make sure you show up to class though, he isn't the easiest teacher, but you'll definitely enjoy his class.

Dr. Hoffman is one of the few professors I've had that is willing to change how he teaches based on student feedback. He's eager to help students and actually helpful when you ask him questions. He has a few pedagogical tendencies that can make class frustrating or unclear, but overall is a good teacher.

Good professor, teaches a difficult subject reasonably well, and makes sure that you do understand the subject in office hours. Sometimes he does ramble on for a proof or long derivation for a while, bu he does tie it all back together.
Moderately helpful.  More helpful one-on-one, but if you take the class at 8 am, he is not awake. Ask questions as he is helpful in answering them.

Although Dr. Hoffman just began this quarter, he is an amazing professor. He is very energetic about his work and encourages thinking beyond the application of numbers. He is willing to work with you and is very approachable. Two exams and a final, one quiz (besides exam weeks) and a homework assignment every week. Pay attention and do the
Blunt but kind. Engages in good dialogue with students and is willing to pull you aside and give extra instruction. Does expect a lot from you and grading criteria was very nebulous.

a professor that i respect a lot. a tough grader, though gives a lot of useful feedback and is very accessible out of class. he has a chill vibe overall and is great to conversate with. definitely got a lot out of this class

Grades are only posted at the end of the semester, and unless your projects were outstanding, expect a B. Most of the work can be completed during class. Prof. Aslam is professional and no-nonsense. It;s clear that he's been teaching figural sculpture for a long time. He has a wealth of expertise on the subject. Participate in crits! Give feedback!
Very chill and lowkey professor, but tough grader. How are you going to put 2/3rds of my sculptures on display for half a year then give me a B?

he was a nice guy. always said out of pocket things, caught me off guard a lot. very helpful with his advice. hes a quiet dude, i dont think ive ever seen him sit in a chair. he only gave As to outstanding projects; it might've had to do with the student's dedication too. i was lazy during class sometimes. 

overall a nice dude, gives good feedback

Pascal's classes are engaging, casual, and fun. There is a required online textbook and quiz software and lots of small homework assignments that count for a significant portion of your grade, but they are easy, and Pascal grades them on whether or not they are done vs whether they are correct.

I love Pascal. He is such a funny guy, and I always enjoyed his class. He does call on people randomly, but even if you don't know it you can just say you don't know and he will help you out! A decent amount of homework but nothing hard.

Pascal is an amazing professor. I am a Nazareth College student. I took the French class for the beginners. He will make you participate but in a fun way, won't embarrass you. He is very fun and passionate about teaching his students French. Always comes with excitement in class. One of the best professor I would say. My course name is FRN10101.

I like Pascal. He's a great guy, and wants you to learn. I don't like MLFR201. The class was incoherent. I often had no idea what topic we were talking about, and Cengage's HW served only to frustrate and never reinforce. If you need a tight structure to learn, this ain't it chief. I honestly feel like I would have been just as fine self-studying.

He's very easygoing and hilarious. Let's you do test corrections for half points so even if you get a 50 on your test you can make it up to a 75. Lot's of online homework but nothing crazy hard just daily assignments. He cares a lot about his students and tries hard to make the class fun all while still teaching valuable materials. One of the best.
Really cool guy who kept class positive and made me feel like he cared.
He's a funny guy, but as a teacher has no idea what he is doing.
Skip is absolutely hilarious - a delightful professor and a really interestingrad person! He will definitely be missed when he retires.
I like Skip, he's a great teacher.  He's very deaf friendly and I liked the fact that he would put closed captioning on for them, that what makes him a great teacher.  Take him, it's really worth it.

Lecture was useless other than to hand in the essay which was due. I always paid attention and sat in the front row every class but I always walked out each day questioning if I actually learned anything. Essays can be hard, strict grader, final is ridiculously easy. I can't say I'd recommend him but he certainly is a cool dude, very Jeff Bridges.
Skip is the man, take him!  His essays are tough but very exciting to write!  Take him!!
Great man, horrible teacher.
English teacher as a Film Teacher?  What?? Take Carageorge istead.

He can be cool, but does not like those live action films, he only likes odd animation films which means that he will fail you on your live action.  Take other teachers for this particular class.  Don't bother.
skip is a nice guy, but he only talks about himself 24/7 and we get to write about our thoughts, but he judges too harshly. avoid him.
He is a horrible professor.  Doesn't agree with students' opinions.  Avoid taking him for Film Language, and take other classes with him.

He's a good professor! Very easygoing, fun, and extremely helpful. Likes to make students feel good about themselves and make more inspiring work. Would definitely recommend you to take him if you got the chance!

Skip is perhaps one of my favorite teachers ever. His class is easy because he gives you the freedom to experiment and do what you want. He always has positive comments about everything and helpful criticism. Plus, his STORIES ARE AMAZING. I mean, how often to you get hear about filming in the arctic with temperatures way below zero? Totally cool.
Skip is a god. He knows all there is to know about film.
Good class...you'll enjoy it and learn alot!
Bit of a nut but wants to see everyone do well. Likely to take you out for a beer after class
Skip is a fun Professor. A little wacky and usually a little tipsy...? Generally accepting of alot of different film/animation styles. A good professor and alot of fun in class!
Excellent teacher - very challenging. He has a lot of knowledge and glad I took the courses he offered. I enjoy the emails and am sorry that they have stopped.

Freshman need to quit rating Kleper. This man has shaped and reported more industry knowledge than most will ever understand. Ask him about his research sometime. Kleper isn't an easy-A, but he's among the most interesting people you'll meet in your lifetime.
Without a doubt in the top 3 worst classes and professors Ive had at RIT.

Terrible.  Words can't describe how wretched both the class and teacher were.  He cracked his stupid inside printing jokes.  Never helped to anyone who struggled.  On top of all this he spams people with useless printing news.

tests are INSANE, long, winded lectures, TONS of junkmail, but very approachable. if you have a hard time with him in class, approach him outside and talk to him--he wants students to do well, he's just out of touch with reality.
awful, awful man. boring lectures, trivial tests - sends massive amounts of junk email (im still receiving stuff from him)
No Comments

Professor Yang has great lectures, very engaging. Although much of the course material covered is a review from prior knowledge he makes the class fun. Attendance is a must for lectures and labs. Homework is 1 quick assignment weekly. Would absolutely recommend Professor Yang.

Yang is super helpful and actually cares about his reputation with students.  He was helpful when I needed it, extremely nice and charismatic, and was able to make such a cookie-cutter class enjoyable. He is the only professor I've ever had that sent out an email reflecting on his evals. It's been said before, but I'll say it again: He's the man.
Great and easy class. Show up and you pass.

Dr. Yang is really a good guy. He cares about all his students success and is willing to work with you no matter if you are a head or behind on the subject matter he makes sure you understand it. There were only 6 really easy hw assignments. Definitely reccomend

His class was incredibly easy, only 5 homework assignments. He cares greatly about his CE students and is a hard worker. I'm glad to have taken his class and getting to know our head of the department better.
He's very clear in presenting material and tries to make sure everyone is on track with the curriculum through both office hours and peer mentors. Overall, the class is fun and easy.

This class was both easy and fun. Dr. Yang presents information very clearly and, for what little time the department head has, he tries hard to make sure everyone is on track, even setting up peer mentors for students.
Helpful, gives you clear cut examples, easy to understand.

The class was very straightforward and Professor Yang did a decent job teaching things. He mainly puts things up on a projector and we took a few notes but other than that it was a simple class. I have to admit that I find his powerpoint presentations that he posts online more informative than his actual lectures.

He's extremely nice, and very helpful outside of class if you can find him. He was harder than the rest of the IDS professors, and sometimes didn't explain things very clearly, but just ask him to clarify and he will. Overall, you can't go wrong in IDS with Yang or Melton.

Caring professor. Usually avaliable and helpful. Tried his best to explain materials. Understood that students have other courseworks other than his class, deadlines were extended if reasonable request was made.

He's a good professor; tries to help his students any way he can.  The class can be hard but if you work hard and see him when you need help, he'll help you and make sure your grade reflects your effort and improvement.
Unbelievably good, I hate circuits, or at least I did until this class, Yang is the man.
Nice, good professor. Try his best to make students understand the materials. Always avaliable and helpful.
He's the man. Enough said.

Dr. Bondy made his class extremely easy and accessible. All tests and quizzes were open everything, so our class average was high since we could use our notes and look stuff up during tests. Even with that, I still learned Python very well from him. Nice guy as well.

This man is a terrible professor. The coding is not hard at all but oh my gosh he is so annoying. His grading schedule is perplexing at best having readings, labs, and projects start and end all on different days throughout the week. He'll posts labs on stuff he hasn't taught yet “because you guys are real clever” like what is the point of that???

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Professor Bondy is very kind and understanding of new programmers. His course has a very rigid structure and takes adjusting to but as long as you talk to him he is always happy to help. He is great at responding to his Slack messages, even on weekends the day before a project is due. Anything you need is in the syllabus and lecture was 1.5hrs max.

If you email him he will direct you to the slack or his old prerecorded videos. This course is available to NTID students but he posts the captions external from the videos. He will not respond to your slack messages and if he does it will be to watch his not very helpful videos and blame you for not paying more attention to them.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Lectures were fairly boring at times, and usually are unnecessarily long, but he always posts the slides on slack.  He is very clear about course expectations, and gives very helpful feedback on project deliverables. There are also ample opportunities for bonus credit. Very nice guy as well.

I don't think anybody liked Bondy. 3 hour classes consisted of incoherent rambling and tangents for an hour, and then the remaining time to complete the "labs", really basic programming projects done through google collab. If you know anything about coding you'll pass no problem, but you will learn absolutely nothing because Bondy cannot teach.

The first 90 minutes or so of each 3 hour period consisted of him lecturing, and the rest was used for lab work. However, the contents of the lectures had nothing to do with the labs.
