Dan is very engaging during class.  He did a terrific job of moving the discussion beyond the text and into the business world.
Good professor - take good notes - go to class - very staighforward.  Great depth of knowledge about the real world.  I would take another class with him.
Great teacher very knoweledgeful.  His test are easy if you read the book and ask questions in class.  He gives NO HOMEWORK OR QUIZES.  TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

he sucked. dont take him. he is incredibly impossibly hard, and his tests are impossible too. he teaches 10 secs every class and leaves, he has NO notes, he has NO handouts, the book he uses to teach is BAD....THE WORSE PROFESSOR EVER, DONT EVER TAKE HIM.
Very down to earth guy with quite a bit of knowledge.  I'd love to take another class with him :-)

This is the third class I have had with Alex, I really like how Alex lectures. This class has 3 Applied Problems that are group work, Exams and Applied Problems have extra credit opportunities. The homework problems come from the textbook, but Alex gives the homework problems, so a textbook isn't needed.

Made it through MOPS... Hardest class I've taken so far, and Steele's teaching style did not make it any easier. I couldn't pay attention through any full class. Notes are very hard to find on the website if you miss. Tests are challenging. Homeworks/projects are unforgiving. It's to be expected. For what it's meant to be, it's a great class.

He's very montoned so I did tend to dooze off a lot. Here's where everyone is wrong. He specifically said in the beginning of the semester that if u go the SSE (Society of Software Engineers) on the first floor, THERE ARE COPIES OF PREVIOUS YEAR'S TEST. Just go in and ask to look at it, Steele's exams are VERY VERY similar to previous years exams.
Would not recommend.

MOPs is notoriously hard and Steele's exams are tough (C class average on all three). I thought his lectures were actually pretty interesting, but they can feel a little disconnected from some of the assignments. Ask for help on tricky concepts, go to SI, and put in the time on assignments and you'll be alright. Learned a lot form this class.

A pretty standard professor - expect lots of live coding during lectures (might be a pro or con depending on your learning style). Typically very accessible outside of class during his office hours but be sure to show up with at least some pseudocode. The class wasn't easy but your grade will directly reflect your effort.

Professor Steele is a very notorious in the department. His tests are definitely the hardest out of all the other CS1 professors, but it's pretty doable to get a decent grade in this course if you put in the effort. He does expect people to come into the course with some coding knowledge, but I managed without any prior coding knowledge.

Writes lecture notes on the white board in a very unorganized fashion. His tests are significantly more difficult than other professors teaching this course. Is a very tough grader. Made a final project that required students to code material that was never covered in the course. If it wasn't for this professor my gpa would not be crushed.

I was originally not excited to have this class after seeing Steeles reviews on this app, but I like him more after getting to know him better in class. Its true that his lectures are very long and boring, and I had to rely on plenty of outside resources to figure out the material. But during labs and office hours Steele is very helpful and kind.

Probably the worst CS professor I have had so far. His tests are infamously difficult and he does not grade easy. Will curve, but even with a curve the class averages are laughable. Only perk was that he grades his exams fairly quickly, so you don't have to wait too long for your impending doom.
He's a really bad professor. Don't take him if you have the chance, but I sincerely wish you luck if you do have him.
He's just a bad professor. Fails to explain things clearly and shows attitude towards students. Also acts very entitled.
He's just a bad professor. No explanation is really needed.

To be honest he is not a good explainer. No one understood what he was talking about ever. The only way you will pass with Prof. Steele is if you have prior cs knowledge, if you are a newbie to cs as I was, do not take his cs141 or 242 class, there is a high chance you will fail, but not because of you, but the fact he cannot teach you.
He's notorious for having the hardest tests in the department, but I think you can truly do well if you try hard enough and spend time in the tutoring center to grasp the topics
He was a terrible professor, the class is boring and quiet. The assignments are graded harshly and is biased. The tests are tested on specific things and the class average for tests are around 60.

Exams are not reflective of the content, made difficult to be difficult (not allowed to ask clarifying questions on exams at all). Doesn't answer questions in class and is condescending when he answers. Would not recommend taking unless you want to learn mostly on your own or already know a bunch of C.
Doesn't accept anything late. Doesn't listen to students. Doesn't answer questions. Bad professor.
I liked his lectures, lots of live coding during class. Tests are really hard though and you have to know things to didn't spend much time talking about in class.

Overall I did fine in the class, but I didn't love his lectures, because it was a lot of live coding and he didn't always explain stuff well. His style of teaching requires prior knowledge before hand, especially for CS 141.

I wouldn't recommend Steele to anyone who doesn't have prior experience. His lectures consist of live coding in light mode while he talks in his grandpa voice. I mainly learned concepts from prior knowledge, SI, or recitation/lab. He takes pride in having the hardest tests in the CS department, so be wary of that. Really, he's just "meh".

Loves to live code, depends if you like that or not. I didn't, but it really does improve one's understanding of it. Exams are unreasonably hard compared to the rest of the department (read them carefully), but the final was a total breeze since the others were so difficult.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: He wasn't as bad as some people here are saying, but his lectures can be a bit tough to sit through. I think the main thing is that he doesn't really answer questions clearly, and you sometimes have to ask/clarify a few times before getting a half reasonable response. In saying that, if you know your stuff and study, you'll be fine.

His lectures are really boring and his tests are very hard then other professors. When you ask him a question he always replies with a question when asked a question instead of just giving you a straight answer.

This man, lemme tell ya, besides his boring lectures, he's constantly being super helpful in course discussion posts. This man answers homework questions like the riddler, you will ask a question because you're confused, and then you will walk away with 2, what was I trying to figure out, and what did Steele just say to me?

Professor Steele is probably the worst professor I have had and will ever have. Ignoring the most boring lectures and class content on the planet, for a notoriously difficult class Steele's "help" on homeworks out of class , which he readily gives, consists of him condescendingly not answering student's questions or telling them to read the notes.
Basically unhelpful in course discussions and inconsistent/tough grader.

Stopped learning how to code 30 years ago and it shows. Very tough grader. Took 6% off a project grade because I had one line of Java code longer than 100 characters. Exams cover useless material ("what is the Dutch word for semaphore?"). Not terrible, but avoid.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I've had Professor Steele before in my first CSCI class, and I found myself having the same feelings as that class; it was very hard to pay attention. I found myself stuck, full of questions, and super stressed out to the point where I dropped the class entirely, and I'm hoping that next semester goes better with a different professor.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: is not very helpful in office hours and has long boring lectures. would not recommend.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Not a good teacher, his lectures consist of reading slides and live coding. His slides are not that helpful. Not very helpful outside of class; I met with him in person, he either talked over me or made me repeat myself. Also emails, his only response "refer to the notes/website" and that's if I get a response.
Was willing to help outside of class, but wouldn't let you talk and would talk over you.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Not a great teacher and very difficult tests. His lectures are boring and he doesn't give the best explanations.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: I went into this course scared based off of all the other reviews here, but Steele was not that bad. He live codes a lot, which helps if you pay attention. For the majority of class he reads off of the lecture notes in the Comp Sci website. Exams are tricky. I had 100's in homework and labs but the tests I struggled with. Know how to code before CS

Very boring lectures. Makes random but subtle jokes during his lessons and tends two chuckle to himself while at most two students give somewhat of a laugh. I often find myself falling asleep every class. He's also not great at explaining things. When doing his "live coding," he often just types code without giving an explanation.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Awful professor, he has no idea how to explain or do 90% or what the course covers and it shows in his grading. Often made mistakes in grading which brought down the entire class average. Avoid at all costs!

super weird exams that contain questions on the most irrelevant information (although for the final and the second mid term of this class (copads) he allowed computer use, so they were easy). very tough grading on project, takes many points off if you have one line wrong which causes the program to fail some invisible tests. boring lectures

Steele's lectures are long and boring. His is not helpful in explaining project, and his exams are unreasonable and based on useless information he may have mentioned passingly during a long lecture. If you can avoid, avoid him!
Possibly one of the the worst professors in the computer science department. Criteria is vague and he often rambles during class. Definitely avoid him, if you can take Prof. Purtee.
Very good CS professor. Explores topics in depth so you really understand the fundamentals. If you aren't getting it, his office hours are easily accessible on his site.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: 41% Dropout rate last semester. How he goes home and thinks he's a good professor, i'll never know. Good luck.

His lectures will take the full 2 hours, often for no reason. You will often be interrupted by him if you try to answer his questions. I had previous coding experience and this class was just fine because I didn't pay attention in lectures and instead did the homework, and he didn't care. Recommend if you have prior experience.
just don't do it

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: I had him for 141. He's pretty solid but the class is pretty hard. Definitely make sure to study a lot, it's a hard class and the tests are a challenge. Overall a lot of fun, but the class material is rough.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: All of the other ComSci 1 students with other teachers had great grades, but in his class, 30% of his students were failing when I dropped the course.

Prof Steele's lectures are boring and rarely even provide the important information that you need on homework assignments and tests. He shows his code examples with little explanation and often tests impractical things that no one needs to know. His lectures are very unorganized, and most of the information he provides is unspecific and not helpful

Excellent experience taking Mechanics with Prof Steele. Exams are tougher than other professors, but you learn a lot more in his section. Very friendly, go and talk to him if you need help. He will help you out!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: I fall asleep almost every lecture and he sees it. Still super helpful and patient with me in office hours and I get an easy A on the homeworks and projects. Pay attention in every class or religiously peruse the code he posts ( or both ) and you will have no problem with his tests. Textbook is helpful but not necessary.
One of the best professors in the CS department. Easy tests. Easy assignments (although time consuming). Overall, if you put in the work, this class is an easy A.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. He teaches the class but gives out homework that he expects you to do without even teaching what was in the homework. He expects you to understand basic coding when he does a poor job of even teaching it. Will not be taking another class with him.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Lectures are rather monotonous and two hours is a challenge (try staying awake). However, he knows exactly what he is teaching. Very approachable outside class. Challenging tests.

Steele is a great professor. He knows his stuff and is always willing to answer questions. However, Mechanics of Programming with him was quite difficult. Two things you need to do if you want an A: Read the book outside of class, it'll help you understand everything better for exams. Finally, start your assignments early, especially projects!

Nice dude. He admits that his tests are some of the most difficult of the CS1 professors, but it's CS1 so they're still not terrible. He's usually willing to answer your questions and makes his lectures somewhat engaging. He knows his stuff and makes an effort to be friendly with his students.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: A very nice professor, although the lectures are a bore

Steele is a great professor. He knows that material, and doesn't just read off the powerpoint like other professors do. His lectures are pretty dry, but he is glad to help you during his office hours. One of the better CS professors.

Long, long lectures. Very monotonous  speaker, and cracks really bad jokes, which is always followed by an awkward silence. Lectures are kind of unorganized, and he can put you to sleep if you sit in the back. I've never passed out in a class more than I have in Steele's CS2
no.
If you don't ask questions, you won't get more from him, but he is happy to explain in further detail. Assignments can be tough, but he's not the only one making them.

Ben was an alright teacher. His lectures were long and often didn't make sense. It was almost as if he didn't have a plan for his lecture, they were erratic and all over the place. The tests are alright, and he often mocks students in class. But, one on one he can be helpful. Make sure you attend recitation, I learned more there than in lecture.

He is a very good teacher. Other than the two-hour lectures, which start to get boring entering the second hour, he is good at making the new topic engaging. He was very clear with his explanations and wanted us to learn. His tests are a little tough, but he has clear grading criteria. He made my introduction to computer science great.

This class was very interesting yet also difficult. The projects were bad, at least for me. I just found them uninteresting and impractical, not to mention difficult. Steele's tests were also a mixed bag.  He gets the point across, but his lectures do drag on and can be boring. Take Steely if you're ready to put in the work and seek out help!

Prof.  Steele is confusing in lectures because he uses lots of general statements, pronouns, and "aha!"s that make it hard to follow what he is talking about or what he is referring to. The transition from Python to Java was rough because of the above, as well as his use of very technical vocabulary that he must expect students to know. helpful@lab
Great for visual learners (plenty of diagrams and explanations are concise).  One on one sessions are extremely helpful.  Tough but you will learn.
Wasn't super clear on a lot of material, but I attest this more to the Computer Science curriculum. Awesome guy and decent teacher, would take again.

I don't really know what to say. I had an overall very positive experience. The only issues I had are with how the course is run from an administrative standpoint. The labs can be tough, and can be graded badly, but this is not Steele's fault. His tests are also VERY fair.

He seems like he knows his topic reasonably well but uses confusing examples.  His lectures aren't very straightforward and I always felt pretty confused.  Learned most of the class on my own by working on assignments.  Nice guy but makes odd jokes.

Steele was a very good professor for CS1 and had very fair tests and grading. His lectures may have been a tad boring at times but he taught everything very well and encouraged people to ask questions when needed. He also knew most of the names of people in his classes and commonly called on people by name which was a nice touch for a college class

One of the "awesome" professors to have for the introductory CS courses. He is definitely a harder professor, but I think we all definitely learned more thanks to it. He clearly wants the students to learn, but he doesn't want to just give the students A's, you have to work for it, but its definitely manageable.

A generally good teacher. He's knowledgeable and interacts with the class, and helps you if you need it. The lectures are often dry and do not always prepare for the assignments, but you cover material. Overall a positive experience.

Barely explains basics, and expects you to learn everything else yourself. Wastes lab time going over problem solving, no matter how you write your code you're wrong. Hw is ten times harder than lab. Dodges questions and is a stingy grader. If you don't pay attention in lecture you will be completely lost. Avoid him, I couldn't.

Awful teacher. Very condescending, openly mocked some students. Not clear and not very helpful when it came to help. Highly recommend you seek out SI tutoring. He's a very "My way or the highway" type guy and doesn't have any leniency. At all.

People are polarized on Steele. Lots dropped. I think they just can't handle the labs, which are hard, but great, valuable mind exercises. The lectures are fine, helpful and usually pretty upbeat. However: His tests are ridiculously hard and test on things that were never discussed. Make up for that in the labs and their bonus problems.

Had him for OS. Seems like knows his stuff, and in nice to talk to in person. But very hard to understand what he was talking about, and he just taught off slides. Grading was overly harsh and inconsistent. Projects sometimes didn't relate to the class, and other times were way too difficult for what we were learning. Avoid if possible.
Excellent professor. Friendly and knowledgeable. Can seem strict and dry, but gets the point across and teaches well.
You need to ask questions to do well in his class and be as clear as possible when you do. Get involved in the class and you'll be fine.
Pretty good really. Friendly guy, nice to talk to. Could be more clear in lectures. Tests are fairly difficult but reasonable. Projects interesting but inconsistently documented.
I too would have to say avoid him.

Ben Steele is a terrible teacher. Although he may know a lot he is incapable of communicating it well. He never has time to help out students and his draconian grading policies and refusal to allow test retakes or postponements don't help either. If you're looking for a real understanding of the course material, don't choose Ben Steele.

Very boring and hard to follow in class. His labs are very confusing and its hard to understand what needs to be done at first. Goes around answers asked in class, or doesnt explain them clearly. Least favorite teacher this quarter, would recommend avoiding if possible.
Sometimes difficult to follow in lectures, but he's good if you can get him one-on-one.
HE is an ok teacher. The first few weeks of the class is easy but then when it gets more difficult he can not answer questions. He goes around your question. Not a very good teacher
He's an okay guy, the labs are fairly easy and so are the projects. Be warned though, the exams are notoriously difficult in how they are graded, usually tipping on something trivial.

Although Steele did an okay job, he sometimes omitted some key component of the lesson.  He was poor at answering questions, often proceeding after providing only a very brief attempt at clarification and without regard to whether or not an understanding had been established.  He knows the material; the problem arises in his attempt to convey it.

Computer Science One in python is very easy, period. However, I got a B in the course. Why? Quite simply put, Steele's exams are notorious for asking things that were never taught. Not to mention the man is unable to properly answer questions and will only insult students or tell them to go through pseudo-code again. Nunes- Harwitt is better!

Not bad at all. If you want a good grade, sit towards the front and be invovled: especially during Problem Solving. He really knows his material, although he's not too good with design patterns (most CS professors are not though). Nice guy. Speaks loud and clear. Quick grader.

Definetly the worst professor I have ever had. When you ask him a question he goes on answering something you rly didn't care about and then leaves you with nothing. He grades really hard and is a prick about design. He won't tell you how he wants your design and then takes more points than something is worth away because you didn't do it his way.
His lectures are extremely boring and put you to sleep rather than teach. When you ask a question, he gives an answer to something you weren't looking for. Grading is okay at times.
Pretty easy teacher. He uses student graders and they can sometimes be tough. But he is an easy grader for exams. Not the best professor but good enough for the subject material.

Absolutely horrible professor.  He gave me a -4 out of 10 on design and felt it was justified.  He knows very little about the material and demonstrates that in his lectures.  Avoid if possible, and if not possible, switch your major.

I had Steele for both CS4 lecture and lab. His lectures are OK if a bit boring, and his grading is fair. But it was in lab and one-on-one that he was very helpful; he was very knowledgeable about the tools we were using and willing to help.

He's a nice guy, didn't always know answers to questions asked in class but was more then willing to find out the answers.  Easy grader, I got a B with out having to try to hard and he's was always willing to work with people.

This professor is pretty helpful and an easy-grader. His tests are not that hard, if you study all the slides, you will get a high grade. Always gives an extra credit assignment, so that students can get some higher grades. I would definitely recommend this guy.

He's an alright teacher, nothing special; although he does tend to trail off on very trivial questions during lecture. Homework is hard considering there is no actual solution that he says he wants. There probably are better CS teachers.

Nothing really special about this professor. Was consistently nearly late for class and always rushed off after class. Handled questions asked by the class often incompletely. Not a very good professor.
Pretty good professor. Explained things clearly and was there when you needed help. The course material itself was easy, so you should have no problems getting a B, if not an A.

He claims to have some industry experience, but it doesn't show. He has little knowledge of the material. When asked some straightforward questions in class, he did not know, but he'd have to try it to see what would happen. He has great trouble keeping the class quiet and respectful. Also, the textbook was useless. Nice guy, but I'll avoid him.
Expects you to teach yourself, but he doesn't mention that.

By far the most aggravating professor I've ever had. Tests were more difficult than those of other professors teaching the same class. Asked questions about things he glazed over in lecture. Did a very poor job of explaining the material. Very strict grader, especially if you have him for lab. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Decently easy. Has a very monotone voice and you'll probably learn more from the textbook and labs than from him. He's nice and easy though. Random homework assignments throughout the quarter. Tests aren't too hard and neither is his grading style. Recommended.
Not a bad professor, if you took CS in HS he is a good professor to take just to get through it again.  No out of class assignments to speak of.  Fairly easy grader.  Easy to talk to.

He knows the class materials well, but don't care of anyone learn from his class. You better read and know the the materials before going to his class or else you will be totally lost. He doesn't explain anything in details so you need to learn that ur self. You will most likely fail his class, do avoid him if possible.

He gives a lot of handouts which are really useful, but does not spend enough time explaining them, your on your own for a good amount time.  You can go see him, it would help but not enough.  His tests are hard, I recommend going to the TAs for help.  Try not to get this guy.

He is a fool of a professor. He doesn't explain concepts well nor does he really effectivly go over coding. Avoid this teacher if you value your major and your grade are important to you. Half of my class failed the first test everyone else got C's and D's then a quarter didn't finish the second test and he didn't care...

He was an okay teacher, but nothing spectacular.  He seemed fair in his grading, and the material he covered was adequate in comparison to what the department expects you to know by the end of the course.
Great teacher.  He really knows what he's talking about and is very easy to approach.

He make my life so miserable that I decided to change my major. This was 20041. Very strict on grading the lab, especially commenting.  he cut you no break watsoever.   I personally would avoid him.
He is one of the best CS teachers I have ever had in my life.  He explains everything and has no problems answering questions.  Highly recommended.
Very nice and very helpful, but I don't think I could recommend him. Most classes lasted only an hour and some were canceled. It's hard to say I got my money's worth. RIT isn't cheap.
Lectures and slides get confusing, hard to follow his train of thought in class. Cool guy but just starting off, knows his stuff but is still learning how to teach.
He doesn't give good feedback and wanted us to make a scale model of his design. I am not at design school to copy your work lol.
Class definitely helped me learn a lot. Projects felt slightly random but that could also be me. As long as you show up and do your work, you will be okay.

Seems like a great designer, just not a great teacher. Has a hard time separating opinion from academics, and it results in some serious conflicts on projects. Has some enjoyable project concepts but they're often overshadowed by the struggle you have to undergo just to get decent grades in the class. Just barely not worth the headache for me.

Scully is literally the worst. He grades everything based on how he likes you or your project. Don't know how I got such a low grade. One of the projects is to submit something to a contest and this classmate won it and he still got a low grade in the class (he was POC). Overall horrible feedback(and he advised me to basically redo a whole project)
Difficult to get feedback from. Scully is not an industrial designer so I'm not sure why he is teaching ID classes. Foundations classes? Sure. ID studios? Please look elsewhere.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Scully is a great professor. I wish I worked harder in his class because its really worth the effort. He has a lot of knowledge to give you, and while sometimes it sounds like hes talking artsy mumbo jumbo, he really knows what hes doing.

Amos tries to keep his projects new and interesting. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. I like his honest approach and, for the most part, the integration of design within the projects. The course isn't easy, but it's not terribly hard either. You definitely have to work for stuff, and you'll probably be in the shop to do so.
I'm so disappointed that he is teaching students in RIT. He is a nice guy but he makes this easy class difficult...

Scully is a great choice for Sophomore Studio, but not for everyone. Scully leaves projects vague and open to interpretation to allow for your own creative expression. If you're motivated to do well, and not interested in becoming a generic 'cookie-cutter' RIT design student, take him!

This man is so nice. He will take the time to work with any student, even students that struggle with the class because they hate it. He may bluntly tell you that your piece sucks, but he will give you the opportunity to make a new one and it won't effect your grade as much. He's really cool to talk to as well and he knows what he's talking about.

Scully is a nice person, but he is also the worst teacher I took in my life. He makes this easy course very hard. And I cannot understand his thinking. I just learned how to make plaster and wood, but I did not learn any design things from him. I will never take his class anymore.

Scully is more or less the worst professor I could ever imagine for a foundations class. I can't state one thing I learned. Scully made a fairly easy class difficult with poor teaching. It was a challenge to figure out what the guy wants you to do. Whatever printed guidelines were available were rarely considered. Do not take a course with him.

Scully is very specific about what he is looking for, and it is rare that anyone is able to satisfy him. Instructions are often vague. Not an easy grader, don't expect to just scrape by in this class. A lot of work, and you usually don't get to feel positive about it.

Scully is literally the WORST foundations teacher I've had this semester. I CANNOT stand his personality or his teaching methods. He's super specific about what he wants, but if you give him what he wants he doesn't like it. If you take risks he doesn't like it. If you do anything good, it's not good enough. I wouldn't wish him on my enemies.

While a nice man and decent teacher, I personally couldn't keep up due to lack of explanation. His assignments aren't clear, I don't think he knows what he's asking for until a lucky student accidentally stumbles upon it. This problem with this class is a clarity issue.  As a person, he is funny and super nice, willing to talk, he does his best!

People who hate him don't get design form & are bitter because,unlike most teachers he will give out Cs and Ds to those who deserve them.You can resubmit after crit.People think the class is a waste but the basics being taught are useful. People that think they are already too good for him & the class in their 2nd year need to get over themselves.

To simply put it, he's an idiot. Nice, sometimes, but overall an idiot. Just avoid his class if you can. I usually never write reviews because I don't find them necessary, there's no reason to explain myself because it'll take too long. The fact of the matter is that some will like him and some won't. If you're someone with amazing crafting technique you're going to waste your time no matter what. Find someone who's more challenging for you. Read a book & forget about Form class altogether.

Amos has issues with students if they can't and don't read his mind.  What he finds attractive in form is not what everyone likes but if it isn't his way then you won't get a good grade.  Very limited teacher, he is best to AVOID AT ALL COSTS.  He shouldn't be working at RIT.  He gives teachers there a bad name with his lazy attitude.

Great teacher. If you are cut out for design you will understand his assignments clearly. If you are lazy then don't take his class because you wont appreciate him like the people do who want to learn and progress. I have learned tons from his in the two quarters that I had him. Teaches design like it should be taught. Great 3D teacher.

Excellent tacher. I have learned more from him in 2 quarters than I thought imaginable. He really gets to the heart of design. He is a great professor. I would recommend to anybody who loves design and actually wants to learn. Not too much homework. A well balanced foundation course.

not an easy grader. wants perfection. wants things to be completely off the deep end. unclear. has favorites. enjoyable guy. projects very structured- don't give much leeway. you don't do what he wants you dont get a good grade. Craft important- u paint everything you make. take carson or bell. u'll learn more.
He is a really fun, nice teacher. Sometimes he gives very difficult assignments with not enough time to do them, but he is pretty lenient about redoing projects, and he is an easy grader.
Scully is an enthusiastic professor who is dedicated to his class. Tends to pick some favorites, but generally fair to all. By the end, you will be sick of trash and mechanical fasteners.

He's a nice guy just not too great of a teacher. He is too vague with his assignments and although he may try to explain it to you it just doesn't ever come across clearly as to what he wants. He's an unfair grader and will judge you the entire semester on how he perceives you after the 1st project. If you have an option don't take him as a teacher

Scully is tough and at first, as a freshman, he will drive you nuts. I didn't like Scully.  His assignments were vague and I had difficulty first knowing what he expected, and second providing it. I was unaware lines had emotions. :/  He was kinda skeletal, BTW, Hot if you like dysplasia.
Best professor any 1st yr will have, ever. Well in 3D any way.
Great. Great. Great.
Great guy.  His lack of clarity is meant to provide room for creativity.  There are no clear cut answers in art, I can't believe that other students didn't appriciate that.
awesome professor! wants you to do well while pursuing topics that interest you. his class requires a lot of effort and it gets easier to understand what he wants as time goes by.
scully is a nice guy but doesnt explain what he wants. i dont think his criteques are fair. he gets better as the class goes on. but he is a little biased when grading. unfair grader.
No Comments
Nice guy, however he can't explain anything that he wants.  The critiques are a joke in that class because you don't get any useful information fedback to you.
Scully is an awesome guy, but the class is insanely hard to figure out.  You rarely know what you're doing, and even though he's willing to help you, he's so abstract, it almost doesn't matter :P

Really engaging, dedicated professor. Loves iguanas. Very open to students coming to his office with questions and concerns. Makes powerpoints available online and provides test questions ahead of time. Tests are based on concept application and are all multiple choice.
loves iguanas
Amazing teacher, loves iguanas, gorgeous man, great with pre-vet students, very into biology, very beautiful

Dr.Buckley is mostly a good teacher.  Although his tests are not related to his lectures, he does give you the questions ahead of time.  Also, your always behind on lectures, because he gets overly excited about certain topics, but its not necessarily a bad thing. Overall its an easy B!

he takes points off just to take points off. he is looking for a single memorized answer on exams and it is one he said, your answer may be correct or in the book but if it's not what he said won't get credit. he warns students not to debate over points, however, so seems to be getting away with this.
If your going to take evolutionary biology with him, be prepared to memorize the chapters of the book word for word in major detail. Worst class ever, i learned nothing, all memorization.
He's friendly and he loves iguanas. What more could you hope for out of an evolutionary biology professor?
Has an intense biological background, he's like a BioWikipedia. Awesome, amazing professor.

Pretty good teacher in that he conveys his information well. Is constantly late to class (up to 10+ mins) and takes forever to grade tests bc "he has a life on the weekend" which I found a bit rude. Lets stupid 2nd years ask way too many dumb questions and lets them detract from the lecture material so we are 2 or 3 weeks behind. Overall ok teacher
An absolutely amazing teacher and advisor. He gives you as much respect as you give him, and it was easy to find interest in his class because he is fascinated with it and it shows in his lecutes.

Dr. Buckley is an excellent teacher.  He presents the material clearly, makes his good powerpoint notes available online, always makes himself available outside of class, is enthusiastic about what he teaches, and is just a really nice guy.  I highly recommend that you take a course from him if you get the chance.  He is pretty entertaining too :)
Such a nice guy and pretty good teacher. Get's very into what he's talking about. Only grades depend on very long essay tests and one big lab project.

Very nice!
Class is not as boring as other bio classes.  He really cares about teaching.
Very weak in accounting concepts. She does not know how to lecture. reads from the slides. below the MBA level

She is a really fair professor. Get ready for a lot of reading though. She gives quiz at the start of each class that can only help you, it really helps to read.   Also, prepare to want to take her shopping and help her wardrobe!

She is always there to help you. Tests and assignments are fair. Clear grading criteria. She has good grip on accounting. Reading the chapter before class will help you a lot. Gives opportunity quizzes for bonus.
Shares work experience and insights.  Extremely helpful and available.  Test are fair - focus on material and class lectures.

Very poor level professor. She looks like if she discovers the slides in class and never share her experience. Except once when she advised students to copy last year's auditing workpapers if they work in an auditing firm! Totally off the hook... Not the level of RIT. I suspect the first comment is from her... Very low I said...
Class is easy IF you read material and prepare for quizzes. Very available and inspirational person. She has experience and shares it well including ethical standards.
Hard to follow along. Teaches like the student already knows what is going on and the entire course just feels like review for a previous class you haven't taken.
Lectures were not the most helpful and cut short. Relies on TA's to do a lot of the teaching. Explains topics well though and is very accessible outside of class. Would take again.

Leipold was trying a new "eduScrum" style of teaching this semester and it was very disorganized. It was unclear what was being graded and due when. There was no clear schedule for the semester. She tended to ramble a bit in lectures. This could be a good class if it were organized. Knows a lot of CAD and is helpful if you ask the right questions.

Professor Leipold is a solid teacher. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about CAD and she is pretty funny if you can muster a laugh at 8 am. It definitely helps to know some CAD going into the class, but it is not necessary, and she + the TAs make help very accessible.

Overall, Professor Leipold is good. Sometimes her lectures were a little dry, but her grading criteria was clear and she was accessible outside of class for questions. The CAD work itself is very easy if you have experience with CAD, and even if you're new, Prof Leipold and the TAs are very knowledgeable and willing to help.

Prof. Leipold was great for the CAD portion of MECE 104. She is obviously very passionate about CAD, and covers a lot of content thoroughly and well through the semester. As someone with no CAD experience coming in, her lectures made each week's homework pretty easy to understand and complete.
Very flexible.  Very open to feedback.  You can tell she is passionate about teaching and really cares about her students.
She wants to see you succeed. She makes sure her TA's are available inside and outside of class for help. The one lab and one homework assignment a week were not bad if you take the time to do it.
Easy class. Professor is satisfactory for what the class is. Gets excited about the subject matter which is always nice to see.
Lectures weren't boring, work was straightforward.

Professor Leipold is a decent professor.. Theres not inherently anything bad about her and theres no real red flags that would make you want to stay away but theres not too much going for her either that would make you really want to have her as a professor. She's quiet and makes mistakes often though shes willing to help.

I don't understand why she has so many negative RMP reviews.

TBH, she is not the best professor but she is your only choice if your taking 104 during fall semester. She tends to be very tough towards some issues and can be unreasonable. I strongly do not recommend her to anyone.

I had Kate Leipold for CAD but I already have a lot of 3d modeling experience so the class was pretty easy. It seemed like she gave good feedback to those who needed. Sometimes the homework expectations were unclear but for the most part it was clear what was needed.

comment: Her lectures were kind of dry but she got the information across and she was helpful during office hours. MATLAB projects were annoying though.

Engineering Measurements Lab was pretty easy. Just make sure to attend the labs AND lectures because professor knows when you're only going to one or the other and the lectures are actually super helpful to set up labs later in the week. Fair grader, friendly, easy A.
Professor Leipold is great! Statics itself was a real hard course, and she definetly helps! She isn't the best at helping with coding though.
Meh, she's alright

I took statics with her and I absolutely love her! It was a very difficult subject to study, however, she was always always always willing to go over it again, she is great in office hours and in class. Very clear, very helpful, would take again in a heartbeat.

There isn't a lot to say about her for Measurements Lab. The lecture is only 1 hour once a week and you pretty much just get the theory and criteria for the lab. Sometimes at the end of the lecture it seems she has no material left and tries to share tips about the lab or excel, which can be either useful or boring if you already know them.

Not a lot to say. Had her for engineering measurements lab. Class was pretty simple as a whole. She is typically your only option for lecture professor. I had her for lab as well and it was nice to have the same professor for both. Occasionally unclear with what she wants in an assignment. Frequently available for extra help on prelabs.

She does know a lot about Creo it seems, but she is impossible to follow along with from the combination of her fast pace and insufficient, unclear explanations. In general, she has a huge attitude and is hard to approach. She is hit or miss with being helpful or having an attitude when you ask her questions.

It's very difficult to follow along in Creo when she teaches because she goes very quickly and doesn't stop. I found myself ignoring her and following the identical instructions on PTCU.  She is helpful when you get a chance to ask questions. Grades very strictly and you lose points for just having a different default orientation even if it works.

Kind of spacey in lectures and is prone to more than simple mistakes in lectures. Does nothing but sample problems which sounds nice but becomes a problem when she doesn't take the time to explain the fundamental concepts behind the problems she is doing. She's pretty nice though.

She is not a professor I would recommend to anyone. She always seems to be unsure of what she is doing. Gives impossible questions on the test and thinks she has prepared you well for the test but apparently she has not.

She tries to prepare you for tests with harder HW problems and in class problems only to give you impossible test questions that you're not prepared for. She's nice enough but she mumbles in class a lot and stumbles on her words.  She's the best in her office hours and tries to help in any way she can but not the best in the classroom.

Goes through a lot of the material quickly and it can be hard to keep up in class if you didn't do the preparations before class. When she's there she's pretty helpful but when her kid gets sick (which is often) she won't be available.
Good professor, helpful if you try to seem interested in the topic. Has a comprehensive knowledge base of the topics she teaches after the first time teaching the course. Has a cute kid.

She teaches by going really fast through slides. When we're supposed to work along in Creo, she goes really fast so it's impossible to keep up if you don't have previous CAD experience. She is a nice person though (but a really tough grader).

I had her for both Materials Processing and Engineering Design Graphic. For Materials Processing we did not use the textbook other than reading and it was really too easy. EDG on the other hand was tough. It is her area, she is a stickler for details and will take off points to make sure that you complete your drawings and assemblies correctly.

She is very picky about how you create the part in creo. You have to do it exactly as she wants or you lose points, even if the part is correct and fully functional. She will help you and occasionally gives in-class time to do projects otherwise to be completed outside of class.
She's very boring.She tries to make it interesting but I cant help but fall asleep. She's not very clear and doesn't seem to know the material well. She speeds through all the slides.
The most demanding professor ive ever met ... nice in person, but his policies are terrible. Made me stop taking french courses.

Very bad with deadlines.
Very bad with online course organization.
Will tank your grade for factors outside your control.

I didn't love MLFR410 because there wasn't a lot of opportunity to speak to native speakers and get feedback, so I felt like I was speaking a lot but not improving very much. However, M. Le Blévec is exceedingly kind and communicative, and a pretty easy grader, too. He breaks up writing deadlines to keep us on track and he is very understanding.

Monsieur Le Blévec is super kind and caring and willing to get to know you. In 410 you have several meetings with him and he was always supportive of my learning and ideas. He comes to French club occasionally and anytime I see him on campus we chat. He's very understanding as long as it's communicated by email and he responds within the hour.

Great and funny guy

comment: Kevin has been the best French professor so far (I have taken French for a long time). His class is very fun and interactive. Youll definitely learn a lot of French with him as he is extremely helpful and shows you how to improve daily. I wish I could take more classes with him.
A great french teacher! Rather than lecturing, he prefers leading group discussion and giving projects that help us learn French better than just lectures would. He's also a really funny guy.

Kevin is a really cool guy! His lectures are concise and I loved how he integrated lots of his personal experiences. It's really cool to learn about French culture from a French person. The homework is easy and doesn't take much time. The tests are fair.

AWESOME professor!  Really cool dude who you can talk to very easily.  He's super helpful and is rad about meeting you if you have questionswant to review.  He also played music videos a few times in class (Stromae) to stay relevant and make students interested.

He is an awesome teacher.  By far the most interesting and frequently talks about his life and differences between France and the USA.  He gets off topic a lot but teaches very well. Homework every night and tests can be tricky but I would recommend him to everyone and I will continue to take classes with him.  He  makes the class very fun.

Simply put, this dude is the best. His tests are definitely tough, but the homeworks are literally guaranteed 100s. He's also a ton of fun and shares some pretty great stories about his personal life (he grew up in France)! Great guy, loved the class.
Would probably be a better teacher without the textbook.
Extra

Prof. Daly is an amazing teacher that cares about his students.  His work is difficult and he definitely does not give out A's but if you do his "advanced deliverables" and follow the rubric it doesn't matter how "good" of a writer you are, he will give you a good grade.

As long as u follow the criteria, which are very clear, and turn in your assignments on time, you will receive an A. I got an A- because I messed up on my first assignment and didn't follow instruction. Highly recommend his class.
Pretty simple class. Hard to do bad in his class unless you don't do the work.
Makes the class super fun and engaging, gives opportunity for those to form an identity with writing. Gives a good amount of work, but they aren't hard assignments, and most are for extra credit.

Readings are regular but never busy work, and Professor Daly posts the course outline on day 1. This class changed how I viewed the writing process and what it means to be a writer. Best writing class I've ever taken, and if he taught other writing classes I would take them in a heartbeat.

All of Professor Daly's lectures were detailed in his syllabus, including all turn-in dates, extra credit dates, and all required readings. Professor gives plenty of heads-up about changes to class plans as well as plenty of helpful feedback about how to improve writing skills, despite the class being completion-based. Very approachable as well!

comment: Great guy. Only 3 grades in the entire course, but if you do not do a paper every 2 days or so, this will detract from the grade on the next paper. This was a writing class, so naturally, there was a lot of reading and writing. I considered myself to be a good writer to begin with, but I saw a clear improvement in this class. Daley is very nice, and accommodating if need be, and he has a sense of humor.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']
comment: Professor was a really nice guy, but seems not to understand that this is a mandatory course for all first years unless they have outside credit. Much more work than other courses, even comparing against difficult courses relevant for my major. Papers are based on very vague things and was often left confused what I even needed to do for the class.

Prof. Daly is easily on of my fav professors I've had this semester. He's a really great teacher and all the class instructions and assignments are very clear. Some of the readings are a bit long, but we dont have readings about 2/3 of the time for class - and when we do they are almost always required sources for our papers.
Really cool teacher and cares about students. He was flexible with homework assignments and was not a tough grader. Definitely recommend taking a class with Professor Daly.

Professor Daly is an extremely nice professor, the writing assignments are broken down into parts that are due over several weeks. There are 3 papers throughout the entire course, the reading can be difficult to understand but he will help you if you're confused, you have to do extra credit to get an A but if you do the work, you WILL get an A.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: very nice professor. work load isn't too much. class is structured for you to succeed!

Amazing guy! Definitely take this class. I was so worried about first year writing but prof Daly made it enjoyable. You will have to put some work in but in my opinion this is one of the best first year writing classes you can take. You will not regret taking this professor at all. Great guy and great professor

Professor Daly is light-hearted and has a good sense of humor, however, his class is the complete opposite. The workload is way too immense at the beginning of the semester and puts too much strain on freshmen. Professor Daly is just fine. He gives way too much work at the beginning of the semester but he calms down just a little later on. I can't say he didn't make me a better writer, but I don't know if it was worth it. It was definitely too much work for a gen-ed and the attendance requirements are ridiculous. He is bad at jokes but he's a nice guy.

Professor Daly this semester really helped me become a better writer. He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. The class is based around 3 essays, which if you do all the weekly assignments and show up to class, it isn't hard to get a good grade. If you do this you will get an A in this class.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'So many papers', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Gives a ton of work for a gen ed and has required attendance. In the beginning of the semester he says you should spend about 6 hours weekly on the class, but you will do much more. You're only really graded on 3 papers so if you mess up once then you will not do well.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Prof. Daly is a great person. He is funny, but his lectures are difficult to understand, and the amount of work that is required for a gen ed course is absurd. This teacher is a caring individual who focuses a lot on making sure the students feel happy and comfortable. The class is heavy in papers and checkpoints. As long as you keep up, it shouldn't be too bad. The classes are very relaxed and conversational.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'So many papers']
comment: Professor Daly is a very nice, easygoing person, but his class is extremely work heavy. There are 3 main essays with checkpoints that are not actually weighted into your grade. tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Professor Daly is a great teacher. In many of the reviews here on this site people complain about the amount of work. Every assignment besides the final draft is graded for completion (Yes, that is a 100 for every assignment). He wants you to learn, and his feedback is awesome. I recommend this class, I suck at writing and he made it fun. Do it

His vagueness and little effort to provide clarity on his assignments are only compounded by the fact he made up an "off the books" mandatory class date/zoom. Incredibly work heavy and demanding, more so than the other engineering classes I'm enrolled in. His classes are a bore and he's a little less than eccentric.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Professor Daly gave a lot of work. If you struggle with long readings, do not take this class. I struggled understanding assignments, but ended up with a great great anyways. As a first year course, it's rigorous and sometimes unclear. He's a nice guy, but too many assignments due every other day. Calls on you randomly during class.

Made my freshmen year a living hell with all the constant essays due every two days. Very tough class would not take again. Not a fun experience.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read']
comment: There was a lot of work for this class. I often found myself very bored with the readings. My writing did get better though. Nice guy, just didn't like the class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: From the first class Professor Daly might seem tough and academic, but I would say that as the semester progressed, I have grown to really like Professor Daly and all his quirks. He assigns tons of work - but, I guarantee that if you fully immerse yourself in the class, you will see a huge improvement in your writing. Trust the process on this one.

Amazing professor and human being. So funny! Gave me so much confidence in my writing and helped me submit my FYW paper for an award and I won some money! Gives good feedback, but you do have to work for your grade. Try to read everything you can and come to class whenever possible, but working on your writing is more important than attendance. GL!

Professor Daly has a somewhat playful attitude, cracking jokes once and a while in class and keeping some running jokes. In a class of 19, he was able to give me much more personalized feedback and opportunities to meet outside of class. While the three major essays were difficult, I saw their value in preparing me for the next 5 years.
Animotion was a great wellness class, both her and Kevin Bauer did a great job leading it. Wish they offered a bit more advice on the figure-drawing portion of it.

MJ is awesome! I had her for principles of animation and you can tell she really cares about her students. Assignments weren't easy but they had a clear purpose and really helped me understand and get better at animation.
