comment: Good teacher overall. as with any online, alot of writing. She is rather tough on grading. Not always clear until after poor grade was received, what she wanted.

Suzan Tessier is a good online teacher. She sets a clear grading criteria for discussion posts and homework assignments. The amount of assignments she gives is not overwhelming (Meaning, you will still have a life). She is not a STRICT grader but being lazy with grammar or engagement with activities can affect your grade.

I am taking her now for an online class, I am regretting not dropping out. Some of her assignments are okay; but honestly it just seems like a lot of poorly organized busy work. I really discourage people from taking this class unless you have no other option.

If you want to learn personlity through the book, take the class. She teaches from the book and has a lot of work. Discussion posts and response are pretty specific but manageable. Not an easy class. Quizzes are specific but just read the chapter and you will be fine.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: If you want to spend hours EFFECTIVELY learning about the Psychology of Personality, enroll in this class, buy the required textbook, and then withdraw. Tessier's attempt at teaching her online course reminded me of a dictionary that uses the word it defines as the definition, its overwhelmingly annoying and leaves you exactly where you started.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: There is a ton of work every week.  Took this class hoping to have an easy online class and this was not it.  Makes videos of herself talking with puppets and then you have to do an assignment on what the underlying meanings of it were.  Very strange assingments. Quizzes extremely specific once a week. Many discussion posts and responses to others.

She does not care how well you adapt to the class or not. She does not care how busy you are with your life. Her grading is horrible. In the last week, she decided to drop "points" from my weekly quizzes which brought my letter grade down from B to C. She could care less that I tried hard to study and to pass her 20 question quiz in 20 mins. Avoid!

Love this professor! She's really nice. I had her for an online psych class, and there is a good amount of work expected from you. But as long as you skim the textbook and participate in online discussions thoughtfully, it's easy to get an A. Hope to take her again!
She was a great teacher, really made it easy to pass the course if you payed attention. Would def take another class with her.

She is a really nice teacher. You can tell she knows the material, but she is not always cocky or confident like many professors. As long as you show you care, and make an effort in class and discussions, it's easy to pull off an A.

Tessier does assign a lot of coursework, but about half of it is online discussion. As long as you are able to keep track of homework and submit it on time, show up for lectures, and study the book for exams, it's easy to get an A/B. Offers extra credit. Is flexible if you show effort and talk to her. I'd recommend her.

Worst teacher ever way too demanding, thinks she is nice, but in reality there is nothing you can do in any of her classes to honestly earn a good grade (and we are talking even a B). Take her only if you feel like doing more work than the classes that actually matter and get graded the harshest you have ever been.

It's clear that Shay has extensive knowledge in LGBTQ+ Studies and teaches it well. The workload is not an issue as most say, but they don't show any compassion or care for students. They give vague/unhelpful feedback (only saying "No") that is often negative even when graded well. It's hard to stay passionate about the course/material with them.

I've taken four of Dr. Olmstead's classes and I loved every one of them. They assign a lot of reading if you're not taking this class for your degree, but they communicate their expectations very clearly and are eager to work with students. Bottom line is, if you communicate with them they will be incredibly helpful and understanding.

Multiple readings each week. Nearly all are by white authors. You can't have a class that claims to explore the lives of a marginalized group while only analyzing one facet of said group. You go to class and every student is white too. Shay isn't a bad professor and they teach well; just felt like they lack diversity in their sources.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Dr. Olmstead is very nice and a great professor. There's 25 readings to do before class around 30 pages each, but you can skip 10. Actual class time is lecture/class discussion on whatever was read. There's a final project that must be trans studies related but is very flexible on the format, as long as it's visual somehow.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']
comment:
This course had so much potential to be interesting, but is crushed under weekly 50+ pages of reading. Workload has impeded my studies for my actual major. DERNs are long, tedious, yet provide little in terms of learning. Same with semester projects.

Dr. Shay is nice but I can't think about them without getting frustrated. 0/10

Professor Olmstead is honestly amazing. Their goal is for you to get the most out of your class but not pushing yourself too hard. They can crunch the numbers with you based on the grade you are looking for to determine what assignments you should focus on. Make sure you read the assigned text and use their office hours, they want you to do well!

I've had them for many classes now. They assign a lot of reading but are very caring and flexible with deadlines and issues that might arise. Get ready to read a lot of dense theory papers, but they're good stuff thats really good to know.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'So many papers']
comment: An amazing professor who presents the material in a very interesting and relevant way, however there are up to 3 writing assignments due every week. The work load is intense and overwhelming but it is interesting, there are easier WGST classes to take if you are trying to fulfill a minor or immersion. Is about 6 hours outside of class a week.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Three reading summaries a week and mandatory readings, unless you're terminally online and already deep into gender theory TikToks and niche discourse threads, you're absolutely set up to drown. If you're not ready to talk politics at 10AM good luck!

I was inspired by the dean at that time of the multidisciplinary studies. He truly transformed my life. He led me to ask myself important questions: What would wake up every morning looking for clues to solve rather than an 8 to 5 job? I completely changed my career. Today I run a successful biotech startup in San Francisco & I'm forever grateful!

I really enjoyed Professor McQuade in spring of 2022. He made what would have been a mind-numbing 3 hours engaging with the discussion-style and odd humor. Mindtap assignments were straightforward. His experience gave good insight into the subject. His disability slowed grading, but he was understanding and gave many opportunities to fix anything.

Took his class back in spring of 2022 and it was one of the better classes I've taken at RIT. It's clear that he's knowledgeable about the subject and frequently talks about things outside of the textbook that I found interesting. Homework was done on Mindtap, but he was generous enough to give us ~10 attempts on each assignment and 2 on the tests.

He was the worst professor I’ve ever had. He didn’t give us class materials fo the first 6 weeks of class then tried to give us all of the materials from the semester in week 7 to give us an exam the same week. If you can get a different professor, do it.

He deserves a 0. His class was the worst experience I have ever had. It was concerning when he started the semester discussing a disability, but seriously, if you have a class with him, strongly recommend dropping. Learned off cengage b/c he went on tangents in class for over an hour. Lectures were useless, and he was very disorganized.
This class was asychnronous. He never answered emails, not once. He assigns over 3 hours worth of reading and work to complete EACH WEEK. There was no way to reach him at all. Terrible.
all I learned in this class was the definition of technology and 9/11 conspiracies.

This is my second class with Prof McQuade and the experience was even worse than the first time. We had two assignments, no exams, and no final. The communication and organization was bad enough, I received a B+ based on the single graded assignment we had. Avoid any of his classes if you care about your GPA

This class was online asynchronous. It was the worst managed class I have ever taken. I maybe received 6 emails from him the entire semester and half of the (a whole 3 emails) were him complaining students weren't completing his assignments. The first assignment of the semester ended up not being due until OCTOBER. Worst professor ever. Easy A tho

By far the worst Prof I've had. We've gotten 5 versions of a 16 page syllabus and yet have done nothing and have no idea what is expected of us. Unorganized, unprepared, somewhat rude, just overall terrible professor.

I took this class online in fall '20 in the middle of COVID. The professor had an accident over the summer and the class has come to a standstill. Almost no relevant or useful communication. No work to be turned in I'm not sure how we're gonna be graded. All these things just made a perfect storm to fail. Don't do it to yourself. Take anyone else!

You know that person in your life, whether it be a grandfather or neighbor, who seems to talk about nothing for hours upon hours, rambling about anything that can enter the labyrinth of their mind, and every time you leave them you think to yourself, "God, I worry about him". That's Samuel McQuade.

Not the most PC professor, pretty inappropriate at times, considered reporting several things he's brought up in class. He's a good guy at heart, but not very good at lecturing. A lot of tangents and hard to take notes on important things for the class. He showed up 45 min+ late the first weeks. BUT, if you are patient enough, this is an easy A.

This is the first time Professor McQuade has taught undergrad in 10 years, so it was a bit of a rough time during this semester. All work is online so it's very easy to complete and pass the class with an A. Lecturing for 3 hours is way too much, considering he goes off topic 99% of the time.

I took CRIM 110 as a perspective curse, and I honestly feel like it's the best course I ever took. The lectures, though they did go off topic quite a bit, were extremely educational and I feel like I learned more in class than the textbook could ever have taught me. Prof McQuade definitely knows what he's talking about and is really knowledgeable.

This class was a hour lecture once a week and at first I was not looking forward to it at all. But Sam made the class interesting and easy with his crazy stories he shares. Overall class work was very easy and he was very flexible because everything was online and you were able to take everything until you aced it!
This professor demanded your attention and you were rewarded with a wealth of knowledge and experience. I had him for one course and it was probably the best I have ever had.

Very good teacher, knows what he is talking about.  Has some interesting and funny stories.  His class is actually one I enjoy going to.  A good amount of reading needs to be done, but its all fairly interesting. He gives open note tests.  Get a different teacher if u are easily offended, but if u can take a joke youll really enjoy him as a teacher

Excellent professor. He knows what he is talking about. I must say that you should't take the course if you don't want to work hard but after all the work you have learned a lot. Great teacher! I wish I could have him in other classes. Unique teaching style.
exams are hard (NEED TO READ EACH QUESTIONS FIVE TIMES). Very tricky. A lot of reading. I did get an A but it took way lot of effort. He knows what he is talking about though.

To start, I did get an 'A' in the class. I would recommend avoiding this prof at least for this class. No real knowledge of comp crime. His tests are unfair and have nothing to do with how much of the material you know. You'll either like him or not.

I learned quite a bit. Tons of extra reading not covered on tests which were pretty difficult. He is very full of himself but it is understandable considering his background in policing. My biggest complaint is that i was late to my next class every time
He was teaching for the first time at RIT so he sure made everything VERY complicated. Should teach the graduate courses!

If anyone trash talks Dr. McQuade it's probably because they are a horrible student. He demands only the best work, you will fail miserably if you are lazy. This man is THE source for computer crime studies in the USA.
The name's actually McQuade, moron.
And you spelled his name wrong!  it's McQuaid.
Oh wait, he's actually really good and knows what he's talking about.  Afraid of actual academic work?  Scared to read and do some research?

Teacher is an Egomaniac who babbles endlessly about pointless things, doesnt cover proper material, gives extremely complicated tests and refuses feedback from students. On a last note, you will never get out of this class on time since he loves to talk.
So boring and pointless

Lectures are incredibly boring, he loves to yap. He grades incredibly hard with no set rubric for responses. Every word you use needs to be precise on the exams, exams are all written no MCQ. Attendance is graded and you will lose points for stepping out to use the bathroom (insane if you ask me). He kinda acts like a high school teacher in a way

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Handwritten notes due before every class and flipped classroom format. Very nice guy, but he ends up just talking about his childhood for 20 minutes which isn't acceptable for the amount of money you spend on classes here. His grading is also very harsh & subjective especially from what I've heard from other students in his other classes.

My biggest complaint with Professor Mathers is his exams. I wouldn't recommend taking him based on how he grades . He grades very harshly while never telling us in lectures or in notes what he expects from our answers. Those who understand his thinking and are able to guess what hes looking for will do well (mindreaders)

Collins lectures are very interactive and never boring. I like his teaching style and the way he formats assignments. Only things is he's a harsh grader because he's looking for very specific things. You can't have an ounce of generality when doing assignments or exams.

He cannot give a clear rubric for assignments for the life of him, and feels the need to force students into a set direction without giving any clear guidance or help to get there; he teaches like this is a high school English class, but grades like it's an MIT 4th year course. Class time is always spent sitting doing nothing.

Classes are discussion-led instead of lectures. Videos and texts are assigned for homework – notes are graded. All exams (including final) are weighted the same and  have SAQs. Ff you understand what he's looking for, they're very easy. No laptops or phones in class, many ways to get extra credit, approachable. Overall, interesting and easy class.

I had a really good time with Prof. Mathers this semester. He runs a flipped classroom, making most classes discussions while having 2-3 pages of notes due every Sunday. While all classes are recorded via Zoom and uploaded, attendance does help a lot. Exams were pretty easy as long as you pay attention in class. Extra credit opportunity everywhere.

Nice guy with good intention, but very tough grader and some of the test are almost subjective, which makes getting consistent good grades tough. I had an A in the class and then took the final and do not do good, and when I went to talk about it, he said he "disagreed" with my answers, although my answers were correct according to our resources.

No phones allowed, no computers allowed, no tablets allowed, and participation is graded. Honestly the worst professor I have ever taken nitpicks your exams for specific wording and grades YOUR notes that he makes you HAND WRITE. Every class ruined my morning will, never take one of his classes again.

Prof. Colin is an amazing professor! He is able to get his point across for every lecture exceptionally well. He made it clear what he expected of us and what he wanted us to learn from his class. He was very nice and easy to talk to. There was a decent amount of homework, though doing the homework pays off and is normal for a philosophy class!

He's a great professor who makes the material as interesting as possible. The videos are the most important part out of class, if you don't do them, you will fail. But, as long as you do the videos and attend lectures for discussion, you will do well in the class.

Prof. Mathers definitely knows his stuff! If you are interested in PHIL I highly recommend taking a course with him - however if you aren't PHIL focused, there is a steep learning curve. Nice guy, puts heavy precident on attendance and participation. Class is almost always discussion based, rarely lecture. If you prefer lectures, skip this one.

Very good and approachable professor. Homework is ~2 sets of notes per week (must be hand-written). Lectures are engaging so long as your class neighbors are willing to have meaningful discussions about the content. Does a good job getting everyone involved in the class discussion, so don't expect to glide through lectures without contributing.

Honestly, he's a great guy and I love his style of teaching. My only big complaint is how tough of a grader he is. To be fair my writing skills are not great and I do not enjoy philosophy. If you have some decent writing skills and an actual interest in the topic, it's an easy class.

Lectures are very interesting and Prof Colin very knowledgeable in the course material. Heavy emphasis on group work and participation. Only downside is really just the workload, but it is manageable once you have a routine set.

Gives interesting lectures. Is very clear about what material is going to show up on the exams; simply watching his videos and paying attention in class is all that's really necessary to succeed in his class. Was a pleasure to talk to outside of class as well.

Wasn't expecting this much work for a Gen Ed but he was a great teacher. Definitely make sure you are revising the weekly assignments or the final will be hell. I learned so much from this class and have taken Phil 205 with him as well. Overall would highly recommend Professor Mathers for those who are interested in philosophy and want a challenge.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I believe Professor Colin strives to foster an excellent learning environment. However, the fear of point deductions due to perceived judgment hampers participation. It's crucial to recognize that not every student excels in moral issues, particularly in a gen ed class. Feeling inadequate shouldn't stem from a less firm grasp compared to some peers

This class is way too much work for something offered as a perspective. The class is fast paced and you need to take good notes in class to complete the homeworks. His solution to this is telling you to watch the class recordings when you need to. Colin is a nice fellow but I never thought philosophy was supposed to have right and wrong answers.
Pretty cool guy and makes the class interesting. Lots of work but wasn't very difficult.

Professor Mathers is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he does. My only small complaint is that he isn't super clear on his expectations for assignments, but once you get the hang of it it's not a big deal.

The amount of additional work you will need to do versus other phil 102 professors makes me not recommend him. If you are a philosophy major or have a heavy interest in the subject he may be a good choice as he is a very good lecturer and his class is pretty interesting. You must also put in consistent work into the class or you will be swamped.

Great professor! I wish I was able to take his class in person, because I genuinely looked forward to his lectures each week! Gave a lot of really awesome insight into the things he discussed, and was always willing to see every viewpoint from every perspective. Just make sure you follow his standards and you will definitely have a good time!

Philosophy classes can be hard to conduct with all the discourse in the world. Still, Colin taught an informative and unbiased class that covered various interesting topics for any student. His teaching style introduced thoughtful class discussions that were calm and collected; even when students disagreed on different topics.

Prof. Mathers is an interesting professor. The style of the class was really fun and the material is unlike anything I had seen. Colin made the material easy to understand and graded fairly. This class in particular had him telling stories every class as well as asking students for their stories too. If you're looking for a good class, this is it.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Overall, he's a solid choice. At first I was a bit intimidated by his strict manner of grading, but if you meet with him, he clearly explains why. He explains concepts very clearly in class, and if you pay attention, he will do his best to help you understand. The one thing is to TAKE NOTES in class for the final "lab" or you'll pay for it later.

Prof. Mathers was great at leading group discussions, in spite of our reluctant participation. He's one of those people who you can tell really cares about his students, and he was always willing to stay after and discuss things with students. There were weekly assignments, but as long as you kept on top of things it wasn't too bad.

At beginning of semester, create a word doc in the format of the final "lab report" you need to do for class. Take notes within that document and do all of your weekly assignments in it when they're assigned, copy them into another document and turn that in. If done, you should have zero trouble with the class. Otherwise have fun on finals week.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Tips for success in Phil 101/102: understand midterm/final paper structure on syllabus, then structure EVERY assignment. DURING LECTURES: TAKE NOTE of PEER EXAMPLES (only 1 good one needed) AND prof's answer to assignment questions. Write your revised responses after every lecture and you'll slowly contribute to a completed midterm and final. GL!

I found Mathers's lectures to be very clear and pretty interesting. There is probably 1-2 hours of homework due twice a week, but that's nothing unreasonable for a college class. Mathers seemed to really care about his students and gave us a day off to recharge. I thought he was very clear in grading.
The assignments aren't too hard, but the lab report grading is really unclear and doesn't match the rubrics he gives you beforehand.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: He can be a tough grader. He certainly expects you to know your stuff. It would be best if you took notes other than what is on the slides. He has some fun trivia for extra credit and other opportunities for more credit. As long as you apply yourself, you'll be fine; otherwise, expect to be in for a long semester.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Tough grader']
comment: He gives feedback, but isn't clear. I submitted a 13 pg lab report (Midterm) 3x on mycourses, and he sent it back to me, all 3x, saying it was wrong with vague descriptions why. He failed me for the midterm. Couldn't even give me a 65 being that I cared about the assignment. If you don't like to read, DO NOT take this class with him! 45pg final, 85

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: His lectures were some of my favorites, he explains topics thoroughly and always made me interested in everything we discussed. It does require a good amount of homework, but not anything crazy. I even found his stories interesting, even if they were irrelevant. I thought his grading could be a little unclear, but overall fantastic professor

Very discussion heavy, and he makes you participate. Not too much homework and tests are easy. He tells lots of stories, gives extra credit, will help you on homework and always makes himself available for students. If you are an introvert and don't speak up a lot in class, be ready to get called on. Very caring and kind, get help if you need it.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Although the workload was not incredibly high, it was still more work that you would expect from a typical 100 class. However, that being said if you do the homework the tests are easy. If you are confused about anything, even the upcoming homework he is very willing to talk and help you out. Definitely talk to him if you are struggling.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: The ONLY good thing about Mathers, his exams were straight forward and easy. His classes were exhausting, and the work needed in homeworks for a perspective was more than needed. You need to be present and indulge in discussions, or you ain't getting no grades. You do not want to take him if you do not like reading boring stuff for like random qns.
Great professor! Had him for Introduction to Moral Issues. The HW was very doable and he gave a lot of chances for extra credit. Made class fun with interesting discussions and topics.

Though I didn't like the subject Colin Mathers made it interesting. He was a fair grader and his lectures were funny and interesting. Sometimes the homework expectations felt unclear but it was easy to clarify with Colin's readily available office hours.

Yes, it's more focused on his Philosophy, but who cares you still learn a lot and the class is super easy. There is a lot of homework, however, if you show up to class and go to office hours he will help you complete the work. All exams are based on the homework and the key phrases he gives you. There are no papers either.

Very big into group discussions and participation. A little bit obsessive about things. Does not talk to students as equals, gives simple one-sentence answers to legitimate philosophical inquiries and makes no room for disagreement. Decent choice of readings. Solid lecturing, though he doesn't lecture much. Somewhat hard tests.

He's a nice person and all, but has very specific views about topics he covers so you're either right or wrong, there's no in between. It kinda takes out the philosophy from the course. His homework is relatively easy, and its not that hard to score a good grade as long as you show up, but its not fun either.

Pretty alright, nothing too difficult. Often has students discuss amongst themselves what they feel the meaning behind an image is or a question etc. Randomly calls on people for questions, which really aren't a ton of work. Goes off on tangent a bit too easy, but other than that pretty solid.

Dr. Mathers is not a bad human being, although not a great teacher. He cherry picks which questions to grade, so you don't get credit for all of the work that you complete. Any work you complete conforms to his opinion and he views, leaves very little room for your philosophy. As a 4th year student, this was the most unclear class I have taken.

He is a very good teacher for learning the material, but not great at helping philosophical thinking, but that's difficult to teach in a course that has a lot to cover, so I will give it to him. He is a nice person, but a bit intense. He sort of turned me off to atheism advocacy, as he was kinda strawman-ing the few religious topics there were.

Memorize the key phrases and show up to class! Cannot emphasize enough and it's not hard. He assigns exercises, you do them and discuss answers in class, and then he assigns a phrase that you have to know and use on the test. He's a pretty nice guy and very available as long as you try, but I don't think this is real philosophy.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']
comment: He is all in all a great guy. Very clear in what he wants you to know and how to get there. Readings can be tough but he is very willing to clear things up if things are unclear. As long as you take notes and study those notes, you're getting an A. However, if you want a genuine liberal arts or philosophy education, he does stifle creative thinking

Strange class, I didn't like it at first but grew to enjoy it more as time went on. Study your notes and you're golden for the tests. Easy homeworks, easy tests, no projects or papers. Just make sure you memorize what you need to.

Very structured, NO PAPERS which I loved. He LOVES his key phrases, just take notes during class and study those  super easy A. If you aren't sure on HW ?s, you can ask at office hours, he'll usually tell you how to improve them so you'll get better HW grades too. Content usually interesting, if you want real philosophy maybe go elsewhere tho

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: This class is by far the worst class in my college life. It is not like a typical liberal arts class where you express your opinion and back it up with arguments. He gives key phrase. And if you are not MEMORIZING key phrase and using it on the test, you are completely destroyed in the test. Doesn't care effort of the student.

I felt like the workload for a 102 class was too much for me to handle. The readings are difficult to comprehend and you never actually get the right answers for homework questions. You take notes and get the "key phrase" and must improve your answer on your own. Too intensive for me and much more work compared to other professors that teach this.

A lot of people don't like Mathers, but I think he's a great professor. He is very caring if he sees that you're putting in effort. Few opportunities for extra credit. Lectures are very clear and thorough. He also makes his own videos with captions to explain his topics.

Discouraging is the first word that comes to mind when thinking about this Philosophy class. I had joined the class late and reached out for help, only to be treated like I was wasting this mans time. This was my first and only experience genuinely negative experience with a professor. He discourages other students during class discussions.

He was pretty opinionated. Made it known that he is not a fan of any religion, so that was a little off putting to me. Anyway, read the textbook, write what he wants you to say and you'll be fine. All in all he is a good guy and is very easy to talk to. PARTICIPATE. It is very important to him. Gives extra credit opportunities.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Prof. Colin is very serious about participations and attendance, and remembers every student very well. He likes to call on any student during lecture for group or homework answers, and encourages open discussion in class. Always keep in mind to pay attention and take notes since his tests always base on the answers he gives in class.

A lot of the complaints regard Prof. Mathers is he kills discussion, I think these are typically the people most challenging the traditional view which is fine, but as he said he follows a Socratic method of teaching . Unlike other PHIL courses, not every view is valid, arguments can have flaws. He will listen but expect him to challenge you.

Mathers really doesn't believe in discussion. He runs his Intro to Moral Issues course around a set of questions that he calls the "workbook". His goal is to get you to memorize his answers to these questions and grades you on that. The class has almost 0 real discussion because it's all about these questions and his answers to them.

I didn't really like how he conducted the class. Almost any answer given to him was wrong in some way or another, even if you just used some sort of wording that he didn't like. The discussions weren't very interesting. However, it was an easy class to pass, as long as you did the work, participated a little and paid attention to his key phrases

He's ver opinionated on all topics, especially involving the existence of God. Basically, it's his way or the highway. Most of his lectures were interesting, I especially enjoyed his side stories. Overall, I don't want to continue with Philosophy  mainly due to this class. I wish there were more options allowed.

The best teacher I had this semester, he is very smart and passionate for Philosophy. BE AWARE, you will have a lot of homework but you will learn a lot and he is very good getting students involved in his class. After having a class with him you might consider doing a Philosophy minor or double majoring, best professor ever!

Mathers is a pretty laid back teacher, he often tells stories and actually likes talking about Philosophy. What he wants from tests is very clear, so passing is easy if you pay attention. Make sure to participate if you want the A, and taking notes is a must when he goes over homework. i would definitely take him again.

This philosophy professor is pretty easy. You have to do the homework, but you don't really have to take notes in class, just pay attention to the discussions. He gives out a lot of extra credit. NOTE: you do NOT have to worry about getting the textbook for this class. EVERY reading assignment can be found online, and he gives you a list of them.

His teaching is clear, but he is offensive.  Be prepared to be offended, he makes his opinions clear and if you disagree with him you will not do well in the class.  Also was unfair, gives random bonus points if you know the answers to random trivia questions, overall unfair and a terrible teacher for making his students feel uncomfortable.

It was a very clear cut class. You always knew what was expected of you and these expectations were pretty reasonable. The tests weren't bad either. As long as you payed attention and made sure that you corrected your answers as necessary for the homework, you'll do well. He takes thesame questions from the homework and places them on the test.

Cool guy. Keeps it interesting. Not too much workload. As an introvert, I disagree with the below reviewer saying the class is uncomfortable for introverts. You can speak up one time per class and get full credit, which is perfectly reasonable.
Very predictable, not much room for opinions. Didn't run the course in a way that was comfortable for introverts. Four hours on a Saturday is unpleasant.
You knew what to expect every class. Examples were good and clear. Participation is necessary for a good grade.

Some people are misled to think that, since this is a liberal arts fluff class, any old answer to a question will do. This isn't the case in Mathers's Intro to Ethics. While you needn't agree with him on moral issues (he doesn't make his opinion known), he expects you to find certain flaws in certain arguments, etc. Overall, a good teacher, though.
Great teacher, awesome class. If you're interested in ethics, I would definitely reccommend it. Saturday mornings are a bit tough, but worth it IMO!

The class is easy if you have a tolerance for it. Four hours of ethics on saturday mornings is pretty rough. Descriptions are unnecessarily long and his word rules. You dont get room for an oppinion here. He makes his class rules very clear and they show no tolerance.

Cool and entertaining guy. Made a relatively boring class enjoyable. If you want an A, study the answers to the homework questions (which he gives you in class). That's pretty much all that's on the tests. Easy class.

Colin is a good teacher. Easy to get an A if you attend class and take notes. Homework is to read a chapter and ask questions in a packet he gives. You get extra points for answering questions in class and attending in general. 2 exams - questions come from packet given to you prior to exam. Take this class!
Not bad at teaching.  He always gave me hard times to make perfect opinions that should be matched with his opinions.  That's all you can do is completing questions and read the book.

Awesome, easy teacher. Show up, read the textbook, do the questions and you'll get an A. The tests are made of the questions you've already answered - just study those and you'll do fine. Also a really interesting teacher.
he is a horrible teacher. He has one test and if you do bad, your done for, also his class is boring.

Mathers is an excellent professor.  He is very clear and comprehesible.  He does not grade harshly and is very open to help out with assignments.  The textbook is used for about half of the work done.  The other half comes from discussions in the lecture.  I recommend this professor.

Good professor. Questions on exams are straight out of the workbook. As long as you attend class & pay attention you'll do well in the course. Class is fun & interesting-- the professor does a great job of explaining concepts.
He's such a troll in class. He takes advantage of the subjective nature of philosophy by preaching his own philosophical ideas. He's pretty slow on grading.

Good: Attendance NOT mandatory, easy+blended class, approachable. Bad: SLOW GRADER, limited and unclear feedback, does not check email, inflexible with argument topics, teaches nothing in class, completely useless! My grade would be better if he provided timely feedback. We were on our 7th assignment when he graded the 3rd! Grade Approx: B-
Good human being and whenever I went to ask doubts, he was very much there to help me with his ideas. Would recommend to everyone.
He is a great person and gives you whole lot of space to learn and explore new things.
vague in teaching, not helpful.

Prof Mooman's course knowledge seems very surfacial as he stumbles if you ask him a question and usually replies with a non definite or very generalized answer. Lectures are vague and have no depth and the guy doesn't even make his own notes or slides and lacks organization. Doesn't expect much from students either.

Professor Mooman is an intelligent guy (as could be presupposed) but he is not an effective lecturer for early CS courses. I can imagine his higher level courses are more his level based on talking to him. Being self-taught, I did learn.   He does want his class to do well and encourages exploration, but he will be a difficult lecturer.

Professor Mooman is a nice guy, but he is not very good as a teacher. He tend to just read off the power points, and it's hard to get help from him, as he usually sends you to other people. Hs lectures are long, and it seems that he is not always 100% sure of what he is teaching, You have to teach most of the material to yourself.
Good professor, great sense of humor, but sometimes its hard to understand him and goes way off-topic most of the times. Always there to help you.

He truly is a nice guy. Was very umprepared to teach our class as it was given to him 2 weeks before school. Very helpful on tests . Wants you to pass his class. Not sure if he'll be teaching this class again as he usually teaches the higher levels. Only gives Midterm and Final for tests.

He is a good human but has a long way to go as a professor. He is not clear with his course structure and highly lacks organization. He is too wavering, therefore, after a while into his course it gets difficult to trust him. You will often find him go off topic and discuss irrelevant things. You have to be a self-learner to get thru his course.
Industry oriented guy, Helpful, tries his best to teach, but sometimes not very clear. Not tough at all in grading.   Exams can be tricky though

Well, Mooman's a good guy and earnest in trying to help you succeed but there's so much to Computer Science and he doesn't really explain anything- most lectures go off topic and are generally a waste of time. Start the labs early and get whatever help you can, if you don't know Comp Sci- well, if you don't know Comp Sci, god have mercy on you.
You wont learn much from the lectures. You have to practice hard for the exams.
great teacher
Good and helpful professor. Try his best in whatever teaches. Exams may be unexpected!

Didn't seem like she knew what she was talking about. Assignments were incredibly vague, projects were unnecessarily tedious. Assignments and coursework were clearly not her own. Presentations were hundreds of slides long and incredibly unhelpful. Nice person, awful teacher, and hoping that she gets better next semester and makes her own slides.

Seems like she means well, but she's pretty worthless as a professor. Assignment are 'easy', but only in the sense that one could access the information online. Expectations are not clearly reflected in lecture and she is often caught off guard, many times be erroneous/unclear information in her own slides. Would not recommend.

She's doesn't seem to know how to lecture, most of the slides we get are clearly not her own and sometimes she seems to be reading them for the first time with us.  Homeworks/Quizzes fairly easy.  Tests were on the long side but it seems like she's working on that.  Projects seemed like they were outside the scope of the class.
She's really nice, but not a good teacher. Lectures seemed unorganized and unclear.

I think this was her first semester teaching (and RIT's first semester coming from quarters), so assignment requirements were unclear and the curriculum was unorganized.  Future sections with this teacher will likely have higher clarity.  Professor is easy-going.
Lousy.

By far the worst experience I've had in an online class. The final project is a 10 page research paper for which he gave no feedback on, just a grade. His exams are RIDICULOUS. 100 questions, 2 hour time limit, very specific questions (e.g. in what year was the Magna Carta signed? 1213, 1214, 1215, or 1216). I greatly regret taking Siena's class.

Siena is great, although he had to leave during the middle of the quarter the time we did have with him was very enjoyable. Most entertaining 6-10p class I've taken. He teaches with stories from his experience. Very funny and helpful professor. He is awesome... and not bad on the eyes!

This is my second course with sps and I highly recommend him as a professor. His teaching style and methods always spark my interest..he also isn't bad on the eyes. I would strongly suggest taking a course with this instructor.
If he marked you as incorrect for a test question but you provided a good argument such as citing one of his previous lectures or the textbook, he would award you full credit for the answer.
Great class!! He teaches from experience and with a lot of great stories! Made the class fun and the material memorable.

Awesome guy, he tells a multitude of stories that relate to the topic on hand... most are very humorous.  His tests are fair, just read the main topics of the book and you'll be set.  Probably the best teacher I've had so far, very enjoyable and I looked forward to it every morning at 8am so that's saying something.
One of the best professors around, gets us to THINK!
Great prof. Always available during offices hours. Made the class project orientated, with no exams. Learned a lot about the topics and how to make a PCB.

Attend class or else you will get lost. He does not bother you about attendance. He is an AWESOME teacher and VERY helpful during office hours. I would love for him to be my professor again! By far the BEST EE teacher I ever had.
No Comments

Glen records all his lectures, so you don't really have to come to class, but you should if you want to witness his funny comments when presenting any 3D project/demos. He cares a lot about his students and will help you solve any issues with your 3D project(s) in or outside of class, just email him/talk to him/communicate!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Solid professor, gives great feedback and very helpful at office hours!

Had him in an online course, only taught via tutorials he pre-made online for autodesk maya. didnt teach us how to use it. Graded as if weve used the program for our entire lives, when I started learning it 3 months ago.
Easy class with a couple of tests and hw

This professor is so chill. He is willing to work with you if you miss class. This class is pretty chill, because you get to go to the observatory near campus. You get to work individual, and work with classmates. Homework's aren't too intense. If you need help, making office hours are super easy by emailing him or easily show up to his office.

tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Professor Nordhaus does not assign a lot of homework and usually will check in with his students to make sure all of his students turn in their assignment if they forget or did not finish by the end of week or some special occasions. He's also a good supportive professor to his students!
Hands down, one of the easiest class this semester. If you ever have to take Intro to Psychology, take it with him. You will not regret any decisions, trust me. He's deaf, btw, but still amazing.

Hauser is deaf, so if you aren't familiar with sign you will have to be prepared to listen to an interpreter for the whole semester. My only gripe with his class was the difficulty with communicating with him. Besides that he is an extremely driven and interesting professor. Easy class because he cares more about learning then grades.

All around wonderful professor, everything is online and open book so there's no need to take notes during lecture. He's a very nice person and not too strict although having diversity events being a part of the grade is an annoyance.

This would have been the easiest A I've ever gotten if he didn't have a required 'diversity event' writings that required a lot of effort to get to. Otherwise he sets up the class for you to get pretty much get no less than a perfect score. Everything is open book and open note online so you don't actually have to go to lecture if you don't want to

Really thankfully to have him as my psychology teacher! His lectures are so interesting and easy to understand. He is not too strict, very friendly and his stories are hilarious. If you want to take an Introduction to Psychology, I highly recommend you to go for him as your teacher! You won't regret it.
Class was very easy. Just go for the attendance. Make sure you take all of the online homework seriously because they heavily impact your grade!

Prof. Hauser's class was one of the easiest A's at RIT - he gives you a two week period for each quiz and three full days for the final.  All tests/quizzes are open book and online, so you really can't mess up if you do your work. Really interesting lecturer, really knows his stuff and an all around great guy. Highly recommended.
Pretty easy going, i stopped going to lectures half way through the course because all the work is online and right out of the book.

Simple class to take to get rid of a behavior/social science lib arts. He has daily online quizzes from textbook chapters every week, get points for going to class, and just a essay to write with ample time to do. Easy A if you go to class and put effort in the quizzes. Great professor with great stories and passion for psychology
He is deaf, however this does not affect the class very much. He is very intelligent and knows the material well.
His lectures are entertaining.  It's like watching television or reading a good book--you have fun and you still learn a lot that is relevant to life.  I highly recommend him.  He's HOT!
He is excellent at teaching but is not invested in the course. He is completely useless outside of the lecture. But its an easy A

With him being deaf with 2 interp. you do need to pay a little more attention than usual. He's quite smart and knows his stuff. He has some really interesting and funny stories and conveys material well. His tests are moderately difficult. Remember to get the practice book, it really helps alot since most of the questions are taken from it.
Great teaacher, very excited to be teaaching and conveys material well. Very nice guy to interact with
No Comments
Truly great teacher! One of the best I've ever had!
He is a really good teacher and assignments arent ureasinable- easy to get a good grade if you pay attention and turn in your work on time- tests are very reasonable- great teacher

Great teacher, makes class amusing.  He is deaf but the 2 interperters for my class were wonderful.  Tests are easy if you are good at memorization as he pulls all the questions from the practice booklet.
great teacher. very smart.
Test was much harder than expected... interpreter sometimes hard to follow.
No Comments
Good, and great learning on cloud and distributed systems at OSU.
Deserved for BEST professor award in "LinkedIn" University. I am sure.
Didn't respond to emails.
H.B. is super caring and willing to help students succeed. His class is definitely on the easier side, but I still learned a lot.

H.B. is a breath of fresh air. He's caring, passionate about security, has great lectures full of detail and explanations, and you take away a lot from his labs. He is one of the most supportive professors I've had and gives you great feedback on assignments. His grading is fair and if you have any concerns he is all ears!

HB is one of the most caring and interesting professors I have encountered. Knowledgeable in security, and a fun lecturer. I went to his office hours and we chatted for hours about life and work. Offers fantastic advice and truly cares about his students. Incredible person and a kind soul, I wish I could take another class with him.

HB is an awesome professor. He is still new to teaching but he puts in a lot of effort to make the class engaging. He grades fairly, teaches the material well, and is also very nice with ensuring everyone in the class is keeping up. He is also clearly a subject matter expert and I wish I could take more classes by him!
NO comment

Dr. Jonen seemed a little nervous and inexperienced the first semester I had with him, which made him seem strict and somewhat egotistical.  After that I think he learned what teaching is all about and he has definitely matured as a professor and one of the best out there.  To be a good professor it is important to be able to relate to the students

Student Oriented; wants to help u learn & will go out of way to adjust 2 help students Material is tough, fast paced but tests are from book & class ?s He narrows test material 4 you.  Get B+ in class & A in lab & you'll get A.  Bookreading is MUST Lots of personal initiative 2 learn material Class is presentation style-?s on reading no info lectur

This professor is so full of himself and that gets in the way of his teaching. his tests are gernerally unfair and he never curves. if you ever have a problem, dont waste your time talking to him about it. AVOID HIM
No Comments

Dr. Walders has a very clear-cut schedule. This semester she assigned a reading assignment (typically around 20 pages PS. Dont underestimate the full page of small-print text) every two weeks. A RAQ (Reading assessment quiz) was given after the three-day reading time slot (11 questions in 25 minutes). She then assigns a discussion or activity.
She's fair - and class is well-structured.
group based learning is how the class goes, if thats for you take the class. Professor Walders is amazing and the course is hard but not crazy

Professor Walders is an incredible professor. The "flipped classroom" approach to teaching was executed well, and I enjoyed the entire semester. Be prepared for a number of small tests and a lot of in-class work, but it really does help you learn the material. If you care about actually learning the material, take her class!

Positive Psych (Online) - Modules were well organized, not too heavy nor too light in material.  Prof. Walders does a great job in getting grades back in a timely manner and is extremely fair in grading.  I also really like that she added personalized feedback on assignments and discussions.  Definitely would reccommend!

She is an excellent professor, I take intro to psych with her and it's my fav class this semester. She is funny and super nice. Very clear and exciting.  Be ready for a lot of reading though. We read a whole chapter before each class and then get tested on it, we discuss the chapter afterwards. i personally see it as a great learning strategy
Kate was fantastic, open, helpful, thoughtful, and friendly.  If she wasn't in a field of study I had no interest in, I'd take every class she taught.

As a new online student at R.I.T, I felt contented in my progression due to Professor Walders' enthusiasm and consideration. She was responsive to my questions and concerns. Professor Walders expressed her thoughts and feelings with mutual respect. I hope my future professors are as phenomenal as Professor Walders! Sincerely, Natasha A.
Awesome teacher! take this class with her if you get the chance!!!!
Walders is awesome and there is no reason to take this class with anybody else.

Awesome teacher! She is very helpful, clear, and organized! Weekly discussions are fun to engage in. Weekly quizzes are not to hard if the reading was done. Highly recommended to take this class with her if you get the chance :)(took this class online)

I'm currently taking an intro to psych class with Kate online. The entire class is structured well, and is VERY organized. Each week, the due dates remain the same. She's also open to any questions. She wants to see you succeed!

Fine professor, but I often found class boring, he let us out late sometimes, and the class was more centered on art than AI than I would have liked. There's a sign-in sheet every class. I appreciate how he tries making class interactive, but I often didn't find his activities too engaging. He also isn't the easiest grader. He's nice enough though.
One of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure of working with. Definetly would reccommend any class taken with him
Best advice is to listen to sit back and listen to his lectures, they're very insightful. His grading is not harsh at all.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'So many papers']
comment: Great professor, just unfortunate that most of the people in his class are not in the major. He was very passionate about the material and cared about getting to know all his students despite there being 100+. If you're looking for an easy A to fulfill a requirement this is the place but try and reward the effort this guy puts in.

I took the class because I needed an art perspective and by the second week I was already tired of the class. If you love art history and listening to long lectures he's fine, but the work is extremely boring. He's good at what he does but be prepared for lots of reading and not much excitement.

This rating is more about the class than him. If you are taking this as an easy artistic perspective, it was easy but personally found it extremely boring. I feel like these reviews misled me. I didn't pay attention from the midterm to the final and I got an A.  Each absence takes 1/2 a point off your grade.

It's basically art for engineers, and man it would be hard to fail if you put in an ounce of effort. All he asks is that you come to class, take notes, and raise your hand once in a while. Exams are just essays, homework is a weekly reading quiz, and there was one short project in the beginning of the semester. Take him for the artistic perspective

Dr. Fogelson was a great professor. His course was very easygoing, the one thing that was slightly difficult was the midterm for which you have to know the names of all the artwork you've previously discussed, so taking notes on that will help. The final was take home and open book which made it a breeze. Show up to his class, he cares about that.

Dr. Fogelson was one of the best professors I've had. You can tell he really cares about the discussions and his students even though he may be a "junior" professor. I interviewed him once and he said his favorite part of the class isn't about the work, it's about the discussions. The discussions were amazing and made me want to participate.

Prof. Fogelson is really great. You can tell he cares about his lectures and the content is actually really interesting even if is has nothing to do with your major. You don't really have to do anything in class except listen, but it helps to take some notes to review for the midterm/final. Very chill class, great choice for an art perspective.

Dr. Fogelson is great. He isn't going above and beyond, but I can't think of a single fault. He is really knowledgeable about the course material, and his lectures are great if you are interested in the topics. This class is super easy and chill, and I think the stuff we cover is really useful. Great choice for an artistic perspective.
She really cares about her students success and is willing to spend extra time on subjects the class is struggling with. However, the syllabus is disorganized and deadlines are often unclear.
She is a highly skilled professor
Try to avoid her, we complained about her last semester but the chair person still give her classes I don't know why!
Great class! Advise anyone to take it with this professor
VERY NICE AND HELPFUL. SHE REALLY CARES ABOUT HER STUDENTS AND THEIR SUCCESS. I WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND TO TAKE HER CLASS. I LEARNED A LOT OVER THE PAST COUPLE YEARS THAT I HAD HER.

Dr. Bajorski is one of the best professors in the statistics department. He will not make it easy, you will have to think hard and put in effort to do well. That being said, his coursework and lectures are interesting and ultimately rewarding. His grading style is very reasonable, if you put in effort and work hard you will do well. Great professor
He speaks with a Polish accent, but is mostly fluent. You are allowed a formula sheet on tests. Tests are trickier than homework problems, but not terrible. Lectures are dull.

Professor Bajorski genuinely cares about this students success.  He answers questions very promptly and his tests are VERY fair.  The only thing I did like was that the lectures are long but I really like that he doesn't automatically assume that everyone is a math professional.

Professor Elahi was an absolute joy to have. He let us go early every Friday just so we could get dinosaur. The assignments were flexible and quite honestly fun. Occasionally he would let us have class outside or modify the assignment depending on how the class was feeling. If you can take his course I would highly advise it.

Lectures were fine, kind of boring, but you can tell she is passionate about the topics taught. There are a lot of practice problems both posted and given in class but there are very few of them with posted solutions. Also, no notes or anything really was posted besides the lecture slides which were only used half the time.

Lectures are very clear on the fundamental concepts. Reviews materials needed from Strengths 1. I think adding in the real life applications to the material taught was a good way to show the importance of this topic compared to other intermediate elective courses at RIT for ME.

She's a great professor! Her lectures are super clear, and if you're confused her office hours are very helpful. She gives hints as to what'll be on the exams, and it's clear she cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Dr. Iglesias is an amazing professor and person. Her lectures are a good combination of theory and examples, and she is very easy to communicate with outside of class. She learns the names of all of her students, and it easy to tell that she truly enjoys teaching. As a result, I consider her to be the best MECE professor I've had yet.
She is a total sweetheart. Always available outside of class via email, always willing to help. It's outstandingly obvious that she genuinely cares about the success of her students.

Professor Iglesias was great. While she rushed over a lot of the theory she was great in doing practice problems so no matter what you at least understood how to do the problems. Very accessible outside of class and more than willing to help or answer questions inside of class. A definite take if you can.

Dr. Iglesias is HANDS DOWN the best professor I've had this semester, especially with covid. During split classes she makes both students in class and online feel included and able to participate. She teaches really well through examples and is very clear about what will be on quizzes and exams.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Still remember getting 5/30 points on an exam question for making one error. Rest of the work was right, but a wrong step in the beginning ended up getting me the wrong numerical answer. Because of that I was never able to recover for the rest of the semester.

Iglesias is always very excited about the classes she teaches. She's very helpful in class and in her office hours and she cares a lot about each individual students' success in the class. She's a very effective teacher and is very passionate about her job.

I liked how it was easy to reach her in office hours and questions during class. She prepared us for the exam really well. The fact that she dressed up for Halloween was really cute. She showed that she really cared for her students.

Dr. Iglesias is one of my favorite professors at RIT! She is incredibly caring to her students and funny in class, but also has very thorough lectures with lots of helpful examples. Most quizzes are class activities and homework is great preparation for tests, which are very fair. I highly recommend taking Dr. Iglesias if you can!

Dr. Iglesias is one of my Favorite MECE Professors. She gives clear examples in class and wants her students to succeed. Exams are straight forward, as often in class she alludes to what the exact problem types will be, so if you've done the homework you're fine. I would 100% recommend her. Hopefully she will start teaching Strengths II.

Professor Iglesias is really good at giving solid examples and explaining the content thoroughly and in a way that makes sense.  She draws clear diagrams and explains every step of the problem.  Exams and quizzes are straight forward as long as you are willing  to put the time and effort in to the homework.  Would 100% recommend her for strengths

Strengths I is a lot of work but Patty teaches it so that everyone understands it. Do the homework and you'll do well on the tests. She does a ton of in-class examples that are tedious but necessary to understand the material. Would definitely recommend.

She goes through the lecture material pretty quickly in class but posts the powerpoints of them online.  She spends a lot of time doing examples with the class and takes time to make sure you understand what's going on.  She's really helpful if you go to office hours and will answer any of your questions and makes sure you understand the material.

She's not the best lecturer in class, but if you go to her office hours you will realize what an amazing professor she is. She will help you with your homework and also answer any questions you have about the course content. In class she tend to fly through the material, but if you go to her office hours, you will truly appreciate her.

She is great at making you understand the material, she will explain things in great detail, and involves people to help with examples (if you sit in the front, it will be you).  She gives "quizzes" which are just problems to work on with a partner, and she still helps you with it. Exams were fair, and exact hw problems.

Great professor.  It was her first class teaching outside of NTID I believe, and she did great.  Her accent wasn't terrible, even comical sometimes.  Her quizzes are fair and she genuinely wants everyone to pass and will go out of her way to make that happen.  I strongly recommend her.

Hands down best professor I've ever had. She uses power points in class and posts them online, in class instruction is clear and organized. She's incredibly helpful in office hours and is generally a nice, chill person. She really cares about her students and will host review sessions before exams.

Dr. Iglesias is one of the best professors I have had. She is very enthusiastic about what she teaches and she spends a lot of class time working out example problems on the board. She is helpful during office hours and makes sure you understand everything. She truly cares about your success in the class. Had her for statics. Definitely take her
Dr. Purtee has some of the best lectures i've ever taken. His style of teaching on the fly and live-coding keeps lectures lively, engaging, and sometimes comical.

Amazing professor. Really cares about students, is lighthearted and loves doing crazy and fun examples in class. Fair exams and a pretty easy grader. He definitely tries to take the stress out of Mechanics, and while it still won't be easy, you will learn significantly more and have a better time than with other professors. Fast grader.

Purtee is the kind of professor who goes to lengths to make sure students learn everything and understand the material. He just wants the best for everyone. He's also a very lenient grader, tries to pass as many students as possible . Assignments are of moderate difficulty, and you learn a lot about implementation of algorithms to real problems.
Amazing lecturer, very engaging in class, answers all questions and is absolutely hilarious. It was a pleasure to take Mechanics with him and RIT will be a worse off when he leaves next year.
Real nice guy. Down to earth, and easy to talk to. If you have anything going on in your life he's very understanding.
Great professor, hilarious, provides examples for everything, extremely interesting lectures. Definitely taking his further classes
Adam is really cool. He makes the class interesting when he interacts with students. He answers any question you ask, and makes sure you understand it thoroughly. He's nice and easy to talk to.

I'm hopeless when it comes to computer science- I don't even know why I chose this as my major. However, this professor helps me with whatever I need help with, he always readily responds to emails and has good office hours. Take this man if you can.
Best CS professor at RIT, though Heliotis is awesome too.

One of the best instructors I've ever had. Loves to play around and it always feels like he's learning with us. Incredibly smart almost to a fault. Will explain very complex things quickly but if you ask him he will go over them very thoroughly. If you enjoy CS you will laugh. Attendance isn't mandatory but I wouldn't miss his class for anything.

Amazing lectures and understands the content beyond what the slides explain. Missing class is a bad idea, but he's always willing to accommodate student's schedules outside of regular class time. Understanding of unavoidable technical issues and personal emergencies. Firmly believes in partial credit. Best CS prof I've ever had.

He is a fresher in teaching but he does his very best in delivering concepts and make everyone understand. Provides good examples to make you understand concepts. The best thing about him is that he is very proactive and learns from students. He possesses good knowledge and he got better day by day in teaching. He is very friendly and light hearted

best to keep the class interactive and he know his stuff really well. He will always listen to your solutions and give you feedback immediately. A thorough professional, he graded our tests very quickly.

He does his best to keep the class interactive and he know his stuff really well. He will always listen to your solutions and give you feedback immediately. A thorough professional, he graded our tests very quickly.
This guy REALLY loves talking. He even told students to stop taking notes during his lectures. His work isn't hard, but he will not be a big help.

For ENGL 210. My peers and I never fully understood anything in his class. Lectures were unclear and he was unclear. I sometimes wonder if he even knows what he is talking about. Asking him a question is like looking up a word in a dictionary which then uses more words you don't know.

His grading is so unclear and he doesn't articulate assignment instructions in a clear way, which ends up turning into bad feedback. His lectures are hard to follow, not because they're difficult, but because he comes across as not even really knowing the material himself which makes it hard to ask for clarification that makes sense.

His work is so unorganized, a lot of miscommunication on what he wants done on the assignments, there is no clear grading for the essays and draft work, and the texts get confusing until class discussion. I will not take him especially as a freshmen student, you will be so confused.

This professor was one of the most unorganized teachers I have ever had. He did not know what he was doing and did not communicate what he wanted us to do clearly. That made it that when we submitted the essays he gave bad feedback because he did not communicate what he wanted. DON'T TAKE HIM
not clear grading

His lectures made no sense-- I don't think he even knew what he was saying most of the time. His assignments are vague, and his feedback is generally unhelpful. Somehow turned interesting topics into confusing and boring nonsense... The course isn't very difficult though. It is easy to get an A/B+ on the papers.

Two main downsides: lack of clear, outlined rubrics and rambling. The professor would ramble about class content for far longer than needed, and the length of the class (1h 15m) made this worse. Assignments are given instructions but not rubrics, therefore you can't know exactly what you're being graded on. Feedback was often confusing as well.

Lectures were hard to understand, Made us read incomprehensible readings as STEM/Art students that didn't help me personally with developing my writing. Acted like a high school teacher since he got angry at us if we used our phones in class.

Dr. Lattanzio is a great person but is a confused and erratic professor. His lectures are all over the place; his organization in regard to assignments is very poor, and he can barely keep track of his schedule. He assigns about 40 pages of readings due every other day which is doable but simply unnecessary if this isn't part of your major.
He said a swear word once
Professor bad. Do not take

A teacher that is very hard to understand as he wore a mask on and off during class, was not clear at all.  The readings were uncomfortable and questionable. His feedback on essays were confusing and hard to understand , when i tried to fix them, they were not good enough changes. I got a 72 on my final essay with very little feedback.

Although it was sometimes hard to follow his lectures, I enjoyed the discussions in this class and the books we read. Get ready for lots of readings that sometimes don't make sense but usually fall into place once class discussion starts the next day.

the class was fine, but there was no chance for small group discussion for many of the very complex topics. he seems very nervous talking about the course subject matter and it feels a bit like we are supposed to be using these heavy issues as a silly little writing exercise rather than giving them respect. Despite all the readings it was OK

Not a bad teacher but takes forever to give you feedback on your drafts. I once got feedback on my draft that I submitted a week prior the night before the due date for the final paper. There are daily readings he wants done which will take up over an hour of your time, which aren't even graded (just discussion related). Would not take again.

I took his asynchronous class and I would do anything to stop others from taking it. While I did pass, it was a nightmare. He wont tell you about any assignments beforehand, promise. He gave us MULTIPLE group projects. I couldn't get in contact with anyone in my group, so I emailed him for help and he said, "do it yourself, life isn't always fair."
He was tough with his grading. Although he cleared most of the doubts but when I needed him the most he didn't help. Very harsh on the work done in my case.

The class structure could almost be considered bearable, but with this professor, you can say goodbye to all hope of actually enjoying the class. Constant disorganization, useless feedback, and awkward discussions are some of the highlights of his class. You can throw away any hopes of receiving clear instructions for assignments.

comment: I took him for FYW and this course has nothing to do with my major. The class consisting of mainly gender and sexuality making it hard to learn if you aren't interested. He has 4 essays that are a majority of the average but they aren't that bad just dull. He only cares for students who share his interests for these topics. Gives a lot of reading.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Overall he's a good professor. But, honestly, you should rename the class to "FYW: Gender and sexuality". 90% of what is discussed is about topics like this. He might be somewhat boring but he makes the class very easy to pass. I hated the class but i did the work and got a B+. (I didn't hate the class because of him, I hated it because I was forced to take it as a requirement to get my degree.)
Great Teacher. Loved Him!

When I took him he was fairly new, so keep that in mind. Easy grader, impossible to understand. His assignments are unclear and he doesn't post grades anywhere. If you talk to him he'll clarify and he honestly wants you to learn, but I would not take a class with him again. Ever.

Took Lattanzio for First Year Writing. He isn't too bad but the material was boring (I don't like writing). Papers are only a few pages long (there's 4 of them) and 1 quiz
you need to take a class with her
COLLEEN IS CHAMP TEACH!! SHE IMPRESSED MY SKILLS TOO MUCH!! THAT IS MY FAVORITE ONE!! PLEASE TAKE UP THIS ONE.

Great young professor! He was forthright, great at explaining things and made class enjoyable. Was
always happy to answer questions after class and was patient with everyone. Practical exam grading was lenient. He even threw in some of his own slides at the end of the semester about website hosting.

His lectures were good but I mostly learned the material through the homework. There's a significant amount of work for this course but it doesn't feel overwhelming. Exams are worth a very small amount, and we can use resources (CSS/HTML docs) for practical work. He creates a good environment for his class and I felt comfortable asking questions.
Online labs and readings that are easy and informative. Cares about his students. 100% would recommend.

comment: He gives us a new project every week and that project is insanely big and should take two weeks. He lectures really fast on complicated matters and expects the assignment to be done perfectly. His goals are unrealistic and impossible. Also he messed up my final grade from fall and it still hasnt been fixed.

She is really fun to listen to in class, gives great lectures, and in lab she was really helpful with any questions. Her grading felt pretty inconsistent, and would often take excessive points of with minimal explanation/feedback
Very helpful to students. Such a nice lady and a wonderful teacher.
good lab.
no lab is good enough, expectations are ridiculous, very unorganized and inconsistent.
Great professor, really cares about her students.  Helps students out well.  Would recommend!!!
