comment: This was an online class and was set up wonderfully. Reading was heavy but supplemented by his lectures that focused on what he found important and tested on. A few writing assignments every couple of weeks, and discussion boards were largely graded on good research and participation. Very good class. Easy A
very nice
Very nice and great professor
Wonderful prof

McCluskey is great! Discussion based classes, basically can discuss anything that interests us. Will cancel assignments if he feels there is too much. Great guy, super nice. Kinda cute in a nerdy way. Class discussion can get boring but overall great class! Highly recommended.
i graduate in 2007, robert Paine was a great chemistry profesor.
Dr Paine was one of my favorites. Good guy, great teacher.
Cool dude, very funny

She is a nice woman but a tough grader. Other lab instructors give sample data to use, she does not. She is not helpful with the challenging calculations. She is never satisfied with your lab reports so do not expect an A in her lab.

Avoid if possible! Extremely tough lab professor when lab should be an easy class. You have to put a lot of work in on lab reports and Ayo is a tough grader on them. Lab reports range from 5-7 pages when other instructors have their students write 2-3. Get a teacher with an easy A. It's not new material you are learning, so have fun with the labs!

Ayo is a difficult lab instructor. She makes you work hard and put in extra effort. Lab reports were never written well enough for her. Even though Ayo is a tough grader, she does know the material. Taking her lab improved my knowledge in chemistry.

Ayo is a pretty solid lab instructor. She's a bit of a hard grader, but that is manageable. She's willing to help if you ask for it, but you actually need to ask for it. She also demands you respect the rules of the lab, which is important.

She's such a fun lady, I hate that she's retiring. She lets you write like a human being which makes this class really easy. Her grading policies are simple and you usually get a chance do redo your papers. As long as you do the work a passing grade is easy.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read']
comment: The GOAT of RIT. As long as you know how to form a sentence, you'll get above a 90 on all your papers. Her feedback is fantastic and she LOVES Grammarly. Alot of reading to start the semester but it became less and less as the weeks rolled by. Highly recommend!!

Favorite professor at RIT. Her class has a lot of work, but those are really helpful in further academic studying. She is the kind of professor who is really good at inspiring students and providing thoughtful suggestions on not only academic studying but life.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Lots of writing but they're doable.

Fall 2017 This is MY personal experience, it may be different for you: I detested every day in this class. For one, it was hard to understand what she wanted in each Writing Project, but she insisted that the instructions were "black-and-white". I went to the Writing Commons many times and watched them not understand the prompt. It was a bad time.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Pretty good prof. A little to liberal bent for my liking. I think still harkens back to the 60's 70'd. I prefer a neutral prof who will allow me to develop my own point of view without reprisal. But a good teacher who cares. Do the job, get a good grade.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Lots of reading and writing, but it's first year writing. She really wants her students to do well and truly cares; she gave me an extension for a major project because of my anxiety. This extension saved my grade. She's readily available outside of class and very easy to talk to. First year writing isn't a fun class, but she'll get you through.

She seems to know what she's talking about and has good methods, but she doesn't develop her thoughts enough. Confusing and boring. The class gets meta. The project is fun but the overall class was just annoying.

Very very strict, she is a wonderful person to talk to, but as a professor? Not so much. If you want to pass her class I hope you're ready to stop doing work for your other classes. Boring topics and overly long papers. I passed with an A and would not even think about taking any of her classes after this.
She is awesome. You'll learn a lot in her class. However, you will have to work with her pretty good, so you can get an A.
She is a great professor and picks a very relatable topic for our essays.
Literally the sweetest. She reminds me of my grandmother. Her assignments can get a little boring, but over all an easy A if you do your homework and get your essays in on time
Little bit strict but very nice and helpful.
A really nice teacher. Do your homework and you will get A.
this class was the easiest B you possibly earn
She needs work at teaching people how to write.  i was totally confused throughout the whole quarter.

She is the easiest A you can ever get in Arts of Expression. Just do your work and you will get the A. However, she is one of the most biased individual out there so be prepared to argue back if she tries to rip you apart. Not a very bright woman!

I actually don't believe in perfect attendance but this was a class that I looked forward to attending. You can actually get her to talk about her days of protesting and helping out with desegregating schools in the south a while back. She's a rebel and a really good teacher to talk to one on one.

Professor Swartzfager is a goddess of writing seminar. I thought I would hate this class going into it but she makes it easy and fun. You get out of class between 45 minutes and an hour early almost everyday (as long as you finish your work). As long as you do all 3 papers and the journals you will have no problem getting atleast a B. 2 thumbs up!
She is a very good teacher when it comes to writing. You write three essays and she is a very easy grader. Not that bad of a class.

A really nice teacher.  The class was very interesting, and straight forward.  As long as you come to class, and do your work, you should get a good grade.  Be prepared to write well.  Definitely one of my favorite teachers for this quarter!

Great class - the globalisation topics that were covered made the class more interesting and makes you want to go to class. As long as you try your best, do your work, talk to your classmates and attend class you'll be fine. I wasn't looking forward to the classes at the beginning of the quarter, but it has turned out to be a fun and enriching clas
No Comments

I took SOFA 101. Very friendly and easy to talk to. Helpful insight, I'd recommend taking advantage of office hours too. The one thing is that I will say is that he doesn't respond to emails as fast as I'd like, and also didn't grade projects until the end of the semester, so you won't know what your grade is until the very end.
Amazing professor who is clear on their teaching material as well backed with an experienced background. Professor has genuine commitment and interest to their students and class topics.

Wendy is a lovely professor who knows how to do her job. Even in an online class, she ensures that all of her students' voices are heard and that they are engaged in the conversation. She is a great resource to have outside of the classroom and gives personalized feedback. Even though YOPS wasn't the most exciting, Wendy made it more enjoyable.

Gilmore is a very caring teacher who tries her best to help her students.  YearOne is a 0 credit class that is required so just show up and do a few assignments to pass.  Gilmore does her best to keep the lessons less boring.
FYE is not much of a real class, therefore it is easy. She is alright.

She is an effective teacher and does not give a lot of work but is a hard grader. Only 1 pop quiz so reading isn't really that important. Seems concerned about how her students are doing in the class.

She gives little to no partial credit, has no clear grading criteria, HW takes hours, exams are worth over 80% of your grade, and she is impossible to understand. The exams do not match the HW or examples in class and she is an impossible grader. Worst teacher I've ever had. The exam retake can hurt you if you do worse.

0/10, would not take again. This professor spends maybe 20 minutes on a topic and will immediately jump into examples without thoroughly explaining. The material covered on tests will be in the general ballpark, but mostly nothing you've seen before.

DO NOT TAKE!!! Wanda's classes lack formulas and definitions. I had to drop her class because this mingled with her own math errors made the content nearly impossible to learn. If you have the time to read the whole textbook maybe she'd be fine but I lacked this time.

Oo lala! She's so nice but if u want to pass u need to literally just pay attention and do the problems, maybe sit in the front. You will probably and definitely need a study group to do the homework, it gets long. Tests are exactly like in class problems. Back up back up back up. best class to eat a big breky in
Legit worst professor I have ever had or ever will have. Pleas avoid
Very unclear lectures, you are better off skipping. Homework takes absolutely forever and exams do not reflect homework. There were times she would just not show up to class lol. Avoid if possible

Genuinely the worst teacher or professor for any subject I've had all my life. Soft spoken, bad handwriting. Attendance not mandatory but if you miss more than 3 lectures you can't take a makeup test to replace lowest test grade. Gives very little partial credit on tests. Homeworks take several hours. I would recommend any other professor.

comment: Hard to Understand

Wanda's lectures are often hard to follow and are filled with mistakes. This class is already conceptually challenging, so be prepared to self-study. Exams are surprisingly fair (she allows you to cross a problem off; you're given 11, and you solve 10), and the questions are mostly simple. Exams are also worth ~80% of your final grade. Good luck!

I almost pity her, as she does not seem to be all there. She is often confusing herself and cannot make it through a sentence at times. She gets overwhelmed with the problems she is choosing to show, and then argues with students when her mistakes are pointed out. I feel bad, as she is extremely old and frail. I think she needs a break.

Wanda is a fine person but a terrible professor. For her lectures she just stands at the front of the class and does textbook examples, so I found it to be a complete waste of time since she doesn't introduce any way to attack the problems differently -- she just follows the textbook and that is it. Her grading is extreme.

Great human being, fantastic office hours, terrible Mulitvar & Vector professor.

Homework is extremely long. Don't plan on getting it done by yourself. Work with others and you'll be golden.

Be prepared to do your own learning because she pretty much gives you notes without much help in her lectures. I'm not sure about how helpful she is in her office hours, but class alone was not very conducive of "learning," I mainly had to figure out how the subject worked on my own.

Wanda is a nice woman but a bad professor. She is easily overwhelmed by her own examples and heavily includes physics concepts in her teaching. Show up to class to do your homework and hand it in. She does well teaching unit one but everything after that is on you if you make the incorrect decision of taking her class.

comment: Not worth the tuition

Objectively, the worst professor I have ever taken, and hopefully that I will ever take. Never answers questions clearly, even after the question is repeated to her. Her tests are about a month after the topics were "covered". She erases the example the second she finishes them. Very bad handwriting. I would give a 0/5 if it let me.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: She is a nice woman, but an objectively bad professor. Lectures are just examples pulled out of thin air that are often difficult to relate to the text book. Her best days are obviously behind her, she struggles to do basic arithmetic and often has to fix mistakes and gets stuck on simple algebra. Not 'difficult' just a headache of a class.
This is the worst professor ever. AVOID! grades only on homework and exams. Homework is submitted physically and does not respond much to questions.

First off, already rough being an 8 am course, but she required that if you wanted to retake one of the three exams at the end of the semester you only missed 3 classes which is virtually impossible. She is difficult to follow, her teaching style is only giving example problems and does not explain the foundational concepts to solve the problems.

Wanda's lectures can be hit or miss, but staying engaged and using unstuckstudy as a study aid can help. The tests cover what's shown in class, so going to lectures and doing practice problems is key. Overall, a challenging but manageable course.

Her best days are clearly behind her as a lecturer. Her exams are riddled with errors and bizarre problems, in class examples are pulled out of thin air with little continuity. If you aren't good enough to self-teach, you have a very large uphill battle to pass. You can retake one exam with good attendance, and she's helpful in office hours.
Wanda Means well, but she is clearly too old for teaching

Don't take this class unless you love to self-teach. The teacher is very quiet and oftentimes I can't understand what she is saying in the class. Her lectures are awful and the tests are unorganized. The exams are tough and there is no extra credit. She throws in questions from other topics she says won't be on the exam.
Her lectures are very difficult to follow. I would avoid taking this class if possible.

The instructor is hard to follow when she is teaching, she does not talk loud enough and has messy handwriting on the board. She skips steps in examples when doing it for the first time making it difficult to follow. It is clear she understands what she is going over but she is explaining like we already know. Go to Alexandra Niedden on YouTube.

I truly hate to give people bad wraps since she seems like such a nice woman, but she is the reason that I am switching out of math major. She is impossible to follow in lectures, skips several steps, and even when students ask her questions, all she does is leave them more confused than before. She is nice, but well past her time teaching.

She is a great professor. A nice person too. Believe me. I get that some people thinks that she lectures so much and her lectures sometimes are not so connected, but she is one of the better MATH-221 professor at this school. Her tests are definitely easy to study, she makes it pretty clear that what is going to be on the exams.

Wanda may be past her prime and makes mistakes when going through problems, but if you pay attention in lecture, you will learn. She also clearly cares about her students, only one homework assignment is given per week, and test question mimic homework and examples shown in class.

I'd recommend Wanda as a professor if the alternative is someone like Bautista.  Sure, her lectures are laughably bad, exams are riddled with typos, and course communication is often lacking.  However, she at least shows kindness and gives the impression that she wants her students to succeed.  She also allows formula sheets for exams

Wanda teaches the class quickly without much explanation. Most of the test questions are based on the homework but copy down everything she writes if you can read it because sometimes her exams have random curveballs from a single class example and no homework. The best way to study is do the homework multiple times and similar problems.

Expectations on whats going to be on exams, how she grades homework, how she grades exams? No one knows she has an incredibly unprofessional syllabus. Can't understand her, hear her or read her writing. Wanda's time is past due, maybe she was good 30 years ago. The fact RIT employs this woman when her rating is this low is concerning and quite sad.

Lectures are nothing more than loosely strung together problems with little to no context. Frequently skips steps with no elaboration and allows for no time for questions before the problem is erased and a new one begins.

Multivar is conceptually very difficult and Wanda's teaching style doesn't make it any easier. Lectures are just examples which aren't written anywhere else to look back on and the homework is graded randomly. No prep material is given for tests, so you have to look back through the homeworks (ignore niche material and most of the textbook).
Go to class, read the textbook, do the homework, and study and you'll do fine. Lectures are very hard to sit through but there are no better Multivar teachers at this time. Good luck.

Overall, I don't believe Wanda is a bad professor. Her class is hard, but it's mostly conceptual. I believe the only thing that you should look out for is her handwriting, as it is not the clearest always. Some people enjoy her class others don't I think it's the concept of the class though rather than the professor. Study and you'll do fine.

Homework is a large pool of problems, she decides which ones should be graded, and there's only 10 homework assignments altogether, never goes over them.Terrible lesson teacher/explainer, only does problems in class ripped from the textbook, and does a worse job of explaining them, makes SO many mistakes, even on the final exam test.

Wanda is so darn sweet I dislike giving her a bad rating, but she is by far the worst professor I have had yet at RIT. She does not go by textbook fully (dont rely on it for tests), she speaks too softly & doesn't fully followthrough with her own examples she seems to pull out of thin air

Attendance is not mandatory but if you want a chance at retaking one of her notoriously difficult exams, you better go to every lecture (sneaky new policy). She is earnest in her attempts to be a good teacher but she is past her prime. Accent, mistakes in examples, etc. make lectures incomprehensible. Only way to pass is to do it yourself.

In class, her handwriting is awful, she makes many calculation errors, and never understands student's questions. She grades homework based off 2-3 problems, leading to unfair grades. She provides literally 0 feedback on homework/tests. She doesn't explain much and if you lose focus for any more than 10 seconds you will be lost the rest of class.

Wanda is a very smart woman but is not a good teacher. Her thick Russian accent can be hard to understand and read what she writes sometimes. She rarely finished problems when explaining and leaves very little time for questions. The homework is all on Quizlet though, which really helped me.

Handwriting is difficult to read. She occasionally loses track of the problem on the board and has given wrong answers to problems, too. She is a quiet talker, so sit up closer than usual. She is incredibly sweet, though. However, if you are in her class, pay attention. n goes to M to N to m and back & forth. It's confusing at first. Good luck.

Horrible teacher. Constant mistakes, seemingly forgetting material, and she can't even read her own hand writing... Managed to get out of this class alive due to good grades on the tests, but that's from teaching myself. If she's your only option be a little scared but u can manage Anyone else is probably better. For those who do take her Ms are Ns

Notes are illegible and she is incapable of using computers, making it difficult for her to use MyCourses well. She makes mistakes in lecture material constantly, with every other problem getting derailed by some error. Be prepared to get a tutor and study the book. Might be a bad grader too, I shouldn't have done as well as I have in exams.

This professor was clearly capable and intelligent about 20 years ago. Unfortunately, the years and language barrier have not helped her. Online lectures were a nightmare. I stopped attending because her examples were incoherent, she often would make an error halfway through, and wouldn't stop and check her own work. I read the textbook to learn.

This class was incredibly painful. I have never cried over a class before, so if anything, this class gave me a new experience. The lectures were difficult to understand and feedback to questions were unhelpful. Heed my warning, avoid this class at all costs.

The lectures were uninformative and rambling and Wanda often didn't really understand what students were asking when they had questions. The worst professor I've had for a math class at RIT. The problems she teaches are convoluted, and she constantly marks tests/teaches problems wrong. Teaches way too fast, very poor at clarifying when a student is confused. No partial credit. Worst professor i've had in college by far.

Wanda is an interesting character. Teaches from example but you will pick the material up. Differential equations is like her strong suit and flows really well with her. Her accent is a little rough at first, but you will forget about that. Take her for differential equations if you want to remember the material.

DO NOT TAKE. I had to retake multivariable after failing the first time around. But even the first time around my test grades were at least above a 45. Wanda's a really nice lady- but she's a terrible teacher. She has a hard time articulating what she's doing and also tends to make a ton of mistakes during her teaching. comment: Wanda is one of the hardest professors I've taken thus far. She wasn't as horrible as every one said but definitely made me want to pull out strands of hair sometime. tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Accent was too thick for me to understand sometimes. Really bad teacher.

Wanda wasn't a terrible teacher, but I also wouldn't call her a great one. Her class examples were always convoluted and only slightly related to the topic at hand. The tests were fairly straightforward, but there were always some curveball questions. She takes off a lot of credit for small errors making the class very frustrating.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.  I had to do the majority of my learning outside of class and then in the end I had to drop it on the very last day that I could because it was bringing my GPA down. She does not prepare you well for the tests and she has absolutely no clarity. I wish I had listened to upperclassmen before when they told me not to take her.

Wanda is a pretty good professor once you get used to her teaching style.  She will first do a lecture to introduce new material, and will then do several examples on the board.  Her accent is thick, but it isn't hard to understand what she is saying.  Tests aren't hard if you do the homework.  She has great stories about living in the Eastern Bloc

Oh-la-la, I should have read the reviews. Wanda is a horrible teacher with an awful accent and horrible handwriting. She also make tons of mistakes while lecturing and gets argues with students when they try to correct her. She assigns ridiculous amounts of homework, that sometimes will take me 3hrs to complete. Avoid her at all costs.

Wanda is hands down the worst professor I've ever had at RIT. Her "syllabus" included  a copy of all of the chapters we will be covering in the book and that was it. She never included how she broke down the grades for the class or even the academic honesty policy. She always makes mistakes when she's lecturing and gets mad when you point it out.

Wanda has very good intentions, but could be more engaging in lecture. Although some of her in-class examples end up erroneous, but she goes back and fixes her small mistakes. Exams cover the elementary topics, which means even if you have a basic understanding of the concepts, you'll pass. Overall, do your homework, attend class; and you'll pass.

She was the worst professor when it came to teacher, so be prepared to work on your own. She does not explain the material very well, at least in class. However she is very nice and is very fair when it comes to the tests.

She is not the worst teacher. She does not explain the concepts in the most clear manner but she will teach you the calculus and how to apply the theorems. She is very fair on her tests and if you pay attention and do homework you will get an A in the class. Doesn't explain the calculus conceptually. Also, she is a very nice, genuine person.

She is literally the worst professor I've ever had regardless of the subject. You can't understand what she says, or follow along with anything she does in class, so be prepared to teach yourself. Her grading style is weird. I've gotten tests back with a lot of partial credit, and others with none. I tried asking for more, and she simply said no...

Gives one homework assignment each week and there are three or four exams and the final.  She doesn't really explain what she's doing, which makes the class a lot harder.  You need to be willing to study a lot on your own if you want to do well in the class, but she does do a lot of examples in class which are very similar to the test questions.

Wanda prepares you for her stuff. She basically teaches you how to solve the problems on the hw/test in class. She does have an accent, but she's not incomprehensible. Be warned, though, when asking questions, do not hesitate to ask several times the same questions and be blunt, because she might not answer the question on the first try.

Hard to follow sometimes but does a lot of examples on the board. Study hard and take good notes for the tests and final and you'll do fine because all of the exams are questions similar to the in-class examples.

I don't understand what Wanda has such a low rating. She was a great professor for Multivariable and Vector Calculus, and I would recommend her to any of my friends. The lectures were long and unorganized. She often gets lost mid-problem, making it even harder to understand what's going on. She doesn't speak clearly, even her handwriting is barely legible. I highly advise picking staff instead of Wanda if given the chance.
I honestly don't see why so many people don't like her. You will get over her accent, and her tests are VERY fair, but comprehensive. All in all, I had a good experience
really hard class

Even though she doesn't give a lot of homework or assignments, you are going to have to work extra for her to give you a good grade. Homework are not long and you have a week to submit them. Tests are not straightforward. Tests are hard. Detail is important. She is incredibly helpful outside of class, and probably one of the nicest professors.

Oh-la-la she's awful. Seriously skip out. You will not understand a single thing through her lectures so you just have to learn through someone else or by yourself. She messes up on problems 247 Test questions are hard to understand and difficult. Sometimes a chapter test could only have problems from one section. Seriously don't take it with her.

I thought Wanda was a clear, good teacher. Listen in lecture and she covers all the material you need to know. Take good notes and study and you should be fine. Has some mistakes as all math teachers do but not enough to disrupt class. Tests were pretty easy if you listened, did the homework, and reviewed. I would recommend her for MultiVar Calc.
Heavy Polish accent. Runs class in a very traditional way; lecture and homework from book. Class is easy if you pay attention and take notes.

Listen to everyone else, avoid at all costs!  I thought maybe I could take this teacher and it would be an easy A or B and I would just deal with her.. didn't work out very well.  Her tests are NOTHING like the homework or her class examples, class average on every test was below failing.  I repeat, avoid at all costs.

You will get used to her accent, Her tests are straight from the textbook and notes. She is EXTREMELY helpful and nice outside class and will. Her biggest problem is that even though she will solve a ton of problems in class, she will not cover the theory or overarching concepts behind the problems AT ALL which may be problematic in future courses.

If you mention you have Wanda on campus everyone has heard about how bad she is. I couldnt understand her. The tests were impossible and half the time the tests were so unclear. She a nice person, and tells little jokes here and there, but she is the worst teacher ive ever had. I never had an issue with math until now.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!!!!! She is a nice lady but is the worst teacher ever. She can't teach, is very unorganized, talks to the wall, you can't understand her accent, her tests are SUPER hard and is not clear what she wants you to do on her tests. She tests us on material that she never taught us or isn't in that section of the text. AVOID HER

She is the worst professor I've ever had.  She is impossible to understand, and always chooses the most roundabout ways to do problems, without showing alternatives.  Her tests are vague and unclear of what she wants from you.  She refuses to use mycourses because she doesn't believe in internet, so forget ever knowing your grade. Never Again.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The department made her change her tests because they were too easy and now they are ridiculous.  Cannot understand anything she says in class or anything she writes on the board. Homework on the other hand, is reasonable. Most material was self-taught through the assignments. Don't understand how or why she is still a professor

Very hard to understand in class - the mix of her accent, the math, and staying awake makes for a 2 hour hell. If you go to her office hours she is extremely helpful, but other than that you will end up teaching yourself something. DEFINITELY don't take an 8 am with her
Terrible. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. It is dull and you never learn anything. Makes mistakes at the board. Only does problem examples. There is always somebody sleeping in class.

Though she has an accent, she speaks slow enough you can understand her and is willing to repeat as necessary. Explains in detail, all homework answers are in the solutions manual and the tests are the easiest I have taken, just know your formulas. Great if you have trouble with the algebra portion of Calculus, you won't be tested on it.

Take someone else. Anyone else, really. 'Difficult to understand' is the understatement of the century. Homework is mandatory, but she does hand back the solutions with work, which is really awesome. Same for tests. Couldn't understand a word she said. Couldn't see the board. Be prepared to learn out of the book.
Hard to understand but thats not really the problem, she doesn't teach or explain anything at all and you pretty much have to teach it to yourself if you want to do well.

She has an accent, but its easy to understand. She writes small so sit in the front. Her test questions straight to the point, but don't ask things directly (nothing as basic as: Find the derivative of __). She gives out almost no partial credit, so check your work. Overall I thought she was a very good teacher. I would take another of her courses.
Honestly one of the best teachers at the institute. I strongly recommended her if you want an easy A and to understand multivariable calculus
Hard to understand. Does not teach. Hard to even understand test questions.

Just awful. Worst professor I've ever had. She cannot teach and lost our graded papers with her other class numerous times. Could not answer questions, half the time couldn't understand the question. I don't know what she does to make her a professor but she is awful. Avoid like the plague.

She was a true challenge at first. Her thick accent is hard to understand. She gets confused by questions and only goes over examples during class. She gets better later in the term as you start to understand her. She has a sense of humor. Frequently says "excuse me" for no reason and to no particular individual during class.

She know's what she's talking about but hasn't mastered how to pass her knowledge onto others. She can but funny at times but basically, you need to teach yourself the material if you want to do well. There is no partial credit on exams so make sure you study hard. She does come up with some clever examples to help you remember things.

AVOID AT ALL COST!!!! DOES NOT GIVES PARTIAL CREDIT. Only one hour exams... Disorganized. On one of my test (out of 8 problems) I got 6 perfectly right and the other 2 problems I was expecting partial credit. Guess what!!!?? I got a 69. NO PARTIAL CREDIT. AVOIDD!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Can't understand a thing she says. Explains things in the worst ways. Just avoid at all costs.

She is very funny at times but also very hard to understand. She works through problems very quickly, usually too quickly to follow. Her exams are nothing like the homework and are very difficult; she does not give much partial credit. If you are naturally good at math and can teach yourself she is a good professor otherwise she is very difficult.

Avoid.  Accent isn't as bad as some people claim; it's manageable.  What isn't manageable is the teaching quality.  Working through "such problems" have little to no bearing on the tests, and she makes more mistakes than any professor I have ever seen.

Refuses to answer direct questions from the students. Works through problems on the whiteboard while ignoring over-arching concepts and principles.  Does not come prepared to lecture the class beyond one small scrap of paper.

Refuses to answer direct questions from the students. Works through problems on the whiteboard while ignoring over-arching concepts and principles.  Does not come prepared to lecture the class beyond one small scrap of paper.

Very friendly teacher, with some corny jokes. You will get used to her accent quite easily. She teaches what you need to know but you still have to make use of the book to understand the material properly. Low level for homework and exams. Easy A if you study a little bit and do the homework.
She speaks 5 languages, and English is not one of her strong languages. Extremely hard to understand. Avoid.

She was a very hard teacher. Urgg so frustrating listening to her everyday gave hw out from the book every class. Test were mad hard. dont listen to tht guy up there must have been tht kid tht knew everything in class...
She is definitely one of the best math teachers at RIT.  I took her class last year and she was really helpful both in class and during her office hours.  Would definitely recommend taking her again

absolutely terrible. gives little to no partial credit on test, cannot understand her lectures, gives wrong equations, messes up examples more often than not, and gets confused by students questions so she just moves on and leaves it unanswered. do not take unless you want to teach yourself
Heavy accent and chicken scratch handwriting, that's all you need to know about Wanda.  By far the worst teacher I've had at RIT so far.  Avoid.

She isn't all that bad. Her writing and speech can be tough to understand, but she is kind of funny and definitely teaches what you need to learn. Definitely use the text to help. Homework level is low. Grading policy is nice especially if you can ace the Final
Her foreign accent makes her hard to understand sometimes and her writing is illegible but the homeworks and tests are very easy to pass if you understand the basics of the material.
An absolute joke, her class is an easy A if you read the book, do the homework, and DON'T listen to a word she says.

Wanda is a terrible professor.  She might know what she's talking about at some points, but can't teach it.  She stumbles over words, and her handwriting is ridiculous. However, if you go to class and do homework, you can pass.

Worst calc professor I have ever had. Stumbles upon her words. Did not know what the fundamental theorem of calculus was. Makes constant errors on the board. Thick accent. The only good thing about her is that homework counts at 30% and final replaces lowest test grade. Useless teacher, I taught myself. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!
Hard to understand most of the time, writing very hard to read, ridiculously hard tests
She isnt a very good teacher. avoid her if u can. i already knew the material before the class and the way she taught got me confused. Shes nice and all but shes a horrible teacher
Terrible. Confuses herself often, rarely understands students questions and can never answer them.
Avoid at all costs!

Seems easily frustrated by the material.  Confused by students questions so she leaves them unanswered.  When half the class leaves in the middle to go read the book themselves, something's wrong.  More like an independent study than a lecture.  If you skip and do the problems yourself, you're no worse off.
other instructors at the Rochester Institute of Technology should be ashamed to have her hold the same title as them.

She reads the book to you, gets confused and messes up examples. Don't commit anything she is saying to memory... It's probably wrong. When asked if the test is open book her reply was "I don't care".

Absolutely useless. Has really no right to be teaching us discrete math. Has trouble counting to 13 (she skipped 12).Much of her time is spent saying, "hokay" or "back up" because she makes so many mistakes. Many times (2/3) she would grade our tests, give them back to us, and not record the grades. She is horribly disorganized and lectures = crap.

She has a accent... and when she starts stuttering and repeating herself SHE DID SOMETHING WRONG and doesnt know where it is in her example.  The tests were fairly difficult.  She can't really explain things too clearly while talking, but if you follow along in the example you should be fine... that is if she doesnt mess the numbers up midway.
I had her for multivariable calculus.  She has a strong accent, but it is managable.  She goes through examples in detail, and draws very good pictures that help understand the topic.

Not the best teacher, but very nice.  Willing to help if you need it.  An easy class if you have a backround in the information; she is a good teacher to have to review stuff but not to learn it for the first time.

She's easily confused during examples, the class is a waste of time she doesn't explain anything, she assigns homework but doesn't collect it, gives weekly quizzes directly out of the homework and you can use your notes and your book if you ask, and we had formula sheets for the test, probably all to make up for her lack of teaching
Has a very strong accent, but nice overall.  She actually let us use our notes and book and all three tests.  If you can handle accents, then take her class.
Easy...not bad just do work
you dont undertand her, she doesnt know how to explain things, and shes always making mistakes for everything
Her tests are not incredibly difficult and her quizzes are easy if you know the material.  She doesn't assign homework and attendance is not mandatory.
Unless you already know the topic, avoid her like the plague.
Very friendly and personable once you scratch the surface. Very thick accent.  Moves very quickly through the course material. Always willing to give extra help.
No Comments

Horrible teacher.  I never missed a class and sat in the front.  She still never knew my name.  I couldnt understand anything because of her accent, she gives no homework to help bring up grades and her hand writing is unreadable.
She's no nonsense...kinda difficult ..moves a long soooo fast! Im still writing down the problem when she has already finished explaining it.  I cant learn this way.

Kinda hard to understand, and just teaches out of the book. Still cant figure out how we're supposed to do the problems when she cant. Oh, and it is a she, for whoever didnt know why his name was Wanda :P.
Has a strong east european accent.Very helpful outside of class.Makes sure that everyone understands the subject.Exams are easy.I can't figure out why his name is Wanda!
Difficult final

(She retired after Fall 2017) Prof. Clark is one of the most caring professors I've known. Lots of homework and a few heavy tests, but she is in Bates every weekday in the afternoon to help you. 5% extra credit if assignments are turned in a day early. Lectures are very theoretical, but still clear. Her class was great, she will be missed!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Dr. Clark is a tremendous professor. There are innumerable opportunities to learn from her. She is incredibly accessible and very kind. Make sure you do your work, and you will learn a lot from her.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']
comment: Dr. Clark is a sweet lady who knows everything there is to know about Calc pretty much off the top of her head. On top of being really kind and patient, she allows you to be flexible and offers a lot of extra help outside of lecture. She does indeed care for the mathematical success of her students.

Best math professor I've ever had. I hated math in highschool but she got me really interested in the subject, her Bates tutoring hours are super accessible and daily, and she's super patient and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. Probably the best teacher at RIT, she's amazing, so thankful I had such a good experience with college math

Professor Clark is the best professor I've had so far! She is always available for help in Bates and in her office and she is very good at resolving any questions that you have. Her tests are very fair and she gives extra credit for early assignments. Also, she is very understanding if you're out sick. HIGHLY recommend!  AMAZING professor!!!
Best math professor I've ever had. Always available for help at Bates study center, so patient and genuinely caring.

If you are opposed to doing workshops and HW or already have a hectic class schedule, Dr. Clark's classes are not for you. Prepare for a lot of assignments but also be prepared to walk away actually learning the material. One of the most patient professors I've ever had during my time at RIT. Is very frequently in Bates Study Center to help.

She is such a great teacher who will help you with anything you need. She is almost always available for help and offers tons of extra credit. Just try a little bit and you can easily get an A. She doesn't have too many hard set deadlines and accepts late homework, so just don't loose track of all the stuff you have to turn in.

Fantastic professor for anyone who is willing to actually put in effort and learn the material. I had her for Project Based Calc II, and we got 5 points extra credit for every early assignment. 4 worksheets per week and one homework, all really relevant to the material. She was always in Bates from 4-6 for extra help. Highly recommend.

She is one of the best professors I've ever had the privilege to have. She sincerely wants you to pass and gives you plenty of opportunities to catch up if you fall behind. Not only would I take her again but I'd suggest her to anyone that has her as an option. It's hard to think of a better professor.
Clear and great at depicting manipulation to derive functions and definitions. Great at showing examples. Verbal explanations are a bit more clumsy, but more often she shows an example.

There is so much extra credit built into this class. Each homework/workshop assignment has a 5% bonus if it is handed in early. These assignments combined make up a greater percentage than exams, slightly. Exams are straight forward. If you put in the time for the assignments, you'll get an easy A. Dr. Clark is also always available for help.

Professor Clark is a very sweet lady who provides many opportunities to succeed. She assigns a lot of homework, but offers help sessions that allowed me to get an A while also understanding the material. It's a lot of work and the tests are long, but she is a great teacher who grades fairly and does a great job of actually teaching the material.

A wonderful professor, she goes over the material very well and gives you plenty of time in-class to try practice problems and go over the material.   All of the course assignments are on her website as early as day one, and any work you finish early, you get extra credit on.   Tests are straight forward, and she tries her best to prep us.

Really learned a lot from her. Was in the Bates center all the time for extra help which she was willing to give. Fair grader and knows what she's talking about. There was a ton of homework so make sure you have extra time to spare to get it all done.

I took Clark for both MATH181 and MATH182. As someone who isn't great at algebra but loves calculus, I did very well in her class. She does give a LOT of homework, but I thought it was really worth it. They assignments are very similar to her exams which means the exams aren't bad at all.

Very nice lady. Accepts late work, allows make up exams, and gives you lots of bonus points. Her lectures, however are quite boring. I suggest only taking her if you know the material well and want an easy grade. Otherwise, you're very likely to fall asleep in her class.

Professor Clark is awesome. Be warned that it is a lot of work, but it is easily manageable. A lot of extra credit opportunities. A downside though is the fact that you're not taught *why* certain methods work or the derivation of the theorems. But, hey, that's what the book is for!

The best math professor I have had by far. This is the second class I have taken of hers and I don't regret it. Her class is very structured and she shows plenty of examples and is willing to explain when you don't understand either during or outside of class. Her worksheets provide useful practice. However, sometimes she confuses herself.

Absolute best math professor. Anyone here giving her a poor rating is most likely due to their poor effort and laziness. She knows her math inside and out. You could walk up and ask her any question from any class, she will think, and tell you how to approach it. Amazingly brilliant and easy to talk to. Always available for help. Do the work.
Fantastic professor. I didn't realize we had from the book homework for six weeks and so I had a D in the class. She let me make up all six weeks for full credit. Nicest. Professor. Ever.
Lots of work but there are no surprises. Weekly homework, workshop labs, worksheets for each class period. The review tests are very similar to the tests that are given.

Had her for all my first year calculus courses (pbc2, pbc3, and multivar).  Take this professor for your calculus classes.  There is lots of work, but it is worth it.  She is available for help.  If something wasn't clear in lecture, the worksheets step through the material well.  Exams are fair.  She keeps a timely update of your grades online.

This professor is extremely helpful. She answers questions well and is available every day M-F in Bates. She has a lot of smaller assignments that make up a decent portion of your grade, and posts practice tests online that are very similar to the test. VERY HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

Easy teacher. A lot of HW and Labs though, but since they are required they result in doing well on the tests. The tests are easy plus she gives you a practice exam that is almost the same as the test.

Dr. Clark has been the best professor that I have had at RIT. I wish she was teaching Multi next quarter. She is a very liberal grader. There is a lot of work. Something like 9 homeworks, 27 worksheets, 15 labs and 5 exams. But she is always available to assist you if you get stuck. Gives extra credit if you hand in your assignments early.

The material is the level to be expected, but she is one of those profs who talk to the board and stand in front of what they write. the homework covered things we didn't know how to do in class and her grading is very inconsistent.  Honestly I have no idea how she has such a high rating here, everyone in her classes strongly dislikes her.

She was an extremely good teacher for very difficult material.  Her lectures were concise and notes were understandable.  The worksheets definitely helped for learning the material.  The only thing I disliked, the homework included applications we hadn't learned (had to read sections of the textbook in order to do the problem).

Easily the best math teacher I've ever had. I haven't done any calculus since high school and had no issue just jumping into multivariable with her as the teacher. She's extremely helpful and always in the Bates study center. Exams can be difficult, but homework provides a good grade buffer (and she gives extra credit fro early submissions).

The Doc is very kind & very willing to help. However, she assigns a lot of work. Expect 2 worksheets every class period and book work due Friday. You do get class time for these but it usually isn't enough. On the final you get to use a cheat sheet but it tends to run 3-4 hours and be pretty difficult. Would definitely take again. Amazing Prof!

She's a great teacher and very interesting. She will spend the time to teach you outside of class, and she spends 2 hours a day in Bates, but if you just drop by, she'll also help you. For honors kids: she'll let you make the class count for honors as long as you do her three extra problems every 3 weeks or so.

Had her for calc 2,3 and diff eq.  She gives 5% EC for early work and is always there to help you.  Definitely recommended for anyone taking the calculus classes.  She is very organized and hands everything back the next class including hw, tests and labs.  Got A's for all 3 classes

Dr. Clark has it all: the talent to solve complicated mathematical problems, the skill to teach her knowledge to others, the motivation to create her own labs and worksheets, the dedication to grade all work promptly and comprehensively, and the conscientiousness to take the time to address all questions to the satisfaction of their posers.
Her lectures can be difficult to follow at times, but she is incredibly helpful when you ask for help.

Sometimes the work can be hard but she's always able to help. She's walked me through entire problems, she's checked my homework for errors before letting me turn it in, she's just a sweety. She tends to make mistakes in her notes and examples, but if you stay on top of things you can pick out the mistakes and she'll correct them.

Professor Clark was a fantastic professor in terms of how much she was able to teach me. Unfortunately though she gives quite a huge load of homework (though she packs in 5% EC). Other than that she is very helpful in her office and the tutoring center and is a very kind woman who will explain something right after the exam if you are interested!
Had her for calc 2 and 3 and now diff eq. She gives a lot of work but it's worth it. She's extremely helpful if you don't understand something.

Project-Based Calc III: Awesome professor! Only 40% of grade is exams. Workshop + worksheet every class + weekly homework = a lot of work; however, it is worth it. Extra 5% credit for handing in any assignment a day early. TONS of office hours..she will practically do your HW for you she is so helpful. EASIEST WAY TO GET AN A IN CALC III! TAKE HER!

I took Dr. Clark for the entire calculus sequence 282,283 and 305. She is the BEST professor I have ever taken and I do not say that lightly. You have to do the work but if you do, you will understand calculus. She is willing to answer any questions and is always available to help.

Worst class. She gets frustrated when you ask questions. Gives 8 packets a week that are at least 4 pages each plus about 20 book problems. Labs are very hard. Our TA didn't even know how to help us half the time. Tests are every other week and the material is on topics we covered 2 weeks before. Just way too much work and stress.

She is the best professor ever!  She gives a lot of work but it is all very manageable.  He lectures are very clear and the tests are based on exactly what she teaches. She gives a lot of partial credit and is always available for help at any time.

Dr. Clark was a great professor. A typical week consists of 3 worksheets, 3 labs, and bookwork. They are all pretty challenging but I've never gotten less than a 95 on any of them. She's always willing to help and anything that you turn in early, you'll get five extra credit points on. Exams are every other Friday and they are easy. Take Dr. Clark!

Gives alot of work. 1-2 worksheets per class. But the work is do-able. She gives you time at the end to do it as well. Extra credit for handing work in early. Very nice and approachable. Tests are a big difficult, but if you study and ask for help when you need it you'll be fine. Definitely one of the best math teachers at RIT.

She gives really good notes and is very approachable. The daily worksheets aren't that bad and she will always answer any questions. Take advantage of the extra credit on the worksheets and homework...They can really give you a cushion for the Final Exam. The only tricky thing could be the exams.

Assigns a lot of work, but it's doable. Lectures are easy enough to follow if you are paying attention. Extra credit for assignments done early. Practice exams online are helpful. Though fast paced and a heavy work load, I would definitely recommend for a thorough understanding of the material and applications.

Very nice lady, but assigns excessive amounts of homework, does not explain the relevance of topics, does not include practical examples in class or on assignments, and goes out of her way to make lectures thoroughly incomprehensible.  Writes with one hand, erases with the other; stands in front of example problems.
Teacher gives really hard and pointless homework. She has no life and grades for hours on end. Her tests are really easy I have a 100 average, but her workload is off the deep end
Awesome math teacher! Lots of homework but a ton of chances to pull up your grade. One of the nicest ladies you'll ever meet.

Worksheets are a joke and homework is pretty easy cause shes in the lab alot and answers all your questions.  Also very clear teacher and makes things really easy to understand.  Tests aren't bad at all and she puts up practice exams that are close to the real thing.  Labs are a joke you just click and press the mouse.  Plus shes like my grandma.

Worksheets are pretty easy, especially if you see her for help on them in the study center, HW is usally easy for same reason.  Labs can be pretty hard, and Tests can be difficult but cheat sheets are alowed.

Extra credit on hw and worksheets if handed in early. Worksheets are sometimes impossible though. Tests are often vague/ambiguous, but usually (not always) similar to the practice test she posts online before each test. If you do the work you should be fine in getting at LEAST a B, probably an A.
Very easy but alot of work Very very helpful
The best. Nice old lady, very helpful and clear. gives fair amount of work. If you do the homework and worksheets, A- guaranteed.
Awesome teacher. Gives a lot of work. If you do the work you can't fail. She gives opportunity to make up worksheets. Her grading policy greatly benefits you.

Doctor Clark is a good prof. Her teaching style is great and she hands out worksheets on the material that are very helpful. However, she gives way too much homework. Despite this, I definitely recommend her.
Very approchable, very helpful.  Lots and lots of HW, almost rediculous, but if you do it, it boosts your grade alot, and you will ace the tests and quizes
Great teacher.
great teacher, uses mathematica
One of the best professors I have had at RIT. He is very knowledgeable and constantly looking for feedback from his students.

design thinking and concept develepment is easy and he knows it. He likes that it's easy. It's not supposed to be hard he says. He even admits he has RIT come after him saying his class is too easy and he says "ik, that's just the way the subject is". This, my amigos, will feel like a 5th grade class. do ur essay (no more than 1 page!) and get ez A
Generally unhelpful and makes it hard to succeed. Not very understanding or compassionate. I would not recommend this professor to anyone who does not like unfair and unjust policies and procedures.

Zeke is a great professor, he's really down to earth and wants you to succeed. He said in our first lecture that he tries to give as many As as possible, so if you participate in lectures and do the work, he'll reward it.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Easy going guy. Willing to help you along. Lectures are very short, most of the class is working on a semester long project. If you put the time into the project, it won't be a problem.
Zeke's Design Thinking class during student exchange program made me pursue a career in Design Thinking after graduating from RIT. 'nuff said.

Zeke is funny and cares for his students. He is very approachable and gives honest feedback. His purpose is not to create a stress culture in his classes but to help students go out of their comfort zone to learn about the cases and apply theories for analysis. If you put efforts, its easy to get an A in his class. Pay extra attention to deadlines!

Design Thinking & Concept Development was one of my favorite classes. Zeke taught it in a non-traditional way where it wasn't so much about the grades but about the fact that you were learning and truly utilizing what he was teaching. You get to pick your semester long group project and honestly you learn a ton about product design. Easy A
Great guy.  Tries his best to make a boring subject interesting.  Definitely recommend taking him.
great management class, great guy

Zeke is a great professor, really helpful and very good about getting the information across.  However, due to some serious circumstances outside of the classroom, he struggled keeping up with grading and filling us in on project details.  Super nice guy, would recommend him any day if he comes back after this semester.
Take this professor for Strategy and Innovation. Should be no debate.
He comes off as a hard teacher but in the end he aint too bad
this is hands down worst person i have met in school so far.

The MOST condescending, LEAST understanding professor I have ever had. I would highly recommend NOT taking his classes. At least twice as demanding as my other Anthro class worth the same amount of credits.
He is very rude and hard professor. He gives a lot of assignments which are time consuming. Midterm and final examinations are long papers.
The man is like Steve Jobs, minus the innovation, genius and creativity. So basically just an ass. Fortunately his reign of terror is over, a gift for the next generation of engineers

Probably my worst major-specific professor to date. Topic seems straightforward with lab and reports, but he makes it much more difficult. Tries to act like a "supervisor" but comes off passive aggressive/arrogant. I get reports need to be clean and concise but he's more of a nitpicker. I suggest you make good chemistry with your team and tank.

Parthum is easily the worst professor I've had at RIT to date. He gives the impression that his assignments are open-ended and is therefore vague on details, but has very specific expectations that are never stated. He acts contradictory as well, and is very difficult to talk to due to the fact that he never allows others to finish a sentence.

He is an extremely hard grader. He will say one thing, then say the complete opposite thing the next. I've gotten into a habit of recording his lectures because he takes back his word so many times. He will take points off of your report if it isn't the carbon copy version of what he wants. You'll have to read his mind to get a good grade.

Average grade on his labs is in the 60s because everybody loses 20+ points on the landmines he's hidden in each lab...of course he never mentions this until well after he's harshly graded you. Grader tells you how to title graphs & grades fairly as a result; Parthum randomly takes over a section's grading & penalizes you for "bad graph titles".

I don't know what the other students problems are (maybe they did not get it, or were too lazy to do the work) but Prof. Parthum has been one of the best teachers I have had here at RIT. You may have to work hard and he is VERY detail orientated, but I am paying a LOT to go here and I learned more in his classes than anyone else.
Good teacher... knows a good amount(a huge amount about wafers)... can be hard at times at grading... good tests and quiz's... an amazing lecturer and clear concepts...

Overly strict, but in the end it works out kindasorta. He treats his students like employees to the end. I agree with the previous; I get the impression that he fabricates many stories and experiences. Don't get the book (nontrad), read the notes for quizzes, write the papers well, kill yourself for the project and with great luck you will get an A

Another one of the MET program's worst.  He may be qualified to make wafers, but he is not qualified to teach.  Lecture notes are scans of the textbook, and he just reads them.  A senior level class and the only thing i know from going to class is that he's wasting my time.  Fire the Xerox and Kodak leftovers and get some qualified teachers.
very good teacher highly recomeneded. He knows his stuff and is good at teaching and answering questions.  He is a fair grader.
A very informative professor with industry experience and insight.  Makes you do your work, but is very available for help.
Good guy, knows his stuff. One of RIT's up and coming professors.

Parthum was ok. His quizzes were very unclear. He admited to putting trick questions on his quizzes. Just gives you notes right from the book. Fairly lenient on grading too. You will learn more with him than with Castro, but Castro grades easier.

Had him for astronomy. He would manage to cram at least 35 slides every lecture and after the 2nd week I gave up trying to actually take the notes. Also, since he relied so heavily on Powerpoint slides, we didn't have time for in class problems. Class was overall boring and difficult which is disappointing because astronomy is so interesting.

He's not a bad person, but he kinda sucks at teaching. He's genius when it comes to astronomy/astrophysics, but won't make you understand the basic kinematics and such. Gives a tone of in class stuff. Uses WebAssign, which is waaay harder than his test. Which, btw, have a little to do with whatever we do in class. He's really willing to help thou.

hes a good guy. i didnt have any trouble in the class. he is always helpful if you ask question. not the most interesting lectures but the rest is good. tests were easy if you know your stuff. not an intimidating guy, very laid back.
He's a good guy, always willing to help you. great 1 on 1. kinda boring in class. grades tons of in class stuff, that gets kinda annoying.  curves the tests, not terribly hard to do well in.

Phil's awesome! He's really funny and laid back (in grading too)which makes a required class more enjoyable. He made me more confident in my writing and offers good feedback and will have a conversation with you about whatever. If you do the homework and essays, you're in good shape. And I feel like I finally learned how to write at a higher level!

Phil's hilarious. The top choice for a writing class at RIT. He's a great guy and really willing to work with you to make your writing better. Class is discussion based so just have something to say and you'll do fine. Highly recommend him. 10/10 would take again.

Phil Shaw is a RIT one-off. He wants to go home as much as you do, so he's super laid back. I always looked forward to class because he makes the discussions engaging and hilarious. Definitely take him as a professor for any class.

Gives amazing feedback on all big assignments and there were only three major papers due for the entire semester and he gave plenty of guidance throughout the whole process. There were smaller discussion posts due before almost every class and we went over them in class each day. Overall, a great guy who loves his job and is always willing to help.
He's a bro. Gives out great feedback, and is a respected guy. Loves helping out students and is there for you if you have trouble with a paper. Would take more classes with him if I can!

Super awesome guy and really loves his job. Can I also mention he's adorable? He really cares about students to succeed and makes writing actually fun. The only class I enjoyed attending at 9 in the morning.
Great teacher for summer bridge!

Very cool, relaxed, open guy. Has a casual attitude and treats students like equals, encouraging original thought and honest responses. Assignments aren't super structured, so you have to really be willing to think about what you're going to write, but the open-endedness lets you explore only the parts you're interested in.

He's hilarious and really laid back. He's clear, concise, and approachable. He likes, and often shares, funny videos. Phil is also wicked adorable. He'll help you if you need it. The coursework is interesting and really goes where discussion takes it. Our class spent a lot of time discussing power, authority, and control in the context of writing.

What a guy! Gives mini discussion post assignments and one final paper over the entire semester rather than many papers. Unbelievable sense of humor, yet he gets the material across, he's also an easy grader. Would highly recommend taking his class!

Such a bro. His teaching style: inclusive to those with English as their second language, caters to the students, and is awesome; even his unlikely story of how he got into academia is awesome. Cares about his students learning, but not at the cost of their GPA; do take!

Great Professor and probably most entertaining classes that I've ever taken, and it was both interesting and informative. This guy takes a throwaway gen-ed intro class and turns it into something that is as fun as it is valuable. It is worth actually taking this class for this professor. There is a decent amount of work but it is not difficult
awesome guy...
Good teacher, fair grader, funny, hasmproved my writing

Keeps class interesting with his humor and stories, all the while getting the material across in ways that are understandable. Very fair grader and is always available for help via email or office hours! Great professor
Class is tons of fun, was probably the only reason why i would ever have a 8am class. fair grader, super helpful, and really funny.
BEST TEACHER EVER!
Great Teacher, hard grader. Very funny and likes to tell stories in class

He keeps the class fun, it is never taken too seriously. There is a lot of freedom in your writing selection, and he treats students like equals without losing his authority over the class. extremely fair grader,and helpful and available if you need to go over papers.

Very good teacher, makes a dull subject interesting with an element of humor. The class uses an effective textbook, which lays out writing in an understandable set of 5 sections. Very down-to-earth, and is quite personable. I recommend people to take his classes!
AWESOME !!!!
He's funny and entertaining. Makes the boring material interesting. Fair grading. Helpful. Definitely recommended!

comment: Highly enjoy Professor Wadle, is very funny and tries to make Critical thinking compelling to his students. The class itself was difficult and sometimes it was hard to fully understand what he was saying, so going to office hours with him is highly recommended. Most quizzes are take-home and they can be easy if you pay attention and take notes.
Great guy overall. Very funny, knowledgeable, and smart. Informal, and a great teacher.

Professor wadle is a great Professor. I didn't really enjoy his class a lot just based on the topic, but he tried his best to make things enjoyable and his class is structured in a way where you will pass as long you do the work. Would take him again for sure

Professor Wadle is very chill. I recommend taking his 103 for anyone looking for a simple, relaxed, intuitive, and practical ethical perspective. The textbook was nominally required, but not doing the readings didn't really hurt my understanding. open-note quizzes, no projects or group work, handful of 2ish page homework sheets throughout.

TERRIBLE TEACHER! Can't teach at all and you can barely understand him through his labored breathing and his ums and ers. OLD AND HAS TENURE! Run away! My class of 60 ended as a class of 12 (no lie) I dropped week three, my friends followed.
This guy is just a senile old fart that needs to retire. He's completely incompetent and inept. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS! I seriously can't understand why he's still a teacher

First of all, a really sweet and approachable man.  Always willing to help, but rarely can.  All notes are online and those are clear enough.  Listening in class may hurt you more than help.  Allows a lot of make up credit for tests and quizzes.  All of the homework is online and fairly easy.
Good Guy...REALLY BAD Teacher. He would try to help but it never really worked. Students would correct simple and big mistakes made by him during class. He is getting old and seemed a bit senile.
WORST PROFESSOR EVER. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS.

It seems as though Professor Hart really tries, unfortunately he is just horrible at teaching. He spends 2 hours lecturing based on slides, this doesn't aid in the learning process because he is completely incomprehensible. He often adds material to the tests that has not properly been covered and assigns copious amounts of homework. Avoid!

I should have read the ratings. It is the same as most other people's comments. He doesn't follow his schedule, skips around chapters, and gives out unexpected quizzes. Half of the time, he makes mistakes when he's teaching the class. We never use the textbooks in the course either, which doesn't help. He needs to retire.
Please AVOID this professor...every comment on board is very true. I'm taking his class now and if i could have avoided him, I would have but he was the only one teaching the evening course.

He is just the sweetest person ever!!!! he explains really good and is helpful outside of class!!! there are bad reviews for him because students simply don't understand math! take him if you get the chance!!! I got an A :)

HEED THESE WARNINGS! This man cant teach to save his life. He will start reviewing a test with I cant believe you guys got this wrong, and do it on the board himself and stare at his answer wondering why its wrong. 10 minutes  later students will point out several mistakes. This professor will make your course 1000 times harder

He loves teaching and math, but there comes a point where it is better for society if you just call the quits.  Much too old and incoherent to be teaching.  Does not follow syllabus at all, puts surprise material on tests that was not forewarned, and constantly makes mistakes while 'teaching'. Unless you already know the material DO NOT TAKE!
It is difficult to learn in class and he is very confusing , everyone ends up lost; if you come for an hour of extra help, however, you get everything figured out.

Overall, he is a very nice guy.  He's also pretty flexible when it comes to grading as long as you come to class and don't sleep. Unfortunately, he can't teach.  At all.  I was confused the enitre quarter.  He gets confused when he's teaching.  Often, students correct him during class.  Nice guy, but probably needs to retire.

Restating the same words louder does not help students understand.  Managed to take my interest in taking additional math for my degree and turn it into not wanting to take another math class again.  Only reason I did as well as I did, is because my wife is great at statistics.

I thought I would do fairly well in this class, but it was aweful.  Prof. Hart is wayyy too old to be teaching...he's basically incomprehensible.  He skips all over the place--assignes and grades homework before he teaches the material<<that sucked.  Possibly the worst prof. Ive ever had.

He's a nice guy, but he really shouldn't be teaching.  Made mistakes on nearly every question through the quarter. Students had to correct him all the time. He made a lot of stuff far more difficult than it had to be. Doesn't check or grade homework, but do it anyway. And the book really sucks, doesn't explain things well either.

YO..DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM TEACHING!!!!!YOu will seriously regret it. He has no clue wat hes doing. He constantly making mistakes and his teaching style just sucks. The only way to pass this class is to learn from the book cuz the teacher will not help you what so ever.

ths professor was late, unprepared, unable to hear our questions, unable to answer our questions.  this professor was unable to correctly answer his own math problems on the board without the class correcting several mistakes.  this course was SELF tought. and SELF learned.  the professor make each class harder and more confusing.  this professor w

This professor is all over the place. Does not follow his syllabus, teaches things two weeks ahead of schedule so you can't keep up. Makes a ton of mistakes himself, should not be teaching college level.
If you have trouble with math, do not take his class since he does not explain things well.  Otherwise, it is fairly easy since he always allowed test-corrections.
DO NOT TAKE HIS ALGEBRA CLASS!!! He is the most senile, clueless, and near retarded teacher I have ever had and probably in the world.
dudes an idoit sucks at math and is confusing as all hell pray your good at math or he will mess you up
Professor Hart has no social skills whatsoever.  Anyone that has not had precalculus will struggle if they don't teach themselves.
flexable with grades but he makes a lot of mistakes on homework and on borad in class.

(for management sciences)This class was bad, thank god I took algebra in high school and just needed a refresher course, Hart cannot teach. He makes MANY stupid mistakes when trying to teach you the material, it's easier just to learn it from your book. He's nice and does TRY to be helpful though...
