comment: Dr. Hosseini is great. Very informative class.

Professor Hosseini is the best Professor I have had in college. His passion for the topics he teaches really motivates you to give him the same energy in return and because of that you end up learning a lot. Gives a lot of insight into how to examine the structure of a problem, and how that would affect how a possible algorithm would be designed.

Professor Hosseini was very well versed in the subject and encouraged us in every sense to take up the subject and perform better. Had a significant amount of examples for the course material. Has good knowledge on the course topic. Gave super good feedback on the course research project and how we could make it better.

Professor Hadi is enthusiastic about algorithms and uses a lot of in-class activities during lectures. Homework required problem-solving but didn't require formal proofs. Reviews of previous lectures were also given at the beginning of each lecture.

Currently taking him for Algo 261. He really cares about the student and one of the best professor in RIT CS Department. Even in the 9AM class, his lecture does not make you sleep and its also very interactive with lots of jokes and insights. May he sustain this energy for rest of his teaching career. But in general, this course is really hard.

Professor Hosseini is a fantastic professor and a great person. His lectures are super informative and he covers all the material in-depth while still keeping it relatively accessible (sometimes moving a bit too slow). Great at answering questions and gives tons of examples. Homeworks are hard but not impossible, but the final was insanely hard.
Loves his students and really cares about their success. Covers a lot and does so very well in an interactive way. Could not recommend him more.
Amazing and very knowledgeable. You will not get bored; he uses various things such as videos and group work to keep the class interested and involved. Definitely take the course.

He is a very passionate professor who really tries to make the material interesting and makes sure the students actually understand the material. I think honestly if you share the same passion, he is definitely a person you would like to take classes under or do research.

Great at organizing class and ensuring it was productive and inclusive to all. He is very enthusiastic about the material and teaching the material to his students while encouraging students to think deeply

Fantastic professor! Great at organizing class and ensuring it was productive and inclusive to all. He is very enthusiastic about the material and teaching the material to his students while encouraging students to think deeply about the material.
Great lecturer and he posts his powerpoints on mycourses.  Each homework has two weeks to be completed, but they can be pretty challenging.
Great person to add to your professional network. Very informative, kind and experienced professor.

Very Group based, not a hard class, she goes over everything that will be on the exams and tells you a lot about the short answers, you just need to take note of it. The textbook is helpful, but the slides are the most helpful. Be prepared to present twice during the semester, don't slack off, do your work and just put in some effort.

Not bad of a professor. Her lectures were a bit boring but its fine. The exams were pretty average, no cheat sheets though. At least the final exam was take home. Not too much work. Lets me know what to improve on and fix for better grade on homework. Project was graded heavily.

Prof. McGowan is simply the best. If you can take a class with her, do it. She is one of the most student-focused professors I've had and it is clear that she actually cares about the students and our learning when making her lesson plans and assignments.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Prof McGowan has solidified my interest in business and I am very excited to continue learning from her for the rest of my college career. Class was very hands on and while lectures bordered on boring, it's ok because this is an intro level class.

She is perfect for incoming freshmen. She cares about her students, and gives you everything you need to succeed in your future years as a student. She is easy to talk to, and all the assignments are very outlined as to what is required. Couldn't ask for someone better, everything in her class is important and applied in the real world.

She was a great teacher, made the lectures fun by involving her idea of jokes. The class was very fun because there was a lot of group work which helped me become close to people in the class. She loves when people participate and she loves talking outside of class. She's super sweet and very understanding of everything.

Molly is great and her tests are very easy. She gives you a study guide of each tests and 95% of the test is based on her study guide. The other 5% is extra information that you might or might not need. It would definitely recommend her class. Easy participation grade by bring in news and engaging in lecture.

She spends the half the class having kids do individual presentations on managerial topics and the other half lecturing. Two very straightforward tests. Some journal assignments outside of class. She's very nice and caring about the students. Passionate about her topic, wants kids to do well.

Two tests that are almost all multiple choice and pretty self-explanatory. Big on participation and presentations. Lectures can be slow and boring. You can easily get away with just surfing the web in the back of class.

Very idealistic and believes in the horribly written book she uses for the class. Naive, often did not address high level questions, wholesome, and gave a large amount of busywork. She could possibly be better, but the Leading Others class is trite and painful.
She is a cool professor, but her monotone voice will lull you to sleep. Other than she knows alot. I took her Leading others class and i learned some good stuff
Experiential leadership was a great class, and I learned alot.
Somewhat helpful in class. Not always the best at explaining. Homework is all optional and ungraded. Final exam replaces every grade you had in the course that was lower than it.

He is genuinely concerned about his students learning the material and will make sure answer any question students have. Homeworks are handed in for completion, quizzes are hw problems, and tests are just retooled quiz problems. He also has a hilarious dry sense of humor.

I've had him for Multivar and Diff Eq. There are 2 tests, a final, optional homework and 10 quizzes.  Each quiz is an exact homework problem. Every grade lower than the final is replaced by it. Some of the lectures can by confusing but he is willing to explain and really tries to get students to understand. If you do the homework you should get an

Dull lectures. Okay teacher. Quizzes are homework problems. Will drop any grade lower than your final. Assumed you already knew too much. Methods weren't rigorous enough for a math class. Gave you an idea how to do problems, but you really had to work on your own to fully grasp things.

Professor Hamilton is an excellent math teacher. If you attend class and pay attention, he will teach you the material. He makes sure his students understand everything and is very open to questions. His tests really are no surprise, they are much like the homework. I would highly recommend him.

He is extremely helpful and always willing to take the time to explain anything you ask. He also tries very hard to make sure students understand the material rather than just talking and writing on the board. I would recommend him.
The goat. That's all you need to know...

Probably the best professor I've ever had at RIT. Lot of work, yes, but it never felt like busy work or that it was getting out of hand. (and if it was, was very easy to get help) Always looked forward to the class, felt like it brought a lot of CEs together since it is so group based. Highlight of my degree has been IDE w/ Soldavini 100%

Amazing professor. Lectures were informative and flowed well. Homeworks are easy if you paid attention to lectures/slides. Exams were fair and strongly tested your understanding. The labs will take up 10+ hours to work on per week, so allocate enough time for that. Make sure you choose your group mates wisely, it makes or breaks your experience.

IDE is a difficult class, but Soldavini teaches it the best. She's funny, smart, and is great at lecturing and making sure everyone understands the topic. The class is very group-lab heavy, and the final project is difficult! Expect to put in a lot of effort for this class, as its a writing intensive class with a lot of programming and hardware.

Very helpful during office hours and her exams are very fair. The labs are pretty difficult but that makes sense since this is a lab heavy class. The IEEE papers can take FOREVER to write and also a learning curve on how to write them. The TAs for this class are also very helpful during office hours since some labs are a bit confusing.

This is easily one of the best 3D animation professors at RIT. He makes sure everyone gets thurough critique and does his best to involve everyone in class. He is pretty laid back while also staying an effective teacher. He not only teaches about animation itself but about how to care for yourself during the process.

Mark is, without question, the best animation professor at RIT, but his classes are what you make of them. You can get good grades with simple projects, but he'll also support you every step of the way if you choose to push yourself. Though he's slow with returning grades, his energy and care for his students far outweighs the inconvenience.

I really loved Professor Hosking as my first year writing teacher. She helped to gain a lot of confidence and ability in my writing skills and really prepared the class for academic writing we will have to be able to do for the rest of our lives! I would highly recommend her for any class, I'm sure she'd be awesome!

Professor Hosking is a very nice person and a good teacher when it comes to writing. The issues that I had throughout this semester were mostly with the contents of the course and not with the professor so I may be a bit biased in my opinion. It seems that she is very strict on what she considers "good writing" and you're grade may suffer from it.

First Writing with her was clear, concise, simple, and straight forward. The first teacher to actually make writing interesting and not boring. She didn't explain details that were not necessary; she told you exactly what you needed to know in a very simplistic manner.   Definitely choose her for your professor if you get the chance
If you listen to what she has to say and put in effort it is an easy GPA booster
She was super nice and graded the essays and quizzes fairly easy. good teacher overall
Had her for the freshman writing class, felt much more like an actual writing seminar than a class. Definitely helps prepare for professional writing.

I had Prof. Hosking for Arts of Expression: Inescapably Human.  3 simple quizes on the books,1 project, and one creative writing piece.  She skipped the other project that we were supposed to do because we ran out of time.  It was an interesting and easy class.  I would highly recommend it to anyone who needs an arts of expression credit.

You have 3 papers and 5 quizzes through the year. The quizzes test what you know from the book, each questions is absolutely ridiculous and it's impossible to get a 100 on any of them. She makes you work your ass off in class, it's incredibly boring and attendance is mandatory. You don't want her for writing seminar.

Professor Whitney is a very thoughtful and well-spoken professor. There is a lot of reading required, but most of the time a rough skim is sufficient for class time if you are in a crunch for time. I would very much recommend taking one of his classes, he is extremely knowledgeable in various different subjects.

Professor Whitney is very kind and does not ask for much in his class. While some lectures can be slow, he tries to inject humor and is very personable. There are a few papers throughout the semester and often weekly writing assignments, but they are not long.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Awesome class. Loved it a lot. Professor made sure to give out interesting articles to read so coming to class was so fun. Homework is easy and showing up to class counts as participation. Easy and enjoyable!
thanks for a great class

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: Awesome teacher! Very interested in the topics he teaches.

Really nice guy who is very passionate about the subject. The tests were hard, but you could earn all the points you need for an A with extra credit alone. He's also open to suggestions; he replaced our final with a series of essays when we asked him to.

Very passionate about his work. Does a great job getting students involved and making us want to participate. Assignments are not difficult and extra credit is a huge help. It is sometimes hard to pay attention but he made me interested in the topics. If you have the opportunity, take his class. You will definitely learn something
so far pretty easy assignments, mainly lecture with group discussions to answer basic questions, have yet to find out for exams otherwise very openminded

Extremely boring and dry lecturer. No sense of humor or personality. Doesn't make any effort to engage the class with the content. I don't understand how this class has any connection to my chosen career or why I should care about it, and I'm not looking forward to the midterm based on what I read on here.

For the exams, this professor expects you to be able to memorize a bunch of paintings, and she updated the list of paintings for the finals after she posted the study guide assignment, so don't be proactive in this class. Lectures are also very long and difficult to pay attention to with AI images every so often. Instructions are not very clear.

Warning: dont take this unless it is required. I needed an artistic perspective and thought it would be easy, but its not. If you dont care about art its hard to follow. Lectures drag, lots of ultra specific memorization, strict rules, you gotta put ur stuff in front of hall before exams, , sign in required also.
Long classes, boring lectures, slow grader,

Extra credit doesn't justify requiring the memorization of 35 different paintings, their titles, the artist and the date. Despite being a new teacher she clearly took her teaching methods from the 40's. You could take flawless notes of every word she says and still not have the information required for the midterm.

Reads off her computer screen for lectures, which makes them pretty boring to listen to. Many people thought they were AI-generated. She does offer extra credit for both the midterm and final. She's a sweet person outside of class, but she seems like a new professor, and having her read off a script was really boring to listen to.
Liked him.

Great Professor, very knowledgeable and allows you to experiment with the big projects. Will provide lots of resources and detail about any topic, even outside of class topics. If you pay attention in class and do the work, you should have an easy time. Can be unprepared at times, but makes it up with the amount of time he is on Slack.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: The professor tends to set a lot of expectations on students and then communicate with the external stakeholders not to have any high expectations for the students.

Has faced a neurodegenerative disease or brain damage in the past. Has difficulty speaking at normal pace and volume. Also has trouble with critical thinking and cannot think of an original thought outside of memorized textbook. Tech knowledge limited to floppy disks. May believe RIT is his nursing home. Do everything in your power to avoid him.

Professor Keller was the toughest professor I've ever encountered throughout my years in RIT. He has very vague instructions on assignments and grades the work any way he wishes. His grading was very rough, as if you do all the work, you will only get an 80. You have to be above and beyond to earn credit

Only half way through his class and I'm dreading taking it. He has weekly discussions that he requires the class to participate in. While this may seem fine, he grades you on how well your opinion differs from his. Grading has been tough for this reason so far. I accidently turned in an incomplete assignment and he had left a somewhat nasty comment

Professor is extremely boring, monotone, looks at notes on what he's going to lecture about. To an ESL student his words are no more different than just mumbles. Would strongly suggest changing/switching if you have a choice.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: If you are interested to become a project manager this is a great class, otherwise - take another. This man is by far the most monotone professor I have ever had. Speaks very slowly, and expects very specific answers. Combine that with the most boring material I have ever taken, and you get the most mind numbingly boring class you will ever attend.

Extremely boring. Talks very slow and is very quiet. You need to be able to fight off the boredom, otherwise you will fall asleep. Takes off points on gate reviews without giving a rubric or mentioning what he wants included. He then complains to the class that no one followed his non-existent list of requirements.

A continuation of horrible classes taught by Keller. Strongly recommend against having him as a professor. The only way to get through this class is to try to fight through the boredom by counting the seconds of awkward silence and looking at someone else's computer screen.

- Encourage well to students to participate in class discussions. - Provide friendly atmosphere to the class - Give good feedback to students' discussion assignments - Can be critique toward students - Tough grader as well
Not fun at all
He should be fired. F
I strongly not recommend you to take with him. Please take someone else!
Richard is the worst professor ever I had.... Failed!
Instructions in assignments are not clear to understand which is awful. It is hard for everyone to understand what the professor wants to see.

The class was not a fun experience. Prof would never use powerpoints and instead typed up word documents and projected them. Always looked for very specific answers and if the wording was a bit different, he'd say you were wrong. He'd wait for minutes for someone to raise their hand so there was LOTS of awkward silence. Weird sense of humor. Yikes!
Yikes.
He's very clear about expectations for the course and his lectures are engaging. He goes through enough examples in class to make the homework and tests manageable.

It is clear that Dr. Fuentes is passionate about the design of powertrains and their components which makes the class enjoyable compared to other upper level electives. While there is a lot of material to cover, I think he does a great job of breaking everything down in a way that every student can understand it.

Powertrain isn't an easy subject to learn, but Dr. Fuentes made the class easily one of the best I've ever taken at RIT. Lecture presentations have a perfect amount of information in them; I found myself using them instead of my own notes when doing homework. Feedback is second to none. Would recommend to anyone. I wish I could use more than 3 tags

Prof. Fuentes is the best professor I have ever had at RIT. He is very good at articulating the concepts in class and does tons of examples to reinforce them. Only 3 easy hw problems a week and an easy weekly quiz. He also tells you exactly what to expect on exams and is very clear about what's expected. It is obvious he wants you to do very well.

He's just a really good teacher. Great lectures, always does good examples, and he tries to get to the theory underneath the material. Not a lot of homework or quizzes and the problems are all similar to the exams and what you cover in class.

Great prof, goes off slides but does it in an interesting way. Gives theory first and then examples which are very helpful. Would defiantly recommend over Prof Ivancic for this class. Lots of homework and assignments (not specific to him but to the class) but not unbearable.

A real stand up guy. Sometimes difficult to read symbols and numbers, but he's glad to clarify and is very consistent. If you don't understand in class just go to office hours, he'll work with you for as long as you need and really cares about your success. Show up, take notes, follow the examples, and you'll do great. Great professor.
A good professor especially compared to other MECE professors. His handwriting for various symbols is hard to get use to. Nice guy, wants to see his students succeed.
Quizes are just like the exams. Wants students to understand and do well.
This was one of the best professors I have had at RIT. 10/10 would take again.

He values the success of his students, and puts forth the effort to help you succeed. His quizzes are easy and he basically shows you the exact type of problems that will be on the test. Great guy as well.

Stacy is passionate about what she does and she is very dedicated to helping others whenever possible and is generally very sweet and understanding. However, the class is very very fast paced. All students at one point or another fell behind in class, and I heard this is a recurring issue in her classes. The work isn't hard, the pace is.
Very friendly. Very motivated. Also collaborated with her to enhance web design course
Excellent teacher! Ms. Bick is very knowledgeable about her field and she cares about the success of her students.

She was the most awful teacher I had. She did not what she was learning and often relied on the students work to learn the material herself. She always screwed up my own work and wouldn't give me a postponed date for her own mistakes. She gives loads and loads of homework and never tells when the due dates are, you have to figure out yourself.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']
comment: Gave no feedback on assignments or grades prior to end of course. Grading seemed arbitrary, students with similar work received different grades. Class was disorganized with nonspecific goals. Grading seemed to be influenced by personal feelings towards students. Don't talk back in class.
Seems like he enjoys teaching the subject, uploads a lot of materials to help you understand the concepts taught in the class. Overall was a great professor in my opinion.

He's dedicated to teaching and making sure everyone understands what's going on. His lectures aren't perfect, but he more than makes up for it with his demeanor, jokes, and genuine desire to see students succeed.

Made CS2 a lot harder than it should have been. It's not supposed to be a hard class, but his lectures and problem solving sessions were meaningless. Barely anyone knows how to do the PSS' because we don't learn anything in lecture. Recitation is the only time of the week we learn ANYTHING and it's taught by a TA. Tests are on things barely covered
Nice sense of humour

This man is a legends. Absolute living unit with a heart. Linked lists? EASY. Queues? EASY. Take this mans class and open your mind to a world of possibilities. In all seriousness though he is a very good instructor.

comment: This sub is anyways difficult, and he does not help make it any easier. He is very caring and will help you always when you ask for it, but his lectures aren't that great. Would not recommend if you have other better options, but he is okay. He may be better for more difficult courses, nut he ain't made for an intro class.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He was a very decent CS1 Prof. Clear and Concise lectures, albeit a little unorganized sometimes. Can talk a bit quiet, so sit near the front. Will add in small bits of humor to lighten the mood and is always willing to answer questions. Would recommend :)
Very helpful teacher if you put in the time, I went to his office hours all the time, he helped a lot.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Straightforward course with a clear introduction to healthcare informatics. Lectures are easy to follow and connect ideas to real-world examples. Workload is reasonable and expectations are clear.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: MySQL is a rather straightforward thing to learn, but the conceptual topics covered such as normalization cannot be learned unless you go to class. That being said the professor is more than willing to help his students even if it means staying late into the night to get them to understand.
He knows his stuff but can be boring in class and lecture a lot.

Marco is a good teacher and is always willing to lend a hand to the students. The class that I had was very hard to pay attention to because all the information was read off of slides, however that is not my style of learning. Overall, I would recommend him as a teacher.
Great guy, cares about his students and does a good job with material that can be boring at times. Always willing to help those in need.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Disorganized & unsafe. Supplies are given last minute, quizzes are frequently forgotten, & the syllabus isn't followed. Instructor provides no safety guidance for woodworking—students told to use any wood or knife, no mention of saw blades or dust masks. Excessive readings assigned before Day 1 and materials cost thousands before aid releases.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: ARCH 611: Instructor cross-applies ARCH 631 content, causing overlap and confusion. Quizzes are frequently released late or forgotten. Courses are built week-by-week with no clear plan. Week 0 assigns many hours of reading to learn before session 1. Unprofessional and disorganized. Habitually unprepared; undermines student learning & trust. Really!

Don gives excellent feedback on your work, and he will expect you to improve on the next assignment. If you pay attention to the changes he suggests, you will do well. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and really cares about his students.

He was the instructor for the snowshoeing class I took. He was knowledgeable about the sport and gave good instructions. He also had interesting stories to tell while on our "adventures". There was 1 meeting and two days of snowshoeing.

Don's a nice guy, but not the greatest professor. He often left me confused with assignments and didn't answer questions clearly. He seems indecisive when asked for opinions but come time for critique he's brutally honest and gets more knit picky. He know's what he's doing but isn't great at articulating that to students.
Knows a lot about studio and architecture. Grades easy, gets back work in reasonable time and lectures are relevant.

Professor's really nice. Always willing to help students. Inconsistent with assignment explanations at time. Great for first year students. Will share his on the field work experiences with you. 4x5 film assignment unclear, otherwise alright. allows re-do's occasionally. great guy, great professor. if you can take him, take it!

He's a great first year professor! Some projects are tough, but sometimes he'll let you re-do it for a better grade. Exams aren't designed by him in PA1, no exam PA2. 4x5 Film project tough-lacking explanation. Overall, great professor. Strict about attendence. Always show up and make sure you have fun! critiques usually very honest.

I enjoyed Don's class. It was really easy but not a waste of time. Don knows a lot about being a professional photographer and taught me a lot about the business. He is always willing to help and is very nice.

Don is a nice guy, but doesn't always teach well. His lectures are often unclear and he doesn't teach very technically. He is often confused with what he's talking about and doesn't always answer questions correctly. One time, we went shooting on location with 4x5 cameras and no one knew how to load them. Don left us and went off on his own.

Dr. Worrell is incredibly kind, intelligent, and knowledgeable. She is thoughtful, entertaining, and so reliable as a professor. I took her for Health Communication (COMM344) and loved this class! She is engaging, fun, and very fair. Take this class if you can!

Tracy did a good job of communicating expectations and I think for most people effectively communicated the material. She did a good job of making the class as interesting as possible despite how dry the material was.   Better, more organized powerpoint slides. I had a hard time going back through to reread things I missed or didn't understand.

Doesn't grade anything, has no clear grading criteria.  Her standards vary from student to student, giving one lower points on a project for using centered text, and praises another.  You will learn absolutely nothing, everything I learned was from guessing or online resources.  However, if you turn in all assignments, it should be an easy A.
Easy class but you have to know what you are doing. Helpful with advice but you definitely need to teach yourself the material. Very confusing assignments and grades pretty late
The only challenging part is trying to figure out what is going on. get good at doing things at the last minute and teaching yourself. also never grades assignments until like 3 months later
She doesn't actually teach anything. "Word art is cool". Nuff said.
have no idea what she is talking about. teach yourself

Without a doubt the worst teacher I've had from preschool to now.  Rarely less than 15 minutes late to class.  Doesn't know anything about the material or what she is doing. Shows youtube tutorials as her lectures. Gives vague assignments and doesnt even know when theyre due herself.  Not sure what RIT is doing by hiring people like this... AVOID!!
Avoid at all costs. Teaches nothing but expects a lot. Often says things that are the OPPOSITE of what's accepted in the industry. Means well, but simply shouldn't be teaching.
Haha, Marianne... Avoid this professor no matter what it takes. Prepare to teach yourself if you have to take her - you will learn nothing unless you do.
She is nice, but is very vague with instructions. She contradicts herself and doesn't teach at all. She's horrible.

She is a very nice lady, but teaching is really not meant for someone like her. Her lectures are, in a nutshell, completely worthless. She is all over the place and unorganized and forgets the majority of what she assigns or teaches. I just think she is too busy to be teaching classes on top of everything else she does at RIT. Avoid if possible.

Absolutely useless. Can't remember her own assignments half the time, and has almost no knowledge of the programs she teaches. She had us doing vectors in Photoshop, raster illustration in Illustrator, and Flash in After Effects. Her personal workis terrible, and she is incompetent as a teacher. You have to take her, but bit ofadvice; don't listen!

She is a very nice women, but she is not a good teacher at all, and her lectures are all but useless and pointless. She is not clear on due dates, and does not even understand the computer programs enough to teach us. Her grading is really stict too, if your work does not appeal to her, she will give you a bad grade           AVOID HER IF POSSIBLE

She's a nice woman but not a good teacher. She is never clear about assignments or due dates and doesn't reply to emails. Her lectures seem like she makes them up as she goes along and she's very unhelpful so you have to teach yourself. Thankfully the assignments aren't hard once you figure out what they are.
Don't take any class with her that involves a computer, she can't teach you things on a computer. She looks up tutorials online and in books and can't even do them herself. Prepare to teach yourself.
No Comments
She's a very nice woman.  But you don't learn very much.  She pretty much lets you do whatever, but provides no real instruction.

Madhu is very very unclear with his grading criteria and expects us to understand way more Python than necessary. This should be a beginner's class for a major that does not deal with coding, and yet it is extremely difficult and over the top. The final project especially was very unclear and difficult.
Literally the worst professor in the program, in some ways worse than Wanda. Avoid at all costs, if you see him teaching your class all the sudden, heed my warning and swtich out

Worst professor in the ISE program. Assigns many assignments each week with no information on what he expects, then gives lectures about how nobody is able to complete the assignments correctly. Exam/Quiz questions are extremely nit-picky, he asks questions about minor details from his lectures. Avoid if possible
Very bad professor. His tests and assignments are unclear. He never gives them back and he give a lot of them. So you have no idea on what you are doing right or wrong.

Absolutely the worst professor ever, the whole class is failing or close to it and he acts like he's the best teacher ever. Promotes questions then shoots you down if he thinks the question is 'dumb' or too simple. His tests and quizzes are extremely nit-picky, so unless you memorize the book you're in trouble. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

I took him for C++. I had never programmed before in my life,but I was able to get through the class. If you go to him early in the week after he has assigned a project he is very helpful. He asks questions to make you think and come up with the answer. Quizzes are straight from the text! This class is not at all easy but going to his office helps!

I took programming with matlab / c with him. He is one of the worst teachers i have ever had. If you asked him for help he would tell you to look in the book. HE never wanted to help out and his test were really hard. You had weekly projects that were difficult and he would not help with those either.

Python isnt her strong suit, constant 5-10 errors in code. Was lenient with grading to compensate. I took away minimal Python because I had to start from ground zero and it was stressful and annoying when the content from the class was unclear, hard, and impossible to clarify due to prof accents and misunderstandings. contact 5-10 errors in code

She tried her best, but was certainly not qualified to teach this course. It felt like she didn't know python, and I often felt like I could teach the class better than her after having read through the slides once. If you are in her section, I suggest reading through the slides on your own if possible, as she will be behind pace and make errors

I think Prof Kibris did her best to teach GCIS-123, but I don't see her being remotely qualified for the position.  She was not comfortable with the content and regularly made errors during, often needing to send emails with corrected files after class.   I believe her students would have gotten more from reading the slides on their own time.

I do believe she tried her best, but her best was honestly really bad. She often did not know what she was doing, she made mistakes (which is ok just not to the extent she did), then had no clue how to fix any of them. All in all, she should not be teaching this course, she does not know anything about python  

I cld write more, but thrs a 350 lmt

GCIS-123 is a tough class overall, and Prof. Kibris was assigned to teach it during her first semester at RIT. I do believe she cares about her students doing well; however, her not understanding what we were doing made the class even more difficult. Take this rating more as a reflection of GCIS-123 and the department, not necessarily Prof. Kibris.

Pros: - The class is focusing on improving your ability to work with others. - It is easy. - Professor Ardis gives quiz(open book, laptop is allowed) on every lecture to make sure you understand what is taught. - You can train your English speaking(If you're not a native speaker).   Cons: - This course is time consuming.

Excellent professor. Provides daily quizzes to make sure that you understand the material the day it's taught. In addition, he provided short, but useful lectures that stepped through each concept taught in the class. In-class activities were very helpful.

Course: Verification & Validation.  Ardis is a good teacher, although his style doesn't match with me very well - I have a hard time paying attention.  Otherwise, he is a good teacher, knows the material and is willing to help.

Had Ardis for personal SE. It was a simple class but Ardis was able to explain pointers in C very well and could answer questions effectively.  Allowed some late submissions which helped because some due dates were not always stated. Dismissed class early when he was done teaching, but stayed around in case you needed help on work.

Professor Young is very nice, extremely helpful, and a good teacher. Unfortunately, the person who said she is very disorganized is right. The final is today and I have no idea what my standing in the course is. The scary thing is that I'm not sure that she knows either. Good teacher and very helpful, but I need more structure as a student.
Isn't very organized.
very helpful, always willing to sit down with students until they understand. Yes, she does bumble here and there, but quite frankly it's not that bad.

Probably the best teacher I've had for Univ Physics, but that's not saying much as they all suck. Would argue with you when you asked questions, but after a few minutes of arguing she'd finally realize what you were asking and explain it. Class is hard, but it's Univ Physics, it's meant to be hard. This prof was easier than most UP profs.

Dr. Young is tough professor in terms of the work she gives you. There is a lot of work to be done in the course of 10 weeks. However, all that work (Labs, Homework Webassigns, and Classwork) will definitely pay off when you take her exams. The exams are really fair. If you have questions, she WILL make herself available for you. She really cares!!
This lady talks WAY too much and the book for the class sucks which makes it even worse! She's the only person who teaches Optics at RIT so she's unavoidable if you must take this class... :(

Anne isn't a bad professor.  She knows her stuff and is helpful.  I guess it depends on what class you take with her.  I recommend astronomy as its an easy A, but physics 3 was incredibly difficult with her.  Overall she cares about her students..
if you have to take physics 3, take her, she is probably the greatest teacher for such a hard course. She is very nice and just an overall fun teacher, and lover of physics

Stellar Astronomy She was very unorganized. The class was only an hour long, but she crammed so much information into that time. It seemed like she was just throwing handouts at us. Material had to be learned on your own through reading or just by doing the homework. Grading was a little confusing, too. Pulling an A in this class was very difficul

She was not organized at all.  Not clear when she taught.  Was not helpful at all. Assigns web assigns twice a week, and hand in homework on paper once a week.  Many many worksheets (no help from her)must be there every day, dry material, she does not make it interesting at all. Knew more before I went into the class.  She decreased myunderstanding

The best phyics prof. I've had here. Not saying much at RIT, but it is meant as a compliment. Class is rather confusing; taught too quickly, but that is not her fault. Very willing to help outside of class. I found her more helpful outside of class than in because it was 1 on 1. Focuses on concepts, and the homework reflects that. Gives extra cred.
she's always a compleat mess and is somewhat crazy
Great teacher, best physics teacher I've had.. I know at RIT that isn't saying much but she's really good.  Not easy always, but good.

A closet Calc teacher, this lady will derive equations until you are blue in the face. That being said, she usually offers good drawings or examples and grades easily (Bonus all over the place).  Very helpful if you ask her a question one-on-one, but sometimes has strange way of explaining in class.

Second semester ive had her. Decent teacher but always willing to help if you dont understand. This semester she has been alot better than she was in the last. Pretty fair teacher, definitely worth taking her course.
avoid if possible

This was his first year teaching at RIT, and he did an alright job. Class is all project based, and the projects are not too bad, but they are super time consuming. If you have prior coding experience, this class will not be too bad. If you are new to coding you will have to work your ass off if you want to do well.

Mike is fun and chill, he's an easy grader and understanding, but he isn't a great teacher. He hardly gives thorough or proper crit unless prompted and seems generally unknowledgeable about more modern animation. He's great if you're taking an animation class as an elective, not if it's your major and you're looking to build solid fundamentals.
takes a while to grade
Probably the worst Professor I've ever had.  Doesn't use MyCourses, illegible handwriting, low talker, tests cover a wide range of topics which are hard to study for.  This guy needs to retire.

His homework is all hazy theory questions. He made us write one program: strip all but four header lines from a text document formatted as an email. 2 lines of python. Lectures suck, handwriting sucks, brutal tests, graded unfairly and pedantically, I ended up not going and now I have an incomplete I'm struggling with. Oh and he's probably 104.
Handwriting illegible. You have to sit in the front row to hear him. Does not answer questions well. Avoid if possible.
Handwriting is completely illegible, mostly reads from a slide show. Speaks too softly to be understood. You have to teach yourself to pass. Avoid if possible.

Handwriting is indeed illegible. Simply clicks through slides without really explaining them. If you don't already know everything about computer networks then you will most likely spend the quarter doing TONS of independent learning outside of class and still end up failing. AVOID!!
Don't ever think about taking this professor. AVOID AT ANY COST. He doesn't curve and he doesn't explain things well. his handwriting is not understandable at all.

One of the worst professor. His teaching skill is v.poor.Don't expect to attain something with him except boring and sleeping.His grading is mystery. If you have extra money and time ,you can lose them with him.

His homework assignments and tests are very ambiguous. He also grades your homework ambiguously. And his lectures are not clear at all. He merely read off slides from the book. Not recommended at all.

Pretty much impossible to understand. Doesn't know what the class is doing while he's teaching. Expect to try and figure everything out on your own. Acts as if the entire class knows what he's talking about, so if you don't you're screwed. Bring a pillow.

Poor teaching skills, messy handwriting, repetitive and often irrelevant notes, mixes up Java and Fortran occasionally. He knows his stuff, but I'd avoid him unless you've already taken a CS class before.
Sometimes the workshops aren't great but Ireland really cares for all his students. Tests are extremely fair. Very funny guy and relate able if you are into nerdier culture.

Doctor Ireland is, in my opinion, among the best that the RIT math department has to offer. His lectures include a lot of concise information, and he often times arrives at class early to answer random physics questions in an enthusiastic manner. This guy is the real deal, he's entertaining, and he makes time for his students in his office hours.

Professor Ireland is a super nice guy who cares about you doing well in his class. He's slightly disorganized and is liable to forget about an appointment or meeting, but he means well and will give you a firm foundation for Calc 2. I had taken the class previously and struggled to stay awake during 8am lectures, but he still kept me engaged.

Ireland's fantastic. He's funny, interesting, exciting, animated, knowledgeable, intelligent, caring, realistic, and reasonable. He takes lectures at a fast clip, so don't screw around too much, but he'll help you every step of the way if you need it. Also, you should 100% ask him space questions, he'll talk for hours and it's great.

My favorite professor by far. Incredibly clear and interesting lectures. Made 8 AM calc interesting and worth getting out of bed 3 times a week for. As a bonus he even wore a t-rex costume to class on Halloween. His class is not the easiest but is fair. He's always willing to help and responds to emails quickly.

An absolutely amazing professor, I adore him. He's a great man, a great teacher, and he's just a human. Some professors put on a persona but he's just him. You can get to know him and talk to him about anything. His homework is based on completion, not how well you did.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He is a good person but he moves too quickly and doesn't go into detail about the material he is teaching. You tend to be spending most of the time rewriting what he has written on the board than actually listening to what he is saying which doesn't always make sense.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Hilarious', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: One of the best math professors I've had at RIT. Take any classes with him you can. Very nice guy, loves math, and super funny. Also, as a bonus, his degree is in physics, so he's not super super strict about notation.

Probably the best math teacher I have ever had. He is funny and personable, not to mention extremely easy to ask for help and always provides ample support. He give lots of partial credit on tests and quizzes with plenty of in and out of class review materials.
If you were to scribe this man in two words,they would be be the words, Very spicy
One characteristic I really liked about him was his use of gaming references to make the subject more interesting.

Professor Pavia has given me amazing insight into the world of writing. She helped me explore my passion for writing and is just a great professor overall. There's lots of class discussion, including discussion posts, but none of it is too taxing. Best professor I've had in a long time.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment:
Weekly Quizzes: Easy. Midterm and Final: Not Half Bad. Group Project: Not hard, just don't put it off. 
Lectures: Incredibly monotone. Even though he establishes this at the semester beginning, it's hard to pay attention for the entire duration of the class and you miss so much because of it.
Weekly quizzes on readings he gave us, five homework assignments and a final group project were the big grades. Very animated lecturer and overall chill guy.

I am not interested with the subjects of the class I took with professor Hansen but his teaching made the class interesting. The class was over 100 people, considering the size of the class, Professor Hansen did a great job engaging the students and teaching. If you paid attention in class and studied for a couple hours the exam was very easy.
while hansen is fully aware that his voice puts people to sleep, he is a fascinating person and made the class interesting. i am not interested at all in MIS but the class was enjoyable overall.
Amazing professor. One of the smartest professors I've ever had, but also one of the best at communicating with their students. Just amazing at teaching.
Super fun teacher. He always makes the lectures fun and the quizzes, homework, and tests are pretty easy. There is barely any homework.

Professor Hansen is a terrific lecturer, and I would absolutely take his courses again, but be prepared to take notes and LISTEN. For MGIS 130 specifically, all of the expected knowledge came from slides and lectures. It was very easy to follow along, but I'd definitely recommend coming in with an open mind and preparation to take GOOD notes.

His lectures are always very interesting and he has a great personality. He keeps the class engaged with a mix of lectures and class activities to help understand and apply concepts. If you do the readings the quizzes are easy. Great professor, my favorite class all semester.

Professor Hansen is a fantastic teacher. He is great at explaining concepts and his classes are always engaging and very interesting. He definitely values hard work. If you are the type of student that tends to go above and beyond in your assignments/projects, it is impossible not to get an excellent grade in this class.
Sean Hansen is a great guy! he cares about learning and not just grades. Take his class and you will love him

One of the best professors at RIT. It's a shame that I have no more opportunities to take a class with him. He makes learning the topics at hand interesting and enjoyable for all, and is willing to help any students who need extra help understanding the subject.
Sean Hansen is an amazing professor. He gives few homework assignments throughout the semester and gives you plenty of time to complete them. I loved going to his class, he made it fun and enjoyable.
great class at RIT
Super Chill Just remember to do the readings or sit next to someone who has!
Best professor I've had at RIT, teaches you useful information and keeps the class enjoyable.
Very good communicator. His powerpoints are extremely helpful and lay out the exact material that will be on the test. You learn a lot in his classes without having to do much work.
Excellent communicator, easy explanations on complicated topics. Clases are constantly related with today's world

Hansen is a pretty cool guy but avoid taking him at 8am, he is much livelier if you have him later in the day. 6 homeworks, 2 tests, one group project. The group project was kinda tough and he graded it pretty tough. The homework and tests are easy and he grades them leniently.

Really awesome professor. He truly cares about his students and the material. One of the best at RIT. However, He takes FOREVER to grade assignments so don't plan on knowing where you actually stand in the class until your final grade.
Best professor ever. Would recommend him for SAMD and Capstone class.

He is very interesting and very smart professor. I look up to him and he is every students dream for a teacher. Hes the most understanding, repectful teachers ive ever met. he is a very easy grader too! very helpful and funny and nice.

Dr. Hansen is very intelligent and is overall one of the best professors I've had in the College of Business. Lectures are concise and to the point. Very fair at grading, provides personal feedback on all assignments you submit online. Nice guy, cares a lot about his class, so when people fall asleep/don't pay attention he takes it personally.

He's clearly one of the best professor I ever had. It's very rare to get professor like Dr. Sean Henson. His lectures are very clear and interesting. I learned so much about the topic from this professor. BEST BEST BEST PROFESSOR EVER...
this man is a gift from MIS heaven hes soo  clear and concise and hes always there for anything u need if u dont take him ur a fool!

One of the best professors at RIT! He is very helpful and knowledgeable about the material. I do believe some of his lectures should include more hands-on practice of material when needed.  I would recommend him to anyone.
Awesome professor! Uses powerpoint as main tool of lecture, but includes modern and relevant examples for everything. Very easy to relate to real life. Would definitely recommend Sean.
THE BEST OF THE BEST!

Professro Hansen is definately the coolest MIS Professor. Very easy and comfrtable to talk to-even if it's small talk. He takes student's opinions into consideration and molds the class after it. Very understanding and willing to help. I wouldn't take an MIS class with another professor
Great professor very easy to talk to and helps out whenever you need. just do the work show that you wanna learn and you will do fine.

Hansen is one of the coolest MIS professors in the college. If you haven't taken a class with him yet, he's highly informational and entertaining. Definitely worth your time if you can find a section he is teaching.

Professor Oleskyn is an amazing professor and probably one of the best math teachers I've had so far. He taught the class super well and always gave great advice during the workshop periods. Always very accessible and accommodating too. Funny person to talk to, I highly recommend this professor.

He's a nice teacher, he'll help you anytime if you ask for help. One important thing is you need to be on time for the class for the pop quiz and test. i was late one time and i missed a pop quiz and not able to make up. And i suggest you to remind him if you email you work and didn't get a grade. however,i enjoy his class9/10of the time.Fun class

Can be extremely helpful if you only take the time to raise your hand and ask him a question. He will do his best to answer your questions fully, and if you show up and participate, you will probably be fine. Due dates for assignments can sometimes be unclear, just keep asking him about it until he tells you the actual date it will be due.

I hate this teacher.  He's extremely disorganized and came to class unprepared.  He lost one of my test tapes and then proceeded to blame that on me, and also told me I couldn't take the test over.  Thank god he found it that weekend.  I'm not the only one he's lost tapes of.

I disagree with most of these ratings. I really like Ritchie as a teacher, although he does pick on certain people. If he knows you're shy, he'll make you do things in front of the class more often. won't give up on explaining something to a student. PS: it's your responsibility to read the syllabus, we're in college for crying out loud!

I disagree with everyone - I think he is an AWESOME teacher. You may not have understood him but he was always clear to my classes. True, he never responded to e-mails but I would love to continue on with him if he taught the higher classes.

He is TERRIBLE at getting back to you!!  Does not respond to emails and does not explain A THING!!If you don't read the syllabus you will not know what is due.   I wouldn't have even know we had to do a paper if I didn't read the syllabus!!  He did not mention it once or collect it, you had to go to him!!  Would never take a calss with him again.

He's terrible at feedback! Even after we told him that we needed more he still didn't do a good job of telling us what we were doing wrong!  He comes to class unprepared, takes forever to grade things and doesn't even know how to sign things in the book before he comes to class.  I hope I never take him again.
Well I hated how he always picked on me : ( I know im being a baby about it. The one thing i liked about him was the fact that he helped me make the decision to switch my major...meh
He's not the best at feed back so you're never really sure what you're signing wrong.
Very nice individual, interesting lectures. Go to class, pay attention and participate in class and you will get a good grade

He is a very, very nice man. However, he struggles to convey much of the content in a fully coherent way. He will bend over backwards to help you understand what's going on, but lectures are hard to get through. Grading is based on 3 exams and homework average. Tough to bounce back if you have a bad day. One of your best bets for this class, though

Professor Barth-Hart is a really friendly guy and super passionate about math. Like others said, I really wanted to like him. However, his teaching is all over the place and his lectures never prepared me for the homework or the tests. I had to rely on reading the textbook, and even then found the homework and tests to be super difficult.

As much as I wanted to like him, he's really not a great teacher. Lectures are long and rambling, and he moves through content really slowly. On average I'm probably only taking notes for half the class. The one redeeming quality is that the class was really easy (at least online). Tests were open note with multiple attempts. Also he uses WebAssign
Definitely passionate, but I personally don't think he was good at explaining everything

My best description of this guy is that he rambles and rambles and rambles and rambles. I gave up trying to pay attention to the lectures when he got to talking about snowmobile bolts in calculus class. Trying to comprehend what he is saying is near impossible. He is a very passionate teacher and a great guy, but his teaching style is very very bad

Professor Barth-Hart is a very kind and passionate man, however, his style of teaching the course online is very rough. It consists of a zoom lecture with very little written notes and most of the time trying to comprehend what he is scribbling on the whiteboard. The homework seems to have nothing to do with what he teaches. Not learning much.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Great guy, super nice, willing to work with you to an extent. Not sure he's quite figured out how to run an online course. Doesn't understand the stress his class format causes. There's twice the amount of work to actually understand the material than any other 200 level course and there's exactly 9 grades in--one mistake WILL ruin your grade.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. He said this class would be online asycn, and that our class time would be office hours. However about halfway through the semester we realized he was lecturing during them and expected us to show up to class and watch 30-90 min video lectures outside of zoom. Didnt teach well, felt like i learned nothing

He's an amazing professory that is easily able to convey complicated ideas, but he gets ahead of himself and will assume a complete understanding of these ideas for his homeworks. If you put in the work, you will learn a lot, but he won't make it easy with the assignments. Go to his office hours!

Barth-Hart is very nice, and very accessible outside of class. He's also a very generous grader. Homework is very manageable too. But his lectures are very hard to follow. He's very helpful if you talk to him outside of class though. He had twice as many office hours as any of my other professors which is very helpful.

If you have a passion for math and an ability to learn on your own Prof Barth-Hart is the professor for you. His lectures are mostly teaching edge cases and proving information, you are expected to have learned the base information from the book. Utilize office hours, they are worth it.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I quite enjoyed class with Professor Barth-Hart. He is extremely passionate about the subject and it shows. His classes consist of only lectures and examples, which are phenomenal. Pay attention in class and review notes and the class should be easy.

Professor Barth-Hart is one of the most passionate individuals in the math department. However, his teaching style is beyond incomprehensible. His regular rants and overly complicated examples can be very difficult to grasp. Lectures are dry and hard to follow. Although Barth-Hart does have the best office hours and explains things well 1-1.

This professor is very passionate about what he does, but his lectures can definitely get a little boring. Don't make the mistake I did of skipping class way too often, if you are able to pay attention to the lectures then you should be alright. The homework is easy and you have unlimited attempts.
One of the worst professors at RIT, do no recommend him at all. His teaching method is all over the place, and I honestly learned nothing from this class. Had to teach myself everything.

Barth-Hart is one of the better RIT math professors. You can tell he really loves the subjects and loves teaching. A lot of people complain about his rants but they are often related and insightful. Many of his rants helped me to open my eyes to certain aspects of math. If you're just getting through the class to be done with math, he's not for you

His lectures are a lot of rambling and his few examples don't line up with what's on the exams. He also doesn't follow the textbook. He does grade the exams kinda easy but it's not fun to go into it without having a clear idea of what he expects from you.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'Caring']
comment: He's a good guy, but he doesn't teach you ANYTHING relevant. Be prepared for a lot of extra help from the Internet and Study Centers. The few things you're graded on are worth a huge amount, and he does not prepare you or give you the resources to do well on them. This includes the very few homeworks and exams. SIT UP FRONT TO HEAR HIM!

While Dr. Barth-Hart has to be the sweetest professor I have had at RIT, he is not the most efficient. He goes off topic a lot, and his two hour lectures are hard to get through. That aside, he does care about his students' success. He will do just about anything to help you pass, and he gives ample extra credit opportunities.

His lectures consist of him talking for the majority of the time, with the occasional equation being written on the board. This style of teaching works for some, but most of the student, myself included, found his method to be ineffective at absorbing any knowledge. He is passionate about math but needs to work on making sure we actually learn.
great guy

He doesn't necessarily 'teach to the test', but that is generally expected in higher level math courses. His primary objective is making sure you understand AND enjoy the material. He gives a lot of tips and tricks for doing what could otherwise be very tedious calculations. He is generous with grading as long as you explain your ideas/work.

Lectures can be dry and a little scatterbrained, but his examples and explanations are among the best I've ever seen from a professor at RIT. Incredibly passionate about the subject, which shows in his lectures. Some homework, but not too difficult. Tells you what is on the test ahead of time. Highly recommended.
Very pristine and pure treatment towards concepts and abstract approaches.

Barth-Hart is the greatest professor I've had at RIT.  He is so passionate about math and teaches to the test. He specifically told us the layout of the final, including what the topic of each question was. His lectures can be boring, but he is an excellent professor.

He is the nicest and sweetest old man. He knows his material so well and you are truly blessed if you take his class. He teaches slow, but that's only to make sure you fully understand the material. -spring 2015

The man loves what he does. If you share his passion for math, you'll love his class. Otherwise, you may find it painfully boring. Class is all lecture and no participation, and very little required homework is assigned. Go to class and pay attention, and you'll be alright. If you don't understand, he is more than willing to help you until you do.

8 o'clock lecture will require gallons of coffee, zero class participation in lecture and very disjointed and scattered teaching style. The material isn't bad but he displays it haphazardly.  If you need help or extra time on something he is accommodating.

Scatter-brained. Brilliant, but impossible to follow. Lectures are disjointed and have nothing to do with homework or exams. Office hours may help, but only if you need just a little help. Few assignments, but VERY HARD, because his lectures will not help you. Literally everything in every lecture is incomprehensible and assumes too much knowledge.
Lecture material much different from assignments...
I didn't enjoy his class much. It seemed very unorganized and hectic. He didn't rush teaching, but he went back and forth on topics quite often. It was tough to keep track with what he was saying.

Professor Barth-Hart is one of the kindest, overall best professors I've ever had.  He loves math and truly cares about each and every one of his students.  Homeworks and exams are very fair.  I would definitely recommend him to anybody for any class he teaches.

Good teacher very interested in field.Very enthusiastic. Sometimes unclear in lecture but if you ask a question or go to office hours and makes sure you understand.Relatively easy grader.If your interested take him.If not, then pay very careful attention.Gives homework. Doesn't collect.

Excellent guy, very interesting but lecture can sometimes wear on you.  Very helpful.  One time I came in on a whim for some help and he gladly devoted the next 2.5 hours to helping me understand everything.  Has a very good outlook on teaching and is very considerate.  His tests are challenging but good for the material.

very cool nerdy guy. very interested in his field and if you have scrap if interest in theoretical mathematics take a class with him. likes to go on tangents about stuff that was WAY over my head but still interesting. tests right off of class examples. pay a little attention, and you will be good

Good teacher overall, sometimes the lecture can get a bit on the boring side, but other than that he presented the material in a clear and meaningful way.  I got a D in discrete I yet I got a B in this class - he's very fair about grading things, also.  Only 3 small "due" homework assignments the entire class.

Good luck to anyone who ventures forth into the realm of online learning with this man. His orchestration of the online learning environment is that of a fish out of water. His organization is horrible, his instructions are muddled and don't bother asking for him to clarify, you will only be more conufused . This class didn't need to be this hard.
He can't use a good teaching methods. He focuses on Participate. This is not fair. I got "C" with him

i admit that he is one of the toughest teacher but i learned a lot from him professionally and personally. he is language is hard to understand but he likes to push his students to learn more out of the class. he LOEVS dialogue and examples of existing company and he is obsessed of Tech
This man is useless and needs to throw in the towel, he does not explain any assignments and refuses to help you when you ask.  He takes forever to give your grades if he gets you them at all.
Great Professor.  You will learn so much.

Spent the class lecturing about things either unrelated to the material or things already gone over in the homework assignments. Weekly quizzes with poorly worded questions. Barely graded things all semester (large projects included) and inputted essentially all the grades on the very last day he possibly could. AVOID. AT. ALL. COSTS.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Professor Goodman is an absolute joke. He's infuriating, he decided to grade everything at the last minute, and he doesn't know how to teach. His class is unbelievably boring and he somehow seems to care less about the class than we do. Stay away from this mess of a professor

Gordon's a nice guy but his lectures are too long and don't tell us anything new that wasn't covered in the assigned readings. There's a quiz and lecture every Tuesday; I recommend you skip at least 7 or 8 Tuesdays, since he takes off the lowest 5 quizzes anyways. Assignments are due Thurs, which you can skip if you did it at home; fairly easy work

Attendance was mandatory to a degree, but he isn't really a great teacher. His course is extremely easy and won't really help you ever except for some stuff with photoshop. I wish I didn't have to take the class but I'm glad I got him instead of a harder professor.

Definitely not a bad person, but his class is terrible. He assigns a lot of reading and isn't clear about what specific things you need to focus on in said readings to pass his quizzes. Some of the quizzes range from questions about hardly touched topics to "name one thing you learned in these readings". He's also terrible about grading.

He is a fair professor. There is work. If you do it you will do fine. I had him for an introduction level class, so it wasn't bad.  One thing was that he would post assignments very last minute some times, and his grading wasn't very consistent.

This professor is the worst. He rarely grades anything and his lectures are long and useless. You don't even need to go to class, you won't learn anything. He rambles on random subjects and that's it. He says he'll give homework and then won't post it for days afterwards.

Worst Programming Teacher, I had Joe Pietruch first, and it was such a drop off in quality going to Gordon. I recommend anyone looking at programming to wait for a class taught by Joe because he is so much better than Gordon. Gordon is incoherent and is boring. The code he supplies runs on forever, and has more comments than content.

Terrible teacher all around. Although the class is not hard, there is overall very little graded work, but he takes extreme amounts of time to grade assignments. He is monotone and rambles incoherently. Avoid at all costs.

I don't mean to be mean, but this man has no business teaching. His presentations were dreadful to the point I'd rather endure physical pain. He didn't teach whatever the class was supposed to go over, but instead pushed some agenda of his upon us. I've taken two of his classes now, and regret doing so both times.

Literally the worst teacher I've had. It took him so long to grade projects that he had to give everyone a pass/fail, based on like 2 minutes of observation, in order to meet the grading deadline. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!!!

WORST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD. I HAD NO IDEA WHAT HE WAS TALKING ABOUT THE WHOLE ENTIRE TIME. he zones out during class also and if you even look away from the screen for a second, he does something and while you are copying it down,he switches screens so you cant do anything. I warn ALL NMD students: DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!

DONT TAKE THIS PROF if you are a NMD student. You will learn NOTHING. Does not teach & grades VERY harsh. Refuses to answer emails. Grades are not posted until MONTHS later. Got our grades for the 1st project the DAY BEFORE withdraw deadline(WEEK 8!) - only after complaints to his boss. Other section has all A's and B's - our sect. has C's and D's.

He has to have been the worst professor/teacher I have ever had. Always shows up late to class, hands back grades days before revisions are due (when other sec's have had theirs back for weeks). Almost impossible to get a hold of and never explains his grades no matter how many times you beat his door down. Stay away from this joke of a professor!

One of the most boring teachers I've ever had. He is CONSTANTLY unprepared and bores you to death with his lectures. He talks the whole time and we copy his code verbatim. He could spend ten minutes explaining something that would take a normal person one. He forgets to post code after classes, talks with his eyes closed, etc. AvoidThisClassIfUCan

hands down WORST professor at RIT. knows what hes doing but royally fails at relaying to it anyone else. classes consist of frantically trying to copy his code down before he switches screens and moves on to something else. you have no time to actually learn anything. i've even tried the sit back and listen approach no copying code but absorbed nad

He seems like a decent person and is willing to help if you approach him. I'm sure he knows what he is doing but he doesn't know how to relay the information. He gives guidelines on what he wants in projects but he doesn't give grades back. Do not take him if you need things clearly explained and you don't like learning mostly on your own.

Gordon Goodman is a seemingly nice individual. This being said it takes more than this to be able to teach a class in computer programming. His class had little value and I didn't feel like I walked away with anything useful. He doesn't put up grades frequently at all. His classwork was us copying his code verbatim. I unlearned things I alreadyknew

Without comparison, the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Has absolutely NO knowledge of the subject he teaches, and constantly comes to class unprepared. Most often we spend classes attempting to debug the shoddy program he cooked up 5 minutes before he showed up. No grades until it was too late to drop. Dont give this guy ur money.
Worst teacher I've ever had in my life. He doesn't teach - he does everything himself and makes everyone copy him. His voice is monotone. I want to kill myself when i'm in his classroom.
Worst Professor EVER. No Grades. No Projects. MEAN!!!!!!!
Worst professor I've had at RIT. No grades. No project requirements. Plus he makes derogotory comments and hates minorities.

tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: It's hard to understand her sometimes. She makes it so that you have to do all assignments because the grade is made up of three tests, attendance, and weekly essays. There's no other sources other than her lecture and even then she doesn't out full detail on the slides.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I say "lots of homework" but that just means you have a weekly essay to do with an accompanied reading. She goes by fast with slides, but information is always available on mycourses. Simple, easy, just a little boring in the beginning of the semester when starting out.
Good class to take if you have to take an art history course.
easy just boring class :)

Really great professor, the type you always want to have in college. His depth of knowledge in the material is incredible, not an easy class but commit yourself and you will succeed. Always available for extra help or questions. One of the best professors I've taken.

Had him for Strengths of Materials. Great professor!! Tests were fair, and not that hard. 3-4 homework assignments due per week, but very helpful at office hours. I would HIGHLY recommend Professor Merrill!

Great teacher. Always trying to help. Uses book every night for homework. Lots of homework but if you do it you shouldn't get below an 80. He wants you to understand and will help as long as you ask for it or participate.
Good teacher.  Lots of homework but It does help you learn Statics.  Has a grader do grading, so don't blame him for that.  I would take him again.

Decent professor, had him for statics & strength of materials. He can be tough old man at times. One day he'll say how well the class is doing, then say how little we know later in the week, you get use to it tho. Very willing to help in office hours. Gave extra credit. I would take him again.
His grading is very inconsistent, avoid at all costs.
Global literature last semester with Dr. Ray was, and still is, the hardest class I've taken. Despite this, his class was also the most rewarding and intellectually engaging class I've taken.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: I am a CS major and never imagined I could learn so much about the history of computing in an English course! Dr. Ray encourages discussion and we often had lively debates about super relevant topics. I will definitely take another course with him.

Dr. Ray is a truly inspiring professor to have a class with. He is able to emphasize the importance of the class's subject matter and frequently connects lectures to present day events. This class only has 4 grades (3 of which are essays), so that can be a bit stressful. Still, he communicates what he wants on them pretty well. Would reccomend.

Discussion intensive. We got to read some amazing stories that were adapted into motion pictures. I loved the way Dr. Ray helped us think about how a specific medium has certain strengths and weaknesses. Also, I was grateful for the extensive feedback on my essays.

I am a Computer Science major and I learned more about the history and ethics of computing from this English course than from any of my CS classes. Professor Ray really pushed us to questions the pros and cons of technology and provided a lot of context for new developments such as generative AI. Highly recommend.

If you don't do the readings, you'll be very confused. He's open to extra credit, which you might get midway through the semester. Attendance is mandatory, but only light participation is required. 

Whenever he cancels class, you never have to make up work, which is great. Grading isn't awful; there are opportunities to make it up.

I learned a lot in this class. Professor Ray balanced lectures with a flipped classroom approach, where we responded to prompts in small groups. He provided a lot of feedback on my papers and definitely helped me improve my writing. I plan on taking another course from him.
Pretty interesting lectures.  I felt like I learned a good bit about the history of copyright.  I think some of his presentations were dry, however.

I liked the way he lectured. He knows what he is talking about. There were often readings to do outside of class and then he went over them in depth during class time. This class was split, taught by two profs,  and he was in charge of the intellectual and creative piracy part.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Class was largely included student presentations; he had a tendency to be combative. He struggled to understand a perspective a time or two and would bring up other sources to "knowledge gap" others. Ironically he was also very dismissive of other sources if it doesn't enforce his strong political bias. While not wrong he can comes off strong.

The class was split into discussing about the reading and watching the film counterparts. Attendance and participation has the most weight, and there's 2 papers (3 if you didn't present a final project idea). All readings are provided, except Watchmen. He leaves feedback on your essays and the workload was doable. Enjoyed the readings and films.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Professor Ray is great! You can tell he's passionate about what he does. If you aren't a reader I would stay away from this course, however, if you find you have an appreciation for literature this class is for you. The entire semester is based on three essays and attendance and participation.

Prof Ray is really easy to listen to and its not hard to keep up. He's got a really interesting perspective and while he did struggle understanding someone else's perspective a time or two, for the most part he is really open and willing to hear your part.

Amit Ray is an inspiration and one of the only professors I had this year that I actually learned from.
