Towsley is an amazing professor who respects your time and work. Grading criteria is clear and quizzes are pulled directly from the textbook, ensuring success if you put the work in. His lectures are concise and clear, and every homework question is selected to teach you concepts without becoming a burden. He's also always available outside class!

Had Towsley as well for 182 and he was just as good for 190. This class is a lot more lecture heavy, but that is just the class itself and not Towsley. Gives workshops that are very similar to the tests and is very clear about what will be on a test. Gives multiple attempts for quizzes. Towsley is just the goat.

Towsley is amazing; lectures are very clear and engaging. As long as you pay attention and attend class you will do just fine. There are weekly quizzes but these quizzes are based off the textbook (free and online) and he tells you which problems, so it is easy to get an A. He makes the class as easy as possible for such a hard subject.

Makes learning Calculus genuinely enjoyable. he helped clear up a lot of the questions I had brought over from my previous calculus class. However, he does pick up on work near the end of the semester, but if you're willing to put in a little work, his class can be very rewarding.

Towsley is a fantastic teacher!! His slides are really nice, there's just enough info that you can understand the material when looking back, plus he uploads the slides. He also solves examples on the whiteboard during the slide show which helps improve understanding; He is one of the best math professors I've had at rit, overall I recommend

His lectures go a bit fast, but he explains everything very well and does well answering questions. His notes/lectures are very organized, which made it easier to study when I went back through my notes for tests. He also posts a lot of resources on the course page.

Professor Towsley really cares about the success of his students and puts a lot of effort into his classes. The material is difficult but lectures are well organized and many already have extra notes which are accessible online. There is one group project and weekly quizzes alongside regular exams.

I had Towsley for Prj Based Calc II. Considering the difficulty of the class itself, he made it seem manageable. he had 3 midterms and a final with a quiz every week. quizzes were copied and pasted from the optional and ungraded textbook homework, so do it. lectures were dense, but he was easy to understand and actually had legible handwriting.

Professor Towsley is great at the standard criteria of a math course, presents the material clearly, makes sure you understand the topics, and giving fair exams. However what I really enjoy about his class is that he connects the material to other topics and future uses with a focus on computer science, showing us why we are learning the material.

Overall a great professor. He gives workshops after lectures most days and they are perfect review material for any exam. His exams are very fair. I will not say they are easy but if you properly devote time to study you will do just fine. He gives a quiz every Friday but the questions are given to you in the syllabus so review is easy.

Towsley has been one of the best math professors I have ever had. He explains everything extremely thoroughly (take notes and youll be fine) and does not require you to buy the homework. Also, the quiz questions are all in the textbook. Extremely caring man and is very approachable. If you can get him for a class, do not hesitate to do so.

He's amazing. I have no idea how I got an A in the subject when I literally hated the second half of the material (not his fault, if anything he made it a whole lot easier). Took him for another class later- material was easier and he was still great.

One of the best Professors I have ever had especially for math. Professor Towsley was very patient and caring when I was struggling with the material. You don't get that with many university math professors. It was hard material. Even helped me out with my Calc II class. 100% recommend.

He really does everything he can to help you get a really good grade. His homework are harder than the tests, but you have unlimited tries on most of the homework so it essentially forces you to do the problem correctly. His extra help directly correlates to test problems so I would highly recommend going. Overall very understanding and helpful.

Towsley can teach clearly and efficiently. His lectures are good, detailed explanations. He uses WebWork so the textbook is optional. He gives a reasonable amount of HW, 10-15 problems a week and a weekly quiz (4-5 questions) which you can retake at least twice. His tests are fair + he provides a formula sheet. Always available to answer questions.

Towsley is a bit awkward, but he can teach very competently. His lectures are pretty good, and brownie points for textbook-optional (WebWork GOAT). He doesn't give a crushing amount of HW, usually 10-15 problems / subject. Exams are fair, provides a formula sheet. I need to note his support during COVID remote learning is outstanding.

comment: Professor Towsley is great. The lectures are very clear and teaches exactly what you need to know for homework/quizzes/tests. Tests are fair. Quizzes are easy, they are just textbook problems given ahead of time. He will give a 10/10 for workshops as long as you show up and attempt to do the problems. Overall, pretty nice.

tags: ['Respected', 'Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor Towsley is a really great teacher for calculus 2. Going into it can be nerve racking after hearing about how difficult calculus 2 can be, but he makes it easier than it sounds and really teaches the content well. As long as you do the homework and study for the quizzes and tests you will be fine.

He is very knowledgable and very good at providing a variety of examples showing different methods of completing a variety of problems. He prepares you well for exams and quizzes. Quizzes are just homework problems, and the final project was Matlab. Sometimes the webworks were difficult due to the random generating of values.

Makes calculus fun and easily understandable. Although lectures can be dry, they are very informative and are relevant to tests. Quizzes consist of homework problems so its easy to get 100%'s if you care enough. Overall a great professor.

He will go through each problem step by step, making Calculus II fun and easy to understand. You will have to be regular and attentive during class time to ensure an A grade. He is always ready to help and answer questions during class time and office hours.
Great professor. Fair tests.

Adam is a great guy! He's accessible outside of class and really wants to see his students succeed. His tests are fair, and he does weekly quizzes based off of the optional book assignments. He doesn't overload on assignments. He writes pretty much everything on the board, and when he does skip a step, he says out loud what that step was.

Adam is probably one of the most fair professors I have had. The tests aren't easy but aren't overly hard. The amount of homework is reasonable. The quizzes are given off of the homework which is optional, and he goes over everything in a much better setup than the book. Over all would recommend.

Overall not a bad professor. He doesn't explain content at times which can be difficult but he tries to go into more detail when the entire class seems lost. Honestly, the biggest issue I had with him was the lack of reviews. The class has a ton of content and he didn't give reviews for any of the exams which made studying very hard.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He goes kind of fast but other than that, a very good calc teacher. He explains everything clearly and is very helpful in office hours/during workshop.

Adam was a great Calc teacher. He was very down to earth, and always was there to help you learn rather than to ruin your grade. The hour long workshops are a drag, but unlike most other teachers, he won't make a big deal if you leave a few minutes early. Great guy all around.
Don't be afraid to ask questions. Adam is a really great guy who wants you to succeed, just speak up.

Adam was an amazing professor I thought his class was very informative, and his lectures are clear. He gives very reasonable test, quizzes, and homework that you will do well on if you pay attention and give them a little work. He is also a fair grader.
Makes calculus seem easy with his clear explanations and online homework with unlimited attempts. Lectures aren't exactly thrilling, but you'll learn the material and probably get to leave early.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Adam is a nice guy, and a very good teacher. His lectures were very clear and I was always able to understand the material. He's a great teacher and a great guy. There's online homework that you can just lookup the answers to. There's a quiz every friday, but he gives sample problems so they're easy. Not much more than that, the test are pretty fair.
Always available to help. Wants his students to succeed and it shows. Text book was not a necessity, but it did help to have. I would gladly take a class with him
Great professor.  Always available to help.  Wants his students to succeed and it shows.  Text book was not a necessity, but it did help to have.  I would gladly take a class with him again.
He was a great professor! Very fair and curves tests. Quizzes are mainly from the homework assigned in textbook. Cheesy math jokes but you can tell he cares that we all do well

I really enjoyed taking this course and lab with Dr. Barnes. She is passionate and truly cares about her students. Stephen is a really nice guy but is a victim of this teaching tools. very disorganized

I've had this professor 2 times now and I am taking him again. Super easy professor who is well versed in his field and really interesting to talk to. tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Loved Professor Cady! He's very fair and easy to talk to. There are daily quizzes so make sure you go to class. If you pay attention and ask for help when needed, this course is an easy A. Professor Cady is a really smart guy, pick his brain and you'll learn a lot!

Great professor who is very enthusiastic about the subject. Most of the assignments are group projects and are easy to do. He teaches important design concepts to make it easy to understand but you'll still learn a lot. A really nice guy and very flexible with due dates on assignments as well.

Holly is one of the nicest and down to earth professors I have ever had. I look forward to having her for the rest of the degree I pursue. I cannot express this enough, she is so so nice! She cares about how her students do in her class and cares about them as people too! She does her absolute best to ensure that we understand the material in both lab and lecture. She is also so great at explaining what is wrong with the code you wrote, and exactly how to fix it.

Professor Holly is probably the best professor I had in my major, she cares about you as a person and your grades. Her lectures are straightforward forward and she fixes her mistakes in a quick second. She is very informative and gives you great feedback!

First off I think Professor D is really nice. Lectures are a tiny bit boring but she uses power points well and posts them on my courses. I recommend her.

Mere is the best HANDS DOWN, she is a beyond excellent PA 1, 2 & 3 professor. She can be tough but it only makes you better.

This is for HIST350, "Terrorism, Intelligence, and War". Easily one of if not the best professor I've ever taken at RIT. Lectures are incredibly interesting, filled with fun anecdotes. Tribunals (debates) are enjoyable and at no point was the class overwhelming with work

He is a great professor. Class was very easy. Some may find his lectures boring if ur not truly interested in the topics, but he does not test on anything he lectures on, so you don't really need to listen to them. tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This is a super easy class. There's a ton of reading, but in reality, none of it is truly required. Quizzes are nice because he tells us what kind of questions will be asked. There's no homework other than reading. He took attendance at the beginning of the semester, but stopped.

Dr. Henning is an easygoing professor. He asks that you come to class, listen to lectures, do some readings before discussions, write two papers, and take two exams. He always goes over what could be on the exam a week in advance. The papers were both around seven pages, but only asked about the contents of one book each. He wants you to succeed.
Great professor! Gives a lot of good feedback and is a great professor to learn from! Seriously one of the best professors I've ever had at this school, and I wish I could take more classes with him!

He is a phenomenal teacher. I wasnt expecting any good classes my freshman year but I was surprised. He stressed the importance of understanding race in the history of America, spoke respectfully of all parties, didnt glorify the founding fathers and rather spoke of them in terms of basic facts, and respects honesty and character. 10/10.

Dr. Henning is the best history professor I have ever had. He brings to his classes historical perspectives that go beyond information presented in the four or five required text books. Overall really easy class. Grades consisted of a couple in-class essays on reading material. Watched a lot of movies about American history. Nice guy and easy grader if you've read the material.

I took with him two classes and I really enjoyed them. He is very nice guy who cares about his students. He assigns bunch of books that are not really relevant to most of the lectures. Tests are essays and if you take good notes during the lecture, you will do well. If you want an easy liberal arts class, take his class!
Good teacher. Uses in class essay tests for your grade. Usually lectures but also shows movies to supplement. If you go to class you will do well.

A great guy and a great teacher. Lectures are semi boring but you learn a lot. He doesn't take attendance so if ur smart in history you do not need to show up a lot. Books he assigns are a little lengthy but turns out i hardly used them. Two test and a final. He will tell your whats on the test so go to the class before it. Easy A or B

Good choice for a mandatory liberal arts class. As said before, the only tests are essays.  I found it incredibly hard to stay focused/awake in class or even get to class in general because its pretty boring. He's a super nice guy though.  As a hint, be sure to go to the class before a test because he tells you what's going to be on it.
Nice guy, wants to help. The only grades are essay tests. For a history class it lacks discussion, but a good choice for a liberal arts.
Very easy! Very boring! This class made me fall asleep every time.  Tests are just essays, and you don't need to do the readings as long as you pay attention a little bit in class.
The work load assigned is not small but not impossible. He is a fair grader and an understanding professor. History can be dry but you will learn a lot from him!
Very boring professor, but extremely nice. Will go out of his way to answer questions...and a fairly easy essay grader. Would recommend.
Great professor.  Can be boring at times, but is usually quite interesting; ask him about his trips to Japan.  Fair grader, doesn't care much if you miss a few classes.  Definitely recommended.

He's a pretty cool the guy, the class is pretty easy as long as you take notes. He tells you exactly what is on the tests.
He was one of the worst in my entire college career. ranks in the top 2.

If you cant write well, dont take him. I got C's on all of my papers. Somewhat hard of a paper grader, I thought they all deserved B's. Boring lecturer. Assigns too much reading and gets behind in lecture.

He assigns so much reading and you can barley keep up with.  Meanwhile he is about 4 days behind the reaading he assigns for class and more then 100 years behind in where a assigned paper wants us to be

Easy teacher, class is a bit boring sometimes but he explains everything, you're aware of what is on each test and papers aren't so bad. I had an A without working too hard. I'd take him again. He's a great guy.

After a withdrawal, I was not looking forward to retaking this course, but I'm thankful it was with Prof. Lindberg. His lectures were extremely clear and his tests were pretty clear cut. Keep up to date on the labs and their abstracts and do well on the tests and you're golden.

Great teacher!!! Should take Univ Phys 1A with him if at all possible. Clear teaching style and throws in jokes to keep your attention. Great Professor, very approachable, makes physics easier. He is willing to help and work with the student to make sure that they understand the material.

(University Physics) Great professor. Very approachable, very interested in getting students to understand material. Quizzes and tests are fair- he doesn't make them super difficult just to trick you. Workload is average.

Great professor, he's friendly, approachable, clear, and helpful. Physics is not easy and his class is no exception but he presents the information very well and tries to give partial credit where he can.

Very good teacher. Gives examples on just about every problem you would see on a test, and is crystal clear with his explainations. Throws in a few jokes every now and then, and also is very approachable outside the class.

Seriously this professor is probably one of the best physics professor around. he taught me everything that my high school physics teacher tried and more. highly recommend. he will do anything to help you get by and get the best grade possible. he makes rit physics doable. hands down best physics teacher around

greatest ever

I was excited about this class but was surprised by the lack of communication Rachel offered. She makes clear instructions and such but don't expect person emails or one-on-one conversations.

She is the first teacher that made me want to withdraw from a class that I was halfway through in my final semester. She is extremely picky about every assignment and her guidelines are outrageous! She makes the class much less enjoyable and gives a lot more work that is irrelevant and useless. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

A very strict professor. Will be honest and will tell you your work sucks. Not very flexible when it comes to DSO accommodations. work will be critiqued harshly and you most likely won't get very good grades if you don't do it in the right program or the right way. not the right professor for students looking to get into 3D character design

Gary is very passionate about 3D and cares about his students. He is very interactive and will take the time to help you understand things. His projects are very open for creativity and individuality and provides decent feedback after grading.

Gary has his flaws but overall is a good professor. He takes some getting use to, as when you first have him he seems cold, but he will give you decent critiques. He is not very good at making assignments/criteria, so be prepared for periods of confusion. He is a professor that gives as much as you give, when you don't try he will reciprocate it.
Just no

Gary is such a great professor once you get to know him. At first, he comes across as intolerably stubborn, bossy, and frightening but it's just an act. He doesn't want unmotivated slackers attending his class. He's actually a giant teddy bear at heart. Yeah, he's pretty great at teaching and he knows his stuff. I think he is very intelligent.

Took Philosophy with this professor online and this was by far the worst class I have taken in college. Lectures were pre-recorded that you have to watch, about 1-2 hours, plus readings. Quizzes and discussion posts every week and are really hard. Absolutely did not learn anything in this class and was a complete waste of my time.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Tough grader']
comment: Took this class online with friends. The class discussions and will hand out 50's even when you try your best with a 700 word count + discussion post. Gives zero feedback and the class is an absolute joke. Its more like an automatic machine then an actual class. When confronted about the grades he always just says " review the grading criteria"
In all my times here at RIT, I have NEVER had a professor this bad. I would honestly not recommend this professor at all.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Took this class online for for professional ethics, He goes by jack sanders for some reason. The class itself is a lot of work. You can keep retaking the homework however the answers change. Discussion posts aren't graded fair as I sent out an email to the entire class and very few were getting full credit. No feedback for the discussion grading

Watch the lectures, read the materials, participate in the discussions and take the quizzes(over and over again!).  Invest the time to do all the work. You get a chance to  make up at the end of the course but I would not suggest waiting till the end if you have to make up. The lectures were interesting and made me think.
PHENOMENAL lectures!  Freaking phenomenal and completely mind-blowing!  He treats you like an intelligent adult, whether you deserve it or not! Phenomenal, life-changing class!
Professor Sanders is a fair professor, and he spells out how you can easily get an A in his class.  The reading can be dense and overwhelming, but if you can get past that, you will enjoy his class.
Even though the subject matter is awful, Sanders presents it well. Only had online but he was always fair and allowed work to be done mostly on own sched. Even discussion posts.

Took Sanders for Philosophy and Business Ethics. His classes are complex. You absolutely must acquire the books and do all of the readings as well as participate with legitimate, researched responses to discussions. You can ace to class if you write well consistently and keep retaking  quizzes. Very knowledgeable. looks like a greek philosopher.

I had this professor for two onlines classes. Both time he has been very clear on what he wants. He gives you plenty of opportunity to get a better grade and improve your test scores. You can always go back to improve. He is flexible and willing to work with you. There is a lot of reading and you won't pass if you don't read the material.
GOAT

Chazz is a chill guy and a great professor. His sense of humor is just fantastic and he keeps the class lively. He's always willing to help if you have any questions and is good at explaining topics in a clear fashion. His tests are easy as long as you do the homeworks and practice problems. Overall he's a great time.

Chazz is a lot of fun to be in class with. He is a lovable guy because of his awkward tendencies which cause him to make a lot of jokes. His quizzes and tests are easy, as long as you know your stuff. Take his class and enjoy surfing the sine wave!

Chasse is amazing!  He is really helpful and always available and willing to answer questions and re-explain difficult topics.  I had to miss a few classes for states, and he met with me outside of class for 2 hours to teach me exactly what I was going to miss.  highly recommend taking him!!  I already signed up to take him again next semester!

Dr. C is the best! He is the first math teacher I have had at this school that has a personality. BY FAR the best thing about him is his willingness. He came in on his day off to meet me to help with homework when I was struggling and helped guide to places to raise my grade. I wouldn't have passed without him.
Lectures are really boring but the exams and quizzes are really easy. Everything he tests on are on his review sheets and there is a lot of chances for extra credit.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor Ivanov is extremely dull and extremely quiet. Lots of opportunity to improve grade: replaces two lowest homework with highest homework grades and gives two make-up quizzes and one make-up exam. All homework and make ups are online. Practice tests are exactly like the actual exams and quizzes. Read the textbook and you'll be fine.

Listen closely to his lectures because he gives very insightful thoughts but he might not write it on the board. His handwriting is different from typical American handwriting because he is Serbian, but it is legible enough, especially if you are listening to what he is actually saying. It is not difficult to get a good grade in this class.

He grades on very few things, and you'll need to self teach. He gives a ton of extra credit, including a make up exam at the end of the semester, so his class is extremely forgiving. Attendance is "mandatory" but not very helpful because it doesn't affect your grade. Lectures are very dull but he often gives practice versions of tests and quizzes.

Hard to understand, his notes are illegible and his grading system doesn't make sense. There is usually homework due every two weeks but that varies as well. I've pretty much had to teach myself everything in this course. The only good thing is that he gives quite a lot of extra credit.

Attendance was mandatory, and an absolute waste of time. Struggled to complete his example problems in class, and when he did, he did so incorrectly. Poor communication, awful handwriting, all-around terrible experience

Great teacher, learned a ton in Data Comm with him. People did struggle in the class, but he turned a lab into extra credit and I think overall people did well. Very cool dude, has a lot of good stories about hacking things based on the content material. Can't stress how useful the class was tho, would recommend if you have the time to work.

One of my fav professors at RIT. I was scared after I read her reviews, but she is extremely nice and cares a lot about students' learning and understanding information. Exams were writing assignments and were fairly easy, reading quizzes, and a lot of in-class group work. She clearly gets information across and uses interactive learning

Probably my favorite Prof. She is super energetic and SUCH a good teacher. Best class is Cancer Bio. She will make you learn the material to get a good grade for sure, but that's why you're taking the class. Cell Molecular was hard but I learned so much. I have no doubt that all the bad reviews are just bc the material is hard. 10/10 Prof.

Dr. Wright is an amazing person who is very caring of her students, she is very clearly knowledgable of the material she is teaching as well, the issue comes in that her teaching style is not effective for a majority of people. Be prepared to teach yourself off Google as lectures are minimal.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']
comment: First, she's a wonderful person and her cheery attitude really brings up the whole class. Unfortunately, she also has little to no teaching ability. Oftentimes, she can go off on tangents, gloss over difficult concepts and elaborate too much on simple ones, single students out in class and get insulted at classroom humor. Avoid her classes.

One of my favorite professors! The material she teaches can be a bit challenging but she is more than willing to have 1 on 1 meetings with you to make sure you do your very best. Content is clearly communicated and easy to follow. Highly recommend!

Dr. Wright is a great lady, but I would never recommend a class with her. She's intelligent, but her active style learning is not effective and I don't think anyone had any idea what was going on in class. The exams were impossible and seemed like the questions were about random things. Even if you study you have no idea what's on the exams.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Tests are tough']
comment: Gives you no clear notes. Nothing to study with. Worksheets you get in class do not have answers so you are left wondering if it is even right. Expects you to know the information and has you work with other students instead of teaching you. Does not provide answer keys to tests so hard to tell what you got wrong but willing to answer questions

Uses an "active learning style" which comes of as random and doesn't seem to have a clear path. Over does easy concepts and brushes over complex subjects. It's really hard to follow if you are used to typical lectures. Exams are crazy hard, everyone failed the first one because of her poor wording and obscure genetic problem solving questions.

This would be my favorite prof in this school for this semester! Dr. Wright is an awesome prof that makes you think really hard about the "why" and "how" for every point she teaches and the amazing thing is she can explain the points really clearly and thoroughly! Besides the classes she's inspirational, caring and extremely kind! I love her!

Dr. Wright is one of the nicest people I've ever met but her classes are difficult. I had her for intro to bio and then again for cell bio. I get very stressed before exams because I know they're going to be confusing and Im always right. On the bright side, if you ask for help, she is more than willing to do so.
Sets the class up like a highschool class, so it's very easy to follow. The material isn't necessarily easy, but she presents it very well and answers questions clearly. Very lively and kind.

Dr. Wright is Great! She knows her stuff and can be really helpful one on one. The class itself is tough and the book is incredibly dense. But if you pay attention and just learn the concepts and cell machinery, you'll do well. Just expect to study alot, go to the study sessions. Not a class for someone not interested in the material.

The course itself is hard, but if you do what you're supposed to you'll be fine. Read the textbook. Dr. Wright is very helpful and interactive. Her models really helped me understand. I liked that we didn't do the same thing every day. Take the bioportal quizzes over until you get 100. At office hours she will explain anything, including tests.

For Biology of Cancers she was a really great professor. Got me 10x more interested then I was before I entered the class. 3 papers to write which she is very helpful in providing feedback. The class isn't so much work but it is something. Very interactive course. I would highly recommend taking this course.

She is a bubbly and kind person, HOWEVER as a teacher she is horrible. Her tests cover maybe 25% of actual material taught in lectures and the rest is concept based. instead of teaching material she uses foam pieces and blocks to try and explain but it never works out, Just make sure you do all your homework and online quizzes and you might get a B

STAY CLEAR!!! Sporadic teaching. Tries to help but cannot explain simple concepts. No answer keys posted for any tests. Final is cumulative but unless you ask about ever single question there is no way to know what you had right or wrong. Overall one of my WORST experiences at RIT.
Her tests are extremely, extremely difficult and her teaching seems random. There isn't much to learn from her class but she has high expectations. Nice person though!

I took her for cell biology, hated the class.  She is kind of all over the place with her notes, and worksheets, her test are absolutely the hardest test ive ever taken, ive studied the notes, book and had a tutor it still doesnt work.   the book sucks and doesnt help any.  I wouldnt take this class again.... her test are impossible!

Cell Biology with Dr. Wright was a pleasure. Her exams are thorough, not difficult; if you pay attention in lecture, and review her power points and study guides for each exam, you should be more then sufficiently prepared. She is extremely approachable and really understands the material. She honestly cares about the well being of her students.

her test is pretty difficult. just study hard and pay attention to class. and yes I think you should take Perry for Cell Biology. I hear lot about Perry and they say lot of positive things about Perry

There is a reason you use this site, because you need advice. My advice is AVOID AVOID AVOID her AT ALL COSTS! Shes very nice, but her tests are ridiculously hard. Grading scheme: 70%test (drops one test), 20%group assignments, 10%presentation.
Difficult to understand at times and lectures are both quick and somewhat random. Helpful if you go and ask for help but it takes a lot of focus and studying to do well.

Dr. Wright is a terrible teacher.  She just talks and talks and doesn't allow time to process and understand what is going on.  50% of her class is "FYI" and then she says "this is for your general information, but you won't need to know it for a test".... THEN WHY ARE YOU TELLING US IT?!  I thought the class was very unorganized and scattered.
Professor Wright is an expert on the subject. Very smart woman. And adorable. I had her for molecular and learned a TON.

This is the person to take it with if you want to learn about cell biology. She knows her stuff, she is a little challenging but she is really passionate and will help. You can get an A on tests and its all multiple choice. Pay attention and study hard. Plus she's not that bad looking :). 89.5 = A

Her tests are ridiculously difficult. She tells you that one thing will be on the exam, and it's not. She asks extremely specific questions. And she spends more than half of her class time going over "FYI slides, which you don't need to know". But you will see them on the exam. Take Cell Bio with Perry.
Not a bad professor, but her exams are too hard and it sucks because most of the grades come from the exams.

As a professor she is really good. She posts up slides and is very helpful and will answer your questions. She tries to make a great effort to make sure you understand. Her tests are a hard, multiple choice, and makes you think. Really good class. You need to read the book and pay attention to lectures. If you put in a good amount of time then = A
don't take cell bio with newman/wright. you checked this site for a reason. here's your advice, rochester.
Nice, kinda spacey at times, but teaches well. Tests can be challenging, but are always fair. A pleasure to have as a prof for the second time.

Dr. Write is a good teacher, sometimes a little out there but really nice and will answer all questions.  Does not make you come to class but it's wise to do so.  She is pretty cute...so its helper there :)

Julia is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I don't think her personality is for everyone, but with that said, I also don't think she's that hard to get along with either. Julia respects hard workers that take responsibility for their own education.

Highly unstable, ego driven and treats students like her servants. I don't understand why she teaches, she's not an educator. Overly concerned with her legacy.  Thankfully she moved to the University of Montana.
Don't do it! awesome artist but worthless teacher.
took the class outside of my major. very difficult, but she is an amazing potter. if you really want to learn and push yourself, take a class from her.
This teacher has done nothing but tell me things to do, then yell at me for doing them.  There is a habit of MICRO-MANAGING her students, to the point where they feel bad about themselves.
I agree with the rest of the comments at this time.
No Comments
No Comments

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Anju Gupta tries her best. She has a very sweet soul - but I honestly don't think she even knew what class she was teaching. Her lectures consisted of no examples and rewriting the textbook on the board. She was offended when you asked her questions. You'll never know how you did in the class, because she has to curve the test so severely.

Prof Critelli is an adjunct Professor in the Computing Security Department.  Great class, definitely would take it again.  He is able to keep lectures that might be dry fairly entertaining with real world examples and stories.

Super nice and always willing to give help and feedback on hw emailed to him before its due, great resource to take advantage of to do well. The excel is not always that simple and the lectures can sometimes be a stretch when applied in the labs. Overall, it's not hard to figure out if you put the time in. Final exam was very difficult.

Prepare to teach yourself throughout this entire class. This professor will allow you to submit assignments in advance for feedback, but that feedback is never entirely accurate. The biggest downside of this professor is you must essentially beg to get the Excel equation answers for what you did wrong. One of the most frustrating profs in saunders.

Great professor. Hes very funny and caring. Email him your homework for feedback and you are most likely going to get a 50/50. Uses excel to do the homework and in class exercises / notes. Excel is pretty simple. Final exam was hard but you are allowed to have a formula sheet and use excel which was a big help...

Professor is very nice. He has many HW and Class Assignments all based on excel and his lectures. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow but he does a good job and is very passionate. Definitely email him any questions or hw to look over as he will always give feedback and corrections ensuring you can do well. Final Exam was difficult.

Such a bad Professor for finance. really unorganized, doesnt want to help students will make you figure everything out on your own. Tests are hard, refuses to give any study material other than the syllabus. timed exams and sometimes the right answer isnt even available. So so bad

worst class & professor I have had in 5 years at RIT. Prof is not responsive to students concerns. Lectures are all over the place, messy excel sheets, VERY hard to follow. Tests really hard/heavy, barely have enough time. he ALWAYS makes mistakes on quizzes/assignments leaving u confused. I would rather drop out of uni than take him again.

Barely answer your questions, just ask you to work by yourself. Wondering about what's the meaning for such a class if the teacher don't answer questions. Do not reply email. Feel bad about that. Don't know about his other class, but If I have another choice I would not take his FINC 742.
Really great teacher, but really tough. You will learn a lot, but it won't come easily!
It is a good combo of tough, with opportunities to get a good grade
Not gonna lie, he is hard. Nevertheless, you will learn a lot and you will like him at the end. Plus he makes the class very interactive and interesting.
He's an excellent professor. You can learn real and new things in his class.
really good teacher, but also tough.  Makes you work for your grade.
No Comments
best professor in RIT and very understanding

She is one of the best professor in RIT and very understanding. I would suggest anyone to take her if you have chance. You will not regret I can guaranteed. She is not easy, also not too hard on you. If you participate, write papers on time you will have easy A.

Honestly the best professor I have ever had in my three years of college, she's super kind and clearly cares about her students. she's super lenient during the current difficulties we are all having, and gives students extensions and mental health days. I could not recommend her enough!!!

If you have the opportunity to take Dr. Ma's course... DO IT! She has been one of the most energetic, kind, and caring professors I have had at RIT so far. She knows how to run a lecture and make sure her students understand the content. She also incorporates some fun projects into the class for all skill levels.

great professor and the work he gives you really helps you understand the topic more. You will actually be using social media accounts in the class and that is awesome when you compare it to the topics taught. He is very understanding and a really nice person too

Dr. Ma's class was the only one I took this semester that was stress relieving rather than inducing. She cares far more about you understanding the material and being engaged rather than quizzing you on every little thing, so as long as you give it your all, you're set. Look forward to taking a course with her again.

Dr. Ma is such a kind and caring professor and I would highly recommend taking her. She is very accessible outside of class and she is always willing to help and answer any questions. There were few assignments outside of class, so as long as you put in the effort, you will do fine.

Dr. Sims knows the topic extremely well and teaches exactly what you need to know for his class. The lectures were very entertaining and always stayed on topic. I am very happy that I took this course, and would recommend it to anyone who is interested in International Political Science.

Professor Sims gives good lectures, although the ban on using laptops to take notes seems unnecessary and antiquated. He gives very harsh feedback on essays. The first two tests were reasonable, but the final was extremely difficult and did not follow the same format as the previous tests.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Assigns a lot of readings but explains them very well in class. He stops every so often to make sure everyone understands what he's talking about. Lectures are very in depth.

Classes are just lectures, but he is really good, goes over the readings during class in a way that makes complex material make sense. He really knows what he is talking about. Tests aren't hard and are online.

Prof. Sims gives clear, informative lectures. No homework, but expect ~30 pages of reading per week. Graded only on participation and multiple-choice quizzes. You'll need to buy several books. Paying attention and taking good notes in lectures is critical, but if you do, the quizzes are easy. Overall a great class, if you like the subject.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This had to be one of the worst classes I have ever taken. This professor is super boring and is hard to pay attention to while in class and if you dont pay attention you will get lost and he will not care.

Professor Sims did a great job of keeping people engaged and explaining the themes of the reading assignments. There are reading assignments every class, but they are usually entertaining and relevant to events happening today. If I get the chance, I will take another one of his classes.

Simple 50min lectures. Remained very unbiased towards political situations in class. More focused on teaching info than opinion. If you take decent notes and pay attention the class is fairly easy and doesn't take much outside time. He can seem a little, for lack of a better term, eager to prove you wrong though. But overall a decent prof.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Very knowledgeable on the material. Show up to class and take notes and you should basically be set for exams. Took this during the pandemic so we watched movies for homework and it was interesting and relevant to class. Would take again 100%

Dr. Sims is an amazing professor. He is kind and gives great feedback on work. He will pre-read your essay rough drafts before you turn it in. He is pretty reading heavy but he explains the readings very well in class! He is one of the best professors I have ever had and I have taken many classes with him!

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Lecture heavy but if you come to class and pay attention, the tests are easy. He thoroughly explains the readings you have to do in each class so don't be daunted by all the reading.
He said he loved our class, but he only loves us because he wants to educate us

If you truly enjoy learning about history and philosophy, this is the course and professor to take. There will be a lot to read, but every bit of it is worthwhile. Papers are not long, nor are there many. If you put effort into the course you will be graded accordingly, and you will absolutely better your understanding of the world around you.

Extremely boring class, can be hard to pay attention, especially because he is very flat toned. Sometimes you can't even hear him. You have to read all homework or else you will be lost and confused. You have to write a lot of essays and he's a tough grader. For the final, he makes you write two essays which are long and stressful.

Professor Sims is an Incredibly knowledgeable and intelligent Political Scientist. He approaches international relations with the seriousness it deserves, and expects a lot out of his students. I could see his courses being frustrating for non Poli-Sci majors, but he is a fair grader an an amazing lecturer. Read, ask questions, and u will do fine.
Tough Grader, be prepared to read tons of book, be really to empty your pockets buying lots of books. Attendance mandatory, take tons of notes, hard! Easy to fall sleep during class! Dont take 8am!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Doesn't put grades in MyCourses so ask him directly. Lots of reading, and didn't allow our class to have "electronics". So you have to get a hard copy of the reading. Straight out of grad school and sometimes condescending. Gives good feedback on papers, which makes up most of your grade. Explains the reading in great detail, take lots of notes.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Tests? Not many', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: You will only learn this. Be good guy, not bad guy

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor Sims is right out of graduate school, so he does act a bit condescending towards undergraduates who aren't even PoliSci majors. Although, he is accessible through office hours and will critique papers prior to submitting them to get a good grade! ALSO: super hot
Complete waste of time and money. Avoid her classes at all costs.
One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Her class was a complete waste of time. Half the time, she was going on meaningless rants, and the other half I had no clue what she was saying.

Very passionate about what she teaches. Lengthy video-heavy online lectures. Wouldn't be that bad, but unfortunately she has a very thick combination of accents, making her very difficult to understand. Few assignments, mandated attendance for full class time.
One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Has no clue what she is talking about.
Absolutely awful professor. Don't take her class.
Not a good professor. Goes on random tangents about information that does not matter and her classes were a waste of time. Avoid.

Class time was wasted on trivial activities like watching movie trailers instead of meaningful lectures. Went on endless rants such as a 45-min talk about wearing clean clothes to an interview which could have been condensed to 5-min. Assignment criteria didn't match industry standards, leaving us unprepared for real-world scenarios. Would avoid

Prof. Bhole was an awesome teacher to have for ECON101. He was absolutely clear in his explanations and was very caring towards his students. The quizzes and Exams are online but without knowing the material its a bit difficult to pass. He is the best professor to have for ECON101. It's a shame he doesn't teach ECON201, I would have loved his class

Professor Bhole is very concise when it comes to course content. Based on my previous knowledge from econ, he makes the content way more digestible (though a little boring at times). As long as you follow the examples from the notes, draw some graphs, and look up a few extra examples on chegg you'll do alright.

Dr. Bhole is an outstanding professor for ECON. He taught us the topics in a way that was easy to understand and went at the right pace. He won't overload you with work and the way he teaches the class really adds to your understanding of the economy.

Professor Bhole was a great instructor for the class. He is willing to help outside of class on the material. He posts the slides on his website. he does give weekly quizzes but are not difficult as long as you have gone over the slides.

His lectures are clear and straight-forward. The practice question and quizzes are on the material he goes over in his lectures, so if you pay attention you'll be fine. He posts the power points for lectures, it's good to look them over before class, typically they are not very long. He is always available and willing to help outside of class.
He is a great professor. If you follow his lecture and practices, you will be fine.

He is really easy teacher. He understands life happens, and is super willing to help you out. He is also incredibly accessible outside of class, so if you need help, you got it! The lecture consists of review his powerpoint notes that he provides before class. I typically read the notes before hand. Overall, great professor.
not really good at teaching difficult concepts.

Also have him for Game Theory right now. He is really good at teaching economics, but I rate him the way I did because he is super accommodating and really wants you to succeed. Some of the professors at RIT really could learn from this guy as far as being patient with students and promoting learning the material over testing you on it.

This is the only economics professor i actually liked in the program. Economics made no sense to me and i have since switched majors, but this guy was really easy to understand and you could tell that he wanted you to pass. I was able to somehow understand the material and pass with B+. Helpful Office Hours. Lots of review questions.
Tough class, but a lot of fun if you work hard.

Had Professor Bhole for Game Theory and Industrial Organization. Not easy classes, but if you show up and do the optional practice problems you can get an A. He tends to curve tests and offers many chances for extra credit! Classes are heavily theory based, so be aware that there might not be many practical applications outside of the classroom.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He definitely knows his material and is usually able to answer any question related to the topic. He gives no mandatory homework but the practice is very helpful. If you have a hard time understanding Indian accents, I would not recommend taking his class. His handwriting is not much better although he does type up some information and project it.

He is not that hard to understand when compared to other people at RIT.  If you pay attention in class or at least go over the in class slides once or twice on your own in addition to doing the practice questions, an A is a realistic outcome.

No homework. Grade depends on tests and 'participation' (show up and pay attention). He has an accent but speaks well, I had no trouble understanding him. Very knowledgeable and willing to go slowly if you ask. (He lists a textbook but I never got it and still did well). Do the practice questions! (some are on his tests)
He is well educated, he tries his best, but he is still not good in teaching. Also, you need to deal with his strong Indian accent.
Bharat can be a bit hard to understand sometimes, but if you pay close attention, you will understand. Class participation definitely matters.
Cannot understand a word he says. Flys through lectures like nothing.
Great professor. Very nice, understanding, and easy to work with. Gives all the material you need to get above 100% on his tests. He's clearly improved throughout the years. Always happy and smiling.

Very friendly and will answer all your questions as long as you ask. Did not need to purchase a text book as he provided an ebook for all his students. Attendance is not mandatory but it is obviously helpful in preparing for tests. He posts most of his notes online which helps as well. Great professor, would recommend!
He is a good dude, real funny, and always in a good mood.  He was also an excellent teacher :)

Great teacher. His accent doesn't take long to get used to at all. Great sense of humor, he made the class enjoyable. If you don't get a concept it's your own fault because he gives plenty of opportunity to ask for clarification.

Excellent professor. Hard working. One of the best to take Microeconomics with. Don't know of a better 1. Never read or bought the book. You don't need it. Got an A. Very comprehensive notes. They are most important. If you FULLY understand them, quizzes and tests will be a breeze. He is a young Indian professor with doctorate degree. Great Guy!!!

His tests are difficult but with some studying and re-reading of your notes it shouldn't be to hard to get an A. He curves his grades and allows test corrections on all major exams.  I will certainly be taking his classes again.

Little homework and it's usually easy. The tests are very hard in comparison to the homework. If you don't want to put in A LOT of effort studying, even if he curves a lot, you probably won't end up with the grade you want. Overall, he is helpful and reasonable. If you want a challenge, this professor is for you.

Really good teacher, jokes sometimes, yes his tests are hard but you really come out knowing what's what. I would recommend him, it's a struggle, but little homework only 3 tests. Fun class discussions too.

Classes are pretty interesting. He allows a lot of people to participate which will bring up your grade. Homeworks are really easy. Tests are ridiculously hard, but he curves them but letting you do corrections and lowering an A to about an 80.

Great teacher! If you want to learn economics take him. His tests are hard but he curves it accordingly, he's more interested in making sure the students understand the material. He's very helpful outside the classroom. I'd say he's a must take if you want to be challenged or are going into anything with economics!

Difficult class. Teaches at low level, tests at high level. High curves, though. Many graphs, too much math, barely any conceptual teaching. Will go on tangents and will do easy examples, but give you hard problems for homework. His notes aren't that helpful. However he will go out of his way to work with you and is extremely well-versed in his field.

I took Dr. Burnette for Intro for Macroeconomics and Macroeconomics. I was able to pull off an A in both classes. His exams consist of 3 parts: multiple choice, short answer(written response), essay questions(math problems). Pay attention, go to office hours, do homework, study before tests and you are guaranteed an A. Good Luck.
hard tests, bu manageable if you do the homework. I never looked at the book and still managed to pull an A.

Difficult class, but there is a HUGE curve, so if you actually go to class and pay attention, you will do fine. MC sections on tests are difficult because they aren't discussed much in class, but you have a chance after the test to get half the points you lost on MC back. Essay sections are easy if you payed attention.

Prof. Burnette was EXTREMELY helpful.  As long as you're willing to put in the work, he's more than willing to work around your schedule to meet with you.  Working with him one on one is what prepared me for the tests.  The class is challenging, but not hard.  You just have to do all of the practice questions he suggests before each test!

very hard class. very hard to get an A. if you work hard it will be worth it. He gives big curves to his grades. Writes a lot of sloppy notes on board but gives good online notes. Would recommend if u want a challenge

Most helpful professor I've ever had.  Cares about his teaching and his students if you put in the effort.  The class is hard but he does more than you could ask for to help.  It's rating the professor not the class...

He is very very tough. His exams will contain nothing of what he thought in his class. Grades homework and class participation but you will notice that no one actually can participate. I agree he has a lot of knowledge, but I guess student are here to learn. they havn't done economics ever before.

I would bet money that the people ****ing about how hard this course is either didn't pay attention in class, didn't do the required work, or suck at algebra. It's a challenging class but if you're an RIT student you might want to learn how to deal with that.
Hardest class I've had at RIT, and I'm well into computer science. Avoid.

Some of you guys need to stop whining... the class is difficult and the tests are real hard but he gives away so many free pints for them via curves...he's willing to help during office hours and overall is a really great guy. Stop complaining and start studying.

This guy is ridiculous. His notes sometimes contradict what it says in the book, which is evident in the tests. The class doesn't seem that hard until the tests, then you feel extremely violated. If you like to pull your hair out, by all means take this class.

Burnette is the kind of guy you wanna hang out with. He's not really the guy you want teaching your class. His tests are absolutely ridiculous, but so is the curve, at times. He's a big Mets fan, so he's got that going for him.
HIS TEST ARE RETARDED HARD he doesn't prepare you for them, and expect you to spend tons of time out of class just practicing problems

Burnette is a great guy, but the class is excruciatingly difficult to the point where the class average for a test was a 49%. But the curve is huge. The class is also very boring and sometimes you can't wait for class to be over.

Very difficult class, but he is a great guy and helpful outside of class. The tests are very hard, but with a curve being distributed on each one (a 50% curved to a C-). Though it's very hard, it's very possible to get an A or a B with effort.

Likes to go off on tangents during class for a good 20 minutes or so. Notes are very broken hard to read his writing and he likes to stand right in front of the notes. You are not prepared very well for his test because you are not given anything like the questions that are asked. But yet is always available to talk, even though it doesn't help.

OMG! Not an easy class, but not everything can just be handed to you... lectures are boring, he is a very "global" teacher, jumps around a lot, and VERY hard to follow... He can be helpful if you see him during his office hours..the tests are hard... he only takes attendence for the first 2 weeks.... Not the best teacher, not the worst

Teerrrible terrible teacher...DO NOT TAKE HIM...he doesnt explain a single thing.  If you ask him a question he says its wrong, proves its right but says oh no its wrong...dont do it to yourself guys...just don't...
He is a great guy, who is there to help any and all of his students.  This class is by no means an easy A, but with some drive its very possible and you can learn a lot.

He says in the beginning of the course that he has a set number of A's and B's which he gives out. Some people may find this a bit unfair. His tests are moderately difficult but he does curve them. If you did well and understood economics in high school then this course shouldn't be too difficult, provided you put a little effort in.

The class is easy. He explains things pretty well. If you pay attention to his lectures, it isn't hard to do decently on the tests. Burnette is an easy-going guy, and generally a good person. He doesn't take attendance either.
Dropped this class after 6 weeks, it was too much, no way to get even a B, not worth it for an elective

THIS IS THE HARDEST CLASS EVER!the curve is ridiculous though. a 24% in our class curved up to a low D.This class is so hard,but he never takes attendence and is actually a really cool guy. If you go to his office hours and try, you will pass his class, just show him your trying.  And his name is Jeffery, not Jeremey.
very hard... but a big curve
Easy class do your work and you'll pass. very boring class though

This professor is my favorite professor I ever had in college. She is very flexible, and very reasonable. When I had issue mental health, I tend to not do a lot of homework. She understand my struggle with mental health, and because of that, I was able to catch up to my work. This is reason why I want give her have great rate!
She's very mellow. If you're polite and participate, she's happy.
hard for Chinese student
BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!!
Once you do her assignments and attend all of her classes. You ll be her favorite student. She is very sweet person. You should take a class under her when you need an easy A.
Melissa is the textile friend you never knew you needed.
There is a crippling amount of work for this class yet its easily my favorite class since she does such a good job teaching. Plus she really goes the extra mile for her students in and out of class.
Great knowledge of subject and very interactive class! Would definitely take it again
More lectures, less classwork. The faculty turning their grades in late.
*THIS IS A TEST*
Easy course overall. 3 multiple choice exams. Homeworks are the hardest part.

Dr. Kennedy was a very engaging professor to have. He loves students who participate, and the more engaging you are, the more he is likely to give you leeway for late work or absences. If you keep in communication with him about issues you're having he is extremely helpful.
Very group project heavy. Will cold call. But overall he makes sure you know your stuff. I would take it again but be prepared to work in a group.

The material itself isn't hard, but the professor makes the class more stressful than it needs to be. Frequent cold calling, strict grading over small details, and very little flexibility with deadlines. Participation feels more tense than productive.

If you had the option between taking this professor and getting the plague... get the plague. He will go through your group's google drive while screensharing on Zoom, he will expect you to be attentive and answering questions at 8am (and will cold call), and will air out your business/publicly humiliate you in front of the entire class.

"I am not here to not only educate you, I am here to inspire you". He really pushes you but in a kind way to get you to buy in. I read more papers in his class than I did in my all of my courses combined over my 4 years at RIT. My only warning is not to take his classes if you don't enjoy reading. #TheRealDrDre

Just graduated from RIT and Dr. Hudson was such a fantastic mentor to me and many other students. He really cares about his students and is a very nice guy. Go to him for anything and he will find a way to help you. I will miss him very much. Thank you Dr. Dre! You really helped me navigate RIT.

Dr. Hudson is a good teacher. The class has a lot of reading abd writing. He stresses reading and comprehension a lot. He is also very understandable and approachable. I would recommend taking him for any class he teaches. I am a senior and it was my first time taking him and I wondered why I havent taken him before.

Tons of writing and reading journal articles in Dr. Hudson's class. We wrote a paper in genomics and submitted to a journal. He is very down to earth and cool. He is also very compassionate. He will always find time to talk to you and he knows how to relate to students. I would highly recommend taking him.

Dr. Hudsons genomics course is a lot of reading research papers. Take home exams are a lot writing. Dr. Hudson is very reasonable and down to earth. His said his style for upper division courses are designed to prep you for the next level. I highly recommend him especially for research.

I was really scared to talk to Dr. Hudson because I thought he would be intimidating as the dept chair. I went into his office and he was so nice. He was able to help me with a situation I had. Every time he sees me he ask me how I am doing. You can tell that he really cares. I cant thank him enough.

Dr Hudson is great. Just finished bioseps with him. Very understanding and will explain things 10000 ways until you get it. Although he is busy as the dept head, he always has time for you and makes you feel like you belong. I will miss him when I graduate.

Dr. Hudson is an amazing professor. The lectures were great. He explains the material very clearly and does review before each exam, which really helps. He goes over doubts and questions as many times you ask.

Just had Dr Hudson for cell mol bio. Very solid prof and a nice guy. You will do well if you listen to him. He is very organized and grades exam very quickly. If Dr Hudson is teaching a class, I am taking it.
