Funny and energetic in class. Goes over a lot of examples, but minimal notes are taken. Content is difficult and almost all of your grade comes from three exams. Weekly quizzes help track your learning for the material.

Varela is awesome! He teaches the lectures in class at a perfect pace and stops and makes sure everyone understands before continuing on. Takes cheating seriously. Straight-forward homework and if you do this and understand it then you'll pass the tests easily. Very willing to help in office hours. Highly recommend!

Lecture was presented with clear and concise notes. All lecture material was posted online as well. Practice problems frequently assigned, but were not collected for credit. Exams were 50 min in class as were very challenging. Did crack jokes in class sometimes and was personable. Able to approach him outside of class.

Overall a decent professor. Goes over material fast so you HAVE to ask questions if you don't understand something or you'll fall behind. Final was way too long and hard. Weekly homework and quizzes make up a small portion of your overall grade. Helpful in office hours but they are limited.
Decent professor, answer question effectively and teaches the concepts very well. Hilarious, but he id quite a tough grader on tests. Much better than the other dynamics professor.

He make sure you understand the material and he'll answer any of your questions.  He uses the book a lot with almost all of the class examples from them.  He does a lot of these which is helpful. Overall he's a decent professor.
Easy class if you do many practice problems. Any tests and quizzes were problems straight out of the book.
He's a nice guy, hard to understand at times, and sometimes isn't clear in lectures but his quizzes are from the homework and tests are only a few questions. Overall not too bad.

Exams are only 2-3 questions and can be ambiguous. Grades are only like 8 quizzes, attendance, 3 exams. Can be a picky grader. Essentially reads textbook. Not the clearest of lectures and can't really draw. But he will meet with you.
Terrible teacher. Doesn't explain the material well; horrible at getting papers back to you; unfair grader. Don't take him.
Sometimes confusing, but makes time to study in the ELC.  Fair grader, tests have lots of easy points to get.
i think he is good

Very helpful and very supportive to students. ALOT of bonus points ( participation and quizzes).
Unfortunately, every week he gives a homework and a quiz, and worksheets are uploaded after every single class. Overall, he gives many work to do but amazing explanation and character.

Prof Beck is one of the nicest and most caring professors at RIT. He is definitely an expert in his field, but it sometimes felt like he wasn't transferring a ton of his knowledge to us. I feel like I didn't learn nearly as much as I was hoping to from his class. Assignments are straightforward and exams are mostly vocab.

The class was very easy to understand and very easy to do good in. You have two exams and 3 projects but if you do the weekly assignments and go to the lectures you will do just fine in this class. On the exams he takes problems directly from the weekly assignments and on the projects you can work with a partner which was nice.
Super easy class and very interesting, all you have to do is the homework.

Duane is the definition of a professor who goes above and beyond. Every lecture was enjoyable purely because of his personality. Duane was always eager to teach and gave off the impression that he genuinely wanted his students to learn and be successful in the future. The homework and exams were easily manageable by reading the textbook.
Duane is a real Gem. He is such a great wholesome caring guy that is always there to help. I would definitely recommend this professor.

Prof. Beck is hands down the best professors I have ever had. Hes incredibly easy to talk to and it is clear that he cares about the success of his students! As long as you pay attention in class and do your homework, it should be an easy A.
Beck is the nicest professor I've ever had. He isn't there to trick you. He wants all of his students to succeed and its evident. Just show up and do the work and you'll pass with ease.

Duane Beck is fantastic! His classes are really easy but he keeps them interesting and funny. He's worked in the industry for years so he knows what he's talking about and he makes sure that every student is succeeding and cares about everyone's education. Class and projects are very easy. Just don't bring up Chinese steel around him! (IYKYK)

Duane knows what he's talking about due to his years of experience in industry and in academia. You can come to him with just about any problem and he'll be able to help you find a solution. His classes are definitely too easy, but he does a good job of making sure that students absorb the material.

Duane cares about the success of his students. If you get a bad grade, he will let you redo it within reason. Usually cancels Friday class to let students work on the assignment. Midterm is the trickiest part of Duane's class and is based on one lecture about giving presentations. 5 misses allowed. Easy A if you show up and turn in assignments.
Great professor. Caring, knowledgeable, and flexible. Class is super easy. At least once a week class is option so there is time to work on homework, and the homework takes less than 30min to do.
He explains everything that you need to know in a clear way and is always willing to help. He also makes the class laugh and takes the class outside the classroom to explore other machines.
Class is a lot of fun and everyone is often laughing. Passing this class is easy as long as you do your homework and show up. The tests are easy to study for as long as you do the homework.

Duane has a lot of real world experience and is good about applying it and making what is otherwise really boring material somewhat interesting. He wants all his students to pass and knows it is boring so he makes classes very easy. Provides study guides before exams with all the questions on it, but you have to show up to class to get it.
Tough guy
Very nice professor, always willing to help you. Easy class to pass, just show up and that's it.
Took this course as a technical elective. He's a great professor and very inspirational. Offers help if you need it.
Great Professor ! Two thumbs up,  He teaches with Knowledge and his own experiences. Homework Is easy make sure you do it!

Most criminal justice  professors are great and prof Dicaro is one of the best , he is great. Come to class, participate, take notes and I am sure you will pass.  One midterm and One really fun group project. There is a final put its optional, only two people took it so as you can see its an easy class. its an easy A if you just do a lil work
Great professor, slides were very informative and the two grades are Midterm (easy) and Group Project (fun). Great CJ class

Great Professor and funny guy. Took roll call by last name. Kind of lengthy take-home midterm, big but fun group project and no final. We even had a field trip to the Rochester 911 center. Very approachable after/before class. Fun class participations. Answers emails quick. Great person to stay in touch with. Cares about his students.

Easy class, he said in the beginning of the quarter that there might be a final, there wasn't, there was a group project, and a mid-term, put in a little effort and its easy. Also, he a really nice guy and classes are short.

Whoa, completely wrong. This teacher is fantastic, he's extremely friendly and easy to talk to. His class's are short and he gives you a handout for every lecture which he bases his midterm on. The class consists of a lengthy take home test and a big group project. Put in some effort and it's easy. One of the better professors in CJ, and no final.

Nice guy who I think genuinely cares about students, but he is just not a good teacher. A bit more helpful in office hours, but still tough to understand what he is trying to teach you. Also, he assigns way too much homework, although he gives a lot of extra points on homework at the end of the semester

Changed tests to all short answer and is relentless with how strict his grading is on each problem. Useless lectures, I spent most of my time with every grad tutor. Lectures wasn't mandatory but there was a pop quiz every week. Unclear about what material to emphasize on and made us do many MasteringChemistry problems without teaching us how.

Absolutely terrible, assigns 50+ homework problems on MasteringChemistry, none of which have anything to do with what you do in class. Nobody in the class has a clue what is going on. Be prepared to teach yourself an entire course in organic chem.
Class was relatively easy, he provides old exams, of which half the questions are copied word for word. Haven't learned anything, but not too hard to earn my A.

The class isn't easy, but he is a really nice guy. He is really intelligent and sometimes has a hard time explaining things clearly, but not a bad teacher. The class wasn't too boring and getting an A was possible if you worked for it!

You would be better off teaching yourself. He gives 5 bonus points for going to class but lectures are useless. His tests have nothing to do with what he teaches.And the essay questions are ridiculous. grading is inconsistent. it seems easy at first but tests are 90% of the grade and they are very difficult.  but 75=B.

Worst professor I've had so far at RIT. Can't teach, makes the subject impossible to learn. After 2 quarters with him, all I've done was lower my GPA by getting 2 B's in his classes. DO NOT take him. If he's the only one teaching organic, WAIT for someone else!! You will be thankful. His lectures consist of him drawing random reactions.

He really is evil. This class is horrible bc Smith doesn't know how to teach. He is always 5 minutes late to class, and never answers question students ask in a straight manner. He called me stupid once, when I went to his office hours. NEVER again. I had a freaking 4.0 until I had to take his class!! Read the text. His lectures are useless.

CAN NOT TEACH. What he covers in lecture seems simple, but the test questions are WAY more difficult. Often takes the first 10 minutes of a 50 min lecture to set up, or 20 minutes to pass out a test, and wonders why people don't complete it. Assigns homework to topics that will be covered in future lectures. Incredibly frustrating. Avoid.

Attendance isn't mandatory but might as well be due to extra credit. Never administers tests on time, usually 10 to 15 minutes late and wonders why students don't complete exams. Lectures are difficult to follow and never follow the syllabus. The only way to learn anything in this class is to talk to the TA's and to read text independently.

Dr. Thomas is a great guy, with that said organic is hard and his teaching style is so so, but there is so much to the subject that he did the best he could.  Ive seen grades for other classes and he seems to get an avg of a B for his , The book is very helpful and is used constantly he may not get to everything he puts on a test,which is a problem
Organic is hard enough...dont take him. Nice guy but horribly hard to follow when he is teaching. Had to curve tests by 30 points and willing to give a D to students with 30%.
He is never on schedule with the syllabus but he expects you to read the chapters on you own time and he tests you on them even though he didn't lecture on them! Seems like he is totally clueless.

I went to every class, I went to office hours, I had a private tutor, My dad is a chemist and gave me supplemental reading material, I did all homework assignments, I read the book cover-to-cover, I asked questions and reviewed every test and quiz with Dr. Smith, AND I had study partners... and you wanna know the result? A C+! WHAT?!?!

Great Professor if you really want to learn stuff. easy accessible, and very knowledgeble, if you just want to earn the course credits, you might have a hard time. it is really a good course for some body who is interested

Worst teacher I have ever had at RIT. Might know a lot about the subject but definitely does not portray it to the class. Can NOT teach. Stick with Turner if you are thinking of dropping, he is much worse!!! Each test is formatted differently so in addition to memorizing the book/material/hw you have a different test each time. :(
Unfair and unclear grading. Avoid this professor if possible.

Professor Jacobs is very passionate about open-source and covers it in-depth and breadth in the class. Plans and assignment times changed a lot, sometimes being moved weeks forward. Attendance was mandatory with no benefit of going or paying attention, and lectures could get boring.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Cares about student feedback and working with them to make course better with each iteration of it. humanitarian speakers boring are for people who care more about private industry but I signed up for the course that has "humanitarian" in the name. other than the speakers, great class.
Very kind and accessible. He is one of the most understanding professors I have ever had, and is a lenient grader. Always available for outside help and responds quickly to emails.
Very disorganized. Not recommended if you enjoy any semblance of structure in a class.
The class is pretty easy, but assignments are not explained very clearly and can be confusing.
Incredibly disorganized. Input the wrong grade for assignments on several occasions. Not recommended.

Overall a very fun professor. You can tell he is really passionate about open-source and is involved in many communities at RIT. My only complaint would be class organization. There are always discrepancies in the syllabus and projects are very vague. Both SJ and the TA seemed to have poor planning which was annoying at times.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Overall, good class. Not very difficult. Its one of those classes that you get out what you put in. However, you can use this class as an easy A too.

Fun professor, even at 8am. Prof Jacobs was very personable, and I enjoyed his class a lot. IGME 110 was kind of a special case in which the meeting times were more of a workshop/work period, and all of the learning was asynchronous, but the way the class was structured was pretty good. There were some bumps bc of covid online learning, overall ok.

Oh god. This has to have been the worst class I ever took. A Production Studio where we produced almost nothing. The class spent the semester working on a Point and Click adventure. There are 19 people in the class, and it's a PROGRAMMINGDESIGN major. No dedicated art majors, no motivation, and teacher missed half the classes. Avoid at all costs!

Was great for GDD1 was critical of some project ideas but only because the students didn't take time to really research or pitch game correctly.  Lots of reading, sure but often draws exam questions straight from the main ideas of the passages not the little details.  Easy exams as long as you mildly pay attention
Often too critical about student ideas and projects. Canceled class FIVE minutes before it started (8am class) TWICE. Horrible communication skills and is often biased towards women.

While I understand Game Design is a new and upcoming field, that should be no excuse to teach it like one. We were required to buy 4 textbooks; one was barely referenced on the exams. He procrastinated grading. He cancelled class twice (one time 14 minutes before class). His lectures have little focus. Do yourself a favor and avoid this professor.
More work than any other HCI section.  Assigned overed 300 pages of reading material on the 7th week!
Oh yea, Jacobs is the man!

Insightful and understanding about the difficulties of the program. He is very knowledgeable about the material he teaches, and is great at explaining difficult concepts to learn by providing a plethora of examples and visual aids. Assignments for his classes match their intended objectives with fair difficulty. He is an overall caring professor.
Very kind and understanding professor. Always prepared with great lectures.
sweet and wonderful

Wonderful and sweet professor!  Kurz gives us insight on the history of American education as well as the history of Deaf education and gives us the opportunities to look back at what education was like in those times.  Very eye-opening and fun course!
His lectures are on point and he invites class participation. It's usually easy to sit back and enjoy. It's also very applicable from the literature.

If you're genuinely interested in philosophy of mind, I couldn't recommend professor Suits enough. One of the most brilliant professors I've ever encountered, he teaches with the intention of imparting knowledge and wisdom.

I'm not sure whether my experience with Dr. Suits was positive because he's a good professor or because Symbolic Logic is a good class.  It's probably a combination of the two.  You should take Symbolic Logic, and you should take it with Dr. Suits.

Suits hit the sweet spot between math and philosophy for me. This class, Symbolic Logic, is pretty simple if you have a logic or engineering background already, but Suits did his best to make sure even people new to boolean algebra have plenty of footholds. Assignments were short, frequent, and quickly graded. Easy credit for my immersion, too.

Suits is calm, patient, an interesting lecturer, and seems to genuinely enjoy philosophy. Abstract concepts have never been so successfully communicated to me before taking his classes. As long as you show understanding of the topics he's presented you will do well in his class. If you are truly interested in philosophy, take his classes!

Taking Intro to Ethics with this professor can be easy since there is no homework, just quizzes. The attendance is not mandatory. You just show up in the class for quiz and exams. But beware, there is not a lot of points in quizzes and tests. You can lose a lot of points over bad quizzes and etc. Easy professor but Be careful of quizzes and exams.

He is a very nice guy, always making little jokes.  Teaches the course at a bit too much of an elementary level, but explains things well.  I can't speak for his other courses, but if you are considering taking Philosophy of Mind, take it with Aguilar instead.  It's his area of expertise, and he teaches it *incredibly* well.

The textbook is a little hard to understand but he clarifies things in class. However, he is extremely BORING! Most people are on their laptops but if you are able to hear his lectures you should be able to pass easily.

Great teacher, made topics a lot of fun and really enjoys having conversations with students in class and is open to their ideas. Would love to take more classes with him. If your are a Philosophy major or concentrator make sure you take a class with him. And ask him about Epicurus!

This guy is utterly useless. He creates his own text is an absolute egoist about it. His lectures are mundane and put half the class to sleep. He doesn't make himself available outside of the class. Avoid at all costs

Great guy! Interesting lectures for the most part, and clarifies difficult readings daily. With the exception of 2 philosophers, he makes understanding difficult-to-read passages a breeze. Tests are take home, quizzes open book. However excitement of class discussions depends on your class.
The notes you take can cover 50-60% of what is in tests. The rest -- you find yourself through reading.Lots of difficult reading. Overall the teacher is very nice and helpful

4 tests, 3 of which were take-home. You never knew when he'd hand out a test because of his disorganized nature, but you get a week & they're all straight out of the reading so time was never an issue. Lectures broadly covered the material and went into several  philosophical sidebars. Take if random discussion is your thing; avoid if it's not.
This is the most chill guy you will ever meet. He's a fun teacher, nice guy... Take his classes if at all possible, it's an easy A and fun.

A great, great teacher. Has a fantastic teaching style. He has a great sense of humor that makes being in class and participating a joy. It is true his test are lenient but the lack of emphasis on the grade makes me want to sit, listen and interact all the more instead of trying to memorize everything. I would take him again in a heartbeat

This guy is great!  He makes an interesting topic even more interesting than it has to be the uninteresting topics are better.  He is really funny and energetic and the way he teaches keeps the class awake.  His grading is really lenient and his tests are really easy, if you copy everything he writes you are sure to pass.
Easy grader, makes the class interesting. Definately take him if you get the chance.
Just excellent.  I don't think any professor in the Philosophy department can beat Dr. Suits' teaching style.  His lectures are never boring, and his grading is very lenient.  An A+ professor!
Class was Asyncronous, with one weekly lecture followed by work on Achive. I learned a lot from this class and Dr. Schenkel made it super interesting to work with these topics!

This class was mostly online, there are lectures once a week in person, but they often got cancelled. Shes a good grader and is quick through lectures. You will be required to buy an online textbook and complete most the assignments through there. One thing to note is, she has a pretty strict no technology rule in lectures.

I like this professor since she was easy to talk to through email or after class. The lectures are okayish. But it's a super easy class in my opinion. attend class and you will be good. Theres only two exams. Most of the homework is on Macmillian and only four discussion posts and one 4-5 page essay is all you have to do to pass the class.
Uses mandatory outside textbook for assignment submissions. Getting above a 40% costs 108$. Dropping this class and looking for another.

Took an online Health Psyc course from this instructor. She's pretty knowledgable and gives you good feedback. A lot of cool topics and interesting videos. The last project is awesome. Read the book, do the assignments, and you'll be good.

Dr. Schenkel is a really nice professor, but I don't feel like she did anything to teach us. It was an asynchronous class and the main source of learning was an online textbook with quizzes. No lectures or work from her. I don't feel like much stuck with me either. But if you're just there for the A, I'd recommend her.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Loved this class!! Really interesting topics and learned a lot. She gets back to you quickly when you email her. Good at helping and answering questions. Quizzes are straightforward. Very cool videos that make the course interesting. Take her if you can!
She's a solid prof. She's really responsive if you have problems and is willing to help. If you stay on top of your work you'll be fine.

I really like this professor. Her lectures are interesting and the material is sound. Her tests can be difficult, but they are taken from the class lectures. She tells a lot of stories, but they are terrific and reflect what she is teaching. I loved it! Also, great videos. Take her if you can!

Dr. Schenkel is an okay professor, scatterbrained at times but usually because she wants to talk about something interesting. She posts the lecture slides so attendance is semi optional, but she usually asks questions on the tests that she doesn't go over in the slides. It's a psych class. Show up, have a pulse, and you'll do fine.

Dr. Schenkel is one of my favorite professors and she effortlessly makes her classes enjoyable with her tangents and experiences. Her classes are powerpoint-based and if you study those, you're set for exams. Easy A with interesting topics as well.

Makes class fun and a bit laid back. She loves to cut into side tangents, which cuts both ways in how it impacts the lecture. She acts a bit ditsy at times, but is really invested in this materials, and that is projected outwards to the class. Here wasn't any homework, but the lecture notes were great to study from for tests.

So I took this class based on the reviews here... and I regret it.  I thought this would be a cakewalk. The extra credit is SONA stuff, the tests are hard, unless you make it a priority to study for 3 days to get above an 80.  And my friend and I wrote our papers together (they were very different) and I got an 86 and she got a 96.. thats fair

Great professor for ab. psych. 4 exams with one drop including cumulative final if you choose not to take it. One paper but it's easy and opinion based. Lectures are fun and there are TONS of great videos. extra credit adds 4 points to your average! Take a course with her if you can!!!

Had her for psychological testing. Interesting class. Some fun assignments but a good amount of work .. A lot due at the end. She is really good.. Knows what she is talking about. I would take her again.
Abnormal Psy -- great class with Dr. Schenkel.  She makes all of the lectures very interesting and combines them with movies.  Excellent Professor!!!
Great teacher, certainly not timely with grading though. All you gotta do is show up and know the lectures and videos.
Good class. Tests can be hard. Study the lectures and class notes.

very interesting information, very nice professor. she uses videos a lot which keep it interesting, but goes through power points really fast. tests get harder as the quarter goes, but if you know the book, you will get an A. also, lots of extra credit opportunity.

She's pretty knowledgeable and gives you good, solid information. She doesnt take the time to even learn your names and doesn't care if you show up to class. Tests are straight from the powerpoints and videos.
I love this class. A lot of good information. One of my favorite professors at RIT!
Good Prof. Tests are clear and straight from lecture. Study from the slides and you will do well.

Had her for abnormaol. Great Class. Lectures were interesting. A lot of good information and good videos. She kept it very interesting and went off topic to talk about cases. Four exams, she takes the top 3. Study from the powerpoints. I would take her again, plus she is pretty cute!

This ended up being one of my favorite classes for the quarter. You're only graded on 3 exams and an essay so you have to be careful and do lots of extra credit. My only complaint was that we wasted 10-20 minutes a day while she figured out how to get a DVD to work. Lectures were interesting and full of videos and examples.
She is very discriminatory against foreign students.  Boring lectures...all she does is read from PPT..isn't helpful at all...

Dr. Schenkel is absolutely awsome!! She is the BEST!! Her presentations are succint to the relevent material and yet she can make the material come ALIVE. Psych is not my major, but because of her teaching, level of caring for the student, and exteme helpfulness, I would LOVE to take another class of hers. I would HIGHLY reccommend her to all!!!!!

Dr. Schenkel has been the absolute BEST!! She is extremely helpful and insightful, and I have learned so much from her in just the 1 class. Her presentations are succint,material is up to date and relevant to what is tested, plus she makes it very interesting and really holds the attention of the class. I would not hesitate to reccommend her at all

Not the best professor. She plays a dumb blonde a lot of the time.  Her voice and facial expressions were really annoying.  The textbook was so boring I never opened it.  Her lectures didn't help for the tests.  I wouldn't recommend her.

She has had the same powerpoints for the past few years.  She just reads them to you while you fill in the blanks in your handouts.  She gave out 4 point of extra credit on your average and the final is optional.  3 Tests, 1 final - she will take the best 3 grades.

She is one of my favorite professors that I've had thus far.  The tests are from the textbook and the powerpoints, which are posted online.  The book is very technical and boring, but she makes it interesting when she presents it to the class.

One of the best teachers I have had at RIT, and psychology isn't even my major!  Extremely kind and easy to get along with.  Tests are multiple choice, and come straight from powerpoint lectures.  Lots of information, but she makes it interesting.  I would love to take another one of her classes.
Awesome prof.Good lectures, take her class.

This was the first asynchronous class I ever took, so it was a bit confusing at first. I know it was also a big adjustment to switch it to online as much of the class is discussion-based. However, with time, it got more routine and Dr. Condry was very accessible. I really enjoyed having her as a professor!
Developmental Psych was awesome! Light workload but I still feel like I learned a lot. Only one quiz a week and two tests the whole time. Participation matters. 10/10 highly recommend

Prof. Condry is a great professor. Her lectures are clear, interesting and fun. She is very approachable and communicates well. I had never taken a Psych class before, and her passion for the subject showed me how truly interesting psychology is.

I'm currently getting close to finishing Research Methods 1 with Dr. Condry, and I wish she was teaching RM2 next semester. She's very attentive to and understanding of the needs and issues of her students, and has a lot of great insight for presenting the course materials in a thought-provoking and accessible way.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. Class is very interesting and enjoyable, and she makes it easy! Only tests are a midterm and final. There is also a 4-6 pg paper. If you go to class, you can't get below an 85 on a test - (I got an easy 100 on the midterm).  I would love to take another class with her. TAKE HER, you won't regret it!

Condry is 1 in a million as far as a professor goes. I cannot offer her enough praise for being caring, understanding, approachable, respectable and flexible. Her classes are difficult but she makes them well worth attending and being a part of. She is the only reason I had hope ( as a disabled person) that Psychology was the right career path.
She is an easy going teacher. Read your materials and invest your effort in class. She assigns a lot of work but they're not really that hard.
Take her classes! She's a great professor. You won't regret it.

I had Professor Condry for Scientific Writing.  Be prepared for a lot of writing.  It is not hard nor is she a tough grader but it can feel extremely overwhelming.  She is very helpful and a likable person.  Just make sure you memorize APA references correctly since she kept on quizzing our class on this until we got it right.

Interesting class, overall not that bad but ALOT of work! She makes papers due way too often and when papers aren't due you still have a lot of work. Not the worse psychology class but definitely a lot more work then I expected , this class is the most work load of all my class. However maybe it's just because it's a writing class?

I absolutely love Prof Condry!!  She really cares that you understand her topics.  I have had her for 3 different classes now and each one has been absolutely amazing.  If you have the opportunity, take her class.
Really awesome and caring teacher.  Class is Really easy.  If you didn't do well on the tests it probably means you are brain dead and never came to class.  She is awesome

I had Condry for intro Psych. She is an awesome professor,very helpful, and cares about your success in her class. She was always straight foward about was was on the test and even gave study sheets. I hope thoses of you that are taking this class get lucky enough to have her!
Professor Condry is the best Psych. professor!  Her class is REALLY easy.  getting below an 85 on the tests probably means you NEVER looked over notes or did not come to class.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

The content of the class was extremely interesting and Condry did her best to illustrate the core concepts. Tests could be a bit ambiguous, but in-class discussions and easy papers raised grades substantially. Great professor overall!

I felt thet this professor's content and organization was not up to par. Yes she smiles alot and tries to be helpful, but I don't feel comfortable with her knowledge base. Frequebntly she seems to mix up studies and the results. Exams didn't reflect the content that was discussed most of the time in class. NOT impressed at all. Cannot reccommend
Child Psych isn't really my thing, but she made the class pretty interesting. Shes also my advisor and will go out of her way to help you. She is one of the best professors in RITs psych program

One of the best professors in the RIT psych dept. Highly reccomended. Course content can be difficult,however this professor is willing to go the extra mile to help you. If you have any difficulties she is willing to help you. Lectures are excellent and engaging.Just purely amazing. I learned a whole lot. TAKE HER CLASSES!

Laura gives clear lectures, is generally really good about responding to questions quickly, and clearly wants to help you. The labs are challenging without feeling needlessly hard and are satisfying to complete. Instructions and grading criteria are very clear. I would definitely taker her again. Best online class I've ever had.

Good professor. The class was well organized and the labs were challenging and fun. I thought overall it was a good experience and despite giving us a fairly difficult final project, she understood that and graded accordingly. Definitely wanted the students to actually go learn instead of grind our gears for perfection.

I took a computer graphics class with her online. She is a good professor and makes sure to keep up to date notes. The only real problem I had with her is that halfway through the semester she stopped responding to emails/ it took awhile to get a reply. Other than that she's a good professor.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: She is a terrible professor and very disorganized. If you're eager to learn take much more qualified professors who who are very knowledgeable about this field.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: She was an okay professor, but the textbook assigned was literally very hard to understand and she gives out way too much reading. Beware of pop quizzes that you get every week based on the readings. Quizzes are online, easy if you do the reading. Exams are mediocre at best.

The weekly quizzes on the readings for this class were really hard. Even if you read, they are only five questions and its hard to get all of them right. Other than that, I took this as a gen ed and the class was really enjoyable. You NEED to read the textbook assignments, but the readings aren't a lot of work
She doesn't take attendance and doesn't ask much, but if you don't do the work you better be ready not to pass.

The class wasn't very interesting to me but the teacher was great and engaging. She gives weekly quizzes online with 10 questions. The tests are multiple choice, a few short answer and one short essay question. She gives way too much reading for one week but I was able to pass the quizzes by skimming the readings and using the power points.

She's a great professor, and she absolutely loves what she teaches. She understands when you have a boatload of work and other issues that make life horrible. She's very clear about the content, and class is usually enjoyable if at least one person does some reading. The reading can be boring and dry sometimes, and there is a lot of it.

Very cool dude. I love him but sometimes he likes to scare you but I realized he's doing that to make you want to work harder. He's a great teacher. He will get mad if you miss his class, especially when you don't text him or email him letting him know first.

Manki Cho is one of my favorite professors ever. He cares about his students on a level different from the rest of not just the math department, but all of RIT. Project-Based Calculus 2 is not an easy class. You will need to work for it; do the optional homework and you'll succeed. It's not too much.

I loved being in Dr. Cho's class. He is very good at teaching Prob and Stats 1. He is kind and very helpful during office hours. The lectures are amazing. He makes us understand the topic instead of memorizing formulas. The quizzes are from the textbook examples and the exams from the homework. As a result, he made us practice a lot. Loved him!

Took Cho twice, first when it was his first time teaching at RIT, second was 2-3 years later. As usual he is funny, knows what he is talking about, and easy if you do homework. If you show you care you will do well. His personality is one of the best I seen for a non major class at RIT. His accent he has isn't an issue and clarifies if have a prblm

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Dr. Cho is the best math professor I have ever taken. He is hilarious and makes lectures entertaining and concepts easy to understand. He comes off as strict but that does nothing but command your respect for his class. Definitely do the homework as it helps a lot for the quizzes and tests.

Great professor. Hilarious and cares about students. Accent should not be a problem. Tough grader, but he makes sure you know his expectations. Quizzes, exams, and one 5% project are the only graded items. Final is 35%, which I thought was a lot, but it worked out. Gives a lot of detail about what problems will be on quizzes and exams.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He does a really good job teaching and is very willing to help you anytime. Has a tough accent to understand, but you get used to it. A lot of the quizzes were from the homework which he doesn't collect but definitely do them to practice. Tests were pretty straightforward.

Cho made the class incredibly easy and make sense. He taught in a way where you derive the material yourself, but it wasn't a crucial part of the course. He is Korean so he has a bit of an accent sometimes, but for the most part he is easy to understand. Definitely suggest.
Great professor. Homework was optional, but still a great way to study for the .1% who did it. Accent takes some getting used to but not hard to understand.

Dr Cho is easily the best math teacher I have ever had. Great guy, has a slight accent but easy to get pass. Very open to explain things that you have questions about. Very knowledgeable. His style of teaching makes you understand the subject. 10/10 would take again, for any class.
If you don't get an A in this class it simply means you didn't do the work. It's impossible to fail.

A knowledgeable professor who can be both serious and light-hearted. Very willing to meet during office hours or by appointment and will try to explain. However, he has a thick Korean accent and it can be hard to understand him at times. The tests and quizzes can be very easy if you do the homework. Don't do the homework, and you'll struggle.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']
comment: Manki Cho is one of the best professors I've ever had. He conveys the material very clearly and is very accessible outside of class and very willing to review course material as well as material from past courses. He is very forgiving and genuinely wants his students to pass, so long as they prove they know the material. I would 100% take him again

Professor Cho is an all around great professor who really does look out for his students' grades. He will purposely put the easiest questions on his tests and quizzes. The practice tests are identical to the actual test. The person who sat next to me always did the homework and every workshop had at least two homework questions on it.

MATH171 with Prof. Cho was way harder than it should have been. I felt as if this class was too low of a level for him to teach and he didn't understand that the class was just trying to learn the basics of calculus. Smart guy, just not the best at teaching. Tests were impossible, Ive never seen kids get straight 0's on a math test until this class

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Hilarious']
comment: Calc 2 is a hard topic, but Prof Cho did a great job teaching it. He clearly explains concepts, and if you need extra help is great one-on-one at office hours and willing to meet outside them if you need also. Study from his practice tests!! The real test is similar (sometimes SAME ques. used!!) Also very amusing during lecture, kept it interesting
Professor Cho has quickly become one of my favorite professors. He's smart, witty, and teaches the material clearly and concisely.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Caring']
comment: This guy is the best. I have taken this class more times than I care to admit, so take it from me when I say he's the best there is. Returns grades faster than anyone on campus. Easy project portion. Sometimes duplicates some problems from practice exam onto real exam. Is truly on your side. Was very forgiving when I had health issues with him.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Prof. Cho is an effective teacher. This does come with some strict policies. Attendance was mandatory. From his syllabus "To be eligible for a letter grade of A or B, a student may have no more than 3 unexcused absences from lecture. Each late counts as 1/2 an absence." He his a strict grader. I found his class to be very stressful.

Professor Cho does an excellent job going over the material and has a great sense of humor. Reading the textbook is not necessary, though you might find it helpful if you are having trouble understanding any of the concepts covered in class (alternatively, you could meet with him during office hours).

Professor Cho does everything he can to make sure his students succeed. He's very approachable if you ever need any help, and he has a great sense of humor which keeps his lectures interesting. I'd recommend him to anyone and plan to continue taking his courses myself as the years progress.

Dont just look at the rating, read He does have an accent, but that doesn't affect his teaching at all.  His homeworks are "optional", but I recommend you do them.  They don't take too much time and his quizzes are entirely based on the hw 90% of the time. He is not an easy A. His exams after the first were pretty challenging, but nothing crazy.
One time he he gave out a quiz and everyone got like a 40 and he didn't drop the quiz grade. His tests are also waaay harder than they should be. He has a decent sense of humor though.
You need 12 pages of writing for the whole quarter so it's not too much, but the material forces writing about a certain topic. There is little flexibility for the topics of the papers.
extremely knowledgeable of course material, has a strong idea of what direction students should take, follow guidelines and you'll get a good grade

This is an intelligent professor. Dr. Connor challenges your thinking and has you learn beyond your expectations. Good grades aren't difficult as long as you participate in the process. Be open and take his classes. I have twice, and would again if he had more available.

Very sarcastic. Do your work and he'll like you, you really dont need to be a great writer to get an A, just follow the way he wants the paper done and your solid. Hes not very helpful but the class is simple, you write three long papers. Thats it.

Kinda wings it in class, but easy A as long as you just do what he says. Its real simple, not a lot of work, hardly any readings, movies in class :D You write maybe one paper a quarter? Easy A, he even cancels classes on occasion! Reccomend.
He was horrible. He made us do a ton of work and I don't think I got anyhting out of it. The only nice thing is he is lenient on grades.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Margaret is nice. However, she has been the most frustrating professor I've ever had. She doesn't give full feedback until after you've turned everything and gotten your grade. She assigned projects every 2 weeks and you only get a week to complete revisions. She's also rly boring, the projects too. And she isn't always clear on what she wants.

Pence is a tough grader, but I do learn a lot from her class. The only problem is that she assigns a new project every two weeks, meaning theres a project due every two weeks. Her grading is pretty intense but it does make you better.

Few times I emailed her with questions and she did replied me back right away. I am pleased with that. Also she helped me many times when I was stuck working on Illustrator during class. Margaret is nice, laid-back, fair and likable professor.
Took Vector Imaging with her (basic Illustrator class.) Grades pretty fairly. Moves pretty quickly. Knowledge of the subject not the best, as shown through personal examples.

She may seem dry and little boring at first, but once you warm up to her she's extremely helpful. She s patient and corrects you till you get it right. You'd have to work hard in her class and her work is amazing so she knows what she's talking about. Great class for a foundation and if you're trying to sharpen your artistic skills.
doesnt grade on effort, grades on ability, even than plays favorites.
Cared a lot about the students. The only class I enjoyed out of my foundation courses. If you try hard you will get an A. Also lets you do re-dos to improve your grade. Great Prof.!

excellent material.

Awesome teacher! One of the best! Definitely an easy A if you do all the homework she assigns and turn things in on time. Easy A! Cannot stress it enough!

Professor Jen is awesome!! One of the Best professors I have had. She brings in her own experiences into the class and shares so much information. Never a dull moment. Professor Jenn is an excellent professor!  She brings personal experience into the classroom and makes learning more about the process and experiences then a grade on a paper.  She provides a true learning experience.  Very highly recommend!
Professor Jen is the greatest! Excellent teacher with tons of experience. She is very helpful and cares a lot about each one of her students. I highly recommend taking a course with her.

She is AWESOME!! Very easy courses ever! I learned so much from her, she loves to share her experiences, very open mind, and very flexible! She always share interesting topics! I suggest you to take this courses with her!

Professor Jenn is an Amazing professor and Amazing person. She shares her knowledge in a clear, selfless way. We learn from others experiences and knowledge. She was an awesome professor who always tried to keep class positive despite the dark subject. She was always helpful and the assignments were easy if you did the work and went to class. Professor Jen is the sweetest, nicest, and most hilarious professor I've ever had the pleasure of taking a class with. Her essay assignments are a little vague, but she's an easy grader and ultimately values class discussion more. Lots of fun, take a class with her if you can!

By far the best and most engaging teacher I have ever had. She is a professor that actually cares about the student and the substance of what we take from the classroom. She is simply DA BEST.

Best teacher at RIT. Take a class with her and you won't regret it! She's hilarious and she finds a way to make tough situations easier to learn about.

I couldn't have asked for a better writing seminar teacher. It's worth waiting until sophomore year to take it with her. Seriously. You won't regret it. Prof. Jen is hilarious, the class discussions are interesting and you will laugh your ass off more than once. Take her. Seriously.

Although I have never really enjoyed writing,this class was great. Professor Jen was very helpful and made the class interesting and enjoyable. I would highly recommend taking her class.

Very fun and caring professor! Always willing to help out her students, and very knowledgeable about her field. Lectures are filled with lots of personal anecdotes that are sure to keep your interest! Great sense of human and very personable with students, as well!
Lots of fun. Takes an interest in her students. Never a dull moment. Even her class is offered at 8am, you will go just to be amused. I'm totally taking more of her classes just for kicks.

She is the best teacher! She is really interesting and brings her personal experience into her stories. She doesn't load with work, and doesn't require you buy textbooks. No finals. Ive taken two classes with her and will take more. Love her.

A very nice and lenient teacher. If you don't want to worry about a lot of work, pick her.
Very good professor. I think everyone should take a class with her. She is very blunt and to the point and has a very good sense of humor about it. Very lenient and fun professor.

i LOVED this class so much. jen made everyone interested, laugh, and learn at the same time. everything a perfect prof should do, she did everyday. i wish that i could take more classes with her in the future! definitly the best professor i have ever met/taken here at RIT. if you dont get her you're missing out.

omg she is by far the most fun professor that i've had at RIT! Hilarious and makes every class something to look forward to. Her grading is kinda challenging but it isnt hard to get an A if you put in the effort. I am definitely taking her in w&l 2. No final, loves letting us out early. Amazing!!!
she's awesome ...i dont mind going to her class

Great speaker; really knows what she is talking about. Best class I've taken
great teacher

Tina is a decent lecturer. Her knowledge is kind of outdated and has an ill get back to you attitude. Other than that, she is the sweetest person and buys pizza for the class occasionally.

Incredibly nice lady. Distinctively "human" compared to other professors. However, tests/quizzes/labs are slightly hard graded. Easy 5 pts extra credit. Be prepared to do a mini presentation and term paper for networking!!!

This lady is living in the past.. She does not have a clue about anything she teaches. Often goes on side rants about how she worked for IBM. Chapman is a decent professor, she is very clear with her material and presents it well.  Offers Extra Credit oppertunities, grades fair.  Don't be surprised if she starts talking about her former job at IBM though, seems to be a trend among all their ex-employees at RIT

Freshmen Seminar wasn't bad. We only had class about half of the time, the rest was quest speakers. Reflection papers were easy, so was any other homework. Semi pointless class. But she was really nice, and always seemed happy.

She was a nice lady.  The class was okay but there is a lot of information.  The book wasnt necessary for me and I good decent for myself.  Keep on top of EXTRA CREDIT bc that does end up helping you out in the long run.

I don't understand the negitive views below.. I have never had problems with professors here, she is the first one I havent really liked.  Lectures unclear, can misguide you in lectures.  Does not return your tests for you to study from. Good teacher, lectures sometimes got boring but still able to pay attention. Test desks were tiny. Tests were very fair, recitation was used for quizzes every week (could leave once they are done).

He explains concepts very well, and very in depth. If you are just trying to get through diff eq and not care about an in depth understanding, Brooks may not be for you. He was just kinda eh. I learned more by myself then in lecture. ChatGPT was a better teacher. Nice dude, just not a good teacher.

He's really hit or miss. Some things make a lot of sense; others don't make any sense. He kind of skips over half the steps to solve problems assuming we know how to do it. 50/50 chance of being a good professor for you. My experience was bad, I've heard others swear by him though. If you get bad vibes in the first week, trust your gut and find a different section. I didn't and I regret it.

I say this as nice as possible: don't take his class. He is a nice person I give him that, but his grading scheme and teaching ability are the worst. 73% of our grade is exams, no extra credit, no curves. Way too large of a lecture hall to teach, and he did not teach a single thing. Notes were very unclear and he would spend way too long on tangents and no time on important material. Multiple complaints to the TAs over his poor teaching during TA recitations. His YT is helpful to teach yourself. Take with anyone else if his class is over 100 seats.

I wish i comprehended the warnings. those of you who don't get it, here: absolutely nothing matters in this course. no structure whatsoever. no due dates, quizzes dont matter, exams don't matter, no grading. and if you aren't able to add structure to it yourself, you're cooked. He probably is the worst math professor at RIT. Not because he doesn't know the content but because he is so lazy and refuses to offer any resources. Professor Brooks is known to be one of the best guys I've met in college! Based on his actions, he really cares about his students and he wants everyone to pass. If you felt you did poorly on a midterm or quiz, then you didn't have to turn it in and it would be replaced at the end of the semester by the grade you received on your final.

One of the worse professors I had at RIT. The exams were outright ridiculous in terms of difficulty and his teaching style was horrendous. 100% of your grade are just quizzes and exams so do be mindful of that, I highly recommend you take another professor for your mental sanity.
He was so much fun to listen to and although the material was difficult he would break everything down if you didn't understand something and didn't make you feel stupid for asking. Highly recommend

comment: loved bernie!!! honestly if you put the work in for this class you'll get the results you want. hw is optional and I did none of it. quizzes you dont have to turn in if u dont want to but the grade gets absorbed by your final, so be careful. tests were all easy though if you studied, and lectures were essential to attend. recitations helped too

One of the best professors ever. He is a little goofy and often didn't prepare much for class, which made lectures feel very genuine. He was never just copying off of notes, and always gave many examples of problems. Homework was not worth any credit, but tests were easy.

Good teacher and fair grader. The whole class is based on tests, brush up on trig integrals and integrals by parts and you have an A in the class. Homework is not required, but good practice and study material for those who need it. 10/10 professor.

comment: Clearly very passionate and very smart. Tests make up like 80% of the grade and the grading is weird. But overall, great guy and knows how to teach

Very clear about what is asked of you. Felt the course was a bit too simplified. Often felt like we were only scratching the surface of the material. Wish more attention was focused on pushing past the basics. As a result, unclear if learned what is fully needed for future studies in this field.
Good guy
no regrets

Math Finance has a lot of subjects that I've never learned before and this class was extremely difficult for me. However, Dr. Brooks is extremely helpful during his office hours. He has sat many hours with me to help me understand course materials. Definitely taking him in the future.

Wonderful, good lectures, light homework. Has a very good way of teaching that makes it difficult to not understand. Make sure you do plenty of practice examples before exams. There are quizzes at the beginning of class rather than homework.

He's not bad but not great. Quizzes every class, and will run into situations where he doesn't give you enough time to finish or check your work because he gives you too many problems. He should learn to either cut back or give you more time. Time management isn't that hard.

Brooks is one of the best professors I've ever had, I took him for Diff Eq and I enjoyed and looked forward to coming to class today, he is also super accessible and helpful outside of class for help. Can't recommend enough, he's also hilarious and creates a great classroom environment, and is very clear about tests and quizzes, no surprises

Dr. Brooks is amazing professor! He does give a quiz everyday but they are useful since you keep up with the material; furthermore, he is very clear in teaching and funny. I would recommend him for any class; he is a truly passionate professor.

Great professor. He was able to explain everything clearly, but expect a quiz everyday, if you are taking math-231 (Differential Equations). None of the homework is required so this is his way of getting grades in and making sure students understand the material.

If you go talk to him during office hours he's helpful. The midterm was open book and open notes, easy. The final was take home and slightly more challenging. Be prepared to use Excel a lot in this class and be prepared to read the textbook. Otherwise you're going to have trouble with the homework. HW was pretty short each week,
Best calculus teacher I've ever met.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He typed up all of the notes and simply read them off the projector. It was hard to follow and he almost never did examples. Also the final was 80% of the grade.

Hands down the best math teacher I have ever had.  Canadian, so you know he is insanely nice. Bags of milk and rivers of chicken fat... lol (insider)... "I stop and I ask how does this sit with you and you say...?" ... "Plain vanilla"... "Add one to the exponent divide by whats up top... now that your safely outside the bottle neck of integration."

An outstanding professor. Explains concepts in much the way I think. Appropriate for the whole spectrum  — will not bore the best students or leave the worst behind. Will help you the best he can. Funky grading scheme where 80% of the grade is from 2 tests (or one is you choose to skip the optional mid-term).
Great teacher with a good sense of humor.  Would definitely recommend taking him as a teacher. NO GROUP PROJECT!!!
Honestly the best professor I've ever had, explained concepts beautifully and had a great sense of humor to boot. I had him for two quarters and looked forward to his class every time.

He is the best teacher I've ever had throughout my education. He doesn't have favorites, rarely praises individual work (a good thing), and doesn't discriminate against slackers. He is very lenient with giving points on exams. Also, he spends the break (10 min) helping people and answering questions. He also answers questions during the lectures.

Brooks is easily the best professor i've had while at RIT. He is very helpful, willing to re-explain anything during class if you ask, and during workshop he will help you. He tends to ask further questions to make you think about it more, instead of providing the answers. He lets you go early a lot of the time and is very laid back and funny!
Great guy; explains things the same way that students think.  How does that sit with you? Love his sense of humor as well :)

Awesome teacher. Very good at answering questions. I transferred from a different Calc class into his because I heard he was fantastic. The rumors were accurate. Take good notes and study your notes before tests and you will do fine. Great sense of humor and an interesting guy to talk to! Highly recommended!

Canadian Professor is absolutely fantastic. I am terrible at math and he made complex integrals seem within the realm of reasonable computation. =P Also, he is hilarious. If you don't pick up on Canadian humor you'll miss it, but Canadian Professor cracked me up all quarter. Every other thing he says is an easily missed joke. Fair grader. Take him!

He's a good teacher! I was registered late and my advisor fit my schedule for the first quarter so I didn't know most of my professors before attending class for the first time. Now I feel I'm so lucky to have him as my calculus teacher!!!
Took him for multivariable calculus, great guy, funny, easy teacher. What more do you want?
Easily the best teacher at RIT

Great prof.  Gives optional homework every night, and a quick 2-3 minute quiz every class.  Great for helping your grade.  Teaches by example and is rather clear in said examples.  Been waiting for another chance to take a class with him...

He is a wonderful professor, that gives a lot of examples.  If you learn by example, and not with theory first, this is the professor to have.

Great Professor. Has great stories to tell to lighten things up, and shows his passion for mathematics clearly. However, I'm still not sure what he means when he says "sit side by each." Must be a Canadian thing... Highly reccommended, though.
Major Hottie
great "prof"... now "how does that sit with you?"
Great teacher, lots of fun. Seems like that great high school teacher you never got to have. Fair tests and great class structure

He's super helpful and clear. He's kinda quirky tho, he'll ask you "how does that sit with you?" or tell you to mumble something about the bottleneck of integration. and in canada they drink their milk from bags.
He is the coolest ever

He makes all of the material super easy to understand and is very clear on what you will be expected to know for tests. Its clear that he enjoys his job as he always has a smile on his face and is always willing to help

I was worried about taking American Politics until I met Prof. Griffith. He makes all of the material super easy to understand and is very clear on what you will be expected to know for tests. He's the best professor I have had so far. He is still fairly young so he can connect with his students and actually care about them to. Super passionate about his teaching 10 out of 10 recommend.

Had him for American Politics and probably one of the best professors I've ever had. Has 2 online quizzes a week that are super easy. Had trivia at the end of each week for bonus quiz points which can and will make up for entire quizzes you may have neglected to complete. Genuinely cares about his students.

Easy to pass as long as you show up to class and read the online textbook. Structured in an engaging way. Exams were online and final optional if you like your exam scores (or else it replaces one). My only criticism is the quizzes and exams (open note) seemed to be based purely off the textbook not in class material. Textbook was online and free.

For the summer course, I actually enjoyed his video lectures. They felt like youtube videos I would watch when I wanted to learn stuff, so honestly a great dinner companion. Hes clearly passionate about wanting to teach us. Ngl, if he posted content on youtube I'd prolly tune in occasionally, if the topic was interesting.

Really liked this professor! All exams were online except the final, but the lowest exam grade was dropped. If you show up and do the work assigned on time, you'll never have a problem and will pass with an A.

Dr. Haraden is one of the kindest and understanding teachers I've ever had. His class is very accessible to those who just want to get their credit and get out but also will teach you something. He "gamifies" the class basically into DND with quests and characters while also adding humor into otherwise boring lecture topics.

Pretty interesting class, and with the online exams and the assignments that didn't take too long, he definitely knew that students were taking it as general elective perspective classes, not as pre-reqs.

I've had Dr Haraden for Research methods 2 and and worked with him on senior capstone. He's one of the most caring, and hard working professors I've ever had at RIT. This professor has a amazing way to keep students engaged within his classes and is super fun and nice!

Tests aren't bad, some are online and open note, all quizzes are online. Kind and willing to answer questions about anything psych related. 
Overall recommend.
I love RIT
Will is an awesome professor ... you learn a lot from his class, but he doesn't demand much.  Incredibly laid back, and very dedicated for an adjunct.  Rock on, Will.

He was an amazing teacher that spoke to the class on a more informal level and drew many analogies that help me and my classmates learn complex material by relating it to concepts that we already understand.

Monschientastic!!! Great teacher. Helped me a lot and I would recommend him to anyone.
Will is a great professor. He made programming really easy to understand and is lightyears better than most of the other IT professors. Definitely recommend his classes.
Concepts were explained well and justified. He is down-to-earth, and using the WebAssign platform made grades come back in a timely fashion and aided in reinforcing ideas.
Gave many opportunities for extra credit, for class participation. Take them. Lectures and expectations are clear. Liked he made AI connections with this class.

All of his assignments (exams included) can be done with online resources. As other people have mentioned, it's best to save your time and not show up to lectures. He is pretty chill though and does offer many extra credit opportunities.

Just read off of slides using examples directly from the textbook, so I kind of had to learn the material outside of class. This is a required class for my major. Barbosu made the class accessible, explaining the concepts and insisting on applications. Tests are clear and you get the grade immediately after class.  Many opportunities for bonus points and he is very flexible if you have a problem.

Took the class after being recommended by a friend and I'm glad I did. Everything is clear and organized and prof is available during office hours. If you have no other option other than to take this class, I recommend not going to any of the lectures. He didn't talk about anything used on tests. Chucks extra credit points every time a student answers a question, and throws numerous other ways to get extra points at students, rather than decreasing class difficulty. This distorted the class dynamic and distracted from several lectures.

Very long boring lectures that most people skip. Everything is on a website you have to pay $100 for. People recommend him on this only because he gives lots of extra credit and allows any resources during the test so people just look up all the answers. If you have to take him, get all the extra credit you can and just buy a Chegg account.

comment: When it comes to Stats I, Mihail Barbosu is the best at RIT. I've heard horror stories about this class from friends with other professors, so in comparison Barbosu is great. Took online 1/2 last semester and worked very well.

Prof explains clearly and is fair

comment: Most of his lectures were going through slides he didn't share with the class (until the pandemic disrupted the semester), so class time didn't feel valuable. Uses Webassign heavily (quizes/exams/hws), grabs mostly from the textbook directly, only quizzes (4x, 20%) and exams (4x, 80%) are graded, has attendance/participation as "extra credit" but based on how many "checks" you get compared to the person with the most. No Partial Credit. Accepts rounding mistakes, but that's it.
the professor treated the class like high school students. the class was too easy and covered too little content too superficially. a lot of homework on the little content, however.

Not a bad professor by any means. Gives good and timely feedback on assignments, very knowledgable, and overall a decent guy. My main gripe is with his lectures, I eventually needed to tune them out so that I wouldn't keep falling asleep. Lectures were always pretty dull. He is very knowledgeable but struggles to make things engaging. Weekly homework assignments didn't always correlate to lectures and quizzes. Homeworks were somewhat difficult as any mistake would result in a zero, but he would sometimes tell you exactly what to do.

Professor Fossum provided very clear and thorough lectures, including diagrams and examples of the flow of data in complicated scenarios. Homework assignments went beyond the lecture material but didnt fully reinforce the lecture material. The weight of homework was non-uniform, resulting in the grade being hard to calculate until week 12.

This is the most real feedback you're going to get: this professor does not care about anybody. When I say rude, he is quite possibly the most rude man if you even do one thing wrong. Do not expect a good professor, and avoid him at all costs. Is extremely inconsiderate and is also a horrible and very boring teacher. If you have no choice, have fun

Professor Fossum helped to make a quite difficult class manageable and even enjoyable. He's alright, assignments were very oddly spaced and at times sporadic (no assignments for weeks at a time, and then you have one due literally every other day). He teaches the material well and wants you to learn.

Lectures are beautifully explained, no bad questions exist, classwork was light with 0 mandatory homework, and though some rules are strict, she's as lenient as can be when you show the effort. I would take her for every math class ever if I could.

I only had her for Critical Math, but I loved her!
was
so nice, reasonable, and explained things really well. I just wish she taught the Calculus class I need.
Gave incredible feedback and was extremely helpful during the learning process. Also was very forgiving with absences. Amazing professor.

Her class rewards you if you put in the work. A large portion of the class is group work so if that's not your jam then you might consider picking a different class.

Addressing obvious concerns, Olga has an accent, but everything she says is clear and thoughtful. This professor is not great with students with learning disabilities and sometimes does not like when you do a problem a little bit differently in a way that makes it better for you to understand.

She was a bit difficult to understand but she was very considerate and made things very easy to understand, her exams had basically all the stuff she taught in lecture and she made us do a lot of practice which helped a lot.

Probably my favorite math teacher in a long while. Comes well prepared to each lecture, obviously has a love for the subject, and teaches in a way to maximize student understanding. Very easy to understand, ask questions and talk to. Lovingly stern, teaches in a no-fluff way, everything she presents is something you should hear.

Great math professor. She teaches from the head and does not use the textbook except for homework, which is optional. Weekly quizzes that are 2-3 of the same exact questions from the homework. She truly cares about her students and is always willing to help. Tough grader on notation, but most professors are.

I took Tsukernik for my freshman year Calc A, of which I was not prepared for and not willing to try in. I got a 0 on the first quiz. Great if you're willing to learn!
She is an incredible professor. Everything she says is very easy to pick up on and understand. She is also very caring towards all of her students. Genuinely an amazing professor.

Olga grades very harshly with notation errors at the start of the semester but does it to ensure you don't do the same thing and get points taken off on a test. She can be critical but is genuinely a really good professor and a nice person, and is accessible when you have questions about the content. Highly recommend her class.
Best math professor I have ever had. Genuinely cares about her students and is open to questions at any time. Her lectures are engaging and clear, helped me understand calculus for the first time.
Best professor for MATH 171, 172, helped me get back on track in math, do the homeowrk even tho its optional, then go to office hours.

Concise explanations, super caring, and helpful. Truly wants her pupils to flourish. She's always open to questions, whether during class or office hours. I also highly recommend doing the textbook homework (though not mandatory) as it can drastically improve quiz grades and reinforces in-class material. Perfect professor, highly recommend her.

She is an amazing professor ever I have seen. Her explanation is definitely clear if we could not understand. 

She always make me motivated. 

I would recommend students to go to her class because she will help you very much.

Prof Tsukernik is the reason I passed Calc A! She is by far the best math teacher I've ever had. She explains everything very clearly and very neatly. She will help you if something's confusing you and she really wants you to succeed. I retook Calc A this semester and my grade went from an F to an A! Cannot recommend enough.

Prof. Tsukernik is a fantastic instructor, she makes personal connections to students, and has a good sense of humor. Homework is easy, but tedious. Absolutely necessary to do textbook homework if you want to succeed. Trust me, I tried to go without it and almost failed. Exams have review packets, and quizzes every Friday reflect homework.

Professor Tsukernik is such an amazing calculus professor! Although she is a tougher grader it definitely helps develop good habits (especially with notation!) and she is very receptive to questions during class. She makes sure to take the time to learn everyone's name which truly made a difference for me. I definitely recommend taking her course!

Genuinely the best math professor at RIT, and was so amazing and caring towards the whole class! I'm not good at math, but she gave me the confidence I needed to pass! I would genuinely recommend her class!!!

She is the reason I don't hate math. Smth about the pace of her lecture works really well for me. After getting used to her accent and taking decent notes, the class was a breeze. Having to purchase cengage was a pain and there was a lot to do. But the practice was worth it.

Professor Tsukernic is an amazing teacher. She is a tough grader, but is extremely open and transparent about why she deducts points and what can be done to improve. She tends to lecture a bit quickly, but is always open to questions and will repeat herself if asked. She conveys the material very clearly and I would definitely recommend her class
She was amazing. She taught very well and goes above and beyond outside of the classroom to help her students. Would 10/10 recommend. Also, very sweet and caring person overall.

one of best prof's Ive had at RIT. not a comm major, but he made the class interesting and funny. real relaxed guy, made half the class online, which were just easy discussions. two speeches, 1 by yourself, 1 in a group. no final. grades super easy. hardest part were the quizzes but theyre only 8 of them. class was a cake walk, but he is helpful
Easy class, awesome professor. 90% of the class was online discussion and open book online quiz. It doesn't really get much better than that.

No one wants to take this class. That said, Mason is a friendly, polite young person who makes it totally palatable. The class still requires a lot of outside work, but the classroom is a fun atmosphere. He decided to make his class half online.
Kearns was extremely passionate about accounting.  His tests were hard, but if you studied then they weren't that bad.  I think he's now retired though.
He is a great teacher and really wants you to learn.  He does collect HW every class, but as long as you attempt it you get credit.  Recommend!
He is a very kind person and really wants you to learn. Again the reading, not skimming, and studying are the key to his class. Once your done, you will know accounting.

I took Intermediate Accounting 1 & 2 from Dr. Kearns 28 yrs ago at Frediona State College.  Based on the comments that I see today, Dr. Kearns is the same.  When you pass his course, you will know your stuff! He takes great care in helping folks that seek his help.  Dr. Kearns is a very nice man & one of the most wounderful teachers in my college e

I didn't care for his style of teaching.  If you don't mind professors that assign reading and then homework based on it BEFORE they've taught it, then take this class!  I found it difficult doing homework we hadn't learned how to do and it didn't really reinforce any concepts for me.

professor kearns is a great teacher if your an accounting major and want to thoroughly learn the topic; however, the class requires rigorous attention and reading everyday if you are to pass his tests.if financial accounting is required for your major and you want a decent grade, do not take him. i know many people who have withdrawn or failed.

A good professor, but may sometimes play favorites.  As mentioned below, it can be very hard if you don't know much about Accounting to start with.  Hard grader. Class average for tests are very low, with the last test around 40%.  Curbs tests grades. but offers no extra credit.

Please pay attention and do the homework if you going to take his class. Very hard at the start if you don't know accounting, but with a little common sense you will be fine. Test seem easy to me and I only study 30 min per test but a lot of people fail. LOL. HE A EVERY HELPFUL TEACHER and one of the best teacher in RIT cuz his class not a BS class
Hard class if you do not know accounting. Very nice teacher willing to help at any time. Do all the homework and study like crazy and you will pass.
Make sure you do the homework and read the chapters.  Going to class explains everything that is unclear.  If you can do that you will get a good grade.

This is a very hard course for those of us that have never taken accounting before.  It is A LOT of work and hard to get a good grade.  However, the professor is very nice and his lectures are very clear.  Homeworks due every class and please do study hard and smart for his exams, they are difficult.
if your not majoring in accounting, its hard

Excellent! Hard if you don't care about the class/do the work. As a professor one of the best I have had. Very Understanding, willing to help, straightforward, makes you feel comfortable. Understanding the material is the hard part... Take him. You won't regret it as long as you're willing to work (or have he time to work at it).
Very nice teacher, but if you don't do homework and stay on top of things, you will fail.

While the lectures and slides can be tough, There is extra credit opportunities which i have taken half and i ended up passing this class well. some of the classmates ive worked with have been difficult. this is better suited classes for Artists.
