comment: Not a good professor if you've never taken an art history course before. I wouldn't've been able to do well in this course if I had not had previous context. She's very enthusiastic about her subject, but disorganized with confusing instructions, and she had heavily unrealistic expectations regarding reading and outside hours put into the class.

I cannot express how much this class sucks! I had the worst group so I had to do the work of 3 other students. I would never recommend taking her unless you're looking for a tough art class. She made my life a living hell for 15 weeks. She'll expect you to give genuine feedback on the artwork in class, this is without saying that I suck at this.

If you're an engineering student, don't take this class for an art credit. She expects serious effort, and the group project can be difficult depending on your group. She's strict about artist choices and creates the groups. The topics often felt redundant and confusing—maybe I should've listened to my art major friends about Tani.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: The class itself was okay and actually even interesting at times. Lectures were almost always too long for class time. Changed the syllabus very often, usually more than once a week with no notice, often adding new assignments that took a significant amount of time. I found this to be very inconsiderate and stress inducing.

I don't know why she has so many bad reviews, Ellen is such an amazing professor!!! The people complaining must've not been in her class or just never paid attention, because everything on quizzes/tests/essays etc. are literally just from lectures and slides...Its so easy to get an A.

Professor herself was very kind and willing to work with you outside of class. Most of class is just lecturing or watching a video. Some projects require you to visit an art instillation either on campus or off, which can be time consuming and annoying.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Lectures are very boring if you are not into art. She posts the slides for every lecture so you can use those to do well on the quizzes. LOTS OF BUSY WORK. She changes assignments due dates with no notice and there are TONS of readings for each week, but theyre not that 'mandatory'. She is still understanding and flexible if you show you are trying

If contemporary art is not your thing I would not recommend this class. However, this was a pretty easy class. Quizzes are open notes and the final is a presentation. You do get good feedback on assignments but sometimes it does take a while to get your grades. Tani is a nice professor who provides a lot of resources to students.
At times Professor

Disorganized, bad time management, constantly changing homework,  with almost no notice. If you are not art-inclined do NOT take this class to fill perspective credit. She is a tough grader and expects high level of art analysis. Many students were thrown into this class. She is rude and takes forever to input grades. Does not work with students.

He is not helpful when you ask questions. He really seemed to misunderstand that he was not teaching his graduate students. He wasn't there when I went to his office hours, his grading methods are not consistent, his protocols are badly written (especially in that they're full of typos), and his lectures are extremely difficult to understand.

Dr. Eddingsaas is a nice guy. Bad teacher. He's so smart that he cannot understand why his pupils do not understand. Only gives 1 example for each type of problem. It will ruin the grades in your other classes. The homework is not helpful, too hard, and often wrong. Avoid like the plague (even tho u need the class D:)

Tough class. Expect really difficult tests and Practicals. Don't expect him to hold your hand or help when you are lost. Kinda a grouch but extremely knowledgeable. He knows a ton, I just wish he was more happy about sharing it.

My favorite professor of all time. He is not a hand holder, you have to attend class, lecture slides are not provided. He knows his stuff top to bottom. You will learn so much if you aren't incompetent. I only wish I could take sys3 with him before I leave.

He is an old grouch and proud of it.  I loved the class.  You must show up and spend time learning the material.  No late work is accepted, so do it on time.  If you do your work and aren't an idiot you'll be just fine.

One of the best professors in the NSSA department. He's not a hand-holder, so don't expect to get coddled. Doesn't post slides, so attend lectures. You WILL learn when you take a course with Barido, and you WILL learn the material well. If not, then you're probably failing the course because you were expecting him to walk you through like a child.

People will often say that they learned a lot with barido as a teacher. What they fail to mention is that Barido does not in fact teach you anything. He will instead patronize you and make you learn everything on your own. He takes pride in failing students and otherwise ruining their lives. He's the sole sys2 teacher. Avoid this guy and this class

I've taken a few classes with George. He's one of my favorite professors. I can be very difficult if you're not paying attention, but if you're genuinely interested in the material and pay close attention in class you can do well. He can be very strict, but he's very upfront about what he expects so as long as you deliver you'll do fine.
Had Professor Barido for Comp System Fundamentals an Sys Admin I. I thought he was fair in CSF but he ruined my life in Sys Admin 1. Take only if you feel like dealing with an old grouch.

I had him for OS Scripting. touch class when you take it with this guy. He know's his stuff but doesn't know how to teach. The practicals and labs were extremely hard so if you don't know what you're doing before you get there, you better figure it out fast! ..And pretty much on your own :(

Very good professor, and very knowledgeable about his subject. Learned a lot about UNIX and lectures were interesting. Already knew Windows stuff because I am a Windows Admin for a fortune 500 company. Take him, he can be a bit hard but you will walk away with a wealth of information

My second time having this professor. Can be very hard, and won't post his PowerPoint slides anywhere, so pay attention in class. His labs are pretty lengthy, I find myself spending a lot of extra time completing the labs. As long as you pay attention in class and take GOOD notes (he allows cheat sheets on midterm & final), you should be fine.

While it may seem like he's a hard professor (and he can be), he definitely knows what he's talking about. Show up to class and take notes--they won't be posted anywhere. Pay attention and you should do fine.

He knows his sutff well.  However he will force you to do a lot of study on your own.  He is a total jerk if questions are asked.  Also exams and practicals are far harder then what he teaches in class.  He is a very qualified as$hol3.

Barido is a very hard teacher. He teaches Unix commands via slides, but doesn't make them available to the class. Mid-term and final exams are VERY hard, often requiring you to memorize very obscure things. Practical exams are also hard, and are very complicated versions of otherwise simple tasks. You'll learn, but not before being broken by him.

Omnipotent.  Extremely knowledgeable about subject.  He assigns a buttload of work and doesn't announce important dates.  Lectures result in boredom and slides are not posted.  Puts students on blast if they're sleeping or talking.

Very Dry, his lectures are boring, but the man definitly knows what he is talking about. He managed a large crew @ Kodak for a long time....nothing replaces actual work experience.  If you ask a question, don't expect it to be an easy answer.  He is hard, you can't bs him at all, but he is fair, thorough, and you will get a lot out of him.

He is one of the worst professor I've ever had. Very boring, lecture with slides but don't provide them for students. Extremely unhelpful, such as answering your questions with his own questions. Seem to have an ego problem.
He went over the midterm exam in a way that anything I did not know on it before, I then knew which helped a lot.  He knows his stuff very well, I would take a class with him again.

Love to grind on students who are not paying attention in class. Very dry and thought provoking stimulation lecture. Used powerpoint slides in his lectures but does not provide a copy to students so you are force to take your own notes. Very picky on the grading potion.
A little bit of a stick in the mud, but cares about helping his students.  Lab sucked, still got a B though.
75% of the class is online exams, the remaining 25% is attendance. Easy class, professor has good stories about his job as a cop. W

Lofaso is an amazing and caring teacher. He truly just wants you to learn and enjoy the material, grades and work come second. Has a ton of funny stories from his career. The only real work is some MC quizzes that take 3 minutes and take home exams. Cares about people showing up and paying attention as a form of respect, which the guy deserves.

Dr. Charlie LoFaso is a gem of an individual and stellar teacher. This class had 3 exams and they were only multiple choice. He gives great study guides. He tells great stories and is understanding. I missed the first week of class for a surgery and he didn't dock me points because I communicated with him. Go to his office hours. He will help you.
A great funny man, my favorite proffessor!

Great Teacher. Fun to talk to; lectures mostly follow slides, but he has many interesting stories to tell that help you engage and learn. Quizzes and Exams are online and pretty easy, and attendance counts for a large portion of your grade, so if you show up to classes, you'll easily get a good grade.

Funny guy with some great stories to tell. Clearly knowledgeable about the subject and asks very little of you. Show up to class and you got yourself an easy A. 

Attendance is the majority of your grade. Other than that were some open note online quizzes and exams which were just a reflection of whether or not you were awake during lecture.
Great professor

Professor Lofaso is amazing. You can tell he truly cares about his students as he consistently interacts with the class. The lectures can be lengthy, but are engaging and easy to comprehend. He incorporates his personal experience with the justice system into the lectures to make the material taught in class more valuable.

Good lectures, off PowerPoints but he tries to make it as painless as possible. Truly cares about his students and uses his personal experience in the criminal justice system to connect to any material he teaches. For 220 he had weekly 5 question quizzes, no other hw or a paper, and 3 online tests. Set up perfectly and I retained everything I need.

Although I only took Intro to Criminal Justice because I needed a perspective credit, Prof Lofaso was one of my best professors this semester. He has a ton of personal experience in many of the topics he speaks on, and his lectures are always both informational and entertaining.

Joe is really good professor with a lot of experience in the field. Tries way too hard to relate sustainability to the course when it does not apply. If you have something to discuss, dispute or ask he is very willing to hear your comments. Group project heavy so be aware of the people you sit near.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Professor Rosenbeck was a great guy with a real world experience that he really passes on to his students. He enjoys class participation and loves to talk about his material. There are five group projects which makes the material engaging. Just remember to do his readings cause there are sometimes pop quizzes and it'll only help your grade.

Spends very little time lecturing. I took her class as a once-a-week 3 hour night class, but she never kept us the full 3 hours. Most classes she split us up into pairs or small groups to work on class exercises that were basically just mini projects. Super easy class but an amazing professor.

No exaggeration, one of the most inspirational people I have ever come across. Be ready to be provided with a flurry of personal stories that all tie back to having perseverance in your professional and personal life. This instructor really makes the class feel like its a family rather than a typical RIT course and I truly enjoyed that. Excellent.

Awesome! She is inspirational and has a lot of experience as a business owner. 1 hour of lecture and then 2 hours of team project. I dreaded this part of the class every week because of the presentation. NOT GONNA LIE, she took me out of my shell after about 10+ different presentations, and I will never forget Org. Behavior because of her. A+++

Get ready to be taken out of your shell if you take Valarie. She's an amazing and interesting human being and really cares about her students. The class itself is pretty easy, but by just showing up you retain important information through her class activities. You'll end up being okay with public speaking afterward.
Nice

Professor Upson is a real gem here at RIT. Very entertaining and tells stories about her life that ties into the subject at hand. A typical class is 1 hour of lecturing with 1 or 2 hours dedicated to team projects. She does not give out homework, instead your grade is dependent on 4 quizzes and a final, she drops your lowest quiz score. 10/10
Very easy if you keep up to date with the subject matter.
Moves quickly and has bad handwriting. Takes attendance daily with mandatory quizzes, kicks people out for texting in class (auto -2% to semester grade). AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.
Very big on the details on how his class works. I liked calc but he made me hate it and a class that was originally 40 students ended up with only 9 to finish the course. STAY AWAY!

one of the worst professors i've ever had. expects you to know everything and understand it all right away.  may be a smart man, but a horrible teacher.  quizzes and exams are very different from homework and classwork.  watch out!!! and if you have him, do not text in class or he will freak out!  HORRIBLE!!! UT needs to get rid of him!!!!!!!!!!!
Collects homework, and grades for correctness.  Gives a quiz everyday that is pretty much unrelated to the homework.  Takes forever to grade exams. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!
He knows what he's doing, but he can't teach it well to anyone else. WATCH OUT!
Probably the worst teacher I have ever had. UT needs to fire this guy before things get worst.

I just had this teacher for Linear Algebra & Numerical Methods. Do not take this prof, even if you have no other choices this semester, just wait until next semester to get another option. This was the worst math teacher I have ever had at UT. I had to purchase another book and read the entire thing cover to cover to pass this class b/c the book he
TERRIBLE TEACHER. Good at math, but BAD as a teacher. Expects you to get it right away. He takes off points for not doing the problem the EXACT way he does it. AVOID HIM!!! Save yourself from an F!
NOT VERY GOOD
Worst teacher ever, I can not believe that they let him teach.

This guy is by far the worst teacher I've ever had.  He'll spend 30 minutes doing one problem, expecting you to get it right away.  Quizzes everday, and not only are they very hard and nothing like the HW, but he only gives you enough time to get about halfway done.  His grading is overly critical as well, avoid him at all costs!

Very difficult teacher. Had him for Calc II and we started on chapter 8 of the book instead of chapter 5 like we were supposed to. Since math builds on things from previous chapters, it was nearly impossible, especially with quizzes every day.

What a horrible professor. Gives quizes every day which are way harder and are not similar to the homework in any way. He will take off points for not following his exact formatting rules on quizes and tests, and will even take off points for not formatting your work his way. It is better to not take the class than to take it with him.
Tests were not similar to homework or quizes, turns an easy subject (linear algebra) into a very complicated class, avoid if possible
I was in his class for one day, and then dropped out of it.  Hint: DONT TAKE HIS CLASS.  He doesn't explain anything.  He may be good at math, but sucks as a teacher.  He should not be on a tenure.
He made this class way harder than what it really was. He was not a good professor for Linear Algebra.

this guy is terrible. He teaches from a powerpoint and doesn't explain himself at all.  I wouldn't suggest that you take a class with him. Also, accent is a little to thick to understand what he is really talking about.
No Comments
Most of the class time is group work among the students and he teaches using an overhead and powerpoint slides. His teaching is not very clear for those of us who are not Einsteins.
Dr. T is a blessing to the chemistry department. He will do whatever he can to help you succeed

Had him for a few different classes and he's great! Casual-ish but well-directed lectures. Gives you some slack when it comes to assignments (late ones). He's also very patient when you ask him questions and doesn't make you feel silly about it. You can tell he really cares about students' learning.

Always ready to help students, lectures were pretty engaging. Despite the difficulty of the material, he taught it intuitvely and the tests are very forgiving with tons of extra credit opportunities. Final was not stressful at all thanks to him adding an entire bonus test to the grade.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had! If you have a chance to take his class do it. the material of the class itself was hard but he presented it in a way that was easy to understand and offer lots of extra outside of class time help! Amazing professor 10/10 recommended.

Dr. T is awesome. I had him last semester, and he is the reason I decided I wanted a minor in chemistry. He is super conversational and does a great job answering questions. I also like that he talks about how the reactions covered in class are applied in the real world. Every test has extra credit built in. Awesome professor!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I had the pleasure of having this professor for my Orgo Lab when I had been taking Orgo Chem originally with Dr. G. After dropping her, I retook Orgo again with him for the Spring semester of 2020 and he was amazing! Very fair grader, awesome out of class and provided chances to increase your grade while also ensuring you are learning. Best guy!

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is very good at breaking complex content into easily understandable material and often uses humor to keep lectures interesting. I highly recommend professor

Literally the best professor. Very engaging, and really great at answering questions. Likes to have fun and talk to us, asks how the class is doing before he starts kind of teacher. Super responsive to emails and almost always gives extensions when u ask. You can tell her cares. Friendly neighborhood dad energy.

He made Orgo 1 a breeze which is really saying something. Lecture attendance is not mandatory but I actually wanted to go. Very nice and approachable. If you don't understand homework (it's on MasteringChemistry and can get difficult) just email him and he'll explain it same night. Thorough lectures and decently easy exams.

SUCH an amazing teacher! You can tell he loves his job and chemistry. Super helpful if you have a question about the content and really down to earth. Definitely sets you up for success in the long run.

Dr. T is amazing. His lectures are fun and engaging, he is a super open professor and will talk to you about anything. He has a clear schedule that he follows, which makes it very easy to keep up. He also makes himself accessible if you have any questions or concerns. Dr. T's love for chemistry is infectious and it is awesome

Not only a great Professor, but also a great guy. Truly cares about his students doing well, and is very accessible. Had him for orgo lab, and he was more help than my orgo lecutre prof prepping for tests. Also a very fair grader. Will make you work for the grade, but gives you the tools. Best Prof i've had at RIT, could not recommend more!

Lecture slides were available before class to preview or print. The textbook was open source, and freely available online. There are no stupid questions, and he'll take the time to answer yours, either in class or in office hours. Almost any time you catch him in his office, he's willing to talk to you, even outside of dedicated office hours.

Professor Tusch is an incredibly caring professor that both cares deeply for his students and enjoy spending time helping them. He has helped me with my organic lab questions and reinforce lecture ideas enthusiastically. 10/10 one of my favorite professors and I am willing to die for him.
Doug is an amazing professor. He makes organic chem easy to understand and does an excellent job at explaining topics.

Organic II lab is simple for majors. The first two labs you learn reactions and after that, you have to identify 3 unknowns. Without giving you the answer, Doug is really helpful and pushes you in the right direction.

He was extremely approachable, answered promptly, and allowed free questions/discussions. He really cared about how students did. Used free textbook :) Gave extra credit, curves, and super fair practice tests. Exams were very reasonable. I would not have been able to do well in this class without such an excellent professor like him!

Full  of herself even though she doesn't know what she's talking about. Opinionated and doesn't care about whether we learn, just wants to prove her point about being all-knowing. I am so glad I am done with this class!  Avoid her at all costs if you can.

This was an AWESOME class! It is the best class I've had in a while. Complete hands on - we learn by doing and reading current articles - not from a book.  No tests, but work intensive.  She is very knowledgeable and super helpful; she really cares. And the P2P project experience is AMAZE!!! We got to do a REAL campaign with a budget!

One of the best business professors at RIT and I highly recommend her. I took this class and another of hers at the same time, the work is mainly group work and some small individual assignments. She presents the material in a fun way that allows her points to get across very easily. She is helpful and cares about her students and their success.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor Boveda has a clear vision for the Marketing class. We had the excellent opportunity to work on the Peer2Peer project. The semester was difficult since the level of responsibility is near to working in the real world, but I felt so prepared when I came to work at my first corporate job!  Love the class since it was rewarding!

Adriana is by far one of the top business professors RIT has to offer. I took two of her classes in one semester and there was a lot of group work, but she makes up for it with no exams throughout the semester. She's fun, very personable, and truly cares about your success as a student and a person. She's approachable and will guide you if you ask.

Marketing sem is a difficult class, but extremely rewarding when you put in the effort, time, and energy. In some instances, I learned more in that class than I did at my first co-op! Adriana definitely teaches in a more unconventional way, but if you take it all in and work hard, you won't be disappointed with what you learn.

Most confusing professor I've ever had hands down. Not clear on assignments (which there are way too many). A ridiculous amount of group projects with different groups which are also confusing. She gives no feedback on your work just a random grade in the grade book with no explanation. She also cancels class a lot. I don't recommend this professor

Total waste of time. You have to build your blogger on your topic is all i heard. Need class to graduate otherwise this was a total waste of time. Lots of pointless busy work with confusing deadlines and grading.
She seems nice and friendly, but she is very picky in homework, which is also too much. If you really want to learn, you could like her. Otherwise don't take this class with her.

Easy class, not too much pressure.  Pay attention and do the work and you'll get a good grade.  A little too easy, and according to my internet marketing teacher she didn't cover everything he thought was important.

Harshest grader I've ever had. Not clear with how specific her grading is. If a period is out of place you are wrong. I learned absolutely nothing and you probably won't either. Horrible individual communication with her students. Can't read her handwriting on feedback.

She was not easy, but not extremely hard either. I put in moderate effort, but barely got an A. I learned a decent amount, and I think for an intro class it was just the right amount of work and difficulty. I would recommend, but does require some work.

Great professor, kept students' interest and rarely went the full 2 hours midway through the quarter.  All of the homework was from the online McGraw Hill connect program, which is GOD-AWFUL.  Half the class had grade-ruining issues with the program.  Luckily, Prof. Boveda said she'll stop relying on the Connect program, so she gets 10/10.
Good teacher, the Connect web service she uses is terrible though

She was very helpful. As long as you asked her for what her expectation about the assignment you should be fine. Quizzes are usually easier than homework but she said otherwise. It wont matter as long as you read the book, you will be fine.

Took her for Principles of Marketing, she's a great professor! Really enjoyed her class. Very nice, kind, and helpful-funny too! I forgot to submit my homework and she let me submit it the following day with deductions. Only annoying thing all hw is online and quizzes, and they're tedious. Other than that, I highly recommend her, best professor!
Best teacher i have had so far, makes marketing interesting and is quite funny. Likes to interact with her student as well as class will require work esp. your marketing plan project

AWESOME PROF! Take her class! Lectures=not boring at all. She uses online software for hw/quizzes. If u use grewal website they give u w/ book to help u "study", ur guaranteed 80% on hw since some activities are identical to hw online. If someone drops in ur grp that means more work on your plate, so choose ur grp members wisely.

Adriana (she recommends you address her by her first name) is so friendly and helpful, but the software she uses for out of class assignments is horrendous:   costs $20, words questions unfairly, does not give feedback, and **GLITCHES OFTEN**. As homeworks and quizzes count for a decent portion of the final grade, be careful with them.

She is really nice and helpful. She also is really understanding. So long as you put a little bit of work into the class then it is an easy A. Quizzes are online, and for everything she gives great guidance.
She knows her stuff. Her class may require some of your time, but you actually learn so many things about Marketing. Very helpful outside classes. She's also VERY nice. Would recommend her!

This professor is one of the BEST I have ever had!! She is really laid back and is just SUCH a wealth of knowledge about everything, electronics in particular. She puts up power points but just for referance. She is just AWESOME!!quizzes are hard, and you cant **** with her, she knows her****.
coolest class i ever had

I took Proj. Mngmt & Practice online went into the class thinking it would be overwhelming. It turned out to be great! As long as you are involved in the course (Discussions) turn in things on time and show interest, you will get at least a B! He's really fast at replying to emails and helping!

Professor Khorram has difficult exams but gives tons of practice problems to prepare. He also gives practice problems in class but exams tend to be much more difficult than anything given in class. He is always there to answer questions and definitely wants his students to succeed. To succeed in this class you need to attend all of the classes.
Grade was based only on 4 exams, but they were generally pretty easy. They were also pretty short, so one missed question could mean the difference between a 100 and a 75.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things']
comment: He was an awesome Philosophy teacher who really knows the subject. For an intro class, he doesn't go too in depth, making it very manageable even if you dislike Philosophy. Tests are based only on PowerPoints, which he uploads. Attendance isn't required, but gives extra points towards grade if you show up.

Entire grade is based on 4 quizzes, made philosophy very interesting and he's funny and upbeat. Although he would post the slides like 2 days before the quizzes but that's because he wants people to go to class. I would recommend him highly because of how chill he is.

A wonderful professor that cares about the subject he's teaching and his students. Tries his best to make the lectures engaging and does a great job. Very understanding and kind. Your grade is based on only 5 quizzes but you only need the slides to do great on them. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I enjoyed going to class :)

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: No final, 5 exams over the semester each worth 20%. Prof was very passionate and helped make the subject a little bit more interesting. Doesn't post much of anything on my courses but is very easily to communicate with one-on-one. Pay attention heavily in lectures and take detailed notes. Lots of readings.

One of my favorite classes at RIT. Lectures remind me of a Ted Talk, and he often ends classes early. No textbook, all of the material is from slides he created. The final grade consists of 5 tests and no final. Some reading outside of class, but no other homework. If you pay attention to the lectures you will do great. Highly recommend!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Caring', 'Graded by few things']
comment: His class is focused around discussion so doing course readings before coming to class is very important. So no homework, you're graded by just exams and a paper. This shouldn't be a problem as long as you turn them in on time, he only accepts late work with a medical excuse or other emergency. He cares about his students and he wants you to learn.
Missed a deadline by a little and wouldn't accept it for a grade, otherwise he's fine

The entire grade of the class is 5 quizzes. He gives around 5 free points on them too. I went to every lecture and took notes but learned barely anything. The only homework is readings that will help you learn more. I did not do them (might be why I didn't learn much) but they are very hard to read and long. Don't think I could recommend him.
great prof. one of the best teachers at rit. I have taken multiple of his classes and always look forward to his class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: There are ONLY 5 quizzes. t/f then short response. I thought itd be an easy A but bombed the last three. I went to every lecture and wrote notes, but learned nothing. There are readings to do that will help a lot for lectures and quizzes.
Solid Professor. As long as you have a brain that thinks, then you'll be just fine.

PHIL 101 is an easy course (just 5 quizzes), but regardless, the actual content of the lectures and readings are excellent. Prof. Aguilar is very passionate about the field of philosophy, and his coverage of the material during class is well-paced and engaging. His personality and enthusiasm make him one of the best lecturers I've had so far here.

You can tell he really enjoys teaching about the philosophers he's talking about in class. He genuinely likes debating with students about their opinions on the ideas presented. The topics are a bit abstract but really interesting and seemingly a good intro to the field. The whole grade is 5 noncumulative tests that are very simple.

To be honest, I did not find him too easy, but he is a pretty forgiving grader and he was very willing to give exceptions for deadlines and such. Most of the difficulty comes from the pretty long and in-depth readings we were given. His lectures are a bit hard to follow, but he is definitely passionate about what he teaches.

Prof Aguilar is fairly easy going when it comes to his class, even more so the bigger it is. My class less than half the people showed up on a regular basis. His lectures are pretty boring only because of the subject material, he personally has great energy. Also go to the last class of the semester, it is one of the most important.
Really liked him. Easy A.

Good professor if you need to fill an ethical perspective. Lectures got a bit long and boring sometimes, but he tries to make them an interesting introduction to philosophy. If you come to class and pay attention the exams are an easy A. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you aren't there you will struggle on the exams. Overall a good professor.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Good professor. Enjoyable lecturer. Took philosophy 101 with him, and if you paid attention in class and took notes, the 5 tests your grade is based on are easy. He has non-mandatory attendance- don't be fooled. All the important info is ONLY in lecture. no notes on mycourses, nothing. Go to class and you don't even really need to do the reading.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Lectures can be pretty interesting and are usually discussion heavy. The grading consisted of participation, 3 exams (essay questions) and a final paper. He's really passionate about this subject and is clear in how he presents information, but he can sometimes get carried away in over-explaining simple concepts.
Professor Aguilar is an amazing professor. He gives good lectures and the class is very straightforward. You only get 5 exams, worth 20 points each.
Good teacher, and his tests weren't that difficult although his lectures were pretty boring. The tests had all multiple choices along with bonuses. You will do fine if you study.
Had class discussions on topics that would sometime throw our schedule off a little but we covered all of the topics. There were 3 essays and 1 final paper of 7 - 10 pages. No other homework.

The class is easy, but this man's lectures are soooo boring; he repeats himself a lot and over explains very simple concepts. It's a good class to take if you want an easy A, but just make sure you bring something to entertain yourself with if you decide to actually show up.

Very kind and approachable, very passionate and a clear grader, free bonus points included on everything, but honestly if you pay attention, it's very hard not to get 100 on everything, even if yyou don't read a single reading assigned, would definitely recommend

Prof Aguilar is an amazing professor. Take him for whatever course you can. He is so passionate about his field and always finds a way to make the lectures interesting. The tests are a bit challenging though but he really gets you thinking. Plus.. he's also really nice and you'll enjoy him! :)

He is a great professor. I had no interest in philosophy and he makes it as interesting as possible. I never did the readings, just take notes and study his hand outs. There are 5 tests, each out of 20 points and whatever your 5 tests add up to is your grade. There are 5 bonus points built into each test.

Jesus is a great teacher who is enthusiastic about the subject he teaches.  He portrays the topics well and makes you think about the moral issues introduced.  He will ask you to buy some books for class but you really don't need to.  He posts many of the readings online and many of the books can be found via google.  I would highly recommend him.
Easy tests, boring lectures. No real need to show up to class - just use SparkNotes and listen to him answering questions before the test.

Ignore the idiots that rated this guy a 1. This is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Crystal clear, easy grader, passionate (and extremely knowledgeable) about his field. I wholeheartedly recommend his class if you care at all about philosophy. Easy A if you pay attention and learn.

Amazing class. Extremely interesting, really gets you involved in thinking about the material. All you have to do is read, show up and take decent notes, and you'll do great. Four in-class tests count for 100% of grade. Tests are 2 essays. I wrote 1-1.5 pages each essay. Reviews material directly before test.  Easy A for me. Had an average above 98

I didn't like the how he teaches his classes. I respect that. I always fall asleep when I come to his classes. If you want to actually learn, then go ahead take his class. As for me, I was just looking for a LA class to fill up. Big mistake.
I'm not much of a philosophy person but he made it very easy to understand.
Very interesting class. He's a really good teacher. Not tested on text, tested on lecture, but he refers to quotes. 4 exams no final. No papers. No projects. Take notes, study notes you'll do great.
Very easy professor. Lectures are thought-provoking, and he tries to make the material clearer by using real world examples. He does tend to repeat himself quite a bit though. Highly recommended.
Great lecturer. Just show up, listen about 50% time, easy. no final, 4 exams total. very fair questions on exams. draws funny little doodles to help visualize scenarios. highly recommend.

He is a fantastic teacher, great at explaining things and making you understand them.  He quotes the book often so it's good to at least skim through it.  His lectures are the whole tests, but they are very easy anyway.  He also has a review for the test right before you take it.  Overall, take him if you have the chance!
great professor! very nice and keeps the class interesting... can tell he is interested in what he is teaching. fair grader.
Good teacher, although he had to try and handle a large class of about 70 students which sometimes proved to be cumbersome for him.  He is a good teacher and fair grader.
This guy is the man. I highly recommend this class, it's an easy grade. He fully describes all topics and there are four tests for the quarter, all in essay form. Very fair grader.
Only thing that held him back was stupid questions from students.
All readings are printed out for you, very clearly covers topics.  Tests are all essay.  Fair grader.  I would recommend for anyone.

Easy to approach and grading is fair. Made long, late classes enjoyable. Had him for 2d animation and grades were based on whether our animations were believable or not, so you don't have to be an artist to do well in his animation class. Gave constructive feedback on how to improve

Fun teacher to have. Easy to approach and grading is fair. Made long, late classes enjoyable. Had him for 2d animation and grades were based on whether our animations were believable or not, so you don't have to be an artist to do well in his animation class. Gave constructive feedback on how to improve our projects.
She always tries to help as much as possible. Easy going teacher.

GDD2 with Cody was the chill class I needed to survive the hellish junior year. He's ridiculously chill and gives you the respect you deserve as a third year student, while also making sure that everyone is on track to get their work done. 10/10 would take again.

Cody is one of the best professors I've ever had and one of the best in IGM. He is really nice and funny and just all-around great guy. He's really understanding of situations and cares about his students. He's responsive in emails asking for help, and he will sit with you in his office and work with you until your code works. Definitely take him!

Super great. I learned an incredible amount in all of Cody's classes. He really cares about students doing well, is very helpful, gives good feedback, and has great lectures that are easy to follow along with. Besides that he's a real cool dude, very funny and friendly. Take him if you can. I really loved and valued all his classes :)

Good professor, good projects, good class content. Entertaining to listen to as well. Class was pretty quiet in my section but I would suggest taking classes with him. So far one of the most valuable courses I have taken at RIT, much better than the prerequisite web dev course. Gives good options for both New Media and GDD students
approachable and fun , take him

One of the most approachable and fun professors I have had.  He's very helpful, extremely fair at grading, and is an all-around funny guy.  Homework is graded promptly and project outlines are clear.  Lectures can get a little boring if you're familiar with the subject.

Cody is the best teacher in IGM since Joe P left. His classes are interesting and taught well, he's very committed to students. He's an easy grader, it's more about putting in the effort and showing interest than checking the boxes. His sense of humor copy pasted from reddit but he doesn't overuse stale memes  too much.
Really easy class. I enjoyed it. Lots of projects but if you do your work its smooth sailing.

Took him for 110, taking him for 220 next semester, and whenever else I can. Literally the greatest teacher I've ever had probably. Love him to pieces, good professor and will make you feel like you're good friends, too.

Take his class if you can! He knows his stuff and gives a lot of practice exercises in class, and you code along with his class examples. Tries to make lectures fun and keep students alive in class. Exam questions are from a practice review packet he gives, so you know what to expect. Very helpful if you have trouble with the projects.

Cody was one of the greatest professors I have ever had. He knows his stuff and is very good at explaining and making sure you understand the topic. He is easily approachable and is very willing to help you if you need it. He made the class extremely fun, and made boring stuff enjoyable. Definitely take his class.

Take him if you can! He's an awesome guy and is always willing to help you. He makes lectures that SHOULD be boring actually quite interesting. He was my favorite professor for this semester. Some might complain about the workload, but it's really not bad if you manage your time well. It's hard to do bad in his class unless you don't do the work.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Lectures are often boring as he rambles on.  When you get a question wrong on exams, quizzes, or homework no reason as to given why.  Miss two classes he drops your grade by a whole letter grade (A to B, B to C, etc). Oh ya and his grading on true false questions.  Right +3, Wrong -2, Blank +1.  Don't actually answer them and take the free point.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Wants you to read everything 4 times. If you don't get it try again. Missed negative sign makes the answer wrong and no partial credit. If he likes you you'll do well, if not you're screwed. Tries to be funny and fails miserably.

He claims to give partial credit if your work shows you understood the question, but will give none. Will often cancel office hours when he shows up to them for various reasons. Gets extremely upset and defensive against any ind of criticism or disagreement. Is proud of how many students drop his class as if he thinks it means he's a good teacher

I learned a lot from Takahashi but it wouldn't show in my tests. I'm typically a pretty good test taker but I was pulling C's on all of his. He does warn you about the difficulty in the beginning of class and he's not wrong. I think half my class ended up dropping. He also has a ridiculously strict attendance policy.

Takahashi is the worst professor I have ever had. People say that if you pay attention you will learn a lot, but that's not true. You will have to spend hours teaching yourself on your own because he will do nothing but berate you and claim you don't try hard enough. He is a tough grader and gives zero partial credit. Avoid him if you can.

This class was impossibly hard. I got a 58 on my first exam and that was actually a pretty good score compared to what other people in my class got. Exams are graded unfairly with no partial credit. Homework has no completion component to the grade, just 3 random problems are selected and graded for correctness. I'd avoid this class at all costs.

Takahashi is a very reasonable professor, he lays out what he expects and he does not joke, all the things on the syllabus are for real. But you will learn a lot if you are willing to.  He is extremely passionate and willing to help to students and goes to great lengths for both the material and the students. You won't get an A, if you care.

Don't count on him for any help in his course. He does not teach material in class. His tests are impossible and most questions/ subjects were never mentioned prior to testing. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. Most take this course because it is required, but as far as Takahashi is concerned your life is Linear algebra.

This course was extremely tough and it will require everything you can muster. However, he warns you on the first day. You need to pay attention every second of the lecture or else you will be left in the dust and have no idea what's happening. Switch professors or drop immediately if you struggle in the first few weeks. Office hours are important.

On the first day he will give you a list. Be honest with yourself... if you are not ready to do EVERYTHING on the list then switch classes immediately. The tests are all questions from the homework and class. They are difficult to complete though so take the time to learn it well the first time and REALLY understand it.

Takahashi is a great guy and really wants his students to succeed. However, he does not make that success very easy. Many of his test questions are directly from lecture notes or hw, but those problems are not at all easy to do in a testing environment. He moves quickly, but will also go out of his way to help if you need it. You won't get an A.

Takahashi will tell you on the first day of class that his class is tough and if you just want to get it over with and get a good grade to change to a different section. However, he is a fantastic professor and really into teaching. You'll learn a lot in his class, but you might not get very good grades since the exams can be long and challenging.
Difficult class, not the worst teacher but definitely not the best either.

I took discrete with him, and he must be one of the most genius professors at this school. Can be VERY hard to keep up with, so don't get behind!!! If you're willing to put in the effort, though, I'd highly recommend taking him. Gave lots of partial credit in discrete, I can't speak for other classes. Class average was a C .

If you get stuck with this, drop or switch immediately. He is obsessed with proofs and often derails from the topic at hand. I had him for Calc II. His tests are extremely difficult despite being direct copies of examples sometimes. He gives almost no partial credit. If you do all parts of a question correctly but get a wrong answer you get 1/10.

Mr. Takahashi is a genius professor, but his exams are very very difficult and the way he teaches students is so confusing and hard to follow his lecture. If the question worth 10 points and you do the process right but the final answer is wrong, he will give you 2 out of 10 points. I DO NOT RECOMMEND TO TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

His classes are constant notes with no explanation. If you don't attend office hours you will likely fail. He has little to no partial credit on exams. The exams are the hardest thing I have taken in the entirety of my college career and they are extremely difficult to prepare for because of the amount of proofs that need to be memorized.

For most, Takahashi was probably a hilarious professor. He's really knowledgeable and sometimes derails. One day in Discrete Math we began talking about Linear Algebra topics. My suggestion if you get him is to study your notes religiously and go to office hours. If he knows who you are, he's willing to help you out.

Do not take a class with this guy, your life will be living hell! His tests are impossible! Every question consists of proofs and not anything that is like normal problems the homework. Grades extremely harsh. Does not get the hint that people are only taking the class because their major requires it.
Will reduce your grade drastically if you miss more than 2 classes in the semester. A letter grade for each one after if I remember correctly.

He holds students to higher standards than most. Tests were alright, except for the final, which focused a lot more on the material at the very end than the previous material and was overall very difficult. He is a very funny guy and cares about his students.

He is brilliant, but I would never take this class if given the option. I got shoved into this class by my advisor for my first year. Drop the first chance you get, he seems like a very level headed, good professor, but he grades EXTREMELY HARSH. Only graded homework and tests, tests are worth 300660. Class Avg was C, he tests are very hard.

Takahashi is extremely passionate about math and it shows. It is a very do-able class if you are prepared to put the in the work needed. Homework due every other class. Attendance is 10% of grade. Only 3 tests and a final for graded assignments other than HW. Awesome teacher, goes on tangents sometimes, but overall would definitely take again

Takahashi is a very great individual and he is truly there for his students. He will help you until you fully understand a topic. He will help students until 12AM during his office hours on many occasions. Given this, this will likely be the hardest course you will take. It requires many hours of studying. Lucky to get a C without 110% effort.
He is a really good professor. I learned a lot from his lecture and he also inspired me to declare a minor in mathematic

Prof. Takahashi's passion for math really shows in his lectures. His energy during teaching helped to keep me alert and actively listening. Also, he was consistently available for extra help and always willing to help students as much as it took to get them to understand.

He always says that if you understand his lectures, you will do well in his class, but therein lies the problem.  His lectures are a giant mess  of poor handwriting and personal notation scribbled in almost random locations about the board; they are extremely hard to follow and very fast paced.

Like many have said, this professor goes on many tangents. He is not extremely helpful during class and hard to understand, constantly pushing you to go to his office hours. He will not go over homework problems in class nor post review problems for tests. Tests are far a part, meaning they cover a lot of sections. Formula sheets are not allowed.

Very hard class. Very hard to keep up with note-taking, and are almost forced to come to office hours as a result(which he sometimes cancels). When he does have office hours though, he is very willing to help. Be ready to put in 3x the amount of credit hours in extra, per week. Also, give up weekends.

I'll start with saying this man is very intelligent, but should never step foot in a classroom.  His lectures are incredibly hard to follow, makes up his own homework and lectures. Didn't even finish all the material and expected us to learn it all on our own for the final. Somewhat helpful in office hours, but cancels them often and unannounced.

Very very tough professor. Really makes you go above and beyond the basics of the class. He's a very nice man, but I know of many friends that took diff eq with other professors and easily passed, and I'm most likely going to fail his class. More than half of the class failed his 2nd test, no curve, just keeps going.

The worst professor I have taken so far, and most likely the worst I'll ever take. He goes off on tangents, uses his own notation, doesn't explain concepts very well and is just an overall bad professor. The average grade for the class is an F, and he does not curve the grade. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. BEWARE!!!

He is quite possibly THE worst professor I have ever had. Half the class failed the 2nd exam, and he only you extra credit if you got above a 90. Can't explain the subject at all, keeps going on tangents, then scribbles the remaining lecture on the board then dismisses class without explaining anything. Expects student to use his notation.

Lectures are clear. He does go off tangent all the time and rush through the rest. However if he doesn't cover something in class then it's not on the exam or homework. Very flexible and accommodating homework and test schedule. Test are taken straight from lecture examples and homework problems.

Uses his own notations causing confusion in the class. Does not curve any tests even when roughly 2/3 of the class is at risk of failing. Goes off on tangents about things unrelated to the class and then rushes to finish lecture. Goes above what is required rather than focusing on what students do not understand unless you go to office hours.
He is an excellent professor, but he expects his students to do a reasonable amount of work outside of class. Does not curve tests. Has very accommodating office hours.

He acts like a real person compared to other professors, he actually has emotions and cares. Intro to Psych is a GPA booster, his quote. He basically gives you the answers to tests. Interactive and funny lectures. Textbook reading is suggested but I could not find the time, sorry. Take notes during class and show up, you'll succeed. Take it.

This class is easier to understand if you know physics, but if you move past the heavy physics-based portions then the class is fine. Lectures were nothing special but he did demos each week + he went out of his way on review days to make the midterm and final bearable. He's also a hilarious lecturer, which made it worth it to go to class.

He's a funny guy, but my GOD can he go on tangents. The class is physics-based and he's a physics nerd, but those two things make the class impossibly boring/hard for someone who doesn't fully understand physics. The textbook is practically unreadable, and he simply reads from the book or slides during lecture.

He doesn't really enjoy developmental psychology, but he made the class really easy so we would all do well. If you go to class he gives you the weekly quiz answers. He lectures on Tuesdays and Thursdays are class discussions. If you speak once you get credit. Tests are super easy because you go over answers ahead of time. Study the weekly quizzes.
Real passion for the subject. Highly recommend going to his office hours with any question, he will be more than happy to help.

Professor Goodwill was a good teacher for the first 2 weeks but he got some chronic depression and ever since then, he has always come into class very tired and in a terrible mood. He started belittling students when more clarification was requested. Makes students figure out the Calculus instead of giving us an example first. Very strict grader

I hope I have Mr. Goodwill again this year. He stays on task, will take the time to answer student questions, and tells personal stories to motivate us for tests. He doesn't pile on work, and just give us enough to make sense of the unit. Office hours with him were extremely helpful.
Great professor. Cares about the students and actually wants them to do well. Would take him again if given the choice

Taking Goodwill? Get ready for a C. His workshops and homework will not in any way prepare you for the quizzes and tests, as on those he just spikes the difficulty to an unreasonable amount. Also his lectures are unclear. He likes to make a bad analogy and when nobody understands the material he gets upset. Bad lecture+hard tests+unfair graderno

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Great teacher BUT grading system is an ABSOLUTE MESS. All the times I have had him, nobody has above a C or D before the Final Exam..... Very frustrating. I have a 3.5 GPA and his 2 classes are my only C's.
Quizzes every week and 3 tests throughout the semester.  Willing to go out of his way to make time to help you.  Makes class interesting

He is super organized and a really helpful professor.  He will fit his schedule around yours for office hours and if he can't meet with you in person will skype with you at crazy late hours.  His tests are tough, but fair so you should use the classwork activities to study off of- not the study guides (they are usually way easier than the tests).

Best professor I've had at RIT. He is understanding and funny as hell. You can go to his office almost anytime, in or out of office hours, and he is more than happy to do anything to help you. Be it rephrasing a topic, putting it in terms you understand, etc. Extremely unorthodox way of grading, but I found it to be more than helpful and very fair.

Goodwill was very understanding on a personal level and very practical on a academic level. He understands that Math isn't everyone's whole life, unlike some professors at RIT. You must take diligent notes in nearly every class to get a decent grade however. Tests are difficult, and he tends to ask odd-ball questions. Good professor.

He was very helpful in class, he'd stop the lecture to answer any questions and everything. Class format is very organized and you always know what you need to learn for upcoming tests and quizzes (it is all laid out on the schedule!)  Pretty cool guy as well. Funny and clever, he'll make you laugh quite a bit. Made me actually enjoy calc

He is literally the worst teacher at RIT. Doesn't teach, puts problem on board tells you to solve it, 20 minutes later when everyone is confused he tries to solve it and can't. Horrible, class average was a 50 by the end of the year. STAY AWAY, GOOGLE IS MORE HELPFUL AT LEARNING CALC THAN HIM

Here's why I'm gonna get a 2nd C in his class: always begins lecture with an example, leavin you oblivious of today's topic until later;  class ends and you have no recollection of the lesson; workshop is 2 days after lesson; makes you work super hard for something with little credit (no one bothers); he has 6 kids and 4 classes -- slow grading

Grades are arbitrary.  Takes MONTHS to return quizzes (not exaggerating).  Quizzes are cumulative which is great unless you haven't gotten the last 3 back and don't know what you did wrong.  Gives you gold star stickers for participation (yes really).  Would never take a class from him again.
can be very confusing and talks about random stuff at times

Great professor! TESTS:none. QUIZZES:weekly, cumulative, in that you can/should retry questions from a previous week. HOMEWORK:usually weekly on MyMathLab, sometimes multiple 20-40 problem assignments due in same week, but flexible in due dates if visit OFFICE HOURS:super flexible, helps explain topics or help with homework. Totally recommend him.

Take this professor. He teaches realistically - he tears math down and builds it back up. He hates "magic spells" and will teach you the logic behind everything (sounds worse then it is, but is tremendously useful.) His grading "skill system" leaves a lot of room for a late comeback, and he will help you pass.

Goodwill is a good teacher and is fun to have.  A few problems with him are that he sometimes gets distracted in class and rambles leaving less time to learn and he spends too much time trying to explain his math philosophies rather than teaching. He is a good teacher and I would recommend him, but he needs to spend more time teaching during class.

Really awesome professor! Very clear and approachable, and willing to help students outside of class. Interesting approach to grading-quiz on each subject and these can be retaken on following quiz days throughout the semester. Also lighthearted and funny!
His class is so damn fun and chill. 2 hours in class without falling asleep

Professro Tim is extremely helpful. He does whatever he can to make students learn. He loves teaching math and he is significantly good at it. He is a math nerd. He is funny. Students don't get bored in his class, at least I didn't. He has an excellent method of testing students. You can always get an A if work hard.Also, he uses my math lab-v good

Confusing lectures, often allowed students to work at board so rest of class copies an incorrect example. Grading is pretty arbitrary so suck up and go to his office hours. He is fun to have in class though very laid back.

Excellent professor! One of my favorites so far. Explains all the concepts crystal clear and will gladly sit down to help you if you don't understand something. Awesome sense of humor too and very much approachable! Easily, one of the best math professors at RIT :]
Wonderful sense of humor. great teacher
He's the man.  No tests, just collects some work in folder you turn in, can easily copy, and get an A. Just be sure you get him for the next in sequence or your screwed.

Best Professor ever!  He really understands what he teaches and will find a way to help you understand, all you have to do is ask.  I went from a D with a bad professor to an A with Goodwill.  My only regret is that I couldn't take him this quarter.

Excellent math teacher. In fact, best math teacher I ever had. Even though that I suck at Math, with his help and support a got a B. He takes his time to explain whatever needs to be explained, he never rushs when the class doesn't understand something. Very funny and nice guy, always smiling and takes everything easy. ( GO AHEAD WITH HIM!)

Great professor tons of fun to have and his classes are always fun, can grade tough but always makes it possible to help a bad grade. he let my class replace our lowest 2 test grades with the final, we only took to tests too. i still visit his class just to hang out with him

He treats the study portfolio like it's the most necessary component of the class.  More of the students time is spent perfecting past material in the portfolio than learning and understanding new material.  He is very helpful and approachable, but he believes his portfolio is the best and only way to teach, which, it is not.

He can definitely make your week extremely stressful, but he's a great teacher and loves teaching.  Doesn't use a textbook but guides you through building a portfolio of organized notes which is tedious but makes for great study material.  Fun to listen to, appreciates hard work and honesty.

Favorite calc prof. Fun to have and doesn't require a textbook so money saved, BUT WARNING, even though a textbook isn't required for purchase, he makes you create your own textbook through organized notes that he checks for points. It is very helpful but WILL take numerous hours to complete ESPECIALLY if you fall behind at the end of the course.

Tim is an interesting character. He cannot decide how he wants to teach his course, but on whatever method he attempts he will put his heart into it. You can always approach Tim with problems, both personal and in math. He's a great caring guy. He can make your week REALLY stressful, but it will pay off in the end. Does a decent job overall.
The best. Knows how to teach. Never gave up on me, even when i was struggling.

Always helpful and loves teaching! Great professor, actually made me miss calculus when I was done. I would highly recommend!  He wants you to try your best and do well in his class, something that is hard to find in professors now.

TAKE HIS CLASS. One of the best teachers I have ever had. I hate math and enjoyed class, even doing well in it. You'll use the text book he wrote, but he gives you a copy of what you need for homework. He helps you a ton and while some problems are more difficult, it is totally worth it. You HAVE TO WORK, but core questions will seem SUPER EASY.
Great calc teacher!!! Would never want a different professor for this cl03ass. Workshops are easy and tests and quizzes are not hard if you look over note sheets. Definitely Recommended!
