comment: This was Austin's first semester teaching. He did a great job teaching in a practical setting and relied more on showing rather than telling. He was always willing and available to help if you needed it. All around a wonderful professor.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Austin is a new professor, so his teaching skills still have room for improvement. However, he is really nice and always willing to help. If you ask him to do things (like make an EXTRA exam study guide), he will. I definitely recommend him for DSA 1, as he is extremely flexible but still teaches a lot of good material
Great professor
The way he has his slides is confusing. I'd say he expects you to get it within the first time he explains it to the class. Didn't find his teaching style effective.

In his first year teaching, Austin has already managed to break free of the awful powerpoints from prior DSA classes. He is clear and concise in his lectures and treats his students like the competent programmers they should be at this point in the curriculum and hosts ample office hours for those who are falling behind.

Austin's lectures aren't that good, because I found myself lost or confused at the end of most classes. I had to go to others for help and wondered why he couldn't explain them clearly as other students did. This isn't the professor for you if you enjoy being frustrated at doing work you have trouble figuring out.

He's not the best at teaching at all for sure, he's a little shaky with laying out the concepts and explaining it well. Other students I've talked to would agree that his teaching style isn't that good or helpful. Had to go over and reteach the material myself for a while.

Professor Zhang talks pretty quietly and lectures every class. If you don't have much C++ knowledge beforehand, you won't learn much and will need to learn things on your own. The course materials are different from other IGME 209 classes. He's a younger professor, so I bet he'll improve his teaching style as he continues to work at RIT.

Very sweet and laid back. Gave us Fridays off. However very disorganized. rarely got back to emails, only graded one assignment all quarter. Class mostly relies on textbook readings and quizzes. Final grade seemed to factor in zeros for assignments that were not required on the syllabus and she did not write back to me when I asked her about this.
The professor's teaching style was disorganized, and they struggled to convey the material clearly. Key concepts were poorly explained, leaving students confused and unprepared.

Professor often cancelled class and assignments.  Changed due dates leaving new expectations very unclear.  Never graded anything, was just given an arbitrary final grade with no idea if it was deserved or not.  Talked non stop about her graduate classes.  Left the impression that the graduate classes are where her time and effort may be spent.

Shes a good person but her teaching skills I think are not that good. Her my courses and syllabus is very unorganized and changes the due dates around often. Her materials are all over the place in my courses and is hard to find. Group projects for business plan we work with our groups. Most of the time this class is to work with your group.

She's kind and understanding. Very knowledgeable and willing to help if you ask. This class mostly consisted of working on one group project with multiple deliverables throughout the semester. She does not really stick to her syllabus and gives little to no direction when sending you off to work on your project leaving you to figure it out yourself

Professor Thiuri is extremely kind and compassionate, showing lots of care and attention to the needs of her students. That being said, classes can be frustrating as she talks in circles, sometimes never covering expected topics. Be prepared to do your own reading/research OUTSIDE of the textbook/in your free time, as tests are never set in stone.

She focuses more on current events than the textbook readings making tests more difficult than necessary. She is nice and very knowledgeable in business. Most of the class is group projects and reading the textbooks. Be prepared to never know your grade because she doesn't grade anything till the end of the semester.

Most difficult and unprofessional professor I have ever had at RIT. She barely gives instructions for assignments and takes points off for things never mentioned in the instructions. She doesn't lecture and gives exams that are impossible to do well on. She is also extremely rude and takes forever to respond to emails if she responds at all.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: The teaching method of this professor doth resemble a jest. Within this lamentable chamber, the professor's disregard doth masquerade as instruction. Students are abandoned, the knowledge unaided whilst she doth impose her limited beliefs without heed for true enlightenment. Verily, 'tis a marvel if any doth attain learning amidst such a trashcan.

Most useless class in RIT Business. Better than a philosophy class at making you regret being born. Teacher feels like she hates you and she forces you to have camera on at all given times. Please do not take expecting easy grade only take if you really don't want to go outside and touch the grass.

The lectures are manageable if you pay attention, the exams can be challenging. He offers a lot of flexibility with assignment deadlines and extra time for submissions, and the course includes one individual and one team project. The course however has a tight schedule, which leaves no room for unexpected events which can disrupt the semester.

Very easy online course and can be done in a mater of days since it is asynchronous. Many but not all the terms can be found on quizlet. She responds to emails very quickly and is helpful. Overall very easy class

All the work can be done in 2 days max. So make sure you do it before classes start. It's the easiest A you can get. All the answers to the exams are on Quizlet. The syllabus is super clear; if you email her, she will respond quickly with clear instructions.

Took MED201 online, it's only offered online. She responded quickly to emails outside of class. Very easy course, chapters and final exam are there from day one. Just takes time to complete it. An easy A for me.

Spent an overall 15-18 hours on the course and got full marks on every task. The final is the only thing that is partly challenging as its timed but does not matter as the answers are all online and you just need to google them quick. Easiest course youll ever take, can finish the whole course at once, the final is available to do from day 1

Easiest class that you can finish in a couple days. I did it as soon as it opened up before classes and did not have to think about this course for the rest of the semester. Most of the question on the final came from the self tests and be sure to study the suffix and prefix terms as those were on the final

Online class that is self paced - do it as soon as it opens up on mycourses!! Should take about 2 or 3 days to complete - biggest time consumers are the 1000 flashcards you have to type in, and the 300 question TIMED exam - must complete all activities to do the exam - great for emailing if you have a problem. 50% of grade  classwork / 50%  exam

Probably one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Finished the entire thing in less than 24 hours. All you do is go through the power points, take some tests that you can take over and over until you get a 100, and then a final exam. The final is 300Q, 150 min (yikes) and 50% of your grade, so just be prepared. Over all VERY easy.

I found this class super boring. You just have to fill in a powerpoint for the lecture. Study from the powerpoint for the test (but she even lets you have a cheat sheet for them). Wasn't interested at all though.

I took her med term class, and I spent a good 5 hours a week on it and the only reason I passed was my sister and Google.  The final did not AT ALL reflect what they emphasized in the course.  The students who reported this class as easy must have  all gotten together with Google to do the final. Answers for the final are not on Quizlet btw.
Extremely easy for Human Biology. Grade is only based on exams. Her lectures are pretty boring, but she always posts her slides online. She is a sweetheart as well. Very nice to all her students.
Easy class, everything is on the powerpoints. Teacher is boring, learned more from powerpoints than listening to her.
Medical Terminology was really easy. Self paced and you do it on your own time. 300 question final was nuts though! Highly reccomend if you need a 2 or 3 credit Liberal Arts (Gen Ed) filler!

I took her online class Medical Terminology- SO EASY. If you actually want to learn the material the course is probably hard, but it's great if you're looking for a quick and easy online class. I finished the course in two days and received an A and four credits.
Very nice online class, it is so good if you know the material. I never meet her, that all about it :). But if you really need this class you can take it. This is all right believe me.

Was scheduled as a classroom course but it turned out it was online. Super easy class-- you can pretty much do ALL of it in 8 hours on the last day if you put it off like I did. Easy quizzes you take repeatedly until you get 100 and the final (worth 50% of your grade) is simple as well. Easy class, easy grade. Take it if you can!
She's decent. Class isn't too difficult, you just have to write 4 essays, which includes a group assignment. It's a small class but easy if you pay attention.
She seemed genuinely interested in making us better writers. I don't understand why the other commenters struggled so much, I had harder writing assignments in high school.
If you're not already good at writing essays, don't take this class. Her essay prompts are confusing and boring and rely on equally confusing and boring essays that she assigns to read.

Stay away from this professor. I'm an engineering major and I was spending more time on this class than math & science combined. She expects way too much and the papers we had to write were irrelevant, confusing and pointless. I feel like I wasted all of my nights staying up till 4am writing because I have to retake the class now anyway.

Completely ridiculous. Don't take her because there are about 20 other professors most of which will make the class an easy A. I took her freshman year and after 4 quarters that class is still my only B. Expects way too much dedication from a class that is required and no one takes by choice.

She really knows her stuff and loves english/writing, but she is not set out for teaching. Her lectures are boring and confusing, and she is a tough grader. She definitely favors some students and isn't nice to others. All of the topics that we had to write about for our essays were dumb. I was so bored the whole time.

Really nice guy - projects weren't too hard. Most people seemed to get a decent grades. Some projects are a bit open, but he generally likes the direction people go in. It's a fun class - he's pretty laid back.

Honestly? James Holland  ruined 2D for me this year. he has trouble explaining/clarifying assignments, and his assignments take HOURS to decipher. if he decides he doesnt like what you create, then he trashes it. He grades based on the "c is average" principle. consequently only one person in my class got an A, even though many deserved one.

Super easy class, but I really only learned about audio terms and not implementation. The projects are simple as long as you record your sounds and don't half-ass everything. His obsession with black and white movies is a bit silly. It would have been nice to see modern examples of everything he talks about.

Al is a fantastic professor, I learned a lot more in his class than any other. He's always willing to help with your code. Even though the concepts behind the code are sometimes challenging to grasp, the code itself isn't that hard. He's also good at explaining everything in terms that you can understand. 12/10 take his class

Great class to take, I felt I learned a lot compared to 101. Al may not be a fan of JavaScript but was incredibly helpful in not only teaching us how to do each concept, but helping us understand how the concept worked and the reasoning behind how and why its used. Amazing professor, and a pleasure to be in class with. Pretty jazzy guy all around.

Takes an incredibly long time to grade, making it very hard to gauge how well you are doing in the class. Programming assignments often went far beyond what we learned in class. Although helpful, he would sometimes leave us to our own devices to figure out complex problems. Great guy and helpful occasionally.

Prof. Biles is a great lecturer, and an even better professor. He is really down-to-earth, and obviously cares about his students. Very approachable and helpful outside of class as well. Would definitely recommend him!

Biles gives interesting lectures, but the projects were completely useless. Really easy class one research paper, a power point presentation (that you do the voice-over), and a 20-things I learned in this class project, portrayed however you wish. Biles never graded any of my assignments, and just gave out A's. Also there is no textbook.
the class is hard not the professor. lot of work but biles is one of the better lecturers. if you can get lawley take her instead

Very good at teaching the material.  If you need help, he will go over any material you need.  The workload is fairly easy, as he wants you to focus on the quarter long project.  Like any class, you will get out of it what you put in.

Lectures were quick and didn't pay attention, the labs are based off of the lectures but you can get by without knowing the lectures.  HW is a 8 pg paper and a 5 min ppt on it, but its easy since you can pick ANY topic.  The "final" is a 5 min ppt on what you learned in the class.  Just take notes in the lecture and you're pretty much good.nice guy

Introduction to Interactive Media was a horrible, useless experience for me, but I sat through the first session of it ever and it was a group class between several professors, not just Biles. In labs he experimented, giving either too little information or too much technical stuff without really translating it in English perse.  Easy class though.

Yes, he does have a monotone and there is very minimal class activity.  He provides notes online so you don't have to take any and he provides a study guide that covers pretty much the whole exam.  Overall, very boring but if you at least try and attend class you should have no problem, I'm no schooly but I got through.

This class was relatively straight forwards, but it was taught through power points with little explanation. I'm ranking him so low because the professor put a zero in the grade book, for a completed and on time assignment, until a few minutes before final grades were due. He did not respond to the multiple emails regarding the zero.
Strong accent which makes him hard to understand at times but he knows his stuff and efficient teacher, no fluff

I took this instructor 30, YES 30, years ago and I've been thinking about him because of the things he said 30 years ago about Israel/Netanyahu and Russia/Ukraine and how they have come to fruition. I wasn't even a history major and I loved all the classes I took with this professor. I'm glad I told him how amazing he was.
I took one of his classes and end up minoring in political science thanks to him. Great lecturer and very accessible outside of class

Kaylani is the most powerful lecturer in the history department. Write down everything he says, and study for 10 hours. Roughly 1 in 10 students gets an A. It is true that he has no tolerance for total ignorance or intellectual illiteracy, so many students get shot down in class for not knowing the word "autarky" or Chomsky, Keynes, and Schumpeter.

Can barely understand him, and cant read anything he writes. Constantly tells the students that they are stupid because they don't know some obscure fact in history. Even the kids that liked history got tired of talking and being told that their opinions were wrong. He teaches his view of what happened in history and is not open to debate about it.

Great Teacher but makes you work extremely hard.  The tests aren't to bad if you take good notes but make sure to study them.  He doesn't require attendance but the things he says in class may not be in the book but WILL be on the test.  Overall very good class extremely smart guy

Modern European was one of the most intresting I've taken. Kaylani is easy to listen to and he is passionate about what he's teaching. Tests weren't hard as long as you went to class and paid attention. I'd like to take another class with him in the future.

Hard, but great professor. Wants his students to understand history, not memorize dates. I enjoyed his class, and learned alot. If you listen to lectures and DO NOT MISS CLASS, and of course read you will do fine. Test based 90% on lecture material. Take him.. You will learn more.. Do not expect an A, but you will learn value of a good education.

Out of any teacher I have ever had, I would say that Dr. Kaylani has had the greatest impact on my academic life.  He is the first teacher that has made me actually enjoy history, and want to know more about it.  Studying for anything became much more bearable, and even enjoyable after taking him.  Because of this, my whole GPA went up.
Amazing amount of insight.  Makes you want to learn the material outside of the class, which is something not many teachers can do.  Sometimes I wonder why he teaches at a tech school.
One of the most intelligent professors ive ever had.

Probably the best teacher I've had to date.  Doesn't waste any time, and knows so much about what he is talking about it sometimes scares me.  Holds students up to the same standards to which I think he holds himself.  He made me want to learn the material myself more than any other teacher I've ever, and that's the most important thing.
Amazing Professor,  will give you all the facts you need to know about the Middle East.  Highly recomended.  All you have to do is listen to class lecture and take notes to get east As in exam.
If you want to read 30 pages a day for the rest of the quarter, take his class.

A very challenging but informative professor.  Grades came from three multiple choice tests, no final.  He has a ridiculous amount of insight into politics and history, and is a really nice dude (as long as you ask intelligent questions!)  Would recommend for anyone seriously intersted in history.

Had Kaylani for European and Mid.East History.  He is one of the most intelligent people I have ever met.  I feel like a much more educated person after having taken his classes.  He is a touch teacher, but if you actually care more about your education instead of just your grades - TAKE HIS CLASS.

The best professor I've had so far.  Has a frighteningly sharp intellect and his lectures keep you hooked the entire time.  He really made me want to learn the material.  Dr. Kaylani should just open up his own institution.  I'd go.
I took 3 courses with him because of his tough teaching style.  Though I didn't do well in his classes, I learned much more from him than I would from other history professors (Newman is also great)

Very tough grader....grades came from only 3 tests and they were extremly hard...does not curve at all...notes are taken directly from his mouth, and he talks too fast and has an accent so its hard to understand...studied a lot but still did not do well..
he sucks, puts down students, don't take
The only professor able to keep my attention at this abhorrent school.  I wish I had taken more of his classes.

One of the best teachers i've ever had.  Extremely knowledgeable and motivated.  He has a way of getting ahold of your attention and being interesting like no other teacher. He is demanding, and an excellent educator.

Kaylani is like no other teacher you've ever had. His excitement over the material is evident in everything he teaches. He has pretty demanding expectations for his students, but all his tests are multiple choice (but usually difficult multiple choice).
very good, but tough
Tough but very very good.

Amazing professor, really passionate about teaching is truly kind and is willing to explain things that I should probably know but don't. I have never had a better professor during my time here at RIT. Relatively easy class if you pay attention and he makes it rather easy since he's quite a good teacher.

Prof. Wong was always ready to help and had a structured, easy-to-follow grading system. HW and Quiz happen once a week pretty easy to study for with the ebooks webassign. Explain things in Gen-Z terms and makes puns here and there. Willing to help you understand problems from bottom to top.

Very entertaining lectures (uses slides, but makes sure to make them fun with memes and jokes to keep you awake). He will help you in any way he can and is very easy to reach. Wouldn't recommend leaving the homework for last minute, but he is lenient on deadlines (that he has control over) if you have a valid reason.

I guess he really did change the structure to his class because he is nothing like the older reviews. He allows you to work in groups in class if you want to. He's funny and explains concepts well. Out of the other 181 professors he is definitely top 3. Makes it very easy to pass the final due to the nature of how he teaches his class.

Dr. Wong is a fair grader. Homeworks and Classworks make it easy to grasp in-class content. Class is structured quite well and exams are reasonable(he gives you an index card to use as a cheat sheet and most formulas are provided).

Always communicates info about exams/assignments very well. Exams generally followed lecture work and review materials/practice exams. Recitations are mandatory but very helpful. Towards the end, the quizzes in recitation had lots of extra credit. Prof. Tony is hilarious and makes lectures funny and interesting.

Funny and makes the lectures very enjoyable. However, he is utterly terrible at structuring his class and setting up materials to help you on the exams. We had to use literally five separate services to turn in assignments and interact with the class. Exams are reprehensibly hard, so be prepared to do everything assigned and still barely pass.

Super nice and fun guy, I guess he changed his class drastically cuz his class is nothing like what the older reviews say. Lots of group work, class average on tests is like a B, lot of extra credit opportunities, and grade is really more from effort than just the tests, since each test is 5% of final grade. Material gets a lot harder near the end.

To preface, I am doing mediocre in his probability and statistics class. So I reached out to him and asked for extensions and he has been EXTREMELY lenient and kind. Just based off that alone, he seems to care more than other professors who couldn't really care about whether you have erroneous circumstances or other classes.
Dr. Wong is a good professor who does his best to make a boring class interesting. His tests are very difficult and cover the hardest material. Averages are usually 50-60.

I abhor stats and he made me enjoy the class. Lectures were great, super accessible outside of class, and very caring of students. After our class averaged a 58 on the midterm, he changed the grading system to ensure less people would fail the class. His exams are hard but he allows notecards and holds review sessions, study and you'll be fine.

Dr. Wong's class isn't necessarily difficult but his exams are. The class does not prepare you for the exams at all. He says that if you study all of the homework, practice exams, reviews, lectures, and example problems you'll be fine. That would take hours upon hours. He is a strict grader and takes pride in the class average being a 60.

VERY difficult exams. He moves very fast, covering things other classes don't, such as R. He is a very good professor but the exams are insanely hard. The average on our midterm was 58 which he was "disappointed with," and the average on the final was 66, which he was pretty "happy with." From what I've seen, tests from other profs are much easier.
Dr.Wong is awesome!!! He makes the material interesting and is actually funny. The tests are very hard, so prepare. He is my favorite teacher at RIT!!

Very caring for students, takes feedback and criticism and alters class accordingly, and is quite hilarious to boot. The exams, homeworks, and quizzes were a little heavy and the concepts were hard, but he made them bearable, fun, and interesting. If you have the chance, take him. Don't say groundhogs are better than marmots to his face though. :)

Great professor. Very passionate about math, makes you want to learn. Puts memes in lectures. Quizzes and exams were take-home, but were pretty difficult as a result. Every assignment (minus exams) had a collaborative Slack channel where you could help and get help from the Professor and other students to get unstuck on problems.
Tony Wong is a great professor. He always brings great energy to the classroom, which makes borings subjects seem fun.

All assignments are straight forward and fair. Only assignments that are difficult are exams, but they are take home. Lectures are funny and you are able to work in groups for most assignments. Highly recommend, but be prepared to put in work.
Struggled to follow all semester long. Hard to contact and reach.

So yea yea he's a great guy. But his Prob and Stats class was HARD. Ive taken UP2 but this class was harder, idk if its bcuz tony or the subject itself, but its not all sunshine and rainbows. He does NOT make easy tests, quite the opposite. Class averages of like 50-60 on his exams occured. Yes hes the nicest + helpful af, but BE READY for math251.

Tony is a great professor who went above and beyond by adjusting his class to help ease the burden on students when the whole school was feeling overloaded and burned out due to no-break COVID semester. Very available for office hours and keeps lectures interesting with random jokes and/or tangents. You definitely wont want to skip them.

Tony is an amazing professor and is great at simplifying the difficult concepts of this class. He writes these goofy-ass questions on his homeworks that make them fun to do, and you can't find a powerpoint of his without a joke or a comic in there. His office hours are some of the best I've been to as well. 100% would recommend.

Professor Wong is an absolute godsend. His lectures are crystal clear, and he is extremely dedicated to being as fair and transparent to his students as human possible. He is extremely accommodating and extremely supportive of his students. Despite my difficulties with the subject matter, I couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Very hilarious and easygoing guy, his problems are definitely /r/fellowkids material. I used to have calculus-phobia, but his teaching definitely makes me love calculus again. Weekly homework is 10-15 problems long, so try not to wait until the last moment to do it. Probably the only complaint is his long midterm tests, 15 problems in 100 minutes.

Tony's dedication to math allows him to help his students through problems without flat-out giving them the answers. Witty, attentive, and always well dressed, Tony is the kind of guy to give you his jacket on a rainy day and at the same time calculate the amount of rain falling on the ground per second. Newton was a fraud!
Tony has passed the vibe check.
Very helpful, great energy, amazing jokes

Tony Wong is one of those rare teachers that not only loves what he is teaching, but also loves teaching in general. If you are ever confused with concepts, Tony teaches you in the clearest and easiest way possible. Tony teaches and speaks with passion, enthusiasm, and with a certain friendliness that is hard to find.
The best no cap.

Not a great class with Abby. Projects were vague, and you were expected to do things to her tastes. We spent ten weeks doing gesture drawings. Felt very much like a Drawing I course, not a senior level illustration course. Abby is very nice, but I didn't learn much.
Abby was a great teacher.  The class requirements were a little tedious but were relevant to the Illustration industry.  After the first project you can choose your medium.

Dr. Shipp REALLY loves physics. He teaches with enthusiasm, tries hard to make the subject palatable, and clearly works hard to make students understand the material. He doesn't just follow the activities manual or textbook, he clearly has thought about what makes sense to teach and how. Made good friends at tables. It's still physics, though.

I liked Dustin a lot more than my UP1 professor. He really knows his stuff, has a passion for it, and isn't afraid to be honest because he knows how to help students. It seems as though the ability to answer questions is hard-found in the RIT PHYS department, but Shipp goes out of the way to help, making videos and giving quizzes and etc. 910

Loved taking from him. The average for the quizzes were really low but he curves at the end and they really help you prepare for the final. We never use the textbook and mastering phys. is used only for the homeworks. Tests are department-wide so don't expect them to look like the quizzes. Incredibly fun guy, loves optics to death. Would take again

Well physics 2 is insanely difficult. However, Shipp knows his stuff better than anyone. He goes loves having tables work to get equations on their own, before giving them to you. If you don't come to class.. you'll fail.. end of story. Definitely one of the most fun professors I've ever had, even though I probably won't pass his class.

This was my first course in quantum computing. I really enjoyed listening to Dr. Vogt, as he puts it, "ramble about quantum". He is very knowledgeable and really easy to talk to. I was actually surprised how down to earth he was. If you are interested in photonic quantum computing he knows an extreme amount about linear and nonlinear quantumoptics.
Good class. Good professor. He is easy to talk to and knows his stuff. I'm taking quantum machine learning with him next semester.

I really enjoyed being introduced to quantum computing in this class. The class is homework and project-based, with no tests. It's pretty easy to get an A if you dedicate yourself to the homework. If I were to describe him, he is a combination of a frat guy vibe (in a good way - he uses their verbiage a lot) and Albert Einstein. Fun professor.

Very kind professor. If you paid attention to the lectures alone, you could do most of the homework with no problem. It is clear to me that he didn't go out of his way to make his class impossible; instead, he tried to make it as accessible as possible. He is really funny too.

Ryan was hands down the most hilarious professor I've had at RIT. It's clear that his goal was not to make the quantum computing class hard, but rather to create an opportunity for students to learn the subject and ask questions. He offered many extra credit quantum computing questions for the homework (I think this is a feature, not a bug).
clear stuff

Great lecturer, but the exams were difficult without reviews. Expects you to really understand everything for the exams without providing much information beforehand. Homeworks were not hard, the final practical was easy, just the exams should have had more prep. Take him.

Very lazy, doesn't provide practice problems and hw is just part of a 7 part project, so we don't have any clue what the exam looks like. Grades way harder than he has to, and very slowly. If you care about your grade, AVOID HIM AND TAKE PARK. Lectures are interesting but that's it. Slides are no good. You're on your own pretty much.

As amazing as his lecture is, his test is very difficult, not much review materials for test and the slide sometimes do not incorporate include materials for the test, very informational but the grade is not worth it

knows his stuff, can explain things very well, and is caring. however, there is no good way 2 study 4 exams (major part) other than office hours. completely blindsided by format of exam, the slides arent helpful bc tests are handwritten + application based (lots of stack diagrams) and they don't rlly take u thru the process. grades painfully slow.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I was COMPLETELY blindsided by the good reviews for this section. Don't listen to what reddit and RMP says if you care about your gpa, stress levels, and a proper structure TAKE PARK INSTEAD. Olson is a really great person; but the way he carried this class was overwhelming, unorganized, and extremely confusing.

Mr. Olson definitely understands and is passionate about information security, and it shows in this course. During my time in this class, he ran a flipped classroom type of format, which wasn't great but from what it sounds like, he won't be doing this same format again. If you care about the topic, he will teach it to you.

Professor Olson is the most underrated professor in the department. He grants extensions without needing to check in with him, he holds a zoom meeting that anybody in the class can attend instead of coming in, and he keeps his students updated on current cyber news. But, assignments are lengthy and they are often quite returned late.

I think Olson is the most underrated professor in the CSEC department. He is knowledgeable and actually does a lot of red team stuff on the side. He is genuinely caring and is willing to answer any question. Gives free extensions if needed. He provides the option to go to lecture online. Only weird thing is that he makes everything due at 8pm.

Olson is great, lectures were fine. The whole class is Zoom optional. Assignments were way harder than what we learned in class but AI is allowed so 2 week assignments were easy. Only about 5 assignments for the whole course. The Midterm was online with 3 tries, similar to final. Not a single lab. Late form automatic yes for a week extension.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Amazing professor, and is genuinely awesome in general. One of the best CSEC professors at RIT, and is totally awesome in class. The weekly quizzes were hard and a bit unfair sometimes, but the labs are awesome and really taught me a lot and that's where the class is the best. Made sure we were doing things right and would help if we ever got stuck

Olson is overall great. Lectures were engaging. Attendance was not required, and lectures were always streamed on Zoom. Assignments were often confusing, but the next lecture would help. mid... literally like I don't think he actually grades his assignments. I submitted assignments half complete but because of "you get extra points for turning in early" I got over 100s. Is he scary bad? no. but if someone else is out there with a 4 or higher just take them.

worse professor for ever....don't wast your time with him....i am a math major, but i drop his class.

he is really crazy pro..i ever had....never organize his notes...every day quiz..but you never know where is the quiz come from. I am a "A" student for math..but this class make me really sick...Don't take with him.

Worst prof ever. I ended up withdrawing from the class. I went to my advisor and she said she cannot wait for him to retire because he gets some type of pleasure from failing the students. DO NOT TAKE!

You either love or hate his teaching. If you want an easy ride, don't take him. If you want a to learn a lot but not be handed any grades, take him. Very approachable- definitely one of my favorite professors at RIT

At first I hated this teacher but after awhile he is pretty good. Not the best ever but pretty good at explaining and willing to help, although he seems intimidating. Damn if you can get this guy DO IT. This "Does anyone know who's birthday it is today?"

Awesome professor, one of the best I've had so far at RIT.  He's very difficult, but an excellent teacher and even though you might not get the grade you want, the classes are enjoyable and you'll learn the material.

Really smart professor. Didnt get an A but would recommend him to anyone. He somewhat challenges you, weekly quiz and hw. Has an amazing ability to make up jokes on the spot and knows a ton of bdays(or at least claims to know). Really really entertaining

amazing teacher very smart and entertaining

not my kind of teacher, gives you problems to see if you can master, not to see if you understand, does not grade on a curve, helpful if you ask, knows what he is talking about, derives everything, tons of class grades, weekly quiz,hw once or twice a week

Awesome teacher

great at giving a window into the professional world, and providing feedback to further your development in that area

Old man who needs to retire. Luckily doesn't have the strict policies like other old professors.

actually dont bother showing up. I tried to show up at 8 am and it wasn't worth it my grades improved when I only read the textbook and the slides not showing up to class. I have her for calc B and I wish I had taken her for calc A.  She is the best professor I have had at RIT.  She explains things really good.  She is awesome.  Take her whenever you can you won't regret it.

Best Math teacher I ever had.  She is so willing to help
fair

Awful. Just awful. Stay away. She can't explain anything. But I don't think she even understands Calculus enough to be able to explain it. I had a friend in another profs class let me borrow his notes.

Quite honestly the worst teacher I've ever had. She treats those in her lower level classes horribly.  Had a family emergency. "You should have used half the time."

Timberlake is a great professor.  She really wants her students to do well.  She will help you with any question.  Go see her in her office.  You have to work but I learned more in her class than any other math class.  She knows her stuff
The best math professor at RIT.  Take her if you can

This class is the same as any other math class, if you sit with the right people who help you rather than distract you, ask questions, AND you do you homework, you'll be fine. She is a fairlenientreasonable grader, gives bonus points if most of the class doesn't get a problem right. If you don't pass this class it's your own fault...
Worst teacher hands down, seriously

She did not teach anything. She is the worst math teacher I have ever seen. I took her because it said she was easy on here. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU DONT UNDERSTAND MATH. DO NOT TAKE HER. PLEASE. FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY
She talks like she is the busiest person in the world!
Great professor. Very easygoing and helpful, always very kind and really wants to make sure students succeed. Always makes herself available for extra help.

She makes the material very easy to understand through her use of practicing problems in class. She drops the lowest test grade and makes practice tests for every test. We get homework every class on MyMathLab, but it only takes about 30 mins.The only thing that I'm not a fan of is the fact that the homework usually isn't posted until 11pm.

She consistently reminds you that "you don't know the material if you're in my class" and when she asks if someone has a question, she immediately states "We don't have time for that, we have to move on, come to my office hours". Loved her. She made the class easy and understandable. You have to go to the class otherwise you get behind. Homework nearly everyday, my class had MyMathLab which was frustrating at times. She drops the lowest quiz grade and replaces lowest test grade with your final exam grade. Loved the way she teaches.
The best professor I had at RIT.  Very helpful and you learn a lot
Great teacher.  If you go to class and do your hw. you will get a good grade.  Collected hw.
the best math teacher I ever had.  Sign up for her class if yo can get in.  they fill up quick.  She explains everything really well and will work with you until you get it.

One of the best math teachers I have ever had.  Take her if you can.  Her classes fill up quick.  she explains everything really well and is willing to help you with any questions.  Very patient and has a great teaching style.
Nice lady - seems to know enough to teach the class. Math will be math.

I honestly don't like her. She's one of those teachers who teaches out of the book, and not by knowledge. I feel she knows her stuff but doesn't know how to teach. Nicest professor I have!  Really helpful, wants to make sure you know your stuff, and wants you to succeed.  I had her for Calc for management science, but I already took calc in high school so the class was extra easy for me.  But even if you've never taken calc, you shouldn't have a problem as long as you listen to her and follow her examples.
The best Calculus teacher I had this year.  I wish I had her for my other calc classes.  She explains everything really well and will help with any question.  Take her if you can.
Nicest professor ever. She is the best, by far my favorite professor so far. Any thing you are unsure of she will go over until you understand. Take a class with her you wont regret it!
Clear, friendly, and fair.  Afraid to push the class to a high school or college math level. Often insultingly easy. But I blame the math department more than Timberlake.

She is the nicest teacher that I have ever had. Very helpful and wants to make sure everyone understands what is going on. Drops the lowest quiz and test grade. If you fail her class you seriously must have been trying to do it on purpose. Highly recommended!
She is legit one of the nicest people ever and a great teacher. If you can not get a passing grade in this class you're probably lazy and don't do anything
Great teacher, very clear friendly and willing to work with students.

She was a fantastic teacher.  Very approachable and always trying to help. One of the best math teachers i have ever had. Her tests are not the easiest but she drops your lowest grade. She wants you to do well in her class

Her students' success is important to her. She always makes sure the class knows what's going on, which is helpful if you're a little lost. Tests are fair and often a bonus question is provided that can boost your grade. As good as a calculus class gets.
GREAT TEACHER. GIVES A LOT OF HW, THOUGH.
She is a great professor.  Always ready to help.  I have her next quarter too.  Do your hw and you'll get good grades on the tests
The best calc teacher I've had.  Failed it before with another teacher.  Timberlake made it so easy to understand.  I wish I had her first.  Take her if you can
Easy teacher, but you need to pay attention. The class is basically impossible to fail because she drops your lowest test and replaces it with your final.
She is the best.  Very helpful and clear.  Great notes all of which are posted online. I wish I had her for discrete 1.  Take a course with her, you won't regret it.
Good professor who gets her point across without going too far out of her way. Compared to the other professor I had last quarter, she is an amazing professor for discrete math.
I love this teacher. She is sweet and very willing to help students. Her class had an easy pace and I found it very easy to follow topics.

A relatively simple teacher, but she teaches what she likes, not what is really useful to computing. She does make the material pretty easy, but will take a while to deliver your grade to you. Lastly, she barely uses MyCourses so be prepared to take a lot of notes.
A great calculus teacher.  Take her if you can.  Fair grader and always willing to help

Great teacher and very sweet woman.  She is very clear in her teaching style and is extremely willing to help after class.  She treats you a little like you're in elementary school, but she's great if you don't know the material.  Otherwise class can kind of drag.

Took for her Discrete2 for tech. Very sweet lady who really cares about what you're learning. I would take her again in a heartbeat if needed. She thoroughly explains material and is nice with grading. Attendance not mandatory, but it can boost your grade if you're borderline.
She was the best calc teacher I've had here at RIT.  I wish I had her in my earlier clasees.  Very helpful and nice

The best.  I wish I had her for discrete 1.

This was my first math class at RIT.  She was such a great teacher.  Lots of patience and really made sure you understood the material. I'm taking her next quarter as well.
She is one of the best calculus teachers I have ever had.  I hope I can take her for calc 2. She takes the time to really answer your questions.

I got put in her class by accident because of a goof-up in the offices after I got a 4 on the AP exam....I know all the material and work faster than everyone else in the class by proxy; she's great if you have no or little experience in the subject but if you're coming off an AP, and you already know the material, you're in for 10 weeks of boredom
The best math teacher i've ever had.  makes it so you can really understand it.
Awesome.  She is so nice and helpful.  Do your hw and come to class and you'll do great.  I have really learned a lot so far this quarter.
Great class.  Hard topics made easy.  Took discrete 1 and 2 with Timberlake.  She is very helpful in and out of class and very easy to talk to.  I recommend her
She is a great teacher.  This is my first quarter here and she is great.

I took 4 calc classes with Timberlake; she was amazing. I'd made attempts at some of the classes with other teachers and failed. She will hold your hand if you need it, and gives partial credit on tests, etc. Highly recommended.
I thought she was a wonderful teacher. I really hate math but I thought she did an awesome job. I would really like to take her again
I just finished the course.  I learned so much.  I actually took this course before and failed.  I wish I had taken Prof. Timberlake first.  Awesome teacher.

Extremely nice, and very helpful. Gives fair tests and quizzes. Had her Q1 for calc foundations i, and could really tell that she cared about how well people did in the class.

A great teacher.  We are going over review that we should know. Since there are prerequisites for the course, but she still wants to make sure that we know the material.  Very helpful, just go see her and she'll help you with any topic.  I've only had her for a few weeks but I think she's great.

Very nice lady-- picks and chooses which HW assignments to collect so make sure you do them. Also takes attendance randomly so it's important to show up. The tests and quizzes weren't too bad- she really wants to see her students do well. The workshops make for an easy grade too-- sometimes a bit tricky but manageable.
A great professor. Explains things real clear.  Always helps with your questions.  Take her if you can.
This is the second course that I've taken with professor Timberlake.  She is great. You can understand the material and her tests are not hard.  Do the hw and you'll get bonus points.
One of the best math teachers I have ever had.  Very helpful and encouraged questions.  I am taking her again next quarter.

I personally felt like i was in a kindergarten class the whole time. She speaks down to the students and if you ask a question in class, for the rest of the class she will single you out to ask if you understood what she just said. Very condescending.

She is a truly amazing teacher - a rare breed of person - always willing to help. I would highly recommend her over any of the other math teachers especially if you've come through one of Longs classes a little shaken up
great teacher.  Explained everything really good.  Answered all questions.  Take her

She is more than willing to help, anyone that has suffered through Dr. Long is grateful to have her, I guarantee it. Very kind, comes off as a person instead of a robotic teacher. I personally adore her.

She is like a high school teacher. Very nice and helpful.. and clear.

She is not bad as she is cracked up to be. Very nice, sweet. She does a -decent- job of teaching the material but learning via homework is sometimes necessary. Eh, not bad. Nice teacher. Very easy with grading and tests. But dont rely on her teaching skills. Make sure to do homework so you know whats going on for sure.
very  helpful
great teacher. very helpful and supernice! If you struggle in math she is really good at explaining stuff.

Best writing teacher on campus, really wants to help you learn. His class is relatively easy as long as your fine with writing semi long papers (3-5 pages) depending on the class. Is not all that he is cracked up to be. He is extremely unclear about what he wants and has a poor choice in books to discuss.

Great professor. Very chill and flexible guy. His class is not very hard. Participation is required. He is a fair grader. Absolutely the best writing professor at RIT. Sarnowski is extraordinarily chill and friendly. Grading is fair, and you get the vibe that he really wants to help you improve your writing. Do whatever you can do to get his classes, you won't regret it.

I had Sarnowski for Writing Seminar this past quarter. I have one way to sum it up: DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO GET INTO HIS CLASS. You will NOT regret it. He puts in the effort of being a great teacher. He tries to get you to think really deeply. He cares about students and makes himself available and helpful.

The effort he puts into his teaching really shows. Mad Men on the recommended materials list? Check. Philosophically interesting class discussions? Double-check. Best writing seminar professor there is!He gives 1 essay per week(2 pages)and little reading. Taking class with him really improved my writing skills. Gotta work to get the A though.

comment: He doesn't know much, but he sure knows Ohm. Dave is very smart, emphasis on very. The downside to this is that the jumps he makes when teaching aren't the easiest to follow. He's great at his office hours though, so if you want to pass, go to every single one and work through the homework. the work is difficult to understand, but not hard to do.

May get a little off topic during lectures. He is very smart and LOVES to help people when they come to his office hours. Go to them as often as you can and you're guaranteed to pass the class (regardless of the quality of your test grades).

Had him for Digital Signal Processing. Wish he'd have spent a little less time lecturing so that we'd have had more time to work on labs, but he's an awesome professor nonetheless. He teaches senior-level courses, so it's going to be difficult, but he'll help you as much as you need him to. He knows his stuff, and he's pretty relaxed about grades.
He is an amazing professor, I did not have a class with him but he was kind to give a hand.

Just do the work.  He will always help in anyway he can.  Lectures are great if you're interested, if not just read up later.  He will customize every lesson to what he thinks is most important.  Handing in stuff late is a ok.  Very laid back professor.  You would be lucky to have him.
He doesn't know much, but at least he knows Ohm. Seriously though, he is tough but always willing to help.

The Professor is tough. He teaches at an accelerated pace, and if you do not speak up you will be left behind. He shows outstanding dedication to his students and is willing to help all the time, often staying in School late.
The Best Professor I have ever taken. Is willing to sit one on one to explain a question no matter what time it is. The tests are easy similiar to HW. So HW is a must.

Dr. Orlicki is a genus, but has trouble getting info across to students. His labs are difficult and extra help is necessary. Not a good professor for novices. He is very lenient, and will allow you to retake missed exams. He is far more helpful with one on one.

Brilliant professional, just not a very good teacher for basic principle classes. Very willing to help with any issues, but usually does not have time unless you get to office hours early. Labs are extremely work intensive. Only take this guy if you already have a basic understanding of subject.

Enthusiastic and very knowledgeable about the subjects covered.  Can sometimes be confusing but is very happy to clarify any topics and questions.  My advice to people who find him difficult is to ask for clarification and continue to do so until you truly understand.  Overall I loved the guy, he was interesting with some fun jokes and stories.
He is a very cool and fun guy but he can't deliver the info clearly. One on one might work fine or his office hours. If you know the material go ahead and take the class otherwise you will struggle.

He is definitely a genius, but not a good teacher. He rambles on about the subject and goes too far ahead and the class gets very confused. He gives labs every week, in which you almost always need his help with, but his office is packed during office hour with kids who need help. He wants to help and will try to help but he is terrible atexplaning

A smart guy but if you do not understand what is going on in class then you will struggle. Seek him during "office hours" He will give sufficient time in order to help you understand and get through the class. Overall a good professor.
not great at teaching definitely a genius but he is not a teacher.

He's a nice guy, although his lectures are quite boring. He often didn't give enough time for exams as well. Homework was assigned straight from the text, which I basically learned everything from instead of him.

He really is a good guy interested in helping his students. Not very captivating in lecture classes but very reasonable and helpful in the lab. Even if you can't stay awake in his class, make sure you do your homework and stay behind for help in the lab. At a computer, he really gives his all to the student.

He is a good guy, overall sound. But when it comes to teaching and conveying a message he is not efficient. Talks about things not related to solve HWs and Test qs in class. 80% people are sleeping. Rather choose another professor.

This guy seems like a nice old man, but he is a HORRIBLE teacher.  He spends days on end storytelling or discussing one of the simplest concepts at the expense of several more complicated ones.  When it comes to tests just forget it.  He tests on probems out of the book - none of the material is covered in class!  Do yourself a favor and stay away!

Good professor, had a lot of stimulating conversations with him and hes an absolute wealth of information. Helped me pick up some essay topics and where to start, class is sorta boring... But that's to be expected, but this guy made it much much better, you can tell he actually enjoys helping you, and he wants you to become a better writer.
Good professor. We had to write 3 essays, the last one ended up being our final, so we didn't even have an actual final. I thought he graded very fairly.
Good teacher.  My class is real easy, it's just writing about the upcoming presidential debate.  But conservative comments/viewpoints make him a little shifty.  Cool guy though.
huff is the man, laid back, listens to your ideas, good teacher

If you don't write what he doesn't enjoy reading (mystery/crime) then you won't get a good grade. Wants everybody to add a thrill into their story (not alwas possible depending on what your form) and never understands where you are going with an idea, no matter how many times you explain it. He annoyed me all quarter.
Very laid back and makes the class interesting. Lets you go anywhere with your writing and the format of the class is also comfortable for people who are not used to sharing their work.
He is very clear and his homework is very easy, very solid class

Ke is a very nice person but a very bad lecture giver. His homeworks are very in depth and take a lot of time. Quizzes are very difficult. He posts solutions ahead of time which makes getting good grades easy, but learning difficult. There is only one exam which is a final with 40% of grade yikes.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Homework and labs are killers, they will take hours to finish and are graded very harshly. If you think you wrote enough, write another paragraph. learned a ton though, and lectures were pretty enjoyable. If you miss any though you'll be way behind.
Literally amazing.

Fantastic professor. Fair grader. Average workload. He really cares that his students understand the material, and will go out of his way to ensure they do. Lectures are generally interesting and he's very knowledgeable about the subject matter. If he doesn't know something, he'll find out.

One of the smartest individuals I have ever met. His passion for MPS and imaging science shines through whenever he speaks. His lectures fly by and although his assignments are time-consuming I have never felt it to be a waste of time. Interesting and informative. Everyone should take his class!

David Long is the probably the best professor you'll ever learn from. He packs an incredible amount of information in in a way that's easy to understand. David will give you the basics (and then some) of about 80-90% of the classes you'll be taking in the future (if you're Motion Picture Science or Imaging Science), so work hard! It'll be worth it.

David is actually a genius.  SOFA103 is a class that needs a good instructor and David is just that. His knowledge translates to his teaching as his lectures are incredibly informative yet still very interesting. He's very approachable as well! He is a very tough grader and makes you work for grades, but he wants you to succeed!

David is the best professor I have had at SOFA. He is extremely intelligent which makes his lectures interesting and it means he adds extra information from his time at Kodak as well as endless trivia material about film, digital and the film world. Highly recommend for people interested in material, certainly not an easy A.

David is extremely intelligent and really funny. His lectures are genuinely interesting and very informational- he just needs to slow down a bit. At times he goes too fast through certain sections and it would be easier to keep up and understand if he would slow down and make sure everyone is on the same page.

This man is one of the smartest and most respectful people I know. If you don't get something, David helps you and makes sure you do get it. And on top of that, he's actually really hilarious and has had such an interesting life(he's won an Oscar!). The class is really difficult, and David's a tough grader, but he knows its hard and helps you a ton

He's literally a genius. He really knows his stuff, and he makes sure you know it too. If anybody else taught it, nobody would pass. This course is based on how good of a professor can teach it, and he really teaches it. Be prepared to work your ass off though; it's tough material, but if you work hard he'll know it.
great professor
He's a great professor and makes you learn a lot! It's  tough material to grasp, but he makes it interesting. Take this professor if you can.

Course material can be difficult but he realizes this. Get your homework and labs in on time, study for the quizzes and final and you'll do fine. Very approachable if you don't understand something. Don't copy the powerpoint notes but rather write what he lectures orally and what he writes on the board - very important! You can use notes on quizzes

all the upperclassmen talked about of horrible fundamentals of computers and imaging was, so I was worried at first. However, the class is very interesting and David Long is very knowledgeable and really knows how to teach the material.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. His class is very easy just because he knows how to teach complicated information in ways oblivious students can understand. He knows his stuff very well, and is full of random interesting facts. Don't be afraid of taking FCI 8-12 +2-4, its early but he understands this, so its not that bad.

Professor Parker is a teacher who wants you to do well and develop writing skills that benefit you in the long run. The extensive effort she has put into her planned assignments is outstanding, but sometimes the main point of a lecture can get a little lost with long stories. Besides that she is a very caring teacher.

Don't hesitate to take this teacher. She is the absolute best! Professor Parker made me enjoy writing when I didn't enjoy it before. Class is fun and laid back and you get a lot of opportunity to work on any assignments she is assigning. She cares about students thoughts and doesn't grade too hard. She is always accommodating.

Professor Parker is by far the best teacher I have ever had. She truly cares about her students and their success. She teaches a lot of valuable lessons and honestly just keeps class really fun and engaging. Professor Parker is always accessible outside of class and answers emails pretty quickly. Take this class with her over anyone else!

Professor Parker is a great professor who runs a fun and easy class. All of her assignments have meaning and never felt like busy work. She is an easy grader as long as you follow her rubric. I can't recommend her enough, she relit my love for writing.
