comment: I like Spadaforda as a person but he wasn't a good professor. He changed his teaching meathods from the semester before (which was really easy) and way over compensated. This class was like a graduate class, 70 page readings, mandatory attendance, 4 group projects and pop quizes (which he did away with).
Italian accent from attractive professor ... easy to pay attention to lol. Extremely happy to help and answer questions; passionate about what hes teaching.
He is a very good looking smart professor, love his classes and his energy. Welcomes comments and questions, straight forward.

I had him for Global Business Environment. Lots of HW reading assignments. The only exam is the final (which was a take-home essay.) You will also have 4 group projects. He gets super enthusiastic but the class is all over the place sometimes and I found it hard to follow what exactly I should be taking away from this class.
Great prof, no hmwk and tests are all group projects. Very knowledgeable, enthusiastic and fun!
Prof Spadafora takes the time to explain things well. Has an Italian accent but isnt hard to understand. PowerPoint is primary course material and is made available for students. Great class!
Awesome professor. Cares about students.
One of the best in this department!

Dr. McGowan is a great professor. The course load is a bit heavy (lab) but doable. Provides feedback and is happy to help both inside and outside of class. The class is very formulaic, so you know what to expect next. As long as you keep on top of due dates, you will do just fine

It's not that difficult of a class, it's just time-consuming because that's how lab courses go. All things considered, McGowan is a great professor. Lenient with grading, very helpful in person and over Discord, and provides good feedback on lab notebooks. Doing the labs themselves is a bit tricky, but not bad when you have a partner.

In the first class, Dr.McGowan created a Discord and told us to communicate through that for any questions. I had a few things happen while taking his class, and he was flexible with deadlines and in-person attendance. I would be on call with someone at my table. The lectures were videos. In-class work was labs, daily check-ins, and problem sets.

Only good things to say about this guy. He was available at almost all times and extremely helpful, was always very clear with grading requirements, and is lenient when a student is struggling. Dr. McGowan raises the standard of a good professor.  Highly recommend taking his classes, it might be tough but he'll always be there to help you.
Had him for ad lab, McGowan is the absolute best, grades labs fairly and is super useful during class time! Answers Slack messages ungodly fast. Wish I had more classes left to take with him :(

McGowan is very good teacher. Physics is hard to make lively, and he does his best to keep the class awake. He has very clear expectations for the test and gives similar practice tests. I would recommend him as professor.

UP 2 is inherently a difficult class, so no professor is going to make it perfect. Dr. McGowan makes physics as enjoyable as possible though. He does require everyone to put a lot of time into the class, more than any other in my experience. But it's all worth it since all his assignments are good practice to go along with his great lectures.

McGowan was a great professor for UPII. If you do all of the assignments and go to the LA sessions, it's impossible to fail. He always worked in a lot of dry humor into the lectures and the class was generally enjoyable.  Also, study past exams! They are nearly the same as the new ones (at least when I took it!)

Dr. McGowan is a tough grader, but so is the entire physics department.  He's fair though.  He's very good at explaining things.  I enjoyed the nerdy references he makes a couple times each class.  Also, he collects pages out of the manual each week (assigned as "practice") so there's a little more homework than just MP. Clickers are necessary.

Even though the class was hard, Dr. McGowan made it more understandable.  The LA sessions are super helpful in my opinion. He is a guy who is willing to help you do good in his class if you put effort in it.

McGowan is easily one of the most underated physics 2 professors. For one, he's always available if you need help, and organizes several TA sessions a week. It's a hard class no matter who you take it with, but I thought he eased the pain a bit. Also, I love the super dry humor, even if others don't seem to understandappreciate it!
Lectures are dry but he is very good at teaching concepts and reinforcing them.  Is very nice and helpful if you have questions.  Tests were difficult and confusing.

Dr. McGowan is a bit of a nerd and will frequently reference sci-fi movies. As a teacher he's pretty good, but he's only been teaching for a few year and teaches a lot out of the activities manual. He does iClicker questions everyday as a form of attendance and you have to go to him if you want help. Overall a good teacher and would take again.

All in all, he wasn't a bad professor, better than many of the ones in the RIT physics department. I say he used a textbook because he teaches almost directly out of the activities manual (which is not necessarily a bad thing). Decent professor.

Lectures are clear. No quizzes. Homework weekly and it's a group thing. Very nice guy and helpful in class and office hour. Make sure to do the problems in the lab manual! Most of the short answer problems on the exams are similar if not exactly the same. Oh and he often has jokes that most people may or may not get.
TAKE HIM, the others are referring to aron Mcgowan (with one a)thats his cousin. This is the legit Mcgowan and he's amazing!

He is a nice professor and is extremely helpful in office hours. His lectures can be pretty monotonous, but he throws in some corny jokes once in a while. He has several conceptual iClicker questions every class that serve as attendance and participation. Good professor, but difficult class.
Available during office hours. Very manageable if you keep up with the work.

He is a very smart guy, a bit corny at times, and he does a fairly decent job of introducing new topics. sadly, he does boring and drawn out reinforcement of topic and he seems to have a minor understanding that his coursework isn't the only work students have to deal with. he give frequent and significant work, even if there is a test

Professor McGowan is a very smart guy and a good teacher overall so long as you pay attention in class and keep up with his work. Definitely don't go in expecting an easy grade. If your expectations are a little more level and you're looking to actually learn however, I would highly recommend him.

Very friendly professor. He is absolutely passionate about what he does but is very difficult. If you want to really learn the material in depth and be challenged, I highly recommend him. If getting an easy A or B is what you want then I do not. Never get behind in his class, do the homework, and red the book and you will do well.

This guy knows his stuff. He is a brilliant guy who will push you hard. Physics is his life. As long as you think in precise math terms too, you will understand him, otherwise get your internal math to english translator going or open your textbook. If you are prone to sleeping, you will because of his monotone. Hard class, brilliant guy.

He tends to get the material across in lecture but he has a very dull speaking voice and puts little to no emphasis in presentation. Usually available for help after class hours, but you might be better off getting study help from Bates. You almost never get work out of the textbook and do nearly everything in the 'recommended' workbook.
He is a new teacher but he is very helpful and the tests relates to what he teaches and assigns for mastering physics.  highly recommended

only gave one midterm for this class. unless you ask you know how you're doing in the class twice: when you get the midterm back and after the semester ends on SIS.
never uses MyCourses, so you cannot see how a homework/quiz affected your grade thru-out semester.
includes Qs on exams that were never talked about

had him once before, wouldn't rec

Very, very funny professor, and super informative too. He explained everything clearly and often gave us opportunities to get extra credit. Tests were a bit hard but we could make cheat sheets for each one, so it wasn't too bad. Homework isn't bad either, only a couple questions every week or so. Overall great professor and great guy

Professor Richmond is a fantastic teacher. He incorporates humor into his lectures, and uses demonstrations to keep class interesting. While his sense of humor was certainly sharp enough to deflate a few egos in my class, I felt overall that it was all in good fun.

Professor Richmond took a very confusing topic, special relativity, and made it fairly easy to understand and incredibly engaging. His lectures were thoroughly enjoyable and engaging. The class had very little homework. He was very helpful outside of class and clearly wanted students to succeed. Tests are a bit confusing but very doable.

Richmond is charismatic guy who gives entertaining lectures that are both funny and informative. I have no problem with how he teaches the class, it's about the work. The homework is heavily based on what we cover in the notes that week during class, which is pretty normal. However, the tests then do not reflect the homework in any shape or form.

Turned physics from one of my worst subjects, historically, into something I wanted to learn. Very funny, sarcastic, mean in a caring kind of way. Challenges your thinking to make sure you know you are correct. He gets tired and wants to leave just as much as you do. Would take him 100% again. Threatened to turn me into an Atwood machine 10/10.

Richmond definitely fits the classic description of the kooky professor, so Special Rel with him was a fun class which went by way too fast. That being said, he teaches the same material from his website every year and you could easily not attend a single lecture and ace the (2) tests.

Prof. Richmond is a saint. He is the nicest professor I have and he is hilarious. I don't know if all of his classes are like Special Relativity, but that class is very hard for some and not bad for others

10/10 Richmond is the best professor I have ever had. His examples in class are clear and entertaining. He knows how to keep your interest in a lecture. Very funny guy (he will please fun at you, don't get upset, he does it to everyone). His jokes are to keep you interested, not to hurt you. Will call you out at random so know your stuff.

Respects his students. ASK QUESTIONS! He's more than happy to explain concepts and why things are. Funny. Make sure you study ahead so that you don't have to jam last minute studying in. It much easier that way. Since there aren't many tests, is crucial that you score well on them.
His class is funny. You have to put effort in to understand it though.

Dr. Richmond is by far the best teacher I have EVER had. He makes every lesson interesting whether it be through hilarious examples or fantastic teaching and makes me feel like there is no doubt that I chose the correct major. Not only is he a fantastic professor, but he is also always there for you if you need help with the content!

Smart, sarcastic guy; has the capacity to be pretty mean. If you're easily butthurt or don't like working hard, don't take his class. However, if you wanna learn, he does crazy stuff with his written and in-class examples, explains material comprehensively to make sure you understand, and gives plenty of opportunities to make up for bad grades.

I only had him for half the quarter and he was wonderful. He is an awesome teacher that just gets your attention and he is super clear.  His test aren't the easiest, but I actually learned  in his class and he kept me awake!
Funny
Very good at teaching the material, but tests and HWs are extremely difficult.

The best professor I've ever had. Clear, focused, interesting lectures. Really likes what he does and it shows. Respects students but you'll lose that by sleeping in class / not showing up / interrupting class. Take if you can.
Excellent professor, very clear, and helpful.  His tests and homework can be extremely difficult but if you take the time and go over his notes you shouldn't have a problem.  Take him if you can!

Had him for special relativity and UP Ia he is an excellent teacher and is very knowledgeable when it comes to physics and how to teach it. He is funny, his classes aren't easy A's. and he dislikes stupidity.

Had him for Special Relativity, University I and Modern Lab I. He is the MAN. He will call you out at random, so you better know your material if you don't want to feel terrible. Even if you know, he'll still crush you. Explains things simply and interestingly, yet you still get a thorough (and sometimes advanced beyond other classes) understanding

I had heard Richmond was the best Physics professor at RIT and when I saw he wasn't teaching University I this quarter, I was really bummed. Boy was I surprised when he walked into class on day one when I had registered for a different teacher. His class was awesome! That said, the tests are very hard and it can be a struggle sometimes.

Definitely the best physics prof at RIT. kind of hard but extremely interesting. i looked forward to every class and they went quickly. loves planets, rockets, and examples with death in them. very helpful. hw is interesting and not too long. tests are hard but it balances out in the end. easy quizzes are 2% bonus on your final grade.

Awesome professor, makes great jokes during class. His lectures are very interesting. I enjoyed every single one and looked forward to them. They were thought-provoking. There are occasional pop-quizzes to make sure you're glancing ahead to preview the next class, which honestly helped. Two tests, midterm and final. Willing to help clarify points.

Not a bad professor teaching-wise, but very mean/arrogant. Loves to put students on the spot and make them look stupid. Example: asks a student to provide an equation; while they look through their notes he immediately writes the equation on the board, so everyone laughs at you. Very hard to concentrate when being laughed it.

Dr. Richmond is awesome, nothing more needs to be said about him. He teaches in a way that makes you want to learn the material (otherwise he'll embarrass you), and even if you know the material he makes fun of you. This keeps the material interesting... and truly keeps you engaged in class. Plus he's a good looki' individual.

Very interesting lectures, he always held my interest and I learned a lot.  Extremely strict grader tough and not very fair. I switched in late and was not allowed to make up work, thus dropping a letter grade.
just barely went over material in class, homework nearly impossible. Labs helped me learn the material, very effective. Tests impossible. Final absolutely impossible.

After having Dr Richmond for Physics 1, I purposely rearranged my schedule so that I could have him for Physics 2 and waited a semester to see if he would be teaching Physics 3. Class was interesting, especially since I got to participate in almost every demo (Jackie Chan, Mr. Bicep) - a great prof
nice Professor, very helpful, his class is not that easy but he let you learn a lot of stuff.
Awesome guy, really tries to convince you the concepts.  His homework is tough, but if you sit down and take the time to do it, it's no problem.

The guy belongs in an elementary school.  The way he teaches/talks is the most annoying thing I've ever seen.  His tests aren't overly hard, but you have to read his mind. No partial credit.  If you are deaf or have another disability expect to be offended at least 1x.  Look out for his temper.

He is nerdy all right. He seems to have a good grasp on Physics but he makes exams too hard. He doesn't give partial credit on HW's as its done online and he doesn't grade them.Quite animated while giving lectures.
Great professor and person. Course was relatively easy overall but the homework was challenging. Learned a lot.

Dr. Dholabhai cares a lot about how he presents material in a course, and it showed during his lectures. Lectures were great, but covered an exceptional amount of material. Homeworks were hard, but doable. Exams were a breeze. He's a super personable professor, and I'm happy to have taken the class with him, even though it started at 5 pm

Professor Aponte clearly cares a lot about his students, but this class just wasn't for me. A lot of the lectures felt same-y, and there overall isn't really anything I took out of this class. Assignments are also not graded until the very end of the course

Didn't grade anything until the day grades were due and gave everyone 100s. Lot of lecture, three main projects and a presentation. All projects can be done with a group, not too hard just time consuming. Professor Aponte was really easy to contact outside of class but I probably wouldn't take any of his classes again

He didn't grade anything for the whole semester until the last day of classes or give any feedback for it, he just have us all 100s. The work wasn't difficult, just time consuming. We had 3 group projects throughout the semester and we could choose to write a paper, do a presentation, record a podcast, etc. He was very easy-going and was often late

Very nice professor. However, only had one grade in for the semester until last min, but he gave full credit for everything so no complaints. Most times class was talking in a circle for 1h 15m. Learned a little, but easy A. Did take a long time to respond to emails and assignments did not have super clear instructions, but you could figure it out.

-There is 6 days left of the semester and nothing has been graded, including assignments done during September.
-Showed up late almost every class, sometimes 15-20 minutes late.
-Instructions for assignments were extremely clear. When questions were asked about instructions he would say that he will get back us on it but never did.

I had Dr. Aponte his first year at RIT. There were plenty of bumps in the road, but he changed his syllabus each time so the students wouldn't suffer. There are a lot of lectures, but they are very interesting and reflect current events. Your grade is based on 3 2 page papers and a final project, but they are all easy A's. Absolute legend.

Friendly guy who lectures for most of class with a couple videos and participation questions(not graded). Reading in the class is based off articles and aren't mandatory. Only grades for the classes are 3 essays and some activities in class. Easy class to take for a gen ed requirement.

Tries to make the class as interesting. Easy grader, if you do what she wants. Only two tests a semester. Gives VERY EASY reading quizzes to take attendance. The only thing I didn't like were the labs because normally the assigned group were full of idiots who don't do much or don't do it right. Easy to approach & ask questions. Very knowledgeable.

She is horrible. She accused me of cheating which i didnt. She also gives labs and most of the time your group is full of idiots. She also doesnt explain the labs at all and the sheets she give dont make sense to anyone but her. She treats you like an idiot when you ask a question. She is horrible

Lectures are dull, but don't worry -- reading the book is more important to do well on the tests.  Jackie always tries to be fair, and is easy to talk to.  By the end of the class, you'll be surprised how much information you've picked up without really trying all that hard.  This is a mark of a good teacher... or an easy major.
Great teacher, very approachable. Grades fairly and understands problems
Not too bad of a teacher, sometimes gave out lots of work.  Not too hard.
Can be tough, but is also informative sometimes. an okay teacher nothing special
This course is about research foundation and not hard. Also, it includes a lot of examples to explain research stuff and several tasks to do (not difficult).
Professor was unrespected and very tough in graders.
just avoid
Insightful in how to conduct research. Helpful course.
Useful course for PhD research. Great teacher, very different from other professors at RIT.

Great professor. Engaging and fun lessons. Really important to not miss class because he shows the signs in person and looking things up will not make up for what you've missed. A lot of vocabulary and not much homework.

Professor Haywood is an amazing professor! It can be intimidating at first, but overall it's a very beneficial great course! There will be many group projects/activities, and there is a final presentation at the end of the semester.
Fantastic. I don't normally like learning languages but Barry made it easy and fun. He's a great lecturer and a great guy.

Barry is a very understanding and helpful professor. He works with the pace of your class. I struggled a lot for a bit, but Barry really worked for me so I could get back on track. He enjoys talking and sharing some fun stories and learning about his students. He forgets to put up assignments on Mycourses he will give you extra time to complete it

Barry is a great professor and a great guy. Sometimes he struggles a bit with the MyCourses and posting assignments. If you email him about an assignment he will get back to you within a decent amount of time & he will fix any errors in his assignments. You will need to participate by answering questions and sometimes signing in front of the class.

Barry is a really sweet guy who cares about his students. He cracks jokes and creates a safe environment by making small talk. The grading seems weirdly specific but he doesn't explain the reasoning behind the grade, but I never really asked so maybe he would explain if you asked. Never feel bad to ask for clarification!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: One of those professors you can establish a good rapport with. He's fairly laid back, although sometimes his teaching style can be confusing. As long as you ask questions when you're lost you'll be fine.

Barry is very chill and absolutely hilarious. He is an awesome professor in class, but is hard to communicate with outside of class. If possible, try to go to his office hours if you're confused about something instead of emailing to ease communication barriers. also MAKE A CLASS GC. he also gives NO feedback which is hella frustrating.

Barry is nice and an awesome professor in class. His communication is confusing outside of class. The GoReact/MyCourses websites were poorly structured/organized, and I was always confused when trying to do the homework that he clearly explained in class. He gives NO feedback. Its frustrating to get an 80 on a test with no feedback explaining why.

I love Barry. I am an engineering major, so ASL is kind of my stress relief. Barry is a very relaxed professor, and he makes his class very enjoyable. He is very patient and makes for a positive learning environment.

While Dr. Bev was a sweet person, I genuinely saw YOPS as useless and a waste of time. She would make these activities and discussions that had nothing to do with the subject into mandatory participation activities during class, which was so boring. I played a lot of Clash Royale in her class

Dr Beverly has no idea what she is talking about. She has the unique ability to ramble on about very sensitive subjects, genuinely believe she is saying something important, and then have the comment come out as utterly offensive. As a teacher she is does not engage adequately with the activities or the students - I dreaded coming to her class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Textbook readings almost every class, and a reading quiz that day in the beginning of class. Lecture heavy- they aren't too interesting and they seem longer than they actually are. But its a fairly easy class. You're only allowed to miss two classes before you have a grade reduction. Doesn't post grades.
Great prof! Easy to understand, very kind and approachable. Good teaching style and very reasonable workload. If you just pay attention in class you'll do good. 10/10
Great prof!

Tuncer is a nice person but overall a bad professor.. Our midterm was a whole two chapters more than all the other classes.  She does not allow make-ups for quizzes missed, & one kid came into class 2 minutes late and she did'nt let him take the quiz and just gave him a zero. Do not take this professor or you will basically have to teach yourself.
She is a fine math teacher, sometimes it can be hard to understand what she is saying and she very often misunderstands peoples questions. But for Calc 1 she was overall good.
Great professor!

Very sweet women, took over for another instructor. However, sometimes overexplains some topics and underexplains others. If you have never taken calc, you might struggle as she kind of jumps right into things
Very nice, class was easy, but I also took calc 1 in high school. Just do the homework.

Not hard if you're not an idiot. Very easy weekly quizzes with questions from the homework, which have their answers posted. 3-4 questions per Monday quiz, and you can just retake it within a week for most credit back, which you can use your previous attempt while taking. Homework is usually 4 questions from a short 10-15min video very easy class.

Professor Tuncer's a great person but at least for me I couldn't understand anything she's teaching me.  If you're considering taking her class please note that she has a pretty thick slavic accent and it made my time in her class a lot more difficult than it should have. Also the class is tedious, 1 quiz every week, 3 homework quizzes, and 3 exams

i've never had a teacher who would give me migraines every day after trying to interpret what they're saying. if your english is weak, do not take her class. her accent makes it hard to comprehend anything.

Dr. Tuncer is super nice and lenient. I once wrote the right answer on a quiz, crossed it out, and wrote a wrong answer with a frowny face and she gave me full credit. She does a good job explaining theory and her tests and quizzes are very fair. The only thing is she's a little disorganized and doesn't really post materials. Still an easy class.

Nigar is very nice, however she is not a good teacher. She goes so fast and does not explain what she does. She gives worksheets for hw. Every Monday there's a quiz on it. She doesn't post the answer key, and does not go over the questions. Most of the time, they are on material not covered in class. Her explanations to questions don't make sense.

For the course being Calculus II, she makes the class manageable. She is super sweet, but it should be noted that she does almost nothing online, and teaches exclusively on the white board. That being said, everything she does is explained thoroughly. Everything she does is covered in textbook. Quiz and HW once a week, overall she is fantastic.

She took over the class halfway through the semester and did a good job. not a particularly tough grader, however the homework amount REALLY shot up when she took over (allegedly this wasn't her fault tho - just worth pointing out). Easy to access and did a good job explaining concepts, would recommend for calc 1
Overall great professor. She was very understanding and helpful when i needed it. I got to know her a little during office hours and she just overall is insightful. I would take her again!!

Took her a year ago so maybe things have changed, but I typically found myself teaching myself the concepts after class as she outlined theorems without much elaboration. Exams were graded inconsistently and there wasn't much communication on what to expect to see on them. She was very nice though and seemed to care about students.

Calc I as a Monday/Wednesday class (2hr each). Mondays were 1 hr lecture, then work on practice problems as a group. Wednesdays are a 1 hr lecture, and then a topic quiz. My Friday recitations were optional. Pretty easy grader. I already had calc knowledge before this class, but I think she breaks the topics down well for those new to calc.

. She gave good/ informative lectures. 
. She made herself quite available out of class for extra help. 
. She gave clear criteria for exams.
Great professor. Easy to talk to outside of class.highly recommended.

Tuncer herself is a good person. She is funny and respectable. However, her lectures were hard to follow. She was always trying to improve what she was doing, but it never seemed to fully work. I taught myself a lot of the topics we covered in class. She seemed to teach like we already knew the topic when we did not.

I have very mixed feelings on Professor Tuncer, but I wouldnt say that's a bad thing. Make sure to interact with her and ask questions- she's a very friendly person who's a much more effective lecturer when students are engaged. Do ask for extra help- she's a terrible lecturer but great 1 on 1. Bad if you don't get to know her, great if you do.

Weekly quizzes, daily homework, confusing lectures with no sense of direction and full of mistakes.  Professor Tuncer is friendly and smart, but cannot teach a class well and has very confusing grading criteria.  The entire class, including the TA, was unaware of an exam the day after Thanksgiving break.  Would not take this professor again.
Professor is extremely confusing, doesn't give enough info for exams.

Tuncer is very great with workshops. Most of the time, workshops take over at least 30 minutes of the class. However, the lectures are very heavy and she goes through them very fast. It's best to email her and have her send the lecture notes, if applicable. Otherwise, I would refer to The Organic Chemistry Tutor on YouTube.

During workshops she really tries to help you understand for the lecture, quizzes are weekly and are based on the textbook and workshops. Exams might be difficult but if you go to office hours with her she can be really helpful for understanding the material.

Overall good professor for calculus. There are weekly quizzes but the questions are taken directly from the homework so as long as you complete the homework, youll already have seen the quiz essentially.

Mary teaches her class through PowerPoint lectures that are all posted to MyCourses, which becomes very useful when studying for her tests. Although the amount of material can be overwhelming, as long as you skim through the book and take notes or use the PowerPoint notes when studying for the exams, it's a pretty good class. Not SUPER hard.

Lectures are boring. Fell Asleep a few times. Attendance is taken sometimes. Stay awake for the powerpoints. Powerpoints given in mycourses. Read the textbook a couple times more than just once and a study guide she gives for the tests and you will pass.
Nice professor. Loves it when you email and see's her in her office for class related questions and help. Gives out extra credit and funny.

I went to every class, but I don't really think you have to since the study guide tells you exactly what you should study from the textbook. Love her lectures, even if it occasionally feels repetitious and long.

Took her in the fall, taking next sequence with her as well. She is amazing, my favorite professor. I showed up to class only like 1xweek and while I dont know what my participation grade was,  it couldn't have been too bad bc I still made a great grade overall. Puts PPs all online & gives specific, detail study guides for all tests in advance

Long, dull, boring. The material is interesting, but I honestly felt like she was talking AT me the whole time in this monotone voice. Classes felt unbearably long because we just sat there listening to her go through slide after slide. She definitely knows her stuff, but I wish she had engaged more with the students. Study guide was worthless.

Fantastic teacher, going to great pains to get her again next year. Her powerpoints and lectures give you exactly what you need to know for the exams (there are 3 of them, each 20% of your grade and then a final paper that's 25%). As long as you take notes in class, you'll be fine.

Mary is great; her classes are never boring because she loves what she teaches and incorporates cool material from the media.  Always willing to answer our questions and doubts. I've chosen her 3 times for part I, II, and III because I have enjoyed her class and her teaching methodology. She also blushes and laughs at things, it's funny!

You really need to fact check Bob. I have learned that some of the things he's told us are incorrect. For example, he claimed a thermal camera worked "by sensing heat" and not by IR. But "IR" is in the camera's name! He sounds very convincing, but if you fact check him, Ive found he's wrong so many times.

I like Bob but he is very monotone which makes him hard to read. The first few assignments are graded quickly but the rest aren't put in after a while. He is a tough grader, very specific about what he wants and if it isn't right you get multiple points off. The assignments are laid out well, he doesn't always give you the information you need tho

Professor Rose is a tough grader, and posts the feedbacks for several first assignments later in two-third way into the semester so there was no room/space to improve. There are no clarity on objectives in the assignments,  Professor Rose would ask us to look around if there was something we are struggling with. Test is easy and average light.
Great guy!

One of the most difficult professors in the entire department. Takes off huge number of points for trivial reasons. Grades things very late, sometimes days before the next milestone is due, so you can't learn from your "mistakes". Doesn't realize this is a college class and not a full time job in the industry. Good luck getting an A with him

Genuinely one of my favorite teachers at RIT. Her lectures are incredible and entertaining enough to keep you engaged. Exams can be difficult, but they're fair and she tells you what you need to focus on beforehand.
Dr. Michel is passionate about biochemistry and cares for her students. She makes it very clear what is expected of you. Her class is fairly easy.

Really love this professor, she's very animated and gives great lectures. She explains things very clearly and simply so anyone can understand. She draws things on paper and projects them which I like because then the lesson goes step by step instead of just reading through slides. Very helpful outside of class as well.

An extremely easy teacher, with very easy tests. She made chem 1 seem like the easiest subject to exist. Her notes weren't descriptive but she would go through it with us and explained well. High school chemistry knowledge really came in clutch. The lowest exam gets dropped and the final was online and group work. Very easy.
She is the best, easy A class, and made chemistry fun! She does dumb things down but chemistry seems daunting then she is the best professor to take

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Dr. Michel is an amazing professor. I absolutely loved her class! Her exams were written based on her notes from classes, if you attended lectures and took good notes her exams were an easy A. I learned so much from her and she was such a fun professor. I truly have nothing bad to say about her.

tags: ['EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I took college chemistry already, so this class maybe was easier for me than others, but I think she underestimated her students. She must be used to teacher higher level students because she really dumbed down everything. She also said she was learning everything with us a lot because this was her first time teaching such a low-level class.

Dr. Michel is an absolutely awesome professor. Don't be scared by her older reviews, she is extremely kind and understanding, and very clear about what she expects you to learn in her classes. Attendance is highly recommended because it makes exams much easier. Great professor and a great person, would suggest taking any classes possible with her.

Biochem 1 Exams come straight from her lecture notes and assignments posted. Super easy to get an A in the course if you work for it. Her homework assignments are easy, takes roughly 15-60 minutes to complete each one, and you're only given 1 per week. There are no surprise questions on the exam, and if you pay attention to lecture, you get an A.
Tests and quizzes are so easy as long as you go to class. Her quizzes were basically random attendance and her test questions came right from her notes that she writes on the board.

Dr. Michel is super nice. Her grading criteria is super upfront if you show up and pay attention then you'll get a good grade. Studying for the tests are easy and only off of what she gives you in class. Super awesome.

Chemistry Connections is about resources. The guest speakers were very interesting, but the rest of the material was dull. As a professor, she seems nice, but a little condescending. I would take another class with her if she taught anything other than bio

Dr. Michel is a very good professor.  It is nice to have someone who is so considerate of the needs of her students.  I learned a lot in this course even though I was really nervous in the beginning.  I think a lot of people are intimidated by complex science and blame it on the professor, but they need to take responsibility for themselves.
useless teacher.don't know her teaching.waste my time and waste my tuition money.advice taking another prof.hate her and hate her style.
This class was such a waste of time since she doesnt teach anything. She thinks she is actually helping students but she isnt teaching biochemistry. She's barely teaching high school freshmen biology
Dr michel is one of my favorite profs at RIT!!  This class is super hard but she answers my questions and is really helpful.  plus no boring powerpoint lectures!!

She simply can not teach. Often she patronizes students and assumes that everyone knows nothing. She barely skimps the surface of what is biochemistry and instead focuses on some inane fact as her talking point. She is unprofessional and often appears that she just tosses things together. She doesnt even use powerpoints. She's beyond useless.

Teaching methods were terrible. Her notes leave out most of the information from the book. Her grading on tests were harsh and inconsistent. I feel like I haven't learned anything I was supposed to. She also never explains anything very clearly and you end up having to teach yourself. I highly recommend taking this with another teacher.
She made us memorize tons of useless things that we didn't need. Tests were hard, with her grading even worse. Hated the class, hated the way it was taught, recommend taking the other prof.

This teacher was absolutely horrible.  One of the first teachers to make me want to change majors.  The first thing she told us on day one was "I will never make you memorize anything"  which is a total lie, if you dont memorize the entire book your done for.  Her tests need to have txtbook answers word for word or she takes off points and you fail

AWESOME TEACHER! Super nice too. Dr. Michel makes metabolism seem "cool". Exams are pretty easy if you attend class. Exams are based on notes taken in class. She doesnt make you memorize mechanisms. No cumulative final!! Just final poster project - EASY!

His voice is floaty and bland. In fact I can hear it drawling in the background right now as I rate him in his own class. He seems like a nice guy who means well, but seriously.. learn to hold your class's attention. He's just rambling. This is ridiculous.

Took his online child psychology course this summer. Everything was clearly laid out, which was good because the course required a lot of work. Weekly writing assignment, five timed exams and discussion posts/responses. Got an A but definitely had to work for it.
Extremely boring lecture. Stands in the front and goes off the powerpoint for the whole two hours. Tests are difficult if you do not read through the assigned text.

Prof. Baker was a disappointing professor. While the class material can be interesting, he was more focused on getting information across than keeping things interesting. As an 8am, this class was torturously boring. The tests do come right from the book, so if you don't mind doing the work on your own, and not having a stimulating professor, enjoy

Really good teacher. Easy grader. Easy tests. Listen to the lecture and take notes. Lectures are based on the text completely so make sure to read as well. Really easy stuff so not hard to do a lot and get an easy A.

Easy, multiple choice is easy and if you go to class not only do you not really need to read the book but you get bonus points on certain days just for being there. Hes fair and with the lowest test dropped you can screw up once. For our class there was NO cumulative final, amazing.
easy, sometimes funny, nice guy

Really nice guy. Lectures are a little boring, but the class is so easy. Tests are fully from the book, nothing extra cause his powerpoints are straight from the book as well. Interesting class, just a little boring. Easy A
Boring teacher. Easy A.  One last thing: he reads off powerpoints.  If you ask him to describe something in further detail,  he tells you that he doesn't know and to look it up in the text book.
Boring as hell. Tests are based almost 100% off of the book. Doesn't take attendance, no final exam. Drops lowest test grade. Just go in to take the tests.
What a bore!  Avoid at all costs!

She's a great professor who is willing to work with you. If you need an extension, just email her asap.
Great professor in general.

First time having a deaf professor but she was great! Always made sure requirements were clear and was always available to help when needed. Gives amazing feedback which definitely help my writing. Definitely a lot of writing but a lot of them were enjoyable topics to write and analyze about. Great professor and would love to have her again!

25% for 4 Exams making 100% of your final grade. Is not accessible outside of class and tests are made horribly. Will have to study a lot and have understand the material and study a lot. If you have one bad test you have to do almost perfect on all other exams to even do well in the class. He is a great person and knows what he is talking about.

Great person, bad professor. Lectures are spirited and generally interesting, but don't corelate with his difficult and poorly worded exams. Only grades in the course are 4 exams, none of which are curved. Does not always respond to emails. Best to communicate in person. No textbook so the curriculum is a bit all over the place.

He is a funny and kind teacher, but unfortunately his teaching and grading skills aren't the best. Your entire grade is based off of 4 exams, and there is very little you can do to curve your grade. Even for the tests, the questions and answers are poorly worded and formatted, so expect to ask the professor for clarification on some questions.
Too much on his plate for him to handle. Does not care about the impact he has on his students. Unaccessible
meh, so bad. Don't do it

he is very slow and not productive to keep update each students grade.. he will put all our final grades in last day of the grade due.. all i can say that there is no excuse of him to get better person as program director of biomedical sciences, couples of teaching in different courses and working with research student.

he is lack of communication in emails, not great accommodation for students needed... i am telling you now he will not even care about you have accommodation needed... he will keep talking all over and over and never take his time for each students who really care about academic or whatever it is.

I had professor Osgood for clin micro. You can tell he's a smart person and nice however a lot of his knowledge is dated. Many times his power points have wrong/ dated information on them. His tests always have mispellings and many questions have nothing to do with what we learned in class. He never responds to emails.

Tests are hard and not relevant to lecture
theres nothing to study besides his powerpoints
very incompetent with technology

Overall, I would say avoid taking microbiology, if possible. Very inconsiderate of students and doesn't really care for students' accommodations and does not read his emails. The grade is based on 4 exams, all exams are counted for, unlike his previous classes where one exam grade used to be dropped. Hard exams, powerpoints don't help

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: He's one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Lectures are engaging and full of information. First test was pretty hard and caught me unprepared but the rest were fine. Your entire grade is based on the best 3 of 4 tests over the semester. He's generally fast at answering email questions.

Dr. Osgood is an amazing professor! I love how passionate he is about the material! He is so caring, and really animated. However, intro to infectious disease was hard. He likes to be tricky with his tests! There were four tests, all multiple choice, no final, and one is dropped. Be sure to study and go to class so you can get a good grade!

Grade is based on 3 exams and 1 final. Thats it. Be prepared to study, listen, take notes. Exams are mostly MC, some short answer. He is Interesting, has a couple good stories, matter of fact. True professional. Class could use a couple of other assignments such as HW, maybe a paper/essay to fill out the lecture, demonstrate competency, help grade.

4 exams are the only thing your grade is based on but he drops one of the exams. Can be a little confusing but managed a B in the course which I am happy with because I thought I was getting a C. The final exam was the easy! Study before exams and go to every class and you will get a good grade. He is helpful outside of class as well!

Excellent at lecturing the materials and presenting it in class. However, his exams are ridiculous: ask questions that are way too specific when he tells us to understanding the general concept. I suggest if you wanna take this class you memorize every bit of material because this is not an easy A/B class, especially if you are worried about GPA

He is an amazing professor when it comes to the teaching aspect.  He is very clear and explains everything very throughly.  But, when it comes to his test they are so difficult, they get better as you go on.  He sometimes ask ?s on topics he never covered!  You have to work really hard for this courses.

Never take his class.  He isn't there to help.  When I went to his office to get help he rolled his eyes saying I should have asked questions I had about the test during the test.  But funny thing is he wasn't even there to administer the test- ten minutes into when that test was supposed to start a random  woman came in to hand out the tests.
He started off as a good professor, but went downhill as the quarter progressed. His tests often repeat the same questions more than once and they often cover material we never discussed.
Good prof!! I recommend students who are interested with infectious disease stuff to take his class.Not an easy A but you will understand the course better with him

One of the best people to work with. Clear about everything and makes sure you understand and know what is expected of you. Helps out when you don't understand something and makes sure that you do understand it. Great teacher!!

Took her for an online writing class. She was great at giving feedback and being clear in assignments. However, she's terribly unpunctual. Grades would often be entered late. In fact, none of my essays for the semester were graded until the last day to turn in grades (after the semester had already ended!).

Caton is great. She is clear about what she wants mostly and is a pleasure to work with. The main thing you pretty much have to do is DO IT. Just do the work and you will be fine. I promise. Trust me I got As on her assignments when I thought I messed up royally. Plus she gives extensions most of the time.

Gives extensions in almost any scenario. Knows that writing is far from students favorite subject when they are taking this class, so she will make it bearable. Funny professor. She really cares about her students too.

Took her for freshman writing, it was an extremely stupid class with far more homework than for any of my engineering classes or any other subject. You have to read a lot the first 6 weeks at least, and if you miss 3 classes then your grade is down to a B- or possibly lower. Take an easier teacher if possible.
She didn't grade any thing till the last day for the grades , she is horrible and she didn't respect international studnet , i don't recommend taking  with her any class

she is very understanding and if you fall behind she will work with you until you are caught up however she will not hold your hand you do have to do the work . good to approach if you have a problem. As someone with dyslexia this is one of the hardest classes I will ever have to take. she mitigated the suffering  dissipating the workload  over t

Took Freshman Writing with her, and the writing assignments are very open. For the research paper, which was the main assignment, you could pick absolutely anything that pertained to the topic, leaving it very open for the student to decided what her or she wanted to write about.

Not a bad class if you are a decent writer already.  The main downside of the class was that everything we did was about fandoms and feminism.  This can get repetitive quickly.  Thankfully she keeps class fairly informal and laid-back, so it isn't too bad.

Terrible teacher, incredibly inconsistent grader. I took Writing Seminar with her online and her teaching consisted of assigned reading, then right a paper on it. Even if you met with her as I often did to go over grades or papers it usually had no effect or help on my understanding of the course. Avoid her...
You will regret taking this Professor. Well, at least for me.

I don't find anything from this course. She just grades paper and does not explain why she gave the score. Even though you write your paper according to the question, she gives a bad grade and if you complain, she does not know how to explain it well so I don't feel like I am learning from this class.
She is unclear, hard grader no matter how much you try it's not worth it. If you want to take this course, please avoid HER, CATON.

Easy professor. Pretty few assignments, and they're all easy. She is an easy grader as well. i submitted what I thought was one of my worst papers ever, and I got an A- on it. Just do the assignments on time and participate and you'll get an A.

Had for freshman writing seminar. Professor C'Dog is awesome. She's super friendly and helpful. You do have to do the work, but it's not dull. Very few reading, the non-text book ones are interesting. I would take writing seminar with her again.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Lectures are pretty standard and she tries to encourage class participation with questions but is quick to move on based on the class energy and time constraints. The reading excerpts provided are long and supplemental material at best since she covers the highlights in class. She's knowledgable and passionate but doesn't utilize any engaging flair

Prof. Hutcheson's lectures are a struggle to sit through. Luckily, most of the assignments are based on readings or outside research. The lectures have interesting content, but she isn't a very engaging speaker, and lectures make up most of class time. Readings are interesting but long. Skim them, then go back and read the interesting ones.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Willis as a guy is really chill and he has a passion for criminal justice. That being said, his lectures are basically just him reading the textbook with occasional yelling for 3 hours. The few assignments were really disjointed but if you read the book a few times you'll be okay. The best part of the class was the Q&A with the FBI agent.

I've sent 4 emails to him over the course of this semester and he never responded. We sit for 3 hours and listen to him yell and shout. He pulls up the online textbook and reads it, no slides. Leaving you to take all your notes after class, as you don't know what to look for in the huge blob of text and he goes too fast to even write anything down.

I loved taking Professor Willis' class. He almost reminds me of Anthony Mackie in the way he is able to make his lectures entertaining with jokes, especially when it's a 3 hour lecture on a Thursday evening, yet still be able to cover topics in depth and make you understand them.

this class gave me multiple panic attacks. only three things other than the final are graded (all tests). he shouts OFTEN, and while i respect his passion, he just reads off the textbook. you will need to take notes outside of class as he talks too fast to take in-depth notes in real time.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']
comment: The lecture is 3 hours long and he talks the entire time, but he rarely writes anything on the board he just reads from the textbook. He posts nothing on mycourses, not even the syllabus, so if you miss one class for any reason you will be left behind. There are only 3 assignments in the grade book and they are all tests..... worst class ive taken

He's an adjunct professor which means its very hard to reach him outside of class since he's not on campus. Readings for a test are up to 150 pages. He never puts everything that's going to be on the test on the study guide and sometimes puts on the wrong thing. Will not be taking him again even though he's an interesting guy.

Possibly the best professor I have ever had. As long as you try a reasonable amount you will do well. If you are having trouble he will help you all you have to do is ask. It helps if you communicate with him often that way he can understand any situation you may be in. Overall great teacher and inspired me to minor in criminal justice. 10/10
Understanding, would like to learn any subject from him. The way he teaches is awesome.

Jason Willis is an amazing professor his tests aren't impossibly difficult and aren't meant to be. He doesn't give extra points on anything he does grade fairly. If you do the reading or if you take notes and study them outside you will do amazing. if you refuse to read and go to class good luck. Its a 3 hour class but rarely reaches the 3 hours

While some people think his class is tough, if you put in the time to read the textbook (which he assigns for you to do) and you listen during his lectures you will be fine. You can tell he really wants students to succeed and his grading is pretty clear-cut. Plus he's just a genuinely awesome guy.

Willis is an okay guy, but his tests are crazy hard and he only gives 3 of them. His lectures are also super confusing -- he goes on a lot of tangents and sometimes starts shouting (which is really unnerving) and other times he mumbles and you can't hear a word he says.  As a 3-hour lecture, he doesn't do a very good job at utilizing his time.

C++ is a crime against humanity, but at least this class is incredibly easy. As long as you show up for mandatory in class assignments and get all other work done, this class is a breeze. Sunny goes out of his way to answer specific questions students have and is a good professor.

This class was super chill, only NEED to go on Fridays for quizzes/class activities. Pretty much a nothingburger class, but Sunny is a nice guy, very helpful in office hours, gives clear expectations as to what you need for quizzes/exams

Enjoyable class. Just went through slides but was engaging as much as he could, with the nature of the class anyway. I did not go to the lecture much as the class went on, besides fridays for class activities and quizzes. Always fair with grades and a nice person.

Dr. Kim is a wonderful professor and a great resource if you are interested in the audio field. He is a tough grader and takes his class seriously, but he will always provide help if you ask. RIT is lucky to have such a good professor for their audio classes and I enjoy every class I take with him.

Professor Kim is my favorite professor at RIT and I highly reccomend him to anyone taking any Audio Engineering courses. He is involved with a lot of modern audio research and techniques, so if you're interested in going into the field, he's a great reference.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Fundamentals of Audio Engineering was fun with professor Kim. A mixer of ear-training, written tests, listening quizzes, and mixing projects for the class. Doesn't post lecture notes so take your own. Recording project was fun and professor Kim gives you good feedback about your mixes. Written tests are super easy if you study your notes.

Class was not easy, but fair. It's an elective but you'll devote the same if not more effort than you would a core class. Dr. Kurdziel is knowledgeable and engaging on the topic, there's weekly homework and three tests that are challenging but not impossible. It's a night class, but he's a fun guy who will joke around and is fun to talk to!

Professor Mike is very knowledgable about cryptography, and is funny. But CSCI 462 taught by him is much much more difficult than the other sections for no particular reason. His expectations for homework and exams are vague, and exam is a huge part of grade. Althought you do learn a lot of useful information about cryptography algorithms.
Great professor. He makes the material very interesting and is very knowledgeable about crypto.
Dope professor. Class was fun and he did an amazing job of explaining the material. Top 3 professor so far at RIT. Had him for crypto and totally recommend.

Carlos teaches straight out of the textbook. There is a total of 6 hw assignments and 3 tests. Tests are 2 to 3 questions each. If you pay attention the class isn't bad at all. For BVP, homework is painful but the book he uses (and a useful solutions manual) can be found online free. Tests are all made up very close to test date and usually based on anything he was intent to cover in the review class before the test. Tests are much easier than homework. Very easy grader, very forgiving, cares most that the students learn.

If you want to learn BVP, professor Lousto is a good choice. Homeworks have fewer but harder problems. Three tests plus the final give you the pace for studying. He follows pretty much the book, what makes it easier to study for tests. I went a lot to office hours and that helped.

Good Professor. I learned a lot on numerical analysis. I liked the book the professor chose. Good number of sets of problems and three tests give the opportunity to learn the material. I'd take the second part of the course with him.

I liked very much this course. We had 8 sets of homework's with a dozen problems each. Enough to learn the subject if you do not copy the results from other students. The tests had 5 questions. Again enough to complete it in the time allotted. I also liked the book chosen for the course by Burden and Faires.

Looked like he spent about 5 minutes on each lecture. Assigned questions from the book and told the grader to grade them. Didn't seem to respect the students, and wasn't helpful during office hours. Tests were easy but had very few questions but there were so few assignments which were graded so poorly that I could not have gotten an A.
Matrices and boundary problems from a single book when usually it is given from two or three different books is a plus for this course.
Homework/test every week. Clear expectations and schedule. Follows mostly the book which is helpful and adds some clarifications here and there. Very good professor. You end up learning the material.

Accent is very tough.  Tests always have only 3 questions.  Not very clear at answering questions.  Teaches directly form the textbook without preparing so he frequently gets confused on the material.  Frequently makes mistakes in notes.  Tests are straight forward.

Accent is really tough, had trouble understanding him all quarter. The material is hard but he walks you through it well. Tests are a large percentage and they are only three questions, so you better not mess anything up too badly or you find yourself with a C very quickly
Doesn't give out that much HW and test are only three questions which are pretty easy.
Homework is worth 20% of the grade and only assigns maybe one per week, eight questions long. Very easy to get an A if you come to class and do a little studying outside of class.
I don't see why people don't like him. He gives hw once a week for two weeks then a test. Tests have three questions and are not that hard. Overall, better than i expected

This is the worst teacher I have had since I've been in RIT. I'm not even sure he knows the subject, I went to his office once and it took him almost 20 minutes just to understand what a question was asking, and this was a question he had assigned for homework! His tests have 3 questions, and he is very vague on what will be on them. STAY AWAY!!!!!
Had him for year one, great guy. Made the class actually very tolerable and sort of interesting. He promotes group discussions and tries to be as relatable as possible. I'd recommend him to anyone.

He is very serious and has a military background. His class has three goals: To work in a group, experience long term project management, and have opportunity to speak/present in front of the class. The actual topic of the class doesn't matter. He grades on those goals, but not on the overal project.
He is a chill, nice guy. Is not strict or unreasonable. Treats class as a constructive discussion.
He gave less homework than the other discovery teachers but attendence is manditory.
Good educator, but the mandatory nature of the coursework makes the class ultimately unsatisfying.

Took Electronic Devices Spring 2022. Good lectures but doesn't use slides and everything is written on the whiteboard. DO NOT SKIP CLASS OR YOU WILL MISS SOMETHING. Otherwise he's a great professor and is very thorough in explaining the concepts.

He is a great professor! He has many years of experience and knows what he is talking about! He has no slides so you will need to pay attention when he writes, but he explains concepts well and gives the solutions simply.

i strongly appreciated her teaching methodology and the layout of her course. the readings are dense but are genuinely very important concepts to learn imo. also just one of the most caring and considerate professors i've ever had, and provides immense amount of feedback/room for dialogue when working on projects.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Had her for an 8am. What a terrible way to start the day. This class was boring. I got bad grades on my papers after her giving me advice. Would not recommend even though the class is really easy.

A great instructor who provides lectures that are understandable to students. Someday, she gives half of class time to students to break up in groups and discuss about the materials presented in class. The exams and quizzes consisting multiple choices can be tricky so make you read the questions carefully before deciding the correct answer.
great class
Provides class notes, teaches practical side of topic, hates the Yankees.  Don't fall asleep in class!!!
Easy professor. Teaches an upper level process engineering class. No math only concepts! Tests are short answer questions. Notes are online.
tough class if you are not good
Generally easy, remembers most students.  Ungraded homework, all test allowed 1/4 page of notes.  No final in the course.
Great teacher. Definitely recommend taking her if you don't mind actually doing work and learning.  One of few you want to take whenever you can.

I had her for solid modeling and DDT. She is probably the best professor in the MET department. She will take the time to guide you and assist you if you go to her office hours and ask for help. Really hot teacher also :) YOU MUST HAVE HER AS A PROFESSOR DO NOT GET MARIO CASTRO!!!
Good looking, well actually HOT! She seems to be very compassionate, considerate and above all helpful. I wish I met her in person to tell her all the above! Thank You Dianne!
This is a great professor and she is just a very helpful lady. Kind, generous and just down to earth. I recommend her for any classes because you will enjoy her company and value her information.

Great teacher and a sweet lady. she gives lots of second chances for homework and projects her grading is not tough so if you can draw it is okay. Alot of homework but she dropped two of them if you do the in class assignments she is very helpful when ask questions
Good looking and teaching professor. Her experience in industry is evident as she explains things. Very helpful in answering questions.

Felt real anger during lectures, which was basically every class. They were incredibly boring and I can still hear her voice. Sometimes did not fully open submitted work and incorrectly graded based on that. Gave empty or open-ended responses to emails concerning incorrect grades and questions.
great writing class
Amazing

Professor was really cool. No tests, quizzes or finals. Small homework assignments. 3 essays through out the quarter, and you could rewrite them to get a better grade. Writing class on animals...he took us to the zoo!

The class is very boring. Goodwin is long winded and generally drones on but he's not terrible. Tests were super easy but he grades labs poorly. He starts you out at 80 and then gives you an arbitrary # of pts back if he likes it.
Tough class, but Goodwin worked hard to help me
No UP2 professor is going to make sure you learn like this one. Put in the work, and he will make sure you come out the other end ok.

UP2 is hands down the hardest class I've ever taken (only non A or B grade I've received in my life), but Professor Lusignan does everything he can to help you. He is a thorough and funny lecturer, and very kind. He's extremely lenient with due dates, and gives a good amount of extra credit. This class is hard, but he wants you to succeed.

His lectures are incredible, but attendance is absolutely mandatory and there is a lot of homework. This class is extremely difficult but that is in no way professor Lusignan's fault. Be ready to study outside of class and keep up with a large worload.

Lusignan is one of the better physics professors and does his best to make the class interesting and fun. UP2 is incredibly difficult and tedious, however, and the flipped-classroom layout makes an already complicated subject even worse. Much of the class time feels wasted on super-specific examples which are far more complex than the exams.

The class is tough but Dr. L prepares you well. He assigns 2 homeworks weekly with one being for correctness and one for effort. He posts up an insane amount of practice and he uses iClicker with questions ripped straight from previous tests. He is a great guy and is very knowledgeable and quite entertaining.

He had us do the lectures and notes at home with videos, which actually was pretty cool because then it gave us time to work on the challenging stuff and ask questions in class. He REALLY knows what he's talking about. He also always starts class off with some quotes and small stories, which was always cool. Would take again

Lusignan's lectures are amazing, hilarious, and inspirational, and he is always actively engaging in conversations with students. Be prepared to do a LOT of homework, he's not an easy professor at all but you WILL come out of his class knowing physics. Exams are a cakewalk in comparison to his homeworks, so think about it as cramming ahead of time.

Dr. L is great for teaching physics. Definitely one of the best at RIT for the subject. Be warned, however, that this man gives a ton of homework. There are weekly online and written homeworks that sometimes take many hours each. Especially true in the week before an exam. You WILL know physics by the end of the semester. Best of luck out there!

Lusignan is the best professor I've had at RIT thus far. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He wants to support you in any way he can whether that be regarding physics or literally anything else. He has lots of stories to tell and will keep you entertained. If you need help he will ACTUALLY help you understand material

Lusignan does have lots of work, with clickers, spotchecks, and problem sets, but you will learn physics. It feels awful in the first week or two, but you get used to it, and if you pay attention in class and put some time in and do all of the assignments, the exams will be fairly easy and require minimal studying. Overall would recommend this prof
Pretty good all around.
