comment: Dr. L is one of the best UP2 teachers at RIT. You have to be willing to work hard, complete all prac problems, go to recitations, & office hours > pays off & well worth it, became my fav class of the sem. Lots of hw but if you take the time to learn it you will do better on the tests. Reversed learning approach >hard stuff in class, easier-ish hw

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', 'So many papers']
comment: Lusignan's approach to UPII is to bombard you with assignments in the hope that you eventually just get it. It's gone be a grind, it's definitely going to be overwhelming, and you're gona hate it by the third week. However, you will learn physics. Other than that you can tell he really cares about students success, and is accessible outside class

UP2 is a very difficult class to teach and learn, but I would say Dr. Lusignan does a pretty good job of teaching the concepts. The workload can be daunting, especially at first, but Dr.L provides many opportunities to practice, is very forgiving about due dates, and gives lots of extra credit opportunities. I'd say take him if you can.

Dr. L is fantastic. He made understanding UP2 a whole lot simpler, and was always excited to answer any questions I had. Seemed like a fairly generous grader. He was also great to just chat with before and after class about news, science, or personal stuff!

Dr. L is amazing and I would definitely recommend him to anyone taking university physics. UP is really tough in general, but Dr. L puts in so much effort and you can tell he wants his students to succeed. His class is very well organized and he is great at conveying the important material. He's very approachable and helpful.

Really cares about students and wants you to succeed. Did his best to accommodate for us having extra stress from the pandemic, and adapted to improve the course as went along. Great help in office hours.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Lusignan is a true gem. He really cares about the success of his students.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Uses expertta but hw is a low percentage of grade so use the hw like review if you need it (or chegg them). I disliked the reliance on FlipItPhysics videos but you can just skip thru them and he covers them in class. Group and individual labs are fun and actually help you learn! iclicker quizzes for attendance, but he gives you most of the answer.

Professor Lusignan uses a proper flipped classroom approach using FlipIt Physics, and most class time is spent on practice. In-class lectures are clear, but his volume tapers a bit at the end of slides. He was also very responsive to changes in due dates and providing help for questions on homework that a lot of people in the class struggled with

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Caring']
comment: Dr. L has to be one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. He really loves what he teaches, and while he bombards you with cheesy memory strategies, they are extremely effective at solidifying concepts. This is a notoriously hard class for sure, but if you get him, you will definitely have a good time.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: UP II is hard, regardless of who is teaching the class. Lusignan is probably the best professor you can have if you want a good grade. Lots of extra credit, he teaches well, and really wants to help, but exams are standardized by the department, so be prepared for that.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: The most passionate professor I've had at RIT. This dude sincerely cares about the students he teaches and how effectively he's teaching. I am astounded every class at how much he would like the students to be successful. Tons of work but it's manageable.

I really liked the guy but he simply did not teach. He did not lecture at all. The material we learned from is usually considered supplemental material. I don't know if he can even write on a whiteboard.

I love Dr. Lusignan. It was not an easy-class but he is very encouraging and helpful. He gives a lot of advice and extra-credit assignments. He is funny and try to make us less stressed. The labs were great and he is a very good chatter. I loved it. Just study, ask a lot of question, do not be afraid to. And attend classes, it really helps!

A great professor who genuinely wants all his students to succeed. Physics is a lot of work, but he helps by not taking much off for late HW and giving lots of extra credit. Gives clicker quizzes during class so attendance is mandatory, but he gives you the about half the answers. I got an A- with a B test average curved. Makes lectures pretty fun.

He was available out of class all the time even though I never went to office hours. Great professor, really wants everyone to pass and gives a lot of extra credit. Had a horrible experience with Physics 1, he turned my perspective of physics around and actually enjoyed coming to class, even if it was 8am.

Charlie is an amazing professor, he communicates material extremely well. If you care enough about the class to listen to him, you'll understand the material. He gives out a lot of extra credit opportunities and wants to see everyone pass. He also curves tests which is nice to see.
He is very boring but also really easy. Labs were fun and he always tried helping out with whatever he could.

If you go to his office hours his explanation for concepts are way more straightforward than presented in his lectures. During his lectures he tends to over simplify simple concepts. I would not blame him, if I had a PHD in physics I would have trouble dumbing down from polymer physics  to alberga physics. Overall nice guy well respected.

Always available to help whenever you need, even late at night through email. If you go to office hours and put in genuine effort, you will get all the help you need. Trys to put humor into what many people find to be a dry, boring , difficult class and I would highly recommend him for Physics 111. There is a lot of HW but it is helpful .

Boring lectures, has a tendency to over explain simple concepts and make them seem more confusing than they actually are. Tough grader too; he doesn't mind taking off lots of points for trivial or careless mistakes on exams.

Lectures are very, very boring and he has a tendency to make simple concepts seem more complicated than they actually are by overexplaining them. Tough grader too;  he has no problem taking off lots of points for careless or trivial mistakes on tests.

I have taken him for several classes and he is amazing. I did some undergrad research with him a few summers ago and I didn't get much help from him when I encountered a problem but every class with him has been a treat, I try to take a class with him every quarter. Definitely take him if you can!
I don't know how anyone could not like him. Real good teacher, real cool guy. Definitely take his class if you can.
Best teacher ever, if you listen and do the work you'll get a good grade, not hard at all.

This man is not just smart but he understands more than just his field. He seems to enjoy teaching but likes to force students to come to realizations on there own. I think that makes a better teacher rather than having you regurgitate lectures. Funny accent but you can understand him. I would  recommend if you like to class topic.
Great guy in and out of the classroom. He is there for you when you need help. He tries to make learning as fun as possible and in college you can't ask for much more.
Jake was a difficult professor in that he wouldn't give me straight answers for things, but i learned a lot by working through problems by myself with his guidance.

I'd be willing to bet the negative comments were from the same person... probably a disgruntled arrogant physics type who got a C... he's a pretty good teacher and his classes are comparatively interesting. Maybe not my favorite ever, but one of the better professors I've had.
Jake is the best professor i have ever had.  He has an amazing set of values in edifying his students and making them more intellectual as a whole. Not one minute of is feckless.

Dr. Noel-Storr is a wonderful, insightful and challenging teacher for COLLEGE STUDENTS. His level of interaction is stimulating and thought provoking for those with a post- high school mindset. He is enthusiastic about challenging his students. He DOES NOT hold the hands of the students and allocate "nap" and "coloring" times.
Jake is very helpful. He is passionate about what he does. He is fun and makes class fun. He is always available for help.  Pretty much... Jake is awesome.

I don't think he's cut out to be a teacher since he can't make up a decent lesson, not to mention he just copy-and-pastes the instructions/grading for each project he's assigned us. I don't think I've learned anything in that class, though I will say it helped me understand my research more,(but only because he made us write about it so many times)

When I wake up in the morning, I DREAD going to this class. I stare at the clock, wondering when it will all end. OMG, he holds us late when we have other plans, really IMPORTANT plans. Another thing, on one of the assignments, me and my lab partner got the same grade. Not so bad, but I had written TWICE as much and it was on topic. AVOID AVOID!!!!

What a dork! This guy has the best British accent, but he's so boring it cancels himself out! He never hangs around for research, and he's assigned the same project six times with just enough difference in it that you have to redo the whole thing every time!! He's also extremely biased on how you treat him. Which is funny.
One of the most useful and reliable guys to work with in senior design. Will go out of his way to help you.

This guy is the worst professor at RIT. He doesn't have a PHD yet he is teaching classes! He is useless both in and outside the classroom. He doesn't care whether you learn the material or not. Read the textbook that's the only way you are going to pass the class. I swear this guy should be straight up fired.
He's a good guy and the class didn't require much teaching, but he relied heavily on his teaching assistant and all we really did was come in, sit down, read the lab, do the lab, and leave.
He is bad

He a nice guy, but his analogies and teaching method leaves you confused a lot on what he is talking about. He he famous for the saying "It's really easy." When slack says this most of the time people in the class were lost on what was actually happening
No Comments

Very interesting class. She definitely knows her stuff and is enthusiastic about the material. I learned a lot in this class. Quizzes, daily homework assignments, ear training, compositions, and musicianship final make up the grade so don't worry if you bomb one thing. In-class exams were too long so you have to rush to finish. Would recommend.

Ms. Toca is always clear about what she expects from her students and lets you know if you need to work on something outside of RIT Singers.  At the same time she challenges you to figure out what you need to work on.  Ultimately, Ms. Toca has helped me to become a better singer, student, and person.

Class was really easy, barely took any effort to get an A, but we learned just about nothing. She's a new professor but she basically just reads off her notes for an hour and plays some music. Really easy artistic perspective, but don't expect to get anything out of it.

Had him for 20th c. art since 1950. 66% of the grade: take-home essays for the midterm & final. The other 33% a museum paper and "discussion" index cards that we submit at the end of every class. At first he always spent the full 3 hours lecturing, which put me to sleep, but then he brought in films. Allows rewrites and is very understanding. :)
I think that Alan Singer is such a great man. He gives great feedback and is so inspiring. The assignments aren't that special but he gives you every chance to try new things and grow.

I am not sure why students don't like him. He is a very helpful professor, although his grasp of IT in an IT based course is beneath that of most of the students. Thanks to him I learned about a new subject and my work has improved. He tries to be supportive and i appreciate his effort.
He was not clear on some of the projects he had us complete

-Gave assignments where 50+ images were required within a week (and wanted quality) -unclear instructions -unorganized class -showed up to class 20+ minutes late (every time) -left class for (meeting) during the middle of lectures for 10-90 minutes -nothing on canvas. Majority of my class dropped it during the first few weeks. Don't take his class.

Shows up 20+ minutes late to every lecture, then leaves mid-lecture for 10 minutes to an hour. Did not give clear feedback on work. Did not update canvas or have a clear grading curriculum. Disorganized curriculum  (unplanned). I majority of class stopped showing up within weeks of this class due to his teaching. Please do not take this class.

Gets a worse rep than he deserves. When not overloaded with a ridiculous amount of classes, he was way more organized and had time to dedicate to us. Gives great individual feedback & professional help. Will repeat things when asked. Still a little messy & hard to reach outside class. Understanding about absences as long as you do the work.
Completely disorganized and extremely vague in his instructions. Takes FOREVER to post grades. Do NOT recommend this professor at all.

Chris was one of the best professors I've had for a class. His presentations are very clear and concise (and full of cat photos, too), and he gives practical examples for the stuff he's talking about. He'll grade his exams on a curve if too many people get questions wrong and is always open to feedback.

Does a phenomenal job of teaching and grades in a way that makes you feel like learning the material matters instead of just trying to get an A. One of my favorite classes this semester. Super receptive to feedback at all times and actually cares.

The only reason he taught here is because he took this class when he went here and he didn't like it, so he came back to make it better (and succeeded). Funny and practical career advice and he's clearly very knowledgeable in computing security. An adjunct who actually cares is hard to come by, but he's one of them.
Great prof. He was super transparent and was extremely accessible for students. Also really funny, and the lectures are not boring at all! By far my best prof experience at RIT!
He is very friendly and a good lecturer. The course itself has a good amount of homework, but he makes the course material easy to understand and he has a food sense of humor.
He is very resonable if you need help

Homeworks take an hour at most if you payed attention in lecture and can usually be finished in 2-3 short methods. The majority of the class is graded on 3 projects but he basically gives you all the pieces for and the challenge is to tie them all together. There is also a test and final, but they review concepts learned for through the project.

Bruce Herring was a decent professor, although he could use some improvements. He could slow down the pace. Also he encourages people to ask questions, but he doesn't give time to let people ask questions. He also doesn't really teach a lot of concepts and just reads off the slides occasionally. He also makes the exams really hard.
Put Woolie lore on an exam for extra credit. Lectures were really engaging and aided by a clear interest in the subject. Awesome class for some random elective.
Great professor who has a deep interest in the content he teaches and is always happy to share that interest with you. Also, the first professor ever to put Woolie lore on an exam.
A lot better towards his students than the Woolies. Made some random elective I decided to take last minute a really enjoyable, engaging experience.

He has a bit of an ego, and he would look down on those who were struggling, especially at the beginning (telling them they will "find out how to fix it later" and/or telling them to "figure it out outside of class"). 
People quickly stopped asking for help and were hesitant to respond to in-class questions. 
I do not recommend professor Herring.

The teacher is fine. He is very informed on the stuff that he teaches and is pretty social. GCIS-124(JAVA) the teacher isn't super important because the lectures are the same for all of them. The class has 12 main units. Normally 2 homeworks per unit, one quiz at the end of a unit, and an exam every 3 or 4 units. Learn a lot in the class

Bruce is the best professor for 124 hands down. He is funny, actually answers questions, makes the lectures interesting. He not only codes with you in class, but he also goes beyond the lectures to give you a deeper understanding of java. The class is hard, but he tries his best to help you in any way he can. Use the tutoring center!!

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment:
Great guy, better teacher. 

Herring's lecture style may seem dry to some, but if you pay attention, his way of explaining subjects makes things very simple; instead of diving head-first into complex topics, he first describes how to approach them, and once you are familiar, you learn about the underlying concepts behind. 

Must take professor!

Professor Herring speaks pretty quickly, which was really good for focusing with ADHD. Every section of GCIS-123 is taught using the same slides and same homework, so he is not the reason why this class is hard. He is very open to questions to the point where he will eat up a lot of the class time answering them (very non-judgemental).
Herring wants his students to succeed and is good at handling students with all levels of experience going into this class. Very approachable and worth taking.
Herring was a chill and good professor, definitely need to pay attention during class because all class work is a grade. Make sure to use the tutoring center to your advantage!

Great professor. I feel like he made himself more available than he should have. Students were reaching out online at 10pm and he would respond promptly even on weekends and holidays. Great guy, great at conveying information, and very tolerant of rude students.

He's a great professor when you ask lots of questions, but most of the material you are expected to basically learn on your own. The project is pretty easy if you go to class and ask clarifying questions. A funny professor who makes the class more bearable. I would take it with another professor if possible, but Bruce is a solid backup choice.

Great professor, take him if you can. Tries to make lectures fun and engaging by telling some jokes. Makes it easy to ask questions without you feeling dumb. It is clear he wants you to succeed and is accessible outside of class.

Bruce is a kind, caring, and funny instructor. The class and lecturers are a little fast-paced but the Discord server associated with the class makes it all the better assuming you're not asking a question at an ungodly hour like 2 am. Oh, also attendance is mandatory considering there is a small-weighted 5-question quiz every day. Overall amazing!
His lecture is not clear at all. He does not really know how to explain things. He also ignores me and my questions which is unacceptable. Cannot understand why people like him

Bruce is a great professor. People complain a lot about this course, as well as GCIS123, but the complaints are not his fault. The way it's set up, Bruce has to go fast and there is a lot of work (every professor for this course does this). He stops and answers any question and never refers to a question as "stupid." Can't take it? Change majors.

Professor Herring was a very good teacher, but one of the flaws he had was "freestyling" his code at times, and taking a long amount of time to figure out what was wrong, since he was trying to make the code more efficient. The course does assign a lot of homework, but overall, it isn't too difficult (mostly), and greatly helped me in the long run.
While learning python, He explains the materials well. and is easy for you to stay on track. If I have to complain, I would say the SE department lecture slides are sometimes too long for the class.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This professor goes way too fast, classes are boring an monotonous. I won't recommend this professor at all

Professor Herring knew a lot about the course material but paused a lot on slides as if they were never seen with a lot of "um"s. Feedback was vague and required lots of follow-ups, but was responsive and thorough through follow-ups. Grades were also very slow to be returned at 3-4 weeks each.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Bruce is a terrible teacher, his lessons are just as awful as his usage of parenthesis. His overall attitude isn't great either, he just gives off the vibe as this arrogant someone who gets paid to teach off a white screen. In my opinion, you should just find a different professor, especially if you are learning to code for the first time like me.
Really love Professor Herring, made the class worthwhile to come to as he seems to be a genuinely nice and funny guy. Would take him again in a heartbeat.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Herring is a really nice guy and a pretty good teacher. Although his lectures could be boring at times, I found the notes he gave useful and he is also helpful during labs.

Super nice guy. Strongly recommend taking a course with him if you have the option. He goes out of his way to make sure everyone succeeds. He understands the material super well and uses his real world experience to enhance the lectures and keep them interesting. Great prof.
Gives great examples of when we would use certain topics in the real world. Love Professor Herring and how he presented the work that the SE department wanted us to learn.

Herring has very, very good lectures/slides and can explain things well. His exams aren't pushovers nor are they unfair. That being said, CS2 will make you cry. No professor can save you from that. It sucks. Herring, however, is a solid choice that won't be an extra barrier. I do find him a bit scary to talk to, though.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: If you want to do well and get your work turned days (not at the last hour) before its due, go to Prof. Herring's office and ask questions if there are any concepts you are confused about. He can also explain where you are doing well/poorly on assignments during office hours. This helps you perform better on future assignments and exams.

Bruce Herring is a great professor because he is fair and easy to talk to. Prof. Herring is a great resource for understanding concepts and he will work with you during office hours to ensure you have the right idea. Lecture attendance is basically mandatory as you will not understand the material without it. If you put in effort, he will notice.

Very structured. Prints note packets that are fill-in-the-blank versions of the slides. Does not post the filled-in versions on myCourses, so unless you have a friend in class who is willing to lend you their notes, you won't get all of the information if you don't go to class.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Herring is a pretty decent teacher. Although his lectures could be boring he gets his point across.

Herring was a great Computer Science I teacher, and I'm disappointed I won't have him for CS 2. His lectures were very helpful and clear. He's also very approachable and accessible. He didn't create the curriculum for the class, so I can't accurate judge his personal standards for how much homework he assigns.

This class is definitely challenging but prof. Herring's packets and lectures helped break the information down so that it was more manageable and easy to understand. He was always very helpful during lab sessions and office hours and I never felt like I got stuck on any one thing for too long.

I really enjoyed having Bruce Herring as a professor. He's very knowledgable, approachable and always willing to help both in and out of class. He's willing to meet outside of his office hours as long as you give him some prior notice. I'd be happy to have him as a professor again in the future.

Professor Herring was amazing. I had him for CS1 and immediately knew I wanted him for CSII as well and it worked out great. Awesome funny guy with clear and concise notes and a very experienced individual in his field. Highly recommend his class.

Absolutely loved his class. All lectures were based off of easy to follow handouts/packets. Exams were straight forward and he was willing to give partial credit everywhere. Watch out, his lectures were pretty dry and easy to fall asleep in.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Herring is a solid teacher that lays out his lectures clearly. Regardless of what professor you have you will get a homework and lab each week as well as a final project. Lectures, while informative, are extremely boring and require you to be focused the entire time as he leaves fields blank. Online notes are also incomplete which is a hassle.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Bruce is amazing, if you have an option on getting him please do. Super nice person and genuinely cares about you if you put forth the effort to build a relationship. He also gives packets that are pretty much study guides for exams. I am taking him for CS142.

His approach to teaching is a bit aloof. He won't go out of his way to help you; you have to come to him. When you do ask for help, he'll answer quickly and clearly. I do prefer this for a project-oriented class, though I'm not sure others would agree.

Lectures tend to be a bit boring but he gets key points across fairly well. Easy grader, accessible outside of class and willing to help whenever you're stuck on an assignment. Class is an easy A if you pay attention and do the homeworks.
Lectures can be a bit dry, but he is always available outside of class and willing to help.
Great professor that makes class and lab more enjoyable!

Bruce is a fun and great guy, but his lectures can be dull. I still took him because I had him for CS 1 and enjoyed his class. Missing lectures will leave you confused but he is always available for one-on-one. He is very helpful when you go to him outside of class time. Overall a good professor

Herring is actually fantastic. He is very good keeping the class on track and relaying the concepts in clear and understandable ways. Labs are especially good because Herring will take time out of his day to sit down and help you with any problem you're having. The class was reasonably challenging, but more because of the department, not Herring.
Herring is a good professor. He knew what he was talking about and could explain things clearly. The class was hard but nothing unreasonable.

Herring is awesome guy! He's willing to help if you need it and his lectures are very clear. He might not know everything about python but he is humble about what he doesn't know and will find an answer for you. I really enjoyed his class.

Herring is a great professor for anyone that has little to no experience with programming. He provides in-class examples using Python for each lecture, while posting the slides each week. Some of the assignments may be challenging, however you can always reach out to Herring outside of class during office hours or email for help.
Professor Herring is a great professor. He is able to teach effectively and tries to make the class as fun as possible. I had no prior coding experience, and I would still recommend him!

I came to RIT not knowing any programming whatsoever, and I feel like Prof Herring made it incredibly easy to understand the material. I was able to get the hang of Python through the lectures and homework, and when I didn't understand something, he was extremely accessible outside of class and during office hours. He's chill and easy to talk to.

Bruce is a great professor. Little jumbled on slides sometimes but he conveys the topics clear for student and is always willing to help when needed. Not only is he a good teacher but he is easy to talk with and if you get to know him class becomes very enjoyable with light jokes to break up the heavy work load that CS requires of students.

I can't blame Prof Herring for not knowing some unique RIT CS things since it was his first semester here. But I can blame him for not knowing how to teach Python to freshmen, since he did not know Python himself! He openly admitted to it in class! I would not choose Herring again, he was chill tho.

Out of all the professors in the building, Bruce Harris certainly isn't the best. I would definitely recommend against him as a teacher, as his lectures are awful!!!! You will struggle if you have no prior knowledge with him as a teacher, as his lectures have almost no content.

Spring 2017 was his second semester teaching ever, so if you've never done any programming you might want to pick someone else for CS 1- sometimes during lecture he'd say something backward and he's not always on the ball with Python. HOWEVER- he's really great one-on-one, and if you couldn't make his office hours he'd find another time that works.
Fantastic professor!
Bruce is the best, that's all anyone needs to know. Truly.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']
comment: Although Professor Herring is a great person, having someone try to teach you intense programming while he's learning it himself at the same time is not a good combination. Although I'm sure he'll get better as time goes on, I would advise to either know a lot of coding beforehand or take another professor.
Great professor. Was thrown into teaching straight from industry and he handled it well. He's the type of professor that is very practical and reasonable about the way he handles teaching.
He is a great professor. By making the class interesting, I was inspired to change my major to Computer Science.
He makes the course interesting and helps all of his students to the best of his ability.

Brucie is the man. Lectures can be boring but if you ask him for help outside of class he will take the time to help you. Show up to his review sessions because sometimes he gives extra credit for just showing up.

Honestly loved Bruce, he's a good character and even though he had some difficulty teaching python, he really did want to make sure everyone succeeded. I'm taking him for his CS 2 course next semester, and I honestly can't wait. He's always accessible and very responsive to emails, love this guys.
Very helpful outside of class. He is willing to meet with students outside of office hours.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: One of the best CS professors out there. I would take this guy again in a heartbeat. He is very helpful during and outside of class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: He does his best to make the class as reasonable as possible. When going to office hours, he tries his best to help students understand the content and  benefits help them with problems on the homework and labs.

The structure of the class is forced by the department and should not be  factor while rating this professor. He always tries his best to help the students and is readily available if you email him. When meeting with him during office hours, he is very helpful and explains things very well.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Although he came into this year with no knowledge of python, he seriously put in effort to learn along with us, the tutoring center is a must for all CS classes, grading is fair as long as you follow the criteria
First time teaching this class, he doesn't know python, he hardly explains anything during lectures. Homework grading is very unfair.

tags: ['LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He's a good professor of literally anything but python. He came into the fall semester of 2016 with absolutely no knowledge of python. The class is all python that's a serious problem.
sure, Almost impossible not to get an A
Almost impossible not to get an A. I did almost nothing and managed an A.
Great person. Just attend her sessions, do the work get an A at the end. Fun & enjoyable

Pathways Service: Easy in-class projects. No homework, quizzes, or exams.  Meet with her once to talk about life, and go to class = 100%.  She is very very kind and caring, and she tries to make class fun.  She is a very genuine person.  Best professor for the class.
Asbestos a professor as you could ask for.
Amazingly helpful and super nice.  Super nice with side of nice....oh...and google her...she's awesome.
Great Teacher. Always there to help out in any situation. Ran a really fun class. If you can get in her class take it.

What a great person! Her class was the highlight of my week--I wished it was more often than 1 hour/week. She really cares about making your time at RIT what you want it to be. She connected me to a community service group and sends out personal emails to check up on you if you seem to need it.  I'll be staying in contact with her for a long time!

she is amazing!!! Will help you out in any situation at any time.  Easy to talk to and relate to.  Her class was the highlight of my day!  She wrote an amazing book too and met the band kiss!! She is kick ass haha and she is a lot of fun.  She does really fun class activities.  Also, very understandable and it is an easy A.

She is such a nice and helpful person - I don't think I could have asked for a better FYE instructor. She just wants to help you with whatever you need and to make FYE as fun as possible. When you meet her, you immediately start to like her. If you have a choice for which FYE teacher you want, pick this one.
She is one of the greatest professors you can take at Rit! She is fun to work with, sweet, and she assigns hw to you that are easy to complete and also fun to do in the meanwhile!
She is extremely nice and helpful. Once you first meet her, you feel very comfortable around her. If you ever need to talk to someone, she's the one - she wants to help.
He's a new professor though I claimed to be a jedi master... He still has much to learn with the force
one of worst professor i ever experience

Aaron is an amazing professor. Aaron gives amazing critique, he's very fair and kind, his lectures and lab activities are very well thought up and planned. I can't speak enough praise of his class, DDDD 101 was an amazing introduction to the 3D major. Lots of work in this class, so do your best and put in as much effort as you can.

tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Aaron Powell is a great professor. He knows the material well, explains everything clearly, and is always willing to help. Labs are fun and engaging. He is not a tough grader, but if you do not put effort into your projects he will notice during critique.

Aaron is an awesome, practical, and thoughtful professor! He helped me become a much better 3D artist by providing honest, and helpful critiques which ultimately has made my work quality better overall. The workload is not bad as long as you don't try to do it all last minute and communicate with him. Overall do your work, and you'll get an A.

I learned a lot in his class, but Powell creates a learning environment that is unnecessarily stressful. Is constantly yelling, cursing, and disrespecting people that aren't in the room. The final critique consisted of the entire class (professor and TA included) shouting out things they thought were bad. I always left class on edge.
Great professor. Always willing to help and solve any problems or questions you have. Great at critiquing works and helping you improve. Always enjoyed going to his class.
He is the best teach I've ever had, and one of the most kind and caring mathematics teacher! Love you professor kifle!!

I love math, but learning from him was difficult. We had an amazing substitute teacher one day that really put into perspective how bad he is.  He's a nice enough guy, but maybe not cut out for teaching. Is confusing and makes errors, only to correct them days later. Only passed because I had already taken AP Calc.

one of my favorite professors. his lectures are helpful when doing the homework and studying for exams. exam topics are clearly covered in class. his tests are hard, but always generously curved. he's also very helpful in office hours, and will spend as much time with you going over examples as it takes for you to understand the material.
One of the worst professors I have ever had. Coming from an engineering student

Professor Kifle is a good guy who knows his stuff,  but is not good at teaching. His accent makes it difficult to understand him in lecture. He gives almost no partial credit, and his quizzes and tests are short, meaning if you get one question wrong you are going to get a poor grade. Really have to work to get a good grade.

Mr. Kifle is a very nice guy once you get to know him, and he is very willing to help you as long as you ask him. Although sometimes it can be difficult to understand him because of his accent, but he is very patient and humorous. Tests are harder than average, but he will let you know what type of questions will be on the test in advance.

Does not really convey the material very clearly but will do his best to help you if you go and see him. Not an awful teacher but certainly not the best. Does curve the class at the end (very largely I might add). Light homework load, explains specifically what will be on tests, but you do have to put in work and effort or you will struggle.

Gives almost no partial credit, grades very hard, gives many examples but doesn't necessarily explain how to apply the concept to other types of problems.  Definitely would not take him again, although there was a curve of almost a full letter grade at the end of the course.

He very often tests you on topics you never covered in class or in the text book. Generally, he the problem is he treats you like you already know half the stuff you came to his class to learn. If you're really good at math, you'll be fine. If you're iffy (if you just stopped to think about it) I would encourage you to find a different professor.

Prof. Kifle is amazing! He is super clear about what he wants to convey and he knows his subject well. His lectures are always lively.  He always makes us think about things rather than accept them blindly. Great teacher :)

Spends a lot of time in class going through the proofs of certain theorems and goes over many examples. He's very enthusiastic about the subject and if you're ever stuck on something he's more than happy to help you out. Tells you what to expect on every test, and lets you use formula sheet.

He's such a nice guy and is really there for you if you need any help at all. You get a cheat sheet for your exams but most people still did really poorly for some reason. 4 tests and quizzes make up your entire grade. Really enthusiastic but teaches right out of the book. Curves the class and lets you know that. Definitely take him if you can!

Hagos is my boy! He's a jolly man with a fun accent and somehow inspires a positive environment in a calculus class. His tests can get difficult but he is willing to curve them to help his students out.    "Christmas starts with C, so does curved!" - Dr. Kifle

Prof. Hagos essentially writes on the white board what is written in the textbook. In class, there is very little interaction between student and professor. The tests are not difficult, however they are graded strictly and very little partial credit is given.

I had him for Diff Eq. I like math, but he made it miserable. He read from the book, copied it straight (even then would still mess up the equations). Zero partial credit on any problems, so drop one negative and you are done. Very disorganized and condescending. He messed up almost every example done in class. Average final exam grade was a 50.

He expects you to know the information as you go. However he is always in his office if you ever need help. If you struggle in math I highly recommend another teacher, well me and the 4 people who doped his class this semester. Lastly, he grades randomly, not even the TA knows how he grades.

Very unorganized and hard to follow. Tests and quizzes are only a few questions, ergo if make any simple mistake, poof! There goes half your grade. I'm a math major and had to withdraw from his class. Avoid at all costs.
Horrible Teacher, Very Inconsistent Grading, Messes up his own examples in class. Avoid

Professor Kifle is an extremely helpful teacher. He effectively communicates the course material to the students. He does give a lot of homework but it helps you understand the material and prepare for quizzes and the exams. A majority of the exams consist of homework, workshop, and quiz problems. If you do the homework you should have an A.

This guy gives absurd amounts of homework when each problem takes a page or more to complete.  He reads the textbook verbatim in class as a method of teaching which is supremely unhelpful.  Avoid at all costs.

Professor Kifle is very pleasant if you are willing to put in the effort to learn the material. He has a fairly heavy Caribbean accent but I don't find it too difficult to understand. You can tell that he likes to teach and is very intelligent, he will help you to help yourself. One of my favorites so far at RIT.

Not a good teacher. He tries to help, but just confuses everyone even more. He will refuse to help on certain problems as well. I got an A in the class, not sure how, because he never posts anything online and doesn't give back all of your work. I don't think I have learned any Calculus.

I had him for PB Calc 1.  He is a nice person and will go out of his way to help you if you ask.  He gives challenging problems for classwork, but tests and quizzes are easy -or- are the exact same problems (so you should know how to do them).  Very lenient in his grading.  South American accent, I like it. 1 Homework assignment a week. I got an A!

He's an absolutely useless teacher. He spends the majority of class just writing examples with no explanation, he's hard to understand, he has even been unable to solve some of the questions he assigns. His grading is inconsistent, sometimes he gives partial credit while other times he takes off lots of points for tiny mistakes. Avoid if possible.

Terrible Teacher. He is hard to understand, give little to no help with anything, assigns only the hardest projects and problems to do. Worst math teacher I have ever had. Only up side of this class is that if you get an A on the final he will give you an A for the class. If not he averages everything.

Spends the majority of the class writing equations on the board. When a question is asked he doesn't really get to the point. His accent is hard to understand. He only assigns the hardest problems for HW and labs. If you study his equations well, his tests and quizzes are easy.
tests are tough

I have had 3 classes with Royka now and during scheduling everybody tries to get into his classes. He is really one of the best teachers CIAS has! If you follow his advice to boost your portfolio and get an internship or job, you will have a lot of success. His projects are always current, clear, creative and make great portfolio pieces.

Awesome professor. He has been in the real design world so he knows what people want.  Lots of work, which is great and all of his projects are real projects that are going to boost your portfolio.  If you care about school and want to earn your grade, I HIGHLY recommend him for he is da bomb.

Royka is definitely the best professor at RIT in regards to his passion for design and love of teaching. I give him my highest recommendation- take every class he teaches! His courses are challenging, but the work pays off when your stellar portfolio lands you the job you have had your eyes on. He will truly help you succeed as a designer.

If you want to succeed as a designer take as many classes with Royka as possible.  He's one of the most respected professors in the graphic design department at RIT right now. He's extremely helpful, and will push you to reach your potential. His projects are thorough and concise & will overall benefit you as a student/professional.

Royka is one of the most amazing professors I have had. I have learned so much from him, and by the end of every class I know that it was worth my time. He isn't an easy grader, but he is fair, and will only give you the grade you deserve. He is the most helpful professor I've ever worked with, and really defines and refines students as designers.

Royka is an incredibly dedicated professor. He's genuine and is passionate about design, which is clear in the classroom. His teaching method is different in that he gives his students a real life perspective of design and how it will be applied. I will continue to take his courses and strongly recommend him.

Highly recommend to take all his classes!!!He is one of the best professors of Graphic Design program and always willing to help students with school projects and portfolio reviews. If you really care about your portfolio, his class will definitely help you to gain some great pieces.

Royka is by the far the best professor I've ever had! He is very understanding and truly cares for his students success. He has met with me outside of his office hours to help me when I really needed it. He will go out of his way for his students which you don't find in other professors. He even brings in candy and pop tarts! He's just wonderful :)

Royka is by far one of the best professors currently at RIT. He goes out of his way to help his students succeed. I have had 3 classes with him in the past, and he customizes each one to get the best out of the students. Every class was unique and challenging in its own way. He will push you to do your best. He genuinely cares about his students.

Royka sends clear emails informing students everything they need for each project. He is interested in your portfolio and happy to give advice. His projects are designed to make your book as complete as possible, ranging from print to web projects.

Graphic design students at RIT: I highly suggest taking at least one class with Royka. He was my instructor for Symbol & Icon. He's very clear about what was expected in his class. He goes above and beyond to make himself available to students. He lays the groundwork for anyone to design amazing logos & icons, which can be used in your portfolio.

Royka is a great professor and really knows what he is talking about. He is serious about attendance, if you miss one class you will get an early warning. He takes the time to meet with students outside of class, to make sure you're on track and providing help. He is willing to help any student prepare a portfolio and work on getting an internship.

Overall a Great professor! He legitimately cares about his students & wants everybody to succeed. He even goes out of his way to meet with students to make sure they are on track. If you have the chance to take him, I definitely would! :)  (He does expect you to go to EVERY class though, so if you like to skip a lot i'd go with another professor)

Entirely unqualified to teach the subject, frequently would use AI to supplement his own knowledge of the subject matter even if it directly contradicted the up to date documentation on the software we were using. Impossible to communicate with in a timely manner, failed to update my final grade in the course until 3 months after the expected date

Super reliant on AI. Every single assignment was generated by Claude. I saw him use Claude Code to generate the next semester's assignment one time.  Makes the class seem super difficult while also not caring about the subject. He barely knows what he talks about and can only recite what's on the slides.

The class is pretty fun if you are into a class with projects and no exams, but they are pretty big and time consuming. If you ask for extensions he was pretty lenient. He is new to the department so a little confused about the material at times but I honestly learned a ton about app development from him.

Horribly reliant on ai, to the point where I feel like I am collaterally being dumbed down by it. He was not knowledgeable enough to teach this course, so he used ai for making notes, feedback, and code, including 'vibe coding' some examples which didn't work. Said to ask ai questions if you didn't understand his notes or to fix your code.

Professor Takats was a great professor and someone I'm really glad I had. His class provided me a lot of  useful experience that I've actually used since (including a good project to put on my resume), and he was always easy to reach if I had questions or needed help outside of class.

Professor Takats would usually show up late to lecture, often frazzled and unprepared for teaching the material. The lectures were often boring and a little difficult to follow at times due to his frequent rabbit-holes. But overall, he was a kind person, fair grader, and very available and willing to help outside of class.

Good person, bad professor. Every lecture he forgets about something, and gets passive-aggressive when you ask questions despite the lectures being extremely bare-bones and giving a lot of assignments that require knowledge he barely provides.
Class is pretty good, do a group project for a non-profit. Sometimes a little unclear in expectations, but was a really good experience and learned lots.

pretty good professor! he sometimes seems to not know the details of what he's teaching, but regardless he gets the material across in an effective way. extensive office hours if you need help with anything. there is a group project in this class, which i don't love but i understand why he does it. homework is not often, and is very doable.

JP is a good dude, but man does he suck at teaching. He has no idea how to code and has to constantly google if he's doing things right (but doesn't allow students to look up anything). The rubrics are unclear, and you can get points off for random things that aren't on the rubric or even stated in class. Most boring lectures in the IST department

Takats is quite a funny guy and says a lot of very funny and random things during class, but his lectures can be a bit dull. Extremely easy class as long as you do the homework and put in some effort. He is hard to reach outside of class. No tests, just the midterm and final which were both practicals that if you follow along, are cake.

He was a great professor and throughout the course, he was pretty funny which lead to the classes being a lot easier to follow. The homework is not bad at all, Zybooks is what the textbook is on and there was a unit due at the end of each week, then the occasional quick lab, or towards the end we had a larger project. Overall very manageable.

Takats is seriously funny, but sometimes he's so quiet you can't hear the jokes. Struggles to gain respect from his class. It's okay to look at documentation, but he looks at it so often that it's hard to tell if he even knows what he's talking about. Very bad at communicating outside of class. Class is really easy, though.

John Paul's lectures and coursework are really helpful for learning HTML, JScript, and PHP. He is really flexible and understanding with deadlines if you are transparent and open with him. His lectures are really thorough and he makes sure that everyone is on the same page. I really enjoyed his classes and wish that he taught more courses!

He has been meeting with outside of class times to get caught up in the course and genuinely wants to help it seems. Although the class is pretty basic and topics can be boring I think he does a good job of explaining it and he got me interested in the web development field.

John manages to make this class a disorganized mess. The assignment instructions are never correct, and he constantly forgets to either assign them altogether, or throws things on at the last minute. His communication skills are virtually non-existent, and never responds to questions via email. Lectures are nap inducing.
Good and easy to learn under!

Takats can be a little dull sometimes, other times he has a pretty subtle sense of humor. Classes are mostly just lecture notes with some demonstrations, homework assignments are pretty easy with clear rubrics. He is very good on giving feedback if students have issues. Overall a nice but pretty average professor.

Gets easier as the semester goes on, because there's less homework. Otherwise, Takats is the pinnacle of default teacher. Boring and inflectionless. I'm learning, but only as much as I need to pass the tests and do the homework.

Although many might say that his lectures were boring, I found them to be quite amusing. Prof. Takats has a very low-key humor that you will be able to catch if you are paying close attention. Regarding his ISTE-140 course, although he gives quizes at the start of class, they really help in keeping your mind fresh on the content.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Lectures are usually dry since it's primarily him talking to the class with little interaction. Homework assignments are frequent but easy to complete. If you take him as a professor you will get feedback usually within a day or two of submitting an assignment and he will be very communicative on what can be improved. Overall a good professor.

Takats is a very nice man and is understanding if you have to hand in an assignment late but man are his lectures boring. He reads the slides for the entire time. Once I realized this, I stopped paying attention. I would take the quiz at the start of every class, then play games for the rest. Very easy grader and the exams/practicals are easy.
Good class but lots of assignments so it is easy to fall behind. He is lenient with due dates most of the time.
He's spacy and rushes through the lectures. It takes him a while to turn back assignments. The class is easy.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: This professor is new. However he practically rushes through the material and example codes basically making you rely on the TA for a reasonable explanation or help. He's an adjunct so don't expect much availability. The course is easy overall. If you want the better experience, Get Jim Lenone or someone else who can actually TEACH.

Heavy Russian accent, difficult lectures. Feel free to take the class, but be prepared to go to office hours for either of the other (very god) thermo teachers. We were best bros though because I took Russian as a foreign language. Good Luck.

His accent is tough to understand, and his diagrams are awful, but Comrade is a great guy, I would take him again for other classes.  He is very helpful with in class quizzes and is great in office hours as well.

There were very few times when I walked out of class feeling like I knew more than when I walked in. I felt discouraged to go to class after both midterms after he essentially yelled at students for not performing well. My experience was one that was not particularly pleasant and when I went to sign up for my next classes, I made sure to avoid him.

He's a clear professor; has clear guidelines, expects you to ask questions if you don't understand something, and loves answering them. Very reasonable in grading-strict, but fair. He has industry experience and cares about his students. I would highly recommend taking his class. He also has a great sense of humor!

He has a thick accent, so sit near the front if you want a chance to hear him. He also writes small and badly. Taking notes is kind of hard, a TA suggested to close your eyes and write what he says, not what's on the board. He's a nice guy and quizzes are partner quizzes with help from him. Tests are brutal. Go to class! Trust me.
thick accent makes him impossible to understand. class wasn't too hard, though the final is worth 50% of the grade so its hard to know how you're doing in the class

He's very helpful and willing to help students.Class is fast paced and can become difficult if you miss a day of class. Do your homework and in class assignments and you will get a good grade. I would recommend him.
Political Science Professor Sarah Burns is the daughter of the CIA Director. You should bring her flowers and candy everyday and be very nice to her.

I found her class both interesting and easy. Idk what the person below was going on about. There's a weekly reading quiz consisting of 3 questions, a 3 page midterm essay and 2 essays written at finals week. Certainly not the "hardest level 100 class". Personally I was engrossed in the material, she kept lectures informative and interactive.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Ive never worked so hard before for a level 100 class. Participation is 30% of your grade so definitely dont miss a class. There are weekly reading quizzes that she grades like its a graduate level class and same goes for the midterm essay. The final is two essays written on the spot at finals week about the entire class material.

The class is interesting, makes you think but other wise isn't hard, quizzes are weekly and easy if you do the reading.  There is a group presentation and a final essay to write, certainly not hard but the group work depending on your group can be challenging. Classroom participation is a must, again, easy if you do the readings.

Don't take this class the teacher is horrible and speaks in a pompous manner. Her team projects are ridiculous in scope and are the majority of your grade.
Not a good prof at all. Knows her stuff to some extent but does not know how to teach what she knows to others. Pointless assignments. Avoid at all costs
Horrible, horrible teacher. If you are considering this class, turn around and run as far as you possibly can.

Worst professor I've ever had. Zero connection between her and the students, and extremely rude. Vague instruction but then penalizes for misinterpretation of those vague instructions on group projects which is all the class is made up of. Impossible to read.

Spent more time during class posturing and trying to make an appearance as a "tough" teacher than actually teaching. Disorganized, always changing her schedule. Consistently left a 50 minute class 10 minutes early. Lectures were little more than her reciting the names of topics from the book and reviewing those names from past weeks.
One of the best professors that RIT Kosovo has and the best prime minister.

I don't think I've got the pinpoint words to express how awesome of a professor he is, but if someone asked me to build the perfect professor, the build would end up being like him. His ability to explain everything intuitively and put the whole economy in context and make it fun is magnificent. I look forward to many classes with him.
great Econ class, take it
Definitely the best professor I've ever had!

Besnik Bislimi is a living legend. He is the best professor I ever had and literally the smartest person that I have ever met. He makes every class fun and he keeps us engaged. Besnik has also a great sense of humor and he combines it with academic excellence. If every university had a Besnik, the world's average IQ would be higher.
One of the best proffessors Kosova currently has. He is an expert in his field. It was my honor to learn from his teaching.
He is a walking economic encyclopedia.
No Comments
He is a pretty good proffessor. His lectures are not the most interesting (I don't know how economics can be interesting) but he's pretty good at it. His tests however, are pretty hard.

Mitel made this class tolerable. It was co-taught by him and another professor, and he made the class actually understandable. He's a hardware / wireless guy who works in industry so he really knows his stuff. Great person to know inside and outside the classroom.

Very knowledgeable in what he talks about. Be prepared to know TCP alot, and all of it's functions.  Lots of written content by him that you can reference, so if you dont know something in the class, reference them.

Long, dense lectures. Full of important content though. Prof is an expert who is currently working in industry, he has a lot of knowledge you won't get elsewhere. Not the most outgoing, but is still friendly. Labs can be challenging, ask questions and don't attempt them solo. Expect to spend time outside of class working on them.

Professor Kuliner has the best explanations of low level networking, and guides you through what actually matters. There is a lot of notes (hundreds of pages total) across each section that you should read if you want to genuinely understand the content. The TA can sometimes be a miss because he does not put much effort into finding one.

Mitel is very caring and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. He really wants his students to learn and be prepared. Unlike some networking professors at RIT, he did an amazing job tailoring so security students could enjoy it. While he does have a tendency to go on tangents, all of the class material is laid out clearly in the lecture notes he provides.

His grading is awful and he'll just throw in rude comments in your homework. He was never helpful whenever you try to ask him about a concept you don't understand. A lot of homework and 10 labs minimum. His lab instructions and lab reports are not in sync because he does not do his lab instructions.

He does not teach very well, often rambling off about the glory days of his work experiences in the 80s or about the nitty-gritty details, while missing the overarching points. He also is not very nice, often making degrading jokes about students and misgendering them.

Lectures were consistently unhelpful and full of tangential wisdom that could be important at some point down the road, but definitely not for first-year students. Has plenty of experience in the industry, but teaching skills are seriously lacking. Also, quite rude to a few students. Deviates from the curriculum.

Mitel is very caring and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. He really wants his students to learn and be prepared. However, he is very bad at lecturing. He CONSTANTLY goes off on tangents. Even when on topic, he struggles to explain the information effectively and reads right off of the documents he makes. You can still get an A, but you'll hate his lectures

Quizzes are somewhat hard, horrible with instructions, writes everything himself and barely knows how to do the labs. Says slides say how to do everything... not true. Agree with Feb 3rd post. Funny guy so try to get on his good side and he may be more nice and lenient towards you. Wouldn't take him again, but don't stress if you have to take him

Not much good to say about him. Funny but doesn't answer questions, tells you to just look at the slides, and writes terrible instructions. You will be very confused no matter how hard you try. He also writes all his own stuff and does believe in the internet at all.

Don't take him for an 8AM, his lectures can be boring. However he is super knowledgeable and nice. Also no text book is a massive plus in my book. He also changed some of the course material to be a bit higher level, there were times when I was confused but mostly I think the changes were good.
Honestly, extremely knowledgeable in the field but lectures can be boring. I had him in the evening, so I was already tired as is. He kept the class very simple but could sometimes be disorganized.

I've had Kuliner for two semesters in a row now. I've given the benefit of the doubt. He is nice, and wants you to succeed, but by god he cannot write clear instructions to save his life. The entire semester he constantly needed to make clarifications for his own poor wording again and again. You're not screwed if you get him, but it's a pain.

I really like this guy, he is very kind, outgoing, and funny. Always said hi to me whenever he saw me even a full semester later. Tells stories during class, always tries his best to be helpful, very easy to talk to, hands down one of the nicest professors I had this whole year. Not the best lecturer, but will always be there to help you.

Mitel Kuliner is a great person. As a professor, he is not so great. Since he works in the security field, he teaches at a very high level. This was a 101 class and I felt like I was taking a third or fourth year class. I came into this class with no prior knowledge about the security field and I was not able to learn much in the class.

Mitel is a very caring man and he's very respectful of students' time. Labs are easier because he gets rid of parts that he feels are no longer relevant. However, it can be hard to understand the wording on his assignment sometimes, and his lectures are pretty boring.

Coming into this class, I knew absolutely nothing about CSEC, and after taking the class, I can't say I learned much more. Mitel Kuliner teaches at a very high level and his lectures are very difficult to decipher. For students who want to take CSEC-101 and are in the CSEC major, I highly recommend going with another professor.

My biggest issues are his lectures. They are very informative, but so, so boring. If you already know your stuff, you're golden, otherwise write as much as you can, at least to abate the boredom. Other than that, he's a great prof with tons of industry experience if you have any questions about what it's really like to work in csec. Labs are easy.

Adjunct professor with no set office hours so good luck catching up with him if you need extra help or have a question. Labs are time consuming and difficult. Lectures - boring. Sent an email the evening before the final, (20 minutes before to be exact), indicating he would be in the network lab if anyone had questions. His idea of test prep.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Hilarious', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Really enjoyable professor. He has a lot of useful anecdotes due to industry experience, and keeps the class interesting-enough despite it being mostly just talking at you. Some of the written assignments felt like they could have been worded a little better, though. Sit up front and take good notes and you'll do just fine.

Overall, he is a very caring guy. The class itself was nothing special, a typical 101 class. He put a lot of effort into making sure we understood the labs and even tried his best to give us more than we needed in order to gain understanding. Tried to make a fairly boring class as interesting as possible. Overall, nothing amazing but nothing bad.
Love class! Networking great! Why he like red so much?
Mitel knows his networks!!!

Mitel is a caring guy and extremely knowledgeable. He is hilarious in class and tells it like it is from someone who is currently in the industry. He really really cares about the class and wants us to be excited. Does things for the class other professors won't.
Great professor, he knows that our other classes have a lot of workload so he would be fine extending deadlines and what not. Doesn't curve grades though.

Kuliner is a great professor, has an extreme amount of knowledge in his field and is currently associated in the field for security and networking. He is caring and knows that classes should be balanced and will work out extending deadlines or work and what not. Overall the subject for networking is hard but he does a great job of teaching it.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Hilarious']
comment: Mitel is an interesting guy and certainly has a ton of relevant experience from the industry. He can be pretty funny too. However, he usually isn't very helpful in labs (which can be brutal), doesn't seem to look at slides before he's teaching and sometimes just glazes over slides and tells us to read it on our own.

Demarco makes this course bearable. The original course is boring and dry but the professor knows that so he tries his best to get through everything and teach a bit of life lesson on the side. He is willing to sit outside of class time and talk to you about what ever. In conclusion, Awful course-Awesome Professor.

This class is extremely boring and the teacher knows it which makes it a little easier to deal with. The content of the class is useless which can be self taught on a coop. The midterm and final are simple and the group projects are a joke. Teacher doesnt mind laptops which makes the 4 hours pass by quicker. All notes are posted on mycourses.

Incredibly boring class, but he knows it and will tell you exactly that on the first day.  Seriously, prepare to be bored every class. Projects are straightforward and easy, midterm and final are short and simple. It's a very easy A. The class is horrible, but he's a real nice guy with plenty of stories and experience.

He tells you up front that the class is boring.  But if you come to class, kind of listen, and do the 4 very easy group projects, you will almost definitely get an A.  Bring a laptop to class to keep entertained, and pay minor attention to the lecture and you will be fine.

Get this guy for Needs Assessment if you can. He has a ton of experience in the field and will give you great advice on everything. He also acknowledges that the class is boring and will give you an A as long as your group finishes the (easy) projects. Midterm/Final are very easy too.

I've had him for 3 online classes. He's nice and easy to contact if you need help but you won't receive a single grade from him. His online lectures and exercise instructions are also very outdated (i.e. deprecated functions) as if he wrote them several years ago and recycles them each semester without checking to make sure they're still relevant.

Don't waste your time and money. The instructor is very poor, online lectures are 15-45 minutes per week (for a 3 credit hour semester) and lack adequate baby-steps for the target students, the whole course is presented via copy-paste code, many students couldn't even complete mid-semester projects due to all of these issues. It's bad.

This professor seemed like a helpful teacher at the beginning, but slowly became worse overtime. I wasn't able to fully undertand php and javascript like i was suppose to. And, his final group project was ridiculous. Really bad, please avoid.

Dr. Vullo is a great teacher, Web and Mobile I isn't exactly a hard class, so you might have trouble taking him in a different course. One of the problems I have with him is that he doesn't give enough detail in some of the projects and tests. For example on the final I completely misunderstood what he required for a certain part.

First half of the course had in class exercises which were just tutorials from the internet. Second half of the course was doing work that you didn't have to attend class for. Rarely explained anything. Easy grader, but terrible class.

Very disorganized. Didn't provide a syllabus or clear project guidelines. An easy grader though and extremely helpful if you ask. Just not your cup of tea if like to know what you're supposed to be doing.

I took the class having no experience whatsoever with HTML or CSS. That being said, I got an A just by showing up for class and trying. If you ever get stuck, you can always ask him for help during his office hours. There were no quizzes or tests, just projects. Just go to class and you will get an A and learn something too.

Nice guy and is sure to give you a good grade if you show up to class and try. He isn't always clear in his lectures, but if you ask him for help, he will help you. He doesn't use a textbook for this class either, which is nice.

Nice professor but never available when you need help.  Assumes everyone knows basic html so he moves really fast when showing how to do something.  His midterm and final exams are hard even if they are open notes.

Not a bad guy. Busy work every day, but nothing terrible. Teaches the basics pretty well and is very open to questions. Pretty relaxed and easy class if you have any past experience with HTML or Photoshop. Posts notes and presentations online, as well.

Nice guy. He made this freshman level class interesting, even though I was only re-taking it because prior credits did not transfer from my old school & I knew most of the material already. He is very clear about what you need to do for projects, & if you know the material & finish lab early, you can leave, which is nice when you have a night class

The subject matter was relatively easy but he was very approachable when you had a problem. He explains things rather clearly and makes sure to give you back your results on time. He gives you a list of exactly what he wants in the projects. If you follow the guidelines, you'll do really well. He also bought us breakfast for our last class.

Great professor. He is amazingly clear what he wants and he really teaches you what you need to know. The class actually is not boring and he mixes in a lot of visuals to make the class more at ease like watching videos and playing music during class.
Vullo is a nice and easy professor for anyone.  Classes aren't long and boring, teaches the material well. Good guy, good course
Very easy class and interesting too. He is more than willing to help you learn what you need to know. A fun professor to have.

Dr. Pough is a great professor! He posts all sorts of review material online and you can e-mail him responses to sample test questions, and the prepared question is posted online and is 1/2 of the testt grade. If you really love biology you can easily get an A. work in groups for the online quizzes and it's easy to get a 100 every time.

nice person and knows a lot but his tests are really confusing... you'll never know whats going to be on the test no matter how hard you study. I'll take him and just make sure you do all the HW and the Quizzes...you won't learn a lot but you'll pass the course with a decent grade

I do believe that the professor do try his best to explain, but Intro to Biology was just too hard for me and I didn't understand a single thing. Take the class only if you can truly understand the very very IN-depth information about biology.

i dont know where the material from the exams comes from, his lectures & the book don't really pertain to each other.  exams are impossible to score well on--but if you take the time to review every review asgn. he puts on mycourses, youll at least come across the vast majority of questions on the test.the correct answers will remain mystery though

This professor is very helpful, but the class is really hard. You better have a love for biology and reading because you'll have to stay in the book for this class, the lectures are boring and doesn't pertain to anything your supposed to be studying about. Just try and make sure your on top of the daily quizzes and the hw, because you'll need to!
Excellent teacher! Really smart
Great professor.  Very difficult class, but it's one of the few thats worth the amount of time put in.  If you go to him before assignments are due it will be a HUGE help.

Interesting teacher. Make sure to go to class as to not miss the activities that count as points toward your grade (they really boost it to counter the uh, 60% avg for the tests) Tests are really difficult. Memorize the material and try to guess what goofy questions he'll have on. The pre test sessions online REALLY help. WRITE YOUR ESSAYS BEFORE!!

Great professor...gently eases students into topics that are not very easy to grasp. Also gives great recommendation letters. If you have a problem he's always around to help out AND he's got a great tutoring program set up including tutoring at home from your computer and the tutors are really nice too =)

Wonderful professor, skilled teacher, smart man. His lectures are sometimes interesting, but you can get away with not going if you read the book. Heavily weighted in-class activities are not good to miss. Live by the book...test questions transcend simple fact retention. Lab component is 50% of lecture grade, usually taught by a different PhD.

I have seen people not touch the book, and score well on his exams. He takes his questions for tests primarily from his lecture materials, which are well-supplemented by the book. If you want to do well in this course, READ the book. He gives bonus points for Clicker responses. He takes plenty of grades, so midterm and fnl don't completely kill you

Excellent teacher.  Explains concepts very well and is a fair grader.  He trys very hard to make sure that we succeed and is very interesting.  Take his Intro Bio class!!  His tests are difficult for people because they are not used to thinking about stuff instead of memorizing.

Excellent teacher.  He is hard, and will make you work, but if you put the time in, you will get a lot out of the class.  His midterm and final exams are hard, but much of your grade is based on other things.  He is interesting and brilliant.  He's definitely one of my all time favorite teachers.

There are a million ways in Dr. Pough's class to ask a question and get it answered. If you come out of this class and still have questions, it's because you never asked them. His tests are tough because he's asking you to think more deeply than your used to, but it's a good thing! You can get a 60 on his exam and still get an A in the class.

Dr. Pough will probably be one of the most interesting people you will ever meet. Getting a B is easy, as long as you do the weekly readings and come to class. Getting an A can be tricky. Going to his study sessions before exams is key to getting good grades on the exams. His lectures are always entertaining, and he will keep you interested.
Clear, very helpful, but alot of reading required
What is he talking about????

His lectures is pretty clear but you have to live and breathe with your Bio textbook in order to understand everything he has to teach... His quizzes is pretty easy but Midterm is really challenging so you will have to commit a large amount of time to read through the assigned reading and flash cards is pretty helpful with the facts and etc.
Pough's lectures are completely supplementary, read the book, kick back in lecture and get an A. He is a very nice guy and wants to help you, just don't get freaked out in lecture.
Lectures are boring as hell.  If you want to get an A, you have to suck up and live by the book.
great class if your willing to get off your ass and read the book and pay attention during the lecture.
His lectures are damn blur~ confusing!!! but we r gonna stucked with him for one yesr! god help me!
