comment: Great lectures but know that the work load is a little much if you're just taking this for a gen ed. There are at least two chapters and quizzes due weekly, two midterms, a final, a community service project, and an ethnographic essay. As long as you do the work (actually do the reading and take notes) you will be just fine, tests are very fair.

So much work for a 100-level class. We had anywhere from two to four 20 question online quizzes per week. The class average for the midterms is in the 60s ... girl what. The exams include questions from articles that we are not required to read. You need a 94% to get an A . Doing too much. He is also passive aggressive.

He assigns papers with extremely low word counts, which makes completing the assignment to the criteria he wants very difficult. He grades harshly and gives very little feedback. He lectures on very basic ideas, and then on the test, has you answering specific questions on one tiny reading from the beginning of the semester.
aimers is great and extremely knowledgable. i loved this anthro class

This was one of my least favorite professors I have ever had. During tests, he talks to himself, texts with the sound on, and laughs while grading other assignments. He is very disrespectful to other students in class and actually laughs at you when you answer a question wrong. While he is very knowledgeable, he is also quite elitist.

For an intro class, there was the workload of a 300: two large projects, two midterms, and a final. His projects had requirements that were not content related. Lots of reading, and weekly quizzes. I went into his class with a strong interest in anthropology, but I'm walking away discouraged. He teaches this class too intensely for what it is.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Do not take ethnography and film with him. On top of the up to 4 quizzes a week on readings that are almost all over 10 pages, you watch boring films that put you to sleep in class. There are tophat quiz questions every class for accuracy points on the readings and films. You have to make a 10 minute film that goes with a multi page paper.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I like Dr. Aimers as a person. But as a professor, I feel like he gives too many projects, especially for a 100-level course, both due around the same time. 1. you have to interview an immigrant and 2. basically do community service. quizzes based on book chapters are online and given every chapter. they're EZ. he's probably better w higher levels

Dr. Aimers is a cool guy and is much better for the upper-level classes than the lower levels. This class is a ton of work, but makes sense for a 300-level class. He seems reluctant to give an A on assignments, so don't expect to receive one often. Overall, this class is interesting and he seems to enjoy teaching it, even if it's a lot of work.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: This was a 100 level class and it could have easily been mistaken for a 300. Expect a TON of reading/notetaking, and quizzes on each chapter. He is not very helpful when people have questions either. If you can take a different professor, I would.

assigns every homework and other assignments before the class even starts so you will never know what you have in the class until the very end of the semester.  For example after the first week I had a 6% in the class, because all other assignments for the rest of the year were zeros.

Aimers was genuinely one of the hardest and most annoying professors I have ever had. I participated so much in his class, because no one else would, only for him to give me and 80 on participation. He gives the amount of work of a 300 level course for an introductory level course.
Class isn't that hard if you prepare for exams, just lots of reading and homework.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: People hate on him, but it's hard to be super engaging in a class this informative. I hate when people say this, but for a 100 level class...SO much work. Weekly chapter quizzes, 2 big projects, 2 midterms and final, LOTS of reading: 2 textbooks. Participate so he knows your name, sit In the front and be engaged. Nice guy, lots of work.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: nice professor but this class is so boring

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: For an intro 100 class it was WAY too much. There's multiple quizzes online every week, and a few papers. He is an extremely picky grader with papers. There's 2 midterms and a final and they are extremely difficult if you didn't attend class everyday. He is a nice professor, understanding, and accessible outside of class but I wouldn't take again.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']
comment: For a level 100 class, it was difficult. Prepare to read lots from the textbook and multiple readings including a book. Super helpful and always answers emails. Is willing to do whatever to help you succeed.
very heavy workload for a 100 level class. I would never take this class again. tests are hard.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Expect 2-8 readings that are at min 15 pages long every week. U will be tested on them so know them. He is not an easy grader and you have a lot of projects that you need to start early. He grades on opinion heavily. There is too much work for a 100 level class. He is no help and treats u like ur dumb if u need it. Dont take him if u dont have to.

Dr. Aimers is a good teacher, but his lectures can be boring and drag on longer than necessary. His test are insane. The level of detail that needs to be known to pass a test is unreal. I got great grades on every assignment besides for his multiple choice test. Nice enough guy still. Didn't go to class much, but neither did most students.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: In this class, you will watch many films. Many of them are quite disturbing however, it is a reality for some people.

Attendance was not mandatory however, participation is graded. The course was somewhat confusing to navigate. This course has quite a bit of material to go over in a short amount of time. Prof. Aimers is a Mayanist so this course is right up his alley.

He is extremely interested in his field and I feel like he doesnt understand that people are only there for a credit. He is extremely rude if you do not understand an assignment or how to do something. He is the worst Professor I have this semester due to his attitude with his students. If you need help, do not expect it.

This class is very well constructed by Dr. Aimers. The films he shows are so interesting to watch even for the non-anth majors. Readings compliment the films and they are so eye-opening! If you are looking to develop critical thinking and to become aware of issues in other cultures, this class is an absolutely amazing opportunity to do so. Loved it

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Dr. Aimers is the best professor to take any anthropology course with. I took many courses with him. He expects you to read A LOT, be prepared to study hard. But his lectures are very inspiring (be ready to to fall in love with anthro), readings are great. I fell in love with this field thanks to him. You work hard, but you get more in return!

This class was a level 100 course he treated it like it wasnt. There was 2 major projects that actually needed you to plan. 1. Project was an action project and the other was a interview project. And he had two midterms and a final! He was also very rude to anyone who asked him questions or was unclear.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Solid prof, if you need help all you have to do is ask. Finals are based around short readings he gives you throughout the semester, if you don't read them you'll struggle.

James Aimers was one of my favorites. He is very passionate about his classes and brings humor with his knowledge. This can be hard and confusing material, if you study, take good notes, and attend class, you will do fine. He is always willing to help you as well. I genuinely enjoyed his class though it was confusing at times and not super easy.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read']
comment: James knows the material very well. Taking this course has expanded my knowledge of anthropology and topics that relate today. If you take this course, it's best to get the books early and take notes on the vocab. It's a lot of reading and work, but none of it is boring. It's also best to engage in the discussion too. He explains the material well.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Overall really good teacher. Such a good attitude and passion for teaching, he wont put you on the spot in class. Always answers emails quickly and gives great feedback if you have questions on anything. There are two midterms which are very specific and no amount of time studying will make you do well, but homework grades make up for this. ily

Professor Aimers has a lot of homework for each class. I never found the reading boring. The homework is typically a 10question vocab quiz and 14 short responses. They will be based off the reading or videos, all of which are very interesting. The midterms are VERY specific. Review EVERYTHING and do it well. Not too challenging :) he's very kind

Aimers made me loved going to anthro class every time. While attendance is not mandatory, you are graded on your overall participation. He does't exactly explain assignments in class but it is all on canvas with plenty of time to do them. His lectures where fun and interesting and he has a lot of experience. Good class to take!!

Amazing professor. He clearly knows his subject matter well but is willing to admit that he doesn't know everything about everything. I think people give him a lower score because participation is so heavily weighted but he makes it so easy to participate and he really wants you to so it's your own fault if you don't. He wants to help you succeed.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: He is very passionate about his work, which you can clearly see. However, he seems to assume that everyone is majoring in anthropology when this isnt the case. I took it my first semester of freshman year, and it was challenging. His grading criteria is difficult as no one got a 100 this year on either of the 2 major written assignments.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Extremely vague, subjective grading style. Poorly structured class. Expect long, dry readings for homework and a participation portion that ranks students based on how often they speak in relation to other students in the class.

He is very passionate about his field and that is quite clear, but his attitude is frustrating. The questions on the test are either common sense or super detailed. Participation is really important, but the chances to participate are limited. The final includes an essay portion in which you write three essays and he only grades one of them.

Definitely wouldn't take his class again. Not even sure why my advisor placed me in it during my first semester. Lectures are very boring and so are the readings. He expects a lot which can be expected from a professor but he's vague about what he expects. You'll find out what he expects after the assignment is graded.

He is definitely very passionate about his field and although the material itself is not very difficult, he is a very harsh grader. He was also harsh in the participation grade despite the fact that I never missed a class. He provides very little feedback for his grades. If you read the text you can get a good grade.

You have to read the textbook to pass the course!!  for the most part the class isn't very hard but it is time consuming and you need to put in effort. about three short writing assignments that require some research, and three tests total (including the final). The tests are hard. His lectures can be interesting if you care about the subject.

He knows a lot about anthropology, but expects that out of his class. It's an intro class and he wants us to be anthropologist. Test are super hard and really specific and he grades essays insanely hard. Good Luck! I wouldn't recommend ANTH 100 with him.

Aimers is a great guy who is very passionate about his field. Participation is a big part of your grade so keep that in mind. There are tons of opportunities participate in class and there are interesting discussions to take part in. He manages to keep his class fresh and interesting. Definitely take this class. He is a great guy!

James Aimers is an incredibly knowledgable professor so if you are thinking about majoring in Anthropology, he is a very good professor to take. However, if you are just taking the class for credit, I would try and go with someone easier. I learned alot but didnt do very well. Also participation is graded on a curve, which makes it very competitive

Very experienced expert in his field, so if you're looking for a career in Anthropology, it might be a good idea to get to know him. And that's easy, given that he's so friendly.  But. His teaching style was nonexistent -- everything was taught to us by other students via group projects. Probably would've been very interesting if he taught it.

Be careful. He doesn't outline assignments well at all in class, can be quite pompous and somewhat rude, and apparently has no problem dropping your grade down an entire letter and a half despite perfect attendance that is supposedly worth only 10% of your grade.

Yes, he's hard. But if you do all the work, you can manage a B easily. He spreads his grades out on assignments such as the textbook material and posting onto the school's wikipedia page. He's also very helpful if you e-mail or go to him. I didn't really pay attention in his class but I did all the work. Test grades were average but managed an A-.

Very knowledgeable in the field, many published works, will poignantly spot mistakes, reads every line of every bibliography and then gives you a good grade with opportunity to revise.  As a general rule--just take my word for it: read all assigned material TWICE before the test, and hope you don't read slowly or have ADD definitely not High School

took cultural anthro, really fun class! He showed interesting clips and kept powerpoints interesting and helpful. Need to read the book for the quizzes but the nice part is that the quiz questions tend to show up on the exam. The writing assignments are challenging but fair. Tests aren't hard.

Thought this class would be a lot easier, esp since I had already taken a 200 level anth course. Well, I was wrong. I like Aimers a lot as a professor but he definitely expected a lot out of the students for an intro level class. Tests were harder than expected but bearable. The material was interesting but I just couldn't devote the time to it.

Highly enthusiastic teacher. Reading quizzes require you to do the reading but they are a big grade booster. The wiki assignments were relatively short and easy considering they were the bulk of the final grade, and he makes it clear what he wants from each assignment and gives constructive feedback which is useful in improving your writing.

Good teacher. He was clear on what he wanted from every assignment (detailed assignment documents are available online) and gave clear and sufficient feedback. Really interesting material and he's quirky, but engaging. The reading quizzes are really thorough. Tests are specific, but all multiple choice. Don't take for an easy A, but it's worth it.

Seems laid back in class, but he is a very hard professor. If you dont like reading or writing WIKI entries in 400 words or less on a chapter 170 pgs. long, then DO NOT TAKE! He is a stickler on citations, and grammar. He is not afraid to tear your paper apart. And his main form of testing is multiple choice...and not the easy kind either.
I have to agree with the two previous comments. The professor can be particular and critical with grading, yet scatterbrained when it comes to the lectures. I regret taking this class.

I like him, he has a fun, energetic vibe that made his classes somewhat interesting. I'm glad I took this class because you really realize that a lot of american ways of doing things aren't the only ways, there are many other equally valid ways of doing things. This class isn't an easy A though, so don't take it for that.

Weekly online quizzes, and article reading. Final paper on Material culture was kinda tough. Powerpoint posted after each lecture. Very Nice and helpful, and enthusiastic about subject matter. Will reference his Maya Archaeologist site alot. Recommend, not highly but he's a good guy.

An interesting class, though this could be largely related to the subject matter. Fairly substantial reading with weekly reading quizzes. You will find out what material culture is, and write, what I found to be, the most difficult essay I have written for a 100 level class. Very serious about plagiarism.

He is a very intelligent man who knows what he's talking about. He puts all slides from class online. A participation grade is required and is somewhat difficult to achieve since everything is clear. I wouldnt recommend this course as a core since there are easier courses offered. Extremely hard to get an A. Is very strict with plaigerism.
i liked this class a lot, it was very interesting. i would definitely recommended taking a course with him.

nice guy however I DON'T RECOMMEND THIS COURSE IF YOU WANT AN A his lectures are interesting and easy to understand however tests are specific and more difficult than necessary he also grades the paper too harshly. he is one of those professors who give As VERY SPARINGLY

He's undoubtedly an intelligent man with a great personality and great interest in what he teaches. He uses power point and many visual (and auditory) aides to support the material. However the level of his expectations for a 100 level class are significantly higher as are his standards in grading. The class is interesting but certainly a challenge

awesome guy, really helpful. he has easy online quizzes to boost your average. tests are fairly easy but he has some really specific questions that aren't really fair. only one paper, 1500 words. we all had to lead a debate on a controversy with 3 other people. again, nice guy but more work than some of the other 100 level courses
AWesome professor, he is real nice and love for people to ask question so he can answer them, very liberal and easy-going! I will recommend anyone to take his class!

Tests based on lectures. Plays music before class and shows videos. A very nice intro to anthropology. One text book is hard to comprehend (Woodward) but he does go over them in lectures and answers your questions on it. I would recommend this class
I've only had him a month and I've learned so much. I've always been interested in Anthropology and he has made my introduction into this field very enjoyable. He's really fun!
not a very hard class. very easy going and willing to answer any questions.
People who do poorly in Technical Theatre usually didn't do the readings. Pay attention and take notes, even on the readings, which you should do. Ask questions. Very kind and understanding.

johnnie is by far the best theatre professor/ the best professor in general at the entire school. such a sweetheart and cares so much about his students. He is so passionate about the stuff he does, if you have a chance to take a class with him do it! Always willing to walk things through with you, not much work, does take attendance.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Johnnie is an amazing professor. We met for only 50 minutes a week on Friday. The class was simple and was graded out of 10 points. Show up and participate in the class, and you get a 10/10 for the day. You get one grade dropped at the end of the semester. The activities are nothing hard, Johnnie will walk you through everything. Would recommend!!

Really nice guy but a 94 in the class is a B+ so expect to get a lower grade even if you work really hard. Lectures are extremely boring and very long time-wise but exams are solely based on what he says in class. There arent a lot of assignments so it's easy to keep up with but I just wouldn't take this class unless you're a theatre major.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Caring']
comment: Open office hours, and very nice man. no pp presentations, lectures are all just him standing at the front and explaining terms. online tests are open note, use your textbook for those. tests are difficult mostly from a 'list everything in this category', which makes it easy to lose points. 40 mandatory hours of stage crew, most positions manual

Johnnie Ferrell is a great guy, but I don't recommend this class if you don't intend on studying something similar. The Production Crew is a bit of time-consuming work outside of class. The class seems a little over the top for a Gen-Ed, but he's a very nice guy.

Very nice guy but his class is extremely boring and he seems to forget that not everyone in the class was a theatre major. I had a hard time paying attention because the lectures were extremely boring and tests were sometimes difficult because he named things in class differently than the textbook did. Was an extremely boring class and professor.

Definitely cares and deadline lenient but goes on and on about stuff that isn't really in the textbook or pertains to class. No slide presentation or notes to copy, talks too quickly and randomly to really take many good notes of your own. Texts are unnecessarily hard for the class, not all the information is in the textbook or talked about.

Johnnie is a literal gift from heaven. He is so accommodating and willing to help, you just have to keep communication open with him. He knows so much about lighting and tech theatre and is just such a great person. He's so easy to talk to and has some great stories. If you show up to class, you'll pass.

If you aren't interested in technical theatre the class is boring. His lectures are boring and he more often than not gives the wrong textbook pages. His exams are extremely hard and no matter how much studying/reading of the textbook you do, you will struggle. I will say he is lenient when it comes to the technical reviews and prop papers.

Johnnie has a heart of gold and is willing to help his students out, especially when theyre going through a rough time. Lectures can be dull, but Johnnie is so passionate and such a nice guy its worth it. Also sometimes treats class with food while doing stage crew work. Johnnie deeply cares about and recognizes students he sees are trying.
you definitely wont get an A if you dont study but the assisgnments are easy, makes you do outside work for criedt like go to plays and working stage crew for a week. lecture are SOOOO dry and boring

Johnnie is such a great guy! Class is a little dull if you aren't super into theatre, but that being said, I learned a lot from his class. He is such a sweet guy you wouldn't want to disappoint him. A bit of work just for gen-ed, but I'd say worth it for Johnnie.
Johnnie is so nice! His class may be a little boring when you have to watch videos. A large chunk of your grade is participation in a stage crew.

I found this class super boring, but definitely go to class, its only MW, and its way easier to learn the boring info from him than try to read it in a textbook.  You also have to do 45 hours of crew work, which sucks and takes up valuable evening/weekend time, but was super easy.  Johnnie is also a great guy and super willing to help anyone out

Class is easy, but the assignments can take awhile. There aren't a ton, but you'd definitely have less work taking thea 100 instead of Johnnie's class. If you do take this class, know that an A is a 97 (Johnnie is a SUPER easy grader, 9.8/10 on assignments is easy) and you'll spend 45 hours doing crew in lieu of Friday class. Johnnie is awesome.

Fantastic professor and great guy overall. Super nice and is willing to help you with anything. Really loves what he does and it shows. Has you go about the theatre space and learn by doing. If you are a theatre person, take his classes. You won't regret it. Being on a build/light crew with him is a lot of fun and highly recommended.
Super nice guy, easy class. tests are really straight foreword and there's a lot of partial credit opportunities.
Johnnie is great, he is very nice and loves what he does. His class is easy if you go and pay attention, and the tests are very straight forward.

Took Theatre Tech with Johnnie, and he is the nicest person I have ever met! He's my favorite professor by far. Easy tests. You get to build the sets for plays & musicals. Such a nice person to work with!!! I recommend this class for anyone.
Great class if your seriously interested in lighting design. Very abstract class, one exam but mostly based on class discussion and participation. Recommended for basically any class.

Johnnie is seriously one of the nicest people I know. If you show interest and talk to him he really knows his stuff. He's kinda disorganized with class lectures but I recommend going anyway as a lot of the exam material is lecture based. Crew hours count for 33% of the grade so make sure you get them done. This is not a passive learning class.
Great guy, fun and easy class. Enough Said.

Avoid this class, crew hours are the biggest load of it ever. Its ridicuolous out of class hours for a 3 credit class. Dont even go to class and tests are the most pathetic excuses ever. he as a person is as flaky as they get. BORING TERRIBLE CLASS

Johnnie is AWESOME.  Had two classes with him; he's also my boss at stage crew.  Really nice guy, rambles sometimes, but pretty funny and really does what he can to help you out.  Show up every day and you'll do fine.
as long as you come to class you get an automatic A+ = )

Of course this wasn't the most fun class in the world, but Johnny is seriously a gem. He tries his hardest to make it interesting, and you actually feel terrible when you don't go to class, simply because you don't want to let him down.

THEA 130: very nice man, but frikin BORING class. (though I suppose it's hard to make nails and screws interesting...) don't take it if you're looking for a FUN way to fulfill a fine arts. THEA 129: still a nice man, much more enjoyable class... we actually build and do stuff.
Johnnie is the most personable professor that I have ever had.
No Comments
Johnnie is the best professor that I had the entire time I was at Geneseo. Any class that he teaches is worth taking.
Best class ever
Johnnie is the best, very helpful and a great guy!

This is man has to be one of the kindest sweetest guys alive.  He is always busy but will always find time for you and he genuinely wants to help his students...  His classes are laid back and fun but educational
Very cool guy.  Always busy cause he's involved in everything, but he's willing to work with you.
one of the nicest, most easy-going professors you will ever meet.  he really cares about his students.  easy grader.

Fall semester 2022 was his first year teaching. Class is extremely disorganized. There are two textbooks required for the course, one of which we didn't use. His class is extremely lecture heavy and hard to pay attention to. Although he helps guide students with studying, we skipped multiple chapters due to disorganization.

It's pretty basic stuff. A lot of it is all in knowing your terms. I haven't read a single page of the book and still get high grades on HW and exams.
Exams are on paper.
Super nice guy overall. He does talk a lot, but he obviously is telling us everything from his business experience, which is awesome, because he's not a teacher but a businessman.

Professor Tang's class suffered from a significant lack of organization. Assignments/quizzes were frequently handed out with barely legible writing in both English and Chinese, and contained frequent errors. Additionally, students are required to provide their personal phone numbers for the class.

Prof Tang's class organization was nonexistent, would hand out assignments/quizzes that were written with barely legible english/chinese writing. The Chinese characters and pronunciation were frequently incorrect for Mandarin Chinese, and was inconsistent on standards. Additionally she requires you to give her your phone number for the class.
do not take her class if you don't really want to learn Chinese.

Professor Tang is a very sweet person. But she would frequently ramble during the class about unrelated topics. Use Taiwanese standards for a Mainland Chinese class. Had unrealistic expectations to speak Chinese at an almost fluent level. She was inconsistent on grading standards/expectations.

Professor Tang repeatedly overstepped personal boundaries, gave unsolicited advice, gossiped ab ppl, & exhibited narcissistic qualities. Students who defend her for having good intentions need to recognize that intentions don't matter as much as impact. So many ppl dropped the class when I took it. Class was disorganized & expectations inconsistent

Do not take this class! You will end up not learning or understanding anything. Professor's english isn't good and is incredibly hard to understand what she's saying. Long class, No canvas, or any technology allowed. Also just really unorganized and too close with students. She has called me on the phone several times for being late to class.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Professor Tang is one of the most caring professors. If you respect her, she will respect you. I took her for Chin 102, 201, 202 and she honestly cares for her students. It can definitely be challenging, but remember, Chinese is hard! You have to put the work in to learn. She also always provides extra credit opportunities under test and assignment

I'm not sure why so many people rated so poorly, I really enjoyed Professor Tang's class. The homework isn't difficult, but you should expect to have at least one assignment per week. She is also very accommodating when it comes to the getting work done if you act respectfully in class. If you are willing to put in the work it is 100% worth it .

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: ridiculous rules like no water, can't leave to go to the bathroom, must remind teacher to hand in homework or no credit is received. Can be very unclear with what's being asked. Professor's english speaking isn't great, may have to piece together words to understand her. BUT the way the class is graded makes it easy to get a good grade. LONG CLASS!
very unprofessional and unorganized teaching style

I only took this class for a semester because one semester was enough. Going into the class, I was very excited about learning the language and culture but after the class, not so much. I would not recommend this class at all unless you are very patient . The professor does not really teach but expects very complicated midterm and final projects.

I definitely do not recommend taking this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. You will most likely not learn anything. I took the class wanting to learn chinese because I have always been interested but I did not learn anything.

One of the worst classes I've taken in Geneseo. Professor Tang has no clue how to teach and often writes and teaches things incorrectly. Many Chinese international students frequently see mistakes in her lessons which are planned on the fly. On top of this her grading is arbitrary and is not reflective of her syllabus whatsoever.

Professor Tangs Chinese class is without a doubt one of my favorite classes here in Geneseo. She is an extremely caring teacher which forwards a lot of moral integrity. Her class is both challenging yet rewarding and I can say for a fact that she doesnt advocate any sort of misbehavior outside and especially inside her class is any medium. Take!!

Her teaching style might not be your favorite, but she has good intentions. I can tell she caring and always tries to help her students out.  Sometimes she can be unclear with what she expects from us and that can be a problem. This class is for someone who is open-minded and patient. If you aren't going to even try a little, don't take it.

Very sweet woman who is very invested in her students' progress. If you do not do the work assigned, you will not do well. She can often be unclear and confusing but will make up for it in extended office hours and extreme flexibility to meet an individual student's needs. If she sees that you are interested and try it is easy to get a good grade:)

Do the best to avoid this teacher! she has no ethice and unprofessional, you will get confused in the class as she misrepresents the Chinese culture and she lack of knowledge about Chinese even though she came from China. She made mistakes always in both Chinese and English grammar in the quiz and exam questions. She is unqualified as a teacher.

I took the chinese class with her last semester, try very hard but got a B. She only give A to the student whom she "like", and she expect student to do favor for her. Always asked student to go to the clubs which are not related to the class for getting extra credit. She never teach any concept about the Chinese grammar and sentense structure.

Jasmine Tang is without a doubt the most helpful professor I have ever worked with. She will go far out of her way to help students genuinely interested in her course. Additionally she works around the clock on educational events on and off campus. Extremely kind professor and a true public servant. I would take her class again in a heartbeat

One of the best people I have ever had the pleasure to meet.  Jasmine will go out of her way (and I mean farr East out of her way) to help her students She is caring and wants her students to learn!  She grades modestly and the class is more interest and effort based than militant.  TAKE THIS TEACHER if you like to smile and learn some amazingness

She's fabulous and hot! I just love her classes! She would provide us with everything which has to do with Chinese culture! Learn from her and you can know a big country! It's fun especially when you would like to go on a trip to China! Just kidding!

Could be one of the worst professors in Geneseo. Dr. T is a good person and is a really caring professor for 216 however he has no clear direction in what he is teaching . kind of all over the place and sometimes only does announcements for the entire 50 minute class. However if you read the focus pages the quizzes are very easy.

Gives you everything you need to know for the tests, only 4 in total- no final or midterm. Always open to office hours, cares about his students and is very enthusiastic about the material. He always makes class fun or interesting. Easy A as long as you take notes in class and occasionally read the textbook. Lots of chances to earn extra credit.

Great professor! Extremely caring about his students, makes sure everyone is on the same page within the class, and also makes himself available if you just need someone to talk to. This class did not require a lot of hard work. Follow along to his lecture slides and complete his study guide and it's an easy A. Also give out extra credit!
