comment: Self-centered professor who hates bio majors. If your a bio major get ready for a baised horrible man.

Respect the seed and harvest and you will do well, he's an amazing professor and genuinely cares about his students, don't be afraid to go to office hours either he is really helpful and very fun to be around

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Most people really love Barnabas. I thought he was fine for chemistry lab but I don't think iI would want him as a lecture teacher. He is very friendly and has lots of energy but it honestly was too much sometimes.

My favorite professor so far--very inspirational and motivating. I found him to be super helpful and willing to spend the time needed in order to make sure you understand things. Go to his office hours and have conversations with him, you won't regret it. Put in the work, and you will love what you get out.
He's my fav bean

I had Barnabas for chem lab and I loved him. Highly recommend. He is clear and inspirational and makes lab fun! However, I have also had him for Chem I and I did not enjoy him as much in this setting. I liked him better than the other chemistry professors, though. He curves his tests so that the average is a B, so that is a HUGE plus.

Barnabas was a great professor for gen chem. He wasn't the most concise teacher for a few of my friends, but he helped me understand chemistry for the first time in my life. He is very funny in class and clearly cares. His tests and grading scheme are up to the students by vote, and tries to get everyone at least a B-. I wish he taught orgo
Don't be fooled he does let you pick you your exams, but usually they are hard. His office hours aren't really helpful either
The class itself is pretty easy. He allows students to choose what types of questions and how many questions are on the exam so choose wisely!

A nice guy, but not a particularly good teacher. His lectures and notes can be very confusing, and he wasn't very helpful in office hours. He did a few example questions throughout class time, but it was hard to get him to come over and give feedback. His tests are ridiculous.
Barnabas is an amazing man. He is so happy to help anyone and everyone, and wants nothing more than his students to be successful. He will make your chemistry experience a good one!

I loved Barnabas for Chem Lab. He was such a fun teacher to be around and really tries to get to know and talk to each and every one of his students. He is very inspirational and truly wants you to do well. However, it isn't a walk in the park. You have to go to labs and if you need help go to office hours. Overall, great guy and super funny!
Hes  so sarcastic and doesnt take stuedents seriously at times. its also hard to understand what he is saying.
He is a funny man. Don't trust the curve. Chem II was literally all math. Practice the review questions and quizzes and you'll be fine. Go to class you need the notes.

"You reap what you sow." If you go to class every day and understand how to do the in class problems, you should be good for the tests. Also do the quiz questions before any test. Practice so you can do all the questions fast. Time is of the essence on tests. He is a genuinely caring professor.

Barnabas is my favorite teacher in the whole world. He is very nice and willing to help anyone with anything. He lets you make the test which lets you know what to study. I would go to his office hours every day for help and just to talk  to him because he is so nice. He is willing to help you out with every thing and anything. Very kind.

He's a great guy but lets students vote on the type of test they would like to take so one person can vote to make the test next impossible for everyone else and he will do it. He can be very hard to understand sometimes. If you can get into his crowed office hours then defiantly go. To get above a b- you have to beat the class average.

If you go to his office that is way too small for the number of people that visit him, but he will check the answers to your lab. At the beginning of the semester, I was doing poorly because I am not good at labs, and got a C- as a mid semester grade, but after going to his office hours a minimum of once a week, I ended up getting a B.
Nice teacher who makes lectures interesting.

Barnabas is a wonderfully happy man who wants to help his students in every way possible. He LOVES chemistry and will let you know every chance that he gets. Seeing him for class truly made my day, a joy to have as a professor and would recommend him to anyone. Stay happy.

Barnabas is always around to help, all you have to do is email him or go to his office hours, Even for the first lab or pre-lab. He likes people who work hard and ask for help even on the simplest of things. He will give you all the equations you need and all the inspiration you need, Stay Happy!
All I'm saying is If Kevin Durant knew him, there would be a new real MVP.

Barnabas is a great guy that is always willing to help all of his students! His office hours are very helpful and you should take full advantage of them. He is a tough grader, but if you visit him often in his office and go over your labs and pre-lab assignments with him, you will get good grades. I highly recommend him for any chemistry class.

He is such a sweet person who really does care about his students but he does expect a lot from his students. Use the TAs they are your friends. Also this class is time consuming. If you already have a busy schedule I don't recommend trying to squeeze this in as well. The labs aren't super difficult but they are tedious.

Barnabas really is an awesome person. For lab if you follow his instructions from pre-lab lecture, actually do the pre-lab, ask questions throughout the lab, and go to office hours, you'll do fantastic in lab. Like it isn't an easy class, but if you put in the effort, you'll be fine. He's such a happy/caring professor!

The great thing about Barnabas, besides being a really friendly, happy,  approachable teacher, is that when he says he will help you as long as it takes to understand the material, he really means it. He does a great job of explaining the lab procedure step by step, and anything you don't understand he will help you with in his office hours.

He's a nice guy and he definitely knows his stuff, but I had a really hard time in this class. He does try to help you out though, he lets the class choose the test format and he makes the class average a B- for the final grade.
He is a nice person, but his teaching isnt very good and basically I am teaching myself organic chemistry, but would not recommend if you are someone who cant teach themselves

He's a great guy, but isn't for everybody. I got by with just bothering my classmates to help me understand material, because whenever I go to his office hours, he mostly says "read the (poorly written) manual". Its good to self teach, but if you want help, TA's are your best friends(mostly). If you have him, know what you're in for.

Great person, AWFUL professor. Doesn't teach material, just takes words from the book. Can't explain things - he'll get flustered if you ask a question. I literally had to teach this course to myself. I would HIGHLY recommend taking a different teacher that will actually prepare you for orgo 2. Very frustrating when orgo if not a strong point.
One of the sweetest professors! His positivity never ceases to brighten my day. He's got a great sense of humor and makes lab not as unbearable.
Probably one of the best teacher I've ever had. He's so helpful and he truly wants all his student to succeed. I wish all of my teachers were as great as him and explained the material as well.

The most amazing lab instructor you could ask for! Extremely clear in his pre-lab lectures. Very helpful and approachable during office hours. He's extremely optimistic and enthusiastic . He will give you the grade that you deserve. Only caveat: he grades on a curve so you have to do better than other people in your class. Also, he is hilarious!

Barnabas is a very kind professor who will guide you toward the answer of a difficult question rather than coming out and doing the work for you. He is a fair grader and will give random extra credit for best lab technique. He is very philosophical and cares a lot about his students. Hopefully I can take Organic I/II with him.

Barnabas is so helpful if you go into his office hours. Organic is a hard class no matter what, but if you take the time and go into his office and put the time into work on your own his tests are very bearable.

Barnabas is a great teacher for organic. He is the most helpful professor I have ever had at Geneseo. The subject matter isn't easy but he does a good job telling you what you should really know and focus on.

Hands down one of the best professors at Geneseo. Overall not a hard lab at all if you do your work and show up to lab. If youre confused he is more than happy to help. There is no reason that you should come out of this class without an A if you put the effort into it. DEFINITELY TAKE HIM FOR 119

Barnabas is an extremely helpful and fun lab professor, he constantly encourages you to challenge yourself and tries to teach not only chem, but important life lessons. He is willing to work with you to achieve the grade you want to have, and makes time to help you do this.

Take his class only because he has a curve. AVOID HIM at ALL costs for Orgo 1 though because he does not know how to convey the material to students. Basically says a sentence or 2 and waits for 3-4 minutes per slide while students copy down stuff. Orgo 2 is fine because you know the basics of Orgo. You learn everything yourself

Spends the first 30 minutes of class giving a demonstration of the lab and answering questions, but refuses to clarify instructions once the lab has begun. This made for a lot of teamwork, but at times I was truly lost, and I hated bothering my friends. Also, beware of grade deflation: my B+ turned into a B- because of where I fell on the curve.

Barnabas is a fun, nice professor. He's quite picky with grading though and tends to challenge you rather than answer your questions bluntly. However, he will gladly help you during lab and office hours if you need anything and truly cares about his students. Remember to keep your notebook up to date and keep your prelabs for the final.

Obviously he knows a lot about the material, but he struggles to covey all of that to students. Some tests were impossible and others were way too easy to make up for the hard ones. Just use the book to teach yourself and do practice problems and you'll be fine.

Really nice person. helpful. class is bases mostly on textbook, so if you read your textbook and do the hw problems you should be good. takes student opinions for test. Pretty Good teacher. Slightly easy grader.
Horrible. With the curve you'll probably get an okay grade but if you need orgo for the mcats or biochem, stay away. He is essentially a rambling idiot in class.

Whoever decided to let barnabas teach orgo must have been high. We didnt get to 4 chapters that all the other orgo classes got to, and the tests were totally random. Worst professor I have had at geneseo thus far.

Barnabas is the worst thing that has happened to the chem program at geneseo. i learned nothing, taught myself everything. He is incoherent, dumb and could not answer any questions during class. He is not a nice person despite what you will hear. His tests were unfair and didn't test the subject at all. I am now completely ill prepared for the MCAT
Don't get me wrong, he is a great teacher for chem lab and an interesting person to talk to. However, as an orgo teacher, he is utterly incompetent and has no idea what he is doing. Avoid.
Great guy but grade depends on T.A. if you have someone whose name begins with a K quit, but Barnabas is one of the nicest guys, and always willing to help.
Barnabas made lab interesting and fun and always tried to make everyone happy.  Grades have a lot to do with who your TA is but for the most part the class is easy.

Always ready to help so long as you are an honest, hard-working student.  Constantly repeating his mantra "Stay happy" :) Easy to get along with and makes lab enjoyable even though it's still a lot of work.
Great guy, but the curve is unfair. An 88.9 is a B.
Barnabas is a nice guy. I'm not amazing with Chemistry, so I didn't do so well, but he really tries to help and he tells a lot of jokes. He genuinely cares about the students too.
Barnabas is a nice guy. I'm not amazing at Chemistry, so I didn't do so well, but he really tries to help and he tells a lot of jokes. He genuinely cares about the students too.

I would highly recommend lab with Barnabas. He's always extremely helpful and happy.  Promotes "Planting for 100% Harvest" and "stay[ing] happy."  Such a great professor and human being!  (Note: there is a final exam for lab; save your pre-labs!)

Barnabas is one of the funniest and nicest professor i have met so far. Chemistry is his 2nd passion, right behind Golf (haha). He has office hours in which he is willing to help you solve problems and understand lab procedures. He also has TAs that have their own office hours to check your work.

Everyone at Geneseo should meet Barnabas.  Coolest, most down-to-earth guy ever.  Helpful with labs, and gives great life advice to boot.  Chem lab itself is very picky with grading, but he doesn't do the grading, LI's do.  My favorite prof here.

This class is very difficult.  Although I am not particularly apt in sciences, I don't feel like I get enough practice at the things he teaches.  He says things once and you never really hear about it again.  Tough office hours, but a very genuine approachable guy, the class and material are confusing but I'd like to think he does the best he can.

I must admit his attempts at cheerful wisdom were a bit annoying. However, he is a good, helpful lab instructor and his pre-lab advice can be invaluable (especially because the student instructors don't know how to answer your questions so often).

barnabas is the coolest person on the planet.  he is amazing, and he will help you with anything.  he is really the nicest guy ever.  he is willing to clear anything up and spend as much time with you as you need.  he is smart and just really awesome.  you definitely want him as a prof.  he rocks.

Absolutely the nicest guy ever.  He is so willing to help you...go to office hours if you need help.  I found chem lab was picky with grading...I followed each lab word for word and still only had a B+.  Keep a good notebook!  Highly recommend Barnabas!!

Nice, funny, and helpful, but sometimes he can try to trick you as to what assignments are due when. Do not skip pre-lab by any means. Make sure you know where he is during lab because there's no guarantee your ULI will be useful.
I loved Barnabas. He just wants everyone to be happy. I would recommend his class to anyone.

Barnabas is a great lab instructor!  He is always willing to help if you are having trouble, or just chat and make sure you are "staying happy and having fun!"  If you can take a lab with him, I highly recommend it.

he does not know what he is doing. he literally copied the textbook into his notes and reads it aloud in class. he is a great person, and I would like having him for lab, but as a professor, he has no idea what he is doing

Strikes me as a nice guy, but his teaching style is TERRIBLE.   Basically reads the textbook aloud in lecture. His powerpoints are so wordy that its impossible to absorb any information you'll be so busy frantically trying to get it all down.  Saying that a class will be fun is not the same as making a class fun.
Best lab instructor ever.

Great professor. Genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Do the work he recommends and you will do well. Went to him for help and he remembered me the rest of the semester and was always so nice and encouraging. His lectures could be a little more engaging, it helps to read before class so you don't get lost. But overall, just great!

Barnabas is the man!  It was his first time teaching orgo, so he could have been clearer and some of the test questions were a bit of a surprise, but the curve made everything as fair as it could be.  He's also so upbeat that you can't help but like his class even if you just got a bad grade back.
Fantastic teacher.  Always happy, keeps the class interesting.  Really cares about the students he teaches.
Barnabas is the man. his notes are a little lacking but with his example questions and the questions from the homework, you see almost every question before the exam.i highly recommend him.
Barnabas is a great guy. I've had him as a lab instructer for 2 semesters  and I recommend him to others. He'll help you stay happy in a frusterating course.

I heart Barnabas for Lab.  He is always helpful and cheery.  He tries to get you to use your understanding and won't just give away answers, but will always push you to do your best and enjoy what you're doing.   He's a good guy and I recommend taking him.
Very acecssible and helpful. He wants you to pass as much as you do. You have to do the work, but he will help you if you get stuck.

Organic Chemistry is hard no matter who your teacher is.  Barnabus is always willing to help you during office hours and his practice problems in class are helpful in studying for the tests.Hemakes class enjoyable.  The powerpoints help if you use them along with the book.  To do well in the class you need to keep up. Barnabus is a fun teacher.
genuinely sweet and very enthusiastic about the subject matter. a great lab instructor - very patient and understanding and accessible.
Very Nice!  Extremely helpful and wants people to do well.  Very accessible

One of the nicest professors ever however--BEWARE! He can be tough to understand sometimes and his handwriting is atrocious. He's young and I'd recommend a professor with more experience--but he's a really nice guy and there's no reason to avoid him beyond the fact that you might learn a bit more with someone with a few years under their belt.
He is a very easy going professor and always readily available to assist in any questions you might have. A great guy.

Barnabas is the man!  He's very friendly and very helpful; he's easy to flag down in lab if you need help, and even if you don't need help he'll come up to you and give you suggestions or just see how you're doing.  If you can take a lab with him I highly recommend it.

Unorganized. Isn't spectacular about responding to emails. Constantly clears her throat when giving a lecture. Writing assignments are way too open-ended... just try your best and hope it's what she's looking for.   But a nice lady overall and the class isn't bad.

Not terrible. Let us out of class early a lot. I really didn't learn much, though. Grading on some assignments isn't that clear. Final wasn't difficult. Did a six-page paper, got an A-.   If you lean at all towards conservative, politically, however, beware. You'll find yourself biting your tongue a lot.
Really not that bad. Class can be boring and her opinions are a little crazy, but she will respect you if you state your own opinion. Not difficult to do well at all.

Class was textbook discussion and very hard to make it through. Unclear, scattered assignments due... unless she forgot about them. 25 page research paper but I still couldn't tell you what the topic was. No clue how she grades or what our final grade would be. No enthusiasm or guidance. Attendance not required, most students didn't bother.
Very unorganized, doesn't seem passionate about the subject matter, weird grader and is just straight up boring.  You can easily get a B, but you'll have a pretty miserable time.

Took his online class. He graded fairly, i thought it was very easy for a summer online class. Of course i had to do the readings and write the essays, but what he expected was straightfoward. The only thing was the group project which was difficult because it was an online class...

Dr. McLean is an overall decent professor to take General Physics with. One thing I felt was excessive was the flipped classroom style he used, where he posted lecture videos to be watched before class. However, the tests were fair in comparison with other physics professors. He is best at explaining things one on one in office hours.

Dr McLean is a super nice person. He was one of the better physics professors. However, he does flipped classrooms which was meant to save class for example problems but instead he mostly did practical demonstrations in class which are not helpful for the tests. His office hours were pretty good though and he explained the math well there.

Physics is gonna be hard no matter who you have. James is really smart. Hes a tough grader for labs. The homework is hard but if you go to the office hours he will help you get every answer. He also puts effort in on learning names. I wouldn't recommend the class... but I like him.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor McLean is alright. He is clearly very smart, but he gets side tracked easily and doesn't always explain things very thoroughly or well. There's lots of CAPA homework outside of class and you DO have to go to class, since his slides don't include much besides pictures. Overall he wasn't terrible but wasn't the best.
The weekly homeworks at some times were literally impossible. They are graded extremely harshly, and the tests were just as difficult. For a 100-level gen-ed class this was far too difficult.

He'll give you every possible resource you need to do well in this class. I was out for 2 weeks with pneumonia and he sat down with me outside of class to set me up for the test. His canvas page has a link to the study guide for each test as long as past exams (and solutions), old homeworks with explanations, textbook links and more.

he is very hard to listen to. he stutters on his words and teaches his lectures from a binder. lectures have nothing to do with the homework and you have to look it up yourself. exams are not hard but you need to self teach. the TA is your friend with him. the class wouldve been easier if he taught it better.

He really does his best to be engaging but the only person interested is him. His lectures don't make a single ounce of sense, the homework is hard, and you will spend hours working outside of class. Way harder than it should have been.
The lectures are seemingly random and have nothing to do with the homework assigned, which was extremely difficult. Do not take if you have no background in physics.

This class was way harder than it needed to be. Dr. McLean tries to get information across but it's not always clear to everyone and is seldom backed up by examples. The homework is never what you expect and as a result ends up being difficult but tests are easily passable by attending class, and taking practice quizzes he offers.

TBH, his class is totally different with his homework. He only teaches the background of the questions and you need to figure out by yourself about the homework. However, if you finish your homework (you get 10 chances to answer each questions of the homework), even you did bad on the exam there is still chance to get B or above.

There's no point in taking this class. If you took AP Physics in high school and did well, you already have the credit and don't need this course. If you didn't, this class will be too hard to get a decent grade. The homework is long and tedious and often confusing. McClean is nice enough, but not an adequate teacher. Don't bother.

I dont recommend taking his class without a physics background. Very hard to understand the concepts hes teaching, since both he and the textbook he wrote are vague and difficult to follow. Often I felt completely lost when doing homework problems despite a lot of studying, and had to drop because of the impact on my GPA.

This is insanely hard when stated you do not need a physics background. I ended up dropping because I didn't want an F on my GPA. I did put in the work and effort, the textbook he created is useless. Professor Mclean does not show how to solve problems, he just briefly states how. Was hard to follow at times

If you've never taken physics before (in high school) do NOT take this class. I was forced into taking this course with absolutely no prior physics knowledge, and professor Mclean said that wouldn't be an issue, but it was. I understood nothing in this class and when I asked for help or further explanation, I found myself even more confused
Solid teacher. Nice guy. Found the topics interesting even if his lectures weren't always

Not worth taking for a gen ed science credit.  Harder than it needs to be unless you are exceptional at physics you will struggle.  The class average was around 72.  There is barely  anywhere to turn for help when doing the CAPA homework.  The textbook is confusing and does not explain anything clearly.

Well, the highlight of every class is that he plays musicvideos for the first 5 minutes. I think this class is such a pain though, CAPA online homeworks are sometimes rather tedious and half the time I feel like he never even taught us enough to answer the homework questions. Plus, he wrote the textbook so you don't even have another source soooo.
While he seems like a pretty nice guy, his lectures are extremely hard to understand and the textbook is no help because he wrote it.

A really genuine guy. Taking physics to clear out one of your general sciences is never the easiest course but a professor like Dr. Mclean provides well. He puts nearly all the class material on line so attendance is very voluntary. An appreciation for physics prior to taking the course always helps.

McLean is very good at teaching compared to other physics professors Ive had but with that being said, analyt 2 is still very difficult for a 100-level course and is very time-consuming. if you go to class, pay attention, do hw and study hard you can prob do well. Doesnt curve class but applies only rly small curves to tests which dont help much.

If you have an interest in physics and basic knowledge, then you'll find this class very interesting. McLean's lectures are more consistent with the exams than the homework, so expect to use the textbook for outside work. Overall, a very kind, helpful, and approachable professor, especially during his office hours.

Good professor. He is smart, approachable and has a great sense of humor. His examples and methods of explaining things aren't the best and he goes pretty fast, but he will help you if you need it and will always try to make the material fun and interesting. He always makes Ice Cream in his physics 3 class, and its the best thing ever!

Very nice professor. His class is very hard though and nearly impossible if you have not taken Physics before. He is helpful during office hours but isnt great at explaining things during his lectures. If you enjoy physics this class is for you. If you dont, its best to stay away.

You really need good phys and math skills going into the class. The topics are difficult to understand. He dosent explain them too well. The WebAssign hw is tough and the tests arent any easyer. You really need to read each chapter if you want to have any idea what you are doing in this class.  Study hard and you just might get out with a B!

Don't take any classes with him.  The exams are near impossible and very unfair.  He will ruin your GPA and find humor in it.  He's very smart but expects you to do the same work as an ivy league physics major.

Professor McLean was easily the best professor I had this semester. Extremely intelligent guy. You should have a background in physics before you take this course though. Homeworks can be difficult, so can labs. It was well worth it, though. Great guy.

McClean is a really good guy and  can be very helpful, but without a background in physics, a lot of studying, and a lot of effort on homeworks, it would have been very hard to do well in this class.  Not an ideal way to satisfy a core requirement.

extremely witty and tries to make physics interesting. tests are pretty difficult so attend all review sessions. CAPA is very annoying since it comes every week. class says intro, but you should have a physics background if you want to do well. decent class overall, but you have to be willing to work

Good class but you should have some background in physics first.  Weekly homework assigments on CAPA are fair and convenient.  5-6 mini tests are kind of hard but he gives you lots of sample problems beforehand.  The final is so easy though.  Curving also helps.  Office hours are good and he's just a funny guy.

Mcleaen is a nice guy but his tests were difficult and way more difficult than the homework assignments.  He's pretty helpful in his attempts to put examples and pretests up to study from.  For a 101 class I found it VERY difficult and was often frustrated from the confusing lectures and felt underinformed for the homeworks
confusing lectures, confusing testssssssss!
Dr. McLean is awesome! A lot of people had trouble in the class, but if you make sure to do the CAPA homework it's really pretty easy. Lectures are typically pretty confusing, though.

The class is tough, there's no getting around that. Online homework assignments every week and a test every other Wednesday. Labs were tough, too. McClean  is very helpful if you go see him. Trys his best to slow class down but there's a lot to cover. Not very organized though. Study from the CAPA - the tests are almost the same, just harder.

Dr. McLean is a funny guy.  He acts goofy on purpose, and he sort of waddles around the room.  ALso, he plays a music clip before every lecture.  This class was difficult though.  I would probably steer clear unless you've taken Physics before.  Lectures are confusing, but if you work with someone on the hw there shouldn't be a problem.

Mclean is a very nice man, but unfortunately he can't teach. I left analyt 3 wondering exactly what i learned, and it wasn't as much as i would have expected. His tests were fair and he curved a bit. He is helpful one on one, but i would leave lectures confused most of the time.
Good math skills are required for this class. All the homework is on CAPA and he posts the basics of his lectures online before his tests.  His lectures are confusing, but the class isn't too bad.

This class in a word..HARD. He's a great guy, nice and good with student feedback. However you must be good with math and physics to do very well. the notes are basic and its hard to apply to homework and tests. take another science not this
very easy if you do all the work, sometimes he has a hard time explaining things but if you get the equations you'll be fine
I was hyped for this class, and then the class started.  Teacher has difficult tests and the material is far too hard for a 100 level course.

Please don't take this class unless you're decent with physics and math already. Not an intro class. Lecture material seems extremely straighforward and easy, and then you get to the homework. The homework is exponentially more difficult than any examples done in class, same with the quizzes. Run.
Excellent class.  Very math-oriented but not difficult.  Do the work and you'll be fine.  Also, office hours are very helpful if needed.

Hes a really good guy, tried to make class interesting. Do your homework and make sure you study for quizes. Hes really good with student feedback so talk to him. He helps a lot on home work if you go to his office hours. The quizes and tests are hard though.
Wow.  How can a low 100 level Physics be this hard?

Very orunganized! Lecture material seems elementary but homework and tests are very difficult. The notes he gives are barely helpful at most. He may be a smart guy but he doesn't know how to teach or explain lower-level material.

6 quizzes as apposed to large tests. Capa assignments for hw. Good man. Helpful during office hours. Highly intelligent, yet willing to help and repeat as needed. Class goes a bit deeper than is usually expected in a 100 level course. Not reccommended if you have not had physics in high school.
As long as you work at it, this class is not that bad.  He also is very helpful and he puts ALOT of effort into the class to help you pass and excel in the class.  He is an awesome prefessor.
dr. mclean was by far my favorite prof this semester, he has so much enthusiasm, made the physics class bearable.  he answered the questions i e-mailed him quickly.  really enjoyed the class
No Comments
Tough grader, but very willing to help you make your work better.  Definitely a lot of outside work for a one credit hour lab.  Really nice guy though.

though brant attempted to appear kind and fair, i felt very singled out and uncomfortable in her class. instead of being forthright and accepting her teaching mistakes, she unfairly blamed the students for not comprehending the material. avoid.
This class was 400-level, and it felt like one. She spelled out exactly what was expected: read the textbook, participate, etc. Would take again.

Really sweet lady, wonderful person. But her exams and study guides have NOTHING to do with the exams. The class average was a 67% for people that studied. The class teaches the lectures like everyday, then she will speak briefly for the other 40 mins or so. Would not recommend taking the class if you care about your GPA. Great human being though.

She expects all students to read the required texts and be prepared before class, but our time in class is largely discussion-based, and she places a lot of emphasis on career readiness and presentations. It seems like her higher-level classes are treated with a lot more flexibility and respect for students; take that how you will.

Lectures were engaging and interactive. There were few tests and assignments, and all were graciously graded. She expects a regular amount of reading from the textbook. Overall I felt that I learned a lot and it did not take up a significant amount of my time or effort.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Caring and knowledgable professor. The exams are based on readings. Lots of in-class group discussion. She's a very fair grader with clear expectations. Helpful study guides and class review before exams. Not a difficult class but effort is definitely required for a good grade. She can be funny at times. Only issue was the amount of reading.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I took WGST100 with Dr. Brant this past semester and she treated it was too harshly for a 100 level course. If you don't participate in every single discussion your overall grade will tank regardless of showing up to every class and doing well on all the assignments. She is also very passive aggressive and awkward. Wouldn't have her again.

A good, insightful class. A lot of reading but honestly you can skim since she goes over the readings in class anyways. The tests are easy if you know the book/readings. She is passionate about feminism and the class was very woke. For anyone who likes human rights and politics this is a good class for you.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: worst class. its honestly made me have mental breakdowns in the library after 5 hours straight of working on this class. we have multiple exams a week, with 3 min for 5 questions, lockdown browsers, and 3 exams, one every 2 weeks. I read the textbook, watch lecture vids, watch and read other assigned materials, and its still not enough.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I took WGST 100 with her. There is a lot of readings every night, in the middle of the semester, she realized it was too much for a 100 level course. Theres 1 textbook, but I found it for free online. There are 3 papers & 3 exams that are short responses. Overall, not a bad class, and I think she gets a bad rep.

I took WGST 100 with Brant, but that was not an option. For a 100 class there was alot of readings, she finally realized it was too much readings during half of the semester. Theres one textbook but I found it for free online. Other than 6-7 nightly readings, three papers and three exams. All fairly easy. Overall not a bad course

Tests ask hyper specific questions. She is also a stickler against AI and puts her test questions into AI and Google to trick students when they look it up instead of doing the reading. Overall, cares for her students and wants you to succeed though
Exams were wildly confusing and asked for overly specific answers that were barely touched on in the readings. Professor Brant is pretty easily reachable and responsive, though.

Professor Brant was very awkward in class. She does not seem like her job, nonetheless, I enjoyed the class a lot and it was really informative. There are three exams but if you see her for office hours and explain what you understand than she can help you to at least understand the harder material. She is a great person, awkward professor.

Dr. Brant's class was very informative on Women in Politics. Dr. Brant is very informed on this topic and is very well organized when teaching it. Def would recommend this class it was one of my favorities

Dr. Brant is awesome! The lectures go by extremely fast and if you raise your hand you will feel like your apart of it. Textbook is required and you can't really get away with not reading it like other classes. She does keep a text book in the class archive at Milne so thats cool. I really recommend this class it was great!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: She is definitely intimidating to begin with but she really cares about her classes and is just trying to scare you into focusing. Definitely keep track of readings and participate or she will get upset. A couple papers and tests that weren't too bad. One group project but she made it really doable and fair. Def would take another class with her.

She is really rude across email and really is a stickler about reading the textbook. Her exams are word for word from the text book and if you are not close to the definition she will subtract ten points. I took this class to be an easy A and it has turned out to be one of the biggest drags. Avoid if possible

Hannah was the worst professor I have ever had. She talks about her students and fellow faculty behind their backs. She clearly hates teaching and her students. She plays favorites. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of any classes she teaches in the future.
Amazing professor, really cares about students! If you stay up to date with current events you will be fine with in-class discussions.

Professor Brant is truly a great professor although her classes are difficult she truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Even though she has strict rules she is a kind grader and gives good feedback if you go to her office hours.

Brant is a professor I will never have again, when I had extra time for exams, she forgot to give me my extra time on my online exam and made me fail it. When I tried to explain to her, she told me that she could not change it. The exams were questions that were so complicated and was not even on the lectures or readings. Brant is making me fail.

One of the best teachers I had. She is nice, hardworking, and passionate. If you do your readings (easy) and don't sleep in her class you will be fine. She will respect you if you do the same and you will learn a lot. Gradings are on Quizz (at home), multiple questions exams (2), and a final project about something you are interested in.
Professor Brant's courses are difficult and it is definitely not an easy A. Do the readings, and go to her office hours and you'll succeed.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Dr. Brant teaches a clear and concise course where participation (which is graded) is based on the readings done before the class. If you don't read, you'll struggle. She sets clear expectations for the class, and whether or not students choose to do the work required for the course will determine if they succeed.

Dr. Brant is one of my favorite professors here at Geneseo. She is always so helpful and genuinely cares about her students. She is often misperceived, and I know many of the awful ratings given to her are flat-out untrue. Students who rate her poorly are the ones who choose not to read the assignments or show up to class at all.

Brant is very fair. Try to read the textbook but if not, STUDY HER LECTURES. Her lectures are informative but I wish there was more engagement, but she makes great powerpoints w good info Reach out to her for office hours, she's helpful for in class and out of class questions. As long as you go to class, you should be fine. We had 3 quizzes

I regularly attend class as well as go to Dr. Brant's office hours. She does not teach Political Analysis effectively. I am currently working with a tutor just to earn the current grade I have. She certainly does not make sure students comprehend before moving on to the next topic. And she is disrespectful to students.

Professor Brant is a very intelligent and considerate teacher. She goes out of her way to make sure that her students are understanding the material and checks in to make sure each class is doing well. I felt very fortunate to have had Professor Brant for two classes while at Geneseo.

I thought Professor Brants class was very fair. As someone who is not necessarily interested in politics, she made this class as interesting as possible. She is also very quick to respond to emails. While this class was a little challenging, her goal is not to fail anyone so as long as you keep up with the work and participate, you'll be good.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Online Savvy']
comment: Dr. Brant conveys material clearly and has concrete expectations for her classes. This is a difficult course to teach, which is why some students who fail or don't like to read will rate her poorly, but she posts video lectures and has detailed slides and lectures. If you do the readings and watch the lectures, you will do well.

Dr. Brant has the reputation of being the best professor to teach statistical analysis.  She is very organized and speaks at a good pace. The material is easy to comprehend because she is purposeful with her speech. She's also nice :)

Whatever you do if you need to take an American History for your gen-ed DON'T TAKE THIS. First of all she takes attendance at the start of every class but she says that if you're not there within 5 minutes of class starting you will be marked absent. The structure of her exams are unfair. Powerpoint heavy but yell at us for taking the notes on them

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: She was not able to convey the material in a effective or engaging manner. She contributed to a overall unpleasant & discouraging learning environment with how she handled participation. Definitely recommend avoiding taking a class with her

The teaching of this class was *subjective on many levels. The only dozen assignments over the semester were of quizzes, tests, and a project. The material presented in lectures is irrelevant to questions within the quizzes and tests. Her lack of encouragement and engagement with the class reflects her poor relationship with students. *Polarized

The notes are unhelpful and she seems to think the entire class doing poorly is a reflection of us and not her. I taught myself this entire class in order not to fail and put in more work for this 100-level class than any of my 300-level classes. I think as a newer teacher she still does not know what she is really doing.

Dr. Brant needs to learn how to teach.. She rambles on in class. Not to mention, while she seems nice to your face, you should hear the disrespectful way she talks about students in her office.I attend class regularly and do all the readings, but the tests seemed like they were written by someone who hasn't read the textbook.

Dr. Brant is organized, well-informed and passionate, yet caring, easy-going, and generally a pleasant person let alone professor. Course material is relevant, thought-provoking, and easy to have a good discussion on in class. Don't take her if you want to float through a class. Be respectful and proactive and she will be very approachable.

Pr. Brant is a very good professor. She cares about her student, takes feedback and is willing to change the course material and the pace of the classes if students are struggling. You do need to go to class and read the assigned textbook chapter is order to succeed in this class.

To get a good grade you do need to go to class and atleast skim through the textbook (I read it to the fullest tho but it isn't neccesary all the time). Test and quiz (weekly) material is a mix of slides and textbook content. I missed class twice and still was able to do well. Hanna does care about her students and takes feedback seriously.

If you can take PLSC110 with any other professor, you should! Professor Brant is a horrible lecturer, and then she puts things on the tests that were neither in her lectures or covered in the textbook.

Great professor! Course was discussion-based and she kept the discussions going and on-track quite well. Feedback was always detailed and helpful. Seems like she cares a lot about her students and takes into account their well-being when designing and modifying the syllabus. Content and assigned readings were well-selected and engaging.

This is my second class with Prof Brant and she is one of the most organized caring professors I've had. She lays out what she expects and the lectures are great. She makes sure our group projects are going well and hold students that aren't participating accountable. Lots of women politicians visit class and talk about real world work!

professor brant is so understanding and caring! you can tell she truly wants her students to succeed and learn! she even helped me save a failing grade on the last night before final grades were due (I was failing because of personal problems, not the difficulty of her course) I dont know another professor at geneseo that is so helpful and sweet

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Brant has done a great job organizing her class and letting students know what is expected/needs to be done each week. She is also accommodating and teaches the class well. Uses a lot of current events which is nice. Tests aren't too bad if you take decent notes and do the readings. Understands what students are going through and adjusts to help.

Worst Professor ever! Professor Brant can't teach this course very well at all! I find myself more confused at the end of class. I hired a tutor to help me - and that is the only way I'm passing the class right now. Seriously - a tutor does a better job than Professor Brant!

Professor Brant is a great teacher for this course. She gives weekly quizzes (which are all multiple choice from quizlets). The short responses and extended responses within the quizzes are easy. You do not need to actually read the textbook. Just watch and take notes on the video lectures. ALSO... SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT. 5 points on average for one
Really great professor. You learn about stuff that can't be taught from a textbook in this class. Great class. Interesting. Pleasure to go to.
Dr. Scipione is the funniest guy! His stories will keep you so entertained! Loved his class! Take it if you have the chance!
Great teacher with fascinating stories to be millionaire

Super easy class. You don't learn much about writing, but you learn SO much about really how to live life comfortably. You only need to read one chapter out of the books he assigns, so you can actually borrow from someone else if you want. He comes in about 15 minutes late every day, but I would still strongly recommend for any class!

This course is a good GPA booster for those who already know how to write well. There is no writing instruction so if you are looking to better your writing, this class will be ineffective for you. Lectures are all personal stories that can get very repetitive. No textbooks, no readings. You wont learn much but you'll never have to work hard.
GPA booster!!!!!!! take any classes with him.

Rarely will you find a teacher or class like this. The papers are easy and has never given me a grade below a 90. He spends the entire class talking about his life and it's really fascinating to hear. He comes in late often. I suggest bringing a computer to do work for other classes to do while he talks. Lecture never correlates to the papers.

Scipione is a fantastic professor! I would take this course every semester if I could. His writing assignments are easy and short and he grades them fairly. Other work is minimal and fun. His lectures are just his personal stories- he's led an amazing life so I never want to miss them. He teaches in retirement so I only wish he taught more classes.

A very kind and helpful professor. His lectures are rather pointless, but they are interesting. He grades papers very easily and actually has useful comments. I recommend going after class to his office hours just to chat - he's had a very interesting life and can usually help you in whatever career choice you want to take.
He's the best! Kids literally beg to get fit onto his class roster on the first day b/c it's that popular...
Dr. Scipione is a great guy. He treats his students as equals, which is refreshing for someone in the business dept. If you have any writing skill, it will be very easy to get an A.

Dr. Scipione is the man. He teaches an interesting INTD class and shares his life experiences with his class. He focuses more on your writing skills than he does the content of your writing. He's a very casual and affable professor.
Easy class if you already know how to write a paper. If you can stand the ramblings of a rich old conservative ****, then this is an easy A for your INTD 105.
he wont give you the grade he says he'll give u at the end of the semester

Prof. Scipione is such a nice, interesting, easy professor.  His lectures consist of him telling stories about his life... and that's it. The great thing is, his life is fascinating.  This is a class you look forward to going to.  He doesn't teach the most educationally challenging class, but the life lessons you will learn are invaluable.
Tells the funniest stories and literally doesn't care what you write- will give you a 95+ everytime no matter what. EASY A.
Smokin' hot professor in a rockin' class ; )
No Comments
No Comments
Scipione's class is a breeze. He drones on about how wealthy he is. Often brings up his VERY conservative opinions.

this guy is my favorite professor in Geneseo. Loves to talk bout money and how wealthy he is. very easy going. you do absolutely nothing in class. you sit there and listen to his life stories and pretty much it. and you will learn great deals bout marketing. TAKE HIM IF U WANT TO GET an A

if u can get him, take him.  it's a joke but he's the necest guy i've met on this campus.  really loves to tell u how rich he is and wants to help u get rich too

This man is a genius. The amount of real world experience he passes on is priceless, yes sometimes you may find urself dosing off, but for the commenters who say he has added nothing to their ed. that is BS. Paul is the only Prof. who offers his rich exper. to his kids. Pure Marketing GENIUS.

scipione is the worst prof. i've had so far. i learned nothing from him and he was no helpful at all b/c he was never there in his office! he was very disorganized and didn't get to his point most of the time. he just talked about stories about his college and family lives. this class sucks...

I am taking Scipione for MGMT 385- Consumer Behavior this semester. Let me just say that he is the best teacher I have ever had. His class is easy but the discussions are great and I learn so much.He always tells really interesting stories and the man has so much marketing experience that he's a joy to listen to. Take every class that he offers! :)

this class was an easy A, wouldn't recommend it if you want intellectual stimulation, but if you're looking to bring your GPA up, scipione is the way to go. he's always late & talks a lot about random topics, but he's a nice guy and you can learn more than you'd expect to if you pay attention to the relevant discussions
One of the best professors at Geneseo.  His class is lecture time that is devoted to exploring the aspects of health care.  TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!!!!!!!!

Scipione is the man.  He has been very successful in the real world and I feel like he is passing that knowledge on to his students.  His classes are never boring and don't sweat showing up late to a class, because he runs a little late on some days.  Don't miss an opportunity to take his class.
He's a great guy and very interested in helping his students.  He's definitely a talker, but he makes the time go by fast.  I would definitely recommend him for any class!

Easy grader and always shows up to class late, which is cool cause then you can too. However, talks a lot about random subjects and repeats his life stories a little bit too much. Overall, a sweet guy but if given the chance, will talk your head off.

Paul is one of the best teachers at the whole college. His lectures are never boring and he knows how to keep your interest up. He is always willing to help for whatever reason, and he is a cool guy to just talk to.  Oh yeh, you dont have to show up to class on time because he wont be there.

Health Care Marketing is great! He makes the class very interesting. You won’t fall asleep in this one. Small Class, Good Discussion, Great Time. Although, class never starts on time and sometimes goes over.

Really good professor. I took him for Chem 1 (which I did poorly in) and Chem 2. He helped me immensely and is super clear on what he expects and is always able to help. He gave practice tests that were similar to real exams and were super helpful. My favorite professor so far. Real great guy, its unfortunate he left Geneseo.

Tate is a really good guy, and clearly cares about his students. Sometimes he's a bit confusing but he always makes sure to go back and explain and answer any questions. He's very clear about his office hours and willing to set up appointments outside of class. As far as gen chem professors go, he's a pretty solid choice and I would recommend him.
very sweet and easy professor, cancels a lot due to weather

Prof. Tate really cares about his students succeeding. The lectures are dreadful and only half the class typically shows up. While lectures may seem boring, I would recommend getting a group of friends in the class and rotating who goes to class each day because attendance is graded based on a code. Have them send the code in a text. Study!

Professor Tate is a sweet, caring professor, but is prone to a lot of error during lecture and tends to make a lot of typos on practice tests, slides, and on actual exams. He grades fairly, and applies generous curves. He is not very good at explaining concepts to large groups of people, but if you study hard you will be fine.

May have done better in this class had so showed up to lectures, but they are incredibly boring. The homework was always impossible and did not help with the test. For exams, using the practice exams are your best bet but the tests are always difficult and hard to prepare for
Birds are everywhere

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I've never struggled more in a class then I did Chem116. However, Dr. Tate is one of the kindest and most understanding professors I've ever had. He is a very fair grader and is always available for help and feedback. I passed 1/4 exams and ended up with a C+ in the course; homework and online quizzes are so crucial so always turn those in on time.

His class was challenging but fair. You definitely have to put in a lot of time and effort to do well. Homework really helps to boost your grade and the practice tests are very similar to the real tests. He is always willing/available to help and wants you to succeed.

He is a very understanding professor. His lectures can be boring and sometimes confusing. Helpful if you have a good chem background, if not, you need to work very hard. Homework helps to boost your grade, tests can be tricky. He is willing to do whatever is best for his students. Wasn't too helpful in office hours, he's kinda socially awkward.

Tate is a great guy. He is very understanding and will work with you to do well. His lectures can be a little dry but from a chem class it really isn't bad. Tests can be a hard but he gives you lots of homework/quizzes/ extra credit to help you! He really wants you to do well! I would definitely recommend, he is a great guy!

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor Tate is a bombing comedian during lectures. He is awkwardly funny. The class is not hard if you have a decent understanding of high school chemistry. A lot of his class is self-taught since lectures aren't that helpful.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: He is a great professor for a General Chem Course. He is understanding of students abilities. Could work on time management, but you HAVE to work for your grade. Practice the problems and you should be fine.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He's a genius, but his lectures are very boring and it's hard to stay engaged. The homework helps pad out your grade because the tests are really hard.

Abonado is a nice guys and seems like a good professor because he says as long as you submit an assignment, it will be an A. This is not true. For all the assignments throughout the year I would get grades lower than As, which was fine, until he just did not grade my final paper making me fail the class. So me personally, I wouldn't recommend him.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Out of all of the INTD classes I would say this is one of the easiest. You have to participate and do the readings but the assignments are chill and the prof Is laid back. Attendance matters but if you have to miss he is really chill about it. A little group work through the year but its not bad, also not too many assignments through the year.

Dr Granger is a great teacher and a very simple grader. You have these responses about each chapter but they are very simple and he pretty much gives a 100 for just submitting. The class may seem boring, but if you just show up and submit your work then it is an easy A.

Dr. Granger was one of my favorite professors I've taken so far at Geneseo. His class is extremely easy and he is not a tough grader at all. While in class is a but boring, I feel as if the class contributed a lot to my major (Block 1 for EDUC students) and that I came out of the class more prepared to go into a field of teaching. Great Prof!

Super chill class. There are a lot of mini assignments but they don't take very long and it is easy to stay on top of if time is managed well. I would find it really hard for anyone to get lower than an A- in this class. Not stressful at all.

tags: ['Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Attendance is ABSOLUTELY not mandatory. I think you could pass this class without going a single day. But I would recommend going- Granger is an awesome professor. He sometimes gets off track during lectures but that keeps it fun. The content is interesting and builds upon itself in a really cool way.

INTD203 with Granger is a really easy A as long as you do all your work. It's a class you def should attend as you are placed in small discussion groups. Granger is a really nice and sweet guy and supports all of his students. He gives good feed back and really wants you to do well in his class. Def recommend.

His Brightspace page is extremely organized and his lectures are pretty much straight out of the textbook so be prepared to come to class knowing the material. He is almost always available after class, as long as you stay on top of the homework assignments, and participate in group discussions you should be fine. His grading criteria is fair.

Granger truly cares about his students and gives great feedback. Super easy grader and as long as you put in a little effort the class is an easy A. The big project due at the end of the semester takes a while so don't wait till the last minute to start it. If your an education major 100% take INTD 203 with Granger.

A very wonderful professor. In my class, he put the textbook as a PDF online a few days after our first class. You do have a hefty project due at the end of the semester, do NOT slack on that. Other than that, he only lets you miss three days of class and the textbook work is split up in groups amongst the class, midterms and finals open note.

The class itself is actually really easy, it's very easy to get an A on everything he assigns, late work is accepted, my only qualm is that his lectures are the most boring thing I have ever experienced. I have never heard one person say "et cetera" more times in 50 minutes in my life...actually insane. He's nice, a lil quirk ball though
I love Professor Granger. He is super sweet and understanding. He is an easy grader and gives great feedback. It is very easy to participate in class.
Granger is an amazing professor. Gives great feedback and really cares about his students. He is an easy grader and wants his students to do well.  Take Humanities with him!!!
He's so amazing, so easygoing and easy grader. Understands you have other classes he's the best.

Honestly granger was the sweetest professor I've had so far. Class seems like a lot first day but it's super easy if you read your section of the chapter. Huge history research project at the end of the class is overwhelming but not bad if you manage your time right. Easy A!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Shy and nice but his lectures were so dry. Best to keep up with the reading, or at least skim it so you can participate. Weekly hw assignments and the looming threat of pop quizzes (though we never had any). Final project is SUPER important, don't slack on it.

Dr. Granger is an AMAZING professor. He does love the textbooks so I would def get them whether they are free online or from the bookstore, and he encourages participation a lot since it's somewhat apart of your grade. Lecture heavy but such an easy going person as his grading is amazing. I would take another class with him for sure.

Dr. Granger was a fine professor. Nothing too special. Really really easy class. Really really boring professor. Basically taught everything to myself through the textbook. He doesn't explain any of the assignments so just do the assignment and you'll probably get a 95. Easy grader but there's a lot of papers.

Granger is one of the best education professors that I have had at Geneseo by far. He doesn't make the work too strenuous for his students, he wants them to read, learn, and discuss these issues in our schools so that we are more socially aware to help our future students. He's easy to get ahold of outside of class, and overall just amazing.

Do not question it, and just take the class with David Granger. Literally the best prof ever. Super accomadating and nice man and always gives very clear and concise instruction. All the tests are online and untimed, such a great guy.

Dr. Granger's class is the easiest class on campus. I barely went to his class and got an A in class. All the hw answers are online, and the final and the midterm are easy and you take them home. You have 2 reflection papers but they're very easy. Take this class for an easy A.

He is a nice person.  The class seems intense at first but there is not much work to it.  I spent no more than 20 minutes each week on homework except for the final weeks where I did the final project.  He is sometimes boring but he wants the best for his students

The workload for this class is light and fairly easy. Dr. Granger is a good professor my only complaint is that he does not explain why he took points off on essays in the feedback he gives; rather he makes irrelevant comments. Still an easy A.

Not much to say except he cares, hes not a tough grader. Only thing I really worried about was the final project. Every other assignment was manageable. If youre thinking about taking him, just do it. Easy A.

I took INTD 203 as an online class during COVID, so maybe Dr. Granger is good in a normal year. Everything is from the textbook. Annoying final project he doesn't help with at all. Very condescending in emails. No communication even though it's the only class he taught this semester. Wish I could get refunded whatever money went towards paying him
Dr. Granger is the nicest and easiest professor to talk to. The class is a good amount of work, but he is passionate about what he teaches and makes the class interesting

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Professor Granger was the best professor I have ever had. There is no surprises, on the first day he gives you a syllabus for the whole semester and everything stays that way. He is very understanding that students lives are more than just his class and always answers questions clearly-no vagueness. Read the book and participate. take it w/ him!!!!

He never expects anything he hasn't explicitly said. He is an amazingly easy grader as long as you dont go above and beyond. you never have to work hard, hes very simple, and you dont NEED to read the chapters to the books, just be vaguely relating to topic. You will excel and hes better than the other teachers 100%

A really easy class to take for education and non education majors. You do use the textbook and have to buy another work book from main street which is a must have for class. There is quite a bit of group work but its all very easy. If you miss class you'll be more than fine. You can find answers for chapter questions on quizlet too 10/10

Granger is awesome. He is a really chill guy and gets along well with all his students. At first his class seems a little intimidating but you really start to warm up to his style of teaching. The class is mainly structured by students teaching students but the way he organizes it really works and helps.

Professor Granger is great! the class is intriguing especially for education major sbecause its about education in America. his lectures can get boring occasionally, but he is very nice and genuinly cares about his students. accomodating to students and easy to communicate with. The class is not a lot of work and it is interesting

comment: Professor Granger's class has been my favorite so far at Geneseo. He gives you a syllabus in the beginning with what you will do every day for the rest of the semester so you always know what to expect. Be prepared to read the textbook (which is not a bad read) and you will be set. Only two exams, two essays, and one final project.

Professor Granger is a really nice guy and his class is relatively easy. As long as you participate and study for the tests, you should be okay. The final project is kind of heavy but as an education major, you're kind of stuck with it no matter what you do. Overall a great teacher and very understanding and caring about his students!

Had him for HUM220, got an A with some ease. Just show up to classes, pay attention and take decent notes (along with trying to read a good chunck of material and you'll do good). We had small quiz or two, our tests were 2 shorts essays, and we had 3 essays throughout the semester. He'll help you improve your writing. Hoping to get him for HUM221.

Very easy class, He only gave 1 quiz the entire semester. 3 easy essays, and only two tests (Midterm and Final), plus he told us what the topics were for the final. There are multiple group discussions throughout the semester. Diligent note-taking  during lectures, and spark-noting is plenty to get you through the discussions, essays, and tests.
Easiest class I have taken so far. Great guy, easy grader. Knows a lot about the topic. Classes are repetitive (group discussion one day, presentation the next), but I didn't mind. Only two tests.

Granger was clear and professional. The material was easy to understand and also interesting. He showed a tolerance for student opinion as well. His comments on tests and papers were helpful, and he stuck to the rubric provided.
As a last semester senior, this class was amazing! Interesting but not unnecessarily difficult or stressful. If you show up and read SparkNotes even 12 of the time, you're going to get an A.
Such a nice professor. So impressed by how well he knows his material and how he strives to make sure his students understand what is going on. And, he makes the material interesting.

Granger realizes that this class is a somewhat lame prereq. for education majors, and tries to make it as laid back as possible. Reading assigments once or twice a week, 3 response papers(2-3 pgs), 1 "beliefs" paper(3 pgs), 1 presentation, tests are short answer + an essay.
Take humm with granger.  You will not be disappointed.  Wants kids to actually get something out of the class rather than always worrying about a letter grade so his class is laid back and very easy.

Definitely recommended for Humanities. I took it the first time with a different professor and failed so I'm re-taking it with Granger and will probably get an A-. Overall, Humanities is a heavy course but Granger makes it manageable and fun.
He strives to be helpful, and he's soo nice! He makes me want to do the readings, and his discussions are engaging. I would recommend him to anyone.
Dr Granger is a great teacher.  He is very clear, his tests are straight forward.  Everything on the tests are have been emphasized in class.  Nice guy, helpful.  Take him
We do the same rountine for most classes which can be good and bad. There are 4 papers and a midterm and a final. Overall not a bad class.

Really easy hum professor. Really engaging in class and really funny. I dont dread this class with Granger at all. Less reading than all other Hum professor. You can just sparknotes all of them and you will be fine. He only tests on what is said in class and he gives you soo many choices on papers and exam questions. I am taking him for hum 2

Love Professor Granger.  He is fair and understanding of students and their needs.  Very predictable which is awesome! Does not grade papers hard based on their grammar...but more for their content.  He is open-minded and welcomes and validates everyones input on a subject.  I rearrange my schedule to get classes with him.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Quite a boring Professor.  Every day in class is the same.  The textbook is useless and just getting through the questions is torture.  Fairly easy grader but gives everyone in the class the same grade for all the papers (89, 91, 93, 94) in that order.  I recommend steering clear of this professor for INTD 203.

Awesome Prof.  Class is easy and predictable.  Group work almost every class.  Some days he lectures more than others. Some powerpoint presentations. Midterm, Final and 3 papers, but he gives you lots of choices for all.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

He is a nice guy and cracks little jokes here and there that are actually quite funny.  The class is boring and predictable, but I like knowing what to expect.  The only bad thing is that there's only two tests and each of them covers 8 chapters!  4-5 papers and presentation.
He is a nice guy but he is really boring.  The class material is not that interesting and he does little to change things up.  Not a hard class but not a lot of fun either.
This teacher was very nice and helpful.  Class is predictable but I enjoyed that.  If you read it will be easy.

Dr. Granger is soo helpful. Goes out of his way for his students and he's so easy to talk to. Do your readings, come to class, and discuss important issues. You'll be fine. Yeah, its kind of redundant but he makes the class interesting!

This class is a joke. One day you do group work. The next day you watch someone's group present to the class. Repeat these two exercises over and over and over for 20 weeks. Easy class but boring. Exams are easy as long as you study the notes you make or from the book. he's very generous with partial credits on exams
Granger is really helpful in this class. He grades relatively easily and he knows what he's talking about. The material may be dry but he keeps the class interesting with group discussion.
He really wants to get to know all his students and is interested in your improvement.

This is a boring class but Professor Granger does what he can to help us learn the materials. He is very relaxed and easy going. Always willing to help. And he grades fairly and somewhat easily. I loved taking this class with him!

You have to take this boring class so you might as well take Granger cuz he is SO EASY. his tests are a JOKE. you do group work every other class and it's based on the textbook. Incredibly passionate about his topic of choice...prepare to be exposed to the arts.  Monotone lecturing and awkward silences often in class but he gives great help with writing.

He is very nice and knows what he's talking about.  His writing assignments are broad but he gives a chance for re-writes and his revisions help out a lot.  The reading was confusing at times times but he cleared this up in class discussion.  Overall, I would consider taking another of his classes.
Fair grader, nice guy.  His class is very discussion oriented- a lot of reading, but take this class with him if you can!
the class isn't bad. the reading is hard at first but he explains it well. no tests, the only grades you get are the papers, which arent really that hard. a little boring but an easy A.
Boring but easy.
Class was boring, but the tests were easy and the papers wern't bad.

All the comments about class structure and predictability are correct. I liked him a lot and he was a nice guy. I felt guilty cuz I stopped going. His papers were easy and his tests would have been, if I had prepared at all or at least attended class.
The class was very boring but easy. The reading was difficult but he clarified it in class. He is very easy to work with and very helpful.

This class has TONS of reading but there's no way around it. He is by far the best Intd 203 professor. Classes are very predictable and involve a lot of in class small group discussions. If you have to take this class take it with him!

VEry structured class...wish he would allow class to discuss certain issues more in depth b/c he tends to dominate the discussions.  All in he is an open minded guy who likes to hear a lot of dif. views.....def. best to take this class w/ him

classes were very structured so that you knew what was going on each day in class. very easy grader if you tell him what he wants to hear. after talking to other people in intd203, he is the best teacher for this course.

He's a philosophy professor, so if you like not having specific guidelines for papers, he's good. Also, he is very interested in helping the students. And yea, he does take attendance. But overall, it is a very easy A.
Very nice guy, although the class itself isn't very interesting, he does try very hard to mix it up. Takes attendance
He is such a great professor and a very easy grader. But he does take attendence so you have to go to class.

LOVED Mrs. Ridler. Definitely goes in the rare gem section of professor sorting. She clearly cares about what she teaches and actually made class bearable most days. Dr. Ridler is the kindest professor I have ever had. She went out of her way to make zoom school enjoyable and took time to get to know students as best as she could while being online. He is a really funny guy. The exams were tricky but the papers were easy.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Was very skeptical of abstract art before taking his course but he completely opened my eyes to it. super helpful with anything you need for your project from advice to fixing broken equiptment. absolutely LOVED this class allows you to do almost anything you can think of for your projects

Are you looking for an easy grade and some arts and crafts? Then Dan is not for you. Do you want to be challenged and make some serious art? Then this is the professor to take. fun class, very flexible about design ideas. He's helpful and easy to talk to. Also a major babe.
Dan is awesome, I highly recommend taking any of his classes.

The guy is just terrible.  Unless you play his game, you aren't going to do well in his class. He's always late for class.  He doesn't respond to emails, phone class, or anything.  He only helps the people he likes.  I'm pretty sure I didn't learn ANYTHING about art this semester.
leaves the class room in the midle of class  lectures are incurate and very arrogant

I would definitley recommend his classes, he's an awsome professor.

Hardworking professor! He makes a lot of interesting and awesome art works!! Remember to go to see his recent show “A Set of Separate but Related Moments” in E3 Gallery! = D
Amazing. I love this class already. He is so much fun. Not just a professor, but also a cool and nice guy.
Great teacher.  Really interested in his students' work and always willing to help.  It's pretty difficult to get an A, but he's a fair grader.
Good professor, knows his stuff, but grades pretty harshly on assignments, and doesn't always seem to take into account artists capabilities.

Awesome professor- will spend any amount of time you need helping you-- As a bonus, he's is very active in the campus outside of the art dept- AWESOME characteristic you won't find in hardly any other professor
good teacher, good class.  i actually learned alot too.

Geneseo dean needs to start weeding out these professors who are only there to talk about themselves and not positive and actually teach so students learn.

worst marketing professor ever... too arrogant... and he looks mad everyday... this professor oh damn... totally lost my interest in marketing

Lectures can be dry but you only can miss a certain amount before he deducts from your grade. If you listen to lectures and study the power-points you'll do well on the tests. The group projects are easy.
