I'm an A student, I never get B. But I got C from this course. I spent at least 4~7 hours a day to try to keep up with the course materials. But, you can't expect that what you learn from class will be on the test. Grading is arbitrary, he doesn't care about the type of problems for test, he just simply take them even it's not what we've learnt.

class test averages were in the 60s, literally impossible if you dont study and practice them. dont even bother with going to lectures. and his classes are so boring, suggest not taking this unless u absolutely need to

Got an A.  If you can do the practice exams within 1.5 hours you're good for the tests (and open notes if you need them).  He goes through stuff fast, but will answer any questions you have.  Even so, you'll be teaching yourself a lot of the time. People seem to be down on this guy, but I think he's decent.
Just review old exams. Everything is open notes. I was worried at first because he just told you do it all on your own, but ir is manageable. Just go over old exams before a test.
wow. good luck.
terrible teacher. i withdrew from his class but unfortuantely i'll have to take it again and he's the only professor who teaches the course! :0
here's the book-lemme know if you need any help aka the course in a nutshell (averages on tests were in the 60s)-however you WILL teach yourself this material and you WILL learn it because you did

Fairly straightforward class.  Don't really need to go to class as long as you know how to do examples on his practice tests.  If you know them, the real tests aren't bad at all.  I got 90s on them all.

Where do I even begin? I wanted to learn and maybe I did. But tests that compromise 90% of our final grade that are IMPOSSIBLE TO FINISH ON TIME are not representative of my skills as a student. Truly ridiculous. 10 % is devoted to a project which is a complete joke and a waste of time.

So the class seems easy, but the tests (which are 90% of the grade) are awful! Not only are they long but they're not like class information at all. Horn doesn't teach, and is more of a mentor. He is unhelpful and confusing. I really detest this class, even if some of it's useful information, it isn't presented as it should be. UGHHHHH

He's nice and an easygoing person but his lectures are hard to understand and not interesting. Go to his office hours a lot to go over your paper because he could grade it down if there's one thing you didn't cover because he didn't tell you to.

The class is pretty easy, but he is not the best at explaining things. You should definitely read the book because he will talk about things in lecture that you would not understand if you hadn't read the chapter. He is a very nice man and will pretty much write your programs for you if you ask him to help you.

Lectures are, well, boring. I struggled a lot with labs too. However, if you go to see him for office hours, it's better to get help from him; if you try to get attention during a lab you'll probably end up with your hand sticking up in the air for a while- too many people asking questions at once. Not bad, but not great either.
It's an easy class, but you really don't learn much.
Absolutely one of the worst professors i had to suffer through at Geneseo.  Stear clear, this man has no idea how to teach.

Good teacher.  a lot of interesting lab work with spreadsheets.  there is only 2 tests and they are very hard so study up.  I enjoyed the class because you learn a lot of information about using spreadsheets in business.  Good Luck!

Really sweet and a nice person, but kind of a space cadet. Really just takes lectures straight out of the books (images and all) but somehow is still hard to follow. Very soothing voice... made it hard to stay awake. I like her as a person but I struggled with her as a prof. Class wasn't that hard though anyway.

Not a good professor at all. She is nice, but doesn't know much about her subject material, and when questioned by students she rushes to sound like she knows what they're talking about when she doesn't. Very boring. Take the class when someone else is teaching it.

Interesting lectures, easy homeworks right from book that help grade, easy presentation, hard tests, but she grades other assignments easily enough that you should do well as long as you read the book.  Also, she's always willing to help during office hours or shortly after class.

This class was all over the place, and he honestly never seemed to know what was wrong with his code. Tests were more difficult than expected. He's super nice and available outside of class. He also grades your tests with you and gives you a chance to fix your work.

He's a very nice guy/person, but he is terrible as a professor. It's just tough to follow his lectures and curriculum, and I felt like I was teaching myself the entire semester. He also copies things straight from textbooks, which doesn't help. So I would not take another class with him.

Copies note straight from textbook that he told us we had no need to buy/rent. No calculators needed in class. Not good with elaborating on notes or explaining most things. Personally, my pre-calc from hs was not enough prep whatsoever, but also his expectations are high regarding what you should have for knowledge coming into class. Nice guy tho.
A pretty solid math professor at Geneseo, can be difficult to understand sometimes. Not my favorite but a very safe option

Took every class in the book with Ahmad. His use of formula sheets make it very possible to do well on every single test. Tests align with old tests/ study sheets, both accessible. Ahmad is such a genuine/ down to earth human being. I graduated, but if I could take a class with him now, I would. Would love to have a beer with him, awesome guy.
He's one of the best math professors I've ever had!

Dr. Almomani is an exceptional math professor. His ability to break down complex concepts into simple, understandable steps made learning enjoyable and engaging. His dedication, patience, and genuine passion for teaching created an inspiring and supportive learning environment, and I am deeply grateful for his impact on my education.

I had him for 230 and it was by far the worst class I've taken at Geneseo. Painfully disorganized - he showed up to each class without a plan and relied on students with prior coding knowledge to "teach" the class. Homework and exams were brutal and grading was very subjective. Weekly tutoring was needed to survive this class. Avoid at all costs!!!

Coming from some experience with calculus in high school, I had a slight advantage, but still found his tests to be very difficult. Homework and quizzes are easy, but tests are very difficult. Very nice guy and his lectures were really good. Review notes, and examples he posts because some test questions are exact.

Very nice guy, very fair grader. Tests are hard, but he gives a lot of points for what you can get done. Weekly homework online through cengage, gave us a free textbook link. Overall super wonderful teacher. Was very accessible through office hours, and always willing to answer questions. Teaches in a way so you do better in high level courses.

Prof. Almomani is a terrific professor who always looks out for his students. He gives out extra practice for each topic, which helps a lot and is sometimes even on quizzes or exams. Although the coursework is tough for those who take the course for Edu requirements, he makes sure to take time for students. Exam scores are given back in good time!

Professor Almomani is a great professor and person. Yes, this class can be difficult because it is a higher-level math course. However, professor Almomani does everything in his power to help all of his students understand the material. He is very understanding and gives a lot of partial credit and extra credit. He also makes Calc 2 fun! :)

I hated this class, I have never cried so much over a class before in my life. The tests were very difficult, it felt like he took the hardest examples from class and put them on the test for fun. During one of the exams he gave probably 45 extra minutes because no one was finishing on time. The homework assignments were very hard and took hours.

Absolutely the best professor I've ever had. This is a difficult class but he makes sure everyone knows what's going on . Made it clear he wants his students to succeed and obviously loves what he does. Really nice guy and a really great professor. Highly recommend taking a class with him, I would take every math class with him if I could
I have never had a math teacher who has made me not fear math but he creates a comfortable environment. He also is probably one of the most understanding and caring professors I have ever had.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Caring']
comment: Professor Almomani is amazing! He is always willing to help outside of class and provides his students with all the necessary tools to succeed. Tests can be challenging, but he offers the opportunity to replace your lowest test grade if you score progressively better on each exam. You must attend class to do well! He is a sweet, understanding man!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']
comment: I loved Professor Almomani!! I am a Bio major and Math is really my favorite, but Almomani made it enjoyable. The tests tend to be hard, but if you study youll do fine. I definitely recommend taking him if you have to take Calc 2.
El mejor profesor que he tomado en mi vida. No duden en tomarlo!

He has honestly been one of my best professors here at geneseo. He is very easy to read and his tests and quizzes set you up for success. He gives ample feedback on all of the responses and has a lot of opportunities to allow you to receive extra points. He wants people to pass and wants us to feel good about putting in the work and succeeding

Make sure you watch the movies she posts on the syllabus because they will be referenced in exams. Exams are online and you have ample time to complete them. There is a class participation grade but I barely went and still got an 80. Just make sure you do all the readings and questions for homework.

Maggie Rex is one of those professors that gets what it's like to be a student. Her lectures, tests and assignments are extremely straight forward and solely based on presentations. She does not allow any laptops however but for most people that was not an issue as she posts the presentations on canvas. Would defiantly take again.
Great professor! She was so passionate when taking about sociology.

Professor Rex is one of the most agreeable, interesting, and insightful professors I have encountered here at Geneseo. The class was very relaxed, but tackled super important issues in a really refreshing and interesting way. She is very responsive and easy to talk to, and has open note, take-home tests. She makes sure that everyone can succeed!

professor Rex is an amazing sociology professor, she makes the class so interesting with visuals and talks about relatable shit. tests are super easy but notes are definitely required. No computers or phones are allowed in class

He embodies kindness, dignity, and compassion, and has left a beautiful mark on my life that I will never forget. Despite my language difficulties, he excelled at teaching me and understanding my needs. Words cannot do him justice; he deserves the utmost appreciation and respect.

Dr. Markowski is a nice guy, but a bad professor. We skipped over many topics because he would spend weeks going off on tangents about small things. He doesn't allow you to make up unplanned class activities. Tests are impossible and asks questions about stuff that's not in the textbook or was never talking about in class. Avoid if you can.
Literally the worst professor I have ever had.

absolutely TERRIBLE professor, his exams are impossible and are not related to class lectures at all. Grade in class in only based on three exam scores and one group project which are impossible to do well on. He never responds to his email and is a terrible communicator. The class is not the problem, the professor is.
DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR PSYC251!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I cannot emphasize this enough, you will 1000% be better off taking someone else.
Nothing like he teaches biopsych! Take home exams and not too difficult. I definitely recommend taking this class with him, but make sure you show up.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I love Dr. Markowski... however I also love to study. Dedicate 3 hours a day to studying you will get an A. He will tell you what sections in the text book are fair game, you have to read ALL of it. His lectures are entertaining to me... and he has lots of office hours. Grading is tight, only 55 points. Meaning no more than 5 points off for an A.

If I could rate him a 0 I would. His tests are awful. His lectures are rambling and get so confusing. He doesn't accommodate you at all and doesn't care about you or your grades. IMPOSSIBLE to reach him outside the classroom, he doesn't answer emails at all. My experience with him is THE WORST experience I have ever had with a teacher/professor!!

Did not organize lectures well. Topics kept being pushed to the next test and the final exam covered a broad range of topics with not adequate time to go over them all. I got A's on the first 2 tests and D's on the last 2 bc lecture quality went down. Go into this course with any professor ready to spend a lot of time and effort
He was awful

He's a very knowledgeable, captivating professor who does more than a reasonable amount of work to help you learn the subject matter. Still, he made us watch a cringy video once. So, I have to give him a very negative review.

Dr. Markowski is genuinely one of the funniest most caring professors who really wants his students to do well in his classes. I had him for Biopsych which is a tough class but his lectures were so funny and entertaining. If you get the opportunity to take a class with him do it!!

Grade is completely dependent on test scores, attendance is mandatory. He doesn't use the powerpoint to lecture he just talks. He also does multiple choice questions in class that count for like 10% of your grade. Tests are only like 20ish questions so if you get a few questions wrong you're screwed. He does drop the lowest test grade which helps.

Vincent Markowski is the worst professor I have ever had. I studied so hard for his exams and failed every single one. There is only 20 questions on each test and no curve. You're only graded on exams and final project. I am a hard working third year student and I have not failed a course until this one. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ANYONE ELSE.

I don't want to give him a bad review because he is a very good teacher but his tests are impossible. There will be stuff on the exam that the textbook covered that he has never talked about. The best bet is showing up to class but his lectures can be very boring because he goes through maybe two slides per class.

He is funny and very good at describing things, but biopsych will by no means be an easy class. Your grade is just exams, a group project, and attendance. If you don't test well, I wouldn't suggest taking him. With that being said, he very clearly explains things and wants input from students. He is a good professor despite being a difficult grader

Overall he is a good teacher, a lot of in class assignments with groups so if you don't show up it will effect your grade, although each assignment is graded out of 3 points. Good luck getting him to answer a single email, you have to see him in person in order for your questions to be answered. Gives good feedback on papers though.

Yes, he was a goodish teacher but he is so boring. so boring. He takes forever to answer email, you have to try and catch him after class or if you need to email him you need to do it days ahead of when you want him to answer. I like that he is helpful with paper feedback and that we did little partner things too. He basically reads off the slides.

I had him for a neuroscience class and he was awful. He's nice and not boring to listen to but you will not be able to get a hold of him outside of class. you only have 4 tests and maybe 2 other class assignments. You are graded by very little things so there is literally no room for error. He grades on a point system which makes 0 sense. stay away

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']
comment: Contrary to popular belief he is a good prof. Not only has he helped me pass this class and grasp a better understanding of the concepts, but he also is very dedicated to what he does. He gives great feed back on the paper that you have to write, and is always willing to help you if you put in the work. Its work but so is every psych 251 section.

I was disappointed with having him as a professor. It never helped me when I wasn't doing good in the class; he listened to my problems but didn't help me resolve them or offer anything to help. "study better". Every test is worded horribly.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Markowski is an okay professor. Can be confusing when explaining things. Super long lectures and tests are extremely difficult. Also, there is no running tally of grades in Canvas, if you want to do well there is tons of work.

Class is a drag, but that's due a lot to the subject matter. He is impossible to reach outside of class. He never responded to emails and provided zero support during online classes. Rescheduled our final twice and told us nothing about the format. The day of, he never posted the exam and no one could reach him.

The semester-long paper project wasn't too bad, but he provides the rubric he uses to grade it after you hand in the assignments. Would've liked a little more direction with the requirements for each section, but overall not bad. He seems like a nice guy, had him online so it's hard to tell

Markowski is a fair or even lenient grader, but he seems unwilling to give 100. He is clearly knowledgeable. He did not give rubrics or specifics about projects. He is not good at communicating via email. He also required synchronous quizzes for an asynchronous class, and was not good at communicating about resolving it for multiple students.

Dr. Markowski knows what he is talking about it and explains things in an effective way, often using examples. However, he is very unresponsive to emails and the class is graded mostly on tests. Use your TA for review. I took his class during COVID so Markowski himself wasn't very accessible.

Just dont. Dr. Markowski is the hardest professor to get ahold of. I could never find him for help. I felt disregarded. He said hed review my paper and then at the end of the year said haha I forgot. He is boring and the other professors available for the courses he teaches are so much better.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'So many papers']
comment: I really don't get why people hate Dr. Markowski so much. He can be tough with tests and doesn't respond much to emails, but he's accessible in office (which wasn't possible due to COVID, which sucked). If you take good notes in class, his tests are totally doable. The paper project is graded pretty easily too. Just show up and listen.

He does not answer emails at all. He is inconsiderate and does not care about students. This pandemic really showed Markowskis true colors. He did not change his expectations or students, did not answer emails , and was not understanding of everyones unique situation of how being home.

I had him as an adviser. he is absolutely rubbish, does not help or care about his students, and very discouraging, talked to him first semester freshmen year about my low 3 GPA, he said my grade is to low for Med school, I did not listen to him and worked hard and now I'm on track to get into medical school. Don't let anyone bring you down!

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: He's unresponsive to emails. I do not like the lack of feedback he gives his students. He's lectures are decent. He explains the material, but he expects students to pick up on the information quickly as if biopsychology is an easy topic. I wouldn't recommend him.

Worst Professor Ever. He doesn't reply to e-mail when several students are confused and has to the most unclear directions for assignments and expects us to figure it out by ourselves. HE does not care about the student's success and is quite frankly a terrible teacher.
I really liked how during lectures everything wasnt written on the board. He talked slow so everyone could understand and process what we were learning.
If Lord Voldemort existed in real life his name would be Vincent Markowski.

You get graded on 3 exams, 1 group project, and "participation " points. His exams ask the most obscure questions, not on any of the main information in the book. His participation points aren't really just participation, he only gives you points if you are correct. If you ask for help outside of class, he just tells you to make flashcards.
I really dislike Markowski his tests are very difficult and specific

Take an intro bio class before Markowski's class... your grade will thank you. He is a great lecturer and will spend more than enough time on the slides and discussing topics and questions from students but you have to be prepared to study REALLY hard if you want that great grade. Overall he is a nice guy and you will learn a lot.

I don't know why he has such bad reviews! I love this professor, he's such a good lecturer, stays on the power points for like 5 minutes each and explains everything in lots of detail to make sure we all understand. It's definitely not an easy class at all, but its expected but if you work hard and study you will do fine!

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Loved him in lecture. Solid lectures that were rarely boring. There is a LOT of material and you have to know it really well. If you don't read you will do awful on tests. His tests are very hard and extremely specific. Prepare to read and study hard.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Tests are tough']
comment: Honestly if you put in the work and really try, a good grade is really attainable. He is pretty straight forward with what he wants and his tests are hard but manageable if you go to lecture and read the textbook. There is one group project which he grades very fairly and there are clicker questions in every class

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Markowski is clearly very passionate about the subject, and he likes to tell a lot of really funny stories to help you connect ideas. Class is always interesting. A good amount of tested material comes from the textbook, so you HAVE to read. Also - he barely puts anything on his slides, he mostly speaks, so you have to go to class.

Do anything you can to take this class with another teacher. Half way through the semester he added a new condition to the paper that forced everyone to go back and reshape everything. He does not explain what he expects from you but is an extremely harsh grader. He does not test out of the textbook but doesn't give you enough data in class.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Great 251 professor! Very clear in what he expects from students. Grading is fair, and he gives helpful feedback. Tests are somewhat difficult, but if you attend class/read the book, they're manageable. Go to his office hours if you have questions. Speak up in class.  Lastly, if there's a TI, use him/her! Great class overall.

I really liked Markowski at first - he's definitely better than other psych 251 professors I've heard about. Although it's a dry subject, he tries his best to engage students. He explains grades and is pretty clear in what he wants. I was getting all As and Bs which is why I was confused when I received a C at the end of the semester for no reason.

Funnyapproachable, very passionate about his field. You get assigned a paper and presentation (one due midway + other due by finals). Paper was a struggle but he's an easy grader. 4 tests drops lowest. Read the textbook over once and reread the notes from class and you're all set. In-class electronic questions are graded for attendance.

Worst professor I've had at Geneseo. He never even taught us the last 3 chapters, which was the entire last exam. He had us read it from the text. He is not helpful at office hours and often isn't there or tells you to come back another time. His paper grading is completely arbitrary. He never answers emails. He is rude and arrogant. Do not take.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I've taken orgo, genetics, ecology, cell... THIS was my lowest grade. He makes it impossible to get a good grade. I'd give him draft after draft and he would say it looked great then give me a 75. I put so much time and effort into this class. He never answers emails and never tells you what he wants. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

drop this before you even begin. save your GPA while you can. Case and point: I took calc, chem, bio, and chem lab the same semester and THIS CLASS was my lowest grade. I spent just as much if not more time on trying to get through this hell of a class as I did on all my other classes.

Literally the worst professor ever. Never responds to emails, never explains what he wants. Went to his office hours after EVERY CLASS determined to get straight answers and help, instead getting condescending comments, told to "consult literature", or literally asked to leave because he had other meetings to get to (during his office hrs...).

Lectures are great. Test questions are from the test bank that comes from the book publisher. You can read the book 3 times and still wonder where the hell the questions came from. VERY difficult class. Uses clickers to grade on attendance, participation & understanding of material. He was VERY helpful when I approached him.

I thought he was great. Best professor I've had at Geneseo. The class was interesting. If you had questions after class he was willing to answer them. If you paid attention to class the test were fairly easy. I didn't read the book much although it helps with the tests.

This teacher was horrible. He had very straight forward lectures that seemed like very simple material in class but the tests were hard and completely based off the textbook. The semester long paper was also hard. He would give you an outline and then never grade based on that outline. He doesn't answer emails and doesn't help during office hours.
Arrogant and doesn't respond to emails or give assignments back in a timely manner. If you can avoid him; DO!

Very difficult professor. In class material seems very self explanatory but tests are ridiculously hard even with hours of studying. Also he gives outlines for the papers but doesn't follow them in grading.Very unhelpful as well in office hrs (if hes actual there and not at the gym) many times wouldnt answer questions and ask "what do you think?"

Dr. Markowski is a great professor. He knows what he is talking about and is very clear with both his lectures and his expectations. As long as you read the chapter and study the power points before each exam you will be fine. Work through the paper at a steady pace and GO TO OFFICE HOURS with questions. He is more than willing to help.

Great guy, good sense of humor and really helpful. He appreciates it if you go to his office hours and show you are putting in effort. Pretty dry material, but he keeps it interesting with class activities. Definitely read the textbook and know all key words & definitions. Tough grader but still possible to do really well in his class!

Dr. Markowski's field of study is biopsychology, and it certainly shows when he attempts to teach 251.  His lectures are scattered, have no direction, and are almost entirely irrelevant to what he tests you on.  I can honestly say that I don't remember anything we learned in that class, but if 251 is taught right it's a very helpful class.

He is a good professor and a really good guy. Very easy going, lectures can be slightly dull but there is almost always groupwork and discussion to break it up. Very willing to help with whatever you need. Only thing I would mention is this: He seems so easy going that you expect grading to be easy, but are not really that easy so I was unprepared

Biopysch is a difficult class to begin with, especially if you're not biologically orientated (like myself), however, Dr. Markowski was able to explain the material in a clear understandable way.  His exams are fair,just read the book and look over the powerpoints and you should be more than fine. He's helpful (and willing to help) outside of class

He's a great guy who can be really helpful at office hours. He seems to have a hard trouble keeping up with the syllabus, and isn't really clear with the information. Nice guy but you have to do work outside of the class to maneuver through the tests.

Tests cover a lot of stuff that he doesn't cover in class. Make sure you at least get the bolded words from the book down before exam. The multiple choice are hard but only worth .5 point and the matching and short answer are really easy and worth 1 point (each matching) and 5 points for 1 short answer.

Do not take with him. So boring. He's a very nice guy, but he doesn't cover any material in class and he grades a 50 point test out of 30. You go into the test not knowing what you're supposed to have learned because lectures tell you nothing, and the book is even worse. Also have to purchase a $40 iclicker.

Professor Kang has made my interest in law, politics, and government increase significantly. In class, I didn't just learn for the sake of being able to study for an exam or how to write the final paper. I learned in a way that helped me to navigate better how politics operate in our daily lives. This is a good skill to have, especially today.

She shows up late for every single class including on exam days. It's very unprofessional and not fair that she shows up late and deducts time off our exams. The exams were difficult to pass if you didn't memorize all the PowerPoint slides. Very unorganized and flustered in lecture. Don't waste your time taking her class!!!!

She gives straight forward tests (multiple choice/fill in the blank/ true false) which are based on in class notes (powerpoint). Takes attendance daily. I think she is hilarious I really enjoy her lectures- if you take good notes and study them you'll get an A

Showed up at at least 8:45 for an 8:30 class every day while attendance was taken at 8:30. Spends half the class reviewing what was learned last class making it very boring. Is extremely strict and doesn't allow students to leave class. Very awkward when participating in class. Easy tests and class but wouldn't recommend her as a prof.

Professor Kang is a really nice person, but for a 100 level class, she treated it as a 300 level. Essays were sometimes unclear, and out of 3 tests, 2 of them were mostly fill in the blank with no word bank. It was cumulative, so you needed to know everything. but other than that, she clears things up when you talk to her individually.

Although Prof Rahimkhani is a sweetheart I disliked his teaching methods. We went over the same things over again throughout the whole semester. The class moves slowly and is far from dynamic learning. Unfortunately he is a fairly uninteresting teacher. I felt unengaged and bored during most lectures and most students seem'ed to feel the same.

Rahimkhani is hands down one of the best professors in the Political Science department. He believes multiple choice tests do not define a person therefore the few tests he gives are on one or two chapters with less than 15 easy questions. The only thing he really cares about is the essay at the end, but he guides you and is very supportive. 10/10.
Really nice professor. Very helpful outside of the class and during the office hours. So if you study it's not hard. Would recommend him for comparative over other professors.

Although Rahimkhani had a heart of gold, he did not make a good teacher. His lectures were confusing, disengaging, and uninformative bc he couldn't translate his thoughts into words well. He was vague about test dates, chapter assignments, and paper deadlines  none are on the syllabus, you MUST regularly go to class where he says them verbally.
Super, super nice man, very caring for students. If you read the textbook , go to the lectures and study adequately an A is easy.

He's a very reasonable and down-to-earth guy. He goes easier on grading depending on the performance of the class. I feel bad as it seems like he was sort of put into the position of teaching this class last minute. Lectures tend to be boring and not helpful for the tests, if they tied in more with exams then I reckon attendance would be better.
This professor was useless. I asked to help me out a couple of times but was rude about it. I have taken several online courses and by far it was the worst with her. Never again. Dont taker her!
Was a super nice professor, quite helpful, final was fairly long but nothing too difficult if you paid any sort of attention at all during the semester.
so easy and shes so nice

Easy class. No tests, just a few quizzes which you do in groups. The final is take home, but took awhile to complete. One long research paper towards the end of class, which if you know APA format, you'll get an A. Class was fun and she was always enthusiastic. Outlines for the chapters in the book were graded every class

Was disappointed. She made us read the chapter before class and do a (outline) reading assignment. Went to class knowing the material. PP were just outlining what we read the night before. "Quizzes" were group work. Papers just needed to be in perfect APA format for good score. Final at home exam was way too specific and way too long. Do not take.

Prof. Meyer was great and super understanding. There is a lot of reading in the textbook and with links she gives in Brightspace. However, these readings are not needed to still do well in the class. If you pay attention in lecture, take notes, the class is somewhat easy. On her exam reviews she gives the test questions word for word, basically.

Professor Meyer is one of the most caring teachers i've had. She is extremely understanding of situations. Her lectures can be hard to follow but if you do everything required you will do good in the course. Professor Meyer is also a light grader who just wants you to succeed

She is very passionate about her teaching and it shows. While her lectures are very talk-heavy, she does give students lots of materials to help enforce the information. Her tests are also very easy, as the study guide almost 1:1 resembles the questions that'll be on the exam. She is also a nice grader, so it's impossible to actually fail.

The class was mainly enjoyable, she knew what she was talking about, lectures could get boring, and sometimes the class was sued as a political push instead of a learning environment which I didn't love. The papers were not that bad and easy enough to get good grades with little effort. She gives exam guides which are really nice too.
She knows what she is talking ab but the lectures were a tad boring.

Absolute sweetheart. When I had an incident with the testing center, helped me rectify it and allowed me to retake the exam at no penalty. Extremely accessible & concerned with the well-being of her students. Only mark against her is that she doesn't provide notes ahead of time, but she explains her reasoning well.

Dr. Meyer is an incredible teacher. She is always willing to help inside and outside of class. Spends time in class on videos and talks about them all. The slideshows are a little boring as they all are the same style with no pictures but she brings joy to the work. The tests are easy and she gives all the questions to you before the exam.
Meyer is super nice; I thought the material was interesting but the way it was presented a lot of the time was a little dull. Pretty easy to talk to and she grades really fair. Nothing crazy though.
Dr Meyer is amazing she is so understanding and perfectly prepares you for all assignments also she is just a very good person

If you're just starting the Sociology major/minor, this class is a must-take. The professor is nice, caring, and definitely wants students to do more than just pass the class. There are 2 papers and 3 exams for this class and the discussion posts are graded by completion. Exam questions are ripped straight from the review guides. easy A if you try.

Although I wasn't particularly in love with the material and class itself this professor made it so much more bearable. I didn't do well on the first test, and she asked me to meet with her, I did a lot better from there on out. She wants you to succeed and will help you I highly recommend class with her she is passionate about what she teaches.
One of the nicest professor I have had, she truly cares for her student and is so nice. lectures are fun and you get to watch a bunch of movies in class too

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: She was so nice and caring. She went kinda fast during lectures but explained things well. She's clear on what to study for, reading isn't super necessary but would definitely get you better grades on the tests for providing examples.

Prof. Meyer is an amazing and kind professor. Her lectures are very informative and interesting.  There are a lot of outside reading requirements but nothing overwhelming.  She also gives you the exam questions prior to the test.

Only take this class if you're interested in the subject- it's a lot of work. Weekly online discussions, tests are ridiculously long (3 two-four page essays then a 3.5-7 page essay) but she gives you 2 weeks to do them. Also an 8 page research paper. There were times I had no idea what she was talking about because of the language she was using.
This professor was amazing. She was always understanding of my awful mental health. I would take this professor again.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I love lisa!!! the only thing that was difficult was that she lectured very fast and if you missed something, she doesnt post the lectures until the week before an exam which isnt very helpful. Make a group chat w/ people in ur class and study with them!

Lisa is the nicest lady. The class I took with her is not my best subject so it was kinda hard for me but she's a superrr easy grader. Every class is just notes but she is very knowledgable. There are two small papers and 3 tests.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: If you attend class and participate you will certainly do well. She provides students with everything they need to succeed.

I had Prof Meyer for Gender and Development. Her lectures are interesting, and she is extremely knowledgeable about what she is talking about. The questions she puts in PowerPoint are similar to what is asked on midterm and final. Not really a tough grader, but you should definitely put effort into her assignments. She is super encouraging.

Professor Meyers is such an easy grader and if you attend her lectures you'll have all the material for the exams. Her exams are lengthy but they're online and as long as you have the notes you'll do well. There are two big projects and a few tests but the workload is not bad.If you have the chance to have her as a professor I would take it!

So I took Intro to Soc with Meyer and it was AMAZING. She was so nice and it was an easy A. BUT I signed up to take her SOC281 and it was a whole different world. Tests were 4 essay questions which she expected to be 20 pages long and we had a long research paper too.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Professor Meyer gives great feedback for reports, and she is very enthusiastic when during lectures. She was very engaging and was passionate in the material, she was a great professor to have. The only con of being in Professor Meyers class is that she gives a plethora of reading assignments.

Professor Meyers definitely cares about her students and is very passionate about global social change and it comes through in her lectures. The most important part about doing good in this class is attending the lectures because they provide the all the information for exams and discussion posts. You really don't even have to do the readings.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']
comment: Dr. Meyer lectured for the entire class without taking a breath, and then didn't post the lectures unless you begged her to. So, if you miss even one word of the lecture, you will struggle with the two assignments and midterm/final (which were 4 separate papers, by the way). She is very nice, though.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Caring']
comment: Professor Meyer was accommodating this semester and really cares about students doing well. If you go to class, get the notes, and fill out the exam review guides, you're good to go. There are 2 major assignments that as long as you get done, she grades fairly. Overall, prepare for a bit of reading, but nothing unmanageable.
Accepts most late work, class enjoyable enough but often boring, not exciting- more a chore, she didn't always give great explanations

So, I decided to take Sociology 105 class expecting this class to be an introductory level course with light coursework. However, in terms of the PowerPoint slides that she posts for the class along with the exams that she posts, this class more so feels like a level 200-300 course. To give perspective, my first exam for her was 1400 words. Beware.

Professor Meyer is my favorite Soc professor that I've taken in Geneseo. Her lectures give you everything you need for tests so go and take notes and her assignments/tests can be long but are easy and she is not a very hard grader and she's very understanding if you need an extension.

She is the best professor I've had so far. I would say if you go to all the lectures, you probably won't have to do the readings because they both cover the same material, but skimming the readings is good to find examples. The tests aren't too hard if you do the review sheet and the assignments are slightly lengthy but easy.

Gives a review sheet for all exams and exam questions are taken from the review sheet so you know all the possible questions beforehand. Lectures are really boring because she doesn't stop talking fro the whole hour and 15.

Lisa is an amazing professor, she is extremely passionate about her teaching. She is easy to talk to, and emails back at any time of the day. She provides test outlines that are exactly, or very similar to, the questions on the test. The tests are all writing, though not hard at all. She lectures daily but they're extremely interesting.

She's a really great person. Her lectures are all handwritten, she doesn't like slideshows. You have to go to lecture in order to do well on tests but the answers are honestly all word for word from her notes. The content was very interesting to me.

Wonderful lady! She is very passionate and it shows in her teaching and inspires students. You don't need to read the textbook, you just need to copy down all of her notes because it will appear word for word on the tests, so go to class! Not hard to do well if you put in the work. Fairly easy grader if you know the content. 3 tests and 1 project

Take notes or watch videos all class long. If you skip class you just won't have the notes for that section. She reads off her paper/notes the whole time.3 tests and 2 projects which aren't bad. Need to know the answers to the study guide since the test is made up of questions taken right off of it. Don't need to do the readings but they will help.

She changes the way she teaches the class. When I told my friends what I received for my grades so far they were confused. Most comments were talking about not enough information. This makes no sense because the papers I compared mine to were so much less and they got 100s when I received 80s. She made me hate sociology and do not recommend.

Super passionate about what she does & shows cool videos. Have to put in the work to get an A but I think people's biggest problem would be being too lazy to do so. Picks a few questions off the study guide word for word for tests so do them. Projects are easy. Textbook is good for examples for tests, don't necessarily need to read it all the time.

Super passionate about what she does & brings in lots of interesting stories/videos that relate to the topics. You have to put in the work to get an A but it's by no means difficult. I think people's biggest problem with doing well would be being lazy. Picks a few questions off the study guide word for word for tests so do them. Projects are easy.

amazing professor!!! so passionate about what she teaches and really wants you to do well. go to her office hours and she might even give extra credit! super lenient if you need an extension on anything. great woman!
Two projects and three tests. If you do the study guides and study them religiously, you'll ace the tests. Super nice, many films. My best class right now.

I took Meyer's class last semester, and it was a really enjoyable class. I took it for gen ed credit, and I don't regret it. Her exams can be difficult if you don't know what to expect (I almost failed the first one), but once you get to learn her ways it's possible to get an A. She can be a bit scatterbrained but overall a very interesting class.

Definitely must attend to do well because she doesn't do powerpoints, and the readings are necessary to get an A on the exams but her grading is extremely fair. She is extremely reliable when it comes to emails, and well-read on her information. She's inspirational when it comes to her subject, and highly respectable. Take this class!

I honestly failed the first exam for lack of studying (my fault) but the next two got As on after just doing the reading. She'll respond to every email you send, with paragraphs of information and shes well read on everything she teaches, and highly respectable. You must go to her lectures, because she doesn't do powerpoints but I loved her class.

Professor Meyer is incredible! She is so passionate about her lectures. Don't be fooled by her easy going attitude, she does expect her students to work. Her upper level courses are truly enjoyable and you will learn a lot but it takes a lot of work. Upper level classes have take home exams. Make sure to set time aside for they are time consuming.

Two projects, 3 essay tests. It's pretty straight forward and make sure you do the readings because they will help on exams. Topics interesting and notes easy to follow. Breaks things down pretty good.

Took it online over the summer for two gen ed requirements. Skimmed readings. Two big projects, discussion boards, and an essay test at the end of each week. Such an interesting topic and powerpoints were great and informing! Highly recommend!!!

Didn't really do the readings but the class was pretty straightforward.. She shows a lot of films. Her tests seemed difficult but she is a very easy grader. I think someone turned in their paper late but she seemed pretty accommodating.

Sweetest person ever, very accessible. However, she can be disorganized and sometimes it seems like she doesn't know what she's doing. If you don't understand something use the textbook or go to her office hours because sometimes she explains things better one on one than in a class setting.
Definitely recommend this class! Take it over the summer online its so interesting, not hard if you do the readings.
Fully engaged with the class and with the subject. Not an easy A

She's great! Gives awesome notes and is ready to answer any questions. Throws her views on you a little bit but hey you end up learning a lot of interesting stuff which isn't something I can say about my other classes

Every class is just her ranting about the evils of capitalism. I agree with her on most issues but she spends the entire class preaching her clearly biased views.  The class itself is easy enough aside from the 10-20 page take home test she gives right in the middle of midterm week.
Seriously one of the BEST teachers I have ever encountered at Geneseo. Assigns interesting readings and is happy to answer any questions you have.

Prof Meyer is the sweetest lady on the face of the planet & my favorite professor at Geneseo. Go to class, take good notes, participate, and you don't even have to do the reading unless you're an idiot. Take classes with her!

Great Professor, interesting and fun in lectures and making everyone feel at ease when participate in class. Really inspiring. But Professor Meyer, if you ever read this, would you give less long assignments plz? the longest paper I have ever written was in your class.

Meyer is very sweet and clear and her class is pretty easy to do well because there are not many assignments. She grades easily as well. However, the class was sort of boring because it explained social issues really simply and took a pretty socialist outlook on everything.

Great class! I love prof Meyer, she really enjoys what she does and teaches very well. I didnt read the text  and still did very well, just go to every class and take good notes and you should be fine. The few major assignments you have are pretty tedious, definitely don't save them for the last minute. Tests aren't too bad, as long as you study

Professor Meyer was so fun and she always talked loud and clear for us to stay awake in class. She only believes in take home assignments but they aren't easy at all. If you break it down for one essay question a day, its not so bad. I didn't read the textbook at all and I only attended about half the classes and still got an A-. TAKE HER CLASS!

Great professor! Easy to understand even if you're not good with math), very helpful, reviews before tests and tells you exactly what you need to know. You MUST read the text to understand what's going on, but it's a funny book. Workbook chapter assigned every week. 3 test and a final project (very easy). Take this class with her!

Very interesting course and taught well.  No homework assigned other than a chapter or two before class.  She is very interested in this topic and is very helpful.  However, if you do not like writing, do NOT take this course.

No powerpoints, strict lecture but writes the main points on the board. Take home essays and assignments but they are not a cake walk. Grades on guidelines that are not specified in assignments. Very hard to make an A on take home assignments. She is willing to read over assignments and make comments as many times as you would like

Great professor! I think reading makes tests a lot easier to get through, and class notes also help. Attending class and reading assigned texts would be pretty helpful. Three worksheets (easy!), and a mid-term and final is the course work. My mid-term and final were over fifteen pages, but I don't think that's always necessary. Take her!!

Definitely recommend her for this class. VERY helpful, incredibly nice and easy to talk to. Sometimes gets confused during class but it was never a huge problem for me. Easy A if you hand in weekly assignments. She's probably my favorite professor at Geneseo, take anything she teaches!

Definitely recommend her for this class. VERY helpful, incredibly nice and easy to talk to. Sometimes gets confused during class but it was never a huge problem for me. Easy A if you hand in weekly assignments. She's probably my favorite professor at Geneseo, take anything she teaches!

Definitely recommend her for this class. VERY helpful, incredibly nice and easy to talk to. Sometimes gets confused during class but it was never a huge problem for me. Easy A if you hand in weekly assignments. She's probably my favorite professor at Geneseo, take anything she teaches!

Good teacher. Highly recommended for SOCL 105. If you have any interest in sociology or world affairs, the class is a good, easy choice. No tests, only 3 big TAKEHOME essays and a big TAKEHOME midterm and final. Either read OR go to class- both not necessary. I failed, only because I didn't write the 3rd essay and only did a quarter of the final.

One of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She is super easy to talk to and very helpful, lectures were interesting. There is a lot of writing for this class, but if you go to class and take notes you dont have to do most of the reading to get good grades, just be thorough in your papers. The exams are take home too.

This class was SO easy.  I went to less than half the classes.  You do not even need to read, you will just need the book to help you answer questions on the exams.  The country worksheets were easy.  I got an A without reading or attending class.

Definitely a good class to take.  You don't really need to read the textbook, because all tests are outside class, but I would suggest browsing it, anyway, because she can tell when people don't read.  Her textbooks are a little old, but she ties it all into current events.  Overall, it's an easy A, and you get S and M for it!

Pretty good professor. Lectures were pretty boring, but work was easy. She's a very easy grader, assignments are pretty lengthy and time-consuming but there's only five of them, including the mid-term and final. Reading is only really important for the final and midterm, both of which are take-home. I recommend this class.
Tests were take home and easy as long as you took good notes in class. Other assignments were time consuming, but not difficult. I really enjoyed this class and got an A just by showing up.
I have never done the reading but I still have an A. She's really nice and willing to talk things out. Tests are take home. A lot of writing in this course.
Boring lectures. Meyer is a great teacher but shes a tough grader. I hated this class because it was so boring. Dont take this class unless you like writing long papers.

Not a good teacher.  Unnecessarily high volume of work for a 100 level class.  Says "umm" literally more than 200 times in a fifty minute class making paying attention an impossibility.  Nice lady, though.
Great professor, tests are a bit difficult, tends to stay on syllabus, appreciates class discussion and participation

Assigns a lot of work and is a fair grader.  She always gives very good interesting lectures (even if the topic is boring) yet for some reason shows a lot of videos also. (I much prefer when she talks)  She is helpful and very pleasant to talk to outside of class.  She is also the type of professor who can change your mind. Great Professor.

Young, down to earth, cute, and a decent teacher also. She gets a little mixed up with stats and numbers sometimes like others said but she was good in the computer lab teaching SPSS software, and that experience can help you get a job someday
Dr. Meyer is an awesome professor.  She assigns lots of reading but goes over all of it in class.  Lectures are interesting and she shows a lot of films.
Awesome teacher. Extremlely helpful and makes stats interesting.
One of the friendliest professors I've ever had. Beautiful, young, helpful. She sometimes confuses concepts in Stats but I'm sure she's a much better Sociology teacher.
Amazing Professor...sometimes assigns ridiculous amounts of work at the last minute though.
It's Lisa Meyer.  She's great, cute, and dresses like an Express/Lerner NY model every day.  Love her!
This dude promised extra credit for a week if we made flashcards then doesn't give extra credit. I get you want people to make flashcards but don't promise extra credit and get my hopes up.

He definitely made orgo 1 much harder than it should be.. The chart he gives out for the SN2, SN1, E2, E1 rxns made NO sense, and actually confused me more. Exams were def harder than the other professors, and I really want to know what is with him throwing NMR questions on exams and hws. (they're soooo long..) Gave almost no extra credit stuff :(
His lectures are sooo good. Very helpful and organized. Much better than other orgo professors. He is very smart so he can explain anything clearly. Not an easy class but I liked his lectures style.

Dr. Helms is a very good professor for Orgo 1, and the class is not as bad as people make it out to be. The class is 80% tests, so if you get one bad grade you're kind of screwed. He can be a little hard on his students at times, but he just wants you to do well. The class is “harder” than if you take it with the other profs, but you'll learn more.

Dr Helms is a great professor especially for orgo 2. He is very clear and while attendance isn't mandatory it is super beneficial to show up to class. He gave two different opportunities for extra credit this semester which really helped and he started to put bonuses on the tests which helped. If you can take his class, then do it.

BEWARE: He makes Orgo harder than it needs to be....orgo is hard on its own but he always emphasizes that it's a "weeder class" and tries to test the character of his students. He makes you WORK for a good grade. He loves chemistry and is a good educator but a difficult one. May the odds be ever in your favor.

If you don't show up to lecture, you don't pass it's simple as that. Reading the textbook can suffice most times, but the examples Helms provides is the primary reason one can do well. Orgo is tough as is, but this class was worth the rigor and difficulty compared to other Orgo II professors.

Dr. Helms is a great lecture professor but isn't the best for lab. Was honestly very stressful as many times due dates and expectations weren't clear. Due dates changed without notice (after staying up many a night to get work done). The in lab portion itself is easy and straightforward, but the out of lab work and analysis is the toughest part.

Tests (3 exams and a final) make up 80% of your grade. The written hws are great examples of what his tests will look like. Don't be surprised to see online hws with 60-80 questions each. Dr. Helms is extremely helpful and wants to see you succeed. He does not curve exams, but is willing to be flexible if you approach him with a reasonable request.

He is great! Lots of office hours and an SI. He wants to help, so if you are struggling through the class, do not hesitate to reach out! I really enjoyed being in his class, but they fill up insanely quickly during registration.

Dr. Helms is hands down the best professor I've had at Geneseo. He focuses a lot on MCAT questions since principles of Orgo is for chem majors/pre-med students. Even so, I'm a neuro major and on the pre-PA track so I won't be taking the MCAT, and taking orgo with Helms was the best decision I have made!! He is really helpful in office hours too!!

Helms is by far the best professors I have ever had and am very fortunate to have him again next semester. Orgo is hard, but having Dr.helms as my professor I was actually super excited to go to class and learn. He is super helpful outside of class and really wants all his students to do well.

Prof Helms was very easy going and this class was a welcome to the major class. It consisted of a writing assignment each week, each were 10 points for doing the assignment and submitting on time, nothing too hard. The class wasn't required but was a good grade booster and got me to a certain amount of credits needed for the semester.

One of the best Geneseo has to offer. Probably my favorite professor I've had. Usually fast at responding to emails even if you're asking for help on a question. Laid back and makes the class interesting. Probably wouldn't have enjoyed orgo as much if I didn't take it with him. People who rate him down probably expected orgo to be an easy class

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']
comment: Organic chemistry with Helms was the hardest class I've ever taken. I have never gotten below a B in a class and I failed this class after going to every class and taking notes, getting a tutor outside of school, and studying for days before the final. Your grade in this class depends solely on the exams which are close to impossible.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Although organic chemistry is tough, Helms makes it much easier. Unsure how he normally runs it, but this semester he had recordings of the lectures and then re-covered them in-person. It's idiot-proof, and he makes sure that everyone knows the basic. Fantastic teacher, and great guy.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Dr. Helms is hands down one of the smartest professors at SUNY Geneseo. Organic chemistry requires a lot of time and effort and thats the bottom line, but as long as you are giving it an honest effort, Helms will meet you half way and try his best to help. He is definitely one of my favorite professors and gave me a new appreciation for chemistry!

Taking that organic chemistry is going to be extremely hard regardless, Dr. Helms stands out with very clear and informative lectures. Even though it's currently online, I ended up learning more in this class than any other this semester. The only down side is there is literally 4 grades- 3 exams and a homework grade. He's the best CHEM211 option!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Helms was nice and pretty engaging during 1/week in person class but the rest of the class was pre-recorded lectures that were super long as well as textbook reading. The class format made it very difficult to fully learn the material and his office hr required pre-scheduled appointments. Take him in person maybe but take it online w/ someone else.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: One of the hardest classes I've taken. HOWEVER, he is a great lecturer and makes me understand challenging concepts. His office hours can IN PERSON which is SO beneficial. He does not curve, but an A- is 88-90 and A is 90+. The exams are hard, but fair. If you study and work REALLY hard EVERY DAY (study groups help!!), you will get a good grade!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: As on online lecture, he did not use zoom. Only prerecorded lectures on top of the readings you have to do. This is not an efficient way of learning at ALL, and his practice exams are nothing like the actual exams he gives and he is very harsh on grading.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Dr. Helms makes a really daunting class manageable and interesting. He responds to emails very quickly and has office hours where you can meet directly with him to get questions answered. He does a really good job of explaining his lectures. His tests can be difficult but all the questions are fair based on what he has taught in class. Take him!

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Helms is intimidating, and every other review makes him sound horrible. He is a tough professor, but it's because he truly wants you to succeed in orgo. His office hours are a little scary, but he that because he wants you to find the answer yourself and not just be handed them. Definitely recommend for orgo1. I'm taking him again for 2 next sem.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Gives pop quizzes, and holds them over your head like a threat. Must do textbook readings every night, and expects you do to every practice question in book. Very un-encouraging professor. Always makes jokes about how if we make tiny mistakes, real scientists would laugh us out of the room. Creates a very difficult learning environment

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Dr. Helms is a really great teacher and will help you thoroughly understand the material of you put the work in. His tests are difficult but homework give you an idea of what to expect for them, and he'll go over stuff with you really thoroughly in office hours if you need! I'd definitely recommend taking him.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Honestly the hardest teacher I have ever had. He flies through his lectures and expects you to know everything. If you ask him questions he will literally not help you and just try and point you in the right direction because he thinks it will help even though it does not at all. Just save yourself the grade and the trouble and don't take him!!!

Flies through his slides like his life depends on it and then assigns the last 20 minutes to do group work problems which he never actually gives you the answers to. If you ask a question he won't answer it, he'll just answer with another question. This is coming from a student with straight A's so it's not like I'm just not grasping the material

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Dr. Helms is honestly an amazing professor. That being said, he's also very difficult. If you're willing to put the time in, you can do well and actually learn the material. He's super accessible outside of class, as he's got tons of office hours and will make time if you email him. Just be ready to work, his tests and homework are really hard

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: pre med? don't bother with helms. you should try to get the best grade that you can in organic, which will be a lot harder in his class than in others. Gives no curve, even though exams and homeworks are arguably harder than those given by other professors. Yes, you'll learn a ton, but take it with someone who is not cruel.

Condescending professor that made me hate everything to do with the subject. No amount of studying can make you leave a test feeling confident you did well. He was good at explaining the material but was intimidating in office hours and his tests were just ridiculous.

He is a very good and helpful teacher but boy is he tough. If you had a hard time with organic I, I'd recommend taking it with someone else. But he is a very good teacher and is willing to help you out, but it's definitely not an easy class.
Very helpful, and makes lectures interesting with fun facts. Very approachable guy, knows his stuff. Experienced with teaching, unlike some professors. If you study and work hard, you will do well!

Very good teacher, very smart guy. He is very hard, he makes up for it though. If you listen to what he tells you to do to prep for a test, you will do well. Also gives a lot more work than the other teachers

Helms is a very intelligent man. His lectures are very clear and easy to follow and if you don't understand things still, he has an unbelievable amount of office hours. Tests are very hard, you need to study a lot. If I can get an A, so can you.

Helms is by far the hardest orgo professor. His tests are very tough and he assigns a lot of homework. But, he's a great lecturer, and he's brilliant. His class made me love chemistry when I hated it in high school.
If you love being on the edge between passing and failing this is the perfect professor for you.

He's smart and all, but only if you can overcome his **** attitude enough to absorb anything he's saying. He made me hate my favorite science. He enjoys talking about things that'll give you cancer. By the end of class, you'll think that sounds like a good idea.

I STRONGLY recomend him. He is BRILLIANT and is a fantastic lecturer. He is very clear as to what he expects and wants on tests. People try and avoid him because his tests are "hard", I'm not a great chem student, but his tests were fair and kind of easy, the practice tests are very simular to the actuale tests. OWLs for HW are NOT hard nor do they

Excellent professor! Brings in outside information in lectures to make material more relevant. Supplemental instruction, tutoring, and office hours are available. Tests are tough but not surprising, as is homework. Do as he suggests and do a little OWL every day. Orgo is demanding, but Helms made me enjoy it. Taking Orgo 2 with him next semester.
Busted my butt an failed with him..Has no compassion what so ever. Re took organic else were and Got an "A" I know tutor private and going to med school.

This class is very hard but Helms is a fun guy. Make sure you have a full understanding of the procedure before going to lab. His pre-lab lecture will make the experiment very intimidating, which scares you into not making mistakes

Helms is the man... By far the hardest orgo professor but definitely the best. Nothing against Johnson or Geiger, but the kids in Helms' class were much better at orgo. His practice tests are similar to the real exam so study them hard! Owls arent as bad as people say and are sometimes even helpful. Take him!

Took Orgo I with him as a senior adding a Chem major to Math. Taking Orgo II with him because he's so straightforward. Not easy, but I worked my ass off for every test and aced the class. No more OWLs means homework is not that bad. Might scare sophomores, but that's because he'd rather scare you than see you fall behind. Great professor!

Acts like you can master orgo in 1,2,3. Thats when I worried. Owl's hurt your grade an killed time. The man told me dont go into the medical field I will hurt some one because I couldnt do a synthesis problem. Repeated course else were an got an "A". Hes all talk.

Helms is an excellent lab profressor. He knows what he is doing and he is vrey chill when it comes to minor screwups such as broken glassware. Fair grader, expects work/reading to be done beforehand as it should be. Will scare the $#%&! out of you in the pre lab lecture though. "If 2 molecules of this toch you, your skin melts and you get cancer"

Its orgo, its going to stink. But he gives ALOT of work. The homework is you're saving grace, make sure you go to the tutor because acing the homework helps your grade. The OWLS take forever and the program is horrible, causeing more frustration the helping. NO CURVE WHAT SO EVER! Tests are also very hard.

I feel these ratings dont reflect on the class as a whole. Im very use to hard work but the amount of work we recieved was alot compared to the other orgo classes. Owls consumed most of your time, test were way harder than the questions given in the notes, an practice exams, there was also no curve. ALot of false hope was given.

Amazing professor.  I know a lot of people find organic chemistry difficult, but with him an A is entirely within your reach if you just pay attention.  He makes complex concepts understandable and if you still don't get it he will take time at office hours to make your that you understand.
No Comments
Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. I even thought about registering for Chemistry in Society next semester because he's so awesome.

Very difficult teacher, but also very clear and precise. He knows his material very well and does an excellent job at conveying the material to the class. He does expect a lot, however, hard exams, and OWL, which is online homework and terribly annoying. Very helpful during office hours though, really nice guy and easy to talk to. I'd recommend him
Great guy. Loves what he does, and can inspire you to do well. I recommend him to anyone, especially if you're not really into chem but need to take a chem course. My favorite professor thus far.

I hated high school chem and was dreading taking this class but I'm very glad that I was able to! The material was interesting and useful for everyday life. The class is easy if you do the reading and the work and if you ever need help he is always there. Great class especialy for 8:30 in the morning!

Pretty interesting lab, but challenging. Not as big a pain in the ass as the first semester since there's no need to be building giant apparatuses before you even do the experiment. Kinda quirky, pretty approachable, and somewhat of a difficult grader. I'd recommend him.

Orgo is the worst class on Earth no matter who you have as a professor.  Helms is a great guy and a great professor, and by all means does his part very well, it's the material itself that is a problem. Exam 1 is all review, and then everything goes downhill. You NEED to dedicate lots of time and effort to do well. Stay level headed and you're fine
love of my life

If you're one of those people who scourge this site looking for the easiest professor to take, be aware that there is no such professor in Orgo. However, Helms is an EXCELLENT professor. He can actually teach instead of babbling over Power Point slides. The tests are brutal with an average of 65 or so but that's Orgo and not Helm's fault.

Very clear on what he wants. Tests are hard but its orgo after all. Use the models for ring flips and such. Fun guy overall will make it not too awful to be in orgo in the AM hours and orgo lab in the PM. Take his class for orgo actually made me like like it a little.
No Comments

Helms is a great guy and a great professor.  Every day I go to lecture I leave feeling I actually learned something unlike last year.  His tests are challenging but VERY FAIR. If you put effort into studying you will do fine.  People bomb orgo because they get cocky after the first exam. Be realistic, USE FLASHCARDS, and you'll be fine.
One of the best teachers I ever had, great for visual learners!  Made organic easy and I actually enjoyed the class...although you still have to study hard for it.  Thumbs up!
really good prof, but a hard grader with hard exams.
Let's just say: "Dr. Helms is unparalled in greatness" thank you
Definitly the easiest and best chem class that i've ever taken, really awesome guy
Course sucks...hes okay
Good teacher, nice, energetic.
He's so nice and smart and easy-going.  Relates to students very well.  Makes orgo interesting and fun.  Probably the best chem teacher I've ever had.

Terrible teacher. I don't know how she graded but she was strict with grading and claimed she was lenient with grades. You go up to talk to her and she's still unclear about what she wants. Her reading responses can get annoying and you have to put in 200% effort to get a minimal grade. I don't know why people rated her high.

After getting only a B in ap english in high school, I was worried that I'd get a B in this class, too.  But she's pretty easy to please. She always asks the students the discuss their potential essay topics with her, but I never did that. She doesn't remember if she talked with you or not, anyway. it's an easy A.

Filiz is sweet, but her instructions on assignments were very unclear and caused a lot of confusion among the class.  There are 3 essays and the final is the revisions to all of those essays.  Attendance is mandatory; she takes attendance every class. Do your work, and you will be fine.

Filiz is wonderful!  She is such a kind and sweet person.  She is very knowledgeable about the subject matter and passionate about it.  The only downside to the class was that it should have been labeled as an Orientalist/Postcolonialism class instead of English 170.  The entirety of the class was analyzing texts from a postcolonial perspective.
Was very good at teaching INTD, better teacher than her husband who teachers HUM

FIliz is the best! She is the first professor I've actually connected with here! She is so kind and understanding! Definitely take any class you can with her! She lets you fix your work and is a very fair grader! Most people hate their INTDs but I would take this class again if I could!

Easily one of the best professors at Geneseo.  As long as you show up to class for the group discussions and do the assignments you'll be fine.  When I asked about a topic for my paper he gave me a list of at least a dozen sources to draw from.  Its a shame he's retiring next semester.

SO BORING. i never went all semester. i disagree that he's an easy grader or helpful outside of class. i spent a lot of time on my paper and i don't think he graded it fairly. he also NEVER answers emails. really annoying.

He's SO boring.  You learn nothing in class, it's not material you'd expect to learn about. He's an easy grader & attendance isn't necessary but to me all that stuff wasn't worth this hellish year with this man.  He doesn't give you any general ideas for what the midterm & final will be on he's so broad and a poor explainer. boring. useless.
Bearden's class is so boring!  I don't feel like I'm learning anything.  The plus side is the class is pretty easy and you can do well without putting forth too much effort.
extremely confusing, always will to help out in office hours, but that doesnt help if you cant understand the point he is trying to make.
don't take unless you have to. he is really nice guy and friendly but i never feel like i learn a single thing in his classes.
No Comments

Bearden is a really nice guy.  I didn't learn much in this class, but it's not a class I wanted to take anyway.  He grades generously, and there wasn't a ton of work.  He could be interesting at times, but he wasn't in general.

Prof. Bearden is a great guy. He is extremely helpful if you ask for it, especially during office hours. The class is pretty easy in the beginning, but it gets more difficult as the course progresses. He tries to be clear, but often he moves too fast so meeting him outside of class is wise.
Very easy prof... you dont really need to go to class.  There are 3 papers that you need complete that are pretty easy but he's boring and unorganized!

Bearden can be boring and random sometimes, but he's a good professor.  Three papers and a couple of survey questions before each class is the extent of the work.  You can actually miss quite a bit of class and do fine.  He also does everything over the internet so it makes it a bit easier.
verrrry boring lectures, i fell asleep all the time. class is pointless because he talks about the most random things.  very fair grader though.
Easy class, just do the bulletin board assignments and you'll do fine.
he's a great teacher! he is so helpful and really trys to make all of his classes interesting!
AWESOME teacher. he's so funny and sweet. Defintiley worth takign a class with him
I wish I could give this man 10 chili peppers! Bearden rocks! Just look at his website and do WebCT postings and you are set.
Bearden loooooves stats.  He was a good prof but some of the work was monotinous
No Comments
No Comments

Nice guy. Lectures are pretty boring. Very helpful in office hours. Class is a challenge so be prepared. Crazy amounts of HW and high stakes quizes. Way too much effort in trying to weed students out in the first course on behalf of the entire physics department. Huge huge huge curve. A ridiculous curve. I think I had a 61 average and got a B-

I actually understand him in lecture.. which is strange because physics is a tough subject and I suck at math.
