I really like that he has multiple demonstrations and videos in every class, so physics isn't just vague equations...I had a bad physics 1 experience and physics 2 with Hager is a breath of fresh air!

Hager took the grading easy for this lab which is great for first semester. My final grade was a lot higher than I thought it would be. As long as you read the lab book before class you'll be fine. He helps with any questions you have, and makes it easy to understand what you are supposed to be doing.
Very helpful. Teaches well. The class isn't a cakewalk or anything but he explains things well.
Has multiple choice tests, but sometimes none of the answers are right. A very unfair guy but whatever.. if you have to take physics here I'd still choose him over Adelson.

Despite how challenging the course is itself, Hager is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students success. Lectures can be a little boring but his demonstrations are usually comical. Tests are identical to the homework sets.  Hes understanding that most students in his class are not physics majors. I would recommend Hager to anyone!

Hagers class is all math based. He is extremely helpful during office hours.I was in his 1st class he taught so going to class was not so useful. The homework is hard. The tests and quizzes are easy if u do the hw. No curveballs in this class. would recommend if good at math(if not good, u shouldnt be taking physics)

I was in his first class he ever taught. He worse in class than Pogo, but he is super helpful in office hours, more than Pogo. This class is very challenging, unless you are mathematically oriented. There is an enormous curve. I would recommend him over Pogo. Don't buy the book. I never opened it. HW is very important.
Professor Waddington is awesome, she is super nice and easy.

Waddington's class was SOOOOOO easy. you don't have to pay attention during the lectures and only have to do about one 10/15 min activity or something which counts towards your attendance. quizzed are online and no tests, there was one group project and one lesson plan adaptation. very easy A!

Prof. Waddington is super sweet and clear when it comes to directions. Her quizzes are open note, although the lectures can get a bit boring for note taking. Group work is common but nothing difficult. Lots of class time provided to allow for the group projects. Attendance is required unless you email ahead of time and complete the make up work.

Great professor! Her directions are always very clear. Her feedback on assignments is extremely helpful, she really gets you ready for block 5. She's the sweetest lady, but if taking notes from a powerpoint isn't your thing, then you may not love her class as much. She is a fair grader and is very understanding. I absolutely love working with her!

She is so nice I have loved taking both SPED371 and SPED385 with her. I had a family emergency and she was very caring about helping me work around it at a very fair pace. She is great! If I could take her again I would!

An angel, I love Waddington. So lucky to have gotten to take SPED 371 with her and cannot wait to have two classes with her next semester. Course load is very fair, Waddington genuinely cares about all her students. So helpful during office hours!

I love this woman with all my heart; she is a literal angel. She is one of the best professors I've ever had at Geneseo. Her lectures are engaging and full of expertise and information. She clearly knows and cares so much  about what she's talking about, and she is the kindest soul. She's the perfect professor; I cannot recommend her enough.

I love Waddington so much. She is such an amazing person and you can tell she genuinely loves what she does. She says what is good in your work first before what needs to be worked on, which I feel is really important. A lot of professors don't even do the first thing. If I could take more classes of hers I 100% would!
Waddington is such a queen she has so much experience in the field and she is so amazing

Professor Waddington reminded me of why I wanted to pursue education to begin with. Her passion and knowledge is unmatched and she truly practices what she preaches which is important. She gives very clear expectations, and provides feedback that is useful. She is always there. One of the best professors I have had in my four years of college.

Professor Waddington cares about and believes in her students so much. She is so knowledgeable since she has just left the classroom. Her feedback is constructive and specific. She takes the time to answer all your questions and never makes you feel like they're insignificant. I am sad to be ending my last course with her!

One of the sweetest professors I have ever come across. I had her in the fall and she improved so much and took the feedback and is a great teacher. She really practices what she preaches and is so empathetic toward her students. Her class is relatively easy but you learn important practices about interactions in the schools.
I love Professor Waddington! Very applicable skills taught and I love her. Such a sweet heart!

Professor Waddington is a very kind person, however, her teaching style is completely comprised of lecturing. She basically read the textbook to us. We did no hands-on activities or discussions. She never asked for participation, so by the end of the semester, she still did not know anyone's name.

Professor Pastizzo is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at Geneseo. You can tell how much he cares and wants his students to succeed. Can't say enough good things about him! Definitely take him if you can!

grade consists of 3 short papers and 3 exams. he made our exams online and let us do them at home. he also gave a study guide that gave a lot of insight to the exams. he's really lenient and funny. class was easy and I still learned a lot. definitely take him if you can

Dr. Pastizzo was awesome during COVID. He was kind and had optional review sessions every week where he did his best to keep it fun. His tests were a bit tricky but the answers could be found in the textbook if you really look for them. He was a great professor and Im really glad I chose his class!

Dr. Pastizzo is willing to do anything for his students. He is very reasonable and approachable. His lectures are interesting and he treats you like a person, not a wall. I only used the textbook a little bit because I was able to attend all of the lectures. I had him during COVID and the tests were untimed which really lifted a weight off me.

Pastizzo is such a nice guy. His tests are pretty tricky though and not all of the info can be found in the slides. You need to read the textbook (which he wrote btw) in order to find test answers and even so they can be impossible to find. That being said, he offers extra credit and YOU SHOULD DO IT IF YOU WANT A CHANCE AT AN A.
Very kind and understanding. He extended the due date for a test because he knew how hectic the semester was due to the pandemic. Hes willing to help and cares a lot about his students.

very kind man that just wants to see his students succeed. willing to work with you outside of class. take home exams given a few days before it's due. super into his work and loves participation. take good notes when he speaks not just what is on slides.

tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Dr. Pastizzo is one of the best professors I have had at Geneseo. There are 3 take home exams and no textbook for this class (he teaches with research articles). He clearly cares for all students and is very willing to help you inside and outside of class. You won't regret taking this class!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: Pastizzo is great, he cares a lot about how his students are doing and he really makes an effort to make sure you understand the more difficult topics. He gives extra credit opportunities and will curve your tests. Homework and class work help balance out grades so it's important to go to class so you get the credit for them.

For an 8:30AM stats lecture, he made it interesting. He really wanted us to understand and was really cool. SONA systems extra credit, and sometimes he just gave us answers for the first few exam questions. He wants all his students to do well. Some homework, exams are tricky but doable if you study.

Awesome professor and super nice! Pastizzo was very clear with his assignments and test. Fast response with emails when you need help and always helps you when you have a question. Test is based on everything in assigned reading and lecture slides. Do what is assigned and you'll pass the class no doubt.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Dr. Pastizzo was one of the best professors that I have had at Geneseo. He made a not so fun class really interesting and enjoyable. There are a few papers but he gives you time to write them and a clear description of what he wants from you. If you need help go to office hours!! There are also a few exams but he tells you exactly what to study!

He's a very dedicate and responsible professor. Very approachable and always give you helpful tips on your papers and on your study. Everything that he provided was useful! Quality professor for sure, would love to take another class with him again.

Pastizzo is passionate and extremely knowlegable and tbh adorable. Lots of dad jokes. Will stop class to comment on stuff going on out the window. understanding and helpful. very kindhearted and funny man.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Dr. Pastizzo is the best professor I have ever had. His exams are based entirely off of his lectures, so attendance is mandatory. He doesn't use a textbook, he teaches from research articles. The material can be dry, but get a cup of coffee and take good notes and you will do great. Also very helpful if you contact him outside of class.

He is very passionate about stats, I learned a lot about applications of stats for my research endeavors (class is conceptual which is helpful for IRL application).  His tests are  confusingly worded , but if you ask him questions on the wording he helps out! I would also take good notes in his class his tests are heavily based on his lectures!

Dr. Pastizzo is AMAZING! He genuinely cares about students. He is precise in his expectations, gives thorough feedback, & helps you develop your writing skills. APA papers are tough, but he is willing to help both in & out of class The class material is interesting & challenges your ability to critically think about psychology.  Highly recommend!

Pastizzo is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Genuinely cares about helping his students. I would definitely recommend taking stats with him, he goes out of his way to explain things until everyone understands. If you aren't good with math go to his office hours, he really cares.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: He's really strict about making up tests. You have to be really really sick to make up a missed test. However he's a very fun professor and really cares about his students. He explains things in an easy-to-understand manner as well which is super helpful for people like myself that are very very bad at math.
Dr. Pastizzo demonstrates a willingness to meet with students during office hours.  The topic was interesting.

I took this class online over the summer. It was super easy! The textbooks had his power point slides at the end of each chapter and a  practice quiz. You had 28 hours to take the test. They were untimed and you can "save" it through out the day. I recommend taking this class if you can teach yourself.

Give Pastizzo a chance for psych stats! People say Ruddy is easier but Pastizzo was great this semester. 16 points of extra credit (on a test grade) and 25% in class participation which was easy to have full points.

Very awkward, nice guy but constantly confuses his students. He will talk in circles or go off on tangents out of nowhere. He also gets distracted in his lectures and will start talking about some other topic in the middle of explaining a concept. He makes simple topics really complex but he's willing to give a lot of extra credit for those needing

He's a bit like a goofy dad but I would absolutely recommend this course with him. He writes the textbook for the class so the only thing I was irritated by at first was that I couldn't rent it but totally worth it.
He's a really tough grader with difficult tests.  Makes not too hard material very difficult
The tests are definitely hard, but he's a nice professor. He's very thorough during class.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM! If you are not amazing at math good luck! Tests only get harder and more obscure, & class feels like hours and hours long. How he got tenured i will never understand.

He seems like a nice guy but he is one of those people that loves math -__- His tests are very hard and this class made me seriously question my psychology major. If I walked into this class without knowing what it was I would have thought it was just a pure math class. I hate math. Hard and BORINGGGGGGG

Really great class, and VERY informative. Dr. Pastizzo is obviously passionate about the course material, and that passion cannot help but inspire you to learn! This is my second class with Dr. Pastizzo; class discussions are always really interesting, but tests can be difficult if you don't attend class regularly. Make use of office hours though!

Really nice guy. Very accomodating. Slept through the final by accident and he still let me make it up. Statistics is very boring, but he knows what he's talking about. Pretty difficult grader, but offers opportunities to improve. Really nice guy, but perhaps look for an easier professor as this class is likely to hurt your GPA.

Pastizzo is pretty average. He teaches a boring subject in an average way. I would have been totally lost if I hadn't taken AP Stat in high school. Sometimes vague. Makes jokes that are so bad they're kind of funny. Not a bad guy, but you'll have a better time if you get Ruddy.

Real tough, but he's definitely softened since he had a kid (I took 250/251 with him). He's helpful, he can be a bit verbose (he looooves words) but class discussion was good and if you don't understand he will try other ways to help you get it. Easy to take notes in class, too. Just tough on tests and papers.

He is a very difficult professor.  When he grades your paper, he grades you on exacting style of writing and not content.  Gives you obscure comments that won't help you improve your writing to his standings. Taking his class caused my other classes to suffer.

I enjoyed having him as a professor & plan on taking him for 251 as well. His tests are hard but if you pay attention in class and/or have a predisposition to math/stats, an A is definitely possible. Does throw in tricky questions that require you to really grasp the concepts. Don't regret my decision to take him over Ruddy - I've learned a lot.
Made stats so much harder than it had to be. Hardly gives any partial credit on long answer test questions and I found him patronizing. Take stats with Ruddy, it will make your life so much easier.

He is a very nice professor & is more than willing to help if you ask him. You can tell that he wants us to succeed. The problem is that his tests are ridiculously hard. No matter how well you know the information, there is still no guarantee you will do well on his tests. I practically memorized the textbook and still failed most of the tests.

His powerpoints are very clear, and he is a very good professor.  Labs and quizzes are pretty easy.  He makes the tests difficult though.  He gives really hard questions, and is not willing to compromise.  If you're not a good test taker, don't take his class.

He is a great professor, knows his stuff, always willing to help... but his tests will beat you senseless - I'd recommend the class because I learned a lot, but you have to study study study and get his help in office hours.

horrible class. uses big words, doesn't always focus on stats. open to help, extra credit offered. he wrote the book, and I didn't understand a lot of it, plus if you didn't understand the class there was no way to understand the text. tests are very hard. other professors are much better.
nice guy, very funny and smart. teaches stats well and easy to understand. tests are wicked hard, remember to read the book and study!

he is a nice guy but for some reason his mere presence annoys me, and i get the feeling it does for other ppl in the class too. course doesnt have a text book and  focuses on empirical studies- makes it hard to take good notes from his lectures and the material can be hard to grasp. study guides are vauge but tests are not bad and hes a fair grader

Boring class, but Dr. Pastizzo was a great professor. Interesting, enthusiastic, and very fair. Tests were challenging but he let you know exactly was was going to be on it. Put so much work into class you could really tell. Clear, organized, and real pleasure to take a class with.
Stay away! Very very very subjective grader. I learned a lot in his class but I was miserable the entire time. He was arrogant and made me feel stupid.

dr. pastizzo is great. he is one of the most fair profs  i have ever had. his pop quizzes are announced a day in advance and they are open note. his test questions come right out of the test prep in the  book that he wrote. he is fun in class and loves what he teaches.

got a C+ even though i worked my butt off in this class. very interesting and challenging, but test questions are much more specific than what he teaches in class. Should't have to fight so hard to pass a prerequisite class like this on.

he wrote the book, very helpful, very clear, wants students to do well. the material can be difficult, but attempts to help with grades, open notebook pop quizzes-very easy, and tests with fair questions! highly recommended!!!
He wrote the book. read it, go to class. study.  you'll do fine.

Although he may seems nice in class, STEER CLEAR.  The teacher's tests ask vague questions that expect specific answers. His grading is subjective and often harsh with little room for discussion.  Your grade will reflect your how linguistically similar you are to the professor, not your knowledge of the material.

Dr. Pastizzo isn't easy, but it's doable. We didn't have a book which kinda added to the confusion,and made attendence manditory. Tests were challenging, but he searched through papers for extra credit. Papers are extreamly hard. You  *need* to write it early and let him read it over/correct it. He's willing to work w/ you so you get a good grade.
No Comments

The material itself is extremely boring but he tries to make it more interesting. His exams are pretty difficult and it's hard to understnad what hes looking for in an exam. I would suggest taking someone else if possible.. you cover the same thign but exams are easier i hear

great guy in and out of class, his material is absurdly boring but he is really cool and still makes class interesting and even fun. he's very entertaining and personally gives review classes the night before exams, which are kindof hard but he's very helpful if you just ask.  i def recommend

Dr. P is very intelligent and entertaining.  He tries to make the material interesting and covers the material thoroughly, at times his explanations can be a bit confusing.  He is always willing to work with you. I enjoyed having him as an instructor.
Dr. P is a very good guy and professor. but his exams are hard. i studied so hard for his exams but i got very low grades, which was very depressing.

I'm a big fan of Dr. Pastizzo...he's a great guy, funny, interesting and insanely intelligent.  He's really fun to talk to and is very approachable if you need any help with anything.  His tests are fair, and he personally does review sessions, which is awesome :)
No Comments
Great guy.  Goes off on crazy tangents but its fun.  Tries to make the class as easy as possible for you.
Great teacher, makes class very interesting! I love him!!
Very nice guy. Class is usually entertaining. Class was let out early several times. My fav pysch professor at Geneseo!
Great Teacher who made sure everyone knew what was going on in the class. Tried to get to know each student personally. Knew when students didn't understand material.
Very fun guy, Stats is a hard class and he knows alot but makes class tolerable with his corny jokes; also tests are fair and easy!
great teacher. outlines tests before test day. tests come from hw and in class assignments. very understanding and extremely willing to help if you have questions. i definitely recommend him.

Great teacher, although I've definetely become dependent on the notes he posts for the chapters, which can get scary when the test is a week a way and he hasn't posted 3 chapters...so remember to read your book
I hate math and this was one of my favorite classes ever!  I was dreading having stats at 830 in the morning, but i never missed a class and was always awake.

One of my favorite professors so far.  He is young, doesn't put the class to sleep, makes things as easy to understand as possible, lets you out early often, and there isn't a lot of HW.  If you are going to take this class, take it with him, he's the man
Very nice guy and lectures are engaging. Seems to me very easy but I used to be a math major.  Study guides on line that almost replicate exams; you can't go wrong.
Nice guy; hard tests.  Psych 250 is literally a math-course, but required for Psych majors.

Professor Abonado is the sweetest and kindest man you will ever meet. You will have to read articles and books throughout the semester but they aren't very long and they are easy to read and be prepared to talk about them in class. You will need to participate in class about the readings but if you participate a few times you will be fine.

Advanced Poetry Workshop Spring 23 was awesome! Workshop was great because of Al and the class itself. He's super easy going, lets you take your final portfolio any direction you want. He does want you to strengthen your poetry skills; workshops are great, laid back and teach you so much.

Professor Abonado is truly a sweet man. He cares about his work and shows that, and he makes the class interesting. While I did not love this class at all, I really enjoyed Professor Abonado. I would definitely take a different class with him.
This class was easy yet also interesting. As long as you show up, participate once or twice per class, and turn in your work on time, this class is an easy A.

Albert is a great professor and really helped me out when I had to take writing seminar. Writing has always been a challenge for me but he made sure that this class was more than just writing a ton. This class is really a hidden gem, he cares about his students. Thank u professor Abonado!

He's a great professor, very laid back and understanding about late work. The only complaint I have is that he got a little behind on grading but overall he's awesome and I would take a class he teaches.

Abonado grades everything based off of 7 very easy to follow criteria. Basically full credit on everything you turn in. He really cares about his students and was a great prof. attendance wasn't mandatory as long as you emailed him

Best professor I have ever had. I love the way I was graded for this course. You need to follow seven easy rules to get an A in the class. I have never loved or been good at writing but I loved this class and would recommend him to everyone.

easy grader, but gives amazing feedback. graded on just a few papers. comprehensive lectures, and he is endlessly patient with questions and analysis. papers do have a really quick writing oeriod, but theyre 3-5 pages max, so its manageable
really easy class, just submit the work and you will be fine. no real papers (just 1-2 page reflections) and like 4-5 interviews

Super easy and fun class, Abonado does not expect a lot out of you. He gives great feedback. Only negative is that it is super hard to contact him, he barely responds to emails which is tough during a pandemic.
he is a very nice guy but he is also pretty disorganized, the class is alright, gives good feedback for essays if you do the work you will get a decent grade

The most understanding professor I have had. He recognizes that life happens and will do his best to accommodate your circumstances. Help him out by being an active participant, which keeps the class interesting. He assigns interesting readings and will use his humor and input to ease into class discussions if no one is talking.

He is DEFINITELY the person to take 201 with! He really exposes you to different kinds of writing, gives great feedback, (whether you're still in his class or not) and inspires you to keep writing long after his class. The class itself was so enjoyable, and not too much work at all. Probably one of the best people I've ever met!!

Great class with a cool guy. There are papers and poems every week, but he makes them interesting to write. Readings due every class, but they are fun to read. Al is a great guy and loves talking about your work. Participation is almost half your grade so just make sure to talk. Would definitely take this again!
HE IS THE BEST. RATINGS DO NOT LIE.
Avocados are not only a superfood, they are a Super Food. In guacamole, cut up on crackers with a little nutritional yeast, teaching Fundamentals of Creative Writing, avocados cannot be beat.

Big Al is an Adonis amongst men. You may not like it, but this is what peak performance looks like. He has thighs for days and drinks ranch from the bottle. In all of my three months at Geneseo I can say that - without doubt - Mr Avocado is a true gem. He makes the English department a little better and my days a lot brighter.

My favorite professor I've had, lecture can be a tad boring but you can tell how much he loves the topic. As long as you do the readings and understand you'll be perfectly fine. Is very understanding about attendance and will make up exams on his time if you talk to him. Exam grades come back before the next one and are open book

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Amazing professor! Really enjoyed taking his class. Didn't stress me out at all. I'd recommend taking especially for a gen ed.
Lectures were a bit boring at the end but its history...He's super understanding. As long as you do the readings and answer the questions he puts on Brightspace you'll be fine!

I really liked Jurnack and I'm surprised he only teaches like two courses...As long as you do the readings and pay attention to his lectures you should be fine. There's no exams, instead there's just responses which are honestly not difficult, just remember to print out the readings and use them in your writing.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: His class lectures were a bit boring, but the workload was not bad and he is very understanding.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Very light work load. Very knowledgeable in his field. Unfortunately I find his field on the uninteresting side. Lecture heavy.
Honestly, super low workload. Yes, he is lecture-heavy but everything is pretty important and entertaining for the most part.

Rich is given a bad rep on here. His lectures were pretty interesting, albeit he only shows a picture on the screen while he talks. However, the class is extremely interesting if you give it a chance, and he is such a kind professor who gave us candy for Halloween, is an easy grader, and lets you redo your essay if the grade is low.

jurnack knows what hes talking about, but he is so boring and a horrible lecturer. he only shows one picture and doesnt ever know what hes talking about to explain it. all assignments are writing and are fairly easy, the readings are boring.

Gives great feedback on essays and lets you redo them after he gives feedback. Slides were very vague and lecture's were extremely boring. Class gets cancelled so often to the point where it felt like more classes were cancelled then actually held. Takes forever to grade responses and rarely responds to emails. But overall a nice guy.

Honestly, Jurnack is much closer to a 3 than a 4, but some of you guys are hating for no reason so I'm gonna give him some extra credit. Super chill guy and a very easy 100 level course with barely any work (which he lets you resubmit if you get a bad grade) and no quizzes/tests. Only issue is he's a pretty boring lecturer, but the content is good.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: A really really nice guy. Very knowledgeable of his field, but isn't super interesting to listen to. The writings are easy, but he doesn't just give out good grades(fair).

Do not take his classes. He will ramble the whole period about random historical figures and events with two pictures on the screen and that's it. There are 6 papers and 1 final research paper and he takes months to return grades for them. Not sure if participation matters bc I was sick of wasting my time by the third week of classes.

tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Do not take him. He drones on and on ab random historical stories and only has pictures in his presentations so there is nothing to keep your attention. He takes forever to grade the papers he assigns. There is no clear structure to the class. Attending class would help to know what's going on but it is such a waste of time.
He clearly likes history but very much dislikes teaching it, very unorganized, takes months to grade any work turned in and gives little or unclear feedback. I would not take him again.

Bad, bad professor, lack of organization and very unclear a lot of the time, take his course seriously, gives you a book to read 3 weeks into class that you weren't required to get, and homeworks are based on this making it hard to complete assignments. Assignments also take months to get grades.

The entirety of the class, I wished he was my high school history teacher because his classes are reliant on class discussion and towards the end of the semester, only 3 people were showing up to classes so it didn't work too well. He assigned a lot of reading but I learned a lot in that class. I wish he taught more history courses.

Prof. Jurnacks fine. I get the sense he loves history but might not necessarily love teaching it. Ive heard hes a hard grader but from my experience he wasnt that tough. He didnt give much feedback, which I wouldve liked, but he was nice and the class was interesting.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Prof. Jurnack doesnt care about teaching. You will pass just fine, but if you care about school youre going to be frustrated by him. He doesnt respond or give feedback. He barely grades. I got a 100 in the class, mostly bc I bet he didnt read what I wrote and just slapped a grade on it. Annoying, but Ill get over it and accept the easy A.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Really chill guy, but don't be fooled! He's a very tough grader for a 100 level class. only half the class shows up for the lectures. Def a good idea to go to class on discussion days. Class is comprised of 3 take home exam papers and 7 one page responses that should help grades. Pretty easy and straight forward as kong as you can write decently.

Jurnacks class style is very laidback, but his grading is not. Hardly anyone showed up to lectures and he cancelled class often. Grade was based off of 3 papers, response questions and maybe discussions. I answered his response questions and did essays based off of notes I tried to take in lecture and did kinda poorly, ending with a B+

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: Lectures can seem very long and dull. He cancels class all the time but that doesn't really set the class back at all. 3 fairly easy essays but he is a tough grader on them. 1 paragraph responses due each week which are easy to get 100s on if you go to class. Some reading to do that will help with essays

Professor Jurnack's lectures were boring and hard to follow but the class itself was very simple and it was easy to get a good grade. If you know how to write a decent paper, you'll do fine on the 3 essay "tests" and the responses are really just checking if you know whats going on in class. An easy "A" class if you put in a little work.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Jurnack is the most boring professor I've had. He expects you to read more than you should for this level, and when he cancels class he expects you to understand what's going on without any sort of class discussion. His essay prompts are too vague, his feedback on papers isn't useful and generally comes off very rude. Wouldn't take his class ever.

Professor Jurnack is a pretty chill guy. His lectures are pretty boring though. Quizzes every week based on the previous lecture so you have to go to class. DO all the readings as they will help you write your three papers. No tests. Overall a pretty cool dude

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Take extensive notes on the readings. Five question quiz at the beginning of every class on last class's lecture. Take extensive notes during class. Often cancels class. Exam papers flexible and straightforward in content. Participation preferable, not necessary.

Really loved taking his class. We usually had homework due every week. A few questions on an article of his choice. Tests were a little hard so you definately have to study. Also, two group presentations. Overall, he is super nice and pretty funny. He makes everyone feel comftorable and willing to participate. Would highly recommend.

I loved Professor Volza! His class ran the same everyday so you know what to expect. There is homework due every class but it's easy. You do 2 group projects during the semester which weren't too difficult. The hardest part of the class was the tests. He gives a review sheet that has all the terms that you need to know but is usually 80-90 terms.

Volza is a great guy. He's kind and funny! Class is straightforward, and answers for the exams essentially come right out of the textbook or his slides, which he uploads online- he will give you a sheet with all the terms you need to know on it. He likes to have you do presentations, so be prepared to work with other people. Would recommend!!

**THIS IS HIS IMMIGRATION CREATIVE WRITING CLASS**
it was the most boring thing I have ever endured.barely took attendance. each class was a useless yap sesh who knows the point of it. We only had 3 assignments total and the final was easy. nice guy but boring  stupid  useless class. nobody ever knew what was going on.

If you need a language requirement, do not take Latin with Wes. He spends half of class talking about himself, so you don't actually get to the important things he promised he would cover, which you will then still be graded on. He is arrogant and disrespectful in his office hours, so those are useless way to attempt to get help as well.

a very kind and accommodating man, cares about your wellbeing and wants to work with you. His essay prompts are extremely vague and he rambles all lecture so nothing ever really makes sense. Gives credit for the first three assignments as long as you do them. The final essay hits you like a truck- didn't teach us how to write and grades harsh.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: A decent guy, rambles through the long lectures with absolutely no structure, could just sleep through class. Only grades based on 5 papers, three of which are "short essays" but are basically quizzes. Papers have zero prompts or guidelines. Harsh grader and can tell if you didn't read. Don't miss an assignment or your grade will tank. Good luck

I had Professor Kennison for only half a semester, and he is by FAR one of the greatest teachers I've ever experienced. He relates history to today perfectly and effortlessly, and always introduced new perspectives with absolute passion. If you remotely care about your education, take his course the moment it's offered. You owe it to yourself!

He's a great dude but has really unclear grading and assignment criteria, I literally never knew what his expectations were. I also didn't like how disorganized the class was, due dates weren't clear and he never knew where were were in the syllabus or what reading we were on.

Wes is very passionate about western humanities. There are only 5 grades for the whole class, and he only gives out 100s if you've taught him something, which is difficult considering he's been reading these papers since the 70s. Most of the class is spent listening to him talk about hyper-specific parts from the texts.
He is really nice, but the course is just writing so he can be a really hard grader. It's a course just based on books and need to pay attention to small detail.

Wes is a great professor and I'm very surprised by some of these ratings. If you enjoy a professor who can talk about anything and make it interesting, Wes is the man for you. Overall an awesome, caring, funny professor who makes learning fun!

Wes is a great professor, and although his class wont make you suffer, Ive ultimately learned a lot from him. Its a mark of him being a good professor that you can get a lot out of the class without feeling overwhelmed or stressed out.

Horrible professor. Don't ever take this class with him. Kennison loves to hear himself talk and cares very little about opinions other than his own. You will find yourself bored in class and struggling to stay awake. The course is graded based on 4 or 5 assignments that are based on little criteria and graded harshly. DO NOT RECCOMEND THIS CLASS!!

I recommend sleeping through class and just turning in assignments at his office. Lectures were extremely boring and not related to assignments. Prompts did not require any reading beyond the Sparknotes. Definitely an old-school style teacher. Nice guy though.

I took this class abroad and it was a great decision to take it with this professor. Wes is a great person, but as a teacher he doe ramble and go off on a tangent at times. His class abroad (different than at Geneseo) consisted strictly of papers as tests, and a personal journal. He is easy to talk to and if you do it will help you do well in class

Wes is wonderful. He seems a bit scattered, but that's because he's busy trying to make the school a better place for the students. He grades mostly on effort, so if you show up and turn everything in, you'll do fine. If you need structure and strict deadlines though, do not take this. He will take assignments for full credit the last day of class.

Wes is hilarious and kind, but he talks about himself a lot. The only graded work was portfolio, a final, and a research paper. Many people in the class rarely showed up and most of us still passed. If you want to get a good grade, focus on the vocab and learning the declensions. Study every week if you want to get a solid grade and do well in 201.

Wes is the classic image of the pseudo intellectual, foofy, arrogant professor type.  Listening to him ramble for 2 hours at 8:10am was borderline unbearable.  That said, the time and effort needed to get by in his class is little none.  You can basically push the class to the back of your mind and ignore it all semester, which is ideal for hum.

Do yourself a HUGE favor and take Humanities with someone else.  Kennison  puts in 2% effort all semester, and grades are pulled out of thin air with no justification or notes about what was wrong. You will be kicking yourself out of the shear intellectual stagnation and utter ridiculousness of this class. He really doesn't seem to care.

Taking a class with Kennison is like watching a one man show where he tries to intellectually challenge himself, and you die of boredom.  He is the most arbitrary grader I have ever seen using his own made up criteria. Now I know that taking a teacher who calls himself arrogant was a mistake because that is exactly what you're going to get. Easy A

Wes is an interesting fellow, and will certainly make you laugh. I've only taken 1 semester of Latin with him so far, but I learned a lot. I'm taking Latin Reading Group with him this semester hopefully. There aren't many assignments or tests or quizzes to speak of, just go to class and participate in his conversation and you'll do well.

Ken is all about participation and stimulating discussions. Unlike most HUM courses, you are not reviewing the synopsis of the book but connecting text-to-world and self. I would take this class again if it weren't at 8:05AM-9:45AM (1hr, 40mins). Sometimes he cancels, ends class early or shows up late. Regardless, I highly recommend.

People who think Wes is a good teacher can take a seat. He talks about (1) himself, (2) how he's better than you cause he traveled, (3) Italy, (4) how he knows more about everything cause he's been to Italy. Boring and not as intelligent as you'd think. Lectures reek of his blinding privilege. Take his brother, McClure, WAY better & you learn.

Great professor. Lectures aren't very structured and he does take awhile to get assignments back, but he's very entertaining and keeps class interesting. Put in the work and you'll learn a lot and do well.

I think that Humn in general is very useless for 95% of students by nature, and it seemed like even Wes didn't know what to do with a few of the books, since he would just ramble about random anecdotes that don't have anything to do with the course. So, lectures were somewhat pointless and the few assignments/exams were highly subjective essays.

Kennison is a great guy. If you make an effort in his class, he will treat you well. He is easy to meet up with if you need extra help and yes he is passionate about his going abroad programs. He did alot of work in Nicaragua to build a school and he deserves to be proud of it. He keeps in touch with alot of former students

I liked humn 1 and was looking forward to this class, but it was terrible. He just talks about himself and how he took students to Nicaragua.  He gives papers back months after you hand them in with seemingly random grades and useless comments. Take humn with someone else.

Wes is a great guy, but probably not the best of professors. Grades seem pretty arbitrary and he gives obscure paper topics. Class goes by fast, but mostly he talks about the life and times of Wes Kennison.

Just finishing my second semester of Latin with him. He fully understands that we're not going to become Latin translators, he's more interested in us getting something from the course that will help us in our professional lives. Gives stressful tests but "doesn't take the grade". He just wants to see that you're trying, it can be annoying though.

Wes is not all he's talked up to be.  Class is more interesting than other humanities profesors, but he talks alot about himself.  Grades seem pretty arbitrary, and our final grades seemed to come out of nowhere, considering three out of five assignments were not returned.  Nice guy, not the best professor around.  Hard to contact if necessary.

Wes Kennison is amazing, and has a lot to offer. I can understand how some may see him as a bit too talkative, but please do give him a chance. He is an incredibly smart and very nice guy, and he has given me a very refreshing perspective on many things. If you are an open-minded person, you will definitely get something out of his course.

He talks a lot of talk, but didn't deliver to my class, at least. Told us he'd help us write better and then didn't give feedback on half of the assignments. Infuriating for an English major, to say the least. My grade felt pretty arbitrary.

Kennison is by far the best professor I've had at Geneseo. He knows so much about so many different topics.  The information he teaches is usefull for every day life, and you walk out of the room feeling smarter and more worldy, yet not stressed.  He's very easy going and understanding- DEFINATLY take him if you have the chance.

I loved taking class with him. His lectures are really enjoyable. If you want to do well you need to think outside the box because he wants you to teach him something. I would love to take more classes with him in the future.

Consider yourself blessed if you get to take humn with Kennison.  I felt smarter just being in the same room with him, I would literally take this class WITH HIM AGAIN just for fun and to get all the things I may have missed the first time around.  Come to class, pay attention and think you will do well! Such an interesting class BECAUSE OF HIM!!!

he rarely worked off of students' ideas for discussions. he always went back to what he thought. he does tell interesting stories. VERY unclear about what he wanted for the essays. he was rarely there for his own classes and gave out pointless assignments! waste of time!
Extremely intelligent.  His papers are tough because you have to teach him something for an A.  If you do outside research on a topic that relates to the text, you'll be fine though.
Awesome teacher. Very knowledgable and fun to listen to. A lot of reading but he is open to answer any questions you have. Take him!!!

Take him.  Everyone hates humn, so don't judge a humn professor on the material.  However, Kennison does a good job of trying to keep the class interesting.  The exams are easy.  He likes participation.  He tells lots of personal stories.  He relates the books to the present day, often to politics (he is Geneseo's town supervisor). Good for HUMN!
Class was good.  He has lots of great stories and tries to make some of the incredibly boring texts interesting.  I thought he was great.  Definitly recommend him.
My favorite teacher so far.  He can really get you thinking.  He has entertaining stories.  He's great for political courses, as he's in politics.
i hated the class and didnt read the last few books and still did very well.  the material is very very boring but he is quite interesting, his stories were fun, i would recommend him
He is very good, i love him cos he grades reasonably and of course doesn't give too much reading but u still feel learned by the end of his class

absolute joke! hahahaha.  I thought i would have had to read for this class but nope.  Didn't even open the last 10 books of the semester, didnt read dante, hamlet, the prince, any of that****, and still got a B+.   hahahahahaha.  He thinks hes a real intellect, but no again.  He was beaten by me.

This was a frusterating class.  He was an interesting lecturer but got so far behind we were discussing books in class that we'd read over 2 weeks ago.  Tests weren't returned 'til the day before the next test, so we went into the final only knowing 2 test grades and neither of the 2 essay grades.

before i took the class i had a strong interest in st francis.  unfortunatly i learned very little about st. francis from class.  wes's lectures were irrelevent and he went on horribly boring tangents.  his grading was very subjective and he was never clear with instructions.
Very Good professor.  If you actually want to learn, take him

Wes was a great INTD professor! His grading system is perfect for INTD (he grades on how much you improve) I had so much fun with that class and the material and found myself wanting to learn more about the topic (St. Francis). I would suggest Wes any day
kennison is very interesting and loves to play devil's advocate. his classes are very entertaining even for an 8:05 class.

I really didn't like Wes.  He's a crazy hard grader and was very unspecific when giving assignments.  He is very passionate about what he teaches (Intd. 105 St. Francis), but I often became frustrated with his lectures because they seemed irrelevant.
excellent professor, very knowledgeable about the course matter (st. francis of assisi), makes lectures interesting, overall a great class and great professor

Very interesting class....hated the grading system.  Worked so hard on the 12 essays and 4 books, still got a C.  If you want a teacher with character go with him....if you want a good grade go elsewhere
dont quite know why i took both humn's with him.  Hes a really tough grader.  I dont really understand his system and probablynever will

Wes gives no diection when giving instructions.  His lectures are irrelevant to what we are talking about.  He gets behind in class, and then expects you to read four books and write a paper during finals week.
worst teacher I have ever had, too subjective, his class lectures had nothing to do with the exams or papers so it's not even worth the hassle to go to class
Knows what he is talking about, few papers

Wes is an awesome teacher.  I had the pleasure of studying with him in Siena, Italy.  He is passionate about his love for history, art and literature. He can't help get his students involved in what they would normally pass by without even noticing.

wes was great for humn I.  he does like to lecture, but if you listen you will learn a lot.  didn't find him to be a really tough grader.  he is also really good about getting back to you in email or meeting with you outside of class.
THis is an overrated professor.  He's a nice guy, but overworks the students and is very difficult with grading.  I recommend the cliff notes.  No one has time to read 15 books in one semester.
I disliked his methods

I loved Arthurian Romance, and I took two classes like this with Wes.  He's a lecturer, that's true, but he connects well to the text.  A bit arrogant, I agree with that.  But generally speaking, worth my time and money.
really wierd sayings: gotta take em down like a pinball machine
keeps HUM I from being a complete bore.  quite funny.
rude, arogant, stubborn
YOU had to teach HIM to get an A... great lecturer, horrible grader...

Professor Victoria Farmer is a knowledgeable and organized professor. I took her at the Wilkes Honors College at FAU. Her class is laid-back and discussion-based, with straightforward tests. She ensures students truly learn the material and clearly cares about their success.

Farmer is the best professor in the political science department and it is a shame that she is leaving. She is a tough professor but extremely smart and available to help students. My only complaint is that her last test was inconsistently harder than the rest. The level of difficulty on her exams is very inconsistent.

She is very effective at making a class like her so she can make everyone accept what she says even if it is downright mythical or based off her own form of logic.  She is very negative and cynical. You do not need a teacher that drags you down everyday.

Dr. Farmer is extremely understanding when it comes to assignments and the factors that might make an assignment more difficult to hand in at a certain time. She is also very thorough with course material always making sure clarity on a subject/topic is had by all students in class. The class is also made more interesting by her love of South Asia.

Dr. Farmer is brilliant. Her class is challenging yet you learn a lot.Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended to do well as her lectures are very informative. Complaints: spent way too much time on India in the last unit,takes too long to grade papers,textbook is very wordy. However, overall she's one of my favorite professors so far.

She is not easy, but if you attend all of the lectures and write down EVERYTHING  she says or pay attention and understand it, you honestly can pull of above 90 average on her tests. She explains the material so clear and slow that makes you feel like you are a dumb kid sometimes. She is soo fair and helpful with respect to office hours and essays

I can tell how much effort she has put in by the carefully selected reading materials. Never met a professor with such great concern for students. Since I was first time abroad, she even helped me with my papers and some difficult readings. More importantly, it's in her class I find directions and build confidence for all my study now and later on.

I can tell how much effort she has put in by the reading materials.I have never met a professor who has so much concern for students. She was so helpful after class. She helped me with my papers and some difficult readings and more importantly, she helped me find directions and build confidence in all my study later on as an international student.
Hands down best professor in the department. Shes engaging and interesting to listen to and she works her butt off to ensure that students fully understand the material.

Dr. Farmer was one of the best professors I had during my year at Geneseo. Shes passionate about the subject material and her lectures are always clear and packed with lots of important information. She grades fairly and her tests are easy if you go to class, take notes, and read the textbook.

Her classes are taught at a level above average. Low on the use of technology, she requires that you take notes by hand - a good thing to help you retain knowledge better, not as good if you are a slow writer. Very effective in increasing knowledge on subject matter, and writes excellent recommendations. Worthy of connection beyond the classroom.

Although this course looks at statistical findings, it's understandable for the non-mathematical student. Dr. Farmer goes over the information in as many ways necessary to ensure students understand the concepts. It is an extremely valuable class post undergrad and is undervalued. Dr. Farmer's extremely knowledgable and will always assist students

Dr. Farmer is the reason I'm still at Geneseo. She is the best professor I have had here not only because of her outstanding teaching skills but her dedication and general concern for  students. Although a lot of effort is required to obtain a high mark, her intentions are to make us better students  and more well informed citizens in the long run.

I learned so much from Comparative Politics with Dr. Farmer. The course lectures were well organized for Comparative Politics.  It is important to do the course readings and take good notes in order to obtain a good note. You get the grade you work for. Dr. Farmer is always willing to help her students. Great course!!!

Hands down my favorite prof at Geneseo, lectures are stimulating,but the course work in intense and the tests are difficult. HOWEVER, if you put in the time and use Farmer as a resource, you can do well. She is beyond accessible during office hours, and is truly a brilliant woman. Hope to take her again in the future.

Don't take Farmer, unless you are a serious Poly Sci major...or have no other choice. Her lessons are convoluted and extremely scatterbrained/unorganized (still hasn't finished grading our essays that were handed in over a month ago). Tests are extremely hard and every question is meant to trick you. Very egotistical and impatient with studennts.

Dr.Farmer is a no nonsense kind of a professor! She is crystal clear about what she expects. She is a tough grader, but by no means unfair or unreasonable in her expectations. She is straightforward when you visit her in her office and extremely helpful. She's a great go to for discussing future plans as well. One of the best in the department!

She is wonderful! You will learn a lot! She is not an easy grader and you must put in a lot of time to get an okay grade. If you're focused on getting good grades you might not want to take her. If you really want to learn a lot do! I love her class! You MUST read the book AND go to class. Best for PLSC majors. It's a hard class for GenEds.

I had Professor Farmer a number of years ago, when she was a professor at  another university, for a class on Western Europe. I am glad to see she is still teaching. I thought she was an excellent professor, interesting and well read. She was also encouraging and her advice eventually led me to law school. Thanks, Professor Farmer!

She is a great professor to learn with, but in reality you don't need to go to her class to do well in the exams. She is helpful if you wish to talk about some related topics to the class or your essays, exmas. she is very willing to help, but for some reason studying doesn't help people in this class. People consistently get the same grades.
I learned so much from her. College is about learning, if ou put the work in you will do well in the class...a B is a amazing grade in her class!

I learned a ton in this class and I thought her assignments were great if you are truly seeking to learn the material. However, I will probably not take her again-its not worth it-her class was my lowest grade. You have to put in a ton of time if you want above a B

By no means does an easy professor, but if you go to class and pay attention, you'll learn a lot.She does have a tendency to unfairly snap at students in class at times, but outside of class is probably one of the most accessible professors there is.Do the reading, go to class, ask for help, and let it slide off if she snaps at you, you'll do fine.

Politics of South Asia: she is in love with India so we spent most of the semester on India which was frustrating because we didn't cover any other country. That said, she is extremely smart and I learned a great deal. She is a tough grader but not impossible to do well. B+ is a very good grade with her.

Learned a lot in this class. It was very hard but if you are going to continue in plsc, its worth it. She is a tough grader but not impossible and she's very accessible outside of class. Do the reading, if you are not prepared she WILL call you out on it. Overall a very good, knowledgeable prof though she is a bit hard and harsh.

I read & re-read every chapter of the mindnumbing books, copied her notes word for word, and STILL only ended up with a B-! Class was very frustrating due to the impossible grading/workload. She also picks favorites and then talks down to everyone else. Def a women on a power trip so TAKE ANOTHER PROF for Poli Sci credits.

One of the most intelligent professors here. That said, her classes are far from easy, once you get past the 100 level. You will read real books, not a textbook. Very accessible to students. Go to class, read the books, talk, and you'll do well. Tests are hard but not impossible, especially if you do the reading.

I had her for both 223 and 120 in the same semester. As someone stated she does begin to have students that she prefers part way through the class: the ones that show up, do the reading, and participate. She is not a very easy grader, but is clear about test material. Do your work, go to class, and you'll enjoy it and learn a lot.

Professor Farmer's Dev World politics class was extremely boring. You don't really learn much and the books are completely mindnumbing. The class is easy though but not worth taking professor's rudeness to students

Dr. Farmer is easily one of the most intelligent professors I've ever had-- but she's a Poli Sci professor, not a teacher. She just doesn't really know how to get the material into your head short of yelling it at you. She grades very hard, and tears essays to shreds.  Don't anger this woman. Her vengeance shall be swift, terrible, and exact.

Dr Farmer is an excellent professor and really knows the subject matter.  Her grading isn't easy, but if you put in the effort and go to class you can definitely get an A.  Bring drafts to her for editing, or just go ask questions- she is extremely helpful in office hours.  Of all the teachers I've had, she is the most  accessible to her students.

She is a very smart woman, but such a harsh grader! You have to really stay on top of taking notes and following the lecture. The material is interesting, but the tests are hard to do well on because theyre all essay questions and out of 25 points. So if you get 3 points off, thats already an 88 out of 100. I would recommend if you want to learn.

Professor Farmer is very knowledgeable about what she teaches. If you want an easy 200 level plsc course do not take this one! It is a lot of reading and studying if you want to get an A. Participation counts so come to class and read the book. She drops the lowest test but be warned: don't take the last test which is an 8 page book report.
Prof Farmer is neurotic and a little crazy but she knows her stuff.  She is a nit picky grader so even if you go to class and do the reading your tests grades may still not be that great.

I think I'm in the same class as the person who rated professor farmer previous to myself, and I must say for the most part He or She's correct. She gives us an unreasonable amount of work and studying for the tests in no way assures a good grade.VERY tough teacher is her reputation around here. She knows what she's talking about though.

She is absolutely insane, she must think the class you take with her is the only class you take based on the reading work load. The tests are so specific from the reading. She wakes up everyday and wishes she was Asian also.

I loved proffessor Farmer's class. If you see past her neurotic tendencies she is a great professor who really loves to teach. She is sometimes brutally honest but don't take that personally. Will meet with you at all hours of the day, early morning or at night. I hope to take S. Asian politics and her developing world class. Professor not to miss.

painfully easy, esp if you're a poli sci or IR major. spends most of class talking about how class is going to be run, not on the material. you can easily get away with not doing the reading. if you're willing to sacrifice actually learning something for an easy A, she's your prof.

Attendance important only when Professor goes over current events in the studied countries.  If you memorize the important points for each test, you'll do fine. Drops lowest score.  Professor helpful outside of class as well, but she takes way too long to actually begin class.
I love professor farmer!
boring class, u learned nothin, everythin is from the book just read n pass the class, rushes everythin, seems like she got 2 personalities. not a good teacher take someone else.
my favorite polsci/IR professor so far!
Loves those that participate.  Sometimes talks down to class (especially if no one can answer questions on the reading).
I hated this class, wrote one 12 page paper on a topic that you picked in the first week, so if you picked a bad topic you were screwed, also the book was very boring.
very helpful in office hours, uses scare tactics but is actually a very nice lady, obsessed with India

Great professor, when she actually gets into the material. Spends a huge amount of time each class going over how she is going to run the class, leaving little time for the actual material. Tough grader as well, but very helpful outside of class

Ive taken just about all of the professors in the political science department and Dr. Farmer is by far the best. She actually looks for your input and was always will to help out with any questions. Shes old enough to know a lot but still young enough to remember what it was like to be a student.
No Comments

Decent class, she's a great professor and is very helpful. She likes to hear what her students have to say about topics and she is very knowledgeable. Has a sense of humor, and is a fair grader. All we did in this class was write a research paper on a topic of your choice, not that bad of an assignment

Love him. He's clear in lecture and good at answering questions. Go to office hours at least once, especially if you're a chem/biochem major. He's so friendly and always smiles and waves when he sees people around. He's also the department chair so make sure you don't get off on the wrong foot because you might find yourself needing his help.

Dr. Peterson was an amazing professor. He's passionate about what he does, and you can tell he wants everyone to succeed. He's thorough in answering questions, is very approachable, and keeps things organized well. He does lots of worksheets and review in-class to help you prepare for the test. I would 10/10 recommend taking him.
he's a great prof and probably the reason i passed chem at all
teaches and explains well, chill guy, nothing bad to say about him
Peterson is a great teacher and is very friendly

Analytical chem with Dr. Peterson was an easy course provided you paid attention to lectures and did the homework yourself. The tests were straight forward with point recovery options available after the exam was returned to you. Everything is clearly laid out and thought through to make sure students can get the most out of the course content.

I had Professor. Peterson for my Chem 129 Lab, and he was amazing. He is very kind and is always free to help with the lab procedures if you are having trouble. The lab papers were graded by his TAs and were fair grades. He did want everybody to finish by a certain time but would allow you to stay after to finish the lab. Great Professor.

Dr. Peterson is a super kind and helpful professor. I was so nervous for chem 116 and although it was difficult he taught very clearly. Class was mostly practice problems. At some points his lecture lacked a little bit of a solid foundation. I would've liked more solid notes rather than practice problems however everyone learns differently.

Dr. Peterson is the best professor I've had so far at Geneseo. His lectures are clear and he always makes sure you can ask questions and he answers them well. He wants you to do well in this class and always offers help. He is such a sweet guy overall and if he is an option for any class you take definitely pick him!

He is a super nice guy and very helpful, his lectures are very interesting. He gives a good amount of extra credit and his tests are fair for what we learn. If you get the chance to take his class definitely do, homework was pretty easy and only weekly and only 4 exams.

Dr. Peterson was an excellent teacher for an introductory chem level course! Homeworks and pre-lecture assignments were easy and a great grade booster. Also, very keen on giving extra credit (2% maximum added to your total grade)! Tests are easy if you take good notes and understand the concepts. Final was a conglomeration of old test questions.

Peterson is great! Very nice guy and makes the learning process for chem very easy. Take tests seriously and study the homeworks. As of this review, they dropped the letter grade for an A to a 92%, you can get 2% of extra credit, and an entire test gets dropped (4 tests total). BTW the final was also pretty easy. Just study the old tests.

He is my favorite chem professor. Only wants you to do well in his class and loves his students. Very flexible when it comes to work and all of the exams are all multiple choice. Sweetest man on the planet, if I continued being a chemistry major I would only take classes with him.

This was my first semester with Dr. Peterson in lab and was the first time I truly enjoyed a lab. I enjoyed the inquiry based experiments and making determinations on our own, instead of structured experiments (like CHEM119). The semester had with a DIY research project turned experiment that Peterson helped you through when necessary.

Had him for so many classes, he is the reason I am graduating. He is one of my favs. Always willing to help even when it's not for his class. He cares about us a lot, and likes to make dad jokes. Courses are challenging but he will walk you through things when you are confused. One of the best instructors I have ever had

Genuinely one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Very clear and concise when talking and is very passionate about what he does. If there's ever a question he makes sure that he answers the question to the understanding of the student asking. Also had him for chem 209 and was very approachable if there was ever any issues.

Prof Peterson is very kind, accessible and willing to work with students to make sure they succeed. The class was all material that was taught to most NYS HS chem students, but Prof Peterson still kept things interesting. 3-5 Pre-Lecture readings a week and 1 homework assignment (10-20 Qs) was typical. Very hard to not receive an A in the class.

grading was tough, but he is very accessible both inside and outside of class. the class was a pretty large time commitment for a two-credit lab, but that's more about the class structure than his teaching specifically. he is forgiving and was more than willing to help with any questions or concerns i had during the semester. id recommend him!

comment: Very tough grader with limited explanation to why the grade was received. Was not good at answering questions asked from the class or explanation of the topic. Also was not very accommodating to extenuating circumstances.

comment: Although I only had him for lab, I felt that Peterson was a very good professor. His lectures are easy to understand and very interesting. He is also readily available to help and very accommodating if there is an issue. As long as you put the effort in you will do great! Definitely taking another class with him in the future.

He is a great professor. Extremely intelligent and willing to help. Anytime he isn't teaching a class, even if it isn't during his designated office hours, he is willing to help. I made sure to have him has my professor for my lab next semester. Just make sure you are vigilant with sigfigs.

Dr. Peterson is kinda scary at first, but once you get the courage to go to office hours he is one of the nicest professors I've ever met. If you're struggling with a lab, he'll help you out a ton, especially with excel because I had no idea how to work excel.  I'd definitely recommend taking a class with him.

Peterson's teaching is geared towards the smartest students in class. He likes to keep his job interesting by presenting questions that are challenging to even him. He is passionate about what he does and would definitely win Chemistry's Next Top Model. His tests are definitely difficult. but he can admit that and will curve accordingly.

His tests are very challenging, but the curves are usually pretty good. Lectures are very confusing and so are the notes. Makes mistakes all the time in lecture and on tests. SI sessions are super helpful. You can do okay if you work really hard.

Peterson is an excellent professor!! For someone who struggles a lot with chemistry, he definitely provided materials necessary to practice and succeed (ex: lectures posted online, practice tests, SI sessions). His tests are often ridiculously challenging satanic, but he is very generous with the curve if the whole class does not do well.

I seriously loved having Dr. Peterson as a teacher. He is such a nice and approachable guy outside of class. His tests are very difficult, but the final is based off his tests almost identically, so it's not bad He is extremely knowledgable and passionate about chemistry and I would recommend him. He also curves VERY generously!!!

Professor Peterson makes this class harder than it has to be. The averages for the tests range from a 55-70, but he does add a very nice curve. Make sure you do well on the first exam because it gets a lot harder as the course progresses. SI sessions are really helpful.

Very difficult course to do well in. Average test grades ranged from 50-60s and tests are very difficult. Too smart to be teaching general chemistry. Notes are very unclear and you must study hours just to get an 80. Very sweet and not bad to look at.
Peterson made Chemistry bearable, he was very specific on things you wouldn't be tested on and just an overall great professor. Highly recommend him.
He' s really passionate about what he does an genuinely wants people to do well. He ended up re-curving our tests mid semester.
Prof. Peterson is a great professor. Make sure you pay attention in the class.Won't curve a little if you need to get a high grade.So, stay alert!
Super friendly and approachable professor! Recommend him.

he is very nice and will help you with anything you dont understand makes a note to learn everyone in a lecture class' name doesnt believe in e.c but is understanding and does a huge curve. i went to class 1/3 times a week and just did the mastering chem hw the night before the test and got a had him for lab too and would recommend blogs r easy pts
one of the best professors I've had by far. tests are challenging but fair. as long as you read the textbook and go to class you should be fine.
