Physical Geography is a boring class, but he makes it enjoyable.  He's funny and he presents the material clearly.  Usually, he ends class a few minutes early.  The tests aren't very difficult IF you study the notes for a few days.  Overall, he's a very good teacher.

Definitely the coolest prof Ive had so far. Very funny, makes class go by fast, labs never take full kab time. No homework, 3 exams, 2 lab quizzes. Study for the tests, go to class more often that not, and relax cause you're getting an A. Aagesen is the man.

Amazing teacher and amazign guy. Tests are not hard, and the class is interesting. Even if if wasn't, he would make it interesting because he is hilarious. He came into class one day with a dress on. He truly cares about the students. Amazing!!!
This guy is amazing. He's hilarious and we are always laughing in class. The class is really easy and interesting. My favorite teacher!!!
He's a great teacher, he's funny and entertaining, tells interesting stories and you never have to read the book to do really good on tests that are right from notes he basically gives you!

Great guy, makes me want to get out and explore the world. I had him 2 years ago and still am looking for another class to take with him. I didn't even care about my grade at the end because class was so intersting
The guy's awesome.  His tests are multiple choice and T/F.  If you study a little and go to class, it's an easy A.  Labs don't usually take the full time either.
excellent teacher, fun in class, & very helpful

By far, one of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure to meet. Thoroughly enjoyed his classes, and it's a rare occurrence when a teacher takes the time to get to know his students on a personal level. Just can't say enough about this guy. 5 stars.
Fun, interesting, entertaining!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment:
Dr. Oberg is a good guy! I sometimes found his lectures a little hard to follow and struggled to keep up with some of the readings, but I still earned an A because of my writing and in-class participation. I'll put some advice on how to succeed in Oberg's class in some of his own words: 

Show up, Talk, Read, and Do good work. (...and don't cheat)
i loved oberg so much hes a very kind and caring professor.

Took obergs class on American Indian Boarding schools. VERY interesting professor and topic itself. Very difficult grader in that he expects a lot of effort and work on your part. A grade to be proud of after working so hard but He's just a good guy in general and that shows in his work.
you negotiate your grade at the end of the year - have to participate in class if you want a good grade (papers can help you a little but)
You "negotiate" your grade at the end of the quarter- the guy pretty much knows what he wants to give you and is pretty unreceptive to feedback.

Dr. Oberg is my favorite professor. I took EXP188 (American Cornerstones) my first semester, and I actively felt my brain grow. Lectures were run as one big class discussion, welcoming input and opinions from students. Dr. Oberg is suave, funny, a true academic, and he also doesn't do traditional grades- he asks you what you deserve, which is cool.
One of the best professors on campus

Professor Oberg is an absolute gift to SUNY Geneseo, he is by far my favorite professor! The class is extremely easy if you are proactive and participate! He always wants his students to succeed and I love that you get to argue your grade! This class was amazing and I recommend it to any enthusiastic students! My advice is to be honest with grades!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: LOVE OBERG Took this class Spring 23 he's become one of my fave professors. He's hilarious; cares about his students. Can come off a bit abrasive, but just talk to him, go to office hours if you're struggling. He wants you to succeed. No tests but GO TO CLASS. Put in the time and energy, think critically about what you're learning  you'll get an A

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Love this man. Took HUMN 220 over the summer (In England!) with him. You have plenty of books to read but just offer an opinion in class here and there and actually try with your paper at the end of the trip and you'll get a good grade. He lets you argue for your grade and most of the time agrees with you. Sarcastic exhausted dad vibes.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Oberg is very funny and very nice. Unless you want to spend all semester working away researching, DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!! He lets you grade yourself which seems nice but he is extremely harsh with the grading policy. He's a great guy, not a great guy to take a class with though. Class can also be awkward bc he has the whole class critique your papers

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Oberg, he is super passionate about what he teaches and he makes the discussions interesting. He cares about what everyone has to say. Make sure to participate in class and show effort and it is an easy A.

He is very knowledgeable and passionate and it truly shows when he teaches and gives feedback. Make sure you can hold yourself accountable for researching (if you're taking 302). Participation matters greatly, but so does improving and learning from your peers and him.

He is a good professor but directions are very vague. Gives tough critiques. Let's you pick the grade you think you deserve and "negotiate/defend" why you deserve it. Participation will carry you. Attend all of his chat sessions to show you care and you will be good.

Oberg is incredibly passionate about the material. Im an Ed major who did not think that I would care about this class but he truly brings the material to life. He does not believe in grading assignments, assigning a wholistic grade at the end of the semester in a meeting where he has you share what grade you think you deserve and why.

(This was COVID-19 semester, so take this for what you will.) Clearly passionate about what he teaches. Can't say I'm a fan of his "argue for your grade at the end of the semester" style, but he's a good professor and willing to make adjustments for what you need. 2 papers, but I think he requires too many sources (30) for a 10-15 pg paper.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Oberg really rubbed me the wrong way at first but by the end of the semester he was one of my favorites. His lectures are really interesting and he really knows a lot about Native American History. Also the class is DUMB EASY. Don't buy all the books, just buy 2 of them that are used the most. As long as you show interest you'll do well.

Although he would not take attendance, participation counted a lot, so it was important that you were present in participating in discussions. He is a very hard professor and does not hold class very often. He is kind when you talk to him in person, and seems like he does not expect a lot, until your gardes come out. Overall ratingnot good.

If you write well, this is the Hum for you. 3 papers and participation is all there is. Class discussion and course material are interesting, sometimes fascinating. He leans left on the political spectrum, so I especially recommend to anyone knowledgeable via mass incarceration, war in the middle east, inequality, etc.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Oberg is extremely knowledgeable, and expects you to know it all too. He's not afraid to speak his mind if he doesn't like you. The amount of reading was impossible to keep up with, but you don't have to do it all if you're good at making stuff up on the spot. You NEED to participate - your grade is made of participation and a handful of essays.

A good professor, don't do the essays the night before it will not end well.  He is really funny and doesn't hold you longer than necessary. Does stress participation so don't think this a class where you can just not show up and do well.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: I actually really enjoyed this class. The books weren't too bad, and his discussions in class made them better. DO NOT do the paper the night before. Always do the reading so you can participate when he discusses it.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: He is very opinionated but in all is a great professor. Tough grader on his first couple papers but if you go to his office hours he will help you a lot. Will proof read essays for you and tells you if you're going in the right direction. Not a bad INTD at all.

Ultimately he's a cool guy, but very opinionated and expects a lot of reading for a 200 level course. He's a harsh grader on your papers, but that is all it is to the course; reading and papers.  If you have the time to read nine books in one semester, he's decent as long as you participate in class. Personally, I've never done so poorly in a class

Oberg assigns a lot of reading and it is a very tough grader. That being said, he is a very good professor whose class can really open up your mind. You'll do well if you do the readings and participate in class. If you're looking for an easy class or easy gen ed, this isn't it. But if you're willing to work, this is a great class.

It's all essay-based so if you can write, it's an easy A. I read maybe half of the books. Just participate and show up most of the time and you'll be fine. Also, the discussion was generally very engaging for HUMN. Oh, and he hates Thomas Jefferson and it's hilarious to hear him talk about it.

Oberg is a great professor. He's easily my favorite professor at Geneseo. He is very passionate about what he studies. Funny and cynical, he makes the class worth going to whether you like the topic or not. Constructive but very fair with grading. If you work hard you'll do well. I highly recommend him

Teaches the humanities very well. Be prepared to speak up in class. He grades it on participation and 3 essays so make sure you can write well and take a stance. I'm glad I have him but I'm wary to recommend him as I don't think he works well with everyone

Good professor, lots of readings but can mostly be skimmed. Good discussions and lectures in class, and will help you if you ask for it. Very important to make comments and participate in class. All 3 exams are take home essays, ~5 pages, that require plenty of quotes and evidence from the texts, but require no citations. In short, take the class.
He knows what he is lecturing about, and be prepared to speak up in class. He asks really thoughtful questions, and overall I'm glad I have him.

His teaching style is very hit-or-miss. He has great discussions in his class and is very helpful in office hours. He knows a lot about his area, but not a lot beyond that. He has very strong opinions about things and he definitely lets you know.
Do the reading assigned and take notes.He may know his material but I found him to be rude in class.The good thing is all exams are take home essays,so that helps.

Comments saying that this is a hard class which requires reading are justified. This shouldn't be a bad thing, come on, this is college. Oberg is a excellent teacher and a fair grader, participation is extremely important. Show interest in his class and he will help you out. Extremely knowledgeable and funny
He is kind of an a** hole. But he knows his stuff. He has dry humor that makes the class fun, but he is arrogant in person and not very helpful. If you get stressed out easily, don't take him.
DO THE READING! The assessments are based on what you've read and Oberg can tell when you aren't prepared. He's extremely knowledgeable but a bit intimidating.

This is a great class.  Don't believe what people say about it being really hard. He gives out papers and no mid-terms. do the reading, write an essay with eveidnece, and speak in class, and you got nothing to worry about. Do those things and it is an easy a

A great professor and an awesome class. He is passionate about Native American history and it shows. Starting this semester he has decided to do away with tests - our grades consisted of 10 essays (the two lowest were dropped) for 80% of the grade and in class participation for the other 20%. Expect to do most of the reading and go to every class.
Dr. Oberg likes to joke, likes the Bills, and likes to hear himself talk but he is a good teacher if you like history you should tak him
Interesting to listen to, but kindof a **** when it comest to politics.  Needs to keep his own views out of lecture.
Very smart professor. Learned a great deal in his classes, but highly stressful as well.  Very helpful to some students, and absolutely useless and dismissive with others.

Took the INTD about the lost colonies of roanoke. Oberg is really knowledgeable on the subject and knows everything on the topic. The class focused more on the subject as opposed to the writing which defeats the purpose. If you're a weak writer, don't take this. If you're a strong writer the class is a breeze.

I really liked his class. I thought that it was very interesting. Yes, there was LOTS to read, but if you did the readings and came to class it was easy to get a good grade. Beware of the 20 page paper... not hard, just long!!
You always have to read every assignment he gives you in depth. It is best to always participate in class to get a decent grade.
No Comments

Seemed easy at the outset of the class. If you state something he doesn't agree with in your writing he may not adequately explain the drop in your grade. He's a nice guy and lecture is rather enjoyable. Sadly, he is a professor that allows or even helps foster an environment where you have to suck up to do well. Anticipate unnecessary stress.

His exams are take home papers and that doesn't make things easy. There's lots of reading to do and he's a very hard grader on papers. He does say a lot of interesting stuff in his lecture but his notes are useless in writing the paper. He'll really lower your grade if you don't participate. I don't recommend him if you're not a history major.

I give him credit, he is very into Native American studies and makes the material very interesting. However, he is an unbelievably hard grader and won't give reason to your grade.  He is also impossible to reach outside of class, never being at his office hours even when he says he will extend them, and not believing in appointments.

He is a hard grader. I felt like I learned very little and I went to just about every class. I think he has favorites. He's not very approachable for everyone. I give him credit he does try to make class lively. Don't take him if your not a history major!

Don't listen to some of these comments.  I hardly read anything, but by going to class and taking great notes, I received two A's from his classes.  He is an amazing teacher. Speak up in class, and just skim over the material, you will do good.

Native American History he is very passionate about the subject and it comes through when he is teaching it, expect a lot of notes, challenging reading and papers to write but you learn a lot. Don't ask too many questions he gets annoyed
he is not as hard of a grader as everyone says, i am not even good with history and i got higher than a B on a paper, and he didn't give any tests... i think he is interesting and worth taking
Funny guy, lively lectures.  If you go to class and he sees you, I think he'll be nice to you unlike what the other people are saying.  I think...

He is a very smart man, and very funny in class. HOWEVER he was very unhelpful out of class, and gave people attitude or talked down on them when they tried to reach him for extra help.  He is a ridiculously hard grader.

oberg is an amazing teacher! he knows everything on the subject and doesnt even look at notes! smartest man alive! and real funny.  he is kinda a tough grader, but if you try hard and do the reading youll be fine. he likes the Bills!
Oberg is a genius. The class is really hard but if you take the time to do the reading you will get a lot out of it. He is also really funny in a cynical and morbid way.
very hard grader, but I learned more in his class about writing then ever before- but be ready to work

Oberg is amazing- excellent. Really tough grader-has been known to give out Fs for really bad essays (a C means you worked hard and wrote an average paper), but you cheat yourself by not taking his class. He teaches really well, is fun and entertaining, and is nice if you are a serious student.

the guys amazing. he doesn't use any notes to teach, he just knows it all. but he uses it against you, and tries to make you think you know nothing. he grades ridiculously too. never got anything higher than a B on anything, didn't meet anyone that did either.

Knows what he's talking about, but that's the problem...  He's arrogant, and an unusually difficult grader.  For the most part acts as if his students will never achieve the same level of understanding as him.
Very interesting but a hard grader.
hard grader, but very helpful
You take a ton of notes and are not allowed to use them for his take-home tests.  He doesn't like to give anything higher than a B.
awesome teacher
No Comments
No Comments

There are only 4 tests in this class. That is all you're graded on. He doesn't really state what's on the test and doesn't always cover what's on the test in the lecture. Do not take this class with him if you can avoid it.

Do not take this class if you don't have to. Very tough grader. not very helpful on the papers even though he says he is. He doesn't understand that he's the issue when the class average on a test is a 68. You're pretty much on your own.

4 tests are your only grades the whole semester. They weren't too hard, but go to the TA reviews, they give practice questions that really help. All of the questions were from lecture, not the book, so I wish I hadn't spent money on something I didn't need. Overall, not a bad class and he makes it pretty easy to do well.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']
comment: 4 tests. Lectures were recorded and posted, we had a TA who did review sessions before each exam. Accessible via email and was good with accommodations, I needed to take my final early and he was very nice about it. Make sure you study the links and videos from class and don't buy the book! All of the exam questions were from lecture.

I loved Bazzett's behavioral res class! It was synchronous zooms that were not mandatory, but most of the class usually went. He lets you keep handing in drafts for the papers until the due date/ until you get a 25/25 which is a huge plus to taking his class. He is super nice and wants you to succeed in this class.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: I had Bazzett for a previous class and I thought I would enjoy being in his class again but no. He grades really hard for all the papers and if he doesn't understand something he writes question marks all over and barely gives any feedback. This is a tough class so be ready to write the way he wants.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Each class period is a lecture and the notes are always posted online. He makes the subjects interesting and engaging and will tell you in class possible (very probable) questions that will be on the test. There are only 4 grades which are the 4 tests and while they are challenging he reviews in class and prepares you well. Very nice too!

Bosch is my favorite bio professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but his slides do not always have the information you need to do well on tests. He can be a little disorganized but he makes lecture and lab fun! He is quick to answer questions through email. He is also very accommodating for student athletes and other school organizations!

Dr Bosch is one of the best science professors I've ever had. I studied abroad with him, and he went above and beyond to accommodate my directed study. He was so caring and helpful, you can tell he really loves what he does and knows what he is talking about. Lecture and powerpoint heavy, but is more than willing to help if you need it.

I had Dr. Bosch for the second half of my BIOL117 course. He has a solid understanding of the concepts but goes incredibly slow. We were always falling behind with the material. Other than that, he is methodical in his teaching and will ensure that everybody understands the concepts. Also, would clearly outline what would be on the tests.

I had bosch for the second half of bio 117 and let me say thank god. Yes, he might be slow but he does the work to help you understand everything and if you are willing to be on the same page with him I say you'll have a great time. His tests were hard for me but it might not be for you if you are a good test taker.

Goes very slow in lectures. Wastes time in lecture on confusing case studies. Approachable if you have questions. Tests are easier than Lewis's. Just read the textbook. Great if you are a bio major. Does not grade attendance but lectures are important, sometimes he teaches something slightly different than in the textbook

He is an amazing professor who is incredibly passionate about his work. One of the most approachable professors here. He is always willing to answer questions and really wants you to learn the material. Make sure to utilize his office hours. It will be save you.

I really enjoyed having Dr. Bosch for the second half of Gen Bio I and II. He speaks softly and comes across very caring. You can tell he is passionate about biology and he wants everyone to succeed. He is very approachable. He and Feissner make a good team, he goes slow in lectures, and tests, similar to Feissner's, are very doable.

Dr. Bosch gave great feedback on assignments and reports, and he was very considerate and caring in regards to my concerns. He genuinely cares and is enthusiastic about his teachings. I would definitely take him again

Absolutely amazing teacher. It's very obvious that Prof Bosch knows so much about what he teaches and puts every effort into helping his students excel. He does give a TON of homework and the tests are super hard but if you use the resources he gives you the class is easy

Dr. Bosch makes the subjects he teaches so interesting. When he teaches Gen Bio with Feissner, it is truly the dream team in action. He explains everything clearly, and is very accessible outside of class. If you don't do the homework though, you won't do well on the tests.

The nicest professor you'll meet on campus. Read the textbook and pay attention to lectures to do well in his class. He was very enthusiastic during lectures and he doesn't fly through slides so it's easy to take notes. If you're confused about anything, stop by his office and he'll break it down fully to make sure you walk away understanding it.
One of the nicest professors at Geneseo! Literally so nice and cares so much about his students.

While Bio 117 is a tough class, Dr. Bosch makes it clear what is on the tests based on what is on the lecture slides. However, it is still a lot of material to keep track of (and the questions on the tests include both application questions and questions based on definitions), so this class still requires quite a bit of studying.

Professor Bosch's teaching style is very boring and dry. It would be easier to have him as a teacher if he was first - instead of having Dr. O'Donnell first, who was energetic and kept the class very interesting. I had a hard time staying awake with Bosch. His lectures don't align with the textbook pages he gives. Overall, He is an OKAY teacher.

I currently have Bosch and O'Donnell (they switch halfway through the semester) and Bosch is just so caring and loves biology he gets so into it. He's adorable and he really makes an effort to help his students out! if you email him hell answer quickly and he wants everyone t do well, he isn't out to get anyone

Bosch is my favorite professor at Geneseo. He is so knowledgable and enthusiastic about what he teaches! He can be a little disorganized and takes a while to grade. However, he is a really nice guy and he actually wants his students to succeed. Also he has a very soothing voice. I highly recommend Bosch as a professor.

Great teacher! One of the only professors I've found at Geneseo that actually cares about you and isn't trying to destroy your GPA. He will really try to help you out and wants the best for everyone. Definitely recommend taking him!

Every other year Bosch teaches ecology when one of the professors go on sabbatical. The only problem is that he is NOT passionate about the subject an thus makes it an unpleasant to be in his class. Not very knowledgable about the subject and puts minimal effort into his lectures, can be interesting when he talks about research experiences abroad.

Bosch was one of the easiest professors I have ever had. Just take notes on the PowerPoints before the tests and you should be fine (although I don't think he teaches ecology too often). He takes one hundred and twelve years to hand assignments back, so you're probably better off badgering him for your grade so at least he'll finish yours.

Great class, great teacher.  Can be tough to understand what he wants sometimes, but if you put in the effort and talk to him if you're confused, you'll get a good grade.  Great with extensions or understanding if you need extra time with something.

LOVED this guy. I figured I'd be a ecology pro without studying, but after I failed my first two exams he actually reached out to me to come see him. After I started going to office hours my test grades went from 60's to 90's. Ended up with a B+ in his class, which I'm pretty sure he just gave me for my effort at the end.

He is very clear in class, but I don't find him extremely approachable. His grading on tests is sometimes very unclear, especially since his handwriting is illegible. He is very slow at grading things so it might be two months before you know what you got on an assignment. He has made it pretty clear that he cares about his other classes more.

bosch is the man went to class on average 2/3 a week and only crammed the night before each test, he jokes around and shows videos like everyday, some of the stuff he says in class is just facts that hes doesnt even test on, lab is easy and boosts your grade since they count together as one class, some of class material is boring but recommend him
Really loved this class. Learned a lot. Dr. Bosch has so much background in his field and is super approachable. You should definitely take his class.
Very nice, down to earth guy.  Very interested in the students work and loves to show little demonstrations during the bio lab even though he's just a supervisor.

Dr. Bosch is Great!!! He is so  helpful and he really cares about how his students perform in his class. If people put in the adequate amount of time they are sure to excel and do well! Also if they are having trouble he will be more than welcome to help.

Bosch was the only reason I took this class.  He is a great, enthusiastic professor and a down to earth guy.  Lab was the most unorganized but relaxed lab I have ever been in.  Lecture was good and power point slides were great.  Four tests, one poster research project, and the final isn?t cumulative. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! BOSCH IS AWESOME!

Plays favroits. If you not one of them an you go to his office to ask a question an one of his favroits shows up, he will blow you off an talk to that other person. Practice exams are worthless as are the study guids. Also openly admitted to not wanting to teach a spring class which was mandatory in order to do research the following semester.

Dr. Bosch is very arrogant and is a fan of favoritism. I do not recommend him. If he doesn't like you, he's not impartial at all and your grades will reflect it. Take Dr. Harvitsen, the nicest girl you'll ever meet!

Dr. Bosch is a great professor to take. Bosch is constantly going out of his way to help his students. He is a great guy and works hard to keep his students happy. He is always willing to take time out of his schedule to help.

Really, really awesome guy and a decent class. Ecology isn't what you expect--but Bosch tries really hard and he's really passionate about it. I highly recommend him and I'll definitely try to get him for another class sometime soon.
you have to like bosch in order to take his class. Everyone who took this course liked him, even though the material was less than what i expected. He's a cool guy, did a nice field trip!!! :)

There is really not that much work throughout the semester, but the tests can be really hard.  You need to study a lot for them and there is a lot of info he expects you to know.  The review sheet that he makes does help somewhat.  Overally not that hard and he is a good teacher who knows his stuff.
Interesting lectures, some times. He makes the class harder than it needs to be and tests on random things. I didn't learn anything in his class. He also gives busy work.
A great professor.  Easy to talk to, approachable, understanding, and dedicated.  Tricky test question require thought and much studying.

i don;t know what the first 2 comments are about, obviously theyve got the wrong dr. bosch. He's the coolest professor. KNows what its like to be human and a college student, well sympthathize with you. Hey, he's super cool.

Makes an easy subject matter difficult, by not being clear on what he wants.  He lectures on one thing and tests on another. His questions on tests are often misleading, also.  He's a nice guy, just needs to improve on the teaching...
A very misleading man with very misleading questions with even more misleading answers. This man is evil, don't listen to everyone's lies.
Awesome professor.  Test do require studying but nothing to major.
great professor!  easy class, and definately fun! one of my favorite bio classes thus far
Simply Superb!
Dr. Bosch was by far the best professor I had at Geneseo.  Definetly a really cool guy and I learned so much from him!!
Dr. Bosch's class was tough at times, but his review sheets were awesome and very helpful. He's a reasonable guy and if you're genuinely interested in the class, you'll do well.
He's such a nice guy.  His exams can be a little tough, but if you go to class and read when you're supposed to, it's not that bad.  He's ALWAYS willing to help you out if you need it too.
I cant really say whether his class is easy or not because I was in his Bio 128 which basically just tried to help freshman bio..but he no doubt is a very helpful and nice person

Dr. Bosch is very willing to help students in office hours, but I find that his tests are unfair.  He tends to ask misleading and confusing questions that seem like 2 answers would be correct.  The book isn't much help, you must go to class to do well.
I absolutely adore Dr. Bosch!!  He is one of the nicest professors I've had, and he really cares about his students!!  And his classes are interesting too!!
he's okay, i didnt like his grading style but it was a joint class with another prof, didnt like the style of class at all

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Very difficult to understand in lecture because he mumbles. Doesn't explain things well even outside of class. Test questions are very unfair and difficult to even understand. Also a tough grader. Nice guy though.

Dr. Bailey is decent with lectures. I did not read the textbook. The worst part was his exams were way too long for the half an hour you had to take them.  Also Dr. Bailey is very smart but not great at explaining things to people who are learning. Because of this going to his office hours was useless and you really can't get extra help from him.

Dr. Bailey is a great professor that actually wants you to learn the material and understand it. If you keep up with the material, read the textbook, are active in lecture and ask questions at office hours or in lecture, he will help you as much you are helping yourself. You do all those things, an A is easy to get

Dr. Bailey is a fast-paced lecturer, but his lecture slides are sometimes difficult to understand. Reading textbook is key to success and understanding in his class. Exams are difficult due to, at time of writing, short time to take exams individually (~35 mins). Has sarcastic sense of humor which is sometimes funny, sometimes intrusive to lecture.

Textbook is optional but he encourages to read along to clear any confusion but there was so much confusion. Lab is disorganized, lectures are word-heavy + overwhelming. He's a nice person, but he goes through lectures too fast + information on slides are too vague when looking at them out of class. Need to take good notes + ask questions to suceed

Bailey is a nice guy and great professor. Definitely for this class, READ THE TEXTBOOK, his lectures are good but sometimes you need a better understanding. Class is not hard unless you make it hard so do every little assignment to get your grade up. He's super accessible as well by email or before/after class. Would take his class again.

He comes off scary at first but then you pick up on his sarcasm. If you make a clear effort, he's always willing to help. He tries to give points anywhere he can. Sometimes he could be confusing when asked a question so just google it and he doesn't care. Labs are in groups. Super chill and funny guy, pretty easy lab
I enjoyed Bailey's class. He did a good job teaching the information, and his tests were similar to the knowledge checks that were posted online.

Professor Bailey is a nice guy but teaching isn't his strong suit. I found myself very confused during lectures because of the way he stated concepts. The textbook and learning curves will be your best friend in this course. His office hours are helpful though so go to them! SI sessions are also crucial.

SO, i technically didn't have him for bio 117 i had him for 117 lab but god was he amazing. He was better at teaching some topics than my actual teacher most of the time and he is so accessible and very nice! If you had trouble with anything he was willing to do the work to help you understand it so you can do the work better.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Bailey is supportive and wishes for everyone's success, but teaching might not be their strongest suit. There's an expectation to dedicate at least 15+ hours outside of class to remember the material covered. The lectures are repetitive and becomes challenging to retain and comprehend the class content.

5 stars for accommodation, 1 star for the way the class was run. Biochemistry with him was extremely difficult. Did not curve- most people ended with a c- to a c+ for the class. Gave you 30 minutes for each exam. Test questions were nothing like the homework. Exams actually tested your ability to extract from Google for 30 minutes

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: This is the class you will spend the most time on this semester. This guy seems intimidating at first but is actually a really nice prof and cares that you do well. To be honest I was so turned off by how dense the course was; you don't learn, you just spend your time studying and analyzing concepts before tests that you will not care to remember.

Dr. Bailey is an amazing professor, he is very naturally smart and you can tell he cares a lot about his students doing well. He is always wanting students to come to his office hours, and he takes time before every exam to let us ask questions about topics we are confused about. He takes unfair questions off of his exams which boosts your grade!

Bailey is really cool- I think the issue lies with a 1 semester biochem course, which by nature has to be rushed. Everything is always confusing, but I feel Bailey could have done more to focus on the main ideas (which even those I didn't know). He curves so even though we all have learned nothing the grades look fine: good for GPA, bad for MCAT

Dr. Bailey was great. He gives very in depth lectures that can get confusing, but he is very accessible outside class and is always more than happy to answer any question you may have, no matter how simple. He clearly wants his students to succeed and it shows.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Dr. Bailey is the best bio professor I have had at Geneseo, mostly because he genuinely cares about the success of his students. He loves being asked questions and is very clear about what he wants students to know for exams. In order to do well in his class, you need to study for at LEAST a week beforehand and know the ins and outs of his outlines

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']
comment: Dr. Bailey is really knowledgeable on many aspects of Biology. He doesn't just read off the slides, but he covers a lot of information and his tests are difficult. Sometimes hes explanations for questions are too complicated to understand but he will work with you endlessly until you understand. Would highly recommend.

I believe Dr. Bailey is one of the smartest professor in the biology department and easily my favorite. He is a good lecturer although he can speak fast; he keeps the class involved with tophats and funny remarks. His in class book clubs make sure students read articles and come to class knowledgable. I would 100% recommend him.

Travis is the most amazing professor I have ever had, yet his exams are extremely difficult in order to live up to the standard the Geneseo Biology department prides themselves on. Yet, i urge you to take Dr. Bailey if you really want to learn Cell and have a fair chance at a good grade.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Take cell with Bailey. Easier than Hoops (but still the hardest class I've ever taken). Great man, helpful and very honest about intentions and expectations. Always asking students how he can improve lectures, not just at the end. If you put the work in (reading and the 5-6 group homeworks) then you can do well.

Dr. Bailey is a very nice guy.  He's helpful and reasonable, and gives extra credit questions on exams.  However, he is way too smart for his own good.  He doesn't explain things in a way that is easy for students to understand.  I pretty much had to teach myself the material from the textbook.  There is a lot of group homework but it isn't bad.

Cell biology with Dr. Bailey was the hardest class I have ever taken. Cell biology, however, will not be easy no matter who you take it with. I suggest Dr. Bailey greatly. He cares about his students, but is very direct. I read the textbook thoroughly and studied in every way I could. This class changed my life.

This class won't be easy. You will HAVE to attend class, read the text over and over, and review until you pass out. However it is completely worth it and you will thank yourself. Dr. Bailey is incredibly brilliant and worth taking this class with. If done right you will finish this class much smarter than when you entered

Bailey was a wonderful professor and Cell was a fascinating course. The concepts in cell aren't particularly difficult but there is SO MUCH material so success requires a lot of preparation and memorization. I only bought the essential cell textbook and I was fine and I recommend studying from the textbook, because his slides can be disorganized.

He's a good lecturer, but sometimes not clear. Office hours are great to clear up any confusion. Comes off as very intimidating, but he's actually a sweet guy who really cares about students and wants you all to do well. Only had 3 tests including the final - 2 fair and 1 hard. Definitely would take another class with him!

Again, I recommend Bailey. This was his first time teaching developmental here, so sometimes it was a bit messy, especially in regards to lab. However, he is a super fair grader and is extremely helpful in and out of class. There is a lot of material and it is very challenging. The textbook is a hot mess, but Bailey's helpfulness makes up for it.

Bailey is a really nice prof who wants his students to do well and isn't trying to trip them up. The class is difficult and there's so much material to cover that you will need to put in a lot of time if you want to get a good grade. He tries to keep the material interesting using videos and is very helpful/approachable during office hours.

Bailey is a good professor who cares about his students success. His tests were difficult.. but so is the class. He is the only cell bio professor I have heard of giving curves on exams. Study the textbook, go to office hours, d take notes in class and you will do well. Very helpful in office hours. I would definitely recommend Bailey over Hoops.

Bailey's class could be interesting, but I feel like the way he lectured made it kind of boring. His powerpoints usually either had no writing or too much writing to copy down. He's really good on taking student feedback though so I'm sure this will improve. Tests were difficult and you were never really certsin what would be on them.

Dr. Bailey's class was difficult but manageable. I did not put an extreme amount of effort in and got a decent grade. Use the textbook, follow his power points and know the learning objectives on the unit sheets. Very nice guy and very fair.

Though Bailey's teaching style is one of a kind, it kind of works. As long as you follow what he covers in lecture and his explicit learning objectives you will do fine. Tests are doable if you study well with a heavy reliance on the textbook- especially tables and figures. The final was a challenge. I recommend him

Good guy but boring. Spoke very fast, couldn't understand enough info during class. More useful to read the textbook than go to class. Good at responding to student feedback. Group hws relatively easy (grade boosters), exams insane, never knew what was on them. Frequently gave misinformation about exams. Reviews were more confusing than helpful.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: Attendance is mandatory for this class even though the material on tests (by which there are very few and grades are heavily weighted on) is not from lecture. The tests are extremely difficult even if you have read the required textbook material. The time limit on tests is outrageous (35 mins and 70 questions). Nice, funny guy, not a good teacher.

One of the worst professor's I've ever had. Says he has office hours but never tells you the days or times. Comes to class late every single day. Is harsh about attendance. Lectures have nothing to do with exams except for the countries name, harsh grader on the final paper. Media journals are easy 100s, some of the exams can be found on quizlet.

He is an incredibly nice man and his lectures are interesting to go to. With that being said he can be lazy. He has told us that his lectures add "flavor" to the textbook but for the first exam neglected to tell us what we needed to read in the book until the day before. Exams are online and incredibly nitpicky and has many questions that are wrong

Tests are online and completely based on the textbook. As long as you have the textbook open in front of you, you should have all the answers. Media journals are an easy A as long as you do them. Final paper is time consuming but straightforward. His classes aren't really helpful but he's funny and he has an attendance policy so you should prob go.

All tests are online and come directly from the textbook. Virtually nothing you learn in lecture will be on the tests, but if you read through the chapter and keep the book open during tests you will be good. Lazy guy, which makes it easy to get a good grade.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Dr. P has a good personality. He cares a lot about attendance, and threatens to take points off FINAL grade for every absence. He tries to have interesting lectures and up to date references, even though most of the test info comes form the book. He's a lenient grader on writing assignments. The course load is fair, and can be an easy A .

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: One of the best professors I've had. He keeps class interesting and fun. You learn a lot while still having a fun class. You have to read a lot but it's very helpful for the exams. Definitely would take another class with him again.

Mohammed was the best Professor I had this semester! Long class, but he gets you though it by keeping it interesting. He wants you to do well and genuinely cares about you. Absolutely hilarious and the class itself is not that difficult. Just putting the work in will absolutely get you an A+

Best way to learn a lot of info. Fits Everyone. If you are just trying to get an easy A, he's the guy. All tests are taken online outside of class and you can use all notes and books. 1 large paper for the whole semester that is a moderate amount of work but is graded very easy as long as you put in moderate effort. He really teaches a lot of info.

All his tests are online. Most of the material is not from class, but in the textbook. the students know more than he does, and his test questions are from students quizlets. he once gave us a test about a topic and didn't cover it in class. He then went over the material in class THE DAY AFTER THE QUIZ WAS DUE. no respect here, awful professor

Good old party Partapurwalla.  Attendance is 0% mandatory to pass,  but he's a really funny guy, so it's generally worth going at least occasionally. Learned a bit, but if you have any idea how foreign governments work you'll do fine. Easy A.
He's a wonderful teacher. He might get off topic sometimes but it makes class more interesting, and it allows you to learn about more recent events in world politics today.

I had him at 830 in the morning and would find myself falling asleep in his lectures. He has an attendance policy due to the fact that you could clearly take the class online (all the tests are online), and gets annoyed when people dont go to his class, and acts like his lectures are essential. The tests were completely based off the text book.

Partapurwala is an extremely lazy and uninspiring professor. I do not believe I learned any important information in his class, and I certainly will not be taking any classes with him in the future. If his students matched his effort, nothing would have ever been completed. Joke of a college instructor

He's the nicest professor I had this semester. I did well in his class, although I'm not sure I deserved it, as most of his tests were online (yet still difficult somehow). Text book is n absolute must. Paper at the end of the semester isn't too terrible, he's a pretty lenient grader on essays (he likes to give 100s). Interesting class in general.

Mohammed is a cool guy- but, he is definitely pretty lazy- and it shows sometimes. All the exams are online. His lectures are very clear and supported by many examples- however, since he doesn't make any of the test questions, the lecture information is usually not helpful for the exams. Just read the book.

Super awesome professor! He's funny and tries to make the material engaging for those who may not like politics. Three tests which are online and one final (which he will curve if you do badly). One paper which is also pretty easy. Overall great professor and great class :)
Every test is online or take home including the final.  Class consists of watching videos and jokes that are so bad they are funny.  If you take comparative, take it with Mohammed
The man. Funny, engaging, easy class. Read the textbook and you'll get an A

He tries to make the class fun, but he is awful at this job. He is very VERY unorganized. He copies test/quiz questions from schools  which is reflective of his lazy character. He is more of a TA than a teacher really. Avoid him.

Really nice guy. Test questions are pretty straight forward but ask really detailed things. Classes are not really well organized and certain material are not available in in textbooks and slides are not really detailed so it'll rely on your note taking skills.
He was a great teacher. we did a lot of case studies, so a lot of information. But overall it was a good class. I learned a lot

Mohammed really wasn't a good teacher at all, his powerpoints were extremely confusing and his tests asked questions that he never talked about in class, on his powerpoints, or in the textbook.  He was a nice guy but one of the worst professors I've had at Geneseo so far. I was really interested in the course but he made me doubt it.
Good teacher. Powerpoints helped. Exams were tough

Interesting class. 3 essays, fair grader. I wrote 4 drafts per paper to nail them. be coherent, use outside info. or info. from another class if you could, its impressive. interesting class discussions. you need to participate as it is 10 % of the grade.

I would say that hes a nice guy. For this class he was asked last minute to do it so hes not really interested in it. Cancels class a lot- makes participation easy. Takes questions on tests right out of book. easy to talk up grade if you have a good point

Terrible Terrible Terrible. Cancels class a lot, and by a lot I mean at least a third of classes. Doesn't know enough about the subject matter to effectively teach anything about political science. Thankfully hes an adjunct, hopefully gone soon if he's not already.

Very lazy man.  Cancels class left and right.  However, the man does know his stuff and if you pay attention and take notes during class and read and highlight the main points in the textbook, you should do well in the course.  Also has a mild sense of humor at points.  Course is comprised of 3 essays and 4 exams.

Very easy class! We didn't have a midterm, only a few really easy quizzes and a final. A lot of people didn't do the readings, but I would recommend memorizing the vocab, as that is pretty much all you need to get 100s on the quizzes and final. The class can be boring, but she does a good job of trying to engage the class as best she can.
She's nice but not super understanding when it comes to missing any classes, even right before a break. Work takes a long time (many hours) outside of class.
I loved taking Med Anth with McCaffrey. I had a challenging semester and she had been so accommodating to my personal circumstances. I truly enjoyed her class and kindness!
class is super easy. one textbook however her lectures are all from the textbook so the readings are unnecessary. sometimes very repetitive so class may be a little boring. VERY ESAY CLASS
Easy class for credit but got an 88 on the midterm after having a 99 average all year to get a A-.

The lecture was kinda boring, but she saved a lot of people's grades at the end. A lot of people failed the midterm, so she let the final count double to replace it, and she was pretty clear about what would be on the tests. I was able to get through the class without the textbook.

Prof. McCaffery is very knowledgeable in medical anthropology and explains topics in an engaging manner.  This course had a lot of reading assignments but they are manageable.  There are also two exams and a project.

She was a little dry at times, but attendance alone was 20% of your grade. Only one paper, 3 quizzes and a cumulative final. No technology and everything handwritten. Readings were a lot, but you only really needed to know the vocab. Easy A, chill class
Professor McCaffrey is one of my favorite professors, her teaching style is very hands on and she cares about what her students say. She is open to listening and the work in that class is very easy.

Professor McCaffrey was awesome! She was very helpful in making the class interesting to those who were not anthro majors, she was extremely knowledgeable on the topic, and she was very kind to different opinions. I think she is awesome and was a great fit for such a tough topic!

This is a really good class, it is quite a bit of reading with 10 reading response papers, a group presentation, a documentary review, and an ethnography, but she is flexible with deadlines and an easy grader. The class is mostly lecture but is always engaging, best anthropology class I've taken so far. Dr. McCaffrey is perfect to teach this.

A lot of work for a 100 level class, but MacCaffery is very nice and if you go to her office hours she's super helpful. Attendance is mandatory and you will usually have one homework assignment, along with a reading due every class. You may be called on in class to talk, so be prepared. Three quizzes, one big project, put in effort  an easy A.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: She is 100% the best professor to take this class with. She may seem a bit strict at first but she really has her students best interests in mind and is very understanding if you need help. The workload was a lot at times but as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class you'll do just fine.
She is a terrible teacher.  Yes, she knows her stuff but lost my final project and then said it was stolen.  Had other people in the class complain that their projects were broken or dirty.

Her lectures were very organized and included lots of strategies. But she took off unnecessary points on the test. Tends to run late for office hours. I had to wait 20-30 min for her to arrive on days I went to go see her. When I got there and asked all my questions, I was certain I would receive an A on a lessonplan but she gave me a B. BECAREFUL!
She is great! She really knows what she is doing. I loved this class! The tests were laid out and the class was helpful. She gives review sheets and chapter reviews.

She's an amazing teacher, she knows a lot about Special Education, and is the perfect teacher in every way. She really helps you out and exams/assignments are super easy. She likes it when you participate a lot.
All I have to say is take this class!! The most amazing professor on this campus.

one of the best professors i've ever had. very funny and interesting to listen to. gets to know all of his students. very easy to get an A in the class if you show up. you only need the anxious generation not the textbook. all of the material is very meaningful

Great class, easy A as long as you show up and actually do the little work assigned. DO NOT buy the textbook. I'm someone who always buys the textbooks even if I don't use them, in case, but you 100% DO NOT NEED the textbook. Later in the semester we read another book that I also ended up buying but I think actually read once, can get by without it

Professor Linton is very passionate and includes his personal experiences during lectures which relate to the content which I found very eye opening. He creates a comfortable and open environment for everyone. He also brings snacks and candy to every class. Never a dull moment with Professor Linton.

He genuinely builds connections with his students and is understanding of anything that comes up. He tells a lot of stories from his experiences and is engaging. Sometimes his test questions were very random, but overall not bad. Would take a class with him again!
Take this class!

I took two courses with him. Literally the best professor, cares deeply about all of his students and only wants them to succeed. Develops amazing relationships with everyone and will always be there as a resource for you. I would take his class again just for fun.

Prof Linton is the best. Theres three quizzes throughout the semester but they are so easy if you attend class. He sets up his class to make sure you pass. Be ready to interact in class with him and others. Buy the book before you need it cause you will be using it in class not outside. 100% would take another class with him.

Best professor I have had at Geneseo. He cares about students and will do anything to help you succeed. You take quizzes in groups and have one presentation that is very laid back. You do have to read some books and then the assignments for the books are very short and straightforward. I recommend Dr. Linton he is the best!
Dr. Linton is a fun and energetic professor who cares about his students doing well. He also brings a big basket of snacks and candy to ever class which is amazing. Easy A would recommend.

Mark Linton was one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. He is so funny, and his classes are so interesting. He takes the time to get to know you individually and learn more about you. His class isn't bad at all, the work is very manageable and all classes are interactive. Would take this class over and over, he also brings snacks!!!

Dr. Linton is by far one of my all time favorite professors. He was incredibly caring and understanding when I was dealing with personal issues, always made me laugh, and took time to get to know me. Class was a little unorganized at times, but I gave him grace for it as it was his first college class he taught. Would definitely take again!

Prof. Linton was a great person. I loved getting to know him as a person, but as a professor, he was unorganized and gave unclear directions. The class was interesting but didn't focus on adolescent development, which is the topic of the class. Class is an easy A and you'll meet an amazing person, but if you need structure this isn't for you.

Dr. Tang's classes are tough, but he gives back what you put in. He went above and beyond to help me prepare for actuarial exams outside of class. He explains difficult concepts clearly and genuinely cares about helping students who put in the effort.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Although he can be funny at times, he is actually the worst professor I've ever had. He doesn't use email, he can be pretty quiet, he can be hard to understand, and he isn't even all that good at teaching; I've had to teach myself 90% of the whole course.

listen, I love Dr. Tang as a person, funny guy, but as a professor... extremely hard to get into contact with him outside of class, very heavy accent makes it hard to understand him, and he just reads out of a packet and doesn't really explain anything. Don't bother raising your hand in class, if you ask him a question he will not understand it

Tang's class is horrible and is not reachable outside of class since he doesn't use email. Nobody understands what he is talking about the entire time. He is nice and funny sometimes but very hard to understand

The professor doesn't thoroughly explain calculus problems—he mostly reads out steps without working them out on the board. Calculators aren't allowed either. If you're a strong self-learner, this class might work for you, but if you rely on in-class instruction, you're better off choosing a different professor.

Dr. Tang is one of the best professors I've had at Geneseo. He's challenging and gives a lot of homework, but it really helps you prepare for quizzes and exams. His weekly Problem Sessions to review HW are super helpful, and while he's hard to reach by email, he's always available in person. He genuinely cares about his students and their success.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: If possible, do NOT take Calc 3 with Dr. Tang. His lectures are terrible and you will likely have to teach yourself most of the material. He has a problem session once a week to go over all the hw he assigns, which lasts 1-2 hours. Besides that, he has no office hours at all and good luck trying to contact him outside of class time (you can't).

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Learned nothing from class, all on my own. Supposed to be exam prep class but every student failed the exam. Graded by one assignment at the end of the semester

This class was extremely unorganized. Tang left his students in the dust as no exams were graded the whole semester. Students in class would ask when exams would be graded his response was always "I am busy." This was unfair and humiliating on the Geneseo Math department. The only two assignments that were graded was two homework assignments.

I took this class because I needed it for my major. Halfway through the semester, we received two homework grades. As the semester went on we were given no other grades. We took 3 exams and 1 final. It is finals week and none of our exams have been graded. This is unprofessional and Tang left students in the dust with an unknown final grade.

You will never receive assignments back from this professor. Writing this it is the last day of classes for the semester and he has only graded the first two homeworks. He has not graded our first exam yet which was done in February, it is now May. His lectures consist of reading the textbook and writing down formulas but not showing how to use it.

SO. MUCH. HOMEWORK. Not only that, but he refuses to upload any of it online, and prints out the lecture slides instead of posting them. HE WILL NOT HAND STUFF BACK and doesn't post grades. He doesn't answer emails EVER. It is April and I've gotten back two of the ten or so assignments that we have done... he also hasnt handed back the first test.

Hands down the worst professor I've had. He doesn't teach anything, he just reads problems that have already been done and acts like you shouldn't be asking questions. Has 2 hour hw sessions every week outside of class and assumes you don't care about the class if you aren't there. Made me reconsider being a math major, don't take a class with him.

The first few weeks Dr. Tang seems intimating, but if you work hard and put in the time, you will grow to like Dr. Tang. A bit difficult to understand at times but lectures are important and useful. Everything he does is to ensure you become a GREAT mathematician and he constantly reminds you to strive for perfection. Has a great sense of humor.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: He is rushing the material this last month. In a months worth of time we will have 3 exams including the final. Hes rushing material. Hes even assigning things for us to do during study day. Do not take this Professor. He is also making us do a take home final suddenly and says itll take another 5 hours to add to the 5 hours his exam will be.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: This is the worst person in Geneseo currently. He does not care about his students. He changed the exam time on all of us last second when there is only 10 days left. We are taking two exams one week apart from each other during finals week. Do not take this professor he is not worth it. He thinks his course is the center of the world.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: He doesnt care about his students or their well-being. If your looking him up now do yourself a favor. Take another course with another professor this man is too much. He is unfair and doesnt respect his students. Just save yourself the headache now. He doesnt care about your health or his. Good luck if your stuck with him.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']
comment: He is so disorganized. The first exam happened a month later and even with 6 weeks left he wants to do the last 3 exams. Meanwhile theres still 12 chapters left. His syllabus tells nothing of what is needed or what exams cover what. He wants exams and problem sessions not during his allotted time and mandatory in person. Its a pandemic right now!

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This man should not be teaching during the pandemic. He does not understand his students or understand that not everyone can drop 3-5 hours for a mandatory meeting in person outside his align class hours. He had us to a mandatory in person exam during covid and would not help other students who aren't here. He just should not be teaching bc covid.

Dr. Tang may be the hardest working professor in the country. He developed and runs the Actuary Program. He deserves a lot of credit and he doesn't let you fool yourself that you understand a concept... an amazing professor. For those who survive through his ambitious homework you'll be one of the strongest math students in the math department.

He holds review session at night for students who have questions on the assignment. There're three tests and then final exam. Final exam is the fun part. He will point out the incorrect questions after you submit the exam for the first time. And then, you have second correct it as a second chance. Most classmates got above 80 in the class.

Take this class if you're willing to put a lot of time and effort into it. There are problem sessions every week and a quiz every Friday. Dr. Tang can be intimidating in the beginning, but he really cares about his students. Assignments can pile up sometimes, but if you go to the problem sessions, you're fine. Dr. Tang is also hilarious.

Dr. Tang is more dedicated to students' success than any professor I've ever met.  If you want to become an actuary, talk to him as soon as possible.  He seems intimidating at first, but he is such a nice guy, very funny, and understanding.  His classes are harder than other professor's but you'll walk out knowing more.  He is awesome.
Probably my favorite professor at Geneseo. So funny! He gives harder material than most of the other professors who teach calc3 but will help you out if you work hard.

Dr. Tang is hands down the best professor at Geneseo. He cares about his students and goes above and beyond to help you.  He makes you work for your grade, but is very considerate when grading.  Loved his class more than any other class at Geneseo.  Greatest man alive.
Very straightforward-just know the homework inside and out and test will be easy. Awesome guy to talk to.

Dr. Tang could do better at explaining, but mostly Actuary was hard because it needs to be hard if you want to pass the first exam (I did). Tang had hw due on days class wasn't even held. The problems were stressful and sometimes the textbook didn't show how to do similar ones. But Tang is so nice and is in his office ready to help AT ALL HOURS!
Dr. Tang is a great professor.  He demands a lot of work.  Its not a walk in the park.  But you walk out knowing it all.  Hes a very nice professor.  Fun to talk to and very understanding

Tang is an awesome professor, but you will do a lot of work in this class.  However, you really learn the material well, which is great as this course is geared toward students planning on taking the actuarial exams or studying statistics in grad school.

I almost failed this class, so I had to drop. I had some experience in math from AP Calc so I remembered some things, but his explanations are always longer and harder than necessary, and his accent doesn't help. Problem sessions were mandatory and lasted hours. Nice guy, but don't take the class unless you're a math/physics major.

There is no teacher in the Math department more dedicated than Dr.Tang. If he is not teaching, he is almost always in his office, even on Sundays. The homework is always challenging but the weekly problem sections are incredibly helpful. All of his classes take a lot of work, but you leave feeling like you've actually learned something useful.

He is a kind man who wants to help you learn as much as possible. He gives tough HW problems which are not always explained how to do in the textbook. But the nighttime problem session helps you a ton. If you put in a lot of work, you can get a good grade. 2 tests & a final.

Took calc 1 in high school and again with Dr. Tang. can be a little hard to understand his accent sometimes but he is very funny. problem sessions are a pain but they help A LOT he gives you a "second chance" on the final which helps alot. he does play favorites though and will let you know if you are one of them. i would recommend

Professor Tang can be intimidating for the first weeks of classes, but that's just to weed out unmotivated students.  Tang is a very funny man who strongly cares about his students.  Problem Sessions can be tedious but they're always helpful and everyone leaves with a smile on their face. Every math major should take Tang once before graduating!

The assignments were straightforward, his grading criteria is reasonable, and he is very accessible if you need extra help. The only thing he can improve upon is the organization of the class, but it improved by the end.

I really liked Sohrob's class. He's super knowledgeable with a big vocab. Sometimes a bit wordy, which made it harder to stay focused. Only a midterm and final, with homework that supported the lectures. He genuinely cares about his students wellbeing and is flexible with deadlines. He even brought snacks on the last day! Loved him!

Sohrob is such a helpful teacher and is willing to work with you if you are having a hard time in his class.
He also brought the class snacks, which made my day!

Sohrob is a very well-spoken lecturer, but that is the entire class. Take notes and stay awake as much as possible. The content is interesting but can get repetitive. Do the HW and learn the vocab and the exams will be easy.
Professor Ma was interesting. When I had her for this course, she was very patient and all, but I didn't enjoy the class structure. It was just not helpful for me.

Dr. Ma is truly the sweetest. Her class is organized where you lead discussions based on assigned readings. The class is well organized and instructions are clear. If you ever need anything from her shes readily available and willing to help. Class often ends early and is not overly difficult as long as you do the assigned work and show up to class
such a queen literally love her so much

comment: The sweetest professor you will have! The class is all discussion based and you will have to read the readings prior to class. Not many assignments but she is an easy grader! Highly recommend

Dr. Ma is amazing and I 100% recommend her! Class is discussion-heavy, readings are manageable & participation matters so make sure you read! Papers are not difficult as long as you address the criteria, which is not too difficult. She'll provide sample papers/projects to help. All in all, she's kind & cares for her students.

Professor Ma was a caring yet informative professor. Class participation and small group work is important however she makes the discussions super clear and easy to follow. Her work and grading is fair and she is understanding if you need an extension. I will always recommend her class.
best professor ever, and so sweet

Don't get me wrong Ling is a great woman and very knowledgeable about China. I have been enjoying her class but damn is there a lot of work. Hella reading for every class and participation is 30% of final grade. You only get 3 absences so use them wisely. Great woman, interesting subject, but a lot of work. If you put in the work you'll do well.

Professor Ma is a super kind woman. She is very caring about her students and her work. Her class was never boring, and the readings were very interesting as well. I was struggling during the semester I took her class, and she was very kind and helpful with helping me get through the class and get a good grade. She is very genuine.
She is so amazing! She is my favorite professor. All the material you learn is so engaging. Do not hesitate to take a class with her. One of the kindest professors you will ever meet.

Professor Ma is truly a kind woman. She cares about your knowledge in her course and will help you with any questions you have. Participation matters but it's really the bare minimum, she respects her students and all she asks if for your respect back. Show up to class most of the time and raise your hand. I love professor Ma!
If you are unsure of taking a course with her, take one. She is kind and is here for you to learn. She is not like most professors here at Geneseo.

Ling Ma is a very nice professor and her class is very easy but if you are someone that doesn't attend class or like to speak much your grade can suffer since attendance and participation is 33% of your grade. The class was very boring to me since most of us didn't have much to say on readings and she would drag out the class to talk.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Most caring prof I've had in all of undergrad. 2-5 readings per class, heavily graded on participation (just speak up 1-2x a class, doesn't have to be insightful), 7 papers (1 page each), notes graded at end of course, only 1 major paper. Very understanding and sympathetic. Brilliant woman, she got her phd in this subject so she's passionate too!

A real gem, best professor I had at Geneseo. Always wanted to come to class and was comfortable speaking out. Readings were interesting and she was very understanding. I went out of my way to take classes with her again.
Ling Ma is amazing she is very caring and very nice. Taking any of her classes is an easy A if you do your reading, participate in class, and put a little bit of effort into your papers

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: I have taken two classes with Dr. Ma and both have been great. The content assigned is always very interesting, and in-class discussions are generally a blast. She doesn't grade harshly, but still leaves very useful, detailed feedback and has always been willing to offer advice for research, and point students in the right direction.

Prof. Ma is the best teacher I've had at Geneseo so far. She is caring and knowledgeable, and makes herself quite available to students . I normally don't rave about teachers but she is definitely worth raving about. Like any class, you have to read and participate to do well, but it's well worth your time. If you like history definitely take this.

Absolute queen. Knows so much about the content, and I have never felt more confident and relaxed in a classroom setting. I asked more questions and spoke more in this class than ever before. Every class is a real mental workout, and the long in-person classes fly by.

Dr. Ma is a queen. She is brilliant, kind , and caring. Even a class on China at the 400 level is accessible for those who do not necessarily have a background in the history. She is a generous grader and is always willing to be accessible and is usually very accommodating. Definitely take her class if you need a LACANNA credit, She's amazing!

Professor Ma is amazing. She is a genuinely kind, caring and down to earth person. She's also an amazing lecturer and her passion for history shines. Words cannot express how much I love her! Take her class, seriously! You will learn a lot. I have a much greater appreciation for East Asia.

Dr. Ma is the nicest professor as Geneseo. She's super helpful and easy to talk to. You HAVE to go to every class, and you HAVE to say at least one thing per class. Participation is probably half your grade. Other than that, expect small assignments, papers, and readings. Just show up and answer a question or two and you'll get an A

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Prof. Ma's Women and Gender in East Asia class was reading-intensive, with about 2-5 short readings a week, and most classes we spent the time discussing the readings and giving our take on them, so actually doing the work and participating matters, because its a big part of your grade. Lots of short papers to write, she's an easy grader, though!

Professor Ma is one of the best at Geneseo. She is incredibly passionate about history and it shows. She assigns really eye-opening readings, her lectures are informative and thought-provoking, and she is just an all around sincere, compassionate, and awesome person. You will get a lot out of her class. Can't recommend Dr. Ma enough.

I love Prof. Ma's class. She is truly caring, funny, and easy to talk to. We got to read so many eye-opening things about East Asia, most very short primary sources. She expects participation but she never makes anyone uncomfortable. I don't have any problem with attendance. She lays out rules clearly in the syllabus and she is a fair grader.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Prof. Ma comes across as very nice and caring for her students, and for the most part was. However, participation matters more than she will let you know until the course is over. Many students in the class went into the final with an A and due to the final and participation finished in the C-B range. Be aware.

Amazing professor! Very kind, passionate, and understanding. All she really wants is for you to pass and learn about the subject. I am planning to take another of her courses. It's worth it. I highly recommend!

I LOVE Professor Ma. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I think she realized that she graded a bit harshly at the beginning of the semester so she was pretty lenient at the end, and she ended up dropping an essay. There are discussions about once every week or so, and you are graded on participation, so do the readings.

One of my favorite history professors so far. All of her lectures were informative and on top of that, they were interesting. Instead of writing one large essay at the end there were two smaller papers and five one page assignments. The midterm and final are tough but if you put the time in and attend class you will do fine.
Super easy class. She is a very nice and fair professor. if you do your work, you'll get an A
I really enjoyed this class, would take again. Super kind and cool professor.
Really great lectures, interesting class. Also quite clear on what the grading criteria was.
Really knowledgeable and kind professor. Very passionate about what she was teaching. I was not particularly interested in East Asia, but she made it super interesting. Would recommend.
He makes me want to cry

Kincaid is the worst professor that I've ever taken in my Geneseo career. Didn't post anything for half of the semester and then graded on basically nothing. He is a joke of a professor. I took macro with this professor and it was a terrible experience. Wed go weeks without having any communication with him and he never responded to any of the follow up emails I sent him. The online textbook cost $300 and I ended up teaching myself most of the material for the year.

Professor Kincaid is one of the most unorganized and unresponsive professors I have had in my time at Geneseo. Lectures were a waste of time since all he does is ramble. Easy A, took micro with him and was only ever graded on HW assignments which were easy to get a good grade on. Still have yet to have a quiz and its April- granted we are now online because of COVID but we had not been tested before we left for spring break.
