he was the most clueless and unorganized professor I have ever had. half the time he just seemed lost and had to redo his work. plus instead of using canvas he just sends out a bunch of emails everyday flooding your inbox in no specific order

he seems to know the material but just has absolutely zero clue how to communicate it. Grades are completely subjective and based on whatever number pops into his head while he makes stuff up for the gradebooks

Dr Kincaid is a very very nice guy. However, he is by far the most unorganized professor I've ever had. Period. He is terrible at presenting materials. He always confuses himself, let alone students. He c0nstantly forgot how to do the problems during lecture. He didn't give quizzes /homework back almost at all and grades are arbitrary. Terrible
Professor Kincaid is late to every class. He is constantly confused by the material and does not actually teach anything. He is hands down one of the worst professors I have ever had.

Didn't show up to the class for 3 months and managed to get an A. Didn't learn a single thing cause everything is online and on google. He is a nice, funny guy who will try to help you but he is not the best lecturer. He obviously know a lot about his field but he isn't very good at explaining it. His lectures were interesting but I found that most of the tests came from the textbook.
Dr. Kincaid has a lot of knowledge outside of economics and his lectures are really interesting. I would recommend him to anyone.
The worst professor I've ever had. Avoid at all costs.

Everything from his homework to his tests are online and everything is fairly easy.. However, the final is written and costs at least 25%.  Would take for credit but not if you want to learn economics for your major.  I was very confused when he taught lectures.

The class was so-so but it was all online. I read the textbook he taught out of in my boxers each morning instead of going to class and I pulled an A. If you're just looking to get a gen ed requirement out of the way he's a good teacher, but if you're looking to learn something I'd recommend looking somewhere else.

Took Kincaid for micro and learned almost nothing. All the work is online, so getting an A isn't difficult except the final is 25% of the grade and is written. Great class if you don't want to show up at all, since all the real work is open bookonline.

Allison is an angel and I highly recommend taking a dance class with her. Even if you're like me and don't have a ton of dance experience, she will support you and push you to be your best. No complaints.

Allison is probably the nicest professor at Geneseo and possibly the world. She is super welcoming to newer dancers and the only thing you really have to worry about is the core/stability exercises during warmups
I took my first ever dance class with her and felt so welcomed and like I was receiving the feedback and help to help me grow in her class. I loved it!

Allison is amazing. One could say I'm biased because she was my ballet teacher for 5 years at my dance studio through my youth, though, she is exactly the same as a college professor. This is college so she does take it more seriously but only because she seeks for every student to try their best. She is so sweet and makes everything very fair. :)

BEST professor I ever had, especially for a writing requirement.  I didnt even agree with his opinions most of the time and still got an A in the class. very smart and cares about his students.  i am better off after taking his class!

I read all these comments and think it really must be one person saying most of this. He was awesome! All my friends in the class LOVED him and there was really only two people that were in class who didn't. This course was great because it covered stuff you never hear about abortion. well, his view of the world is extremely bizarre, he seems pretty crazy, and really is, but the class wasn't terribly hard....all you had to do was spit back his world views and opinions to him and you'll get an A, I didn't read any of the books, and just pretended to believe in everything he did and that made class easy

his class was entertaining, but i can't say I actually learned how to write. I don't blame it entirely on him though- i think the concept of the INTD needs to be rethought. I don't think he still teaches this class her anymore, but I wouldn't advise anyone to take it if he did.

One of the few professors that actually cares about his students inside and outside of the classroom. Incredibly down to earth and has a good sense of humor. As long as you can critic an article, state a argument for/against it, and support your argument then it's an easy A. I thoroughly enjoyed this class, and I wish he taught more courses here.

He was very entertaining in class. Half the time we didn't actually stay on topic, but it wasn't necessary. It was just fun to talk about life in class. Fairly easy grader if you just were clear and concise. However, one thing that was irritating was that I didn't really learn from my mistakes because he didn't comment back too much.

He was AMAZING! The only prof here who doesn't want to "Lewinski" Obama. He's really into common sense and the real world. Cut through the BS lies we hear all the time and actually gave evidence for what he was saying. The mindless sheep hated him, but the majority of us LOVED him. He proves Conservatives can be rock-stars too! Bindig is the man!
Dr. Roz cares about his students deeply! He is so nice and an awesome human being

Professor Rozalski is great and clearly has a passion for what he teaches. His insight and shared experiences were very unique but important to hear about for the topics covered. This was a class I was greatly looking forward to and was very pleased by the outcome.

Dr. Roz is extremely nice and definitely cares for his students. He is a tough grader but often gives good feedback as to what needs fixed and sometimes allows for corrections. He also talks really fast but part of it is intentional teaching, and he accommodates by playing captions on the screen. He will also make sure there is snacks every day.

Dr. Roz is one of those professors you can tell LOVES his job. Overall, he is a phenomenal professor who is super passionate and involved in Special Education. His grading scale is a bit intense, but the work and activities for the class are not too overwhelmingly difficult. Great professor who I would definitely recommend and take again.

I really liked him, the class was a little boring but that's okay, there's also a lot of group assignments so pick normal people. Also he will give out a homework pass to whomever is the first person to participate on the first day of class and then never hand out a homework pass again so be that person

I don't get the hype for Roz. He's a nice guy but his class is hard to follow and he talks so fast. You have to get a 98 in the class to get an A which isn't terribly difficult. The class is just a bunch of group projects that he is unclear about, it makes it hard to get individual feedback. Wouldn't recommend unless you really like the subject.

Honestly idk why everyone loves Roz. He is a nice enough guy to his students, but grading is unclear. He shares stories of his past students, including students from a brutal and inhumane wilderness retreat for troubled teens, that prove he supported a system that abuses children. He told these stories for laughs, lost respect for him right there.

Dr Roz genuinely cares for his students and strives to push them to do their best. His leectures are entertaining and he incorporates a lot of group assignments. The downside to his class is his harsh grading policy where you have to get a 97-100 in order to get an A. Great guy though and he brings in snacks if you get hungry :)

Dr Roz genuinely cares for his students and strives for them to push themselves as much as possible. Downside is that his grading policy is harsh where you have to get a 97-100 to get an A. Lots of group projects but good lectures and takes everyone's thoughts into consideration for his teaching style. Super nice and he brings snacks!

Dr. Roz is an amazing professor although a tough grader. To get an A you need a 98 in his class. A lot of his assignments are group projects make sure you have a strong group, review rubric many times when working on assignments and attend his office hours if you have questions or need help. Very helpful in office hours, responds quick to emails

Very kind professor and makes his lectures interesting. Make sure you are in a good group because most of the grades are group work. He allows you to make revisions and it is a low-stress class overall. Highly recommend him even though it is challenging to get above an A- in his class due to his scoring methods.

Dr Roz is super nice but he tries to camouflage his mistakes by being nice. I learned a lot, but his expectations can be too high. Needing a 97 for an A is insane. When you ask him for assistance he tends to make a plan that he rarely follows through with. Way too much group work that does not allow for individual feedback.

Professor Roz is one of the best professor in education that Geneseo has. I found him very hilarious and he genuinely wants everyone to learn what he is teaching. I have nothing negative to say about him. Take a class with him and you will not regret it.

Roz is easily the best professor ive ever had. he zoomed in w my project group the night before a presentation to reassure us and he saved us so much anxiety. genuinely loves his job and his students! :)
Very accommodating, practices what he preaches. In terms of method, he is ideal. An exceptional teacher. If you need help, he is quite helpful and respectful.

Dr. Roz is one of the best. Seriously take his class and you will not be disappointed. The only critique I have is the grading. He divides the whole semester into 400 points total and you need to earn 390 of them to get an A which is a ridiculously high bar to reach especially with group projects being involved. Still a solid 10/10 professor.

This is the second time I have taken a class taught by this teacher. He is a little disorganized at times, but he gives you all of the resources he uses so you can access them before class. He is so kind and wants everyone to do well in his class. He has so much knowledge and experience working with children and class was always enjoyable.
There has very seldom been classes where I have been sad when theyre over. This was one of them. Roz is incredible and so so kind. Great guy.

I took Dr. Roz as a freshman and loved his class, and took him again as a junior. Funny, kind, caring, respectful, really a great model for future educators. Lots of group work but is really understanding of group dynamics and want to work with everyone to make sure the work is divided equally.

Unfortunately, Dr. Roz left our class halfway through the semester due to health reasons, but he truly was the best teacher I have ever had for those few short months. He so clearly loves his job and enjoys coming to class everyday. As an education major, it really opened my eyes to what it is like to love your job and do what you are meant to do.
Great guy.

Dr. Roz is amazing! His class is so interesting and you will learn more in this class than in any other class in SOE. He has such passion for education and is willing to go out of his way to help his students. Ask questions and you will be fine!

Best professor in the SOE. He is incredibly passionate and intelligent, and brings a level of humor to the classroom that most professors don't. Not the easiest class by any means, but he truly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.
Great Professor.  I have learned so much from him.  The only class in Block IV where you will actually learn anything.  He knows so much!!

Dr. Roz is the best professor I have ever had at Geneseo. He has such passion for what he does and he really respects his students. He expects a lot of his students, but he is more than willing to help you whenever needed. The class is very interesting and he is EXTREMELY knowledgeable on behavior management. Take this class or you will regret it!!

what a jerk! He talks badly about other professors and makes fun of them. How UNPROFESSIONAL!  I have never seen anyone as arrogant as him.  He does nothing but stir up trouble in the block between students and professors.  Yuck

Great professor. Very intelligent and knowledgable on the topic. Expects a lot, but for a high 300 level course, he should. Always has hidden meaning to everything he does which sometimes can be frustrating but other times is cool. I advise taking him.
He is so great! Seriously one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so qualified for what he does its almost scary. Love him!

Dr. Roz is the best professor at Geneseo. Take a class with him before he leaves the crappy education department like the rest of the good professors seem to do. He has a passion for what he does and it shows. He may not be the easiest professor, but I have to say that he is the most FAIR person I have ever met and he treats his students with respect. Dr. Roz is THE BEST thing that Geneseo has going for it.
No Comments
SOO GREAT!! Knows so much, extremely willing to help. Wants everyone to love what we do and do everything well! Take him if you have the chance, you will learn so much!

The best teacher I've ever had!  The class is by no means easy, but I have never learned so much.  I have never had a professor who thinks about everything he says and has a reason for everything he does the way Dr. Roz does!
will help you with anything, including stuff that doesnt have to do directly with class. Although sometimes you get frustrated, with an open mind you can see that he has a reason for everything.

Very hard professor- feels like a level 300 class
Very bad professor. Hard grading. Should be reported and removed from teaching.

Good luck learning anything from her! She was unavailable, disorganized, frequently canceled classes, and graded the majority of assignments in the last few days of the semester. yo mohammed is the man and a half. his tests are online and the journals are pretty straightforward. GO TO CLASS you don't have to pay attention but if you miss attendance once its 3 points off final grade. his sense of humor is on point and he's a pretty lax professor.

Loved his class.  Great teacher who would keep the class lively with random humor.  Calls out whatever he feels like during class and gives extremely reasonable test.  Had a semester long massive paper but still brought a very respectable economic approach to developmentgrowth.  If you want to get the most out of your economics degree. Take him.

Not a pushover and doesn't coddle, but isn't unrealistically difficult. Some online assignments & exams. Textbook important/pricy. Very helpful, cares about students' progress. Probably the most writing I've had to do for any class in any department. Tests were extremely long, and the term paper was longer. Learned a lot, however, and he is a great teacher. Lectures come strait from the book, but the text is very good. Much work is needed for an A, but work hard and he'll gladly reward you. Recommended for PLSC majors.

Minette cares a lot about her students. You have a lot of assignments in this class but they actually relate to things you'll need to know in the real world. They are all pretty much common sense. Minette is really nice but she gives SO MUCH WORK. We had a different paper due each class time and she never let us out early even if we finished the discussion for the day. A one point we had like 3 projects due at once. She thinks she helpful but she just talks at the class the whole time.

She doesn't know how to use technology half the time. Multiple assignments circulate at once. Directions for assignments are unclear. Her grading style is ambiguous. Professor Beabes was a business professional herself before she became a professor so her real-world experience is very helpful. You learn a lot of important skills in this class such as interviewing, how to write letters, resumes, and presentations. She is a hard grader but as long as you go to class and put in the effort you will get an A.

Minette clearly does not what she is doing. There are at least 3 assignments circulating at once with no clear directions on how to complete them. Each assignment is graded rigorously, even project outlines. All assignments must be up to her standard even if the requirements are met because once again there are no clear directions.

I took professor Beabes's INTD-205 class to fulfill the requirement. For most professors, this class should've been a breeze with a few essays and assignments here and there. In her first semester as a professor, she gave us an absurd amount of work with absolutely no guidance on how to do so. Not a bad person, just a terrible professor.

Mansokku is very nice and knowledgeable on quantitative methods. However, the professor would often make mistakes and run out of time, making the information more confusing. The course material was difficult to understand and I had to teach myself most of the material.

Only had to take this class because I had to from registration and it was not a good class. Attendance is mandatory and there were many days he was correcting what he taught us the class before. Professor Lee is an extremely knowledgable expert economist who will try to teach graduate level concepts in a 100 level course. Easy A if you pay attention in class and prepare for exams in some way. 3 tests and 2 page case study papers on interesting case studies. She is not the best lecturer but the information is pretty interesting and easy to work with.
Professor is nice but exams are a bit tricky. Class attendance is mandatory! One could do well if they study hard.

Prof. Zook is very nice and approachable. Her tests are difficult if you don't study and read the textbook. You must attend class to receive participation points for in-class-assignments. I loved this class and i recommend her for anyone looking for an interesting class.

comment: She is a great teacher-the material is very clear, and I have no problem understanding what is expected of me. That being said, she is not always the kindest. Learning during COVID is stressful, and she is not very accommodating to the needs of her students. Things often fall through the cracks.

This class fills up fast, so take it if you can get in. There's of review throughout the year so you remember all of the information by the time the final comes around. She is very accessible outside of class and a fair professor when it comes to assignments and grading.

She is by far the best professor to take this class with at Geneseo. She keeps lecture interesting and relevant, and as long as you understand the slides you will be set for the tests (your lowest test grade is dropped). She is always available outside of class and has way more office hours than other profs.

Dr. Wendy Pogozelski is singly the most caring professor I have encountered at SUNY Geneseo. While I gave her a (4/5) for difficulty, that is mostly because of the intense workload I required to memorize and understand her material. High focus on slides. Office hours are rushed, but very helpful. Ask questions because she likes engaged students.
just work hard

Has a lot of examples that are really in depth but doesn't make it clear what we have to know and don't have to know. Tests are made up with questions that are very detailed and irrelevant to the core material. Not that helpful during office hours. Unfortunately she is the only biochemistry professor right now so there are no other options.

She is so helpful and makes the class very interesting. Everything is given a practical application so you can understand why it is important to learn it. She gives a lot of help on homework and is a very fair grader. Overall, this is one of the best classes I've ever taken at Geneseo and I cab't wait to take Biochem II with her next semester

Pogo is definitely one of the better teacher's I have had as a biochem major. She's very smart and her lectures are interesting filled with lots of applications. Sometimes she can be a bit neurotic but shes really passionate and it shows. I would recommend her to anyone interested in biochem! Tests and hw arent bad you just have to study a lot!!

Dr. Pogo's class was very interesting. She takes everything we learn in biochem and gives us some sort of application or story behind it that makes it even more interesting. Tests were fair and homework helped apply what you learned in class. You don't need to read the text because her notes are pretty good. Id definitely recommend taking her class

She is very helpful at office hours and is a very nice person.  However, her notes are often very unclear and contradicting and she doesn't always do the best job explaining things.  Her exams are mostly fair.  Great 300 level class but Dr. Pogozelski needs to be a lot more concise and clear.

I think she is a great professor for this class. She tries to limit the amount of memorization and instead teach the application of the science and how concepts link together. She's not the most social of professors and has to make an effort, but she is excellent one on one and her office hour time is gold.

Pogo is one of the best Chem professors I've ever had. She may seem a bit intimidating at first but GO TO HER REVIEW SESSIONS!! Shes very helpful and friendly. She teaches a lot of material based on how it is actually used and makes a lot of stuff interesting that way. If you show her you care about the class, she will notice. TAKE HER! :)

Dr. Pogo is a great professor.  She knows her subject very well and shows interest in it.  Tells some great stories about her experiences.  She's kind of intimidating, especially in office hours, but I'm not sure why, she's really nice.  Pay attention, go to review, do homework.

If you make calc errors easily, this is not the class for you. She's a nice person and it's obvious she cares, but she offers none to little partial credit which is a killer on tests. If you don't love chemistry, I would take it w/ a different professor. Incredibly hard class. Incredibly strict professor.

Dr. Pogo's classes always come with a discalimer. It seems as though she cares a little to much about what freshman in her class write about her on this website. She is an extremely intelligent woman who knows her subject well. Apart from being too self-conscience, Dr. Pogo is a good teacher and her class is doable if you are willing to do the work

she can be nice and she can get angry and be mean.  she gives no partial credit and it's really easy to fail her tests - they are hard and she is kind of an unfair grader.  she likes office hours and she's good at teaching one-on-one.  she messes up notes a lot though, and sometimes confuses herself and that can be frustrating.  she's really smart.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. She does not give out ANY partial credit and doesn't seem to think you're working your butt off as it is. She seems to think everyone is a chem major. Save yourself and take this class with anyone but her.
No Comments

Wendy is one of the most amazing professors ive ever had the pleasure of having. go to class and just do the work, it really isnt difficult if you stick to her slides. Office hours are awesome too. Amazing.

Chem II was an excellent class to take.  Excellent comminicator and always more than willing to go the extra mile.  Her tests, though difficult at times, are directly based off of the lectures.  She Shows enthusiasm and brings a lot of examples and demonstrations. Being polite and respectful are as critical as attending class. A definite choice.
Stick to her notes and you will do good. She is one of the BEST professors in SUNY Geneseo. If you want her to like you be very "respectful"...

Class structure and notes are extremely helpful and review sessions really reinforced everything very nicely.  She really bends over backwards for all her students!  Do take the extra mile to be polite with her though.

One of the best teachers in Geneseo. I took both chem 2 and biochem 1 with her and so far I got nothing but praises for her. One thing: BE VERY RESPECTFUL, no joke...  100% of the exam comes from her notes/lecture.
Wendy is an amazing professor!! Take any class you can with her! She is very devoted to helping her students and being fair.
always be ontime, go to her review classes, easy multiple choice questions on tests but tough grader on long answer work, keep up with the homework and you'll be fine

She gives NO partial credit, so even if you demonstrate understanding of the concept but make a stupid mistake, you fail. She has an air of superiority and smiles derisively at students who ask questions. She assigns work before teaching how to do it. The class is too hard for a 100 level. She's not mean, she's just not fair.
No Comments

Her notes are not powerpoints so you have to go to class but they are straightforward and she tells you exactly what is going to be on the tests. You have to keep up with material because there are quizzes and homeworks that alternate every week. I would definately recommend her.
i love her.  straightforward, fair, and helpful, but can be a little shy and flustered at times.

Pogozelski makes biochem such an interesting subject! Class was swell, the lectures were interesting, and she's very, VERY helpful if you need the extra help. She also adds humour to the class! (ah, those wonderful little stories about her Hopkins experience!)

NICE lady, very perky and energetic, nice notes to go along with the pre-lab lectures. She expects you to pay attention and know what you're doing BEFORE you walk into lab, which can be a problem for some since Orgo lab isn't necessarily easy. She does her part well though and I'd recommend her as a proctor. Only gave 1 quiz this semester.
Tough class, She expects A LOT, but she is kind, fair, and will help you if you need it. Do not try going to the bathroom during a test ;)
She is an awesome professor.  Makes the subject easy and likeable.
best prof geneseo has!  did a great job simplifying a difficult subject. she was great in general chem but biochem is obviously her thing.

Wendy is the most awesome professor ever!  She made classes interesting and her tests are very straight forward.  She really cares about her students.  (Oh, and her vintage 80s outfits are the best thing ever!)
Wendy is great. Class is setup so that if you work hard you will definately succeed. She is very fair and easy to learn from. I will definately take biochem with her.
always there for help, go to the tutor for homeworks, REALLY willing to get to know you by name and work with your grade if you're struggling

Overall, she is a good professor.  As with any science major course, it takes a lot of time to study and do the homeworks.  There is HW/Quiz, alternating every week.  She is very responsive via E-mail, too.

She is a very nice woman and incredibly fair.  She gave me points on a quiz when the answer was wrong but there was outside circumstances.  Her tests I feel are a bit harder than the quizzes and homeworks you do, so you do have to spend time studying.
Tests fair, hws every other week, quizzes every week hw isn't due. Very nice and approachable.
No Comments
No Comments

She does, indeed, have self-esteem issues, but some of these may be warranted.  She's extremely bright in her field, but she doesn't have a handle on how to impart her knowledge to her students.  It takes more than being nice to be a college professor.

Great teacher extremely nice, though not easy to get in contact with outside of office hours/class because she's continuously busy.  Biochem is still a hard class, but her lectures are definately not boring.
Easy to understand and a nice person, but she has some self esteem issues that she really shouldn't have because she really is a good teacher
Goated. That's all
Extremely dense exams

Be prepared to put in some physical effort, especially during warmups. It was extremely intimidating for me as someone with no dance experience to keep up with the pace of everyone else, but we are all graded by our ability, not perfection. Oh, and the tests can be annoying to study for so make sure you take enough notes during the lecture portions

Professor French made sure that this beginners class was made for BEGINNERS and expected as much. She ensured there was no judgement and was very fair when it came to injuries. Exams are a little difficult if you don't pay attention in lecture classes, but the questions at the ends of slides are literally the same. Have those, and you'll ace it.

Professor French is high energy, caring and kind. Class has a lecture day and a movement day, two tests that are mainly based on lectures but had some movement questions. Attend a performance and write about it, choreograph a two minute dance with a group and write about it. Attendance is mandatory (otherwise there are makeup assignments)

Class is split into movement and lecture classes. Lectures are a disaster. Movement classes are somewhat fun, but do not tell her you're a dancer unless you want to be called out to dance in front of class the whole semester. She is very nice and enthusiastic but can be passive aggressive, too, if she becomes slightly bothered with the class.

Dance 100 was taken with the expectation the course would be easy. The class is divided into two days: lecture and movement. You cannot miss a class for the makeups are quite lengthy and difficult, along with movement days demanding lots of effort and physicality for full credit. Professor French, although nice struggles with disorganization

I took this class for my gen ed art, she is an upbeat professor and does not expect a lot. In-class participation is easy and she doesn't mind if you mess up as long as you try. A lot of material is covered, so studying is important for the tests, but there are only 2. Final is a group choreographic project: 2 minute dance and reflective paper.

She calls people out when she thinks they can't see the board or when they mess up dancing. She reads off the slides and just watches videos. There is a lot of content to her lectures which is too much to keep ahold of. The movement days are somewhat fun only if you know dance, but don't take her class if you don't know anything.

She calls out people for their flaws or points at people in the room when she calls them out for not being able to see the board. She is really nice at times but when she gets frustrated she comes off as mean. She rushes through slides for the bigger units that she should cut down. The movement days are fun though.

This professor was really passionate about dance and made the class that many dread to be a ton of fun. Just try and you will get credit for participation and if you miss a class the makeup assignments are fair and easy. Exams are not too challenging but you definitely need to study for them! Go through the slides and know the names of people.

The only complaint about this prof is that canvas is a hot mess. There is this authorization thing and it's very difficult to navigate. But a pretty fun class and lots of laughs/ and friends were made in this class. If you want an easy A I would totally recommend this class. Just make sure that you keep up with the assignments and you will do fine.

Professor French is very sweet but a horrible teacher. Her lectures are a mess, and so is her canvas. Participation alone won't get you a good grade because she makes her tests pretty difficult. You have to attend performances outside of class and write about them. If you want a good gen ed, this isn't the class. She treats it like a 300 level.
There are two written exams. Questions are lecture heavy and I read articles for test help. The studio is a great time. She makes the class very fun and motivating!!

Professor French is very caring and wants you to succeed. Your attendance is graded, there are 3 non-cumulative exams, and extra credit is offered. You will have to study since there is a lot of material, but studying will guarantee a good grade.
I had no idea how to dance at all, but she made sure that even if you were like me and didn't know what you were doing, you still could participate and enjoy it!! I recommend this prof!

French was a great professor and really enthusiastic about her work. That being said be sure to really study her notes for the tests because theyre really detailed, almost unnecessarily difficult for a dance 100 level course (each test average was a c for the class). She also grades attendance which is a huge chunk of your grade so dont skip.

Professor French is really amazing teacher. She is very attentive to all of her students and is really passionate about dance which makes the class really entertaining to be in and keeps you engaged all of the time. She has lecture classes and studio classes that alternate depending on the style you're learning that week. Highly recommend her class

A great professor. Easy to do well in the class if you pay attention and do the work. Understands that as college students we don't always want to stay in class the whole 2 and a half hours so he lets us out early occasionally. If he taught any other classes I would definitely take him again.
interactive, direct and his slides are easy to follow, easy tests, definitely recommend him.

A Monday night, 2.5 hour lecture sounds terrible, but it is actually not too bad. You need to go to class because of the quiz but powerpoints are easy to follow. Tests are so easy if you pay attention. The essays are a little hard but he gives you enough time to get a good grade.

This was Bauer's first year at Geneseo. Although a 2 and a half hour class on a Monday night sounds daunting, Bauer is good enough to make it worth it. Always clear and concise. The class is very easy if you put in the effort to do well. If you need to take this class as a poli sci major (like me) or just for a gen ed, I definitely recommend it.

By far my favorite professor I've had at SUNY Geneseo. I had a difficult time this semester with keeping up with work and he was incredibly understanding and helpful. He always made time to meet with me and clear up any confusion I had. His lectures are really interesting and he does a great job explaining everything and making it interesting!
Dr. Lalena is amazing and does a great job during lectures. However, he is a very harsh grader on writing assignments.

Really good guy, clearly passionate about what he teaches and is super understanding + he acts like a real person. The brightspace work is really light, lectures are good so I barely even opened my textbook. I would just suggest actually doing the listenings and occasional super light readings he posts online. Make sure to participate, great class!

Dr. Lalen is a good professor in Music History I + II, as long as you take notes, do the readings study for quizzes, participate in discussions, and complete Brightspace quizzes. He assigns a midtern paper and a final presentation instead of big tests. Thinking Through Music II (reading + paper) is tougher, so put in the work or risk a C-.

A G.O.A.T for real. Super chill guy, and maybe its because this class is required for my major but was super understanding given the circumstances I was facing this semester. Textbook is "mandatory" for this class, but I did the entire class without reading a thing in it and did fine.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: He was an amazing professor with so much knowledge! He relates everything to things that we can understand as students in the 21st century. It's often hard learning history from times like the 12th century but Professor Lalena makes it so much fun, and very interesting.
jazz  songs are big part

Dr. LaLena was very nice. I didn't know a lot about the subject beforehand, and I learned a lot. The writing assignments and quizzes were easy, just study and put in a little effort. He likes class participation, and took attendance. He seems like a really cool dude, and took the time to hand-write comments on all papers.  Would take again

LaLena is a cutie. He's really passionate about the topic he teaches and clearly loves what he does. He would sometimes get annoyed when students weren't participating so for his sake, just act like youre enjoying it. The assignments are easy and little is asked of you.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: This was my most enjoyable class last semester. Dr. Lalena is passionate about the subject which makes his lectures appealing to any musicians. We were only required to write one medium-sized paper with flexible due dates littered throughout the second half of the semester. Dr. Lalena is very easy-going and it's near impossible not to like him.

Dr. LaLena is a new professor at Geneseo so he is learning the environment but he is a very good professor and a great dude. He is very understanding, particularly with assignment deadlines which is very helpful because he wants his students to produce their best work.
jazz songs are big part
I absolutely love Dr. Iyer and would take all my physics classes with her if I could. She is very understanding and kind. Also accommodating for students.

Iyer was the best. She was so much better than my analyt 1 professor. I feel like I actually learned from her, which for physics is saying a lot. If you have to take analyt 2 with anyone, take it with her.
She's so sweet! The subject is hard, but she makes it enjoyable and does the best out of any physics professor at Geneseo! 100% would take with her again! SHES AMAZING!!

Very nice if you are respectful to her and don't go on your phone during lectures. Pretty good at explaining concepts but sometimes goes quick. Tests are fair and she gives partial credit unlike the other physics profs which helps your grade a lot. Overall would recommend for physics 1.
She kills your curiosity. I was so close to hating physics because of her. I would never ask her questions outside of homework

It's a shame that she seems to sweet in lecture, but she is awful at teaching this class. The tests are consistently based on the hardest possible questions that she, of course, doesn't cover in class. She offered some extra credit on tests we all did poorly on, but there was barely any for the final and that average was 62% for the class. Avoid!!

This is the worst professor I've ever had. She seems so nice and sweet in lecture and makes herself seem willing to help u succeed in the class. That's absolutely not the case. She says to feel free to email her with questions if you can't make it to office hours, I emailed her numerous times, no response at all. Expects you to know physics already

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: THE WORST professor at Geneseo. She is completely unresponsive to student needs and outright refuses to provide help outside of office hours. If you can't make it, too bad. She's "busy" and couldn't care less if you fail or succeed. She is a horrible rude person and will accuse you of cheating if you ask for help on something you don't understand.

You better be nice because this prof goes from happy to infuriated in an instant. This happened to me when I missed class for a FUNERAL. Anything sets her off. Her lectures are confusing. Going into office hours is unhelpful, and it feels like you're navigating a minefield anyway. If people do too well on a hmrk, she'll accuse everyone of cheating.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Physics lab was still difficult in my opinion. However, she can be amazing help! I think it's because there are less people compared to lecture, you get more personal learning time, which helps extremely. I definitely recommend going to her office hours though. I think professors' abilities to help students are really shown outside of class.

She is a sweet woman who has many office hours throughout the week . I wish she didn't assume that everyone has taken a physics course before. Personally, this was my first physics class and I struggled a lot. If there isn't a future where physics is necessary for u, rethink about staying in class. I'm partly glad I stayed and partly wish I didn't.

While PHYS is a tricky subject the difficulty can be either magnified or lessen by the professor and the willingness of the student to try and learn. While Professor Iyer appears tries to help her students but it seems sometimes there is a disconnect between them and her. It can be really uncomfortable approaching her regarding questions in physics

She really doesn't like people who have never taken physics before. Very nice and funny at first, but then I became ashamed/nervous to ask her questions, and it wasn't just me who felt this way. Goes through material very fast. It wasn't just me either, and seriously consider getting a chegg so you don't have to wait for a tutor to be available.

She's an awesome person and great at keeping lectures upbeat. She does a lot of examples in class and is always available in office hours, so she helps set you up to do as well as you can on homework and in tests. I hate physics but enjoyed going to all her classes and didn't feel as lost and confused as I expected to.
Occasionally confusing because of how intelligent she is, but extremely helpful, fun, and willing to answer any question you have. One of the school's best professors.

Iyer is very nice, very smart, and very helpful. She can be very unclear at times, though. Overall, she's a good teacher, but Freeman's better. Take with him if you have the chance -- for any physics class.

Extremely smart, so smart that she kind of has trouble organizing her thoughts.  She's extremely helpful outside of class and I think if you go to her that she'll help you out better there if you don't understand something.
I love her, she makes physics easier than i ever thought it could be...u definitely wanna take her for anylical physics 2
I think Dr. Iyer is very nice and helpful
No Comments

This teacher babbles on and on...I can't understand anything she says. She is very nice, but she will confuse the hell out of you. Do the capa and make sure you read the book, but don't bother going to class unless you want to take a nap.
nice lady. don't go to class, you'll do just as well (or better) doing the homework and working out of the book. Confuses herself sometimes.
No Comments
No Comments

This professor lectures for the entire class and talks the math out, instead of showing it. This professor had a mistake in her powerpoint slides every day. During one of our classes, we were given a problem to complete, then she realized there was a mistake, then gave us another problem, there was another mistake, then cancelled the rest of class.

I'm not a fan of this professor. She is a nice person, but she can't teach. She doesn't have an effective way to explain the material making lecture very hard to understand. The only way I am doing well in the course is because of my SI. To top it off, she failed to show up for one of our tests. I wouldn't take from her again.

She is a new professor and is a nice person. However, she is not meant to teach. She is very bad with her explanations and is not very helpful during office hours. You basically teach yourself the material. If you took AP chem you will do well, but that's pretty much it. P.S. she says "essentially" basically every 5 seconds!!!!!
Annie and Reece are the best in the sociology department, recommend them to everyone.

Absolutely amazing professor, especially having her in her first semester teaching at Geneseo. SOCL241 is the reason I want a minor in soc. Extremely engaging lectures, fun topics, and very fun group projects and activities. I only wouldn't recommend this class if you really cannot work in a group.
Prof. Ferguson is super kind and non judgemental

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: Very helpful when it came to issues within the class. Occasionally a tough grader but it depends on the assignment. LOTS of reading and note taking. Pop quizzes are somewhat often.

Super caring and fun professor! Gives in depth feedback on your work and is passionate about what she teaches. Classes were fun and engaging, and you can catch up easily if you don't go. Would take again if I could

Prof MV is super friendly, caring, and approachable! Participation (group work) matters, but the tasks are simple and boost your grade. She is willing to answer questions. Her tests are really hard, so definitely don't skip the readings! I would definitely recommend her!

She is the best Biology professor I have had here so far. She cares about her student's averages and doesn't just grade based off of a few tests. She speeds through lectures but posts full notes after on Canvas, and she doesn't give too much homework at all .She gives us learning objectives before tests which is AMAZING.

Had her in her first semester here. Tests were really hard. You have to pay attention in lecture and read to understand the material. The difficulty of the lecture material never lined up with the difficulty of the tests. She realized students were struggling and provided more support with practice questions and some extra credit options.

Absolutely horrible. Calculus is already a tough course. Leave it to Ms. Ramsay to make it tougher. Do not take this class. I don't ever rate professors but when my grade goes from a B+ to a C because the insanely hard final exam that had a mean score of a 44% and a high of a 60% wasn't curved, this is the first place I came.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Quizzes 1-2 times a week, 3 questions on each so ur basically screwed if you dont go to class and understand whats going on that week. The class barely has any homework, but the course is almost impossible to keep up with at her pace. 5 Homeworks were on delta math, but they barely lifted my grade. Do not take the course with her.

Quizzes were given every week and sometimes 2x a week. We also had 2 exams. All homework was done through Delta Math which was pretty much my grade saver. She would only give us around 10 minutes to do a multiple question quiz that each had multiple parts to them. It was never enough time. Very boring class as I already knew most of the material.
Great Professor.  Helpful to a fault.  Thorough understanding of Political Science.  Absolute clarity in explanations.  Personable, accepting, and friendly.  Fun guy and intellectually stimulating.
Really good guy, class was very clear, not too difficult, and he usually lets you out pretty early, which is nice

CP is a great teacher, but sometimes hard to understand exactly what he is thinking.  He did not express the great amount of text book use there would be at the beginning of the class, so I relied on the one in the library.  Bad idea. I scanned 17 chapters onto  flash drive.  Do yourself a favor... even if he says you do not need the book. Buy it.

CP is the man! Very knowledgeable of the curriculum. He puts a innocently humorous spin on the material more often than one would expect a prof to do. Very laid back guy, always helpful, and optimistis for the futures of both his students and the comn dept.

This class can be fairly interesting, but also challenging at times. The textbook is used fairly often in the first month or so, but not after that. Basically, in this class you complete radio projects, such as recording a 30 second news story. Getting interviews is really annoying. Get in a good group for the final project.
One of the best in the comn department!  great sense of humor and always willing to help his students!!
He's a very heplful professor and technically knowledgable. You will never forget CP.

The nicest professor you'll ever meet and great in production classes IF you go into the class not knowing anything.  Do not take a non-production class with him, you won't learn anything.  So helpful and excited!

One of the nicest guys you'll ever meet.  Pretty interesting and easy class.  As long as you read the text you'll be fine in the class because that's where he gets all of his lecture and test material.
Easy easy class, just read the text once before a test, and you'll be fine.
Great teacher, very sweet. He's very willing to help you out.
Very easy

He is the most helpful, sweet, nice, and experienced Communication professor at the college. He has done everything from being a camera-man to directing news. Ask a lot of questions and you will understand more.
One of a kind.  YOu can sleepwalk thru his class and get an A.  Can get pretty boring but you can't NOT like this man.
Pruzynski RULES!  He's a really nice and understand professor who goes out of his way to help students.  People complain about the  easiness  but not all Comn students know how to edit!
He's just a jolly guy who likes to have fun.  You won't learn a lot about using the equipment from him though.

This is for her 323 class. Intro to linguistics is hard enough in english let alone spanish. she has 1 hr of office hours in the middle of the day no one can go to. She can tell we clearly don't understand things yet keeps going. When you ask a question she just confuses you more. I have had 2 tests and they just keep getting worse.

Just generally not good professor to teach entry level Spanish. Teaches the entire course in Spanish which personally did not help me any when it came to understanding. Bizarre grading and cold calls in class- if you don't know the answer its just humiliating. She is probably better off teaching higher level language courses

She was kinda a weird teacher, her grading standards and assignment guidelines were pretty unspecific, but she was always willing to answer clarifying questions, even if we had to meet outside of class to do so. She was also very nice and continued to support me even when our class ended, which I appreciated as a first-year student.

She doesn't specify exactly what she wants & then takes it out on you for not understanding what she wanted. She doesn't tell you about certain assignments until day of. She doesn't give clear instructions and then says you must come to her for clarification but even then she doesn't clarify very well. She gives you bad looks for not understanding

This professor is definitely not who you should take a class with if you want to actually learn a language or get a good grade. The entire course is taught in Spanish... mind you it is ELEMENTARY level 101, and she goes through her slides extremely fast.

Worst professor ever. This professor does not teach but lectures at you and expects you to learn spanish through powerpoints that she talks through with no practice of the actual language. I had gone to her office hours multiple times asking for help. She told me: she had no time to create practice questions, I wasn't ready to graduate, and more.

She seems like a nice lady but her teaching is awful. She doesn't really teach anything really. You get homework that you need to teach yourself how to do, then she goes over it in class. Rinse and repeat.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I had professor Castillo for multilple classes. As a person she is great but as a professor not the best. She assigns a lot of homework and lectures for way too long. It is very hard to stay awake in any of her classes. She is also rude and plays favorites with certain students. Avoid her if you can, take professor Costa or Dr Bernard instead.

She is very picky with what she wants on her assignments. She claims to be organized on Canvas but isn't. There is homework every class and the topics we discuss are not related to the tests at all. She is a very nice person but a terrible professor.
She says she speaks in English and Spanish in the Course but its a lie

Worst professor I've ever had. We were never taught properly. Very rude/unprofessional on many occasions. When I asked for help due to certain circumstances, she refused and said to figure it out on my own. She used multiple illnesses against me towards participation, and even telling me to come to an exam with a fever, which ended up being COVID.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Not trying to sound mean. She is a really nice lady, but as a professor she is pretty bad. Not sure if it is her teaching style or the fact that you can't really understand her English, but she made the class way harder than it needed to be. Also the exams were different than the classwork itself which made studying difficult.

This class became dreadful a few times during the semester, mostly because of how much work she tried to assign at the same time. Group work was annoying, but easy. The only thing that was really unfair was having attendance be mandatory, regardless of the fact that administration had told students that it wouldnt count for the semester.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I enjoyed her class so much I am taking her 201 class next semester. She's a really great resource as a native Spanish speaker. She also really seems to understand that different people in the class have different motives for taking the class, and somehow manages to teach in a way that works for everyone. She's super kind and understanding too.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Tough grader']
comment: You learn a lot from the class but there are a ton of assignments and projects throughout the semester. Memorize in class examples and you should be prepared for tests, although you need to do well on translations as well to get a good grade. Those are not as easy to do well on.

Dr. Castillo-Rodriguez was a determined and helpful teacher! I think at times, she wasn't perfectly clear with certain assignments, but she was open to hear what anyone had to say. She would hear us out and if something seemed reasonably unfair to us, she would change it if possible. Like most professors, I can tell she enjoys teaching.

Her teaching style is different than other professors but you will get used to it. She assigned a lot of homework but I think they improved my writing and grammar. Going her office hours also helped me a lot. She cares about the students. She sees the personal improvement of each student. Sometimes she's picky but not the worst.

Overall I like her class. She is passionate and knowledgeable about the class. Her class could be tough since there many requirements and hw. But all of them are for you and helpful. She accommodated the class if it seemed that everyone not following the class. Go to her office hour. It is absolutely helpful. And she cares about students.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: She was a nice professor, however, she was very unclear of her expectations were for her class and would even take points away from your overall grade for it. She is also a very tough grader and is very picky with what she wants to see. She also assigns a lot of work for this class

Im not going to lie, Arabic, a class I took for fun, sunk my grade. Its the only class I have ever gotten a C in and it was really tough for me. That being said, Akil is an amazing man and meeting him was a pleasure. Im generally terrible at learning other languages, but he was receptive to students and a very caring individual. Hes worth the grade

Akil's a gem.  He often launches into tangents laden with warm, ridiculous Middle Eastern humor.  He doesn't take himself seriously, which has potential to make you love him or hate him.  If you don't care about the class, you can pass without really learning anything.  However, if you care about learning Arabic, Akil will make it enjoyable.
He's a great professor who really loves his students. Take his class. You won't regret it.

Akil is great. He really takes the time to make sure everyone understands what he is teaching. If you ever have a problem, just ask him. He does go off on tangents sometimes though, but they are interesting tangents. He is a funny guy and loves jokes.
there aren't enough professors like Akil at this school. He is hands down one of the best.

Akil is the best. He really does try his best to make sure everyone understands, he goes above and beyond and standards I previously set for trying to learn such a hard language. He understands the students and is highly respected. Take a class with him.

Akil is a great professor. He went above and beyond to make sure every student understood what was going on. I finished 202 last year, but I wish I could take Arabic again! Overall funny guy and fair grader.
He's one of the best professors i've ever had. I highly respect him.
I love him he s super funny and cool, makes the language seem possible. highly recommend to anyone.
Professor Aljaysh is a wonderful professor that does more than he gets paid to do. I enjoy the enculturation of the Middle East into the class as well. He is quite affable and very funny.
Lousy and uninspiring. Actively competes with students and demands the utmost respect from everyone around him while not respecting anyone else.
He was fine, I guess. He won't give a 100 for anything; I got a 99 for everything. But the class wasn't hard but you have to go because attendance is graded. Don't buy the over-the-head phones.

Andrew Watkins-Alocer has the unique ability to remove joy and passion from playing music in his ensembles. He has very high expectations for his musicians, but he does not convey them in a caring way - instead, he treats students disrespectfully, and after Fall semester, over half of the Jazz Band quit becuase his class was unbearable.

He's a great guy with a deep passion for what he does. The way he conveys information can sometimes be a bit confusing, and he does zone out from time-to-time, but he is a very easy grader and is just a fun, relaxing, easy time in his class. He's always available outside of class to help students and always engages with students.
She was the worst professor I've ever had. I couldn't understand a word she was saying and the content seemed ridiculously hard and confusing. Didn't give anywhere near enough time on tests.
please stay away from professor park. avoid her if you value your education and grades.

I am confused about 99 percent of the time. I feel like a failure every time I try and do a homework assignment. She gave a 2 hour test that she wanted done in 50 minutes. She isn't really easy to understand, and when I asked her for outside of class help she ignored my email... I would never recommend this class.
Useless is the only word to describe her!!!
difficult and hard to understand but oh so hot!!
Flexible online course.

The workload in this asynchronous course became tough at a certain point. She is very understanding and makes an effort to work with students. She assigns one homework weekly, but it requires thoughtfulness and will take hours to complete. Assignments consist of reading or watching music content, then writing an analysis.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']
comment: Took her MUSC100 course online over the summer. Most of the course is just writing assignments, which are easy, but she does care about word count and page length. The frequency of these assignments were sometimes too fast, but the final essay was alright. She's an easy grader so don't worry about quality, I got a 100 for meeting requirements.

Golec has a very Professor Snape-esque teaching style in which she will walk around the classroom trying to find people who have made mistakes in their work. It didn't really seem like she cared all that much about how her students were doing in the class, and if I have the option to choose another professor later down the line, I very well may.

Professor Golec is a very straightforward professor. She definitely wants to make sure you understand the material so don't be afraid to ask for help. She easily cleared up any confusions I had, she's very nice to talk to individually. This class was extremely easy for me cause I have tons of musical experience but it might be tough if you don't.
An easier class if you know about music. You can tell she really wanted everyone to truly understand what she was teaching.

Professor Golec is about as straightforward as the material itself. It's not too difficult, but not really fun in any way. She's nice, but the class is kinda boring. Easy A for me. I'll take a boring easy class over a crazy and hard one any day of the week. but yeah :/

Just a generally extremely cold, uncaring professor that clearly does not want to be teaching. If you have a music background, you will be fine, but beyond that little will be gained other than a letter grade and moving on to the next step. As someone very passionate about playing piano, she very nearly killed all my interest.

Golec is a great professor but only for music majors. The amount of material we are supposed to memorize is insane.Taking this course for a gen ed, it's simply way too hard. I spend hours doing homework for this class and still get bad grades on them. Feels like I'm wasting my time.
Easy A if you have a music background, however, do NOT take if you can't read music. Book is mandatory since it's a workbook, however, attendance isn't necessary if you understand the material

Class was far too immersive for a gen ed. She seems to expect everyone has background knowledge and a vested interest in the history of music, when I was placed in this class for the credits. 2 page papers every week, have to go to 6 concerts and write essays summarizing those, and an 8 page final essay. Try to avoid this class if possible.

I know nothing abt music and this class was easy! At first seems very fast paced but you get used to it. Weekly assignments based on material given, usually requires you to read through something than write about it. IMO, way better than quizzes. Many people didnt go to lecture, but helped a lot with assignments. Makes everything available online.
she was mean and she never read my emails. she graded very harshly even through I was one of the only to get all my work in on time.

Professor Golec provides weekly assignments that she expects you to make at least a page long, even when there is not much to write about. She does not get back to you with emails and even stated that she does not respond. All of this goes with her unusual grading style with most things out of 400 points, the midterm out of 2000 and the final 1500.

Golec is helpful when you ask for help and she does want people in her class to succeed. You need to show up for most of the class days to do well in the class. She goes really fast in the beginning of the semester and it does take time to get used to it. I recommend: DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T KNOW HOW TO READ MUSIC!

Unreasonably difficult for an introduction level class, no accommodations for COVID whatsoever, and if these are the accommodations, than I don't want to see what the normal class is like. She may be passionate about what she teaches, and she may touch others with her teaching in a way I don't get, but if you think this will be fun... think again.

Here is your classic "My class is the most important thing in the world, so you should focus solely on it, and forget everything else." kind of professor. Both MUSC 110 and 120 are unreasonably difficult for intro level classes, that both require 8 page research papers. She has made no accommodations for COVID and it shows, to be Frank STAY AWAY!!!

Took this class to fulfill one of my last gen eds as it was one of the few available online fine arts credits. Golec was a hard grader, taking off so many points on homework grades for minor mistakes. She also required a final exam and an 8 page final paper for an intro music gen ed class, taught asynchronously online in a pandemic.

She grades each assignment out of 250 points and the midterm and final out of 2,000. If you email her asking for help on an assignment she literally copies and pastes the exact same directions already given. Not to mention she gave hw during finals week on top of an 8-page essay AND a final. 2 assignments brought my grade from a 96 to a 90...

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: This class was awful. I took it as a gen-Ed & it was so much work. She takes attendance very seriously, assigns lots of hw and grades it thoroughly. She gives tests pretty often too. Her accent makes it hard to understand her. Shes not very approachable either. If music isnt youre thing but you need to fulfill the gen-Ed, dont take this class!

She takes attendance every day so go to class. She explains things very well and gives you time in class to work on what you learned. She grades homework harshly so check your work before you submit it. If you know what you're doing and go to class she will like you. It shows that she wants her students to succeed in her class. Put in effort though

This is not the gen ed class you want to take. It is a trap class and is very hard even if you do attend class. She takes attendance but her way of teaching is to give us handouts and then have the students give presentations on them. No homework outside of class but you have to attend 6 concerts. The tests are very hard.

MUSC 100 with this professor does is not the easy gen ed you want it to be. Their are many out-of-class time commitments (going to concerts and bringing her back a program) and her tests are very hard. It is almost pointless going to class as she does not efficiently explain things, instead choosing to make students do presentations on her content

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Doesn't seem like a gen ed at all. You definitely have to put in the time and effort in studying for the exams or you won't do well. She's a tough grader but gives out study guides which are helpful.
Very good professor her exams are not that easy but shes gives you a review sheet and if you do it youll be perfect.

If you have a music background and love music, definitely take this class. However, if you're not experienced with reading music definitely do not, because it is almost entirely musical notation. Dr. Golec is a great teacher! She is very good at explaining things, and I really liked her as a person. She is very engaged and always answers questions!

She takes attendance every class and you have to bring both of your textbooks to the class every day because of in-class activities with the books. Class materials are easy as long as you pay attention and do practices.
Took basic musicianship (MUSC 110) with Golec. Easy A. Numerous homework assignments but they're easy and boost your grade. Golec is witty and loves what she does.

She is a genius in music. She can answer any question. There is a LOT of reading involved. Make sure to come to all classes and participate (she will ask for volunteers to read poems or reviews). Golec is a fair grader and will explain her grading system. Will not put up with bad behavior.

Dr. Golec is one of the most unpleasant professors I've had the displeasure of dealing with in my entire college career. She is unhelpful, unreasonably tough, and expects way too much. AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE

Golec is a genius in music. She knows so much, but with that being said, she expects a lot out of her students. It is an intro level class for non music majors, but it seems like the opposite. I learned a lot in this class, if you pay attention and read the textbook, it is not too bad.
Golec is great! She isn't easy but she is very fair and willing to  help. Its manageable if you put in the work.

Professor Golec's class is strictly memorization. Her tests are fairly easy. Her Basic Musicianship class is the easiest I've taken at Geneseo. She's also really pretty and dresses like a model. Plus!

She works really fast, and if you have played a instrument or understand music it is an easy A. She is very specific on how she grades, but she always reviews. If you don't understand something she will review it multiple times with you. The homework is a must, and the tests are relatively easy if you do well on the homework and quizzes.

Golec doesn't normally teach 110, but the usual professor was ill. I have no complaints about Golec. She was clear and always willing to help and slow down if the class wasn't understanding. There's a TON of assignments, but they're easy if you really take the time to do them. If you have any musical knowledge at all, this class is easy. Take it.

Music history is a fun class with her. That being said, she expects a LOT from her students. Don't take her if you want to cruise through and expect an A. She is a fair grader there's just a ton of info! Her handouts are really helpful to study from

Soo nice! Don't really need the text book for her intro to music history. She gives out outlines everyday which are extremely helpful! Participate in her class or she will give quizzes. Overall she is insanely smart and an amazing professor to have

I thought this class would be fairly easy but was wrong. It required a lot of outside studying, and Professor Golec teaches the class as though you have background knowledge of the material. In order to do well you must read the book thoroughly and be prepared for her pop quizzes. You do end up learning a lot, but this class is rather stressful.

She teaches this class just as hard as a 300 level which seems unfair. She does not answer emails. I'm doing alright in the class but if I did not have a pretty extensive music background I would be completely lost, and probably failing.  Don't take this for a fine arts credit if you cannot already read music and understand its basic forms.

For a class designed for non-music majors, she relies too much on background musical knowledge. She is pretty intimidating as well. Most people usually give up once they see how hard the tests are, but you really need to put work into this class in order to do well. Much harder than a gen ed should be. It's harder only if you don't put n the work.

Great teacher and kind person. She truly wants to help students and have them do well, but you have to be willing to put in work as well. As long as you do the reading and complete the assignments the class isn't hard. Tests are straightforward. She's not boring or mean towards students at all
LOVE HER.
The funniest professor I've had so far...

Professor Harrigan is the BEST professor in Geneseo no doubt. She cares about students and about what she teaches. The class is easy but feels meaningful with crafts to help you think deeper about the topics.

THIS IS MY FAV PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME EVER!!!! Omg. Harrigan is super sweet, super funny, super animated and full of life. I NEVER had a boring lecture. grade is entirely on class participation and then 2 projects. No exam, no book. She made everything super easy to understand and is an amazing storyteller. If you have the option, TAKE HER CLASS!!!
Lovely professor. Very unconventional class, but still felt like I learned a lot. Hardly any assignments outside of class. An easy A if you are willing to participate and listen to feedback.

Harrigan has the sweetest most bubbly personality. Her passion for the content is reflected in every lecture. She truly cares about her students and wants everyone to thrive. Focus on group projects (pretty painless), class discussion, and participation. Easy to meet outside of class. So sweet and kind, very high energy and loves her family & work!

Meredith's kindness is endless. The class itself was so interesting and therapeutic. The range of topics we discussed were productive and meaningful. I STRONGLY recommend this class to everyone because of how important it is. Meredith makes you feel heard, understood, and valued. I hope my future educational endeavors include her as an instructor!

Real-life angel. I love Meredith, she truly cares about her students. Took comn209 with her, a super easy class, 1 test only, and a semester-long group project. 100% recommend taking a course, any course with her!

I took her for Interpersonal Communication. She is amazing 10/10! I recommend that everyone takes her courses. She is very chill and caring about her students. The class is made up of everyday lectures about learning concepts and vocabulary. Harrigan does an extraordinary job of doing that and helps you understand. You will love class with her!

Prof. Harrigan is fantastic. She is super sweet and cares about her students and the material. The whole class is focused around 4 group projects, 4 project reflections, and 4 individual papers, along with a final exam. She is very enthusiastic and makes the material interesting. The final project decides the format of the final! Take her classes!

Meredith is very lecture heavy but she makes everything really easy to understand. If you have any issues, just talk to her, she will always find a way to make things work. All of the classwork is pretty straightforward. Her classes are very by the book but if you try to have fun with it, it's not bad at all!

Dr. Harrigan is by far the most genuine, passionate, and caring professor at Geneseo. Her enthusiasm and passion can't be beat and it's quite honestly inspiring. If I could be mmh when I grow up, I would be in pretty good shape. Her lectures are engaging and excellently supplement the textbook reading (which I recommend for an A). 100% recommend!!!

Professor Harrigan is a fantastic professor. She is probably the most fair professor I have met. The amount of work you put in is probably the grade you will get. Her lectures are kind of useless, but attendance isn't counted (but she does notice who comes and doesn't). She isn't as bad with APA as some will say, but I would learn it. Also read!

Although it is true Dr. Harrigan makes you work for an A in her class and I found her tests to be harder than a typical 100-level course, if you put in the effort, an A is 100% doable. She's extremely helpful & responsive if you ask, and I feel like I learned a lot from her. Will definitely take classes with her again

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tests are tough']
comment: The material itself is not hard to understand but the way she tests is difficult (the way she words the questions, answer choices, etc). But you figure out what types of questions she may ask fairly quick. There are a bunch of 3 piece papers that she grades VERY harshly. She is a stickler for APA so you have to watch out for little mistakes.

Harrigan is a ray of sunshine. I didnt really like the class material but she made it fun. For some reason I could not do better than an 85 on her tests and my essays never improved because she has awful handwriting and you cant read her comments. But, I still highly recommended because you learn so many life lessons and she is amazing

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Dr. Harrigan is a very nice woman. Very mother-like, incredibly friendly, and clearly cares about her students. The class only has 7 grades: 3 tests and 4 papers. The tests are fair, the papers are pretty rigorous. You must follow APA format guidelines TO THE TEE. The one thing I didn't like about her is she doesn't give tests back for review.

If I could be half the professor mmh is, then I'd be a lucky person indeed. Her enthusiasm towards her subject and her overwhelming positivity are infectious. The lectures hardly feel like 2.5 hours and she does a phenomenal job weaving theory and practical application into a format that is understandable. Perfect APA, study, & you'll do great.

She does her best to make the subject clear but the class remains miserable. She grades insanely harshly on the papers. If you are not intimately familiar with APA, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. A really good- but not 100% perfect- paper with only 2 mistakes (typo or form) will net you an 80. (33/45). 5 mistakes takes off another 3 points (66%)

Harrigan is a kind professor and very well put together. She is very organized and likes to have a schedule but this class is not as structured bc of the collaboration with foreign university. She works with her discomfort  becoming VERY flexible- changing due dates and work based on what benefits the class. I Love her personality for this class

mmh is an amazing professor!  She is very sweet and kind and she truly wants her students to do well in the class.  There are four 4 page papers to do throughout the semester and a total of 3 easy 50 multiple choice tests (2 unit tests and 1 cumulative final). I highly recommend taking any class you can with her!

One of the greatest professors at Geneseo. Never in a bad mood, super enthusiastic about the course material, very knowledgeable and helpful all around. Like someone said before, expects perfection on APA format, which is the only thing bad I can say about her

Not many professors could keep me interested for a 2.5 hour class, but Harrigan did. Her lectures are interesting and enthusiastic and her happy, sweet, bubbly personality is contagious. Tests can be hard, definitely need to study. A few written papers - fair grader. Wonderful professor, good class - definitely recommend!

Loveliest lady at Geneseo. There are no negatives to her personality: she is direct, caring, very knowledgeable about the subject and is inspired in her field.  If you take a few classes with her at once, expect back to back tests, (not a criticism.) Even if you don't like the material that much her sweetness will get you through it. :)
If you really wanna understand and embrace the core of it, its worth it. I have grown to be a better person by taking this class!
If you really wanna understand and embrace the core of it, its worth it. I have grown to be a better person by taking this class!

Absolutely loved coming to class. So fun and Mmh is enthusiastic, bubbly, and energetic. Course material is interesting and fun. Tough grader-- watch out for APA 6th edition formatting (perfect it). Tests are tough but read the book as well as learning class material and you'll do fine. Highly recommend the course

Harrigan is a very smart, nice person.  Great lecturer, although I found her tests a little difficult. Gives good feedback on papers, but is kind of obsessed with apa.  Bottom line:  she's very nice, competent, and committed.  Take her if you can.

I've taken Comn 103, 248, and 317 with Harrigan and she is the most engaging, interesting and helpful professor that I've had at Geneseo. Her knowledge and interest of the subject matter make you interested, too. She just wants you to do well, and as long as you attend most classes you will.

By far the best professor I have had so far at Geneseo. Never before have I had a prof. who cared more about the success of her students and their ability to understand the material. Both her 103 and 345 classes were extremely interesting and I learned so much from each one. If you do the work and take the time do understand it, you will do well.
