I want to be Meredith Harrigan when I grow up. I can not say a single bad thing about her. Class is optional and relaxed, tests are easy and multiple choice if its a 200 level, 300 includes essays but not bad, fairly predictable topics. She is just amazing.

Meredith Harrigan is an amazing professor. I am taking a class with her right now and I absolutely love it! She is an extremely warm, friendly and engaging professor. I actually pay attention! She is always helpful and willing to answer any questions. She will never belittle you or make you feel stupid. I plan on taking many more classes with her!

Dr. Harrigan is my FAVORITE professor. She's so cheerful, and going to class always brightens my day. She is a wonderful lecturer, and she definitely knows how to make things interesting. I've never skipped her class, and I was actually disappointed when she had to cancel class once. Fair grader, nice person, awesome professor.

mmh is one of the most engaging lecturers on campus. She's incredibly energetic and keeps everyone in the class on their toes. I wasn't really interested in the subject matter, but she made learning it incredibly fun. She gives great feedback on papers, too. Take as many classes as possible with her.

She is awesome.  Very organized and helpful.  I've taken 4 classes (103, 211, 248, 345) with her and I've learned so much.  She really wants you to learn and she makes it easy for you.  If you pay attention in class (which is not difficult) and use "the language of the course" in every paper you write, you're golden.
MMH is intelligent, organized, and passionate about class material and students. She makes a department with so many incompetent professors much more enjoyable!! Take her class!!!!!!!!!
No Comments

Although I got an Ain this class, this was by far my least favorite class all because of the professor. She was so boring and class was painful. She also took our in-class reflections as attendance so you had to be there. Most of your grade was dictated by 4 quizzes, all of which were difficult and required outside knowledge, in order to do well.

Offered lots of extra credit opportunities for her THEA 100, she made the class easy and was not hard at all. Mainly did these reading quizzes which were not that hard at all and then the final (which she gave you multiple chances to get out of). She was a little hard to get ahold of outside of class, but not a bad professor overall.

Gives what she gets---respect her and she'll respect you. Participation is an absolute MUST, but also not hard at all. Don't be afraid to be wrong. Was slightly forceful sometimes, but ultimately you could choose your level of investment in all activities.

Looking forward to having her again.

Tracie is a good professor. She is nice but she is really looking for participation from the class. A lot of extra credit is offered and I got out of my final by going to see a free play. If you read the plays or an in depth youtube video you will be good! Before the quizzes, she will answer any questions. I didn't mind the class!

This was her first semester teaching, and it has probably been my least favorite class. Yes, it is manageable, but you'll have a multiple choice and short answer quiz on 100 page plays that you have a few days in advance. The quizzes look for very specific information, she expects participation, gets strict and won't hesitate to yell at the class.

tags: ['EXTRA CREDIT', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: This was a fun class and made me interested in the theater in which I knew nothing about beforehand. Put in a moderate amount of effort and you will get a high grade. Professor Thomason asks for your attention which should be easy for any college student. Offers a lot of extra credit opportunities too.

She does not know how to teach or create a lesson. Her syllabus was basically useless and she didn't give it to us until we were a week into the classes. If you want to learn something and actually get something out of the class, do not take Theatre 100 with her.
If you get the chance to take theater 100 with her do it. Her class is very easy and she's a wonderful professor who cares about her students success.

UHHHH she makes you literally tell the entire class your trauma like if I wanted my therapist Id call her. I feel like Im getting hazed and I hate her, this is absolutely awful. She called out a girl in class who has DIABETES for eating M&Ms when her blood sugar was low. People should never have to talk about their personal lives publicly.

Dr. Cylke is an amazing teacher. This semester his class turned online and i'm not going to lie it is a little difficult being asynchronous but Dr. Cylke checks in with all the students personally and makes sure they are on track and are doing well. If you plan your time out and stay on schedule to get things done in time, you'll have no problem

I highly recommend that if you're looking for a course in sociology that is not a lot of work but also in depth and interesting, that you take a course with Professor Cylke. The main grades are made up of book notes (you have to prove you read 6 books) and they're interesting and easy reads. You get a lot out of this course, highly recommend!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Prof. Cylke is a great professor. While the topics can be very heavy and sad, he makes them understandable and why we should care. Most of the grade is based on reading&taking notes on 6 books. He also gives you the midterm and final right at the beginning of the semesters if you want to start early. Overall, great class and super informative.

Cylke makes a point of caring for his students. You can always ask for an extension and he even cancelled our final due to stress levels. He is a good teacher and the class is really interesting. I would say one of the best classes I have taken. He makes it hard to fail and there are book notes every two weeks. If you budget your time you will pass

You read 6 books in this class. I honestly didn't feel the need to go to class when the midterm was based on a brand new article. He literally had people start writing their names on a paper to give them .25 points added to their grade for showing up... He's a nice guy but the class was rather uninteresting to me. He doesn't allow laptops or phones
Just wanted to come on here and make this comparison--EVERY single one of his lectures feel like a ted talk!! A good one!! Great class.

Literally love Professor Cylke! He is one of best and most understanding professors out there. Late assignments have no penalty. Theres definitely lots of reading and note taking in this class, but everything is doable and he usually gives you full points for just completion. If youre happy with your midterm paper, you can opt out of your final!

He is a very nice professor and very understanding. Allowed late assignments. However, the work load is extremely heavy. 6 books, page by page notes required. He also gave weekly lecture videos and required notes for those too. The books do provide a better understanding of the topics, but it was an excessive amount of work. Not worth it.

Best professor I have ever had. He is extremely caring and always tries to make things easier for you if you are going through stress. The class work load was not a lot and the topics were genuinely interesting. If you need to take a sociology class, take it with Professor Cylke!!
Absolute angel. Cares about his students and does not give too much work at all

Kurt Cylke is funny and cares about his students. I loved his class & him, but his lectures did drag. There are no tests or quizzes. There are six books you read & take book notes on but you really don't even have to read the book if you just jot down a line from every few pages. He takes attendance, but you don't miss much if you skip sometimes.

His lectures are so insightful and has you question things that you would never have questioned before about tour society and the things happening around us that we do not know that is happening. I was sick the majority of our spring semester and he was super understanding and flexible with assignment deadlines. He is the BEST!

Makes you read 6 books and do page by page notes for each. I skipped an entire month and got a B but you NEED to do the book notes. Attendance isn't mandatory but is 10% of your grade so tread lightly. I rarely did the work in its entirety, and got 80 & 90s. Cylke is a GEM... Bless him. Just use upperclassmen book notes, you'll be fine. EASY GRADE

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Super chill guy, really passionate about his subject, but his lectures can sometimes drag on because of the lack of participation and note taking. You'll read 6 books that are interesting and informative that you take notes on. Each book is given two weeks but he gives tips on how to be a better reader and is very lenient with deadlines. good class

Classes get very dry and boring on multiple occasions. Also, prepare to read six books that can be interesting at first, but make you lose interest as you get deeper in. However, professor Cylke himself is great. No tests, clear grading criteria, fine with late work, always lets you make things up, super understanding, etc... boring, but an easy A
Good professor but get ready to read 6 long books and take page by page notes. Takes the point out of reading at least to me. 2 easy papers that he gives you on the first day of class. Easy A class

Insightful and thought-provoking class. You have to read about six books and take notes on them, but they really helped you understand sociological issues in America. 2 easy take home essays for the midterm and final.
He gives you enough time to get your assignment done.

Professor Cylke was fantastic. I took SOCL 102 for my minor. The class was lecture heavy and at times dull. Yet the information and data presented was truly eye opening and at times shocking. Cylke was so helpful outside of class. He really wants everyone to learn as well as receive an A in his class.

He's a great professor and the class very informative. By taking this class I found it easier to participat in conversations of topics such as welfare reform because of how much I learned by taking this class. He is very understanding and gives extensions when needed. No tests. Midterm and final are short papers and he gives them to you the 1st da

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'SO MANY PAPERS', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Cylke's lectures are rich and highly interesting. I would strongly suggest his class for Soc. majors. But there is a ton of reading and writing--far beyond a 100 level. He makes you outline each page for six 300 page books (great books tbh but still). Also a midterm and a final. BE CAREFUL.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Good proffessor, fair grading and a quality learning experience! take the class for sure:)

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Dr. Cylke is an excellent professor. I really did learn tons, and the coursework was manageable. If your like me and needed a GPA booster before graduation, but also wanted to learn something, this class is a must take. Four short book reviews and two take home tests, that was it. He even gave out extra credit once or twice- huge incentive.

Easy class and knowledgeable professor. I really learned so much in this class. Two book reviews, two exams (midterm and final that are BOTH take home), and two projects. Attend to class, incorporate information from lecture in order to guide you with the book reviews and exams. The projects took a little time but they are manageable
Prof  cylke was one of the best professors I ever had.
Easy class and very nice professor. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Professor Cylke is clearly passionate about the material, he'll show you graphs and charts about social and economic problems until you've seen them all, but the projects are straightforward and the tests are take-home with opportunity to revise for higher grades. 2 Projects and a midterm and final for this semester, really easy course load.

Professor Cylke is one of the nicest people I've ever met. This class, while sometimes dry, is one of the best classes I've ever taken. We did 2 projects throughout the semester and the midterm and final were take home exams. Definitely recommend this class to anyone remotely interested in sociology.

Professor Cylke is a really great professor. You can tell that he is extremely passionate about sociology. He gives a midterm and a final, both essay exams and two semester-long projects. It is a great class, especially if you want to come out of it learning more about the world. I would definitely recommend him to anyone!

Could not be happier with Cylke. He's a genuinely interesting person and cares a lot about the material he teaches.  I wasn't happy with my first test grade and he let me rewrite one of the essays & gave me that improved grade for the entire test. He's a very nice man and is definitely willing to help you with whatever you need assistance with!
Prof Cylke is very smart. I like that he's so involved in the Geneseo community.

Dr. Cylke seems to change to a tough professor that is much different from before. his tests were ez because were take-home. but now students need  to read a lot stuff and prepare all the long essay topic(7 for mid term) for a real test. it may need more then 6 hours extra class reading per week.
Summer course, amazing professor and person :)

Cylke is amazing! He is very entertaining and gets his point across using movies and clips. Very eccentric and a little goofy! You don't really need to attend class to do well...i skipped almost every other class and still got an A. You just need to check the syllabus so you don't miss some assignments and tests. Exams are very easy!

Prof. Cylke is awesome. He bases his classes on what topics students want to be informed about. Class can get boring. Its only  mandatory to get notes. Do the readings and go visit him in office hours and you'll do fine!

Really good guy and not a hard grader.  Very understanding on the work you turn in.  Class mostly just him talking with his strong liberal views.  Doesn't present the other side, sometimes very frustrating.

Cylke's a pretty cool guy. Class topics are interesting but broad, readings are essential. Going to office hours will help you get a better grade because he likes to see that you're engaged and interested. Requires quite a bit of work outside of the classroom for a 100 level but it's a pretty easy A.

Cylke was a great teacher! He talks most of the class period, but he REALLY knows his stuff. If you are having trouble, go to his office hours. He will give you everything you need to know. By everything... I mean point out the answers. Do the readings. Go to class. You will do great!

Great Professor! He changed the way I view worldly issues. While his opinions are strong, I found it useful to hear a different perspective than what the media is feeding the country. His class is not boring, unless you have no interest in what is happening around you in this world.... he turned an Undeclared into a Soc major! Well done

Professor Cylke is a very nice guy. His class can be pretty boring, he talks most of the time, some topics are more interesting than others. Final is take home and he is willing to let you make up your own papers and projects. Didn't like the class but did like the professor and ended with an easy A-.
Very disorganized. Poor communicator.

Really like professor cylke. He is a very nice guy. The material in this class was sometimes a little boring but he gives three options for grading and the exams are just papers, the final was a take home. I went to his office hours before exams and her was very helpful.
Interesting readings, and occasionally an interesting class. Professor is very nice and helpful, but at the end of the semester I don't feel like I've learned much.

This class is not for people who like to think on their own. The professor is not interested in any opinion or thought that does not match his own. If you decide to write your actual opinion on a test you will fail the test. Lectures are full of flawed arguments and biased statistics.
Very nice man.  Helpful if you go to office hours.  He is very opinionated about touchy issues.  Go to class and read all of the material!

This entire class was opinion being taught as fact. There was no room for disagreement or discussion, either you agreed with him or you were quiet. I pride myself on my academic integrity, and I did not like having to lie about my views in order to pass the class. On the bright side, the course work isn't too hard. All in all not pleased.
Great class, great professor! Would recommend to everyone. The class is easy and you will learn a lot. Thumbs up!

He's the best, he really teaches you a new way of looking at everything around you. You need to take what he says with a grain of salt, he's got strong opinions but welcomes class discussion/debate. Assigns a lot of reading but it isn't the end of the world if you skip some. Gives grading options, easy A if you show up and write good papers

Excellent! If you want to get anything out of his class, then DO THE READING! Otherwise, I don't understand why you'd come to class. Very reasonable, if you show him some effort and that you're working with him on a class, he'll work with you. Very knowledgeable and always willing to hear others' POV and hash things out.

One of the most amazing professors ever.  I convinced at least 6 other firends to take this class and they all love it.  Gives you an entire new view of..  ..everything.  Go to class and read the books. He lets you choose how you are graded tests are fun
Really cool guy and a very interesting class.  Several grading options.  Reading not necessary to pass, but most of the discussions are based off reading.  Definitely recommend him.

very helpful with students... wants to see effort includes primarily attendance, would like you to participate but understand if you dont. i recommend taking a class with him. self discipline helps with this class. 5 short papers can be handed in on different dates i waited to the end. dont do that...

He is a very good professor.  Class is interesting and he is very knowledgeable.  I learned a lot in his class.  Also his grading is very easy and there are choices on what to use as a grading way.  Reading the books isnt really necessary to do well in the class.

I have take 4 classes with Cylke since I have been here and he is sweet. He is definately dedicated to his work and students. He is extremely flexible and pretty easy grader. Take every class you can with him!
He is a really great teacher. His tests were just short essays. This class was very interesting and I didn't even want to skip.

Such an amazing teacher. I learn more in his class than all of the other teachers i have ever had combined. Not even kidding. It wakes you up to a million things no one has ever told you about the US. He is extremely intelligent and because of him i'm majoring in sociology. Is NOT boring! If you only take one class at Geneseo, take his.

Cylke is an awesome guy - very helpful and will give you a break if you really need it. His teaching method is pretty cool; takes a bit of getting used to but he's great once you're adapted. I wouldn't recommend taking an 8:05 class... it's tough to get out of bed, even for Cylke, but I'd definitely recommend him as a professor.

Cykle is a really good professor with amazing personal life experience to add to class.   as a memeber of his 8:05 class i can say that while it is hard to get up sometimes, i probably wouldnt go to the class as often if i wasnt a major fan of his teaching method.  sometimes he swears a lot, but i love his class. totally recommend.

really nice guy but SO boring! class participation was 75% of your grade which must've been the only reason anyone came to class.  3 short papers on the topic of your choice, okay grader, pretty much laid back about everything.

I enjoyed this class. It def.wasn't really easy and you had to really grasp the information to be able to express it in the essay tests he gives but the information was so intersting. It really opened my eyes about certain issues and I would recommend it if you are open minded and willing to see different sides of the story. Good Class

His class may seem a little sketchy and it involves a lot of his opinions. Very helpful, nice, and easy to talk to. Makes his students comfortable during office hours. Not intimidating at all. GO SEE HIM! If you have questions on anything or a grade, see him about it. I got my midterm grade bumped for a B to an A- just by talking to him about it!

I agree with everyone who said his personal opinions are what the class focuses on. I also would have to say some of his data is a bit sketchy. He tries to make claims assuming the class is stupid (like saying something is statistically significant when it is NO where being so-most ppl wouldn't notice unlses you took a stats class!) Nice guy though

Prof Cylke is a very nice and helpful teacher! you can tell he really cares about his students n is more than willing to help if you seek him out.  However, this class is reallly boring and you dont learn much.  You have to write 6 papers.  He doesnt give specifics about what he wants nor do you learn alot to write your papers on

Seems like a nice guy, but his teaching leaves a bit to be desired. It's tough to believe his claim to impartiality on the first day when class seems to revolve around his personal opinions concerning social issues. It's true,he expects you to sit and gasp at the numbers he throws out. Class is a bit unorganized. Take notes on the movies!

This class is very interesting and contains a lot of information.  I would stay away from it if you are not interested.  He provides a lot of information.  Grading is very liberal.  He is a good professor.
Cool teacher...can keep you interested even at 8:30AM! Most of the time...

This guy should not be teaching. He spits out numbers that come from manipulated data. He essentially feeds the class propaganda. He is not a scientist, as his methods are not analytical. I challanged him frequently in class but then he started to ignore me. So then he failed me for a BS reason and I had to appeal it. Also a poor advisor. AVOID HIM
7 essays, a bunch of books we never read, and a presentation. No tests but no learning. no due dates, doesn't care about ANYTHING.

Very approachable professor.  The class structure is left up to you as far as how many papers and tests you want to take.  Cylke is simply easy going, obviously prepares for class, knows his stuff, and a great professor and person.
Tough grader, but allows make ups. Helpful in office hours.

The class covers interesting topics- the book list is great, but the way he taught got on my nerves. He expects you to just sit and gasp over the stats he shows you, and he assumes that we have no conception of the way our world is working.

Early class so I didn't go that often but I still did well cuz I did the readings and understood them. I liked him a lot, actually. It's too bad I hate getting up early. I'd definitely take him again.
If you like obsessing over poverty and discussing how wonderful it is to pay taxes, you'll love his class; very lax-in good and bad ways, and very nice.
Great guy, very lax on assignments, definitely reccomend
An awesome class; lectures are interesting and structured; lets you decide how you would like to be graded; interesting readings; very approachable. Definitly changes your perspective on society.
The class is very dry. The reading is okay. He requests specific entries for personal journals but doesn't clarify when you seek his help.
Awesome guy.  He'll change the way you look at things.  Take this class!
Awesome professor. Even if you don't like sociology take his classes anyway. Very inspiring and thought provoking. He is awesome!
He is a great prof.  Defiinitely makes you think about the world we live in and question some of the crazy things we do
I love this guy, very approachable, helpful, clear.  Go to his office hours! even if its just to talk.  Great teacher who is open to new ideas.  Also his book list is great.

Had him for an advisor.  Very cool person.  Super in class-very laid back and approachable.  Very smart, and expects students to do their work.  He also drank more coffee than I did, which is a feat.  I would recommend him for people who are ino sociology
very laid-back and approachable. great professor and knows what he's talking about
No Comments
Great professor. Class was so good, it inspired me add soc as a minor
A quality course
awesome professor in every way :-)

Very helpful, patient, nice professor. That being said the class was much harder than I anticipated. Class lectures don't help much but labs definitely do. Worst part of class are the 5 projects that took a lot of time for each. Tests weren't terrible but average hovered around a C. Cool class but as said, much harder than I hoped for a 120 course.

Great prof. I wholeheartedly disagree with the naysayers. When I took the class (twice, because I screwed up the first time), I found his lectures to be helpful and he was very helpful with the projects. To those who say he hasn't helped u with the projects, he IS willing to help but only when you've made some progress on your own.

Although he tries his best to explain, he confuses me with the projects.  Part of the reason was due to my failure to catch up, but even those who understood the material spend many days trying to figure it out.  He promised to curve the overall grades at the end of the semester, but failed to do so.  I got a C in the class (which was class avg)

Although he's a really nice guy, I wouldn't recommend taking him for Computer Science.  I don't think he is interested in helping people out with the projects.  Every time when I go to his OH, he seems annoyed. I think I'm the average student in the class.  Take him if you are interested in starting off your first semester of college with a C.
Worst proffesor i have ever had do not take his class
Great Class, The class is especially good for computer science majors, very challenging and eye-opening...

Absolutely abysmal professor.  Unable to teach, projects impossible, didn't teach syntax, just gave basic insight on the foundations of compsci and java.  Quite possibly the worst class I have ever taken, with one of the worst teachers.
Good teacher, very nice guy. Was very patient with everyone, even non-majors in CS 119. Projects require significant time, but he clearly stated this at the beginning of the course.
Great professor! Extremely helpful and understanding! Very patient with non-majors and new programmers who put forth effort. Would definitely recommend for CSCI 119!...

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: If you keep up with the papers, online quizzes, and exams, it should not be that hard to fail this class. In terms of papers, the professor can be harsh on APA, but gives amazing feedback on what needs to change and how to perfect on the next paper + beyond! I would take this or any class with her again! I took this course in the summer.

Professor Trible is a very caring person that will help you outside of class or if you just send her an email. Graded homework takes forever to get back, which was frustrating because future assignments went off of previous assignments we never got the feedback on. There are many presentations and a lot of group work. I didn't really use the book.

Best professor I've ever had. She will help you out with anything you ask about. She's super friendly! Sometimes she messes up assignment due dates/extends them/etc. But that's okay. There is group work, and you do presentations- But they're easy, and she makes it fun for you. Had 1 midterm, got a 100 on it- Just make sure you take down notes!

Professor Trible is super nice but she's also new, which means sometimes she's disorganized and got way too assignment-happy to the point where she couldn't keep up with it. If you hand in everything ON TIME (she will halve your grade if you don't) and show that you put effort in, you'll get a good grade.

No exams, all busy work. They're pretty easy, but it's really tedious to do the assignments. Really easy class overall, and probably the easiest BCOM professor. Working in groups is awkward and sucks, but this isn't a bad class overall. Professor can be unclear with deadlines and assignments, but this is probably because she's new. DO NOT BUY BOOKS

Dr Roth is a very kind individual; however, her class was among the most inaccessible I've ever taken. Her reading list is long and uses language that isn't necessary to get the point across. The class caused unnecessary distress with readings we did not get to discuss in class, to the point where I now resent the class for eating my time.

I LOVEEEE Roth. I've had her for two classes over 3 years. Her lectures are always so interesting and engaging, making 50 minutes feel like 2. She is very responsive to emails and gives great feedback on any/most assignments. She's honestly one of the best professors I've had at Geneseo. The class itself was very fascinating. Definitely recommend!!

A great professor, really good at explaining things deeper. Easy class, just need to try and put effort. READ!!!! Most of the class is just discussion surrounding the readings that we had. Good class to take for a gen ed.
She is a very understanding and helpful professor. Class is very easy besides a few papers but any other homework you don't really have to do.

I loved the course this semester, super interesting material. Heavy participation so don't be afraid to speak, the final is a group project also which was okay if you like the people in your group, she makes sure it's fair as well.

Easily the best professor I've had here at Geneseo. She is genuinely passionate about what she's teaching and her lectures are super engaging. There's a lot of reading but I found them super interesting. She's a little bit of a tough grader but there's only a few "hard" assignments. You can tell she cares for all her students.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Look, I love Roth. I've taken Medicine and Morality with her and thats where she shines. But if she's available for 130 don't take it with her. Her expectations for an intro level course are ridiculous, even my philosophy major friends agree. She's a lovely woman and she'll help you in any way she can, it's just way too much for an intro class.

She genuinely makes an effort to connect with students and is very understanding about medical and mental health issues from my experience. Her lectures are open and discussion-based and overall very interesting. Sometimes she assigns a LOT of reading but they're usually very easy to read and make sure you actually read it or you will be lost.

Amanda Roth is such a kind professor who really cares about her students and their overall well being, as well. She is so interesting to listen to; her passion in what she's talking about is refreshing to see, and makes listening to her ideas and questions engaging and thought-provoking.

I left every class with my mind buzzing with ideas. She always presents both sides of an argument and really makes you think about all perspectives. She's very flexible and is there to help her students. She passionate about what she's teaching which engages the class. Her questions are thought provoking and interesting. Her points stick with you.

Prof Roth is an AMAZING person. She is extremely relatable and is really open to talking about things the school does wrong. Granted, she was a tough grader on our essays but I felt like it was for the right reasons (e.g. not connecting to the course). I loved this class!

I really enjoyed this phil 236 class with Roth. Class mainly consists of discussions about articles youre supposed to read. Take notes and the few assignments due throughout the semester wont be too challenging. Not a super difficult grader and is very caring for her students. Accepts late work too as long as you email her with a valid reason.

PROF. ROTH IS A TRUE GEM!!! SHE MAKES LIFE SO MUCH BETTER. def take her!!! YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT. You will never leave the classroom without learning at least 5 new things. SHE SHOULD BE A DISTINGUISHED PROF. OF PHILOSOPHY. that should say it all.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: She is the type of Professor who is will give you the grade you earned. Remember a professor is not there to help you always, at the end of the day they work for the school, not for their students.

Professor roth works hard to makes her course interesting and beneficial. She assigns 2-3 articles or papers for each class and uses them for class discussions. Some of the readings are challenging and boring, but most are enjoyable. Professor roth is also very approachable and accommodating, she even offers a single-use 3 day extension for papers

grade based off of 2 tests, 2 papers, homework and participation. very straightforward class, i would 100% take again. this has been my favorite class at Geneseo so far and i'm not even a philosophy major

Concepts touch upon the 4 major bio ethical principals of philosophy: autonomy, beneficence, justice, & utility. We spend so much time understanding it at the start of course and it all connects back throughout. We spend a lot of time examining many philosopher's POV but she does a great job of dissecting each point for our understanding.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Prof. Roth bring so much structure to her class! Very caring person that breaks down all of the concepts in Philosophy without going to in-depth. Reading is heavy and requires deep understanding of text. Class lecture is 85% of the time. Made us write 3 papers on case studies, just editing one after the other. Has very simple surprise quizzes too.

I thought this class would contain more history and be more interesting than it was. Lack of focus in topics and even on women and gender studies and more on race and disability and other issues. Boring and not worth taking.

So many papers! Also, she is a tough grader. The classroom is very dynamic as she does not stick to one teaching style. I disliked the class, but, I think she's a motivated professor worth taking. Specifically, if you are interested in gender studies.

Huge problem when a prof says you can't use scientific knowledge in Medicine+Morality class. How you're supposed to evaluate medical ethical dilemma's, without utilizing scientific evidence to back an argument, i'll never know, (oh wait, you can't). It's worse when the teacher has zero understanding of basic science. Stay away science majors.

Professor Roth is honestly one of the kindest, most amazing professors I've ever had. She goes over every reading in the class and is always happy to answer questions. She's also very clear and concise about each concept and she always provides clear instructions for every assignment. She is a passionate person with a positive attitude.

Excellent professor! I would definitely recommend taking a class with her if you get the chance. Dynamic and passionate about her field. Usually lectures for about 50-75% of the class, and the rest is class discussion and student participation. Expects a lot, but you will get a lot out of her class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: have to do the reading! takes attendance!

Professor Roth is interesting to listen to. I definitely know much more about women's studies after having taken this class. She does not grade anything except papers and participation, and she is VERY harsh on them. She basically told us she doesn't give out A's. She also doesn't give clear guidelines and docks points for petty things.

Dr. Heap is the best professor I've had at Geneseo! He encourages class participation in small group activities which helped us all grow closer as a class. I truly looked forward to attending class each day because he's hilarious and has the best dad jokes. Please take a class with him if you have the chance, he's amazing!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Lovely professor, RIP to him since he lowkey got fired, but like amazing class, really good guy, abstract algebra is very hard but like its a 300 level math class so that's a given

Prof Heap teaches how I wish every math professor taught: straight to the point, less emphasis on proofs, more emphasis on clear examples. The problem I had was that everything he taught was on the test, and it was all worth 1-2 points or so. It's a fair system, but it's difficult because you really have to prepare for literally everything.

Easily my favorite professor I've ever had. Ask questions when you don't understand something. Study class notes for exams and go to office hours or email him if you are stuck on homework problems. Exams are much easier than homework. Heap is really funny, and he cares a lot about his students even though he pretends he doesn't (he's a Scorpio).

I usually love this professor, but this class changed my opinion. There are certain classes that should not be taught in a flipped classroom style and this is one of them. He tells you you will fail the exams. You are expected to have problems ready to present before material has fully been covered. Take this class with a different professor.

Heap is one of the best professors I have ever had. He cares a lot even though he pretends not to. He is a tough grader and he will push you to your limit but you will learn a lot. His classes are hard but participation is everything and you should definitely go to his office hours. I would take his class again.

Heap is a great person and professor, he is great at keeping students engaged with his humor and at making the material understandable for everyone. His office hours are very helpful. I do think that he could be a little more mindful of his types of humor, he sometimes makes me feel dumb for asking my questions. Other than this, he is really great!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Take him any chance you get especially if you are a physics major since he often teaches all the math classes that are required for that major.

I really liked Heap but he didn't do enough in class examples. Luckily the SI for the course was really good and I felt like I really got the material after her sessions. This class was quite a bit of work but if you put in the time you will really know calculus. Heap is really funny with dry humor so thats a nice bonus.

Best professor I've ever had here at Geneseo. Teaches everything very well and is VERY accessible outside of class. Go to class, do the homework, study, and you will do perfectly in the class. Super funny and makes class fun. I definitely would take any class with him again.

100% would take a class with Heap again. Honestly, one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He's very sarcastic and makes many jokes throughout class, which is not like many of my other math courses. Tests are weighed heavily, but he teaches everything on them and does not throw curve balls at you. TAKE HIM!

I am adding another rating because I meant to say tests ARE fair, and he is such a good professor that he deserves the correction. I'd also like to add that he doesn't require a textbook for his class so you save money and have a great experience. Anyone with the opportunity to take a class with Heap should. You won't regret it.

Heap is an amazing professor. I came in having background in Calc 1, but he would be perfect for someone with no knowledge in Calc. He writes all the notes down on a white board, along with practice questions. Very easy to follow and is glad to help in and out of class. Tests aren't very fair and homework is easy 100. Helpful, kind, and funny.

Absolute best teacher/person I have met at Geneseo. He is so helpful in office hours and is so patient when you don't understand something. His lectures are interesting and his comments are really funny. I wish I could take all my math classes from him. Take his classes any chance you can.

Heap is great guy to be around, but his grading system is pretty harsh. Your grade is based on your test. Homework doesn't count for much. Heap himself is a hilarious sarcastic man, you'll enjoy coming to his class but make sure you study hard. Heap is very straight forward, so don't expect him to be super nice to you if you do something wrong.

Aaron is quite literally the GOAT. As accessible and friendly as he is intelligent and witty. I've taken 4 classes with Aaron (two of which started at 8:30!!) with plans for more in the future. Best math teacher you'll ever have tbh. Also, no textbooks!

Aaron Heap is a gem from Texas. His cowboy boots rock my world. His lectures are clear and he is always available to provide help to his students. You have to work in his class, but if you do, you will see results. 100% recommend.

By far the best math professor I've had. He kept class fun and interesting even for those who are not math fans. The book is optional, which is nice and he is very helpful on homework when you need it. He truly cares about teaching and his students.

Notes are phenomenally organized, and it's very easy to copy them down. Best teacher I've ever had in this respect.   Tests are taken straight from his webwork assignments. Reviewdo-over the hw right before the tests and you'll do just fine!

Best math professor I have ever had. He really cares about his students and is willing to help however he can. Tests are hard but fair. Must put in a lot of effort to do well but he makes it enjoyable. Definitely recommend for any math class.

I took 223, differential equations, and a directed study with him. Best professor ever. He truly cares about his students and wants to make sure you understand. He is also really funny - my favorite is when he has joke test questions worth ten points at the end.  Example: tell me a story/draw a picture

While Heap is a great professor, his teaching style is NOT for everyone. Tests are fair. Overall a good professor, just know rate my professors won't guarantee he'll be good for you. Also, he truly cares about his students.

Had a B going into the final and came out with a C-. Tests are fair but he docks an enormous amount of points for arithmetic errors, which is frustrating due to the fact that you cannot use a calculator on exams. Homeworks weren't terribly difficult.

Heap is a fantastic professor! He explains problems in class really well and is also really good about answering qs that you have. His notes are clear and tests are fair. Homework is online. You can tell he really likes teaching and he's also really funny! I recommend taking any class with him!

The best you can get. He made this class so easy and fun to learn. Didn't use the textbook, only get it if you want to study from it. Homework is online to boost your grade and he responds to questions via email pretty quickly. Great guy, I'd take any class with him.

The other ratings say it all... Heap is a great professor. Very clear notes and extremely helpful.  Never rushed through problems during office hours, even when other students, in much harder classes, were waiting.

Without a doubt, Heap is the best professor in the math dept. He explains everything clearly and he makes sure you are well prepared for tests. He does give a lot of homework, but they help you a lot in preparing for tests. I would recommend any class with Heap.
Excellent professor! He loves working with his students to make sure we understand. He isn't easy and he expects us to work hard, but he helps us to succeed.

Dr. Heap is an excellent professor and probably the best in the math dept. Class is always enjoyable and you learn a lot. There is a lot of homework but doing it definitely helps for the tests. 3 tests and a final all worth 20%. First 3 were easy but the final was a lot harder than expected. You must take at least one class with him as a math major

I think this was the first time Heap had ever taught proofs in Geneseo. His notes are very clear and he helps you out as much as he can during the tests. But I don't think he realizes how much homework he gives the class... we all used to suffer through it because they were sooo long and one would be due each week.

What can you really say about Heap? EVERYONE KNOWS HE'S THE BEST! Seriously, if there is ANY seats opened for his class, TAKE IT! He's extremely helpful, nice, and will help you out as much as you can. Tests were pretty straightforward and the webworks all count as one test so it helps your grade out a lot.

Prof. Heap is one of the best Professors in Geneseo and he's probably the best in the Math department.  He is not a very difficult teacher and WebWorks makes doing HW and studying for tests simpler.  He's a very nice fun guy and his lectures are quite clear.
Heap is a great professor. He uses webwork for homework assignments in this class, which guarantees you a 100 on homework (which is worth a large part of your grade).
He's probably the best professor I've ever had. If you have the opportunity to take any class with him, sign up immediately.

He's a really great guy and one hell of a professor. I took pre-calculus prior to his class, attended every lecture, and didn't have to crack the book more than a few times. He's very willing to help, and his class is structured a easy to follow. Definitely try to get into one of his classes.

Prof. Heap is the Man! He is extremely helpful and approachable. He's got a Math Teacher sense of humor which prevents lessons from getting dull.  Homework is made mandatory by WebWorks and can get difficult at times (especially during sequences and series) but Prof. Heap is always willing to help.

Heap is an awesome professor! I took him for both calc 1 and 2. He is very clear and is extremely helpful. Homework is online so you dont need the book, and his tests are very fair! One of my favorite professors here so far, and I'm not a Math major.

Heap is a good professor for the most part. He's helpful if you ask him after class.  Usually gives extra credit too. I feel like he does a pretty good job of explaining everything. I think he's the best you will get in the math department.

A graduate of Rice University and an extraordinarily gifted professor, Dr. Heap is no doubt overqualified for SUNY Geneseo. Even if you don't care for the material, you'll be impressed by his chalkboard skills. He may be a bit arrogant, but it's justified by his  intelligence and proficiency.

Helpful, intelligent, friendly, dependable, and fast paced. It's a great class but take care not to miss it- sometimes he gives out extra credit on days when few people show up. Homework is done online.
An excellent professor,  can be difficult.  Study.  do not even bother with the book he bases the test off of the homework and lecture (do not skip class)  If you can get into his classes take it

Heap is the man!  One of the best professors I've ever had, which is really saying something at Geneseo.  Take any class you can with him.  If you pay any attention at all, it's almost impossible not to understand and love the subject matter by the time the class is over.
Best EVER. Very clear instruction in class, always helpful outside of class. He makes me want to be a professor. Not to mention he's really cute.

Dr. Heap is one of the most down-to-earth, accessible professors I have had in my four years here at Geneseo.  If you have any questions, he doesn't even have to make himself available, he is there to help you on call.  Words can't possibly describe how much I like this man...as a professor and as a person.

BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD! hes really great at explaining things, suprisingly since he's so young. he writes down everything on the board. there is no reason why you shouldnt understand everything thats going on in the class- he makes it very easy. definitely take him! he wears cowboy boots :)
Heap is awesome. he is extremely good at explaining the material and making it fun too. Take whenever you can.
cool guy.  Class can be difficult, and lots of homework, but he definitely wants you to do well. fun to joke around with, so going to office hours isn't bad at all.

Yo Dr Lamy is chill, He pretty cool most of the time  but I dislike it when he wont give me a fist bump. HE ONLY GIVES ELBOW BUMPS. who in the entire world does that? LIke what. He calls me by my nick name so W.

I had Dr. Lamy as a professor in high school. First and foremost, he is one of those teachers who if you don't call him Dr. Lamy or Sir and call him Mr. Lamy he would ignore you completely. Very mean to students when all they did was try their best.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: The absolutely hardest class that i have ever have I would never want to repeat this class ever.
He is the worst teacher ever doesnt even accept feedback
Easiest class I have taken at SUNY Geneseo.  I wish that I had chosen to be a Spanish major.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Seriously, stay away from Delano Lamy, he isn't clear whatsoever, and has a very snotty attitude. He also is extremely slow at grading papers, and does not review try to help you. He barely ever answers his e-mails, and if he does it's extremely late.
Hes horrible, completely useless and mean. doesnt take feedback very well even when its totally in good faith. AVOID his classes! I unfortunately cant but if you have an option just dont take him...

The class covers the basics which can be difficult. Needed at least an hour of studying/homework per day. Nice guy! Go talk to him in office hours. YES he speaks English as well! (Although class is in SPANISH)

He's a pretty cool dude, goes over things in detail and drills them in. He takes attendance but you would be stupid not to go. If you did well in HS spanish no reason not to take the class. DO YOUR HOMEWORK, its an easy grade that counts for a lot. He isn't very organized but it doesn't really hurt your grade. Also he's very well dressed.
This class was great. I really liked Professor Lamy's personality and the topic was interesting. He's kind of hard, but if you pay attention in class you will be successful.
speaks little english and talks spanish very quick..not helpful.. hard grader..gives little hw but it counts a lot. attendance is mandatory
HE speaks in spanish, so you have to pay attention, and he doesn't have a very high tolerance for people who don't try or pay attention. Put your work in and he'll like you.
hard grader, gives little homework but the homework he gives count a lot for grade
Hard teacher, hard grader. He speaks Spanish throughout and won't clarify anything in English. You must speak fluent Spanish or understand Spanish to do well in this class.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Grade was based on attendance and two papers. He's a tough grader on the papers and since they weigh heavy in grades, there little room for error. He refuses to give advice on drafts so you get one shot at it. It's not an impossible class but I wouldn't take it for as an elective requirement.
Class was only graded by attendance and two papers.

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: He is very confusing during lectures and talks about nothing for 20 mins before going back to the topic. His online lectures make more sense than going to class. The class is only graded on 2 papers and attendance. Have to do the readings for every class leading up to the essay or you will fail. Overall, not an insane amount of work which was good

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: only grades on two papers and grades you based on others' work. if you write a good paper with the correct information you could still get a C because he thought someone did better. not fairly graded at all.

One of the best professors I've had here at Geneseo so far. Very knowledgeable and teaches in a way that makes sense & is interesting. Class is graded by only two papers but if you go to class and put some effort into the papers you will do well, and he's very clear about how the papers should look. Very accommodating & passionate about the subject

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: The class was graded by only two essays. I did not go to class or read anything until I started my paper and I got 90s on both of them. I put a lot of work into them though, they were not easy. The material is boring and the professor tends to go off on tangents but he's a nice guy. he responds to emails and helps a lot.

My favorite professor I've had in my entire time here and it's my Senior Year now. As long as you read the class is easy and he even outlines exactly how the essays should look for you. He tries to make theory fun and succeeds.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Professor McLaughin is a really nice guy but this class had a lot of reading, like at LEAST 40 pages per night. Really nice about extensions though if you ask. You're only graded on discussion posts and 2 papers which are worth 70% of your grade.

Easy a because the study guides are just like the tests. Know those and you can easily get a 100 since its multiple choice and true/false. Attendance is 25% of your grade so show up and youre good. Lectures are dry, long, and a little boring. The remaining portion of your grade is 1 essay and 2 tests. Easy but again hard to sit through

I was confused pretty much the whole class. Class mandatory. I taught myself the majority of the theorists, but Dr. McLaughlin just gets wrapped up in the material thinking we all know what he is talking about. Beware of his second coming comparisons (lol), and his urge to talk about his success a lot. But he's pretty awesome, and VERY nice!

Professor McLaughlin is a true intellect! This class is very hard, but it forces you to become a great writer. He is very kind and wants to help his students. He provides many opportunities for questions and is very helpful during office hours. He even lets assignments be turned in late.

Prof. McLaughlin is honestly a great guy, he may say some things that are blatantly liberal, but he is open minded to an extent. If you go to his office hours and go to class, it should not be hard at all.

The concepts are not necessarily difficult but he's out to fail students and will find any excuse to. He's not a great lecturer, his class is boring, and group work is just another pointless section of his class. His essays aren't assigned until the later half of the semester, but then you don't get feedback in time to improve your work. DON'T TAKE

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Graded by few things', 'So many papers']
comment: Super nice and enthusiastic about the environment. Loves class participation. Attendance is mandatory for a good grade. 3 huge papers to count for final grade no tests. He will give extensions if you ask ahead of time. Take good notes on what he says and use it for the papers. You will do fine. Super sweet man. Take it and just put effort in.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Dr. McLaughlin admits classical soc isn't the most exciting thing first day of class. However, he does his best to keep students interested and sets up class discussions. Attendence (20%), two exams, and two essays. Easy to do well if you pay attention during lectures and take some additional notes as well as read the case studies.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Graded based on attendance (25%), essay 1 (25%), essay 2 (25%), term paper (25%). I went to every class and rarely paid attention after the first few classes. 2-3 articles every night 35-40 pages. I never read them until using them as sources for essay 1 and 2. He gave a final grade hours after handing in an 8 page paper doubt he read it.

Dr. McLaughlin is great! His voice is very monotonous, which can throw you off in the beginning, but he's a cool guy. Exams aren't too hard if you DO THE READINGS and look over the lectures. He's very clear with what he expects from you and even gives study guides. The essays are quite clear as well and he's always willing to help if you need it!

Incredible prof, whose passionate style and life-changing insights into the phil. of classical sociology theory stem from his sexy education. Lectures are tough to grasp bc material is heavy, but his taut lectures and helpfulness after class do help. Tests difficult, but study guides clear. Reading heavy. Two tests, two essays. 93.33 is A.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Class is VERY low energy. But if you do the readings prior to class and prepare it is manageable. Grading is average. Do what he asks and you will do fine. Go to him and ask for feedback and he is more than willing to help. Just be prepared for the second coming prophetic re-telling of the Creation Story of the Bible.
His lectures are a little boring but if you read the mycourses articles and cite a bunch in your papers and write mediocre papers youll do fine

At first I couldn't stand the guy, but once you get past his dry lectures and monotonous voice, he's actually a really good professor.  Extremely clear on what he expects; tests are based on study guides but do have short answer.  Essays are dissertation style, but he will help you through them to achieve what he is truly asking for.  Boring & good

This was my least favorite class. Sitting through his lectures twice a week was painful because he was so boring. He is a nice teacher but is so dull. You have three test a semester but I suggest writing the optional essay instead because it is much easier than the test. Going to his class was so depressing.

Not a hard class but I think he expects a little too much from an intro 100 class. somewhat harsh of a grader on the essays but tests are very easy as long as you study the study sheet he gives which has ALL the info on the test. Attendance doesn't matter all his slides are online and the pop quizzes are extra credit. Pretty boring class though.

Really cool guy. I actually enjoyed going to his class. Lectures are a bit bland, but I mean, it's math. Make sure to work with people, ask him questions and use the textbook for the labs. There are 40 points worth of labs (3 points/lab) and 20 points for 3 exams. I didn't pay attention in class, but studied for the last two exams and got an A.

He is literally the easiest teacher for Soc Stats. The labs he gives is 40% of your grade and they're easy to get 100% considering you can ask him questions while doing them and compare with the whole class. Tests are like the practice tests. I don't pay attention as well as I should and I've missed classes being sick and still obtained an A.

He is a nice professor and tries to communicate clearly yet sometimes how he explains things gets lost in translation. I think for an Intro to Sociology class, it maybe goes too far into depth about the advanced theories and their origins. You really have to pay attention to begin to understand how the things he is saying connect back to sociology.

Its an introductory level class and he makes it extremely boring and you have to put in so much work. He is nice guy but the amount of work you have to do for his class is way overboard and extremely boring. He only grades you on three exams so if you do bad on one of them your grade is screwed. I wish I dropped the class when I had the chance.

This class is way different then expected, and was going to immediately drop it if it wasn't how interesting and intelligent McLaughlin was. I took this class because he's such an AMAZING professor. I learned more in my entire career. Hard if you don't understand but worth it. A plus in my book. Thank you professor.

He's a great guy, but the class is very boring. He gives pop quizzes 3 times a semester, but it's up to 8 extra points on your overall GPA (motivation to attend!). The entire grade is based on tests, but he is a generous grader and an even nicer guy. Also, the books are a boring read. Not the funnest class, but McLaughlin is fine.

McLaughlin is a great professor. He sets a date in which students turn in drafts of their papers. Its not mandatory, but extremely helpful. He will actually look through it and give you feedback. I honestly say I learned in his class, and I can't say that about many professors.

TAKE this professor.  Paul is one of the kindest and most interesting teachers i have ever had. if you actually do his work and are interested in the class the tests are really quite easy. he shows you interesting ways of thinking about the world and allows you to expand on important concepts

DO NOT take a class with him. He makes a simple 100 level class unnecessarily difficult, boring, and frustrating. He forces his opinions on you and argues with his students. He actually aims to piss you off. AVOID AT ALL COSTS! I went to every class and killed myself for a B...trust me, don't take McLaughlin. Go with Wahlstrom, or any other prof.

I've taken two classes with him.  Socl 102 was really interesting.  Tons of reading, 2 tests, 1 paper, and extra credit quizzes.   Socl 335 is boring for the first 2/3 of the course but the end is really interesting.  Tons of reading and writing (4 Papers).  Nice guy but not the easiest professor.

What's with the negative comments? Great professor! Tons of reading but manageable, and very interesting material. Tests aren't bad and one essay. If you actually want to learn something worthwhile, take this class! Very smart, has very good ideas that he's excited to share. Will make you a better person. Maybe.

Flies through power points so you can't write everything down in time. Has questions on things not talked about in class. Out of class essay (required) was graded extremely harshly because I didn't mention his favorite case study. Assigns a lot of reading which is required. Makes his opinion clear and constantly interrupts students
his lectures were so boring the readings were intense, and in the papers he just wanted to hear his own opinions. but always with a smile.

Absolutely the most tedious and mind numbing experience of my life. His irrefutable and self-focused grading policy did not allow much leeway for those who did not agree with his opinion.  Some of the texts were horribly written and almost unbearable to sit through.
I think everyone in my class had an A for Speech! He's such a great guy.

I don't personally like the way he taught Soc 100, but I feel like I'd enjoy him as a teacher in a different setting teaching a different topic. You could easily never go to class and still wind up with an A as long as you do some of the readings and study the review sheet he posts before every exam.

I think that he was a good teacher generally speaking. I'd take this INTD class over again, just makes use you go to him for comments on each of your essays so that you know exactly what he thinks is wrong, and if you do what he says and correct it you'll probably do well in the class. Don't miss more than 2 classes or it drags down your grade.
Tends to shoot down everything you say and assigns dense readings without explaining them well. Plays Devil's Advocate to everything, which gets very irritating.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Celia is great! super passionate about what she does and is hilarious as well. This was her last class that she was teaching before retiring, I'm so glad I got to take a class with her.

The most amazing professor I've ever had in Geneseo. Her Austen class is a MUST. She is so quirky & lovely and makes class so interesting, wonderful, and entertaining. Her heart is made of gold too and she is so sweet and understanding. Very fair and generous grader & will do anything to help, even if busy. I will miss her dearly after graduation.

Celia Easton is an incredible professor. And while this class is not an easy A, it is not terribly difficult to get one if you actually get involved with the class. She is very humorous and kind, and offers real-world applications for the texts we read. If she is offering a class, I would snatch the opportunity!!

An excellent professor! She really knows her stuff and she has a great sense of humor. The class is a bit difficult because of the required material, but she's a fair grader and gives fantastic lectures. If you can take HUMN with her, do it!

Very condescending-if you don't agree with her, you're wrong. Had to read every book carefully and discuss it tirelessly. Useless comments on papers-not much room for creativity in writing. Didn't explain the final exam fully and most of the class came unprepared. Hard exam-made us quote from every book. Stay away if you have a brain or an opinion.
A very tough but fair grader, she is smart and witty and will not be BSed. An excellent professor who knows what she's doing, and more importantly, knows how to teach it.
deep, funny, stimulating, down to earth yet challenging

I graduated from Geneseo in 2001, but wanted to add my comments about Prof. Easton because she's great! She explains everything very clearly, and is a fair grader. If you put the effort in, you will enjoy the class and get a decent grade!

Amazing professor. Delivers a perfect balance of historical perspective and unique ideas. She has a very dry sense of humor which I absolutely fell in love with from the first day of class. Paper topics can involve fair amounts of creative writing and are infinitely more interesting than the essay in place of which I'm writing this review. *sigh*

Celia Easton was an absolutely amazing professor.  She had a wonderful grasp of the subject matter and was a lot more down-to-earth than other professors of her intellectual calabre.  Definitely not an easy A, though.  Then again, few courses at Geneseo are.

She's very challenging, but she makes you want to put forth nothing but your very best. She might be the most brilliant person I have ever met. She's hilarious but doesn't know how funny she actually is, which makes it great.

i dont know what the deal is with you guys but reading is not the end all be all in this class. i think its the difference between an A and a B, unless you dont know how to write at all. bull**** is an art that even easton can appreciate.

Have to read, of course, good class discussions, very interesting and interested.  Personally, I loved her, though I didn't read as much as I should have.  Oh, and she likes people who are involved in class discussions.
She's very helpful and actually interesting to listen to. Theres only so much you can discuss a book and she does it righ to the right level. No over analyzing. Overall a good choice.

she is the only teacher i don't ever block out with daydreams. her lectures are really interesting and she has a great sense of humor if you pay attention. she is very helpful with improving your writing. she's great.

You definately have to read.  She makes fun interesting some times but most of the time its not all that exciting, but not painfully boring.  tests arn't too bad as long as you read.  fair grader on papers.  i'd take her again.

I graduated from Geneseo in 1996, and I still remember Dr. Easton as being the best professor I have ever had.  She is truly wonderful, and knows her stuff inside and out. I would go back to school just to be in her classes again. I highly recommend her!
class is interesting, she's very excited about her job!! interactive, not just lectures, so you really should read for class.
Her lectures are interesting, her tests are pretty easy (if you study), but her papers are killer.  No lie, she is awful at grading them..
she's great
great with senior seminars.  very, very willing to work with students.
She gives great practice tests, and you don't really have to do the reading
Very helpful and knowledgeable. There were only two tests, but her reviews were always fair and she wants you to succeed!

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Went through a ton of material way too fast and is a harsh grader. The exams as well as the cumulative final were weighted so much its almost impossible to pass.
She teaches way to fast and isn't fair with the test at all.

Honestly the best professor I had all semester. She is great when it comes to office hours and just wants you to succeed. Has quizzes every week but they are just to make sure you are progressing. Attendance is mandatory but you can attend online. She is great, love her and her class.

This professor is straight forward and will work with you if you put the work in and participate. If you try you will do fine and this class was really not that bad. Just keep up and don't skip class!
Hated this class. There is 2 exams and they are very heavily weighted. Weekly take home quizzes that barely effect your grade. Very nice just not my favorite. Attendance is a grade.

Birgit is a good professor except she teaches really fast and does some of the math in her head. She does not grade easily but is very understandable about attendance and being on zoom. She doesn't give a lot of work but she gives enough and it is hard.

She does a good job preparing us for calc, it really does feel like a high school environment though. Weekly quizzes are worth a lot and there are only 2 exams and the final. Some extra assignments and handouts here and there. There is a review presentation but it's easy and worth 5% of the overall grade. Free online textbook, use a regular calc.

Highly recommend this class for a Gen ed! Fairly easy and interesting if you enjoy music. Kimball is very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. Course consisted of lectures and CD listening. No homework, just tests and listening quizzes. Study a lot outside of class to do well on the tests and quizzes. Offers a lot of extra credit.

Lectures are very boring, but he's a nice guy and very knowledgeable. He is an easy grader, and the listening quizzes aren't that hard if you study. There's a textbook, but we barely discussed it in class. Attendence is taken sporadically. My only complaint is that the lectures are really boring, and he isn't very organized.
Prof Kimball is super sweet and passionate about what he teaches. You do have to teach yourself some of the material, but the class is overall very interesting.

The workload is super heavy. If you're not a music major and just taking it for outside credits, it's really not an easy A. You have to spend a ton of time memorizing and preparing for the quizzes which are 100% of your grade. Although sweet, he is a very boring lecturer and doesn't really help you learn the content through class.

Professor Kimball is an absolute sweetheart that knows how to play every single instrument in that classroom. If you're looking for a music credit, an easy A, or just something for fun, definitely take this class. You will have to attend a few concerts (I think 5) and there 6 quizzes for the semester. It's a bit of memorization, but the same format

Professor Kimball is easily in my top 3 of favorite professors at Geneseo. He is the absolute sweetest man, and cares deeply for his work. He will have the nicest and in-depth conversations with his students when they want to talk to him. This class and Professor Kimball made me realize how much I loved Music, and missed it from high school.
Professor Kimball might be one of my favorite professors I've ever had at Geneseo. His quizzes aren't bad and he is the nicest man you will ever meet. Very passionate about what he does. Love him.

Although this class was a little difficult, I loved Professor Kimball. He is a very sweet old man, and it is very clear that he loves his job and what he teaches. His class was interesting and I enjoyed talking with him about my family traditions. If you take his class be sure to study for his listening quizzes or you will most definitely fail.

Dr. Kimball is a really nice guy. If you're interested in something he's teaching, take it. He can ramble in his lectures and sometimes you'll have no idea what's going on. Listening quizzes can be tough at first, but they aren't too demanding since he usually picks easy songs. Just listen to the songs he gives you and go to class and you'll pass

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Withdrew after the first quiz because I knew I failed miserably. He talks about nothing important for the first half of his lectures then MIGHT get to something pertinent. You need one book from the bookstore and one from main street. You have to put a lot of effort into memorizing artist names and titles of songs. Really boring class.
He is very sweet and helpful. Quizzes are a bit tough at first, but eventually get the hang of it. Can make do without the textbook.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: James Kimball is a very nice professor. However his class is a lot of work and all of his quizzes require memorization. There are 6 quizzes including the final which isn't cumulative and one paper. You also have to attend at least 5 music related performances throughout the semester but any extra ones you go to will count as extra credit.

Kimball is probably one of the smartest people on this campus. His class is fun and he's a cute grandpa type but sometimes can be boring. He is so talented and demos all the instruments he has. The tests are difficult because you have to memorize about 70ish songs during the year, usually about 15ish per test. Take if you're good with memorization.

He's a cute old man that can play basically every instrument ever but be prepared to study. He gives out study guides so you know exactly what to expect but tests cover a lot of content. Listening quizzes can be tricky but once you get the hang of studying for them you'll be okay. Don't procrastinate reviewing for a test till the night before.

Check mycourses for format of listening quizzes. Tests are all multiple choice and TF, pretty easy. Study for a few hours before quizzestests and should do fine. Don't really need to go to class. Class is more or less just watching youtube videoslistening to him talk.

I love Professor Kimball! He is very passionate about music! He makes the class interesting. He can play an assortment of instruments. He is an ethno-musicologist, which makes him extremely knowledgeable about world music! He plays song clips and videos too. you can earn credit by attending music events. I loved this class! I highly recommend it!

Class is pretty boring because kimball just goes on and on about randoms stuff but you should go because the notes you take are exactly what the quizzes are on. Quizzes are hard so make sure you study and memorize everything. Easy class if you go to class and study.

He is an amazing teacher who is quirky and really funny at times. He's very intelligent and you can tell he really loves his job. I would recommend him to anyone that wanted to take one of his classes. Very sweet guy.

My partner in a group project didn't contribute, I had to do it all by myself and ended up getting a zero for "a lack of communication" and "not following directions" despite the fact that I communicated with my partner best I could, and informed Professor Krumrine of the issue.

Dr. Krumrine is generally nice, but her lectures can be very boring and she gets side tracked. I really struggle with the exams and then the final was very long. Plus your required to complete 4 labs. And a discussion post weakly.
Get good grades on exams and labs. Open book tests

Amazing lady, all her classes she teaches are regimented in the same way so no surprises. She's very understanding only flaw really is that she can be disorganized sometimes. Tests you want to spend a few days studying for and attend class and take notes. Awesome lady

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: She is a lovely person. Her lectures are just her talking. I'd recommend taking notes and recording the lectures. Not much information on the slides. Exams are on her lectures. She lets you use notes for exams, but she might change that. Do not use AI in her class.

Have had her twice so far, thank god I don't have her again. Her lectures are very dense, & the tests are kinda rough. The class average for exams was in the 70s range. Definitely do NOT play games during her lectures, no matter how boring (I know from experience), as there will be things she said during class that will be on the exams. Good luck.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Krumrine has a great class to fulfill WRTG105 credit. If you are interested in anthropology you'll enjoy. Since it is a writing class there are 5 main papers, but gives easy points to get your grade up if writing isn't your thing. Accssesible and gives good feedback, she's very kind and passionate.

Prof. Krumrine is very nice and enjoys educating students on human growth and development.  She gives engaging lectures and relates them to personal experiences and examples.  There is a lot of reading required for this course that are needed for the tests.  The exams contain too much to answer sufficiently in the class period.

It was hard for me to do well with her teaching style as she just lectures everyday. Although class is not mandatory and she does post the slides not all the information is on the slides so you have to go to class and actually listen to her. Exams are open note but so hard to finish in the time slot. A lot of information for a 100 class.

Not much teaching is done over intersession- all prerecorded lectures dated from Covid.  Tests are based off reading and open notes, but too lengthy to complete in time adequately.  Additionally there was a group presentation, which can be difficult to make work over intersession.  I would suggest taking this course in person.

I took this class because I wanted to learn about the history of apes but boy did I regret my decision. Discussion posts were so boring to read and respond to and you had one every week. The tests were impossible to finish in time even though its open note. Labs were also graded harshly. If you are looking for a fun elective, this isn't one.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Test heavy']
comment: Prof. Krumrine is wonderful, this was the perfect intro course! Her class is laid out in a great way and she is so responsive to emails! Her class requires readings and lectures that are 100% necessary to do well in the class, don't skip these! Exams are long, but if you pay attention to readings, lectures and films each week you'll do well!
