cons: very unclear about what she wants when it comes to assignments multiple spelling issues on handouts and tests refuses to compromise (I was told that because I was sick for most of the semester, that my absences, when it came to grading student teaching assignments, wouldn't be held against me...) pros: has brief moments were she seems nice

She is a great human being. But she doesnt give much feedback for tests. She takes forever to grade and grades really hard. Got our midterms back a week before the final. She says a lot of activities are extra credit but in order to get a good grade you have to do them. She is bad about giving much of a heads up before extra required class time.

Professor Salmon is a very outgoing teacher who is very unorganized. She never once brought up our textbook however expects us to read because that is what our midterm and final exam are on. Very disappointed with her as a teacher, expected better.

She is very disorganized. Her office is a mess. She is a nice woman. She talks very fast and often leaves out important details. When given outside of classwork it is almost always in groups and with very unclear grading criteria. Make sure to read the textbook before the midterm and final or you probably won't pass.

Salmon is a bizarre human but really likable. She is very helpful when it comes to field visits but her style of teaching lacks structure. She doesn't teach out of the textbook but will expect you to read it and stay caught up within the chapters. If you need help from her email her, Her grading criteria is also often not clear.

Extremely unorganized professor. She talks about so much in class that has nothing to do with what she will test you on. Gives a lot of extra credit but she grades extremely hard. If you try to talk to her about a grade you will get shut down almost immediately. She is always right and everyone else is always wrong. Stay away from her...

First, her class is so unorganized. Every class, all she ever did was ramble on about pointless stuff and never used the textbook but her impossible exams revolved around it. Also she doesn't breathe when she lectures and will repeat herself 20 times and take a huge loud breath and continue. Expects a lot but is a joke and disappointing professor.
Annoying

I was not a huge fan of Dr. Salmon. She was very unorganized and didn't give feedback in time to edit lesson plans which we had to present in front of a real classroom. Although she had great stories to tell Dr. Salmon did not take into consideration other students ideas. It was either her way or nothing.

Super sweet professor, clearly enjoys education and has experience in classrooms.  Cares about her students, offers lots of extra credit, not a lot of homework.  Clear grading criteria, easy to talk to outside of class, although sometimes disorganized.  Overall good class.

Dr. Salmon is kind of all-over-the-place, but her class really prepares you for teaching. She will straight up tell you if she thinks you are unfit to be a teacher, but it is because she is so passionate and knowledgeable about the field. She is super sweet and caring, and gives a lot of extra credit! Definitely take her if you have the chance.

Professor Salmon is a professor you absolutely should take, for education majors. She is very enlightening and always willing to help you any way she can. Her multiple choice questions are hard BUT she gives you so many extra credit oppurtunities that it would be hard not to do well in her class. Also, she is hilarious and she has awesome lectures!

My opinion may be unpopular, but I wasn't the biggest fan of Salmon. Although I really enjoyed her class and I learned a lot from it, her tests are tough and she seemed to try to talk some students out of continuing in the school of education. Hear my warning, if you take her, you have to show her that teaching is what you really want to do.

Dr. Salmon is a very passionate educator and so sweet! That being said, while I enjoyed going to her classes and learning from her experience as a teacher - THIS CLASS IS NOT EASY. She will not go over the book, yet all of the MC for her exams are based off of it, so READ! And don't skip! If you're willing to work really hard, take this class.

Dr. Salmon is a wonderful professor and person. She explains everything clearly and makes sure you are well prepared for everything. I have enjoyed having class with her and am sad that she doesn't teach anything beyond Block II. Take Salmon if you get the chance, you won't regret it.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! She is very nice and clear about what she wants. She will go out of her way to help her students and is very sincere. She makes classes interesting and engaging and will always put a smile on your face. I would strongly recommend her!! She's great!!
Salmon is one of the best professors in the education department. She makes class interesting and time seemed to fly by. She is very approachable. I would highly recommend her!

She is one of the best teachers in the education department! She knows what she is talking about and I always loved going to her class! Her exams are a little challenging but if you show up to class and read the chapters she assigned, there is no reason you cannot get a good grade!
She is very upbeat and is very willing to help any time you ask!I enjoy her class a lot.I recommend her!
Salmon is such  a sweetheart! You learn  alot from her class and she is willing to go the extra mile for you.

This woman is a show, and it is absolutely fantastic. I could sit and watch her exist for days without getting bored. She is extremely engaging and would do anything for her students. That being said, her office is a trainwreck and she's a bit unorganized. Still, I feel like I'm learning a lot from her.

Anyone who says a bad word about Dr. Salmon has to be a terrible student.  The woman is a saint, she will do anything for anyone.  Not only do you learn a lot from her but she really does care.  She doesn't teach straight out of the book, keeps it interesting but yes the MC on her exams are tough.  Everyone should take at least one class with her!

Very Enthusiastic and a wonderful person in general. Very knowledgeable about special education and is very approachable any time you need her. My downfall were the tests because I am a horrible test taker, and she pulls multiple choice from the textbook that were very specific and not particularly covered in class. Other than that shes great.

Very enthusiastic and passionate about teaching which is great for a prof of future teachers. She knows a lot about teaching and you will learn a lot from her. Sometimes disorganized but she is extremely helpful and wants everyone to succeed.

very enthusiastic! can be a bit confusing because she tends to speed through material. a bit slow at getting grades back, but the class is based on a generous point system. in my opinion, it would be very hard to get anything less than a B. MC on tests are hard, but each question is worth a fraction of a point. lots of room for extra credit!

I think she is wonderful because she loves anyone who shows enthusiam.  I took her once already so i know what she expects, but if you havent had her before, it is hard to get a good grade on any lessonplan, so I advise seeing her in advance because she is particular about certain things, especially objectives.I love her and she makes me smile!

I can't stand this woman!!  She is so particular about what she wants on assignments but doesn't tell you until you've gotten the assignment back.  All we did in class was colored pictures and she gave me a B+.  Which by the way took her all semester to get back to us- work that we finished in september was handed back in december!

Dr. Salmon is a very sweet lady, who genuinly wants to help you. Her course is pretty easy. Although you do not need to do the readings for class, there will be stuff from the book on the midterm, you get a study guide though. Sometimes she moves a little fast, but if you ask her to clearify she most definitly will.

Very boring class - she always does the same thing. You could really learn all the material for this course in a month. For a class with such easy material should be an easy A but Dr. Salmon makes it very hard to get a good grade. Don't take her if you can avoid it.

She is really nice and fun.. if you suck up to her. If you ever have a problem do not go to her as she will use it against you later in the semester. so moral of the story.. suck up and you will be fine
Best teacher ever.
Shes great!  I miss her sooooo much!  I had to drop her class due to another teacher being nasty but i will forever miss Susan Salmon!!

When you go on and take other classes you'll appreciate her.  She teaches you a lot, but it seems boring, pointless, and easy b/c she's so good at it. I initially felt she wa a bad prof. and now wish I had her fro all of my education classes.
Shes actually not an easy professor. Not clear on what she wants. Picky about how you write the reflective paper.
Very easy but a pain in the butt.  Make sure you clarify any questions you have on quiz or test because she deducts points and won't give them back.

I love Dr. Salmon.  We didn't really learn much of anything in her class, but she's an easy grader, and she actually cares about her students.  I had a car accident on my way to a field visit and she called my room as soon as she heard to make sure I was alright.  She actually cares.
Takes off for things she doesn't explain...thinks she is always right
No Comments

This was a pretty pointless class, so it's hard to think too highly of the professor.  We did not learn anything new, we mostly drew picutres and created different works of art. Dr. Salmon is very nice, but is also very passive.

Okay teacher. Kind of annoying to listen to and is very vauge about what she wants. You do the same thing every day in groups which gets a little boring, but at least she is very excited about what she is teaching.
She is an okay teacher. She is very excited about arts & careers but you don't really learn anything.
Wallace is a good guy. Notes are online in advance so you don't need to take them. Always willing to help. Can be a little dry with straight lectures but the exams are reasonable.
If ur willing to do the work and have ANY familiarity with calculus at all, its an easy  A. Always in his office and VERY willing to help when in there. Great prof. Highly recommended!

this class is seriously a joke. i have never been good at math but he explains things really clearly and gives a million examples so you know what to expect on his tests. the tests are basically the same as the study guide too. he can be a little boring, but it's worth it just cause it's so easy.
great, helpful teacher.  loved his classes... a little boring sometimes, but always answers questions and is very thorough.  good guy to take a class with.
THOUGH I AM NOT A MATH PERSON, HE WAS VERY HELPFUL.  HE IS A GREAT GUY AND I BELIEVE HE WAS FAIR.
Great guy, decent teacher.  He seems like he gets a little nervous in class sometimes but he's very helpful and very smart.  Take a class with him.
he is a really nice man, always willing to help you, if you ask questions, he will help you, lots of work, but i guess you have to expect that for a calc class, i would recommend taking his class
HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE.....do I need to say it again!!? Boring, Hard Tests, Does not answer questions correct. BAD BAD TEACHER!
Nice guy whose not intimidating in the least. Eager to answer all questions, even horribly moronic ones. Tests are pretty easy, helps to have done some calculus in high school.
Mad easy course, nice guy. Just take it. I suck and hate math, but am doing fine. He explains things well. Hes a good teacher and makes a course that could suck ass bearable and amusing.

Don't take calculus with him unless you are really smart or have taken it before. What he explains in class has no relevance to homework problems. He doesn't take the time to really material, if you don't understand it. Sweats a lot in class... pretty fun

Ok I don't know what the other raters are on, but he is not easy like they are saying. His classes are incredibly boring, and he loves trick questions. Most things he talks about in class are not on the exam. Overall, NOT GOOD!
Better than most, not as good as some
He is very helpful and his tests are easy.  He enjoys his office hours too much.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Talks so fast, mumbles, hard to understand. Honestly, I'm writing this during class because I'm just so sick of her. She just talks the whole time. It's one of those classes where you count the minutes until you can leave, even if film is your passion. It's painful. She makes it painful. Some people shouldn't be professors.

She spends so much time talking about one topic that we were on the same movie for around two months. You could show up to class maybe twice a month and you wouldn't miss anything. If you don't write exactly how she wants you won't do well and the fact that our only grades were essays made it hard.

I honestly love Okada. She is super chill and clearly loves what she teaches. This is my 2nd time taking her and I really respect her. As long as you do the work asked of you and participate regularly, I don't see why you would have a hard time in her class. She is great!

Jun Okada's teaching style sometimes makes me wonder how she was hired. Taking her for my INTD 105 course was absolute torture. She is very opinionated, and what she thinks is ALWAYS the right answer. While I have not had her for film studies, it's clear that she should stick with that subject instead of trying to teach INTD. Stay away from her.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS', 'Caring']
comment: yes she is opinionated but she knows her stuff. she made this subject so interesting that i'm taking another class w her. if you're not open to different opinions and interpretations, then you'll have a hard time with this class. but i totally respect her. as long as you contribute to discussions and participate, you'll do great

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: I enjoyed this class and she's not as bad as ratings make her seem. She is very opinionated but she's passionate. The class is lecture/discussion heavy with occasional textbook use. 2 essays, midterm, final exam and group presentation. If you go to every class, you will do fine. She's ALWAYS willing to help, it's just up to you

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Jun Okada was disorganized in her lectures and occasionally late showing up for class. However, she does know about film and the material can be enlightening, even inspiring. She's a tough grader on essays, so make sure you meet with her before your paper is due to discuss the content.

Don't. Intro to Film was much harder than it should've been. Only enjoyed a couple of the films we saw, and the essay prompts were very unclear  and challenging. I could never focus on her lectures. The class is very time consuming. She is unacceptably  late to our final exam.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Unorganized, showed up a half hour late for our exam, hard to meet with, hard grader on essays
Jun Okada saved my life, and I am forever grateful.
There is one word for her, and it is terrible. Steer clear!

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Professor Okada is honestly the worst professor at Geneseo. She is so opinionated and if she doesn't agree with you, you are automatically wrong. She is an extremely hard grader. Do not take her class

Jun Okada is a bad teacher. She is rude, judgmental, unprepared for class, un helpful, etc she dismisses students if they not share her views. Her prompts for her papers are not written well, and on top of that she won't grade you on your writing style, its off your substance. The papers were easy though. In any other Intd I'd have an A. Avoid her.
Rude to students that don't share her personal opinion on the subject material

Professor Okada rarely used clarity. She assigned busy work that she would mention in class but then didn't explain specifically what she wanted for the assignment. Several times she emailed the class late Sunday afternoon about a paper to be written or read/film to be watched for Monday's class. In addition, she repeatedly called students stupid.

An unprofessional teacher. Often unprepared for class, says "Um" before starting virtually every sentence. The kind of teacher who makes a mistake and acts like its the classes fault. Overly tough grader on her essays for an intro course. Midterm and final tests are pretty easy and probably the only redeeming quality of this class and teacher.
She picked the most boring movies for us to watch.  There is a lot of reading but if you put an arguement in your essay, then you will do fine in this class.
There are only three essays in this class, but the lectures are boring and she rambles a lot.  The class was not very enjoyable to be involved in.

She doesn't value her students opinions. Picks bad examples for movies. Her lectures are very basic but slightly varied from the textbook which makes for boring reading and boring lectures. She uses a microphone to speak to like 60 kids which is infuriating. Pop quizzes. She has clear favorites and dismisses the rest of her student's opinions.
The most unhelpful professor I have ever had. Highly recommend not taking any of her classes.
Babbles incomprehensibly at the front of the classroom, unable to use a DVD player, self absorbed, takes this class WAY too seriously. It's a boring, deathly class do not take.

She's very rude and doesn't take responsibility when she makes a mistake. Pushy, lectures are boring, and doesn't think anyone else's opinion matters.  Her behavior would be understandable if she had significant prestige, but her resume is not even that impressive. Horrible woman, only knows Asian film.
Tough grader and boring lectures, but a very nice woman who cares about the material and is willing to help. All you have to do is ask.

I loved her personally, however yes she's a seriously hard grader. She's willing to help her students though, and gives second chances on essays. The films are painfully boring, I had to staple my eyes open, so go to class. Not an easy A at all but at least she's friendly and willing to help.

It's a shame that she is the only film professor at geneseo.  I took this Intro to Film Studies for a fine arts requirement but she is an obnoxiously hard grader, very condescending, and often outright rude.

Incredibly Rude, Absolutely awful how rude she is.  Would not take anyone's opinion into account but hers on a daily basis for Film and DID NOT KNOW THE MATERIAL. Honestly not too difficult, but if you get on her bad side, good luck enjoying the class.

She cannot speak well and her lectures are completely pointless. There's two papers, and a midterm. The midterm is solely on information from the textbook and she is not very clear on what she expects from the papers. I went into this class thinking it was an english class and I was disappointed to learn it was actually a class for film majors..

Literally the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are basically reading out of the textbook and directly repeating what her dumb powerpoints say. She chooses boring movies because she just does exactly what the textbook uses as examples. Never directly answers questions. Really dumb. Annoying to listen to. Class is painful to go to.

I don't seem to agree with many of the other comments on here.  While I can see where they might be coming from, I don't think they are very representative of her.  At times can be slightly condescending, but it's rarely uncalled for.

Okada's hard. Her tests are hard, she grades papers hard, but with that being said, it's still not a bad course. She knows what she's talking about and the movies she shows are (with the exception of Battleship Potemkin) enjoyable. Take her if you don't mind doing the work.

Horrible professor. Her lectures are completely pointless and devoid of sense. She is a rude person, a bad teacher, and an overall pessimistic, feminist nut. Going to her office hours is like a trip to the DMV: Extremely long wait and completely rude and offensive when she comes. Do not take this class.

Fairly misunderstood--her classes are for people who want to learn more about film, not those who just want to watch movie and get an easy A. Somewhat moody and not always lucid but between the readings and discussions, you can figure it out. Tests rely heavily on textbooks and discussion so attendance is recommended. Took 3 classes with her total.
Worst professor you could ever get. Makes no sense while she is teaching.
READ THE TEXTBOOK - all questions come from it verbatim. Her lecture is mostly pointless unless you don't read. Film screenings and recitation sessions are important. Very few grades, so be careful.

an okay class, but kind of hard. not really the best teacher, just kind of rambles on about stuff in no logical order. The topic is somewhat interesting though. I think this class would be better given to film majors, unfortnately they dont exist at geneseo... don't take this unless you are REALLY interested in film or it'll just be annoying.

Unfortunately, this class ended with a sour  note. She grades too harshly, and has a knack for creating confusion where confusion does not belong. Could be a decent teacher, but for this class, overall, she wasn't.
She is rude sometimes and doesn't make sense when she speaks.  Her classes are all lecture and she doesn't explain anything very well.  She grades too harshly too!  Stay away!

She ostensibly uses a rubric for grading, but more often than not arbitrarily assigns the average score for each category. She never explicates her ideas and is very condescending. I would avoid this professor!

If you are at all conservative do not take this class.  While I agreed with her views on topics, I often sympathized with students who do not; she zeroed in on such students in class and essentially refused to hear (or accept) their perspectives.  Moreover she cannot simulate class discussion for the life of her.  I would not recommend.

Nice woman, but cannot spit out a clear thought for the life of her. The class is mildy interesting, there are some boring films, but also some more recent interesting ones. Anyway, you don't really have to stay and watch the movies; you're never tested on them. Tests are made up of completely random multiple choices questions all from the book.

This is the worst professor I have ever taken.  She has the communication skills  of a frustrated teenage genius with PMS.  She cannot foster productive group discussion.  And she sits her office hours with her door closed while she talks on the phone about her personal life.  Avoid her.

I think she's very good. She's willing to put in the effort if the student will. If you are a serious academic film student wanting to learn serious film scholarship, this is THE class for you, but if you think Michael Bay is the acme of film making - look elsewhere.

She is really making an effort to make film classics better.  I can tell over the past 2 weeks it's getting easier and more interesting.  I think she was just new and is adapting.  By next semester she'll probably do a great job.

This professor is the most incompetent I have had in three years of school. This is a 200-level course with 13-14 pages of writing, pop-quizzes, shes asks long-winded, incoherent questions, alienates intelligent students in discussions, complains about students, will not respond to emails (even when I had mono), and generally has a poor attitude.

Not a hard class, all you have to do is read the book, but she is a pretty bad speaker. She does try to help you if you talk to her though. I thought the class would be more narratively based, but it is pretty technical, and not nearly as much fun as I thought it would be.

stupid film classics... BE WARNED this is NOT an english class.  Okada geared the class for film majors.  If you dont know anything about film already, DONT take her class.  She studders alot and cant figure out what she wants to say.  I went to talk to her about how I was doing in the class and she simply asked me for a withdraw form!
film classics may not be for people who aren't that interessted in the classics of film history (silent), but overall, its a good intro class on film.
No Comments

Film classics, you think it sounds cool, but it's not.  Unless of course you are into an hour and fourty minutes a week of watching SILENT black and white films.  Then you're probably all about this class.

He is funny and caring. His lectures are not helpful as he goes too fast. He provides notes, but they are confusing as they don't go in the order of his slides. He gives extra credit if you ask. If you have him as a professor, I would keep in mind that you will need to be doing a lot more work outside of class to understand his lectures.

Professor yokoyama is one of the best chemistry professors at Geneseo. His class is somewhat difficult as all the tests are online, but if you put in the effort you should manage to pass with a good grade. He's also a great guy and super hilarious during lecture and lab, so if you are debating taking 118 with Yoko, you will probably be fine.

Struggle fest!Combines analytical physics and 1st year chemistry.Lectures were very equation heavy, lots of graphs with no idea of how to use them. His lectures are pointless; he would just read the equations off the board. The tests were horrible, I didn't finish half the time with only 2 questions with notes.Adds points to scores for his benefit.

Totally recommend this course to satisfy scientific literacy requirement. The course is clearly outlined and he is an extremely caring professor! He wants you to understand the material and succeed overall. Be aware the lab online is an additional 160 dollars for lab material and is time consuming.

Very friendly professor, willing to work with students! Tends to go through lecture material fast but provides a lot of in-class review before quizzes and tests. He also helps by giving you a personalized video message after quizzes to tell you what topics you need to work on. All in all a very nice professor, I would recommend him!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Professor Yoko is a really good person who seems to genuinely care about us and he always makes really good jokes. But, I haven't learned a single thing in his class. He is extremely hard to understand, it's almost like taking chem in a different language. Going to all my SI sessions is how I'm passing. Don't take if you're bad with accents.

I love yoko! He is really funny and he gives personal online recordings for what you need to improve on and what you did good on from the tests. The only complaint I have is sometimes he says the test will be exactly like the practice test when in reality it's not. But maybe that was just for 204, I had yoko last semester too and it was def better

tests are very difficult for gen chem 2 and the homework takes anywhere from 4-10 hours a week. i think he would be better as a professor if the class were in-person; he had trouble adapting to the technology. he does genuinely want his students to do well and is very accessible in class and through email

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']
comment: Class is very difficult in itself, however online is a different story. Professor Yoko tried his best, but struggled keeping up with the technology aspect which is understandable, but also hurt us all in the long run. Excessive amount of homework, great guy though.
Great professor, teaches a tough subject though

I absolutely love class with Dr Yokoyama. He tries his best to make class enjoyable and funny and at 8:30 in the morning that can really help to stay at least somewhat focused. He is very nice and conveys information well. If you put in an ounce of work outside of class it shouldn't be hard to do well. Dropped lowest test and not a lot of homework.

I took it as a bio major, so doing this class with other rough science was a time. I had to withdraw. He is interesting in lectures but there are tests basically every 2/3 weeks and none are dropped. Add on the homeworks and quizzes and it is a LOT of work. You have 50 minutes for tests with multiple choice and short answer, he does give partial.

Kazu is wonderful and so caring. He really wants his students to do well. Each time I would reach out to him with a question he would respond within the hour. Even though I didn't meet him in person because my class was online, he was so sweet. I HIGHLY recommend taking CHEM 104&105 online with him!

Very nice dude. Really wants everyone to do well in his class. May come off as intimidating the first day, but he does everything in his power to make sure everyone gets a good grade. All his lectures are posted online, which makes it easy to teach yourself if you skip class. Pretty thick accent though, hard to understand at times. Kazu rocks.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: His lectures are straight from the textbook and offers no new information he actually leaves information out that is later on the exam. He then puts up slides of math problems for about 2 seconds and says "if you know this your good" and then moves on. I strongly encourage you read the chapter before the lecture and understand it forward and back.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Inspirational']
comment: He was a very good prof, as long as he knew you were trying, he would be likely to give you the benefit of the doubt and round up. He also gave great life advice, such as "some of you may say that you don't check your email, but you'll never get a job, so yeah, do that." Stand up guy and helpful prof, but you have to do the assignments or you fail.

Its what you expect out of a lab, but he just supervises and teaches the pre-lab lecture but the LI's do all the work as far as grading (hope you get a good one). He has a great sense of humor and even the most boring labs always turn into a good time. Love taking Dr. Yoko's classes!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: If you get the pleasure of getting to know Dr. Yoko he is very approachable and personable. He cares about you and wants you to be successful. His office hours are key! The lectures tend to be long and boring but his office hours are one on one and if you come with questions it will be golden! He takes attendance so be there!

5 exams before the final, drops the lowest one. SUPER FAIR &NICE GUY. I went to almost all his office hours &did problems with him that I didnt understand. The book is UNNECESSARY just do the previous exam &sample exam that he provides. He cares about your grade and really knows the material. Excellent prof, wish he taught chem118

I'm very confused where these ratings are coming from. Nothing is explained in this class. He skims through 100+ slides in a single lecture barely scratching the surface of any topic. Compared to this gen bio was ridiculously easy. The curve is so extensive that yes you can get an A, but its pretty much worthless because you don't actually learn.

Yokoyama is one of the best chemistry professors on campus, he is always there to help you. Greatest lab professor and definitely the best for Gen Chem 1. Curves a lot and very easy if you do minimal work you should be able to get a B+ easily. If you care a little, this class is an easy A-. However, it's an easy A regardless of how bright one is.

Although his pre-labs were long, he draws sketches for the procedures so you would't mess up the actual  lab. During Lab, if you needed help, he wasn't hesitant to come to you. Overall, I hated taking it Friday afternoons, but taking Lab with him made it fun!

Yokoyama is the best teacher to take for General Chemistry! All his questions come from last years exam he gives you or the sample exam he gives you. If you do both, your golden! His online quizzes are super easy and all the answers can be found, and he is very helpful at office hours!
I had Dr. Yokoyama for Chemistry Lab and he is one of the nicest Professors and funny as well. Do your work and you will pass. I would take his class again. Really enjoyed his class.

Gives plenty of opportunities to improve grade, such as an extra bonus point for going to office hours, and having 5 tests so that the lowest was dropped. Attendance was taken during class, since it is an 8:30. Notes are fill in, and are a summary, most of the time taken verbatim, from the textbook.

Tests are curved and the lowest is dropped. There are a lot of homework assignments and quizzes that are online. Don't wait until the last minute because it can take awhile. Most answers can be found online. Easiest professor for Chem 116
One of the most genuine professors you will ever meet. His pre-lab lectures are very helpful in preparing you for the lab.
Although his accent may have people tune out quickly, he is there for you if you have any questions during his office hours. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE PRACTICE TESTS!!!!
I was so afraid to take chemistry because of bad experiences in high school. BUT IT LOVE IT. I find myself looking forward to class. AMAZING TEACHER.

Yoko is a little hard to understand because of his accent. Very easy to tune out and not pay attention. Provided a ton of hep during office hours and really cares about students. Test questions are taken directly from sample exam and the final is questions from the tests but with different values.

Yoko is such a great teacher for your first college level chemistry class. Spend time on the online homework and you'll get a good grade. Tests can be tricky, definitely find older versions and DO THE PRACTICE TESTS!

Dr. Yoko is hilarious and a really nice guy. Pay attention in lecture and do the practice tests.  A lot of test questions are straight from the Sample Exam or the online quizzes. Don't leave the quizzes till the last minute - they can take hours if you don't know the material very well. He appreciates if you go to review and sit in the front row.

I highly recommend Prof Yokoyama for Chem 1. He has lots of office hours, holds in-class and out-of-class review sessions (go to the out-of-class ones!), gives at least two sample exams for each test (do these and you will get a good grade!!!), and drops your lowest test. The online quizzes are a bit tricky and an A is set at a 95, which is tough.

He is my favorite teacher at Geneseo. He is the perfect example of what & how a professor should be. Despite the large class size he knows who you are, recognizes & acknowledges hard workers. He is straight forward - No matter what, you definitely have to teach yourself some material, but fear not, because Yoko is the most welcoming person ever.

His class is really easy. I never went to the actually class itself. I just looked up the power point online, and read the textbook. If you do the sample exams, you'll get an A. He also drops your lowest test!

Had to teach myself a lot, his accent was extremely difficult for me, and with only fill in the blank packets, I found it difficult to pay attention and learn anything from him. Most of the learning was done out of my book!

How could anyone dear to give this man less than a 5 for easiness? You will not find an easier teacher in the science department. Generous curves, and lectures are simplified to a 1st grade level. Fantastic, funny professor. Perfect for Chem 1.

Such an amazing chemistry professor!! Really understands what he is talking about.. From time to time he cracks jokes in class. Read textbooks, and understand quizzes and sample exams and you will be fine!! His curves are also very generous!! Best chemistry professor EVER!!
Great Professor, although I hardly went to class I got a B without the textbook. He gives homework which is extreamly helpful and DO THE PRACTICE TEST, test questions mimic these almost exactly!!!!!

The BEST professor I've had at Geneseo. He really does out of his way for his students and actually cares for his students. His accent can be kind of tricky, but he is funny enough that he makes fun of it. As long as you use his lecture slides, it should be a pretty easy class -- plus, he curves and drops lowest exam! He's literally the best.

I could never understand a word that came out of Yokoyama's mouth. His notes/ lectures are easy enough to understand, but actually reading the book was extremely helpful.  As long as you have a good grip on the material his tests won't be too difficult.  Homework and quizzes are online and are easy.

Chemistry is not an easy class and does require lots of self teaching. Yoko does not really do many example problems in class, however, tests are pretty straight forward, and often questions are directly off of sample exams. Do the work and you will get an A, slack and you won't.

I recommend him to anyone! Has good slides and great notes!He gives a lot of homework quizzes and 5 tests but all give you more opportunities to improve grade. Tests are multiple choice later on and also the final.Got an A-, originally thinking I would fail. Also don't be afraid of office hrs. Hes very nice. He also gives practice tests for exams!

Yoko is a really nice & funny person but not very personable in his "100" classes. If you try really hard, you'll probably get him to know you. His powerpoints and notes are very clear but you MUST read. That is the best way to make it through his exams. He goes faster than the other Chem. classes Overall, not a bad choice & accent is not that bad.

Great professor!! highly recommended. very helpful during office hours, unlike most professors at geneseo. highly knowledgeable, clear notes. accent is not a big deal, people just use that as an excuse! take his class! it's awesome.

I love Yoko! He is one the BEST and most helpful professors. He posts hints for the homework assignments and will help you complete them during office hours. He tells you almost exactly what is on the exam. He is very generous with curving and since homework is worth 40% of the grade, it is impossible to get anything less than a B+. TAKE HIM.
Not a bad professor. Had clear powerpoints, and told you what you needed to know for tests. Couldnt understand him unless you really paid attention. Nice guy a pretty good professor.
He is the coolest guy ever! His teaching was really fun and easy. The way he grade was fair. If you don't understand something, hes always welcome for his office hours.
he's a really nice professor. he's helpful and his powerpoints are clear. he tells you what to study. probably the best professor i've had.

Seriously, the best professor i've had yet. He goes above and beyond to help you understand the material. If you attend class, and pay attention, you'll do fine. If you don't understand something, he's very welcoming during office hours and will help you until you know the material by heart.

He's one to avoid! Really bad at teaching and his tests are almost always harder than material covered in the textbook. Even studying the practice questions doesn't help much. Also tries to embarrass and turn students against each other.

I had him for the chem103 lab.  the lecture sucks, but the lab is pretty easy.  Kazu is funny and approachable but his thick accent sometimes makes him slightly incomprehensible.  The labs are pretty easy to get 100's on but I don't feel like I'm retaining too much of the information so the final might be bad news. He's nice, the lab part is easy.

Chemistry is an interesting subject, but this class was boring. I often found it impossible to understand what he was saying - he has a thick accent. I didn't think his powerpoints (used every class) were very good either. Studying the book is the easiest way to learn the material. I skipped class a lot
He's a very funny guy, and very nice. If chem isn't your strongest subject, he still makes it manageable and somewhat enjoyable.

Kazu is a great professor. The online homework sucks, but he will help you immensely with it if you ever need help. The tests are hard but as long as you do the sample exam and and study it it's not all bad. The online quizzes(the second one is brutal) are not bad either. Go to office hours and he'll start to really like you :)

Not one of my preferred instructors.  Near incomprehensible speech and a riduculous amount of homework made the class unpleasent.  The homework is almost impossibe at times and it takes at least 15+hours a week.  Tests are ridiculous and he gives multiple formulas we do not use. Not a bad proffesor, just unsuited for a freshman class.
He puts random pictures in slideshows and brings simple toys to demonstrate chemistry concepts.
He rocks!! He is funny, interesting, and approachable. He knows what he is talking about, and his sense of humor gets the class going. I highly recommend his class.

he is a VERY nice guy and is very understandable and funny, however i found it practically impossible to keep up with his MasteringChemistry assignments which took me on average a minimum of 10 hours each week. it is very easy to get him to postpone due dates, however that doesnt always help.

he is a really sweet guy, but his accent makes it impossible to pay attention to him, especially at 8:30 in the morning. and the online homework is SO annoying...so much, i feel like you would have to sit and only do that to get it completed.

He wasn't necessarily the greatest professor in my opinion but I found the online homework and the lectures pretty difficult to understand at times. I just didn't like the fact that everything was technology-based. I do better when I'm physically writing notes, not when I'm reading them. He's funny and very approachable.

very nice guy, knows his stuff but doesn't necessarily explain it the best, OWLs are a pain but it's part of the course so you deal with it, his tests have multiple choice exactly the same as the practice tests, he gives out bonus points all the time and will postpone due dates very easily with enough persuasion
greaast

This guy is amazing. I loved his class!! He's an all around amazing guy, but get used to him saying "extra credit"-9 times out of 10, he's joking around. One thing that sucks are the OWLs-they're tedious

This class was a joke.  Yoko is a nice guy.  80 % of every test was identical to the 7 or 8 problems we had for homework throughout the entire 1/4 of the semester!  I think our class average is above a 90.  Easiest 300 level chem class I could ever imagine
Two Words.  He rocks.

He's a cool, nice, and decent professor. My main complaint is that I feel it was too easy for some people to get an A in the class. He curves up A LOT, gives A LOT of extra credit, and then curves everything else on top of that. The only other complaint I have is that he's a bit unclear at times because of his accent, but it rarely affects hisclass

The class is hard but Yoko curves well. (scaled curve)If you hate the subject, you can't possibly sit through it. I love chem and math, so naturally I took this course. If youre one of the many bio majors that want pchem for the chem minor (which isn't of much value, transcript wise), take the baby pchem course.
Great professor. Easy A if you do everything that he asks, go to review sessions, and do the OWL homeworks. Definitely take his class.
his class is easy and he's willing to give you high grades. and he's so cute!
He nice and he's pretty entertaining.  Just go to review sessions for the tests and study and you'll do fine.

Yo this dude rocks. He says if your willing to try, he will pass you. My friend was getting 20's on his tests, and he still passed with a C. If you try, he will hook you up. Not to mention, he is a very qwerky and funny man. Take him.
Dr. Yokoyama is the best! We love him! He expects you to work hard, but it's worth it!

I loved Dr. Yokoyama! He was hilarious and made class very interesting. His tests are hard, but he gives a lot of make-ups.  He also gives you a second chance for all hw assignments. Definitely recomend him!
Great teacher.  Best notes ever.

Yoko's the man!! Tries hard to help his students even though is his tests are impossible! If you put a good amount of effort into the course he will know and he will make sure you pass despite your grades! True, he may be difficult to understand initially, but you eventually learn to understand him.

his class is rediculusly hard, when you go for help, you dont get very far due to the language barrier... Very nice professor, not a fan of chemistry myself... He's difficult to deal with, but id give him a 4.5/5 for personality, hes a funny guy.
Dr. Yokoyama is the cutest man alive!!  I love him and his class!!  He exams were very hard, but he was very easy to get along with and get points back on exams!
great guy, fair, funny, sometimes hard to understand

He is a great professor. Hard to understand at first, but you get used to his accent. He also is pretty funny sometimes and tries to know students by name. He gives a lot of resources to prepare you for exams and quizzes.
No Comments
Kazu's a cutie!  We love him!  Although we could've gotten more out of p. chem, for a second year prof, he's A+!

Dr. Gee's class is very straightforward. Review the powerpoints and pay attention to readings and you will do well on the test. RINs are not hard either, just make sure you pick the right type of article. Check with her during office hours if you have questions. She has her sick days and may change the syllabus but Amy Gee is a great professor.

no extra credit, disorganized and changes due dates last minute, sometimes difficult to get into contact with (travels frequently), cancels class a lot. Overall this class was far too disorganized for my liking. Does not give clear rubric for certain assignments & grades harshly on RIN. Exams fairly easy.

Her lectures are word for word from the book, you don't really need to read/buy it unless you really want to. Tests are very fair & easy with a short answer section. Only have to write 2 one page papers that she gives a rubric & an example paper so they're easy an 20/20. Attendance is mandatory but she makes class interesting.

Dr. Gee was alright. She was pretty disorganized and often had to correct herself, because she told us the wrong information previously. My recommendation is just to read the textbook and PowerPoints and go to class for the participation. There were 3 tests that were pretty reasonable and 2-one page papers. If you read carefully, you will be fine

Dr. Gee is a decent professor. She wasn't the best with communicating outside of class and was a bit disorganized which made it challenging sometimes. The content was interesting and relevant, but tests were challenging. 2 papers and 3 tests. Came off being strict and organized but ended up changing assignment due-dates a few times last minute.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Amy Gee is clearly passionate about what she teaches, although she did travel frequently for research, she tried to stay on top of things as much as she could. This class was only graded on 5 tests, all with multiple choice and some short answer. The tests were fairly easy but she grades the short answer strictly.

She's passionate about her topic, but her lectures don't really teach you anything and most of the test material comes from the textbook. The class was very disorganized and chaotic and felt more like a high school class than a college one. An easy A if you read the textbook before exams, but overall not a pleasant experience.

Amy was an absolute pleasure to have, she made child development very interesting and made you think a lot back on your own childhood. She was very straightforward about what she expected and was very approachable if you still didn't understand. Definitely read the textbook or else you'll be pretty screwed. Just read and pay attention in class.

Dr. Gee is a wonderful professor! Her lectures are great and her stories are charming. Her tests are fair, but require a lot of studying and preparation. She is very approachable for asking questions, going over exams, etc. Loved Dr. Gee! Would absolutely take a class with her again.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Prof Gee was easily one of the best professors I have ever had. She made child development super interesting but also very easy to understand. She shows a lot of good supplemental videos during class and her study guides are very helpful. As long as you go to class and read the text book you should have no problem getting an A in this class.

Very confused why this professor has awful reviews due to the fact that I had a great experience with him as my professor. Great professor! His lectors were great and very interesting! He gives out a lot of homework but it's very beneficial for the exams! He is the reason I got an A. If I could take him again I would!

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: He gives out a lot of work. his lectures are boring and hard to understand. His exams are hard . I would not take him again. made me hate history way more than already did.
wonderful professor.

he stutters...a lot...he doens't teach anything...he doesn't help you when you ask him...and he goes off on tangents of his trips...maybe if you were a good teaher i would actually care where you've been...but i don't...he ripped me apart for saying that it was mean to bind womens feet...HELLO!...it WAS!...he should go to china and never come back

Nice guy; easy to talk to him.  Very knowledgable in his field and explains everything you read about. Sometimes he may explain so much that he can get off on a tangent, but loves to teach and wants  students to understand topic.  Encourages class discussion.  Midterm a bit difficult, but fair grader.  Fair grader on papers.

Dziwenka is a great guy. He puts all of his elcture notes online and is very VERY helpful with any questions. He is the easiest grader ive had in any history class ive taken at Geneseo! do your work, and its an easy class to do well in
don't expect to learn anything from his lectures but the class is easy if you do the reading

So so so boring.  Very hard grader.  Tests are horrible because you have to study for hours and really know your stuff because you can't understand him when he's teaching.  Obviously he goes over the no attendance policy too because he takes attendance and if you miss you have to write a paper.

Very Boring.  Listening to him at 8:30 was a chore, but he takes attendance so you have to go to class.  Expects you to become best friends with your group. Tests are okay but because its so hard to pay attention you have to study for them.  Avoid him if possible.
He assigns a term paper over Thanksgiving break...which is mean.
No Comments

I was in his first class ever taught at Geneseo.  The class is as dry as a popcorn fart.  He is a pretty easy grader but it is very difficult to learn anything. This is a writing intensive class.  Good luck

They act like we don't have other classes and have a lot of quizzes. The quizzes used to be due like the day before their class and before we covered the material (this is ok because you can use the textbook). The only thing I liked in the class were some of my friends :)

grading criteria is unclear. they dont know what they are teaching. cannot handle different opinions. the list goes on. this is an intro level class and they act like you dont have other classes. i pray for anyone that has to take them.

They are very kind, but they don't do well when other people have opinions that differ from their own, as they are very, very woke. In the middle of class, they would make things up and wouldn't know how to respond, and are weirdly possessive of their slides and won't share them with anyone. Attendance is required, and they won't accept any excuse.

I literally watch this professor make up stuff on the spot.They are very kind but awful at teaching the material. It is a very easy class.Does not respond well to people with different opinions from them. They claim attendance is mandatory but then reads right off of the slides that they refuse to post. Doing way too much for an intro level class.

I like Genevieve but they are not particularly organized or responsive outside of class. This class is pretty easy and every quiz is open notes, but super textbook heavy. Lots of kids do not participate in class which caused a lot of awkward silence but overall it was okay.

I want to root for them but I don't like how they teach. Everything feels jumbled, they compare us a lot to their past Indiana class, doesn't take feedback well, not responsive out of class, pushes people to speak, mandates attendance but doesn't come to class if speakers come in, and I didn't learn a lot. I had high hopes for them and the class :(

While they are a nice person, this class sucked. Assignments and papers takes weeks if not months to get graded. Attendance is mandatory, and the majority of the time all you do is group work. The amount of articles and videos you do every week for one weekly quiz is ridiculous. Notes aren't uploaded so if you miss a class you wont have them.

This professor is so unbelievably lazy. No assignments are graded until the end of the semester. Attendance is required even though you learn absolutely nothing in class. They do group activities every single class to avoid teaching... The only hard thing about this class i having to sit through it. Prof is nice though, just sucks at their job.
not good at actually teaching any material

There was an unclear grading criteria and inaccessible by emails(only got my emails answered about half of the time).The structure of the class was a bit too strict, the final presentation was supposed to be 5-8 minutes with a 3 minute Q&A which seems like a bit too much for a 100 but it ended up getting turned into an pre recorded presentation.

This class was extremely hard for no reason. His tests were nothing like what he covered in class. He couldn't explain anything during class, and the class was painful to sit through. The highest anyone got on a test was a high 80.

Accent is strong, personally it was difficult to understand him. He wouldn't understand the questions I was asking him. The class was straight from the textbook. If you don't understand the textbook, good luck in the class. A lot of homework that was not planned properly so you would be stuck doing  100 Mymathlab questions before exam.
Very difficult class. Lectures were very difficult to follow

Professor Ludwig is new. He is very enthusiastic about this class. His lectures are a little long, but easy to follow. You do not always need to do the readings to understand his lectures, but you should do most of them. He is very understanding. You have to work to get an A, but it is easy if you try your best. Definitely take a class with him!

The sweetest professor ever. He is a little clumsy and awkward, but super nice and tries to be as organized as he can. It was his first time teaching at Geneseo this semester, but he did an amazing job. He values participation in class discussions, so definitely participate!! Does everything he can to help all his students.

Professor Ludwig first of all is just a great guy.  My class topic was intellectual history and he does a great job of sharing his opinions but always wants to hear from the class. Participate in class discussions and you'll succeed.  I highly recommend him unless you despise reading.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: I actually had her at St. John Fisher. Nice but young. Tough grader for sure. Writing is not my forte so maybe it's just me but I didn't enjoy her class as much as I thought I would.

INTD 105 Viruses- I am a science major and was never good at writing/English. She made the class based on many different assignments so that not being the best paper writer did not kill your grade. She was open to feedback from the class and very willing to meet/edit papers/help you. She wants you to do well. Young, caring and personable.

Showing up to class with all the readings completed is a must. Papers may seem difficult at times but prof. Betts is extremely helpful in office hours. If you put in the time and effort she will help you succeed. Honestly one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. Would highly recommend.

If youre looking to have her as a professor for an INTD course find someone else. She took over a month to grade an essay and made last minute homeworks that took hours to complete. I went to her for help, she made a thesis with me and then when I submitted the paper told me my thesis was took weak. Shes overall kind in class but expects too much

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Her 100 level classes are taught like a higher level class. Her grading is a little harsh for an entry level class.

Professor Betts is very relatable and generally knows what she's talking about. She is very young, in her mid-twenties, which honestly threw me off at first. The class is heavily discussion-based, and you WILL NOT PASS if you do not participate in these discussions! Also, she grades essays very unforgivingly, but may sometimes let you do revisions

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: This class seems like it is going to be an easy A, as a senior I just wanted to boost my GPA. Papers were graded way too harshly and didn't make sense. Don't take this class unless you're an absolutely amazing writer. Class itself isn't that difficult, but doesn't seem like she wants you to succeed. Way too difficult.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: This was an enjoyable 100 level English class. Rachel gave good feedback on the writing that we did get back although sometimes it seemed as though she did not read some of the reading she assigned us herself. Overall though it wasnt a painful experience and I would take a class with her again.
Great.
LOVE her, take.

This class was cross cultural and I highly recommend. Not only was the content interesting she made it so easy to understand. The content is a lot with only 2 exams but she makes study guides for the exams which made it a lot easier to study. She also does in class activities which makes it easier to grasp the concepts that are being discussed.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Test heavy']
comment: If you are not an extremely left winged opinionated person, she is going to be a harsh grader towards you. She assigns countless mini papers pretty much every week, sometimes two a week, and she docked me so many points over the semester because she didn't agree with my opinion on a matter.

She posts all her slideshows, has activities almost every week so get the books she tells you to, you'll need them for sure. Very amazing teacher though, she is so nice and so respectful, had a midterm and final but those were our only two tests, also had a writing assignment but other than that the workload was very doable.

DO NOT TAKE! She called me dumb because I failed the midterm and then said theres nothing I can do to get my grade up. So unhelpful when you need help, lots of reading, long study guide that doesn't help with the actual test.

Super great class to take over the summer, she understands that students have their own things going on like work and only has work due MWF, no weekend, also lenient abt late work. I'm sure she'd be amazing in person as well. Also gave great feedback on everything submitted. i cant say enough good things abt professor Katz!! Lovely person

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Very sweet, not much else to say I thought this class was relatively easy, attendance is not mandatory at all. The class is not what you'd expect though in terms of content so just beware.

Katz is amazing. I took her for Couples and I learned so much. The tests are pretty easy/fair IF you do the review sheets which you need the books to do. They are life savers. I struggled a lot with the final paper and discussed it with her and she helped me find a topic that I really liked and sources. She is so helpful and kind. 100% recommend!

I loved this class with Dr. Katz, she was so kind and caring. I really enjoyed her class. She posts all lecture slides online in case you can't make it. Would recommend going on the days where you do the journal activities in class because it's free points for the tests! Overall such a fun and useful class, and it wasn't difficult.
She definitely cares about her students and works to help everyone achieve the best grade possible
Shes the best. Cares about every single one of her students in such a selfless way. The class is fun and interesting and definitely easy but still gets you thinking. No complaints

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: I love Dr. Katz. Lectures are optional but they're really good so I recommend going. Class grade is based on discussion board assignments and two tests that are on lecture and textbook. Overall really loved this class and Dr. Katz is an amazing professor. Definitely a favorite.

DR. Katz is an absolute angel. The class was optional, but still go because she makes them interesting, and she's so nice to talk to! There were 4 tests and then about two activities each week, and you have to read the book, but it's actually pretty interesting. I definitely would recommend this class or Dr. Katx for a professor in general!!

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Dr. Katz is my absolute favorite. I had her this past fall for 452 and you would be crazy not to take take her. She provides in depth feedback on rough drafts for the papers (like 3 pages handwritten suggestions), and works with you until you get the material. She wants you to be successful and she's in your corner 100% of the way. Sweetest person!

Dr. Katz is one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She is a wonderful person and she gives great lectures. Her feedback on papers is very helpful as well. Take a class with her; I highly doubt you'll regret it.

Dr. Katz is really the light of the psychology department. She has such a great heart and a caring soul. Her lectures are ALWAYS interesting and she prepares well for them. The readings are long but usually amazing and you must read for the daily quizzes (easy if you read!). Her tests are specific but if you participate in class they're manageable!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Katz is a great professor and is clearly passionate about what she does. This class required a lot of reading and the tests were very specific, but she's a very forgiving grader.

She is incredibly entertaining especially with a topic like Human Sexual Behavior.  The readings can get lengthy but if you put the time into them, they can be incredibly interesting.  She also goes over them in class.  She really wants people to do well and like her class so she gives study guides which are helpful but her tests are extremely hard

I took this class online over the first six-weeks of summer 2015.  I like that Dr. Katz took the time to meet with her online students before the summer began.  I do not see her as a "bully" at all (as it states in the post following this one, however, my only interaction with her was once before the summer began and by email.
I know Dr. Katz gets rave reviews, but I found her passive-aggressive.  As the semester progressed, she essentially tried to bully me out of the class.  Very rude and unprofessional.

Katz has a passion for Clinical Psyc, and you can see that in each lecture. This class would have been an easy A if I was good at time management and test preparation. Her study guides are titanic! Despite that, she is super nice, helpful, and understanding.  I would take 352 with her if I could. One of the best in the Psyc department at Genny.

Daily quizzes mean you have to do the reading and come to class. Quizzes range from easy to impossible. Makes an hour long class go by in seconds. Clear expectations for papers. Tough tests, similar to how tough some of the quizzes can be. Great lecturer, really funny and nice outside of class.

She appears fine, funny and helpful unless...she doesn't like you. I was lucky and did very well but in my opinion, those she doesn't like will receive subtle jabs and nasty, pointed comments. You know the kind, where no matter what you say and how you say it they will find a way to criticize. Better hope she likes you - or else!

This prob. won't mean much along w/ so many great comments, but she's not as great as she seems. Comes off as funny & approachable. Usually she is. But in class she shows her personal biases, even if they offend students. Not going into details, but I feel uncomfortable around her now, as she literally criticized EVERY ASPECT of who I am in class.

absolutely amazing and energetic. Has great and relevant stories from the days she use to do therapy. Excited and interested in the subject. Class is easy, take notes fill out the study guide and you will be fine
Favorite Professor so far. Hard to understand where anyone can find negative things to say about her.  She will challenge you, but will help you get the grade you want. I highly recommend her to all.

I couldn't have asked for a better professor for my 352.  Dr. Katz is an intelligent, passionate and extremely fair person.  She really wants everyone to do well.  Come to class and DON'T PROCRASTINATE and you will do well and learn a lot!

The class is very difficult but Dr. Katz is extremely helpful. I suggest getting any questions clarified in the beginning so that you can keep up with learning SPSS. She responds to emails but for papers I also recommend going to office hours or making an appointment.

I've had Dr. Katz for 2 classes, and she's one of my favorite professors.  I've never met a professor who cares so much about her students, not just academically, but in their lives, careers, and futures.  I can't describe how much extra help and guidance I have received from her.  She's also a great teacher... funny and engaging.
Has gone out of her way to help me, esp in  planning for after graduation. She really is caring, but also has high expectations for students.
kind of passive aggressive, seems really nice, but wasn't very clear with expectations and grading.  Disappointed because of all the good things I'd heard about her.

I have never met a more caring prof.! She's an awesome teacher too. You never want to miss class because you are always doing something fun. The tests are difficult and you need to study but it is easy to do well in the class.

Dr. Katz is very funny and really nice. You'll have a lot to study for, but go to classs and take notes. Understand the material and memorize all your notes before the exams. The class papers are not too bad either. Overall, she's good.

She is a great and funny teacher, just finished her Doctoral and is always there for you if you need help with anything.
No Comments
She's wonderful! Funny, nice, and constantly trying to recruit for the Anthropology Dept.  And if you ask, she'll do the howler monkey scream for you! She's a blast!
she is excellent.  She is very responsive to steudents, and cooperative as well.  She is cool too!
she's amazing! I just sit there laughing at her comments on fecal matter. She really is inspirering. I wish every teacher had so much passion!
Really nice, from buffalo to boot (woo hoo) andhas a sense of humor too!!
i have never done so little work in a class and still passed - also, she's cute

Took Geog 102: Human Geography with him, 8am two days a week. He is a sweet guy, you can tell he cares. But his voice is the most monotone, dry, quiet thing in the world. Lectures are very very boring and he is not engaging what-so-ever. I could not resist doing crossword puzzles instead of paying attention to him.

Hes a super sweet guy who cares about his students but the lectures are so boring. I didnt learn much in the class other than things I already knew. There wasnt much structure to the final paper as well. Overall, its an easy A but tedious course.

Professor Favro is a nice guy, and this is his first semester teaching at SUNY Geneseo. However, he does not make his classes interesting enough. The information during lectures is very vague. He takes attendance each class, but it is so difficult to not do other work during class, or even look up on google more info about lecture topics.

Had Dr. Freeman for gen II lab. I see he has a lot of positive reviews so I know I may be the minority here but everyone in my lab section also got around the same grade as me. Weekly quizzes are VERY challenging. You absolutely need to attend his office hours to do well on the labs and quizzes.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Avoid if possible. Makes lab more difficult than it needs to be for a 1 credit course.

I had him for 2 labs not lectures. He is a nice man and allows make-up work if a lab is missed or done wrong but he is a harsh grader considering general physics is an entry-level 100-level course. the quizzes we have every week will sometimes be easy but then other weeks be hard and about things we haven't covered in lab or lecture.
Most of his labs are taught by an LI, so as long as you have a good one, you are all set. My LI was a kind grader, so it made this lab easier overall.

Dr. Freeman is a good lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory but being in class helps. Videos are posted for every topic throughout the semester.

Homework assignments are challenging. Office hours are helpful. Exams are a majority of your grade, and they are challenging. 

He wants every student to succeed, but you definitely have to work hard!

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Tests make up the majority of your grade and even then they're extremely difficult. The homework is 20+ questions each and extremely difficult. Lectures are useless, you learn "special cases" that aren't used outside of maybe one question on the exam or homework. The class is more memorizing 20+ equations than anything else.

This was the worst class I've ever taken. What you learn from lecture is useless for trying to complete homework or do exams. Homework takes forever to do and is excessively hard. Has notes online that are again basically useless. Exam average the entire semester has been between a 40-55. Wont give back exams, or let you look at them. Do not take.

Dr. Freeman is ok for lab. He'll hand you almost all of the work/answers needed, but will not hesitate to knock points off for anything he finds even the slightest difference in. He'll grade your abstracts like he's being paid to find errors or things he doesn't like. Otherwise, he was helpful and you could tell he had a passion for physics.

This class was one of the hardest courses I have ever taken. Freeman not only makes this class possible to understand, he makes it fun and (relatively) straightforward. He gives amazing lectures and will help you completely understand every physics problem in office hours or if he's available. He cares so much about his students and it shows.
Alright Dr. Freeman!

This was the hardest class I've ever taken. There were times where I couldn't even fathom how to do a question. That being said, going into office hours really helps. He will show you how to do even the hardest questions step by step and in an intuitive way. Looking back after the class, I think it caused the most growth I've had during college.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: If you go to lecture he gives you a solid basis of the material, which helps with hw sets. The hw sets take a lot of time/are hard, but if you review them they help a lot for the test. Use the practice problem set to study too. This class starts out easy and gets really hard quickly. He has weekly quizzes so write clear work on the hws to do well.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Dr. Freeman is such a great teacher! He is always willing to help outside of class and has literally sat in office hours with me for hours even outside his office hours just so I would understand the material! You have to put in a lot of time into the class but that is just because the material is hard! Totally would recommend!
Dr. Freeman's classical was one the best classes I have taken at Geneseo. It was at 8:30 but getting out of bed was easy when I knew I was on my way to his classes.
Excellent! His excitement for physics is put into his lectures and activities.

This is an extremely difficult class and even though Freeman is great, I found it incredibly challenging. However, Freeman is very good at teaching and explaining concepts as well as helping with hwk problems. Quizzes and tests were very hard and you need to put an insane amount of time into this class to get a good grade. His demos were awesome!
A tough course, but frankly, all physics courses are very difficult.  He is extremely helpful in explaining concepts both in and out of class.

Freeman is an AMAZING professor for physics. Its a challenging class, but he goes through all of the homework step by step so going to his office hours helps ALOT! Overall he is really clear and knowledgeable. He also loves to talk about baseball. One of the best physics teachers I've had.

The man is a genius.  He loves physics almost as much as he loves having students come to office hours. He generally cares about his students and makes a point of learning everyone's name. However, his class is hard and takes a lot of effort.

His teaching style is the same as other teachers who just read off power points.  The difference is that there's no powerpoint to look at or download later.  Has enthusiasm for the subject, but he's draining mine.

The fact that I really like Freeman despite my immense hatred for physics says a lot for him. He is entertaining and enthusiastic and keeps class alive with demonstrations. But - physics is miserable. Prepare to work.

Dr. Freeman really loves what he teaches. One of my favorite professors this semester. Midterm exams were online. 75% were all or nothing credit-wise and that absolutely destroyed my grade. Homework is online and can be challenging even for Majors like myself. Overall great teacher though.
The class itself is fine, but Webassign killed my interest in Physics.  This is coming from a Physics MAJOR who had a great deal of interest before taking the course.

This teacher is really excited about physics.  to demonstrate the concepts he always has demonstrations and computer simulations.  once you learn his method of solving problems, its very hard to mess up even complicated problems, because his methods are very universal.  I'm and physics major and so far he's my favorite teacher I've had here
He's a good teacher and really attempts to explain everything. Course material is difficult as are tests. Plan on going to class everyday and office hours for help. Extremely smart dude.

Dr. Freeman is quite possibly the most amazing teacher I've had yet at Geneseo. He gives amazingly clear notes; I have yet to find something on the capa assignments that I couldn't figure out using the notes I took in class, in Analyt I or IV (taking now). I can't wait to take him for Advanced Mechanics and any other 300-level courses he's teaching
Strong resemblance to Bob Sagat. Great teacher if you are interested in physics. i wouldnt suggest non majors taking courses with Dr. Freeman.
i fell asleep so many times. i withdrew -- couldnt stay awake.

Not a very helpful or clear professor! He might be good for Analyt phys, but he is not good at explaining physics to students who are NOT physics majors! Not helpful at all during office hours since he treats you as if you were stupid. I don't feel I learned anything during his lectures and they put me right to sleep.

He is my hero!!! He is not only a professor or an instructor, but also a real teacher - we do not only learn the instructions, but we also see a role model of how a mature and responsible man should be like. We also learn a lot from his organization style and his dedication to his job. His teaching? Rock!!!

Super smart guy, knows exactly what he's talking about and is willing to help outside of class. The course itself is a little challenging but its more because of the subject matter and less because of Freeman
he made me feel stupid when i asked him questions.  really likes people interested in physics.  got an E, then took it with padalino and got an A.  go figure.
i couldnt stay awake in this guys class. god im glad im not a phys major anymore...

Wow... what an amazing professor. If you are not comfortable with physics, he makes it so clear! He brings everything down to the most basic levels, and will always answer any questions you have. Tests are  challenging but not too bad. Take him if you can, he is great!

This guy rocks. I had him for analyt I, and got stuck with Iyer for analyt II. I snuck into a few of Freeman's classes though for analyt II, and it just blows my mind how much better he is. Iyer's not bad, but freeman just makes things so much easier to understand. Get him if you can!
He's a great teacher.  I went to class maybe 1/4 of the time, and he didn't seem to dislike me at all when I talked to him.  This may have been because I was getting an A in the class, though
Good teacher, helpful if you go to class and do work, if not he holds it against you. Don't take this to help your gpa, because it is very hard and he doesn't curve grades

his 2nd semester class fills up fast for a reason: freeman is awesome. great teacher, really brings things down to their most basic level, so he's really easy to understand. if you persistently ask questions, he'll like you. won't help your grade, but when you want to get overloaded for analyt II...

He is really smart, and is by far the most clear teacher i have ever had. Nobody ever has questions because he explains it in a way where everyone gets it the first time! He is also very nice and approachable. If you can get into his class, TAKE IT! He is awesome.
An amazingly smart physicist who happens to be a very good teacher and a really nice guy.
such a nice guy, always willing to help you during office hours. usually clear during classtime, but CAPA is a stinker
very enthusiastic, fun teacher! Dr Freeman rules! "Whats the moment of inertia for this object? GET OUT OF TOWN!!!! ABOUT WHAT AXIS??!!" Thats my favorite line.
he doesnt like people who dont go to class
Not a bad teacher but difficult to deal with.
