Takes forever to grade and is incredibly unhelpful if you have any questions. He refuses to check his email interesting class topic but impossible to work with him

The workload was manageable for a 400-level class, but don't expect anything to be graded during the semester. When he actually does grade, his criteria is overly critical and unfair. Constantly late to class and feedback on assignments doesn't affect your grade, even if you make the corrections he suggests. Do not take a class with him.
Most condescending professor ever!!!!!!! Unfair grader, not understanding on a power trip.

Artificially increases the difficulty of his class via subjective grading, has a high expectation of students in regards to attendance but is late to every class, and grades everything way too late. If he was held to the same expectations he holds his students, he would be fired a long time ago. Also doesn't help he thinks he is smarter than he is.

I would not recommend Professor Kleiman to anyone. The subject was interesting, but he made the experience unenjoyable. He doesn't like questions that challenge his point of view. He requires a lot of information from you while requiring you to be concise. He doesn't like students using outside sources at all. Be careful not to touch a nerve.

Professor Kleiman would absolutely be qualified for teaching courses if qualification were determined by knowledge alone. However, he is one of the least pleasant professors to interact with on all fronts. I do not feel I am granted any form of respect besides the basic courtesy outlines he is obligated to uphold as a professor.
I don't know who hurt this guy, but his grading style and lack of empathy certainly affects his students. For your sanity, please avoid.

He stands in front of the room and speaks in the most monotone voice ive ever heard in my life for over an hour. I sat right in front of him and asked questions and he never cared to try and learn my name(whatever, but still). somehow made a fun and interesting class so boring. but not too much hw ig, but you will get 5/10 on all assignments.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: I think a lot of the ratings for this class are unfair. history classes are longer I can imagine that if history isn't your thing you could easily get bored/ sick of it. But as a history major, I thought this class was great. Every book assigned was super interesting. Kleiman has his quirks but is super nice and the workload was fair and managable.

Showed up late everyday and was behind in lectures. Very nit-picky when he grades. Gives tons of reading; full books, and short papers with short turnaround. Is very rude, does not care, and is patronizing. Will fail if you don't go to class. Very serious about participation. Has a fake rule about plagiarism and will probably accuse you of it.

Dr. Kleiman is very clearly knowledgeable. However, his lectures are painfully dull, and the homework he assigns is outrageous; full books and several lengthy videos both with very short turnaround. Grading is also pretty brutal, demanding very specific formatting and nitpicking. However, if you are diligent and study hard, you can get through it.

Professor Kleiman was the most patronizing and sexist professor I've had. I made it through three weeks of this class but ended up withdrawing after he accused me of plagiarism, which was confirmed not to be by another history professor. Make sure you don't ask him a question that he doesn't know the answer to, his fragile ego cannot handle it.

Took this class as a Gen Ed and my only regret was not dropping it sooner. Kleiman was late to almost every class, was uncooperative in office hours, and assigned a ridiculous amount of work. Absolutely not worth all the stress.

This professor has a completely flipped classroom so before class you have to watch 1-3 hours of lecture videos and take notes to talk about in class. If you use any source other than the ones he gives you, you will get a zero on the assignment. It is VERY hard to do well in this class because it is very demanding.

Ive skipped a few classes and am still doing okay in class. He's an extremely tough grader and is harsh with his comments and feedback. (for example, my midterm: "NOOOOO" "this is not a sentence" and "weak writing") so if you take this course with him I genuinely wish you luck.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: The content of this class is super interesting. However, Kleiman is a very dull individual. He makes you watch his 2-hour lectures on your own time... and then you all you do in class is discuss them. The reading is extensive as well. If you are a history major, take his class because the content is great. If you are taking it as a gen-ed, don't!
he uses the flipped classroom method- you watch lectures outside of class. Very annoying and time consuming. Discussion can get boring and hard to pay attention to. Take good notes.
He shows up late to class everyday, a rude person, and a tough grader, Kleiman if you are reading this just know you need to work on your attitude and maybe ease up on the grading

Ok, so, this guy is very pretentious and rude. He almost never made time for us to see him, especially when he was supposed to have office hours. He expects you to summarize way too much in 125 words, his lectures are watched outside of class, and I withdrew from his class and switched out of his advisory because he was just unhelpful.

I liked his class, but that's because I'm biased. I'm not a big fan of the flipped classroom style of listening to lectures outside of class then using class time to review the material, though I will admit it does have its advantages. Nothing to write home to about. I enjoyed his class, but he's definitely not everyone's cup of tea.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Classes are very interesting. They're clearly structured and offer a good analysis of the topics, I've taken 3 of his classes now. He can be a stiff grader but will help you better your writing if you reach out for help. Show up to class, read the material & try your best and it'll be good, plus you'll actually learn grow as a student & historian.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: I was not a fan of this guy. He offers little help and comes off arrogant if you ask for any. The lectures are outside of class and every class period is just a discussion which I didn't bother going to and still did fine. You have to read a lot and his grading on papers is ridiculous.

Kleiman is OK. His lectures are interesting but he's very demanding of your time. Class is important for participation points but he makes you watch lectures on your own time, which can be multiple hours each week. He isn't clear with grading criteria and is a super harsh grader. He's quite arrogant, rude, and unhelpful when you ask for help.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: The class was great and informative, however, it is very writing-intensive and graded very heavily. The amount of lectures and live class twice a week tends to make the workload heavy. Read all the books given and spend double the time on your papers due to tough grading.
I wasn't interested in the topic when I enrolled, but Kleiman really brought it to life in class. Great course.
Stellar professor and stellar course on an interesting topic.

Unreasonably cocky and rude at times. I'll give him credit that my class was far from perfect and many times people didn' read the fairly reasonable workload but once we moved online and he had to grade multiple papers he just got unbearable for me. Read and participate and you will be fine.

Kleiman is absolutely brutal. He makes it very clear how disinterested he is in the classroom, and is my least favorite teacher ever. His lectures couldn't be more dry and are incredibly boring making the class impossible to enjoy. He is very unhelpful in class and at office hours so there is really no winning. I would avoid him at all costs.

Professor Kleiman is extremely dry. He makes you read pointless books, and write essays on topics that have no real value. He is a horribly tough grader, and he expects you to know how to write even though it's a class BASED ON college writing and how to improve. Unless you're a history major, I STRONGLY advise not taking Kleiman.

I would recommend taking another 302 if you can, but if not, Dr. Kleiman has made me a better writer by taking this class. If you're willing to work really hard and dedicate the time necessary to do well in this class, take it. Periodic assignments throughout the semester. Often late to office hours. Sometimes patronizing and demeaning to students.

Dr. Kleiman's 204 class was pretty good. I liked the books we read. He writes quizzes so you can't just sparknote them. One paper, one midterm, one final, and quizzes on the books that we were supposed to read for class. Lecture can be a bit dry at times, but if you answer questions and have a good group, you're in for a good class

Dr. Kleiman is a very smart guy. However he is not good at clearly articulating what he wants with papers. He is a harsh grader and nitpickey professor who would obviously be happier researching and writing than teaching students.

His lectures could get a little dry at times but the content itself is super duper interesting. Plus the class was really very easy. Most of our readings were whole books that we could read at our own pace and just have it finished by a certain date (they were good books). Very little day to day homework, and super cool topics
Prepare to be lectured every class. The majority of the final grade is based off of the midterm and finals which are essays with few multiple choice, and he is an extremely hard essay grader.

Professor Kleiman made my experience taking 302 as painless as it could have been. He lays out all the assignments for the semester on the syllabus and makes your grade based on many different things rather than just the major paper. He's a bit shy and reserved in class and office hours but gives meaningful feedback and cares about the subject.

Taking INTD  (Industrial Food Chain) with Kleiman is definitely doable. Almost all of the classes are discussions or occasional movies. He's a bit of a tough grader, but if you are a decent writer the class should be a breeze. His personality is a little dry. The content is interesting if you care about that stuff

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: If you go to class, take good notes, and read the books you should have no problem passing this course. He is a bit of a tough essay grader but generally fair. Lectures can be a bit dry but he is thorough and always pauses to ask for questions from time to time. I would take this class again and I would recommend it for an easy-ish B.

He does give you what he expects you to know. He gives you test questions, which is extremely helpful, so there are no surprises... unless you are required to make up a quiz because he makes you write a full essay as opposed to the simple multiple choice he gives the rest of the class, which is unfair- he is boring so wouldn't recommend to anyone.

Super easy class, but you have to show up to get lecture notes. Don't bother buying the textbook, but def watch the movies and read/skim the books. Tells you what is on exams. Quizzes are easy. Only thing- tough essay grader.

Lectures could be a bit long-winded but he puts up Powerpoints to look at while he's talking. The reading quizzes count so having some idea of the books he assigns is important. Overall the class was interesting but participation and asking pertinent questions definitely make it more interesting and help to pass the time.

I took Jordan Kleiman for an INTD and I did not do well at all. Firstly, he's incredibly arrogant and does not provide good help with his papers. He's a super tough grader and treated this freshman intro class like a 300 level class. He expected our papers to improve 0-100 if he was to give anyone a good grade ever. Definitely would not recommend

Have Taken a couple classes with him.  most of his classes are similar which is helpful.  like to reread certain books.  quizzes are easy 5 question multiple choice normally and the tests are not that bad.  the paper can be long for non 300 level but very easy to get at an 80 or higher on, but hard to move up into the 90s
Just don't.

You definitely need to go to class because all the notes are spoken during the lectures. Gives detailed study guide for the midterm and final and if you learn those you will ace them. Reading quizzes are annoying but decently easy. He's really passionate and a very clear and interesting teacher. If you go to class and pay attention you will ace it

Great guy with great intentions.  Not an easy A but an extremely fair grader.  tests and quizes are exactly what you expect them to be, and as long as you do the reading and take notes you're good.  Absolutely must participate in class though, and attendance is not mandatory but you probably will do horribly if you dont come.

Really nice guy, gives harsh but good feedback on writing. He expects a lot, and because of him I wound up expecting a lot more of myself as well. Also, go to office hours. Seriously. It will make your life ten million times better in this class. (note 'better', not necessarily easier)

I believed Jordan Kleiman to be a very good professor. He is in love with his subject and his passion is intoxicating for the first few weeks of class. He is intelligent and very opinionated. We were given detailed exam review sheets and ample time to get focused. The books assigned were simple to read and short. He is a great teacher.

This class is just downright tough. He never lectures. Whatever he assigns you to read, which is usually a decent amount, he makes you discuss in groups in a class, then he discusses with you. Very strict essay grader. I half-assed this class and did ok I do not advise that though. Do your reading and go to office hours and you'll do well
Good professor.  High, but reasonable expectations.  Willing to help you if you seek it out.
The workload is enormous, he is kind of high on himself, and i dont like his teaching style.  This said, do all the assignments and you'll get an A or B
Kleiman is extremely arrogant and rude. He is unwilling to help his students and looks down on them.

His lectures are very clear and easy to understand.  He gives you the questions on the quizzes beforehand so you know exactly what to study.  The lectures come with an overhead outline.  Definitely take this class.  He's really nice.
he's ana amazing lecturer, gives great feedback and just adorable

this is an intensive class and he flies through it. keeping up is tough but he's very flexible about due dates and he's available outside class. he was extremely in helping me set up and research my final 20pg paper, but he's particular about writing mechanics. participating in group discussion helps your grade-

Although Dr. Kleiman is a fairly good lecturer and is without a doubt knowledgable about American History, try not to take high-level classes with him (220, 221, or 300 level)  He is extremely arrogant and doesnt allow students to reach their own conclusions-- maybe the most important part of history.  His arrogance/pessimism makes him a bad choice

I absolutely adored his class. He's such a nice guy, and he puts up pictures on a slideshow to go with his lectures. Our notes are entirely from lecture, and he puts up an outline on the overhead. He makes U.S. History fun, I didn't think that was possible. All in all this class is great. Make sure to take detailed notes and you'll do great on the

He makes U.S. History fun, I didn't think that was possible. All in all this class is great. Make sure to take detailed notes and you'll do great on the
h is a great professor and is very helpful.  Kleiman really knows his topic.  As far as 220 and 221 all geneseo professors are hard.
This class was a lot of work but I think it's a lot of work with any teacher. Kleiman is a nice guy even though he can sometimes seem cold. I highly suggest him!
I had Kleiman for both 221 and 155. He was pretty easy and interesting for 155 but way too hard for 221. He expects way too much out of his students and adds too much un-needed stress.

Clearly liberal professor, doesn't use a text book at all. Tests and lectures from his own personal notes. we had to read four 300-400 page books and write papers on them (100 level class here professor!!!) 2 tests, mid and final.
Very difficult if you take him for research methods.  He has very high expectations, is never satisfied, and assigns ridiculous amounts of reading.  Take him for 204 but take someone else for 221.

Great Lecture. Great teacher, however he is very arrogant and not helpful at all. He does not help students when they go and see him. He talks in circles and waits for the students to tell him what he wants to hear. He needs to work on his people skills.

This is the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are engaging and he is extremely helpful. Mr Kleiman is your friend. You just have to put the work into the class. Take the time to do the reading and write the papers. You will get a lot out of his class. I wish every teacher was like  him.
Very interesting class and I recommend taking it.  He lectures everyday from a pre-made outline.  He's a tough grader on papers and tests.  He's very helpful if you come to him w/questions.
Fairly easy, promotes thinking on your own
I hate history but he has made me finally be able to get thru a history class.  Amazing so nice and helpful.  I cant say enough good things!
The readings suck but the class is incredibly easy.
Very very nice man, very easy, will help you greatly with papers if you see him ahead of time about them.  Highly reccomend him.
Great Lectures but he does talk a little fast. I highly suggest taking him
No Comments

Love Brooke!! I took her J-pop course and she's very excited about her work and to share that with students. As others have said, it's important to attend classes as much of the material she covers in person is not available online.

Above all, Brooke is a total nerd. If you show up to class and do the homework with some passion for music showing, you will do well in this class.

She is kind and understanding, and the grading is very reasonable, but there is a lot of (interesting and intense) music analysis homework over the course of the term.

Textbook is free online.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Prof McCorkle is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. She cares about her students a lot. I definitely recommend taking opera with her, if you put in the work you will receive an A

Professor McCorkle is very passionate about Opera. There is a bunch of extra credit opportunities outside of class. I would recommend going because she is very picky on details in regards to the answers on her quizzes. There was a group project where we had to create a Podcast. You don't need the book at all. I ended up liking to listen to Opera

Brooke is crazy passionate. She's super dorky and adorable, gives you tons of extra credit opportunities and all you have to do is go to class. Okay, no one really went to class half the time, BUT YOU SHOULD. She actually makes you want to learn. Seriously, easy time just study before the quizzes. You'll do fine and you might actually like opera!

She is easy going and quirky. The class can get really awkward if there is no participation at all. The INTD I took was about movies so it was just preparing for your paper the whole class. She is extremely caring and helpful. There is a movie night some weeks where you watch different movies and input a discussion post.

Took class Spring 2016 and it turned out to be a lot harder than expected. The tests covered a lot of material and the listening sections required short essays and exact dates and movement for pieces. She is very nice and if you go to class she will work with you. The lectures were ok but I definitely recommend actually reading the textbook too!

I would study for hours multiple days but there was just too much expected. If you miss even one class you'll feel weeks behind. Test layout is difficult and graded based on whether or not she thinks you know enough. You're expected to know every specific detail and there's A LOT of material covered. Would not recommend unless absolutely necessary.

Would not recommend. There isn't enough space here to describe how this class took over my life. She expects you to know every little detail, and grades very harshly although test questions are vague. I did end up getting an A in the course, after lots of stress and hard work, but I would avoid taking another class with Dr. McCorkle at all costs.

Not specific on grading criteria for tests and other assignments. Takes points off arbitrarily if you don't directly quote what she says in class on short answer questions. In a course that's supposed to be a music survey course, she only taught what she was interested in and left out important composers. Would not recommend.

I love Professor McCorkle! She's so fun and made the class really interesting. If you go to class and pay attention you don't even have to read and you'll do good on the tests. The tests are easy! The group paper was easy, and there's tons of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely take her!

Easy A class. Professor McCorkle is a cute and quirky nerd. She loves movies and music and this class is all about that. We are required to watch movies and write short paragraphs about its music. This class can change your perspective on movie music.

I had Professor McCorkle for the JPop class. While there was more history and older music than I expected, the class was really easy. Come to class, do the discussion posts, and participate in the group project and you'll be fine. She's friendly and really interested in the course material. She also gave us a ton of extra credit opportunities.

She was an excellent professor! She had a quirky and unique personality and was very interested in what she was teaching as well as extremely lenient and personable with the students. The class was always interesting and easy to succeed in!

Key to get A: take good notes in class. Easy A, 10 EXTRA CREDIT POINTS ON YOUR AVERAGE. Exams are so easy, basically covers the terms covered in class. She is so nice and funny! I loved her biology lab

Professor Reinhardt seems to be unsure of the topic she is teaching, leading to lots of confusion on her part. Disrespectful of student's time and class structure is poor. Overall would not take again.

I am generally a good student and I enjoy the topic of genetics but ended up hating this class. Dr. Reinhardt might be one of the worst professors I have encountered in the biology department. would not take a class with her again, tough grader. She has said to students that she doesn't mark everything wrong that is wrong and it's up to you to ask her about it even if it wasn't marked wrong the first time. Does not clearly answer questions in class, expects you to know things in depth even if it is your first time encountering it.

Dr. Reinhardt was a great professor for Genetics. I thought the lectures were clear and the tests were very fair. Her homeworks were an asset to better understanding whatever topics they included. When I took her, there were a very fair amount of extra credit as well.

This class was tougher than other sections from what Ive heard. I did a lot of extra credit and still ended with a B. I feel like I learned a lot but it was kind of hard to predict what would be on the tests, and the hw was always hard

Reading before class makes the lectures much more easy to digest. Make sure you go to her office hours as her slides arent very detailed and she is not always the best at explaining in class. She is totally willing to help. Hw is tricky but easier than the tests and the tutors help. Review the class objectives and do the textbook questions to ace!
Poor lecturer, Doesn't explain material well at all. Talks off of slides not made by her and asks very poorly worded questions on tests

Took Genetics in fall '16 when she was new. The class was challenging and put in a lot of work on the textbook, but she is a fair grader and easy to talk to if you have any questions. 4 tests, the final was cumulative, with in-class questions, and homeworks that made you think. (had extra credit for homeworks when I took it)

Evolutionary biology - interesting class. Topic - hard. Reinhardt makes it hard to do poorly in the class. Quizzes - weekly/bi-weekly on chapters in the test book (Returns half points missed). Tests - 4 total tests (MC and Short answer). Papers - 2 on evolutionary books/papers. You only need to do 5 out of the 6 and she drops the lowest grade.

She's new and still gaining her footing as a professor and still has A LOT of kinks to work out. She is very caring and dedicated to teaching and I know with some time she will be much better. Try and get into another genetics class or take her 10 years from now.  Tests are HARD and LONG and class was unbearable.

She's sweet, but an awful professor. She talks to you like you're a colleague and doesn't know how to explain. Professor Tramte was awesome! He's a really nice guy who cares about his students. I am not musically inclined in the slightest and had to take this class to fulfill a fine art requirement. Prof. Sargent is an awesome teacher. His lectures are backed up with real life military experience that allow you to gain more from the content. Great Professor. 100% would recommend.
Great lecturer and is able to draw in lessons learned in his life and time serving with the military to give the students an insight into history/war like none other.

Where do I start? Professor Sargent is an awesome spirit to be around. He loves what he does and wants all of his students to succeed. His lectures are very engaging and at the end of the year he showed us pictures and videos from his military experience and it was really awesome.

I am currently a senior and Professor Sargent has been one of my best professors since coming to Geneseo. He is a very laid-back professor who gives plenty of time to do the assignments. He wants you to succeed and he is very knowledgeable with military history. Overall, I would highly recommend you take his class.

This is my first year at Geneseo and boy did this class set the bar. Professor Sargent is super laid back, understanding, and even funny. If I got the chance to take this class again I would 100/100 times.

Legitimately the best course I have ever taken here at Geneseo. Professor Sargent's lectures are very engaging. He is funny and the content is very interesting. Graded by 3 papers + Attendance+ + Interview with a veteran. Also went on a field trip to the Vietnam War Wall Memorial and the war plane museum. This class exceeded my epectations.
My favorite professor, would definitely recommend. Makes class enjoyable and not alot of work.
Best teacher in Geneseo

Take him, its an easy A, field trips, learn a lot of American history this professor takes advice from his class, cancels class too. He also gives 3 essays with interview with veteran. YOU WILL LEARN SO MUCH FOR A FREE A

One of the best professors I've ever had in all my 4 years here. Makes learning about military history super interesting and fun, and he's got great jokes. The class is an hour and 40 minutes, but he never went longer than an hour and a half. Your grade is based on attendance, 3 papers, and an interview. I can't say enough wonderful thing about him

prof sergent is so funny and made lecture engaging. so kind and understanding that you have a life outside of school. he made a seemingly boring class interesting, 4 papers to do that he gives a lot of time for and are fun to write. def would reccomend love this man
Sargent is one of the best professors on campus. HIST 120 was one of the best classes I have taken so far, he cares for his students and loves what he teaches.

As a senior, this was my favorite class I ever took in college. Sargent is AMAZING!! I learned so much in this class. Even if you don't need this class for credit, find a way to take it. He is absolutely hilarious and so knowledgable.
Theres four papers during the course and no tests, he gives you pdf's of all textbooks so you don't have to buy a million. I didn't read a single thing papers are easy
loved this class and the professor is fantastic!!

Dr. Sargent made a humanities class fun. I did not expect to enjoy a mandatory gen-ed class, but it ended up being my favorite class this semester. Absolutely take this class if you can. The only grades were participation and papers but as long as you put in the effort it is easy to get a good grade in this class.

Everyone dreads the humanities requirement, I'm glad I took it w/ Sargent. He is very knowledgeable and does his best to make lectures engaging for students who don't want to be in the class. All readings are available for free. No exams; four 5 page papers that reflect on reading. Sargent is kind-hearted and wants his students to enjoy content!!
Great professor. Take him any chance you get. He understands that hum is a class everyone hates and makes it bearable. Write a few papers with reasonable effort and you're good to go.

If you don't take your Humanities class with Professor Sargent, you are genuinely missing out. He is hilarious and engaging (even in a class with admittedly pretty boring material). While I would suggest actually doing the readings to do well on the papers, he's not a tough grader. If you do what he asks and show that you tried, you'll do well!

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Respected', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Prof. Sargent is definitely one of the best at Geneseo. Attendance is mandatory, but class is not boring. He makes lectures really interesting. Lighthearted and great person overall. Do the readings and pay attention in class and the papers will be a breeze. Easy and low-stress way to get your HUMN credit.

One of my favorite professors at Geneseo! If you go to class he will make you laugh, and a genuinely kind guy. He makes it clear from day one that he's there because he enjoys it and wants to teach, and makes something dry like philosophy really stick. Brings in surprises every one in a while to change class up and really engages students. 10/10.

Sargent was one of the best professors I have had at Geneseo. He really considers that all people have to take HUMN, even if they aren't interested in it. All you have to do is show up to class. Minimal papers. Reading assignments for HW. Respects you as a student and your time. I can not say enough great things about this professor.

This class was honestly one of the most interesting and easy classes I've taken at Geneseo. Yes you did have to go to class because he took attendance by worksheets in the beginning but he's so easy going and the way he lectures is really interesting. There were two paper and one test but he literally told you everything that was going to be on it

Professor Sargentt is a one of a kind professor, yes you do need to read the books in this class, but if you get a general idea of your readings and listen to his lectures, you will find this class to be easy. He makes your life simple and knows that you are there for the credit, so he understands you. If you have a chance to take him, plz do so

I walked into this first day of class with no excitement but after taking this course I wanted to become a Humanities major. Gosh,the way he teaches is so nice. He teaches so simply and does fun activities to help you remember the contents. I was skeptical about writing 5 papers each 6 pages but he made us write what we were interested in. #LOVEHIM

Omg, what are you doing if you aren't taking Sargent? This man understands that we are students and things happen. He is so clear with grading and also teaches so well. You can never hate his class and he is an amazing professor. Super easy and understandable. Few papers and your good to go. Sargent is my favorite professor on campus.

Everyone dreads taking HUMN but I got lucky when I signed up for this class. He knows nobody wants to take the class but he makes it so fun and the papers are easy As. My class was 4:30-6:00pm but I never dreaded going to it. Do yourself and your GPA and your mental health a favor and take HUMN with this man!!

Sargent is an AMAZING professor. I withdrew from HUM twice before taking it with him and he literally makes it interesting to read about Marx, Shelley, Locke and anyone else! He is truly amazing. Please do yourself a favor and take humanities with him, you will actually learn and have fun doing it. He is approachable and really nice!
Sign up for his class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: He is a great prof! You'll read about one book a week, but you won't need to remember all the readings in order to get a good grade. Great lectures, and grades only four papers that are based on the readings. Awesome class!

Of all the humn profs at Geneseo he is definitely the best one. Class attendance and expectations are fair, lectures are interesting, and papers are graded very fairly. If you can follow his slides you're all set for the papers (there are 3 + 1 final that is slightly shorter in length).

I looked forward to coming to class every day. Lectures are very informative and entertaining. He cares a lot about his students and the class material, which is reflected in how he engages with the class.
Dr. Sargent is a great professor and makes lectures entertaining. A quiz for participation every class engages students in the material. Great class to take, highly recommended
Great Prof and an Easy Course, Very Kind and Understanding with students needs.

A great professor that makes learning humanities interesting. The class was twice a week so it was 90 minutes and I was never bored or falling asleep. He also was very accommodating throughout the semester as I was going through job recruitment season.

I had to take this course to graduate so I was not looking forward to it. He breaks the class into parts, so there is group work, a short video, quizes and Lecture. I found him engaging and ended up paying attention. Best of the Humn Profs? in the top 3 for sure.

He is an awesome professor who makes great jokes and incorporates little videos into his lectures to keep things interesting. For the course you have to write a some papers, but as long as you answer the essay prompt, you'll do fine. Easily one of the best professors on campus and I would highly recommend to take his class if you can get in.

Literally my all-time favorite professors. So funny and understanding. He makes what could very easily be the worst course ever very fair and enjoyable. the nicest and most enthusiastic professor. definitely worth waiting to take hum if you cannot get into this class.
Good class

Super nice and makes dad jokes that he loves when you laugh at. Easy pop quizzes that are basically the homework questions. Essays can literally be written over night and you still get an A. Want an easy hum class? Take him! He usually has a waiting list. You won't regret this easy class my dudes.

Required course. I wanted to take it from a history person rather than philosophy or Eng. I enjoyed it, some parts are boring, but that is the course itself. Hard to get excited about Nietzsche.

Worst professor I have ever had. She is so beyond unclear and gives the most pointless assignments that don't help at all. She is rude over email and gives unnecessary assignments. Not helpful. Just overall terrible, disorganized, and unclear professor. Would not recommend under any circumstance.

Loads of HW for a 1.5 credit class, and an unfair grader. A lot of presentations. The assignments are just chaotic. Awesome! She wants to see you grow as a student and really improve your writing and overall communication skills. No this class is not an easy A like other INTD 205 classes but it will definitely prepare you for the future. The course consists of a lot of work but it is completely worth it. Prof. Landy is one of the nicest professors on this campus. She genuinely cares about you and your understanding of the topic. assignments are unclear, theres always like 4 projects due on one day, not good if your uncomfortable speaking in front of people. loads of group projects that she gives you about 2 days to do. honestly take with another teacher. crazy work load on top of already crazy schedule.

Professor Landy is the most caring professor at Geneseo. She is a tough grader and gives lots of work, but you actually improve. She is always willing to help students. If you want to learn and improve your communication skill, I highly recommend her.

Very nice professor. you got a LOT of work to do, but every assignment is defin useful. You did every report, assignment, memo, letters in Google drive, and she will keep editing it for you. It is very useful. I feel I learned a lot from this class.

THE worst professor for Business communications at Geneseo. Take literally anyone else. The workload is insane and grading is very unclear.  Every other professor is an Easy A, but she makes it way harder than it needs to be.  I ended with a B+ with an INSANE amount of extra work and sucking up.

awful teacher! do not take a class with him unless you want anxiety

No respect for any human, acts as if he is paying good money to have slaves in the audience to ridicule and embarrass.  Absolutely no faith in the education system he is a part of, though he will tell you that himself multiple times.  Overall unhappy person who enjoys spreading his misery.  Picks on particular students way more than others. Enjoy.

You either like him or you dont like him. If you don't like him and you never contribute, he is going to become the bane of your existence. If you do like him and contribute and attempt to be a genuine student, he's the best professor you will ever have.

Very intellectually engaging and provocative but self-defeating. YOU'RE LESS LIKELY TO GET INTO LAW SCHOOL WITH A B GRADE IRREGARDLESS OF HOW MUCH YOU GET OUT OF THE CLASS. Incredibly intelligent, incredibly tough. Reading and class participation are a must. If you are committed and willing to work, Professor Deustch will be one of the best professors you ever have. Professor Deutsch is quite possibly the most difficult teacher I've ever had. I've had to work harder than ever in his class and really put in some serious effort and long hours. ok, so, hes is a great teacher. However, his grading is definitely offset.  I am learning a lot, working very hard, but only earning a B in the class.  He is VERY rude. He is a wealth of knowledge and incredibly intelligent, but this is all overshadowed by his severe hate for his students. I have never been so insulted by anyone in my life. He is by far the worst teacher i have ever had a geneseo. he doesn't teach at all. he rather spend the entire class yelling at his students about how stupid they are. he also calls out the students to make them feel stupid. if you can avoid taking him i would. he is a bitter old man who doesn't care for his students.

Dr. Deutsch is the best professor in the political science department.  He expects a lot from his students but a good grade in his class is extremely rewarding.  He is also a tremendous resource for pre law students.  I plan on keeping in touch with him post-graduation.
Checks attendance every day, despite this being against school policy. Also his tests are nonsensical and his voice is soporific.

I heard that his class was good preparation for law school.  I'm in law school, and his class hasn't helped me at all.  Law school professors are generally much nicer, more knowledgeable, and have a better teaching methods.  His abrasive personality and the awful way he treats students decreases interest in the subject.  Take Sciarrino instead.
Best professor I ever had.  Very tough but an excellent teacher.

This man is really, really difficult. Be prepared for him to go off on random, on-his-high-horse tangents about how the world isn't an easy or nice place and how you're in for a rude awakening, and yadda yadda. Be prepared for about four hours or work a night..nightmarish class. He's nice in his office hours, but a monster in class.

Had him for 3 classes.  I'm in law school now. Law professors are far more understanding and less abrasive.  His stories of what law school is like are just wrong.  Mega briefs are a waste of your time and his.  Take Sciarrino in Business if you want to learn to brief the right way.  It's called a brief for a reason.
Do all you can to avoid him.

If at all possible avoid this class.  You will work harder in this class then in all of your others combined just to pass.  He believes that we are all only concerned with GPA and success and should take hard classes to gain more knowledge.  He doesn't even have open office hours, you have to make an appointment.  He is scary.

Closest we have to a law school professor. His classes are the hardest in Geneseo. Requires a great deal of reading. DO THE READINGS. He takes attendance, and it is mandatory. If you skip his lectures you will not pass the course. Very tough, but if you like the subject matter, or plan on attending law school, his courses are a MUST.

I took political theory from him and i learned how to cry and how to be scared.  The final is worth 50% of your grade and the mid-term 35% so if you're more  of the paper writing type and not really good at tests you're basically screwed.  He will yell at you if you walk into his class .5 seconds late but then he will keep you 10 minutes late.

Definitly very good professor to take if you want to *learn* anything. His classes are not "blow off" classes and he is very intimidating. Not for the weak in spirit. However, if you can suck it up and work hard... you'll walk away from his classes a better (smarter) person for it.

Theory with this guy is like taking a grad school course, while managing a business, and also not speaking english. He's very arrogant at times and spends the majority of class time lecturing, when he says at the beginning he wants class participation. Knows zilch when it comes to current events; no quizzes. Do the reading...twice at least

He is extremely knowledgable, and actually pretty easy to deal with in office hours.  He comes across as very miserly and miserable with life, but if you are willing to work twice as hard as for your other classes, you will get a lot out of it.  An A- or B+ in a Deutsch class is worth way more than an A in any other class.

i have had deutsch for 2 classes and am looking forward to another one. he is super hard and expects a lot from his students. he's not out to trick you on tests. he presents the information in a clear manner. you have to pay attention and you have to be willing to read 300 pages a week. but you get so much out of his class, really rewarding =)

The WORST prof I have ever encountered. Material he taught was the only good thing about his class, and it didn't make up for his negative attitude towards his students. He is a hypocrtical miser. STAY AWAY!!!

It's funny how his biggest pet peeve is when students are late to class, yet he consistently keeps us 6-8 minutes after the end of class with his jabbering and virtually assures that we'll all be late for our next class. What a hypocrite!

haha the person below me mentioned how he yelled at someone for "spacing out".. that was me! He seriously is so miserable. However, im about to take my 4th class with him. Absolutely the most misterable man on campus. Do the extra credit paper, it will save your grade!

His class is absolutely excellent to sleep in.. until you wake up and see him sitting at the front of class. Great advisor, brilliant man. Visit during office hours, get to know him. Get an A if you read, attend class and pay attention. Fair grading policy. Take class, do your part, get an A.
No Comments

This was one of the worse classes I've taken. I ended up dropping it and taking it elsewhere. She seems kind, but is unfortunately not a very good teacher. All the lectures were pre-recorded and quite lacking in helpfulness. Practice problems tended to be much easier than exams. Maybe her in-person classes are better?

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: She's a fantastic professor. Everything you need to know for exams is clearly taught in her lessons. She breaks down chapters into different lessons with a corresponding worksheet for that lesson. DO THE WORKSHEETS! She's easily accessible outside of class and super helpful. The exams are tough so be prepared to study for hours for a good grade.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Would take again']
comment: Geiger is easily the best professor to take Orgo 1 with, by a longshot. She lectures for about half the class, and then the other half is spent in groups working on a worksheet. Her tests are extremely fair, and she is an unbelievably nice and helpful person. Orgo is hard, but you're crazy to take it with anyone else.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Prof Geiger is amazing. Her lectures are interactive and you do practice problems at the end of almost every class to see if you really understand the material. Her tests however are on the more difficult side. She is very helpful in office hours and really wants students to understand the material not just a good grade. Read the textbook!
Very rude and condescending. One of the worst professors I've had.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: Geiger was nice but a very tough grader. The first class I really struggled with and couldnt get a grasp on. She lecture for half the class then gives your group a worksheet that is very hard to complete in twenty minutes. She is nice and tries to be helpful, but in the end your grade might struggle because of her teaching method and grading

Geiger is honestly, one of the best teachers I have ever had at Geneseo. Orgo is hard, regardless who you take, but she's very dedicated and so helpful during office hours. She's super peppy and funny and overall a wonderful teacher. Just make sure to be on top of her lessons and do the recommended reading. She is a very harsh grader however.

First off, Organic Chem will be hard no matter who you take it with.  But Geiger makes it bearable- she really wants to see her students succeed and is very approachable for help. The entire class is going over the lectures before class and doing worksheets in class. Curved final grades around the average (average becomes a B) which is nice.

Didn't lecture more than 5 times all semester. Gave lots of group work which was all graded for the most part so it forced you to read the notes the day before because your grade on it. Orgo is hard no matter what so needless to say she was not an easy grader. Really liked her as a person and a fast grader.

I heard she was the best organic teacher, so I decided to take here. However, this year she switched to "reverse classroom." This may work for some classes, but not for orgo. She barely lectured (maybe no more than 10 times this semester). This especially doesn't work for a class where the textbook is absolutely horrible (plus many mistakes).

Dr. Geiger is very approachable. You must print the lecture slides prior to class or you will have difficulty keeping up. There is an extremely large amount of material on each exam (especially compared to other institutions) and little time to spare; if you don't know the answer, you may as well move on.

She is a very nice person but doesn't do a lot in lab. Most of the lab is taught by tas and she only does the prelab. She's easy to talk to and her husband wrote the lab book used so she knows all about it. *strongly recommend taking the semester after chem 1 not during.
Great professor. Really loves what she's doing. Always happy to help in lab.

Absolutely awesome, very helpful both in class and in office hours. Reading the textbook helps, and the online homeworks are linked to it and very helpful. Exams and group quizzes are difficult but passable. From Costa Rica and has an accent, but is easy to understand. Can use molecular models on exams. Lectures and class work are very helpful.

She is a great professor and definitely keeps the class entertaining instead of boring. The tests and quizzes are definitely hard, but she is always willing to help people out. Make sure to go to her office hours. She is always super helpful and tends to round up the grades of people who go to them. I definitely recommend her as a professor.

Orgo is hard no matter where you are or who you take it from, but she presented the material in a way that is relatively easy to understand and remember. If you don't print the lecture slides, you will NEVER be able to copy all the notes. Her accent made her a little more difficult to understand, but not impossible. Extremely helpful!!

I've taken orgo with both Christina and Dave and I prefer Dave because he's easier to understand, but Christina is still a great professor. I just get caught up in trying to understand her through her accent.

Lab with Geiger is a lot of fun and she is very helpful.  However, she is very picky with your lab reports and will take off points for little errors so make sure you put enough work into them.  Very helpful during office hours and loves talking to her students and getting to know you during lab.

Dr. Geiger is by far the best professor I've had at Geneseo.  Her tests and quizzes are difficult but as long as you put the time and effort in, you will do well.  She is very responsive and helpful during office hours and wants everyone to succeed.  Her class is challenging but if you do the work you will definitely learn a lot.
She's great. Material is very hard though, be prepared to work work work

Christina is a pretty good professor. I personally had a hard time with her accent at first but it's something you get used to and is funny at times. Don't get on her bad side or you will never get off. If you break an arm or have a traumatizing event happen mid semester DROP! She will give you no leeway or help you in any way

Cristina is a good professor. Very clear and makes sure all students understand. She moves quick in class, so print the notes out before coming to class. She definitely favors the students doing really well. Tests are not super hard, but they're definitely difficult. The quizzes are harder than the tests.
wonderful at presenting info. funny and enthusiastic. makes orgo semi enjoyable

Professor Geiger is a great organic teacher. She makes class  fun and she is very interested in the subject. The online home and her quizzes are not overly difficult but they do not prepare you very well for what her test will be like. If you want to get a decent grade in her class do all the suggested assignments. Over all she is a great teacher.

Prof. Geiger hasn't been one of my favorites to say the least. She is very judgemental and once she develops a negative opinion of you, there's no going back. I found her to be very rude on several occasions. Her practice tests and quizzes aren't indicative of what her tests will be like. I was very glad to be done with her and her class
This class is tough (organic chemistry, after all) but Cristina is extremely enthusiastic and makes everything very clear. She makes herself very available outside of class. Take this class!

Awesome teacher. Very enthusiastic and helpful. She knows all her students by name - even the ones who never show up to class. I wish I had given more of my time to her class - she is the kind of teacher you want to be proud of you.

She really wants students to do well, and fully explains each chapter before moving on.  She is always willing to help and is one of the nicest teachers I've had.  She makes a hard class bearable and even fun.  I would definitely take another class with her!
Geiger is amazing and one of my favorite professors here.  She is always willing to go the extra mile and seriouly cares about the student.  She loves what she does and is a great choice for organic.

Easily the best organic professor in geneseo. Teaches every topic until she thinks everyone understands. Makes reviews, review sessions, tons of practice problems. The quizzes were hard, but they made the tests easier. Take organic with her if you can!

The conflicting opinions up may cause some confusion; Yes, this class is difficult, but taking it with her is relatively easy compared to other teachers. She is the best choice for organic chemistry. Don't let rumors of her accent throw you off; her accent/vocabulary is easy to understand and often hilarious!
She is one of my favorites.  Excellent professor and wiling to pull out all the stops.  Show up for class, do the reading beforehand.  I love orgo because of her.  Keeps you awake and interested.

My favorite prof. Excellent teacher even if you don't like chem. Awesome PPTs that he puts online prior to class. Covers a lot of info at a fast pace but does it well. Really knows his stuff & can explain it to you any way that will help. Go to class & pay attention & very little outside study will be needed. Online quizes, test very reasonable.

I got absolutely WRECKED by this class, and I'm not an idiot. It is not fun, it is not enjoyable, and you will suffer.  Cristina. however, understands this, and that being said, she tries everything in her power to make sure you get the point.  Probably the most approachable professor I've had on campus, and I think she's the best choice for orgo.

This class made me drop Orgo and become a Business/Pre-Law major, but Cristina is an AMAZING teacher, plus she cares about you doing well. Very approachable, and the most helpful during office hours, she practically drags out the key to the quizzes, but the course itself will make you cry yourself to sleep, just be ready for it because it's not fun
The best teacher I've had in Geneseo. Subject matter is really hard but she is VERY helpful and VERY clear in what she wants. Keep up with the notes and you'll do fine.

Orgo is the worst class you'll take, and it doesn't matter who's teaching it since it'd still be crap. Cristina is, however, the nicest and most caring professor I've had. She knows the course is awful, and really wants you to do well, and goes out of her way to ensure that. Better than Helms I'd say, but Orgo II material is tougher than Orgo I.
She's very hard, but also very helpful.  She will spend time outside of class helping you, one on one, even.  She's the greatest!
i took general chem and orgo I with Cristina, and i'll take orgo II with her too. the chem department has all these good professors, but she is the best among them!
for someone who doesn't have a PhD and speaks english as a second language, she's amazing.

Had her last year for 116. If you can't learn from Powerpoint, then I'd try finding someone else. The grading curve is awesome though- 85 is an A-, you can get a 73 or so and still have a B. GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS, they will help. Her tests were challenging yet extremely fair, and she was one of the most fair professors I've had. Recommended.
No Comments

People either really like or really dislike this class.  Dr. Geiger is a very smart approachable woman, but her use of Powerpoint is where the line is drawn. I for one prefer going along with the teacher on an overhead, plus she'd fly during lecture.  However, with all the review sessions and what not there's no reason not to get B or higher
She is a really good teacher, explains things well. She'll help you out whenever, but there was one time when I went to her office and she seemed annoyed that I was there- I felt very uncomfortable.

Loved her. Lecture notes are online but i wouldnt depend on them b/c she leaves spaces blank for you to fill in during class.  She devotes some time to practice problems and goes over what each test will be on. You really hafta do problems outside of class to do well, i mean, it is Organic Chemistry

i love cristina but orgo II lab is hard and she doesnt make it much easier on you- dont ask a question or she will make you feel very stupid for asking it- she has favorites too-- but she is a great professor

she's the best...words can describe how brilliant, and helpful she is! she is the most approachable professor i've met in geneseo and i highly recommend her for any class she is teaching: chems is hard but she makes u love it

Christina is awesome. God, this is what I call teaching. If I had an Oscar, I will give it 2 her in a second. Her peru accent is easy 2 understand. She repeats herself a lot so it's easy 2 know the material. Study hard, read notes, make sure you understand everything before tests and go 2 CLASS.
Christina is the BEST chem professor ever!!! Try your best to take her class...i love her...
Cute, small & brilliant! Cristina is just AMAZING!
really good teacher.  she is willing to help you out on anything in order to get a better grade.

She's a good teacher, but a little difficult to understand, plus if you take notes in a notebook instead of the printed notes, good luck because she FLIES some times during lectures.  It's very easy to fall behind, but if you keep on top of things you'll be fine.  She is an extremely fair professor.
FANTASTIC CHRISTINA GEIGER IS THE BEST TEACHER YOU WILL HAVE, WORK YOUR SCHEDULE AROUND HER

Very clearly presented, tests are very fair and surprise free.  The material is challenging nonetheless, so you gotta do some work outside of lecture, but she'll do anything she can to help you.  Nice lady, highly recommended.
Love her...one of the best chem profs. Take her for anything you can.

Cristina is def the best professor I'll ever have! I took her for every chem class I could 116, 211, 212, 213 and 214! With orgo she makes a difficult topic very understandable. She's very easy to work with and cares about her students. You gotta love her
An amazing professor.  She explains everything, she does examples, and the test are surprise free.  If I can get an A in this class, going out 5 nights a week, then anyone can with a little work.
She is by far the best chem professor out there.  Very down to earth and funny!

Cristina is the best!  She is an excelent teacher and a really nice person.  Once my lab professor unexpectedly canceled office hours and she helped me during her own time.  Do whatever you can to take her class (that is if you have to take organic).
20 point curve!!!!!!!
Explains things really clearly, along with tests reflecting the material.  Great lady - I hope I can have her for all my other Chem classes...
Made a really tough class a lot easier.  Clear with explanations and really knows her stuff.  watch out for the jokes though...

One awesome teacher!!! Got to know most everyone's name and there are well over 100 students in the class...very approachable and a great sense of humor. She made a tough (and often boring) class a heck of a lot better
Simply put she made me want to learn chemistry. She is funny, approachable, caring, and smart.  A rare combination in a field known more for its frustration and coldness.  Best teacher in GENESEO. ;)
Wooot!  I love Christina.  Very helpful, funny, makes orgo easier than it otherwise would be.  You can't help but love her, really.
fun class
good
GREAT lady!  Very animated and really tries to make sure you understand the material she's covering.  Very willing to help. SO cute! Gotta love Christina!!
She's really helpful and accomodating.  Most people make the mistake of not taking advantage of it.
No Comments
Best chem teacher this school has.
Very willing to help
nice and energetic lady... one hell of a course load

American Art with this professor and any 200 or upper course is a pain. You will have a lot of outside studying if you want to get an A or B in this course. By the way, she also does written exams in her course too and they are difficult compared to her 100 level courses.
Super awesome. Professor Toothe is such an engaging professor, and her class is very straightforward. Really enjoyable and I've loved taking her. Tests are really easy but make sure you go to class.

Professor Toothe is an okay instructor, but my biggest issue is her strict no‑late‑work policy. I'm not trying to be harsh—I just hope she sees this and considers allowing small point deductions in future semesters. an A is a 95+ and she only puts 5 grades in for the whole semester 3 of those being tests. it's very hard to get an A even if u go to every lecture study and take good notes.

She was an amazing teacher and taught well. You must go to all the classes bc everything she teaches is on the test. There are only 3-4 test but all multiple choice and are easy if you study a little bit. Never would have thought I would like this class but I loved it. You do have to take notes but it is very helpful.

Professor Toothe had some strange rules such as no looking at the clock, yawning or having technology out. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would highly discourage skipping class because although she posts slide lists on Brightspace, they don't have much context behind them. Tests were very specific to the works of art discussed in class.

DONT WASTE MONEY ON THE TXTBOOK. Lecture heavy and the min she starts talking, you better start writing. Unless you're willing to STUDY, you won't get an A. THIS IS NOT AN EASY GEN-ED TO TAKE. 3 exams + a final. Her tests are long
SHE IS A BAD B! I would take her class again and again

This is my second class with Toothe and im taking another next semester! She is an easy grader and a chill person. She does have some silly rules but for the most part as long as you are off tech for the whole class she is nice. Tests are easy if you go to class. I never thought I would like Art History but she made me love it so much! Take her!

She is terrifying on the first day, but once you make it past that she is funny and really nice. The class is not as hard as she makes it out to be as long as you go and pay attention. I thought I wouldn't enjoy the class but I really do. Sometimes lectures are dry but its manageable. Take notes. No computers in class. Tell her you are a Bills fan.

Prof Toothe is pretty funny, and you are only graded on 3 exams. But the questions on them consist of "Did Professor Toothe take this photo that was shown on the slideshow". Which is frustrating because why does that matter? The first exam is worth 20% of your grade, the second 35%, and the last exam is worth 45%.
Very strict

Toothe is a very cool and funny professor. She does not allow electronics at all in her classes so you have to take all your notes by hand. Your grade comes from 3 exams and that is it, no other assignments. The exams only have questions about topics she spoke of in class so as long as you attend the lecture and take notes you should do alright.
No complaints with Professor Toothe, as long as you complete the assignments within the time frame, you can definitely pass with an A!
Love love love her! She truly seems to want everyone to succeed in her courses and is inspirational in the way she speaks about art history! Cannot say enough great things about her!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This class in person is very hard. Tests are the only thing graded and so much material is crammed into each test. Lectures drag so badly. I had the one night a week class from 3-5:30 and wanted to stop attending. But in order to pass you need to attend every single class. This class is 100% memorization. Professor Toothe does bring some humor.

This course taught online is super easy. Each week you either have to submit a short assignment or participate in a class discussion. Professor Toothe is a good professor although she hasn't really taught me anything, I learned everything from our textbook. Not a hard class, great to fulfill general education requirements.

Very knowledgeable. Always get out early. Three exams were the only grades in the grade book but if you pay attention in class and take down key notes this class is an easy A. Attendance isn't mandatory but highly suggested because she does not post any notes online, and as the class is 2 hours long, a lot of information is given. Love her!

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: I took ARTH 173 with Toothe and loved it, grade is based on 3 tests but she goes over all course material thoroughly. She made three hour lectures fun and we almost always got out early. She's hilarious and this class was easy yet interesting. 10/10 would recommend.

She was SUCH a wonderful professor, my gosh! I walked away with such an appreciation of art, and an awe of the creative minds behind the pieces we studied. Toothe makes you feel moved by the art, which is something very rare. Her class is one I would recommend to anyone  from Art History, to Accounting, to Bio, and all those in between.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: On the first day, she seems to be mean but she is actually nice. The only thing you are graded on is 3 exams. Exams are straightforward, she doesn't try to trick you. She gives an opportunity for extra credit which I suggest doing. As long as you go to the lecture, listen and take notes, you will do fine in the class.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Toothe is the best professor I have ever had. I took this class to fill an art credit and she is such an interesting professor. Even though the class can be long and boring at times her commentary keeps it interesting and if you pay attention to her jokes a lot of times they are on the tests (free points). Easy class as long as you pay attention.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Professor Toothe is amazing! Her lectures were super interesting. Take REALLY good lecture notes. Like, if she mentions that her nephew looks like a dude in a painting, write that down because it'll be on the test. Your grade is based on three tests, which aren't hard (esp. as a hsitory major) if you memorize the paintings and reread your notes.
Such a fun and enthusiastic environment. Love this class so much, it is so interesting. She is so funny and easy to pay attention to. Definitely recommend taking this class for art cred

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Your grade is 3 exams (she offers an extra credit paper), theyre pretty long (100 questions) but theyre easy as long as you have paid attention in class and know the paintings/artists by name. Hilary is very knowledgeable on the material and she seems like a cool person too. Overall a very interesting class I looked forward to each week.

Very intimidating the first class, but it's just a front. The only thing graded were the tests. The tests were generally easy, but some questions are definitely uncalled for. If you're just looking to get fine arts credit try to take ANY other class that qualifies. If you're super into art history she's the professor for you.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Hilarious', 'Would take again']
comment: Great teacher! Made art fun and enjoyable.
She gives great lectures and will even let you out early from time to time. One problem I had was her tests, she asks A LOT of "all of the above" questions.
Tests require quite a lot of study time, but it's all memorization. Her attitude is so hilarious it made the class so much more fun! No textbook is required, but attendance is.
malik is one of the best professors in the business school. favorite times in class happen when he rips apart a student's unfounded assertion. if you want his respect, know your stuff.

An excellent professor. Class discussions are thought-provoking and he really does a good job of keeping us interested. He is a fair grader and tests are not too hard. Definitely one of the better courses I've taken.

A really good teacher who keeps the whole class engaged, and really knows his stuff very well. The classes go by really quickly and they are mostly related to current events. Tests are concept not detail based. Everyone has to give a 5 minute presentation on a newspaper article. He made me really interested in international business.

Staebell seems knowledgeable but at times she has difficulty explaining concepts Class is mostly lecture with slide shows that are from the textbook The work we do in class is easier than the homework quizzes and exams The best way to study is to do the Orion program questions on wileyplus because the quizzes and exams have hard concept questions.

She uses the generic textbook slides for lectures. She seems to have a lot of knowledge but sometimes get tripped up on how to explain concepts. She uses nametags and calls people out to answer questions. She does roll call every class, but attendance is just an extra credit grade. Overall she is not a bad teacher though, I have learned quite a bit

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: Horrible and would not recommend. She is the stereotypical adjunct lecturer. Not accessible at all either inside class or during office hours. Homework and tests are extremely difficult for an introductory class. Not helpful at all when students come fourth with questions about upcoming homeworks and tests. Avoid Staebell if at all possible.

Overall, easygoing nice lady.  Knowledgeable but moves very quickly so it's hard to keep up. Attendance is mandatory and the notes are textbook and definition based, while the tests are solving problems using the definitions.  Make sure to pay attention to the practice problems in class. All in all, she is very helpful and wants student success
Easy A, not what you'd expect of a tax class but Towner/Staebell gives good lectures and the 10 tax scenarios can be done in a group- easy A if you show up and put in some effort.
go to class, get the A
Disrespectful, gives 0 clarification, will not help if you try and email her for questions about online homeworks.
She is very discourteous during class. Often calls people out and isn't very helpful when responding to questions. Asks you to come for help if you need it, but won't give it to you.

Her PowerPoints are based directly off of the book, which is very helpful. Her homework assignments are clear and not busy work. You will need the textbook for homework questions, but her teaching is so good that it is not necessary to read. Lectures are interesting and very very helpful. Show up to class, pay attention, and you will do well.
Very nice and very helpful. Tests are open book.

Teaches directly from powerpoints, which are based on the textbook. Textbook isn't necessary, but homework usually covers info we haven't learned in class yet.  Grade breakdown: 2 tests 20% each, Final 20%, Homework 20%, One Project 15%,  and 5% for coming to class. Very nice person, but class can be kinda difficult at times.

SO BORING! Every lecture she reads the powerpoints that are exactly like the textbook. Reading the textbook is almost pointless unless you need it for an assignment on my accounting lab. Really into making you do assignments on myaccounting lab that are too hard for an entry level accounting class. Class average for our 2nd exam was a 68... ha ha
She's a nice lady and is pretty helpful.  Her test are very simple. The homework is much harder but still can be done.

This teacher is awful. She teaches, I use that term lightly, through powerpoints only. You can't learn accounting through powerpoints and then doesn't tell you what is going to be on the test so you are basically screwed. Don't take her class, its awful.

Michelle is a nice person and very casual professor, but packs so much material into the semester that it's hard to remember everything. She goes super quick through her lectures, so don't try to take notes from scratch - print out the slides and fill in the blanks as she goes. Her tests can be challenging, but they're not too bad.

I'm currently taking a course with this professor, and one red flag with her that will give you a C or a D in this course is that her writing assignments do not give rubrics. She is very critical of what you write and does grade on a subjective basis.
a lot of work

She requires attendance, but her lectures arent super difficult to get through. She had some guest artists meet us over Zoom, which was a very cool experience. It was also cool working with students from OCAD. Her accent can make it hard to understand certain things, but its not super awful. There are only a few things that are graded, so beware.
Shes nice most of the time but her comments and reactions to student questions are exceptionally rude. would not reccomend
Lectures are interesting and she makes them entertaining. Extremely nice and caring person. Sympathetic to students. You will not regret taking her!
Great professor, class was easy if you know basic research skills, very kind and caring person. Very easy grader, I do not know why she gets so many bad RMP reviews.

Alla is a fantastic teacher. Her 100 level lectures can be a bit dense so be ready for tons of note taking, but her passion really begins to shine through in her upper level classes. Her tests can be a bit difficult, they require a lot of memorization, but are generally multiple choice. Show up, be respectful and engaged and she will do the same

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: very arbitrary in her grading system. even if you use the textbook and the notes for your assignments, you most certainly will not get a grade in the 90s. very random with her remarks. i do not recommend you take this class

Prof Myzelev is a sweet lady and is really passionate about art history, but the content she teaches isn't that interesting, but it's easy enough to get an A if you keep up with group assignments and readings, which aren't difficult.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class', 'So many papers']
comment: A very nice lady but too many assignments for a gen-ed course. Also the syllabus was never followed throughout the semester, very confusing.

Myzelev is a great gal. For someone who doesn't love art, she at least kept the class interesting. It's an easy A if you go to class. She was accommodating during the pandemic and her TA's always did helpful review sessions. She also has a good sense of humor. I recommend this class for an easy gen ed.

comment: Horrible when it comes to lectures. I did not learn a single thing when it came to them. I suggest taking another fine arts credit.

Prof Myzelev is the sweetest woman to take a gen ed with. Her class was easy to understand and all of the tests followed the study guides and lectures. This lecture is beyond boring. Her tests are incredibly difficult and your whole grade is based off of attendance and 4 tests. Don't know why she is getting bad reviews??? Yes she has an accent, she knows she can be difficult to understand and welcomes students to ask for clarification. She has a great and bubbly personality and loves what she teaches. Group projects with tests. Office hours are good and responds to emails in a timely manner. Tests follow the lectures.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Dr. Myzelev is just a gem of a person. She is so nice and sweet and is super helpful. Gives great feedback and if you come to her, is willing to help. Reading the text book for her class is helpful although not needed. Good lecturer Does take attendance. I had such a great time in her class. Gives HELPFUL study guides for exams. Great professor

A lovely lady who is underrated, this class visual culture was interesting and easy. 10/10 loved it! go take this class right now with her!!!! just look through the slides, she gives you study guides which are very similar to the tests, and you'll be great.

The class is pretty easy but lectures are boring and there was like 10 group assignments that are really tedious. If you study the study guide for the tests, you'll at least get a 75%, the rest of it is based on things she says in class.

Only a midterm and a final paper. Uses a sign in sheet for attendance. Midterm requires a lot of memorization, paper is tough but she gives you work time in class and some guidance, sometimes unclear with her expectations. You can get away without reading but she asks questions during lectures so it's good to know answers and avoid awkward silences
