I had her for DANL 100 & 200. Loved her both times. 1st time in person, second time online. Lots of partner work. Will give clear feedback and is very helpful during office hours. Thick accent, but you get used to it.
She makes it easy to get a good grade, but very boring lectures.

Never did rate my professor because it wasn't needed prior. This is the lowest grade I have received at Geneseo, especially in Data Analytics. Picks favorites and developed assumptions. Lectures are meaningless and the course load is manageable. Need to find a better grading scale and have less group responsibility.

Dr. McGray is an extremely talented professor. She knows her stuff and teaches it very well. If you don't know basic music theory she will help you out but it has to be learned in the first couple weeks in order to understand this class. Keep up with the work (mandatory) and use the resources she gives you (optional) and you'll do great.

Dr. McGray is one of the best professors at Geneseo. She is extremely caring, kind, and understanding. However she also has clear expectations that make her an effective leader in the department and in ensembles. She is respected but it is because she respects her students. I would strongly recommend more people join Dr. McGray's ensembles.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Terrible with communication. He does not hold office hours (only by appointment) and he barely ever emails students back. The classes consist of him lecturing at the students the whole time. He takes a very long time to grade assignments, and it is hard to tell what your grade is during the semester. Would not take a class with him again.

He's super knowledgeable, he's just not great at teaching that knowledge. He's also mad disorganized and not a good communicator, which is not good considering that he's the department chair. He's funny though

Does not post on Brightspace AT ALL. if you miss a class, good luck! You'll have no idea what's going on the next class. Constantly says there is materials online but there are no emails and only vague descriptions of learning objectives per week. No links, pdfs, actual material. You can't even tell when or what is supposed to be due day to day.

Dont get me wrong hes a nice guy he just isn't the best at articulating what he wants to teach. What i do disagree, is that he is understanding. I left for a week due to family issues and was willing to teach me what I missed and let me hand in my stuff for credit. Just, not the best especially if you have very little back ground on music theory.

He is the worst professor I have ever had. Not only is he now the new department chair and power hungry, but he is entirely unprofessional. He is definitely knowledgable in music theory but knows nothing about teaching. He is incredibly condescending when students ask questions, everything asked is a burden.Take this class anywhere else if you can.
Horrible! Don't recommend

Dr. Masci is passionate about Music Theory in general, but this guy doesn't know how to teach. He has no textbook he wants us to buy, and it makes it confusing for me to learn the lecture material. He also gave us no resources for me to study for the final, and if you are required to take this course, you have to teach this course to yourself.

Repeatedly threatened to fail our writing requirement if we didn't fix our papers, even if we received an "A" on the paper. Directions are vague and he gets very offended and replies with passive aggressive comments. I stay on top of my work but at one point I had five papers due for him. You need to take him if you are a music major, but it's bad.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Masci is, at surface level, a really cool person, and cares a lot about music. I cannot however, say he is any good at teaching theory whatsoever. An extremely disorganized class, with no clear curriculum. Way too much homework, that he barely tells you how to do. And worst of all, after a year of this class, absolutely nothing is learned.

Checks to make sure students know what's happening before moving on, and often asks the class what will be most helpful at any given point (i.e. should we do more practice on this or move on?). Very approachable, and actually builds a relationship with students. Homework usually isn't graded, but you really have to do it. Don't skip solfege audit.

Masci is really a great guy. Easily my favorite professor on campus. I took this class because I was interested in being a music major, and he completely convinced me through his teaching. Very personable, very funny, and will take as much time as you need to get you to learn the topic. 10/10 would recommend.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: This professor is ABSOLUTELY amazing, and even when the material gets harder he makes sure everyone understands everything.  This class is very clear, well taught, and the enthusiasm this professor shows while teaching makes you love music theory even more.  Participation really matters, and if you don't go to class you won't understand anything.

Masci is a great guy and keeps things interesting. The class was challenging but he did his best to go over things and answer questions. Definitely need to go over notes and practice outside of class so you don't fall behind. Overall the class was fair. Don't fall behind or you'll never catch up. You must attend class or you'll be lost, no textbook

Easily one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. Yes, he's a genius and sometimes has trouble conveying what's in his head to the class, but he's so good with office hours and explaining things, and he's an extremely fair grader. The class isn't easy, especially if you don't have a musical background, but he makes it worth it.

Prof Masci is a super cool guy and he made Music Theory I interesting and enjoyable. But do not take this course if you don't have any background in music because you will get left in the dust! Prof Masci had a good amount of office hours available where you could ask questions and chat and his tests weren't difficult if you understood the material
Eh, OK teacher.  Pretty easy, no tests.

presented the material in a relatable way.  Clearly identified grading ruberic. No tolerance for goofing off but has a great sense of humor. encouraged attendance due to the college policy. Very little note taking, but notes that are taken will be used on the test or quiz. Its on the board, write it down. Loves movies.

Prof Adamson isn't too demanding as far as English professors go-however when I had his class-Sat attendance was required by the college...perhaps that's why he was soo cool. Definitely one of the more lively professors i've had.

Great Prof! he likes to tell stories that relate to the material and is a really funny guy. He's nice, understanding, and helpful. Reminded me of a fun highschool teacher. I wish i could take more of his classes! don't care too much for writing though. He's definitely a good choice when it comes to a prof.
He tells stories to help make class more interesting; quizzes are easy if you pay attention and there isn't any homework.  Easy class
quite disorganized but easy.  he tries to make class fun but attendance is mandatory, which i dont care for.  if u plan to go to every class, youll do fine
Nice guy. A required class for all business majors. It's boring beyond belief but he tries and he's understanding of how dull it all really is. He's friendly, geeky but fun.

VERY easy class, write 3 easy papers but don't do any work besides that, didn't have to read a single book all semester, great for an INTD class. I'm not a fan of sci-fi but the movies we watched were actually interesting (especially "stay") SO much less work than any other intd..
He is a very nice person.  This class is an easy A as everyone else has said. but, he gets behind schedule, and I learned more about his personal life than about the subject matter.
His class was very easy but even more boring. Nonetheless, it's an easy A and Adamson is a pretty cool guy.
Great guy, very helpful, keeps the class interesting and relevant to today

very good guy.  Wants students to do well and explain the material well.  Teaches topics til everyone understands and doesn't overkill the subject.  Test and easy and very little homework is required.  Textbook is only like $30.  An excellent class to take with a difficult work load for the semester

:Darkside of Technology. Nice guy, puts really good comments on your essays. easy to understand and very approachable and helpful. a lot of reading, but easy to do and essays are pretty easy as well. always willing to answer your questions. i really liked him.
Class was enjoyable. For the most part it was pretty straightforward and pretty easy. Requires minimal studying for A-
Very good professor. Just participate and read the material. It's very easy.
very nice professor. very easy and helpful
take this class with adamson, great information and good speaker

Tony is awesome. I had him for an 8:30 and his energy was incredible. His notes were very clear, and basically just by studying them from class you can do well on the test. He curved the last test by 8 points, so I ended up with an A in his class. Amazing teacher, I learned alot and my GPA was boosted.

Outstanding professor. As an alumni of Geneseo, he understand students and is always looking to help students. I took an 8:30am Micro class, his youthful energy and humor made the it enjoyable and kept lectures interesting. Notes were easy to follow and lectures complemented the textbook very well. Tests were challenging, but very fair.

she is very nice, but she doesn't teach. she expects the text to do that thru homework—fine, but the text is HORRIBLE. very confusing (and $$). she's disorganized, and doesn't offer much out-of-class help, just 20 minutes before class. lots of extra credit opportunities but doesn't add up to much. got an A and still felt like i don't know anything.

Prof. Kelly was really nice and made learning another language bearable. There is a lot of homework and class attendance is mandatory but the quizzes are easy. The tests are difficult but she outlines exactly what will be on them. I would recommend her to anyone anxious about learning Spanish.

She's a really good teacher compared to some of those teaching assistants that the school hires from Spain.  She teaches you a lot of tricks and hints in learning the language and makes learning Spanish bearable.  She gives a lot of HW, her two quizzes are a joke, but her exams are hard.  She goes over what exactly will be on the exam though.

Kelly is a nice teacher and it's just a matter of attending class. She takes participation seriously and gives a lot of homework. However, her test isn't so bad if you study. I liked going to her class.

Nice professor. All you want from a Spanish teacher is someone that doesn't expect so much from a college student learning a new language. Do your studying and you'll be fine...A is easily attainable in her class. There is homework but it is pass/fail. It is worth 15% of your grade...that's a free 100. Just do the work, get an A or B.

A really nice professor.  She is also helpful if you approach her.  She tells you what each section of each test is about, which makes the tests a lot easier.  She also lets you do extra credit.  I didn't like the class, but she was a pretty good professor.

She isn't a terrible teacher, but if you don't really like spanish I'd avoid her. She'll teach things on tests minutes before you take it, and her tests are often confusing and unmanageable. I'd say avoid her, but if you're a gamblin' man take a shot.
Good teacher. Helps when need be. Exams are not too bad. Homework is a joke.

She was not helpful at all in class.  Her tests weren't easy either and I know a lot of people who were seniors saying it was their hardest class they were taking.  She ended up giving me a B even though I don't know how she came up with that grade, but still I highly DON'T recommend her try Brea.  I've heard she's good

It wasn't until I got Gomez for 201 that I realized how boring this class was.  NICE lady, but pretty monotone, and you do lots of group work which sucks. She's also one of those professors that keep the exams after you get them back, so that didn't really help. She isn't difficult, but neither are some other professors, except they're less boring.

She means well but I didn't really learn that much. I think she's better with younger kids, she had us singing the alphabet and stuff in a college classroom like 6th grade. Between her in 102 and a weak 201 class I got my ass kicked in 202

Nice lady, but a little dry. My only gripe is the group work. Being forced to write group compositions just isn't fair, and your grade kind of suffers. However, easy tests, and obviously if you've taken Spanish before attendance isn't always mandatory. I'd recommend her, she's good enough for me.

Boring for me simply because I've taken Spanish before, but only for 3 HS years.  VERY easy, but very boring simply because I already know the material.  However, she is a nice woman, and the workload isn't anything to get stressed about.  Take it for the easy A if you've already taken Spanish.
the work is easy and the tests aren't bad, but its not a class you look forward to going to, she isn't very enthusiastic
Great Professor.  Keeps class moving.  Class can be challenging.
Definately take w/her.  Easy assignments (workbook, compositions, orals), very clear, easy tests.

Sweet teacher. She's not hispanic, but she's VERY clear. Her assignments are creative, her work is challenging enough, although she grades pretty easily. She's NOT boring at all. I guess because there's constantly something to do. She's awesome. Cute too
No Comments
Prof Beeson got married and is now Prof Tucker, look under her name.

Worst class I have ever taken, is way too hard for a 100 course. Only graded by two tests and an essay which he refuses to help with. Lectures are him reading from his notes about very dense philosophy books. This is NOT an introductory course. Doesn't curve tests even when most of the class failed. DO NOT TAKE.

If you hope to gain anything from Soffer at all be prepared to write everything down. He only lectures and has very little apparent structure to the course. He's obviously very intelligent and well-versed in his field, but he's not especially engaging and fails to perform the primary job of a 105 which is to improve college writing skills
Write down everything he says in lectures. No canvas, no slides, everything is verbal. Do not recommend at all.

I don't think he understands the fact that this is a philosophy 100 class. yes he is clearly a smart guy but it sounds like he is just standing in front of the class the whole time and just speaking and never getting to a single point. He has no outline to the class so no one has any clue what's going on

Passionate about philosophy. kind of snarky to students that ask questions. Doesn't use power points or any references on canvas everything is in class lecture off of his voice which is frustrating because he talks fast. Take good notes and don't skip class.

I thought phil of religion was interesting and even I had a hard time paying attention sometimes. Overall I really liked this professor, he has a certain old man charm I found endearing. you'll listen to him speak and know he's extremely smart. I thought the lectures were interesting, but that's all the class is so beware if that's not your thing

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Mixed review because I disliked the class. However, if you actually like philosophy you'll probably like it. Prof stands at the front of the class and talks the whole time and that's it. Only grades are midterm, paper, and final. I didn't go to class much and did decently. You don't need to buy the books because he explains all thoroughly.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This man is brilliant! One of the professors that is so smart it's difficult not to feel condescended on when they answer your questions. Admittedly antiquated teaching style--all lecture, punctuated with occasional hard-to-spell words he writes on the chalkboard. Very very insightful! Pay attention though

I took his HUMN class for 2 weeks and switched to another because I couldn't imagine having this professor for an ENTIRE SEMESTER. The only thing you would have to do is read a 30page lecture that were old essays from past students with chicken scratch as his notes on the side. He had about 3 papers and didn't let you know what the topic was about.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: This class was completely online this semester. There were no zoom meetings held or anything to go over any course material. Instead, he would sent us 30 page lecture notes of old essays that were barely legible due to all of his corrections and add ons. We had a total of three papers this semester and that was what our grade was based off of.

tags: ['Graded by few things', 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: Our class was completely online this semester. This was the absolute worst class I have ever taken online. He had no zoom meetings to discuss the material. Instead, he sent out 30 page lecture essays that were old essays from students. They were barely even legible since he crossed out so much. Our grade was based on 3 essays and they were hard.

Soffer's style of lecture is very old-fashioned; he stands in front of the class and talks the whole time. If you pay attention and take notes, however, you will have a much better understanding of Nietzsche than 99% of the wannabe hipster nihilists who claim to be the übermensch. Soffer reads papers thoroughly and gives good feedback.

I took Philosophy of Religion with him and it was a solid class. You passing is dependent on you going to class and taking good notes along with reading the text. We had two exams both consisting of shorter essays and one term paper. The class was difficult but not terrible He is an intelligent man and once you get to know him a very kind person.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: Lots of books with reading every night. Most likely will not get answers on tests without going to class. Doesn't write anything on the board. Plays the devil's advocate all the time which makes it hard to tell what the point he's trying to make is. Write down every word he says and then re-read for tests. 11 pop quizzes that help grade if you read

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: Not a good professor at all, probably one of the worst ones Ive ever encountered. His lectures are boring and he doesnt stay on topic, he makes you read a lot and gives pop quizzes and sometimes some of the questions are way too specific to get from reading it alone. Dont take him for HUM if you want to get a good grade, hes the worst.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He's actually awful. Definitely the worst professor I've ever had. He goes on and one about random topics that are never brought up again and doesn't give any details about the tests or papers and leaves you to fend for yourself as far as content. To sum it all up he fell asleep during the midterm

This class was 8000% harder than it had to be. He talks for 100 minutes with no break and then tests on things he spoke about for 30 seconds. I've taken a number of upper level religion and philosophy classes, and he is by far the hardest grader (and for a required class). The reading only helps for the quizzes, and the tests are entirely lecture

Comes off as a highly pretentious man though does have interesting points at times in his lectures. The biggest issue is that humanities is a requirement, however he is still highly rigorous in his grading. It would be understandable if it were for philosophy majors however most people honestly don't understand the literature

The grade is based on a midterm, a final, and a paper. Class is him talking the entire time on the book and his lectures are very boring but to get a good grade just write down everything he says and study it when it comes time for the test. You don't even have to read the books he explains them well plus the questions come from his lectures anyway

Soffer seems like a nice guy and is pretty funny at times, but has no visual aid for his lectures. The class is composed of solely him speaking. Be sure to take good notes and study often. The class is graded on three parts, a midterm, a paper, and the final exam, so if you mess up on one it'll be very difficult to pull your grade up.

Expects you to think like a philosopher, this isn't easy for everyone. Also gives random quizzes to make sure everyone is reading. Tests you have to just spit back out what he says in class, Papers are hard, no one does well. There're no power points or lecture notes, he just talks at you the whole time, if you miss something you're screwed

Take soffer for humanities! But only if you are willing to go to class and take good notes. Everything on the exams is explicitly stated in class. You don't even need to read the texts if you pay attention to his lectures, which are very animated and include several jokes. Grades papers a little hard but the exam grades make up for them.

Soffer is a great professor. Yes, the material for the class is very difficult, but since HUMN is required for everyone-- each section of HUMN will be hard. Soffer is from the philosophy department-- don't forget that when in his class. He is clear, fair, and very helpful outside of class. GO TO CLASS. He's great

This was the hardest class I've taken at Geneseo. He is able to spent a months worth of classes on 30 pages of text, and is terrible at explaining in a clear way. I never had any idea what he was saying. Also, if you don't write your essays/papers from his perspective or agree with his points, he'll mark you wrong. Never take him.

Really great professor. For everyone complaining about HUM, its the same everywhere you go. His lectures are straightforward, hes got a sense of humor, knows what hes talking about. HUM is all about going to class and taking notes, his exams are literally his lectures in question form. Just go to class- its not that bad and there are zero suprises
I am so glad I am done with humanities so I don't have his class. Class is a waste of time and absolutely boring. Goes on rants and you don't feel like you go anywhere in class. Do NOT TAKE for Hum!
Such a great professor.  Knows a ton, gives careful lectures, has hilariously dry wit and a sweet goatee.

OMG, do NOT take him for Humanities. His papers were nearly impossible, tests extremely difficult... I went to almost every single class, read all the works, took impeccible notes, and still struggled with the concepts. I did not enjoy my experience with this professor and I advise anyone to pick else to do your HUMN core with.

I took both Ancient Phil and Modern with him. He is by far the most comprehensive professor I've experienced in college. You will NEED to go to class to ace his tests, but he will tell you everything you'd ever need to know about the subject. Made me fall in love with philosophy

This class was nearly impossible! Every question was extremely specific which was insane considering the amount of material covered. Got a C+ even after talking with him. Got a 50 on one paper for not arguing from his perspective...Only considers philosophical viewpoints which are hard to grasp. You would be wise to avoid him!!!

Takes a philosophical view on all the books and the course. Doesn't feel like you make any progress with one class. In class essays are fine but the out of class papers are graded harshly. Went to his office hours and still got a crappy grade on the paper

probably the best-looking sixty-something year old in the u.s. of a. the table tennis mustve done him good. he can lecture throughout the class but the material is interesting and taught in an engaging way. if you come to class, you will probably learn more in one class than you learn in a full semester of many other classes.

Come to class, take good notes, and you'll be fine. Just don't tell him about rate my professor or he might be changing his exams up a bit ;) Great guy though with lots of insights! Fair and impartial in them as well.

Genius professor and funny guy. Plan on attending almost every class if you want to do well. Also, don't bother reading the books unless you feel you must. If you are interested in philosophy at all I would recommend taking this class, otherwise just go for an easier teacher.

If you can do well just by writing down lectures verbatim and remembering what needs to be parroted back on the exams, you'll be fine. Exams consist of a couple essay questions and no multiple choice so you really have to know your stuff.

Brilliant man, he knows everything.  He goes over the material in such detail that you could probably get by without reading the stuff if you just go to class and take really good notes.  Its a good intro class with low work volume and a great professor.

Pretty funny. The class can get tedious considering it's a lecture, but he lets students speak their mind and give their opinions about the texts. A lot of reading, but nobody really reads because he goes over it all in class. He may give quizzes if he finds out the class isn't reading though. Will give you an A if you beat him in table tennis.
Very interesting class if you want it to be.

He knows a lot about what he's talking about, but the problem is HE thinks he knows a lot about what he's talking about. I wasn't comfortable expressing any contrary opinions. Considerable reading, three tests, one paper...not a bad workload at all. I think the material is mostly interesting but it's more or less a straight lecture so it gets dull.

let me tell you about walt soffer.  first off, he is brilliant, second, he is thorough. i worked harder in preparing for his tests than all my other classes combined (talkin 30+hours) take about 10 pages of notes word for word from his lectures and youll do fine.  great for learning, bad for a GPA.. take him if u like a worthy challenge

This man is a genius. If you take a class with him, you will leave with more knowledge about the topic then you thought you could ever get in an undergraduate class. By far my favorite prof. He lectures all class, but if you mind, your not interested in the subject. The assignments are hard though. Come prepared to work.

If you are a free thinker, do not take "Reason & Religion" / INTD 105. I don't know if it has to do with the professor or not, but it was horirble. You baiscally had to be a robot, which is not my style at all. If you're comfortable with not thinking too much, you'd do well in that class, but I don't react well to not being able to think for myself

Smartest professor at geneseo and my favorite. makes the topics very interesting. have to read frequently but its not too much. don't miss class or you'll have trouble keeping up. I learned so much from him and he inspired me to read the great philosophers outside of class. he's also very approachable if you need extra help.

Took this class expecting a basic overview of philosophers from Plato to Hume (as the catalogue) states. Unfortunately, we made it only through 2 of 5 philosophters and about 15% of the reading planned on, meaning the tests and paper included topics and ideas far too complex for an introductory course. Would not reccomend for Phil 100.
great teacher, great ideas, actively involves class in discussion, have to read alot but tests are fairly easy
He is nice, but the class is very difficult to take notes in and tests are graded harshly. I would not recommend this particular course.

Walt Soffer is one of the few geniuses at Geneseo, and he rightly expects his students to be sharp enough to keep up. If you not interested in the subject matter (or learning in general), stay away. But if you actually want to come away with something, take his class.
One of the smartest teachers at Geneseo

He lectures are very hard to understand at times. Most questions he responds to by saying "we'll get to that later" His paper topics are very vague and he grades very harshly, unneccesarily so in my opinion. Only take him if you absolutely must.

At times the topic is difficult to understand. I'd recommend either learning excellent shorthand or just recording the lectures. Very helpful when you ask for further clarification. Overall I liked him.

Wasn't the easiest class, but he's pretty easy to understand. He's knowledgable about the topic and is always available for help. I thought he was pretty fair. I wouldnt recommend slacking off though.
I think he just read his boring notes to the class.  Another of those who made me hate philosophy. Comes off as very arrogant as well. But not a bad guy outside the classroom.
very complicated and hard
very confusing!

Listen kids. He may be okay at philosophy... but please... DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR HUMANITIES.  He consistently gets the WORST SOFIs. He's terribly boring.  Oh and you will do poorly because you have to decipher his philosophical jargon to learn.

This guy has a lot of insights, but can certainly ramble on for quite a while before getting to one.  Don't be fooled by that stoic face either, he has a highly refined sense of humor that he likes to show now and again.  I liked him overall.
i can't say it any better than the last person, so i will just say "ditto."
Rambles on and no, never really emphasizes what is really important to know.  Very vague writing assignment is 40% of the grade.  Hard grader.
No Comments
No Comments
BORING- but cool guy.  He's a tough grader too- just wants what he says.
A wonderful person. Very balanced.
A VERY nice lady. Presents all sides of an argument and is by far the most balanced teacher I have had. She is a common middle of the road person who cares about her students.

Probably the worst teacher I have ever had.  If, and this is a big if, she shows up for class , she teaches straight from the book and usually can't give you any sort of intelligent answer to any questions you may have.
Honestly, she isn't all that bad. Really helpful and willing to work one on one. Not the best clearly but at least nice and more or less communicates the material.
Terrible teacher, Tests on stuff not covered in class, lessons are disorganized.

Like others said, she didnt know how to teach and did waste the class time a lot. Just used materials the book publisher made. But very easy to get an A if you do practice quizes and exams on the website, do hw, and read the textbook.

She is the worst professor ever!! Doesnt know how how to teach the class and gives impossible tests and she doesnt even know the right answers to the questions, if you can take this class with another person DO IT!!!

This is one of the worst professors I have ever had the displeasure of associating with.  She is a complete tool to the McGraw Hill textbook company and gets her powerpoints/homework/some test questions from them.  Absolutely no teaching skills here.  If you want to ruin your life take her class.

Horrible teacher, takes to much time reading off premade power point slides and not enough time explaining how to actually do the work.  She puts questions on quiz/tests that she has never mentioned anything to you about in class.
terrible teacher, multiple choice exams are awful and tricky

Susan is great!!! She is so kind and caring. She isn't necessarily organized, but she makes up for it in her flexible and understanding nature. If you are taking this class, I highly recommend taking it with her! It is a lot of reading, and you do need the textbook, but you will do well and learn so much!

Professor Redditt was overall good. Sometimes she was a bit unclear with due dates, and us students would have to get it out of her. Reading the textbook is important, as class lectures are mainly based on the readings. She talks about her own life experiences quite often. She was a very understanding person and professor, and was respectful.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Prof. Redditt truly cares about her students. She gives amazing feedback on essays and allows the class to engage in meaningful conversations. The course is built around the textbook, so she relies on that for most homework questions and class discussions. Overall, an amazing, funny, and caring professor who wants all of her students to succeed.

She is awesome! Super funny and sweet, but you absolutely need to read the textbook. A majority of the course is participation in discussions based on it. She is fundamentally caring and is willing to help you through anything. She is super accessible outside of class (even though she's an adjunct with multiple jobs) and wants everyone to succeed

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']
comment:
Love this professor, she is caring, organized, and passionate. Her lectures are fun even on thought subjects. However, be ready to read around 5 to 6 books during the semester, most of the time in a week. 
The exams are pretty accessible and sometimes creativity-based.
I LOVE Babovic, I will never not rave about her! I took her class my first semester and second semester, I'm taking an 8am class just so i can take her 453 class. she's awesome.

Very nice in person, but grading is unclear (doesnt say were she takes off points) and will stress you out over low grades. Weekly essays, had to quit my weekend job in order to do well in class. Grading is not really equal to level of work. She did pull through and I got an A--but be prepared.

The entire geology department is amazing! I only had Scotty for the lecture but he was great. He's one of my favorites!
Awesome! Can't wait to take more classes with Scott

Giorgis is really into what he teaches. Can be confusing at times. Diligently read the powerpoints and do the class activities, and you should be good to go for the three exams (incl. final). Very good professor. Helpful during office hours. Makes class very interesting. Tests are fair, but I had to work hard for an A.

Scott is just a wonderful guy and makes the class fun, interesting, and intellectually challenging. This class is all about understanding complex geological processes that actually matter. great

Scott's a really great professor and person. His class isn't very difficult, but it still requires a level of outside work especially leading up to exams. He makes a subject that lots of people would consider boring very interesting. I never wanted to miss class.

not that the other geology professors are any different but Scott is a fantastic guy. passionate about the subject, extremely interesting lectures. I never want to miss class. really friendly and works with you to get the best grade possible. The TA's for his lab are awesome too. Take This Class!

The only disappointing about this class was finding out that he's already married. He's a really approachable, really awesome professor who is passionate about his subject and makes it easy to understand more complex problems. Probably one of the best professors I've had! :)

Fantastic professor/lab instructor.  He made geology interesting to the point in which I might just minor in it.  He is VERY approachable and wants you to do well.  The exams are easy as long as you study your notes and read some of the textbook.  Labs are easy/fun.  Take GSCI with Giorgis if you can.
Scott is Great!!
Really cool guy.  Really cool class.  He looks like a velociraptor.  That isn't an insult.  I mean it in the best possible way.
He is such a nice guy and trys really hard to keep your interest. Definately show up to class, take notes, and pay attention. He is really passionate about what he does.
Scott makes the class interesting, he knows a lot of information. He is very enthusiastic about the topics which makes it more fun.

I am thankful I had the opportunity to take a class with him this semester.  He is helpful and passionate about what he does.  Labs are fun.  Tests are appropriate for the class level.  Wish I had more professors like him

Giorgis made this class very interesting. You could tell he had a deep interest in the material. The book isn't too expensive. Labs tests were unfairly hard, because the labs themselves were so simple that they didn't adequately prepare students for them (the tests). Study a little, go to class, take notes, and you'll have fun.

He is an amazing professor. The course is really easy for gen. ed. and he makes it fun and interesting. Quizzes in class are very easy and you got points for putting your name on the paper. During tests he lets you complete it once then do it again with classmates. There is no homework and the labs are a joke.
He is really a great professor who is passionate about what he's teaching and also knows how to teach. His tests are pretty straight forward. If you need to fulfill a science core, take it with him!

lol dude, he's a really good teacher, its just too bad the class sizes are so big. if you have even a remote interest in science you'll probably be entertained.  half the stuff you look at is cool current event stuff like the tsunami near india and volcanos and stuff. the rock stuff is boring, but i mean, its just part of the course you know?

dont take this guy. hes got mad personality issues. mad hard class. killer tests. trust me on this one. go with farthing. it aint worth all this pain to study rocks. he also mad mellow so hed be sayin quiet down 100 times a day.

I hate science but acutally liked this class. Great teacher, explains everything and tells you what what will be on tests.  There is a group part on all lecture tests.  Lab quizzes/tests are harder but lab it only 1/3 of overall grade.  Very helpful and easy to talk to when I needed help.  Take this class with him!

Over all good teacher. Didn't use the book. Tests can be a challenge but you get to work together on a portion.  Little homework, labs weren't too hard.  Makes material easy to understand for students. He can be funny too.
A solid teacher, very friendly, but not very helpful during office hours. Sometimes he expects you to figure things out, that you do not understand at all.

Great professor. Makes content really easy for nonmajors to understand.  Tests are pretty easy especially since u can work together on a portion.  Book is useless u dont use it at all so save your money

Great professor! Giorgis is the best! He is very straight-forward and fun to listen to. Very good lecturer and very friendly guy. Everything about the class is very concise and understandable and he is helpful with his review sessions and the chance to take exams twice.
amazing teacher! he makes everything interesting and  all easy to learn! best class i toke ever
Loved this class.  Made me want to continue on for graduate degree.  Scott is awesome

Cool guy, explains things well and knows main concepts, although not very knowledgeable about the subject (small details that you can just look up in a book). Book is useless, lab is boring and can be hard. Tests are fair, material is easily remembered but you MUST MUST goto class, otherwise you're screwed :>

first test was really hard, second was really easy. lab is probably the worst.  no actual hw..reading isnt necessary.  he's boring but id rather be bored then struggling to understand rocks.  dont be fooled though, its not as easy as people say.

Makes the class as interesting as it can be. he cracks funny jokes, he's just overall goofy. Really great guy. Easy class. If you go (you don't have to read) the tests are based on in class material.  Easy A.
Sooooooo boring!!!! But he's a nice teacher.

i think hes a pretty cool guy. hes real young and likes to ruffle his hair. i like his straight forward approach, but can see how others might find it boring. overall very nice, and a fine dresser i must say.

Just realize that GSci will never be fun. He's a very nice guy who will really help you out if you see him in office hours. Most people pulled their grades up with the Lab exams, but it was the opposite with me. I had a 95 average in class, but the lab pulled me down to a B+. Not a bad class.
He's a nice guy but the class certainly isn't an easy A if you are really terrible at science.  His class is excessively boring and he reads straight off of his notes.  Don't take the class

Great guy/proffesor overall.  He's young and goofy, but if you just take the notes and listen in class you should be fine.  He makes some pretty good jokes sometimes and listening to him fumble his words every once and awhile makes for a good laugh.
He doesn't seem to know what the heck he's doing, and he wears socks with sandals.  Tries to answer questions during class, but usually doesn't know the answer.

Omg, how boring can somebody be? The only things he seems to know are what's in his notes. Talk about a sleeper class. It's easy tho...Just take the notes, study a lil, and you'll be fine. Don't ask questions tho...he wont know the answer.

Easy quizzes and tests but boring lectures. He's really nice but I can't help falling asleep sometimes... And there are moments when it looks like he doesn't know much at all except what's in his notes.

I loved this class.  He is one of the best, if not the best professor that I've had.  He is young, easy to talk to, and really knows how to relate the material to you.  Any class you take with him will be awesome!!
This class is pretty easy.  He is a nice guy and his tests ate fair and based on notes.  If you study for tests and go to class you will do good. I recommend him for this class
he is a good teacher, just sometimes he gets lost and forgets what he is saying. He is still young and I am sure that he will get better as he goes along.
He's new--he's young--his tests are fair and are based on what he talks about in class (not just random obscure facts that mean nothing)...what's not to like?
AVOID TAKING HER AS A PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS

Great and caring professor. She is super understanding if you have to miss class for a legit reason, just let her know and don't take advantage of her. Little bit of a tough grader on papers but helps you improve on them. Tests are straightforward and you review exactly what's on them beforehand which is amazing. She's hysterical too. Pop quizzes.

Best professor I've ever had!! Cannot recommend highly enough. Really cares about her students and you'll learn a lot. You absolutely have to read, and that can be a lot, but taking a class with Professor Savage is the best decision any Geneseo student could make

Class is only 2 papers and 2 tests and 5-8 pop quizzes. Papers are only about 4 pages and pretty easy to write. Pop quizzes are 2 questions with really easy questions (if you read)

comment: I took professor Professor Savage for intro to philosophy, which I thought would be an easy A.. it wasn't. tags: ['Tough Grader', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

Prof Savage is a very interesting professor. She really makes you think about the concepts and opens your eyes to new ones. She is super helpful in explaining things if you don't understand. comment: She's a very confusing professor in my opinion. The topics were difficult to follow along with. There are weekly readings, usually followed by pop quizzes so make sure to READ!!
Awesome person and professor. Really easy class - just a couple of exams and short essays. Class is very interesting and Heidi does a great job explaining difficult content.

Heidi is the GOAT. She's hilarious and knows that you're not going to show up to every class period. Test study guides are super helpful, and if you can formulate your writing to any sort of philosophical manner, you're cruising. Took PHIL237 and PHIL100 with her and pulled an A and an A-. Highly recommend

Heidi is a nice person, and she's actually a pretty good philosopher. That being said, this class kind of sucked with her. tags: ['Get ready to read', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Heidi is SO nice and also funny! She can be a little disorganized when it comes to what you're supposed to be doing to prepare for class though, which makes it difficult to stay on top of things. She's VERY understanding, will work with you, and truly wants you to succeed. Difficult grader on papers, but tests are easy if you use the study guide!

Do NOT be mistaken - this is not an Easy A by any means. Heidi is freaking hilarious and I think she has a lot of smart things to teach you - but her pop quizzes are very specific regarding dates. Best teacher Alive its simple. Do as she says and work ahead of the class

Seriously take a class with her. She's awesome. Takes student input on assignments, tests are wicked easy, a little bit of a tough essay grader but there are only two short ones. Class is interesting and she is hilarious and respectable. I highly recomend her

Dude if you can't pass a class with Heidi you should just drop out. Probably the best professor at this school, she just wants people to learn. She will do everything in her power to help you succeed.

Worst professor I've had here. Her lectures are just her reading off a timeline. The pop quizzes consist questions like "what is the exact date of 'insert random event?'" She is unorganized and confusing. She gave 0s to 1/3 of the students in our class on our paper, so obviously an unreasonably harsh grader. Save yourself, do not take her.

The nicest professor I have encountered in this school. Her attitude towards education reflects how teaching should be done. Less focus on cramming information into your head for you to regurgitate and more discussion. Tests aren't bad, review sesh.  2 papers per semester, lax with deadlines. She'd rather you tell her it will be late and do it well

She can be very confusing at times and go off on rants but if you go to class you will be sure to pass. She has you write 2 papers that are easy and you have 2 tests. She's very good about working with you if you miss class or if you don't understand something. She's very chill and completely understands that you have a ton of stuff going on.

Prof Savage is awesome. She made me look forward to a 8:30 lecture & I am NOT a morning person. Shes a great philosopher, I learned a lot from her. Very fair on grading & was understanding & helpful when I had missed a few classes because of the winter weather (I commute from the city). She's really funny too. Def take a class with her if you can!

Savage is awesome. She really doesn't care if you go to class or not, but it definitely helps if she gets to know you. She wants people to learn over the course of the semester, but will curve if the grades aren't good. Pretty easy A.
Go to her reviews. Dont have to read the book and she doesnt care if you go to class.

Professor Herzman is awesome!  She is so approachable and willing to help.  I really enjoyed the way she teaches.  This was not my first (or second or third) choice for INTD, but I'm glad it's the one I ended up taking.

Professor Herzman is awesome. It's not the most interesting class, but you'll most likely get a good grade out of it. She lets you submit a paper as many times as you want for it to be re-graded without penalty. C'mon! Go to her office hours for input on papers or just to talk. She's a wonderful woman and a great professor.
do not take this class -.-

my crit reading's 790, writing's 770, and i'm getting a B in this class. Do not take this class if you have any self-respect for your writing, unless you enjoy your writing being disintegrated into fundamental bits by a teacher who's resume barely suffices for high school.

Professor Herzman is the cutest woman you will ever meet! I had her for Women in Work and the class overall was quite interesting. She doesn't seem to give over a B+ but she lets your write the papers over and get you that A. Shes thoughtful and its a fun class!

Very nice and helpful, but this was class VERY boring. Bad Guys in Lit was a marginally acceptable course. Don't expect anything mindblowing because it's fairly straightforward, and we really didn't just focus on "bad guys," just kind of looking at the books in general. Prof. Herzman is fairly knowledgeable and allows ample opportunity for rewrites and such, but the class overall was just lacking.

A very nice little old lady but very boring. Reading material was good, but discussions werent what I expected. No one talked as she couldn't engage the class. I would sit in her class and daydream the entire time. Unlimited amount of paper rewrites which is a plus.

I just recall her being a nice, easy going woman, but she couldn't engage the class while lecturing.  Kind of soft spoken, and the class just dragged since so many kids were day dreaming and sleeping since it happened at 9AM, and thus nobody participated. She does let you rewrite papers an unlimited amount of times though, so that's a plus.

All I remember from Bad Guys in Literature was it was a very long and boring class . The class would take forever since her voice never really carried and everyone slept. You can rewrite papers and such, but I never really felt her grading was consistent. I got a B, but I wish I could have taken something else.

Prof Herzman's grading system is pretty screwed up.  She grades your paper twice, and even if you do everything she asked you to do she wont give you anything higher than a B+.  The class was definitely not what i thought it was going to be like.  I enjoyed most of the reading material though.

She is such a nice lady. You people are ridiculous if you think she is anything other than nice and helpful. She wants nothing more than to help you with your writing and gives you every oppotunity you want to get the grade you want. Class is easy if you try at all

She is a mean mean lady. She makes assumptions about who you are. She considered me to be slacking off when I was really trying my hardest. I don't apperciate some of the things she said to me about my high school education being lost on me. That really hurt. Overall I think she is a big witch.

I thought this class would be very interesting and although she is a nice person the class sucked. It was so boring and the material covered had nothing to do really with bad guys in literature. I would not reccommend this class.

Nice woman but a boring class.  I felt bad because so many kids were out cold when she spoke, but the class was boring.  The courseload is reasonable, but the grading sometimes is not, it's inconsistent.  Average difficulty INTD 105 course, but there're probably some better ones out there.

Although the idea behind the class seemed good, the class itself was not. The woman is a moron, pure and simple. Her class was nothing but awkward silence because she couldn't carry on an interesting, much less coherent discussion. I wouldn't recommend Bad Guys in Lit to my worst enemies.

Okay, the class itself was okay, but she was the most confusing grader ever.  One day you would get a c, the next day, an a.  After awhile, it became apparent she was more high school teacher than anything else, and we just dominated the class conversations making them as ridiculous as possible.

Bad Guys in Lit is a fair course, 2 essays, 2 papers, and some journals, not a real heavy courseload.  You get unlimited opportunities to rewrite your papers, plus she's very helpful during office hours.  Granted the class gets boring at times, I'd still recommend taking Bad Guys in Lit.

She's nice and wants you to succeed.  Sometimes I felt things were tedious or really specific, but overall it's not a very difficult class.  It's a speaking class, so participation and attendance are very important.  If you do your work and come to class, you'll be good.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: She was very helpful and she will like you if you are in class everyday. But beware, she stresses participation heavily and will call on students at random.

Love her! I took her again and found this class to be fascinating. It actually is relevant, in class discussion was fascinating and she always told us what would be on the quizzes. Definitely would take her again if I could! Great prof!

Professor Agostinelli is awesome! She gave tons of extra credit in this class and told us exactly what would be on every single quiz beforehand. She gives a lot of helpful feedback and makes lectures so interesting! Her classes are some of the few Spanish classes I feel I can apply to real life after college. Highly recommend!!

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: -extra credit opportunities (although you get very little points) -easy oral exams (she tells you topics before hand) -super strict with attendance (DON'T BE LATE) -Although the class wasn't that difficult, I found her to be extremely biased toward the white kids, she likes to call on people when their face shows they're confused -participate!

She is a nice person who teaches an interesting subject. Some assignments can feel pointless, but they are pretty short when you do get them. I recommend.

Professor Agostinelli was extremely unfriendly and unapproachable. Her comments during class created a tense and anxious learning environment. Thank goodness for her because she is basically the only Spanish teacher who does not teach literature. Hardly a teacher at all really, kinda funny I guess but mostly just unforgiving and unapologetic. Gives no indication of your grade, has a crazy inconsistent agenda and I wouldnt take her class again. I did well, but I take spanish to learn it not for an easy grade

Young, engaging,organized, very understanding, competent, and helpful. Considering the class I'm taking is Oral Communication, she is adamant about everyone participating. I enjoyed this class and learned a lot, I could focus on learning rather than just studying to pass a test because she doesn't give tests! Participate everyday for an easy A and do your projects, she gives the rubric, just follow it and she will even look it over before you turn it in! You have to work in partners a lot, not too exciting,  but easy

If you can get on her good side within the first few weeks of the semester you'll have an easy time, but if she doesn't like you it will be very obvious and you will get called on a lot in class. She seemed really dull and uninterested in the course. She not engaging at all in my opinion.

Definitely take her. She wants to see her students succeed, seeing as she's a student herself. She's EXTREMELY FAIR - but don't take advantage of her kindness. For all my fellow non-fluent Spanish speakers, she actually speaks at a reasonable pace so you can understand her. Take her!

I had the opportunity to take him twice this semester and I have to say he is tough when it comes to exams, but seems more relaxed with the papers. Dr. Raynor is a very intelligent professor I will give him that. However, he is probably the most arrogant person in geneseo. He does not allow you to do well in classes even his 200 levels which feel like 300 levels and is blatantly rude when you ask questions. He also was the least understanding professor I had during the current pandemic.

Dr. Raynor has a lot of expectations and you should definitely take his class seriously to pass. It's a lot of work but it will pay off. It was a flipped classroom style so get ready for a lot of group projects, presentations, and participation. Office hours can help a lot.

He's okay. You can tell he's extremely educated and has done so much work in the field, but I felt like the class was boring. I never knew how to study and he emphasized how difficult it was... Not bad, but just okay

Dr. Raynor is an intelligent guy, but not a great teacher. His tests for 200 lvl classes are more like 300 lvl tests. Very smart professor. He is very strict about no cell phone use or talking in class. He is a great teacher and obviously knows a lot about what he is teaching.  He is very particular about how you write your emails to him; he wants them to be professional.

Dr. Raynor is not the most intellectually stimulating professor at SUNY Geneseo.  I can say that he knows his topic so well that he can go over students heads.  He does demonstrate a willingness to meet with students during office hours.  Very professional.

Professor Raynor's late policy while taking his Sports and Exercise Psyc class was what's really annoying.  Some of his teaching lessons are fun and interactive but he's very anal about being tardy. The majority of students who wanted to go into clinical psych before this class are not afraid to and don't want to. Hard grader, deflated my GPA

Dr. Raynor is one of the toughest professors I have ever had. His tests are really difficult, even with three weeks of studying, I still received a poor grade.
