Raynor is a very nice guy. Class material is interesting and notes are easy to take with his pre-posted power points (although they have blanks so you need to go to class). He's funny and is clearly knowledgable about the subject, unlike some other professors in the Psyc Dept.

Dr. Raynor is very helpful in his office hours and is really knowledgeable about this topic. He has so many years of experience in the field and it really shows when he teaches. He expects a lot out of you in writing the paper, but he's there every step of the way. Tests can be tricky, but if you study and ask questions in class, you'll gain a better understanding of the material. I loved this class and recommend taking it.

Spent all four years at Geneseo, my least favorite person I've met BY FAR. Arrogant and talks down to anyone who asks a question. Completely unreasonable when you talk to him. I've been an athlete since I was 5 and competed through college, yet he makes this course ridiculously hard - even with countless hours of studying. My only nonA in psych(B-)

Awesome guy and loves what he does. Classes are interesting and engaging. Love taking the course, but pisses me off it ruined my 4.0. Now I can't ever get that. Having said that, it's pretty god damn hard to get an A.

Raynor is a great professor. He clearly loves what he does and seems to have the wisdom of a man twice his age. He's always willing to talk psych with his students. Nice guy. Class was tough but he teaches it well.

Dr. Raynor is great. He goes through his notes pretty fast, definitely print out the powerpoints so you don't miss anything. He's very helpful and his examples are clear. I didn't find his tests hard at all, but you have to go to class, read the book and study. I would recommend him for any class.

Very engaging and interesting lectures with lots of helpful and vivid examples. Shows good movies too. Tests are all MC and pretty hard, need to read chapters meticulously if you want an A. Project is tough if you haven't taken Research Methods beforehand. Very enjoyable class overall especially if you're into sports or exercising.

Raynor is a great professor.  I loved abnormal psych and I would definitely be willing to take another class with him.  He is easy to understand, shows videos to demonstrate concepts, and will do extra research for you if you ask him a question and he doesn't know the answer.  He has a good sense of humor and is very approachable.

He is a fantastic professor. If you show up to his office hours or ask for extra help he will do everything he can to help you. You can tell he loves the material he is teaching. If you take 352 with him be prepared to work insanely hard, but it's worth it.

Great professor. He made sure we really understood the reality rather than just the words behind psychological conditions, I loved the textbook, and he was very clear. If you ask him a question he doesn't know the answer to, he will look it up and mention it next class. Terrific, will definitely take him again.
good teacher...he shows lot of a videos which is always nice but is especially helpful for this class

Dr. Raynor is very clear in his expectations. He's a nice guy, and is willing to help both inside, and outside of class. My one complaint would be that he leaves blanks in P.P. notes online in order to stimulate active listening. But, if you miss a class, you're screwed because you can't look up what you missed. overall, I would recommend him.

Dr. Raynor is very nice but pretty tough. He made health psyc. much more difficult than it needed to be. He even sprung another project on us towards the end of the semester, as if there wasn't already enough to do. The only tests are the midterm and final and there is a TON of material from class and the book to know! Lots of projects too!

Do not ever ask him for a recommendation for Graduate school, or anything else. He will talk about your good qualities but will also point out ALL of your bad qualities. Not what you typically look for a professor to do for a letter of recommendation.
abnormal was interesting and he is a great professor who knows his stuff, although tests are hard-even when you read the book
Don't get me wrong, the material is very intresting, but his test's are impossible.Overall I would not recomend this course, especially since I took the course as a freshman.

Dr. Raynor is a good prof, I've done well in 2 of his courses. He gives a lot of examples and he has a lot of experience with the topics he teaches. He genuinely cares about his students and will help whenever you need it.
this class is hard for a 200 level.  I read the book n studied n didnt do that great.  He gives notes tho on powerpoint n tries to be interesting but overall i woudl not recommend
Dr. Raynor will go out of his way to help you, both outside and during class. He is very intelligent and cares about his students and the subject being covered. He's worth checking out

Dr. Raynor is a great professor! All of his lessons are extremely clear and his notes are given to you before hand in the form of PowerPoint. There are two tests, one debate, and one term paper. The tests were fine if you study, and he doesn't use the textbook too much (good, because it's boring). Overall, a really great guy and a great professor.

he's a jerk. the class is so boring. he tries to act like a college kid by saying "that's whack" and other ghetto language, but can't pass it off as being anything other than a weird old man who likes to swear in class.

She stated her beliefs and tells everyone if they are uncomfortable with that then they should drop the course. She prides herself on never loosing a student to mental health, yet if the student is not an English Major then she believes "they are less than", her words during class. She is funny, she can be friendly, she can be understanding.
You must read every story in great detail and she will call you out directly when you're wrong. You must participate in class, please do not take if you're shy!

I LOVE MARIA LIMA. She is so funny and a great professor! I can't wait to take more classes with her. We have three papers and you can revise them till it is an A. If you are shy and have social anxiety don't take her class; you must participate.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: She is by far the worst professor I have ever taken. She is extremely unprofessional and disrespectful to her students who have different opinions than her. She dismisses ideas that are not hers. I was referred to as "white boy" in her class because she did not care to learn my name.

I learned a lot from Maria and I enjoyed the small class environment. The short stories we read were amazing. I will say she takes attendance and counts participation in each class so you need to put in effort. She lets you revise papers and gives feedback. If you want to do well you will, but I her teaching style might not be for everyone.

I get the feeling that most of the people who dislike Maria Lima simply have bad political opinions. She has strong opinions but they are correct and well-founded, and some of y'all aren't ready to hear them. Which is why this class is uncomfortable for some people. I'll admit that she is unprofessional and unconventional though.

Lima has a very unique personality. She will seem awful at first but I ended up learning a lot from her. She wants you to pass and if you attend each class, she will help you through the papers. We were only given two papers and as long as you attended, you would succeed well in this class. I have learned so much and did not regret it :).

The class is discussion based and attendance/participation is MANDATORY. The readings are very interesting so theres always something to say during the discussions. The class is made up of two essays and one led discussion. You're allowed to keep turning in your essay and making revisions until you get an A. Take her class you won't regret it.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']
comment: you will not get an A if you don't participate. that's why I got a b+, you sit in a Socratic circle and discuss the reading that you did on your own before class. I got A's on the paper but since I didn't talk that much in class I got a b which stinks. she also has a mouth and will not shy away from calling kids out and calling them names

Maria Lima is possibly the most stubborn professor I have come across at Geneseo. She cancels class with the worst reasoning, and shushes students, but makes participation a priority. If you shush a student, obviously they are going to be afraid to participate in the future.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: My god is Maria Lima one of the worst teachers I have every had.  She goes off on tangets about herself, that are not only innapropriate for a professional classroom setting, but are completely irrelevant to the classroom time. She boasts to the class that she is on a tenure and can't get fired, so good luck putting up with her bullshit...

Professor Lima prioritizes participation, but leaves me frustrated being that she doesn't let anyone speak. I am doing poorly because "I don't participate", but apparently it's fine when she rambles off for thirty mins, and ends class 45+ mins early (CONSISTENTLY) because she booked a lunch, or a meeting during our class time. Terrible professor.

I really wanted to enjoy taking a course with Dr. Lima, but she is so involved in her own expertise that if she doesn't enjoy your paper/project topic she will immediately disregard it. Very partial grading, frequently refers to "smart" and "dumb" students and spends minutes at a time talking about her own intelligence. Don't waste your time.

Professor Lima prioritizes participation; however, she never lets her students talk. She talks on and on without thinking her students might be confused. My class literally doesn't know what's going on because she's so unstructured.

tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Maria has too much going on inside her head. If you don't agree with her, you'll get patronized and targeted throughout the semester. Introverts stay away. Strong opinions and not entirely sure what the purpose of the class actually was.

She's funny, but she is terrible at teaching. Her expectations are unclear and it doesn't seem like the class is structured at all. You're only graded on five papers, but she does let you revise once. She can be extremely rude but also extremely forgiving. She's hard to figure out.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'So many papers']
comment: Shes hilarious, but a really bad professor. Hates canvas so things are hard to find. Not very clear on anything. Made a lot of students cry. I wouldnt recommend unless youre passionate about the content and are ready for a challenge, because boy will she give you one. Also doesnt respect pronouns.

I took her Black Humanities class excited to learn but felt like her goal was to prove how much she knew instead of educating us. She will call you out in class and shut you down leaving students afraid to participate, but then gets frustrated when no one talks. One good thing about the class is she does let you revise your essays but good luck...

I took her Black Humanities class and it was disappointing. Professor Lima is strongly opinionated and won't let you forget it. Any opinion or idea you have will be shot down. Her advice is non constructive and she is unapproachable. She will embarrass you in class and is easily annoyed. Unless you want to lose sleep over her grading, DO NOT TAKE.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: I absolutely love Maria. She is very intimidating and strongly opinionated however this is what I really enjoyed about her class. Teaches unlike any professor I've had before, some students take that her being rude and unprofessional but I found her to be incredibly entertaining and interesting. She takes you out of your comfort zone, def worth it.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor Maria Lima is hit or miss. She is very well respected in the English Literature department and is very very smart. She is extremely outgoing but if you show up and participate you will learn a ton from her. All your works are "works in progress" so you can revise papers as much as you want until you get the best grade you can.

Maria Lima is a great English teacher. Although she has strong opinions, she has an open mind and will hear out your arguments. Participation matters, but the class is so engaging it shouldn't be difficult. She will help you revise your paper until it's an A if you meet with her. She gives extra credit opportunities as well.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Dr. Lima is extremely offensive and unprofessional in the classroom. She shares too much information about her personal life and is so disrespectful to her students. If you don't have the same opinions as her then don't say anything because she will not like your papers. She is very rude and will call you out in front of the class. DO NOT TAKE!

Not hard to get an A in her class but not worth it. She can be super disrespectful, close minded, and unprofessional. She crosses the line, and you're doing yourself a favor if you choose not to take her. If you don't share her opinion or see something differently than her, get ready to be attacked about things irrelevant from class. AVOID.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Maria is a great teacher and will help get your writing in shape for the english department. She allows revisions until your paper is an A and meets with you to go over any revisions. Not strict about deadlines. She's very outspoken which some people don't like but is cooler than seems at 1st impression. Need to talk at least once a class for an A.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Maria is a little intimidating at first, but she really does want you to succeed and will work with you to improve. Will help revise your papers to perfection with no due dates, and is very understanding as long as you communicate with her. Class is very participation-heavy, though (she expects you to talk at least once every class).

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Maria is an extremely bright woman and because of that her class can be very interesting but she is very outspoken and it can come off as rude and sometimes disrespectful.  If you are going to take her class be prepared to be told you are wrong/stupid, she only accepts ideas that she agrees with and there is no room for other opinions or ideas

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: My biggest issue with Maria is her use of scare tactics. If you have speaking anxiety or are just shy to speak in class or under a lot of pressure, whatever you do, do not take class with Maria ever. All she expects is participation, you could utter out complete garbage and it would still be better than not talking. Not worth it.

We read A LOT in this class, and I'm not a reader. But with that said, her "textbooks" are just regular novels so don't be too worried. I took her INTD 105 Haiti Noir class and it's my favorite class. Her classes are engaging and she's very humorous, just be prepared to work for it. You revise papers all the time and need to participate to do well.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Lima is a great professor, although very difficult, which she makes clear from the first day. This class will make you an amazing writer, as Lima will tear your work up and help you to grow with each new draft. Take her at least once.

I'll be honest, I'm terrified of Maria. She's very outspoken and is very strict on her classroom policies. She demands respect by intimidation, which isn't really the best learning style for me personally. With that being said, the woman is ridiculously bright, knows what she's talking about, and knows what she wants. You'll learn a lot.

Can be amazingly supportive when it comes to writing papers. She will literally help you revise an essay as many times as it takes to earn an A. However, if you're not good at showing up to class and being there on time DO NOT TAKE. She gets really annoyed with people being late, and won't take any excuses for absences.

Maria is a hilarious woman that cares to death about her job and your success in the class. She lets you write your paper as many times as you want until you get an A on it.  Reading and class participation are important but as long as you read the assignments and talk at least once a class you're guaranteed an A. One of my favorite teachers ever.

I love Maria's class! She is funny, lively, unusual. Participation is a must so if you think you're shy you might not enjoy her as much. She does not keep a gradebook and will not give your essays a formal grade until it's an A. Speaking of essays, she will let you rewrite your paper AS MANY TIMES AS YOU NEED to get an A. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is a mind opener, but in a good way.  You will learn things that you never have thought about and it really helps open the mind.  Maria doesnt even keep a grade book, and grades are based on paper comments that she reviews at the end.  she doesnt take off points for lateness either.  all you have to do is come to class and participate!

I am simultaneously horrified and fascinated by Maria. She is always entertaining, but can be a little harsh at times, and I don't like how she'll sometimes announce grades in front of the class. If you go to see her before an essay is due she is extremely helpful. Read the books, even answering a simple question will get you participation points.

She's easy, but nonetheless, believe the hype. If you find yourself an unobtrusive personality, she'll guilt you into feeling sorry for yourself for not having strong opinions regarding "world issues." A delicious quote of hers I can recall goes "all my white students look the same." Tyler Durden-esque in her views and ultimate hypocrisy.

The nicest, most helpful, and entertaining professor i have ever had. Not a dull moment in her class, and if you are willing to work, she takes accommodation for your effort. Go to class, and hand in as many drafts as you want and she will help you, because she actually cares. Awesome professor and like she will tell you "The best prof. at geneseo.

It is not hard to get an A in Lima's class. She wants you to get the A. All you have to do is talk in class, write some responses, and write/re-write assigned papers.  She never sets exact due dates, so you never feel rushed. Just do the readings for class and you're golden.

I'll be honest...Maria is an opinionated feminist, but what is wrong with being that?  NOTHING!!!  She can back up what she says (like she tells her students to do in her writing) and is one of the most intelligent people I've ever encountered.  She will help you with anything you ask her to and YOU MUST TALK IN CLASS!  Overall, she gets an A!

Maria Lima is a smart intelligent woman and THE BEST teacher at Geneseo.  She expects a lot from her students and will do anythind to help you.  She has made me a better writer.  We are all lucky to have her!

She will spend most of the class reminding you of her political views and how terribly novel they are; annoying only because she never shuts up about it. I dislike the way she does participation grading because making a frivolous comment every day will get you a better grade than making a meaningful concentration even slightly less frequently.

One of my favorite professors at Geneseo. I couldn't be more different than Maria, or have gotten in more arguments with her, and she certainly didn't hold it against me. I learned a ton about english writing, myself, and the rest of the world going back and forth with her. Her intensity leans towards hyperbole to prove a point; highly recommended
She's tough, but she's a real great lady that will help you along in your struggles.

I love her, but understand why people hate her. Pros: confident, educated, articulate, funny, passionate, intriguing. Cons: stupid participation points, will pick on you (sometimes unfairly... but it's humorous to me), can be perceived as offensive. It is not difficult to get an A, & you can rewrite the papers as many times as you want... DO THIS.
Very intimidating and opinionated.  I think some students would enjoy her class, but if you don't enjoy being absolutely required to speak to get a good grade then do not take a class with her.
Shocking hypocrite---preaches open mindedness till your ears blead----but only if you agreee with her. And for all her bravado, she's just doesn;t strike me as all that bright a lady.

Excellent teacher. Facilitates class discussion well, but the 2.5 hour time slot isn't always conducive to engaging opinions from classmates. Remarkably fair. Has opinions, but doesn't press them on students, greatly rewards effort, regardless of opinion. Respectful. Intelligent. Humble.
my least favorite teacher in all of my schooling

i loathe this lady.  she is  the most opinionated person i have ever met, and if you don't agree with her, you will not do well in this class. also places way too much importance on participation and attendance. i would never reccomend to anyone.

Crazy and unpredictable.  The once a week class seemed nice at first but can turn out to be boring after the first hour because all we do is roundatble discussion. You have to speak up and she likes opinionated people. She definitely opens up minds and loves what she does.
She is an absolute liberal freak. Likes to shove her opinions in her student's faces, and uses stereotypes like no other. I will never take another class with her again.

I also had her for ENGL 242 and I'm thinking about taking her for Humn and ENGL 318. I love Maria to death. Very friendly and approachable, loves to rant about sex and politics... there is not a more confident professor in the department. She really gives students a new way of looking at literature after taking one of her classes! Take her class!

Would have been a great professor if she wasn't so arrogant. Don't come to this country and live here and have a career here and then call it a "God forsaken country" she clearly chose favorites and her so called "cute" accent was really just annoying.

Meh. She's alright. She does tend to be very self-centered, and be warned: She gives NO DIRECTION WHATSOEVER writing papers until after she has marked them to death in her un-readable handwriting. She talks very fast and can be a brat. She's very energetic, but it borderlines on annoying most of the time, especially at 9:30am. She's overrated.

I took Literature of the African Diaspora with Maria, and she is definately an interesting teacher! She allows you to do papers over as many times as you want, and grades fairly. The grade you get is how much effort you put in. While she is arrogant, it doesn't take away from her excellent teaching.

Maria Lima is the best professor at Geneseo...no contest.  She inspired my teaching career.  I hate when people say she is opinionated as if that is a bad thing.  Brilliant! I can't put a value on what she has done for me.  I now live on Long Island but I always keep in touch with her because I couldn't have it any other way!

She has no compassion, and is thus hearless.  She will wonder through life souless as a result.  She lives an empty life because of this and she tries hard to fill thr void by making everything about herself.  Take her for one class, and then never take her again.  She is an abomination of human life.

Maria Lima is the best professor I've had in my 5 semesters at Geneseo.  I never zoned out in her class and usually left wanting to continue the discussion.  Make sure you verbalize your thoughts, and you'll be GOLDEN.

Yes, Maria is indeed very opinionated. But she challenges you to hold such strong opinions of your own.  Re-writing papers is a plus, and she makes herself extremely available to students. Because of her, I am more able to talk in class, more confident overall as a student/person... she really is an inspiration.
maria is an amazing person; class is never boring and she lets you rewrite papers as many time as neccessary
Maria Lima is amazing

There is not a more interesting and enjoyable teacher at Geneseo.  She is also one of the most helpful and positive.  My favorite thing about her, though, is the utter random rants about everything from politics to sex.

Take her classes if you want to take a class in Feminism and Marxism, not if you want to take classes in English.  Strong believer in the neo-feminist-pedagogical mode stating, "We aren't going to read books by dead white men in this class."  Easy class, shoves her views down your throat so hard it's easy to know what she wants to hear in papers.

Had Maria for every class I could, even classes I didn't need. She is dynamic, witty, VERY opinionated, but won't force it on you. She helps you learn by letting you correct mistakes instead of penalizing you. Best classes and memories of academia!
No Comments

Excellent professor.  Kind of a tough grader but if your willing to put an effort forth she'll help you get the best grade possible.  Class participation is a huge thing for her.  If you don't want to participate in class discussions don't take this class.  Not too much reading but the reading that is required is fun.  Awesome class to take.
She is the epitome of what an educated, strong, beautiful women is. Fascinating.

Awesome. Just awesome. She likes to have snacks in class and is very relaxed. She uses portfolio grading so even if you don't do too well in the beginning you can still get an A. Loves to chat about current events and is very lively. Allows you to revise your papers over and over again for regrading

utterly insane political views, but she doesn't mind if you just argue right back, she ejoys it actually.  requires a lot of participation, but it isn't tough to find something you wanna say in her class.  she doesn't really have any formal due dates, which is awesome, and you can always rewrite!

If you don't want to talk, don't take any of Maria's classes, it's that simple.  If you do enjoy sharing your opinions in class, be prepared to make Maria one of your favorite teachers.  Tough paper grader, but she's willing to work on multiple drafts with you, often even after the due date.

One of the greatest teachers ever.  Yes, she demands participation, welcome to college.  She's opinionated and crazy but don't let her scare you off to lower class size, you'll learn more than you thought possible from her.

Maria is definitely an ENGLISH professor, so if you can't hack it in the literary world, stay out of the classroom-- of course, this is just meant to make you want to prove yourself... so dive in! Maria is terrific, but does talk alot- fight her to get make your viewpoint heard!
I dropped this class.  This professor frightened me.  She may be an easy grader but she puts you on the spot and there is a lot of work.
dissapointing. If you just want an easy grade this class will do it for you--not demanding. you get the feeling she doesnt her stuff very well.

I liked this prof, but I should have taken a more challenging class.  One piece of advice: if she asks you what grade you think you deserve, give yourself the highest grade possible, because she might really give it to you.  I put A-, should have put A.
Definitely the most entertaining professor on campus with the best hair (and she knows this too). Maria would do almost anything for her students. She doesn't "profess," she educates.

She's a very good teacher.  Participation is 25% of her class grade though, so if you're afraid to talk, you might want to stay away.  She allows revisions on papers and no grade is final.  She's a bit crazy, but not too bad.
No Comments
The woman's a SELF-PROCLAIMED madwoman, but a terribly awesome professor.  Her classroom antics are a blast, but it isn't all fun & games.  Expect a good amount of work, both written and VERBAL!
Awesome, amazing professor. Learned a lot from her. Really opened my mind to new ideas.

yeah shes a little crazy but she likes those who read and talk in class.  plus the stuff you read is great, so thats a bonus.  you get to revise your papers and there are no tests, quizzes or final.  shes great and you'll learn in a creative way.
scary and intimidating as all hell.  crazy middle aged brazilian woman on a mission to drive students into insanity making a million revisions and forcing them to talk
Stalin was more tolerant of competing views than this one. Avoid unless you're looking to be indoctrinated.

Maria Lima is definitely one of my favorite professors here!  She makes you think and gets you into it.  Her grading is fair and easy to understand.  Warning to those who are quiet in class... your grade DEPENDS on class participation.  No shy ones here.

Maria! One of my favorite professors.  She really made you THINK and she was unbelievably FAIR.  Thanks for everything!   And hey, Maria....don't forget to give us a second to THINK!  Your questioning is very thought provoking, we need time to think. =)
Just connect everything to a movie to show that you understand.  It earned me an A.
she is great.  i don't agree with her politics but she doesn't hold that against me.  she is very humanistic.  thought provoking..
The best professor at Geneseo
Maria is absolutely the best professor at Geneseo.  She simply knows how to teach and inspire students beyond their capabilities.  This woman does not receive the acclaim she deserves.
No Comments
Very politically-mided; really inspired me to think and to be a conscious world citizen.
I took a class with Professor Chow and it turned out to be the hardest class ive ever taken at Geneseo. Seems like a great guy but don't recommend as a professor.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: He was alright. He was an easy grader but would give so much attitude if you had questions about an assignment and would never give you a clear answer anyway. His lectures were boring and I could tell he had no planning and did not care about our class.

Fairly easy class to excel in, lecture portion is extremely dry but nevertheless manageable. Two tests throughout the semester, both of which take place online and can be completed through one's basic Googling of the questions. As for Barry, alternates between being very accommodating to being surprisingly short and hostile when frustrated in labs

Barry is a great professor.  Funny, casual, yet highly knowledgable in his subject.  Word to the wise, don't try to BS him, he'll see right through you, but even still, he's very communicable and easy to talk to.  Assigns fairly simple weekly readings for homework, which are gone over in class.

He is not as bad as people say he is. He's pretty good guy. Course is rather semi-difficult but he's tests are easiest ever. I got 99 on the first exam, thought class was a joke, didn't study got mid 80s on next two tests, studied pretty hard got 100 on 4th test and final. He also gives you like bonus points.

If you are not a math major and are just looking for a good grade, do not take a class with him.  If you are a math major, you will learn a crazy amount of math but you will have to work very hard.  I kind of miss having classes with him.

Dr. Friedland is a extremely nice person.  I do have to admit that its not the easiest class because your grade is based only on  the 4 tests.  The tests are not the easiest ones either.  he is very helpful. recommended

Terrible teacher. The tests are only like 4 questions each and make up the entirety of your grade so if you get one question wrong there's 5% of your total grade. Plus he tests on material that he doesn't cover in class or with homework. And he blocks what he's writing on the board so the right half of the class can't see it

Dr. Friedland is easily one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. His examples are always clear and he leads you through the problems step-by-step. In addition, he's absolutely hilarious! Yes, the class is hard and you WILL have to work for your A, but if you go to class and pay attention, Dr. Friedland makes things clear and gives GREAT notes.

Terrible teacher, All he does is stand at the chalkboard and write math problems, he is extremely unhelpful in office hours. The tests are also extremely difficult and unfair, no partial credit or leway on anything. Worst teacher i have ever had

He definitely knows what he's talking about, but he doesn;t explain it, just writes problem after problem. He's so smart that he expects the class to get the material when he skips steps and rarely goes over the homework. The tests are hard and not based on the homework. He expects you to know what to do on the test and it's stuff you never learn.

Absolutely terrible teacher.  Paying attention in class, doing all the homeworks, and studying like crazy will get you an 80 if you're lucky.  His tests are the entire course, and each is only 4 questions long.  He's also about as easy to listen to as nails on a blackboard.  Don't take Calc III with him, even if you have no choice.

For the most part he stands with his back to the board and does problem after problem. For a question to be answered you need to just interrupt him and ask. Grades are based on exams only which are short and pretty challenging. Miss one question and you lose about 20 points. I DO NOT recommend taking a class with him unless you've taken calc before

This guy should teach only advanced classes, he talks like we all know what hes saying and hes about as warm and welcoming as tombstones. He stands in front of class with his back turned to the students and does problem after problem while the class looks at him like zombies.

Personality has a lot to be desired and could (at least when I had him) have been a lot more encouraging to his students.  Tests were short and difficult.  I ended up withdrawing and there were a good number of Es for midterm freshmen grades. I strongly do NOT recommend.
tests are short and really, really difficult. 4+ hours of studying equals about a 58. curves only if the whole class bombs it which happens a lot.

Grades are 100% based on test.  Tests are challenging to say the least.  They're short as well so if you miss a question you will get about 20 points off.  I'd bet he gives out about one A a semester.  Very good teacher though.

Nice guy.  Wouldn't reccomend to take if you're a bad test taker because those are your only grades for the class.  if you do the hw (which isn't graded/collected) as you go instead of all right before the test it may be easier to get the good grade

He gives excellent lectures with great, complete notes.  He drops some humor into the class to keep it interesting.  The grade comes entirely from the tests, which are straight forward and have no surprises. I learned a ton and enjoyed his class.
One of the best courses I have ever taken in Geneseo. Very straight to the point in notes and tests. No graded homework, grade is entirely based on tests, 3/7 of which is the final.
really tough grader.  i def learned a bit, but do not have the grade to show for it.  NO CELL PHONES
Lew is the man!  Pretty hard class, but he teaches it very well.  He is the best math professor I have had at Geneseo.  Very good at increasing knowledge about the subject matter

The materical is pretty difficult, but he is VERY good at explaining things and he always gives tons of examples. He doesn't check the homework, but I would suggest doing at least some of it. He makes the corniest jokes and he wears the same plaid shirt and vest every single day.

Friedland is one of the best professors at Geneseo. I learned so much from him. I got a 28 on the first exam for Calc 3, went to him discouraged, worked my butt off, and earned a B+ in the class. Don't give up if you're doing poorly, just prove to him you can do it on the final. Study the notes REALLY well and be able to do the homework problems!

Five cups of coffee couldn't make linear algebra exciting, and Friedland didn't exactly try to make the class entertaining. That said, he gives better notes than any professor I've ever had and makes the material very easy to understand. Stingy with grades, but if you study occasionally you should get an A.

I agree with the person below me. You really have to decide if learning a lot or getting a good grade is more important to you. Personally, I didn't think he graded fairly at all, but I don't know if everyone had the same problem or if it was just me. I did learn a ton in this class though. He gives good notes.

This is a very hard class. The tests are very short and difficult. He takes off 10 points for simple mistakes.. so it is hard to do really well. And he doesn't curve. But, he gives good notes and is always willing to go over homework problems. He tries to be funny and wears the same clothes the entire semester.

I think Friedland is a great professor and teaches well (don't know what the other raters are saying)It's not supposed to be blocks and cubes and 1+1=2, even though the math courses are filled with education majors! It's college mathematics! You don't get it? Then don't take it! He's great and nice guy, awesome tests, nothing or than that. PERIOD.
Although a very boring class, he explains all the concepts in it fairly well. The end of the year gets harder. He is a nice man in general.

This is defiently not the worst math teacher I have had here, but he's not the best either. He is a nice guy and the class isn't that hard, sometimes its just hard for him to teach well. Overall the class isn't too bad.

Wow what an amazing professor. His lectures are very clear and he always tries to bring things down to a level we can understand. He's always willing to go over homework problems. His tests are short, but not easy. However, if you get your hands on an old copy of the test, it'll save you because they are almost exactly the same. Take him for calc 3

He admited that he never took any teaching classes, but he's still a good teacher nonetheless.  He knows the material very well and is good at helping you to understand it too.  His sense of humor's not too bad either, if you appreciate corny jokes every once in a while.

Not bad...Aced calc because I loved calc...I slacked of in Linear Algebra and got a C-...when I desevered an E... not very personable but reasonable...but be careful...does not give much partial credit!!!
He's a different guy, but he means well. I don't think the same way as him, but it's nice to see things from a different perspective. I would recommend him for upper level classes.

Lew is a great teacher.  His notes are very clear and his tests are short, straight-forward, and predictable.  I had him for calc III, and decided to take him again for ELA.  Do the homework and you'll be fine.  Worst sense of humor ever...which actually makes him funny,  and he wears cool vests.

So far I like this prof.  He is very clear with his notes and explains things clearly.  He is not very personable however, but gets to the point..which is to teach class.  His tests  are surprisingly short but not easy.  take good notest and pay attention in class.

PEOPLE WHO GET Ds AND Es DESERVE IT!! I did well because I paid attention, unlike the other idiots who complain when they are naturally stupid. LEW IS AN AMAZING professor,Hes too intelligent for  idiots to comprehend. This course requires a lot of studying, don;t expect to get an easy A
I thought he was great -- one of my best professors at Geneseo.
worst ever. I dropped and taking again in the spring with a DIFFERENT prof.

he was a real jerk, I did ok on the first exam and went to ask him some questions about what I got wrong, and he made me feel like a retard.  Whatever you do DON'T take his class, I warned my friend...but she got a D too

Lew's the reason I went from a Math major with all A's in HS to dropping the major.  Got an E in Calc 1.  Very self-involved, no care for students. Is his wardrobe still 1 pair of khakis, 1 shirt, and a sweater vest for cold days! We tracked it!

I hated him. I took calc in HS and still failed. He likes his way and his way only. I was very confused - he was a D*** when i went for help too... don't take him... get towsley. I got a E in his course- Hey lew, please retire
I liked him. Gives the best notes, and takes you through all the steps. Tough grader, but his tests are pretty fair, and he curves.

horrible teacher. worked my butt off for a C-. He uses big math terms that no one understands, and when you ask him to clarify, he uses even more math terms. i taught myself calculus because he was no help.

Def. study hard for tests. They are quite short, and even though he curves, they can be a real *. Also, his final is a killer. So make sure you study a while beforehand. And I would reccomend going to classes, or else get notes from someone.
Very straight forward. If you go to class and study the notes there is no reason you can't get an A. Likes to wear the same clothes all the time. Curves tests.
he is really helpful if you seek for help.....work for your A!!!
i agree!  please retire!

This was the only C I ever got and the only semester I didn't make Dean's list

comment: Dr. Hall is a nice person, but checked out halfway during the semester. She canceled our lesson plans and then canceled class multiple times after that. Her lectures were not that interesting and not many attended because it was not mandatory. She does have a lot of knowledge to teach, but I think person teaching is better for her.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: This lady is horrible. If I didnt need this class Id drop so quick. Her grading is absurdly difficult and she acts like assignments are easier than they are. Advice: Take most of the assignments as seriously as a major exam.
Probably the worst Professor I have ever had. She will say one thing and do another. Despite her teaching a class on being professional, she is far from it.

A little clarification the class I took with her was a pass/fail. I feel Dr. Hall gets a bad rep because of how ridiculously hard she grades but at the end of the day she really does care about her students and wants them to do good in her class. I really had a rough time with a group project because of one of my partners and she was very merciful.

Feedback is poor quality and condescending. Grading is very tedious and specific although clear guidelines are not usually provided. She tends to contradict herself in terms of lesson plan grading even when you go to office hours. She is proud of her "tough" reputation. She will make it seem like you will fail her class and as a teacher.

She is nice but an extremely tough grader. I've never seen so many decimal grades in my time as a college student and you are literally left wondering why you lost 0.02 points on an assignment. Sometimes she'll suggest something to you and then take off points for it later. Her textbook quizzes are impossible. So yeah good luck..

Prof. Hall is at best a mediocre professor. Often inattentive to student emails (saying she never received them, etc.), flaky, and arrogant. Quizzes once a week, which began easy and progressed to be very specific & difficult by semester end. Expectations are ambiguous, especially when it came to the lesson plan. Overall, I would never recommend.

Dr. Hall leads you to believe that she is cutting you a break by giving ten question quizzes rather than exams, HOWEVER do not be fooled, since she makes the answers on these quizzes so ambiguous it can be hard to do well on them. Her expectations are generally unclear and the whole class, despite having read the material is on the brink of failing

For some reason that I do not know, Dr. Hall did not like me. She never wanted to hear what I had to say and was not nice to me when I went to see her during office hours. It was very disheartening. She is a truly bitter and mean person and will lead you to believe you're doing well and then she will give you a C.

She shares a lot of personal stories, and experiences with what she teaches. She also provides many sources on group assignments. She is a VERY harsh grader so make sure you follow every detail of the rubric or your grade will suffer. Each assignment is worth a few points but it adds up quickly!

Dr. Hall is hands down the most kind person I have ever met.  She is hard on you to help you.  It sucks when you are going through it but GO TO HER OFFICE HRS.  She is amazing and I would take more courses with her even though she sets the bar so high.
Greatclass!

The worst professor I've had at Geneseo. She is unorganized, unclear in her expectations, and inconsistent. She lies and has no problem throwing her colleagues under the bus to cover her faults. She is impossible to communicate with and an inadequate teacher. I didn't learn a single thing all semester. Avoid this woman like the plague.

This was the worst professor I ever had in Geneseo.  I enjoyed her class even though we did nothing, then she ran away to Ghana without telling anyone and gave the entire class C's.  This is not a joke...and somehow this lady is still teaching. Avoid this teacher if you value your GPA or want to learn anything.

This woman is awful. Her class is definitely well-structured, but she is literally just a mean person. I feel like I'm constantly being bullied by her--clearly, this is not okay, especially for a special education professor. Another thing is that she strongly dislikes men. Watch out.

All of the horror stories are not true if you know how to read a syllabus.  Do your work, hand it in on time, ask her for study guides (she will give them to you), the tests are based on the study guides. The collaboration notebook is NOT hard, start 3 weeks ahead of time and go by the guidelines and you will get full credit! She's very helpful!

Dr. Hall was extremely organized and straight forward. The test at 95% the study guides that she gives you the answers to. She was a kind of difficult grader, but if you work hard you should be fine. Her class was enjoyable.

Terrible, horrible professor.  She seems nice within class but then you are left to struggle on her tests.  The tests themselves are not hard, if you like and are great at memorizing her study guides, but the amount of work required for the tests is way too much for a 50 min. class even if you studied. You must suck up to get a grade higher than  C

I haven't gotten much out of the Educ204/ Sped205 block but they are both pretty easy classes. Hall is extremely understanding, helpful, and overall just a nice person. Show interest in sped and she will love you. memorize the study guides and youre good to go...garuanteed 85 or above on the tests.

I hated this class, when we even had it. Besides the study guides, good luck! She hardly teaches anything she tests. Hall always has to be right, even when she's wrong. She likes to take off points for ridiculous things, smirk, and shake her head like you're five years old. Also, was never prepared to teach us, so how can we be motivated to learn?
She seems nice, but I don't know...I feel like she talks down to people in general.  But she is extremely smart and knowledgbale.

The comments written for Hall/385 are so unfair.  She gave very clear project guidelines with examples.  Tests were never more than 16 questions, you had 30 minutes to take each test, and you got to use your book.  She has not referred anyone in either class, I checked.  Class averages for both sections are in the high 80%. Be fair and honest...

I don't understand how she is still teaching. she did give us the study guide test prior to the test but canceled our section so often that none of the content really made sence. she then wrote up the majority of our class for failing one test since she was grading use on little to no work.Loves to talk about her self.

I love Hall. She gives you practice tests for each test and takes questions word for word off of it and puts it on the real test, which is pretty easy.  Class lectures are interesting to me, but i also think she is an interesting prof. She is really nice, I've never noticed her have favorites. As a non-Special Ed major she is GREAT and EASY for 205

Dr. hall ahd her favorites and ONLY they were treated respectfully. She talked down to students, especially the males. She also stereotyped elementary students and suggested we look at their sneakers and drive by their homes to determine their socioeconomic status. how rude!
Should be fired.  I hate her as a person AND as a professor.  That's a first at Geneseo.  Unfair grading, terrible personality, plays favorites, horrible teacher...don't ever take her!!!

Dr. Hall is very manipulative.  When you ask for help she tells you what she wants then takes off points for it.  Tests are ridiculously difficult and not content based.  Doesn't want anyone to pass.  Was out for surgery during the semester and wouldn't give the sub prof. the tests until that day.  How can you teach that way??  One of the worst...
One way of summing Dr. Hall up: a wolf in sheeps clothing. She seems so nice and helpful, however- it's all a facade. Sneaky and not very helpful. Stay away at all costs!

I wore a button down and black pants to a presentation and she took off points for being dressed "unprofessional" simply because of a personal grudge.  What is unprofessional is her grading technique!

after i dropped her class she went behind my back to my other education professor to inquire about my attendance and performance in that class, and then brought that info to the dean without even telling my other teacher! she seems nice at first but is manipulative and such a hard grader. she never responds to emails and cancels office hours a lot.
Good luck figuring out what this woman wants.  avoid at all costs.
Sweetest lady ever but such a hard grader.  I do enjoy the class but I'm never quite sure what she wants and then basically everyone gets bad grades.  Avoid if you can unless you like a challenge.

She will tell you one thing, and then take points off for doing it the way she told you! She constantly contradicts herself, but she does know a lot of info.  She's a really tough grader when it comes to pretty much everything.  However, she does give out the test questions prior to the test (midterm and final).
take her you will learn so much!!!

I've never rated a prof before but u must be warned: WORST professor at Geneseo. Suck up as soon as you get in her class. I got a 92 and 91 on the midterm and final and got a B in the class b/c she gave me a C on everything I handed in. If you're not a favorite you won't succeed. She is on probation and I can definately see why after having had her

She's a pretty nice woman who will give you more information about the stuff that the SOE won't tell you than most people. She's a hard grader though and quite picky about her rubrics/grading. Just so you know, the description of the assignment on the syllabus is NOT the complete description. Don't follow it for your papers.
great professor - her lectures were informative, class was always taught in many interactive ways, and her grading is fair. thank you for a good semester!

I loved this professor, yes she is a hard grader but I always went ot her office hours and she was so helpful and nice!  I feel so much more prepared for teaching having taken this class I learned so much which as all you education majors know is rare!  Her class is always intresting and she is a really nice person.  She is very clear of what she e

Very HIGH, but clear expectations. VERY knowledgeable woman. IMPOSSIBLE to please. If this was the only class you took it might seem easy. Block IV of Education (maybe they d it different now) is breaking! DO NOT take any other hard classes with this one.
RUN  if you have her for any class...RUN!!!!!!!!!!!
No Comments

take her if you feel the need to lower your gpa.  unfair, has favorites (how unprofessional!), and a terrible teacher with VERY limited understandings of pedagogy. just pretends to be a nice individual...take class with ANYONE else you can find.
No Comments

Kind of Mixed feelings, I only had her half a semester b/c she had surgery,so I thought she was harsh with the grading when she hadnt been there. She really wanted us to succeed though and tried her best to help.Willing to sit down and tell you what she's looking for so you can do well.

Has favorites.  I went to her office MANY times to know EXACTLY what she wanted, and then did EXACTLY what she told me to do, and then she took off points for doing what she told me to do.  She told me to consider a different major, and I have an A in all other education classes.  She's just mean.

gave a detailed description of project. Let us redo the assignment even though she did not need to, it was required to pass the course. Not her requirement but the schools. Tests were fair, gave us weekly quizzes to study from
very helpful, easy to talk with, assignment directions are very clear, rubrics very clear. I heard bad this about her but they were not true. She is a very good professor!

AVOID her at all times. She's one of the toughest graders!! take her if you want to drag your gpa down. she's bitter. she gave us an exam on 9 chapters for a midterm. i dont think you'd like that. avoid her.

avoid this woman at all costs.  She is incredibly mean, unwilling to help, and discouraging.  Her expectations are unclear, she answers questions one way, and then expects something different.  No matter how hard you work, you won't get above a C, and that's if you're REALLY lucky.

You know those professors you should never take?  Yeah.  Escape while you still can! Impossible grading, not open to criticism, and very, very difficult, even if you are a good student.  Multiple people of my class failed, and not all of us are actually bad students.  Switch professors while you can
Excellent professor; very knowledgeable and willing to help; you have to work in her class but it's definitely worth it
Worst teacher and possible person ever.  I will be bitter forever for having her for a semester.

I love Klima. Not only is she a phenomenal person, but an amazing professor. She's very clear about what she wants but understanding as well. She's energetic and makes whatever you're learning about interesting. There was a lot of work, especially for an INTD, but it was worth it. I'm upset I won't be able to take another class with her.

Her tests can be hard and plentiful, but luckily she grades mostly on participation and whether or not you did the homework. She is incredibly amusing, though she is very expressive so you don't really learn the language. But she does teach a lot about the culture and interesting vocabulary if you ask.

Klima is AWESOME, helpful, kind, funny, entertaining. She cares about her students and how they learn/what they think. She always had fascinating things to discuss about the readings and current events. Not too hard but not easy. I want to take more classes with her.

In her lectures she goes through self-explanatory things SO slow. It's a waste. When she gets to important things she has to rush because of this. Her lectures also do not connect to the homework, and neither connect to the test. I am assuming I will need to retake, and I will be prepared teach MYSELF the course. Going to lectures seems pointless.

Dr.Mooney's lectures are okay, they can be confusing at times but can make sense if they are gone through slowly. Her exams can be worded a little confusing, especially non-computational questions. She is a good person and is available outside of class for help if needed. Go to SI sessions as they helped me a lot.

She makes statistics pretty simple and I honestly just feel like it's pretty easy and I think she explains things well. If you still need behavioral statistics, she's a good person to take it with. (Also she curves the tests!)

Mooney is REALLY annoying to have a professor. She is very tough with her grading of the projects, the class overall is very text heavy, and she does a "points" system where you have to get a certain amount of points to do well. I personally am not a big fan of her as a person either. Best to avoid...

I struggled very much with this class. The homework and lectures only slightly matched up, her tests barely covered the topic and she only went over things in class that were computational instead of definitions that were a majority of her tests. Too many tests and a very long cumulative test at the end that was very unnecessary.
yall are being a little too dramatic about this course it's really not that hard. just read the textbook chapters and you'll do  fine

I enjoyed the content of this class but she is not very nice about grading. You get a total of two projects and 3 tests that you MUST do well on or your grade will plummet. I took this class for my major and other people tend to agree that this class is way harder than it should be and she just reads off a script for class.

did better when i didnt go to class and i taught myself the whole semester. she nervous laughs after every sentence and makes material more complicated than it needs to be. HW assignments are hard and take forever, and the mean average of the tests is like a 60. TA will save ur life be prepared to teach urself!!

I wish this class was more interactive, there is no partner/group work ever and rarely even independent in-class work. The hw questions are time-consuming and completely unrepresentative of what our exam questions are like. SI sessions were helpful for exam prep. she adds points to all exams due to such low class means though, which I appreciate.
Mind numbingly boring class but pretty easy. She isn't very clear on expectations for projects and tests are kind of all over the place. Overall nice person, mediocre professor.

She is a good teacher, her class is very easy, tests are super easy and we did two projects along with 2 discussion posts per week. The workload was not bad at all and very manageable, she can move a bit slow for adolescent development and it can get boring but it is still worth going to the lectures because she elaborates in ways that'll help you.

I liked her a lot as a person, she always responded quickly to my emails when I had questions. The TA literally saved my life, I probably would have done awful in the class without her. Do good on the homework, theres like two a week, and you're test grades won't affect your grade as bad as you think. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT its worth it!!!

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken in my life. Every test I take, my grade drops and so does my hope in passing this class. She gives 5 exams in total, the lowest one dropped, a cumulative final and makes us purchase a 130 dollar cengage textbook/ homework questions. The homework is unbearably hard and relates nothing to class material.

This class was brutal. I am terrible at math and have never taken stats before. Mooney did the best she could I think its just challenging content. This class needs a TA for review or SI sessions. Do the homework!! And study like your life depends on it.

At first I thought she would be a boring teacher but she grew on me. She explains everything very well and is open to questions. For this class you need to study a lot because the material is very difficult but Mooney is always happy to help. I like how she structures her class, weekly expectations are predictable.
the class average for each exam was a 60. that is all

- Makes course material more complicated than it needs to be.
- Not very clear when answering questions 
- Does not give adequate time for exams

Actually one of the worst professors I'ver ever had. Lectures are so so vague and she reads everything she says off of a piece of paper. I've had to teach myself the entire semester. Homework would take me over an hour and the tests were hard. Our class average for every exam was a 60 and for every test i didn't have enough time to finish.

I am not sure if I would have been able to do so well in stats if it wasn't for Prof. Mooney. She is an amazing teacher and her lectures make sense. Very accessible outside of class and if you have a question she will take the time to help you understand. The tests are kinda harder because most of the test is definitions rather than the math.

If you haven't taken stats before, you're going to have a rough time. She's boring and struggles to find different ways of explaining things if her way doesn't make sense. Hope you have a TA or SI. However, if you've already taken stats, you only need to show up for the exams as long as you do the homework.

I am taking 2 classes with her this semester and it is so treacherous. Her lectures are super vague and she reads right off of them. The discussions each week are extensive and she grades them so hard even though they're literally 5 points. She doesn't say anything of substance in the lectures so you have to basically teach everything yourself.

Does not speak clearly. Instruction & power points are vague. No explanation how she got to the answer. You have to teach yourself. She won't answer your questions and talks in circles to make herself sound correct. The syllabus is not clear what is expected. Grading is deceptive. She does not know how to teach. She likes to hear herself talk.

I'm not going to lie; this class was tough for me! But anything math related has never been my strong suit, so I don't think it's her fault that it's difficult. The HW assignments SUCK (and I used Chegg for many of them), but overall, I think this class is doable. She is nice and accessible outside of class, which is good. Good luck!

The only reason I passed this class was because I took stats in high school. I'm not sure if it's her teaching or the nature of the course that made it difficult. She drops the 2 lowest hw grades and 1 test grade. The homeworks were ridiculously difficult and asked about material that she didn't teach or test us on.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Horrible teacher. Tests aren't like the class, book or homework problems. U can pass with hard work and extra credit but her class IS really hard. She will treat u like u r dumb when u ask for help and her tests r hard. Read the book and teach urself. 1 exam will be a few days b4 the final. I am sorry if you have to take her class, good luck.
Shes so nice and understanding

I have never really liked this professor for anything I have taken with her. We have 5 exams throughout the semester. The hw is very tedious and takes a while to do, and she assigns another one due the same week. It's not a terrible course but hard to manage while taking others since it's time consuming doing the hw alone & the readings.

Dr. Mooney is caring, but not great at teaching. She literally read off a script the entire class. You have to go to class to write down everything she says since the powerpoints are vague. I studied hard for the 3 tests, which is the only reason why I did well. Literature review due at the end of the semester is 10 pages long, pretty challenging.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Nicest professor ever, so easy to talk to, so understanding, super flexible and willing to give extensions like nothing. The only thing is that you have to go to class her lecture slides are super, super vague. 90% of what you need to know, she says verbally. So you really do have to be in class. Otherwise its really easy and interesting.
This course is tough! But thats not her fault. Doing all the Aplia assignments definitely helps your grade :) She is very understanding and flexible with grading. Would definitely take again!

Dr. Mooney is great. I took her class online and it is not bad at all. You have to complete 2 projects which are pretty hard and can tank your grade but other than that's really all you need to do. She gives you unlimited time, open notes tests, and really wants people to pass. I would recommend her to anyone.

Throughout Covid-19, Professor Mooney has been the most understanding and the most willing to work with students. She understands the stress levels are high, and really just wants to make sure you're comfortable with the material and succeed. I wish every professor could be even just a little bit like Professor Mooney.

She gave no homework. Classwork consisted of 2 projects that you could choose. All of the topics were very interesting. Tests consisted of material from the book and class so you should go. No participation in the class at all. The information was very interesting and I never minded attending class.

Difficult class because it's so specific, but her lectures help clear up concepts and sometimes she gives out candy. Aplia homeworks are stupidly hard and often not applicable to the exams but she does give out formula sheets and tells you what to study. Allows calculators for the exams and drops the lowest 2 hw grades and lowest exam grade.

She's not very helpful and her lectures are HORRIBLE! I'm not sure how she completed her PhD program considering there's a "teaching" portion of the program. She simply doesn't know how to teach! What a shame!

When she lectures its more confusing, probably better off not listening to her. The homework are wayyyy harder then tests for no reason, but chegg the answers. She gave us like 8 tests and one of them was 2 days before the final. You can definitely go to her for questions, I tried not to skip class but it didn't make that big of a difference.

The tests are very much based off the slides, but go to class so that you can write down the extra little details that can pop up for some questions on the test. The hw is tedious but not hard, its easier than the tests. One test drops, and 2 hws drop, plus opportunity for extra credit. Not much outside studying is needed if you just go to class

The class is super manageable. If you don't understand a concept or a HW question she is super helpful in office hours, or will respond super quickly to emails. Exams are really fair and the lowest grade drops. The lowest HW grade also drops. The online HW is a bit of a drag but it really helps with exam prep- the exams are easier than the HW.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Have taken 2 other classes with Mooney. If you study the slides and take notes during them, as well as read through the textbook and add to your own notes, you're golden for the exams. Have a good topic in mind for the paper, and KNOW it. She grades them hard, but is always there to help. Detail in your discussions are a chore, but are key for 5s.

I took PSYC 321 (family development) with Dr. Mooney. She read straight off the slides and the class was boring. She was a tough grader when it came to the paper and exams. She nervously laughed after almost everything. Received a C and I worked my butt off in the class.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: I really liked Mooney. I don't think she's a bad teacher at all. All you have to do, to do well in this class is print out her powerpoints and write down the additional info she says in lectures. Then before the test, look at her study guide and go through the textbook and write down only the definitions she didn't go over in class
