comment: Tests are easy if you pay attention to her  TAKE VERY GOOD NOTES (not kidding I bumped my grade by two letters doing this) you raise a virtual child and write two papers- she is harsh grader for these but I got  a C on the 1st made changes and then got an A- on the second. Weekly forum posts (dont forget to do) plus extra credit do help

Never in my college career have I had a worse professor than Mooney. She does not give clear directions and when she gives outlines for tests, no matter how hard you study, its never on the test. I hope she sees this too. She spends 30-45 minutes on just one slide and rambles, so boring. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!!
Tests are pretty fair. 2 paper that were graded super hard, lose a lot of points for formatting so make sure you brush up on APA style. Long lectures but overall interesting class

Dr. Mooney is a great professor,  she knows her material and cares about her students.  She explains things well, but she has a lot of information on her powerpoints, which she puts online, so paying good attention isn't critical. Personally it was kinda boring, because I took AP pysch so it was not much new info. 2 papers, 3 mc tests, weekly posts

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: She is not helpful at all, write down everything she says in class. Only three exams(fair if you go to class, review the power points, and read the textbook), two papers(hard), and 2 easy online posts each week. DRONES on and on and laughs after everything she says. If you go to office hours, she just repeats what she said in class. Not caring.

Although sometimes Mooney's lectures can be long, she is a great professor. There are only three exams, two papers, and 2 online posts every week. Her exams are easy if you go to class, review the power points, and read the textbook. Before every class, she asks the class if there are any questions that anyone has. Overall very helpful.

She is a super tough grader on her 2 virtual child papers. Go to her &the TA before hand for ANY Q's bc clarifying what u have written is important. Her exams r very fair, & I personally never read the book &only used it to quote for the papers. Dont forget to do the discussion board posts and go to all the ec she offers. She grades out of 430 pts

Mooney is a great professor. She's very nice and approachable and she tries to make sure everyone understands what's going on in class. The class wasn't that challenging at all - as long as you study and keep up to date with concepts you'll be more than fine. She also gives you formula sheets for the tests so you don't have to memorize anything.

She's nice but really annoying. Her lectures are long and pretty boring, her tests are usually completely different from what she says they'll cover in the study guides, and she grades papers harshly and only gives A's if she sees what she wants to see. Don't take if possible!!

Pretty easy A if you do what she asks. Virtual child papers are a breeze, I wrote both of them night before and got A's on both. Make sure you do the discussion board each week because it's a big part of your grade. Tests are fair. She can be a little annoying to listen to because she laughs after everything she says and she changes inflection a lo

Mooney is not extremely hard, the best way to study for her exams are by reading the chapters over and making outlines you can study from. Do all the practice questions in the textbook and you will see similar questions on exam. She gives online homework, which you have the opportunity to do well if you take your time on it & can boost your grade
i'm not really a fan. her tests are mostly fair but there's definitely some unfair questions. she's a harsh grader on the essays and doesn't give much feedback.

This is by far the most boring professor ever. every time i was in class i felt like strangling a cat. she is extremely horrible grader, doesn't even know what she wants on a paper and at the same time she chuckles every time she finishes a sentence. As a bad professor she is also scared to talk to the students. her office hours are horrible. BAD..

The virtual child papers are graded extremely harshly, and I'm an English major who intentionally chooses the toughest professors. I worked very hard on the papers, and was consistently marked way down for unclear and extremely picky reasons. Lectures are very generalized, lack clear examples, and don't cover enough material.

This professor is really easy, but has the most irritating lecture style. Her class is so long, even though she could teach her material in less time. Her tests are easy, but she doesn't give guidelines for the literature review. She also gives a lot of busy work like the discussion board and quizzes. Even though its easy, I learned nothing.

Good professor. This was my second class with her and I feel as though I learn a lot from her.  Class is pretty straight forward and intuitive but she seems nervous when she lectures. 3 tests and a 10 page lit review plus pretty regular quizzes on articles reviewing class material. Very informative and overall and interesting and easy elective.

Dr. Mooney is amazing. If you read her syllabus clearly, go to class, take good notes, and study you should be fine. This class includes a weekly discussion board, 3 papers, and 3 MC tests (which are hard). If you take the time to get to know her outside of class, your experience will be so much better. I would definitely take a class with her.

Professor Mooney's syllabus is clear and to the point. Throughout the year, she requires two projects to be done, and two weekly discussion posts as well. Her class is fairly easy but the questions on her tests may be a little tricky.

Dr. Mooney is very knowledgeable about this topic.  She may not come across as a particularly lax teacher but this class was pretty easy--three straightforward papers based on a program where you got to raise your own virtual child, three pretty easy tests (if you study!) mostly from the lectures, and 2 discussion posts per week on an online forum

Professor Mooney is awesome! She is very good at explaining topics so we can understand them. She is very helpful and approachable. She lets you know what she expects of you on exams. Overall, a great professor! I would recommend her to anyone! I hope to take another class with her.

Professor Mooney is one of the strictest professors I have ever taken. Unless you want to be stressing out the entire semester trying to please her grading system, DO NOT TAKE HER. She gives you rubrics and study guidelines, but is cheap with her grading. She WILL give you a hard time.

Professor Mooney is fantastic, and I would recommend her to anyone. She is very easy to understand, and is always there for you if you need help. Tests and assignments are challenging, but very reasonable. There are plenty of assignments to keep your grade up, but it's not overwhelming at all. Class is  enjoyable as well! Take her if you can!

Super easy class, he releases things on a weekly basis instead of releasing all the modules at the beginning of the semester so you can just do it whenever, I'd much rather just do the whole course in the first two weeks of the semester but whatever.

Professor Barnett was amazing! He made a very complex and confusing topic into an extremely manageable course, all whilst keeping the class engaged! I genuinely loved his ability to teach, his knowledge of the topic, and his positive attitude!

I do not have enough good things to say about Professor Barnett, he is such a genuine guy and really cares about his students and their progress.  The LogiCola for the last two units is a little tedious but nothing crazy.  This was a great class and I recommend everyone who has the opportunity to take it, to take it.

PHIL111 actually felt like the material was being made up on the spot, but Prof Barnett was a genuinely nice guy who clearly has a love for philosophy. Beware for Logicola especially the last two units. Quizzes are online, participation is not expected.

Professor Barnett is happy to give help or clarification! He is very kind, an absolute gem, and has a great sense of humor (laugh at his jokes or else). Quizzes were held online and were open notes, application-based! No cumulative exams. Listen and take notes in class. I didn't use the textbook, but I know the practice problems can be helpful.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Took during the intersession was decent hard without some lectures but answered emails timely and was able to help when needed.

Professor Barnett is the most patient person ever. He is so respectful of everyone and explains the content so well. The last few units get pretty difficult, but he really tries to make it as easy as it can be. Super amazing professor and I highly recommend.
super easy.

Loved taking this course because I am horrible at math, and although it can be confusing, anything is better than math. He uses a very annoying website/application for homeworks, but you get a while to do them. Quizzes arent bad and are mostly online. Very nice guy and very easy to get in contact with.

Professor Barnett is a caring professor, and his class was very easy. His lectures are easy to follow, and his tests are online and open notes. My only complaint is that he uses so much damn LogiCola. I am absolutely sick of that program. Besides that, his class is easy, and the workload is kind of light.

This class was extremely hard for me to understand, but Professor Barnett made me want to go to the class. He is an amazing professor, and an amazing human being. He helped me throughout this class so much, that I got a really good grade even though I deeply struggled. I would 100% take a class with him again just for his character.

his intro to logic class was easy if you understood the material but I got lost for the entire second semester and couldn't learn any of the stuff because it was s o complex. great professor but terrible terrible class.

changed to mandatory attendance halfway through semester. uses a hw software that is frustrating and penalizes you for wring questions (logicola). class is very repetitive but you can get it if you just look at the notes. best option for math course. simple and occasionally entertaining

Dr. Barnett is a professor who truly wants to see you succeed. His course was fun and intriguing even for someone who had no interest in the subject at the beginning. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. I highly recommend taking one of his courses!

Although I have a lot of problems with just how simple this class is (quite literally a monkey could do it), I guess that is a testament to either his teaching or how repetitive the material is. Show up every once in a while and half pay attention and you will get an A. I wish it was a little more stimulating, but I'll take it.

Professor Barnett was the reason I decided to declare a philosophy minor. I took his logic class as a math credit and I loved the material and him as a professor. He is super accessible and really cares about his students. He's definitely the best professor I've had at Geneseo.

Professor Barnett is easily one of the best professors I've encountered in my time at Geneseo. As other students have mentioned, his logic course is easy to follow and he never makes you feel like you are being thrown in the deep end. If you happen to be struggle, Barnett is easy to talk to and will try and help. He is one of the gems of Geneseo.

Professor Barnett is hands down one of the best professors on this campus. He is an amazing teacher and lecturer, and furthermore, he's incredibly human, and understands the difficulties of being a student. Don't miss out on the chance to take a course with him. I respect Professor Barnett a great deal and I would recommend his courses to everyone.

Knows his stuff, did an excellent job curating readings to go along with the course. Approachable, gives thoughtful feedback on assignments, genuinely kind, flexible with deadlines for papers and such. Two papers, two presentations and an exam, plus readings for each class. Wish there'd been more time for discussion in class.

He is awesome, one of my favorite professors i've had, classwork is a module assignment with a reasonable amount of work. Not difficult as long as you watch his lecture video and read the assigned textbook chapter. Logic is difficult to learn but he made it easy and interesting. I loved this class and despise math. HIGHLY recommend him.

Best professor I've had at Geneseo. Lectures are easy to follow, goes over all case studies and exercises in class. Grades are based on completion for the most part. Answers emails fast, gives extensions when needed, and appreciates when you participate in class. TAKE CLASSES W HIM

I have heard a lot of hits and misses for INTD 105 classes. I 1000% recommend taking this one. The work is manageable and his lectures and readings are really interesting. You write 4 essays along but the homework assignments help you write the papers and he is not a hard grader.

One of the best professors I have had. Made online learning engaging. With the way he works out the week, I felt like I was actually learning. He is always sending out announcements making sure we're all on track. So kind through emails. Extremely understanding, but knows when to stand his ground. Loved him! Wish I had him in person!

Dr. Barnett is the most straightforward professor I've ever had. His syllabus is exactly what you'll be doing. He's super easy to reach by email and happy to help you. The homework is really just reading the textbook, doing problems, and taking quizzes. Nothing is too hard. Best way to clear a math credit.

Great professor. Calm and cares about his students and work. The class was not super intense and there were only four papers to write during the semester, along with a small amount of outside work. I learned a lot and enjoyed the class.

Took this class over intersession and im glad I did. When you first look at the material it looks confusing, but he makes understanding it fun. You do the activities until you pass and you get 3 chances to take the weekly quizzes, and after each time it gives you the correct answer. He responds to your work and is quick w emailing back!Never judges

Good class. Tells you what he expects and is understanding. If you need help, he will help you at office hours. If you need extra time, he will extend due dates. Takes his time on material, and often will cancel assignments which are on the syllabus, making the class have a lot less work. Interesting topics, although, sometimes the class was boring

We had to write 4 papers but they were very easy to write. We had student workshops before turning in the final draft of the essay. The lectures are easy to follow but are long. We had textbooks to read but I never did because he never went over them in class. He gives a lot of handouts and takes attendance every day. Very easy to follow in class.

She is an extremely nice person.  Her work is excessive, however, and you really don't learn much in class, you just go over the absurd amounts of work you did. The tests have outlines so they are manageable but it's just overkill with the work

Kathy definitely means well and listens to student feedback, but the course itself is tedious and confusing. Almost all of the work for managerial is online through Connect, so it's not necessary to go to class. It's not too difficult to do alright in the class, but it's no easy A unless you're good at accounting.
I hate her a lot

Horrible, worst professor at Geneseo. Expects you to come in knowing as much as she knows about accounting. If you didn't understand anything in Financial, you will not succeed in her managerial class.

Unless you've had prior experience with Accounting, DO NOT TAKE HER. She gives a lot of work, too much work, with very little time to do it for an introductory 100-level class. Her tests are excruciatingly long and is VERY scatterbrained. She's a sweet lady and is so willing to help, but a horrible professor

She gives a lot of homework and her lectures are usually all over the place. She's always in a frenzy. However, Revekant tries to help you as much as possible. She lays out what is going to be on each of her tests for you as well as the final. But be mindful, she gives a lot of work.

There wasn't much work involved in the class. She assigns a lot of reading but you're never quizzed on it or anything. A huge portion of the grade is discussion based. If you're active in the discussions, it'll help your grade. The rest of her grading is a mystery. Good luck trying to guess which grade she'll give you next.

All you do is watch movies and answer discussion questions about them.  We had two books to read and she only gave us a quiz on the material once or twice.  Never discussed the readings other than that.  Easy A

There are four weeks left in the semester and we have not received grades on ANY assignments. What kind of "professor" does that? Even worse, she keeps piling on assignments, so for all I know we could be making the same mistakes over and over with no feedback.
easy professor just need to go to every class and watch like 8 movies throughout the semester. she grades final paper heavily but otherwise you will get a B to an A- range. fairly easy grader

She teaches it like an English course, which I hated. She didn't give much feedback on assignments - I had her read over my final paper and she said that it looked really good, then took numerous points off after I handed it in! She didn't tell me to change any of the things she took points off for. If you're not a strong writer, don't take her.

tolerance and morality-interesting class. only read the scarlet letter, three cups of tea and harry potter 5 and watched some movies which you write short essays on. as long as your essays are written well and proofread they should be fine. Final is a research paper and presentation on any controversal topic that you choose. Not a hard class

For Hist101 easiest class ever, meet once a week, and pass or fail. She is an absolute sweetheart and if you come to class and participate she will love you. An amazing class for intro history majors and she is an amazing dept chair.
Super nice, willing to extend deadlines if needed.

Mapes is an amazing professor. There are readings, but not nearly as many as most other professors in the department. She will give you honest feedback and as long as you follow it your grade is guaranteed to go up. She is very accessible outside of class, but at the moment at least shares an office with her twin, and it is easy to mistake them.

This is NOT FOR HIST101. Just an overall review. Professor Mapes is a sweet lady. She means no harm but her coursework is more rigorous than 400s. As someone who came to class as much as I could, and participated way more than the average student, I felt that I was cheated out of a good grade. Please consider alternative professors.

Lectures every class but also has great discussion on the readings. Participation is graded. Exams are open note. She is super nice and fun. Made a history class enjoyable for me. You will have a small reading assigned for almost every class.

Dr. Mapes is the best professor I have ever had! For homework a few documents are assigned and there will be a quiz the next class based on them, but they are very easy and you can use your notes. Her exams are also open note, you can bring 5 pages of notes to your exam. Her lectures are very interesting, she truly does care about her students

Dr. Mapes is incredibly kind and caring, always willing to hear you out! The subject itself wasn't particularly interesting to me (non-history major) and this class replaced another class I planned to take. All things considered, Dr. Mapes was very easygoing! The workload was a bit much, (quiz each class, readings, essays) but notes are allowed!

Professor Mapes is honestly the best! She helped me with registration for the spring and is super easy to get along with. She is the best and I see exactly why the school decided to make her the head of the History Department.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: I love Prof Mapes. She is an amazing lecturer. Her tests are very essay; she allows for a sheet of notes for the midterm and the final. And the pop quiz isn't really pop quizzes, they're very easy quizzes, and you get to have your notes for them. You get a 20 pg document packet with reading, and that's the hw. There's only 2 papers in her class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. The class is reading heavy and there is a quiz on the reading almost every class but they are super easy if you do the reading and she is an extremely fair grader. She is accommodating, encouraging, and very accessible outside of class. Overall just a great prof.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Mapes is great, both for HUMN and History. Her classes are very discussion based (almost entirely) and she gives daily quizzes to reinforce reading and attendance, however she often drops the lowest two grades or so, meaning missing class isn't the end of the world. Not a particularly hard grader, and is very helpful at office hours!

I love Dr. Mapes, but this class was definitely too hard for a gen-ed. We read about one book a week and there were daily quizzes on those readings, so if you didn't understand what you read, too bad. Good luck on the quiz. But, everything else was reasonable. She doesn't lecture, so definitely take Dr. Mapes if you prefer that style.

Mapes is a great professor and is wonderful in terms of explaining historical context in a clear, understandable way. As someone who doesn't prefer history courses, she makes HIS250 fairly interesting and engaging. Be sure to take notes throughout the semester, thoroughly read the three books required for the final paper, and attend her lectures.

Extremely nice and caring. Homework readings were boring and long at times. It's a discussion based class so it made things very interesting. A couple of papers and in-class essays. Very fair grader. The amount of reading is the only thing that I was not a fan of but amazing professor overall.

Dr. Mapes is wonderful. She is extremely caring and loves what she teaches and it shows through. This course was entirely discussion based, there was no lecture, so I didn't love that. However, her level of care and passion for the content helps facilitate high-quality discussions. She was also very understanding with remote learning. She's great!

Love Kathy Mapes. One of the sweetest professors I've ever had. Very understanding about personal situations. The class itself is pretty manageable, daily primary source readings with (near) daily quizzes. Then a midterm, final, and an easy paper. Not intense at all and I love labor history. Definitely recommend!

Super nice Professor, class is not easy but taught Humm well enough so I did not hate it. Quizes at the start of every class, then discussions follow till the end. Do your reading because if enough people aren't talking she will call on randos which is fair. Essays she is pretty fair. Lot of reading but makes class modern so interesting.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']
comment: Mapes is a sweetheart and very good at what she does. However, if you're one to skip class a lot or to not listen well during lectures, you won't do well in this class. Be prepared to take a lot of notes and do the readings. If you can do that, you'll be fine. Midterm, final (not cumulative), easy "pop" quizzes, and a paper based on 3 books.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: She gives lots of reading with little time to complete it but she grades fairly easily. Part of your grade is based on reading quizzes which are easy 100s, but the majority is based on papers throughout the semester. She doesn't grade very hard and i put in little effort on all my papers and got As.

Absolutely love Mapes. One of the best professors in history. This is my second class with her and I plan on taking more. Gets very excited about the topics. Midterm and final are very straightforward, asks class what they think should be on it, no surprises. Finals for her classes have been exactly like midterm, and NOT cumulative :)
The best history and INTD teacher. She is a great teacher that explains everything clearly and there are never any surprises. Has great notes and is very passionate about teaching.
Great professor. She is so sweet and funny. If you do your reading and participate in class she will almost always give you a good grade.

Best professor I've ever had.  I was feeling uneasy about a 5 page paper the NIGHT BEFORE it was due so I sent it to her not expecting a full response just a "good" or "no" and she took time to edit the entire thing.  Second class with her and will be taking again.

Prof. Mapes was a huge help to me. I'm a member of the L.I.V.E.S Program and she allowed me to participate in her class this semester. It was really hard at times. But she was always willing to meet with me outside of class. She really cares about you, and she inspired to follow my dream of becoming a writer and take a creative writing class.

Mapes is by far one of the best professors I have had in Geneseo, I wasn't expecting for this course to be so interesting but she made me love it a lot. She does give you reading that is by far mandatory, but its not dry reading, its reading that is very informative and helpful to the course. Just pace yourself, be ready for pop quizzesA

Kathy Mapes is by far the best professor at Geneseo. She really loves her material and is expressive in class. She expects participation but it really helps your grade. Definitely take her if you have the opportunity to.

For an INTD course, it is a lot of work. Only take the class if you are interested in history, because I'm really not and found myself bored with the books.  She gives out tons of reading with little time to do it. She is very passionate about the topics, though, and will be glad to help you when you struggle.

Professor Mapes is very passionate about the topics discussed in her INTD. She assigns alot of reading but it's definitely doable if you have good time management. I hate classes based on student participation like this one but by the end of the semester I was a pro at giving my input. Great Class.
Great class. Really interesting. Not too much out of class work. Expect to complete the readings. They are on the midterm/final.

I loved having Mapes as a professor. She took a boring topic, agricultural history, and turned into something both interesting and fun. Class is all student participation and she is an easy essay grader. I got an A- in her class and wrote every paper the night before it was due. Expect to put time in looking for sources, but every 221 is like that.

She is an amazing professor. Always willing to help and really makes an effort to keep class interesting. Reading is a must because class revolves around class participation and discussion.  She is a fair grader, so if you put in the effort you will receive the grade you deserve. Take her class, you won't regret it.

Great professor. There's a fair amount of reading, but if you keep up with it and attend class, it's impossible to fail. The quizzes, midterm, and final exam are very manageable as Mapes tells you exactly what to expect. You will leave her class with a wealth of knowledge and possibly interest.

She is an amazing teacher, i love her! she works with you whenever you have an issue personal or class related.I took her because she was my advisor and i heard she was good. Im taking a 300 level class with her next semester, can't wait! Also, i came into the class with no interest and though rural history would be boring, she prooved me wrong.

Professor Mapes helped me understand what it means to be an historian. Her teaching style gives students the opportunity to think for themselves and come to conclusions using primary and secondary sources. As a mentor she guided me through the graduate school application process and I am now a 5th year Ph.D. student in American History.
Extremely helpful. Able to make a rural history class fun. Don't expect to get off easy with the workload, but worth it when you know how to write scholarly papers at the end.

Mapes is an amazing professor who I would definitely recommend to anyone. She really cares about the students and wants them to do well. A fair grader and extremely helpful both in class and in office hours. 220 and 221 are difficult courses but with Mapes it wasn't bad at all. Very friendly and personable as well as knowledgable and interesting.
Best teacher ever
She is the best teacher at Geneseo.  She's really down to earth and is just a funny person.  She really seems to get everything and wants her students to also.
awesome!

She is Awesome!!! My favorite teacher at Geneseo. She can make even the most boring sounding topic really interesting.Super down to earth and knows what it's like to be a student- she's not some masochistic conceited professor even though she is extremely knowledgeable, empathetic, intelligent and has a great personality!
Seriously rad gal- very nice, helpful, and enthusiastic. Class is very easy as long as you go and lectures are interesting. Lovely human, great professor!!
Mapes is great. She is really dedicated to helping students. The class is 221 so its alot of work no matter who you're with, but she is understanding and very cool.

She's one of my favorite professors ever. This is my third class with her, and she's both an amazing and really understanding professor. She can make even people who aren't interested in the subject material enjoy the class, and she truly wants her students to do their best. Take her if you can. You will definitely not regret it.

She is always very clear about what she expects of her students. Very little reading for a 200-level class, it's 10-20 pages a class, but you can't fake it, so just do the reading. Very helpful, presents clear outlines of every class. Definitely a great prof to take!

she is very nice and cares alot about her students, one of my classmates asked for an extension on the paper for the class and she just said "um, ok yea y not?" she's very clear and helpful. it's evident that she wants her students to do well. if i take another history class im gonna make sure it's with her.

Terrific, terrific professor. Cares about her students and increasing their knowledge. If you do the readings (and there aren't a lot of them for a 200-level history class) and go to class, you'll be fine and won't have to spend hours studying. Put in the effort, and she will, too.

Also took 250 with her but it wouldn't fit. She's a wonderful professor who legitimately cares about her students. I am competely uninterested in the subject matter but her teaching style motivates me to do the readings and get involved in the class discussions. She's a very fair grader and an overall nice person.

I really liked her. Very interested in her topic and very clear. Always had an outline to go along with her lectures. Encourages class discussion and it is part of your grade. Papers are easy- just analytical book reviews. Tells you exactly what will be on the tests.

Favorite teacher of all time!!! Very helpful if you need extra help. She keeps class interesting. Need to keep up with the reading. Two papers, mid-term, final, and a few pop quizes. I will take her again.
No Comments

She is a great teacher. Tells you what to study for the tests and doesn't put on stuff she didn't warn you about.  Likes it when you participate in class, but doesn't make you and doesn't hold it against you if you don't talk. she is reeaaaalllly excited about her topics, and makes class interesting.

Dr. mapes really helped me with my writing skills in this class. we used so many different kinds of sources that it was much easier to pull things together for a final paper. very easy to talk to and listens to students concerns.

she is the greatest professor that i have ever taken. She is extremly helpful and will go out of her way for students. For the 100 levels that were complaining i hope your not history majors....it just gets HARDER

Mapes is a very intelligent, compassionate professor.  Whenever I need assistance during her office hours, she is very approachable, and very helpful.  The history I learnt at High School is plain boring compared to her approach.  You do have to work hard, but so what?  She clearly knows her stuff.
Tough but fair

Mapes is great.  She assigns a lot of reading, but listens to students concerns and will cut it down.  She is also a very fair grader and clearly lays out her expectations.  She keeps class very interesting.  If you are serious about wanting to learn history and aren't lazy, take her.  She's great.

Dr. Mapes is honest, interesting, a conceptual thinker and serious historian, and EXCELLENT at teaching seminar courses; take her if you are serious about discussing big issues in US history; yes-sometimes gets overwhelmed by emails,but has a husband and two kids!is amazing for working sooo hard

I absolutely hate this professor. She doesn't seem to understand that this is a 100 level class, she makes it seem like this is the only class her students are taking and gives so much work only to grade the papers and tests as if we're retarded. I've never worked so hard for a C in my life.

She assigns way too much work for a 100 level course. Extremely boring person and teacher, difficult grader, assigns several hours of work for class. Definitely do not take her classes unless you like spending every single night reading and writing chapter summaries.

She portrays herself as a caring and helpful professor when she is really the complete opposite.  She does not answer questions in emails or even acknowledge that she has received the emails at all. She treats this 100 level course as though it is a 300 level.  DO NOT take anything from her!

She is overall a nice lady.  But, in class, she nags all the time about not everyone participating.  She is also an extremely hard grader.  She treats 100 level classes like they are high 300 level courses.

What a wonderful teacher and a lovely person! I would recommend this class to anyone... She is very intelligent and she also listens to every comment in class and responds with insightful feedback. Way to go Dr. Mapes!

comment: Awesome professor. Very easily accessible with his office hours. Wants you to succeed and its really your own fault if you fail. Gives you many opportunities to learn. Really funny and approachable.

Professor is unreasonable and makes class harder than it needs to be. Explains things well one on one and always makes time for his students, but does not always make sense in class. tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: Professor Dassault is one of the best professors I've ever had. He sets you up for success and puts a lot of effort in. You just need to do your own part- if you fail, it's your own fault. Go to class, do the homework, go to him for help, and you will do well. Always holds review sessions before tests and gives review guides, is always clear
Great Professor! Explains anything you need him to. Very accommodating and wants you to do well. He goes over anything you don't understand and is overall a very nice person.

Dussault is a great guy who clearly enjoys teaching this course. He's always available during his office hours, and he even reserved the hour following our class period to be in the classroom to go over any questions people have. His quizzes can be tough, but if you review the notes and keep up with homework, you'll do fine.

I am currently taking Humanities 221 with Professor Owens. It is very reading heavy, but if you come to class regularly and have a general idea of what each reading is about, you will be fine. He is also very helpful, very willing to communicate and help through email and in office hours.
Tough grader but a good guy, has clear outlines of what he's looking for, and emailing him is beneficial.

Extremely rude and uncaring. Professor Owen's doesn't even follow his own rubric when grading, which makes it hard to understand what he wants. When you have conversations about it, he tells you to follow the rubric, it's like talking to a brick wall. He grades unfairly and wants to see his students fail. Avoid his class.

I genuinely have had the worst experience with this professor. He has claimed that I have plagiarized multiple times, and it has been found out that I haven't. He mocked me in class for something that I had privately emailed him, and claimed to the school that I had been skipping his classes when I hadn't missed any. Would not recommend this class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Took this for fun, but was an easy grade booster. Do the reading or read some notes about it and you'll be fine. He's very passionate about the material and will make jokes about nobody reading, so if you speak up even once a class you'll be his favorite. Humanities are vital; we evaluate the past to elevate our future

I really enjoyed Professor Owens. As a biology major this class was structured very differently compared to my other classes- however if you attend class and put effort in, this class is an easy grade booster. I regret missing reading checks but his grading is very fair and he really understands his students. I would recommend him and this class!

tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: If u try at all and go to class, you will do well. reading checks that makeup 15% of the grade, easily done by looking at summaries online. Papers are 40% but is lenient grader. Tests easy if u go to class. Overall a great class to take to fulfill credits outside major. IMO an interesting class. He is a genuine guy who wants you to be successful.

Recently took a humanities course with Professor Owens, and unfortunately, I found the experience challenging in several ways. Professor Owens was rude, but I often felt that the lectures were difficult to follow. The material was presented in a way that didn't always engage students.

I didn't like her that much. She just seemed super spacey. She would assign re-writes for our pieces before we had workshopped them in class, and had to re-do the syllabus a couple of times because the spent to much time on random stuff in class. She's obviously well-intentioned, though, and not mean at all.

Prof Faurot made Humn I a very interesting experience. I'm a Biology major and reading books isn't my thing. However, Prof Faurot made the class very enjoyable. If you put thought and effort into her essays and study adequately for her tests, you'll be fine. She also gives ample extra credit opportunities which can significantly boost your grade!

she is very intelligent and quirky. I love how passionate she is about what she teaches. She lets you know what will be on the exams.  Quiz every day but if you read or at least read sparknotes it should help your grade. She is very open to different point of views during class discussions. I wish she taught Humn 2 so I could take her again!

It is extremely easy to get an A in her class, as long as you're willing to put in some work. You have daily quizzes on the reading so, yes, you have to read.  But SparkNotes is usually good enough.  Plus, she posts study questions that are extremely helpful.  As long as you go to class, you're set for the midterm and final.  Take Faurot!!

TAKE HER FOR HUMN1! I wish she teaches HUMN2. Straight forward easy daily quizzes just to make sure you read. Extremely helpful with your paper ideas and intro. Daily quizzes, 2 exams (midterm and final) and 2 papers. I DREADED taking this class but Faurot made it one of my all time favorites!

Class attendance is a must. She has daily attendance quizzes which test if you read the text (sparknotes doesn't cover everything). Reading is recommended, be sure to at least skim it before class. Lets you email/show her your introductory paragraph for papers, and gives good feedback. Exams are fair. Half MC, half short answer with some quotes.

She is a good professor to have for Humn I. That said, the class is much easier if you have a background with the Christian Bible. Reading the texts is unnecessary as sparknotes contains enough information to pass the quizzes. A word of warning, the midterm and final are brutal. Very long format with limited time to do it.

You must go to her class! She has quizes basically every class and they really boost your grade. Read or atleast sparknotes. What really helps bring your grade up is all of the extra credit she gives out. Each is 1 point on your final average and I did about 6 of them got an A without actually getting an A on the tests or papers.

BTW.. she didn't think religious theories trumped facts... just that facts didn't necessarily trump religion. That comment was completely ignorant and hypocritical. And yes, I know who you are. You are an angry atheist who I found completely disrespectful. Respect other people's beliefs if you want yours to be respected. BTW.. I am NOT religious.

The previous comments were made by a certain group of people who were continuously rude and obnoxious in class. She is a very easy professor. Easy A.
false. warped view of the world, thinks that religious theories and grammatical structure trump things such as logic, facts, rational thinking, etc.

She summed up the class the first day by asking everyones name and their religion then acting suprised that atheists/agnostics existed. If you like inconspicuosly having her religious beliefs pushed on you and are a feminist, take this class. Oh, and every religous poem we read is "beautiful."

The only thing i learned from taking Prof. Faurots class is never take another class with Prof. Faurot. Im in "A Hero's Journey" but she turned the class into Faurots views on religion. This class is extremely pointless and I have not learned how to write at all. This woman is completely boring and i would highly advice against taking her class.

Not interesting or fun at all. Often goes on long, irrelevant sidenotes. But if you just want to get through Humn she's a good one. Sparknoteing will get you a 100 on the daily quizzes and journals which pad grade, and repeating what she says in essays = A. Nice woman, in her own little world. Doesn't give any credit to interpretations/opinions/facts that are different from her own. Prof. Faurot has a great talent for disregarding any opinion that differs from hers.  She preaches completely useless information and seems to occupy some form of alternate reality. Sacred in World Lit.- HORRIBLE. BAD TEACHER. Incredibly boring. She is very spacey, very out-of-touch with reality. The information is useless. She is an awesome professor. I disliked the readings so much but her lectures were interesting and she has quizzes every class on the reading but if you sparknoted it or read you can do really well. lots of readings and quizes in every class. Her lecture is sometimes boring and off topic, but she tells you what you have to know for exams and main themes of every reading. You have to write a lot on exams, but as long as you memorize all notes she writes down in class, you'll get an A.

She's a great professor if only if you're interested in religion. So-so. I personally loved the material itself so I found her lectures incredibly interesting, but I could definitely see how she could be really boring. She does put a lot of emphasis on what's important for the tests though. She's kind of a tough grader, and exams are lengthy. However, so long as you do the reading and just show up you'll be okay.

Very nice and a good professor. If you are like me and don't like Humanities, take her. Class may be boring at times, but gives lots of extra credit. I  got an 83 on my midterm that was bumped up to an 88 after attending a speaker. Exams are hard though, but wound up with an A.

If you want to take a class that leaves you with a pounding headache and a feeling of total confusion, this is the class for you. This woman may be nice outside of class, but she manages to make even the most interesting works boring. Anyone who can make Dante's The Inferno boring, deserves a medal of some kind. Avoid Faurot at all costs.

Oh my god, please never ever take a class with this woman. She is so boring you will literally want to put your head through a glass window, thereby cutting your throat and ending your misery. She'll go off on long tangents and you'll have no idea what the frig she's talking about. No such thing as lively class discussions. Stay away, stay away!!!!

Professor Faurot is a nice woman, but a terrible professor.  Her lectures are incomprehensible, and absolutely boring. Very nice lady and a good teacher. Humanities sucks and she doesn't make it too easy, but I would still recommend her. You have to go to class and you have to read (simple quiz every class) but it does keep you on track if you're like me and puts off everything until the night before a test.
Professor Faurot is very nice and willing to help in any way that she can. She grades very easily, too. Class isn't exactly engaging, but I've taken much worse.

very into religious studies... has spent classes talking about the religious significance of inane things like pollen and grass... mindlessly boring indeed.  fair grader and generally nice person. she does make the books boring as heck though, so be prepared to be bored. i pass the time playing games, try to get a seat in the back.

mindlessly boring class. mindlessly boring.

Profe Adams was one of my favorite professors this semester. Though her class was challenging at times, she wanted to see her students succeed. She was a strong support system overall.

This was a online class that was supposed to be in person but the other teacher left.  Videos and Ppts  and she drops the lowest 3 grades and offered extra credit which helps. Responded to emails and offered extra office hours for help.

Professor Adams will not offer you any accomodation for mental health or otherwise. I would not recommend taking a course with her. She cares more about making things easy for herself than she cares about her students and what they experience. The class is also taught at a much higher level than 102 would have you believe.

Professor Adams offers no accomodations whatsoever despite the fact that her course was never meant to be an online course. One of THE WORST courses I've taken in terms of it's impact on my mental health. 0/10 if not less.

For never have taken Spanish before, Professor Adams was very helpful. I enjoyed her lectures and powerpoints. She added fun videos into the class that aid in understanding the subject. She is a very caring professor who really wants her students to succeed. the homework wasn't super clear but she was very easy to reach out of class for questions.

comment: This class is very participation-oriented, so if you're quiet you will be called on. There is lots of homework, but it is simple and easy to stay on top of. Make sure you start the review projects early. Prof Adams is so sweet and wants her students to succeed, and will help when she can while challenging you.

Love her! This class is the highlight of my mornings! There is a good amount of homework, but it's relatively easy if you stay on top of it. Be prepared to be called on/participate periodically because it is an interactive, smaller setting language class, so communication is bound to happen. She wants to see her students succeed and she's so sweet!

She is a really nice person. And yes you need to do lots of works for the class but you learned!!! It is a class that you need to put your efforts in order to receive an A.I am taking Spanish as my third language while I am still struggling with English:(She helped me a lot. If you want to learn Spanish, take her class, it's very helpful.

comment: Taking this class would make you rub your eyes and look again to see if it's actually 101 class because it isn't. Do not take this class for spanish if you are not familiar with spanish and if you're looking for a class that actually matches the level of the class itself.

CLASS IS NOT A BREEZE, YOU HAVE TO WORK FOR YOUR GRADE. YOU ARE REQUIRED TO DO 3 CULTURAL ACTIVITES PLUS SHE CALLS ON YOU RANDOMLY IN CLASS. EXPECT A LOT OF GROUP WORK AND SHE CHECKS HOMEWORK DAILY. I WOULD RECOMMEND IF YOU'RE WILLING TO PUT IN THE WORK FOR THIS CLASS
Love this professor. Definitely take his class!! You will love it!!!! His exams are fun, also lecture is amazing.

If you have the opportunity, take the course with someone else. Attendance is mandatory and you were graded based on how much you talked in class. Lengthy assignments that you could only get full credit for if you go to office hours because there's no rubric for how he wants anything done. There's a final project and a Final exam.

Jeff respects education majors but does not convey material clearly, leading to regular confusion. Participation is key, other than that, you're only graded on lengthy weekly questions and three tests. You also must go to office hours to succeed so keep that in mind. Class is very self-directed; do work in groups without his help.

I have never taken a worse class with a more difficult professor in my life. He is extremely difficult to talk to, not helpful, rude, and inconsiderate. There were multiple times when he was disrespectful to students during class. His lectures are also extremely hard to understand, yet he expects you to know everything that he goes over.

You have to read the entire textbook. After EVERY class you have to write 5 paragraphs reacting to the lecture, and then 5 MORE paragraphs  reacting to the reading (10 total per class, twice a week so 20/week), the reading which mind you is mad long. On top of that he is such a passive aggressive nitpicky grader and his office hours are unhelpful.

I would not wish a class with Jeff Johannes on my worst enemy. For an introductory math class for non-majors, MATH 113 was the hardest class I've taken at Geneseo. There are so many tests, and none of them are easy. He encourages you to ask questions then mocks you for doing so. No professor has made me feel smaller.

Jeff might seem pretty rude at times but he really does care a ton about all of his students. If you put in the effort he expects he is a great professor. I don't like his teaching style but he is very helpful in office hours. His exams are very fair and he wont throw any curveballs at you. Lots of partial credit. Also offers tons of extra credit.

Would not recommend taking this class with him first the first semester of your first year. This class requires you to think much more abstractly with very difficult concepts. Assignments are VERY lengthy with very difficult problems. Start them early. It is essential to ask questions to comprehend topics. Jeff can come off as very overwhelming.

As a freshman I took math topics/Elm ed 140 with Jeff Johannes and failed miserably. Jeff does not make it easy to ask questions and expresses himself with a tone and matter that makes you feel little and dumb. He expects a lot from you and when the work is done it's rewarding yet almost impossible. Take the course with a different professor.

Jeff is so passionate and wants to make sure you succeed and that you become a better teacher. Office hours are super important and he offers a lot of help and flexible timing. The class focuses on group activities like hands on in class assignments and a group portion of each exam. If you want help in the class you need to ask for it. Be vocal!

I'm not gonna lie, Jeff is a hard guy to work with sometimes. His method of teaching is for you to do homework, then he teaches you off the questions you have from that hw after. He also gives nightmarishly long assignments at times, and very hard tests. But he's also a super caring guy who will help you if you put in the time and work necessary.

In class, he is a very good teacher and explains content very well. Out of class, weekly questions are assigned that are near impossible, told its incorrect and gives a failing grade. Very blunt and disrespectful when giving feedback and it is extremely discouraging. Office hours are mandatory to pass, if you don't go, you will fail.

Jeff is a very amazing person with a clear love for math. I enjoyed his class, however he is a very difficult grader and not very open to helping you out. I feel as I learned the concepts well with him but I got a worse grade then I would have got with a different prof. I would recommend switching teachers for lower level math classes.

So much work and he expects you to know stuff that nobody knows. Graded by only tests and 20+ question assignments. Very hard to even have a good grade in this class. He teaches all over the place and is really hard to understand anything he teaches and keep up with him. Do NOT recommend.

Jeff is a passionate professor who really cares about his students. However, his class requires a lot of work - be prepared for challenging weekly assignments and a lengthy final. Unstuckstudy was helpful for practice and prepping, but attendance and office hours are a must to succeed.

comment: Lot of reading and homework and so hard to understand what he's teaching

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: I learned the most in this class with Jeff out of any class in college. Yes he expects a lot from you but puts in the same amount of time and effort that he expects students to. I dedicated countless hours to his class which is what he expects but his class was really rewarding. If he sees that you put in work he will respect you and help you pass.

Jeff is one of the most interesting professors I've had. Yes he is blunt, but that doesn't mean he doesn't care. The weekly questions that he has you do help so much and prepare you so much to be a teacher. He helps you understand why the math you're doing is important. Don't base taking his class off the negative reviews, make your own opinion:)

The most caring professor I have come across. He has a genuine unconditional passion for his students. I have struggled with school (particularly math) my whole life and his patience and accessibility taught me much. Jeff is a wonderful person and will be BEYOND happy to help:) (He may seem harsh, but that is how he communicates it isn't personal).

I am not a good math student, so this could be why I didn't do well in his class. But Jeff made me feel more unable to do math than I felt before. His class is more so self-taught in groups, but he will then go over after. He does have very accessible office hours. But instead of encouraging me to come to them, I was told to drop instead.

Initially, I really enjoyed this class, but that changed pretty quickly and I wish I had just dropped it. Jeff is EXTREMELY condescending, told me multiple times that I do not put any effort into the class when I had almost 100% participation and turned in the assignments. You will fail the weekly questions if you do not do them his way. AVOID!

You will never have a more passionate professor, Jeff cares so much about his students. However, if you are not a math student and are simply taking this class because it is required for your major do not take it with him. This is the most work I have ever had for a math class. The final alone was over 70 pages written out.

When I first looked at Jeff on rate my professor, it terrified me. Jeff is the most caring professor I have. You do have to attend his office hours in order to do really well in the class. There are few assignments but they are hefty and you have over a month to complete. I would honestly recommend Jeff to anyone considering taking his class.

Jeff is a great professor. He really cares about the well being of all of his students. He has office hours Monday-Friday and was willing to help with whatever needed. He tends to have a dry sense of humor which I feel some people tend to take the wrong way. This course was very work heavy, but he was always willing to explain everything again.

Jeff is a super nice guy. He is blunt and will tell you exactly what you're doing wrong, don't take it personally. There is no homework besides weekly questions which are due every month. If you do not attend office hours, you won't do well on the weekly questions. He is very accessible outside of class.

let me start by saying avoid Jeff at all costs. He is a terrible professor and an even worse human being. He is extremely mean to students who don't understand his obscure work. He makes office hours mandatory and they go very late into the night. He will assign very long and complicated assignments that he will grade very harshly. STAY AWAY!

The weekly questions are hard for no reason and he grades them like you're in an upper-level math class. He makes really harsh comments to the class and is known to class out people for not understanding the material. Office Hours are mandatory !!!!

Class was extremely difficult and upsetting. Weekly questions are unreasonably hard, and grades them like you're in a 400 level math class. Things ALWAYS need to be done his way even if he tells you they don't need to be. Makes harsh, passive aggressive comments and is not at all sympathetic. If you do not go to office hours you will fail.

math majors should take this intro class. participation is big part of your grade. requires to write 2 reports and 2 short presentations. you can tell jeff really cares about his students and wants to help. dont know how he is with teaching actual math courses, but i can tell he is passionate about what he does.

If you want a professor who will give it to you straight, then Jeff is your guy. The class is centered around self-teaching among groups. There are lengthy projects that he is deeply picky about. Where do I start with this class. I have had some tough professors in my day especially as a biology student going into the medical field. DOESN'T ALLOW COMPUTERS IN CLASS. print out lectures before class & take notes is the best way to study & get at least a B on a test. All essays are graded by TA (easy 100).

honestly worst class to take for a Gen Ed. The most boring lecturer. Cant use any electronics so she expects you to print out 50+ pages of a PPT for each class. Midterm was pulled from thin air. 0/10 wouldn't recommend to a friend

Flies through powerpoints in lecture and very quiet and monotone. You're not allowed to use your laptop/electronics in class. As long as you copy the notes from online and get the few assignments (group project and final essay) done, it's a fairly easy class.

Very soft spoken so can barely hear her if you don't sit in the front.  Grades are pulled from thin air, doesn't give feedback on essays unless you go see her in office hours, which she never has. Not a lot of work for the class but struggling to get an A because her grading is so wild.

She is an easy grader and is flexible on due dates but I have mixed feelings.  She flies through her slideshows and never mentions anything on the slides so I don't know what to write.  Plus she left for a month so we just did't have class.  But she is very nice and easy to confront.  I liked the material but don't bother reading the textbook.
She was a nice lady. The tests in the beginning were kind of difficult but the final was easy. You should pass with no issue as long as you do the paper and presentation.

I seriously dislike Pipes. She skips through notes frequently because she is "short on time", mainly due to the fact that she has 5-8 students do a 3-5 minute presentation every class. Tests are hard and often worded weirdly, making questions broad and all answers seem possible. Please find a different teacher. You will regret taking ANTH with her.

Took her for a gen ed, but I did not have this group project others speak of. I had 3 tests including final, a reaction paper, and a short SOLO presentation. Grade is based only off those so you don't have a lot of leeway. She is extremely soft spoken and very hard to hear. Tests are poorly worded and unclear. Notes are impossible to take.
Just make sure you pick a good group because the final exam is a group project. Pretty easy. just have to read the notes she posts on MyCourses.

She is very soft spoken so it's really hard to hear her in lecture.  There are 3 tests and a group project.  Make sure you choose a good group because the group project is a big part of your grade.  The readings in the class are extremely boring but important.

I've taken another class with her since this one and I liked her in both classes a lot. She's very clear, really helpful in her office hours and she's a fair grader. There were only a couple essays, and not many tests. Overall I would recommend her to other students. Easy A class.

Excellent professor.  Has a whole range of experiences so he is not just teaching out of a book because he lived through most of it.  Incredibly interesting and offers different perspectives to consider on an issue.  Tests are relatively easy.  The only real work is the case study analysis which is not bad.  There is a research paper. Do it well.

I always come out of Drachman's courses knowing considerably more than I did going in. I took him for 2 200-level courses and I'm choosing to take him a third time for my capstone. You need to know any term he writes on the board. Use wikipedia to look up anything he didn't cover well. Very nice man. Attendance is mandatory. Likely to retire soon.

It's sad that Professor Drachman  no longer possesses the teaching skills to effectively cover the material in the course.  He is an incredibly interesting, intelligent man, but far too often gets far off track.  His lectures become incredibly scattered.  I sadly gained little from the class.

He's a sweet man with a really fascinating history, but he strays frequently from the topic    to the extent that the student is forced to do an unreasonable amount of outside work in order to learn the topics. All he does is write terms on the board, generally only gets to two or three, and the other ten or so end up the student's responsibility.

Brilliant professor and a very refreshing perspective. He was definitely an excellent professor at one time, which is too bad because class with him these days is a nightmare. Lectures are notoriously disorganized, and it's almost impossible to know what he wants from us. His grading policy is arbitrary at best. His attendance policy also sucks.

He is really no longer a good professor. He cannot keep a train of thought and jumps around way too much. His class is not easy because he cannot commit to a topic and explain it fully. Some days he writes terms down and if he does you better copy it down and then memorize it later. All in all I would recommend Koch, Deutsch in poli sci.

Professor Drachman is one of the most brilliant professors at Geneseo. He has lived through most of what he teaches so he is kind of an expert. He is a bit scatterbrained and always goes on massive tangets (his famous "just briefly" line). You do not need to do the readings except for the ones he assigns for the take home part of the midterm.

Professor Drachman is extremely knowledgable about his subject area. The class is literally on Cold War Presidents and their decisions. He goes on  massive tangents during class and expects you to know all the terms he puts on the board. Classes are mandatory because he gives short quizzes. He grades rather fairly.

I found him to be not only highly knowledgeable on the material but he put in a lot of his own personal experiences with what he was teaching.  Yes he had a tendency to go off on tangents but because of him I have realized my passion for International Relations.  He offered many great books to read on your own and I truly think he was the best.

Nice man, goes on tangents a lot so we don't cover every topics. I don't consider him an easy professor anymore. Although he graded the take home part of exams and the paper about easily or fairly, he really graded the in class midterms hard compared to the ones I had in his PLSC 140 class. He also encourages participation from his students.

I heard about the tangets before the class, but oh my goodness. In global issues Plsc346 talked about poppy production in Afghanistan for a week which was totally unplanned. Dr. Drachman is such a nice person, but I didn't get much out if his class. There was just no structure, and everything was discussion. Kind of an arbitrary grader too.
it is necessary to go to class! there are pop quizzes and a few essays. he is very knowledgeable but goes off on way too many tangents.
Great professor.  Let's you know exactly what will be on the test.  One midterm, one presentation, and one big essay on anything that's related to the course.  He is THE master of tangents though.

knows what he's talking about and very helpful. Lectures are decent, more fun if you participate. current events commentaries are easy grades, and for tests, study the terms and be very specific on the short answer and essay parts, pop quizzes are about 4 questions with bonuses and are on lecture stuff...very easy

Great professor!  He gives you a sheet of everything you will need to know before the test.  The tests are fair.  You will have to read a few chapters of his book.  Overall the reading isn't too necessary, just go to class and hear him talk.  He does go on a lot of tangents.  He likes to talk about current politics at the beginning of some classes.

Seems to be a very smart guy, very nice, and encourages class participation. However he goes off tangent too much and digress often so he doesn't give us enough notes to study and don't learn a lot about new topics. His tests are easy if you study the review sheet, research online the words, and define each of the terms by at least 3 sentences

I took lots of classes with Drachman and find him to be an incredibly smart and interesting prof, even if he does go on tangents and say "who's speaking please?" so often its hilarious.  admittedly, you can't rely on him to go over every detail in class, but this teaches you how to study and research.  amzing, endearing, and kind professor!

Hate giving bad grades, because he's such a sweet person. Ridiculously smart. Obviously cares a lot about his work, students,and just humanity in general.Yes, his stuttering IS endearing,but you HAVE to admit it gets REALLY annoying after the first few weeks.TANGENTS RESULT IN MISSED INFORMATION: NEED TO LEARN THINGS ON OWN TO DO WELL ON TESTS!!!!!
Amazing professor. His tangents are what make the class interesting. Also, He encourages classroom discussion.
He's the reason I want to switch to an international relations major.

very smart guy, knows everything but can't leave out the political bias. Also he loves to go off on tangents so easy to distract. tests are very simple usually just matching and short answers. no homework but horrible notes in class. overall not a bad guy

He's a good professor who needs to stop going of to a large tangent. Just because of that he should have been a calc teacher... He knows his**** if you filter out the info he leaves out with his "appropriate" discussians OFF TOPIC. And he is the only professor i know with his own facebook group

To study for his tests write out a paragraph for each of the terms he gives you on the study guide.  He says he only wants a couple sentences for identifications but write as much as you can.  It also helps to go and talk to him about your paper topic.  This will lead to a considerably higher grade.  Also, go to class...he gives pop quizes
Be as detailed as possible in every assignment.

Drachman is sometimes hard to follow.  He's a nice man, but often his lectures are incontinuous and he goes on tangents.  Notetaking is a challenge.  A great deal of independent work is necessary to succeed in his classes, though he doesn't seem to fail st

He jumps from topic to topic, but if you take good notes and fill in the gaps yourself (using google alot!) you learn about a variety of events and issues. Great to talk to in office hours about your future plans / career plans, he has seen and done it all
he goes off on tangents a bit too much, and the stuttering gets redundant, but he is a great man

Incredibly smart, he does stumble sometimes but when he gets going watch out.  Really down to earth easy to talk to.  If you put forth a good effort you will get a good grade.  I would take another class with him in a second.
I couldn't agree more wit most comments. A foutain of info, great asset to the college, esp. Pls,& IR majors. But be aware, he goes off-tangent ALOt, but on PLSC OR IR issues though!

So cute and muddled! He can take forever to get a thought out, and there's always the danger of the "just briefly" comments, but he's absolutely brilliant. Fascinating to listen to, and a real asset to the dept.

I love this man. He can barely put a sentence together sometimes, but when he gets going, you see how brilliant he is. And he's so sweet! I can't wait to take another class with him, Geneseo's lucky to have him.

the most intelligent man ever!!!

i only did as well as i did because i took calculus in high school. he's always there to help if you ask for it and gives review before tests. no surprises, pretty straight forward. also he's hot.

This man is by far the WORST professor i've ever had for any math class. He doesn't give good notes at all, he is very confusing during class and literally does the bare minimum to teach. As long as you're willing to put in the work his class is worth taking.

He's a nice dude and will help you if you ask no doubt, homework is harder than the tests.

The class and expectations were outlined well.  Not a fan of mymathlab for homework but it comes with book.  Allows for student input and uses it to make improvements in his course during the semester.

If you're not a math major and you haven't taken calc before, this class is tough. He's new at teaching college but he got better as the semester went on.
Very awkward and didn't seem comfortable with the material. This Calc 1 class is easy if you have taken calc before but if not, find another teacher.

He is a really nice guy and a good math teacher overall. I hate proofs.  But Tsai made it bearable.  His tests are straight out of the homework and and have all been gone over in class.  Very straight forward.  I got an A. which i never thought was possible.  Recommend him

Teaches calculus as though you you already know it.  He never makes an effort to get know his students despite being a kind, warmhearted individual. His tests/quizzes fluctuate a lot. Explains things well enough and he's always willing to answer questions.  It's almost impossible to fail this class the way he grades.  His teaching comes right out of the book so if you read it and do the homework you should be fine.  He's also a very nice man, if you talk to him and work with him the class is really easy.

he is by far the best math professor i've ever had. im a math major and he explained things very well. he was the most straightforward and simple professor i've had ever. he's very clear and nice. he also has a good sense of humor :). i love this guy and hope to see him again in another class soon!

Class was pretty hard, but it's caclulus and it wasn't meant to be easy.  Grades based on quizzes and tests.  Both are all do-the-problem types with no multiple choice.  Do the homework, it really helps.  Overall a really sweet guy, will usually let you out early because it's such a long class.

While Tsai earnestly tries to teach you the material, he fumbles through examples, makes numerous errors on the board, and fails to truly EXPLAIN the math you'll be tested on. he was a very confusing teacher because he was hard to understand an he never actually gave notes, just read the examples from the book. the class is easy if you've taken calc before or get help from someone who had him for calc the previous year because just about by the end of semester you begin to catch on to his teaching style.

he was too hard. he didnt care that people didnt understand math at his pace...he just taught and if you got it, then great, if not, then you were screwed. grades based on just quizzes and tests...the pressure was always on. hes a nice guy himself...he just doesnt get that not everybody gets the math that well.
Take it with him. Tests and quizes are homework problems that he assigns. Just study those and you will ace his tests. Plus he is really nice and easy to understand.

I found him very easy to understand, both accent wise and teaching wise. He always askes if there were any questions on the homework and will go over them fully with the class. he blows... stinks at teaching and you can never understand what he is trying to teach... he only teaches with examples and never explains anything
Very easy and boring class.  Nice guy though.
he only gives examples and can't explain anything clearly

good man.  quizzes are a breeze, i can't say the same for tests though.  although, if you do the assignments you're going to do well on tests as the problems come straight from them.  classes are short and to-the-point.  final is not cumulative.

The Keymaker.  Well, the material is rather miserable but not impossible -- work through the homework and the tests are almost identical.  Moves at a rapid pace and hard to understand at first, but he's glad to help/answer questions.  Very nice guy and very good w/ his Calculus, plus only 3 tests.

hard..half the kids dropped the class. takes tons of points off for little mistakes on tests.  curves a lot since the class is so impossible.  he knows his stuff, but doesnt convey it too well.  i recommend taking it with a professor that is more approachable and speaks better english
Easy class. Make sure to do the hw because the tests are almost identical.

He never assigns too much work.  He tests straight from homework examples, so it's easy to adequately prepare for exams.  His lessons are organized and clear.  He usualy lets us out early!

he is so nice and so cute. if you go to his office hours or stay after class, he will go over everything with you. his class is fair and not hard. and he always goes over homework. the only bad thing was that he rushed so much at the end:(

Ok so he may not be the clearest person but he tries and I think he can teach really well... As a matter of fact, his final isnt cumultative which is a blessing! He is a really nice guys and not too bad of a teacher.
Very Good, Answers homework questions. Easy and fair tests. Nicest guy!

boring, repetitive and difficult to understand
Wow maybe if I could understand his english or read his writing I wouldn't have had to teach myself statistics

Professor Marchant is very passionate about her work, but if you're not paying attention, she will call you out for it in your 60 person lecture. All of the notes are in her slides but she talks about most of it so you have to be in class to get all of the info. Dr. Marchant designed the course so students do well. As long as you stay on top of the work and don't slack off, you will do well in the class.

This class overall is very easy if you do the study guides for the tests and quizzes. You have to go to class because he takes attendance for a grade and doesn't post the slideshows on brightspace. overall, the class itself is easy but he goes through the lecture slides super fast & doesnt share it with u so everyone is always having to rush to take pics of them before the next. final presentation is pretty easy & the exams usually ask questions specifically about what was mentioned during lecture, so make sure u can write notes fast.

comment: This class is very attendance mandatory.  The study guides for the tests are the same questions as the test and are from the notes you take in class.  However, he does not post the notes online so you have to go to class.  He is very understanding if you can't make it to class.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Graded by few things']
comment: This was a relatively easy course. The textbook is easy to read, and he provides lectures where he goes into more depth about the different topics. He provides a study sheet with questions for quizzes that are similar to the real ones, so if you understand the material you should be fine. There is one group project about a composer and his works.

I cant say enough good things about Prof Bergevin. Tests were word for word of the review sheet he gave us. A few questions you needed the textbook for but not too many. I actually missed an exam by accident and he let me make it up, no penalty. Group project was easy, but he was a little nit picky grading. Highly highly recommended professor!!

Professor Bergevin was super nice! His whole class is just lecture videos but his energy comes through in them. The tests were ridiculously easy. The questions were word for word from the review sheet which is word for word from the lectures. Tons of bonus on tests too. There was a group project but that was easy too. And bonus he is kind of funny.

Professor Bergevin has been awesome for music 120. I took it as a gen ed and it was very easy (it was also asynchronous online). He sends out extremely detailed study guides for your tests and if you know those questions you are guaranteed an A. One group project but it wasn't bad at all. Highly recommend taking this class for a gen ed credit!

Dr. Bergevin is great. A little awkward but a very sweet and understanding professor. Intro to Music History was just an fun elective for me, and it was very easy and interesting. comment: Highly recommend Professor Bergevin for this class. He is accessible if you need help and is very kind and understanding. Attendance counts for this class so you have to go.
