Just overall a big fat NO from me.

He does not teach at all. Worlds most boring class. You gotta teach yourself. Tests are impossible. Way too much homework. sucks eggs. I really wish I could have given him a 0. please just dont take this class, save yourself.

I took INTD-105 with Dr. Beth 14 years ago, and I still remember her impact. English was always my weakest subject, and my HS teacher's only advice was to "write better." Dr. Beth actually showed me how, with patience and constructive feedback. She genuinely cared about my growth and even remembered me years later, always stopping to say hi.

Dr. McCoy is one of the nicest humans ever. There are books you need to read, however, she gave them all in pdf format so you didn't have to purchase. The course is self graded, as long as you try to improve and give effort you will receive an A in the class. There is a decent amount of reading, but that should be expected with an English course.

There is a decent amount of reading but McCoy is very upfront about that from the beginning. She keeps classes interesting and always gives breaks in her longer classes. I can see how one of her courses would not be fun if you aren't interested in the subject, but I am a non-English major and greatly enjoyed the course.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Dr. McCoy is an amazing professor. She does a lot of group projects and participation is important. You also really need to make sure you are reading because everything in her class builds on itself, so it is hard to catch up if you get behind. She gives good, honest, feedback. She is also very funny and understanding if you need an extension.
Beth is quite literally the most understanding professor I have had in the English department. She understands that things come up, and is very accommodating when needing more time for things.
10/10 one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. I had her last year for both semesters, she is sweet and smart and it was a great experience in her class :)

This was my least favorite class I've ever taken here. She is nice but if you don't like English then don't take a class with her, especially this one. There is hard reading, and a tonnnn of group work and participation. So if you don't like talking to classmates don't take this class.

Really great Prof! You will have to do a decent amount of reading, and it helps if you actually know what you're talking about, but you can BS it if you know someone who's done the reading. Very very caring professor, who really cares about the class, and will reciprocate any interest you put forwards. Self graded! Will take again.

3 group essays, but dont let that scare you. tons of guidance and support. so understanding about circumstances. comprehensive materials but not lecture heavy, mix of that and small groups. class focuses on Morrison and Dante comparisons, but dont need to be Dante expert. amazing class

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Beth is the single most caring professor you will ever meet at SUNY Geneseo. The course was self graded and the entire goal of the course was to have some self improvement in a few categories. Respect is very important to her so read what she assigns and she will love you. Amazing course, amazing professor, highly recommend.

The class I took with her was self assessed. I had to read like 5 different books but they weren't terrible. There are 3 collaboration projects and then a final paper at the end but she gave like 2 weeks in class to do it. She wants you to grow and be successful and gives back super specific feedback

One of the best teachers I've ever had. English/lit classes have never been my forte but Beth was really helpful with guiding me personally, and with super specific feedback. Class was self graded but she graded me higher than I did myself, and told me she was proud of me for showing improvement. Made an effort to care about everyone.

I cannot do Beth McCoy justice in 350 characters, but I'll try. She is by far the best professor I've had in my entire experience at Geneseo. She's very fond of collaborative work, but don't let that scare you, she gives you every possible chance to succeed. Some have called her a harsh grader, but I strongly disagree. Also, her feedback is amazing

she's easy to reach but during a pandemic where it would be expected that professors don't assign so much and criticize so much she does the opposite. instructions are unclear and there prompts contain hundreds of guidelines for a discussion post. if you want to torture yourself with this workload, go ahead

Professor McCoy is an amazing professor. She makes sure she and all of her students know all of the students names. I was nervous bc I typically do not like classes with participation, but I spoke frequently in her class. She is very understanding. My final was a self graded essay which I really enjoyed. The material was interesting & not boring

Professor McCoy was, by far, one of my favorite professors at SUNY Geneseo. Not only did she teach topics that should be taught in earlier years of schooling (but is often ignored), she helped me grow more confident in my writing and myself. I took more than one class with her, but this was the last one I was enrolled in, and I am forever grateful.

Professor McCoy changed my way of thinking and helped me improve greatly as a writer. Read the material! Working with the readings is the only way to do well. Participation is encouraged and really helps with the Blog Post assignment. Do NOT wait until the end of semester to do all of the blogs. Gives a lot of valuable feedback. Unpack everything!

Dr. Beth is an amazing, caring professor. I really enjoyed her class. She provides excellent feedback on each blog post you upload which allows you to make improvements each time. Her activities and class is well organized and structured. I definitely recommended taking at least one class with her as an English major.

While Dr. McCoy expects a lot from her students, the work she assigns is very manageable. She has floating deadlines for most work, so don't procrastinate - pacing is graded. She offers many opportunities for extra credit by writing papers. She gives great feedback on work, and she'll make you both a better writer and a more conscientious person.
Just don't

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: If you want a tough grader who wants things her way take this class. Horrible in every aspect.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: The class was difficult but manageable. When the semester ended she did not grade one of my papers and wanted me to meet with her during break even though I specifically told her I can not come back next semester. (I am not from Geneseo and it is an 8hr ride). It is already a new semester and I have an incomplete on the assignment. DO NOT TAKE THIS

Although she is a tough grader she really pushes you to "unpack" and transform not only your writing but your thinkING. On our first essay draft I did not know what I saying and I wasn't sure how to deal with the big concepts we were analyzing. Through her excellent feedback and constructive criticism I became a better writer, thinker and person.

Beth is a caring person, gives constructive feedback, and is accessible outside of class. She truly cares about her work and her students. Reading the books she assigns is a must for class discussion however, she breaks up the reading clearly on the syllabus and tries not to overload students.

Professor McCoy is a very smart and caring woman who gets the bigger picture. She forces you to really dive into the literature and make unique connections, which helps you become a better thinker. Take her class if you want to become a more skilled writer, reader and human being.

Prof. McCoy's Intertextuality class was the most difficult thing I've ever done! Readings were challenging (I'm looking at you Cane!) Be sure to participate and "unpack", DON'T forget to blog (20% of your grade), and essays... oof! On that note, Prof. McCoy will always work zealously and creatively to help you out. Also, I want to marry her.
Kinda annoying, I am politically correct, but she is weirdly overly confusingly politically correct.

Dr. Beth is by far the most amazing professor I have had so far during my academic career at Geneseo.  She is clear, direct, honest, and truly is there to help you become a better writer (and in my opinion, also a better person).  Don't be fooled though, she is a tough grader, but all of her criticisms are constructive and actually helpful!

Dr. Beth helped me to TRANSFORM, not only my writing, but my way of thinking too. She pushes you, but does so because she believes in you. I FAILED the first paper, but I worked hard and managed an A-. Was it easy? NO. Was it worth it? ABSOLUTELY. I took her 3 years ago and am still able to email her if I need help. She is a true gem! TAKE HER :D

McCoy grades very hard and expects a lot out of her students. I would say the majority of her classes consisted of individual work on assigned essays. She offers several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester which I strongly recommend. No tests or quizzes ever. Watch out for forum post deadlines... MAKE THEM GOOD BC THEY ARE GRADED!

Professor McCoy is honestly one of the best teachers I've ever had. She is so caring and committed to her job. She actually cares about her students and understands that we have other classes and lives to take care of outside of class. She makes everyone feel intelligent and makes you feel like your opinions are important. Would recommend.

I learned a lot. I had to work for it but I learned a lot about the English discipline and major at Geneseo. McCoy's lectures are elaborate and at times difficult to follow, but if you trust her enough to follow even if at first you don't completely understand, you'll learn a lot too. I highly recommend her for ENGL 203 and for other classes.

McCoy's African American Literature course was great! SHe places emphasis on participation and "unpacking" your ideas. She always made herself available to her students and she keeps the response papers open for interpretation.

Dr. Beth was absolutely fantastic! It is true that INTD is not a class freshmen typically enjoy. However, I improved TREMENDOUSLY in my ability to write. Is it an easy class? No, you have to work really hard and you will probably get upset multiple times throughout the semester. KEEP GOING. I promise you it is well worth it.
Simply the best teacher I've ever had in any context. Challenging, takes your work seriously, holds you to high standards, and pushes you to THINK. Also incredibly helpful and an excellent mentor.

Dr. McCoy is absolutely fantastic.  One of the smartest people I have ever met and someone that has taught me so much, going beyond the classroom.  You have to work hard, but it is well worth it as the knowledge you obtain at semesters end is what college is all about.  Highly recommend.

She's an absolutely great teacher, but be warned, she expects A LOT. McCoy wants you to work hard to improve as a writer, but as long as you're willing to put in some effort, it will pay off. I recommend this class to anyone who wants to become a better writer within a semester(And is able to work hard!)

Extremely intelligent woman who will challenge the way you look at the world. Don't expect everything to come together at the end of the class - she wants you to start asking questions in her class and begin answering them afterward - and on your own. GO TO CLASS - she doesn't give reading quizzes, but her classes are an experience. Be there.
Best teacher at Geneseo. Changed my life.
Her material is really complex therefore her papers were difficult to write. Gives a lot extra credit opportunities. Extremely helpful. I enjoyed going to her class.
Best class I have taken so far  at Geneseo.  Even if you are a horrible writer, if you work at it you will improve by taking this class.  Definitely go to all of the conferences, they help a lot.

Beth was personable and fun.  The texts were all relevant and useful.  Her feedback was helpful and thoughtful.  She makes you think outside the box and find what really interests you.  I learned so much from her and I'm very impressed with her as an educator.  The coursework could be very challenging, but not stressful.

She didn't focus much on the topic at hand in class discussions but instead talked about whatever made her sound smart at the time with only a few people.  Be warned that jumping into class discussions is difficult unless you want to get your intelligence assaulted.  Boring paper topics and most of the class was focuse around the text, Cane.

A fantastic teacher who really wants to help you. A must for Intd 105 because she will help you understand how to truly write and analyze. She really knows what she's talking about and the class will go by very quickly.

Smartest woman in the world. Very respectable. Hilarious. Class flies by. Does everything she can to make the class a community. And if your writing doesn't improve after one of her classes you obviously didn't go. Shes a tough grader so a good grade on a paper is incredibly rewarding. Don't expect an A in this class without a lot of extra work.

Unlike anything I've ever taken.  The readings are all useful, interesting, and accessible.  There are four response papers and one final paper (5-7 pages).  The point of all of them is to really get you thinking.  Beth is BRILLIANT.  She's also open-minded, approachable, and always willing to help.  Hands down the best teacher I've ever had.

She is a great professor.  I learned how to become a much better argumentative writer because of her.  She was always there to help whenever I needed it and I would definitely take another class with her.  She is a tough grader, especially on the first paper which I got a D+/C-(which wasn't recorded), but by the end of the year I got an A-.
She's really awesome - she really knows what she's talking about. Even if you take the class and don't get A's, you'll benefit from the class overall. She also gives extra credit opportunities.
Let's just say that after one of Beth's lectures back in 1999, she got a standing ovation. She inspired me to be THAT kind of teacher. She rocks!
No Comments
No Comments
Absolutely an amazing professor!  Classes were always interesting, well structured, and enjoyable!
She'll blow your mind.  Make you think in a whole new manner.

I LOVE BETH!!!  She really makes you think.  She's awesome during office hours and I LOVED the class.  She can be a tough grader, but as long as you "Unpack" your thoughts in your papers you'll be fine.  TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! It will be a challenge but IT WILL BE WORTH IT!!!

McCoy is not a bad person but she's a horrible teacher. I learned more about Af-Amer lit in my other survey classes than in her Af-Amer lit class. She's not very open to other ideas. Don't take her unless you like being told that you should feel shame for being white.
Great prof. "Think outside the box" kind of person. If you don't like class discussion, avoid her classes, but if you do like it, definitely take it.

Beth is an AMAZING professor.  She challenges you to think outside the box and question what you have known to be true or taken for granted in your own life.  She's big on participation, and truly appreciates and excepts your comments and different interpretations. Don't be intimidated, she's great!

Very nice professor, but also sometimes intimidating.  She is very into participation and "unpacking."  She really appreciates it when you come and ask for help on assignments.  As long as you get into the discussion in any way, you'll be fine.  Also, she had no final which is always a plus!

There are a few assignments that may seem major, but she frontloads the course, and there isn't a final, so the end of the semester is very easy! She tends to be lax about due dates, so just let her know if you have a problem. She's alway willing to help. She encourages discussion, so beware!

Very engaging. She'll make a huge deal out of participation at the first class, but don't be afraid. It doesn't end up being bad at all. Good material and discussion. Sometimes she's a little over people's heads. It's hard to take Af. Amer stuff with her cuz the class is all white.

Beth is excellent--cares about your ideas, not your grades. Very into discussing your own personal interaction with texts, and very idea-oriented. Smart and provoking, and does not think anyone is stupid. I love her even though she could assign more hard-core work.
Highly discussion oriented, if you don't like talking avoid Beth's classes.  Other than that, outstanding in every aspect.

AMAZING prof- will work very hard to get you to the point where you're examining everything in your own life you previously took for granted-- gets even the most reluctant students to contribute to class discussiong without any force, just by peaking their interest- goes far above and beyond her job
amazing, smart, witty, beautiful, passionate, energetic, all with a touch of class.  She drives the point home.
I never thought I could enjoy hum so much.  She's a great teacher, encourages students' own perspectives.  Classes were interesting, and I was SAD when it was over

she is awesome-a very cool woman who pushes you in an unorthodox way.you don't really care too much about your grade in the class, she gets you too wrapped up in the lessons that make you question things you never did before.feel exhausted after her class
i totally disagree with the advising comment.  she is a dedicated advisor.  she expects responsibility tho

Beth was fantastic.  She was the best prof. I ever had at Geneseo. She made us think, she challenged us at every turn, and she lost herself in the lit. She also created a comfortable classroom environment.  Thanks Beth!
I appreciated her enthusiasm and passion for cultural literature, but it was hard to discuss all viewpoints in my white-only class. She pushed too much for answers we couldn't come up with.
not very helpful as an advisor, either
No Comments
She is AWESOME! I love her. She engages you in topic and you come away with something meaningful. She's the best prof.
Beth McCoy rocks my intellectual world.
tough but helpful and makes things matter
No Comments
Students talk about her like she is the best prof....I don't come close to agreeing.
Very Engaging, challenges you to think and speak your mind...An asset to school
No Comments

She is a great professor and principal. There was a lot of work to do inside and outside of class, but I feel much more prepared for how to teach a class and what is expected of you as a teacher. She is willing to help you as long as you ask for help and are willing to do work. Projects can be tedious but they help you to understand how kids feel.
Extremely disorganized and it is frustrating to navigate her class.

I think she is a kind person, but her directions and layout of the online class was so disorganized. There are many typos and technical errors. It wasn't clear what was explicitly expected. This caused stress among the class. It takes a while to communicate with her.

Absolutely abysmal, and incredibly frustrating. I don't think if I were a weaker person I could have made it through this class as I did. Just makes the same ridiculous suggestions over and over even if your student will stuffer from them and doesn't care about growing you as a learner.

She is the very definition of "disorganized". The due dates in her syllabus are incorrect (because she never changes them). She's an easy grader but doesn't hold back on providing useless criticism. If you are ever confused about an assignment and need any clarification, don't expect an immediate reply. Oh, and do not take her for clinic. Godspeed.
Very disorganized!

Dr. Peck was awesome for my first summer taking classes at the graduate level! She was very accessible and always available when you had questions. Dates sometimes got mixed up but this was understandable since we were taking a summer course that was only 4 weeks. I loved attending the optional weekly conversations about reading. Love Dr.Peck!!

Dr. Peck was incredibly unorganized throughout our entire semester. Her responses indicate that she doesn't read your work for content or context but is mainly concerned with your margins and font size. Dr. Peck gives out constructive criticism about once in a blue moon and all other comments (there are many) are snarky or just mean. Don't take!
Totally disorganized. Wants everything to be fun but then doesn't teach us anything.

While the class itself would not be difficult taught by another professor, her lack of organization and communication makes it almost impossible. Directions are unclear and scattered, not to mention how long it takes to get an email back from her. I have had to email her for clarification almost everyday. Do not take her class if you can avoid it.

Dr. Peck is a very enthusiastic teacher. She really loves to practice what she preaches when it comes to play-based learning. Her class is interactive and inspiring. Im now obsessed with play-based learning! She does assign quite a bit of reading for during the week, but you can get by if you only read what you are presenting that week.
The most unorganized professor I have ever had!

One of the worst professors I have EVER had! She hands out the syllabus and that essentially is supposed to tell you what to do for all your assignments/projects. It is unclear and so is she. I have had to read 100's of pages of text only to have NEVER discussed them in class. She also doesn't have a lot of meaningful activities, also disorganized.
Great, loving teacher. Knows her material well.

One of the best professors in the Education Dept, for sure. She knows what she's talking about, and she's so happy to share her knowledge with you. If you have any questions, she'll help you in any way she can!
No clear guidance and direction... Sometimes I feel disappointed and don't want to attend this class.

Wow. I do not know where to start.  Guidelines (if you can call them that) are unclear... you basically have to draw upon several different sources to have a remote idea of what she wants from you.  Many long term projects.  She's enthusiastic about the material, but not enough to cancel out the frustrations you will encounter because of the class.

She's a nice person, but she NEVER gives directions and she NEVER explains assignments. ASK LOTS OF QUESTIONS if you get her. If you ask q?'s about the work you'll do ok. Once you know what to do the stuff is EASY. She grades EASY too. Lots of the stuff is groupwork too. It isn't vital to read the textbook or assignments to do well. ASK QUESTIONS!

You literally have no idea what is going on. the least clear teacher i have ever had. she is in love with the subject matter but cant help you at all. does not make class useful for secondary ed students at all. avoid if you can but if you cant just go to class and email her a lot. kinda useless assignments and a lot of them

Teaches exactly how she says NOT to teach. In front of the overhead projector. Little to no hands on activities. Drones on about nothing, very boring and unhelpful. She should stick to puppets because she can't teach. Little experience in the real teaching world (what is she only 35?)
He's awesome! Lecture based, easy quiz's, entertaining classes. 10 out of 10 take his classes. There is a lot of group work but it is graded very fair

Harnish is hands down my favorite professor in the business department. He grades very fairly, his tests are easy and he does review for them. Literally a college level course in terms of material but with high school level difficulty on tests. He wants your grades to excel while learning the material, and not to bury you in nonsensical work.
Not hard, did not have to show up to class besides exam days, only hard thing was the final

Dr Harnish is great! He is extremely accommodating; when the final got switched to in-person instead of online last minute and I told him I was past the deadline for the testing center, he allowed me to take it at home! Such a kind person, funny, tests are easy if you pay attention in class, and lectures are engaging. Very reasonable grader as well
Harnish is amazing. There are 3 speeches in the class but it's easy and overall the class is easy. He's funny and nice too.

Harnish is one of the best professors I have taken a class with here. His goal is for you to get something out of his class but not making it unnecessarily hard to do so. His assignments are fun and straight forward. I highly recommend taking a class with him.

Dr. Harnish is awesome. Lectures are easy to understand, assignments are always clear, and tests are easy if you just study a little bit. He always ends class early, super chill. Would 100% take a class with him again.

Harnish is a really chill guy and loves to teach. His lectures tend to be short and follow the reading pretty well. He takes attendance before every class and usually ends classes early. There are many speeches in class The final group presentation is pretty long but easy. He gives usually at least one assignment due on Friday.There's only one test
He's a great guy. He teaches the basics, but makes sure to help you ace it so you have a strong base to stand on in the future. 10/10, would take again, even if he graded tougher.

INTD 205 is mostly presentations, mixed individually and in groups. The hw is online and is usually one assignment a week. Harnish is respectful and professional . No quizzes/tests, just one final exam and he gives you a study guide for it. Presentations aren't bad. Take the class. Easily one of the most down to earth professors on campus.

Good professor. Means well and respects all students. Direction in the class was slightly unclear at times but that's not too big of a negative. Has a good perspective because he currently works as an executive for a non-profit.

Professor Harnish was super caring and made his class very enjoyable. He does take attendance, and it will help your grade if you go. Lenient grader, assignments were not too difficult if you put the work in. Highly recommend him, and I plan to take future classes with him.

Wonderful professor. Shes very knowledgeable about the topics you study and tries to make lectures as interesting as possible. Study for tests and you will do fine. She wants you to pass and will try to help you if needed. I cant explain how much I loved her class!
Lecture heavy, not specific, big on participation. Good luck finding her outside of class

Amazing professor!! Great lectures, full of personal experience from years of clinical experience. The class is work; there is a lot of content to learn and she assigns 4 papers, but any abnormal section would be a lot of work and she makes it so worth it.  Gives out study guides for the test and has very clear, well organized slides online
She's amazing

Professor Forbes is absolutely amazing. I have been sick most of the semester and she really went out of her way to help me succeed regardless. Her lectures are really great and she puts all the slides online as well as some of the quizzes. There are a couple papers but they're actually quite fun to write.

He is such a sweet guy but I would not recommend this class if you are not good at memorizing (or you feel good about cheating like most students) because the tests are not easy. He does not really go over anything that is required for the tests and he constantly pushes them back. He does give makeups which is nice.

I enjoyed having Professor Kimball. The format of this class was 3 listening quizzes and 3 exams. If you read his notes and listen to the CDs he posts on Brightspace, you'll be fine. His lectures won't really help on the tests but if you enjoy the history of music, you may find his lectures interesting. He also gives a ton of extra credit.
really sweet guy, but does not focus on the actual content for quizzes in class. people cheat on the quizzes and he doesn't care

Kimball is amazing! He cares about his students, and will usually give extra credit (at least for the 100 levels). His listening quizzes are mainly based on the CD's given in class so they can be challenging, but usually as long as you listen outside of class and pay attention you should be fine.

He is a very nice man and has a lot of musical knowledge, but all class we would sit there and he would talk for 40min then play like 3 music examples then our entire grade was based on really really hard listening quizes. I'm a music student and I've had many listening quizes before and his were exceptionally hard for absolutely no reason

Prof Kimball is a nice person, however, his class is pretty difficult for a Music Gen Ed. Overall, I would not take this class again and instead take a different Introductory Music class. The quizzes count as 80% of your grade and are pretty difficult if you do not study. Do the extra credit write ups. Also the lectures don't go with the quizzes.

Jim Kimball is the sweetest man in Geneseo, without a doubt. The class had little to no outside work, with one short paper & presentation being about it. We watched movies and just discussed whatever he felt like discussing that day. Greatly increased my appreciation of folk music too! Love his class!!

Easier than expected. Kimball is the sweetest old man, very knowledgable about all things music (particularly folk music). A lot of the classes were boring since he loves to talk, but we had fun in a class of 5 playing the recorder/metal spoons and square dancing. Graded assignments are few, so definitely study for the listening exams.

Kimball is old, but hilarious. He's very charming and straight forward with the information, and really knows his stuff. The class requires a little more effort than expected, and the quizzes can be tough if you don't study for them. Nice guy, somewhat bland class, and textbook isn't required at all.

Adorable teacher and so nice and understanding.  Extremely boring and the tests are so hard.  You have to memorize like 40 songs.  Deff NOT an easy A.  Wouldn't recommend the class unless you're willing to work very hard. But he is a very nice man and will definitely help anyone who asks for it!

Prof. Kimball is a very nice and passionate person. He loves his class and is very knowledgeable about music. The class was boring but the music tests were simple as long as you studied and memorized the songs. The tests were right out of the notes. Class attendance was not mandatory.

For an 8:30 class, it was pretty interesting. Kimball is enthusiastic about what he teaches. Quizzes consist of memorizing songs, which is easy if you take an hour or two to study. He tells you everything you need to know on the test. Easy A if you apply yourself!

The best professor I have ever had. He was so knowledgeable about each and every topic we learned. The material is really interesting if you like music (who doesn't). Exams are a piece of cake because he basically tells you what's going to be on it. Take any course with him!!! You won't regret it.

He is so knowledgeable!  He reminds me of my grandpa! He is extremely understanding about missed quizzes, but this class is not an easy A, however, there are lots of opportunities to do well.  The best part of class is when he brings in instruments to play, or dances around the room by himself, I loved this class, and this professor.

The things he knows are beyond anything you'd ever imagine. He's intelligent and very knowledgable in what he teaches.  However it tends to be about things irrelevant to tests/quizzes/grades.. while interesting, not always helpful.  Study for all quizes they're not easy to BS your way through and they're 80% of your grade.

Jim Kimball is by far the most interesting professor I've come across on the Geneseo campus. To be in a room with him is to learn something new, almost without exception. He draws from an immeasurably vast bank of both knowledge and love. I think that everybody on campus should take Music Of the World's Peoples. Maybe that's just me talking, though
Very interesting class, you can tell this professor is passionate about what he does. Kind of boring and dull at times however. Tests are hard, so study, especially the listening.
He definitely knows his stuff, but trying to see him during office hours for a question a waste of time.  Takes forever to grade things.

Nice guy, knows so much about the performers and their music. Despite this, his tests are not as easy as those in a b.s. core class ought to be.. over half the tests are made up of T/F questions..which he makes tough. He also has listening quizzes but they're easy. I don't know where my grade is at, which is unsettling.. hoping for at least an A-
He is an amazing teacher.  He has old song sheets from every artist we learn about and he can play every instrument!  Super nice and helpful.  Easy to get in touch with.

Kimball is a genius when it comes to anything on music. He's also really friendly and a great teacher! You have to be good at memorizing songs to ace his tests. If you can do that (i put them on shuffle in itunes to test myself) then an A should be easily attainable. I really enjoyed this class.

This class became a lot harder the I had anticipated. I thought Professor Kimball had a wealth of information and appreciated what he had to offer. He did however go off on tangents sometimes that didn't have a lot to do with the class. If you take this class the memorizing and listening tests are def. harder then you would think! Study!!
Very fun teacher, Hes good at getting the entire class involved.  He's not shy about playing music or singing in falsetto (Pretty Funny)  Anyway, great experience all arround.
He is such a nice old man.  He was really into the subject matter.  If you know a little about music, this is an easy class.  Attend class and you'll be fine.  I had a lot of fun in this class.

He is a very intelligent man, and provides many details, but his tests are hard, I felt there was to much emphasis put on listening, and if you don't have listening memorized it hurts you big time, but other than that his class was fun, interesting and can play just about any instrument!

Very intelligent man, quite eccentric. Whatever he writes on the board make sure you put in your notes. Pay attention to what he says in class because he gives answers to the rev. sheets. Know all your notes and your listening examples because he tests on it all.  Easy A if you memorize everything.
Very nice, just make sure you memorize alllll of the songs, what country they are from, etc for tests. The tests are ONLY easy if you study for them.
If you think this class will be easy, think again. a lot of work and the tests are hard! he's a nice man and very smart, but this class was not easy, by any means.

I've taken two classes with him and want more.  He knows so much about anything involving music and has done so many things.  He's a treasure.  his classes are easy and interesting at the same time- unbeatable.
I'll never forget the day I walked into Popular Music and he was blasting Public Enemy.  He's a great professor.  Take folk guitar with him if you get the chance.
Interesting guy but presents a lot of information....there's lots of listening so study up
Very interesting guy. This was one of the best electives I took at Geneseo. He's funny, entertaining and extrememly talented. Don't pass up a chance to learn from him.
I've taken multiple classes with him.  He is funny, interesting, and knows everything about everything.
I have never been so amazed at one persons talent in playing soo many different instruments!  His love of music gave me a higher appreciation of music

I found him to be really confusing for this class.  but makes class interesting by bringing in his collection of random instruments from any given era.  know your listening rep backwards and forwards for any of his classes!

Professor Hart is a fantastic professor. Hart is deeply passionate about what he teaches and his lectures are very engaging. His course is very challenging, but he is dedicated to helping each of his students learn the material. Professor Hart is always very accessible during office hours and will help you with any questions about assignments.
genuinely in love with this man

Intelligent, knowledgeable, and caring professor.  Knows all his students by name.  Gives great and entertaining lectures which make morning classes easy.  Engages in discussion with students and has great metaphors/explanations that make it easy for different people to understand the same ideas.  Lots of respect for him and I would take again.

Professor Hart is probably my favorite professor at Geneseo. Despite PLSC 251 being very difficult and boring, I never felt that way when I was in his class. He kept things interesting, and was always available for extra help on the content. Could not recommend him enough!

comment: He is energetic and gives engaging and fun lectures so although you don't hAvE to go to class you should and he really appreciates that. Gives very specific instructions and detailed guidelines for papers and studyguides. He is really very helpful, especially if you go to Office hours

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Theres not many assignments, and he is not a super tough grader. His test are not that hard either. I went to only a handful of classes but still got 8.5/10 for participation. His lectures are interesting though. Nice guy too.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Prof. Hart is great! I have taken 3 of his classes now and have enjoyed them all very much. he can often go off on tangents and leave some of us confused, it is because he is very passionate and he always takes time for questions and to get everyone on the same page. Expect a lot reading, a small paper, a midterm, and a large research paper

Professor Hart made a tough subject manageable. I really appreciated his feedback that pointed out both the good and any "goofs" on assignments. He's energetic and funny throughout the lectures. There may be times where he goes on tangents, and you lose track of what he said. He's responsive through his emails. Final Paper had a great rubric.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Awesome educator. Made me want to actually learn Statistics, which is no easy task.

Hart is a really great professor. He's super nice and gives good feedback on tests/papers. It's a lot of reading and the quizzes aren't really easy so you do have to read if you want to do well. But if you just go to office hours and make an effort outside of class he explains things really well and is super helpful.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Professor Hart brings a great energy to his lectures and seems excited to teach. This class is heavily writing based. He does not explain what he wants from your writing very well and is pretty critical when it comes to grading the assignments. Also he requires a ton of reading for less than interesting literature.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: He is a great professor. He was very energetic and engaging even during the early class. He gives great feedback on tests/papers, the only thing is that he assigns a good amount of reading that is fairly difficult (I had to read over each one a few times) and has pop quizzes on the reading, but you know they are coming and can read carefully.
Notes can be confusing, but he has the students' best interest at heart. Encourages office hours, posts supplemental notes, nice guy.

Nice, but as a professor, he is not that good. He belittles his students with sometimes insulting comments and the course very heavily textbook based. His example problems are good, but it is hard to understand what he is after sometimes. The course is outcome based, as in the long, confusing tests basically determine your entire course grade.

McGarrah was such a great professor! Some people are just upset because they don't realize you need to do work outside of class to do well.  He was very attentive to the needs of his students and wanted everyone to do well. Everything covered in class was straight out of the book, and his review sessions were so helpful.

He was NOT a bad teacher, I learned alot from him. However he often had a belittling attitude toward his students. It was intimidating. On the other hand, he is a really sweet guy deep down, I think he means well. If you go see him in office hours he's helpful. You can tell he really has a passion for teaching and chemistry.
Enthusiastic about the class, tells you exactly what you need to know to get a good grade in the class. Most Fair teacher I've had at Geneseo.
Dr. McGarrah is a very passionate teacher. he put a lot of effort into making sure every student succeeds. I would strongly suggest taking a chem class with him. I got an A+
I thought he was a very good teacher. He made the class interesting as well as easy to comprehend. He used methods besides just lecturing to help use learn.
disorganized, unclear. Read the textbook, come to class sometimes, you'll do fine. That said, he said he's never teaching this course again so dw about it

Dr. McGarrah is definitely NOT the professor you want to have in an Intro to Chem course. He gives a lot of time consuming homework and his exams are hard and take forever. He's not helpful at all because he just can't teach. Take a different teacher for Chem. You'll thank me.
Terrible professor. Being fired/let go/whatever after Spring 2014. His lectures are so awkwardly uncomfortable. Try to get McKnight for Chem 116 instead.
does not explain the material well...he doesn't care if you go to class but yet he gets angry when you tell him you missed a class. office hours were not very helpful at all.

A nice guy, kinda geeky nerdy, but a sweetheart and honestly one of the only professors not within my major that made the effort  to know my name. Chem 118 is more challenging than Chem 116, but he goes over harder material in class. Do the HW and his old tests and its an easy A.
McGarrah is a very easy teacher, but is poor at explaining the material. He gives fair tests and is a very friendly person, just not the best teacher

Mickey-G was one of the best professors I have ever had! He is very friendly, and is always offering bits of advice, mints, and smiles! Seriously - take class with this man and attend his office hours! You will NOT regret this.

Although Dr. McGarrah may not be very clear with presenting the material in class, his tests are fair and he sincerely wants his students to do well. Of course, you need to be able to do some outside work on your own; keep up with the suggested readings and ATTEND OFFICE HOURS! A little awkward and quirky but a very laid-back guy. I got a B+.

Terrible professor.  Class isn't hard, but he doesn't teach anything so it's up to you to learn it.  Blames you for his lack of teaching skill.  When he goes over a topic, it starts with the most specific and briefly mentions the general. In the last test, it was 40% based on something he showed in 4 Power Point slides. Stay away at all costs.

This professor is TERRIBLE. Avoid him at all costs. Rather than admitting he does things wrong he blames everything on the students and, in turn, makes them feel bad about themselves. He makes mistakes all the time and if you read the book he makes lectures MORE confusing. If you have him, I'm sorry. read the book, and try not to listen to him...

So confusing, terribly disorganized, insecure and rude. You cannot ask questions, slides are always filled with mistakes. Do not expect to learn anything from lecture, teach yourself and you might do ok. If you have to take him, make friends with a chem major.

taking the class was the worst mistake of my life. He is a terrible teacher, doesn't know how to teach and expects you do to all the work on your own. He always has mistakes on his slides and spends a lot of class time fixing it. The tests are very hard, and the class will destroy your GPA. Taking his class would be a foolish mistake.

He is not the most organized. You MUST do the homework and read the textbook, he is not interested in summarizing. If he gives a worksheet know how to answer the entire worksheet. Don't expect to understand something based on lectures. He goes on tangents often and waste's time. Exams are hard. Only people who do well are the ones who took AP Chem.

He seems like a nice person but his lectures are pointless. We spend class working on sample problems that he gets wrong repeatedly which only makes the homework and tests more confusing since you must learn how to do the problems from the online homework. He uses a different textbook that is in a weird order and tests are hard. Nice, but not smart
He is the worst teacher ever. his notes are useless and he does not help, he makes things worse when you go see him. His lectures are a waste of time, you need the textbook to pass the class.

worst professor that i have ever had. lectures are out of order and make no sense. he rambles off topic and obviously does not know much about chemistry. our class corrected his quiz questions every time he handed them out. AVOID

I thought McGarrah was great. He's not the best lecturer, but he's extremely helpful in office hours and the mastering chem assignments he gives are also very helpful. Just read the textbook and pay attention to the mastering chem and you'll be set. And the clicker questions are a great grade booster too.

I had just had him....STAY AWAY FROM HIM! I studied so hard for this class, and I have learned absolutely nothing from listening to him speak. His tests are ridiculously hard. I study so much, and I thought I would do really well. His tests just have the randomest questions on them. He gives a TON of hw online weekly too.

he is the WORST professor ever, he doesn't follow the textbook, the mastering chem hws are based on chapters of the book he hasn't even talked about yet. Lectures are boring!! AVOID HIM COMPLETELY. Test are ridiculously hard

McGarrah is a wonderful professor! Only LAZY people would give him poor ratings. Yes, for science courses one must actually open the textbook every once in a while. This course is EASY if you pay attention. I did not have to attend any office hours, rarely opened the textbook, and got an A. He is extremely helpful, enthusiastic, and fun. Take him!!
worst professor ive ever had by far.
Utterly useless, shouldn't be allowed to lecture for a class ever. Nice guy at least, just useless for a class.
Lectures = confusing. Better off not going and sitting in Milne reading the textbook. "This electron went to Tahiti!"
Worst professor ever. Trust me. DO NOT TAKE HIMMMM

How this man was hired is beyond me.  Taking this professor was one of my biggest mistakes thus far. Don't even go to lecture, it's pointless and confusing.  Read and teach yourself from the book and you will be far better off.  His half a letter grade curve was also not enough.  Exams were very hard. BEWARE

Pointless lectures. You're better off skipping class and reading the textbook on your own. Voluntary review sessions are a big help though. End of the year curve is great and it's not hard to do well if you do all the work on your own. Makes things more complicated in class than they appear on exams. Confusing but the curve makes it worth it.

Lectures are pointless,but fun. He spends too much time teaching simple concepts instead of more difficult ones. He is VERY helpful...tests are impossible but he has one of the most generous end of the year curves ever. I recommend Dr.Mcgarrah...he's a nice guy and very funnny.

mcgarrah isn't a good teacher. unless you plan on spending a large amount of time running to all his office hours & review sessions-dont plan on getting a good grade. He doesnt sway the exam avg like chem professors usually do either. The exam average in my class was a 64 and he said that he was pleased with that. Take a more experienced professor

Great professor!  If you read the textbook and do the mastering chemistry, then you'll do well in the class.  The lectures are interesting, but the exams are mostly from the textbook and mastering chemistry.  He is a really great guy who really cares about his students.  He is always willing to help students who go to his office hours.
very stingy with grades but notes are extreamly great. his tests are based on weird details. but great guy though.
McGarrah is really a great person. I am sure that those who are not doing well are not putting in effort and have never even talked to him. He is really very helpful and accommodating.

At first I thought he was arrogant and cold. After going to office hours and review sessions, he is a really personable guy. I think he needs to know what the student abilities are and once he knows, he's extremely helpful. He'll extend office hours and such to accomodate. His lectures are confusing but, they've gotten better through the semester.

Dr. McGarrah really isn't that bad. People that get bad grades, don't try to get good ones. If you go to his review sessions and take time on the mastering chemistry, you'll do fine in his class. He practically hands half the test over in his practice problems before the test. He is very helpful (if you prove yourself committed to learning.)

The only person I can thank for my B- in this class is myself. While that sounds motivational and all, it's really just annoying because this professor hasn't taught me anything. Students learn quickly that attending class is useless, but are forced to come anyway because McGarrah will kill their attendance grade otherwise. In short: stay away.

He has the delightful effect of transforming a once interesting subject into class after class of meaningless lecture bearing no relevance to anything you will actually need to know. But beware- though you will spend your classes wondering "what am i learning?", you still have to show up unless you want to see your grade drop for no reason at all.

If you show up to every class and hang on his every word it still doesn't matter. You will learn useless chemistry that won't help you on the exam. It's up to the students to struggle through the homework assignments and teach themselves. I understand that it's his second year here but at this point he has proven to be pretty useless as a teacher.

If you came to college thinking "I really love the idea of paying thousands of dollars to teach myself chemistry," then this is the class for you. Lecture tends to review the easier parts of homework we figured out on our own the week before.

McGarrah's lector is useless.  He spends lots of class time trying and failing to use is technological toys.  When he does get things working he rambles on innocently about the most unimportant typic of the chapter.  He is really unhelpful and kind of mean.  The online homework assignments suck.

I had McGarrah for his first year teaching and yes, he was pretty disorganized and couldnt figure out how to use a lot of the equipment, but  that's not his fault. I went to office hours a lot and he was helpful at explaining things to me. have him again for 216 and he is much better this year, cracks jokes during class, a little more laid back
Worst teacher i have ever had in my entire life. plain and simple
No Comments
least helpful professor i have ever had

Frequently messes up on slides, presentations, examples. Generally confusing. Not teaching material. Ended up teaching myself from the book. Uses MasteringChemistry.com for homework assignments. Avoid him if you can't teach your self.
He loves the course material. I thought the final was hard. Have to show up to class because participation part of your grade. Not  very helpful, but I still earned an A. Reads off power points.

Mr. Cook is a nice guy. A little biased toward the Democratic party in my opinion. Lectures directly form power points, so a little dull at times. Very clear about his expectations however. Has a real passion for American Politics! I'd recommend him to all.

Great professor. A lot of reading, and participating every class is a chunk of your final grade. There's no quizzes, only two tests--the midterm and the final-- along with two papers. Both tests were easy and the 150 question final only took me 1 hour to complete. As long as you keep up with the reading and participate, you're guaranteed an A

Good Professor.You will have two tests. Midterm, 50 questions(5 chap. in 1 book, 5 in another) and take home essay. Final 150 ques(11 chap in 1, 10 in another. The second textbook is just debates between two people and u just need to know main idea. I studied for about 1 week per test and got an A in the class. lot of material but straightforward.

Not a difficult class. As long as you participate, you'll be fine. I never used either of the textbooks, though the Barbour one is worth buying because he does reference it. The other one is just the same thing you learn in class. Good time slot.
I personally thought he was a good professor, just got a bit boring and dull. It was an easy class, just know your stuff.

This prof can sometimes make you fall asleep, his lectures are very boring. The powerpoints he uses contain all the information you'll need for a test. I didn't even buy the books. Overall he does teach the material well and is a fair grader.
class was pretty boring - he didn't really add much valuable information to the book, so you don't need to go to class if you do the reading. easy tests, lots of extra credit.

Nice guy and easy class. Tests are not hard, and he's an easy grader on papers. Class kind of boring for it's usually class discussions on topics. His notes are from the book and he e-mails them to you.

Laid back professor. Sends you all powerpoints and materials. The only reason to go to class is for participation points. Tests are fairly easy. I maybe went to half the classes and I am maintaining an A-. Boring but it could be worse.

this class is just like participation in government that we all took senior year in high school except more boring. easy credit opportunities and tests, though. you wont regret it but you wont like it. ps choose him over klotz!
Straightforward. Not interesting, not horrible.  Formulaic, records participation.
Uses a number of examples in current issues that helps learn the topics, however, he is extremely partisan and will let you know if he doesn't like your comment.

Take the class - He's a great professor who warms up to you as the semester goes on. He is very lienent about a lot, and overall he loves to teach and you can see it. His tests are not bad at all, and the information in lecture might go fast, but if you study you'll be fine. You won't regret taking this course!

He's in politics so he can bring in stories about topics.  Also has a few guest speakers every semester.  Daily class discussions that break up time spent on just notes.  The notes follow the book closely.
A very nice guy, a bit boring sometimes... do the readings and participate and u'll do fine. Fair grader and not too bad exams. Has interesting guest speakers come to lectures.

Cook is the worst teacher i have ever had. He is a very nice person, but that does not reflect his teaching ability. He just teaches out of the book, and comes up with DUMB projects or assignments that dont work. I would not waste you time with this class
Class is pretty fun if you participate

Cook was a good teacher with a cute sense of his own humor.  His class could be boring sometimes but he was very easy to understand.  I did very well in his class and learned about current news as well as politics.

COOK SUCKS!!! He doesnt teach crap!! He reads you a book....THATS HOW YOU LEARN!!! He is boring, and his voice is SOOOO ANNOYING!! This man needs to stick to his regular job and quit teaching. Nice man.....HORRIBLE TEACHER!! and he is a **** LIBERAL!
Smart guy, hard grader.
Great teacher - interesting, lots of real-world experience to share.
he doesn't teach!  he just spends the whole time asking students to explain everything.  hard to take notes.

American is a waste of time, the only reason i go to class is because occasionally he has some good quest speakers and he also gives out pop quizes, to do well look over the important parts of the book, he is horrible at lecturing
Fantastic professor. Exams are very fair and offer lots of partial credit potential. He is very entertaining in his lectures and does a great job explaining the material.

Dr. Fletcher is an amazing prof, as long as you don't try and take advantage of his "open door policy." He might tell you that if his door is open you can come by and get help, but don't expect to get it without him being annoyed. The class itself is ok and the homework is doable. If I would've applied myself I could've done better in the class.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Fletcher is an amazing physics professor. The only downside is that there were 3 exams total worth 80% of your grade so if you did poorly on one exam your grade is kind of set for the entire semester. He is super helpful and understanding when it comes to needed additional help and I highly recommend going to his office hours if help needed.

Fletcher is a really nice person, so I feel bad rating him poorly. The material itself was hard, certainly, but the main issue I had was the way he structured the class. Everything about it - the grading, his expectations, what to know - was SO unclear. He would spend an entire class going over one equation only to tell us we didn't need to know it

Prof Fletcher is a good guy and cares for his students. The class can be quite boring however and there are no in class or out of class assignments other than essays. The highest grades in the class are typically high eighties. Makes it hard to really do as well as you should in an intro to writing course.

lectures are clear, grading criteria is clear, he is more than willing to sit with you and explain complex questions/concepts. i was nervous about learning physics online, but he made the material very easy to understand. he's very accessible in office hours and genuinely wants all his students to do well

Dr. Fletcher is good at teaching. However, sometimes he can come across as pretty condescending. Homework is on WebAssign and the questions are significantly more time consuming and difficult than they need to be. He does paper tests, unlike the other PHYS123 sections, which are fine, but if you make one mistake you lose a lot of points.

His finals weigh so much you can fail just with that. Do your homework when he assigns it because its too much for the average student. Not extremely understanding. Good guy but always check on your grade! You guys can be close and he will still fail you!

comment: I didn't do amazing in this class (considering its my major), but I did like like him. He is also my advisor, and extremely helpful with anything you need. For anyone taking  analyt 1, start the HW early. Great guy tho
Best choice for Analytical Physics. If I didn't take it with him, I'd probably fail. You get a lot of partial credit, because he does paper tests. Provides a good amount of study material.

Best professor to take Analyt 1 with. Gives good notes and ways gives example problems. Tests and quizzes aren't difficult if you pay attention in lecture and do the webassign. He often gives solutions to homework in lecture with out students noticing or he will just ask if we have any questions on it. He is all around a great professor.

Fletcher is the best professor I have had at Geneseo.  He is truly one of the best educators at this institution.  I strongly recommend anyone to take a class with him!  He is so, so helpful in office hours.  He will help you even when he doesn't have office hours.  It's unbelievable to me how much he cares for his students.  FLETCHER IS THE BEST!
Fletcher is the man.

It's Calculus-Based physics, (i.e Impossible) He is a very  nice grader but you have to put in some work. Go to class everyday. There are quizzes every week. Do the homework. You will fail miserably if you don't. God help you. Too bad, he doens't teach part III. His exams are written. (Other pyhsics exams are computer based. So, no partial credit.)

Fletcher is really great, he's passionate about how interesting quantum is and he really makes you interested too, the way he teaches makes it very understandable and he is very helpful in office hours, homeworks are long but helpful

Eh. I think I would have rather had capa tests and taken Baker. Fletcher is very conceptual and tends to withhold information during lectures so that you have to look it up and figure it out on your own. He is also a little girl when it comes to distractions in class and yells at the entire class for the few people on their phones. Viva la Pogo

Kurt Fletcher is the man. Incredibly friendly and accommodating. Would recommend for anything. Not 100% clear in lectures but great in office hours. Regards all students unconditionally positively. Obviously enthusiastic about Physics. Tests and Homeworks are very fair.

Dr. Fletcher was a really cool professor. He made the class interesting and was always energetic in class. His tests were very fair and he was very generous with partial credit. He performs a multitude of demos over the course of the semester and collects student's corresponding response sheets for participation credit. Work hard and you'll do well

Excellent professor! He is so good at explaining things, uses a model or toy every class to make physics entertaining. He's always eager to help you in office hours. He played his euphonium for the class. You have to study to do really well on the tests, but overall its not a very time consuming course.

Physics is definitely not my thing, but Fletcher does a great job of making it tolerable.  Interactive lecture demos are pretty cool, doesn't call on you randomly like other profs.  Study the homeworks and old tests he posts, take advantage of office hours, very nice/helpful.  Hard class, but way better than first semester.

A fantastic professor! I really am not all that interested in physics, but going to this class, even at 8:30am is totally tolerable. Dr. Fletcher really wants to help his students and is a genuinally great person. Take Physics with him if you can!

Dr. Fletcher is definetly a good teacher.  He made the class fun and interesting for the most part, which wasn't  easy because a lot of the material for this class was covered in Analyt 4.  The only thing I didn't like about him is he wasn't as helpful as I thought he could've been in office hours.

Extremely unresponsive to students he doesn't like.  If you become "friends" with Dr. Fletcher, you'll enjoy his class.  I was a physics major, with a B average, but I struggled in Calculus.  I asked Fletcher for advice, since he was my advisor, and he told me to drop physics.  He didn't care to spend the time to help and assist his students.

I thought this was one of the best classes I took at Geneseo! He's a great professor-intelligent, helpful, interesting, and demanding on tests. I'm not a science person but was happy to take this class.

Fletcher is the best Physics professor and one of the best professors I have had in my four years at Geneseo.  He makes Nature of Light and Color fun; class is interactive and he is very energetic.  :-)

Funny and can get students interested in the most boring material ever.  Labs are ridiculously easy.  Tests can be quite challenging however, even if you understand the material reasonably well.  Textbooks are worthless, I didn't use them once - save some $ and just go to class once in a while.
This teachter is my favorite here at geneseo.  He is really nice and interesting.  I loved this class.

Dr. Fletcher is by far one of the best professors on campus.  He's funny and really knows how to get a class into the material. I'm not a science person but I got an A in his class because he made it interesting and he was always there to help you out
he's a very good teacher, but his grading system really irked me.  too much emphasis on stupid homework assignments.  how can you have an a average on tests and get a b-?
Wnderful, wonderful man- I never knew physics could be so much fun :)  Id recommend him to anyone.  My favorite teacher in 4 years of college.  The best in Geneseo

There were some Physics majors who adored this guy (most of whom were female, which was interesting, if not odd), but I never really clicked with him.  I found him to be a good presenter, but demanding grader - sometimes a blessing, but mostly a curse.
I am not a science person at all, and I did well in his Nature of Light and color class.  Great Professor.
No Comments

He's a very young professor, in his 20's. I took an English course, but it was about legal writing. The stuff he presents is confusing at times, though I can see how much effort he puts into his lectures. The lectures are often dull and long (it was a once-a-week class). I don't suggest this class for those who are not familiar with the law.

I had her as my advisor, and she was not ideal, aka, she never reached back out to me. However, I also had a class with her. She's okay, but can't reach her outside of class, and it's literally all over the place. Had 1 billion ideas with no execution, so it's super stressful. Other than that though, not great.

comment: Cares about her students, wants you participate, class is disorganize.
She is awesome. She makes you feel welcomed and doesn’t judge. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!
