Way too much work for an intro class. Immediately shuts you down if you disagree with her. The tests are hard and specific. She takes off points for not agreeing with her opinions

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: She is a very confusing human being. She gets very distracted when she talks. Her discussion posts are NOT clear, she doesn't give clear instructions on how the posts should be. Being in her class makes me want to give up on my college career.  Take caution!

Taking this course gave me an extreme disliking towards sociology. I did not like the way the class was structured. Between the discussion posts and the in-class group discussion, it is unclear what she expects from you as a student. This class will stress you out and make you hate sociology. DO NOT TAKE IT!!!

She is constantly all over the place and is super hard to follow, you get graded on weekly discussion posts which you can not repeat a previous students post (even if you have similar thoughts/feelings about a topic) Also every week you get into a group and discuss the readings for the week and there is a lot of readings for an intro course

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: Honestly, stopped attending her lectures after the first month or so, because she tends to go on tangents and we run out of time for the lecture. She posts the PowerPoints anyways. Every week there is a group meeting, split into 3 by last name, where you discuss the readings for the week, so just a heads up. Overall, it was a fairly easy class.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: This class has way more reading and work than an introductory class should have. There's a 2-3 page paper due every week as well as a weekly discussion day for class participation. She gets distracted to easily and can be hard to follow. Whatever you do, don't try to disagree with her even with proof, she doesn't care. Don't tell her your major!!

Her class is way too much work for a 100 level class. You will spend HOURS doing every assignment just for her to give you an awful grade. You never know what she wants for an answer. The tests are open-ended questions that are terrible and never seem to please her... DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
This class was awful. Professor Scott assigned a weekly paper due at the beginning of class, had weekly student led discussions, and tests were hard. Do not recommend.
The amount of shade she threw at people was very annoying! The class material is not hard, but there is a lot to read. I did learn a few interesting things, but it was not worth taking the course :(

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']
comment: during the online class, the recorded lectures were easy to follow and not repetitive or boring. professor scott spaced out the material and assignments in a way that it was easy to follow. and there are 2 exams that were fair since we were able to use our notes and there wasn't a final exam. she is very easy to follow and accessible out of class

the way she teaches and sets up class, especially when it was online, was easy, straightforward, and set you up for success. she gave weekly videos about what to expect and what was due. Her workload was manageable and she was not strict with responses in papers. she is very accessible out of class and one of the best professors at geneseo

Shes a sweet little lady. She makes funny comments sometimes, and shes very understanding about grades. She will stress to you herself that she is very very approachable and available. The class itself being so easy helps a lot too. Theres nothing that you wont already know, she just dives into more specific details.

The TA's grade your reading responses. And being a conservative, I'm not happy with the lack of inclusion for other viewpoints that disagreed with the liberal political agenda. I understand that the school itself is liberal, but tolerance for other views would be validating. Also, it's impossible to do well on tests. They're too harshly graded.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: There are little to no instructions, the TAs grade your weekly reflections ( on sometimes 70+ pages of reading.) Her tests are extremely particular, and almost impossible to succeed for most unless you can remember everything that happens in the readings. Some comments she says are inappropriate and sometimes offensive, shes very stuck in her ways.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']
comment: This class has been torture. She provides little instruction and grades harshly. You are expected to do all of the learning on your own. This is a 100 level class and she treats it like a 2-300 level class. Simply put, its horrible.

Just not a good professor. She's nice and is a well educated sociologist, but doesn't even teach! She reads off of a powerpoint that are facts from google, has the weekly discussion group lead the lecture, and the TA's grade the weekly essays! not to mention she often makes comments that aren't super appropriate to bring up. But, not a hard class

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Lectures one day a week and group discussion on the other day. 2-3 reading passages a week but if you read them carefully you'll do fine on them. Really good study guides, tests are pretty easy but based A LOT off the readings. She's pretty nice but kind of argumentative, sometimes annoys people and accidentally says offensive things.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Prof. Scott is a nice lady, and her class is pretty good, but she not once posted grades the entire semester so it was impossible to figure out where you stood in the class. There are weekly reports due, two tests (study!) and a final paper written about a book she assigns. Good class to take if you need a gen ed social science.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: This was one of the worst professors I've ever had in my entire life. her grading criteria makes no sense and is so specific that its as if she's setting you up to fail. you cannot disagree with her even if her information is a bit outrageous and she's spouting nonsense. Basically, if you are of a diverse ethnic background, don't take her class.

Good professor. In this class rotates between lectures and class discussions. Weekly short papers based on readings, very easy. Group project at the end of the semester leading a discussion. Important to go to class or read. She covers main topics of the readings in class but still need to read for an A.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Very sweet person, but has unclear grading criteria, very mean feedback. Exams are all essay based. You have to read 3-4 articles a week to get points in group discussions but you dont have to read the novel for the final exam just understand the theme. go to class, she notices when youre not there. I got solid B- on all exams, got an A- in class

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Professor Scott is such a sweet lady but not a great teacher. Her classes are easy, meets twice a week the lecture then a group presentation. Have to read 4 articles a week then do 7 out of the 11 mandatory journals about them. However, her exams are all essay based. She gives a study guide but her grading system is arbitrary and makes no sense.

Honestly one of the worst professors ever. She has no idea what shes talking about. She often goes off on tangents and says stupid things like "nazis shouldnt be punished". She specifically picks on students that disagree with her and has gossiped about them. She cuts people off so she can "correct" them. She also grades based on who she likes.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: The grading scheme is completely arbitrary. Information in class is factually wrong. The discussions are important. There is a ton of reading and the homework picks up around the second half of the semester. She is completely out of touch with reality. Would not recommend if you're not a soc major.

Denise is a very kind person and a wonderful and understanding professor. Her class was very interesting and I learned a lot during the semester. There was a lot of involvement with the texts and she does not spoon feed you what you need to know, you have to read the materials in order to get a good grade and participate in discussion.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: I learned a lot in Scott's class. Sometimes she can come off a bit condescending but she has a solid base of knowledge and cares about the topic. Lectures are intense (a LOT of writing, so don't skip) but her tests aren't too bad (the study guide is literally the test). She also has you write journal entries every week which are a grade booster.

She is set in her ways on how she thinks BUT if you just look past that and realize that is how some people are you will learn a lot and you will do well. Her study guides are literally her test questions.  She lets you pick 3/4 questions, giving you space to show off what you know.  Honestly, if you don't do well in her class then thats on you.

Dr. Scott's class is one of the best I've taken so far. There is a lot of reading but Scott selects them really well and you actually learn so much. Only a couple of tests and the study guides are very clear and great tools to do well. This is a very manageable course if you stay on top of everything and Scott is an excellent professor.

TAKE NOTES DURING CLASS. I cannot emphasize this enough. In order to do well on the tests you have to take notes she does not put power points online. Also do the study guides. Beware that there is a ton of reading. Overall this professor is pretty boring but the class is fairly easy.

Dr. Scott is very expressive when you answer questions, but not because she believes you're wrong, but because she is trying to understand your POV. She has 2 exams and a final. For her exams she gives out a study guide along with terms. Rewrite the terms a million times and DO THE STUDY GUIDE! The final: READ THE BOOKS SHE ASSIGNS AHEAD OF TIME!

Denise is a good teacher. It is an easy class. You will have assigned weekly journal entries on the readings that are just a reflection. There are a few essays thrown in instead of tests. All the writing helps you to analyze the readings and contribute in class discussion. The topics are interesting and the class encourages critical thinking.

She's really nice, but the way she sets up her classes make them torture. Students teach on Thursdays, but she dominates the discussion a lot of the time. Weekly 2 page papers and 3 6-page papers mixed in there. One group project. Don't take this class unless you're ready for that. Overall, pretty easy besides the busy work.

Must be well-prepared for tests because they are short answer/essay questions but the study guide she provides has all the potential questions so as long as you outline that and incorporate class notes into it, it is really easy to do well. Also, the journals are a huge grade booster. If you do them, you get credit and lots of feedback.

Professor Scott was very friendly, but the lectures were very dry. She relied way too much on her teaching assistants who grade your journals and exams; every week a different person grades your work and they all have very different expectations which made it very hard to improve. You have to use a ridiculous amount of detail in the essays to pass.

She's an enigma to say the least. Lectures are sometimes entertaining. She says things that are oddly inappropriate (e.g. talking about her infertility issues) but funny. She's a difficult grader and is insistent on examples and lots of detail. Tests are all short answer questions and essays. The class was overall more difficult than necessary.

Class was a drag.  Scott, is not one to accept different opinions from her own. If you feel a certain way she'll let you know that you're wrong. If discussion was short, you stayed the entire time. Very little leaving early. Material was dry and focused on women in India rather than Gender in South Asian societies. Wouldn't recommend her to anyone.

Dr. Scott is amazing! This course isn't going to be roses and lilies as one might expect. She gets down to the grit of it very quickly! I like that she tries to make people understand the importance of accepting and knowing about various types of families that exist and the role this plays in shaping public policy! Great course! I highly recommend!
Absolutely hated her. Gives off a bad attitude and is condescending. Always wants more out of you and is overall a boring class and terrible teacher.
Very interesting class. Thorough study guides are provided for all tests.  Easy if you go to class, do a fair amount of the readings and apply them to your tests/papers.

Great Professor who gives great study guides.  Each lecture is full of information that is directly connected and supports the reading.  Somewhat biased when it comes to some topics, and is not open to opinions that do not support hers but a nice person who genuinely cares about the topics she teaches.

Gives out a helpful study guide for the exams so you know what to expect. I feel like she didn't lecture as much because all she really did was lecture once a week and hold class discussions the other day... even when it was her lecture days, she would just show a video the whole time... journals do help boost you grade though.

Really interesting class, just don't forget to think for yourself. She is a bit biased during discussion, there is really no room for your own opinion. She genuinely cares about the subject, but she is odd in that she smiles when presenting depressing statistics.

Prof. Scott was very...interesting.  Definitely recommend going to see her if you don't do well on her tests (you'll improve your score!) And do all the questions on the study guide to prepare for the tests it'll help you so much!! Nice, but odd at the same time.  Likes to debate and is opinionated. In private she's not as intimidating as in class.

Dr. Scott's Political Sociology class is interesting and structured in a discussion setting, but it's definitely not a walk in the park.  The final essay is really difficult because you're not given any direction, but overall it's a good class.

She's a really nice person, and super intelligent, but she has a really hard time controlling large classes, and if everyone else's interest wanes, yours will, too. Going to office hours really helps your grade- she likes it if she knows who you are

Professor Scott is awesome! She's super nice, the readings are almost always interesting, she's a fair grader, and she hands out outlines before tests so you know what to study. She has class discussions every week, so it's not always lecture either. Overall, I highly recommend her and this class!

Prof Scott is a very nice lady, she tries her best but can be a little scatterbrained at times. Class is easy if you put some time into it, an A is achievable. She gives study guides, making the exams pretty easy. I would recommend the class, I learned a lot.

Overall, she's a good professor.  She's not difficult and really kind and friendly.  At times, she makes sociology interesting but then there are other days when you just want to get out of class.  Weekly journal articles can get annoying but if you do the reading, you should be fine in class.

not terrible but not good. she doesn't give you enough notes. she has group presentations each week, so she doesn't even teach you for 10 class periods. she puts a feminist twist on everything. expects you to use the minutest details on tests which are all essays. i probably would not recommend this class.

I had her this year for intro, and I easily got an A for the class. She tells you ahead of time what readings you have and most are interesting. If you study you do fine (she gives a study guide and picks from that)Two tests and final paper and 8 out of 12 journals on reasings). It's not hard! :)

I took this class my sophomore year as a psych major & human develop. minor.. & thoroughly regret it! At the expense of sounding arrogant, I have to be honest and say that the woman has no idea what she's talking about. She relies on the texts, rarely gives useful notes, & it really seems like grades are given arbitrarily. Take with someone else!
Not a bad teacher, however she relies heavily on the texts and will base much of the exams/papers directly on these. Not good for people who don't do their reading!

Bored out of my mind every class. She goes on long, meaningless rants completely irrelevant to the class. Lots and lots of readings. What she writes on the board during class is completely useless and rarely makes sense. Didnt study and got mostly Bs. Easy grader on papers.

She doesn't let you know what you really need to know for tests, you just have to take notes all the time in class pretty much about everything. You have to do the readings and take notes on them becuase they are tested on. She is a fair grader and as long as you stay focused in class you should be fine.

this class was really easy. she doesn't use a textbook, you read  articles instead, which were fairly interesting. paper and tests were very easy. she is a nice woman and very intelligent, and if she talks about her son, it's only to say that he's fat, which is kind of awkward.

she does talk about her son too many times, its annoying-she just doesn't get it-she does not have the right amount of social skills. She’s the weirdest of all which is probably why the ratings are diverse, but she loves sociology & it shows. she's full of opinions & information. Give her a chance & you’ll learn a lot. If u like socl you’ll do well

I cannot express in words how sick I am of hearing about her 12 year old "wonder son" or her impending divorce. However, her class is ridiculously easy, and if you do all of the reading you will coast through with no problems. Her tests are all essays (short answer/one long one), and she grades ok.
Great teacher.  Tells you exactly what you need to know for her tests and grades fair
Wonderful teacher, cares about her field and her students. Fair grader. Makes every effort to get students to fully understand material, which is usually not too difficult.

Overall, I enjoyed the class.  I registered for this class at the last minute because the required courses were all filled.  I thought it was going to be a lot harder but I learned a lot and she is a great professor who knows what she's talking about and makes class interesting.

Dreadful teacher. She's so creepy when she smiles because you know she isn't really happy. Students never went to class. Her tests are unbelievably easy. Before this, I had never fallen asleep in class. So much for that...

She never dots her i's correctly and that drives me crazy. She smiles for everything but she's not very smart. Her tests are unbelievably hard. I went to every class and did all the readings, and still didnt do well. You think you know one of the essays but she takes off points literally for no reason. She can't spell either.

I LOVED this class. Denise Scott was one of the kindest profs I had. The class is not too in depth, but she gets you motivated on the topic. If you want an A go to class. I had poor (read freshman) attendance and still did well.

Very boring. No one ever went to class and so everyday she would say "now i know it's hard to come to class because of (weather hot/cold, tired, beginning of the semester, end of sem.)" It's not the weather! It's you! Yells and smiles at the same time.

I also took her for Intro Soc. I hate her. She is very subjective, a lot of the grade is based on her personal feelings for you. I scored perfectly on m.c. and would lose unfounded points on an essay. One essay would get an A, another a D. It made no sense. I almost went to the dept. head about her
Great teacher!  Very interesting and if you pay attention in class, you'll ace the tests.  Loved it.

Good class.. if you're not concerned about grades! The material, readings, and guest speakers are very interesting, however, her tests are rediculously diffucult to do well on.. 3 essays in 1 hr. 15 min. which should be given 2 and a half hours to do
Very easy class, if she doesn't like your writing style you might have a hard time.  Only 2 tests, really easy!  I plan on taking more classes with her.

I hate this class more than anything in the world, and I hate her teaching style. She lectures on and on in the most awful tone that makes me want to NEVER EVER go to class! Don't take her if possible
Made Soc. very interesting, and is a really nice women. I would TA with her if I could.
No Comments
very good teacher...i got an A- with little effort
Very nice and funny. Forgot my name once but not in a mean way. He cares about his students and his lectures always have good flow and conclusion and I always feel like I learned something.

The class made no sense. Two large assignments were practically the same thing, but both had unclear directions, making it easy to mix up the two. The syllabus had no information about assignments or due dates on it, only Brightspace. Unclear due dates and assignments made the class overly difficult for what it was.
one of the sweetest professors ever! the class was quite boring but he made it bearable.
Really pushed the boundaries of what I knew. Super enjoyable and valuable experience.

Ken Cooper is honestly the sweetest man ever. He cares about his students well-being and takes the time to get to know them and how he can support them. Just today he took my class to Starbucks to treat us for actually showing up. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him if given the chance.
The sweetest guy. Felt very comfortable speaking in his class

He is a very sweet man who is always very understanding. His class is a little hard if you don't read a lot but his class is like a breath of fresh air in comparison to other college courses because of how nice and understanding he is.

This class was quite boring for me, but I did really enjoy Professor Cooper's enthusiasm and kind-heart. I had quite a bit of fun writing the short story based on an image, and writing the paper based on an architectural site that we had visited and enjoyed. His directions were confusing at times, but he is an overall enjoyable person.

very boring class, but he tried to make it interesting. a few response papers, one 7 page paper, and a reflective final based on what youve already done. easy class, but he gets sad if people dont participate.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Ken Cooper is such a sweet and caring man who loves what he does! His whole class is discussion based so there's no point in going to class if you haven't done the readings. He is extremely leniant with due dates and so understanding of certain circumstances. This being said the content of papers is sometimes difficult.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: I loved having Prof Cooper for a teacher! He made a lot of involving discussions to the material through readings/movies/videos. The novels we read were very intriguing. He gave lots of good critiques and always made sure to give positive feedback with his constructive criticism. Would highly recommend!

I absolutely adore Dr Cooper. He is the sweetest, funniest, and kindest man alive. If you are struggling he will help in such a nice way. He makes classes enjoyable and will listen to his students needs. 11/10 recommend Dr Cooper!!!

Professor Cooper is always available and makes you think the best of every assignment. He can be sometimes confusing, but that is easily resolved if you just talk to him. Flexible and considerate, I recommend this professor.

Tends to have long confusing lectures, but office hours help, and he often gives more. Kindest prof you'll meet. unclear essay prompts, he assumes you always know what he's talking about. takes criticism easily. 3 essays + 2 self reflection (mid/final) make up grade, as well as 20 percent participation. easy to pass and enjoy if you do the reading

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']
comment: I love Dr. Cooper! But his class isnt easy. We read a book a week and had a paper a week. The highest grade he gives on anything is a 95, no 100s. He also grades in increments of 5 (85,90,95). If you put in the effort, you will love the class and he will love you. Go to his office hours too! Hes very fun to chat with.
Cooper is really nice, assigns a ton of reading within a short timeframe. Really easy to chat with and makes sure to try to get to know his students despite being online.

Ken Cooper is rad. His Graphic novel class was a really interesting way to take an intro class and get kinds into writing. As an upperclassman I found it to be a breath of fresh air. It isn't very difficult to if you get the chance and want a fun elective to take, do this one!

The nicest guy ever. I took the Graphic Novel class with him and it was so much fun. We had weekly online discussions and then there was one essay, a research proposal, and a 7-8 page research paper. The books were good and he was always available to meet if you needed help on an essay. SO NICE!

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects']
comment: I appreciate the topic and care and attention he gave to class discussions to make sure this was a repeat of high school lectures since it was a primarily freshman taken course. He gave me the SPECIFIC and tangible changes and direct annotations on my papers earlier one and is a great professor to share work with outside the course.

He is kind, very sweet and understanding. With all these things going on in world like corona virus he gives the student a chance to be able to succeed on their grades if they need to too. Also it was a free textbook. Just do all the school work and participate on discussion then you will suceed.

Remembers you as a person, not a grade. Taken two classes with him, and he always makes the class feel open to everyone. Afraid of looking stupid by participating with a half baked idea? He makes you feel comfortable sharing. Just wants you to try your best, and isn't afraid to be authentic with feedback. Makes you excited about your own ideas.

Cooper is a kindhearted soul who really wants the best for his students, but his class is all over the place. he expects unrealistic amounts of reading to be done for his classes and his essay prompts, as lengthy as they are, are not clear. his classes consist of him lecturing about numerous topics and not really leading a discussion

tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']
comment: Dr. Cooper is an awesome guy but you will only succeed in his class if you attend office hours. Lectures are unstructured and he basically just talks at your for the whole two hours. Essay prompts are not super clear and usually are open to heavy interpretation. Go to his office hours you should gain clarity and be able to earn a decent grade.

Professor Cooper has good intentions, but he talks in circles and his lectures are unclear. He is a thorough grader but his feedback makes as little sense as his lectures do. His book choices are very dry. The essay prompts are literally a paragraph. He's not a bad guy - he just makes no sense most of the time.

Ken Cooper is the sweetest! He cares so much about his students and genuinely wants you to succeed- but he is not an easy grader. Go to his office hours for every paper and it won't be hard to do well.

Dr. Cooper is a genuinely great human being. The class itself (nature writing) wasnt exactly enthralling first thing in the morning, but hes honestly one of my favorites. Extremely understanding, humorous and kind.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']
comment: Amazing guy. Gives great feedback, but somewhat of a tough grader. Prompts are sometimes too vague.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'SO MANY PAPERS']
comment: Cooper's a great guy, very suburban dad. Pretty chill about late work (I got an A- on a major paper that I turned in late). But there's just too much work. You have to get like 9 books and have a new one read each week, along with a short response paper. It's certainly not difficult work, just dull and repetitive. As long as you do it you'll pass.
Such a beautiful man. So nice. So accepting.

Professor Cooper is a great professor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and he made each and every lecture fun and interesting! We had three five-page papers to write on the novels we read and I know that I would have gotten an A if I went to see him more for office hours because he is very approachable and really cares about his students.

Ken Cooper was easily the best professor I've had. He's an overall interesting person. He is easy to have a conversation with and takes the time to get to know his students. One of the smartest people I have ever met. He gives great feedback and helps you become a better writer. I highly recommend!

Hands down my favorite professor at Geneseo. He's very approachable and makes class fun and interesting. This was my second class with him, and I'm taking his class again next semester. Seriously, if you can, take one of his classes before graduation. Very chill atmosphere and interesting discussions; office hours are very helpful.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Took his 70's film class, half of the films are awful. For response papers write about how you feel, he grades each with a check, +, or -,  to "reduce letter grade anxiety", but this grading scale only made me MORE anxious! Research paper is worth 35% of your final grade! Confusing lectures, struggled to break a "B", he's just okay at best.

I took his Pynchon class and loved Dr. Cooper as a person. I think he's a great guy, very kind and understanding, definitely knows what he's talking about. But there is TOO MUCH reading. Cooper does a good job ATTEMPTING to make this as easy as possible. But I found this was WAY above what I'm capable of. The reading level is impossible.

I loved Professor Cooper's class. Easily the most interesting professor I've had yet. I get where others are coming from regarding his lectures (you gotta focus or else you'll get lost), but damn I learned a lot. Really admire him as a person and professor. Super flexible about essays (I wrote a personal narrative!). Go to his hours for essays!

Cooper is funny and a nice guy but impossible to follow. There were only two essays and a final for the class so it's incredibly difficult to raise your grade if you mess up. The lectures are incredibly dry and it's difficult to participate. He often goes on tangents and I could rarely understand his message or point. I wouldn't take him again.

Cooper is a great guy, I don't doubt it. And he cracks great jokes and has clear dad-humor. However, his teaching style is confusing and vague. We are reading 9-10 books and often it is difficult to particulate in discussion. Confusing teaching style, seems all over the place, but offers his help. I probably won't take his class again.

His lectures a little dry, but it's a 400-level class. He seems to be passionate by what he's teaching and has really good dad-humor (haha!) He was always there for me when I needed him, but his papers are a bit lengthy! Make sure you get a head start on them. Group projects were essential to the class. But no exams - just papers.

I can't believe Cooper's rating isn't higher. He is easily one of my favorite professors on campus. I went to his office hours countless times just to talk with him about the class because he's such an enjoyable person! Highly recommend his 70s class. The movies are good if not interesting and the discussion days are great.

I don't know why people think Cooper is boring--his class was always very engaging and very interesting. It's refreshing to take a class where the professor's instructions for the papers is: "write something interesting." Love him.

Cooper is excellent.  He's the first professor I've had who is a genuinely nice guy, without pretension or arrogance.  Go to his office hours, just to chat- it's awesome.  The class is pretty easy; two essays and some responses to the books, all of which are interesting.  HIGHLY recommend- a class on comic books?  Where could you go wrong?

Ken is wonderful. I took my INTD with him fall of my freshman year, and even though I am a chemistry major, I really enjoyed his class. Walden is a bit dense, but he goes over the readings in class. Read the book and listen in class, and the papers shouldn't be a problem. He's also great about proofreading etc during office hours. Great professor.

This class is the best class I've ever taken! Cooper was engaging and intelligent. He's really into sharing ideas and he wants to see you excel. It's not an easy A, but it's not an impossible one. You have to be doing no work to fall below a B. I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and if you get the chance you should defiantly take him!

He is an awesome dude. The readings are difficult at times but he talks a lot about them in class to clarify things. There are only 2 essays, and he's a fair grader. He's also really funny, if you have to take Amrican Lit, take it from him! :)
He's a nice guy, but he's very boring. His writing assignments are vague and confusing, but he's not a hard grader.

Cooper is laid back, easy-going, and interested. his classes are typically centered around an idea he's been brewing over the course of his career... so at times it's hard to get on the same page as him, but overall, he's very accessible and open-minded. he does guide lecture, but thats to be expected, he's a professor. i recommend him.

I'm an American studies major, and taking this with Prof. Cooper was horrible, he did not teach it to the specifications of what the course is supposed to be, which was interdisciplinary. He did not understand that none of the students had seen the films as many times as he had, and had formed opinions that left no room for students ideas.

I was shocked to see that Ken Cooper doesn't have one of the highest rating at Geneseo! He is so engaging, so intelligent, and well.. a cool guy. I have him for an American Studies course titled Filming the 70's.. It really doesn't get much sweeter than that. It's an 8:30 and I don't think I've ever missed if. Great insightful professor! Take him.

Where to begin? Very easy going and easy to talk to. His classes are mostly lecture and very boring. He will use words that sound made up and will lose everyone. A lot of reading but his tests are semi easy as long as you read and attend class. He is a pretty fair grader.

Had him for Major Author: Thomas Pynchon. Got to give him credit for attempting to teach this author, especially his most recent novel which came out just last semester! Funny professor, classes are enjoyable and make you want to attend. Pretty easy grader, too. It's hard to get lower than a B, but challenging to get an A. Definately reccomend him.

Cooper's faults: He understands the text a little too deeply at times and then asks his students about their opinions on the concepts he has constructed through years of individual interpretation.  Essay assignments are vague and up to the critical reasoning of the writer.  His class can be tortuous if you aren’t prepared with the reading <3

nice guy but so boring. takes the majority of the class saying, yeah..thats a point id like to discuss next class. then what the heck will we talk about this class? stands scratching his head saying hmm for minutes at a time.  justifies people not coming to his class becuase the reading was hard. but its really because his class is pointless

I can give you a thousand reasons not to take this professor. he is very unclear on assignments and expects you to read his mind. somehow the whole class got some sort of a B, no As. horrible teacher.

Ken Cooper is pretty much a hippie. As many hippies do, Ken Cooper believes he knows everything about everything. Classes are pointless. He doesn't even give grades on his papers, instead he grades all the work at the end of the semester in one portfolio. Unless you want to revise everything aimlessly or you too are a hippie, avoid Ken Cooper.

Great guy! Hillarious, easy going, helpful, makes you think more in depth and forces you to improve your writing skills. Take a class with him you'll have a great time and he could care less if you miss class!

Cooper is probably solely responsible for enlightening me as a human. His classes are hard because dumb kids can't comprehend the idea of thinking beyond what is actually given in the specified texts. If you are looking to learn, definitely take his classes; if you want an easy grade and someone who hand feeds you the answers, don't. he's amazing.

A jerk.  Although my grade wasn't bad and the class wasn't hard, he'll do nothing to help you out.  He taught two of the same class.  I asked him if I could take the final in the earlier slot so I could drive my girlfriend home so she could have more time with her dying grandfather.  He told me that would require too much paper work.  Seriously.

Honestly, I didn't go to class much, but I kept up with the reading and did all the papers- steady Bs. But the classes I did go to were alright, despite its earliness. Good luck going to see him at office hours- I went once and there were a million other people waiting to talk to him too. Your best bet is to schedule an APPOINTMENT.
Lectured far too much for a literature based class. Annoying manerisims, says "you know" all the time in place of explaining whatever he's talking about. Avoid if possible.
you would thing it is hard to make terrorism a boring subject, but he did so without even trying. very boring, not really clear with what hes looking for in papers and tries too hard to sound smart.

He talks like a surfer. Says "You Know" more often than he actually gives information. He's only a professor because he likes to hear himself babble. He gives assignments and when you ask about it says things like "Write this as if you aren't a student in this class and haven't seen the syllabus". If you don't mind being bored/annoyed, take him

Amazing professor!  A lot of people say he's dry and boring, but you've got to be a little open.  He's tons of fun!! The class and reading has nothing to do with the papers, which is actually a lot of fun.  You get to write what you want, and he loves new ideas!  Very helpful in office hours!
Nice guy, all over the place as a teacher.  Excruciatingly boring more often than not.  Always gives B's to everyone on everything, which is frustrating if you ever try to do better.
I could never follow this guy. It hink he thought he had DEEp thoughts, but really he may have been in his own literary world

Cooper is the most hypocritical, close-minded man. He raves about being openminded, tells u to speak ur mind, but shoots you down if u dont see eye-to-eye with him. Class is easy, but insanely boring, all he does is ramble. He was probably beat up alot as a kid, deservingly. I never again will take a class with this man - waste of my time.
Great guy but can be very boring. The readings he assigns are incomprehensible but it's not like you really have to read them for the class anyways.
He goes off into these random tangents about his kids...it's great... a lot of people think he's boring but it really isn't so bad, he does tend to babble sometimes though
He's really boring, but nice and funny sometimes.

He seems almost condescending sometimes. Constantly gets off topic and can't crack jokes very well. Seems nice, but he's difficult to understand when you want a question answered. Classes are boring, and I wonder if he likes the sound of his own voice. Constantly tries to read facial expressions.

He will not give you below a B I swear. His lectures have nothing to do with what you read in class, but his attempts at cracking jokes are worth the effort of going to class, because you feel bad for him. Take his class to assure yourself a B.

Always my favorite. You need a discerning, intellectual mind to stomach him. If you're slow and don't understand big words, forget it. He does lots paper conferences in INTD, and it's really enjoyable to sit down and talk with him. Very into beat culture, obscure films. Horribly intelligent :)

Horrible class. Lectures are extremely boring and don't even pertain to the material that you are reading in class.  He is willing to help but will tell you to do one thing in an essay and then when you do it he will decide he doesn't like it and penalize you for it.
Hum at 805 with him is not recommended, but at any other time he'd be a great teacher. Do-able assignments and work, enjoys class contribution, talk to him and you'll do well.
He is a great guy with a great sense of humor

In 1994, Ken Cooper co-taught Hum with the late C.R. Bailey.  I loved the dynamics the two shared with one another and brought to the class as a history/english dual approach.  I remember Ken as encouraging, friendly, and always open to new perspectives.
he's a good guy with an unconventional way of looking at things-- he will surprise you. very polite and amiable. looks like will ferrell.  ;)
He's a nice guy and is always trying to help, but his classes can get so boring. I wouldn't really recommend him.

He's a really nice guy who wanted to make you think about how these Humanities connect to real life.  On another hand, however, his classes tend to get a little boring.  He's really interesting, too, talk to him about Gaza.
No Comments
Thinks he is much better than he is...lectures are unengaging
Frau Houghton was easily one of my favorite teachers at Geneseo. Her class was fair but definitely not hard. She is very kind and understanding. Definitely recommend her!

An absolutely wonderful professor. I had a rough time with German before I transferred to Geneseo, but now I love it! I am very sad to be done with German, and I would love to have her again! She is very kind and helpful. Very clear. I actually understood what I was learning. I highly recommend her.

She's wonderful. I feel like I'm actually learning German this semester. You most likely won't get an A in this class, but it's a lot easier to get in the B's than with Klima. She's a much easier grader and she's much clearer in lectures. In 201, she doesn't speak a lot of English though so it gets confusing at times.

Frau Houghton is  wonderful professor.  Her classes demand the amount of work needed to understand a language, and she's an extremely fair grader.  She generally has an attendance policy, but if you go to classes and pay attention you will do well.

I have Frau Houghton for German 201. I haven't taken German in a few years and looked to get back into the swing of things. She's very helpful and has the interest of her students in mind. Put some effort into this class and you will be rewarded with good grades and an immense knowledge of the language. I recommend this class to all!

Professor Houghton is one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She is a really tough professor but if you want to learn a language hers is the class to take. Dont take the class if you just simply want to get the requirement over with take another professor. She is a pleasure to be around and loves teaching.

too difficult for what should be basic french. tests are incredibly hard and unfair. she ended up curving everyone's grade just so that enough of her students would pass. i took 4+ years of french in highschool and barely pulled off a C+. a kid i knew grew up in canada and struggled with the tests. i do not recommend taking any classes with her

Professor Ferguson is truly an inspiration. She is an amazing dancer and always reminds us to get comfortable in our bodies so we can dance better. There aren't many grades in this class so everything counts and make sure to follow the rubric! Taking this class has made me more confident and comfortable in my skin. Highly recommend!

Her lectures are very boring, usually dragging out the same concepts every unit and venting about her personal trauma every class. There's a group activity at least once a week and they're literally the worst unless you have friends. Tests are okay, but the short response portion is graded too harshly and will drop your grade significantly.

Sikka was an okay professor. Her lectures were heavy, and the tests were not based on remembering material but on applying your knowledge to situations. If you take the time to go to her office during office hours, she will guide you if you are struggling. Read the book! I didn't and my grades were suffering. Good person, bad teacher.

I learned more from Sikka than I have anyone else, that being said something I didn't like was how tough the tests were compared to the classwork and exam guides. Uses the textbook material on the exams too. Overall lots of good material but tough at times.

Dr. Sikka's lectures feel extremely unorganized at times, but overall the class was relatively easy. She gives two essay exams which she dosent grade harshly as well. In the beginning I thought the class was going to be hard but it wasn't and I learned a lot.

I love Dr. Sikka as a person but not as a professor. Cross-Cultural Psyc is ALL lecture-based, but she just reads from the textbook I needed to buy. You don't need to buy the textbook Two exams but graded heavily. Since it is her just going through 30 slides each class can get very boring and disengaging

Do not take this class. You know what? Take this class if you want to test your passion for psych. She never shuts up about her niece and great nephew. I've been confused since september. She started crying when we watched a video about malnutrition, which i suppose is understandable but rather dramatic.

She's nice but she doesn't cover enough from the book and the first exam is always a disaster because the essay questions are too hard. You are graded on exams and 5 in class discussions and write-ups. The exams cover a lot, but she gives you a study guide so as long as you study really good you can get a good grade.
A very kind professor who cares about her students. The tests are simple if you read the textbook. She has many funny stories and is always in a great mood.

heard so many bad things about her but she was one of the best psych professors I've had. she's very passionate about her class. people say that her tests are hard but if you just follow along with her in class you should be able to pass without studying. she's also very accommodating if you are struggling.

I adore Professor Sikka, such a kind professor. This class is not hard at all, material is simple and Sikka provides many examples from working with children and her own childhood. I absolutely would take a course with her again. Loved her lectures. Absolutely take this with prof Sikka she's the best

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Sikka is great. My biggest piece of advice is to read the textbook and to pay attention in class bc she gives great examples and the textbook helps you to further understand. Her class is very test centered so if you're not a good test taker- try a diff professor. She keeps the lectures interesting but stay off your phones (she will say something).

Every class is extremely boring and she only talks about her nieces. Tests are hard there is always more than one right answer. She isn't understanding and hard to reach outside of class. However she did boost my grade like .2 percent so I would pass and didn't have to retake the class.

Dr. Sikka was by far my favorite professor. She's hilarious and actually cares about her students. The lectures are heavy and attendance isn't mandatory, but she does randomly take it. She creates study guides for all of her tests, which includes a study guide for the final exam.

I think people are a little harsh on Sikka, I had her for stats this semester and it was definitely a difficut course, but she taught the material very well. Make sure you go to class, or you will fail. Super nice too if you ask for help during tests and stuff.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']
comment: So terrible. You have 4 tests throughout the whole semester and very few assignments you are graded on besides the tests. If you get one bad grade on a test it is very hard to get that grade up. Her lectures are very fast paced and get off track very often. She is a nice woman but the tests are so difficult. Dont show up, won't pass. READ THE BOOK!

The tests were unbelievably hard. 40 multiple choice (mostly apply) questions on 3 chapters filled with information and 2 essay questions. What are the essay questions? I dont know becuase you have 10 possible different ones and you either do all of them or guess what 2 questions are on the test

Professor Sikka often interrupted her own lectures with anecdotes that she described as examples but it was really an excuse to talk about her grand-niece and make imitations of babies crying. Other than that she was a decent professor but I wouldn't take her again

Prof. Sikka cares about her students but has a hard time translating that into her teaching. She tends to say offensive or rude things and calls people out a lot. Her tests were full of errors and at one point a question didn't even have the correct answer listed.

Professor Sikka is a nice person; however, I found it difficult to learn anything of substances because she mostly discusses things not within the course material. Additionally, there are several assignments all worth 0% of your grade, while the tests are 75% of your grade. The tests in my opinion are not fair, difficult, and never updated.

Professor Sikka is not horrible but definitely not the best. To do well you need to read the textbook and study a lot but I would not say it is that difficult of a class if you read the textbook. She prepares you well but takes little time to get to know her students. She will give extra credit on the tests so study because I had over 100

Professor Sikka is a very nice women and means well, she tends to go off on tangents about her great niece and other random information quite often, she complains that we are so behind so she skips a lot of slides in her lectures, the tests are very difficult and you really have to understand the material to do well.

Dr. Sikka is a great woman.  It is obvious that she cares about her students and tries to make the class directed towards how the class learns best.  The tests are very hard which is why I gave her a lower rating but she gives make up exams which will help your grade.  There is barely any homework besides reading.

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: Yep. No. Don't do it. If you have already signed up to be with this professor, switch immediately. I can't begin to tell you how bad of an experience I had in this class. The textbook and the professor use different formulas. Email communication with the prof is good though if you can get her to respond. Run, and run fast. Save yourselves.

She lectures all class and then gives exit tickets at the end so you have to go to class to get class participation credit. We had 3 exams and a paper. The exams are based on textbook reading, so you don't need to go to class to do well on exams. The paper is super easy. She is so flustered all time and class is very confusing.

Sikka does not need to work with people. She is insensitive to students and is making negative impacts. She started using the wrong formulas and doing things incorrectly for "the sake of time." We were constantly confused and never got a clear explanation. Do NOT take this class.

I was texting about a death in the family during her class and she called me out on it, which is fair since she did not know the reason. I told her after class the reason and she told me that not to sound unsympathetic, but I can't listen to her lecture and text about the death at the same time. She's always been awful, but this is unacceptable.

Dr. Sikka is one of the most passionate and professional teachers Ive ever had. She creates such a safe space for her students and deserves so much more love for the work she does than the love shes getting right now. I study in that classroom after hours just because I know that it is a safe place to work freely. 100% recommend.

Dr Sikka is the most caring and compassionate professor here at geneseo. If you are struggling with any of the tests shes always available to help you. She holds review sessions and records them for those who cant attend and sends out study guides. Yes her tests are hard, but she will never leave you unprepared. She truly is the best.

Do NOT take this class. SAVE YOURSELF. I would give her 0 stars. We have one class before the exam and she hasn't taught all the material. The material shouldn't be as hard as she is making it. She not only confuses us, but herself too! She talks about how she hates early classes (class at 8:30a) and yet she still signed up to teach one.
The class isn't too difficult. If you go to class and read the textbook and take notes, you will pass. Professor Sikka is super kind and cares about her students. It's an interesting class!

Professor Sikkas online class consists of little lecture and a long break out rooms. If you want to do good on the test you need to read the textbook and take notes! Other than that, you can tell she really cares for her students and such a sweet person.

Lectures consisted of breakout rooms and barely any content is discussed. Basically read the textbook on your own and take exams, no lectures helped. Would not recommend her as a teacher. Nice lady though.

I think it's a harder class than it should be. The content is very interesting, but the exams and quizzes have tricky questions on it. It is very possible to get in the As for this class though. She is nice and wants you to do well.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]
comment: She's tough but so is the content and to a certain extent, she tries to make it easier to swallow. She can be funny and upbeat but also confusing and a little scatterbrained. Overall shes okay but the class moves fast and you wanna stay on the readings as much as possible.

Prof. Sikka is amazing in other classes but manages to make statistics even more confusing than it already is. The textbook is necessary in understanding the concepts. Copy down the slides before class. There's only about 1 HW assignment a week. She is a very approachable, easy-going and kind professor that wants to see you succeed.

Professor Sikka is very empathetic & does a great job of clearly explaining concepts in class. She provides a lot of real world examples that allow you to further understand the objectives. There is little homework, other than integrative notes assignments, which you are assigned well in advance. She is also very approachable and intelligent.

Terrible professor. She is a very sweet lady but a very bad teacher. She, herself knows statistics well but she cannot teach a classroom filled with students who have never seen this before. People were constantly confused and would correct her and she would fight on how she was "right." This class was a joke because the entire class was confused.

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. She is so all over the place and is unclear in all of her examples. She makes very simple topics confusing by her explanations and shouldn't be a professor that teaches math. She gets confused herself at the board and doesn't explain what we have to know.

She is a great professor who came to teach in our school for a year. She made the learning fun. Attendance was not mandatory but she gives daily quizzes which are very easy if you study her power point. The course is very straightforward. She is extremely helpful.

HE IS SO NICE!! Great prof. does like to ramble about his life which can sometimes be boring. Read his books, and participate, bc he wants to get to know you. Although his class required 5 papers, you will do well on them if you put in some effort and try to write something decent. Never got below a 90 on them, gives great advice. TAKE HIM!!!

He is honestly one of my favorite professors. No matter your skill level in writing, he grades on how much effort you put in-- which is important in a writing workshop class. I really enjoyed his lectures (since he's from philosophy dept), and he genuinely cares about his students. Every paper was interesting and challenging, but never impossible.

Wasn't really excited about the topic of the course going in but he has honestly been my favorite teacher here.  He is very engaging and easy to follow.  Very fair grader.  Take him if you have the chance!
Sauter is awesome. Class lectures are easy to get engaged in, and he is very understanding of your schedule. Always kind and always helpful. I would definitely take another class with him

He's a great professor! He's so kind and so helpful, I would take him for Humanities if he teaches it again. He is very passionate and really into the material. I found him to be a very easy grader at times but overall he does grade quite fair. Papers were around 5-6 pages long each time, the usual!! If he's available for any class, take him!!!

The class is pretty easy, but sometimes it is difficult to understand what the teachers are saying.  Also, there is a lot of singing, dancing, and acting so for people who don't like to do that in front of the class, it might hurt you in the end.  Otherwise, it is pretty fun. and Ana is extremely nice and funny.

Honestly he is a hard grader and refuses to give clear directions. Beware of CAPSIM it is the hardest thing in the class. Also study for a national exam. If you score less than average he just gives you a flat 0

He is a nice guy, but be sure you're with the right people for your group project. Also, don't ask him any questions on CAPSIM, because he wont answer. Overall, one of the nicest and easier professors I have had, and he loves to chat and make class fun and engaging (even bright and early).
Nice guy, but doesn't explain group projects very well, in which there are a lot of. A lot of group work, quizzes aren't bad.

Pouya is one of the nicest guys ever. Class is lecture heavy and he takes attendance. Weekly quiz on Friday's due by midnight but they are taken remotely and open note. CAPSIM simulations weekly. Big group paper and presentation due at the end of the semester that is very challenging. Class is relatively easy and he is a great guy to talk to.
Drones on about stuff that doesn't relate to quizzes or group projects which make up most of your grades. Also don't try to email him because he will not answer.

The most engaging professor I had in Geneseo. His course was really well structured and the course was taught in the most practical way. Participation really matters and although there's lots of work to be done, grading is very fair.

Went from having open-note exams to non-open note, all book based which he did not even touch in class (most failed). 10% of our grade was based on the school of business exam, which no other professor includes. He tries to be interesting, but class is a complete waste of time since we're not graded on anything that occurs in it. Do not take.

Amazing professor. Keeps you on your toes. You need to participate in class discussions every session. I learned more in this class than from any other. He's a great addition to Geneseo and boosts your experience in the business program. Great personality too.

Classes are engaging and require participation. He knows every student's name by the second week and will call on you to weigh in on class discussions. Shows great knowledge of the subject matter and answers emails very quickly if you have questions. Course syllabus is very detailed and self explanatory, so make sure you read it through.

He's incredibly disorganized constantly changing/ editing assignments after the class starts them. Every post, assignment, and announcement has typos or is impossible to understand. His wording is overly complicated, I have to reread things 10x just to figure out what he means. Lectures are unorganized & sloppy. Take this class with another prof

Lectures often felt unfocused and difficult to follow, he often seemed confused about the materials he was actively teaching. The class included frequent in-class writing assignments and homework, but the instructions and prompts could be unclear because he would change them after we had already started writing.

Do not take class with him. His bright space is so freaking confusing and I keep missing assignments that aren't main ones. Requires full undivided attention all the time, his lectures never make sense, and I can never find the right info that I need for major assignments.

Extremely hard to follow during lectures, is all over the place and expects you to pay him full attention, laptops shut, while he gives instructions at a mile a minute. Picks on you if he thinks you aren't paying attention and corrects you even if just to restate to be right and make you wrong. If you can take it with anyone else, DO SO.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: He's nice but lectures are random and all over the place. His Brightspace was so confusing, I kept missing assignments and readings bc of it. His assignments are very confusing/random and don't make any sense. Participation matters, but no one will talk except for the same 3 people. He will call on you if you aren't paying attention

DO NOT take this class. He seems like a nice guy (a little weird) but I ultimately withdrew because his lectures make no sense, no feedback was given and he doesn't explain what he wants you to do. I have a good GPA and taking this class with him was causing too much stress to try upkeep. TAKE IT WITH ANOTHER PROF

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Easy class but try to do the assigned readings so you can participate in the class discussions. Still pretty easy if you don't but he can be hard to listen to and seems like he's coming up with the point of his lecture while he speaks. He does tell you what to study for all quizzes and tests so as long as you study you'll do well.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Very unorganized and has no idea how to lead a class or a group discussion. It is very hard to engage with him and the class material unless your classmates make it interesting. Super confusing professor overall and makes you read heavy with barley discussing anything in class.

This class was horrible. He is very unorganized and his readings are not understandable. He will randomly call on students if you are not paying attention. Would not really recommend taking this class.

ENGL101: Memory, Trauma, and Space. Reasonable workload, homework and in-class writing. Lots of reading. Clear instructions for work. Mainly discussion-based class, which can drag on but that's inevitable for 100-min class and he leads discussions well. Every student does need to facilitate a discussion once. Good professor overall.

very boring and the professor himself is very unorganized doesn't explain things fully and is very confusing during lectures there is group projects and solo projects. the readings he assigns are somewhat confusing and is a big step from an easier class even though it is only a 200 level

Class was good. If you like environmental or are an environmental minor its deff one of the better options to take. Go to lecture and pay attention to what he says and it should be able to get a good grade.

100% the most boring lecturer ever. Not very clear with what he expects on homeworks/on exams. Class is not too difficult because the subject matter is basically high school earth science. So boring but an easy B, A is definitely doable.

An articulate professor who isn't very difficult at all and understands what a 100-level class should be. He uses mycourses to its full potential, and that's definitely a plus when it comes to following your progress in his courses.

Very boring.  His voice tends to put you to sleep.  Pop up quizzes about once a week, winds up being something like 15% of your grade but as long as you're there to take it you get a 100.  3 exams, harder than you'd expect.  Average is around a 70.  Boring as all hell but a good guy.  He actually gives extra credit, which makes a huge difference.

This class is extremely boring and hard to concentrate on. This paired with difficult tests is not a good match. Study, study, study for exams! Go to class, he gives pop quizzes! Study for lab quizzes, there's one each week. He's a super nice guy though, and pretty hot.

Extremely boring, quizes and tests are unpredictable and cannot explain concepts. We had a "sub" professor a day where Professor Laabs was not there, and I learned so much more from that one day then my whole semester with professor Laabs.

I had him for Climate and Energy Change and found him extremely boring! But as long as you show up to lecture & go to lab, this class isn't impossible. His review sessions are very helpful for the test and he often repeats quiz questions on the tests so those are easy give aways.

As long as you show up to class and lab you will get a decent grade. Lecture is EXTREMELY boring. Everybody brings their laptops to stay awake. Attendance is worth 15% of your grade. He has pop quizzes but as long as you hand one in you get a 100.

Boring class (or maybe I'm just not into the subject), but pretty good professor.  Gives 100% on pop quizzes as long as you try (more of an attendance thing), study sessions before exams, very clear about expectations, exams are pretty easy overall. Big lecture though, really hard to sit through for 75 minutes.

i highly recommend taking this class. if you want to think about sexual fantasies about a professor,all day, this class is perfect for you. he's super nice but has difficult tests. other than that if you want something nice to look at for an hour and 15 minutes this class is great.
Ben is the best!  The class was really interesting and he makes it fun.  I am now a Geology major because of my experience with this class.

Best looking professor I've had so far. Typical core class. Do the readings and study and show up for pop quizzes and you'll be fine. The pop quiz can be totally wrong and you'll still get credit. Has helpful study sessions before exams. Power points are online. I recommend him.

It's not so much the slow, monotone voice that makes the class the worst on my schedule-but rather the material itself. STAY AWAY. It's not even that it's difficult--it's just hard to bring yourself to study something that is this boring. WORST CLASS EVER.

Very boring!!! Lectures are pointless. Notes are all put online and the only reason to come to class if for pop quizzes. Tests should be easy. Lab is extremely boring. He's a goodlooking guy, but has the most monotone voice I've ever heard.

Very comforting voice, very nice guy.  Class is kinda unnecessary since the powerpoints are online, but he does give pop quizzes. He really wants people to do well and really loves his subject. He's awesome in lab. I hate the class just cause of what it is, but I'd recommend him as a professor.
SEXIEST MAN ALIVE!!!!!! and a pretty good teacher, know his stuff, loves sand dunes
Ben Laabs is a sex god!!! Deep, sexy voice, doesn't matter what he's saying, just enjoy his rugged good looks

HE IS AWESOME! Really nice guy who will help you out when you need it, and is really hot. He does have kind of a boring voice, but hes funny and a good guy. He also tells you exactly what you need to know for the tests. And he's hot.

His voice in lecture will put you to sleep , but the powerpoints are helpful and everything is straight from the book.  He is a good guy and a fair grader.  He is better in the lab because he is very thorough.  He explains everything very thoroughly, both in lecture and lab.

Completely agree about being monotone, I fall asleep in lecture on a regular basis but I still go because he gives quizzes for participation randomly. Powerpoints are online and come largely from the textbook, so class is otherwise not necessary.  Have lab with him too, much more helpful there and can crack an occasional joke.  Pretty easy course.
he is extremely monotone and his powerpoints are awful. good intentions but extremely boring. his tests are impossible, except the 80/20 individual/group grading (that's a plus).

tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']
comment: Do not take this class with Fuhrman. His class is incredibly boring, and is extremely hard if you dont have any background in music theory. He makes the concepts way more hard than it should be, but he does let you bring a flash card with notes on the final exam.

She's very caring and if you go to see her outside of class she is incredibly understanding and kind. BUT, homework is unclear and disorganized and she often assigns it in class then sends an email with more on top of that. Theres so much hw on top of other classes that i had to use google translate. Didnt feel like i learned anything in that class

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Hated every second of this class. I studied and worked hard only to get a B. It is obvious she does not care about students, and cannot explain concepts well. Tough grader with no clear grading criteria. Hard exams, pop quizzes, difficult homework. Avoid taking this class if you still want to like learning Spanish afterwards.

Prof. McEwen is one of the best professors I've had since being at Geneseo. She is one of the most involved and caring professors who genuinely wants you to learn. If you participate and put in effort, it will reflect in your grade.
Spanish Conversation was one of many classes I took with Rose.  She was the most challenging professor at Geneseo.  As a Spanish teacher, I would not be where I am today if it was not for her.

She's often very unorganized and frazzled. Very kind, but blames you for things that were her fault for unpreparedness. Very passionate about subject. Hard to meet with her outside of class because she is never available and won't show up to your meeting 80% of the time.
Unless you have experience in Spanish courses, don't take McEwen. She is unclear and generally was very rude to students. I only did as well as I did because I'm fluent in Spanish.

McEwen is good and not good. It is hard to tell.  You do learn, but she is always frazzled and unorganized.  She is a great person, but she can definitely have an attitude with her students sometimes. The most frustrating thing about her classes is that many times things are just up in air or on the fly.

Rose is one of the best professors at Geneseo.  She has a big heart and will be one of the people you want to stay in contact with well after college.  If you want a good grade you should study.  If you don't understand something you should ask.  She won't spoon feed you - she actually wants you to learn.

All my classmates who had several years of Spanish prior to this class did fine, but I know students who had never taken Spanish before were struggling a lot. God B's on every test and quiz but ended with an A because she relies heavily on participation. She's pretty unorganized so always ask for clarification.

She expects a lot from you while putting in the bare minimum herself. Best example, she takes points from your participation grade if you show up late but comes in 15-30 minutes late herself (multiple times). Her instructions are confusing (even  in English). Most of the learning you do is on your own

This class was one of the least organized classes I have taken and was highly demotivating for a Spanish major. Exams were on material never covered in class and were just rote memorization of hundreds of random terms. It could have been an interesting course, but was really all over the place with little to no content, mostly YouTube videos.

Class is pretty easy and clear as long as you do the readings and hw. Making an appt or meeting outside class is difficult as she is always busy but when you finally meet with her shes very nice and helpful. She helped me plan out everything from study abroad to all the courses I'm going to take.  Showed up 15 min late to class almost everyday.

she really is a great teacher. always is flustered and usually shows up late, but if you even try to participate you will do well. she stops collecting homework halfway through the semester. Tests are 3 essays in like 45 mins and you usually run out of time though. Overall a good class, but need to spend a lot of time out of class reading

Rose would do ANYTHING for her students when she sees they care and are putting effort in. She always looks frazzled (because of her hair) and also because she is the head of the department and takes on more than any other professor or department head does. She can not say no to a request and tries to help to many people because of her huge heart

She's a very good teacher. Always smiling and never singles you out for dumb mistakes. If she corrects you, it's nicely. She is a tough grader, so watch out. It's not easy, but I don't ever feel very stressed about it. Just study your notes because she likes to give quizzes.

Dr. McEwen expects a lot from you, but that is the standard for SUNY Geneseo.  By far, I learned the most from her and would encourage anyone who really wants to learn to take her classes.  Top notch professor - you will learn if you work.

Very all over the place. Doesn't return papers on time. Doesn't arrive to class on time. Got the feeling she really didn't care about the class. EXTREMELY picky on tests. If you don't write her EXACT words for an answer she marks you wrong. The final was a gift from God which saved me and got me a B in the class.

Although she is a bit scatterbrained I learned a lot from her class that has helped me in future lit classes. She was always nice to me and I would recommend taking a class with her as she's an important person to know in the Spanish dept.

If she doesn't like you, it's obvious. Calls negative attention to people during class. Bad at returning papers she wants edited. Was rude to me when I emailed her about an assignment I missed even though she told me to email her in the first place.
She was so enthusiastic...
Unorganized, Unorganized, Unorganized... would rather be traveling abroad than be in the classroom.

An absolute treasure, Dr. McEwen was by far the best professor at SUNY Geneseo.  Takes an absolute interest in her students.  That's something I never experienced with Gomez. She's sophisticated, energetic and encouraging.

An amazing professor!  She puts a lot of effort into teaching (and everything else going on in her life!) and notices when students do the same for her Spanish courses.  She assigns a lot of work, but if you put in the effort, it's worth it in the end.
very nice lady
Rather irritating.  She gets easily confused and is confusing.

Terrible professor, totally unreasonable, calls negative attention to students during class, extremely unorganized-- never is clear on what assignments are due (often goes against her own syllabus).  Expects students to commit to a specific time after clas

Very difficult comparing her 202 class to the 201 class I had before. She was very understanding when I explained this to her and saw that I was putting the effort in and I was very happy with my grade. Tough in class but a very warm & understanding pe

Rose is so fun to work with! She's a tough grader but she's fair and as long as you put the work in and are energetic in class, she's easy on you. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! She's a great person too. Always willing to help an eager student.
Very tough grader, but also grades the whole course on improvement so it is fair. Nice lady and likes to joke around alot with her conversation class so it is fun.
She's a really nice teacher and she'll do anything to help, but she's also a really hard grader and the class requires a lot of out-of-class time

As another poster stated, she can be disorganized at times, only because she has so much going on (like trying to help out every student she possibly can) and would never hold anyone responsible for her errors. All around terrific Professor and person.
sweet lady, willing to do anything for her students, and makes the class as interesting as possible! Take her shes fun, and not too hard if you study!
She really cares about her students and if you show some effort she will bend over backwards to help you.
Took many classes with her. Really caring and puts all her effort into class. Great professor.
Awful, disorganizes, gives wrong assinments and makes many mistakes.  Also expects a LOT of out of class time.  Take Gomez instead.
wondeful person and teacher- would do anything to help you in or out of class. loves her work and makes class interesting
very sweet, involved, and exciting

Professor is a kind and genuine person who wants to see you succeed, however, do NOT take this class if you are not willing to show up and participate!! It's a huge part of your grade. There's also weekly journal entries, readings, group work, and documentary viewings in class. Exams are easy but don't count for much. Participation is EVERYTHING

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Nightly readings, HEAVY participation policy, 3 easy exams, and a final essay. Content wasn't difficult, but the strict participation and attendance policy significantly affected my grade. Dr. Lewis knows her stuff and is a good professor, but I would not recommend this class if you have difficulty getting to class and don't have much time to read.

It was unfortunate that this class was moved online because it has a lot of interesting content. Prof. Lewis is helpful but outside circumstances prevented her from being accessible, which is understandable. The class is heavy on reading with weekly quizzes. There are also 3 1,000-word essays and 4 tests throughout the semester.

Lewis is amazing!! One of the most interesting courses and professors I have had at Geneseo. She is very passionate about what she teaches. She is a decently easy grader and gives 3 skip days for attendance. Lewis also does Active Learning Points that is class participation but makes the 100 points throughout the semester VERY achievable.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I enjoyed this class. Though it is a lot of work, it feels manageable. Professor Lewis helped us engage with the material we read in a positive way, and I can confidently say that I am going away from this class having learned a lot.
