Very solid professor, I would definitely take another class with her again.

Professor Lewis is a great professor. She assigns many readings, but it prepares you for your 2 pg reflection paper every other week. You have one big scholar profile than a historiography paper at the end of the semester. Participation is a very big part of class. You need to participate. She's very understanding when you need help.

Dr. Lewis is laid back and very kind. Unfortunately, she has an insane grading policy in terms of participation. You need to earn 100 learning points to receive full credit which is nearly impossible unless you do every reading. After the class ended, she changed the grading policy and went against the syllabus dropping my grade 10 points.

I took this class with Dr. Lewis and she was incredibly helpful when it came to writing the essay for this class. She gave very clear expectations for the essay we had to write. Her lessons were also very interesting and helped broaden my understanding of African history. Overall I recommend taking a class with Dr. Lewis if you get the chance.
She is honestly an amazing professor. She really cares for her students and clearly has a passion for what she's talking about!

Very cohesive, interesting, and engaging lectures! Includes class participation or group discussion almost every class, although it's always been helpful. Group projects are sort of annoying naturally, but they are structured well and reasonably-graded. Very informative class and enthusiastically taught.

Had her for African Environmental History. She KNOWS. HER. STUFF. There is a lot of reading for the class, but since she is so knowledgeable, it isnt hard to want to read as she makes you excited about the topic. Definitely recommend to any history major.

By far the best professor I have had at Geneseo. She is very clear on what she expects from student, so while it is not an easy class, putting in the work and participation should result in a reasonable grade.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: Dr. Lewis is great at helping you find a research topic to pursue. I've taken two courses with her and have enjoyed them both very much. She gives students a lot of freedom in which to develop the projects they want to pursue.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I took her for Technical theater. If you do not need this class, DO NOT TAKE IT. It had so much homework including daily readings, 4 papers, 1 project, 45 hours of outside of class work in the woodshop, weekly quizzes and a final. She does offer a lot of extra credit which was the only reason I got the grade that I did.
Takes random points off. Would rather be working in tech than be in a classroom teaching. Expectations are set too high for people who have never designed before.

Prof is a great person, super sweet and is always willing to help, but the one thing she is super strict on is attendance. No matter what happens you will get a few points taken off if you are not in class, huge on participation. Attend class, and put a little effort in and you'll do fine.

Prof. Rozy is a great professor.  The class is interesting with simple reading quizzes and a few papers.  Be prepared for participation outside of class hours if you are considering taking this course as a gen-ed.

Lots of reading, and quizzes based on it. Grades over lots of assignments. The crew hours can be difficult if this is for a gen ed, but there's also lots of extra credit opportunity there. Lecture can be slow, mostly due to lack of participation of students. Rozy is a wonderful teacher, and a very kind person, and I loved taking her class.

Rozy was a very nice professor and had to cover a lot in her class. The class has multiple reading quizzes, all based on the textbook that you need to purchase. The lectures are essentially all just the textbook info in a different format. The crew hours can be taxing, especially if you are taking this for a gen-ed course.

Dr. Nixon is the best math professor i've ever had, he's one of the nicest professors you might ever meet, very flexible office hours (you can always find him) and he's super generous grading wise. very well educated professor and funny as well ( his lectures fly by).

Nixon is a legend. He is a visiting professor, but his policies are better than the other Calculus professors here. 50% of the grade are things that are done on your own time (HW, take home quizzes). Exams are 25% of your grade, WITH test corrections, and the final accounts for the other 25%. Go out of your way to find his section.

I would take the next level of calculus with Dr. Nixon. Convenient office hours, clear understanding of calculus, straight foward. Homeworks are somewhat helpful, assignments are spread out evenly and fairly. Light on in class examples.
Really love the way quizzes were formed, great preparation for the exams. Very generous grader with flexible office hours.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']
comment: It's hard to understand the material during his lectures. If you go to his office hours, however, he's good at explaining things. Quizzes are worth more than the test and you can go to office hours for help on those quizzes.

His personality is quirky and funny, but also painful because everyone refuses to answer any of his questions, so you end up sitting in silence for about half the class. He grades really easily and gives plenty of partial credit, but it's still easy to fail his tests. Get ready to self-teach yourself just about everything.

She is a very sweet woman. She is also extraordinarily intelligent, but she never makes you feel stupid or inferior. Class can feel dry or repetitive at times, but you will always walk away feeling as if you've learned something.

Very sweet and knowledgeable woman. If you do all of the assigned readings throughout the semester the tests are a breeze.  Many small assignments help boost your grade and frequent in-class discussions make the class more intimate and more interesting. Take this professor!

Great for a new professor. Clear and to the point. At first she graded harshly, but as the semester wore on she got much easier. Lots of extra credit opportunity. Interesting class that doesn't feel like a giant lecture.

Let me intimate that Dr M is no pushover. You will spend several hours a semester memorizing hw answers for the quizzes. That said Bappa is one of the most compassionate intelligent & personable beings around. I hope to share more classes w/ this outstanding man as fellow math majors. I know that if I struggle his kindness & genius will see me thru

tags: ['Participation matters', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'Clear grading criteria']
comment: controversial opinion but bappa is really not that bad. do the required readings for sure. yeah, it's a lot of work. but if you want an A it is definitely possible to get one.

He's not perfect  no one is; however, he cares about his students and wants them to pass. Would be better suited for 300+ level. He has a very solid grasp of the material that he is teaching. Clearly, he is knowledgeable. I had a professor who was unfamiliar with the content she was teaching. She has been here for years.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Bappa is not the greatest professor in the sense that you will probably be really bored and not be able to pay much attention, however, he does want everyone in his class to do well and makes it very easy to get an A or close to it. In the beginning you think he will be very strict but I ended up with an A- and I  didn't work that hard at all.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: he's pretty awful to say the least. a ton of homework (i'm talking 5+ hours of reading a night), not flexible with meeting times, and generally not a very nice guy. steer clear of this professor if you want to keep your sanity.

tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']
comment: He is terrible. 40 percent of your grade is based on pop quizzes that he gives and the average for them is around 60 for each one. He doesn't curve. He is so unclear and assigns readings and doesn't explain them well. Terrible man. Terrible class. You lose 4 points a week for not participating. In a lecture based class. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HIM

Bappa is a great professor. At first, I was a little discouraged because I wasn't doing too well, but he is very helpful outside of class and helps you understand what you did wrong and what you can do to do better. There's usually one homework assignment due each week, sometimes two, but its extremely doable. Grades fairly.

Classes revolve around group work which are chosen randomly for the whole semester, and you are forced to do worksheets and presentations together on material he does not teach, because all class is group work. So then you're stuck looking up everything on your own

Such a kind guy, had him for lab and then lecture, now plan on taking his ecology class.  You are well prepared for tests with an understanding of what is on them. understanding abt late work. He is very laid back and makes class participation comfortable. easy to email and communicate with and do well in the class. Would definitely recommend him!
He is a truly caring professor and is very flexible.

Took ecology lecture with him, great lecturer and went to him several times for help. The exams aren't super easy, but he creates study materials that help. He wants you to succeed, recommend taking lecture with him.
Dr Hoven is a fantastic professor. I would recommend taking a class with him if you can.
Pretty chill dude. Took 203 ecology with him. Just memorize his study guides and you will get an A

I took BIOL203 with Professor Hoven and I really enjoyed the structure of his lectures. The lectures are easy to follow and most of the time are quite interesting. He breaks up the lectures with in class assignments that are relevant to that day's lecture and count as easy homework grades. He is super nice and you can truly tell he enjoys teaching.
I had Hoven for BIO 118 lab. He is very relaxed and unorganized, but lab is easy with only a few lab reports throughout the semester

To explain Matthews in one word is lazy. If you're taking the class just for credit you can google translate all your essays and still get at least a b+. That being said, if you are a spanish minor or major avoid this class. You will not learn anything and find out next semester that you havent spoken spanish for 6 months.
Grades hard but fair. Helped me to become better at spanish

Kyle was constantly trying to improve our experience, right down to setting up times that he would be in the dining hall to meet with us if we "just wanted to chat". We completed surveys 2 times during the semester & I could tell that my feedback was taken into account, immediately changing aspects of class. He is eager to learn & super passionate.

A lot of thought is put into each class. He geared this course to our needs as college seniors. We worked on cover letters and applications and focused on unique grammar concepts--many of which I had never heard of. Spanish has a lot of intricate grammar rules and my knowledge of those grew substantially. He was constantly looking for our feedback.

Great for students dedicated in learning Spanish. Test are long and difficult. It is a tough class but you will learn Spanish. Very funny and class is very fun. Very good environment and really cares about all his students.

Worst teacher I've ever had, not only at Geneseo, but the Community College I went to prior to transferring. Would recommend avoiding at all costs. Whether gifted at learning foreign languages or awful, you would fare much better if you took this course with a different professor. You've been warned. When I took this class, 1/3 of class dropped.
I struggled the whole year. Terrible professor

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Save your skin, do not take this class. Do not recommend. Unorganized and had to learn everything on my own on youtube. I didn't know my grade until a week before the final. Boring group-work

tags: ['LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'GROUP PROJECTS']
comment: Poorly organized, with deadlines constantly being shifted around. Obscure grading system prevents you from really knowing what you're going to get until the end of the semester. Doesn't provide feedback on anything but the quizzes (4) and oral quizzes (3). Learned virtually nothing in-class, all learning was done out of the book. Do not recommend.
Genuinely surprised you landed a job here at Geneseo and have held it for as long as you have. Well done.

Professor Matthews is tough for all the right reasons. The way his course is set up, along with the feedback that he provides, allows you to improve a lot throughout the course. With that being said, he assigns a lot of papers with homework on top of them. However, it's not impossible and if you are looking to improve this class is for you.

Matthews is extremely disorganized and I'm not convinced he had any idea what he was assigning. He gave us a final project 2 weeks before our final and then left the country until July, making him very unaccessible. He doesn't post grades online so I have idea where I stand in the class and this class is too difficult for a 200 Spanish course.

He assigned four papers for the semester. For each paper you have to write a draft and submit it. He will correct it and for the next paper you have to correct it and write why your mistakes are wrong. He has his own grading system which is annoying. He is a nice professor and wants his students to do well.

When planning my classes, I tried to avoid Dr. Matthews. I did this after reading the reviews on this site.  But I am in his class now, and I can say that the reviews below hacen falta  la verdad. Dr. Matthews is actually helpful, funny, and brilliant. He may seem intimidating, but I challenge you to deal.   A tip: Watch his videos!

tags: ['ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: He only spoke Spanish to us. More than Half the class hasn't taken Spanish In years or we were clearly beginners. He didn't explain things to us in a way we could understand because we didnt understand fluent Spanish. His job was to teach us and he failed. one grade at the end determined our entire grade. avoid . wait to take it with another prof.

Terrible. He has no passion or personality. I always dreaded his class and I actually love Spanish. I even spent time studying abroad and was successful. He does nothing but talk and takes weeks and weeks to grade papers. If you can help it DO NOT take a class with Kyle. Trust me, anything would be better.

Kyle is quiet and irritating.  He co-taught my humanities class and was the low point of the day.  He has a rude, patronizing way of teaching and often is snarky and talks down to the class.  He puts words exactly into your mouth and does not really value individual expression.  He is not engaging, organized, or interesting.

Matthews is an incompetent professor, period. He is never prepared for class and often changes due dates on a whim. He takes WEEKS to give graded assignments that need to be corrected back and gives homework that he never even goes over in class. He generally just does not seem interested in the class and made a language I love a class I dreaded.

Matthew's class reminded me more of a high school snoozer than of a college lecture; he walks around taking the pen out of your hand to write and corrects you as you speak.  Expect boring group work every single day.  He has no passion at all in Spanish or teaching and assumes everyone is just there to get the gen ed credit/doesn't want to learn

I've done really well in all his classes (A/A-'s) and I recommend him as a professor. I chose him purposely for 102, 201, and 202 because there are no surprises on his quizzes, so as long as you study it'll be really easy. He says he's going to talk only in Spanish at the 200 level but he still explains things in English if you ask him on the side.

Impossible to get an A. He grades everything way too hard for a second semester spanish class. He only speaks in spanish (and does so FAST) so going to class is worthless because you can't understand anything. Not helpful or understanding at all. Just need to learn from the book and do the practice tests, his only purpose is to give you a bad grade

This was his first year at Geneseo, so I won't be too harsh. But to be honest, he was not very clear (he spoke nothing but Spanish in a 100 level class). He kind of had an attitude. I have always been good at Spanish but he made it tough. He makes a few mistakes, he would teach us grammar rules and then say "no wait, forget that, that's not right."

Super lazy, his simulation is a scam, he makes you pay cash for it i believe to not leave a paper trail, so don't pay for it. He hires a helper and promises them a B+ average or higher to do all his work for him. He really could not care less. Besides his faults he is an interesting fellow, but a complete sociopath. Barely responds to email.

Ok. Only take this class online. I cant even imagine how bad this could be as a lecture class. He is awful at keeping things straight. His syllabus doesnt match his moodle calendar (which is a site where most of the working will take place). He lacks clear communication that leaves students so confused. Tests are 100 ques for 70 mins.

The dude did NOT give any information. The only time he sent emails to tell us anything (the only way to tell us) was immediately after I emailed HIM to ask what was going on. He had no idea what he was doing
Just the worst.. can't even argue about it. Students complain about Geneseo because of those irresponsible teachers.
Markulis is a good guy, pretty funny and out there. However, his grades are completely arbitrary. If he likes you, you'll do well in the class, if he doesn't, you might struggle.

Take this class unless you have the personality of a rock. Your grade is based on how much he likes you. You'll get at the very lowest a B+. The simulation is a pain but it IS group work. And how hard can group work really be? He knows the topic at hand is bs, and that most of the business classes are bs. Take it with Markulis, you wont regret it.

He is very different. He tells funny stories but most of the time, they're unrelated to the topic. Go to the classes, it'll help. I don't think it's a hard class, just read all the articles and skim through the chapters (I crammed everything in 2 days before test). Memorize and regurgitate. I ended up with an A-

He is a great guy, very funny and interesting to say the least. On the other hand his tests are awful and the simulation is weird. Make sure if you take his class that he knows your name and likes you.

Easily one of the worst teachers in Geneseo. The mid term and final were extremely hard and almost impossible to finish. In his lectures he talks about things that are completely unrelated to the course 99% of the time. Your grade for the class will be based solely on how much he likes you.

Useless teacher, he comes to class and tells you nothing. Better off not showing up and just reading the book and articles. Grades are based on 2 hard Tests, and a simulation that was poorly written (that you have to pay for!) and time consuming. Take class with any other professor, or offer him money for a good grade because he always hints at it.

Ridicously vexatious Professor. You have two tests that encompass 200+ pages of article readings, 500+ pages of textbook readings and then 30 pages of in class notes. Then he adds random stuff because he feels like it. He gives lots of random and arbitrary extra credit so someone that worked half as hard as you can get an A for no reason.

Beyond terrible. I was looking forward to taking OB because it's something I'm interested in, but his class was awful. He was extremely disorganized, he would go off on a lot of tangents that did not apply to the class, the simulation we used was awful, I could go on for days. This class was very frustrating because he literally taught us nothing.
great case studies, bring props and go all out. he just wants to see how you'll make people solve the case study rather than tell it to them...test's are hard just take good notes in class

If you don't want a lot of work and a huge group project with some test, take Markulis. His lectures are good, , but if you choose not to take his oral exam (2), the paper exam is not anything you can study for. Likes outspoken people, even if you are able to say anything, this will pay of greatly at the semesters end.  Good Luck!

I had Markulis for strat this semester and he is a great teacher. He has a reputation as a difficult grader and someone who makes his tests hard on purpose, but I don't find this to be true at all. It's not easy but it's not hard either if you put in effort. He makes the clas really fun and it's never boring so I always went. Take him if you can!
He is really funny and helpful.  You have to be active in class or he will not grade well.  Do your part and you get a good grade.

No real basis for the grade, only 2 exams, and a large group project.  Reading the chapter before class isn't necessary, but extremely helpful.  Very knowledgable man, his stories, and cases help to pass the time.  Not a lot of work, just study hard for the exams!

Peter is prolly one of the best prof of my life.  His class is hard yes but it will force you to learn and make you want to learn about the subject matter.  He likes people who are outspoke.  Dont be shy and you will have the teacher you have dreamed to have.  Amazing man and a inspiring person.

Very nice guy but the class was a bit unorthidox.  You have to read the chapter before class, then in the begining of class you get a quiz, and then he teaches the material you were just tested on.  there is no final so after the quiz you might as well leave the class.
He never stays on topic and his directions are so vague.
His tests are very difficult but he is a funny guy and makes lectures intersting with his sense of humor and enthusiasm about the class.
I think this guy had a great head on his shoulders, and wanted students to learn what was important.  Extremely intelligent

This guy was the worst professor that I had in the school of business!  His stories went nowhere and it was obvious that he had absolutely no "real" world experience.  His exams were ridiculous and I learned nothing from this guy!
Best and most kind professor I have ever had. Such an awesome, respectful, and funny man.

This class has taken up all my time this semester. Do not take it with other work-heavy classes, because there is so much outside of class work. His brightspace is impossible to navigate, so just accept it. This is probably the most work heavy class I've taken in Geneseo, and some was just unnecessary busy work.

All lectures are from research articles, which are then turned into assignments that must be completed in your group, so hope that you have good partners. He assigns a lot of essays with vague instructions in how they must be completed. However, he does look out for his students and is flexible with expectations.
very easy to talk to but assigns a lot of work for the level of the class. feedback in class rarely matches the grading

Dr. Allen is genuinely one of the sweetest professors ever. His class is very heavy on reading and projects though. Group work is a big portion of your grade, as well as outside classroom work. Miss a few classes and you're behind on class assignments. Try to be at every class, and don't take the course if you're not good w deadlines and group work

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: His expectations are 300-level based. The amount of work for this class made it difficult to maintain my study schedule. I appreciate his approach but it did not feel like a 200-level! His grading slowed as his assignments piled up but you always had a grade within two weeks. Don't take this class if your schedule is packed.

I love Dr. Allen because he is such a sweet man and the class is interesting. However it is a lot of work, I think, for a 200 level class and a lot of group work. There are peer evaluations he considers when grading but still can be frustrating depending on who you are with.

DO NOT TAKE I dont understand how he has such a high rating. doesnt know his students, will try AI Detecting your group papers, but the one he uses gives different results than all the others and takes 20 points off the whole group without talking to you. TA said it is really hard to do just OK in the class. NOT WORTH YOUR TIME!!

I love Jim Allen. Attendance is technically not mandatory, but you have an in-class assignment with your group each class. No exams but group projects, also there are popquizzes and he gives you a heads up. Very kind and wants his students to do good!

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']
comment: too much work for a 200 level class. makes you order the book HE wrote and pop quizzes you on the little analogies from the chapter that you don't pay attention to. every class has one or two group discussion assignments and doesn't give 100s on them. 3 group papers but doesnt give many instructions on it. it is not an easy class. should be 300

He's a passionate educator and a REALLY kind, understanding man. This course was very interesting when I was fully engaged, but it was hard to give 100 percent everyday with multiple group assignments per each class. He teaches down to the last min.The layout of this course can feel draining but it really encourages you to learn and stay engaged.

Dr. Allen is one of the best psych professors I've had so far. His classes are mastery based so instead of exams he gives out a lot of class work thats divided between your group. Also all of his classes are formatted the same so It can be a lot if your taking two classes with him at the same time. Overall amazing professor and I would recommend.

I would not recommend taking him if you do not do well in a "flipped classroom". You pretty much teach yourself everything and in class you work on group assignments which I hated because I always got stuck with people who did not want to do anything. There are pop quizzes but you get the questions beforehand so they are not hard.

Allen is an amazing professor and person. His classes are relatively easy, no exams. 3 group project papers that seem intimidating, but hes super helpful and provides everyone with the necessary resources to succeed. He does "pop quizzes" but honestly tells you the class before. I would recommend if you're an okay writer and can work in groups.

Jim Allen is a nice guy. There were many assignments in this class but he's not too harsh with grading so as long as you put in effort you will be fine. I would highly recommend attending class because there are occasional pop quizzes and regular group assignments. He is very approachable and gives good feedback.

Dr. Allen is sweet and he genuinely cares for his students; for example, he read and gave me feedback on a paper the night before it was due. The reason I didn't give him a 5 is because the entire class is group work/group projects, which is exhausting. However, he makes up for this by offering unlimited revisions (so you can fix your own grade).

tags: ['Group projects', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'So many papers']
comment: I love Jim Allen, he's very dedicated and passionate. He loves it when questions are asked and he is always willing to help. However, keep in mind it is all group work, I lucked out with my groups most of the time but it could suck if you get stuck with bad groups. 4 papers total. Lots of pop quizzes but he isn't too harsh of a grader.

tags: ['Group projects', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'So many papers']
comment: I love Jim Allen, he's very dedicated and passionate He loves it when questions are asked and he is always willing to help. However, keep in mind it is all group work, I lucked out with my groups most of the time but it could suck if you get stuck with bad groups 4 papers total Lots of pop quizzes but he isn't too harsh of a grader Just go to class

Group papers and unreliable peers.Grades depend on their content, so if ur stuck with a bad group, ur done for.Pop quiz after every reading, 3 tbooks to purchase.If u miss class one day, your grade drops by a lot but he lets you make it up only if u email him.Nice guy, but no lecture (slides) whatsoever.U only learn whatever u read.3 papers total

This was not the class for me. It's all group work, and when you get stuck with a bad group there is nothing you can do about it. He assigns readings for every class and often quizzes on them where he asks for very detailed information even if what you wrote made it clear that you read the text. I recommend buying a digital book to use as notes.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Gives good feedback']
comment: I really think Professor Allen is a wonderful person, and I learned a lot in this class. Overall, I enjoyed the class, but I personally dislike group papers. When people in your group don't have the same work ethic, it can be frustrating and if you're an introvert, being in groups every class may be hard. But, I would take a class with him again.

PSYC 452-Super super sweet man. Will always make sure you understand the material. Very apologetic. Graded group work every class. Three papers and final exam. Papers are a lot of work, but his feedback is super helpful. SPSS heavy, but relevant for research

The class is necessary bc it is a flipped classroom, there's very little lecture and lots of group in-class assignments. Allen is a very sweet professor, always comes around to each group to ensure you understand and will help in any way. 3 group papers which are very tedious if you have bad group members. Overall a cool and interesting class

Professor Allen is understanding when you're confused. Class is highly recommended because it can get confusing if you don't show up + classroom is flipped so you do a lot of assignments with a group in class. It takes a bit to get used to, but it actually helps when you're trying to understand difficult concepts. TA is also very helpful!

Love this man. Was VERY understanding during remote learning. This man is honestly the nicest professor in the whole school. A real sweetheart. Everyday, he separates everyone into groups for discussions. However, his lectures are pretty heavy so DO THE DISCUSSION QUESTIONS AND READ HIS TEXTBOOKTHEY ARE A LIFE SAVER.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Geneseo! He is so caring and really wants his students to do well. He goes above and beyond to help you in his office hours and is always available to help via email. While research methods is a challenging class, if you put in the effort and go see Dr. Allen you will do well.

tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']
comment: He's one of the kindest and most knowledgeable professors at Geneseo, and the class was really interesting (but relied heavily on group discussions and textbook readings). The tests were difficult: all essay questions and he grades them so specifically that it's hard to know what he wants from you.

He is friendly, approachable, funny, and loves psychology. Make sure you go to class because he loves in-class group discussions/reports. I struggled with exams because he is very specific in what he is looking for, even though you are allowed to bring notes in with you. It might be worth looking into social psych with another prof.

Dr. Allen is the greatest Professor in the psychology Department. He is passionate about what he teaches which makes it hard not to be interested in the material. He is also very understanding and open to discussion about anything. This professor is one of the few reasons I have remained in college. He is a paragon of what every prof should be.
Study guides he gives really help for the tests

I  enjoyed taking 350 with Allen last summer. The most difficult part was clearly understanding the material we were given. Lots of statistics and charts, which made me lose interest a bit. However,  never hesitate to participate, he is very helpful and wants you to understand the material. He isn't scary at all, just an awesome guy with passion.

Pretty much the nicest guy in the department. The subject is really interesting and Allen teaches well, though we were perpetually behind on the syllabus and spent excessive time on some topics and minimal time on others. Class proceeds by study rather than by topic, so that could be painful. Lots of work, hard grader, would still recommend

I honestly don't know if I've learned anything at all. He is extremely unclear with what he expects, and when you ask him to go over something, his answer is always, "y'all should have that in your notes." I don't know if I've ever been so bitter towards a professor before. Heard he was good in other classes, but NOT in 352.

Uses the word y'all way to much to the point where its just ridiculous. The phrase "dont beat a dead horse" fits this class perfectly. He'll go over the most simple topics soo much but then the test is on a specific detail and if you dont include everything in it its wrong. This class really dragged on. Most of it is common sense.
Really enjoyed the class. Professor Allen is very nice and really approachable. His tests take some studying, but are not so hard that you cant manage them. Highly recommend!!

He is just perfect. His exams are hard but if you take good notes in class and read the assigned books you will do fine. If you have problems with the material just go to his office. He is very helpful

Dr. Allen is quite frankly the nicest man alive. He is just a fantastic person to know. His areas on interest are social and environmental psychology, and this class uses a lot of these issues as examples. Really supportive of students and the department as a whole. He is highly recommended.

His exams are difficult but he is fair grader. I didnt really use the book in his class at all. If your not great at math, no worries most of the test questions rely on knowing the logic rather then the computations. Make sure you attend all classes I skipped once and was lost for weeks.

He is a really nice guy, really cares about the students, I felt like i learned alot about statistics b/c he makes you learn all the logic behind the stats, tests are all written, I'd say if you go to class, pay attention, try hard, & put effot in, you can def do well : )

Dr. Allen is a great person but I was not interested in his class, at all. At 8:30 in the morning, it can be difficult to focus. He wants students to print out the studies but for an env psych class, it seems like a waste to me. The textbooks were interesting, I just didn't like his teaching style. The exams were okay, easier w/ the  study guide.

Allen is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. He is willing to do so much to help you understand the concepts he is teaching, because he cares about them so much. I took it at 8:30am, but turns out it was worth it because of how interesting everything was, and how well he taught.

The logic and mechanisms behind stats are his primary focus - computations take the back seat in his class. Expect to write a lot (in English) for his tests. No homework, but there's an in-class activity almost everyday, so come to class, pay attention, and you'll be golden.

Very nice guy, extremely helpful out of class. Looks over paper as much as you want and willing to give comments. Tests are extremely hard as is his grading on papers. Be prepared to not do as well in this class as in others. Still recommend because the topic is interesting and Allen is helpful and nice

Social Psych with him is an interesting course. He always makes absolutely sure that everyone understands a concept before moving on to the next one. He is extremely helpful outside of class. However, he really is a hard grader, so be sure to prepare thoroughly for his tests.

Also had him for Psyc 288 & audited 251 with him. Heck of a nice guy, extremely willing to help explain things in class or outside. His tests are not easy- usually consist of 5 short answer questions (a choice out of 7 or 8). Gives study guides, but is a really critical grader on tests & papers. Be interested in the class & you should do well!

I never opened the book. Mostly because he doesnt look into the math portion of stats. Basically writing an essay in the bluebooks every test. definitely need to go to class to know the definitions. Need to be able to memorize the definitions and how to do certain things and why they are important. regular stats mad easier than this

attendance counted towards 10% of grade. nice guy, but extremely hard grader on tests. you'll never do as well as you think you did. throws a lot of studies at you and expects you to know outcomes and effects. passionate about what he teaches, funny guy. don't necessarily take 275 if you don't have to

Go to class. tests are difficult, know everything on the study guides he gives out, but still go over all of your other notes. only wrote one paper, easy topic and he pre-read essays and gave comments, which was helpful. very enthusiastic. highly recommended.

his tests are incredibly difficult, he's a tough grader. but he's willing to help, a lot. his class is very boring, I took it at 11:20 and I was still falling asleep in class...overall a difficult class. take it with someone else.

Professor Allen is definately one of the better teachers at Geneseo. He loves his material and not only teaches it passionately, but he dedicates time to making sure that you understand what he is talking about. The tests can be difficult, but as long as you study and put time in, you will be fine. He is very lenient and helpful. Highly recommended

Really hard grader, hard tests, hard papers. Willing to help but it's hard to find times he is available to help.  Subject matter is dry but he tries to make it interesting. He is unclear on many test questions and expextations....be sure to ask. Nice guy.
Overall good teacher. Hard grader, must go to class and take good notes. Tests can be a challenge and you must study. Makes the material half way interesting considering the subject matter.

Social with Allen is a pretty good class to take. He's a hard grader that gives alot of notes and you have to go to class. However, he makes sure that you know everything completley before he moves on. The tests can be prepared for since he gives you then questions to prepare for and allows you to bring 2 cheat sheets. Allen makes the material fun

So dry. Is obsessed with research methods and thinks you should be too. Knows his stuff but assumes you know nothing - teaches down to his students don't take him as an upper level student or he'll make you feel stupid because he assumes you don't know anything about psych tough grader even though the tests seem easy at first
No Comments

Jim is a great professor. He is very organized and will teach you a lot, but he is a really tough grader. You need to give him lots of detail on exams and he'll still find somewhere to take points off. But he's an awesome guy and a great professor, you just actually have to enjoy the subject and try

nice guy but a bad prof. merciless grader. absentminded and unorganized. i wish social was offered w/ another prof. 10-15 pg paper AND you have to turn in full text copies of all your sources. everything about the class was annoying. the book is more interesting than class. avoid if possible.

A very nice guy. Lectures are clear and he makes sure that everyone has the concept before he goes on. He lives up to his reputation of being a tough grader. The class is tough but you learn so much. And he's really helpful and lets you make-up if need be. He does play favorites, which sucks.
He is the nicest guy...  I love everything about him except he is a tough grader in my opinion.
Not my favorite psych professor, lets just leave it at that.
Class is challenging but fair.

Hands down one of the best professors in the psych department.  Very helpful if you put forth the effort,also very understanding of any circumstance you may be going through.However he is guilty of having the absent-minded professor syndrome.

He can be a real jerk, for lack of a much more fitting word if he doesn't like you, and although he is very helpful in the beginning he gets worse with it as the semester goes on, and his clarity is terrible!
I think he's great - very clear - very enthusiastic about the subject matter - you have to work hard and ask questions - if you're dedicated, he'll do his best to get you through.
his stats course is incredibly hard...if you miss one simple concept you can be screwed for the rest of the semester. and don't make my mistake- don't take his class as a first-semester freshman!
He sucks as an advisor and as a STATS teacher...
No Comments

lets you make up tests if you're sick.  :o)  very confusing during stats--spends more time telling you about how ANOVAs and other stats are derived rather than how to solve problems (and expects you to know verbatim how they are derived on exams)

Shes very all over the place when talking through the mechanics of each topic. I dont reccomend because she also claims things would not be on the test and then they are which is why may people did bad on a test. Means well though and is super kind to you if you talk to her. Make sure you go to Si sessions and tutoring.

Very sweet women. Hard to understand in lecture but if you go to her office hours, she's really good one on one. Lot's of homework that can be overwhelming at times especially before a test. Overall recommend she's very caring
good luck. she is hard to follow and talks about all the wrong things. it was hard to understand what she wanted you to do and genuinely couldnt answer half the questions asked in class.

Her slides make no sense, there is no explanation and half the time when she is explain she is confused herself. Very test and quiz heavy and she gives a study guide but the information on it, is nothing like what is going to be on the test.
She wasn't always clear in lectures, but the book cleared any confusion up.  Tests weren't always worded very well, but she is genuinely such a sweet woman.  I enjoyed her class.
A nice lady but not great at teaching. She gets very confused. Tests were pretty easy though and if you read the textbook you'll be fine.

I had Dr Lewis for both Bio 117 and 118. Extremely nice woman, but just not meant to teach. Awful lab professor, never had a clue what was going on, but was an easy A. For lecture, she often rambled about random things and would teach wrong info. Read the textbook, go to SI sessions and do the homeworks and you can get a decent grade.

Dr. Lewis is overall a great person but not very fit for the role of a professor. She taught alongside Dr. Bailey, and even he was confused in some lectures by how she would explain a concept. The concepts she would teach us were a little confusing because she would rant and rant. in general she is not that bad of a professor to have.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Professor Lewis is really nice and cares about her students--go to her office hours!! However, I did find her lectures hard to follow so definitely good to go to SI sessions.
Really nice lady, decent professor, course was split between two professors. Work was manageable.

Shes nice but gets confused about what she's talking about. Sometimes she messes up while lecturing. She also has difficulty with running a classroom, she was not able to get this one kid to stop talking. Overall she's not like the worst professor ever, I just did not love her class and would not take a class with her again.

Lewis is a great professor. You do need to put a lot of work in and going to SI is what saved me. She cares deeply for her students and is accommodating and flexible, I know some people in my class were not a fan of her teaching style but it did work for me. Overall I heavily enjoyed having her as a professor and would highly recommend her.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: Dr. Lewis has difficulty explaining crucial topics taught in the BIOL117 course. I relied heavily on the textbook information and knowledge from my previous AP Biology course. Lectures were a disaster. Tests are easy so long as you have a solid understanding of the concepts.

Do not take this class if you are not a bio major. She is a sweet person but extremely difficult to follow and does not have great teaching methods. I frequently felt completely lost during lecture. I would not have earned an A- if not for the TI. Must purchase Achieve, which is online textbook & homework for about $100. Does not grade attendance

She was very easy to understand and helped map out difficult concepts when asked. Her lectures were decent and tests were fair. You can tell she is really passionate about her work and cares about her students. Like any course, studying will be your best friend, and she gives you all the resources you need to succeed.
Good Person, Not a good teacher.
Gets confused and often gives misinformation. Nice lady but very hard to follow. You have to study ALOT for her tests. Gives fictional case studies that are not helpful.

had her for intro bio lab, she always seemed unsure of what was supposed to be happening. very forgetful and often left us confused to do our assignments alone when she forgot to tell us something, then we would be unable to submit. also had to ask the other professors about every little thing. very nice person but would not take her lab again.

incredibly rude in her comments on tests; not helpful at all, her lectures are incredibly difficult to understand and to follow. She does not prepare you for anything in this class. must've thrifted her phd.
Definitely doesn't have a strong grasp on chemistry and her lectures are very boring. You need the textbook to pass the class. I changed my major after this not gonna lie
Gets mad when asked to re-clarify any concept covered in class. Only grades students based on test performance. Avoid.
worst professor to ever walk out of a university. i believe she got her degree at walmart. having ptsd thinking about this women.

She was a good professor, we went through lectures fast but that's understandable since there's so much material for this class. Found it easier and more helpful for her half of the semester to actively listen instead of write down notes. Overall she seemed friendly, I didn't find the homework or quizzes to be too hard, as long as you study!

She's not an awful professor but in order to get a good grade in this course you really need to read the textbook and make sure you know the material. She tends to get confused a lot during lecture and will give the wrong information sometimes and wont realize until 1o minutes later which is very annoying.
Quizzes are extremely difficult

You either have to go to class and take good notes or read the textbook. I did the former and did fine in the class. Her exams are quite tough and her grading is even worse. You have to make sure she graded your exam correctly because she probably didn't and makes you bargain for points. She gives you a notecard so write everything.

She is NOT good at teaching or being responsive. She taught with Regina Clinton and made tests insanely difficult. You do not have to go to do decently on tests though. She teaches far more than Clinton though and makes your life much harder. I wish that the school would have told me they taught together so I could avoid her.

I took Lewis for Gen Bio lab. Feissner's pre-lab lectures helped me through it because Dr. Lewis herself wasn't too helpful. She would confuse herself during the labs and explaining them, and she wouldn't be able to answer some of my questions. She wasn't terrible, but she wouldn't be my first choice next time.
The class work itself wasnt hard her test were super hard. And she would have a lot of trick questions.
A little bit difficult for being a 100 level class, but she gives question stems before tests and drops a lot of your low grades at the end of the semester. It's not difficult pass if you do the work

This class was hard for a 100-level non-majors bio. However for each test she gave us question stems which helped me get a good grade. Probably would've done worse if it wasn't online. Make sure you read the book

Worst professor I've ever had. Was condescending in our introduction prior to even starting class?? Her exams are crazy hard with only slightly different answers per question. Makes you use lockdown browser to add to this already difficult exam. Last exam average was 67. With 2 points of extra credit. Ridiculous. Not taught like a gen ed.

Case studies are ridiculous and terrible to learn from. Exams are unreasonably hard. Will be tested on material from these fictional case studies, and also from material not taught or mentioned anywhere. Will admit to you that she aims to weed out biology majors early on through these unethical and unacademic tactics.

Bad professor. Condescending, rude attitude. The exams are like reading a foreign language. Slightly changes each multiple-choice question to only leave out one option to confuse you in this class she already teaches like a level 300. Ridiculous.

This is a warning for any student who is about to take Lewis. She does not look to give you points on exams which make up almost 70% of your grade. She is one of the most inconsistent graders and some people will get points for an answer and others won't get any for the way they word it. She acts nice but she really does not care about students.

By far one of the worst professors I've ever had. If you take this class thinking you are going to learn about the introduction of human biology you are in for a rude awakening. She treats the class like it's a level 300 class and the tests are super hard. You will not pass the class if you don't read and practice on mindtap. She does not teach.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']
comment: Its a large lecture class, so you get four tests and that is a large chunk of your grade. MindTap and tophat help a lot though. Shes great. The comments about her speeding through lectures is true, but shes funny, sweet, willing to work with students, and drops your lowest test score. (Keep in mind her tests are crazy hard though)
Lectures do not help you learn anything, talks about things that are not important and always uses metaphors that do not make any sense. Tests are really hard for a required course.

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']
comment: Jani Lewis is a nice lady, but does not know how to teach. She often gets off topic and goes through the powerpoint crazy fast without explaining much. Go to SI sessions and make your textbook your best friend. Keep up with the reading and quizzes if you want to do well.

you will learn nothing in class because everything is explained through weird unrelated metaphors but you have to go to class because attendance counts for your grade. if you read the textbook you'll get an A and she drops the lowest test but going to class was torturous tbh

Nice person and all but WOW she flies through her powerpoint slides way too fast. I always go to class, and I go to exam review sessions and study for hours before the tests but it's literally just memorization of facts that are super detailed. Also the online homework is really a pain and TopHats during class counts towards your final grade

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']
comment: This was her first semester teaching this class & should be her last. She goes way too fast & doesn't give much indepth detail on the material. Very lecture heavy & all tests have at least 5 chapters in each, leaving only 7-9 questions per chapter making it very difficult to be prepared for test. never goes over anything, si sessions will save you.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']
comment: bad

tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']
comment: This is Lewis' first time teaching Biology 103. Her lectures are based on slides that she posts, but they barely correspond with the textbook, but textbook readings and MindTap assignments are required, which makes studying for her exams unbearable. There is no basis for half of her lectures, and she complicated everything. SI sessions saved me.

Mrs. Lewis was probably the worst teacher I had. She means well and is kind, but really cannot teach well and her lectures are pointless. You NEED the textbook, I read that every day and that's where all the test information is. I had her for Intro Bio and your grade is only really based on your tests (80%).

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']
comment: Religiously read the textbook. The lectures are based off case studies which can be very confusing.

She's a really nice women, but she teaches through case studies which doesn't work for everyone. Really read the book and take notes from readings in case it is not covered in lecture and you'll be fine. Study really hard for any type of biochemistry related test she gives, they are a lot harder than the usual exams.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: This course in general is designed to try to kick pre-biology freshman out of the course because Geneseo is unable to handle the large amount of biology majors. So naturally this course is very difficult. Lewis does not make it any better. She gave us a test on 9 Chapters while other sections of 117 had a test on 4 chapters for exam one.

tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Lectures are all over the place and often do not cover what is in the book or test. Read the textbook religiously and you'll have a better chance.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: This class is intended to be a weed-out class, so the tests are pretty difficult. I started to realize that all of the material was in the textbook and that lectures weren't all too important. The best way to prepare for exams is to find practice questions online. As long as you keep up with the material outside of class you'll be fine.
Pretty laid-back in class, but her tests are kind of all over the place and kinda tough.

She's a fantastic teacher (MUCH better than Muench). I wish she taught the whole year. Do quizzes in groups, readscan the text before every class, go to class (duh), and go to the SI sessions and professor review sessions. Dr. Lewis is very kind, approachable, and knowledgeable so don't be afraid to ask her questions as you go.

Lewis is my favorite bio professor I've had. She is a great lecturer and very understanding. However, this is not high school anymore; You have to read the textbook if you want a good grade. There is a lot of info in gen bio and you it's up to you to understand it. Go to the TA every week for review and go to Lewis' review sessions before the test.
Tests are challenging, specific and somewhat confusing. Not very good at explaining things.  Online quizzes and chapter tutorials will help your grade, most answers are already online.
She doesn't tech what's on the tests, too specific.

I love her! She is very approachable and a fair grader. Biochemistry is a tough subject, but her class is taught straight from the textbook. Just do your readings, understand the material, and you should be fine. Very helpful in office hours too. Take a class with her!

She is a pretty good teacher but only teaches half the class while another teaches the rest. Prs questions are a joke and they hardly ever work. Online quizzes are a pain if the wifi doesn't work you can't go back. Very difficult tests that ask specific questions not really relating to class discussions.
She is so nice and knows a LOT about what she is teaching. Also has a lot of energy. Made me excited to go to class. Tough grader, but it is an upper level Bio so I believe it is fair as well.

How can you all rate a professor on a class that's run primarily by the ULIs? Dr. Lewis is a phenomenal professor and incredibly personable. She is more than willing to make time for students that make the effort to meet w/ her. I've taken courses specifically because she teaches them. I HIGHLY recommend her for someone with a true passion for bio!

Pre-lab was awful and the only point is the 10 minute quizzes.  She lectures about random stuff that usually have nothing to do with the lab of thr week.  In lab, she doesn't really do much because its mostly your ULI.  But when grading lab reports and stuff, she takes forever and doesn't explain your grades well.

Very grating, annoying voice. She seems completely unprofessional and couldn't do simple math but expects us to do concentration questions without teaching us about ANYTHING. Posters and presentations were extremely annoying, freshmen bio just tends to suck.

Depends more of which ULI you get, the Lewis basically didn't teach anything we didn't, all the teaching was done by ULI's who are also students mind you, not teachers. You need to follow instructions word for word to get a decent grade. This class was so annoying but I guess necessary

Pre lab lecture breakdown:   10 mins on a multiple choice quiz,                       30 minutes of her talking about things not pertaining to the lab at all and making horrible jokes,             10 minutes talking about the actual lab,               then leave 10 minutes early. Needs to calm it down with the microphone and laser pointer.
Really nice lady - but not a great professor. Not very organized.
Excellent prof.  A bit wacky but definitely keeps my attention.  Hard but fair grader.

Grating, microphone-amplified voice and a deadly boring pre-lab lecture, covered by powerpoint and laser pointer. Many people leave right after the quiz, but Dr. Lewis expects more respect than that. Chances are you can't avoid her. Stay through the lecture to avoid being scolded and for potential extra credit. Use your computer only for notes.
She's nice but the class is confusing to follow

Dr. Lewis insists on using a microphone in lecture which is clearly not needed. When she answers questtions, no one answers because we can't pay attention.  It is easy to get bored.  She tries to make jokes which don't really apply to class.  Is very particular about her rules in class unlike other professors.

Pre lab seems like a pointless class. The lecture is pointless because the same information is repeated in lab.  The only reason we go is to take a quiz, which is given every week.  Many people leave early right after the quiz.  You can get by fine in this class without paying attention to lecture, just print out notes and study for the quiz.
She is extreamly annoying, rambles a lot, I felt like I was wasting my time every week.

she's nice, but annoying. quizzes are random and have a lot of errors which can cause a lot of confusion and poor grades.  her lab lecture was useless; there was a quiz everyday but then most ppl left right after it instead of staying for the whole hour.

She's very nice and seems to know a lot about biology, but not much about anything else. Its funny to hear the dumb things she says sometimes and to watch her students take advantage of her poor classroom management skills. Not very clear but tries to help if you dont undertand something.

The class may not be mandatory, but there are quizes every class (1/week). There are numerous errors in her quizes, which she chooses makes public after most of the class hands them in. Not to mention the fact that the material on the quiz is completly random. They could be based on lab(s) or whatever she feels like that week. Dont take her!

She is very loud and can be incredibly annoying. I'm glad I only have her for lab. Sometimes, I think she just talks to hear her own voice. On a more positive note, she really loves what she does but she should tone it down a bit. Prides herself on being so difficult when all in all, you just need half a brain to master her class.
Being outwardly nice alone doesn't make a good professor. Her feedback isn't the best in terms of editing. She's satisfactory, but I'm sure somebody else could do a better job.

Very enthusiastic.  It is clear she loves what she does which makes class much more enjoyable.  She is helpful and nice.  Class is difficult but not impossible.  Labs are fun.  Wish I had more professors like her!
questions r very unclear. very flaky. prides herself on being a difficult teacher, but shes not so much difficult as unclear. very nice.

DON'T TAKE LABS WITH HER! she is ridiculous; i dun care how nice she is. she doesnt know wht she's doing in lab. might be a smart teacher, but def not a fair grader. handing writeups to her in advacne doesnt work--one group did that and they still got a 65 on it. im very diappointed that i got A's for all my classes except for this stupid lab.

She super sweet and a really great teacher. Always gives great analogues in class to help explain things and you gotta love her powerpoints! Hard tests, but if you know the material, definatly passable.
No Comments

She stumbles around a lecture too often, plenty sleepers in class... If you like a professor that dances around an idea without being too clear, Lewis is your professor. Her exams are "higher application" based (barely textbook context based) She's really nice though. Almost too nice. It's scary.

I actually miss this class. She is very energetic and an incredible people person. Her tests made you think but allowed me to develop my study habits in such a way that I retained more material and learned challenging skills. She made it interesting, and I would probably recommend her for an upper level course.
A challenging but amazing teacher...she is always very understanding and very approachable.  She is always very helpful when you go to her.

Very nice Professor. I had a TA but Dr Lewis came and made appearances frequently. She's a tough grader, but extremely helpful. You can hand your lab writeup in early and she will pregrade it and give it back to you with comments. A smart lady with high standards. Choose your lab group wisely!
More than willing to help with any questions you have on the material. Friendly and really smart...the stuff you learn from her will help you later on even though it seems tough while your taking it.
Print out the powerpoint notes, and read the text.  Freshman bio at Geneseo is a course you need to study a LOT in in order to succeed.
No Comments
will help you a lot with write ups but sometimes thats not enough- she could be much clearer

Very picky grader, but you can go to her in advance and she will look over your work and give it back with comments before it is due. Even after that it is sometimes difficult to understand what she wants.

hard and unapproachable.has a superior complex over the less smart students.extremely hard tests at first gets easier gradually but not by much.assigns too much work too quickly.does not understand that we have other classes.takes forever to return papers
She teaches at a very quick pace, print out the lecture notes to follow along.
She was middle of the road for me. I did not enjoy this class but its more the topic and how it was taught by her than the professor herself

This class actually helped me become more interested in geography and the whole world. Took this class as a chem major for my gen ed. Her tests were quite challenging, especially the wording of questions/answer choices, but I would've done better if I paid more attention. Overall, it was awesome learning about some of the less-developed countries.

Her lectures are the best I've heard and seen from any professor while here at Geneseo. The time and effort put into them, and the presentation slides clearly show she enjoys teaching and making sure everyone can succeed in her classes. Would take again.
I wish I could share my full experience here but there is word limit. do not take this professor she is not worth it. She was not willing to understand or help in any way.
She was very professional and had interesting lectures.
simple class, posts slides but doesn't put a lot of text on them, no problems with her

Rogalsky is by no means a bad professor. Her class is quite organized in Brightspace, and instructions on assignments are clear (and she goes over them in class). The entire class consists of 3 exams, 6 mapping exercises, and 2 extra credit opportunities. It wasn't difficult by any means but to pass you should show up and listen to her lectures.

I think many of these low ratings are unfair, likely because they are people who don't attend class :/ (only 40 of our 75-person class attended regularly). Jen is super nice, and this is an easy class, assuming you show up. We even reviewed test questions/map exercise questions in class. There are 3 exams and 6 map exercises (**Lowest M.E. dropped)

Dr. Rogalsky is clearly interested in this class and makes her students as well. Two actual tests are difficult, be prepared to study. Other assignments in the class are straightforward and pretty simple, but she does hold her students to a high standard on all of them. If you spend the time she expects doing reading and projects, you'll like her.

Dr. Rogalsky is a delightful professor who is very clearly passionate about what she teaches. She is experienced and extremely knowledgeable. I am convinced that most of the negative reviews are from people who didn't go to class, since she gives answers for the assignments in class. So, if you just go, and pay attention, it's really easy.

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: I had to go home halfway through the semester for COVID reasons and she made it her goal to try to fail me. Failed to accommodate me on assignments when I gave her perfect alternatives. Had to eat a 0 for a test because she wouldn't allow me to take it online. Barely passed. She thinks her mediocre geology class is way too important. Stay away

tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']
comment: Rogalsky seems really nice at the start of the semester but she kinda turns to a demon later on. Feedback on maps make no sense. I sit in the A- -> A's for every class but this sucked. Boring lectures. Only way to do okay is reading every word in the book and annotating heavily. Her map exercises, or "hw" never are graded well. VERY tough grader

Will only give u full credit on the Mapping Exams if you write down what she's thinking word for word.  Her instructions are unclear and the powerpoints have NO information.  Genuinely just one of those professors who don't care how you do in the class.

One of my map exercises I borderline failed because I did not understand the instructions I guess, but that grade got dropped. I was scared to take her, but I found her pleasant. I like her honesty and she does give workdays occasionally. Only essay is flexible, 3 tests that arent cumulative, and no real final. Very responsive to questions.

Outrageously harsh grader
Deducts points from work for criteria she hadn't stated
Deducts points by falsely correcting grammar
Unconventional and inconvenient due dates
Assignment instructions and lectures are less coherent than writing/speech she herself deems unacceptable
Always sounds like she has no idea what she's teaching
such a harsh grader, she will take points off for very weird things like where you have placed a comma. doesn't care about students and sticks all her work on her ta
Awful. Terrible. Do not take.

Do not take geography 123 with Rogalsky at all costs. She teaches incorrect information, she is such a harsh grader yet her comments make absolutely no sense or she will dock you off on things that weren't even in the instruction. Her homeworks are so time consuming and are graded so harshly, it is way too much energy and criticism for GEOG 123.
HARSH GRADER

Professor Rogalsky is very harsh on the grading and will nit pick every little thing you do. When I did take her class we had an assignment due and I ended up doing it 2 weeks earlier just to make sure I got a good grade and even though I tried my hardest on it she still picked out the weirdest things to take points off.
Does not listen to student feedback and is not helpful when going to office hours.

goes over things in class not mentioned in the reading for test. Map exercises are time consuming and graded harshly. Current event discussions are a large part of class. Occasionally she will let you have time in class to work on projects as a reward for actually showing up, with free answers as well. Go to office hours if you want her to care

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']
comment: Very overly critical with grading. Seems nice at first but youll quickly see that she can be very harsh. Lastly she treats her students in her 100 level class as if they came in with a background in it when most are there to fulfill credits

Dr. Rogalsky is a decent professor. She is clearly very passionate about her field and is great at explaining concepts in-depth. In class, she's not very personable, but is wonderful for one-on-one help during office hours. She's a very critical grader for the map exercises. Also, make sure to read the textbook as many test questions are from it.

Everything this lady teaches is from the syllabus so there are no surprises, but she is a rude, uncooperative, and uncaring teacher. She wont work with you if it affects her life at all and she is extremely selfish. 75% of the test answers are online so you really dont even have to go to class, but if you have to ask her a question, be prepared

Meh. Seems nice but when it comes to grading your stuff she's pretty tough. Exams are okay but she takes specific questions from the textbook so make sure you read that. Sometimes she will reveal questions that will be asked on exams so i suggest going to class. Allows two opportunities for extra credit. Decent professor but TOUGH grader even on HW

Dr. Rogalsky is very kind and knowledgeable. I learned a lot from class and enjoyed the content. We had to read a lot of scholarly articles, though, and write about them. If you have a background in geography it would make the course much easier. The grading is very meticulous, specific, and semi-harsh, but we received quality feedback of our work

For an intro course, this professor treats her students as if they all have experience in urban and regional planning, and have explicit interest in the field; expects way too much considering many students are non-geog. Lectures are all spoken word, with little information given on slides, making it hard to keep up and to reference when studying.

Rogalsky is so great. I learned so much from her this semester. This class does not require too much work, but going to class and doing the readings will help you pull off a good grade. She is so knowledgable and I hope to take her again at some point!

To be blunt, Dr. Rogalsky is NOT an easy professor. She has very high expectations for her students, even in intro/non-major classes, and her essays and tests are thorough and somewhat challenging. That being said, Dr. Rogalsky is by far one of the best and most knowledgeable professors I've had at Geneseo. I would highly recommend her.

She is the worst professor I've ever had in my college career. She doesn't care about her students at all. I never skipped a class and always kept up with the readings but i still got the worst grade possible. She isn't helpful at her office hours. DO NOT RECOMMEND !!!!!!!!!!! This class brought my GPA down so much

She is an extremely harsh grader on mapping exercises and essays. Tests are not too hard, all are multiple choice with two maps to label, questions can be tricky. Definitely take advantage of extra credit opportunity that is added to the final paper.
As long as you read the instructions closely, you should do fine on the homework assignments, and the tests aren't too hard.

She comes off as a very nice person on the outside but beware that she is an extremely tough grader and will not hesitate to tell you how bad you did on something. she also take points off for not liking the way you shaded maps or the colors you used. There are 3 tests total all multiple choice with mapping and one 1500 word essay. Good Luck

It seems like her intention with grading papers is to make the class feel horrible about themselves. She doesn't care how her class does and the tests have details in them or things that she's only mentioned one time and you'll be expected to remember it. Nice lady but tough class.
Overall easy course, only one long paper during the entire semester. Homeworks are simple and rarely assigned.

Rogalsky is a very friendly professor and more than willing to help if you go into her office hourse. Her lectures are interesting and engaging. The only negative thing is that she doesn't give clear guidelines for what will be on the exams. She tests on information from the lectures and book but she is vague about what she will ask from the book.

I loved this class because if you are not good at taking tests there are other ways to get your grades up. The mapping exercises are an easy 100 if you actual put the time and effort into it and don't blow them off.

I cannot stress enough how much I disliked taking her class. To begin with she expects far too much for what she assigns. When given an assignment directions are generally vague, but then when you get it back she will take off (too) many points for not giving her exactly what she had in mind. She also acts as if you are not taking other classes. :(
Expects too much
Rogalsky is very nice, friendly women who has much experience in what she teaches.  Not a difficult class at all.  Read the chapters the day before each test and you will do fine.

Class isn't hard, but it's annoying. Rogalsky takes this class WAY too seriously for a 100-level, tests are mostly book-based even though none of it is mentioned in class, and you have to buy a review book that is in comic sans. Grades are 3 tests, participation(in-class, online, and mapping), and a 1500 word essay.

pretty easy grader for a 300 level class, but that's about it. she's not too helpful if you're not a geography major (esp if you're an education major). somehow my final grade went from a B+ to a B-... not too consistent.
Very good teacher
You can't get much worse than prof. rogalsky. We're talking about bottom of the barrel as a teacher. I actually got a good grade in her class but wouldn't recommend her to anyone.

She really needs to work on her teaching methods.  It's obvious she knows her stuff and the text is an interesting read but she reads straight from a powerpoint that she later posts online so attending class isnt necessary at all.
VERY HARD class! DO NOT take 377 with her unless you don't have a choice or, don't care if you have a life!!
she uses the same questions in the study guide. Just read the review questions and memorize the terms. Every lecture was interesting and it was my favorite course my first semester

She's a good professor.  Tests are easy or hard depending on whether or not you keep up with the reading or if you come to class or not.  She likes to generate discussions during class and we've watched travel channel shows a couple of times so class isn't always boring.

Every lecture of hers is interesting. She is a very animated speaker and has mostly pictures in and maps in her powerpoints. Since she wrote the study guide, if you go over the review questions in it, you ace her tests.

One word...YIIIIIIIKKKKEEEESSSSSSSS!!!!!  She was by far the worst professor I have ever had (including from the Community college I transfered from). When it came to the tests, all she would say is "it's from the textbook", even though we didnt cover any of the stuff. Then she would ask the smallest details from the textbook. WORST TEACHER EVER!!

This class can be super easy or super hard depending on your knowledge background. Her tests require really specific knowledge. If you know a lot about the developing world and read international newspapers weekly the class is an easy A. Rolgalsky likes to toot her own horn a lot and is sometimes wrong on facts but is generally a good professor.
she is a really nice lady and really easy to pay attention to, but her tests are just ridiculous. they require you to know little facts from the text and its just too much information to remember
Made topic relatively interesting.  Workload is manageable, students aren't really punished for not reading.  I would recommend to friends.

Big lecture so you don't have to go very often. Light workload: coloring("map exercises"), one paper, three tests. Tests are pretty straightforward and are mostly current events related questions. Fulfills two requirements, and you learn a bit of geography and current events. recommended

Loved this class and the way she teaches, but got a C because there is so much matching on the tests that if you screw one thing up, you basically fail. gives 8/10 on mapping exercises without any explanation for points lost besides "more detail more detail". you really have to devote yourself to this class to the the grade you deserve.

Dr. Ware will push you down. She WANTS you to get back up. Fight for your opinion and back it up with justifications. I learned so much about the learning process in this class. Dr. Ware is incredibly intelligent and while she is intimidating, she is fantastic to learn from if you take this class seriously.
As long as you agree with everything she says and spit back her exact opinions you will do well in class. Almost no work is required. Watch what you say because she can be mean and too critical.
Rudest, most condescending professor i've ever had. Clearly only gives grades based on whether or not you agree with her insane beliefs. Worst professor in the SOE by far.

Rudest professor ever,criticizes people for having their own opinions.class is nothing about arts in the community.Molded the class to fit her personal agenda and will only teach about disability(her ideas)and what's wrong with our society. She is relatively easy, she gives breaks from class, but she is very disorganized and will plan to meet with you, then flake.
