She is a brilliant activist professor. If you do not enjoy actually doing MEANINGFUL assignments (which the School of Ed never assigns) then good luck with her class. She is wonderful and extremely helpful as long as you show interest and open-mindedness. She is a breath of fresh air in a rotting tenured pity-those-with-disabilities school of ed.

i took her disability in america intd. didnt have much knowledge on the subject when i started the class, but it literally changed my perception of so many things once it was over. ware is a little disoriented but shes cute and funny and kinda easy especially if she likes you. disorganized but who cares. VERY INTERESTING CLASS. SHOULD BE REQUIRED.
She is a great professor. I would recommend her INTD-105 Disability in America class to anyone. It's a very interesting class, and she is very passionate about it.

keep an open mind and you will be fine. she is an easy grader and although unclear at times about what she expects, she teaches you to think for yourself instead of being a molded "typical" student. i learned more real life knowledge then i could have expected. she is one of the best professors that I have had at Geneseo. definitely worth taking!

Pushes her students to think more critically about the world around them and to apply what they learn in the classroom to how they cope with the world outside of it. Is very receptive to students when they come to her for either help or more information on the subject material, and carries infectious enthusiasm when students enjoy the material.

Although her teaching methods are not the norm for a education professor, Dr. Ware is a great professor that encourages her students to create their own idea when it comes to learning about education.  Don't let her unconventional ways keep you from liking her, if you are open to her ideas you will get so much out of her classes.

Great teacher!  MAy not stick to the curriculum as designed by the school, but teaches you to be an independent thinker who will not always conform to societal pressures.  Extremely nice woman, who always has her students interests ar heart!

Unless you want to learn absolutely nothing about the arts and career curriculum, avoid her at all costs.  She uses the class for her own personal agenda instead of actually teaching the course.  She grades easy, but I assure you, you will learn NOTHING about the arts and career curriculum.

Not very clear in assignments or class material. Little has to do with the course description. Takes offense at other points of view or non-conformity. Teaches from a confusing view of constructivism that is totally opposite of what most people teach.
His tests are ridiculous and hes rude. Dont take him.

If you dont want to fail such an easy HUM220 class, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. He is EXTREMELY rude and does not listen to ANY students opinion. When deciding a hum class to take for gen ed, there are so many other talented teachers other than this man. TRUST ME take a different class
THE WORST TEACHER. DO NOT TAKE. Hes rude and does not keep his word on anything. Again, I emphasize heavily that he is rude.

The worst professor Ive ever taken. Very rude to students and will backlash anything you say. He does NOT take criticism well so dont say anything. JUST DONT TAKE THIS CLASS ITS THE ABSOLUTE WORST. Absolute unfair grader as well.

I made the mistake of skipping class 40% of the time and speed-reading. To pass this class you need to read thoroughly. Study hard. I feel bad for Savellos because he is passionate about philosophy yet very aware that students are bored. One time he didn't know what baby chickens were called so he called them "chicklets." It was great

Savello's tests are ridiculous. He gives you a crazy amount of topics on a study guide and only 3-5 topics are on the test- in GREAT detail. tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']
comment: Elias Savellos is an average professor, he shows up, does his job and then leaves. He explains things well most of the time but then he doesn't explain things well all the time and he only says things once so you have to pay attention. Other than that he sucks, no real metric as to how he grades the tests.
Savellos is very funny and real, but also very  boring. I loved the class, but i fell asleep all the time. In my opinion just read outside of class and go to his office hours.

Savellos is a great guy, but the class can get a little boring. You can choose to either read or go to class- don't do both. He goes over all of the material he assigned in the lecture. The tests are written and you choose between a few choices he gives you to write about, study EVERYTHING on the study guide or you could be screwed. Overall not bad

Ugh. Do NOT take Savellos if you hate sitting in a classroom for 1 hour 40 mins with just the sound of his voice droning on and on.  He does;t use powerpoints or any supplementary material to make HUMN 220 more interesting and I truly struggled to stay awake all semester.

He's great. Phil 217 not very difficult at all if you read and take notes. You're an idiot if you don't go to class because he tells you everything he wants you to regurgitate onto the exams. He posts detailed study topics online way before the test, so study those diligently and you will get an A. Great, energetic lecturer. Will take again.

3 exams are 60% of your grade and they're easy. Pick 3 topics out of 5 and briefly explain, then pick two out of 4 and describe a bit more (1/2 pg each), then pick 1 out of 2 and explain in detail (1 page). Getting an A is tough. 7.5% of our grade was unaccounted for and 20% of our grade he didn't give grades for. Not too bad for hum, though.

Savellos is a good teacher overall. Make sure you participate in class. He'll respect you a lot more. Study! His accent isn't hard to understand. You have to work in his classes. Don't B.S. the tests- he'll know.

He's so awesome! Went abroad with him and LOVED him. He's very clear about what he expects, which makes it's hard not to do well. He really enjoys what he's doing, which makes the class that much better. Highly recommend.

Wonderful person and professor! So smart and understanding. Highly recommend him for Humn I. I took it abroad but I bet he would be just as wonderful on campus. He's very clear about what he expects and if you know what he tells you to, you'll be fine.
Lectures could get long but it was important to be in class and do the reading because he gave hard pop quizzes.
It was the worst class  in my college life.

Savellos is absolutely great. Very interesting guy and easy to talk to. On tests, just write everything you know about a topic and you'll be fine. He's a little scatter-brained but the class is well worth it. He narrows down the content well and knows that most HUMN students aren't philosophy majors. Take him!

Savellos is amazing.  His tests are exactly what is on the study guide.  Pay attention in class and repeat what he says back on the test.  He's extremely helpful and very passionate about the content.  You won't regret taking it with him.  Thank you very much!
Savellos is a nice guy and his class isn't too hard. Since you have to take humn I would recommend taking it with him. It's fairly painless and not horribly time consuming.

tips for savellos in any class: 1. essay test more writing and more detail equals a higher grade. give verbatum back to him what he gives you in class. 2. his study guides are the test. period. 3. office hours are key, he will respect you more. 4. if your'e a girl, he will most likely wink at you but don't get freaked out.

I worked much to hard for an awful grade this semester. I have been told that this is because Savellos has changed as a teacher and person considerably from years past. Keep this in mind when reading reviews dating before '09. You have been warned

This was a strange class. Two or three people would be coldcalled every class to answer absurdly specific questions, essay tests are graded arbitrarily, just a number, no explanation, and he just wasn't approachable. Take with another professor if you can.

I took Reasoning and the Law with him and I have to say that he is a nice guy, but a tough professor.  The class material is hard and he doesn't grade too well.  He marks things wrong, but doesn't always make it clear what is wrong with them.  I got a decent grade in the class, but I don't exactly know how.

Oh Savellos, where to begin.  I had him for Ethics in Business, which I found to be a very interesting class.  Humanities was long to sit through and he is extremely opinionated (papers were kind of hard-but we only had two which was good)...for his tests, give him as much information as possible (he loves when you give him specific dates)

Worst paper grader ever.  Would write red lines on the side of papers with no explanation.  Red lines, that was it.  Did not strike through, or make comments.  Only red lines in the margin.  Very frustrating.

Savellos is an amazing teacher! I took him for Phil 217 and went abroad with him for the Med Roots Humanities trip.  He was amazing at both, his paper requirements are very elementary and his test topics follow his study guides exactly. He is a brillant man and a great teacher. His accent is hilarious and he loves talking about Greece and politics.
awesome guy. extremely smart, very helpful and kind. Took him for metaphysics, phil of lang and phil of law. I'm not a phil major. Really challenges you to think.
He is cool! A true philosopher with true insight. A very smart guy. We take the classes not to get through the exams and the core requirement, but indeed we are there learning a lot.

AMAZING Professor! Absolutely adorable.  Gives a very precise study guide.  He grades fairly, both tests and papers.  However, he does notice if you skip class, but class is fun so it doesnt' matter. He is hilarious if you really listen to him, not to mention he has a great Greek accent.  If you're stuck, take Humn with him.  Def. worth it.

Very interesting man. I hated him at the beginging of the semester, but loved him by the end. He knows A LOT. Trys to get the class involved in the lecture and has a great sence of humor. He does give pop quizes on the reading. His tests are non cummulative and you get study guides for them (USE THE STUDY GUIDE). I would definitly take him again.

What can I say...Savellos was my secret weapon...only professor who thought I was an 'A' writer (I wrote my first paper for him hours before it was due and got an A!).  His tests come right from his study guides...pre-write most topics and you will be all set! (Hint you can find most of his topics right in the index,in headings, or explicitly in notes...no need to do all the reading!)
Gotta love the cute Greek accent

Eh...good teacher, very smart and funny, likable guy who knows what hes talking about. Terrible grader- gives tests back the day of the next one, doesnt give feedback on your work, only a grade...Kinda leaves you with impression he didnt even read your work/test.

I love this guy! His accent is so awesome. But also hes a great guy and he really wants everyone to get something out of humn. He keeps it interesting and factual even tho he's a phil professor. Gives study sheets for exams and picks q's right off it. Best professor to take Humn with, definately.
i LOVED HIM!!! come to class, ask for help on a paper and he'll remember it when grading. study notes from class for tests :) p.s. he loves that he's greek. chat it up with him

Hilarious guy.  Tough though, due to the fact that if the correct answer is point A and point B, and you say B then A, you'll be wrong!  Fairly unapproachable...:(
One of my fave professors ever! Very engaging lecturer and nice/funny guy.  Provides study guides for exams and moderate grader on papers.
Nice guy, makes class interesting.  He's there to help you if you're interested but he's a pretty rough grader.

It has been several years since I graduated, but I can genuinely say that Prof. Savellos was one of the few professors I liked while at Geneseo.  Excellent grasp of the material, intense interest in the subject matter, FUNNY, and a good guy all around.
He was a great professor -- made class exciting!!
Best lecturer ever! Can't fall asleep in that class.
best lecturer ever

Lectures are pretty boring. Most people write notes ahead of time and sit on their phones in class. Mini-quizzes at the beginning of every class, but they are pretty easy if you look through your notes.

Mr. Baecker is a fun, student-oriented, influential, and educated professor. It is important to study the lecture notes, as the test questions he gives are quite obviously based on them. I thought this was the best prof I've had this semester; he was nice and was able to help me when I needed it. Fairly easy grader and very nice, approachable, and funny. HOWEVER, he talks SOOOO fast. If you ask a question, he will go on crazy tangents and take 20 minutes to answer your question. Extremely knowledgeable but be wise when asking questions lol. Fun class overall though.

A good professor!

The class was easy. However, the majority of the grades you'll get will be through your one-on-one meetings with him about your thinking process. Lecture can be boring as most of the time it is him taking notes from students' answers.

He was a good professor and easy grader, it was strange being in a math course with no tests, just weekly meetings. However, he has a very busy schedule and when I couldn't meet with him because his schedule was full, I talked to him about it 3 times and he dropped my grade a whole letter.

Professor Baldwin is a great professor. The course structure is based around weekly problem sets rather than exams. He focuses on students' mastery of the unit (understanding) so you do the reading, go over it in class with some examples, then do the problem sets. He allows remakes as well, and very easy to reach through office hours or emailing

I took Math 104-01 (Mathematical Ideas), a course designed for liberal arts students. However, if you prefer submitting work online, this class might not be ideal. The professor requires an office visit for grading. This guy also uses Calculus Math instead of basic math, and talks about Machine Learning or AI.

There are no exams in this class only problem sets. You always have enough time to do them and if you need to move a meeting he is very accommodating. Lectures can get boring but it is an easy class to do well in. You do not need to be a math genius to succeed.

tags: ['Participation matters', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: The class is now writing 105. This class was so easy. Attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is a part of your grade. I skipped a few times, and he didn't care. Your grade is based on three essays, which you can revise for a better grade. Overall, he's a very nice man and an easy class, although it can be a bit boring.

i don't think i would have found theory of computability interesting with any other prof. it's pretty easy to get a B-C in his classes, but hard to get an A. also can be difficult to schedule meeting times. no tests, so pretty much nothing cumulative you have to really try hard to nail down. definitely one of the easier math professors here

Professor Baldwin is a really nice guy and cares about his students. Explains things very in-depth and hard to follow. Instead of tests, you will have problem sets. You have a week to do them and have to get it graded the week after. Has a free textbook online to use. I was always good at math in high school but found this class to be difficult.

Awesome!!! The only grades are from once a week problem sets and you are allowed to re-do/do another one to replace that grade. You have to be able to explain your work because you get graded by meeting with him to go over the problem set and he will ask you variations of the questions on the spot. He is super helpful, I feel like I learned a lot!

Prof. Baldwin is a very caring professor who wants to see his students succeed and it is very clear. This class tends to be a very repetitive class and essays can be graded toughly, but you always have a chance to fix them. If you are looking for a easy class with a good prof, I would take this. You just may be bored.

Nice guy. 3 essays due. Has bit of a process with essays. 2 one on one meetings needed, peer reviews, a draft, revisons, and a final draft. Attendance doesnt matter. I started with Professor Baldwin half way through the semester because the other professor had left. He was very considerate of the fact that he had only taught us for half the semester and made sure his grading was fair in that way. He really cared about his students succeeding and was always available for office hours.

tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']
comment: Provided free textbook online, which we were expected to do short readings from for every class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it's easy to fall behind if you miss. Didn't give tests, instead gave homework assignments that we had to explain how we did in a 1 on 1 meeting. Fair grader, nice guy, and genuinely helps students wherever he can.

Professor Baldwin really cares for his students and really just wants them to succeed. His grading method is a bit different then other professors but as long as you put in the effort his class is an easy A. Really recommend taking him over any other calc professor!

I really liked him. No exams and the Problem Sets are easy enough. Just make sure to GO TO THE SI SESSIONS, that guarantees an A. He does explain things using intense math, but honestly you don't need to worry about that bc it doesn't pertain to the Problem Sets which is what you are graded on.

Professor Baldwin doesn't give any tests. Instead he gives about 11 problem sets during the semester which are the only grades in the class. The problem sets are pretty fair and he always asks in the beginning of class if anyone has any questions about any set. Also, he always posts notes on canvas and the textbook is free online.

tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']
comment: Just don't. He's too smart for his own good, and grading is based on understanding the material rather than being able to do it. The only grades are homework sets given about once every week. You're graded by meeting with him individually and going over your homework. A lot of times the answers are given in class and posted online so it's really easy. No tests or papers. He's really good at giving students as much credit as possible.

Douglas Baldwin is a really nice guy, and really cares for his students. However he grades weekly homework's on a scale where an 8/10 is perfect work and perfect explanation. In order to get a 10 you have to solve the problems in ways he has never seen or thought of before (btw he wrote the textbook). Calc degraded my self confidence like no other
I had prof Baldwin for intd about secret codes and I believe hes the best instructor anyone can ask for. Hes really caring, love to help, give valuable feedback but hes a tough grader

Prof. Baldwin is a very caring guy. If you are ever sick or anything, he is more than willing to extend your due date. You HAVE to read the textbook pretty much every night and his grading system is stupid, and he grades you on UNDERSTANDING the material. Overall, a pretty decent professor who is too smart to teach this class.

Professor Baldwin is the single best educator I have ever had. He actually cares about teaching and his style of group note-taking and then posting the notes online for review has been exceedingly helpful. Really knows the material and likes to grade assignments one on one.

RUN THE OTHER WAY took this teacher for Calc 1. the hardest class I ever took. Didn't know how to teach the class because he was way to smart for it. comment: Baldwin is a great teacher, although he relies heavily on the use of the textbook. If you can take a lot out of reading the text, you'll do fine. First of all OPEN NOTE TESTS. Second of all, he really cares about you, after I was sick for 2 weeks he allowed to have the rest of the semester to hand in the assignments I missed. He isn't the best teacher in MATH but everything on the tests is in the notes. If you know how to get through a problem you will be all good. Definitely recommend him!

comment: Grades based on his interpretation of how much you understand, not completeness. Can get 6/10 on hw for getting part of one question wrong. Nice, smart guy, who does explain things decently. Baldwin is a really good professor. He always wanted to help me learn the material and was passionate about every topic we discussed. Definitely take him if you get the chance.. As long as you go to class and do the problem sets, you should get an A. Open booknotecomputer was the best thing since sliced bread.

Dr. Baldwin means well, but most of the time is pretty confusing. He doesn't answer questions very clearly, and makes other students in the class answer them. I just wanted to get him to say coolwhip. Amazing guy, extremely helpful. Lots of personal attention. Labs were challenging, but in a good way. Tests are all open book/note/computer. Class was always interactive. Best class of the semester for me.

He is a really good teacher, but you will have to do a lot to keep up with the labs.  He sets aside lots of time for each student, and he's very willing to help. Pretty decent- class was small and sometimes boring due to lack of class participation. Notes are always online so if you miss class its not too bad- but go as much as possible. Makes you come into grade labs which is annoying but class was still worth it.

Baldwin is an extremely knowledgeable professor and extremely helpful. His classes are pretty straightforward and he posts the lectures online so you really don't have to go to class. What a wonderful professor. He knows soooo much, and he wants you to learn. His grading style is awkward, but it works out that even if you do something wrong, if you can probe to him you understand the concept you will get credit. Loved Csci188.

Amazing. I knew nothing about computer science coming into his class, and he made everything so accessible and easy to understand. I write programs for fun now!
Baldwin was my favorite professor at Geneseo..  Gotta love his teaching/grading style.  Take him if you get the chance.
Very excellent prof. Knowledgable and always available for questions. Highly recommended.

Baldwin is absolutely brilliant and possibly the best professor in Geneseo.  His material is very challenging but keeps it interesting all the way through.  If he weren't in the Computer Science department I probably would've transferred out of Geneseo.

i love baldwin

Stacey is a sweetheart and her class is very easy - you don't really need to show up or do the readings as long as you work hard on the papers. She is a fair grader and her grades will reflect the effort you put into your papers, which are the only grades. Listening in lectures is not important since there are no tests. Like a grandmother!
An absolutely terrible professor. Lectures make no sense and she refuses to use an organised lectured method such as powerpoint. She instead gives lectures using a dim overhead projector.
She is a very kind person, but her lectures are scattered and full of random movie clips. It isn't hard to do well in this class, but her grading seems completely random.

Stacey is very smart but she is difficult to follow because I'm not sure she knows exactly where she is going either. She is the sweetest old woman, but lost my papers on multiple occasions. I would take a bullet for this woman, but I would not take another class with her.

Prof. Edgar is very sweet and really just wants everyone to pass so she's pretty accommodating. Sometimes she's not too helpful in lecture and just does practice problems so the key to pass is GO TO TA HOURS!! That's where they go over all the homework and explain anything you need.
Lectures could be better, but TA hours are helpful. READ BEFORE CLASS or you will be confused!!!!

Dr. Edgar is super nice. She brought clementines and cookies to our class every Friday. The class, although small, is entirely run by her lecturing at students. That was the only part I really didn't like about the class. You really don't have to pay attention to get an A in her class, as long as you write good papers (which she outlines clearly).

There are 33 people in my class maybe 9-10 show up each day. She just sits at the top of the class and reads from the book, doesn't actually teach, she's smart but starting to lose it a little. I got a B on both the test and the paper. I didn't even buy the books let alone read them . Humn is a lightweight just make a quizlet before each test

comment: The sweetest woman ever!!! She's a little quiet so sit in the front of the room. She gives a ton of partial credit and acknowledges that you tried (if you actually do). She always answers her e-mails and really cares about her students. The SI sessions for this class are great too and if you do the homework and generally try, you'll be fine.

tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']
comment: Prof. Edgar is sweet, and very knowledgeable, but is unable to pass that information on to her students. She litterally reads from the text and gives no extra insight that you cant find on Wikipedia. We have tried to get her to interact with the class but she waves it off. People have slept in class and she says nothing.

Such a sweet woman. However she isnt the best at explain how to do things in class and sometimes she loses her train of thought. You NEED to go to the TAs if you want to actually understand things. Theyll help you with each of the 13 homeworks and do reviews for each of the 4 exams which are great. Sit in the front for lecture or you cant hear.

Dr. Edgar is a nice person, but I didn't like this class. If you don't understand logic (which is hit or miss), you won't get an A unless you have a friend in class who can help you through it. Go to office hours with the TAs, because you'll get 100s on your homework assignments. Tests were really hard but Edgar does give partial credit.
Professor Edgar is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. The textbook for this class is very short and explains everything you need to know thoroughly.

tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Tests are tough']
comment: Stacey Edgar is extremely intelligent and a kind hearted person. She makes jokes about watching tennis, mostly. This class was extremely difficult for me and there was a ton of homework. She is tough to understand in lectures unless you sit in the front. She genuinely does want everyone in the class to pass, even if it may be difficult.

Stacey Edgar is a hot piece of potato if I have ever seen one. Her intro to logic class was informative and helped with classes later on in the philosophy department. Her TA hours are very helpful. She often shows up to class late because of the intense sport of tennis, but don't be fooled she doesn't play herself only observers at late hours.

By far the hardest class I have taken in my Geneseo career. I took it for my math credit and regret it completely. The material is very hard to understand and she barely explains in class. If you want to pass the class, you NEED to go to TA hours every week. I don't recommend this class to anyone it was brutal. But she does want you to pass.

She's very nice, but starting to lose it a little. The material shouldn't be difficult, but she doesn't explain it well. Her textbook also hasn't been updated since the Cold War, evident in problems about "The Commies". Tests count for a lot, but she drops the lowest homework grade. The TAs are more helpful than her for learning material.

This was the hardest class I've ever taken, I took it for my math credit. Thankfully Professor Edgar really does want you to pass so if you go out of your way to reach out for help, she'll put you in contact with a tutor (who you'll have to pay). You have to go to TA hours to pass the homework, but you don't have to attend class. I barely passed.

Professor Edgar is honestly one of the nicest professors I've ever met. Even if she were an absolute awful teacher, she would probably still have been my favorite of the term. The best part is that she's not awful; she's incredibly knowledgeable about the subject she teaches. Every class is incredibly informative. Papers were plentiful, but not bad

Mrs. Edgar can be confusing in her lectures.  However, she tells you exactly what is going to be on the exams and the TA's give you the answers to all the homework problems.  If you work on a lot of practice problems before the tests, then you will do well in her class.

Mrs. Edgar is a sweet woman, she stays up all night just to have our homework and tests graded for the next class. This class would be a lot easier if it was not a lecture, the material is hard and confusing and in a smaller setting, students could actually ask questions. Learning logic was like learning chinese but she gives lots of resources

This class should be a smaller lecture so people can ask questions. There are TAs available but they're not always helpful either. Professor Edgar lectures the entire time but half the time had to pause and correct herself. A lot of the material had to be essentially self-taught. A hard class but at least I didn't have to take Calc.

Easy class to skip, she's too busy talking the entire class to notice. She's nice, always brings food one day of the week and you'll watch a lot of modern movie clips. The class is dreadful in the morning, you'll want to fall asleep in it with her monotone voice. That being said, zero participation necessary and she's an easy grader on the essays.

She's a very sweet lady but very boring and rants on and on about irrelevant topics. If you can, stay away from this class because honestly you will fall asleep and become a worse writer. You do what she says and it still isnt god enough for her; take another INTD class if you can.

The concepts are difficult. I studied very hard and rarely figured out what I was doing until right before the test. But when it finally clicks, you'll feel great about yourself. As long as you can do the homework (the TAs will help) you should be fine. Save homework, because it can help you study. She writes her own text, very straightforward.
The only hard thing about Logic is trying to stay awake during lectures.

She is such a nice old lady, but the lectures are really confusing and long. She just talks for the full time and sometimes has video clips for you to watch. The tests are also long and are extremely hard. If you don't read, or go to class you probably won't do well. She grades the two essays very easy though so that can make up for the tests.

Professor Edgar is a very sweet woman. However, the way she explains things in class is extremely confusing. If you go to TA hours though, the class isn't hard at all. The TAs help you find all the answers to the homework.

Intro to Logic is a semi-difficult class made impossible by Prof. Edgar.  Sweet woman, but cannot teach this course.  Rambles.  Of little to no help.  The material is impossible to learn because of this.  Her exams are difficult, but she gives a lot of partial credit so most pass anyway, regardless of how little they know. Go to T.A. hours.

Her tests are extremely long and difficult and I did miserable on them. She grades the essays super easy and I got As on both. She will take written attendance if the class is looking small, so if you're on the verge of failing, like me, she will probably let you pass. Just talk to her - she really is the nicest woman.

Really nice lady, but the class was extremely difficult unless you thoroughly read all the books. Her tests were ridiculously hard, lots of obscure quotes that you had to identify and a ton of difficult short answer questions. She grades the 2 papers really easily so that helped bring grades up, but overall it's a really tough HUMN I class.

I am definitely biased because I did not want to take this class, but had to for a requirement. However, I thought it was ridiculous and Prof. Edgar does a horrible job walking through processes and problems.We will go over something so quickly we don't have time to write it down, and then there are questions about it on the test. I don't recommend

Professor Edgar is the most amazing woman I have ever met. Aside from her being an inspiration outside of class though, she makes class fun and easy to understand. Between her emails to give extra examples, and providing TA hours to help with homeworks, it's impossible to fail this class. Plus, it's one of the most enjoyable classes I've taken.
Awesome teacher. Both the sweetest old lady you will ever meet and one of the more brilliant minds in her profession

Prof. Edgar is awesome. Such a nice person and really knows her stuff. Proofs can be tricky at first, go to office hours for extra help with the TAs, it will really help! Take this class, it's very interesting.

Logic. Material is very interesting. She makes perfect sense if you read the book (written by her, her husband, and one of their former students). Not very hard, though proofs appear very difficult at first. Sweetest lady in the world. Extremely helpful. Gave us extra credit for coming in the class before thanksgiving. Take this class.

Logic. Very intelligent woman. She goes quickly. Sort of seems like she lives in her own mind. Difficulty in class is strange; some topics are very easy and some are very hard. Proofs are not as hard as they look. She's very sweet and accomodating.
such a sweet teacher1 it takes a while to understand logic but once you do the course isnt bad just go to calss study do hw n youll do very well sit up front bc she talks low overall love her

She's the sweetest old lady. Brought us Mallowmars and Fruit every Friday. Pretty much just talks the whole time and doesn't ask questions, kind of boring, but she shows videos. Mostly went through Classical Philosophy and some later stuff towards the end. Really knowledgable, very helpful, easy grader. Her Logic class is also great.

She's a very smart lady and often drops really funny jokes in class. She's kind of a quiet talker, so sit near the front. It's tough because it's Logic, but she tries to give every opportunity for you to do well. Very fair and gives extra credit for showing up on days when lots of people didn't. She also drops a bad homework grade. Thumbs up.

Very boring teacher that gives extremely hard tests. Plan on taking on 2 weeks prior study time because there is so much information that studying the night before or even 3 nights before is impossible. Nice lady but very hard class. She grades harshley. Not a class I would take if one had an actual life outside of class. I would not recommend!

Very monotonous. Just read the handouts she gives you, no need to really read the books. If people stop showing up for class, she will take attendance. Not my first choice, but not terrible overall. Went from a 73 on the first test to a 93 on the second. Essays can also be very helpful to your grade.

Class was Philosophy of Love. The only grade we had was our papers. The lowest grade I ever saw was a B+. She is very flexible with due dates as well. I loved how she would always show clips of movies at the end of class. While her talking is sometimes monotonous, she is a very intelligent a interesting teacher.

One of the worst classes I ever took at Geneseo.  She is dull, the tests are very hard and very long ( at least two hours) and she grades papers harshly. All of her paper topics require a significant amount of outside reading and research.   Her lectures consist of her standing up and speaking in a monotone for two hours, no discussion.

Took her for logic last semester and "Evidence" this semester. Today is the day before spring break, so she took my class (18 students) to breakfast at Micelli's on main street - her treat. And we got extra credit for showing up today! (She'll give you extra credit if you show up on, say, the Friday before a break or something like that). AWESOME.

She went over the material so fast in class I could barely keep up with her. I went to every TA and study exam session and still ended up having to withdrawl from logic with a "D" on my midterm. Nice enough lady but her tests are imposssible and her teaching style is not suited for an "intro" level class.
A good teacher who knows her logic, she's funny and has a style all her own. Not always "with it" during lessons though, she sometimes trips herself up.

she hands out a plethora of notes on the books so you can get by with just skimming them...tests are LONG (I came in at 7:40 am and finished at 9:40)-COME IN EARLY FOR THE TESTS!  she grades easy on the papers (give them to her early for feedback)
She is so funny, really sincere too. I enjoy her jokes; she's like a little pug. She's a staunch character! <3
took for philosophy for logical math. hard class. i think the class (material) is just so hard. A LOT OF STUDYING TO DO. just take calc. but a nice lady though.
She's a funny lady, but her tests are murder. She grades papers easier than tests, and is very understanding about late papers.  She's pretty humorous if you can pay attention at 8 AM.

Extremely nice person and an easy paper grader, but her tests cover tons of information and are very hard. I would recommend her for Humanities, but mostly if you know people that have taken her class before, as her tests seem to be similar from past years(she passed around an example test for test 1).I'm assuming thats how ppl got As on the tests.

extremely smart woman, who can do proofs rediculously fast. material isn't that hard and there are tons of TA sessions where you can get help before tests and get hw answers. she is very nice and actually occasionally funny, although she does dress a bit like a mideval magician. overall good gen ed class to take.

Very intelligent and very helpful, but it's hard to keep one's mind from wandering in lecture as the seminar is not discussion based, and only consists of her talking to the class. Lenient with due dates on the 8-9 papers the course requires. Really nice lady.
Incredibly boring class but I came in with zero interest in logic and left truly enjoying it. TA's are extremely helpful. It was my easiest A at Geneseo.

I found her difficult and frustrating at first, but she really grew on me. She's very happy, relatively funny, and a sweet person. She's a great professor and supplies lots of help: review sessions, TAs, and office hours. She also gives extra credit if you come to class on days she expects no one to come. so GO TO CLASS. She's a great professor.
She is a nice woman, but very boring.  All you do in class is listen to her, but at the end you watch a movie clip.  Easy class with only 5 papers.

Wonderful woman! She knows her stuff and loves to talk to you about anything you have questions on. Grades papers fairly. No tests at all - our final exam was a party in the Welles lounge! She also brought us candy/cookies on Fridays. Best teacher ever. :)
great teacher- easy to follow. goes somewhat fast, so keep up or you might get lost. go to class everyday, go to the review sessions, hand in hws you'll get an A.
class can be a little boring, but the work is easy.  She is pretty funny too.

I LOVED this class! The workload isn't that bad, and she drops the lowest homework grade. If you pay attention, go to class, and actually do the work, you should have no problem getting an A! She gives a lot of examples in class that are very helpful for the homeworks/tests. And she is one of the nicest professors here!

Do not take Logic if you don't have to! It is hard and requires a lot of outside dedication. You learn new things each class so don't skip. Go to the TA's for homework help and go to her office hours if you need help. The class aside, she is very nice and actually met with me at Miceli's one morning to go over concepts I didn't understand.

Great Professor! Very funny and down to Earth. Material can be hard, but there are lots of TA hours for homework help. Tests are very straightforward, and she tells you exactly the format and grading system. Can go too fast at times, but is still an awesome professor. Definitely take her if you can.

obviously knows her stuff, but she sorta just goes on through it...really hard to keep up with, especially if you skip a class. pay attention and practice and you'll be fine...not to mention she is one hot piece of ass

Unless you downloaded information on how to do logic into your brain before this class, don't expect it to be easy. by the time you finish writing step #1 of a proof on your paper stacy's done with it and on to the next one. if you ask her politely to slow down she will look at you as if you made the suggestion in another language... GOOD LUCK

Professor Edgar is a really nice lady.  She grades somewhat easy on the papers and helps you out if you are confused. Be prepared to write 5 papers on some topics that can be challenging. Read the books too. They will help you write your papers.  The love movie clips at the end of each class were really nice.

Great professor, go to all the classes, pay attention, work hard, PRACTICE and it will all come to you. Helpful, approachable, very nice. There is a high number of homeworks but she drops the lowest grade. Very, very enjoyable class.

GREAT PROFESSOR! seriously one of the best experiences of my college career was taking this class with her. it's fun and interesting, and she just makes it that much better. don't expect to walk into this class and do nothing...hard work is expected and well worth the effort. great times.

Intro to Logic was a fun and interesting class.  Mrs. Edgar has a unique sense of humor and is a very intelligent person.  As long as you pay attention, do your homework, and study a bit before tests, you'll pull off at least an A- relatively easily.
She was able to make what was a boring unit in high school into my favorite class.

yes, LOGIC IS HARD. even if u like logic or think u know what ur doing, it's still hard and takes up A LOT of time. but once you understand it, the tests are not that hard, TA and friends provide the hw. w/ a tutor, i pulled of a B. but that took hours! edger is a sweet old lady.  she's harmless and has a good sense of humor.  so don't be mean!

For me, logic was only hard at first.  You just need to change the way you think.  She did an excellent job explaining everything, and once i got it, I found myself solving the problems before she would finish the demonstration.  She's also very funny.

BE WARNED: LOGIC IS HARD! She's a great lady and a very funny professor, but she often moves too fast for everyone. It's obvious she knows what she's talking about, but keeping up with her is another story. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS! They practically give you all the homework answers, and they're really helpful in explaining material before a big test.

Edgar has some interesting stories, and great movie clips, but the class was boring, because she would just paraphrase whatever we had to read...there was no analysis on our part, and she did not encourage discussion of any kind..not what I expected from a college philosophy class.
No Comments

I wasn't exactly sure what to expect from this class, and I've been pleasantly surprised by Professor Edgar.  She presents the course material in a way that it is crystal clear and easily digestible.  She is a fine instructor and a charming person.

Logic is hard. Her TAs sucks. She teaches something new ea. day, u CAN'T skip class, takes a lot of outside Dedication. You'll know whats on the test before hand though. But she the nicest old lady ever! She's been through a lot, be nice to her, if not, she won't punish you for it, thats the kind of lady she is. wouldn't hurt a fly. you'll like her
Very friendly, helpful and fair.. Great professor!

class was very straightforward--you always know what to expect from her.  Easy essay grader.  Tests were a bit long with a lot of writing.  I never skipped but since everything comes off her handouts it would be easy to do so.  Incredibly nice woman.

Very sweet lady with a great sense of humor.  I thought I was a horrible writer but i get A- on all the papers.  She's a little boring sometimes but she'll bring in fun movies and sometimes be fairly interesting.  Definately recommended.
Go to class, pay attention... EASY A.
Offered TA sessions, but never helped herself.  Moved very quickly in class and that made it hard to grasp the concepts because they were just thrown at us quickly in a short class.
This class was great!  Kind of boring sometimes but mostly very interesting.  Pretty easy grader.

Wonderful teacher, so helpful and approachable. She loves what she does and knows alot about it and it is evident. Very fair grader, VERY leinant when it comes to due dates. She is so nice it kind of makes you feel bad if you miss her class. Overall wonderful lady.
Very sweet lady, I found her Humanities class boring but she is cool I bet she'd be good for a different class
Liked her for Logic, probably because I liked that topic.  Disliked her for Hum I.  I couldn't grasp it from a Philosophy teacher's prospective.  If I could take it again with someone else, I would.

GREAT professor!  She cares so much about her students and is extremely helpful with making things as clear as she can.  She understands not everyone understands the topic like she does and tries to make it easy.  She gives great help in office hours, too.
very clear, very nice, very good teacher
As long as you go to her class and read the material, you'll do fine.

An awesome lady! If you do the work and go to office hours you'll do very well. Sometimes goes a bit too quickly in lectures in an effort to give as many examples to help you out for the hw's and exams. Good  humored and approachable.
Such a sweet woman!!! I had her for INTD105 and I hope to be able to get her for HUMN!!!! Sometimes its hard to stay awake since her classes are so early...but def. worth getting up for!
shes awesome!  great teacher!  i'm not a big fan of logic but she made it ok.  Not super easy class, but A/B is no problem.
She's a very nice person and the type willing to help.  If you use the phil help center you can't go wrong with this course.
Awesome teacher
Very easy course, do the homeworks, you dont need to come to class- the whole course is in the book that she wrote, very sweet and willing to help
kind of boring, but gives a lot of examples that help more than anything. likeable.
A great teacher...around for help...willing to listen to her students...one of the best at the college
Unique, but very enjoyable (cartoons in class) and personable. Thought she was a tough grader.

Seth is literally the happiest professor you'll ever meet. His classes are exciting and engaging, and hes always clear about how he grades. The tests are only hard if you didn't take good notes. Also, he loves okapis, keep that in mind, it might become extra credit!
Easy tests, grades the final paper slightly hard, but easy class to get an A in. Interesting lectures and solid dude all around.
Seth's a good dude. Class is easy and his lectures are interesting. I usually went to class but a lot of people only showed up for the tests. All notes are online.

Unlike some of the other professors, Prof. Cavello is kind and not arrogant. He states his expectations clearly and his lectures are interesting. He cares about you as a student, and is willing to adapt to anyones learning style. No stress invoved here.

Prof. Cavello is a really nice person. Truly cares about his students. He is my second favorite Geog. prof behind Dr. Norris. Prof. Cavello has traveled many places and gives you insight into those that are pertinent to class. Will change his style of teaching if you learn differently. Always answers  emails promptly unlike most.

Awesome professor! Has so much knowledge and passion, as well as a great sense of humor. He is sarcastic most of the time, but is extremely helpful and kind. Talk to him one on one, he seems really interesting. Take this class!!

Seth is awesome! Currenly doing his PHD and UB, and still makes time for his students. His lectures are very clear, interesting, and easy to follow. You can tell he is really passionate and tests are easy if you study a little. The textbook is entirely optional. Easily my favorite professor at Geneseo so far and I really hope he never leaves.

Class was super interesting and very easy.  Lectures are interesting, seth has a self-depricating humor that makes the class enjoyable.  Very clear on what you need to know for exams, which are very straight forward.
Melanie is OK. Her assignments are definitely interesting and fun to participate in, but sometimes things she would say in class or post on Brightspace were unclear

I took this as a summer class to fulfill an music/art credit. In 6 weeks, we had 6 quizzes, 24 discussion posts, 2 essays, a midterm exam, a final project, and a final exam. comment: The class mostly consisted of reading for homework but instead of discussion in class, it was very simple things like going over plot, characters, etc. Interested in the topic but not personable. Presentation is graded harshly but I found the tests were very easy. TAKE NOTES IN CLASS. Gave a final paper AND exam during exam week which was terrible.

She is a lovely person and this was a very interesting class! There is a lot of material to read but they are good reads. Class consists of three hour exams (not cumulative), one final paper, one class presentation and that's it! She does in class writing assignments which counts towards participation. Thinking of taking her again, she's great!

Dr. Blood was very accessible and eager to help. 203 is the intro to the English major, and Dr. Blood went out of her way to explain the workings of the English department to us, becoming an advisor and an instructor.  In terms of work, you do a lot of reading. Tests are fine if you listen in class. You're encouraged to think creatively. Loved it

Dr. Blood is a really nice professor. Her tests can be a little challenging, but to get good grades you just need to read closely. To get A's on the writing, talk to her about it and follow her rubrics. Her reading choices are always very interesting. Come to class and participate.
Solid.

Great alternative to THEA 100. Smaller class, discussion based, 5 projects, 2 papers, 2 exams make up the grade. Great professor, approachable and always helpful. Definitely recommend Melanie for any class.

Professor Blood is a great professor although I did not enjoy the class that much because it was primarily run by discussions. Luckily, that did not factor into our grade. The grading rubic is great because there are NOexams. Just three papers, four presentations, and class participation(attendance). Some of the movieswere interesting. I recommend.

Melanie is one of my favorite professors. She really knows the material and makes the class pretty enjoyable. Exams are pretty challenging but she gives lots of partial credit and some extra credit if you attempt every question. If you need help she's always willing to point you in the right direction. Not an easy A but a great prof.
Easier ways to fulfill the core, but people who are really into staged theater will like her. Participate in class and study and you should be able to manage an A or A-.
Prof Blood is very helpful and accessible.  Very enthusiastic in class.
She knows her topics!
not the nicest person in the world, but certainly an expert in her field.
Tough but fine. Good for a core.

uses TAs to do the work for her, favors majors, mideterms and finals sometimes have ridiculous unimportant questions or small details. pop quizzes were annoying, books were not really discussed, class was boring, she is not helpful or caring. not recommmended at all

Basically uses TAs to control the class. Meet in large groups every other Friday and also meet in smaller groups to do papers which are due at the large group meetings. Acts like she knows everything and doesn't wanna give you the time of day unless you're a major. WAYYY too much work for 100 level class. Hate theatre more than before i took it

I LOVED this class and Melanie was fabulous. She really knows a lot about theatre and she brought a lot of variety to the classroom, mixed it up with discussions, videos, projects, presentations, etc. Its a great class, and if you are interested in theatre you will get a lot out of it. Seems like a good person, with a stern disposition.  I found her to favor the theatre majors, but then I suppose it's normal.  It's such a clique.  My experience in her classroom was not a good one.

nice professor if you're in sopa, otherwise she won't pay any attention to you at all.  In video production, she tried to explain things to us but half of the time she couldn't figure them out herself.  If you want to learn about editing, don't take this c

A lot of people think Melanie is a hard grader but she's really not. As long as you do your work and are willing to try new things, you will have an A. She likes to get to know each of her students individually and acts like more of a friend than a teacher. I highly recommend taking her classes.
I LOVE Melanie. She actually knows what she's talking about, is really really really nice, and is very approachable.
She's tough but if you give as good as you get she is really rewarding
One of my favorite professors.  Not easy, but as long as you're willing to do the work, you'll get through.  Very fair.

If you are not a theatre major and have no interest in the art, do not take her class.  She is all right overall but she has no curve and you have to work hard to do well.  She's not easy but is willing to help.
Fair professor, fairly easy A.  You write a paper in a group, and there is so much extra credit offered that you can mess up and still get an A.  Take her over Krickmire if you can.
You'll read some Shakespeare and Moliere and some junk you won't care for.  You get to work in the play.  Shes a decent lecturer.  The tests are pure regurgitation though.
She unfairly bounced me out of class, so that her theatre suck-ups could drop/add.  Not fair!  I REGISTERED FIRST!
As long as you do the reading and attend class you should do fine.  Other than that there isn't too much work, and the paper you do is in a group.

Very unclear on what his expectations are which makes assignment's confusing and hard to complete. Lectures was not mandatory for attendance but even with going to every lecture a lot of work needed to be done outside of class to take the notes as he goes through the slides way to fast.
Grade made up of many quizzes and four non-cumulative tests. Tests were open book. Quizzes followed the lectures and readings. Really nice guy and seems to care a lot about his job.
Seems to be very unorganized and weirdly condescending when answering questions. You are guaranteed a 100 on every homework as long as you do it though which is very nice. Not a good lab instructor.
He's a very nice and understanding professor, but seems confused at times especially during any labs. If you take good notes you will do well especially because the exams are open notes.

Be aware for 103: You are REQUIRED to purchase a $150 textbook in order to complete the assignments you are graded on; as they are locked behind the digital textbook. Holtzman is extremely knowledgeable, however he moves at a very quick pace in lecture, making it hard to follow at times. Exams are very topic-dense, covering multiple chapters.

I had him for BIOL 118 (which is a Lab) 
He was almost never prepared for lab and rarely was able to quickly or accurately answer questions. The TA was super helpful and was way more prepared and way easier to ask questions. David also grades Lab Reports and Projects really harshly but your grade will be boosted by the prelab assignments. 2/10 :(

Class is extremely lecture heavy and the lectures don't line up with the tests. Tests are open notes which is good but you could write down every detail from the slides and still do poorly on the exam. The tests will also cover multiple subject-heavy chapters, making it very difficult to study.
Made Human Bio memorable and enjoyable. Lots of material covered at once during lecture. Always an entertaining class.

Biology is a very tough class but required for my major.  Dr. Holtzman does the best that he can to present the material.  It did help having an SI in the class to come up with ways to help students understand the material.

You cover SO much information for each test it can be overwhelming at times. I studied a decent amount and for each test. There are no easy sciences but if youre good with memorization this class might not be so hard for you. Also the final is the easiest test and he curves your grade at the end. I went from a B- to B+

Professor Holtzman is a great professor, hands down. I took him for Bio 314 - biodiversity in belize and it was the best trip of my life. He is very knowledgable and he is always willing to bend over backwards to help. I highly recommend that you look into this program because I would go on it again in a heartbeat.

I gave a review for Holtzman where I gave him a 1 for easiness. I don't think that was a fair review. At the end of the semester he ended up implementing a huge curve and I went from a B to an A. Be aware there is a curve. I still had to work VERY hard for the A though, not the easiest class.

I do not recommend taking Human Bio as a science gen ed. He may be better for bio majors but this gen ed was far too difficult for non-majors. It's an interesting class and it's very possible to get a B, but getting a A would require you to be a mastermind.

Do NOT take this class with Holtzman. He is very knowledgeable on the subject matter, but treats the non bio majors as majors and holds them to the same standards. The exams are extremely difficult even with a lot of outside help. Only take this professor if you have a STRONG background in bio/are a bio major.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. While Holtzman is very knowledgable, he treats this class like it's for bio majors (which it's not). The tests are extremely difficult; I studied hours and hours for his exams and did bad. His PowerPoint slides are all over the place and he does not connect the concepts so it's difficult to know what he's talking about.

Everything everyone else has said is true. He posts lectures after the class and goes through the slides so quickly that you don't get anything out of it. His tests are very specific and hard to do well on. The final grade is made up of the tests only so it's hard to succeed. He treats the class like it's for bio majors when it's just not.
AVOID taking this class if possible! Tests are extremely hard and are only MC (106 questions). He just reads off of the power point. He only posts the power points AFTER lecture.

HORRIBLE. This class is impossible and he does nothing to help. He just reads off the slides and then posts them online after class. His practice tests are nothing like his exams (which are almost impossible to do well on).

Hes a great professor! I would highly suggest to anyone. His class consists of tests (that he always gives you some extra credit possible) and  quizzes and 2 presentations (which are easy As). His lab is difficult and you have to know a lot of specimens in a lot of detail but I learned a lot and was easily my favorite class and professor thus far!

Do not take this class if you're looking for a natural science! His tests are 106 mc questions. His practice questions are always way easier, SI sessions are no help tbh. His grade is based on 4 exams, 20% on 1st two and 30% on last two. Gives no extra credit, unless youre good at bio, don't take this class.

Neural Development with Dr. Holtzman was a really great and interesting class. He was very organized and most of the information was really cool. The only thing I didn't like was that your grade is just 2 midterms and a final so each exam is 30-35%. He is a great professor!

Holtzman is one of the most interesting guys at geneseo. Always posts notes before lecture, answers questions in detail, and provides fair but difficult assignments. Class isnt mandatory but it is extremely helpful. Dont bother buying the textbook, didnt use it once. Beware his lab though, it is more difficult than the class. Also - field trips.

Dr. Holtzman is extrememly knowledgable and has had a ton of experience in the fields that he teaches. He is super easy to talk to and eventhough his classes are difficult you leave with a good grasp of the material and the learning is enjoyable

This class is an easy A. I took it once a week so the lectures were very long, but Professor Wahlstrom fills them with his personal stories and examples so that they are  not bad. Tests are long, but they come straight from the reading. He gives exact instructions for the paper so it is easy to ace. On top of that he offers lots of extra credit.

Wahlstrom is interesting guy. In this class, you will watch an adult film. I am not kidding. It will be the most embarrassing thing you do at SUNY Geneseo. However, his lecture are long, boring, and pointless for the exam. Read the textbook. The exams are 90 questions long. All based on the text book. Lecture are pointless but make it to class.

I took the once-a-week intro class and it was so easy and rather interesting. He's a really nice guy, and has funny stories to accompany the 2 and a 1/2 hour class. Tests are basically vocabulary and readings from the textbook. The final essay is an easy 100, as long as you follow the guide. Minoring in Sociology because of this guy!

Go to class for the notes. Bring your laptop to take notes. Lectures are long and dry but you need to show up to class to get the notes. For the exams, reading the textbook is most important. Skim notes. Make sure you know everything on the review sheet. For the paper, follow the rubric and you'll get an A. Overall, very easy.

Follow the syllabus by reading your textbook and an A is yours. If you want the extra credit from reaction papers and you don't want to write a lot, treat them like worksheets instead. They should be about a page or so each, double spaced, and just answer the questions in a straight-forward manner. To study, review the text by studying definitions.

Awesome professor!  He is really nice and funny.  He made a 2 1/2 hour class seem to go back really quickly.  Fair grader, and up to 6 points of extra credit on your class average if you write two small reaction papers.  Great professor!

the 2.5 hours was kind of painful, but it was once a week so it wasn't that bad. The class wasn't terribly interesting, but it wasn't bad either. The best thing was how easy it was. The paper is amazingly easy. The tests are harder, but you can write 2 reaction papers on movies he shows for up to 6 points on ur grade, making this class an easy A
Great guy to have as a teacher. It's unfortunate he's only at Geneseo as a part-time teacher. Read the textbook and a high A or A+ is yours.

Guy cracks me up with his mannerisms.  Just read the text using the review sheets he gives out.  Only graded on 3 tests and one paper (and a possible 6 points extra credit).  Don't always have to attend.
Very interesting class! It's easy too. Wahlstrom is a great professor.

Great teacher with a lot of fun stories to share. The class IS very long, but it's an easy A as long as you show up and write the papers. He gives a lot of extra credit and although the exams are long, they're not difficult if you follow the study guide and skim through the book.

Great teacher with a lot of fun stories to share. The class IS very long, but it's an easy A as long as you show up and write the papers. He gives a lot of extra credit and although the exams are long, they're not difficult if you follow the study guide and skim through the book.

very interesting lectures for an once a week night class. He makes the 2&1/2 hr worthwhile. However, you must read over all the notes he shows on the projector and some from the txt book in order to take his 100 question multiple choice exam.

very easy class. teaches for 2 hours and 15 min straight, and it goes by faster than some of my 50 min classes. exams are only 50 questions now. find someone who took the class the semester before you, he reuses tests! and check the syllabus, he won't warn you when the paper is due, i learned this the hard way! otherwise, great guy, easy class!

He does not make the 2 1/2 hours go fast. The class takes forever, and it has tons of worthless notes! He basically tests only on the text, and the tests are repetitive and ridiculously mind numbing. Try answering 100 multiple choice questions on little to no information. Choose something else for your social science req., like anthropology.

the class is awesome. he makes the 2 1/2 hours go by so fast. its honestly the only class i look forward to going to. he tells awesome stories...and makes it really interesting. its the only class i don't wanna fall asleep in

He is one of the best professors i have ever had.  His tests are tedious because there 100 questions, but the class isnt too bad, and 2 1/2 hours flys by.  He's also a really cool guy if you ever get to talk with him

He's a great person and the 2 1/2 hour class goes by really fast with his stories, the first test was an eye opener - don't trust the review sheet to help you through the whole test - it only represented about 50% of the questions. Take this class if you can just know the tests aren't too easy
Great guy. He's pretty hilarious in that grandfatherly kind of way, but he is very intelligent and fair grader.  Take his class if you can!

Makes class interesting by giving examples or telling short stories to explain things.He teaches in a way that keeps my attention.He uses powerpoints so that we have something to look at rather than make us try to take notes on every word he says like some other teachers at Geneseo.
this dudes the man, he used to teach at prisons, now he teaches at geneseo, go figure
Very nice and entertaining, makes a 2 1/2 hour class go by very fast! Tests are not too bad, gives one paper but pretty much outlines the entire thing for you. Take a class with him if you can!

Professor Bilo was one of my favorites! Her knowledge and kindness made the class enjoyable to go to and also inspired me to pursue a career in English adolescent education ! As long as you show up and participate in class you will do well!

Bilo is the best. This class is very much participation based, so you get out what you put in. Every day when we started class we arranged our desks in a circle for discussion, but it felt very nonconfrontational and easy to participate. Cannot recommend enough.

You get what you put into this class. The deeper you reflected on the readings, the stronger you became as a reader. As she once said, I can read like a writer. She is incredibly diligent in responding to questions thoroughly and enthusiastically. She is very well-versed, gave us ample opportunity to understand exactly what she is knowledgable in.

Professor B is amazing! She gives kindergartener teacher vibes with how understanding and kind she is. She provided all of the readings for this course on brightspace, no purchase necessary. Drawing for our Graphic Memoir class was not my strong suit, but she made everyone feel so comfortable in the classroom- it was awesome! Love love love Sonya
Love love love Bilo. Could not recommend her enough!!!

She is an amazing professor and helped me a lot with improving my creative writing. She helped me apply for the creative writing track and advanced fiction workshop. She also was willing to read things I wrote outside of class and was extremely supportive and encouraging of all the students in the class.

I took my first creative writing class with her when I was a freshman, and it is the reason I decided to fully commit to the creative writing track. The culture of her classroom is very welcoming, respectful, and calm; you can most certainly tell she knows what she is talking about and I found that the readings were frequent, but entertaining.

The sweetest prof you'll ever have, she is so understading and loves what she does. Class focuses on incorporating her short slideshows into individual practice by the end then sharing with groups. If you don't like others reading your work then this isn't the class for you. She makes everyone feel comfortable and heard. Love her!!

She was amazing. The sweet, young, caring English teacher type. Definitely participate and show up to class and you will do great. The readings are NOT hard at all. Minimal group work except for a big project, multiple extra credit opportunities. Great teacher!

4 credit class, pretty much guaranteed an A if you show up to class. Remember to do the readings, she will go occasional reading checks. Very understanding, caring and sweet prof. If you have social anxiety, TAKE THIS CLASS. It will help you grow so much and learn to articulate your words. As long as you try, you'll do great. Class is very long.

comment: If there is one professor at this college that i love it is professor B. She deserves the world as all she wants for her students is the absolute best. This was a creative writing class, and going into it, I was very insecure and shy, and she fixed my mind set and made me an amazing and confident writer. I owe this lady my life she is so lovely

Prof B. is by far one of the best professors at geneseo. If you want to take a creative writing class I 100% recommend taking from her. You have to read a few short readings before coming to class and then you are prompted a free write near the end which you will share in small groups. Make sure you actually do the readings  and show up.

Professor Bilocerkowycz is really sweet and I really enjoyed taking her class. She is very understanding and helpful. I was falling behind on an assignment and she gave me extra time to work on it without me really even having to ask for it. There is reading for this class but it is all pretty manageable and interesting.

Professor B is hands down my favorite professor ever. She has the kindest heart in the world, and believes everyone walks in her room with a gift for writing. Even when I thought my writing sucked, she lifted my spirits and told me how much gift I had. She is such an easy grader and I recommend anyone to take a class with her.
